en.text: The graduation of the 150th class of Gilead:
Who would have thought that we would have
150 classes of Gilead?
And probably, for you students, you were wondering if you would survive
to the 150th graduation.
Over the years,
graduations of Gilead have taken various forms.
If you look at this photograph,
you’ll notice that for the 7th class,
the graduation was in 1946.
And what do you notice?
The guests who came along were
in the open air, hoping for good weather.
And I’m told there was no—
It wasn’t a ticketed event.
So just those that wanted to come along
came along.
And then notice in the next one here
that we’ve got the president
giving one of the talks
on the stairs leading up to Gilead.
Well, things have changed.
In 1953, the 21st class
graduated at Yankee Stadium,
and you’d imagine that was a huge event.
And in fact, it commemorated
the tenth anniversary of Gilead
and was very appropriate because that was
a very special year, 1953.
That was the year that the U.S. government
granted us legal status
so that we could have foreign students
come and join the school.
And then, of course,
no matter what graduation we’ve had,
there’s always the joyous look
on the faces of those graduating.
That’s the common denominator.
Of course, in recent years, we’ve had some very different graduations as well
—haven’t we?—with no live audience.
But aren’t you happy that we’ve got a live audience today?
Now, after the last few months,
you’ve been through so many lessons
and written exams and so on.
There’s been a lot of training.
And what has been the purpose of all of that?
Well, when we think of worldly institutions and education,
usually it’s all about the students, isn’t it?
It’s all about the dreams, as Brother Morris mentioned.
It’s all about their ambitions
and their success that they’re looking forward to.
But what about Gilead?
Well, you’ve learned very clearly, I’m sure, that it’s not about you.
And if you haven’t, maybe we need to enroll you in the next class as well.
No, as dedicated servants of Jehovah,
we see that nothing is about us.
It’s not all about us.
It’s about what we can accomplish
in praising our heavenly Father, Jehovah.
So now you’re at this point where you’re about to graduate.
Now what?
Now is the time for you to share what you’ve learned with others.
Now, what does that involve?
Does this mean you’re going to go to different assignments
and start up little Gilead classes (you know, informally)
in the back rooms of Kingdom Halls?
I wouldn’t advise that.
So, what does it mean to share what you’ve learned with others?
Well, as has already been highlighted in this program,
your example —working hard—is going to help others
to see in action what you learned at Gilead.
But also we see a very interesting scripture
in the second book of Timothy,
so please turn with me to 2 Timothy chapter 2
and verse 2.
And here Paul is speaking to Timothy,
but he captures the thought of what else we need to do.
In verse 2, it says:
“The things you heard from me that were supported by many witnesses,
“these things entrust to faithful men, who, in turn,
will be adequately qualified to teach others.”
What do we see from this particular verse?
Well, yes, you will teach by your example by doing the hard work,
but also you need to take an interest in others
and, perhaps in a more informal setting,
help them to see the principles and the lessons that you’ve learned
from your Gilead training.
And that’s a very important thing.
We can take the example of our Lord Jesus Christ.
Of course, Jesus’ main focus
was the preaching of the good news of the Kingdom, wasn’t it?
But that’s not all he did.
If we turn to Mark chapter 9,
notice in Jesus’ busy schedule
what he made time for.
This is Mark 9:30, 31:
“They departed from there and went through Galilee,
but he did not want anyone to get to know about it.”
So this was a time when he wanted some peace and quiet.
Why?
Well, verse 31 says
“for he was teaching his disciples.”
So Jesus took time from his busy schedule to show interest
in those who he was training to help them to be prepared for the future.
So that’s a wonderful example for us.
When we look through the Scriptures, we see many examples,
but for the next few minutes, we’re going to think about Barnabas
and how Barnabas
was able to share what he learned with Paul.
And as we think about what happened
in that interaction between Barnabas and Paul,
we’re going to learn five lessons
—five lessons that teach us
how to handle training others and passing on what we’ve learned.
So the first lesson: If you turn with me, please, to the book of Acts
—Acts chapter 9—
this takes us to around the year 36 C.E.
So Saul has already become a Christian.
Now, after a while, he arrives in Jerusalem.
So, what happens?
In verse 26 of chapter 9, it says:
“On arriving in Jerusalem, he [that’s Paul]
“made efforts to join the disciples,
“but they were all afraid of him [I wonder why],
because they did not believe he was a disciple.”
They were thinking, ‘This is going to be a very dangerous thing.’
But now, what happened in verse 27?
“So Barnabas came to his aid
and led him to the apostles.”
So we see, as pictured here,
Barnabas saw the potential in Saul
and believed that, really,
he could be useful in Jehovah’s service.
So he risked his reputation, you might say,
by supporting, or sponsoring,
Saul and taking him to the apostles.
So, what’s the lesson that we learn from this?
Try to see the potential in others.
And don’t worry about if you
perhaps encourage them
and if you give them support
—you sponsor them, you might say—
and then they don’t really turn out well
and that now all of a sudden your reputation
is going to be tarnished.
Remember, it’s not all about you.
It’s what is good for the work.
So that’s the first lesson.
Try to see the potential in others.
Now, if we turn across to Acts chapter 11,
this is about nine years later,
around the year 45 C.E.
Now, in chapter 11 of Acts,
the work is going ahead in the Gentile field
and particularly in the city of Antioch.
So Barnabas was assigned by the brothers
to go and help the congregation in Antioch.
Well, let’s look down in verses 25 and 26,
because as soon as Barnabas arrived there,
he realized he needed help.
So, what did he do?
Well, in verse 25, it says:
“He [that’s Barnabas]
went to Tarsus to make a thorough search for Saul.”
So he went to find Saul.
He remembered that this was a man
who could speak Greek and was well-educated.
He’d be able to help him with the Gentile field.
It’s interesting that when you look at a map, you’ll notice
that it’s about 120 miles
from Antioch to Tarsus, or about 200 kilometers.
It mentions here in verse 25 that he made “a thorough search for Saul.”
Why?
Well, if we compare 1 Corinthians, where Paul lists all the things he did,
many of those, it appears, happened in those nine years.
He was shipwrecked several times, put into prison, and so on.
So he was very busy.
Barnabas sought him out, and then what did he have to do?
Well, in verse 26, it says: “After he found him,
he brought him to Antioch.”
So, what did he have to do?
He had to convince Saul.
You can imagine that may have been a little difficult
because Saul was having a productive ministry.
So he brought him to Antioch.
Then verse 26 says:
“For a whole year they assembled with him in the congregation
and taught quite a crowd.”
So Barnabas didn’t take Paul and say, “Now I’m going to teach you.”
He just had him work along with him.
And as they worked together, that would have given Saul some training.
So, what’s the lesson
that we learn?
Be willing to make the effort.
You see, Barnabas not only
saw the potential
but was willing to go and find Saul
and then convince him to come
and work with him,
and then they worked together.
So that’s the second lesson.
The third lesson is in Acts 13.
So after Barnabas and Saul were in Antioch for some time,
what happened in verse 2?
It says: “As they were ministering to Jehovah and fasting,
“the holy spirit said:
“‘Set aside for me Barnabas and Saul
for the work to which I have called them.’”
Well, now, this is a time when they’re going out in the missionary field,
but notice that the holy spirit mentions “Barnabas and Saul.”
So in this illustration, we see who is taking the lead—Barnabas.
Saul is following along.
But if we look down further in verse 13 of the same chapter,
we see there’s a little change.
Saul starts to use a name that is more common in that area—Paul.
But what does it say now?
“Paul and his companions put out to sea.”
And from here on, it seems that Paul took the lead.
Now, let’s just imagine for a little bit that you were Barnabas.
You know, maybe we could imagine ourselves saying quietly to Saul, or Paul,
or whatever he was calling himself at that time:
“Can I just have a few words with you?
“This is not a big issue, but do you remember
“when holy spirit said we were going out?
“It was ‘Barnabas and Saul.’
“Now, now, I don’t have a big problem with this.
“But, you know, I appreciate your enthusiasm.
But, really, I was the one designated to take the lead here.”
No, he didn’t say that, did he?
The Bearing Witness  book mentions that he wasn’t envious at all.
So, what’s the lesson?
Well, if we’re working along with someone and training them,
the lesson is:
Don’t be envious if they start to excel.
And actually, what we’re helping them
to do is to blossom.
And they will get some of the privileges
that perhaps we would have liked
along the way.
So we won’t be saying, “Well, uhm, excuse me, uhm,
but I’m the one who went through Gilead.”
No, we won’t be envious.
The fourth lesson takes us to the book of Galatians.
So if you turn with me to Galatians chapter 2,
this is around the year 49 C.E.
Already, Peter and Paul and Barnabas
and Titus had all been to Jerusalem,
and they’d had the big discussion with the governing body about circumcision.
Interestingly, when they arrived in Jerusalem,
the account says that Barnabas and Paul were there.
Interesting.
Maybe Barnabas took note of that, that he was mentioned first again,
probably because the governing body remembered that was actually
the role originally.
But now we find that Peter, Paul, and Barnabas
and some others were back in Antioch.
And what happened just a few months after that special meeting?
Well, Paul had to tell Peter that he was doing something wrong.
But notice, please, what verse 13 says:
“The rest of the Jews also joined him in putting on this pretense,
so that even Barnabas was led along with them in their pretense.”
Now I just love this picture.
You see Paul telling Peter he’s wrong,
and have a look at Barnabas’ face.
He looks guilty.
Awkward!
Do you see?
He was caught in the crossfire.
He likewise was getting counsel because he was involved with this.
So, what lesson
do we gain from this?
Accept counsel
even from those whom we are viewing
as the ones whom we’re training.
Don’t feel that we’re
above accepting counsel.
Now, the final lesson is the one probably you thought about immediately
when we mentioned Paul and Barnabas.
I know what you were thinking—Acts 15.
So let’s turn there
And this is after the incident in Antioch.
And it says: “Barnabas was determined to take along John,
“who was called Mark.
“Paul, however, was not in favor of taking him along with them,
“seeing that he had departed from them in Pamphylia
“and had not gone with them to the work.
“At this there was a sharp burst of anger,
so that they separated from each other.”
Now, this is the instance that we usually remember
when we think of Paul and Barnabas.
What led to this problem?
Have you ever thought about that?
It mentions that Paul was very hesitant
about taking John Mark along with them.
Perhaps he remembered on that first missionary tour
when John Mark had gone back,
he and Barnabas continued on into Galatia.
And reading what Paul said to the Galatians,
it seems obvious that Paul had problems with his eyes
and that he was very sick at that point.
So, no doubt, you know, he missed having a young man available
to carry the luggage and to do all the things that needed to be done.
So Barnabas could understand why Paul was hesitant.
He didn’t want to lose the help again.
But then, on the other hand, what about Barnabas?
Why do you think he was so determined to take John Mark?
Well, it could be the fact that he was a relative
(that sometimes comes into a factor),
or it could be the fact
that Barnabas saw the potential in Saul
was the same thing he saw in John Mark.
“This is a good young man.
We need to give him a chance.”
Or could it be that he was still stinging a little bit
after the rebuke in Antioch?
Or could it be that he was still viewing
Saul, or Paul, as a student,
someone newer in the truth than him and someone from whom
he just found it hard to accept his opinion?
Now, we’re not going to play the “blame game.”
Some of us will be working with these brothers later.
But I feel safe in saying this:
I’m sure that Paul and Barnabas
when they think back to that day
would agree that they could have done things better.
Is that a safe comment?
I think all of us have times when we felt maybe we were right,
but we could have handled it better.
So, what’s the lesson?
Try to respect different opinions;
don’t overreact.
Don’t get upset.
Try to work through things
so that it doesn’t affect
our working relationship.
Well, when we’ve thought about Barnabas and Paul,
it really gives us a lot of food for thought, doesn’t it?
Remember those five lessons?
Try to see the potential in others.
Then be willing to put forward the effort that’s required to train them.
Don’t be envious if they get privileges.
Accept counsel if they offer you counsel,
and respect their opinions as well.
We know that you’ll try to implement those suggestions.
Yes, as you go to your assignments,
may Jehovah be with you and bless you.
May you try to help others by sharing what you’ve learned at Gilead.
And in that way, you will fulfill the purpose of Gilead
—to stabilize and strengthen others.

耶稣却不想让人知道他在哪里。”
看来耶稣是想找一个安静的场合
为什么呢？
第31节说
“原来他教导门徒”
耶稣虽然工作很忙
但是他乐意特意抽出时间关心门徒
帮助他们为未来做好准备
他真的为我们树立了好榜样
圣经中记录了很多的好榜样
接下来我们花点时间看一看巴拿巴的例子
看看巴拿巴怎样把自己学到的跟保罗分享
考虑一下保罗和巴拿巴之间发生的事情
我们可以从中学到五方面的要点
这些要点能帮助我们培训别人
并且跟别人分享我们学到的
那么第一个要点是什么呢？
请翻开使徒行传
使徒行传第9章
让我们看看在大约公元36年发生的事
那时扫罗已经成为了基督徒
过了一段时间，他到达了耶路撒冷
那后来发生了什么呢？
使徒行传9:26，经文说
“扫罗到了耶路撒冷，很想跟门徒来往
可是大家都怕他。”
为什么呢？
经文说
他们“不相信他已经成为耶稣的门徒”
他们肯定想，跟扫罗来往太危险了
但第27节说什么呢？
“于是巴拿巴来帮助他，带他去见使徒。”
正如图片所示，巴拿巴看到了扫罗的潜力
他相信扫罗能为耶和华做很多事
虽然这么做有可能危害他的名声
他还是愿意为扫罗说话
他带扫罗去见使徒
我们可以从中学到什么呢？
那就是，要发掘别人的潜质
如果你发现一个人的潜质
就要鼓励他，给他支持
你可能会想
如果他后来没有做好怎么办呢？
不要担心，没有人会因此责怪你
请记住
只要你做的
是为了耶和华的工作，就够了
所以这就是第一个要点
要发掘别人的潜质
接着我们翻到使徒行传11章
时间来到了大约9年后
也就是在公元45年左右
使徒行传第11章的内容叙述了传道工作
正在外族人居住的地区扩展，尤其在安提阿
于是弟兄们就决定委派巴拿巴
去帮助安提阿那里的会众
我们来看看11章的25和26节
巴拿巴一到了安提阿
就马上看出自己真的需要帮助
那么他怎样做呢？
在第25节，经文说
“于是巴拿巴去大数，到处寻找扫罗。”
经文说，巴拿巴就去找扫罗
他知道扫罗会讲希腊语
又受过良好的教育
能帮助他向外族人传道
有一点很值得我们留意，如果你看地图
就会发现从安提阿到大数
有大约200公里的路程
在25节这里提到他“到处寻找扫罗”
为什么呢？
答案就在哥林多后书里
那里列出了扫罗经历的很多事
其中一些显然发生在这9年里
例如，他经历过几次船难，又坐过牢
所以想找到扫罗的确不容易
巴拿巴努力寻找扫罗
后来在26节说
巴拿巴“找到了［扫罗］
就带他去安提阿”
但在这之前，他必须先说服扫罗
做到这点真的不容易
因为扫罗在原来的地方有很好的传道成果
但他还是把扫罗带到了安提阿
26节继续说
“整整一年，他们都跟那里的会众在一起
教导了很多人。”
巴拿巴并没有跟保罗说
“我来教你怎么做吧。”
他只是跟保罗一起工作
而在这个过程中
他给了保罗一些培训
那么我们能从中学到什么呢？
就是要愿意付出努力
巴拿巴不但看到了保罗的潜质
还乐意亲自去找保罗，然后说服他
最终让他跟自己一起工作
这就是第二个要点
第三个要点在使徒行传13章
保罗和巴拿巴在安提阿待了一段时间后
发生了什么呢？
在第2节，经文说
“他们为耶和华服务，正禁食的时候
上帝通过神圣力量说
你们要为我选出巴拿巴和扫罗
去做我指派给他们的一件工作。”
而工作是他们要出发，开始去海外传道
请留意经文先提到了巴拿巴
然后说到了扫罗
在图片中我们能看出带头的是巴拿巴
而扫罗是跟着巴拿巴一起工作的人
如果我们看使徒行传的13:13
就会发现有一点变化
扫罗改名为保罗
这个名字在他传道的地区更普遍
请留意，13节的经文说“保罗和同伴”
看起来从那时起，带头的就是保罗了
现在想象一下，你就是巴拿巴
不管那个时候你叫他保罗还是扫罗
你可能想在私底下跟他说
“呃，我能跟你说两句话吗？
当然不是什么大事，不过你记得吗
当时上帝通过神圣力量让我们出去传道时
说的可是
巴拿巴和扫罗
我可不是在生你的气啊！
你知道的，我非常欣赏你的热情
不过说实在的
我才是这里带头的呀。”
巴拿巴当然没有那么说
《作见证》这本书提到
他一点都没有妒忌保罗
我们能学到什么呢？
如果我们跟某个人工作，培训他
之后他变得越来越优秀
请记住，不要妒忌
我们能够帮助他们的
不就是让他们成长
变得更成熟吗？
他们可能会得到一些
我们一直想得到的服务机会
千万不要觉得
“我可是去过基列学校的
这个服务机会应该是我的！”
不要，不要妒忌他们
第四个要点是什么呢？
让我们来看一下加拉太书
请大家跟我一起打开加拉太书2章
时间来到了公元49年左右
当时，彼得、保罗、巴拿巴还有提多
他们都在耶路撒冷
就割礼问题跟中央长老团的成员
进行了重要的讨论
请留意，当圣经提到这段记载时
所用的字眼是“巴拿巴和保罗”
很有意思吧？
或许巴拿巴留意到他的名字
再一次被放到前面了
可能是因为中央长老团想起来了
一开始是委任巴拿巴做带头的人
后来经文描述
彼得、保罗、巴拿巴还有其他人
回到了安提阿
在讨论过割礼问题后又过了几个月
现在发生了什么呢？
在这里
保罗当面告诉彼得，说彼得犯了错
请留意加拉太书2:13
经文说
“其余的犹太人也跟着他装假
结果连巴拿巴也受他们影响，一起装假。”
我特别喜欢这幅图片
你们看到保罗告诉彼得，说彼得做错了
这个时候，让我们来看一下巴拿巴的表情
他很不自在，非常尴尬！
你们看，巴拿巴就坐在彼得旁边
他犯了跟彼得同样的错误
所以也需要接受劝告
那么，我们能学到什么呢？
要接受劝告
即使劝告是来自我们正在培训的人
也要接受
不要觉得自己已经做得很好了，不需要劝告
我们看最后一个要点
这个要点，一定是一提到保罗和巴拿巴
你们就马上能想到的
我知道你们在想什么
就是使徒行传第15章
请看使徒行传15:37-39
这件事发生在保罗指责彼得之后
经文说
“巴拿巴坚持要带称为马可的约翰一起去
可是保罗不同意带他去
因为他之前在潘菲利亚离开了他们
没有跟他们一起工作
两个人激烈地争执起来
结果就分开了。”
通常，我们一提到
保罗和巴拿巴就会想到这件事
那你们有没有想过这件事的起因呢？
经文提到
保罗不同意带马可和他们一起去工作
也许保罗想到在第一次传道旅程中
马可离开了他们
后来他和巴拿巴继续前行，到了加拉太
如果你读保罗写给加拉太会众的信就会发现
很可能保罗患有眼疾
而在那个时候他病得很重
所以我们可以想象
那时保罗可能很需要一个年轻人帮他提行李
以及做其他的一些杂事
巴拿巴应该可以理解
保罗不想带上马可的原因
保罗担心马可会再次离开
但是另一方面，巴拿巴又是怎么想的呢？
为什么他这么坚决要带上马可呢？
可能是因为他们两个是亲戚
这通常会影响一个人的决定
也有可能是
就像当初巴拿巴看到了保罗身上的潜质一样
他现在也看到了马可的潜质
他可能会说
“这个年轻人不错，我们该给他机会。”
又可能是因为之前保罗在安提阿给过他劝告
所以他还是有些不舒服
还有一个原因
也许他始终把保罗当作学生
因为保罗认识真理的时间没有他长
对巴拿巴来说
接受保罗的意见或许不太容易
声明一下，我们不是要追究谁的错误
我们有些人将来是要和他们一起工作的
不过
我想保罗和巴拿巴如果可以回到当初的话
他们一定可以把这件事处理得比之前更好
这样说应该没问题吧？
我们一定都面对过类似的情况
就是也许我们是对的
但其实应该用更好的方法去处理这个问题
所以我们要尊重不同的意见
这样就不会反应过激
不会恼怒生气
要努力化解分歧
这样就能够继续和别人一起和睦地工作
关于巴拿巴和保罗的记载
其实还有很多值得我们思考的地方
是不是？
要记得今天的五个要点
首先，要发掘别人的潜质
第二个要点就是
要付出努力，乐意去培训别人
第三，不要妒忌别人的服务机会
第四，要接受劝告
最后，要尊重别人的意见
我们相信你们一定会把这五个要点
全部实践出来
现在，你们就要从基列学校毕业了
愿耶和华与你们同在并赐福给你们
希望你们把在这里学到的尽力跟别人分享
帮助别人
这样做，你就能达到培训的目标
也就是巩固和加强弟兄姐妹的信心

titles.ko: 제프리 W. 잭슨: 이제 여러분이 배운 것을 나누어 주십시오!
titles.en: Geoffrey W. Jackson: Now Share What You Have Learned!
titles.cn: 杰弗里·杰克逊：你所学到的，不要忘记与人分享

ko.text: 이제 우리가 늘 기대하는 인사이드 스토리를 즐길 차례가 되었습니다.
진행은 길르앗 강사 중 한 분이신 트렌트 리폴드 형제가 해 주시겠습니다.
작년은 여호와의 백성 모두에게 변화의 시기였습니다.
우리는 융통성과 조심성과 합리적인 태도를 보여야 했죠.
길르앗에서도 이번에 열린 150기 학급에는 변화가 있었습니다.
예를 들어, 150기의 모든 학생은 미국 출신이거나 미국에서 봉사하고 있습니다.
다섯 부부와 독신 형제 한 명은 모두 순회 활동을 하고 있습니다.
이분들이 학급의 거의 절반을 이루고 있죠.
오늘은 미국의 서로 다른 지역에서 오신 세 부부를 만나 보겠습니다.
그들이 어떻게 삶의 변화에 적응하는 법을 배웠는지 그리고
사도 바울처럼 ‘모든 사람에게 모든 것이 되’려고 노력했는지 알아보시죠.
첫 손님은 텍사스주에서 오신 테일러 본샤인과 조이 본샤인 부부입니다.
텍사스주는 정말 넓은데 어느 도시에서 오셨나요?
두 분은 150기 학생이신데 길르앗에 오려면 정규 파이오니아부터 시작하잖아요.
어떻게 정규 파이오니아를 시작하셨는지 자매부터 말씀해 주실까요?
제 경우는 정말 고맙게도 오래전부터 가족들이 좋은 본을 보이셨어요.
두 분은 결혼을 한 후에 최선을 다해 여호와를 섬기고 싶어 하셨어요.
도움이 필요한 곳이 어디인지 순회 감독자들에게 물어보곤 하셨죠.
다른 회중에 가 달라고 하면, 언제나 즉시 가셨습니다.
그런 본은 어머니께 좋은 영향을 미쳤고, 저에게도 그랬죠.
결혼 생활과 가족 부양과 자녀를 돌보는 일로 바쁘셨던 것 같아요.
그러다가 나라 반대쪽으로 이사 가게 되셨는데,
어렸지만 부모님이 달라지셨다는 걸 느낄 수 있었어요.
여호와를 위해 더 많은 걸 하실 수 있었기 때문이죠.
어머니가 파이오니아를 시작하시고 달라지셨다고 느꼈던 때가요?
네. 그럼 정규 파이오니아는 언제 시작하셨어요?
그 다음 해에 언니랑 제가 어머니를 따라 파이오니아를 시작했어요.
본샤인 형제, 형제는 어떻게 정규 파이오니아를 시작하셨나요?
저흰 텍사스에서 봉사했지만, 전 원래 콜로라도주에 살았어요.
아내처럼 제 부모님도 좋은 본을 보이셨어요.
어릴 때부터 파이오니아 봉사, 전 시간 봉사는 제게 아주 익숙했습니다.
제가 10대 중반일 때 부모님이 대리 순회 활동에 임명되셨어요. 재밌었죠.
주말이면 부모님이 방문하시는 회중에 따라갔어요. 학교에 가느라 주중엔 못 갔고요.
특히 고맙게 느끼는 건, 두 분이 말로만이 아니라 행동으로 본을 보여 주셨다는 겁니다.
아, 좋으셨겠네요. 부모님이 대리 순회 활동을 하셨으니까요.
저는 고등학교를 6개월 일찍 졸업하고 파이오니아를 시작했습니다.
그리고 베델에서 일할 수 있는 19살이 되자마자 지원서를 냈고,
그 후 곧 초대를 받아서 몇 년 동안 브루클린에서 일했습니다.
그렇군요. 그러고 나서 베델을 떠나셨고, 두 분은 결혼을 하셨죠.
그런데 어떻게 여호와를 위해 더 많은 일을 하려는 마음을 갖게 되셨나요?
저희는 파이오니아를 하는 젊은 부부였고, 목표도 있었죠.
하지만 신혼이라 결혼 생활에 적응해야 했고,
그 목표를 이루기 위해 어느 방향으로 가야 할지 몰랐어요.
시기적절하게 여러 순회 감독자 부부가 와서 도움을 정말 많이 주셨습니다.
고마움을 표현하려고 하긴 했지만, 얼마나 큰 도움을 주셨는지는 절대 모르실 거예요.
사실, 순회 활동을 하시는 분들은 젊은 사람들에게 도움을 많이 주십니다.
그게 그 봉사의 큰 유익 중 하나죠. 정말 고마운 일입니다.
그래서 두 분도 순회 활동을 하고 싶은 마음이 드셨나요?
부부가 같이 정말 베델에 가고 싶어서 지원서를 내고 또 냈는데, 아무 연락이 없었어요.
그럼 생각이 달라지신 건가요? 아니면 무슨 일이 있었나요?
네. 하루는 편지를 하나 받았는데, 대리 순회 활동을 위한 질문서였어요.
그게 우리가 가려고 했던 방향은 아니었지만,
여호와께서 우리 앞에 열어 놓으신 길 같아 보였어요.
그래서 기쁘게 받아들였고, 순회 활동에 대한 마음이 점점 자라 갔습니다.
그리고 저희는 왕국 전파자 학교에 참석할 수 있었습니다.
훈련을 받으면서 여호와께서 우리에게 바라시는 일을 할 마음을 키워 나갔죠.
그리고 학교를 졸업하고 몇 달이 채 안 되어
저희는 순회 활동을 하도록 임명되었고, 그 일을 좋아하게 되었습니다.
대도시 댈러스에서 대도시 시카고로 가게 돼서 좋았죠.
대도시에 살던 저희 둘이 댈러스에서 더 큰 도시 시카고로 가게 된 거죠.
그곳 사람들의 배경, 문화, 인종, 모든 게 다양해서 좋았어요.
즐거웠죠. 시카고 지역이 정말 마음에 들었습니다.
근데 “하지만”이 나올 것 같은데요. 어떤 변화가 있었죠?
저희가 한 6개월 정도 그 순회구에서 즐겁게 봉사하고 있을 때

파이오니아를 시작하고 나서 2003년에 봉사 훈련 학교에 갔고,
얼마 후에 아름다운 시골 회중으로 임명되었어요.
그 회중에서 아주 사랑스러운 자매를 만나게 됐습니다.
하지만 아까 자매가 변화가 생겼다고 하셨는데, 어떤 변화였죠?
저는 전에 대리 순회 감독자 훈련을 받았는데,
그때 순회 감독자 한 명이 필요하게 됐습니다.
그런데 푸에르토리코가 아니라 오하이오주에 있는 스페인어 순회구였어요.
그래서 기도를 했고, 푸에르토리코를 떠나 오하이오주로 갔습니다.
이사를 도와주러 오하이오주로 오신 아버지를 공항까지 태워다 드리고 돌아오는데
“저 비행기만 떠나면 난 아는 사람도 없고 아무것도 몰라.”
장소만 달라진 게 아니라 모든 게 달라졌으니까요.
미국에 있는 스페인어 회중들은 아주 다양한 문화가 섞여 있습니다.
그래서 전에는 접해 보지 못한 여러 문화권의 형제들을 만나게 됐죠.
푸에르토리코 형제들만 아니라 모두가 알아들을 수 있게 스페인어를 하는 법도 배워야 했습니다.
미국에 오신 것도 큰 변화인데, 말씀대로 여러 문화에 접하셨으니까요.
그런데 사진을 가져오셨는데, 눈이 많이 왔네요?
봉사하러 나가기 전에 일기 예보를 확인해야 한다는 겁니다.
네. 해가 나거나 아니면 비가 오니까요.
형제가 미국으로 가게 됐을 때 자매는 어떻게 느끼셨어요?
전 형제가 그 임명을 받아서 기뻤어요.
그 뒤로 계속 연락하다가 2010년에 우린 결혼을 했어요.
그리고 부부가 함께 오하이오주에서 계속 순회하도록 초대를 받았어요.
이제 막 결혼하신 데다가, 새로 순회 활동까지 하게 되셨으니까요.
어떤 점이 특히 힘드셨는지 형제 먼저 말씀해 주실까요?
새로운 임명을 받아서 일을 시작할 때
자격이 있다거나 준비되어 있다고 느끼기가 어렵잖아요.
순회를 시작했을 때 저희는 나이가 어렸는데,
회중들에는 저희가 살아온 기간보다 더 오래 정규 파이오니아를 해 오신 형제들이 계셨죠.
그런데 갑자기 저희가 그런 분들을 격려하고 도울 책임을 맡게 돼서 부담을 느꼈습니다.
그때 적응하느라 얼마나 혼란스러웠는지 보여 주는 사진인가요?
결혼하고 얼마 안 돼서 야외 봉사에 나간 날이었어요.
서둘러 집을 나서서 야외 봉사에 나가 집단을 인도하고 모든 마련을 했죠.
그때 한 형제가 와서, 참 좋은 형젠데요,
제 어깨에 팔을 얹더니 절 아내에게 데려가서 이렇게 말했습니다.
형제는 제 구두를 내려다봤는데 알고 보니 제가 구두를 짝짝이로 신었던 겁니다.
형제는 친절하게도 봉사를 시작하기 전에 지적해 줬지만 사진을 찍은 뒤에야 알려 줬죠.
전 이랬죠. “여보, 이게 어떻게 된 거예요?”
-이젠 형제 구두를 꼭 확인하시겠네요. -네, 나오기 전에 꼭 확인하려고 해요.
변화에 적응하는 데 뭐가 도움이 됐다고 생각하세요?
아버지와 경험 있는 형제들이 아주 좋은 조언을 해 주셨는데
그들에게 필요한 건 사랑과 애정과 우리의 시간이죠.
형제들은 순회 감독자가 누구든 순회 감독자 마련을 가치 있게 여기기 때문이죠.
우리가 겸손하면 여호와께서 우리를 사용하실 수 있고
‘모든 사람에게 모든 것이 되’는데 꼭 필요합니다.
그들과 친밀해지는 게 정말 멋진 특권인 건 사실이죠.
하지만 동시에 현실을 보고 형제 자매들이 겪는 모든 어려움을 알게 돼요.
그런 어려움 중에는 건강 문제나 경제 문제,
그리고 이민을 와서 겪는 문제도 있죠.
형제 자매들을 돕고 싶은데 그럴 수 없어서 낙담이 됐어요.
제가 할 수 있는 건 그 문제를 여호와의 손에 맡기고,
형제 자매들을 위해 제 시간을 내는 것이었죠.
저는 같이 봉사하면서 격려해 주려고 합니다.
함께 웃기도 하고 함께 울기도 하는데
제 사랑을 보여 주고 무엇보다 여호와의 사랑을 보여 주려고 해요.
잘 하셨네요. 다들 자매의 사랑을 아주 많이 느꼈을 겁니다.
형제에겐 길르앗이 좀 특별하다고 들었는데, 그 이유가 뭐죠?
네, 부모님이 길르앗에 참석하셨고 푸에르토리코로 임명되셨거든요.
부모님은 형제를 낳고 기르면서도 늘 길르앗을 잊지 않으셨나요?
부모님이 집에서 우리 모두가 볼 수 있는 곳에
졸업 사진을 걸어 놓으셨던 게 기억이 납니다.
저는 자라면서 매일 그 사진 앞을 지나다녔죠.
네, 또 부모님이 여호와를 섬기는 방식과 두 분이 나타내신 열정과 사랑을 보고
길르앗 교육이 두 분께 얼마나 큰 영향을 주었는지 분명히 알게 됐습니다.
부모님이 길르앗에서 받은 영향이 어떤 것이었을까요?
두 가지인데요. 한 가지는 두 분이 언제나 성경을 열심히 연구하신다는 겁니다.
어머니 성경엔 메모가 빼곡해서 빈 자리가 없었죠.
아버지는 밤에 우리와 함께 성경을 읽으셨는데,
봉투로 성경에 책갈피를 해 놓으셨던 게 기억이 납니다.
아버진 성경을 읽다가 갑자기 멈춰서 봉투에 뭔가 적으셨는데,
연설이나 양치는 방문 때 사용할 성구나 마음에 드는 내용을 찾으셨기 때문이죠.
또 한 가지로 왕국 권익을 위해 정말 열심히 일하셨습니다.
언제나 두 분의 목표는 할 수 있는 한 많이 하는 것이었고
흥미롭게도 이제 길르앗에 와 보니 바로 그 점들을 강조하더군요.
연구를 해서 여호와에 대한 사랑을 기르고
조직을 위해 최대한 많이 일하라는 겁니다.
지금 수업에서 들으시는 많은 내용이 바로 예전에 부모님이 들으셨던 내용인데요.
네. 부모님은 길르앗에 오기 전에도 어느 정도 좋은 특성들이 있으셨을 겁니다.
하지만 수업을 듣다 보니 길르앗 덕분에 부모님이 그런 특성을 기르셨고
여러 해가 지난 지금까지도 유지하고 계시다는 걸 깨달았습니다.
네. 부모님은 지금 열심히 하는 두 분을 자랑스러워하실 거예요.
그리고 앞으로 임지에서 배운 걸 적용하길 기대하실 겁니다.
모든 부류의 사람에게 모든 것이 되었습니다.”
자신의 생활과 개인적인 기호를 조정해야 한다고 느꼈습니다.
좋아하지 않거나 할 수 없다고 생각하는 일도 해 볼 수 있습니다.
다른 사람을 격려하기 위해 사랑을 보일 수도 있습니다.
오늘 나온 손님들이 보여 주신 것처럼
우리는 좋은 소식을 위해 자신의 생활과 개인적인 기호를 조정함으로
어떤 변화에든 대처하고 어떤 변화든 할 수 있습니다.

en.text: Now we have the opportunity
to enjoy this edition that we’re accustomed to of The Inside Story,
and it’s hosted by another instructor,
Brother Trent Lippold.
Enjoy it.
The past year has been a period of change for all of Jehovah’s people.
We’ve had to show flexibility, caution, and reasonableness.
Here at Gilead, for us too,
Class 150 has presented us with change.
For example, all the students of Class 150
are from or serving in the United States.
Five couples and one single brother
all serve in the circuit work.
That represents approximately 50 percent of the class.
Today we’re going to meet three couples
from different parts of the United States
and see how they learned to cope with change in their lives
and how they, like the apostle Paul,
worked to ‘become all things to all people.’
So let’s meet our first guests,
Joey and Taylor Bornschein, from the state of Texas.
Joey and Taylor, welcome to The Inside Story.
Thank you. Thank you.
You’re from the big state of Texas.
Where specifically are you from?
From Dallas.
Dallas, Texas. All right.
Well, again, nice to have you with us.
You know, to come to Gilead (here you are in the 150th class),
it all starts with regular pioneering.
So how did you both start regular pioneering?
Maybe, Joey, how did you start?
So for me, I feel very grateful that my foundation
started a long time ago with my family,
especially with my grandparents.
They were the couple that after they got married,
really just wanted to serve Jehovah the best way they could.
They would ask circuit overseers where they could move that needed help.
If they were ever asked to go to another congregation,
they would always do it right away.
And so that really affected my mom, which in turn affected me.
How did that affect you?
So for a while after my parents got married,
they might have just gotten a little distracted with marriage,
family, taking care of the family.
But at one point, they made a move across the country,
and they used that as an opportunity to simplify.
And my mom was able to start regular pioneering at that time.
And I just— I remember as a child
how different both of my parents were,
just in their happiness and in life in general
because they were able to do more for Jehovah.
Nice.
How old were you when that happened,
when your mom started pioneering and you saw this change?
I was about nine.
OK.
And so when did you start regular pioneering then?
So, actually, the next year
my sister and I both got to join her in pioneering.
So you were 10 years old?
Yeah.
That is amazing!
Thank you.
Ten years old when you started pioneering? Great!
What about you, Taylor?
How did you get your start in regular pioneering?
So we pioneered in Texas, but I’m originally from Colorado.
So my parents, like Joey’s, set a really good example for me.
Most of my life they pioneered as a couple.
And so pioneering was always just something
—full-time service was something— that I grew up with.
When I was in my mid-teens,
my parents got appointed to the substitute circuit work.
So that was fun.
On the weekends, I would travel with them to visit congregations.
I was in public schools, so I couldn’t go with them during the week.
And I appreciated about them
that it wasn’t just what they said, but they set the example by what they did.
OK.
I mean, that must have been cool.
You had your parents, and they were in the substitute circuit work.
But personally, how did that affect you?
Yeah, so that was just some good motivation for me to start pioneering.
I graduated about six months early,
a semester early, and then started pioneering.
And then as soon as I was able to, I hit 19
and submitted an application for Bethel, and soon thereafter
I was accepted and was able to spend a few years in Brooklyn.
OK.
After that, I know you left Bethel.
The two of you got married.
You’re there regular pioneering in Dallas.
What made the difference for you to reach out
and progress in Jehovah’s service?
So we were pioneering as a young couple.
We had goals, but it can be hard when you’re new
and trying to figure marriage out with some distractions
or with maybe even just knowing what direction you should take.
So we just feel so thankful to Jehovah
that we had some very instrumental circuit overseer couples
that came just at the right time.
We’ve tried to express it to them, but I don’t think
they’ll ever fully understand the impact that they’ve had on our lives.
Well, that is one of the great things about the impact
of those in the circuit work: what they do for young people, for young ones.
And we’re all— I think we’re all so grateful for that.
Would you say then—?
Was that your inspiration to get into the circuit work?
Not really.
We actually had different goals.
We really wanted to go to Bethel together as a couple,
so we applied and applied, and it just didn’t seem to happen.
But you ended up in the circuit work.
So I wonder what changed then.
Did it just grow on you, or what happened?
Well, one day we opened up a piece of mail, and it was a questionnaire
for the substitute circuit work.
So while that might not have been the direction
that we thought we would go down,
it seemed like that was the path that Jehovah laid out in front of us.
So we happily accepted, and little by little
it started to grow on us —the idea of the circuit work.
We were then able to attend
the School for Kingdom Evangelizers.
We just continued to get training and motivation
to do what Jehovah wanted us to do.
And so after our graduation, within just a few months,
we were appointed to the circuit work,
and we love the circuit work.
Where was your first circuit, Joey?
So we went to the suburbs of Chicago,
so it was great—from the big city of Dallas
to the big city of Chicago.
What did you think of Chicago?
It was everything that I could want in a circuit
—so two big-city people from Dallas now going to Chicago, an even bigger city.
We love diversity of background, culture, race, and it had everything.
So we were just eating it up.
We loved being in the Chicago area.
It sounds like a “but” is coming—a change.
What changed for you both?
So after just about six months of being in that circuit
and still falling in love with the circuit work, we got a call
from the branch office that we were
now being reassigned to a different circuit farther north
and a more rural circuit in Wisconsin.
OK, Wisconsin.
Well, what did you think? Tell us about it.
What was Wisconsin like for you, Taylor?
So it was very different for big-city people
going into a rural circuit that was
mostly dairy-farm communities.
So, out of our element, we would drive for miles and miles
when we were out in service with no stores or shops
or bathrooms or coffee shops.
So it took a little getting used to.
Probably, timing now became something you had to learn.
Good.
What about for you, Joey, coming from Dallas,
what was it like for you?
For me, the big change was the weather —the winters.
We didn’t have extreme winters in Dallas,
and Wisconsin had very long, very cold winters.
So we invested in really good coats,
wool leggings, great boots.
I jokingly told Taylor that some mornings I would wake up
and feel exhausted just getting dressed in the morning.
Putting on so much, I guess, also affected bathroom breaks and things like that
—new skills you were learning in Wisconsin.
Right.
What helped you to adjust to this new change?
So although it was a different environment, it was just beautiful to see that, yeah,
it was cold outside, but that didn’t affect the friends, their hearts.
They were warm in their service to Jehovah.
They were so warm in the way that they treated us.
They just adopted us so quickly into a different environment.
We very, very quickly fell in love with the friends in Wisconsin.
Jehovah’s people are amazing, aren’t they?
What about you, Joey?
What would you say helped you to adjust?
Well, of course, like Taylor said,
the love from the friends; it helped us immediately.
But we also actually learned new ways to have fun that we never had in Dallas.
Yeah, you brought a picture.
This photograph is a great picture.
You’re obviously having fun there.
Joey, what can you tell us about it?
So this is actually a gathering that we went to
on the middle of a frozen lake, and this is actually us ice fishing.
Did you catch anything?
We did.
You’re telling yourself, ‘You’re not in Dallas anymore.’
Right.
Great!
There’s also another photo, and I love this one.
What can you tell us about this, Taylor?
So there’s a brother in the circuit who raised beef cattle,
so I got to spend some time getting to pet the little guy and also hand-feeding it
—so an amazing experience and not something that I would have been able to do
in downtown Chicago or downtown Dallas.
You were really there, just ‘becoming all things to all people.’
What would you say you learned
from the changes you’ve gone through in your lives?
So if I’m just being honest, the circuit work
was not something that I had a desire to do.
I didn’t feel like it would make me comfortable or happy.
But Jehovah at times puts things in front of us
that we might not think that we would like or make us comfortable.
But it does.
And I’m so glad that he did allow us to have the opportunity
to be in the circuit work because we love the circuit work.
So it’s just a nice little reminder
that Jehovah will choose things for us or put things in front of us
that maybe we don’t think is going to make us happy
or is not going to make us comfortable in how we
feel with the circumstance or environment.
But Jehovah always chooses what’s best for us if we just let him do it.
What would you say, Joey? What did you learn?
I think for me, anytime there’s a change
there’s always going to be a little bit of anxiety,
uncertainties, worries.
I just really learned to just leave it in Jehovah’s hands
—to pray to him about it— because a lot of times those things
never even happen; they never even come true.
So whatever Jehovah asks of us,
we will be able to get through it because either they won’t happen
or Jehovah will help us and bless us through them.
Those are two great lessons that you’ve learned.
Thank you so much for sharing them with us, and those are two lessons
that will probably help you out in the changes that are to come in your life.
Taylor and Joey, thank you so much for being with us on The Inside Story.
Thank you.
Let’s welcome our next guests coming from the state of Michigan,
Ben and Whitney Frey.
Ben and Whitney, thank you for being with us on The Inside Story.
You’ve come to Gilead from the circuit work,
and the circuit work also starts with regular pioneering.
So maybe you can tell us: How did you, Whitney, start regular pioneering?
So my mom taught me the truth when I was growing up.
And I loved Jehovah,
but by my late teens, I didn’t really know what I wanted to do with my life.
I had a girlfriend who invited me
to support her at a funeral of a young brother
who had passed away in a tragic accident.
That’s interesting.
Maybe you could make—
What’s the connection of starting to pioneer and a funeral?
Maybe you can make the connection for us.
Yeah.
So for me, when I got to the funeral of this young brother,
even though I didn’t know him personally, I had seen
that he had just started regular pioneering
and that he had the goal of going to Bethel when he got old enough.
And I just compared his life to mine.
He was going to give everything he had to Jehovah.
And I had the circumstances to do the same thing, but I wasn’t doing it.
And so I just thought, you know, ‘He didn’t get to finish his story.’
So I wanted to pick up where he left off.
I wanted to start pioneering.
And so when I went home, I prayed about it and I turned in
my auxiliary pioneer application with the goal
of starting to regular in September.
Well, that’s really encouraging —something so tragic
and yet something very positive came out of it.
What about you, Ben? How did you get your start?
So, similar to Whitney, my mother taught me the truth.
My dad was not in the truth during my youth.
I grew up in a rural congregation in Michigan,
and while I respected the truth
in my late teens and early 20’s,
I struggled spiritually.
And the reason is because I wanted a lot out of life
and, at that point, the truth felt very restrictive to me.
It felt like it was holding me back and not allowing me
to get the rich life that I wanted.
What changed in your life then? What helped you?
We had a couple of pioneer elders move into our congregation
who were a great source of encouragement to me.
They helped me to see that serving Jehovah is not about what you can’t  do;
it’s about all the things you can  do.
And the way I illustrate it is with a board game.
If all you did was just learn the rules of that game
but you never played it, that wouldn’t be a lot of fun.
And that’s really how my view was at that time of the truth.
I knew the rules, so to speak, of the truth.
I respected the truth, but I wasn’t involved in it.
So with the encouragement of these two brothers, I really got involved.
I started playing the game, so to speak,
and I started studying the Bible like I should have all along.
And then I also started regular pioneering shortly thereafter.
Nice.
Well, we’re happy you “got in the game.”
Was there anything else, Whitney, that helped you
or maybe inspired you to reach out?
Yeah, when I started wanting to pioneer, I also got into studying more.
And one thing that really affected me was the video To the Ends of the Earth.
I remember watching it and, as I watched it, thinking: ‘That’s it.
‘That’s what I want to do.
I want to go to Gilead, and I want to be a missionary.’
Very nice.
Well, that video is still available on jw.org in the video library.
And that video probably, like for you,
inspired hundreds of people to reach out
and enter missionary service and attend Gilead.
And many of them are still out there
strengthening and stabilizing the brotherhood.
So you both then had
the goal of foreign service —missionary service.
Did you keep pursuing that goal?
Yeah, we certainly did.
After we got married, six months later,
we served where the need was great in the country of Guyana in South America.
Nice.
And you brought along a couple of pictures.
Maybe you can explain these.
Well, the first one is obviously your photo, Ben.
What can you tell us?
So we were motivated by the motorbike scene
in the To the Ends of the Earth  video.
So we got a motorbike when we were down there
—not quite as big or as cool as the one
in the To the Ends of the Earth  video, but it served its purpose.
We were able to travel the territory efficiently
to our different Bible studies and return visits.
Good.
And the next photo —what can you tell us about it, Whitney?
So when the bike couldn’t take us any farther,
we would park it and then we walked.
And a lot of times, that meant through mud across the trenches.
But we didn’t mind. It was fun.
We were enjoying it.
So Ben is being careful on the bridge.
Yeah, you had to be careful because there were black caiman,
which is a form of alligator, that was in those trenches,
so you chose your steps carefully.
Sure.
Well, I know you came back from Guyana.
Did you continue to pursue Gilead?
We did.
Once we returned to the United States after serving in Guyana,
we applied for Gilead, and to our surprise,
we were invited to serve as special pioneers
in the state of West Virginia here in the United States.
OK, so did Gilead remain your goal, though, even though you were there in West Virginia?
It did.
We continued to apply for Gilead,
but then instead we were invited to the Bible School for Christian Couples.
Very nice —so more theocratic education, though.
Uh-huh.
And from there you returned to West Virginia?
That’s correct.
So we continued special pioneering in West Virginia,
and we also got training for circuit work.
Good.
Did you end up in the circuit work?
So we were invited to start circuit work
in the Milwaukee, Wisconsin, area
similar (close by) to the Bornscheins.
And we loved it.
We loved the friends there, and we loved that circuit.
Nice.
But, of course, change came —didn’t it?—a big change for you.
Yeah.
So one day Ben came home.
We’d been there about four years.
We were loving it.
And he came home and told me that we got field missionary applications.
There it is—foreign service.
So how did you feel? Ben, how did you feel?
At that point in our life, we were really enjoying
the circuit work and we loved the friends.
So admittedly at that point, the idea of now going foreign
and having another change maybe lost a bit of its luster.
And we had gotten so comfortable that we had potentially gotten too comfortable.
What about you, Whitney?
Yeah, I thought, you know: ‘It had always been my goal.
‘But now, Jehovah?
‘Now after I got into circuit work
and am enjoying it, now you want me to go foreign?’
So, what helped you?
So we were explaining what was happening
and talking to my family and telling them how we felt.
I was talking to my sister and my brother-in-law,
and he said, “You know, Whit, you feel like you got trained for circuit work,
but maybe circuit work was training you for the next assignment.”
And just shifting my thoughts in that way really helped me.
Yeah.
That’s great advice.
What about you, Ben?
Was there something in particular that helped you?
There was.
I spoke with a brother in the Service Department at Bethel,
and he said that ones in our situation come across his desk frequently.
And he said: “You’re at a crossroads.
“And there are some who turn down the opportunity
to accept this form of foreign service.”
He said, “But for those that accept it,
“who take that step of faith,
“they receive blessings that they
could never have imagined from Jehovah.”
And we can rightly say that has been completely accurate.
We feel exactly that way.
Well, it shows.
So you went off to a foreign assignment.
You continued in circuit work there.
What would you say, Whitney?
How did foreign service help you?
In so many ways.
But a couple of them are just getting to express our faith and trust
in Jehovah in a way that we never would have if we didn’t go.
And one of the greatest gifts was the people that we met
—the local brothers and sisters,
our fellow missionaries, and circuit overseers.
Their faith and self-sacrifice taught us so much.
Beautiful.
And now you’ve come to Gilead.
How has Gilead training helped you?
Again, in so many ways.
While we loved our foreign assignment, it did have challenges.
And I remember praying to Jehovah, asking him for help
with certain things that I struggled with.
And the first week that we were here in Gilead, I saw the answer
to those prayers —specific things that I had prayed about—
answered right in week one, and it never stopped since.
Yeah.
And I’m sure Gilead training will just keep helping you in the future.
You said at the outset, Ben, that you wanted to get a lot out of life.
And I think we would all agree:
You’ve gotten a lot out of life —both of you so far.
And maybe in the next 30 minutes, you’ll find out
just how much more out of life you’re going to get.
Thank you both for being with us on The Inside Story.
Thank you.
Let’s welcome our final guests.
They’re also serving in the United States.
It’s Joshua and Solaydi Rechanek.
Josh and Solaydi, welcome.
It’s nice to have you.
You’re our final guests on The Inside Story  for today,
and I should clarify that although you’re serving in the United States,
you are actually from Puerto Rico, correct?
That’s right.
It’s a beautiful tropical island in the Caribbean.
So my mom and dad moved there
before I was born to serve, and that’s where I was raised.
And they were a tremendous example
for entering full-time service for me,
because when I was one, they actually started in the circuit work.
So it’s just that from a very young age,
it just seemed very natural to have that as a goal, and I’m very grateful.
OK, Solaydi, were you also born and raised in Puerto Rico?
That is right.
I have an older brother, Rafi,
and we both were raised by our mom,
Lydia, as a single parent.
She raised us in the truth, and a little bit
after Joshua came to our congregation, I started to pioneer.
And also I had the privilege to serve as a commuter
in the Puerto Rico branch,
but we were happy to have him in our congregation.
But something happened.
OK, before we get to what happened, we have a nice photograph.
There it is.
So that’s you with your mom, Solaydi?
Yeah, that’s my mom, Lydia.
So, Josh, just to clarify this also,
how did you get to Solaydi’s congregation?
So after I started pioneering, I went to what was called
the Ministerial Training School in 2003,
and after a little bit, I got assigned to this lovely rural congregation,
where I just happened to meet a very beautiful sister.
I like the way you say lovely congregation.
But a change came.
You said, Solaydi, that something changed.
What changed?
Well, I had gotten some training as a substitute circuit overseer,
and then there was a need for a circuit overseer.
But it wasn’t in Puerto Rico; it was in a Spanish circuit in Ohio.
And so I prayed about it,
and off I went from Puerto Rico to Ohio.
What was that like, Josh? Tell us about it.
How did you feel when you got there?
I was— It was very different.
I remember dropping my dad off at the airport (because he helped me move up),
and then when I was driving away, I said,
“I know nobody and nothing even nearby after that plane takes off.”
Because not only was the place different but also everything was different.
It’s very interesting because the congregations
in the U.S. in Spanish tend to be very mixed culturally.
And so I got to be with brothers from many different cultures
that I hadn’t experienced before.
I even had to learn to speak Spanish in a way that everybody would understand
instead of just the brothers from Puerto Rico.
So that’s a huge change for you
—a change of culture coming to the United States and then,
as you say, all these other cultures.
You brought along a really nice picture, Josh.
What can you tell us about this?
I learned this day a very important skill,
which is to check the weather report before you leave home to preach.
Right.
Do you not check the weather in Puerto Rico?
Nope.
It’s either going to be sunny, or it’s going to rain.
Two choices.
Interesting.
What about you, Solaydi?
So Josh has come to the United States.
How did that affect you?
Well, I was happy for the assignment.
It was a privilege, so I wanted to support him.
So we kept in touch.
And in 2010, we got married.
And after that, we received an invitation
to continue as a couple in Ohio.
Well, that’s a big change for you then.
Again, just like Josh, you came to a new country, in a sense,
a new marriage, and a new assignment in circuit work.
What were some of the hard moments for you?
Maybe, Josh, you could share first.
Well, as I said, there was a lot of adaptation.
When you start a new assignment, I don’t think you ever really feel
qualified for it or prepared for it.
And so we were very young when we started the circuit work,
visiting congregations where sometimes there were brothers that had been serving
as regular pioneers longer than we’d been alive.
And then all of a sudden, we’d have the responsibility
to encourage them and help them.
So that could be a bit intimidating.
Sure.
And you brought along another photo.
You can see the confusion of the adaptation.
What can you tell us about this, Josh?
So this was a field service day
shortly after getting married.
And it wasn’t that I was distracted or anything, but we rushed out the door,
went to field service, took the group out, and made all the arrangements.
And then a dear brother, a very good friend, came up to me,
and he put his arm around my shoulder, and he took me over to Solaydi.
And he said: “I’m not going to say anything.
I’m just going to look.”
And he looked down at my shoes,
and, well, it just turned out that I had
put two different shoes on.
And he was kind enough
to point that out before I went out in service.
But he didn’t point it out before he took the picture.
Of course.
Solaydi, what were you thinking?
I was like: “Baby, what happened?
What did you do?”
So you always check his shoes before he goes out then.
Yes, I try to check him before leaving home.
But maybe in all seriousness, Josh,
what would you say were the keys that helped you?
I got some really good advice
from brothers with more experience, including my father.
And there are really two keys we found.
One is to love the brothers, because that’s really what they need.
They need love and affection and your time.
And the other is to be humble,
because the brothers greatly appreciate the arrangement of the circuit overseer,
whoever the circuit overseer is.
So as long as you remain humble, Jehovah can use you
to encourage the friends and then all glory goes to him.
It’s very nice to love humility,
and that’s really what helps us to “become all things to [all] people.”
What about for you, Solaydi?
What were challenges for you?
Well, for me it was the emotional part.
Because it is true: It is a beautiful privilege
to be able to know so many brothers and sisters
and make bonds with them, but at the same time, you face reality.
You see all the struggles that they are going through.
So some are dealing with health problems
or economic problems
or even their status in the country.
So I was not able to help them
in the way that I wanted, so I felt helpless.
So, what could you do for them?
So I had to leave that part
in Jehovah’s hands and give them my time.
So I try to go
with them in service, try to encourage them.
Sometimes we laugh, sometimes we cry,
but I try to show them my love
—and even more important that Jehovah loves them.
Nice.
Well, I’m sure you left a little bit of your heart with all of them.
That’s very nice.
Now you’re here in Gilead.
Was that a surprise for you?
Yes, a big surprise.
And, Josh, I know Gilead actually has a special place in your heart.
Why is that?
It does.
It’s because my parents attended Gilead,
and that’s actually what brought them to Puerto Rico.
They attended the 52nd class.
Right. Good.
So having parents who went to Gilead, did they
keep Gilead in their heart even after they had a family and were raising you?
They did. Absolutely.
I remember they had their graduation photo
up in the hallway, where all of us would walk every day.
So every day of my life growing up I walked past that photo.
There it is, the 52nd class.
That’s them.
And also the way they were,
the way they served Jehovah, the love and zeal that they have:
It’s clear to me—even clearer now—
that Gilead had a big impact on them.
What would you say that impact was on them?
How did you see Gilead training in them?
I think of two things.
One is that they’re excellent students of the Bible and always have been.
My mom’s Bible has so many notes that I don’t think it can hold any more.
And my dad, I remember he would be reading the Bible with us at night,
and he had an envelope that he’d mark the family Bible with.
And all of a sudden he’d stop reading and stop to make a note on the envelope
because he came across a scripture that he wanted to use for a talk
or a shepherding call or just a point that he liked.
So that was an excellent example.
And also they’ve always worked very, very hard for Kingdom interests.
They’ve always had the goal to do as much as they can for as long as they can,
and that just kind of became the family motto.
So it’s interesting now going through Gilead
and seeing so much emphasis placed on exactly those things
—to feed your love for Jehovah and do as much as you can for the organization.
Yeah, I was going to ask you that as well.
Here you are sitting in class, and you’re hearing
to a great degree the same things your parents heard.
Has that helped you at all?
It has.
They must have had those qualities to an extent when they came to Gilead.
But I think, listening to the classes now,
it’s clear that Gilead stirred that up in them
and kept that flame burning for many, many years.
That’s beautiful.
And they must be very proud of both of you
as you apply yourselves and as you will apply the training
and look forward to applying it in your future assignments.
Thank you both very much for being with us today.
Thank you.
In the introduction, we quoted Paul’s words
at 1 Corinthians 9:22.
He said: “I have become all things to people of all sorts,
so that I might by all possible means save some.”
The apostle obligated himself to adjust his life
and personal tastes “for the sake of the good news.”
We hope today’s program has been encouraging to you,
whether it’s trying something you just don’t prefer
or something you didn’t think you could do in Jehovah’s service.
Maybe it’s just getting in the game, so to speak,
or giving someone a little piece of your heart to encourage them.
Today’s guests have shown us
that by adjusting our life
and personal tastes for the sake of the good news,
with Jehovah, we can cope with any change
or make any change for Jehovah’s service.
Thank you for being with us, and we look forward to seeing you
on another edition of The Inside Story.

在分区里，有一个弟兄是养牛的

ko.text: 이제 우리가 늘 기대하는 인사이드 스토리를 즐길 차례가 되었습니다.
진행은 길르앗 강사 중 한 분이신 트렌트 리폴드 형제가 해 주시겠습니다.
작년은 여호와의 백성 모두에게 변화의 시기였습니다.
우리는 융통성과 조심성과 합리적인 태도를 보여야 했죠.
길르앗에서도 이번에 열린 150기 학급에는 변화가 있었습니다.
예를 들어, 150기의 모든 학생은 미국 출신이거나
다섯 부부와 독신 형제 한 명은 모두 순회 활동을 하고 있습니다.
이분들이 학급의 거의 절반을 이루고 있죠.
오늘은 미국의 서로 다른 지역에서 오신 세 부부를 만나 보겠습니다.
그들이 어떻게 삶의 변화에 적응하는 법을 배웠는지 그리고
사도 바울처럼 ‘모든 사람에게 모든 것이 되’려고 노력했는지 알아보시죠.
첫 손님은 텍사스주에서 오신 테일러 본샤인과 조이 본샤인 부부입니다.
텍사스주는 정말 넓은데 어느 도시에서 오셨나요?
어떻게 정규 파이오니아를 시작하셨는지 자매부터 말씀해 주실까요?
제 경우는 정말 고맙게도 오래전부터 가족들이 좋은 본을 보이셨어요.
두 분은 결혼을 한 후에 최선을 다해 여호와를 섬기고 싶어 하셨어요.
도움이 필요한 곳이 어디인지 순회 감독자들에게 물어보곤 하셨죠.
다른 회중에 가 달라고 하면, 언제나 즉시 가셨습니다.
그런 본은 어머니께 좋은 영향을 미쳤고, 저에게도 그랬죠.
결혼 생활과 가족 부양과 자녀를 돌보는 일로 바쁘셨던 것 같아요.
그러다가 나라 반대쪽으로 이사 가게 되셨는데,
어렸지만 부모님이 달라지셨다는 걸 느낄 수 있었어요.
여호와를 위해 더 많은 걸 하실 수 있었기 때문이죠.
어머니가 파이오니아를 시작하시고 달라지셨다고 느꼈던 때가요?
네. 그럼 정규 파이오니아는 언제 시작하셨어요?
언니랑 제가 어머니를 따라 파이오니아를 시작했어요.
본샤인 형제, 형제는 어떻게 정규 파이오니아를 시작하셨나요?
저흰 텍사스에서 봉사했지만, 전 원래 콜로라도주에 살았어요.
아내처럼 제 부모님도 좋은 본을 보이셨어요.
어릴 때부터 파이오니아 봉사, 전 시간 봉사는 제게 아주 익숙했습니다.
제가 10대 중반일 때 부모님이 대리 순회 활동에 임명되셨어요.
두 분이 말로만이 아니라 행동으로 본을 보여 주셨다는 겁니다.
아, 좋으셨겠네요. 부모님이 대리 순회 활동을 하셨으니까요.
저는 고등학교를 6개월 일찍 졸업하고 파이오니아를 시작했습니다.
그리고 베델에서 일할 수 있는 19살이 되자마자 지원서를 냈고,
그 후 곧 초대를 받아서 몇 년 동안 브루클린에서 일했습니다.
그러고 나서 베델을 떠나셨고, 두 분은 결혼을 하셨죠.
그런데 어떻게 여호와를 위해 더 많은 일을 하려는 마음을 갖게 되셨나요?
저희는 파이오니아를 하는 젊은 부부였고, 목표도 있었죠.
하지만 신혼이라 결혼 생활에 적응해야 했고,
그 목표를 이루기 위해 어느 방향으로 가야 할지 몰랐어요.
시기적절하게 여러 순회 감독자 부부가 와서
얼마나 큰 도움을 주셨는지는 절대 모르실 거예요.
사실, 순회 활동을 하시는 분들은 젊은 사람들에게 도움을 많이 주십니다.
그게 그 봉사의 큰 유익 중 하나죠. 정말 고마운 일입니다.
그래서 두 분도 순회 활동을 하고 싶은 마음이 드셨나요?
부부가 같이 정말 베델에 가고 싶어서
지원서를 내고 또 냈는데, 아무 연락이 없었어요.
그럼 생각이 달라지신 건가요? 아니면 무슨 일이 있었나요?
네. 하루는 편지를 하나 받았는데, 대리 순회 활동을 위한 질문서였어요.
그게 우리가 가려고 했던 방향은 아니었지만,
여호와께서 우리 앞에 열어 놓으신 길 같아 보였어요.
그래서 기쁘게 받아들였고, 순회 활동에 대한 마음이 점점 자라 갔습니다.
그리고 저희는 왕국 전파자 학교에 참석할 수 있었습니다.
여호와께서 우리에게 바라시는 일을 할 마음을 키워 나갔죠.
그리고 학교를 졸업하고 몇 달이 채 안 되어
저희는 순회 활동을 하도록 임명되었고, 그 일을 좋아하게 되었습니다.
대도시 댈러스에서 대도시 시카고로 가게 돼서 좋았죠.
대도시에 살던 저희 둘이 댈러스에서 더 큰 도시 시카고로 가게 된 거죠.
그곳 사람들의 배경, 문화, 인종, 모든 게 다양해서 좋았어요.
즐거웠죠. 시카고 지역이 정말 마음에 들었습니다.
근데 “하지만”이 나올 것 같은데요. 어떤 변화가 있었죠?
저희가 한 6개월 정도 그 순회구에서 즐겁게 봉사하고 있을 때
지부 사무실에서 전화가 왔어요. 저희 순회구 임명이 바뀌어서
훨씬 북쪽에 있는 위스콘신주의 시골 지역으로 가게 됐다는 겁니다.
아, 위스콘신주요. 어떠셨어요? 형제는 위스콘신주가 어떠셨나요?
주민들 대부분이 낙농업을 하는 시골 순회구로 간다는 건 큰 변화였죠.
여기서는 봉사 다닐 때 운전을 정말 오래 했는데
그렇게 가도 가도 가게도, 화장실도, 커피숍도 없었죠.
아, 미리 시간 계획을 하는 법을 배우셨겠네요.
그러면 본샤인 자매는 댈러스에 살다가 그곳에 가니 어떠셨나요?
저에게 큰 변화는 날씨였어요. 추운 겨울 날씨요.
위스콘신주의 겨울은 아주 길고 아주 추웠어요.
그래서 따뜻한 코트와 두툼한 레깅스와 두꺼운 부츠를 샀죠.
전 아침에 일어나서 그 옷을 다 입다 보면 기운이 빠져 버린다고 농담을 했어요.
그렇게 껴입으면 불편하셨겠어요. 화장실 갈 때도 그렇고요.
그런 변화에 적응하는 데 뭐가 도움이 됐나요?
환경도 많이 달라지고 날씨도 정말 추웠지만
마음이 따뜻한 형제 자매들과 함께 있어서 행복했어요.
얼마 안 돼서 마치 한 가족처럼 느끼게 됐죠.
정말 금세 우리는 위스콘신 형제들을 사랑하게 됐습니다.
자매는 적응하시는 데 뭐가 도움이 됐나요?
물론 남편 말대로, 형제들의 사랑이 처음부터 도움이 됐어요.
그런데 댈러스에서 해 보지 못한 새로운 것도 하면서 재밌게 지냈죠.
아주 재밌으셨나 본데 얘기 좀 해 주실래요?
얼어붙은 호수 한가운데로 가서 얼음낚시를 했어요.
네, 사진이 또 있는데 좋아 보이네요. 본샤인 형제가 얘기해 주실래요?
가끔 가서 송아지를 만져 주고 우유를 먹일 기회가 있었어요.
시카고 시내나 댈러스 시내라면 해 볼 수 없었을 참 놀라운 경험이었죠.
실제로 ‘모든 사람에게 모든 것이 되’신 거네요.
그럼 여러 가지 변화를 겪으시면서 무엇을 배웠는지 말씀해 주시겠어요?
솔직히 말해서 순회 활동은 제가 하고 싶었던 게 아니었어요.
제가 그 일을 즐겁게 할 수 있을 거라고 생각하지 않았거든요.
우리가 좋아하거나 즐기지 않을 것 같은 일을 우리 앞에 놓아 두시죠.
저는 그분이 순회 활동을 할 기회를 주셔서 정말 감사합니다.
저흰 순회 활동을 아주 좋아하게 됐거든요.
제가 배운 건 여호와께서 우리 앞에 무언가를 선택해서 놓아 두실 때,
새로운 환경에서 그 일을 즐겁게 할 수 없을 거라는 생각이 들지 모르지만,
여호와께선 항상 가장 좋은 걸 선택해 주신다는 겁니다.
제 경우엔 언제나 변화가 있을 때마다, 좀 불안하고 걱정하고 그런 편이에요.
저는 기도하면서 문제를 여호와께 맡기는 법을 배웠습니다.
사실 많은 경우에 걱정하던 일들은 일어나지도 않죠.
여호와께서 무얼 하라고 하시든 우리는 해낼 수 있어요.
그런 일이 아예 일어나지 않거나 여호와께서 견딜힘을 주시기 때문이죠.
중요한 점 두 가지를 배우셨네요. 말씀해 주셔서 감사합니다.
앞으로 변화를 겪을 때, 그 교훈이 큰 도움이 될 겁니다.
본샤인 형제 자매, 인사이드 스토리에 나와 주셔서 감사합니다.
벤 프레이 형제와 휘트니 프레이 자매입니다.
두 분은 순회 활동을 하다가 길르앗에 오셨는데요.
그럼 프레이 자매는 어떻게 정규 파이오니아를 시작하셨나요?
어떤 삶을 살아야 할지 잘 모르겠더라고요.
근데 어느 날 제 친구의 남동생이 사고로 죽었는데
친구가 그 장례식에 와 달라고 부탁했어요.
그런데 정규 파이오니아를 시작하는 것과 장례식이 무슨 관련이 있죠?
네, 친구 남동생을 개인적으로 잘 몰랐지만 장례식에 갔어요.
알고 보니, 그 애는 파이오니아를 막 시작했고
나이가 되면 베델에 가는 게 목표였어요.
그 애는 가진 모든 걸 여호와께 드리려고 했는데,
전 똑같은 상황인데도 그렇게 하지 않았어요.
‘그 앤 하고 싶은 걸 다 못 했구나’ 하는 생각이 들어서,
집에 와서 기도한 다음 보조 파이오니아 지원서를 썼는데
격려적입니다. 슬픈 일이 있었지만 거기서 좋은 결과를 얻으셨네요.
아내처럼 저도 어머니께 진리를 배웠어요. 어릴 때 아버지는 진리 안에 안 계셨죠.
십 대 후반부터 이십 대 초반쯤에
이게 진리란 건 알았지만, 영적으로 어려움이 있었죠.
그 이유는 인생에서 해 보고 싶은 게 하도 많았는데
그때는 진리가 제 생활을 너무 제한한다고 느꼈거든요.
제가 원하는 풍요로운 삶을 살지 못하게 한다고 생각했죠.
저희 회중으로 이사 온 파이오니아 장로 두 분이 격려를 아주 많이 해 주셨어요.
그분들은 여호와를 섬기면 멋진 삶을 살 수 없는 게 아니라
실제로 해 보지는 않는다면 재미가 없을 겁니다.
그게 바로 그 당시의 제 모습이었죠.
진리인 건 알았지만 실제로 해 보진 않았던 겁니다.
이 두 형제의 격려를 받고 저도 비유적으로 말해 게임을 시작했습니다.
오래전에 했어야 할 성경 공부를 시작했고
얼마 안 있어 정규 파이오니아도 시작했습니다.
프레이 자매, 더 많은 일을 하려는 마음을 갖는 데 또 무엇이 도움이 됐나요?
네, 파이오니아를 하고 싶은 마음이 들었을 때,
특히 「땅 끝에 이르기까지」 동영상이 큰 영향을 줬죠.
‘내가 하고 싶은 게 바로 이거야. 길르앗에 가서 선교인이 되고 싶어.’
그러셨군요. 그 동영상은 지금도 jw.org에서 볼 수 있죠.
자매의 경우처럼 수많은 사람이 그 동영상을 보고 나서
봉사를 확장하고, 선교 봉사를 시작하고, 길르앗에 참석하게 됐을 겁니다.
많은 분이 여전히 임지에서 조직을 강화하고 안정시키고 있죠.
그럼 두 분 다 선교 봉사를 하려는 목표가 있으셨던 거네요.
남아메리카 가이아나의 도움이 더 필요한 곳에서 봉사했습니다.
사진을 가져오셨는데, 설명 좀 해 주시겠어요?
첫 번째 건 두 분 사진인 것 같은데요?
「땅 끝에 이르기까지」 동영상의 오토바이 장면이 인상 깊어서,
거기 갔을 때 오토바이를 한 대 샀죠.
동영상에 나오는 것만큼 크고 멋진 건 아니었지만,
여기저기 성서 연구와 재방문을 편하게 다닐 수 있었습니다.
네. 다음 사진에 대해서도 얘기해 주시겠어요, 프레이 자매?
네, 오토바이로 더 갈 수 없을 때는, 거기 세워 놓고 걸어갔어요.
진흙탕 길을 가거나 개천을 건너야 할 때가 많았죠.
네, 여긴 블랙 카이만이라고 하는 악어가 살고 있어서 조심해야 됩니다.
네, 그럼 가이아나에서 돌아오셨는데, 계속 길르앗을 목표로 하셨나요?
