ko.text: 워치타워 길르앗 성서 학교의 150번째 학급이 끝났습니다!
여호와의 도움으로 잘 끝난 이번 학급은
이번 학급은 다른 학급과 좀 달랐는데
평소보다 훨씬 적은 수인 24명의 학생만 참석했죠.
코로나19 바이러스로 인한 여행 제한 조치 때문에
다른 때와는 좀 달랐지만 학급의 목표는 같았습니다.
그들이 어디로 가든 다른 사람을 돕게 하는 것이었죠.
졸업식 프로그램은 학생들이 현재와 미래에 도움이 될
중요한 교훈에 초점을 맞추도록 해 주었습니다.
뉴욕주 패터슨의 워치타워 교육 센터에서 열린
졸업생 여러분 중에는 그때 아직 태어나지 않은 분도 계시죠?
하지만 한 명은 확실히 태어나 있었죠.
워치타워 길르앗 성서 학교 졸업식에 참석했습니다.
베델 봉사자가 아니고서는 흔치 않은 기회였습니다.
그래서 우리는 뉴욕시에 있는 한 대회회관에서
제52기 학급의 졸업식 프로그램을 보게 되어서
많은 분들이 실시간으로 이 프로그램을 보실 수 있죠.
그리고 나머지 모든 형제 자매들도 몇 달 후에 보실 수 있습니다.
따라서 지금은 모든 분들이 졸업식을 시청할 수 있지만
분명 노어 형제는 길르앗 학교를 정말 사랑했습니다.
여호와께선 짐승인 국제 연합이 나타날 것을 아시고
선교인을 위한 학교가 필요하다고 보신 것 같습니다.
어쨌든 제가 말씀드리고 싶은 건 그때 들었던 인상 깊은 연설입니다.
그전에 양키 스타디움 대회 때 형제의 연설을 듣긴 했지만,
졸업식에서는 더 가까이서 들을 수 있었죠.
프랜즈 형제 연설은 주의 깊이 들어야 한다고 말하곤 했는데,
자신의 마음에 새겨진 내용을 쏟아 놓을 때
처음 일곱 구절을 보면 서원에 대한 내용과 꿈이 언급됩니다.
프랜즈 형제의 그 연설은 제게 깊은 인상을 주었습니다.
우리가 잠을 잘 때 꾸는 꿈을 말하는 것이 아닙니다.
그냥 혼자 읽어서는 잘 이해가 되지 않을 수 있습니다.
이 구절들은 자신이 하고 싶은 일을 하느라
바로 이런 의미로 꿈을 꾼다는 것입니다.
그런 꿈을 꾸는 건 성구에도 나와 있듯이 헛된 일이죠.
그 밖의 다른 분들과 함께 살펴볼까요?
지금은 말고 나중에 해 보실 수 있는데요,
「연구 자료 찾아보기」를 사용해서 전도서에 들어 있는 지혜의 말씀을
더 깊이 있게 조사해 보시기 바랍니다.
곧 졸업하는 여러분들에게 여호와께서 하시는 말씀입니다.
그 다음으론 도덕적으로 미련한 자들에 관한 언급이 나옵니다.
여러분은 이러한 사람이 되어서는 안 되죠.
“네 입으로 성급히 말하지 말라”는 말이 나옵니다.
정말 이 세상엔 이 조언을 들어야 할 사람들이 많지 않습니까?
보면 어떤 사람들은 입을 다물지를 않습니다.
잘 때도 말할 겁니다. 쉴 새 없이 말을 하죠.
문맥상 여호와께 말할 때 그래야 한다는 말입니다.
특히 형제들은 공개적인 자리에서 말할 때 이 점을 기억해야 합니다.
자매들도 개인적으로 기도하면서 우주의 주권자에게 나아갈 때
그리고 어떤 언어로 드리는 기도이든 소중히 여기십니다.
“신경 쓸 일이 많으면 꿈을 꾸게 된다”고 말합니다.
따라서 이것은 잠을 잘 때 꾸는 꿈을 말하는 것이 아니라
자신에 관해 지나치게 신경 쓰는 것을 경고하는 것입니다.
이전 그 어느 때보다 공개적으로 기도할 기회가 많을 것입니다.
여러분은 많은 특권을 갖게 될 텐데
공개적으로 기도할 때 너무 길게 기도하거나,
누군가를 교훈하거나 훈계하는 듯한 기도를 해서는 안 되죠.
베델에서도 기도가 길 때가 있는데 이런 생각이 들어요.
저는 사람들에게 이런 말을 할 때가 있는데요,
마음을 쏟아 놓는 개인적인 기도를 드려야 할 때가 있는데요,
더 길게 기도해도 괜찮아.” 이러지 마세요.
개인적인 기도가 아니면 길게 하지 마십시오.
이제, 다음으로 우리 모두가 마음에 새겨야 할
“서원하고 지키지 않는 것보다 서원하지 않는 것이 낫다.”
입으로 죄를 짓지 않도록 조심하라는 경고입니다.
예를 들어 결혼한 분들은 서원한 것이죠.
그 밖의 어떤 서원이든 신중해야 하죠.
서원을 하면 여호와 앞에 책임이 있습니다.
“네가 입으로 죄를 짓는 일이 없게 하고
여호와께서는 천사들이 다양한 일을 수행하게 해 오셨습니다.
하지만 우린 천사들이 하느님의 종들과 관련해서
어떤 놀라운 일을 하고 있는지 거의 알지 못하죠.
우리의 서원을 확인한다는 걸 알 수 있습니다.
따라서 천사에게 이렇게 말할 수 있을까요?
하지만 천사가 우리가 서원을 지키는지 확인하기 때문이 아니라
여호와에 대한 사랑에서 우러나와 서원을 지켜야 합니다.
서원을 할 때는 결혼 서약이든 무엇이든 여호와에 대한 사랑이
그 서원을 지키는 동기가 되어야 합니다.
“신경 쓸 일이 많으면 꿈을 꾸게 되듯, 말이 많으면 결국 헛되다.”
왕국 전파자 학교와 같은 다른 학교들도 있지만
여러분 학급을 가르치도록 교습 위원회가 선정한 강사들은
여호와 하느님을 온 영혼을 다해 섬기는 사람들입니다.
그것이 바로 이 학교가 특별한 이유이죠.
따라서 이 교육을 베풀어 주신 여호와께 감사하십시오.
그리고 받은 교육을 활용해 그분을 영광스럽게 하십시오.
이렇게 하는 것은 5:7의 마지막 문장에 담긴 교훈과도 일치합니다.
곧 졸업하실 여러분들은 이 말씀을 마음에 새겨야 합니다.
그리고 자신에게 초점을 맞추느라 꿈을 꾸지 마십시오.
그렇게 되면 여러분이 길르앗에서 받은 교육이 헛된 것이 될 것입니다.
제 얘기는 여러분이 그렇다는 것이 아닙니다.
하지만 여호와의 말씀에 담긴 이 교훈을 명심하십시오.
전도서의 이 구절들에는 배울 것들이 많습니다.
따라서 「연구 자료 찾아보기」를 가지고 더 조사해 보십시오.
마크 샌더슨 형제가 해 주실 텐데요, 아주 열심히 준비하셨습니다.
오늘 연설할 형제들이 모두 온 마음을 다해 연설을 준비하셨죠.
다음과 같은 주제로 연설해 주실 것입니다.
그러나 완전히 가르침받은 사람은 모두 자기 선생처럼 될 것입니다.”
이 성구를 보시면 어떤 생각이 드십니까?
누군가와 성서 연구를 하는 장면이 떠오르실지 모릅니다.
또는 길르앗 학교와 같은 프로그램을 통해
가르치는 일을 하고 있다고 볼 수 있습니다.
우리가 어떤 영적인 책임이나 특권을 갖고 있다면
형제 자매들은 관심을 갖고 우리를 살펴볼 것입니다.
또 우리와 함께 일하는 사람들은 우리를 보고 배울 것입니다.
하지만 사도 바울이 다른 사람들을 가르친 방법은
그의 그리스도인 삶 전체가 강력한 교훈이 되었습니다.
사람들은 바울의 본에서 무엇을 배울 수 있었습니까?
“오히려 우리는 젖 먹이는 어머니가 자기 자녀를 따뜻하게 돌보는 것처럼
바울은 진리의 소식만 전한 것이 아니라
바울은 “좋은 소식을 위해 모든 일을” 하겠다고 말했는데,
그가 그렇게 한 몇 가지 예들을 살펴보겠습니다.
내가 정신 나간 사람처럼 말하는데, 나는 훨씬 뛰어난 봉사자입니다.
내가 일도 더 많이 했고, 감옥에도 더 여러 번 갇혔고,
매도 수없이 맞았고, 죽을 고비도 많이 넘겼습니다.
유대인들에게 40에서 하나를 뺀 매를 다섯 번 맞았고,
세 번 매질을 당했고, 한 번 돌로 맞았고,
계속 보면 이 밖에도 많은 어려움을 겪었죠.
하느님에 대한 사랑, 인내, 열심, 비이기적인 태도는
바울과 가깝게 일한 디모데를 생각해 보시죠.
여러분의 일을 진실하게 돌볼 사람이 아무도 없습니다.
다른 사람들은 모두 자기 일에만 관심을 가지면서
예수 그리스도의 일에는 관심을 기울이지 않습니다.

아직도 갈 길이 멀구나 하는 생각이 듭니다.
형제 자매들을 어떻게 강화할 수 있을지
그 방법을 찾기 위해 노력하시기 바랍니다.
이제 길르앗 강사이자 교습 위원회 보조자이신
마크 누매어 형제의 연설을 들어 보겠습니다.
여러분은 이 특성, 충성스러운 사랑의 힘으로
앞으로 닥치게 될 많은 시련과 어려움을 이겨낼 수 있을 것입니다.
아마 필기 시험에 나왔던 충성스러운 사랑의 정의를 기억하실 겁니다.
헌신적인 마음과 깊은 애착에서 우러나온 사랑을 가리킵니다.
시편에서 그와 여호와 사이의 사랑을 이렇게 말했습니다.
“내가 당신에게 매달리니 당신이 오른손으로 굳게 잡아 주십니다.”
1세기에 살았던 한 여자는 여호와께 매달리는 아주 뛰어난 본을 보였습니다.
“그리고 여예언자 안나가 있었는데, 바누엘의 딸로서 아셀 지파에 속해 있었다.
이 여자는 나이가 많았는데, 결혼한 뒤 7년 동안 남편과 함께 살다가
단식하고 간구하며 밤낮으로 신성한 봉사를 드렸다.”
우리가 안나에 대해 알고 있는 게 여기 다 있는데 누가가 기록했죠.
따라서 예수의 제자가 될 정도로 오래 살지는 못했을 겁니다.
또 성령으로 기름부음받거나, 왕국의 좋은 소식을 전하지도 못했겠죠.
하지만 더 조사해 본다면 무엇을 배울 수 있을까요?
그가 23살이었을 때, 예루살렘은 폭력과 분열로 가득했습니다.
마카베오 가문의 지도자와 같은 유대 지도자들이 싸움을 벌이자
그 과정에서 약 1만 2000명의 유대인이 사망했다고 합니다.
어쩌면 안나의 남편도 이때 죽임을 당했을지 모르죠.
안나가 47살이었을 때, 로마는 헤롯을 유대의 왕으로 임명합니다.
그는 다윗의 후손이 아니었고 이스라엘 사람도 아니었습니다.
안나 같은 과부를 포함해 사람들의 삶을 힘들게 만들었습니다.
안나는 자신이 소중히 여기는 곳인 여호와의 “기도하는 집”이
메시아가 오고 예언들이 성취될 거라고 믿었지.
날마다 성전에 가고 할 수 있는 건 다 했는데, 상황은 나빠지기만 했어.
남편도 죽고, 에돔 사람이 성전을 재건하고 있잖아.
안나는 상심해서 다 포기해 버릴 수 있었지만, 그러지 않았습니다.
깊이 뿌리내린 그 사랑이 견딜힘을 주었던 겁니다.
그래서 그런 상황 속에서도 계속 여호와께 매달릴 수 있었습니다.
안나는 최선을 다해 여호와를 섬기기로 결심했습니다.
밤낮으로 신성한 봉사를 드렸다.” 올바른 일이죠.
안나는 올바른 장소에서 올바른 태도로 올바른 일을 했습니다.
연약해 보이는 안나가 가장 친밀한 벗인 여호와께
매달리는 것을 아무것도 막을 수 없었습니다.
부모가 아기 예수를 성전에 데려왔을 때, 안나가 거기 있었다는 걸 알 수 있습니다.
아기를 보고 안나가 어떻게 했는지 38절을 보시죠.
예루살렘의 구출을 기다리고 있는 모든 사람에게 그 아이에 대해 말했다.”
메시아가 될 아기를 보고, 어쩌면 안아 보기까지 했을 때
자기 생애에 있을 거라곤 전혀 기대하지 못한 일이었죠.
그러니까 안나만 여호와께 매달린 게 아니라
안나의 믿음의 본은 아주 잘 알려져 있어서
약 50년이 지난 뒤에, 약 50년 뒤에 누가가 그에 관한 기록을 남겼습니다.
마리아나 나이 든 분들에게 이런 말을 들었을까요?
‘안나라는 여자가 있었는데 늘 성전에 와서 떠나질 않았지.’
우리가 아는 것은 여호와께서 누가에게 영감을 주셔서
그분의 말씀에 안나의 삶에 관한 기록을 하게 하심으로
헌신적인 마음과 꺾을 수 없는 충절을 나타낸 안나는
학생 여러분이 따라야 할 훌륭한 본으로 사용되고 있습니다.
안나의 본에서 무엇을 배울 수 있습니까?
소중한 누군가나 무언가를 잃게 될 때,
또는 다른 사람의 불완전성 때문에 힘들 때가 있을지 모르죠.
살면서 예상치 않게 달갑지 않은 변화를 겪게 될 때,
또는 조직 내에서 불공정을 당하거나 심한 오해를 받았다고 느낄 때가
한 예로, 외국어 밭에서 봉사하던 한 형제 생각이 나는데요.
이 형제는 오해가 있어서 장로의 특권을 잃게 되었습니다.
형제는 부당한 결정이라고 느껴 몹시 상심했죠.
하지만 그와 그의 아내는 여호와께 매달리기를 중단하지 않고 영적 활동을 계속했습니다.
얼마 후 지역 대회에서 어떤 형제가 다가오더니 연설 잘 들었다고 인사를 하는 것이었습니다.
그런데 장로였던 이 형제는 청소 자원봉사는 했지만 연설은 하지 않았죠.
“형제가 보여 주신 미소와 긍정적인 태도는 훌륭한 연설 같았습니다.
충성에 관한 그 연설은 이해하기 쉽고 분명했죠.”
“그 경험을 통해 우리 부부가 배운 건 어려움이나 불행한 일이 있더라도,
그런 일 때문에 영적으로 위태로워지면 안 된다는 것입니다.
우리는 거부당하고, 실패하고, 오해 받는 것을
우리 모두가 겪는 정상적인 삶의 일부로 보게 되었습니다.
네, 이 부부는 자신들이 겪는 문제 너머를 보았고 여호와께 매달렸습니다.
이 부부는 ‘빠지지 않고 참숭배를 드렸으며 [올바른 장소였죠.]
밤낮으로 신성한 봉사를 드렸습니다.’ 올바른 일이었죠.
그들도 때론 기도하며 눈물을 흘렸지만 올바른 태도를 유지했죠.
여호와께서는 그들을 잡아 주시고 손을 놓지 않으셨습니다.
다시 장로가 되었고 격려적인 연설을 하고 있습니다.
그럼 오늘 이 연설에서 무엇을 기억해야 할까요?
여러분이 앞으로 시련을 겪을 때, 분명 겪게 되겠죠.
살면서 어려움을 겪을 때, 그런 일은 항상 생기죠.
올바른 장소에서 올바른 태도로 올바른 일을 하십시오.
그렇게 하는 것은 이처럼 말하는 것입니다.
“여호와여, 내가 매달리니, 오른손으로 굳게 잡아 주십시오.”
우리 모두를 위한 훌륭한 본을 알려 주셔서 감사합니다.
데이비드 존스 형제와 린 존스 자매 부부와의
존스 형제는 그곳에서 지부 위원으로 섬기고 있습니다.
이 부부를 기억하는 분들이 계실 텐데요,
이 부부가 졸업한 학급이 나왔기 때문이죠.
길르앗 성서 학교 50주년을 기념하여 제작된 것이었습니다.
이 비디오를 통하여 우리는 많은 것을 알게 되었죠.
그때 이후로 길르앗 학교의 목적이 바뀌긴 했지만,
이 부부의 진심 어린 이야기를 들어 보면 그들이 임지에서
형제들을 강화하고 안정시키는 역할을 해 왔다는 것을
바로 오늘이 여러분 학생들에게 임명장을 나누어 주는 날입니다.
임명장을 받는 날 아침 우리는 아침 숭배에 나갔습니다.
그리고 나선 줄 서서 임명장을 기다려야 했죠.
긴장이 되고 흥분이 되면서, 속이 울렁거리고 떨렸습니다.
재라스 형제가 무엇이라고 말하든 형제의 입에서 나오는 다음 말이
처음 임지를 받은 게 벌써 28년 전이라는 게 믿기지가 않아요.
길르앗 훈련은 상황이 순탄치 만은 않을 거라는 걸 이해하게 도와줬어요.
또 그럴 때 너무 불안해하지 말고
길르앗 수업 중 가장 기억에 남는 부분은
복음서와 예수 그리스도에 관해 다루는 내용이었습니다.
사람들을 대할 때 늘 합리적인 태도를 보이셨습니다.
그래서 수업 시간에 강조한 점은 자세한 지식보다는
오랜 세월이 지난 지금도 잊지 않고 있어요.
성경에 나오는 여러 가지 많은 원칙들을
그렇게 해서 어떤 어려움을 만나든 어떤 상황에 처하든
배운 원칙들 중에서 그 상황에서 꼭 알맞는 원칙을
물론 수업 시간에는 많은 내용을 배우고 기억하느라 바쁘죠.
배운 걸 언제 어떻게 사용하게 될진 모르지만
필요할 때 언제든 꺼내 쓰는 방법을 배우게 돼요.
예를 들면 한 가지 수업이 생각나는데,
이 강의에서 배운 걸 적용한 일이 기억나는데,
저희는 야외 선교인으로 한동안 일한 뒤에
‘내가 정말 이 일을 할 수 있을까?’ 하는 생각이 들었죠.
나 자신이 아니라 여호와의 뜻을 행하고
그렇게 하니까 더 큰 그림을 보게 됐고,
예수께서 하신 것처럼 저도 제 자신을 기쁘게 하는 것이 아니라
형제 자매들을 앞자리에 둬야 한다는 걸 깨달았습니다.
사실, 걱정과는 다르게 순회 봉사가 너무 즐거워서
3년간의 임명이 끝났을 때 그만두고 싶지가 않더라고요.
수업을 받을 땐 보통 그 가치를 온전히 깨닫지 못하죠.
길르앗 학교 수업 때 배운 교훈들을
오랜 시간이 지났지만 그동안 그 교훈들이
제 사고방식을 틀 잡아 왔던 겁니다.
길르앗 학교에서 배운 교훈들이 제 인생과 성품에
줄 서서 임지를 기다리던 때가 아직도 눈앞에 생생해요.
그때 전 너무 긴장해서 속이 다 울렁거렸죠.
지난 세월의 경험을 그 어느 것과도 바꾸지 않겠다고
지금까지 우리는 풍성한 영적 잔치를 잘 즐겼습니다.
나머지 프로그램도 크게 유익할 거라 확신합니다.
이번 달 방송을 마치기 전에 타히티로 가 보실까요?
그리고 백사장으로 둘러싸인 환초들이 있는 아름다운 곳입니다.
아름다운 자연 경관뿐만 아니라 이곳 사람들의 친절한 태도도
하느님의 말씀의 놀라운 소식을 전하는 일을 중심으로 살고 있습니다.
산들과 외따로 떨어진 아파타키섬과 리키티아까지 걸쳐 있습니다.
큰 항구에서 외국에서 온 선원에게 증거합니다.
회중 성원들이 전 세계에 있는 여러분에게
지금까지 여호와의 증인의 세계 본부에서 JW 방송이었습니다!

en.text: We’re delighted you could join us.
Welcome to JW Broadcasting®
for December 2021!
The Watchtower Bible School of Gilead
has now completed 150 classes!
This certainly is a theocratic milestone
made possible with Jehovah’s help.
This 150th class was a little different.
There were only 24 students, which is much less than usual.
And because of travel restrictions based on the COVID-19 pandemic,
all are citizens of the United States.
Though this group was different than in years past,
the goal remained the same:
to strengthen their faith so that they can strengthen others
wherever they are assigned.
The graduation program helped the students
to focus on key points they will benefit from on into the future.
Please enjoy Part 1 of the graduation
that was held on Saturday, September 11, 2021,
at the Watchtower Educational Center
in Patterson, New York!
I’m going to go back many decades ago
—Monday, March 6, 1972.
Now, some of you in the class weren’t alive.
I think I know of one for sure who was alive.
That’s an inside joke, not Inside Story
—but anyway.
And along with my wife, we had the privilege
(and that was rare unless you were a Bethelite)
to attend the graduation
of the Watchtower Bible School of Gilead.
That was the 52nd class.
So we’re in the Assembly Hall
(jam packed there in New York City)
and just enjoying it.
What a privilege for us to sit there
and enjoy that program of the 52nd class!
Now here we are almost 100 (just two shy) classes later
—the 150th class.
And now we’re grateful
because many are tied in live as we speak.
But then the rest of the brotherhood
is going to have it available in a few months.
So boy, things have changed, and they enjoy that privilege.
But that was a rare privilege.
And I remember Brother Knorr was the chairman
of the program.
And certainly, he just loved Gilead.
I mean, that you’ve got to give him.
Of course, Jehovah used him mightily to get it all started there
—1943 was the first one.
But knowing that the beast was coming out,
Jehovah blessed them and said, ‘Yeah, we need a missionary school.’
There was a missionary school for years.
But anyway, the thing I wanted to mention is that I remember an outstanding talk.
I had heard Brother Fred Franz the summer before
at the Yankee Stadium convention,
but we were a little closer there in the Assembly Hall.
And I’ll tell you what; I was just glued to him.
If you had the privilege to hear him, Jehovah blessed—
He had a blessed, beautiful mind.
He could just quote these scriptures.
And I’ve told folks:
“Now, if you don’t pay attention and stay with him,
“you’re going to get lost.
He’s going to lose you.”
But if you paid attention, it was thrilling
just to hear him pour out his heart
because it was all written on his figurative heart.
But he discussed Ecclesiastes 5.
That’s why I was thinking of bringing it up for your class here.
Because this is really directed to you.
And he spoke there about vows.
In those first seven verses, dreams are mentioned.
And I appreciate it because it just struck me when he mentioned it.
The dreams don’t refer to dreams one has while they’re sleeping
because of the busy day.
Now, you can’t get that on your own
by just reading Ecclesiastes with whatever version you have.
It had to do with getting sidetracked
with personal pursuits.
These dreams —these are the things they’re doing.
And that would be “vanity” (as we’d said then).
So let’s just take a moment
(you here in the class and others who want to follow along in Ecclesiastes 5)
and just touch on some of the nice things.
And, of course, you could—
Now, don’t do it right now, but you can do it later.
You have access to the Research Guide
—an in-depth understanding
of this wisdom in Ecclesiastes.
And Brother Franz addressed it.
For example, verse 1 says: “Watch your step.”
So this is for you soon-to-be graduates.
Jehovah is saying: “Watch your step.”
Don’t stop doing that.
You have thus far, so continue to “watch your step.”
And he mentions those morally “stupid ones.”
That’s not you.
You can avoid that.
And then I love this in verse 2:
“Do not be quick with your mouth.”
Boy, there are a lot of people in the world who could benefit from that counsel.
Isn’t that true?
It’s like: ‘Does he or she ever shut up?
‘I mean, they must— I bet you they talk in their sleep.
They just won’t shut up.’
Then, anyway, ‘don’t be quick with your mouth,’
particularly in context here
when you’re speaking to Jehovah.
Boy, those are some good things to keep in mind,
especially for you brothers who will speak in public.
But you sisters too, when it’s personal with your prayers to Jehovah,
don’t be quick with your mouth
when you approach the Sovereign of the universe.
Your words should be few.
You do not impress God with vocabulary.
He’s impressed with sincerity of heart.
He loves those who love him.
And in all different languages, he treasures those prayers.
And then he mentions this:
“A dream comes from too many preoccupations.”
In the revised Bible here, it says “too many cares.”
So this idea isn’t just dreams from a busy, busy day.
This preoccupation with self
is being warned against here.
Don’t do it. See, do not do it.
Don’t be preoccupied with yourself.
And for those who are, there are many words from them.
But be careful, you know.
You have the privilege now; you’ll be praying more in public
—probably more than you ever have before.
You get privileges, you know.
And when you’re praying to Jehovah, sometimes—

Finally, you know very well
that we’ve only touched on a few things that you can boast in,
but you’ll want to continue doing that —boasting in Jehovah.
And right now, I know (all of you students) you feel great.
You’ve completed your course. You’ve done it.
You’re graduating from Gilead School,
and now the doors of future activity
are swinging open to you.
So as you undertake your assignments,
whatever and wherever they may be,
do these things, please:
Stay humble,
be happy,
and work hard.
And always esteem highly
the great honor and privilege you have
to “boast in Jehovah.”
Thanks.
Thanks, Bill.
As usual, we thoroughly enjoyed your talk.
Now, our second prerecorded interview
of a Gilead graduate now in his assignment
takes us to Ecuador, South America.
This brother serves on the Branch Committee in Ecuador,
and he graduated from the 142nd class of Gilead.
Notice as he explains
(notice) the positive impact
that Gilead graduates had on him
from his childhood
and how his training while at Gilead
helped him to appreciate what is truly important.
Brother and Sister Tapia will be going back to Ecuador.
Gilead training is a beautiful way
that Jehovah is using divine education
to train people
—not only for their benefit.
By having Gilead graduates
all around the world,
we are sharing the impact of this school
on the brothers and sisters who are working
with these students and future graduates.
It was Gilead missionaries
who first introduced the truth to my parents
and helped them to the point of baptism.
So I have very pleasant memories
of Gilead graduates being around my home since childhood.
The greatest legacy I received through my Gilead training
is the privilege of getting to know
Jehovah’s beautiful personality more deeply.
I have been studying the Bible since childhood,
but doing so with the help of the Gilead instructors
really helped me to make connections
that I had never put together before.
You don’t go to Gilead to learn abilities,
which can sometimes overshadow spiritual qualities.
Instead, a very important part of Gilead training
is the study of Christ’s personality.
And you know, Jesus is mostly remembered
not so much for his abilities
but for how he perfectly reflected
the beautiful qualities of his father.
By getting to know Jehovah and Jesus better,
I was able to better see where I need to improve.
Of course, it can be discouraging at times
to not always act as they do,
but that has helped me
to have the proper perspective and to rely on Jehovah,
begging him for his guidance while waiting for his help.
One of the best lessons I took away from Gilead is
that people are more important than tasks or deadlines.
People are the reason for our assignment,
and that is why I need to show my love to my brothers and sisters.
Honestly, I don’t feel at all qualified for this assignment,
but I have learned that if Jehovah assigns us a certain task,
for sure he will give us what we need to accomplish it.
That was very nice.
We certainly appreciate it.
Now, we have one of the Gilead instructors next,
Brother James Cauthon.
And he’s chosen as his subject
“Thriving in the Trenches.”
Located in the western Pacific Ocean,
the Mariana Trench is the deepest known location on earth.
To help you get an idea of its depth,
imagine that you could stack
the Empire State Building
in the trench.
It would take 25 such buildings to go
from the bottom of the trench before you would reach sea level.
It is also one of the deadliest places on earth.
Why is that?
In a word—pressure.
The crushing pressure, water pressure,
on the floor of the trench is more than eight tons per square inch.
Now, to give you some idea,
that would be the equivalent
of having about 50 jumbo jets
on top of you.
Surely no life could live in that trench.
At least that’s what scientists thought.
But they were wrong.
When they finally developed a submersible
that would take them down into the trench,
they found life teeming
—and not just surviving but thriving.
Now, how is that possible?
It’s possible, friends, because Jehovah, our Creator,
knows how to deal with pressure.
Jehovah knows how to deal with pressure.
And this is a fact that should be comforting to all of us.
Why?
Because the pressure
in this system of things is increasing
—strain, stress, anxiety—
for all people at all levels.
And the Bible tells us
that these pressures are likely to increase in the near future.
But the good news is
that Jehovah does more than just equip his servants to survive.
He can actually make one thrive.
Here’s an example.
Try this on for pressure.
You’re surrounded by men who hate you.
In addition to hunting you down with a view to taking your life,
they’ve spread slander and lies about you everywhere.
Your name has become a reproach.
When people see you coming, they turn and run the other way
because they feel that your time is short
and they don’t want to be caught in the crosshairs.
Wherever you look, it seems like terror is waiting for you.
And as a result of these problems, you’re struggling with depression.
Your own sins are staring you in the face.
The whole experience has taken a toll on your health.
You can’t sleep.
Your stamina is shot.
Your body is wasting away.
Now, that was David’s situation,
and you can read about it at Psalm 31:10-13.
The pressure was real —no question about it.
David’s feelings were real —no question about that.
But something else was very real.
And that was Jehovah.
And so Jehovah was where David would turn to.
Let’s turn to his words in Psalm 31.
Psalm 31—and note his humble prayer
beginning in verse 14.
He said: “But I trust in you, O Jehovah,
“I declare: ‘You are my God.’
“My days are in your hand.
“Rescue me from the hand of my enemies and from those persecuting me.
“Make your face shine upon your servant.
Save me by your loyal love.”
David’s life experiences
had taught him the value of turning to God
and pouring out his heart in times of trial.
And he absolutely knew that prayer,
coupled with implicit trust and patience,
would always bring Jehovah’s blessing.
And you see, friends, the key to not just surviving
but thriving under extreme pressure
is to have the internal pressure
equal to the external.
And when this is true,
there is no amount of pressure that can crush you.
So in a spiritual sense,
David received the internal fortitude or, as some say,
“the intestinal fortitude,”
meaning “the courage and the strength
that would make him equal to the pressure weighing in on him.”
And how do we know that he received that?
Well, let’s go back to Psalm 31 for just a moment.
If you look in verse 21, notice now
the change.
He says: “May Jehovah be praised,
“for in a wonderful way, he has shown his loyal love to me
in a besieged city.”
And then in verse 23:
“Love Jehovah, all you who are loyal to him!
Jehovah protects the faithful.”
And finally in verse 24:
“Be courageous, and may your heart be strong,
all you who are waiting for Jehovah.”
So, you see, David
received an answer to his prayer
—his prayer coupled with his faith
and his patience.
He was waiting on Jehovah.
And Jehovah helped him not only to survive but to thrive.
And he added joy to David
because David went on to find joy and happiness
in his responsibilities and privileges.
So, what do we learn?
(1) David was able to face the pressure
because he had an unshakable faith in Jehovah,
(2) David’s relationship with Jehovah
brought him the patience to wait on God,
and (3) when a loyal servant of God
humbly turns to Jehovah for help,
it is Jehovah’s own loyal love
that has the effect of equalizing the pressure.
And, you know, there’s something else.
David’s experience in the trench reached further than he ever knew.
Jonah, while in the belly of the great fish,
cited words from Psalm 31.
Jeremiah, who had many trialsome times in his life,
often echoed phrases from Psalm 31.
And Jesus Christ himself, the very Son of God—
His final words from the stake
were a quotation from Psalm 31:5.
So Jesus must have meditated on this many times.
And so, friends, like David, Jonah, Jeremiah,
Jesus, and many, many others
—they all trusted in Jehovah,
and Jehovah never failed to make them equal to the pressure.
He’ll do the same for you.
And so in conclusion,
you see, it really doesn’t matter
how great the pressure is.
It only matters where the pressure lies.
Do not let it come between you
and Jehovah and your worship and service.
Don’t let it come between you,
because then the external pressure
will only continue to move you closer
to your heavenly Father.
The life that flourishes in the Mariana Trench gives
a positive example, a beautiful example,
of Jehovah’s limitless ability to help his creation
deal with pressure.
Prayer, trust, and patience
will always be rewarded by Jehovah.
Relief will come.
So remain close to your heavenly Father,
and you will not just survive
the pressure in the trench
but you will thrive spiritually.
Thank you, Brother Cauthon, for your nice, insightful comments
—much appreciated.
Now, our third interview involves a brother
who serves as a member of the Branch Committee
in Sri Lanka.
He graduated from the 146th class of Gilead
—so just four classes back.
Listen carefully as he explains
how Gilead training helped him to see things about his personality
that he needed to refine
to become a stabilizing and strengthening influence
in his branch territory.
Brother and Sister Sivakumaran will be returning to Sri Lanka.
In Gilead, the wonderful thing
is that you get to learn from the beginning
Jehovah’s dealings with humankind,
that vast history.
Learning that is humbling.
How tiny I am
and the small role that I play
in Jehovah’s organization are a realization!
Before going to Gilead, I thought I was a loving person,
because we always think we want to be loving people.
But during Gilead, it was made aware to me
that I had a spiritual blind spot.
There were brothers and sisters that I didn’t really notice before,
and that kind of taught me an important lesson.
It’s not about giving talks,
but really it’s personal attention that brothers need.
So I need to give them my time,
and I need to help them understand
that Jehovah loves them very much.
You know, one word that stands out throughout the training is “mercy.”
Israel made many mistakes,
but Jehovah never picked on them for their mistakes.
He just wanted them to come back to him, and that was a lovely lesson.
As an overseer, I need to ask a question that always,
you know, rings in my my ear,
‘Am I going to criticize, or am I going to commend?’
Just to give you an example, before going to Gilead,
as a home overseer I was strict
and came across stingy, to be honest.
But during Gilead, it was made well aware to me
that I need to change.
I need to be more generous,
and I need to be merciful.
I vividly remember that one instructor said:
“Saying no to everything can be addictive,
and it makes for an easy way out.”
But we were admonished to say yes whenever we can
and to help the brothers.
Summing up Gilead, I can’t do better than Jesus.
Love Jehovah; love people
—that’s the whole training of Gilead.
And some of my feelings
every time I think about Gilead
are that I have a long way to go to put all those details into practice
and to change myself to fit Jehovah.
So, yeah, I have a long way to go, so I’m working on it.
So we pray that all of you soon-to-be graduates
examine yourself to ensure
that you’ll have a strengthening effect on the brotherhood.
It was nice, the humble expressions he shared with us.
Now let’s turn our attention to another one of the Gilead instructors
and a helper to the Teaching Committee, Mark Noumair.
The title of his talk is
“‘I Cling to You; You Hold on to Me.’”
Brother Noumair.
In this talk, we want you to understand
the sustaining power of loyal love.
Because it is this quality, loyal love,
and its power
that will help you face future trials
and challenges with confidence in Jehovah.
Well, you perhaps remember the definition
of loyal love from a written review.
But it’s this: It is love motivated
by a strong commitment and a deep attachment.
And here’s how King David described
the loyal love that existed between him and Jehovah.
He said at Psalm 63:8:
“I cling to you;
your right hand keeps fast hold on me.”
Now, this is loyal love,
‘I cling to you.
You hold on to me.’
Now, in the first century —a woman—
a woman who set an outstanding example
of clinging to Jehovah is Anna.
How so? Let’s find out.
We open our Bibles to Luke chapter 2.
We’re going to read verses 36 and 37
and see what lesson we can learn and apply to you:
“Now there was a prophetess,
“Anna the daughter of Phanuel, of Asher’s tribe.
“This woman was well along in years
“and had lived with her husband for seven years after they were married,
“and she was a widow now 84 years old.
“She was never missing from the temple,
“rendering sacred service night and day
with fasting and supplications.”
Well, here we have it.
Everything we know about Anna is right here.
Luke recorded it.
She was 84 years old
when Luke introduces her to us.
Likely, she hadn’t lived long enough to become a follower of Jesus,
to be anointed with holy spirit,
or to enjoy preaching the good news of the Kingdom.
That’s it.
If  we stop right there.
But what if we don’t?
What if we dig deeper?
What will we learn that will help you?
Well, let’s do that.
Anna was born about 86 B.C.E.
When she was 23 years old,
Jerusalem was filled with violence and divisions.
Jewish leaders such as the Maccabees are at war.
Roman forces under the leadership of a soldier named Pompey
came to restore order, and in the process,
some 12,000 Jews reportedly died.
It is possible that Anna’s husband
was one of these victims.
Then when Anna was 47 years old,
the Romans appointed Herod as king of Judea.
Herod?
This man was not a descendant of David.
He was not even an Israelite.
He was an Edomite.
The Edomites were sworn enemies of true worship.
Now, on top of that, the hypocritical Jewish religious leaders
made life hard for people, including widows like Anna.
So now Anna watches as Jehovah’s “house of prayer,”
the place she cherished, became “a cave of robbers.”
Pure worship is withering on the vine.
What will Anna do?
She could have been stumbled.
She could have reasoned: ‘I supported true worship all my life.
‘I believed the Messiah would come and the prophecies would come.
‘I go to the temple every day.
‘I’ve done everything right, but things have only gotten worse.
‘God let my husband die; an Edomite is rebuilding the temple.
‘What’s happening?
‘Has Jehovah left us?
Should I leave too?’
Anna could have given up, walked away, became bitter.
But she didn’t.
Why? Why?
It was the roots of her loyal love,
that sustaining power of loyal love.
It went deep, and it wrapped around Jehovah.
And she had the power to keep clinging to him
under those circumstances.
Anna was determined to serve Jehovah to the best of her ability.
What did she do?
Again, looking at verse 37:
“She was never missing from the temple,
“[She was in the right place.]
“rendering sacred service night and day
“[doing the right thing]
“with fasting and supplications
[with the right attitude].”
She was doing the right thing
in the right place with the right attitude.
Nothing could stop this seemingly fragile servant of God
from clinging to her closest Friend, Jehovah.
In effect, Anna was saying,
“I cling to you, Jehovah.”
And her loyal love was noticed.
Chapter 2 and verse 38
reveals that Anna was present
when the baby Jesus was brought to the temple.
And when she saw that baby, what did she begin to do in verse 38?
It says: “She came near and [she] began giving thanks to God
“and speaking about the child to all who were waiting
for Jerusalem’s deliverance.”
Can you sense her joy?
Can you feel the joy she had at seeing and, perhaps, even holding
that little baby, the future Messiah?
This was something that this elderly woman
had never expected in her lifetime.
The child in front of her was proof
—tangible proof, concrete evidence—
that Jehovah had not abandoned his people.
And he did not abandon Anna.
So not only had Anna clung to Jehovah
but Jehovah held on to her and
—and  rewarded her.
This is loyal love.
Anna’s faithful record
is so well-known
that some 50 years later, 50 years later or so,
Luke was compelled to write about her.
Where did he get his information?
Who did he talk to?
Did he talk to Mary or interview her or some of the older ones?
‘There was this woman, Anna. She was at the temple.
She would never leave.’
We don’t know.
But what we do know is that Jehovah inspired Luke
to record and to document her life in His Word
so that we could be taught lessons.
And here we are some 2,000 years later,
and we are using her life as an example
of commitment and unbreakable integrity
for you students to imitate.
So, what can you learn from Anna’s example?
You may suffer loss of one kind or another.
You will come face-to-face with the imperfections of others.
Your feelings may get hurt,
you might find yourself coping with an unexpected change
in your life that is not pleasant,
or you may feel that you’re a victim
of an injustice or a serious misunderstanding
from within the organization.
What will you do?
This is what you will do.
You will cling to Jehovah,
and you will experience him holding on to you.
You cling to him.
He holds on to you.
For example,
I recall a time when a brother serving in a foreign field
because of a misunderstanding lost his privileges as an elder.
And he felt the decision was unfair.
He was deeply hurt.
But his wife— He and his wife never stopped clinging to Jehovah
and their spiritual routine.
Then at a regional convention,
a brother approached him and thanked him for the talk
that he gave on the program.
Well, he volunteered in the cleaning department,
but he hadn’t given a talk.
Then the brother now said to this former elder:
“When I see your smile and positive attitude,
“yes, you gave a talk.
“And it was on loyalty,
and it was loud and clear.”
So the former elder now relates this:
“The experience taught me and my wife
“that every challenge or misfortune
“does not need to represent a threat
“to our spiritual well-being.
“We’ve come to view rejection, failure,
“or being misunderstood as normal episodes
“in the lives of competent, healthy people.
Instead of being crushed, we grew.”
You see, the couple looked beyond their hardships,
and they clung to Jehovah.
How?
By imitating Anna.
They were ‘never missing from true worship
‘[in the right place],
‘rendering sacred service day and night
‘[doing the right thing]
with fasting and supplications.’
And sometimes those supplications involve tears
but with the right attitude.
And Jehovah held on to them and never let go.
The brother is still serving in the foreign field.
He is an elder again
and giving memorable talks.
So, what do we want you to remember from this talk?
We want you to remember this:
When you come face-to-face with future trials (and you will)
or challenges in your life (and you will, this is what happens in life),
be in the right place,
do the right thing
with the right attitude.
By doing this, you declare:
“Jehovah, I cling to you,
and I trust you to hold on to me.”
Thank you very much, Brother Noumair.
Anna is a beautiful example for all of us.
No doubt about it.
Now, our final prerecorded interview takes us
to the West African country of Ghana,
where David and Lynne Jones currently serve.
Upon their graduation from the 95th class
in September of 1993,
they were assigned to the country of Kenya, East Africa.
They also served in Burundi for eight years.
Presently, they serve in Ghana,
where Brother Jones serves as a member of the Branch Committee there.
Now, you might remember this couple when you see the video
because their class was highlighted
in the video To the Ends of the Earth,
which marked the 50th anniversary
of the Watchtower Bible School of Gilead.
It was a very enlightening video for sure.
Although the purpose of Gilead School training
has changed since then,
it’s clear from their heartfelt comments
that they’ve proven to be a stabilizing and strengthening influence
where they have served.
So enjoy the video.
This is the day when we hand out assignments
to all of these students.
The morning that we knew we were going to get our assignment,
we went down to morning worship,
and then we had to line up, and we were waiting to get our assignment.
And my stomach was churning, and I felt really sick
—sick with excitement as well as the fact that you knew
that whatever Brother Jaracz said,
the next sentence that came out of his mouth
would determine the rest of your life.
It’s hard to imagine
that 28 years have gone by
since our initial assignment.
But Gilead training really helped us
to understand that things
wouldn’t always be easy.
And that when things weren’t easy,
we should never overreact to situations
but keep calm and trust in Jehovah.
I think one of the outstanding sections of Gilead for me
was the section dealing with the Gospels and Jesus Christ.
Jesus was always kind.
He was always reasonable in his dealings with people.
And so in class, the emphasis was, not on head knowledge,
but on how we can imitate Jesus Christ in our dealings with others.
And I remember a couple of phrases:
People over productivity.
And the kind thing is always the right thing to do.
These lessons are still with me all these years later.
We were taught how to study.
And it helped us to study in a way
that would build a pool or a foundation of principles
so that when we had a trial,
we would have somewhere to go and dip into that pool of principles
that would apply to any situation that we might face.
And it’s true that at the time you go through it,
you’re taking in all the knowledge.
You don’t know when and where you’re going to use it,
but it teaches you the method of:
Let’s store all this in the bank, and then when I need it,
I know where I can go and pick it from.
One example that comes to mind
is a lecture we had that highlighted Romans 15:3,
where it talked about how “even the Christ did not please himself.”
So thinking about that lecture makes me think of a situation
when we had been field missionaries for a couple of years.
We were invited to go into the traveling work.
So I was thinking to myself,
‘Can I really do this?’
But then I reflected back on that lecture
—Romans 15:3: “The Christ [didn’t] please himself.”
It’s not about me.
It’s about doing Jehovah’s will.
It’s about the people you serve.
Reflecting on that helped me
to see myself in that big picture and realize,
‘No, if Jesus could do that, then this is what I have to do first
—I put the brothers and sisters first.’
And we thoroughly enjoyed being in that circuit.
I don’t even know why I was so worried.
Because at the end of three years, we didn’t even want to leave.
The impact of Gilead is not fully appreciated in the moment.
But as the years have gone by,
I do find myself reflecting on the lessons
that were taught during that class.
And I see how it’s shaped
the way I think and feel all these years later.
So I would say, yeah,
it’s had a life- or personality-changing effect on me.
When I think back of standing in that line,
I mean, it is very vivid
in my memory of how I felt.
And my stomach was definitely churning.
But these 28 years, I have not regretted one single minute of it.
Being with the brothers and sisters,
serving in different forms of assignments,
I can definitely say without one shadow of a doubt
that I still would not swap it for the world.
Well, we’ve enjoyed
a rich spiritual feast so far.
But there’s more to come.
What a blessing these graduates will be
to the brothers and sisters in their assignments!
The second and third parts of the graduation
will be available on jw.org later this month.
We know you’re excited to see the rest of the program.
To conclude this month’s broadcast,
let’s go to Tahiti.
It’s the main island of French Polynesia,
a territory of about 118 inhabited islands.
It’s a beautiful land marked by mountains,
waterfalls, and white sand atolls.
The surroundings teem with life.
Manta rays glide through the water
while the land produces
an abundance of beautiful flower species.
The beauty of this island
is found not only in its natural scenery
but also in the hospitable attitude of the people.
Our brothers and sisters of the Vaima Congregation make it a priority
to share the beauty of God’s Word.
Their territory extends from the city center
to the mountains and remote islands
of Apataki and Rikitea.
They witness to the local fishermen at the beach
and to the international sailors at its large harbors,
and their efforts have proven successful.
Currently, the congregation is conducting 107 Bible studies.
And yes, 107 brothers and sisters
from the Vaima Congregation
send their warm greetings to you
wherever you are globally!
From the World Headquarters of Jehovah’s Witnesses,
this is JW Broadcasting!

cn.text: 欢迎大家收看
2021年12月份的JW电视
第150届守望台基列圣经学校的课程
已经顺利结束了
在耶和华子民的历史中
这真的是一个重要的里程碑！
第150届和往届相比有点不同
这届学校只有24个学生
比往届少了很多
由于受到2019冠状病毒病的影响
出行受到限制
这一届所有的学生都来自美国
跟往年相比
这届基列学校虽然有些不一样
但培训目标没有变
就是强化学生的信心
这样，他们无论被委派到哪里
都能大大鼓励别人
这个毕业典礼的节目中会谈到一些要点
这会帮助学生们为未来的委派做好准备
这个毕业典礼是2021年9月11日
在纽约帕特森守望台教育中心举行的
现在请大家观看毕业典礼的第一部分
我想谈谈大约50年前发生的事
那是在1972年，3月6号星期一
我想你们有些毕业生可能还没出生
不过你们其中的某一位
我可以非常肯定，一定已经出生了
因为我对他实在是太熟悉了
那一年
我和我太太十分荣幸有机会可以参加
像今天这样的基列学校的毕业典礼
当时是第52届
我们都聚集在纽约市的大会堂，人非常多
那次的节目真的很棒
能够在现场参加第52届毕业典礼
让我们很难忘
转眼间将近100届过去了
现在我们正举行的是第150届毕业典礼
如今有更多人能参加毕业典礼
现在他们正连线收看这个节目
再过几个月
全世界的弟兄姐妹就都能看到了
变化真的很大
在过去不是人人都有这样的机会
我记得那届毕业典礼的主席是诺尔弟兄
我们都知道他对于基列学校倾注了很多的爱
当然，是耶和华任用他创办了基列学校
第一届是在1943年
之后不久，圣经中预言的“野兽”就出现了
耶和华认为是时候开办一个学校了
一个培养特派传道员的学校
基列学校开办很多年了
我想分享一个毕业典礼上的演讲
是法兰兹弟兄做的
之前在洋基体育场
我听过他在大会上的演讲
但在毕业典礼上，我离他更近

en.text: The preaching work in Turkey has experienced
a period of exciting growth.
The old branch facilities in Istanbul became too small for the increasing needs.
So our brothers found two floors in an office tower
that would provide suitable work space
for Bethel departments.
A nearby residential building provides accommodations for the Bethel family.
To celebrate the dedication of the new branch facilities,
delegates from all over the world came to Istanbul.
Special events and activities were organized to welcome them,
and on May 12, 2018, Brother Mark Sanderson of the Governing Body
gave an encouraging branch dedication talk.
Is it your wish
that we should dedicate these facilities
to the worship and to the praise
of our magnificent God, Jehovah?
In the first century, the apostle Paul wrote about this part of the world
that the good news was “bearing fruit and increasing.”
The same is true today.
The need for Kingdom proclaimers here is great,
and with a new branch dedicated to supporting the preaching work,
our zealous brothers in Turkey are sure that Paul’s words
will continue to prove true.

title: 마크 누매어: 도공의 물레 위에 머물러 있으십시오 (여호수아 1:1, 2)

ko.text: 조직의 마련에 변화가 생겼을 때 받아들이기가 쉽지 않았던 적이 있으신가요?
아니면 그런 변화로 개인적으로 마음이 상했을지도 모릅니다.
그럴 때 어떤 반응을 보이는 것이 가장 좋습니까?
그런 변화가 우리 자신에게 불리해 보일 때는 어떻게 해야 합니까?
이 질문들에 대한 답을 얻는 데 도움이 되는 기록을 살펴보겠습니다.
이 기록은 여호와께서 모세에게 그가 곧 죽게 될 것이며
다른 사람이 그의 책임을 맡게 될 것이라는 점을 알려 주신 때에 관한 것입니다.
‘모든 사람의 영의 하느님 여호와께서 이 회중 위에 한 사람을 임명하셔서,
그가 그들 앞에서 나가기도 하고 들어오기도 하며,
그들을 데리고 나가기도 하고 들어오기도 하게 해 주시기 바랍니다.
그래서 여호와의 회중이 목자 없는 양처럼 되지 않게 해 주십시오.’”
왜냐하면 모든 사람의 생명이 여호와께 의존해 있다는 것을 알았기 때문입니다.
그리고 모세는 “모든 사람의 영의 하느님”이신 여호와께서
자신의 종 한 사람이 죽으면 적절하다고 보시는 대로 다른 종을 일으키셔서
조직 내에서 필요한 일을 하게 하실 것임을 알고 있었습니다.
‘눈의 아들 여호수아 곧 그 안에 영이 있는 사람을 데려다가 그에게 손을 얹어라.’”
그는 영적인 사람이었고 여러 해 동안 충성스럽게 순종해 왔습니다.
하지만 여호수아는 모세의 역할을 그대로 이어받지는 않을 것이었습니다.
마련이 바뀌고 있었고, 이제 한 사람이 모든 일을 맡지 않게 되었습니다.
여호수아는 조직 내에서 이전에 없던 새로운 역할을 맡게 됩니다.
“그리고 제사장 엘르아살과 온 회중 앞에 그를[여호수아를] 세우고
너는 네 권위의 일부를 그에게 주어 [여기서 권위의 전부가 아니라 일부라고 했죠]
이스라엘의 온 회중이 그의 말을 듣게 해야 한다.”
네, 역할이 어떻게 달라졌는지 분명히 알 수 있죠.
여호수아는 모세처럼 여호와를 대면하여 알지는 못했습니다.
모세의 모든 권위가 여호수아에게 주어진 것이 아니라
그가 백성의 존경을 받는 데 필요한 만큼만 주어졌습니다.
엘르아살은 그를 위해 우림으로 여호와 앞에서 그분의 판결을 물을 것이다.”
이제 여호수아는 하느님의 뜻을 알기 위해 대제사장과 함께 일해야 했습니다.
네, 여호수아는 유능하고 하느님을 두려워하는 사람이었죠.
약 40년 동안 광야에서 방랑 생활을 하는 벌을 받았습니다.
그렇게 그는 이미 위대한 도공의 물레 위에서 틀 잡혀 왔습니다.
하지만 이제 이 새로운 마련과 관련해 틀 잡히는 과정이 계속됩니다.
이제 여호와께서는 불완전한 두 사람을 사용하십니다.
바로 지도자와 대제사장이 균형을 이루어 여호와의 완전한 뜻을 이루게 하십니다.
그러니까 불완전한 두 사람이 여호와의 완전한 뜻이 이루어지게 하는 것
예를 들어, 왕들이 다스리던 시기에 웃시야왕이 신권 마련에 어긋나는 일을 했을 때,
대제사장 아사랴는 그가 율법을 어기는 행동을 한 것을 책망했습니다.
또 대제사장 아비아달이 불충성했을 때, 솔로몬왕이 그를 제사직에서 해임했습니다.
한 사람이 약할 때 다른 한 사람은 강했습니다.
한 사람에게만 의존하지 않으신다는 걸 배울 수 있습니다.
베델의 경우라면 한 부서에만 의존하지 않으시죠.
베델의 여러 부서들은 서로 친절하게 대하며 사이좋게 일하려고 노력합니다.
따라서 우리 각자는 겸손한 태도로 필요할 때는 도와 달라고 해야 합니다.
다른 사람들이 여호와의 일을 하는 데 필요한 것을 기꺼이 제공해 주어야 합니다.
얼마나 놀라운 일을 이루고 계신지 분명히 보고 있습니다.
여호와께서는 과거처럼 자격 있는 종들을 계속 일으키셔서
적절하다고 보시는 대로 백성을 인도하게 하십니다.
세계 본부의 부서 감독자들, 지부 위원들,
여호와께 틀 잡힐 수 있도록 도공의 물레 위에 머물러 있습니다.
우리가 “목자 없는 양처럼” 되지 않게 하려는 것입니다.
그런데 사실 감독하는 위치에 있든 아니든
우리 모두는 위대한 도공이신 여호와께서 우리를 계속 틀 잡아 주시기를 원합니다.
하지만 솔직히 때로는 그게 쉽지 않을 수 있습니다.
다른 사람의 불완전성을 보고 상처를 받거나, 조직상의 변화가 생겨서 충격을 받을 때에도
물레에서 떨어지지 않고 머물러 있어야 하기 때문입니다.
예를 들어, 여호와께서 조직을 계속 정련하심에 따라 여러 가지 조정이 생기게 됩니다.
그 과정에서 어쩌면 우리의 임명이 바뀌고 마음이 많이 상할 수도 있습니다.
또는 그러한 변화가 실제로 적용되는 방식 때문에 기분이 상할 수도 있죠.
따라서 우리가 빠르게 변화하는 조직의 여러 마련들 틈에서
다시 말해 위대한 도공의 물레가 돌아갈 때
그 위에 있는 자신에게 압력이 가해지고 있다고 느낀다면,
촉촉하고 말랑말랑한 진흙이 되게 도와 달라고 간청하십시오.
여호와께서 불완전한 사람을 사용해서 불완전한 사람과 일하게 하시는 거죠.
그리고 사람들이 불완전하지만 서로 잘 지내는 법을 가르치고 계신 겁니다.
큰 그림이란 여호와께서 아주 작은 것들로 아주 큰 일을 이루신다는 것입니다.
이 점에 대해 묵상해 보면, 함께 일하는 것의 가치를 깨닫게 되죠.
우리가 함께 일할 때 여호와께서는 가장 많은 일을 이루십니다.
확실한 건 하느님의 보이는 조직에서 일하는 사람들이 계속 바뀌게 될 것이라는 사실입니다.
이런 변화가 일어나는 건 그들이 사망하거나 그 밖의 여러 상황이 발생하기 때문입니다.
하지만 변화가 있어도 일이 중단되진 않죠.
따라서 우리는 이 점을 확신할 필요가 있습니다.
겸손한 감독자들, 네, 불완전하지만 겸손한 감독자들을 계속해서 일으키셔서
적절하다고 보시는 대로 자신의 백성을 돌보게 하실 것입니다.
그리고 여호와께서 계속 자신의 세계적인 조직을 인도하셔서
영적으로 성공하게 하실 것이라는 점을 확신하시기 바랍니다.

en.text: Have you ever felt that a change of oversight
or organizational arrangement
was hard to accept?
Or maybe you even felt hurt
in some way personally by the change.
Well, why do these changes occur?
And what is the best way for us to respond to them,
even if the change seems to be to our personal disadvantage?
Well, let’s open our Bibles to Numbers chapter 27
and examine an account that may help answer these questions.
The account relates to when Jehovah notified Moses
of his approaching death
and the need for a man to take over Moses’ responsibilities.
At Numbers chapter 27, let’s begin at verse 15:
“Then Moses said to Jehovah:
“‘Let Jehovah, the God of the spirit of all people,
“‘appoint over the assembly a man
“‘who will go out and come in before them
“‘and who will lead them out and bring them in,
“‘so that Jehovah’s assembly may not become
like sheep that have no shepherd.’”
Why would Moses call Jehovah, describe him
as, “the God of the spirit of all people”?
Because all people are dependent on Jehovah for life.
Moses knew that.
And Moses knows that when one servant dies,
“Jehovah, the God of the spirit of all people,”
will raise up another living servant
to serve within the theocratic structure,
just as Jehovah sees fit.
So, what does Jehovah now do?
Well, let’s look at verse 18:
“So Jehovah said to Moses:
“‘Take Joshua the son of Nun, a man in whom there is spirit,
and lay your hand on him.’”
So now Jehovah picks Joshua.
Joshua was a spiritual man.
He proved his loyalty and obedience for years.
However, Joshua was not to be
a Moses junior.
The arrangement was changing,
and it would not be a one-man show.
Joshua would now fit
into a new organizational role.
What would that be?
Well, let’s look at verses 19 and 20:
“Then stand him [Joshua]
“before Eleazar the priest and before all the assembly,
“and you must commission him before their eyes.
“You are to confer some of your authority on him
“[notice, not all the authority, but some],
so that all the assembly of the Israelites may listen to him.”
So here we see the difference in this role becoming clear.
Joshua was not to be like Moses
in knowing Jehovah face-to-face.
Not all of Moses’ authority was to transfer over to Joshua,
only what was needed
for Joshua to have the respect of the nation.
And now notice verse 21:
“He will stand before Eleazar the priest,
“who will inquire in his behalf
by the judgment of the Urim before Jehovah.”
Do we see the difference?
Joshua was now to work with the high priest
to ascertain the divine will.
Yes, Joshua was capable,
but he was more than capable and God-fearing.
Joshua was a modest man and a humble man,
and he accepted this new arrangement.
Well, Joshua had already been molded
on the Great Potter’s wheel
for some forty years of wilderness wandering
—discipline that he personally did not deserve.
But now, in accepting this new arrangement,
this molding process would continue.
How would it continue?
Well, we see Jehovah now using two imperfect men
—an administrator and a high priest—
to balance each other out and to make sure
that Jehovah’s perfect will took place.
So, now, two imperfect people
making sure that Jehovah’s perfect will moved forward
—this would be the arrangement.
For example, during the time period of the kings,
when King Uzziah circumvented the theocratic arrangement,
it was high priest Azariah
who reproved him for this unlawful act.
Or when high priest Abiathar proved disloyal,
it was King Solomon who dismissed him from the priesthood.
So we see the balance of two imperfect men.
When one was weak, the other proved strong.
Well, what do we learn?
Well, we’re learning that Jehovah
—again, “the God of the spirit of all people”—
is not dependent on just one person,
nor is he dependent in our case at Bethel on just one department.
And that is why we work together;
this is why we foster warm feelings
in relationships between departments.
Because we need each other.
So each of us needs to be humble enough
to ask for help when needed
and yet unselfish enough to provide resources
so that others can get Jehovah’s work done.
And we see evidence.
We see evidence today of how Jehovah is getting his work done.
Look at what he is accomplishing.
Jehovah is continuing to raise up qualified servants
—again, to shepherd and lead his people as he sees fit.
When it comes to world headquarters departments’ oversight
or branch committee members, department overseers, construction overseers,
these individuals are like Joshua,
who are willing to work together
and to stay on the Potter’s wheel and be molded by Jehovah.
Why?
So that we do not become, as verse 17 says,
“as sheep that have no shepherd.”
But in reality, all of us,
whether we are in positions of oversight or not,
want Jehovah, the Great Potter,
to mold us—keep molding us.
And yet, frankly, it can be challenging
—challenging at times to stay on the Potter’s wheel
and not allow the imperfections of others
to push us off
or the organizational changes that take place
to knock us down.
For example, as Jehovah continues
to refine his organization, adjustments are made.
And perhaps in the process, our assignment is changed,
and our feelings get hurt by the change.
Or perhaps our feelings get hurt by the way that change was implemented.
So when you feel that you’ve been caught in a pinch-point
between the moving parts of the organization
or, more specifically, when you feel pressure being applied upon you
as you spin on the wheel of the Great Potter,
that is when we beg Jehovah
—beg Jehovah to help us remain moist;
beg Jehovah to help us remain pliable
during this molding process.
And tell Jehovah, “Jehovah, it’s not easy.”
Tell him how you feel: “Please help me Jehovah.
I want to be molded by you.”
And then we’re patient.
Be patient and try to see the big picture.
What is the big picture?
The big picture is that Jehovah is using imperfect people
to work with imperfect people —that’s all he has at present—
and that Jehovah is teaching us.
He is teaching us how to make peace
with imperfection.
The big picture is how much Jehovah is accomplishing
with so little.
When we meditate on that, we can see the value of working together.
And when we work together, that’s when Jehovah
accomplishes the most.
So it’s a fact,
the personnel in God’s visible organization will change.
And it will continue to change.
Whether that be due to death or other circumstances,
the personnel will change.
And yet, the change does not cripple the work.
Why?
Because this is Jehovah’s work; it’s not man’s.
So let’s be confident that Jehovah
—again, “Jehovah, the God
of the spirit of all people”—
will continue to raise up
humble (imperfect, yes, but humble),
imperfect overseers to shepherd his people
as he sees fit.
And rest assured that Jehovah will continue
to guide and lead his organization,
his global organization,
to spiritual success.

cn.text: 你曾经因为你的监督改变了
或组织安排调整了
而觉得难以接受吗？
或者
也许这些改变让你觉得自己受到了伤害吗？
为什么会有这些改变呢？
如果改变给我们造成了负面的影响
应对这些改变的最好的方法是什么呢？
让我们打开圣经到民数记27章
看看当中的一个记载
怎样帮助我们找到问题的答案
在这段经文里
我们看到上帝说摩西就要去世了
上帝会委派另一个人接替摩西的职务
请打开圣经，我们从民数记27:15开始读
摩西对耶和华说
“愿赐生命给所有人的上帝耶和华
委任一个人管理民众
可以在各种事务上带头
带领他们出入
免得耶和华的民众好像没有牧人的绵羊一样。”
在这里我们留意到
摩西说耶和华是“赐生命给所有人的上帝”
为什么呢？
因为所有人都要依靠上帝才能活着
摩西了解这点
他知道，当耶和华的一个忠仆去世了
耶和华也就是“赐生命给所有人的上帝”
会寻找另外一个忠心的仆人
也就是一个在上帝眼中适合的人接替他的职务
所以耶和华接着做什么呢？
让我们看看第18节
耶和华对摩西说
“你带努恩的儿子约书亚来
他有不一样的精神
你要把手放在他头上。”
这几十年以来
约书亚已经证明
自己是个忠贞顺服上帝的人
不过
约书亚就是约书亚
他不是另一个摩西
安排改变了！
上帝不再只用一个人管理以色列人
现在约书亚有了新的角色
是什么样的角色呢？
让我们一起看看27章的19,20节
“叫他［约书亚］站在祭司以利亚撒
和全体民众面前
在众人眼前委任他
你要把你的职权分给他
［所以不是给他所有职权，而是把职权分给他。］
使以色列全体民众都听他的话。”
看来，约书亚的角色跟摩西的是不一样的
约书亚不像摩西是耶和华面对面所认识的
没错，约书亚拥有的权利不像摩西那样多
而耶和华给约书亚的
已经足够让他得到以色列人的尊重
接下来请留意第21节
经文说
“他要站在祭司以利亚撒面前
以利亚撒要替他求问耶和华
凭‘乌陵’来判断。”
看出不一样的地方吗？
约书亚必须和大祭司一起合作
以求得到耶和华的指示
约书亚当然很有能力
但他更是一位敬畏上帝的人
约书亚既温和又谦卑
他欣然接受这个新的安排
以色列人在旷野流浪了40年
约书亚也就被伟大的陶匠耶和华
塑造了这么多年
但其实他本来不是需要被管教的反叛的人
约书亚接受了这个新的安排
而耶和华也继续塑造他
上帝怎么做呢？
现在耶和华开始任用两个不完美的人
一个是管理者
另一个是大祭司
两个人要合力工作
才能执行耶和华的完美旨意
两个不完美的人要合作
才能执行耶和华的完美旨意
这就是新的安排
举个例子
有一次乌西雅王闯进耶和华的圣殿
要在香坛上烧香
大祭司亚撒利雅就过来
阻拦乌西雅王并且责备他
另外一个例子是
当大祭司亚比亚他变得不忠
所罗门王就革除了他的职位
这就是新安排的益处
当一个人变得软弱
另一个可以继续工作
所以到目前为止，我们学到什么呢？
我们学到
耶和华这位“赐生命给所有人”的上帝
他的工作不是依靠某个人
也不是依靠伯特利的某个部门来完成的
所以我们为上帝工作时
要同心协力
也要努力促进部门之间的和谐关系
因为我们需要彼此
我们每一个人都要表现谦卑的精神寻求帮助
也要无私地提供资源给其他人
来一起完成
耶和华的工作
我们看到了证据
看到了耶和华怎样在今天用同样的方法
完成他的工作
耶和华继续挑选
而且任用那些符合资格的仆人
来牧养以及领导他的子民
比如
世界总部各部门的监督
分部委员会成员、各部门的监督
建筑工程的监督
他们每一个人就像约书亚一样
很愿意彼此合作
继续保持谦卑的态度被耶和华塑造
为什么呢？
这样我们才不会变得好像17节说的
“没有牧人的绵羊一样”
但是其实
我们所有人
不管是不是监督
都希望伟大的陶匠耶和华塑造我们
一直塑造我们
不过说实话
一直接受耶和华的塑造
对我们来说并不容易
因为别人的不完美
或者是
组织安排的改变
都可能使我们离开耶和华
举例来说
耶和华为了使他的组织更加完善
就继续作了一些调整
在这个过程当中
我们的委派可能改变了
我们可能因此觉得很伤心
或者是改变的方式让我们感到很难过
那么，如果你觉得
组织的调整影响到你
让你感到很受伤
或者说具体一点
就是
你在接受伟大的陶匠塑造时感受到了压力
那么在这个过程当中
你就要祈求耶和华帮助你
可以像陶土一样保持湿润和柔软
也就是保持谦卑
要告诉耶和华
“耶和华啊，这真的很不容易
请你帮助我，我很想被你塑造。”
然后要保持耐心
要努力去看清全局
而这个全局
就是耶和华正任用不完美的人
让他们一起工作
他现在任用的人都是不完美的
耶和华上帝正教导我们
教导我们怎样以平衡的态度
看待不完美
我们要看出
上帝正任用渺小的人成就非凡的大事
沉思这一点时
我们就能看出一起工作的价值
耶和华正是在我们一起工作时成就他的大事
可以肯定的是
耶和华在不同的岗位任用的人一定会更换
而且会一直更换
有的人去世了，有的人的环境变了
总而言之，就是会一直更换
然而，这并没有阻止上帝的组织
继续前进
因为这是上帝的旨意，不是人的
所以我们要信赖耶和华
圣经说
“耶和华是赐生命给所有人的上帝”
只要他认为适当
他就会继续挑选谦卑
虽然不完美但谦卑的人
作监督来牧养他的子民
我们确信耶和华会继续指引和带领他的组织
他的全球组织
彻底完成他的旨意

titles.ko: 마크 누매어: 도공의 물레 위에 머물러 있으십시오 (여호수아 1:1, 2)
titles.en: Mark Noumair: Keep Spinning on the Potter’s Wheel (Josh. 1:1, 2)
titles.cn: 马克·努玛尔：继续接受伟大陶匠的塑造（书1:1,2）

title: M. 스티븐 레트: “정상적인 것을 초월하는 능력”을 얻으십시오 (고린도 후서 4:7)

ko.text: 오늘의 주제는 “‘정상적인 것을 초월하는 능력’을 얻으십시오”입니다.
여호와 하느님은 우주에 존재하는 모든 능력의 근원이 되시는 분입니다.
여호와의 “끝없는 활력과 외경스러운 능력”에 대해 말합니다.
아주 오래전에 여호와께선 엄청난 능력을 사용하여 독생자를 창조하셨습니다.
그 아들도 엄청난 능력을 갖게 되었습니다.
그런 다음 여호와께선 아들을 “숙련된 일꾼”으로 사용하여
능력과 힘이 있는 다른 수많은 것들을 창조하셨는데,
생명이 있는 것도 있고 없는 것도 있었죠.
따라서 여호와처럼 우리의 주요 특성 중 하나는 능력입니다.
그 능력을 좋게도 나쁘게도 사용할 수 있죠.
사실 여호와께선 이렇게 말씀하시는 것과 같습니다.
우주에서 가장 강력한 도움을 베풀 수 있는 나에게 오면 능력을 잘 사용하도록 도와주겠다.
우리가 가진 정상적인 능력을 먼저 다 사용해야 한다는 걸 알 수 있죠.
그분은 정상적인 것을 초월하는 능력을 주십니다.
왜죠? 여호와께선 왜 모든 능력을 주시지 않을까요?
만일 그분이 우리가 충절을 지키는 데 필요한 모든 능력을 주신다면
우리가 아무런 노력 없이 시험을 통과하게 해 주신다고 주장할 것입니다.
즉 인간의 한계 내에서 할 수 있는 일을 다 하면
여호와께서 개입하셔서 그걸 초월하는 능력을 주시는 겁니다.
그럼 사탄은 아무 말도 할 수가 없겠죠.
왜 우리에겐 여호와께서 주시는 “정상적인 것을 초월하는 능력”이 필요하죠?
세 가지 강력한 적의 엄청난 능력과 힘 때문입니다.
“온 세상은 악한 자의 지배 아래 있습니다” 라고 알려 줍니다.
오늘날 땅에 있는 76억이 넘는 사람들을 지배하고 있는 자의 능력을 생각해 보십시오.
바로 사탄이 그런 능력을 갖고 있습니다.
이것은 세상이 미치는 힘 가운데 하나죠.
우리를 나쁜 행실에 빠뜨리려 하는 불완전한 육체의 힘에 대해 알려 줍니다.
따라서 우리에게 영향을 미치는 이 엄청난 힘들을 저항하기 위해
하지만 어떤 힘이나 능력의 근원이 존재한다고 해서
예를 들어, 바람의 힘을 이용하려면 풍차를 돌려야 합니다.
흐르는 물의 큰 힘을 이용하려면 수력 발전소를 가동해야 합니다.
태양의 엄청난 힘을 이용하려면 태양 전지판을 사용해야 하죠.
그럼 우리가 여호와께 능력을 얻기 위해서는 어떻게 해야 할까요?
또한 그분의 능력을 받지 못하게 방해하는 것
심지어 완전히 막는 것에 대해서도 경고하십니다.
이제 그처럼 대조가 되는 예 4가지를 살펴보겠습니다.
여호와의 능력을 받지 못하게 막는 것들과 받는 데 도움이 되는 것들입니다.
그럼 야고보서 1장을 펴서 여호와께서 의심에 관해 하신 말씀을 보시죠.
“그러나 믿음으로 계속 청하고 결코 의심하지 마십시오.
의심하는 사람은 바람에 밀려 출렁이는 바다 물결과 같습니다.
사실, 그런 사람은 여호와께 어떤 것도 받으리라고 기대하지 말아야 합니다.”
이 산더러 ‘여기서 저기로 옮겨 가라’ 해도 옮겨 갈 것이고,
또 여러분에게 불가능한 일은 아무것도 없을 것입니다.”
여호와께서는 놀라운 일을 이룰 수 있는 큰 능력을 주십니다.
따라서 우리는 여호와와 그분의 조직을 의심할 아무런 이유가 없습니다.
이제 능력을 받지 못하게 막는 것과 받는 데 도움이 되는 두 번째 예는
“고난의 날에 낙담한다면 힘이 [즉, 능력이] 빠지게 될 것이다.”
따라서 지나치게 낙담하면 여호와께 능력을 받기가 어려울 수 있습니다.
하지만 우리가 여호와께 기도로 짐을 내맡긴다면,
어떤 문제든 결국 해결해 주실 것이라는 온전한 희망을 갖는다면
이제 이 점과 관련해서 이사야 40장을 보실까요?
“여호와께 희망을 두는 사람들은 새 힘을 얻을 것이다.
그들은 독수리처럼 날개를 펴고 솟아오를 것이다.
달려도 지치지 않고 걸어도 피곤하지 않을 것이다.”
이제 세 번째 예는 반뿐인 마음과 두 마음 그리고 온전한 마음입니다.
비유적으로 “마음이 반뿐인” 자와 “두 마음”을 가진 자에 대해 이야기합니다.
두 마음을 가진 사람은 두 주인을 섬기려 하는데,
예를 들어 세상을 온전히 이용하면서 동시에 여호와도 섬기려고 하죠.
마음이 반뿐인 사람은 열정과 열심이 없고 봉사와 관련해 미지근합니다.
여호와께서는 그런 사람에게 능력을 주지 않겠다고 하셨습니다.
“여호와께서는 그 눈으로 온 땅을 두루 살피셔서,
그분에 대해 마음이 온전한 자들을 위해 힘[즉, 능력]을 나타내십니다.”
그럼 마지막 예로 나쁜 행실과 신성한 봉사입니다.
썩은 말은 입 밖에 내지 말라’와 같은 권고가 나옵니다.
“하느님의 성령을 근심하게 하지 마십시오” 라고 말합니다.
따라서 여호와께서는 그와 같은 나쁜 행실이 성령을 근심하게 한다고
즉 여호와께서 능력을 주시는 주된 방법인
성령을 받지 못하게 방해한다는 것을 분명히 알려 주십니다.
그 말씀을 읽고 묵상하면, 능력을 얻게 되죠.
사도행전을 보면 제자들이 간구를 했을 때 성령을 받았다고 알려 줍니다.
그리고 그들은 함께 모여 있을 때 “성령으로 충만”하였습니다.
또한 예수께서는 “성령이 여러분에게 이르면, 여러분은 능력을 받아 …
땅의 가장 먼 곳까지 이르러 나의 증인이 될 것입니다”라고 하셨죠.
그러므로 우리가 기도로 간구하고, 하느님의 말씀을 읽고 묵상하고,
함께 모이고, 왕국을 증거하면, 성령을 통해 능력을 얻게 될 것입니다.
첫째로 의심하지 않고 강한 믿음을 유지한다면,
둘째로 낙담을 물리치고 여호와에 대한 희망을 갖는다면,
셋째로 반뿐인 마음이나 두 마음을 품지 말고 온전한 마음으로 여호와를 섬긴다면,
넷째로 나쁜 행실을 피하기 위해 열심히 노력하고, 신성한 봉사에서 최선을 다한다면
정상적인 것을 초월하는 여호와의 무한한 능력을 계속 얻게 될 것입니다.
따라서 적들의 능력이 얼마나 강하든, 우리는 승리를 거둘 것입니다.
그리고 사랑하는 우리 형제 자매들은 신세계에 들어가게 될 것입니다.
이 땅에서 큰 환난을 통과하는 길을 통해
부활 마련이라는 지하 터널을 통해 들어가게 될 것입니다.

en.text: Now, my theme is
“Tap Into ‘the Power Beyond What Is Normal.’”
Jehovah God is the original Source
of all the power that exists in the universe.
Isaiah 40:26 speaks
of Jehovah’s “vast dynamic energy
and . . . awe-inspiring power.”
And we know that aeons ago, he used this tremendous power
to create his only-begotten Son,
who became a tremendous source of power himself.
But then using him as “a master worker,”
Jehovah brought into existence numerous other sources of power
—both animate and inanimate.
Now, we humans were made in God’s image.
And so one of our main qualities, just like Jehovah, is power.
We can use that power in a good way
or a bad way.
Now, Jehovah tells us: ‘If you want to use it in a good way,
‘I will help you.
‘You can tap into me,
‘the most powerful Source of help in the universe,
‘and I will help you use your power for good.
I will give you “power beyond what is normal.”’
—2 Corinthians 4:7.
But now, if you think about that scripture, today’s scripture,
doesn’t it indicate
that we have to expend the power that is normal?
Jehovah gives the power beyond normal.
Why?
Why does Jehovah not give all the power?
Well, if you think about it, if he gave us all the power
we needed to keep our integrity,
would that prove the Devil a liar?
Would that prove we  are integrity keepers?
No, it would just prove that Jehovah has a lot of power.
But Satan would claim
that Jehovah is unfairly using his power
to give us a free ride through our test and trials.
But when we do our part,
we do what is within our human limitations,
and then Jehovah steps in and supplies the power beyond that.
Well, Satan can rightfully say nothing.
Now, here’s another question,
Why do we need “the power beyond what is normal”
that Jehovah offers to us?
Well, it’s because of the tremendous power of our three great enemies
“The whole world is lying
in the power of the wicked one.”
Now, you think of a power that is capable of controlling
more than 7.6 billion people on earth today.
I mean, that’s some power of Satan.
Matthew 13:22 speaks about “the deceptive power of riches.”
That’s just one of the powers the world promotes.
Hebrews 3:13 talks about “the deceptive power of sin,”
identifying the power of our imperfect flesh
to try to pull us into wrong conduct.
So we’ve got to have this “power beyond what is normal”
to resist these tremendous power sources that are against us.
But now think about this: Just because a power source exists
does not mean you automatically benefit.
You have to tap into it.
For example, the wind has power;
a windmill taps into it.
Running water has tremendous power;
a hydroelectric power plant taps into it.
The sun has tremendous power;
solar panels tap into it.
Well, we have to tap into Jehovah.
And interestingly, Jehovah provides guidelines
as to how we can tap into his power.
He also gives warnings as to what can impede
—you can even say block— receiving power from him.
So with that being said, let’s identify
four contrasting examples
of what we’re going to call power-from-Jehovah blockers
and power-from-Jehovah receivers.
Now, our first example, doubt and faith
—open up to James chapter 1 and notice what Jehovah tells us about doubt—
James 1:6:
“But let him keep asking in faith,
“not doubting at all,
“for the who doubts is like a wave of the sea
“driven by the wind and blown about.
“In fact, that man should not expect
to receive anything from Jehovah,”
and that “anything” includes power.
In contrast, at Matthew 17:20, Jesus said:
“If you have faith the size of a mustard grain,
“you will say to this mountain,
“‘Move from here to there,’
“and it will move,
and nothing will be impossible for you.”
So with faith, Jehovah gives us tremendous power
to accomplish amazing things,
and we have no valid reason, really,
to doubt Jehovah or his organization.
Now, let’s get our second example
of a power blocker and a power receiver
—discouragement and hoping in Jehovah.
Proverbs 24:10 says:
“If you become discouraged in the day of distress,
your strength [or power] will be meager.”
So being overly discouraged can interfere
with our ability to receive power from Jehovah.
But if we prayerfully throw our burden on Jehovah,
if we rise above that situation,
if we put complete hope in Jehovah that he is going to help us
and any problems we have sooner or later will be eliminated,
then we can receive power.
Open up to Isaiah 40,
and here’s a scripture in this vein,
Isaiah 40:31:
“But those hoping in Jehovah
“will regain power.
“They will soar on wings like eagles.
“They will run and not grow weary;
they will walk and not tire out.”
Well, let’s move to our third example:
being double or halfhearted and being wholehearted.
Figuratively, Psalms 12:2 and 119:113
talk about a “halfhearted”
and a doublehearted person.
And Jehovah hates them according to the Bible:
doublehearted by trying to serve two masters,
trying, for example, to use the world to the full
but also be a servant of Jehovah.
A halfhearted person lacks enthusiasm and zeal.
He’s lukewarm in his service.
Well, Jehovah indicates that such individuals
will receive no power from him.
But do you remember what 2 Chronicles 16:9 says?
“For the eyes of Jehovah are roving about through all the earth
“to show his strength [or power]
“in behalf of those whose heart
is complete toward him.”
Well, let’s get our last example:
bad conduct and sacred service.
Ephesians 4:25-29
encourages us not to steal, not to be deceptive,
not to let ‘a rotten saying come out of our mouth,’ and so forth.
And then interestingly, the next verse, verse 30, says:
“Do not be grieving God’s holy spirit.”
So clearly, Jehovah is making it obvious
that any of that kind of conduct grieves, restricts, limits
our ability to receive holy spirit,
which is one of the main ways Jehovah provides power to us.
In contrast, Hebrews 4:12 says:
“The word of God is alive and exerts power.”
When we read it and meditate on it, we get power.
Acts talks about how
the disciples supplicated,
and they received holy spirit.
It talks about how they were all gathered together,
and they were “filled with holy spirit.”
Jesus said: “You will receive power when the holy spirit comes upon you,
and you will be witnesses of me . . . to the most distant part of the earth.”
So when we pray, we supplicate,
we read and meditate on God’s Word,
we meet together, we witness about the Kingdom,
we receive power by means of the holy spirit.
So summing up our discussion,
if we (1) maintain strong faith not doubting at all,
(2) resist discouragement by hoping in Jehovah,
(3) refuse to develop a half or double heart
but keep a complete heart in serving Jehovah,
and (4) really work hard to avoid bad conduct
and zealously pursue sacred service,
then we will continue
to tap into Jehovah’s limitless power beyond what is normal.
And despite the power of our great enemies,
we will triumph over them.
And you dear brothers and sisters will make it into the new world
either by means of the overland passageway
through the great tribulation —never die at all—
or by means of the underground tunnel,
the resurrection provision.

cn.text: 我今天的演讲题目是
《怎样获得非凡的力量？》
宇宙中的所有力量和能量
都来自于耶和华上帝
以赛亚书40:26说耶和华
“能力充沛，力量可畏”
亿万年前，耶和华就运用他巨大的力量
创造了独生的儿子
这位儿子也有强大的力量
而且他是位“好工匠”
耶和华上帝通过这个儿子
创造了宇宙中其余的万物
包括有生命的和无生命的
人类是按照上帝的形象创造的
和上帝一样，人的一个主要特质就是力量
我们可以用自己的力量去做好事或坏事
耶和华告诉我们，如果你想用来做好事
我就会帮你，你会从我获得力量
我拥有宇宙中最强大的力量
我也会帮你善用你的力量
而且我还会赐给你非凡的力量
根据哥林多后书4:7
我们如果仔细想一想今天的经文
能够看出什么呢？
我们先要善用自己拥有的能力
然后耶和华才会赐给我们非凡的力量
为什么呢？
为什么耶和华不直接赐给我们
所有的力量呢？
如果耶和华这样做
让我们毫不费力就能谨守忠义
能证明魔鬼撒谎吗？
能证明我们是行事忠义的人吗？
不，这只能说明耶和华很有力量
这样，反而让撒但有理由指责耶和华
滥用他的力量
让我们毫不费力就渡过考验
但是如果我们
按照自己的能力尽力而为
耶和华就可以伸出援手
赐给我们非凡的力量
这样撒但就无话可说了
还有另外一个问题
为什么我们需要从耶和华上帝那里
获得非凡的力量呢？
这是因为我们面对的仇敌
也拥有很大的力量
约翰一书5:19说
“全世界都受那恶者控制”
你想一想，我们的仇敌
在今天能够控制全球76亿的人
可以看出撒但的力量真的强大
马太福音13:22指出
财富拥有骗人的力量
而世人都热衷于追求财富
希伯来书3:13说
“罪”也拥有骗人的力量
也就是说，因为受到罪的影响
我们很容易做错事
因此，我们必须要有非凡的力量
才能成功地应对这些强大的
与我们敌对的势力
请再想一想，某个东西具有强大的力量
并不意味着你能自动从他得到力量
你要采取行动
比如，风很有力量
风车可以利用它的力量
流动的水很有力量
水利发电厂可以利用它的力量
太阳也拥有强大的力量
太阳能板能利用它的力量
我们也需要从耶和华那里获得力量
耶和华也清楚告诉我们
可以怎样从他那里得到力量
而同时他也提醒我们，什么会妨碍我们
甚至阻止我们从他那里获得力量
接下来我们就讨论一下
有哪四种情况会帮助我们
又有哪四种情况会妨碍我们
从耶和华那里获得力量
我们先来看一下怀疑和信心
请你打开雅各书一章
看看耶和华谈到怀疑的人时怎么说
雅各书1:6,7说
“不过，人应该怀着信心不断祈求
一点也不要怀疑
因为怀疑的人就像被风吹动的海浪一样
起伏不定
这样的人不要以为可以从耶和华那里
得到什么。”
这当然也包括，不能得到耶和华的力量
我们再看一下马太福音17:20耶稣的话
你们的信心，哪怕只有芥籽那么小
你们就是吩咐这座山说
“从这里移到那里”，山也会移开
这样，对你们来说，没有什么是不可能的了
只要我们有信心
耶和华就会赐给我们非凡的力量
去成就非凡的事
我们真的没有任何理由
去怀疑耶和华和他的组织
现在，我们再来看第二组
帮助和妨碍我们得到力量的因素
就是灰心丧气和仰望耶和华
“如果你在苦难的日子气馁
你的力量就会微弱
也就是说，如果我们过度灰心丧气
就很难从耶和华那里得到力量
但是如果我们恳切祷告
并把重担卸给耶和华
如果我们不过度关注自己的难题
如果我们相信耶和华正在帮助我们
并最终消会除所有的难题
我们就能从他那里获得力量
现在，请打开以赛亚书40:31
看看经文怎么说
“但仰望耶和华的人会重获力量
像鹰一样展翅高飞
他们奔跑不会困乏，行走也不疲惫。”
我们再来看下一个对比
三心二意和全心全意
三心二意或怀着二心的人
耶和华非常讨厌这样的人
因为他们想同时事奉两个主人
一方面他们想尽情享用这个世界
而同时又想崇拜耶和华
三心二意的人
在崇拜的事上不冷不热，缺乏热心
耶和华说，他绝对不会赐力量给这样的人
你还记得历代志下16:9怎么说吗？
“耶和华仔细观察全世界
要施展力量帮助全心忠于他的人。”
经文说的很清楚，对吗？
我们再看最后一组对比
不良的行为和为上帝服务
以弗所书4:25-29鼓励我们
不要偷窃，不要说谎
还有，有害无益的话一句也不可出口
请你留意30节的脚注说
“不要使上帝的神圣力量忧愁”
很显然，耶和华清楚地表明
这些不良的行为会妨碍或阻止我们
从他那里得到神圣力量
而这是耶和华给我们加添力量的主要方式
希伯来书4:12说
“上帝的话语是活的，是有力量的”
所以研读和沉思上帝的话语就能得到力量
使徒行传记载
门徒们向上帝恳切地祈求之后
就得到神圣力量
另外，当他们聚集在一起的时候
也充满了神圣力量
耶稣说
“神圣力量降在你们身上的时候
你们就会得到力量
一直到地上最遥远的地方
做我的见证人。”
所以我们祷告、我们恳切祈求
我们阅读和沉思上帝的话语
我们参加聚会
传讲王国的好消息
我们就能从上帝那里得到神圣力量
现在我们总结一下
第一，如果我们保持坚强的信心
丝毫不要怀疑
第二，如果我们仰望耶和华
而不是灰心丧气
第三，如果我们全心全意为耶和华服务
而不是三心二意
还有最后一点
第四，如果我们努力地为耶和华服务
而不是沾染上那些不良的行为
我们就能够
持续不断地从耶和华那里得到非凡的力量
不论我们的仇敌力量有多么强大
我们都能战胜他们
各位亲爱的弟兄姐妹
你们一定能够顺利进入乐园
不论是走地上的高速公路
就是活着渡过大患难
或者走地下的隧道
通过复活进入乐园

title: 우리의 조직이 이루고 있는 일들—뉴스룸에 실릴 기사를 준비하는 과정

ko.text: 여호와의 백성은 디모데 전서 3:15에서 알려 주는 것처럼
지난 몇 년간 JW 뉴스 기사들을
그 점에 관한 사실 확인을 거친 뒤
거기서 최종 검토와 승인을 받는 거죠.
그 점을 해당 지역의 언론사들에 알렸습니다.
그 문제에 관해 다루는 기사를 실었습니다.
우리 형제들이 여전히 중립 문제를 겪고 있는 다른 나라들의 정부 관리들에게도
대학살을 직접 겪은 형제 자매들의 이야기를 수집했습니다.
자신들의 목숨을 걸고 다른 사람들을 구해 주었죠.
많은 형제들이 그 뉴스 기사를 읽으면서
형제들에 대한 재판이 시작될 때마다 홍보부는
그에 대한 뉴스 기사를 함께 준비합니다.
그 형제나 자매가 어떤 일을 겪었는지,
그들을 위해 기도해 줄 수 있죠.
완성된 기사를 해당 지부 홍보부에 보냅니다.
판결이 나오면 바로 그날 속보로 게시해
이 뉴스를 어떻게 활용할 수 있습니까?

en.text: We have heard from many of you how much you’ve really appreciated JW News
as a source of accurate information.
In contrast with much of the misinformation
posted on the Internet and social media,
Jehovah’s people serve as “a pillar and support of the truth,”
as 1 Timothy 3:15 says.
But just what does it take to prepare a Newsroom report?
Well, under the direction of the Coordinators’ Committee
of the Governing Body,
the Office of Public Information, or OPI,
prepares articles for the JW Newsroom.
Now, they work closely with Public Information Desks, or PIDs,
in our branch offices.
In the following report, some of these brothers
share a behind-the-scenes look
at how articles in the last few years
have been written and published on JW News.
From the late 1960’s
to the late 1990’s,
Italian brothers were condemned
and imprisoned for refusing military service.
A recent survey revealed that more than 14,000 brothers
from that group are still alive.
They were sentenced to a total of almost 10,000 years in prison.
We thought that their experiences could make
a potential story for the Newsroom section of jw.org,
along with comments from secular sources,
so we promptly notified OPI.
When we received that proposal,
we agreed with their assessment.
That’s when we go into action.
We’ll talk about the angle back and forth with the PID
until we have something that we know will work not only for Italy
but for our worldwide audience on jw.org.
Then we interviewed some brothers who had been imprisoned the longest.
They had to face many challenges,
but they also recalled how their loyalty was a great witness,
especially for some prison guards
who eventually became
Jehovah’s Witnesses as well.
This additional information was confirmed and then added to the story.
Then we sent the draft to OPI.
Once the initial article is written by the branch,
there’s still quite a bit of work that has to be done.
We’ll edit the article, select the photos, write the captions,
send it through proofreading,
and then, lastly, the article is sent back to the Coordinators’ Committee
for their final review and approval.
Shortly after the article was posted
on jw.org
and the Italy PID
informed their local reporters,
over 50 media outlets in Italy covered this story
and wrote articles about this topic.
Well, our hope was that by publicizing this information,
it would not only be encouraging to our brothers and sisters
but it would have a positive impact
on fair-minded officials in other countries
where our brothers are still dealing with this issue of neutrality.
The year 2019 was the 25th anniversary
of the genocide in Rwanda,
so because of that,
there was greater interest
in the scholarly community, in particular,
about what happened during the genocide.
One of the things that OPI was responsible for doing
was to collect experiences of people
who were our brothers and sisters; who saw the violence;
and who survived and helped others to survive,
sometimes at the risk of their own lives.
Our office assisted OPI
in preparing the article in two ways:
first of all, ensuring that the release was accurate
and second, ensuring that the article
gave consideration to the perspective
of those who went through the genocide.
Many of the brothers have been able to read that story on JW News,
and it’s encouraged them
when they see the courage and the faith that our brothers displayed in Rwanda.
OPI has the privilege
of assisting the brothers in Russia.
We prepare news items on JW News.
Once a trial begins, then the team works together
to prepare a JW News item.
We have to do lots of research on the brother’s
or the sister’s personal case history.
Were they raided?
Were they put in pretrial detention?
We can introduce the brother or the sister to the brotherhood,
and then they can pray for them.
Once we’ve put together the material,
we send it to the Public Information Desk.
And on the day of the verdict,
we post a Breaking News  update
to immediately alert the brotherhood.
How can you make the best use of JW News?
Look for opportunities to share news items with your Bible students and others.
Many of these reports show how Jehovah’s people
demonstrate love for one another.
Another way is by praying for our brothers and sisters
that we read about in the Newsroom.
We hope you continue to use the Newsroom to stay informed, to be encouraged,
and to remain united with God’s organization
—“a pillar and support of the truth.”

cn.text: 很多弟兄姐妹都喜欢看JW新闻
觉得里面的资讯非常准确
现在，网上和大众媒体充斥着很多假消息
耶和华的子民却是“真理的栋梁和支柱”
就像提摩太前书3:15说的那样
那么，要准备一份新闻稿需要哪些步骤呢？
在中央长老团协调委员会指导下
新闻资讯办事处（OPI）负责为JW新闻室准备稿子
他们会跟各个分部的新闻资讯事务处（PID）密切合作
接下来，让我们听一些弟兄讲述幕后的故事
看看过去几年中
JW新闻稿是怎样编写并发布的
从20世纪60年代末到90年代末
意大利的弟兄因拒服兵役被判刑和关进监狱
近期调查显示
那些弟兄有超过1万4千人现在还活着
他们的刑期加起来接近1万年
我们觉得他们的经历很值得跟外界的相关评论
一起出现在jw.org网站的新闻室里
所以我们立刻通知了OPI
收到了他们的提案后，我们也同意他们的建议
这就是我们跟PID合作的第一步
我们会跟PID反复讨论怎样呈现这个信息
让它不仅能吸引意大利的读者
也能让全球上jw.org网站的人受益
接着我们访问了一些被关时间最长的弟兄
他们面对很多的困难，但他们保持忠贞
做了美好的见证
有些狱警后来甚至也成为了耶和华见证人
这个额外的信息经过证实就会被加进他们的经历中
然后文稿就会发给OPI
我们收到了来自分部的初稿
接下来还有不少工作需要处理
我们会编辑文章、挑选照片
添加图片说明、发给人做校对
最后发送到协调委员会
他们会负责最终审阅和批准
这篇文章被发布到jw.org网站后不久
意大利的PID就通知了当地的记者
结果有超过50家意大利的媒体报导了这个故事
也编写了相关的文章
我们希望通过这样的宣传
让这个经历不仅可以鼓励我们的弟兄姐妹
也会对涉及此类中立问题的国家里一些开明的政府官员
产生良好的影响
2019年是卢旺达种族大屠杀的25周年
所以引起了很多学者的重视
他们想知道在大屠杀期间发生的事
OPI的一个工作就是收集幸存者的经历
他们有一些人是我们的弟兄姐妹
他们目睹了惨剧，幸存了下来
也帮助其他人活了下来
其中一些人甚至冒着生命危险这样做
我们为OPI准备文章提供的协助主要通过两个方面
第一，确保发行的文章内容准确无误
第二
确保这篇文章可以反映出大屠杀幸存者的真实想法
很多弟兄姐妹都从JW新闻上读到
我们在卢旺达的弟兄表现的信心和勇气
就深受鼓励
OPI有荣幸协助俄罗斯的弟兄姐妹
我们准备的报导被放在JW新闻里
每当有一个案件
弟兄们就会准备一个JW新闻的报导
我们需要做很多调查
来了解被捕的弟兄姐妹的整个案件经过
他们有没有被突然搜查？
有没有遭到审前羁押？
我们可以把他们介绍给全球的弟兄姐妹
