지금은 원격으로 베델 컨설턴트 일을 하고 있죠.
세상을 섬기는 건 노예 생활과 다름없지만,
여호와를 섬기는 건 전혀 그렇지가 않아요.
여호와와 함께 일하는 것보다 더 나은 삶은 어디에도 없어요.
그분의 도움을 온전히 경험하게 될 거예요.
저는 생각지도 못한 영적 특권들을 누리며 멋진 삶을 살아왔습니다.
이 세상에서 말하는 성공과는 비교조차 할 수 없는 삶이죠.
자매에게 도움이 된 한 가지 특성은
우리 각자는 어떻게 더 유연한 사람이 될 수 있습니까?
그렇게 하는 세 가지 실용적인 제안을
가유스 글로켄틴 형제가 사회한 아침 숭배에서 찾아보십시오.
마리아는 예수의 말씀을 계속 듣고 있었습니다.
마리아는 우선순위를 올바로 정했고 우리에게 훌륭한 본이 되죠.
해설에 나왔듯이 예수에게 사랑에 찬 조언을 받았습니다.
오늘은 마르다의 입장에서 좀 생각해 보겠습니다.
마르다는 예수를 지원하는 데 큰 관심을 보였는데,
그분이 쉽지 않은 환경인 유대에서 봉사하실 때 숙소를 제공했습니다.
예수를 위해 함께 식사를 준비했을 것입니다.
하지만 예수께서 오시자 마리아는 돕는 일을 중단한 것 같습니다.
혼자서 일을 다 하게 된 것이었죠.
마르다의 마음속에 스트레스가 차오르는 것이 느껴지십니까?
점점 짜증이 나는데 마리아는 앉아서 예수의 말씀을 듣고만 있습니다.
자신을 돕도록 마리아를 시정해 달라고 말하죠.
하지만 예상과는 달리 마르다 자신이 예수에게 조언을 받습니다.
우리가 이런 상황이라면 어떤 느낌이 들까요?
좋은 의도로 어떤 일을 했는데 칭찬을 받은 것이 아니라
“선생님을 위해 이렇게 최선을 다하는데 정말 너무하세요!
그럼 누가 식사 준비를 할지 한번 보죠.”
물론 우리는 마르다가 어떤 생각과 말을 했는지 모릅니다.
마르다가 예수의 따뜻한 조언을 마음에 새겼다는 것입니다.
발전해 나가는 데 무엇이 도움이 될까요?
쉽게 좌절하지 않는 유연한 특성이 도움이 되는데,
이런 특성을 가진 사람은 기분이 나쁘거나 상처를 받는 일이 있어도
유연한 사람은 이 스프링처럼 압력을 받아도 잘 견디고
쉽게 좌절하거나 포기하지 않는 유연한 사람이 되는 데 필요한
유연한 사람이 되는 데 필요한 첫 번째 점은
어려운 순간에 우리가 자문해 봐야 할 점은 이것입니다.
‘나는 내가 처한 현실을 정말로 이해하고 받아들이는가?’
자기가 보고 싶은 것만 보게 될 수 있습니다.
많은 사람은 어려운 상황에 맞닥뜨리면 현실을 부정합니다.
이것은 상황을 있는 그대로 보는 것을 의미하죠.
현실을 직시하는 것은 많은 노력이 필요한 일이죠.
전혀 유쾌하지 않고 감정적으로 고통스러울 수 있습니다.
사도 베드로는 예수를 세 번 부인한 뒤에 그분과 눈이 마주쳤을 때
분명 그는 그 어떤 변명도 하지 않았죠.
이 경험과 다른 몇몇 상황들에서 조언을 받은 덕분에
베드로는 발전하고 자신의 임무를 더 잘 수행할 수 있었습니다.
두 번째로 필요한 점은 어려움 속에서도 의미를 찾는 것입니다.
“왜 나에게 이런 일이 생기지?” 하면서 포기하는 사람들이 있습니다.
살면서 겪는 어려움을 통해 어떤 교훈도 배우지 못합니다.
어려운 일이나 힘든 상황을 때때로 피할 수 없는 이유를 알고 있습니다.
이처럼 큰 그림을 보고 어려움 속에서도 의미를 찾는다면
유연한 사람이 되어 힘들거나 새로운 상황에서도 인내할 수 있습니다.
또 장애물처럼 보이는 어려운 상황을 만나도
하지만 그에 대해 어떤 반응을 보일지는 선택할 수 있죠.
실패한 경험에서 최대한 많이 배우기 위해 노력하면서
뒤가 아니라 앞을 바라보고 새로운 목표들을 세울 수 있을 것입니다.
해럴드 킹 형제가 독방에 있을 때
어떻게 좌절하지 않는 유연한 태도를 나타냈는지 기억하실 겁니다.
킹 형제는 어떻게 상황을 잘 활용해서 어려움 속에서도 의미를 찾았습니까?
나는 기억나는 대로 적절한 성서 연설을 몇 가지 준비하여
따라서 의미를 찾는다는 것은 현재의 어려움과 더 나은 미래 사이에
다리를 놓는 것과 같다고 할 수 있습니다.
그런 다리가 있으면 어려운 상황에서도 인내할 수 있습니다.
현재의 어려운 상황 때문에 압도되지 않을 것입니다.
세 번째로 필요한 것은 자신에 대한 균형 잡힌 견해입니다.
앞서 우리는 현실을 직시해야 한다고 했는데
그러다 보면 슬프거나 낙담이 될 수 있습니다.
하지만 유연한 사람은 실패하거나 어려운 상황을 겪을 때
그 면에서 사도 바울은 좋은 본을 보였는데요.
때때로 그는 자신의 약점 때문에 낙담했습니다.
바울은 죄의 포로가 된 자신을 보면서 느낀 양심의 고통을 묘사합니다.
하지만 분명 바울은 자신이 불완전하기 때문에
9년 뒤에 죽기 직전에 사도 바울은 디모데에게 보낸 두 번째 편지에서
여기 디모데 후서 4:7에 나오는 그의 말을 읽어 보시죠.
“나는 훌륭한 싸움을 싸웠고 경주를 끝까지 달렸으며 믿음을 지켰습니다.”
바울의 문제와 내적인 싸움이 기적적으로 사라진 것은 아니었죠.
바울이 여호와께 훌륭한 봉사를 드리는 것을 막지는 못했습니다.
“난 쓸모 없는 사람이야” 같은 비하하는 말로
삶의 긍정적인 점들과 자신의 장점을 잘 생각해 본다면
자신에 대해 균형 잡힌 견해를 유지하는 데 도움이 될 것입니다.
마르다의 경험은 우리가 좌절하지 않는 유연한 특성을 갖는 것이 중요함을
자신에 대한 균형 잡힌 견해를 가짐으로 그렇게 할 수 있습니다.
성경에서는 낙원에서 어떤 삶을 누리게 될지
새로운 뮤직비디오에서 보시게 되겠지만 미래의 축복들을 그려 보면
우리의 마음이 기쁨으로 가득 차게 됩니다.
그분의 조직을 계속 정련하고 계신다는 것을 기억하기 위해서였습니다.
「살아 움직이는 우리의 역사」 연재 동영상을 통해
우리 숭배에서 노래가 중요한 역할을 한다는 점을 살펴보았습니다.
또 여호와께서 그분을 섬기는 사람들을 어떻게 축복하시는지도 보았는데요.
발네이브 자매는 화려한 직업을 포기한 대신 영적인 축복을 받았습니다.
그리고 밀스 형제는 많은 어려움을 겪었지만
그가 다른 사람들을 도움으로 기쁨을 유지할 수 있게 해 주셨습니다.
프로그램을 마치기 전에 형제들이 보내온 영상 편지를 함께 보실까요?
이번 달에는 에콰도르의 형제 자매들을 만나 보겠습니다.
에콰도르라는 이름의 뜻에서 알 수 있듯이
이 나라는 지구의 적도에 위치해 있습니다.
이곳은 지구 중심에서 쟀을 때 세계에서 가장 높은 지점인데,
안데스산맥에 건설된 이 기찻길은 100년도 더 전에 건설됐는데,
1946년에 도착한 첫 선교인들이 이 기찻길을 이용했죠.
촌타푼타 키추아어 회중은 처음에 격지 집단이었습니다.
형제들은 생활비를 벌기 위해 꽃을 기르고 사금도 채취합니다.
형제들은 모든 방법을 동원해 철저히 증거합니다.
에녹 1, 2호라고 이름 지은 두 보트를 사용해
키추아어를 사용하는 멀리 떨어진 마을들까지 갑니다.
이런 마을들은 휴대 전화 신호가 아주 약합니다.
하지만 이 성서 연구생은 포기하지 않고
신호가 잡히는 곳을 찾아 집회에 참석하고 연구도 합니다.
휴대 전화 서비스를 이용할 수 없는 사람들과는
고주파 무선 통신 장비를 사용해 재방문과 성서 연구를 합니다.
우아오라니어를 말하는 어린이들에게 동영상을 보여 주고 있습니다.
에콰도르에 있는 촌타푼타 키추아어 회중의 우리 형제 자매들이
전 세계의 형제 자매들에게 사랑과 안부를 전합니다.
이번 달 프로그램 사회를 저와 함께 진행해 주셔서 정말 감사드립니다.
여러분 모두에게 우리의 따뜻한 그리스도인 사랑을 전합니다.
지금까지 여호와의 증인의 세계 본부에서 JW 방송이었습니다!

en.text: Welcome!
We’re so happy you can join us
for this month’s program.
I’m here with my good friend
and cohost, Leon Weaver.
There he is.
Leon, welcome!
David, I’m delighted to be here with you.
Now, I’d like to tell you a little something about Leon.
When I was invited into Bethel in 1990,
I was assigned to the Service Department
and Leon was one of the overseers.
Now, in the Service Department,
at times we had to deal with some very difficult matters
and sometimes you needed advice.
And I could always rely on Leon to help me out.
I’d go into his office,
he’d set aside whatever it was he was working on,
he’d listen, and then he’d give his input.
I really appreciated the experience I acquired in the Service Department,
and Leon was certainly part of it.
So this is one reason why I have love
and respect for that brother.
Now, Leon, what can we look forward to in this month’s program?
Many years ago,
Elizabeth gave up a prestigious career
to do more for Jehovah.
How did her decision
change the course of her life?
And we’ll debut a fascinating new series.
It will reveal aspects of our theocratic history
you may not be familiar with.
That sounds very interesting.
Don’t go away!
This is JW Broadcasting® for November 2021.
Through his prophet Isaiah,
Jehovah made a wonderful promise,
one that’s being fulfilled today.
We can read about it at Isaiah 60:17:
“Instead of the copper I will bring in gold,
“and instead of the iron I will bring in silver,
“instead of the wood, copper,
“and instead of the stones, iron;
“and I will appoint peace as your overseers
and righteousness as your task assigners.”
Well, now, this reference to “overseers”
and “task assigners” —that sounds like organization, doesn’t it?
So, what is Jehovah telling us?
He’s saying that we can expect
to see organizational arrangements getting better and better.
Well, if you’ve been associated with the truth for a while,
I’m sure you’ll agree that Isaiah’s prophecy is being fulfilled today.
So for this broadcast,
I thought we’d review some of the improvements
we’ve seen just since World War II.
That’s the period most of us are familiar with.
Now, some of you will be hearing about these things for the first time.
Others will have lived through it all,
and for them it’ll bring back fond memories.
So let’s go back. It’ll be fun!
I call this part “Do You Remember When . . . ?”
Before World War II and for a number of years after that,
many congregations didn’t have a Kingdom Hall of their own.
They were actually encouraged
to meet in private homes
or in rented facilities.
The thinking was that if you
were in a rented facility or a private home,
you had more flexibility.
You could move the meeting place
from one place to the other very easily.
But there were problems; there were drawbacks.
Sometimes the space
would be shared with other organizations.
So you couldn’t leave your
literature, magazines,
speaker’s stand, and maybe even a sound system
in the hall at the end of the meeting.
When the meeting was over, you’d have to pack it all up
and take it away.
But that’s not all.
Sometimes you had to arrive very early and clean the place up
after a particularly rowdy group of people had used it.
And if there were cigar smokers in that group, you were in trouble.
It was very difficult to air the place out in time for the meeting.
Now, remember, in those days, people could smoke in a private hall,
and you could smoke in an airplane —they could smoke almost anywhere.
So this was a real problem for us.
There were other problems.
Before we had a Kingdom Hall in my hometown,
the congregation met in a rented facility.
Now, in October, the place was decorated for Halloween,
and in December, there was a great big Christmas tree on the platform.
We couldn’t move it!
Now, this was in Canada,
and portraits of the King and Queen of England
as well as the British flag were permanent fixtures in the hall.
You couldn’t remove any of it for the meeting.
Yet, to their credit,
many interested persons attended our meetings.
And to them, it wasn’t the meeting place that was important;
it was what they were learning there that counted.
Speaking of our meeting places,
at first, congregations were on their own
when it came to building them.
Now, at times, the most a congregation
could afford was to purchase the land,
and sometimes that land would sit there
for years because it would
take years to get the money together
to build the hall.
And then once they had the money together,
were there enough brothers who could take
the lead in the construction?
Sometimes on a weekend, you’d see
just one or two brothers working away
at the site of the new hall.
You had to love them for their perseverance.
Nowadays,
our Kingdom Hall construction is supervised by the LDCs,
with lots of qualified volunteers,
and practical Kingdom Halls can be constructed in a short period of time.
What about the meetings?
For years, the Theocratic Ministry School, Service Meeting,
Congregation Book Study, and Watchtower  Study
were all about an hour in length.
So were the public talks
—when we had them.
Now, at first, a public talk wasn’t scheduled every week.
There’d be a series of four or eight talks,
if you could schedule that many speakers.
And then, for a while, the congregation wouldn’t have a public talk.
Why was that?
Remember,
the Theocratic Ministry School
didn’t get under way until 1943,
and it took time for the brothers to develop
the skills to deliver an hour talk.
But in time, they were delivering
excellent public talks!
And do you remember
when we had individual handbills
for each public talk
with the name of the speaker printed on them?
Until 1959,
only brothers were enrolled in the school.
For some years, during the first few minutes
of the school there was a roll call,
and the names of all the brothers enrolled in the school were read out.
Now, when your name was read out, you were to answer, “Present.”
A few rebels would say, “Here.”
But you were supposed to say, “Present.”
Now, initially, according to the instructions,
if anyone was deliberately
and habitually absent over a period of time,
he was dropped from the school.
Later, that was discontinued.
Now, the roll-call arrangement got me into a bit of trouble.
You see, in our congregation when the roll was being called each week,
I noticed that there were a few young brothers
who were just a little bit older than I was who would answer, “Present.”
So one night after the school, I asked the school servant
if I could have my name read out at the next meeting.
He warmly commended me.
And sure enough, I got my name read out the following week.
Everyone congratulated me after the meeting.
I couldn’t understand why.
I only said, “Present.”
The problem was that I didn’t know that when you got your name read out,
you were agreeing to give a talk.
I thought I was just signing up to have my name read out.
Well, a couple of months later, on April 8, 1953,
I delivered my first eight-minute talk on the theme
“Proclaiming the World’s Doom.”
Now, why an eight-minute talk?
Well, we didn’t have Bible readings yet.
So when you were on the school,
you were giving an eight-minute talk.
Well, today, we make sure everyone understands what’s involved
in being a student in the midweek meeting.
we received the New World Translation
of the Christian Greek Scriptures  in English,
and we were encouraged
to bring it to the meetings.
So for the Hebrew Scriptures, you would have the American Standard Version
or the King James Version
—mostly the American Standard Version
because it had Jehovah’s name.
So you’d have two Bibles to bring to the meeting.
There’s the one for the Hebrew Scriptures
and then the New World Translation for the Greek Scriptures—two Bibles.
It wasn’t too bad.
But later, the New World Translation  of the Hebrew Scriptures
was released in installments.
So you’d get a volume every year or two.
And as we received each new volume,
we were encouraged to bring it to the meeting.
Now, in time, those volumes started to pile up
so that by 1960,
you might have volumes 1 through 5 of the Hebrew Scriptures,
also the Greek Scriptures, and your regular study aids!
And we had thick study aids in those days.
We had big briefcases and strong backs in those days.
We were really happy to get the complete New World Translation
in just one volume in 1961.
Now, let’s say a word about music.
That’s something that’s near and dear to my heart.
For many years, it was left up to the local servants
to decide which songs the congregation would sing at the meetings.
So the chairman of a particular meeting would select the songs,
but his choice wasn’t always final.
Many Kingdom Halls had a piano
or some other instrument
to accompany the singing.
But often the musician couldn’t play all of the songs in the book,
so we’d have to sing the songs he could play.
We got to know those few songs really well!
But those humble musicians did their best to accompany our singing.
Now, as a result of all this,
the words to those songs we sang nearly 70 years ago
still come readily to mind.
Do you remember the written review?
Maybe you don’t.
Congregations periodically
had a written review of material that had been covered
in the Theocratic Ministry School over the previous weeks.
Now, we had a half hour to answer
about 25 questions.
But then, when the half hour was up,
we would write our name on the paper,
hand it in to the school servant,
and he would take all the papers home to grade them.
Now, if there were 25 questions, you’d get 4 points apiece
for each correct answer—100 points total.
And then a week later, he’d return the papers to us at the meeting.
Now, in the early years of the arrangement (I remember well),
he’d announce the highest and lowest grade to the congregation.
Now, thankfully, he didn’t mention the names
of the one who got the highest and lowest score.
Well, later, that arrangement to announce
the highest and lowest grade was discontinued.
Do you remember when circuit assemblies
began on Friday evening
and continued through Sunday afternoon?
A full program
was presented Saturday afternoon and evening.
There was never a dull moment
on Saturday night.
There were lively demonstrations
that kept our interest
right up to the end of the program.
Sometimes the sets were very elaborate.
For example, suppose a publisher was demonstrating
a presentation from door to door.
Now, today we’d just imagine there was a door.
But back then at the circuit assembly,
there might be a frame with a painted door on the stage,
and maybe even a doorbell for the publisher to ring.
Now, if the householder was supposed to be interested,
you knew it because the house number was 777.
And if the householder was going to be opposed,
you knew that as well because the house number would be 666.
Now, on one program that I remember,
the publisher knocks on the door and a brother dressed as a priest answers.
He puts up a real argument about the Trinity.
Talk about visual aids
—but you never forgot what you saw and heard!
And do you remember when each congregation had a congregation servant
and up to seven other servants:
the assistant congregation servant, the Bible study servant,
the accounts servant, the Watchtower  study servant,
the magazine-territory servant, the literature servant,
and the Theocratic Ministry School servant?
Now, at that time, apart from book study conductors,
you couldn’t have more than eight servants in the congregation.
So unless someone moved,
a young man had no chance of becoming a servant.
So how could a young man reach out for more responsibility?
And how would the prophecy recorded
at Micah 5:5 ever be fulfilled?
There Jehovah promised:
“We will raise up against him seven shepherds,
yes, eight princes of mankind.”
Well, seven represents completeness.
So eight princes—that would indicate
that there would be more than enough men in the congregations
to provide theocratic direction.
But how could that be when there was basically
a limit of eight servants per congregation?
The answer came in 1971.
We were thrilled when we understood
that each congregation has a body of elders,
and there is no set number of elders or ministerial servants.
As many as are qualified can be appointed.
Now, when I was baptized 66 years ago,
you didn’t have to be approved for baptism by the congregation.
The only questions asked of baptism candidates
were the two they answered at the conclusion of the baptism talk.
That led to a few strange situations.
On a few occasions
—much to the surprise of the servants—
someone would rush up
to the front of the hall at the end
of the baptism talk,
answer the two questions,
and get baptized.
Something more was needed
—assurance that the individual really knew what he was doing
and especially that he was living in harmony with Scriptural principles.
So in 1967,
questions were provided so that the responsible brothers
could be assured that each candidate was truly qualified for baptism.
Those questions have been refined over the years.
And today, we go over some 60 questions
with baptism candidates.
The copper has turned to gold.
Do you remember when there were
very few pictures in our publications?
And the few that we had
were usually in black and white
or only two colors.
Today, our spiritual food
is served in attractive publications
in full color.
Now, those of us who’ve served
in foreign-language congregations will also remember
when a new publication in English
might not be available in another language for several years.
Study articles trailed by several months.
Now, that’s before it became possible for the branches
to do simultaneous printing.
So here’s how it worked.
Material in English would be mailed to the branches
by regular mail for translation.
If the translators had a question about the meaning of a sentence in English,
they would use regular mail to send their question to headquarters.
In time, headquarters would answer back by regular mail.
This back and forth —it could take quite a while.
And in some countries, mail service was poor.
Now, today, thanks to special computer programs
that our brothers have developed
and the ability to communicate electronically
and some other factors, we’re able to release
most language editions simultaneously with the English.
What an improvement!
Now, speaking of our literature,
do you realize that it’s been some 31 years
since the decision was made that in the United States
we’d no longer ask for a contribution for our literature?
Later, the arrangement was extended worldwide.
That’s been a real blessing for our brothers!
For example,
when we were asking for contributions for literature,
some brothers in Africa and other places
couldn’t afford to have a Watchtower  for every member of the family.
They were just too poor.
And what about bound books?
I’ll tell you an experience.
In one African country, a missionary noticed
that a young brother quoted a wide variety of scriptures
in his comments, and he got curious.
One day, he asked the young brother,
“How did you come to know so many scriptures?”
The brother replied: “It’s the Reasoning  book.
I read it every chance I get.”
The missionary asked him, “What do you mean
you read it every chance you get?”
Well, he replied: “I don’t have a Reasoning  book myself.
“I could never afford one.
“But I know a sister who has one,
“and she lets me borrow it from time to time.
I read it every chance I get.”
Well, you can imagine,
the missionary went out and bought him a Reasoning  book
and a New World Translation  for good measure.
It was a great investment.
The young brother was later called into Bethel,
and where do you think he was assigned?
To the literature department.
The brothers knew that he appreciated the literature so much
that he’d make sure the congregations had the literature they needed.
Well, looking back,
we can see that the arrangements back then served a purpose.
They were like fine copper.
We do not look down on them.
Rather, we take the view expressed
at Zechariah 4:10:
“Who has despised the day
of small beginnings?”
Now, as those taking the lead saw a better way of doing things,
they didn’t hesitate to make adjustments.
That’s very faith-strengthening.
And the best is yet to come!
As I mentioned in the beginning,
this may be the first time that some of you have heard about these things.
Why not ask someone who has been in the truth for many years
what it was like when he was new in the truth?
That could lead to a very stimulating discussion!
Thank you
for those historical insights, David.
When you think about
how much has changed just in our lifetimes,
you really see how Jehovah
keeps improving his organization.
Next, we have a great example
of someone who has seen all of the changes
we’ve talked about and more: John Mills.
Let’s see how he has faithfully served Jehovah
through multiple assignments and challenges.
I was raised with three sisters, and my mom was in the truth.
I remember sitting on the sofa
and just talking about spiritual things with my mom.
And she taught us to appreciate any assignment that we had
—to see it as something very special.
Pioneering was my life.
Gilead to me was a way to give to others
—to be very busy in service.
I prayed to Jehovah.
I said, “I really want to go to Gilead
but, if it’s possible, to have a wife too.”
And I just thought, ‘Boy, are you pushy!’
You know, and so—
But Jehovah gave me that.
I went to Gilead.
And to my amazement,
there was the most lovely, spiritual sister,
a student in the same class, Lois.
I met her and was able to marry her
one week after Gilead.
Arriving as a newlywed couple
in a missionary home with seven other people
was quite daunting.
But we didn’t let that faze us; we were on our honeymoon.
Colombia was a paradise spiritually.
We loved it so much!
This was the kind of life we wanted.
Lois was a great teacher in the ministry.
I always enjoyed working with her; she was actually a great support for me.
Obviously, Colombia had its risks.
I remember in the mornings, sometimes it got to the point when
I would look at Lois and she would look at me and we’d just say,
“If I don’t see you, see you in the Paradise,” you know?
Colombia became our home.
We traveled the length and breadth
of the country in our different assignments.
We had been over 20 years in Colombia when it became very evident
that Lois’s mom would need our care.
This, of course, would mean leaving our assignment.
It almost tore my heart apart to leave Colombia.
I felt I was abandoning so many privileges
and my treasured assignment.
In the U.S.A.,
we were working as a team,
and I could see Lois really organized,
making the best of the situation.
Helping her mom
was really the source,
in a way, of her deep joy.
Helping others was just a way of life
to Lois.
It doesn’t matter what privilege you have
and what responsibility;
true happiness
is always found in giving.
Really, Lois got very ill.
Lois never cried about her illness
or felt sorry for herself.
She always was focused on others
and would give of herself, even
within the pain of illness.
Now that Lois has passed,
many times I think of her example,
and it just motivates me to carry on.
Here at the Central America branch
I am surrounded by such a loving family.
I resolved when
I went through this situation
with losing my wife to find others
that were in similar situations
and maybe sit down for a coffee.
Just that fellow feeling
of just being able
to show interest and to encourage
another person is a great joy
that I personally find one of the most helpful things
to endure trials.
John’s life of faithful service reminds me
of the truth found at 2 Corinthians 1:3, 4:
“[Jehovah] comforts us in all our trials
“so that we may be able to comfort others
“in any sort of trial with the comfort
that we receive from God.”
Have you ever wondered
why we sing at our meetings?
or why we attend conventions, usually in the summer?
Many who are young in years or new in the truth
may not be familiar with certain aspects of our history.
Yet, this rich spiritual history
is your heritage,
and we want you to become acquainted with it.
So the Governing Body
has approved the development of a new series:
Our History in Motion.
Each segment will look at an aspect
of our worship through time,
similar to what David shared with us earlier.
The series will help us see
that our worship is rooted,
not in tradition or custom,
but in the truth found in God’s Word.
Now, for our first episode,
it looks at the history of singing praises to Jehovah.
It was made in secret,
hidden in the lining of a jacket,
and then smuggled out of the country.
What was it?
A recording of brothers and sisters in Siberia
singing Kingdom songs.
They sent it from one side of the earth to the other
to be played at the 1958 international convention in New York
for an audience of more than 250,000 people.
Why is singing so important to Jehovah’s Witnesses?
Let’s find out in this episode of Our History in Motion.
Jehovah’s worshippers
have long praised him with song.
But how did singing become
a part of our modern-day worship?
The story begins more than 150 years ago.
The year is about 1869
in Allegheny, Pennsylvania, U.S.A.
Charles Taze Russell
is a young man searching for Scriptural truth.
One evening he’s walking along and hears something
—singing coming from a religious meeting being held in a basement.
He goes in, and what he hears sparks a fire
for Bible study like never before.
Later, Russell and his associates
make music’s role in pure worship clear
as they rediscover Bible truth.
Charles Taze Russell
may have come to appreciate
how the power of music can stir emotions
from a music business that his father owned for a period of time.
He believed that “the singing of the truth
“is a good way to get it into the heads
and hearts of God’s people.”
The first issue of Zion’s Watch Tower,
published in July of 1879,
announced a songbook
—the first of many to come.
It was called Songs of the Bride.
It contained 144 hymns,
or religious songs of praise.
The Bible Students sang at their meetings and assemblies.
What was it like to sing these songs back in the early 1900’s?
Imagine that you’re at one of Charles Taze Russell’s lectures.
As you walk in, you’re handed a small sheet of paper.
You look for a seat, but it’s packed.
As the crowd quiets down,
they announce that the meeting will start with a song and prayer.
In a church, you expect to find a hymn book in your pew,
but this is a rented hall.
Then you realize that the paper you were handed
has the song lyrics,
and it also has a place to leave your name and address
if you’d like a Bible study.
So when the audience starts to sing, you join in.
What did songs sound like back then?
Let’s listen to a song we sang for over eight decades.
Here’s a recording from 1916.
That’s a little different than how
our songs sound today.
Compare different versions of this song,
and you’ll notice that the lyrics
and theme changed over the years.
Here’s a version of “All Hail”
by the Watch Tower Male Quartet in 1935.
In our first songbook this song was called
“All Hail the Power of Jesus’ Name,”
which was about, well,
the power of Jesus’ name
with zero mention of Jehovah.
You see, many songs prior to this
were adapted from existing church hymns.
Now here’s the same song in 1950.
Instead of the lyrics
overemphasizing Jesus’ name,
the lyrics refer to “making known God’s will”
and mention Jehovah by name.
Why all the changes?
Because our songs reflect
our current understanding of Scriptural truth.
As the light gets brighter,
we understand the truth more clearly,
so the songs change.
Our first songbook explained
explained the goal to publish
“songs free from objectionable theology,”
and it’s been the case ever since.
We don’t hold on to songs
for tradition or nostalgia.
We sing them because it’s the truth!
From the 1928 songbook onward,
there was a big shift.
Many songs were written by our brothers and sisters.
They put more emphasis on Jehovah’s name,
his attributes, and his Kingdom.
You can even tell by the title
Songs of Praise to Jehovah.
Some of the songs might even sound familiar,
like this one.
Are your parents in the truth?
your grandparents?
even your great-grandparents?
If so, they sang the same song as you
at their meetings and assemblies.
That’s a real legacy!
Let’s fast-forward to the 1940’s.
Some of our brothers were imprisoned for their faith.
The world was at war and needed good news.
So we intensified
our preaching and teaching work.
This is when the Watchtower Bible School of Gilead
and the Theocratic Ministry School started,
and it’s also when singing was reintroduced at our meetings.
Wait a minute!
Reintroduced?
That means we stopped singing at meetings.
When?
Find out in the next episode
of Our History in Motion.
Well, that’s a cliff-hanger!
Would you like to know
why we stopped singing for a time?
You’ll want to watch the second part of this video.
It will be posted soon on jw.org.
And look for future episodes
of Our History in Motion.
Many years ago,
Awake!  magazine
published the story of Elizabeth Balnave.
Elizabeth explains
why she made a major career decision.
How did that decision affect her life?
Let’s find out in this episode
of Where Are They Now?
As a child, I dreamed
of becoming a ballerina.
I trained as a ballet dancer from childhood.
I was taught to give complete obedience to the artistic director,
absolute loyalty to the dance company,
and to put ballet before everything else in my life.
I finally realized there’s no way to get ahead in this world
without compromise.
It just can’t be done.
Such a life is empty and unsatisfying.
The problem is, once you get into that,
you get lulled in by that glamour and glitz.
Now, down the road when you finally see the trap
and what you got into, it’s very hard to get out.
And I always tell young people, you know,
that it doesn’t matter how good everything seems; it doesn’t matter how great.
There’s always a string attached—always.
And then one day, you’re going to wake up and it’s a rope.
And you can’t cut a rope that easily
—meaning you can’t get out of the situation
once Satan has you trapped in it.
And it happens without you even realizing it.
Ballet is discipline,
and I had to figure out a way
to take that skill
and transfer it into my everyday life.
It took some time, but I finally figured it out,
because it’s not a waste.
It’s good.
But what I had to learn was to get out of my comfort zone.
We were in Bethel until 1987.
Jack had a job lined up when we left Bethel, and that was good.
I couldn’t get a job because of my physical health issues.
I probably was in bed for about five months.
Eventually, I started feeling better,
and that’s when I realized how bad the medical bills were getting.
I just dragged myself out of bed and went and looked for a part-time job.
Obviously, through all of this, Jack and I just kept praying.
We knew Jehovah would take care of us.
No question about that.
Eventually, I did get a job at a law firm.
It was a good job.
I actually lasted there 30 years.
Absolutely Jehovah blessed me,
and I believe what he was blessing were my efforts.
I didn’t quit, and I refused to compromise.
When I started seeing that I was really learning this new skill
and I was getting good at it,
that’s when I sat down and I said: “Well, Jehovah, I have this new skill.
I want to be able to use it for you.”
One thing led to another, and I became
a commuter Bethelite for the Legal Department.
I’d say that about 11 years after I had left Bethel,
I was working and all of a sudden, I got sick again with the same thing
—complete rapid loss of weight and all the weakness came back.
I was eventually diagnosed as having celiac disease.
So once I changed my diet, I just started getting better and better.
I stayed with the law firm until 2014,
and then my husband and I retired and moved to another part of the country.
And now, currently, I’m a remote Bethel consultant.
If you slave for the world, you really are a slave.
If you slave for Jehovah,
in my opinion, you’re not slaving at all.
You couldn’t have a better partnership
than you and Jehovah, and that’s how I view it.
And you’re never going to experience Jehovah to the full
unless you put yourself out there for him to use.
I’ve had a wonderful life
of extraordinary spiritual privileges.
There’s no career in the world that is ever going to come close to that.
Wouldn’t you say that resilience
is one of the qualities that has helped Elizabeth?
What can each of us do
to be more resilient?
Notice three practical suggestions
in this morning worship presented by Brother Gajus Glockentin.
Mary kept listening to what Jesus was saying.
How commendable!
She set the right priorities
and is a good example for us.
Martha, her sister, however,
received loving correction from Jesus,
as our printed comment puts it.
Now let us, today, put ourselves in the shoes of Martha for a moment.
She showed great interest in supporting Jesus
by providing him a base during his ministry
in the difficult area of Judea.
Now this time,
Mary and Martha were probably working together
to prepare things for Jesus.
But after Jesus arrived, Mary stopped helping as our text indicates.
How did Martha feel about it?
Now she had to care for everything herself.
Can we imagine the tension rising
within Martha’s heart?
The stress level is increased,
and her dear sister sits and listens to Jesus.
So she asked Jesus to correct Mary,
to order her back to work.
But to her surprise, she, Martha, received counsel from Jesus.
How would we feel in such a situation?
We are doing something well-intentioned
and, yet, instead of commendation, we receive counsel.
Maybe our eyes filled with tears.
We feel the pain in our chest.
We might think we can’t breathe anymore.
Did Martha think for a moment, replying to Jesus, saying:
“This is not fair!
“I am doing everything to support you, and now this.
“You know, from now on, I am listening too,
and I am curious to find out who prepares the meals for you.”
Of course, we don’t know what Martha thought and said.
But what we do know, as our printed comment puts it,
she took to heart Jesus’ loving correction.
What can help us to overcome such a painful moment
and to progress?
The term often used in this connection
is “resilience.”
People who are resilient are able to recover easily and quickly
from unpleasant and damaging events.
It is like the ability of this piece of metal
to tolerate pressure
and go back to its original form.
Let us, therefore, look at three factors that make us resilient
and different from those who easily give up and surrender.
Now, the first factor is facing reality
—facing reality.
Let us, please, open to Proverbs chapter 28.
The question we are asking ourselves in a difficult moment is this:
‘Do I truly understand and accept the reality of my situation?’
Here, at Proverbs 28:26,
it starts by saying:
“Whoever trusts in his own heart
is stupid.”
We might tend to put on emotional blinders
and see only what we want to see.
Many people slip into denial as a coping mechanism.
However, the Proverb continues in the second part, saying:
“But the one who walks in wisdom
will escape.”
This means seeing things the way they are.
Facing reality
—really facing reality is grueling work.
Indeed, it can be unpleasant
and often emotionally wrenching.
The apostle Peter had this experience
when Jesus looked at him after Peter had denied him three times.
Peter faced reality, went outside,
broke down, and wept bitterly.
For sure, he was not looking for any excuses.
This experience, as well as other situations where he received counsel,
helped him to make progress and to fulfill his assignments even better.
Now, what is the second factor?
We call it “meaning-making.”
We might know people who under pressure threw up their hands
and cried and said, “Why is this happening to me?”
Such people see themselves as victims,
and living through hardship does not teach them any lessons.
We, however, based on our Bible knowledge,
understand why difficulties and challenging situations
are sometimes unavoidable.
Seeing the bigger picture adds meaning.
This helps us, as a resilient person,
not only to endure an unpleasant situation or a new circumstance
but also to look at seeming obstacles
and see an opportunity in it.
We all know that no one is perfect.
Everyone fails at something sometime.
So our choice is the manner in which we respond.
We are actively trying to make the best out of it,
looking ahead rather than behind,
setting goals —maybe new goals.
We might remember how Brother Harold King
showed this resilient disposition
when he was in solitary confinement.
How did he give meaning to his difficult situation
by making the best out of it?
He said:
“I arranged for a program of ‘preaching’ activity.
“But to whom does one preach when in solitary confinement?
“I decided that I would build up some appropriate Bible sermons
“from the things I could remember
and then preach to imaginary characters.”
So in our context, we can say
meaning-making is like building a bridge
from present day hardships to a better future.
By means of this bridge,
we make a difficult situation manageable.
We remove the sense that the present is overwhelming.
Now let’s look at the third factor:
a balanced view of ourselves.
Well, we said at the beginning that we have to face reality
which can go along with feelings of sadness and disappointment.
As resilient people,
we don’t take a failure
or a challenging situation personally.
Let us, please, open to Romans chapter 7,
because we want to demonstrate this point
by means of the example of the apostle Paul.
At times, he felt discouraged over his weaknesses.
Here in chapter 7,
he describes the pain of conscience
that he suffered because of feeling captive to sin.
But then in verse 24,
he cries out, saying:
“Miserable man that I am!”
Evidently, though, Paul realized
that his imperfection did not define him.
Nine years later,
in his second letter to his friend Timothy,
shortly before his death,
he stated his personal conclusion of the matter
here at 2 Timothy 4:7.
He said:
“I have fought the fine fight,
“I have run the race to the finish,
I have observed the faith.”
Paul’s problems and inner struggle did not miraculously disappear.
Still, it did not prevent him
from accomplishing remarkable things in Jehovah’s service.
So, therefore, we do not berate ourselves
with self-defeating language,
such as “I’m a failure”
or “I’m useless.”
Reflecting on positive aspects of our lives
and reflecting on our strengths
helps us to maintain a balanced view of ourselves.
So in conclusion,
the experience of Martha reminded us today
of the importance of building
and maintaining resilience
by facing reality,
meaning-making,
and maintaining a balanced view of ourselves.
The Bible contains wonderful descriptions
of how life will be in Paradise.
As our new music video shows,
visualizing these future blessings
brings joy to our heart.
I close my eyes, and I can see A world of peace, love, and harmony.
Come with me, And you’ll see.
You will see.
It’s not a dream, as I’m sure you know. These things God promised so long ago
Are guaranteed, Sure to be.
You will see.
Look around— There’s joy and laughter in ev’ry sound.
Look and see— This is the way our God meant it to be.
Those who fell asleep along the way, They live again; we see them ev’ry day.
Come with me, And you’ll see.
You will see.
The pain and crying there used to be Has gone forever; now it’s history.
Come with me, And you’ll see.
You will see.
Look around— There’s joy and laughter in ev’ry sound.
Look and see— This is the way our God meant it to be.
Jehovah’s word is enough for me. With eyes of faith, it’s reality.
As we see What’s in store,
You can be sure Until the moon is no more,
When you—
Close your eyes and come with me To God’s world of peace and harmony.
Come with me, And you’ll see.
You will see.
What a beautiful song and video!
In our program,
we looked back at theocratic history,
not to be nostalgic, but to remind us
that Jehovah continually improves his organization,
just as he promised.
We debuted an exciting new series,
Our History in Motion,
and saw the essential role that singing plays in our worship.
We learned
how Jehovah blesses those
who serve him.
Elizabeth gave up
a glamorous career
but gained spiritual treasures.
And we saw that although John
has experienced many difficulties,
Jehovah has helped him
maintain his joy by helping others.
Before we conclude,
let’s enjoy our video postcard.
This month,
we visit our brothers in Ecuador.
As its name suggests,
Ecuador is situated on earth’s equator.
It stretches from the Galapagos Islands
to the Andes Mountains
and the Amazon River basin.
This is Mount Chimborazo.
Measured from the center of the earth,
it’s the highest point on our planet
because of the bulging of the earth at its equator.
This train line was carved into the Andes more than a century ago.
It was used by the first missionaries
who arrived in 1946.
Today, more than 100,000
of Jehovah’s Witnesses proclaim the good news in Ecuador.
Nearly 300,000 people attended the Memorial in 2020.
The Chontapunta Quichua Congregation
began as an isolated group.
To support themselves, our brothers raise flowers
and even pan for gold.
But their zeal is for the ministry.
They go to great lengths to bear thorough witness in their territory.
Where bridges aren’t available, they find a way.
They use two boats, named Enoc
and Enoc 2, to reach remote Quichua-speaking communities.
Remote communities have poor cellular service.
That doesn’t stop this Bible student.
Look what he does to get a good signal
so he can join meetings and have his study.
To reach those without cellular service,
the brothers use a high-frequency radio
to conduct return visits and Bible studies.
Our brothers have arranged for talks and the Memorial to be given in Waorani,
an indigenous language that’s not yet translated.
This little girl, whose family is part of the congregation,
shares videos with Waorani-speaking children.
She is four years old!
Our dear brothers and sisters
from the Chontapunta Quichua Congregation in Ecuador
send their love and greetings
to the worldwide brotherhood.
Leon, my friend,
I want to thank you so very much for helping out with this program.
I really appreciated the help.
And together, we send all of you our warm Christian love.
From the World Headquarters of Jehovah’s Witnesses,
this is JW Broadcasting!

和我一起主持本月节目的
是我的好朋友利昂·韦弗
欢迎你！
戴维，很高兴和你一起主持
首先，我想介绍一下我的好朋友利昂
1990年我受邀请来到伯特利
我被委派到了传道部
利昂就是其中一位监督

ko.text: 고대부터 여호와께서는 자신의 백성을 통해 건축하는 일을 해 오셨습니다.
순결한 숭배에 사용할 건물을 새로 짓고 리모델링하는 일을 하며
오늘날 우리가 전 세계에서 진행하고 있는 건축 활동의 규모는 상상을 뛰어넘습니다.
이러한 공사를 위해 수많은 자원봉사자와 장비가 필요하게 되었습니다.
또한 우리는 다양한 어려움에 직면하기도 합니다.
건축 현장에는 심각한 부상을 초래하는 사고의 위험이 언제나 도사리고 있습니다.
모든 건축 자원봉사자들의 생명과 안전을 지키는 일에
이것은 결코 간과해서는 안 될 중요한 문제입니다.
건축 봉사에 참여하다가 심각한 부상을 입었으며
「국제 인명 보호 및 손실 방지 지침서」는 이렇게 분명히 알려 줍니다.
“우리는 … 사고가 나지 않고 손실이 최소한으로 발생하는 환경을
자신의 영성을 반영한다는 것을 모두가 이해한다면
영이 거만하면 걸려 넘어지게 된다”라고 알려 줍니다.
아무리 기술이 좋고 경험이 많은 사람이라도
또한 경험이 부족한 사람이라면 겸허를 나타내야 합니다.
“돌을 캐는 자는 돌 때문에 다칠 수 있고,
장작을 쪼개는 자는 장작 때문에 위험에 처할 수 있다”라고 알려 줍니다.
이것이 우리가 살펴볼 두 번째 부면입니다.
안전하게 작업하기 위해 어떻게 잘 계획할 수 있습니까?
건축과 유지·보수를 할 때 따라야 할 표준과
우리 각자가 져야 할 책임에 대해 알려 줍니다.
유지·보수와 건축 작업을 위한 「작업 위험 분석」 양식도
우리가 잠재적 위험 요소를 파악하는 데 도움이 됩니다.
우리가 어떻게 미리 계획하여 위험 요소들을 파악할 수 있는지
이 배관에 물이 새서 수리해야 될 것 같아요.
그런데 일단 여기에 불이 붙지 않도록 조치를 해야 할 것 같아요.
안 그러면 화재가 날 수도 있으니까요.
누군가가 소화기를 들고 옆에 서 있으면 좋을 것 같아요.
그리고 용접이 끝난 후에도 누군가가 계속 지켜봐야 할 것 같네요.
작업 후에도 화재가 발생할 수 있으니까요.
그럼 지금 가서 도와줄 사람을 정해 볼게요.
일단은 미끄러져서 다칠 수 있으니까, 안전화가 필요할 것 같고요.
안전벨트 사용 교육을 받았는지 확인해 봐야겠네요.
그리고 사고가 났을 때 도와줄 지원 팀도 있어야 될 것 같아요.
지붕에 올라갈 사람을 최소화하면 좋을 것 같은데
밑에서 확인할 수 있는 방법은 없겠죠?
그러면 밑에서도 점검을 할 수 있겠죠?
무사고라는 목표를 달성하기 위한 세 번째 부면과도 관련이 있습니다.
유지·보수와 같은 간단한 작업을 할 때든
형제 자매들의 안전을 지킬 수 있습니다.
따라서 안전하게 일하기 위해 이러한 점들을 기억하십시오.
첫째, 생명을 소중히 여기시는 여호와와 같은 시각을 가지십시오.
둘째, 잠재적인 위험 요소들을 미리 분별하십시오.
셋째, 위험 요소를 파악했다면 위험을 줄이거나 없애기 위해 조치를 취하십시오.
안전을 지키는 것의 중요성을 절대 잊어서는 안 됩니다.
안전을 지키는 건 여호와께 순종하는 것이며
여호와께서 우리를 기적으로 보호해 주실 거라고 기대해서는 안 됩니다.
우리가 사람들의 생명을 구하기 위해 전파 활동에서 최선을 다하듯이
여호와께서는 우리가 건축 현장에서 지침에 순종하여
그것들이 너에게 생명을 주고 네 목에 장식이 될 것이다.
그러면 네가 길을 안전하게 걸을 것이다.”
그리고 그 밖의 모든 건축 현장에서 함께 일할 때
지혜롭게 행동하고 우리의 길을 안전하게 걷도록 하십시다.

en.text: From ancient times, Jehovah has directed his people to build.
The joyful work of constructing
and remodeling buildings
to advance pure worship
has continued in our time.
But who could have anticipated the tremendous scale and need
for today’s worldwide building work,
requiring so many volunteers,
tools, equipment,
and often working in challenging situations?
With all this building comes
the risk of accidents that can result in serious injury.
That’s why we, as Jehovah’s people,
care deeply about protecting
the lives and safety of all our fellow construction volunteers.
This is not a hypothetical consideration.
Sadly, some of our brothers and sisters have experienced
serious injuries while volunteering on projects
—some, the most serious imaginable.
Our Global Life Safety and Loss Prevention Guidelines
clearly state:
“Our goal is to have an accident-free environment
“with minimum loss . . .
“This zero-accident goal can be accomplished
“if each one realizes that his attitude
“toward [the] life safety and loss prevention
reflects his spirituality.”
How can we accomplish this?
Let’s consider three important aspects:
our attitude toward our work,
how we plan for it,
and how we work to avoid potential danger.
First, our attitude.
Proverbs 16:18 tells us:
“Pride is before a crash,
and a haughty spirit before stumbling.”
No matter how skilled or experienced we may be,
we need to humbly follow safety direction.
We also need to show modesty if we’re inexperienced
and let others train us properly
before we begin to work with unfamiliar equipment.
Ecclesiastes 10:9 tells us:
“The one who quarries stones may be hurt by them,
and the one who splits logs may be endangered by them.”
Many aspects of construction are inherently dangerous.
This underscores our second aspect:
the need to plan wisely.
How can we plan for a safe work experience?
We have tools to help.
The guideline Working Together Safely
provides standards for our construction
and maintenance projects.
It also reminds us of our personal responsibility.
Are you familiar with its sound guidance?
Our Job Hazard Analysis forms for maintenance and construction
help us anticipate potential safety risks.
Let’s examine just a few of the potential dangers
it helps us to foresee in advance of working on a project.
This pipe here has a leak and needs to be fixed.
We’re going to have to do a weld here, I’m afraid.
Well, we’ll have to insulate this part here, in between the wall and the pipe.
OK.
Otherwise, we’ll end up creating a fire hazard here in the Kingdom Hall.
I see! Let me write that down.
I was thinking, too, we should assign someone
to stand by with a fire extinguisher while the weld is being done.
You’re right.
And also I think we should put someone on fire-hazard duty
to make sure nothing catches fire after the weld is done.
Mm. I agree. Good idea.
Perfect.
I’ll go ahead and make the assignments then.
OK, I’ll get things ready here.
Let’s do it.
I think that here the brothers are going to need safety boots
so that they don’t slip and fall.
They’re also going to need safety harnesses since they’ll be up pretty high.
What do you think?
Do you remember if all the brothers assigned were trained to work with safety harnesses?
We’re also going to need a support team
to be ready to help in case of an accident.
It would be best if we could have less people up on the roof.
But it’s impossible to inspect things from down here, right?
I have an idea.
What if we put a camera on a long pole
and do the inspection from down here?
We can check everything out from one end to the other.
OK! Great idea, sounds good.
This wise planning reflects the third aspect
of achieving our zero-accident goal:
Pay close attention to direction
so we can work to eliminate or avoid danger.
When working on a large project
or a smaller one, including maintenance work,
the right attitude, planning, and actions
will help keep our brothers and sisters safe.
So remember the steps we can take to ensure safety.
First, have Jehovah’s view of things.
Life is precious.
Second, be wise and anticipate the potential hazards.
And third,
once you anticipate a risk,
take precautions to remove or reduce it.
Never forget how serious maintaining safety is.
It demonstrates obedience to Jehovah
and affects our relationship with him.
While we are working on theocratic building projects,
we cannot expect miraculous protection.
Just as Jehovah wants us to exert ourselves
in preaching to others to help save lives,
he requires us to work obediently
to protect our fellow volunteers.
Jehovah tells us in Proverbs:
“Safeguard practical wisdom and thinking ability;
“they will give you life and be an adornment for your neck;
then you will walk on your way in safety.”
Let us all act wisely and walk safely
as we work together
on Kingdom Hall projects and maintenance
and construction projects.

ko.text: 오늘의 성구와 해설은 두 가지 주제에 대해 다루고 있습니다.
하나는 매우 중요한 사건이고, 또 하나는 매우 중요한 특성입니다.
이제 이러한 점들에 대해 생각해 보시죠.
아마겟돈 전에 어떤 일이 일어날 것입니까?
순종하면 지금 어떤 유익을 얻을 수 있습니까?
그리고 아마겟돈과 순종, 그 둘 사이에는 어떤 관련이 있습니까?
아마겟돈이 시작되기 직전에 여러 가지 사건이 일어날 텐데,
「순결한 숭배」 책 18장에서 설명하는 것처럼, 모든 거짓 종교 조직이 전부 다 멸망되고 난 후에,
여호와께서는 전 세계에 있는 자신의 종들이
최종적으로 강력한 심판의 소식을 전하게 하실 것으로 보입니다.
그것은 인간 정부가 곧 사라질 거라는 내용이 담긴 소식일 것입니다.
그리고 땅의 왕들은 당연히 그 소식을 좋아하지 않을 것입니다.
에스겔 38장에서는 이 왕들이 마곡의 곡으로서 우리를 공격할 것이라고 설명하고 있습니다.
그런데 우리 하느님의 백성이 여러 나라에 살고 있기 때문에,
이 왕들이 동시에 우리를 공격하려면 국경을 초월해서 서로 힘을 합쳐야만 가능할 것입니다.
다시 말해 그들은 함께 협력하고 연합해서 노력해야 할 것입니다.
마곡의 곡이라는 말이 나라들이 구성하는 연합체를 가리킨다고 알려 줍니다.
그럼 마곡의 곡의 공격을 받을 하느님의 백성 가운데는 누가 있습니까?
기름부음받은 그리스도인들 중 남은 자들이 이 땅에 있으면서 공격을 받을 것입니까?
“14만 4000명의 남은 자들이 하늘로 가기 얼마 전에, 곡은 하느님의 백성을 공격할 것입니다.”
나라들은 기름부음받은 그리스도인들이 여전히 땅에 있을 때 공격을 시작할 것입니다.
성경 어디를 보면 그 점을 알 수 있습니까?
“너는 땅을 덮는 구름처럼 내 백성 이스라엘을 치러 올 것이다.”
우리 출판물에서 오랫동안 설명해 온 것처럼, 여기 이스라엘은 영적 이스라엘을 가리킵니다.
따라서 나라들의 연합체가 우리를 공격할 때,
그때의 중앙장로회를 포함하여 영적 이스라엘의 남은 자들은 우리와 함께 있을 것입니다.
이처럼 충실한 형제들이 우리 곁에 있다는 것은 내적 평온함과 마음의 평화를 줄 것입니다.
우리는 그 힘으로 사나운 나라들의 연합체가 공격을 시작할 때
그 시기를 잘 헤쳐 나갈 수 있게 될 것입니다.
그리고 마곡의 곡의 공격 중의 어느 한 시점에 예수께서는 천사들을 보내셔서
전 세계에 남아 있는 모든 영적 이스라엘을 모아들이시고 하늘로 들어 올리실 것입니다.
그렇게 되면 땅에 있는 우리에게 큰 변화가 생길 겁니다.
이제 우리는 기름부음받은 형제들 없이 적과 맞서야 할 것입니다.
하지만 그렇다 해도 누가복음 21:28에서 말한 것처럼 우리는 ‘일어서서 머리를 들’ 것입니다.
왜냐하면 기름부음받은 자들이 하늘로 올라가면 우리의 구출이 가까웠다는 것을 알기 때문입니다.
예수와 천사들과 14만 4000명의 그리스도의 형제들이 하늘 군대를 이루어
나라들의 연합체의 공격에서 우리를 구출해 줄 것입니다.
기름부음받은 자들이 우리를 구출하러 올 때 우리에 대해 어떤 느낌을 갖게 될까요?
많은 기름부음받은 자들은 우리와 개인적인 우정을 쌓았습니다.
그들은 베델과 회중에서 우리와 함께 섬겼고,
우리는 여러 가지 방법으로 그들을 지원할 기회를 가졌습니다.
그들이 예수를 따라 우리를 구출하러 올 때 얼마나 행복해할지 한번 생각해 보십시오!
그 시점에, 그들은 가지고 있는 권한과 능력을 사용하여,
지상에서 시련을 겪는 동안 자신들을 충성스럽게 지원해 준 땅에 있는 사람들을 지켜 줄 것입니다.
오늘 발췌된 파수대 기사의 제목이 “아마겟돈—좋은 소식!”인 것도 놀라운 일이 아닙니다.
네, 그 소식은 하늘과 땅에서 여호와를 섬기는 모두에게 좋은 소식이기 때문입니다.
이제 두 번째로 순종이라는 주제에 대해 생각해 보겠습니다.
최근에 우리는 인사 위원회로부터 순종에 관한 편지를 받았습니다.
그 편지는 코로나19 기간에 배운 교훈에 대해 이렇게 말했습니다.
“아마도 우리가 배운 가장 큰 교훈은 순종이 중요하다는 점일 것입니다.
이 부면에서 여러분은 정말 훌륭한 본을 세워 왔습니다.”
이 따뜻한 칭찬은 전 세계에 있는 모든 충실한 형제 자매들에게도 적용됩니다.
로마서 6:17에 나오는 것처럼, 하느님의 종인 우리는 “마음으로부터 순종”합니다.
여호와의 조직에서 받은 지침들을 통해 우리는 어떤 유익을 얻었습니까?
“받은 지침들을 따랐더니 마음의 평화를 얻을 수 있었습니다.”
성서 연구생을 가르칠 때나 친구들에게 조언할 때 말의 자유가 생겨요.”
“이제 저는 앞으로 주어질 지침들에 순종할 준비가 더 잘 된 것 같습니다”라고 말했습니다.
네, 이 형제 자매들의 말에는 순종의 유익에 대해 우리가 어떻게 느끼는지가 잘 드러나 있지 않습니까?
또 우리의 순종은 믿지 않는 가족들에게도 좋은 영향을 줄 수 있습니다.
미국에 살고 있는 한 자매는 45년이 넘도록 여호와를 섬겨 왔습니다.
그런데 그 오랜 세월 동안 남편은 진리에 관심을 보이지 않았죠.
회중이 사랑과 관심을 갖고 그의 가족을 도와주는 것을 보고
남편은 고마운 마음이 들어, 줌으로 회중 집회에 참석하기 시작했습니다.
집회에서 그는 바이러스 감염 예방 수칙을 잘 지키라는 베델에서 온 광고를 자주 들었고,
그 지시에 순종하는 것이 회중에 보호가 된다는 것을 알 수 있었습니다.
그러던 어느 날 증인이 아닌 친척이 와서 “같이 나갑시다”라고 했을 때 남편은 이렇게 대답했죠.
“나는 베델에서 우리가 나가도 된다고 할 때까지는 꼼짝도 하지 않을 거야.”
남편이 그렇게 대답하는 것을 듣고 자매가 얼마나 기뻤을까요!
야고보서 3:17이 그 답을 찾는 데 도움이 됩니다.
“기꺼이 순종하다”라고 번역된 그리스어 단어는 「신세계역」 성경에서 단 한 번 나오는데,
“기꺼이 순종”하는 사람은 자신의 생각을 빨리 바꾸죠.
분명한 사실이 밝혀지면 자기 생각을 시정합니다.
또한 다른 사람들과 잘 지내려고 노력하는 사람으로 알려져 있죠.
흥미롭게도 1세기에는 동일한 그리스어 단어가 군인들과 관련해서도 사용되었습니다.
성경 학자들에 따르면 유대인 역사가인 플라비우스 요세푸스가
로마 군인들의 순종하는 태도를 묘사할 때 그 동일한 단어를 사용했습니다.
사실, 요세푸스는 로마군이 그처럼 성공을 거둔 이유 하나가
군인들이 잘 훈련되어 있고, 기꺼이 순종했기 때문이라고 썼습니다.
물론 우리가 군인들처럼 실제 무기를 사용하지는 않지만,
잘 생각해 보면 과거의 로마 군인과 오늘날 우리는 비슷합니다.
우리도 잘 훈련되고 기꺼이 순종해야 합니다.
앞으로 하느님의 조직에서 생존하는 데 필요한 지침을 베풀어 줄 때
나라들이 우리를 공격하고 이어서 아마겟돈  전쟁이 시작될 때,
순종하는 것이 우리를 보호해 줄 것입니다.
그럼 오늘 살펴본 내용의 요점은 무엇입니까?
우리는 나라들의 연합체로부터 공격을 받게 될 것입니다.
순종하는 태도를 기르는 훈련을 할 좋은 기회입니다.
하지만 우리가 기꺼이 순종한다면 우리는 보호받게 될 것입니다.

en.text: Today’s text and comments
highlight two subjects:
one, a very important event;
two, a very important quality.
The event is Armageddon.
The quality is obedience.
So let’s consider these questions:
What will take place before Armageddon?
How do we benefit now from being obedient?
What is the link
between Armageddon and obedience?
Let’s start with the subject of Armageddon.
What are some of the events that are taking place
shortly before the start of Armageddon?
Now, as explained in the Pure Worship  book, chapter 18,
after the destruction of all false religious organizations,
we as God’s servants worldwide
may be used by Jehovah to proclaim
a final and hard-hitting judgment message.
That message may announce
that the political system is about to end.
Not surprisingly, the kings of the earth
will not take that kindly.
Ezekiel chapter 38
describes that these kings will attack us
in their role as Gog of Magog.
Now, since we as God’s people live in many different countries,
these kings will need to work together
across national borders
in order to attack us all at the same time.
To do so, they have to combine,
or coalesce, their efforts.
And that is why in our current publications,
Gog of Magog is described as a combination,
or coalition, of nations.
Now, who among God’s people will be attacked
by Gog of Magog?
Will the remaining anointed Christians still be on earth
and also be attacked?
The July issue
of The Watchtower  of 2015 stated this:
“Shortly before the remaining ones of the 144,000
“are taken to heaven,
Gog will attack God’s people.”
Thus, according to this Watchtower, the nations will attack us
while the anointed Christians are still on earth.
Now, where does the Bible confirm that statement?
At Ezekiel 38:16.
Speaking about Gog of Magog, the prophecy states:
“Like clouds covering the land,
you will come against my people Israel.”
Now, as our publications have long explained,
Israel here refers to spiritual Israel.
So indeed, the remnant of spiritual Israel,
including the brothers on the Governing Body at that time,
will be with us when this coalition attacks us.
Now, having these faithful brothers at our side
will certainly give us an added measure
of inner calmness and peace
that will help us to get through the initial phase
of the attack of that fierce coalition of nations.
But then at some point during the attack by Gog of Magog,
Jesus will send out his angels
to gather all the remaining spiritual Israelites worldwide
and they will be raised to heaven.
That event will mean
a big change for us on earth.
We will face our enemies
without the anointed brothers at our side.
Yet, even so,
according to Luke 21:28,
we will ‘stand up straight and lift up our heads.’
Now, why will we not fear?
Because we know that the departure of the anointed ones to heaven
indicates that our rescue is imminent.
Jesus and the angels and the 144,000 brothers of Christ
will form the heavenly army that comes to deliver us
from the coalition of nations.
Now, just think about the emotions
that the anointed ones will feel for us
as they come to our rescue.
Many of the anointed have developed personal friendships with us.
They have served together with us here at Bethel and in the congregations
where we had the privilege of supporting them in various ways.
We can just imagine how happy they will be
when they follow Jesus to deliver us!
At that moment, they will have
both the authority and the power
to defend those on earth
who supported them so loyally
during their trials while they were on earth.
No wonder that our text for today
comes from a Watchtower  article with the title
“Armageddon Is Good News!”
Yes, it is good news for all those who serve Jehovah
in heaven and on earth.
Let us now consider our second subject,
the quality of obedience.
Recently, we received a letter from the Personnel Committee
about the subject of obedience.
Speaking about the lessons we have learned during the lockdown,
the letter stated:
“Perhaps the greatest thing we have learned
“is the importance of obedience.
“In this, you dear brothers and sisters
have set an outstanding example.”
That same warm commendation
applies to all faithful brothers and sisters worldwide.
As God’s servants, we are “obedient from the heart,”
as we read at Romans 6:17.
What does that mean?
We are obedient because we love Jehovah.
How have we benefited from the instructions
that we’ve received from Jehovah’s organization?
A married couple in this country said,
“Following the directions we received gave us
peace of mind.”
A sister in the Philippines said,
“Being obedient gives me freeness of speech
when I teach my Bible students and give advice to my friends.”
A brother in Peru said,
“I now feel better prepared to be obedient
to instructions yet to come.”
Well, you will agree that these expressions reflect how we all feel
about the benefits of showing obedience.
Our obedience also influences unbelieving family members.
Here’s an example.
A sister in the United States has been serving Jehovah
for over 45 years.
But during all these years,
her husband did not show interest.
However, during the pandemic, he noticed
the loving care that the congregation was showing to his family.
And out of appreciation, the husband began to attend
the congregation Zoom  meetings.
There he often heard announcements from Bethel
about taking safety measures to avoid getting the virus,
and he could see how obeying that direction
safeguarded the congregation.
Then one day, a non-Witness relative told him,
“Let’s go out together.”
The husband replied,
“I am doing nothing
until Bethel says we can go.”
Imagine how happy the sister was
when she heard her husband’s reply!
Her son said, “My dad is 83 years old,
but there is still hope for him.”
Now, our final question,
What is the link between Armageddon and obedience?
Now, James 3:17 helps us to find the answer.
There we read that we need to be “ready to obey.”
Now, the expression “ready to obey”
is a translation of a Greek word that is mentioned only one time
in the entire New World Translation
here at James 3:17.
A person who is “ready to obey”
is quick to change his opinion
when he is presented with facts that correct his thinking.
It is someone who is known for his willingness
to get along with others.
Now, interestingly, in the first century,
the same Greek word was also used
in a military setting.
Bible scholars mentioned that Flavius Josephus,
the Jewish historian,
used that same word to describe
obedient soldiers in the Roman army.
In fact, Josephus wrote that one of the reasons
why the Roman army was so successful
was that the soldiers were well-trained,
ready to obey.
Now, how does that apply to us?
Well, of course, we do not use literal weapons as soldiers do.
Still, there is a similarity between those Roman soldiers in the past
and us today.
We too have to be well-trained
and ready to obey.
Why?
Because the obedience that we develop today
will help us to obey life-saving instructions
that we will receive from God’s organization in the future.
When the nations attack us and the war of Armageddon follows,
showing obedience will be our protection.
So, what were the main points of our brief discussion?
Shortly before Armageddon,
we will face the attack of a coalition of nations.
Today’s circumstances
allow us to train ourselves in being obedient.
And as Armageddon comes closer,
we will be protected
as long as we are “ready to obey.”

cn.text: 今天的经文和《守望台》的评论
强调了两个要点
第一，一个非常重要的事件
第二，一个非常重要的特质
这个事件就是哈米吉多顿
而这个特质就是服从
接下来我们会一起讨论几个问题
哈米吉多顿来临之前会发生什么？
服从这个特质会为我们带来哪些益处？
以及哈米吉多顿跟服从之间有什么关系？
接下来我们讨论一下哈米吉多顿大战
首先请大家想一想
在哈米吉多顿大战爆发前不久
世上会发生哪些大事呢？
《正确崇拜》这本书的18章这样解释
在所有错误的宗教组织都被毁灭之后
耶和华上帝可能会吩咐他全世界的子民
宣布一个严厉的最终审判信息
这个信息可能是宣告
这个世界的政治制度，不久就会瓦解
可以想象得到
列国的统治者绝不会喜欢听到这个信息
以西结书的38章描述玛歌革地区的歌革
也就是刚才提到的那些统治者会攻击我们
因为上帝的子民分布在世界各个国家和地区
所以这些统治者为了在同一时间攻击我们
就需要跨越国界，一起联手发动攻击
也就是说他们会聚集起来
集结他们的兵力
正因为如此
我们近期的出版物把玛歌革地区的歌革
描述为集结起来或联合起来的列国
哪些上帝的子民会被玛歌革地区的歌革攻击呢？
到时地上还会有受神圣力量任命的基督徒
并且也遭到攻击吗？
《守望台》2015年7月15日刊19页16段指出
14万4000个受神圣力量任命的基督徒
当中余下的人到天上之前
歌革会攻击上帝的子民
所以根据这篇文章
受神圣力量任命的基督徒还在地上的时候
列国就会攻击我们
那么，什么经文支持这个说法呢？
我们可以一起看看以西结书38:16
谈到玛歌革地区的歌革，预言指出
“你会来攻击我的子民以色列人
像密云覆盖地面一样”
长期以来，我们的出版物都指出
这里说的以色列指的是“上帝的以色列”
当联合起来的列国攻击我们的时候
上帝的以色列当中余下的人
包括中央长老团的弟兄们会跟我们在一起
当联合起来的列国
对我们发起猛烈攻击的最初阶段
有这些忠贞的弟兄在我们身边
这一定会让我们获得更多的内心安宁
也帮助我们获得力量渡过这个阶段的考验
不过
在玛歌革地区的歌革发动攻击的某个阶段
耶稣会派他的天使
集结全球范围内上帝的以色列当中余下的人
把他们召集到天上
对于我们还在地上的基督徒来说
这会是一个很大的变化
我们会面对仇敌
但身边不再有受神圣力量任命的弟兄
不过，虽然如此，根据路加福音21:28
我们仍然能够“挺身昂首”
我们为什么不会害怕呢？
因为我们知道这些弟兄被召集到天上
就意味着我们的拯救已经近在眼前了
耶稣、天使和14万4000个耶稣的弟兄
会组成一支强大的天军
拯救我们脱离联合起来的列国的攻击
现在请想一想，这些到天上作王的人
在拯救我们的时候会怀有怎样的感情？
他们当中的很多人都跟我们建立了深厚的友谊
我们有机会跟他们当中的一些人在伯特利工作
或者在会众里并肩服务，全力支持他们
你能想象他们跟耶稣一起来拯救我们的时候
会有多么开心吗！
到那时，他们既有权力又有能力
保护我们这些在地上的人
因为当他们在地上遇到考验时
我们一直忠贞地支持他们
难怪，今天的经文所引自的《守望台》文章
题目为《哈米吉多顿是个好消息》
无论你是在地上还是在天上崇拜耶和华
这都是个好消息
接下来我们讨论第二个要点，服从的特质
最近我们从中央长老团的人事委员会
收到一封信，内容就是关于服从
这封信谈到
我们在封锁期间学到的一些重要道理
信中说
“最宝贵的经验也许是我们学到服从十分重要
亲爱的弟兄姐妹，你们在这方面做得非常好
树立了杰出的榜样”
其实这句称赞的话
也是对全世界忠心的弟兄姐妹说的
作为上帝的仆人，我们表现“衷心服从”
就像罗马书6:17说的那样
意思就是我们服从是因为我们爱耶和华
那么我们会怎样
从来自耶和华组织的指引获得益处呢？
一对美国的夫妻这样说
“我们按照耶和华组织的指引去做
就获得内心安宁”
菲律宾的一个姐妹说
“因为我服从组织的指引
所以就能在教导圣经学生
和给弟兄姐妹建议的时候放胆发言”
一个来自秘鲁的弟兄说
“我现在受到的训练能帮助我
在将来也乐意服从组织的指引”
相信大家都同意
这些弟兄姐妹的话也道出了我们的心声
就是服从能带来很多益处
我们乐意服从
这也会对我们未信的家人产生良好的影响
一个经历是
有一位来自美国的姐妹
她已经崇拜耶和华超过45年了
但在这么长的时间内
她的丈夫都没有对真理产生兴趣
但是在疫情期间
他留意到会众对他的全家

所以出于感谢
这位姐妹的丈夫也开始参加我们的线上聚会了
在聚会时，他常常听到来自伯特利的宣布
关于怎样在疫情期间避免受到感染
他也看出服从这个指引
怎样保护全会众的人

这位丈夫对他说

你能想象
姐妹听到她丈夫这么说时有多么开心吗？
姐妹的儿子说
“我的爸爸已经83岁了，但是他还有希望”
现在我们讨论最后一个问题
哈米吉多顿和服从之间有什么关系？
雅各书的3:17帮助我们找到答案
这节经文鼓励我们要“乐意服从”
请留意被翻译成“乐意服从”的希腊语词
在整本圣经中只出现这一次
就是在雅各书的3:17
一个“乐意服从”的人
一旦看出有证据表明他的想法需要调整
他就会很快作出改变
这样的人也乐意跟别人和睦相处
有意思的是
在公元1世纪当人们谈论军队的时候

一些圣经学者指出
犹太历史学家约瑟夫斯在描述
罗马军队乐意服从的士兵时
就使用了同一个词
约瑟夫斯在书中记述
罗马军队强大的一个原因是
士兵们都训练有素，而且乐意服从
我们能学到什么呢？

但是我们跟这些古代的罗马士兵之间
还是有一个相似点
没错，我们也需要训练有素以及乐意服从
为什么呢？
因为如果我们今天培养服从的特质
就能在将来
更容易服从来自耶和华组织的指引
而这样做会拯救我们的生命
当列国对我们发动攻击
并引发哈米吉多顿大战的时候
表现服从会保护我们
最后总结一下今天演讲的几个要点
哈米吉多顿大战爆发前不久
我们会面对联合起来的列国的攻击
今天的情况让我们在服从方面得到很好的训练
将来当哈米吉多顿大战临近的时候
只要我们乐意服从，就一定会得到保护

How sad.
Now, this far into the great tribulation.

en.text: An introduction to the book of Judges.
The book of Judges was written by the prophet Samuel,
who completed it in about 1100 B.C.E.
Judges covers a period of some 330 years,
from about 1450 to approximately 1120 B.C.E.
The book primarily discusses the exploits of the judges,
whom Jehovah used to deliver his people from oppression.
In chapter 1,
we read that the Israelites do not drive out
all the pagan inhabitants of the land.
Instead, they subject some of them to forced labor.
In chapter 2,
an angel warns the Israelites
that because they have not listened to Jehovah,
the remaining people of the land
will ensnare them in false worship.
In chapters 3 to 16,
we see that the angel’s words begin to be fulfilled
after the death of Joshua and his generation.
In an often repeated cycle,
the Israelites take up false worship;
Jehovah abandons them to their foes;
the people cry out for help;
and Jehovah raises up judges to deliver them.
The 12 judges are
Othniel, Ehud, Shamgar, Barak,
Gideon, Tola, Jair, Jephthah,
Ibzan, Elon, Abdon, and Samson.
Did you know?
The judges described in this book
were men of faith who led and delivered God’s people,
recognizing Jehovah as the true Leader and Deliverer.
They were not judges in the legal sense of the word.
In chapter 3,
Judges Othniel and Ehud deliver the Israelites
from servitude to the kings of Mesopotamia and Moab.
In chapter 4, a prophetess named Deborah
sends for a man of faith named Barak.
She tells him that Jehovah
will grant him victory over Sisera,
the chief of the army of Canaanite King Jabin,
who is oppressing Israel.
Jehovah gives Sisera’s entire army
into the hands of Barak.
Not so much as one man remains.
Sisera himself is executed by a woman named Jael.
In chapters 6 to 8,
Jehovah uses Judge Gideon and just 300 men
to take the lead in delivering Israel
from Midianite oppression.
Chapters 11 and 12 discuss the exploits
of Judge Jephthah.
With Jehovah’s help,
he subdues the Ammonites who, along with the Philistines,
had oppressed Israel for 18 years.
Chapters 13 to 16 describe the exploits
of Judge Samson,
a Nazirite to whom Jehovah gives
extraordinary physical strength.
Samson takes “the lead in saving Israel
out of the hand of the Philistines.”
The events in chapters 17 to 21
fit an earlier period of time.
In chapter 17,
a man in Ephraim named Micah,
who has “a house of gods,”
hires a young Levite named Jonathan
to serve as his priest.
Jonathan, however, is not of the priestly family.
In chapter 18,
hundreds of Danites who are on their way
to conquer land for their tribe
make a stop at Micah’s house.
They steal his gods
and take Jonathan to be their priest.
In chapters 19 and 20,
men of the Benjaminite city of Gibeah
commit sex crimes against the concubine of a Levite.
The Benjaminites fail to hand over the guilty men,
so the other tribes war against Benjamin,
almost wiping out the tribe.
As you read the book of Judges,
note the harm that can come
to those who leave Jehovah,
observe how merciful God is
when his people repent
and cry out to him for help,
and see why we can trust Jehovah
—our Great Judge—
to deliver us from all our enemies
by means of his Kingdom.

cn.text: 士师记是由先知撒母耳执笔写的
成书时间是公元前1100年左右
士师记涵盖的时间大约330年
从公元前1450年左右
到公元前1120年左右
士师记主要讲述
耶和华任用一些人来拯救他的子民
脱离敌人的压迫
这些人称为士师
在第1章
以色列人并没有把所有异教居民都赶走
以色列人强迫其中一些人服劳役
在第2章
天使警告以色列人
由于他们没有听从耶和华的吩咐
剩余的异教居民将会引诱他们崇拜假神
在第3到16章
约书亚和那一代人去世之后
天使警告的事果然发生了
以色列人每次崇拜假神
耶和华就会将他们交在敌人手里
每当以色列人向耶和华求救的时候
耶和华就会兴起士师拯救他们
上帝兴起的十二士师分别是俄陀聂
以户
珊迦
巴拉
基甸
陀拉
崖珥
耶弗他
以比赞
以伦
押顿和参孙
你知道吗？
士师记提到的士师都是对上帝很有信心的人
上帝也任用他们拯救他的子民
脱离敌人的压迫
士师们将耶和华视为拯救者
以及真正的领袖
第3章记载了俄陀聂和以户
怎样从美索不达米亚王
和摩押王手中拯救以色列人
第4章
女先知底波拉派人去请巴拉来
巴拉对上帝有信心
底波拉告诉巴拉
耶和华会帮助他打败西西拉
也就是迦南王耶宾的元帅
让以色列人摆脱耶宾的压迫
耶和华让西西拉的军队败在巴拉手中
西西拉的所有军兵都死了
一个也不剩
西西拉则被一个叫雅亿的女子杀了
第6到8章
耶和华任用基甸和300名勇士
拯救以色列人摆脱米甸人的压迫
第11和12章讲述了耶弗他的事迹
有18年的时间
以色列人被亚扪人和非利士人压迫
靠着耶和华的帮助
耶弗他打败了亚扪人
第13到第16章讲述了参孙的事迹
参孙是一名离俗人
耶和华赐给他异于常人的力气
参孙“带头拯救以色列人脱离非利士人的压迫”
第17到21章描述的事件
发生在参孙做士师之前
在第17章
在以法莲有一个人叫米迦
他有一个用来拜神的屋子
他请了利未部族的年轻人约拿单做祭司
不过约拿单不属于亚伦家族
在第18章
几百个但部族的男子在寻找土地的过程中
经过米迦的家
他们拿走了他家里的神像
还说服约拿单做他们的祭司
第19和20章
住在基比亚的便雅悯族人
强奸了一个利未族人的妾
便雅悯部族的人不愿意将那些恶棍交出来
于是以色列其他部族跟他们交战
差点将他们灭族
你阅读士师记的时候，请留意
离弃耶和华的人会有什么下场
上帝的子民悔改向他求救的时候
上帝会表现怜恤之心
我们也可以相信伟大的领袖耶和华
会通过他的王国，战胜敌人
拯救我们！

title: 로버트 루시오니: 여러분은 여호와께 “기꺼이 받아들여질” 것입니다

ko.text: 우린 여호와를 사랑하고 그분께 가장 좋은 걸 드리길 원하죠.
또 우리의 희생이 그분께 받아들여지기를 원합니다.
그래서 우리는 조직에서 진행되는 모든 활동에
가능한 많이 참여하기 위해 노력할지 모릅니다.
낙담하거나 심지어 죄책감이나 좌절감을 느낀 적이 있으신가요?
어떤 경우에는 여러 가지 신권 활동을 하느라 너무나 바쁜 나머지
