en.text: It was when my husband was really opposed.
One night, he put a knife to his stomach
and said, “Will you choose me or the truth?”
My husband was cooperative.
He would wave goodbye
as we went to the meetings,
but he wasn’t interested at all.
I felt really jealous
when I saw families sitting together at assemblies.
Because of work
and taking care of his mother,
my husband gradually started missing meetings.
Some in our congregation, with good intentions,
pointed it out to him.
But the way they did this
made him feel misunderstood
and discouraged,
and he put the Bible and the publications away.
I also had times when I wanted
to drift away with him.
I was really happy when I learned the truth.
In my zeal, I bombarded my husband with information,
and that made him worry that I had turned into a fanatic.
I think he was genuinely concerned for his family
and thought that I had joined a weird religion.
One family in the congregation
often invited us to meals
and outdoor activities.
I think my husband appreciated
those small acts of kindness.
I also tried to show that I appreciated him
through my speech and conduct.
When my children and I applied
what we learned in our lives,
I think he gradually became interested in the truth.
The words “safeguard your heart”
caught my eye.
I decided to try and keep my heart
and my children’s hearts
toward Jehovah.
When I went out in the ministry
with my children,
I would point out various aspects
of God’s creation around us.
And before my husband
would come home from work,
I made it a habit to teach them God’s Word.
I made a conscious effort
to see myself in Paradise with my husband.
This strengthened my resolve
to never leave the truth.
I wrote caring notes to my husband
when I went to the meetings.
I was convinced that he would come back one day,
and he did come back.
I did not leave Jehovah,
and so Jehovah never abandoned me.
My husband never embraced the truth.
However, right now all five
of my children are in the truth,
and I feel really blessed.
Being able to serve Jehovah as a family
along with my husband
—the joy and appreciation
just keep welling up.

en.text: It felt like a bad dream.
Our family was really zealous in the truth.
We were playing downstairs one day,
and Mom came down to tell us
she was leaving Jehovah and leaving Dad.
Saying goodbye to Mom, that was the hardest day of my life.
My mother and father became inactive
when I was about four years old.
My father was never really around.
When my mom started to learn the truth,
my dad said she was forbidden from studying.
If we were to go to the meetings, he would take us out forcibly.
He became verbally and physically abusive to my mom.
My parents’ breakup was very tough.
It was a struggle for my mother to raise two boys on her own.
She would work two or three jobs,
and serving Jehovah just took a backseat.
When my parents divorced, my mom was very depressed.
She did the best she could,
but Jehovah didn’t intend for mothers to fill both roles
as parents.
My sisters and I, we made a conscious choice
that we weren’t going to make the same bad choices that Mom did.
We realized that it was up to us.
So I dedicated my life to Jehovah
and was baptized when I was 15.
We thrived spiritually when we didn’t have the opposition from Dad.
Now we could go out in service, go to the meetings freely.
We didn’t have to hide our literature for fear he would rip them up.
When I was around 15 years old,
my mother took us to the meeting,
and she was determined that this was going to be her last meeting.
It was the night of a local needs part.
It was the right time.
Jehovah just opened my mother’s heart wide.
After that experience,
it was like she was a new woman.
My sisters and I have always been a team.
We pioneered together; we moved to Cambodia
to serve as need-greaters together.
They’re both in special full-time service
with their husbands in Cambodia,
and I’ve been serving here in Myanmar Bethel, along with my husband,
for just over 11 years now.
My mom set a stellar example for me to follow.
Her relationship with Jehovah was always above everything else.
It was her example that helped me
to set and reach spiritual goals.
I started pioneering during my senior year of high school.
In nearly 20 years of full-time service,
I’ve spent most of that time at Brooklyn Bethel and Warwick with my wife.
My mother had a very strong influence on my theocratic goals.
My wife and I had the privilege of attending the first School for Kingdom Evangelizers,
and currently we’re serving in the circuit work.
No one needs to be defined by their negative circumstances.
First Peter 5:10 says:
‘God himself will complete your training.’
It might be tough at times, but with Jehovah’s help, you can succeed.
It reminds me of what David said in the 27th Psalm and verse 10;
he said: “Even if my . . . father [or] mother abandon me,
Jehovah . . . will take me in.”
That was definitely the case
in my situation.
Jehovah doesn’t define us by our upbringing or our past.
He sees our potential.
So it’s up to us.
With Jehovah, we can be anything we want to be.

titles.ko: 믿음의 훌륭한 싸움을 하는 사람들—독신 그리스도인
titles.en: Successful Fighters for the Faith—Single Christians
titles.cn: 成功为信仰奋战的人——单身的基督徒

title: 믿음을 나타내는 세계 전역의 우리 형제들

ko.text: 불가능해 보이는 일을 할 수 있게 해 주었습니다.
오늘날 많은 사람들도 그러한 믿음을 가지고 있으며
그 믿음은 그들이 어떤 어려움도 이겨 낼 수 있게 해 줍니다.
믿음으로 어려움을 극복한 사람들 자신의 이야기뿐 아니라
가까운 사람들의 이야기도 듣게 되실 것입니다.
서로 대조가 되는 모습이 공존하는 나라입니다.
많은 사람들이 왕국회관 건축 공사에 참여할
남라라는 젊은 자매가 그런 믿음을 나타냈죠.
남라가 믿음을 나타내어 건축 봉사에 참여하고
이 봉사에서 기쁨을 유지하는 걸 보면서
나중에 돈을 많이 버는 직업을 갖는 거였죠.
회중에서 왕국회관 건축 공사가 한창 진행 중이었기 때문에
저도 가끔 가서 일을 돕곤 했어요.
형제들이 왕국회관 건축 공사에 참여하면서 느끼는 기쁨을
제가 왕국회관 건축 공사에 참여하러 간다고 했을 때
건축 현장에서 제가 한 일들은 다 처음 해 보는 일들이었어요.
전 기술도 없었고 그런 일 해 본 경험도 전혀 없었죠.
정신적으로도 지치고 몸도 완전히 녹초가 되었죠.
남라는 영적으로 균형을 잡을 필요가 있었습니다.
건축 현장에서 열심히 일하는 것도 중요하지만
건축 현장에 가기 전에 먼저 성경을 읽고
읽은 내용에 대해 생각해 보는 습관을 들였습니다.
마음속에 있는 걱정거리들을 다 말씀드릴 수 있으니까요.
여호와께서 저를 돌보아 주신다는 걸 직접 경험할 수 있었습니다.
남라는 전보다 훨씬 더 균형을 잘 잡게 되었습니다.
“공사는 어떻게 되고 있니?” 하고 묻곤 하셨어요.
제가 무슨 일을 하든 그분이 도와주실 거라는 걸 확신할 수 있었습니다.
샤킬도 그런 형제 중 한 사람이죠.
샤킬이 캐나다 베델에서 봉사하도록 초대되었을 때
좋은 목표를 많이 가진 이 젊은 형제가
여호와의 도움으로 그 목표를 하나씩 이루어 나가는 것을 보는 것은
저의 바람은 도와줄 사람이 없는 사람들에게 도움을 베푸는 것입니다.
저를 진심으로 돕는 형제 자매들을 통해
여호와의 성품을 묵상하면 그분을 본받고 싶어집니다.
그분이 나타내신 친절을 나 자신도 나타내고 싶어지죠.
외국어 봉사를 하면 그렇게 할 기회가 많은 것 같아요.
그래서 펀자브어를 배우기 시작했고 후회하지 않습니다.
베델 봉사를 하던 중에 건강 문제가 생겼어요.
어디에 이상이 생겨서 그런 건지 알 수가 없었어요.
그 병 때문에 제 외모도 변해서
아무하고도 만나고 싶지 않을 때가 많았어요.
다른 사람을 영적으로 돕기 위해 외국어 봉사를 시작했는데
제 자신이 겪는 어려움 때문에 그렇게 할 수 없다는 게
저를 비롯해서 샤킬과 가까운 사람들 모두가
그가 나타낸 믿음에 크게 감동을 받았을 겁니다.
그러니까 앞으로도 당연히 저를 도와주실 거라고 생각했죠.
샤킬은 잠을 제대로 잘 수 없었고
장기 부전 같은 큰 문제가 생길 수도 있다고 했습니다.
제가 할 수 있는 일이 없었죠.
샤킬은 계속 영적으로 발전하기 위해 노력했습니다.
제가 처한 상황에 대해 현실적인 시각을 가질 필요가 있었죠.
‘어떻게 하면 이런 상황에서 왕국을 계속 첫째로 구할 수 있을까?
치료법은 있는지 알아보면서 어떻게 그렇게 할 수 있을까?’
결국 샤킬은 외국어 봉사를 계속하기로 결정했습니다.
제가 샤킬을 보면서 본받아야겠다고 생각한 점은
샤킬이 성경 내용을 자신에게 적용하려고 노력했다는 점이에요.
그 속에 나오는 인물이 자기 자신이라고 생각하며 묵상하곤 했죠.
그렇게 한 결과 해결책이 보이지 않을 때에도
여호와께서 자신을 도와주실 거라고 확신할 수 있었습니다.
현재 그는 아내와 함께 펀자브어 구역에서 봉사하고 있습니다.
사랑 많은 장로이자 펀자브어 학습반 강사로 일하고 있죠.
좋은 직업을 가지면 안정된 삶을 살 수 있다고 생각하죠.
형제 자매들도 그러한 생각에 영향을 받아서
여호와를 위해 더 많은 일을 하기를 주저하게 될 수 있습니다.
자트미코 형제 부부는 파이오니아 봉사를 목표로 하고 있었습니다.
부부가 파이오니아를 시작했을 때 제가 물었죠.
이미 많은 일을 하고 있는 거라고 생각했죠.
저는 왕국 전파자 학교에 가 보는 게 어떻겠냐고 말해 주었습니다.
전파자 학교에 가는 건 한 번도 생각해 본 적이 없었어요.
여호와께서는 회중 형제 자매들을 통해 제 기도에 응답해 주셨어요.
자트미코 자매는 좋은 직장에 다니고 있었습니다.
자매가 그 분야에서 추가 교육을 받을 수 있도록 지원해 주겠다고 제의하기까지 했죠.
형제 자매들은 아내가 그런 직장에 다니는 것에 대해
여호와를 더 온전히 섬길 때 기쁨이 얼마나 큰지 직접 보여 줬죠.
아직 결정을 내리지 못하고 있을 때
영적 목표가 있는지, 그 목표가 무엇인지 물어봤어요.
그 질문들에 대해 곰곰이 생각해 보면서
그들은 직장을 그만두고 살던 도시와 집도 떠나야 했어요.
편안한 삶을 뒤로하고 작은 회중에서 섬기게 되었습니다.
여호와 하느님의 인도를 구하는 기도를 이전보다 더 많이 해야 했죠.
현재 이 부부는 여행하는 활동을 하면서 순회구를 돌보고 있습니다.
우리 부부가 대단한 사람들이어서 이 임명을 수행하고 있는 것이 아닙니다.
여호와께서 도와주시기 때문에 가능한 일이라고 생각합니다.
그분은 우리를 여러 가지 방법으로 사용하실 수 있습니다.
하지만 많은 사람들이 가난에 시달리고 있죠.
바카타 자매도 그러한 어려움을 겪는 사람들 중에 한 명입니다.
남편이 맹그로브 숲에서 저를 부르는 소리가 들렸어요.
얼른 소리가 나는 쪽으로 가 보았죠.
그때부터 제가 남편이 하던 역할까지 다 해야 했어요.
그 자매에게 청소나 빨래를 해 줄 사람이 필요할 때
사이클론 케니가 카다부섬을 휩쓸었을 때가 생각납니다.
마당에 있던 부엌이 강풍에 날아가 버렸습니다.
형제 자매들의 집이 큰 피해를 입었다는 소식을 듣고
바카타 자매는 정말 놀라운 일을 했습니다.
그런데도 그 돈을 다 형제 자매들에게 주었습니다.
기쁜 마음으로 형제들에게 그 돈을 주었습니다.
형제들을 관대하게 도와줄 수 있다는 점을 배웠습니다.
여호와께서도 저에게 더 많이 갚아 주셨죠.
그래서 우리는 지금까지 부족한 것 없이
생활비를 벌기 위해 열심히 일해야 합니다.
아이들에게 무엇보다 영적인 유산을 물려주고 싶어요.
아이들이 여호와를 잘 섬길 수 있도록 좋은 본을 보여 주고 싶습니다.
여러 동영상을 통해 도움을 받고 있죠.
아모링 형제 부부가 나오는 동영상을 자주 떠올려 봅니다.
그 가족은 영적으로 더 좋은 환경으로 이주했습니다.
자녀들 모두 잘 자라서 여호와를 섬기고 있죠.
‘우리 가족도 그들처럼 도움이 더 필요한 곳으로 가서 봉사할 수 있을까?’
낯선 곳에 간다는 것은 어려운 결정이죠.
영국에서 에콰도르로 이주한 가족에 대한 거였어요.
그 가족이 한 달 동안 답사를 간 것처럼 우리도 답사를 가는 게 좋겠다고 생각했죠.
다른 나라로 가서 봉사를 할 수 있다면 정말 좋고 신나겠지만
도움이 더 필요한 칼랑고라고 하는 구역으로 가 보았습니다.
아이들은 그곳에 펼쳐진 자연환경을 정말 좋아했습니다.
칼랑고에 가면 노는 것도 재밌고 봉사하는 것도 재밌어요.
그 도시의 경제 상황이 좋지 않았기 때문이죠.
그래서 금요일, 토요일, 일요일에는 칼랑고에 가고
다른 날들에는 이곳 파차카막에 있으면서 일을 하기로 했습니다.
그분이 여기에서 일을 할 수 있게 해 주셨으니까요.
주말에는 칼랑고에 있는 형제들과 함께 봉사할 수 있죠.
단순한 생활을 하는 법을 배워야 했어요.
부모님이 열심히 노력하시는 걸 보면 여호와를 정말 사랑하신다는 걸 알 수 있어요.
그런 믿음 덕분에 이 가족은 행동할 수 있었습니다.
우리 웹사이트의 동영상들이 우리에게 필요한 힘을 주었습니다.
러시아 전역에서 우리 형제들은 수십 년 동안 박해와 금지령을 잘 인내해 왔습니다.
지금도 많은 형제 자매들이 그러한 어려움을 겪고 있죠.
그러한 형제 자매들 가운데 부덴추크 형제 가족을 만나 보겠습니다.
그들은 남편을 바닥에 쓰러뜨리고 수갑을 채웠어요.
남편은 미결 구금 시설에 11개월 동안 수감되어 있었죠.
남편이 거기서 무슨 일을 겪을까 하는 생각에 정말 겁이 났습니다.
아이들을 어떻게 돌봐야 할지 걱정이 되었습니다.
혼자서 아이들의 영적, 감정적, 신체적 필요를 돌봐야 했으니까요.
우리 가족이 겪는 불공정한 일에 대해 생각하면 자꾸 감정적이 되었어요.
기도가 그런 마음을 가라앉히는 데 도움이 되었습니다.
재판이 열리는 날엔 형제 자매들이 와 주었어요.
새벽 1시에 우리 집이 완전히 불타 버렸죠.
우리 가족은 집 근처에 서 있었는데
그때 차 여러 대가 우리 집으로 왔어요.
형제 자매들은 따뜻한 차와 음식도 가져왔어요.
불이 난 지 한 달 뒤에 남편 소식을 들었어요.
남편이 교도소에서 교도관들에게 심하게 구타를 당했다는 소식이었죠.
남편을 어떻게 도와야 할지 알 수가 없었으니까요.
타티야나는 정말 용기 있게 시련을 이겨 나가고 있어요.
그러면 여호와께서 저에게 진통제를 놓아 주시는 것 같은 느낌이 들었습니다.
미결 구금 시설에 있을 땐 우리를 위해 매일 편지를 써 주었죠.
그리고 가장 중요한 것으로 믿음이 필요하다는 걸 잊지 말아요.
이 어두운 날들이 지나면 틀림없이 밝은 날이 올 거예요.
이 모든 일을 겪는 동안 저에게 도움이 된 건
성경을 읽고 집회 준비를 하고 봉사에도 참여했죠.
하지만 이번 일로 여호와의 손길을 느끼면서
저와 같은 상황에서도 다른 사람들을 도울 수 있다는 걸 깨달았습니다.
여호와께서 지금까지 우리 가족을 도와주신 것처럼
어려운 상황에서도 믿음과 용기를 나타내는 부덴추크 형제 가족의 본은
우리도 충실을 유지할 수 있다는 걸 보여 줘요.
우리도 낙담하지 않고 계속 여호와를 섬기면서 그분을 기쁘게 해 드릴 수 있죠.
우리 가족은 여호와를 더 신뢰하고 힘든 상황에서도 당황하지 않는 법을 배웠어요.
이번 일을 겪으면서 저는 더 강해졌죠.
전에 가졌던 두려움을 많이 극복할 수 있었고
믿음과 다른 사람들을 도우려는 열망이 더 커졌습니다.
세계 전역의 우리 형제 자매들은 강한 믿음을 계속 나타내 왔습니다.
그 결과 어떤 일을 할 수 있었습니까?
우리 형제 자매들은 신권 건축 임명을 수행하고,
여호와께서는 우리도 그렇게 할 수 있다는 것을 아십니다.
우리가 믿음을 나타내어 여호와를 위해 더 많은 일을 한다면
그 결과 우리의 믿음은 더욱 강해질 것입니다.

en.text: “Through faith they defeated kingdoms,
“brought about righteousness,
“obtained promises,
“stopped the mouths of lions,
“quenched the force of fire,
“escaped the edge of the sword,
“from a weak state were made powerful,
“became mighty in war,
routed invading armies.”
Faith in Jehovah has allowed ordinary people
to do extraordinary things.
This kind of faith is still active today
and still has the power to help us
through any difficulty.
So let’s travel across the globe
and see how deep reliance on Jehovah
has helped many overcome their unique trials.
As we visit each land,
we’ll enjoy a story of faith
shared both from the perspective of close friends
as well as the individuals involved.
Now to our first destination.
South Africa is full of contrasts
and diversity.
Big, modern cities mix with poorer remote areas.
For many volunteers in Kingdom Hall construction,
this presents wonderful opportunities
but also unique challenges that require faith
in Jehovah.
An example of that is our young friend Namhla.
My wife and I really appreciated
the faith she showed
to make herself available
and to keep her joy in her assignment.
I’m the only Jehovah’s Witness in my family.
What my mother desired the most for me
was to grow up,
go to college
and, in time, get a high-paying job.
My congregation was busy building a Kingdom Hall,
so I would sometimes also go to help.
I wanted to see and feel the joy that those brothers were having
building Kingdom Halls.
My mom didn’t like it when she heard
that I was going to help with Kingdom Hall construction.
She felt that I was wasting my time.
When I arrived on-site, everything I did was for the first time.
I didn’t have skills, and I had never done this work before.
It is not easy.
Sometimes I get tired

continue to show strong faith.

time spent in deep meditation,
and seeking His direction in prayer.

served where the need was greater;
and preached despite persecution.

those actions will strengthen our faith.

于是我们决定在星期五、六、日去那边传道
其他时候还是留在帕查卡马克
我们真的体会到耶和华在赐福给我们
让我们可以继续在这里工作
而我们在这里四天赚到的钱
就足够我们去一趟科朗戈了
我们需要学习过简单的生活
jw.org网站的短片
给我们很多实用的建议
我从爸爸妈妈身上看出
他们真的很爱耶和华
他们真的把耶和华上帝看作爸爸
而爸爸总是会帮助自己的孩子
这样的信心激励他们能够采取行动
jw.org网站的短片
好像推了我们一把
让我们有勇气采取行动
搬到更需要传道员的地区
过去几十年，在俄罗斯
我们的弟兄姐妹面对禁令和迫害
像许多家庭一样
布登丘克一家人
现在还在面对这样的迫害
2018年6月12日凌晨5点半
一群武装人员闯进了我的家
他们把我丈夫按在地上
给他戴上手铐
后来，他们没有经过任何审讯
就把他关押了11个月
一想起他的遭遇我就会担心害怕
她真的很不容易，常常哭
我很担心一个人能不能照顾好孩子
在崇拜方面、感情方面
和物质方面照顾好他们
祷告让我保持冷静
因为我们遭遇的这些不公平的事
让我很难保持平静
我丈夫被审讯期间
很多弟兄姐妹都会到场
他们的陪伴真的给我很大力量
法院判我丈夫有罪
他需要在监狱里待三年半的时间
2020年1月，我们家又遭遇另一场灾祸
我们的房子在半夜的时候被烧没了
我们站在那里不知所措
我儿子叶戈尔建议做个祷告
我不记得他在祷告里说了什么
但之后我就非常地镇定
这时，有些车子开过来
原来是我们的弟兄姐妹
他们发现我冻得发抖
就拿来衣服给我穿上
他们还拿了热茶和食物，都是最好的
火灾发生后一个月
我丈夫被押到了监狱里
那里的狱警殴打他
我听到这个消息特别地难受
因为我不知道我丈夫到底怎么样了
也不知道该做些什么
尽管这样，塔季扬娜一直非常勇敢
有时候我整晚向耶和华祷告
耶和华好像给了我止痛药
让我能减轻痛苦
我丈夫阿列克谢一直很努力照顾我们
他在被关押的时候
每天都写信给我们，鼓励我们
我和孩子会一起读
亲爱的，我们现在要努力培养这些特质
忍耐、勇气、冷静
最重要的是信心
我相信冬天过后就会是夏天
黑夜过后就会是白天
过了黑暗的季节
我们肯定会迎来阳光灿烂的日子
在这段艰难的日子里
参与崇拜活动、研读圣经给了我很大力量
我们也为聚会做准备，积极传道
刚开始，我很害怕
但现在的情况让我看出耶和华怎样扶持我
甚至在目前的情况下我还能帮助别人
我们知道耶和华一直在帮助我们
而且他以后也会继续帮助我们
他们一家在迫害下也不屈服
这让我相信人人都能保持忠贞
无论怎样
我们每个人都能一直崇拜耶和华
让他的心欢喜
我学会在考验来到的时候不要害怕
而是要信赖耶和华
之前我也会担心害怕
但经过这些考验后
我能够战胜恐惧
而且我的信心更强了
也更渴望帮助别人
正如刚才所看到的
全球的弟兄姐妹都表现出坚强的信心
他们是怎么做到的呢？
他们常常研读上帝的话语
仔细沉思读到的内容
不断祷告向耶和华寻求指引
这让他们成就了什么事呢？
凭着信心
弟兄们能够参与组织的建筑工程
学习另一种语言
参加王国传福音者训练班
虽然贫困却很慷慨
搬到需要更多传道员的地区服务
在迫害之下也坚持传道
耶和华知道
我们每个人都可以像他们一样
是的，如果我们凭着信心采取行动
我们的信心也会更加坚定

titles.ko: 믿음을 나타내는 세계 전역의 우리 형제들
titles.en: How Our Brothers Are Showing Faith
titles.cn: 世界各地的弟兄姐妹表现信心

title: 믿음으로, 많은 일을 할 수 있는 문으로 들어가십시오

ko.text: 가브리엘이 도움이 더 필요한 곳으로 떠나는 것을 보면서
우리는 봉사의 직무를 확장할 기회를 놓친 게 아닌가 하는 생각이 들었죠.
다음번 순회 방문 때 순회 감독자에게 한번 물어보지 뭐.
새로운 외국어 집단에서 한번 일해 보세요.
우린 한 번도 외국어 봉사를 할 만한 사람들이라고 생각해 본 적이 없었죠.
그런데 순회 감독자 형제는 스가랴 8:23을 보여 주면서
“나라들의 모든 언어에서 나온 사람”들이 여호와에 대해 알 수 있도록
우리가 어떻게 도울 수 있는지 설명해 주었습니다.
외국어를 배우는 게 처음에는 정말 힘들었죠.
하지만 여호와께서 도와주신 덕분에 조금씩 발전하기 시작했습니다.
새로운 집단의 형제 자매들을 알게 돼서 정말 행복했습니다.
네, 우리는 시간을 되돌릴 순 없죠.
우리는 기회를 놓치지 않고 봉사의 직무를 확장하게 된 것을
도움이 더 필요한 곳에서 봉사하는 데
그런데 한번은 회중에 특별 전파 활동에 관한 광고가 있었습니다.
새뮤얼이 저한테 와서 같이 지원해 보자고 했죠.
어, 사실 난 별로 관심이 없어.
혹시나 해서 네 지원서도 갖고 왔어. 다시 생각해 봐!
열심히 해야 한다는 건 알고 있었지만 지금이 편했어요.
전 제 방식대로 사는 게 좋거든요.
그리고 새로운 걸 시작하는 게 좀 두려웠어요.
제 마음을 검토해 볼 필요가 있었죠.
히브리 11:8에 나오는 아브라함의 믿음에 관한 내용이
누가 여호와보다 제 삶을 더 잘 이끌어 줄 수 있겠어요?
기회의 문이 열려 있었고 저는 그리로 들어가기만 하면 됐죠.
전과는 달리 새로운 걸 많이 시도해 보게 됐어요.
봉사에 대한 생각이 달라졌고 더 많은 일을 하고 싶어 졌죠.
장로 형제들을 통해 지부 사무실에 편지를 썼어요.
지부 사무실에서는 몇 군데를 추천해 주었고
저는 기도하고 조사해 본 다음 어디로 갈지 결정했습니다.
그곳에서의 삶이 어떨지 잘 몰랐지만 정말 기대가 됐습니다!
친한 형제 자매들과 헤어지는 건 아쉬웠죠.
하지만 여호와께서 저를 위해 준비해 놓으신 축복들을 생각하며
지역 대회 때 왕국 전파자 학교 지원자를 위한 모임이 있었어요.
안톤 형제가 저에게 같이 가지 않겠냐고 물어보았죠.
좋아. 그럼 내가 가서 뭐 좀 가져올게.
모임에 참석하긴 했지만 그리 내키진 않았어요.
전 이미 임명을 받아 즐겁게 봉사하고 있었으니까요.
전파자 학교에 가는 게 얼마나 큰 특권인지 잘 몰랐죠.
그런데 순회 감독자에게 몇 가지 질문을 하고 대답을 듣고 나니까
꼭 가 보고 싶다는 생각이 들었죠.
왜 여태 지원서를 안 낸 거야?
여호와께서 절 여기로 인도하신 것 같고, 지금 정말 행복하거든요.
그런데 또 새로운 기회의 문이 있다고 하니까
지금까지 많은 일을 했어도 새로운 일을 하기가 두려울 수 있지.
때론 여호와께서 우리를 올바른 길로 인도하고 계시다는 확신이 필요해.
읽어 보고 여호와께서 널 얼마나 많이 도와주셨는지 생각해 봐.
“내게 능력을 주시는 분으로 인해 내게는 모든 일을 할 힘이 있습니다.”
둘 다 똑같다니까요. 전부 다 가지고 가려고 하는 거.
몇 번 쓰긴 했는데 여행할 때 꽤 유용할 거예요.
네. 또 모르잖아요. 두 분한테 조만간 필요할지.
곧 있을 건축 프로젝트에 몇 주 간 초대되었을 때
하지만 지금 다니고 있는 직장을 생각하니 걱정이 되기 시작했죠.
회사에 이야기할 용기를 달라고 여호와께 계속 기도했습니다.
우선 이렇게 시간 내 주셔서 감사합니다.
일 년 중 제일 바쁜 시기에?
그치만 돌아와서도 계속 일할 수 있을 거란 보장은 못 해요.
갑자기 이 소중한 특권이 무거운 짐처럼 느껴졌어요.
이 특권을 받아들이면 제 삶이 더 힘들어지지 않을까요?
느헤미야 시대의 이스라엘 백성에 관한 기록을 읽어 봤어요.
그 일에 마음을 쏟아 예루살렘 성벽을 재건했습니다.
저도 그들처럼 마음을 쏟아 여호와를 섬길 기회를 놓치고 싶지 않았어요.
여호와께서 제 결정을 축복해 주실 거라는
건축 봉사가 끝나고 나면 어떻게 될지 알 수 없지만
분명 여호와께서 저를 돌봐 주실 거예요.
바로 지금, 저는 여호와의 일에 제 마음을 쏟을 겁니다.
우리는 도와 달라는 요청에 즉시 응했습니다.
어려움에 처한 형제 자매들을 보니까 정말 마음이 아팠습니다.
하지만 우린 그 지역 형제 자매들이 나타낸 태도에 큰 감동을 받았습니다.
집으로 돌아온 아내와 나는 그들을 본받아야겠다고 결심했습니다.
조직에서 수행하는 역할에 대해 감사했던 우리는
우선 우리가 세계적인 활동에 얼마나 헌금하는지 검토해 보았습니다.
이 정도는 헌금할 수 있을 것 같아요. 그쵸?
우린 가까이 있는 사람들에게 관대함을 나타내기 위해 노력했습니다.
우리는 사람들에게 더 많이 줄 수 있는 입장이었습니다.
그 후 우리 회중은 특별 전파 활동에 초대받았습니다.
우리 모두도 자신의 상황에서 최선을 다해야 할 것입니다.
우리가 지금보다 더 많은 일을 할 수 있을까요?
우리는 도울 능력이 있었고, 그래서 실천에 옮겼습니다!

en.text: Oh, honestly, you shouldn’t have.
You’re going to need it.
Gabriel’s leaving to serve where
the need is greater made us feel like we
had missed the chance to expand our ministry.
Why don’t we start now?
We’re not getting any younger.
Yeah.
We could ask the circuit overseer for advice
on his next visit, but I’m worried he’s going to say
we should . . .
. . . join the new language group.
It’s a big need in our circuit.
We’ve never felt like the right people
to serve in a foreign language.
Brother Lindstrom shared Zechariah 8:23 with us,
which helped us see how we could have a hand
in helping “men out of all the languages of the nations”
learn about Jehovah.
Learning was a struggle at first.
But with Jehovah’s help, we made progress
—slowly.
Yes! You did it!
Even though the language was a challenge,
loving our new family was not.
Oh, um, uhh.
I don’t—I don’t understand.
Say again what you say.
Uhm, uh.
Come.
OK.
Oh, thank—thank you!
It’s true, we aren’t getting any younger.
And that’s why we’re so glad
we took the chance to expand our ministry.
If you had told me two years ago that I’d
be moving to where the need was greater,
I would have laughed.
It all started when they announced a special preaching campaign.
My friend Samuel encouraged me to apply with him.
So, what do you think?
Uh, yeah,
no, but you enjoy that.
I know you’re going to love it.
That’s why I got you a form as well, all right?
We can do this!
OK.
I knew I could do more, but I was comfortable.
I like doing things on my own terms.
But really, I was afraid of the unknown.
I needed to examine my heart.
When I read about Abraham’s faith at Hebrews 11:8,
it’s like the words jumped off the page.
“He went out although
not knowing where he was going.”
Who better to be in control of my life than Jehovah?
A door was opened to me.
I just needed to go through it.
And what I experienced changed my life.
Let’s do it, man.
The results of the campaign were incredible!
And the experience pushed me out of my comfort zone.
All right, Gabriel is going to try some food.
Try, try, try!
Go on, go on, give it a try, Gabriel!
It’s good, yeah—really good!
I saw the ministry in a new way, and I wanted to do more.
So I calculated the cost
and worked
with my local elders to write to the branch office.
When I heard back with some suggestions,
I prayed about it and did research before choosing.
There were many unknowns,
but I couldn’t wait!
It was hard to say goodbye to my friends,
but I was ready for whatever Jehovah had in store for me.
At our convention, they had the meeting for the School for Kingdom Evangelizers.
My friend Anton asked if I was going to go.
Hi, Gabriel.
Oh, hi, Anton.
Are you coming?
Uh, to what?
The SKE meeting.
Oh, uh, no.
I wasn’t planning on it,
but all right, yeah, sure.
I’ll go.
OK, then, and afterward, I can . . .
I went, but I felt conflicted.
I thought,
‘I already have an assignment, one that I love.’
But I didn’t fully understand the incredible privilege of attending SKE.
I asked the circuit overseer a few more questions.
And it felt like, this is it!
It seemed right, and all I had to do was apply online.
But that was months ago.
So, what’s holding you back?
I feel like Jehovah led me here,
and I’ve never been happier.
But now another door has opened, and the fear is back.
It doesn’t matter how far you’ve come.
Fear of the unknown can be overwhelming.
Sometimes you need a reminder that Jehovah
is leading you in the right direction.
Here’s one to keep in mind
—Philippians 4:13.
Read it, and just think about how far Jehovah has taken you.
“For all things I have the strength
through the one who gives me power.”
Jehovah is in control.
What was I so afraid of?
I’m bringing too much.
Well, SKE is for two months.
Oh, you’re just alike you two,
bringing every last thing with you.
Can I—can I leave this with you?
It’s been on a few adventures, but it’s still great for traveling.
Really?
Yeah, please.
Who knows, you might need it sometime soon.
Hi, darling, we’re back.
When I learned that I was invited
to work for a few weeks on the upcoming construction project,
I was thrilled.
But that excitement quickly turned into anxiety
because of what I had to do.
I prayed to Jehovah for weeks to give me the strength
to have the conversation with my employer.
All right, Sarah, come in!
So?
I wanted to, first of all, say thank you
for taking the time to meet with me, . . .
I began to explain about the construction project
and how I had been invited to volunteer.
. . . and I would really like the time to . . .
So you want time off
during the busiest time of our year?
Well, yes, but . . .
It’s your choice, but under no circumstances will I hold your position.
Suddenly, this beautiful privilege felt like a huge risk.
Was I making my life more complicated by doing this?
I read the account about the people in Nehemiah’s day.
Their willing spirit demonstrated faith,
and Jerusalem’s walls were built by people
who “put their heart into the work.”
I didn’t want to miss out
on the opportunity to serve Jehovah in that way.
This is my resignation letter.
I had to have faith that Jehovah would bless my decision.
I’m not sure what the future holds when I get back,
but I know Jehovah will take care of me.
For now, I’m going to focus
on putting my heart into the work.
When a disaster struck in the north of the country,
we immediately answered the call for help.
Seeing our brothers and sisters in need was heartbreaking.
But what really touched our heart was the spirit
of the local brothers and sisters.
They were like the Macedonians.
They didn’t have much, but they gave generously from the heart.
When we got home,
Madeline and I resolved to show the same kind of spirit.
First, our appreciation led us
to review our contribution to the worldwide work.
I’ve come up with this figure.
Is this right?
Yeah.
Let’s just thank Jehovah.
We looked for ways to be generous
to those around us.
We discovered that we had
the means to give more, so we didn’t hold back.
And then, our congregation was invited to help
with a special preaching campaign.
. . . reach as many as possible with the good news.
Do you think we could do a bit more?
Could we push ourselves a bit further?
I’d really like to.
It was within our power to help,
and that’s exactly what we did!
I’m bringing too much?
No, of course not.

en.text: When I was in my 40’s, I was divorced,
I had three younger kids at home,
I was working three jobs,
and I had drifted away from the congregation.
I had an acquaintance who was telling me
that I was in a cult
and that I needed to look
at some information that he had.
When I was about 30 years old,
a fellow employee saw
that I was one of Jehovah’s Witnesses
and was trying to access jw.org.
He told me about someone he knew in another country
who could prove to me that Jehovah’s Witnesses
didn’t have the truth.
That made me curious,
and little by little, I was persuaded to look
at apostate material.
I was born and raised in the truth,
chose to dedicate myself to Jehovah
at the age of 16,
but I began to associate with people
who had either formerly been associated
with the truth
or were very loosely associated with Jehovah and his organization,
and that’s really where the apostasy began to take root.
As I was reading this literature,
I saw through it to an extent,
but when you’re drifting away,
you’re looking for a reason not to believe.
I began to feed my mind
with different philosophies, different ideas.
I even studied different religions.
And, you know, I told myself that I was doing that academically,
but it started to influence the way
that I thought and felt about things.
Eventually, the elders reached out to me.
I was very combative with those brothers.
I even made the accusation that Noah’s ark was
a fairy tale, that it was part of mythology.
Those apostate doubts that I was reading
kept going deeper and deeper into my heart.
I stopped reading the publications,
I stopped going to the meetings,
and as a result, my spiritual routine was dead.
So I thought I’d try to find truth elsewhere.
And I looked for something out there that was
in accord with what I knew the Bible taught.
But I couldn’t find anything.
One Sunday morning, I rode by the Kingdom Hall,
and I said to myself,
‘Oh, they’re all in there waiting for Armageddon.’
Immediately when I thought that thought,
I said to myself:
‘Well, at least they feel good about themselves.
How do you feel?’
And the answer was I felt terrible.
Eventually, by skillful use of the Scriptures and just reasoning with me,
the elders got me to realize
that I had been ‘carried off’
or that I had been ‘taken captive’ by human philosophy,
by the deceptions
and the empty reasoning of men.
I actually said a prayer; I supplicated Jehovah
that he would really show me the way to the truth.
And he took away
this feeling of emptiness, spiritually speaking.
I realized that a relationship with Jehovah
—that’s our most precious possession.
I had to get back.
I started to study the Bible with sincerity.
I wanted it to affect my mind and my heart,
and I wanted it to effect change in my behavior.
Now as I did that, I felt Jehovah blessing those efforts.
He began to help me to rebuild that relationship with him.
So I began to use Jehovah’s name.
Speaking about Jehovah became a wonderful joy
and a great pleasure to me.
And the result was that my ministry was very productive.
And it’s an amazing joy
to be able to help someone come to love Jehovah.
I was just so happy
to be back under Jehovah’s wings
and have that peace of mind.
How loving Jehovah is!
He wants to help us.
And what better helper could we have?
He’s the best in the universe.

en.text: Life in Ur was comfortable.
We had all the modern conveniences.
Then Jehovah gave us an assignment we never expected
—one that meant saying goodbye to the life we loved.
But rather than look behind,
Abraham and I looked ahead.
We had seen Jehovah’s hand in our lives,
and we knew he would be with us
every step of the journey.
And he was in ways that surprised us
—ways we never could have imagined.
Jehovah did more than help us;
he fulfilled his every promise.
Saying goodbye
is never easy.
And even though we were excited about our new LDC assignment,
it was going to take us farther than we’d ever been.
It wasn’t just a new routine;
it was a whole new way of life!
With each new move and project,
we thought about Sarah.
She focused on the good things ahead
and not on what she’d left behind.
And that’s what we tried to do.
Jehovah has been so good to us.
We didn’t always know where the next project would take us,
but we did know that Jehovah would be with us
every step of the way.
Jericho was doomed.
People were scared.
When the Israelite men showed up at my door,
there was barely time to think.
But I knew what was at stake.
Even as a young girl, I had heard all the stories.

때때로 제가 가진 질문에 대한 답을
어디에서도 찾을 수 없을 거란 생각이 들었죠.
그런데 제 질문에 모두 논리적으로 대답해 주었어요.
하지만 여호와의 증인의 집회에 참석해 보니까
서로 평화롭게 지낼 수 있다는 걸 깨달았죠.
그것이 바로 제가 그토록 찾던 거였어요.
그래서 저도 성서 연구를 하기로 했습니다.
여호와께서 우리 한 사람 한 사람을

en.text: Fear and war were normal in my home country.
I had many questions:
Why do young people have to die?
Why do my children have to go through this?
God did not create us to make war.
The priests in my church always said,
“It is God’s will.”
Being on the run was dreadful.
More than once, I thought we were going to die.
Eventually, we arrived in Germany,
and I was convinced that the priests there could give me some answers.
I went to several different churches
—but no answers.
I kept telling them: “I’m looking for something.
I don’t know what it is, but I didn’t find it here with you.”
Sometimes I thought I was searching for something
that no one could give me.
One day,
a German woman approached me, speaking in Arabic.
That was amazing for me.
I never had a good opinion of Jehovah’s Witnesses.
I didn’t think I could learn anything from her,
but I gave her a chance.
She gave me logical answers to all of my questions.
In my home country, there are multiple religious groups and nationalities
who hate and fight each other.
But at the meetings of Jehovah’s Witnesses,
I have seen that all people can live in peace with each other
if they get to know our Father in heaven.
He gives love and peace.
At last, I found what I had been looking for.
I lived a life without rules.
I used to get drunk,
I smoked a lot, and I became a compulsive gambler.
My behavior was a complete disaster.
My wife wanted to separate from me.
It was a horrible time.
My wife started studying the Bible with Jehovah’s Witnesses.
I remember being doubtful
—very doubtful.
But there was one thing that started to make me think.
Both my wife and my children looked more peaceful,
more joyful, happier.
That’s why I even accepted a Bible study.
I came to realize that Jehovah loves each one of us as an individual.
That gave me real hope for the future.
Everything I was studying in the Bible
helped me to understand
that doing Jehovah’s will is in our best interests.
This really helped me to quit my bad habits,
treat my family better,
and show due respect to my wife.
If Jehovah hadn’t searched for me,
if I hadn’t come to know him,
we would no longer be a family.
Today we are, indeed, a happy family,
a united family
—united more than ever.
Only Jehovah could perform such a miracle.

但是在耶和华见证人的王国聚会所里
我看到各种背景的人都能够和平相处
因为他们都认识耶和华
他让人彼此相爱，和平相处
我终于找到了我一直在寻找的东西
我生活放荡不羁
我抽烟
吸毒
而且嗜赌如命
我的生活一团糟
我妻子想离开我
那段时间真是太糟糕了
我妻子开始和耶和华见证人学习圣经
我觉得学习圣经没有用，根本没什么用
但有一件事让我觉得非常地好奇
就是
我的妻子和孩子们都变得越来越温和
越来越快乐
所以，我接受了圣经学习
我慢慢学习到
耶和华爱我们每一个人
这让我对未来充满了希望
我从圣经的真理中还学习到
按耶和华的标准生活
能带来最大的益处
这帮助我能戒掉恶习
善待家人
以尊重的方式对待我的妻子
如果耶和华没有寻找我
如果我没有认识他
我们的家庭早就破裂了
但是现在
我们的家庭非常地幸福
我和妻子比以前更恩爱了
只有耶和华
能够施行这样的奇迹

ko.text: 새 정부를 지지하지 않는 사람들을 체포하고 있습니다.
설마 집에 가서 기도하시려는 건 아니죠?
방법은 모르지만, 꼭 해 주실 거야.
기도해 다오, 내가 믿음을 지킬 수 있게.
인내할 수 있게 힘을 달라고 기도합시다.
우리 가족도 돌봐 주실 거라고 확신했습니다.
제가 연로한 분들을 격려해 드리던 때가 있었죠.
이제는 여호와께 드릴 게 없다는 생각이 들 때도 있어요.
또 하느님 앞에서 자신을 낮추려고 결심한 첫날부터

en.text: It’s still chaos in many parts of the city,
with armed soldiers detaining and arresting
those not pledging support
of the new government.
Are we still going to the meeting tonight?
I wanted to do what was best
for my wife and daughter.
But a few of the elders
have already been arrested.
What if I was arrested?
What would happen to my family?
You’re not going home to pray, are you?
I pray at my window three times a day,
every day.
If I even appear to compromise,
what would they think?
I know Jehovah.
And if I trust him,
he’ll reward me.
I don’t know how,
but he will.
Pray that I keep my faith
—that we all keep our faith—
no matter how this ends.
The Scriptures are clear.
We must continue to meet together,
even in small groups if necessary.
Let’s just pray that whatever happens,
we have the strength to endure it.
Dear Jehovah God, please . . .
Eventually, I was arrested.
We miss you so much,
but we’re very proud of you.
We know whatever the outcome of your trial,
you’ll maintain your faith,
and so will we.
Were you scared?
I was very scared,
but Jehovah helps us when we’re scared.
I knew I would be OK
and that Jehovah
would take care of my family.
It all went by so quickly
—pioneering,
foreign language,
circuit work.
There was even a time
that I was the one encouraging older ones.
I miss those days so much.
But now I’m the one in a nursing home.
Sometimes I feel like I have
nothing left to offer.
O Daniel,
you very precious man.
I have been sent to you.
Do not be afraid, Daniel.
Your words have been heard
from the first day you gave your heart
to understanding.
I have no strength.
There’s no breath left in me.
Do not be afraid, O very precious man.
May you have peace.
Be strong.
Be strong!
Happy is the one who keeps in expectation.
Go on to the end.
You will rest, but you will stand up
for your lot at the end of the days.
Hey, just checking on you.
Do you have a minute?
There’s something I’ve been wanting
to share with you.
OK, sure.
Yes, Jehovah does remember me,
and I still have much to offer.

但现在我自己也住在了养老院
我好像已经没有什么可以献给耶和华了
但以理，非常宝贵的人啊
我奉命来见你了
不要害怕

titles.cn: 我们要凭着信心充满力量！

ko.text: JW 방송 시청자 여러분, 정말 반갑습니다!
그가 삶의 진정한 의미를 찾는 데 무엇이 도움이 되었을까요?
어떻게 흔들리지 않는 튼튼한 우정을 쌓을 수 있을까요?
새 노래는 우리가 항상 기뻐할 수 있는 많은 이유를 생각나게 해 줄 겁니다.
노래를 들으면 분명 미소를 짓게 될 겁니다.
낙담이 되는 상황을 겪은 적이 분명 있을 것입니다.
사실 낙담하지 않는 사람은 아무도 없습니다.
그런 감정은 하루 이틀이면 없어질 수도 있고,
그보다 훨씬 더 오래갈 수도 있습니다.
낙담이 되는 원인에는 어떤 것들이 있습니까?
우리를 낙담하게 만들 수 있는 20가지가 넘는 요인들이 나옵니다.
그런 요인 중에는 다른 사람의 행실이 있는데,
누군가가 어떤 일을 하거나 하지 않아서 실망하게 될 수 있죠.
자격이 부족하다는 생각이 원인일 수 있습니다.
그런가 하면 개인적인 약점이나 건강 문제
또는 특권을 잃은 것이 낙담의 요인일 수 있습니다.
우리를 실망시키거나 낙담하게 만들 수 있는 요인이
낙담했다는 사실 자체가 낙담이 되기도 합니다.
위로가 되는 소식이 있는데 우리만 그런 것이 아닙니다.
성경에 나오는 몇몇 탁월하고 충실한 여호와의 종들도
모세는 이스라엘 백성의 불평에 너무나 낙담한 나머지
리브가는 아들 에서가 이방인 여자들과 결혼한 일로
네, 가족 문제가 낙담의 원인이 될 수 있습니다.
“내가 나의 범법을 잘 알고 있고 내 죄가 항상 내 앞에 있습니다.”
실수나 잘못도 낙담하게 만들 수 있죠.
예레미야는 사람들의 반대와 조롱과 냉담 때문에 크게 실망해서
더 이상 그분의 이름으로 말하지 않으리라.”
이렇게 봉사에서 좋은 성과를 거두지 못해도 낙담할 수 있습니다.
자신이 죄 짓는 경향과 싸우고 있다고 솔직하게 인정했습니다.
이 죽음을 겪고 있는 몸에서 누가 나를 구해 내겠습니까?”
낙담이 되는 상황을 겪은 것처럼 우리 역시 그럴 수 있습니다.
이 세상에서 낙담은 자주 겪게 되는 일상적인 일입니다.
그래서 우리가 낙담을 어떻게 바라보는지가 중요합니다.
우리는 낙담을 절대 이길 수 없는 상대로 여기고
자신을 절망과 자기 연민에 빠지도록 내버려 둡니까?
아니면 낙담을 맞서 싸워야 할 적으로 여깁니까?
우리는 자존심, 이기심, 질투심과 같은 감정들은
물리쳐야 할 적으로 쉽게 인식하고 맞서 싸우기 위해 노력합니다.
우리의 성품이 되는 것을 원하지 않습니다.
하지만 우리는 때때로 낙담에는 너무 쉽게 굴복하는 경향이 있습니다.
“고난의 날에 낙담한다면 힘이 빠지게 될 것이다.”
우리가 낙담과 싸워야 하는 이유를 발견하셨습니까?
우리가 “고난의 날”에 낙담한다면 어떻게 될 것이라고 했습니까?
네, 낙담은 우리의 영적, 정신적, 감정적 심지어
신체적 힘까지 빼앗아 갈 수 있습니다.
그리고 우리가 힘이 빠지면 어떻게 될까요?
진리에 대한 열정을 잃을 수 있습니다.
기도나 개인 연구를 소홀히 하게 될 수 있죠.
집회에 점점 빠지게 될 수 있습니다.
형제들에 대한 사랑이 식을 수 있습니다.
이런 일들을 겪고 싶은 분들은 아무도 없을 것입니다.
그러면 어떻게 낙담과 싸워 이길 수 있습니까?
“소극적 감정—극복할 수 있는가?” 라는 기사가 실렸습니다.
치료가 필요한 심각한 우울증에 대해서는 다루지 않습니다.
그런 우울증의 원인으로는 질병이나 독소에 대한 반응, 약물,
영양 결핍, 알레르기, 호르몬 이상, 조울증 등이 있습니다.
이 기사에서는 잠언 24:10에 언급된 “고난의 날”이라는 표현처럼
일시적인 낙담을 극복하는 방법에 관해 다룹니다.
우리의 감정이 생각에 의해 생기게 된다고 단언한다.”
‘생각에서 나오지 않은 감정은 없다’는 말이 있는데
생각해 보지 않은 것은 느낄 수도 없다는 말이죠.
따라서 낙담은 우리가 처한 상황 때문이라기보다는
그 상황에 대한 우리의 부정적인 생각이 원인일 수 있습니다.
그러므로 낙담과 싸우는 첫 번째 단계는
종종 우리의 생각은 마치 기차처럼 꼬리에 꼬리를 물고 이어져서
어떤 특정한 결론에 도달하게 될 때가 있습니다.
이제 여러분이 실제로 기차나 지하철에 탔다고 상상해 보십시오.
기차를 탔는데 잘못 탔다는 걸 알게 됩니다.
종착역에 도착할 때까지 계속 타고 계시겠습니까?
당연히 바로 다음 역에서 재빨리 내리실 겁니다.
하지만 그런 다음에는 어떻게 해야 하죠?
비유적으로 말해, 여러분이 낙담이라는 종착역으로 가는
부정적인 생각이라는 기차에 탔다는 걸 알게 된다면
우리는 긍정적인 생각을 하기 위해 계속 노력해야 합니다.
사도 바울이 에베소서 4:23에서 무엇이라고 했는지 보시죠.
자신을 지배하는 정신 태도를 계속 새롭게 해야 합니다.’
바울은 우리가 생각을 제어할 수 있다고 말한 것이죠.
그리고 불완전한 우리는 그렇게 하기 위해 계속해서 노력해야 합니다.
우리의 정신을 올바른 방향으로 바꾸는 데 도움이 되는
그 무기들은 그분의 강력한 말씀과 성령, 기도
그리고 조직을 통해 나오는 풍부한 영적 양식입니다.
이제 낙담하게 만들 수 있는 몇 가지 부정적인 생각을 살펴보겠습니다.
그런 다음 낙담과 싸우는 데 도움이 되는 긍정적이고
여러분이 잘못된 말이나 행동을 해서 후회가 되는 하루를 보냈다고 합시다.
여러분은 낙담으로 갈 때까지 계속 그 기차에 타고 있을 것입니까?
여러분은 부정적인 생각을 멈추기로 선택할 수 있습니다.
부정적인 생각에 굴복하지 말고 자신에게 이렇게 말할 수 있습니다.
내가 실수를 했다고 해서 여호와 앞에 무가치한 사람이 되는 건 아니지.
“참새 한 마리도 하느님 모르게 땅에 떨어지지 않”는다고 하시면서 우리가
다시 이런 실수를 하지 않도록 그분이 분명 도와주실 거야.
내일은 더 좋은 하루가 될 거야.
한 형제에게서 아주 불친절한 말을 들었습니다.
‘어떻게 형제가 이렇게 행동하면서 책임 있는 위치에서 일할 수 있지?
왜 장로들이 아무 조치도 하지 않을까?’
마치 낙담이 자기에게 오라고 손짓하는 것과 같은 순간이죠.
계속 그런 부정적인 생각에 머물러 있다면 영적인 힘을 잃게 될 것입니다.
부정적인 생각을 긍정적인 생각으로 바꿀 것입니까?
자신에게 이렇게 말하면서 생각을 긍정적인 방향으로 바꿀 수 있습니다.
‘그 형제가 나한테 불친절한 말을 했는데, 평소 같지 않은 걸.
뭔가 안 좋은 일이 있었던 거 같아.
나도 불친절한 말을 하고 후회한 적이 여러 번 있었지.
그 성구에서는 우리에게 이렇게 알려 주지.
“누군가 다른 사람에 대해 불평할 이유가 있더라도
계속 서로 참고 서로 기꺼이 용서하십시오.”
그 형제에게 불평할 이유가 있는 건 사실이야.
하지만 성구에선 “여호와께서 우리를 기꺼이 용서”하셨다고 했지.
분명 그분은 날 수도 없이 용서해 주셨어.
이 일로 형제와의 사이가 나빠지게 해서는 안 되겠어.
형제를 위해 뭘 할 수 있을까?
분한 감정을 품지 않도록 도와 달라고도 기도해야겠어.’
여러 해 동안 직장에서 열심히 일했는데
이제 더 이상 나오지 말라고 합니다.
머릿속이 염려와 부정적인 생각으로 가득 찹니다.
왜 여호와께서 이런 일이 일어나도록 내버려 두신 걸까?’
이런 부정적인 생각을 하다 보면 결국 어떻게 될까요?
영적으로 약해지고 완전히 지치게 될 것입니다.
이런 긍정적인 생각으로 바꿀 수 있습니다.
직장을 잃었다고 여호와를 섬기는 일이 영향을 받아선 안 돼.
여호와께서 필요한 것을 주실 것이기 때문에
물질에 대해 염려해서는 안 된다고 하셨어.
그러고 보니 우리도 필요 없는 물건들이 있는 것 같아.
여호와를 섬기기 위해 더 많은 일을 해야겠어.
여호와께선 절대 우리를 버리지 않겠다고 약속하셨지.
올바른 결정을 내리도록 우리를 도와주실 거야.’
우리는 이 세상의 마지막 날에 살고 있습니다.
우리는 각자 고난의 날을 겪고 있죠.

“하느님은 주는 일을 사랑하는 사람을 사랑하십니다”라고 번역합니다.
그래서 우리 각자의 형편에 따라 그 돈이 얼마가 됐든
우리는 여호와를 사랑하기 때문에 헌금을 합니다.
모세 율법에 들어 있는 원칙에서 찾을 수 있습니다.
그 당시 유대인들에게 주어진 이 율법이
오늘날 우리에게 어떻게 적용되는지 생각해 보시죠.
“모든 남자는 한 해에 세 번 곧 무교절과 칠칠절과 초막절에
아무도 여호와 앞에 빈손으로 나와서는 안 됩니다.
각 사람은 당신의 하느님 여호와께서 축복해 주신 만큼
축제에 참석하는 이스라엘 사람들에게 여호와께서 원하신 것은
당시 여호와의 백성 중에도 문제들이 있었고
그래도 ‘아무도 빈손으로 와서는 안 된다’고 하셨습니다.
우리의 상황이 어떻든, 야외에 있든 베델에 있든,
여호와께서는 우리가 빈손으로 오는 것을 승인하지 않으십니다.
그러면 빈손으로 오지 않는 데 이스라엘 시대에나 우리 시대에나
“각 사람은 당신의 하느님 여호와께서 축복해 주신 만큼
그들이 여호와께서 주신 축복을 깊이 생각해 봐야 했던 것처럼
우리도 늘 여호와께서 주신 축복에 대해 깊이 생각해 봐야 합니다.
시간을 충분히 내서 깊이 숙고해 봐야 합니다.
‘각 사람은 축복을 받은 만큼 예물을 가져와야 한다’고 한 것처럼,
기쁜 마음으로 물질적인 것을 드리게 될 겁니다.
여호와를 위해 이런저런 일을 하고 있기 때문에
매달 혹은 정기적으로 헌금을 하는 면에서
비유적으로 빈손으로 와도 된다고 생각해서는 안 될 것입니다.
우리가 비교적 가난하다 하더라도 그 점을 기억할 수 있습니다.
기꺼이 주려는 세 번째 이유는 예수에 대한 사랑 때문입니다.
우리는 주 예수에 대한 사랑 때문에 기꺼이 주고 자원해서 헌금을 합니다.
‘누구든지 나를 사랑하면 내 말을 지킬 것입니다.
그러면 내 아버지께서 그를 사랑하실 것이고,
우리가 그에게 가서 그와 함께 거할 것입니다.’”
물론 그리스도교국 사람들도 예수를 사랑한다고 말하지만
그것은 그분에 대한 정확한 지식도 없이 그렇게 말하는 것이죠.
하지만 우리는 진리를 알고 헌신하고 침례받은 예수의 종입니다.
따라서 우리는 예수의 말씀을 지키기 위해
왕국 활동에 우리의 시간과 활력을 바칠 뿐만 아니라
전 세계적인 활동을 지원하는 데도 기꺼이 헌금합니다.
지부들을 운영하고 전파 활동과 왕국 활동을 지원하고
근래에 있었던 것과 같은 여러 프로젝트들을 수행하려면
“우리는 비영리 조직이니까 물건을 그냥 좀 주실 수는 없나요?”
우리는 당연히 여호와의 일을 위해 사용할 다양한 물품들에 대해
그럼 오늘 살펴본 세 가지 이유를 기억해 볼까요?
우린 여호와를 사랑하고 그분을 기쁘게 하기를 원합니다.
우리는 할 수 있는 걸 다하기를 원합니다.
물질적으로 얼마를 기부하든 그것은 개인적인 결정이며
다른 사람에게 절대 강요해서는 안 됩니다.
하지만 여러분이 가진 것이 적더라도 가난한 과부를 기억할 수 있습니다.
그 가난한 과부는 성전에 올 때 빈손으로 오지 않았습니다.
가진 걸 기꺼이 헌금한 과부를 사랑하셨습니다.
따라서 우리도 가난하더라도 물질적인 기부를 할 수 있습니다.
우리가 받은 모든 축복에 대해 늘 감사하기 때문입니다.
앞서 이야기했듯이 우리는 낙담과 싸우기 위해
부정적인 생각을 긍정적인 생각으로 바꿔야 합니다.
새로운 뮤직비디오를 보면서 바로 지금 그렇게 해 보시죠.
셀 수 없이 많은 축복들을 주셨지만
하느님의 사랑, 그 무엇보다 큰 선물이야.
누구도 우리의 형제 사랑, 막지 못해.
그 어떤 시련도 내 맘 속 기쁨, 뺏지 못해.
이번 달 프로그램은 우리가 낙담과 맞서 싸워 이기고
기쁨을 유지할 수 있다는 점을 일깨워 주었습니다.
형제 자매들과 가깝게 지내고 영적 양식을 잘 섭취하고
큰 도움이 되는 튼튼한 우정을 기르는 방법도 알아보았습니다.
음악에 대한 사랑보다 여호와에 대한 사랑을 앞자리에 둔 덕분에
여호와를 섬기며 의미 있는 삶을 살고 있습니다.
두고두고 부르고 싶은 아주 즐거운 노래였습니다.
이제 캐나다 퀘벡주의 형제 자매들을 만나 보시죠.
퀘벡은 육지 면적으로만 보면 캐나다에서 가장 큰 주입니다.
천연 스키장, 숲과 같은 아름다운 자연 경관으로 유명합니다.
말코손바닥사슴, 순록, 비버, 늑대, 흰올빼미를 볼 수 있습니다.
교직자들의 부추김을 받은 정부는 곧바로 증인들을 박해했습니다.
주 정부가 숭배의 자유를 탄압하고 있다고 널리 알렸습니다.
그로 인해 수백 명의 여호와의 증인이 체포되었습니다.
처음으로 재판을 받은 사람들은 에메 부셰 형제와 그의 두 딸이었는데,
1950년에 캐나다 대법원은 그들에게 호의적인 판결을 내렸고,
그로 인해 여호와의 증인이 퀘벡에서 전파할 법적 권리가 확립되었습니다.
오늘날 형제들은 숭배의 자유를 온전히 활용하고 있습니다.
그리고 여러 나라 사람들이 일하러 오는 항구들에서 공개 증거를 합니다.
수십 년 전에 우리의 활동을 중단시킨 법이 제정된 곳도 있죠.
부셰 형제는 라크에체맹이라는 작은 도시 출신인데
현재 이곳에 있는 회중에는 71명의 전도인이 있습니다.
전도인들은 많은 농장이 포함된 매우 넓은 구역에서
모든 사람을 만나기 위해서 노력한 결과
여러 건의 성서 연구를 사회하고 있습니다.
이곳은 한겨울에 평균 기온이 영하 12도 정도입니다.
하지만 기온이 훨씬 더 내려갈 때도 많이 있습니다.
추운 날씨에도 불구하고 형제들은 따뜻한 교제를 즐깁니다.
전 세계 메이플시럽의 70퍼센트 이상이 퀘벡에서 생산됩니다.
메이플태피라는 사탕이 유명한데, 이것은 단풍나무 수액을 끓여 졸인 다음
눈 위에 뿌려 굳히고 그 위로 나무 막대를 굴려서 만듭니다.
지금까지 여호와의 증인의 세계 본부에서 JW 방송이었습니다!

en.text: Welcome to this month’s edition
of JW Broadcasting®!
Here are a few highlights from our program.
Bill lived for music,
but it left him feeling as if something was missing.
We’ll learn what helped him to have a truly meaningful life.
Good friends are a blessing,
especially during hard times.
We’ll learn how to build
strong friendships that endure.
And our new song
reminds us of the many reasons
we have to be joyful.
It will make you smile!
This is JW Broadcasting.
No doubt every one of us at one time or another
has faced a discouraging situation.
Really, no one is immune
from discouragement.
This feeling may last
for a day or two and then subside,
or it might last longer.
What can cause us to be discouraged?
The Watch Tower Publications Index
lists over 20 factors
that can contribute to discouragement.
Some of them are these:
another’s conduct
—what someone did or didn’t do
that disappointed us;
problems in our congregation;
feeling inadequate;
our own personal failures
—what we’ve done or failed to do;
health problems; and loss of privileges.
There are ever so many things
that can cause us to be downhearted.
Even the fact that we are discouraged can be discouraging.
We feel guilty for being discouraged.
Here’s the good news.
We’re in good company.
Some very prominent and faithful servants of Jehovah
mentioned in the Bible have been discouraged.
Moses became so discouraged
over the complaints of the Israelites
that he said to God: “Please kill me right now.”
Rebekah was so distressed
because her son Esau married pagan women
that she told her husband, Isaac:
“I am disgusted with my life.”
Yes, family situations
can cause discouragement.
David was tormented by his sins.
At Psalm 51:3, he wrote:
“I am well-aware of my transgressions,
and my sin is always before me.”
Our mistakes can weigh us down.
Jeremiah felt so discouraged
by the opposition, ridicule, and apathy he met up with
that he told himself:
“I am not going to make mention of [Jehovah],
and I will speak no more in his name.”
Yes, poor results in the ministry can discourage us.
The apostle Paul frankly admitted
at Romans 7:24, 25
that he struggled against sinful tendencies.
At times, he felt miserable over this conflict.
He said: “Miserable man that I am!
Who will rescue me from the body undergoing this death?”
Faithful men and women
faced discouraging circumstances in the past,
and so do we.
Discouragement is a part of life in this system.
We should expect it.
Yet, it’s important to consider
how we view discouragement.
Do we view ourselves as helpless victims of discouragement
and let ourselves sink into a quagmire
of despair and self-pity,
or do we view discouragement as an enemy
that we must fight against?
We easily recognize that feelings of pride,
selfishness, envy, and such things are enemies.
We battle against these bad feelings.
We don’t want them to erode our faith
or gain a foothold in our personality.
Yet, sometimes we may yield all too willingly
to discouragement.
Why is this dangerous?
Please read with me Proverbs 24:10:
“If you become discouraged
“in the day of distress,
your strength will be meager.”
Did you note the reason why we must fight discouragement?
What did Proverbs 24:10 tells us will happen
if we allow a “day of distress” to discourage us?
We’ll lose our strength.
Yes, discouragement can drain us
of our spiritual, mental, emotional, and even physical strength.
And what can happen if we lose our strength?
We can lose our enthusiasm for the truth.
We may lose interest in prayer or in personal study.
We could slack off in attending meetings.
We could develop coldness toward our brothers.
Our zeal for evangelizing can weaken.
We may even want to give up.
We don’t want any of those things to happen to us, do we, brothers?
How, then, do we fight and defeat discouragement?
Discouragement is a feeling, an emotion.
What causes feelings or emotions?
An article entitled “Negative Emotions —Can You Overcome Them?”
was published in the October 8, 1992, Awake!
This article didn’t discuss serious cases of depression
that may have a medical or physical cause,
such as a disease,
a reaction to toxins, medications,
nutritional deficiencies,
allergens, hormonal problems,
or bipolar disorder.
Rather, it discussed how to overcome
moments of discouragement
like the temporary “day of distress”
mentioned at Proverbs 24:10.
Under the subheading “We Can Control Our Thinking,”
it stated this:
“Many who work in the field of mental health
“maintain that our feelings
are caused by our thoughts.”
It’s been said that ‘you cannot experience a feeling
without first experiencing a thought.’
So then, feeling discouraged
isn’t always the situation that we face
but the negative thoughts that we have about the situation.
The first step, then, in fighting discouragement
is to identify the negative thoughts.
Sometimes we say that we have a “train of thought.”
It means we have a series of thoughts
that lead to a certain conclusion, or destination, if you will.
Now, imagine yourself
getting on a literal railroad or subway train.
Soon you realize that you’re on the wrong train.
It’s taking you to a place you do not want to go to.
What do you do?
Do you stay on the train all the way to the wrong destination?
Of course not.
No, you get off that train at the very next station.
But what do you do next?
You switch to the right train.
Now, figuratively speaking,
if you realize that your mind is getting on
a train of negative thoughts that are leading to discouragement,
can you get off that train?
Certainly.
But you need to switch to the right train of thought
that will lead you to a peaceful state of mind.
That’s the key.
We need to replace negative thoughts
with positive, upbuilding, spiritual thoughts.
Keeping our thinking on the right track
is an ongoing process.
Notice how the apostle Paul put it
in Ephesians 4:23:
“And you should continue to be made new
in your dominant mental attitude.”
Do you see how Paul confirms that we are in control?
We can change how we think.
And because we’re imperfect,
we have to make these changes continuously.
It’s not a losing battle.
Jehovah has given us powerful weapons
to help us make our minds move in the right direction
—his powerful Word,
his mighty holy spirit,
the power of prayer,
and healthful spiritual food from his organization.
Let’s consider some negative thoughts
that may lead to discouragement.
Then, we’ll consider upbuilding, positive thoughts
that help us fight discouragement.
You had a bad day.
You said or did the wrong thing, and you regret it.
It’s become a “day of distress.”
The thought enters your mind, ‘I’m worthless.’
That’s the “discouragement train.”
Will you continue to stay on this train of thought,
taking you to the state of discouragement?
Remember, you have a choice.
You can reject it.
Instead of giving in to that negative thought,
you could say to yourself:
‘Wait a minute. Stop!
‘That’s not right.
‘Just because I made a mistake
‘does not make me worthless in Jehovah’s eyes.
‘He’s told us that he knows that “we are dust”
‘and that he’s merciful.
‘And Jesus said that “not one sparrow
‘that has fallen to the ground is forgotten by God,”
‘and that “[we] are worth more than many sparrows.”
‘Yes, Jehovah views me as precious.
‘I’ll pray about this,
‘and I’m sure he’ll help me not to make that mistake again.
‘Tomorrow will be a better day.
Thank you, Jehovah.’
Let’s take a second example.
A brother has said something quite unkind to you.
This has become a “day of distress.”
The thought comes to your mind:
‘How can a brother behave like that
‘and still be in good standing?
‘He’s not a good example.
Why don’t the elders do something about it?’
Now, that’s discouragement speaking,
calling for us to “get on board.”
If we stay on that negative train of thought,
we could lose our spiritual strength.
But we still have a choice.
Will we replace those negative thoughts
with positive ones?
We could get our mind on a positive track
by saying to ourselves something like this:
‘Well, that was an unkind thing for him to say.
‘This is not like him.
‘Maybe my brother just had a bad day.
‘He’s as imperfect as I am.
‘I’ve said unkind things too, at times,
‘and have regretted it.
‘He’s probably feeling the same way.
‘I remember Colossians 3:13 says
‘that we must “continue putting up with one another
‘“and forgiving one another freely
‘“even if anyone has a cause for complaint
‘against another.”
‘Well, he has given me a cause for complaint.
‘But it says Jehovah has “freely [forgiven us].”
‘He has certainly forgiven me countless times.
‘No, I am not going to allow this
‘to ruin our relationship.
‘How can I help my brother?
‘I’ll pray for him.
‘And I’ll pray for myself
‘that I don’t hold feelings of resentment
in my heart.’
Let’s consider a third example.
After years of hard work at your place of employment,
your position has been terminated.
You’ve lost your job.
It’s a “day of distress.”
You’re filled with anxious, negative thoughts:
‘How will I care for my family?
‘What will the future bring?
Why did Jehovah allow this to happen to me?’
Where will this train of dark, negative thoughts lead you?
Certainly, discouragement will set in,
and you will become spiritually weak and exhausted.
You still have a choice.
You can replace those negative thoughts
with thoughts such as these:
‘OK, I’ve lost my job.
‘What should I do?
‘Stop serving Jehovah?
‘No!
‘Jesus said that we should not be anxious over material things
‘because Jehovah will provide
‘if we keep his Kingdom first in our lives.
‘He also said to keep our lives simple.
‘You know what?
‘There are things that we don’t need.
‘So that’s what we’ll do
‘—simplify our life and do more in Jehovah’s service.
‘Jehovah promises never to abandon us.
‘I’ll throw my burden on him,
and I know he’ll help us make the right decisions.’
Brothers, we’re living
in the last days of this system of things.
We’ll have our days of distress.
Sometimes these come because of our own imperfection
or the imperfection of others.
But we also realize
that the Devil wants to discourage us.
Revelation 12:17 tells us
that Satan’s great anger is directed
toward those “who observe the commandments of God
and have the work of bearing witness concerning Jesus.”
The Devil will try to take advantage
of situations and problems that we face
to fill us with discouraging thoughts and drain us of our strength.
Now we stand at the very threshold of the new world.
Let’s fight discouragement
with all the weapons Jehovah gives us.
Continue to study God’s Word,
making it a part of your daily life.
Pray incessantly to Jehovah for his powerful spirit.
Keep close to his organization.
God has promised to give us the victory.
Fearlessly, we join in repeating Paul’s words
at Philippians 4:13:
“For all things I have the strength
through the one who gives me power.”
Our first video
is the experience of Aino Ehtmaa.
As we’ll see,
she endured many “days of distress”
for being one of Jehovah’s Witnesses.
Notice what she did
to remain faithful and joyful.
When I was young, my father wrote to me the Bible verse:
“Your word is a lamp to my foot, and a light for my path.”
And he said: “Keep that always in mind.
Remember God’s Word and live by it.”
I was born in 1929
in the city of Võru, Estonia.
My family was religious, and my God-fearing parents
lovingly cared for me and provided everything that a child would need.
When my father learned the truth, he gave each of us a Bible,
and we began to study it together.
My father was arrested in the summer of 1948.
Estonia was then under the Soviet regime,
but he was still working as a schoolteacher.
The local Department of Education asked him to come by.
He went dressed in summer clothes
and wearing sandals, but he never came back.
At midnight, we heard someone banging at the door.
We opened it, and soldiers came in
and demanded our passports.
We put the passports on the table, and they just said,
“You are under arrest.”
Pagari Prison in Tallinn was a place everyone was afraid of,
and I was afraid too.
I remember that I was taken down the steps
to the basement to a long corridor.
There was nothing in the cell besides a bench.
They slammed the door shut,
and that is when I became a little scared.
But then I prayed to Jehovah to help me,
and a sense of peace came over me.
I laid down on the bench and fell asleep.
I was given a ten-year prison sentence
as an enemy of the State.
A year later, we were transferred to Russian prison camps.
Spiritual food was hard to get.
It couldn’t be sent by mail.
But the angels somehow still provided for us,
and we always had something.
Even a single verse
or a good thought can help in prison.
In any case, God’s Word should be in our heart.
We should never forget it,
even if we can only remember one verse.
At one point during my sentence, I was allowed
to live outside the prison camp.
One Witness family took
me and two other sisters into their home.
Living outside meant that the guard was not watching us all the time.
We were able to spend time together, and we could preach a little.
We even went from house to house.
Eventually, I moved to a dormitory
because there was not enough space.
And it also meant that the literature could be stored at my place,
because if they arrested me, it wouldn’t be a big deal,
but if the brother was arrested, it would be much worse.
They raided my place one night.
They put all the literature on the table
and asked me where I got it.
I said, “The angels are bringing it to us
and feeding us all the time.”
So I was sentenced to another two years
for possessing literature.
Then, for the first time,
I heard that Jehovah’s Witnesses were officially banned.
What a good feeling it was
to be recognized as one of Jehovah’s Witnesses!
That really gave me joy.
I saw Jehovah’s help in that things were never too hard
for me to bear.
If things were getting too difficult,
something would always change so that I could cope.
There was always that feeling that someone was looking after me.
I never felt alone or abandoned.
If only we could be faithful all the time,
then we would also be happy.
But sometimes we fail, and so we lose joy.
Faithfulness gives joy.
In prison, you can stay faithful if you don’t leave Jehovah
and if you don’t forget to pray
and if you always remember why you are there.
You are there because you are on Jehovah’s side.
I was not a thief; I was not a killer.
But I was one of Jehovah’s Witnesses,
and that is worth being in prison for.
If you’re enduring persecution or any sort of trial,
you’ll want to remember what helped Sister Ehtmaa.
She kept herself spiritually nourished
even when literature was scarce;
she cherished God’s Word, the Bible;
she fought discouragement and anxiety with prayer;
and she stayed close to fellow believers
—something we all need to do.
Strengthening relationships with our brothers and sisters
is especially important
as we move deeper into the last days.
In our next segment from our series
Lessons From The Watchtower,
we’ll learn how to build strong friendships.
Friends give me help
when I need them the most.
They make me laugh; they give me
practical assistance whenever I need them.
They’re just a real source of joy in my life.
When I see my dear friends
going through difficult times
but still serving Jehovah
—that really encourages me with my trials.
Friendship—it just enhances
and enriches a person’s life.
I don’t think that friendship is
something that I find too natural.
I’m shy by nature; I’m hesitant by nature;
I feel inadequate by nature.
In my mind, Baruch was simply Jeremiah’s secretary.
I had never considered that after spending so much time together,
it would have allowed them to draw closer as friends.
When I studied the article about Jeremiah and Baruch,
it made me reflect on friendships that I have.
When you work together for Jehovah,
it takes your friendship to another level.
Jehovah’s people will have
a depth and a dimension to their friendships
that will not be shared by those who are not serving Jehovah.
In the article, I really loved the point about communication.
Being open with others
allows them to be open with you,
and that just allows
a friendship to flourish.
I can have a very bad view of myself.
I appreciated the reminder
that you will see the bad side of any friend —that’s just normal.
But good friends remind you of your good side.
That is like Jehovah talking and reminding me
how much I’m loved by him.
I’d heard that Keith, an older brother,
was returning to Britain for some medical treatment.
He was much loved—deeply respected.
You try to picture, to imagine
what’s going through his mind
—his fears and anxieties.
I felt very inadequate, but I realized
that it would be the loving and kind thing to do to speak to him.
So we spent some time together; we talked.
I felt honored just to say a prayer with someone like that.
I was really touched by Keith’s response.
He clearly and deeply appreciated that,
and I felt thrilled to have done just a little something
that helped and supported him.
I’ve worked with someone
that I never expected to become very close to.
Charlotte —she’s the opposite of me,
but I came to realize quite early on
that she’s an amazing listener.
Charlotte is more than a friend
—she’s now family.
I love my family very, very much.
At the moment, I’m the only one in my family
who is one of Jehovah’s Witnesses,
but I’ve never felt that I was truly alone.
Jehovah has always provided brothers,
sisters, mothers (you know), uncles, aunties.
He’s always given me everyone that I needed.
I feel that I’ve had a lesson powerfully reinforced
of the blessings of genuine friendship.
When we make an effort
just to give Jehovah a little something,
he can add his blessing.
In my experience, the person you don’t expect
actually turns out to be
a very special friend.
When you work with different brothers and sisters,
you really appreciate that they are gifts from Jehovah.
“And he will give all of you into our hand.”
Working hard for Jehovah and being genuine
—that will attract other brothers and sisters.
We will never forget the friendships that we make right now.
Jehovah will use those friendships to help us through the great tribulation.
Those helpful suggestions
appeared in the November 2019 issue of The Watchtower.
That article emphasized the importance
of forging strong friendships now,
before the end of this system comes.
During the great tribulation,
God’s enemies may try to disrupt our unity.
But we can be confident
that nothing will break our bonds of love.
Our friendships will last
not only through the end of this system but for all eternity.
For many years, we’ve published the life stories of Jehovah’s Witnesses.
Have you ever wondered:
‘What happened since their stories appeared?
How are they today?’
Well, we’re pleased to introduce
a new series: Where Are They Now?
In our first episode, we’ll hear from Bill Mullane.
His story appeared in the Awake!  magazine
some 35 years ago.
At that time, Bill had made a major decision
that would affect the course of his life.
How has it turned out?
Let’s see.
Music expresses things
that you can’t express in any other way.
It is so powerful.
It’s just an amazing gift.
Before I got the truth, I lived for music.
I played hard and heavy rock and roll
in bars and clubs around the New York City area for many years.
To me, I just found it to be a very depressing atmosphere.
But then I developed a love for classical music,
and I would practice six hours a day.
I applied to The Juilliard School for the performing arts.
I was accepted,
but I did not attend.
Deep inside something was missing.
My life changed drastically on February 16, 1973,
because that’s when I learned the truth in a taxicab.
I came to Bethel on February 16, 1979.
When I first came to Bethel,
I had to put music aside for a little bit.
I started working in the pressroom,
and that was a completely different environment for me.
I also worked with landscaping.
I worked in construction over at Wallkill,
and I also worked with drafting and engineering.
These were things I was not good at,
but I really felt I learned so much
from doing these things that it really kind of groomed me.
And I think that when Jehovah looked at me,
he said, ‘Well, we got somebody we have to work with here.’
Just as you tune your instrument so it can be played in tune,
Jehovah tunes you.
He teaches us to keep things in their place
and put worship of him first because that’s where it’s proper.
When Jehovah became number one, everything else took its place.
Back in 1981, I met my wife when I was playing music at a wedding.
We fell in love with each other.
As our love for Jehovah grows through the years,
our love for our mates grows.
Now, I didn’t leave music completely, because I still had a love for it;
I still practiced as much as I could within my Bethel schedule
and within my whole theocratic schedule.
I don’t miss it being number one.
I just feel happier now that it’s in its proper place.
In 1995, when I first came over to Patterson,
I was working with Audio/Video Services.
Since 2016,
I’ve been working with music —working as a music editor
and as a music composer.
Working with brothers on a piece of music
is a real blessing and a privilege.
Jehovah is letting us take advantage of a tool that we all like to listen to
but now using it in a way that praises him.
Our whole motive is not to earn money.
Our whole motive in using music
is to glorify our heavenly Father, Jehovah.
And we get music from all different cultures.
It really unites Jehovah’s people.
Music—it has a very special power in being able to reach the heart.
Now, there are times when we just sit around
and just jam and play,
and you’re really talking and communicating with each other.
There’s nothing like it.
I’m happier now
knowing that I’ve lived a clean life.
Do I have any regrets?
I have no regrets.
What I did when I was 22 years old
was the best thing that ever happened to me
because that’s how I came to know Jehovah
and that’s how I was able to find a balance in my life.
Our happiness doesn’t depend on our job.
Our happiness really depends upon our spirituality
and our relationship with Jehovah.
That’s what life is all about.
It’s a wonderful life.
Bill has no regrets about the life he’s chosen to live.
By putting his love for Jehovah ahead of his love for music,
he gained many spiritual privileges
and a happy, meaningful life.
The apostle Paul wrote
that Jehovah “loves a cheerful giver.”
That was the subject of a recent morning worship
by Brother Anthony Morris of the Governing Body.
We’re going to talk about money.
Now, the fact is,
we never beg for money.
But that’s not to say
that we can’t talk about money
in Jehovah’s organization
—the earthly part.
So it’s long standing;
there is a balance here.
Going back to The Watchtower, a long time ago, it says:
“We have never considered it proper to solicit money for the Lord’s cause,
“after the common custom [referring to Christendom]; . . .
“It is our judgment that money raised by the various begging devices
“in the name of our Lord is offensive,
“unacceptable to him,
“and does not bring his blessing
either upon the givers or the work accomplished.”
So we do not need to be coerced into giving.
We gladly use our money to support Kingdom activities.
So that stands to this day.
But we’d never want to come to the conclusion that we can’t talk about money.
Money has to be discussed in these last days in this system.
It “meets a response in all things.”
So I thought we’d take some thoughts from the Kingdom  book:
three reasons why we’re willing —so willing to give.
Some beautiful thoughts.
Well, the first one is connected
with “doing what is pleasing in [Jehovah’s] eyes.”
And finding
the Second Corinthians reference here
is so crucial in helping people understand
that we don’t beg for money.
But, nonetheless, we have to talk about it from time to time.
Here in the ninth chapter,
donations and such were being discussed.
And then this profound, inspired thought,
which is reflecting Jehovah’s thinking,
is in verse 7
—2 Corinthians 9:7:
“Let each one do just as he is resolved in his heart,
“not grudgingly or under compulsion,
for God loves a cheerful giver.”
So there we have it.
We’re happy to give to Jehovah.
When needs arise,
and the organization brings it to our attention
—for example, disasters and such
like the report we had at the annual meeting
about the increase in disasters—
millions of dollars of God’s Kingdom money
was used to help our brothers.
But when it comes to giving,
it’s an individual responsibility, as the verse says,
“resolved in his heart [or her heart], not grudgingly.”
And the footnote addresses the word “reluctantly.”
So it’s not like we embarrass people
or beg them, saying: “Look, you’re well-off.
Why aren’t you giving more?”
Well, that’s not their business; that’s not our business.
We have to resolve it in our own heart.
So while we discuss money,
we never come across like we’re putting people
—trying to get them
to even grudgingly give just so we get the money.
That’s not this organization.
Of course, Christendom, they are experts at begging for money.
So we love Jehovah.
We want to be the kind of person that he loves.
And notice that beautiful expression: “God loves a cheerful giver.”
One translation put it nicely:
“God loves people who love to give.”
And that’s true.
So we want Jehovah to love us.
So this money we might have
—whatever amount, depending on our own personal circumstances—
we’re happy to give to Kingdom interests.
So that’s the first one: We make these donations
because of our love for Jehovah.
Now this second one, this is interesting
—a heart-searching principle found back in the Mosaic Law.
Turn to Deuteronomy chapter 16,
if you would, please.
In Deuteronomy 16,
you’ll see the connection.
While this applied to the Jews at that time,
you’ll see how it applies to us in our day.
We’re going to read verse 16 and then verse 17 of Deuteronomy 16.
“Three times a year,
“all your males should appear before Jehovah your God
“in the place that he chooses:
“at the Festival of Unleavened Bread,
“the Festival of Weeks,
“and the Festival of Booths,
“[now notice,] and none of them
“should appear before Jehovah empty-handed.
“The gift that each one brings should be in proportion
to the blessing that Jehovah your God has given you.”
So if you let that sink in,
this is what Jehovah wanted to be conveyed
to the Israelites who would attend these festivals—“none.”
Now, he didn’t say,
‘If you’re well-off, if you’ve had a great year
(as opposed to some that were poor).’
They still had issues back at that time,
even though it was Jehovah’s nation.
But he said: ‘None should appear empty-handed.’
So that takes in all of us,
whatever our circumstances are,
whether at Bethel or in the field.
Jehovah doesn’t approve of us coming empty-handed.
What would help us not to come empty-handed,
in this case, back in Israel or in our time either?
Notice verse 17, and this is a lot to think about:
“The gift that each one brings should be in proportion
to the blessing that Jehovah your God has given you.”
So there we have it.
You stop and reflect that they were supposed to do that,
and we can do the same throughout the year.
Reflect on the blessings that Jehovah God has given us.
You have to take time to do that; you have to give that consideration.
“The gift that each one brings should be in proportion to the blessing.”
So adding up these blessings,
then we’re happy to give out of our material possessions.
So a profound thought there,
and something to reflect on so that we don’t find ourselves
—when it comes to contributions on a monthly basis or whatever—
empty-handed, perhaps thinking, ‘Well, I’m doing so much here and there.’
Well, money meets a response in all things,
and you have to take that into account,
even if we’re in the poor range.
Now, the third one is connected with our love for Jesus.
Let’s turn to John chapter 14, if you would, please
—John chapter 14.
We give and have voluntary contributions
because we love our Lord Jesus.
And notice what he stated here,
John 14:23:
“In answer Jesus said to him:
“‘If anyone loves me, he will observe my word,
“‘and my Father will love him,
and we will come to him and make our dwelling with him.’”
So appreciate how Jesus put it—“if.”
So it’s a responsibility that falls on us individually.
But if we say we love Jesus
(we’re not like Christendom
with this proclamation of their love for Jesus,
—they really don’t even know the real Jesus, frankly,
until they get an accurate knowledge of the truth),
if we’re in the truth
—dedicated, baptized servants of him—
if we really love him, we’re going to observe his word.
Now, that means not just carrying out the Kingdom work,
putting our time and energy into it,
it also means money.
We are willing to donate money to support the worldwide work.
We’re not ashamed to admit
that it takes money to have these things operate
—branches, supporting all of the preaching work,
the Kingdom work, and all these other initiatives
that we’ve had in recent years.
It takes money.
You can’t go to people that you buy things from and say,
“Well, look, this is a non-profit organization,”
trying to shame them, saying, “Well, can you give it to me?”
No.
They want their money and to be paid for the various things
that we have to use to accomplish Jehovah’s work.
So something to keep in mind, those three things:
Our love for Jehovah —we want to do what’s pleasing to him.
We count our blessings from Jehovah.
Then, we have our love for Christ Jesus.
And we want to do whatever we can.
So how you do it with the financial contributions,
that’s a personal decision,
and Jehovah dignifies us with that.
We never want to be shaming somebody
that we think should be doing thus and so.
That’s a personal matter.
But keep in mind, sometimes, if you are poor
—remember the widow.
So she didn’t come there
to the temple empty-handed.
She didn’t have much, but Jehovah loved her.
Jesus loved her for giving what she had.
So even when we’re poor,
we’re expected to give monetarily.
And it’s because we love Jehovah, we love Jesus,
and we appreciate all the blessings we receive
during the year and are grateful.
As we’ve discussed, we fight discouragement
by replacing negative thoughts with positive thoughts.
Let’s do that right now.
Please enjoy our new music video.
It’s entitled “Always Rejoice.”
Look at the sky; take it in. Feel the sun on your skin.
So much our God provides— blessing our lives, helping us grow.
But even more than this, his love is a gift; we’ll never let go.
Sing to Jehovah with all your heart. Serve him through all your days—
No greater joy could there be than this, No matter what we face.
Always rejoice! Always rejoice!
Always rejoice! Always rejoice!
Family and brotherhood— Unity feels so good.
Beautiful gifts from God, building a bond no one can break.
Freedom may be denied, but joy deep inside no one can take.
Sing to Jehovah with all your heart. Serve him through all your days—
No greater joy could there be than this, No matter what we face.
Always rejoice! Always rejoice!
Always rejoice! Always rejoice!
Earth will be a paradise for all eternity. Jesus’ loving sacrifice truly sets us free.
Sing to Jehovah with all your heart. Serve him through all your days—
No greater joy could there be than this, No matter what we face.
Always rejoice! Always rejoice!
Always rejoice! Always rejoice!
Always rejoice! Always rejoice!
Always rejoice! Always rejoice!
Always rejoice! Always rejoice!
Always rejoice! Always rejoice!
Always rejoice!
Now, didn’t that bring a smile to your face?
Our program reminded us
that we can successfully fight discouragement
and remain joyful.
Despite many hardships,
our Sister Aino
remained faithful and happy by staying close to fellow believers
and keeping herself spiritually nourished.
We learned how to build strong friendships,
which are a blessing in times of need
and discouragement.
Bill put his love for God
ahead of his love for music and has enjoyed
a meaningful life serving Jehovah.
And this month’s music video
is a happy song
that we’ll want to sing
again and again.
Now let’s visit our brothers and sisters in Quebec, Canada.
Quebec is the largest Canadian province by land area.
This is home
to more than 24,000 brothers and sisters.
The province is known for its natural beauty:
the St. Lawrence River, thousands of lakes, waterfalls, ski slopes,
and forests.
Quebec is rich with wildlife:
moose, caribou,
beavers, wolves,
and the Snowy Owl.
Jehovah’s people began preaching here in the 1920’s.
Government opposition
stirred up by the clergy began almost immediately.
our brothers held a 16-day campaign
to publicize the State’s disregard
for freedom of worship.
That led to the arrest of hundreds of Jehovah’s Witnesses.
The first to be tried
were Brother Aimé Boucher and his two daughters,
one of whom was just 11 years of age.
the Supreme Court of Canada ruled in their favor,
legally establishing the right of Jehovah’s Witnesses
to preach in Quebec.
Today, our brothers are taking full advantage of this freedom.
Montreal is the province’s largest city.
Publishers enjoy public witnessing
in Montreal’s popular tourist areas, subway system,
and ports, where workers come from many countries.
They preach to students
attending the city’s eight universities and many colleges.
In Quebec City, they even preach in front of the government buildings
where decades ago laws were written to stop our work.
Brother Boucher was from the small town of Lac-Etchemin.
There are 71 publishers
in the congregation here.
Their vast territory
includes a lot of farmland, but their hard work to reach everyone
has produced several Bible studies.
The average midwinter temperature here
is about minus 12 degrees Celsius,
or about 10 degrees Fahrenheit, and it often gets much colder.
Despite the temperature,
our brothers enjoy warm association.
Quebec produces more than 70 percent of the world’s maple syrup.
A favorite candy is maple taffy
—made by boiling the sap
from maple trees, pouring it onto snow,
letting it harden, and then rolling it onto a stick.
Our brothers and sisters in the Lac-Etchemin Congregation
send us their love and greetings.
From the World Headquarters of Jehovah’s Witnesses,
this is JW Broadcasting!

ko.text: 첫 인간들이 여호와 하느님의 통치를 받기를 거부한 이후로
이 세상에는 악과 고통이 가득하게 되었습니다.
땅에 평화와 공의를 가져올 것이라고 가르치셨습니다.
그 왕국은 언제 통치를 시작할 것이었습니까?
그 점을 어떻게 알 수 있습니까?
예언적 의미가 담긴 꿈을 꾸게 하셨습니다.
하늘까지 닿을 정도로 엄청나게 큰 나무 한 그루를 보았습니다.
그런데 그 나무가 잘리더니 그루터기만 남게 되었습니다.
“일곱 때”가 지나자 그 나무는 다시 자라게 되었습니다.
그 꿈은 두 번에 걸쳐 성취될 것이었습니다.
첫 번째로 이 꿈은 느부갓네살왕에게 성취되었습니다.
그는 하늘까지 닿은 그 나무처럼 강력한 세력을 떨치고 있었습니다.
하지만 그는 “일곱 때” 동안 잘려져 있게 되었습니다.
실제로 느부갓네살은 7년 동안 정신이 나가 있었습니다.
그래서 그 기간 동안 통치를 할 수 없었습니다.
일곱 때가 지나자 느부갓네살은 제정신을 되찾고
이것이 그 예언의 첫 번째 성취였습니다.
두 번째 성취는 하느님의 통치권과 관련이 있습니다.
다시 말해 그들은 하느님과 그분의 통치권을 대표했습니다.
하느님께서는 그들이 바빌론 사람들에게 정복되게 하셨습니다.
하느님의 통치권이 중단되는 기간이 시작된 것입니다.
그 기간은 그분이 자신을 대표할 새로운 왕을 세우실 때까지 계속되었습니다.
이번에는 하늘에 있는 누군가가 왕이 될 것이었습니다.
일곱 때는 문자적인 7년보다 긴 기간임이 분명합니다.
그 점을 어떻게 알 수 있습니까?
일곱 때가 그때까지도 끝나지 않았다는 점을 알려 주셨습니다.
“나라들의 정해진 때가 차기까지 나라들에게 짓밟힐” 것이라고 말씀하셨습니다.
따라서 일곱 때는 그 기간의 두 배 즉 2520일입니다.
예수께서 하늘에서 하느님의 왕국의 왕으로 통치하기 시작하셨습니다.
곧 예수께서는 자신과 함께 하늘에서 통치할 자들을 모으는 일을 끝마치실 것입니다.
우리와 우리의 가족을 고통스럽게 하는 모든 문제를 없앨 것입니다.
우리를 진심으로 사랑하시는 왕의 통치를 받으며
행복하게 살아가는 자신의 모습을 그려 보십시오!

en.text: Ever since the first humans rejected Jehovah God as Ruler,
our world has been plagued with evil and suffering.
But Jesus offered hope.
He taught that as King of God’s Kingdom,
he would restore peace and justice to the earth.
But when would that Kingdom begin to rule?
According to the Bible, it is ruling right now!
How do we know that?
Consider what happened over 2,600 years ago.
Jehovah God caused Nebuchadnezzar,
a King of ancient Babylon,
to have a prophetic dream.
In the dream,
Nebuchadnezzar saw a giant tree
that reached all the way to heaven.
The tree was cut down,
but its stump was left in the ground.
After a period of “seven times,”
the tree grew again.
The Bible indicates that this dream
would have two fulfillments.
The first had to do
with King Nebuchadnezzar himself.
He was very prominent
—like the tree that reached
all the way to heaven.
But he was cut down for “seven times.”
This happened when Nebuchadnezzar
lost his sanity for seven years.
During that time,
he was unable to rule as king.
At the end of the seven times,
Nebuchadnezzar regained his sanity
and started ruling again.
That was the first fulfillment of this prophecy.
What was the second fulfillment?
It had to do with God’s rulership.
The Bible says that kings in ancient Israel
“sat on Jehovah’s throne.”
In other words,
they represented God and his rulership.
However, most of those kings
became disobedient to Jehovah
and so did most of their subjects.
Because of their disobedience,
God allowed the Israelites
to be conquered by the Babylonians,
who destroyed the city of Jerusalem
in 607 B.C.E.
From that time on,
no more kings represented Jehovah
in Jerusalem.
Thus, 607 B.C.E.
marked the beginning of the seven times,
or the period when God’s rulership
would be interrupted.
That period would last
until Jehovah installed
a new king to represent Him
—this time, someone in heaven.
When would that happen?
In the second fulfillment of this prophecy,
the seven times must be
more than seven literal years.
How do we know?
For one thing, nothing significant
relating to God’s rulership happened
seven years after Jerusalem was destroyed.
And centuries later,
Jesus indicated that the seven times
had not yet ended.
In a prophecy about the last days,
Jesus said that Jerusalem,
or God’s rulership,
would “be trampled on by the nations
“until the appointed times of the nations
are fulfilled.”
“The appointed times of the nations”
are the same as the “seven times.”
When would those “times” end?
The Bible book of Revelation says
that three and a half times
equal 1,260 days.
So seven times is double that number,
or 2,520 days.
In Bible prophecy,
a day can represent a year.
That is the case with the prophecy
about the seven times.
They represent 2,520 years.
Counting forward from 607 B.C.E.,
2,520 years
takes us to the year 1914
—the year that the seven times ended
and Jesus began ruling from heaven
as King of God’s Kingdom.
That began a period
that the Bible calls “the last days.”
Soon,
Jesus will finish gathering
the rest of his corulers to join him in heaven.
God’s Kingdom will then undo every problem
that afflicts us and our families.
Imagine living there
under the rulership of a King
who really cares about you!

cn.text: 人类的始祖拒绝耶和华上帝的统治

高得顶天

过了“七期”
树又再次长了起来
圣经透露
这个梦会有两次应验
第一次应验在尼布甲尼撒王自己身上
他就像那棵高得顶天的树
很有威望和权力
但他像树一样被砍下
经过“七期”
这是怎样发生的呢？
尼布甲尼撒失去理智
有7年的时间不能治理国家
在7年结束的时候
他恢复了理智

这就是这个预言的第一次应验
预言的第二次应验
跟上帝的统治权有关
圣经说
古代以色列的历任君王
“坐在耶和华的宝座上”
也就是说
他们代表上帝和他的统治权
可是，大多数的君王都反叛耶和华
他们的人民普遍也不服从上帝
由于他们的反叛
上帝允许巴比伦人打败以色列人
在公元前607年
巴比伦人毁灭了耶路撒冷城
从那时起
耶路撒冷就再也没有君王
代表耶和华施行统治
因此“七期”开始于公元前607年
上帝的统治权在那时中断了
这段时期会持续到
