title: 제149기 길르앗 졸업식—결론 연설 및 임명

ko.text: 케네스 쿡 형제가 할 다음 연설을 위해
쿡 형제의 연설을 잘 들어 보시죠.
여러분은 이 목표를 향해 경주를 해 온 것입니다.
즉 생명의 경주의 일부분임을 잊지 않았습니다.
충실한 하느님의 종들은 목표를 하나씩 이루면서
그런 목표들은 경주의 여러 구간과 같습니다.
목표들과 달리는 속도가 다를 수 있죠.
최종 결승선 너머에 있는 상에 도달할 때까지
우리가 그 상을 계속 추구하도록 도와줍니다.
하늘의 희망을 추구했던 사도 바울을 생각해 보시죠.
바울은 결승선 너머를 볼 수 있었고,
그분은 매우 고통스러운 지상 행로를 걸으셨지만,
충절을 지키고 그 행로를 끝까지 걸음으로
그분은 자신이 누리게 될 끝없는 기쁨을 보셨습니다.
그는 자신 앞에 놓인 기쁨을 위해,
우릴 위해 자신을 대속물로 주는 데서 오는 기쁨
다시 함께 있을 때 누리게 될 기쁨에
그분은 결승선 너머에 있는 상에서 눈을 떼지 않으셨습니다.
이제 우리가 생명의 경주를 완주하는 데
첫째, 경주의 각 구간을 어떻게 달려야 합니까?
경주의 각 구간을 어떻게 달려야 합니까?
각 구간 즉 연속되는 목표가 있습니다.
디모데 전서 6:19은 그 최종 목표 즉 상이
탄자니아의 한 마라톤 선수를 본받을 수 있습니다.
경기 도중 그는 다른 선수들과 부딪혀서
그는 더 이상 메달을 따기 위해 뛰는 게 아니었죠.
여러분을 넘어지게 만드는 경험을 할지 모릅니다.
다른 사람의 말과 행동에 영향을 받아
믿기지 않는다는듯이 말하는 장면을 상상해 보십시오.
갈라디아의 일부 사람들에게 어떤 문제가 있었든,
우리 모두는 이 교훈을 잊지 말아야 합니다.
그들도 격려를 받아 똑같이 하게 될 겁니다.
계속 형제 자매들을 안정시키는 역할을 하십시오.
모든 것을 여호와의 영광을 위해 하셨고,
자신의 발걸음을 밀접히 따르게 하셨’다고 말합니다.
우리가 상을 얻는 데 왜 필요한지 알아보겠습니다.
수업 때 믿음의 본들에 관해 많이 배웠죠.
참을성 있게 여러 달을 기다려야 했습니다.
여호와께선 일이 잘 풀리게 해 주셨죠.
강사들과 또 도움을 준 많은 형제들은
여러분은 수업을 통해 온전한 유익을 얻었습니다.
앞으로 우리 모두가 어떤 새로운 시련을 만나든
믿음이 필요하다는 점을 잘 보여 줍니다.
실제 달리기 경주에서도 계속 잘 달리려면
또렷한 영적 시각을 가지고 앞을 바라봐야 합니다.
결승선 너머의 상에 계속 초점을 맞춰야 하죠.
믿음이 없는 사람은 볼 수 없습니다.
하지만 믿음이 있으면 볼 수 있습니다.
여호와의 약속들에 계속 초점을 맞출 수 있는 것입니다.
바울은 이 영감 받은 말씀을 기록하면서
보지 못하게 하는 일이 없게 하라고 격려했습니다.
그것은 우리에게 점점 더 커져 가는
보이지 않는 것을 계속 바라보고 있습니다.
하늘 희망을 가진 사람들에게 이 말을 한 것이었지만,
이 말씀에 들어 있는 사상과 바울의 격려는
참생명 즉 “영원한” 생명을 위한 경주를 하는
우리가 굳은 결의로 초점을 잃지 않는다면
매일 충실히 여호와를 섬길 수 있습니다.
너의 시선은 똑바로 정면을 향해야 한다”고 말합니다.
그렇게 하는 데 큰 도움이 될 것입니다.
여러분의 훌륭한 믿음과 본을 본받을 것입니다.
계속 하느님의 뜻을 행하는 데 초점을 맞추십시오.
또는 다 이룬 것 같다는 생각이 들 때가
물질과 같은 다른 것들에 관심이 가게 될 것입니다.
자기만족에 빠지는 일이 결코 없게 하십시오.
여호와를 섬기며 누리는 특권을 소중히 여기되,
더 중요한 것 즉 여호와를 기쁘시게 하고
그분은 늘 앞에 있는 것을 보셨습니다.
이제 우리가 살펴볼 두 번째 특성은
왜 경주를 하는 데 용기가 필요할까요?
예레미야를 저수조에서 꺼내 주려고 왔을 때
덕분에 그는 계속 용기를 나타낼 수 있었죠.
용기는 결승선까지 가는 길에 놓여 있는
하느님의 뜻을 행하기로 굳게 결심한 여러분 앞에
상이 기다리고 있다는 걸 잊지 마십시오.
우리가 보고 있는 일들은 일시적인 것입니다.
믿음과 용기를 가지고 계속 나아갈 것입니다.
앞서 말한 탄자니아의 올림픽 마라톤 선수를
부상을 당한 뒤 그는 붕대를 감고
메달 때문에 계속 달린 게 아니었습니다.
결승선 너머에 있는 더 중요한 걸 본 것입니다.
경기 후에 그가 한 말에서 알 수 있는데요.
경기를 시작하라고 저를 보낸 게 아니라
그가 고통 속에서도 계속 달릴 수 있도록
훨씬 더 중요한 경주를 하고 있습니다.
참생명을 얻을 수 있는 방식으로 달리기 위해
우리가 받은 것들을 잘 활용할 책임이죠.
예수의 본과 앞에 놓인 상을 열렬히 바라보면서
길르앗 학생 여러분과 모든 그리스도인을 위한
그리고 그 후에 있을 결정적인 시험 기간에
지상 낙원에서 영원한 생명을 상으로 받게 될 것입니다.
생명책에 지워지지 않는 기록으로 남게 될 것입니다.”
그 시험의 날을 무사히 통과할 것입니다.
그들은 앞에 놓인 상을 똑바로 바라보면서
믿음, 용기 그리고 그 밖의 모든 경건한 특성들은
충실한 자들이 참생명을 얻게 해 줄 겁니다.
길르앗 훈련을 활용해 경주를 잘 달리십시오.
퐁스리 형제 부부는 태국으로 돌아갈 것입니다.
톰슨 형제 부부는 잠비아로 돌아갈 것입니다.
힘찬 박수를 보내는 소리가 들리는 것 같습니다.
커잔 형제, 다시 한 번 부탁합니다.
제149기 길르앗 학급에 초대를 받았을 때
앞으로 우리에게 어떤 일이 있을 것인지
또한 우리를 마음으로 따뜻하게 환영해 준
매일 이런 질문을 받은 것 같습니다.
인내와 사랑, 다른 사람에 대한 관심,
양들을 돌보는 방법에 관해 베델 가족에게서
우리는 베델 가족이 나타낸 훌륭한 본을 항상 기억하고
다른 사람을 대할 때 그 본을 따르기 위해 노력할 것입니다.
또 인도하는 형제들이 여호와와 그분의 마련을
따라서 그 형제들이 나타낸 훌륭한 본을 통해
우리가 성경을 더 폭넓고 깊이 있게 이해하도록
우리는 이곳에서 한 모든 경험 덕분에
더 잘 그려 볼 수 있게 되었습니다.
우리는 임명을 수행할 때 이곳에서의 기억과
그리스도인 특성을 더 잘 나타내게 됐다는 것을
땅끝까지 지으신 창조주 여호와에 관해 말합니다.
힘이 없는 자에게 기력을 채워 주신다.”
여기서 말하는 능력이란 그런 것이 아닙니다.
소년과 청년도 지칠 수 있다고 말합니다.
여호와께선 어떤 종류의 힘을 주실 것이라고
그 힘은 우리의 신체적인 힘이 허락하는 한,
우리가 신권 활동을 할 수 있게 해 줍니다.
또한 이 힘은 시련을 인내하게 해 줍니다.
이 구절은 희망과 힘을 연관 짓습니다.
여호와께 희망을 두고 그분의 힘에 의지한다면,
길르앗 졸업식 사회자로 임명을 완수할 수 있을지
그런데 벌써 졸업식이 끝날 때가 다 됐군요.
이 성구도 희망과 힘을 연관 짓습니다.
우리가 하고 싶은 기도가 이 구절에 담겨 있습니다.
모든 기쁨과 평화를 가득 채워 주셔서,

en.text: With those lyrics ringing in our ears,
it puts us in the mind for the next talk
to be delivered by Brother Kenneth Cook.
The title is “Look Beyond the Finish Line.”
Brother Cook, you have piqued our interest.
You have completed your Gilead schooling.
You’ve done well, and we warmly commend you.
You’ve reached the finish line for this school.
When the program concludes, you will be a graduate.
You’ve run this course, so to speak,
with that goal in mind, haven’t you?
Yet, through it all, you’ve also kept in mind that,
for you, this experience is a part of a bigger race
—the race for life.
Like determined runners,
loyal servants of God keep moving forward
after each goal in their service to him.
Such goals are like stages in a race.
Some of our goals and our pace may vary
from person to person based on circumstances.
For you, Gilead School
is a goal, or stage, that you have now completed.
But keep running!
See, we run until we reach what our faith shows us,
the prize waiting beyond the ultimate finish line
—everlasting life in the service of Jehovah.
The promises found in God’s Word
move us to keep reaching out for that prize.
Consider the apostle Paul, who was reaching out for the heavenly hope.
At 2 Timothy 4:7, 8,
he indicated that he had reached the finish line.
His prize was in sight, and it was reserved for him.
He said: “I have fought the fine fight,
“I have run the race to the finish, I have observed the faith.
“From this time on, there is reserved for me
the crown of righteousness.”
With strong faith, Paul could see beyond the finish line
and he yearned for the reward that he would receive.
And then there is Jesus’ example.
Just before breathing his last,
he cried out: “It has been accomplished!”
Throughout his earthly ministry,
that goal to accomplish Jehovah’s will for him
never left his sight.
No matter how painful his life course proved to be,
Jesus kept his integrity and finished that course,
like the true Son of God that he is.
In all of this, Jesus saw more than just the finish line.
He saw the endless joy that was waiting for him.
So powerful is Jesus’ example
that Hebrews 12:2 urges us
to keep it centered in our sight.
We invite you to follow along there with Hebrews 12:2.
It says: “. . . as we look intently
“at the Chief Agent and Perfecter of our faith, Jesus.
“For the joy that was set before him he endured a torture stake,
“despising shame, and has sat down
at the right hand of the throne of God.”
Who are we urged to look at intently?
The “Perfecter of our faith, Jesus.”
And what did Jesus look at?
What did he see?
He saw the joy that his faith placed directly in front of him.
Jesus focused on the joy that would result
from his life course of perfect integrity,
from providing the ransom for us,
and from being back alongside his heavenly Father.
Jesus never took his eyes off the prize waiting beyond the finish line,
and neither should we.
Let’s look at some important lessons
that will help all of us to complete the race for life.
We will consider two main points:
first, how should you run each stage of the race?
and, second, qualities that will help you
to run like a true Christian and win.
Now, for the first point: How should you run each stage of the race?
The race for life is a race of endurance,
and as mentioned, it includes stages, or successive goals.
We strive for each goal at our individual best pace
and with a clear focus on the ultimate goal, or prize.
First Timothy 6:19
calls that prize “the real life”
—that is, everlasting life in perfection,
either in heaven or on earth.
As mentioned, your Gilead training
is now a completed stage of the race for you.
With humility, apply all that you have learned
and remain focused on the endless joy ahead of you.
When hardships and difficulties come
—and they will— keep moving forward.
If you are knocked down by anything,
get back up and run with determination,
with everything that you’ve got.
Be like the marathon runner from the country of Tanzania
who ran in the 1968 Olympics held in Mexico City.
At one point during that race, he was bumped by other runners,
and he fell to the ground so hard
that he gashed his knee and dislocated it.
He also smashed his shoulder against the pavement.
Yet, after receiving some medical attention,
he refused to stop running.
He continued in the race.
His pace was slower, but he moved forward toward his goal.
He was no longer running for a mere material prize.
He was running to complete the race
with his honor intact and that of the land he represented.
He finished the race.
In the race for life,
you may experience times when you feel as if someone or something
is trying to knock you down.
What will you do?
Learn from what happened to the Galatians.
When some in the first century allowed the speech and actions of others
to knock them out of the race, notice what Paul said to them
at Galatians 5:7, 8.
Imagine that he has an incredulous tone
as he speaks to them and states in verse 7:
“You were running well.
“Who hindered you from continuing to obey the truth?
This sort of persuasion does not come from the One calling you.”
What was the problem?
Some in Galatia had allowed themselves
to be persuaded by false teachings,
and they were no longer obeying the truth.
They gave in to pressure.
Also, in verse 13,
Paul refers to the danger of “fleshly desires.”
Whatever happened to them,
those Christian runners were “hindered,”
as he said, because they took their eyes off of the prize.
All of us must keep that lesson in front of us.
If we do, we will never be hindered or thrown off course
in our pursuit of the real life.
We will be rock solid in our focus.
When others see that you are looking straight ahead toward the prize,
they’re helped to look in the same direction.
Continue to be a real stabilizing influence
in the branches where you will serve.
So for our first point, how should you run each stage of the race?
Run at your very best pace
and with a clear focus on your ultimate goal
—the real life.
Now, for our second main point:
qualities that will help you
to run like a true Christian and win.
We run as true Christians
when we follow the example of Christ.
Jesus’ example of doing all things for Jehovah’s glory,
despite the suffering that he endured,
is one that we must follow.
First Peter 2:21 reminds us
that “Christ suffered for you,
leaving a model for you to follow his steps closely.”
Let’s consider two qualities
that Jesus had in abundance and that we must imitate closely
—faith and courage.
For each quality, we will look at why we need it to win.
So we begin with faith.
Now, you do not need to be told what faith is.
You have it, and you’ve learned much about examples of faith in your studies.
We need faith because faith helps us to endure,
and faith helps us to remember
that our trials in life are temporary.
We look ahead with confidence,
we see beyond the troubles of today,
and we trust Jehovah every step of the way.
You needed to have faith after you arrived for this school
and then had to wait patiently for some months for your classes to begin.
True?
You no doubt wondered: ‘When will the classes start?
How will they be carried out in a pandemic?’
You waited, and in due time your faith was rewarded.
Jehovah saw to it that things worked out, didn’t he?
Your instructors and so many others working with them
ensured that the school moved forward safely
and that you received the full benefit from the classes.
That experience highlights the kind of faith
that all of us will need in the days ahead
whenever new challenges arise.
You could say that 20/20 vision will be necessary
for each of us to keep running successfully.
And I don’t mean the year 2020.
True Christians look far ahead with clear,
spiritual vision —that’s the point—
and remain focused on the prize beyond the finish line.
Those without faith cannot see it.
They cannot focus on things unseen.
But those with faith can see it.
That is why they —why you—
remain focused on Jehovah’s promises.
The Scriptures urge us to keep looking ahead.
An example of this is found
at 2 Corinthians 4:17, 18
—2 Corinthians 4:17, 18.
Now, when writing these inspired words,
Paul was encouraging the brothers
not to allow problems, difficulties, and persecutions
to cloud or block their view
of the glorious reward that was set before them.
Please look at what is said starting in verse 17:
“For though the tribulation is momentary and light,
“it works out for us a glory
“that is of more and more surpassing greatness and is everlasting;
“while we keep our eyes,
“not on the things seen, but on the things unseen.
“For the things seen are temporary,
but the things unseen are everlasting.”
Again, these inspired words
should move us to look beyond the trials we face
and to remain focused on what is ahead of us.
Paul was speaking to those with the heavenly hope.
But the encouragement and meaning behind these words
apply to all who are running for the real life,
that is, for the things “everlasting,”
as it says here.
When we are determined and focused,
we are helped to press on each day.
Proverbs 4:25 tells us to “look straight ahead . . . ,
fix [your eyes or] your gaze straight ahead of you.”
To keep doing that, we need faith.
We need good spiritual eyesight to see
what is otherwise “unseen,” as Paul said.
Keep in mind that the objective of your Gilead training
is to strengthen and stabilize the field and branch organization.
Whether a brother or sister,
your example of faith goes a long way in doing that.
Others will imitate the faith and example of a determined runner.
When you are settled in your assignments,
keep your eyes of faith set on doing God’s will.
Danger can come when you start to feel
that you’ve achieved most or even all of your goals.
What could be the result?
When we lose sight of the race and of its prize,
our interests will focus on other things,
perhaps material things.
Don’t let this happen to you.
Never allow distractions to pull you off of the Christian course,
and avoid ever becoming self-satisfied
because of privileges that you may come to enjoy.
Focus on the real life, and remain humble.
Appreciate your privileges in Jehovah’s service,
but remain focused on what you desire most
—pleasing Jehovah and doing his will forever.
As we read earlier in Hebrews chapter 12,
when Jesus suffered unjustly to the point of death,
he endured “for the joy that was set before him.”
He always looked at what was ahead of him.
The reward that he longed for was clear to him.
It was that real to him.
We must always remember Jesus’ example as we keep looking ahead.
Maintain your strong faith by reading God’s Word every day
and applying its counsel in everything that you do.
We endure in the race with courage
when our faith is strong.
And that is the second quality we will now look at
—courage, why we need courage to win.
True Christians have courage that stems from their faith.
We live with hope, with expectation
—and not just any expectation
but “assured expectation,” as the Scriptures call it.
When your rescue is assured, it gives you courage, doesn’t it?
Imagine how Jeremiah felt when Ebed-melech
and 30 other men arrived to pull him up out of a deep cistern.
What could have seemed hopeless was now a moment filled with hope,
and he continued on with courage.
Courage moves us to look beyond any obstacles
that may stand between us and the finish line.
The fact is that nothing promised in God’s Word will fail to come true.
So take courage.
Keep in mind that your determination to do God’s will
means that for you the prize will be waiting.
Jehovah cannot lie.
Therefore, as you go to your assignments,
remain calm and assured of Jehovah’s help.
True, great changes have taken place in the world
since you arrived for Gilead School.
But though the world is changing around us
(and certainly not for the better),
remember Jehovah’s promises.
What we see happening is temporary.
A pandemic—nothing new!
Jesus foretold it —didn’t he?—
“pestilences,” he called it, “in one place after another.”
So we’re not shaken by this.
We have faith and courage, and we keep going, don’t we?
Think back to the Olympic marathon runner
from Tanzania whom we mentioned earlier.
After being injured, he was bandaged and then continued to run.
It took courage and determination to run,
and sometimes walk, through the pain.
When he eventually crossed the finish line,
he was cheered by the small crowd remaining in the stadium.
Now, try to imagine:
He was limping with his bandages blowing in the wind,
but he moved forward toward his goal.
For many, the race would have been long over.
But that man was running for something more than a material prize.
He saw something greater beyond that finish line.
What was it?
We find it in what he said afterward.
When he was asked why he continued on in the race, he replied:
“My country did not send me 5,000 miles to start the race.
They sent me 5,000 miles to finish the race.”
That sense of responsibility
gave him the courage to go on despite the pain.
He saw a greater purpose, and he returned home with honor.
We too have a greater responsibility
and a far more important race.
We owe it to Jehovah to keep running the Christian course.
He and his Son gave everything,
you could say, so that we can keep running.
We also owe it to others to set a good example for them
that will motivate them never to give up.
And we owe it to ourselves to use what we have been given
so as to run in a way that we gain the real life.
We are certain that you have both the faith and the courage
to run with the eyes of your heart
looking intently at Jesus’ example and at the prize.
So in review, what is the overall lesson
for you Gilead graduates and, really, for every Christian runner?
It is this: Run for the real life at your very best pace
(Jehovah will help you),
run with a clear focus on your ultimate goal,
and run the course with faith and with courage.
When will the finish line be reached?
For those who will live forever on earth,
the Revelation Climax  book states this in chapter 11:
“By exercising faith throughout Jesus’ Millennial Reign
“and during the decisive test that follows,
“these will be rewarded with life everlasting in Paradise on earth.
“Their names will then remain indelibly written
in the book of life.”
For true servants of God, that “decisive test” will be nothing to fear.
They will never drop out of the race.
For them, that test will be just another day on the calendar, so to speak.
They will keep going
with their eyes fixed on what is ahead for them.
Faith, courage, and all other godly qualities
will carry loyal ones into the real life.
Use your Gilead training to run the race well.
Strengthen others to do the same.
See the prize ahead of you.
And follow Jesus’ steps closely.
Run the race through the approaching great tribulation,
and then keep running like a true Christian.
Because of the circumstances, the students have already received their diplomas.
But we know you would like to see them
and hear where they are being assigned.
So I’m happy to have Brother Ronald Curzan with me.
He serves as a helper to the Teaching Committee.
And why am I happy?
Because he’s going to pronounce
all the students’ names for me
and let us know their assignments.
Brother Curzan, we are waiting on you.
Brother and Sister James
will be returning to Trinidad and Tobago.
Brother Kasambala will be returning to Malawi.
Brother Lee will be serving in the United States.
Brother and Sister Luzitu will be returning to Congo (Kinshasa).
Sister Manansala will be returning to the Philippines.
Brother and Sister Mejia will be returning to Colombia.
Brother Mkorongo will be returning to Malawi.
Sister Mtetwa will be returning to Zimbabwe.
Brother Pereira will be returning to Brazil.
Brother and Sister Phongsri will be returning to Thailand.
Brother Reyes will be returning to Mexico.
Brother and Sister Santiago will be returning to the Philippines.
Brother and Sister Sossou will be returning to Côte d’Ivoire.
Brother and Sister Tendeng will be returning to Senegal.
Brother and Sister Thompson will be returning to Zambia.
Brother Tkachuk will be returning to Ukraine.
Brother Zak will be returning to Korea.
Thank you, Brother Curzan.
Well, we have seen them couple by couple
and person by person.
But would you like to see all 25 of these happy graduates together?
There they are.
We can just imagine the applause
from all of your individual apartments and homes out there.
Ron Curzan is still with us,
and that is because we are going to have a letter read from the class.
And since he already knows how to pronounce the brother’s name,
I’m going to let Ron introduce him again.
The class letter will be read by Brother Phongsri.
“To the Governing Body and the Bethel family:
“We were so excited when we received our invitations
“to attend the 149th class of Gilead.
“However, when it was announced
“that the 149th class would be postponed,
“anxiety filled our hearts
“as to what our future would be.
“To help in allaying this anxiety,
“the Governing Body made loving decisions
“to comfort us.
“We never felt abandoned or forgotten.
“One thing we were absolutely confident of
“was that the Governing Body would do all they could
“to make sure we had the class!
“We are ever thankful for the Bethel family
“who warmly welcomed us
“into their hearts and their home.
“It seemed every day someone would ask:
“‘Do you need anything?’ or ‘How can I help you?’
“We have observed this beautiful, obedient Bethel family
“and have learned a lot, especially how to show personal interest
“in concrete ways during difficult times.
“We can say that we had practical lessons
“in endurance, love,
“concern for others, trust in Jehovah,
“obedience, and shepherding.
“This is an example
“that we will take with us in our hearts
“and try to reflect in our dealings with others.
“Once the school started, we could see Jehovah’s hand in the arrangements
“and how the brothers taking the lead trusted in Jehovah
“and the arrangements he had in place.
“As one of our first lessons,
“we want to follow their fine example
“in showing trust in Jehovah
“for whatever lies ahead.
“We were touched by the sincerity
“of our instructors, ‘gifts in men,’
“who helped us to broaden and improve
“our understanding of the Scriptures.
“It is our heartfelt desire
“to do as the psalmist sang
“at Psalm 105:1:
“‘Give thanks to Jehovah,
“‘call on his name,
“make his deeds known among the peoples!’
“Yes, we want to share what we have learned
“with humble hearts,
“all to the praise of our Grand Instructor,
“Jehovah God.
“More than that, we are determined to use all that we have learned
“to continue to grow spiritually
“and be used in whatever way Jehovah decides to use us.
“All that we experienced during our time here
“makes us appreciate
“our loving worldwide brotherhood all the more
“and continues to give us insight
“into what it will be like to live together
“in Jehovah’s new world.
“We take all these memories and lessons we learned here
“on to our assignments,
“and we are determined
“to follow your examples
“in bringing honor and glory
“to our heavenly Father, Jehovah.
“Your brothers and sisters,
the 149th Class of Gilead.”
Thank you for the beautiful sentiments expressed in that class letter.
They were truly heartfelt.
I concluded my opening comments
with Deuteronomy 8:17, 18.
In part, it said: “Remember that it is Jehovah your God
who gives power to you.”
You have had five months of wonderful instruction.
You have learned so much
that you likely did not fully appreciate before.
You have been elevated personally by this experience.
It has improved your knowledge of God’s Word.
You may have already noticed that your Christian personality
has developed even further than when you came.
But always remember:
The gifts you have attained are not by your own power and strength.
Please find with me
Isaiah 40:29-31.
The thought of a source of power
is woven throughout the Scriptures.
Verse 28 is speaking about Jehovah, the Creator of the ends of the earth.
But let’s now read chapter 40, verse 29:
“He gives power to the tired one
and full might to those lacking strength.”
I’m old and tired.
Is Jehovah going to infuse me with physical power and strength?
I wouldn’t complain if he chose to do so,
but that is not the kind of power being discussed.
It’s not physical power.
Well, how do we know it isn’t?
Look at verse 30.
It says, even boys and young men get tired physically.
Verse 30 says:
“Boys will tire out and grow weary,
and young men will stumble and fall.”
So then, what kind of power
can we expect from Jehovah according to these verses?
It’s power to reinvigorate us spiritually.
The power to help us carry out our theocratic activities
to the extent our physical strength allows.
It’s the power to endure the trials of life.
Now, verse 31:
“But those hoping in Jehovah
“will regain power.
“They will soar on wings like eagles.
“They will run and not grow weary;
they will walk and not tire out.”
In that verse, hope and power
are linked together.
By hoping in Jehovah and depending on his strength,
we can soar like an eagle
far above the challenges we face.
We can accomplish the assignments we are given.
I wasn’t sure if I could complete this assignment
as the chairman of Gilead graduation.
But here we are at the last part of the program.
Consider with me a final Scriptural thought
—Romans 15:13.
Here, too, hope and power are linked together.
We can consider this as our prayer for you,
the 25 graduates of the 149th class.
Verse 13:
“May the God who gives hope
“fill you with all joy and peace
“by your trusting in him,
“so that you may abound in hope
with power of holy spirit.”
Trust absolutely in Jehovah and not in yourself.
If you do so, the verse said
you will “abound in hope
with power of holy spirit.”
Holy spirit reminds us of the fruitage of the spirit.
Make it a project to work
on each of the nine aspects of the spirit
mentioned in Galatians 5:22, 23.
We love all of you.
I’m still open to Romans 15.
My concluding comment to you
is in the 33rd verse:
“May the God who gives peace
“be with all of you.
Amen.”

en.text: ‎Can you imagine seeing a valley full of human bones
‎that slowly assemble themselves;
‎grow sinew, muscle, and skin;
‎and then come to life?
‎It must have made the hair on Ezekiel’s neck stand up.
‎But Jehovah gave this vision not to frighten us but to give us hope.
‎That hope is expressed in the title of chapter 10,
‎“You Will Come to Life.”
‎The statement is recorded at Ezekiel 37:5:
‎“This is what the Sovereign Lord Jehovah says to these bones:
‎‛I will cause breath to enter you, and you will come to life.’”
‎This chapter will help you answer these intriguing questions:
‎Why did the exiles in Babylon say that their bones were dry?
‎In what way was the modern-day “Israel of God”
‎in a deathlike situation?
‎How did “the Israel of God” experience a gradual restoration,
‎and when did they “come to life”?
‎How do you feel about being part
‎of the “extremely large army” that Ezekiel’s prophecy foretold?
‎You are living proof
‎that the prophecy we’re about to discuss
‎has been fulfilled.
‎The Governing Body considers it a privilege
‎to serve along with you in the large army of loyal ones
‎who give Jehovah pure worship.

ko.text: 이번 인사이드 스토리에 오신 것을 환영합니다.

온 가족이, 부모님, 누나 부부, 형 부부, 동생 부부
현재 한국 지부 사무실에서 일하고 계신데,
제가 처음에 베델에서 일한 1년 반까지 계산한다면
이렇게 말하는 이유는 두 번 임명받았기 때문이죠.
그건 베델을 떠나는 평범한 이유는 아닌 것 같네요.
모든 남자가 19살이 되면 징집 대상자가 되고,
얼마 후에 입영 통지서를 받게 됩니다.
결국 교도소에서 1년 반 형을 살게 되죠.
하지만 바로 가진 않을 수 있어요.
제 경우에는 처음 재판을 받고 나서
어떤 계획도 세울 수 없는 삶이 힘드셨겠네요?
하지만 언제라도 교도소에 가게 될 수 있다는 걸 알았기 때문에
돈을 버는 데 시간을 사용할 것인가?
제가 가장 먼저 한 건 기도였습니다.
“계획을 세울 때는 우리 생애에 아마겟돈이 오지 않을 것처럼 하고,
생활을 할 때는 아마겟돈이 내일 올 것처럼 해야 한다.”
내일 오지 않을 것처럼 계획을 세우기로 했습니다.
네, 그럼 조금 아까 우리에게 얘기해 준
세 가지 중에서 어느 것을 선택하셨습니까?
제가 호텔에 도착한 대표자들을 환영하는 모습입니다.
실제로 제가 교도소에 들어가게 될 때를 위해
사실 그 기간에 제가 영적으로 성장했거든요.
우리에게 긍정적인 영향을 주는 것 같아요.
베델을 떠나 교도소 생활을 시작해야 했을 때
그때 얘기를 좀 해 주실 수 있나요?
손을 흔들어 주고 저를 격려해 주었어요.
한 형제는 언제나 저를 기억하겠다고 했는데,
그 말이 제 마음속에 계속 남아 있습니다.
교도소에서 어떻게 지내셨는지 말씀해 주실 수 있을까요?

또 “제게 이렇게 훌륭한 믿음의 본을 남겨 주셔서 감사하다”고 말하고 싶어요.
우리 마음에 감동을 주는 아름다운 경험담을 들려주셨습니다.
가족의 역사를 우리 모두에게 알려 주셔서 감사합니다.
이스라엘 지파들은 누구를 섬길 것인지 스스로 선택하라는 말을 들었습니다.
오늘 네 분의 손님이 해 주신 경험담을 통해 배웠듯이,
분명 우리가 하는 선택은 매우 중요합니다.
그 선택은 우리에게, 우리의 가족에게, 전 세계 우리 형제들에게,
오늘 경험담을 듣고 힘과 의욕을 모든 분이 갖게 되셨기를 바랍니다.
그럼 다음 인사이드 스토리에서 여러분을 뵙겠습니다.
끝으로 149기 학급의 모습을 담은 사진을 보실까요?

en.text: Over the past few years, we have all looked forward
to what has affectionately been called
The Inside Story.
This time it will be conducted by another one of the Gilead instructors,
Brother Richard Chilton.
Take it away, Brother Chilton!
Welcome to this edition of The Inside Story.
At Joshua 24:15,
the tribes of Israel were instructed
to “choose for [themselves] . . . whom [they would] serve.”
Well, our four guests today
have had to make some choices of their own
—choices that no doubt contributed
to their qualifying to attend the 149th class of Gilead.
Let’s learn more about the choices they made
and who helped them to do so
as we meet our first guest,
Brother Sung-hee Lee from South Korea.
Welcome, Sung-hee.
Thank you.
Please have a seat.
Well, Sung-hee, you come from a family of worshippers
who have been faithfully serving Jehovah for three generations.
Tell us about them.
Yes.
It began with my grandmother.
She was the first to become a Witness back in 1970.
I’m so grateful to Jehovah that all in my family
—my parents, my sister and her husband,
and my brothers and their wives— are all faithfully serving Jehovah
to this day.
Well, that’s certainly a wonderful heritage to be a part of.
Now, your current assignment is at the branch office in Korea.
How long have you been serving there?
Well, if you count the first one and a half years I served at Bethel,
that would be nine and a half years.
I say that because I was reassigned.
I actually left Bethel to go to prison.
Well, now, that’s not something we typically hear
as a reason for leaving Bethel, is it?
What happened?
You see, in South Korea, all males become eligible
for military conscription when they turn 19,
and a draft notice comes sometime after that.
As for us, Jehovah’s Witnesses,
because we refuse military service,
the result would be a year and a half sentence in prison.
But you may not go right away.
Now, that’s interesting.
What would be the factors that would determine
when your prison sentence would actually begin?
From the time you receive a draft notice until you actually go to prison,
especially in recent times,
that time period was unknown and different for each brother.
A lot depended on the judge you got.
As for me, I had to wait five years
from the time I first appeared in the court
until I finally went to prison.
Well, was that frustrating for you to, in effect,
have your life be placed on hold for five years?
Honestly, yes.
But understanding that I could go to prison at any moment,
I had to make a choice
—a choice as to how I was going to spend my time.
Do I use that time
just staying at home doing nothing and planning nothing,
since I could go into prison at any moment?
Or do I use that time to earn some money
for the time when I’m finally released from prison?
Or
do I use my life to the full, pursuing spiritual things first
while I could do so freely?
Well, that’s quite the situation to be in.
What was your thought process through that?
What did you decide to do given those circumstances?
So the first thing I did was pray.
I prayed and prayed.
And while doing research, I came across an article
in a December 1, 2004, issue of The Watchtower,
which was entitled “Trusting in Jehovah’s Loving Care.”
In that article, there was a quote that said:
“We should plan ahead as if Armageddon
“would not come in our lifetime
but [live] our life as if it would come tomorrow.”
Well, that was the answer I needed.
So I decided to plan ahead
as if my prison term wasn’t coming tomorrow.
OK.
So given those options
that you mentioned to us a minute ago,
what did you decide to do?
So I decided to pioneer.
I also volunteered
at the international convention.
Here I’m welcoming the delegates as they arrive to their hotel.
I also even got accepted to Bethel.
Here I’m working in my assignment.
And here are the brothers and sisters working in the Computer Department,
where I work.
How nice!
Well, let me ask you, how do you feel, Sung-hee, that you benefited
by choosing to pursue spiritual pursuits
while you were waiting for those five years?
Pioneering and Bethel service
really helped me to prepare my heart for the time
when the call finally came to go to prison.
And it was during this period that I really grew spiritually.
Well, I guess pioneering and Bethel
can have that positive effect on a person, can’t it?
But the day did finally arrive —didn’t it?—
when you had to leave and begin your prison sentence.
We can only imagine what
a sobering moment that was for you.
Do you mind telling us about it?
Yes.
When the day came,
many in the Bethel family came outside
to wave me off and to cheer me on.
It was a moment that I’ll never forget.
One brother, he even said he would always remember me in his heart,
and I really cherish what he said to me.
Well, that was very encouraging, no doubt.
Do you mind talking about how life was
for you in prison?
There were definitely moments when I felt anxious.
But my three fleshly brothers and many other Korean brothers
also served their time in prison.
And their choices and experiences
helped me decide how I was going to spend my time in prison.
So I decided to make a list right away
of what to do while in prison.
I made some spiritual goals such as reading the Proclaimers  book
and reading other publications.
And a group of about seven to eight brothers in the same prison cell,
we discussed the daily text together
every day in the evening.
We called it evening worship, similar to morning worship in Bethel.
Well, that was certainly a wise use of the time that you had there.
What can you tell us about the current situation in South Korea
for our brothers in connection with military service?
Just a few months ago, the authorities adopted alternative service
for proven conscientious objectors.
Under this arrangement, you are not labeled as a convicted criminal.
And you don’t live in a prison cell
but live in a more communal living arrangement.
But there is one thing about this alternative service:
Instead of your prison sentence being a year and a half,
you have to do alternative service for three years.
Wow! OK, double the time.
You know, our hearts really go out to our brothers and our sisters
who have served time in prison “for righteousness’ sake.”
But you were able to complete your prison sentence.
What was next for you once you were a free man?
Without hesitation, I immediately filled out
another application to return to Bethel,
and I was accepted to return to Bethel.
Well, good for you.
We’re glad that worked out.
If we could just circle back for just one moment.
You had mentioned
that there was one thing in particular that was especially helpful to you
that helped you endure that difficult time in prison.
Do you mind telling us about it?
Of course.
Many brothers and sisters around the world
wrote to us brothers in prison.
And I personally received a number of them.
In fact, I brought some of them here,
right here, with me.
That someone
who never met me, who never knew me,
wrote such encouraging,
comforting letters, . . .
Yes.
. . . it really warmed my heart
and really comforted me.
It made me feel that I’m never alone
wherever I am in the world
and that I was part of a very special,
close, loving, international brotherhood.
So I read them over and over again,
and I saved all of these letters.
Oh, that is so encouraging, Sung-hee.
But I have to ask you, why did you bring these letters with you to New York?
Actually, some of these letters came
from Bethelites right here
at world headquarters.
I wanted to meet them in person
and tell them how much I appreciated
all those letters and prayers
and how they really helped me to get through my time in prison.
We could certainly understand if those would have been
some tearful reunions for you.
Well, in conclusion, Sung-hee, I just have one last question for you.
You had mentioned earlier that when you were deciding
what you were going to do with the time you had before going to prison,
you said that the first thing that you did was pray.
Why was prayer so important to you?
Through these experiences, I’m absolutely confident
that Jehovah both hears and answers our prayers
when we are faced with choices.
And also I am confident that by means of the prayers
that were offered in my behalf,
Jehovah helped me to stick to the choices that I had made
to stay loyal to him.
So please keep praying for our brothers in prison
wherever they are in the world.
And please keep writing them letters.
Well, I can assure you, Sung-hee,
we’ll continue to do just that.
Thank you so much for sharing your encouraging experience with us.
It really touched our hearts.
Well, next on our program,
we’re going to go all the way to West Africa,
where our next guests will be coming from, the country of Senegal.
We’ll meet Alain and Achaïe Tendeng.
Well, Alain and Achaïe, welcome.
Nice to have you with us on The Inside Story.
Thank you.
It’s a pleasure to have you.
Now, I understand that your current assignment
has you serving at the branch office in Senegal, West Africa.
Now, Alain, Senegal is your home,
born and raised.
But, Achaïe, I understand that you come
from the neighboring country of Mali.
In fact, I was told that your mother
comes from a very interesting part of the country of Mali.
Can you tell us about it?
Yes.
My mother is from Timbuktu.
In fact, when I was young,
she took me there to visit her family.
Now, Achaïe, you are probably the first person that we have ever met
that has actually been to Timbuktu.
What is it like?
Well,
as you can see on the screen,
that is what the region of Timbuktu looks like.
It is in the Sahara Desert,
which stretches on for thousands of kilometers.
Well, it’s obviously a very vast territory.
But what can you tell us about the people of the Timbuktu region?
The people there live a nomadic lifestyle
and are nearly all Muslims.
Actually, both my two parents are from a Muslim background.
Now, that’s quite interesting.
Given that background, what were some of the challenges
that you had to face in becoming one of Jehovah’s Witnesses?
Although I got baptized at 15 years of age,
I didn’t always make the best choices in my teen years,
and I had to suffer the consequences of those choices.
However, in my early 20’s,
I decided to build a strong
and personal relationship with Jehovah.
To be able to do so, I received help
from spiritually mature brothers and sisters,
such as pioneers, elders,
missionaries.
For example, this is my spiritual mother on the left side of the screen
and, on the right side of the screen, her missionary companion,
who is still serving in Mali faithfully
for 45 years now.
All of these mature persons helped me
to see the value of personal study
and “thinking ability.”
Once I got this good habit of reasoning on Bible principles,
I could make good choices that pleased Jehovah,
such as leaving my well-paying job
and starting pioneering.
It was not easy, however,
because there was still this family pressure
for me to get a good job and earn a good living.
But I’m still striving to try to make good decisions
that please Jehovah.
Well, that’s encouraging.
In spite of the pressures that you had to face,
you obviously continued making good decisions,
because you were eventually appointed to serve
as a special pioneer—weren’t you?— in the southern part of Mali
in a region called Sikasso.
Tell us about that, please.
Yes, I was so happy there.
The preaching work was wonderful.
I really enjoyed it.
And this is the Kingdom Hall where I served.
And one day, we received a visit from a circuit overseer
—a single circuit overseer.
OK.
Now, I could see when you made that comment, you looked over at Alain.
So we can only assume that, Alain,
you were this young, handsome,
single circuit overseer
who visited Achaïe’s congregation in Sikasso.
Is that right?
Well, I visited the congregation.
But we had already met previously at a circuit assembly.
So we knew each other.
But at the time, there was nothing special going on.
OK.
Well, thank you for the clarification.
We appreciate that.
But since we’re now talking to you, Alain,
maybe we can hear a little bit about your story.
Did you always want to be a circuit overseer?
Well, no.
In fact, when I was a boy,
I wanted to become a Catholic priest.
Oh, really?
Yes.
Being raised in a Catholic family,
at 13, I went to get training
by one of the Catholic religious orders.
But after just the one year of training, I chose to leave.
Although I left,
I still had a love for the Bible.
One day, I went to one of my friends
to see if he would like to play soccer with me.
But he was about to have a Bible study
with one of Jehovah’s Witnesses who was a missionary.
So I decided
to stay and listen.
Over time, I came to really love
what I was studying in the Bible.
And eventually
I got baptized at the age of 17, as shown here.
Wow!
Now, that’s quite interesting.
You had mentioned to me before
that your parents are not Jehovah’s Witnesses.
How did they respond to your becoming baptized as one?
Well, it was not easy for them to accept.
They had an expectation of me
helping support the family financially.
At the same time, I really wanted to pioneer.
So it took several years and much struggling,
but eventually I was able to enter into the pioneer service.
Was there anyone in your life at that time
who helped you to stay spiritually focused
as you were trying to achieve these spiritual goals?
Oh, yes.
Like Achaïe, while working
toward entering into the pioneer service,
I too chose to associate
with spiritually strong ones in the congregation.
Missionaries, like this couple,
helped me to see the importance
of putting and keeping
spiritual things first in life.
And this helped me to remain focused.
Eventually, I was able to serve in unassigned territory.
Going throughout the territory with my motorbike
was a really good time
that I enjoyed there.
Oh, you know, I’ve always wanted one of those.
Yes.
And later I was invited to attend the School for Single Brothers.
And after that, I was trained in the circuit work.
And this couple shown here is the missionary couple
who first started my Bible study.
He’s the one who provided the training for the circuit work.
Oh, we can only imagine that they must have been so proud of you,
to see the spiritual progress that you had made.
But now let’s fast forward just a little bit in the story.
At this point, now, you’re serving as a circuit overseer.
Achaïe is serving as a special pioneer in Sikasso.
And, Achaïe, you’ve been sitting there so patiently waiting.
Thank you, by the way.
Would you like to continue the story?
Yes.
When we got to know each other better,
we decided to get married.
In fact, we were married in Senegal on a Tuesday,
and later that same week, we had to be
in Guinea-Bissau for the circuit assembly.
OK, if we could just pause for just a moment here.
So if we’re understanding this,
Alain, please, please tell us
that there were no circuit overseers or substitute circuit overseers
available in all of West Africa
who could cover that circuit assembly for you.
You were married four days and had to be in another country for an assembly?
There was no one
who could take care of that assembly for you?
Really?
Brother Chilton, that was fine.
As you already know, the blessings of Jehovah
are far beyond any sacrifices we can make in his service.
We really loved that work.
We loved being with our brothers and sisters.
Oh, yes, we really loved to preach with them.
You can see in this picture—
Preaching with them —it’s really so special to us.
Seeing them in this picture even brings very nice memories.
Yeah.
We enjoyed also being with them in their homes,
seeing their strong faith, and seeing their love for Jehovah
despite the challenges they were facing.
We really came to love them very much.
Well, just taking a look at your happy smiles in that picture there,
we can see that you not only loved the work
but that you loved the people that you were serving.
But as we know, changes come, don’t they?
And you received the change of assignment from the circuit work
into Bethel in Senegal.
In fact, I understand this picture
was taken just two months before you came to New York
to begin your Gilead training.
It’s with Brother Splane providing a shepherding visit to your Bethel family
—beautiful family, by the way.
Now, from our previous discussions, it became very clear to me
how much you both love and appreciate the young people
who are in our organization.
From your personal observations,
what would you say were the things that you saw as key elements
to their achieving spiritual success,
from your own observations?
What I have observed
is that young ones who make the truth their own
and who keep their spiritual routines
to be able to continue building
a spiritual, personal relationship with Jehovah
and who continue to associate
with spiritually mature brothers
who can help them keep their focus
are those who are more successful
in their Christian course of life.
I really pray to Jehovah that all our young ones
may have this same experience
—that they may “taste and see that Jehovah is good,”
as mentioned at Psalm 34:8.
If they do, they can see that Jehovah is able
to open doors for them where they think that there is no door to be opened.
And that will lead them to a long and satisfying life
without any regrets.
Oh, those are some beautiful comments.
Thank you very much for that, Achaïe.
What about you, Alain?
Well, looking back,
I can see that Jehovah has really been kind and good to us.
He has provided brothers and sisters, mature ones,
who helped us to have the courage
to put him first in our lives.
Their choices encouraged us
to make good choices.
And Jehovah has blessed us in ways
we could never foresee.
And we are confident that he will do
the same with all our brothers and sisters,
including young ones
who courageously put Jehovah first in their lives.
Well, we thank you both so much
for your encouraging comments.
And our prayer will be that Jehovah continues to bless you both
as you both keep making wise decisions in his service.
Thank you so much for joining us today.
Thank you. Thank you.
Well, last but certainly not least,
we go all the way to the country of Ukraine
to meet our next, final guest on our program.
Let’s give our attention as we meet Brother Anzhel Tkachuk.
Welcome, Anzhel.
Thank you.
It’s a pleasure to have you with us on The Inside Story  today.
Now, Anzhel, it’s often been said
that a person’s story
takes us on a journey of a lifetime.
Your story, however, my friend,
takes us on a journey of several lifetimes.
Isn’t that true?
Yes.
You know, my great-great-grandfather
and great-great-grandmother
were the first Jehovah’s Witnesses
in my family.
And here you can see them
in the 1940’s in Ukraine.
Well, that is definitely
a wonderful heritage to be a part of.
Would you say, Anzhel, that the choices
that members of your family made over the years
had a direct bearing on your being here
attending the 149th class of Gilead?
Definitely yes.
You know, they were serving Jehovah for many, many years.
They had a very hard but interesting life,
a life full of many different stories.
For example, when my great-grandfather was exiled to Siberia
because of being one of Jehovah’s Witnesses,
my great-grandmother would send him magazines
hidden in bottles of pork fat.
You said pork fat.
OK, now, that sounds pretty interesting.
Can you tell us more about this “secret pork fat recipe”
of your great-grandmother?
OK, so my mom took some photos
and sent them to me to explain how it was done.
So as you can see here, first this fat was melted
so that you could have liquid fat;
then we needed to wait so that this fat would become hard and thick.
Then a magazine was wrapped in linen
and a hole was made into the fat.
And then this wrapped magazine was put in the hole,
and more fat was put on top
to hide this magazine, and now it’s done.
Now you have both physical and spiritual food in one bottle.
Well, there it is, everything you need to survive in Siberia, right?
Well, let me ask you, did the guards in Siberia
ever find those magazines hidden in pork fat?
Sadly, yes.
And that’s why they added an additional five and a half years
to my great-grandfather’s exile time in Siberia.
But soon, his son, my grandfather
was exiled to Siberia too.
And here you can see my great-grandfather on the left
and my grandfather on the right.
Well, now you shared with us some details about your great-grandfather.
What can you tell us about your grandfather, depicted on the right?
You know, he was so zealous for Jehovah.
While in Siberia, he was helping in supplying Bible literature
for local brothers and sisters
though it was not always safe to do it.
Well, clearly they were both courageous men.
When were your family members allowed to leave Siberia
and return to Ukraine?
It was in 1967/1968.
And it was then when my grandfather started
to reproduce Bible magazines and books,
and the whole family helped.
That’s amazing!
Were there any particular methods
that they used to accomplish this?
They used several different methods.
For example, they used
a special photo machine like you see here
to make photos of the magazines.
This and machines similar to these machines
were used to make,
so to say, “handmade” literature.
Well, just looking at those photos,
we could see
that the men in your family were both courageous and zealous.
Yes, they were.
But so were the women in our family.
Here in this photo, you can see my great-grandmother with her daughter,
and it was she who sent
these magazines hidden in the bottles of pork fat.
And here you can see my grandmother on my mother’s side.
She was a Witness too.
And here you can see her with her children.
And this little girl with a guitar is my mom.
And, you know, once the government
wanted to separate them.
They wanted to have a public hearing
to take all her children away.
Why they wanted to do it was because it was when in the Soviet Union
all children were forced to support political ideas of the government.
But my grandmother’s children chose not to do it.
Now, that’s interesting;
the children made this choice.
But what about your grandmother when she was forced to make this choice
between what the Communist Party was dictating
and what Jehovah said, what did she do?
She wanted to prove and to show that she was a good mother
and that she was a good mother because she was one of Jehovah’s Witnesses,
because she believed in God.
And, you know, even during this hearing,
one woman stood up and screamed,
“Don’t listen to her, as you will become one of Jehovah’s Witnesses too!”
But people said, “No, we want to hear more.”
So she kept going.
And when she finished,
all the people voted in her favor
that she could keep all her children with her.
And here you can see my grandmother years later
with her family—children and grandchildren.
Wow! That is an absolutely incredible story!
Obviously, Jehovah blessed her for her loyal efforts there.
But, now, Anzhel,
as you reflect upon the decisions
that members of your family have made,
how have their decisions affected you?
You know, they helped me to love Jehovah with all my heart
and to put him always first in my life.
Can you provide us an example of that?
Yes, for example, in Ukraine
all young men are required to do military service.
But I, like many other brothers, chose not to do it.
I chose civilian, or alternative, service instead.
So I was still living at home.
And the government gives you any work that they want,
and you need to do it for two years.
If you don’t mind my asking, what job did they give you?
So, OK, they sent me to clean sewers
and water systems.
So I needed to go inside these tanks, which were so filthy,
and I needed to clean them out.
And for me, it was really very hard work.
And sometimes I felt very sad about my situation.
Yeah.
We’re so sorry, Anzhel, that you had to go through that.
But we certainly appreciate your loyalty to Jehovah at the same time.
What helped you to get through
that difficult period in your life?
For me, it was my family.
I would think about my grandfather, grandmother,
great-grandfather and great-grandmother.
And I thought: ‘They showed me how to do it.
‘They showed me how to go through it.
They showed me that with Jehovah’s help, I can do it.’
Well, you have learned some very powerful lessons from your family.
And now here you are at Gilead.
You’ve completed your Gilead training.
And we can only imagine how proud and happy your family must be for you.
Can you tell us, though, what has been the highlight for you
from your Gilead training?
Yes, Gilead has helped me to see more,
to understand more, and to feel more
—to see more this wonderful history of Jehovah’s people
(this wonderful heritage that we all have),
to understand more these wonderful, deep Bible gems
(Bible lessons for my life),
and to feel more of Jehovah’s love
and the love of the brothers and sisters, especially here.
You know, my family, they had just a few magazines,
a few books, and a songbook,
but it was enough for them
to build strong faith in Jehovah.
So in the new world,
I want to see all of my big, big family.
And I want to share with them these wonderful gems
I learned here in Gilead while they were sleeping.
And I want to say to them, “Thank you
for setting such a good example of faith for me.”
Anzhel, you have certainly touched our hearts
by means of that beautiful story.
Thank you for sharing your family legacy with all of us.
We really appreciated that.
Thank you.
Well, as we mentioned in our opening comments,
when the tribes of Israel were instructed
to choose for themselves whom they would serve,
their response is recorded at Joshua 24:18,
where they said: “We too will serve Jehovah,
because he is our God”
—a wise choice, indeed!
As we’ve learned from the experiences
shared by our four guests today,
the choices that we make do matter.
They matter to us,
to our family members,
to our worldwide brotherhood,
and especially to our loving God, Jehovah.
We hope that you have been both encouraged and motivated
by the experiences you’ve heard today.
Until we meet again on our future edition of The Inside Story,
please enjoy this brief, little snapshot
of Class 149.
We were not disappointed.
Thank you, Brother Chilton, along with the students who assisted you.

《基列有约》这个节目，也很期待这个访谈
这一次基列导师
理查德·奇尔顿弟兄会主持这个节目
有请奇尔顿弟兄
欢迎来到本期的《基列有约》节目
在约书亚记24:15中
约书亚让以色列各部族
“自己选择......他们要敬奉谁”
今天我们请到的4位学员
都曾作出过一些选择

한 사람이 성경 인물 이름을 말하면
다음 사람은 그 인물의 마지막 글자로 시작하는
성경 인물들에 대해 많은 점을 배웠습니다.
가족이 함께 노아 방주 모형을 만들었습니다.
우리 아이들은 오리지널송을 거의 다 외웠어요.
성경에 나오는 사건으로 연극을 해 보기도 했어요.
두루마리 휴지로 우리 아들을 칭칭 감았어요.
다니엘서에 나오는 형상을 주제로 가족 숭배를 했어요.
그러니까 흥미를 느끼고 더 잘 집중하죠.
그 어떤 어려움도 이겨 낼 수 있습니다.
이 가족들이 한 제안들을 적용해 보는 것이 어떻습니까?
어쩌면 이미 그렇게 하고 계실지 모르죠.
가족이 좋은 영적 일과를 유지하는 데 도움이 되는
자녀가 소품을 만들고 고대 의상을 입고
꼭 값비싼 소품이 있어야 하는 건 아닙니다.
또는 JW 방송에서 본 내용을 근거로
이미 어디에 있는지 다 아실 겁니다.
이제 십 대 자녀가 있는 가족을 위한 제안을 살펴보죠.
자녀가 고르게 해 볼 수 있을 것입니다.
자녀가 왜 그러한 목표를 세우게 되었는지,
어떻게 그 목표를 이룰 계획인지 물어보십시오.
자녀가 직접 고르게 해 볼 수 있을 것입니다.
가족 숭배 때 JW 방송을 보는 것도
단지 영상을 보는 것만으로 끝내지 마시기 바랍니다.
방송 전체나 각각의 부분을 시청한 뒤에
가족이 함께 그 내용에 대해 대화해 보십시오.
코로나 때문에 우리가 할 수 있는 봉사에 제한이 있지만
우리가 어떤 다양한 봉사에 참여할 수 있는지,
가족들은 그러한 봉사에 대해 어떻게 느끼는지
부정적인 감정이나 스트레스에 시달리고 있지는 않은지
부모를 위한 훌륭한 제안들이 실려 있습니다.
여러분이 어떤 어려움을 겪는지 알고 계시고
여호와의 도움으로 이 모든 시련을 통해
앞으로 있을 일에 대비할 수 있을 것입니다.
위로가 되는 이런 아름다운 말씀이 나옵니다.
물론 우린 이런 시련이 끝나길 바라죠.
우리는 여러분 모두를 위해 계속 기도하고 있습니다.
부모, 자녀, 전 세계 모든 영적 가족을 위해서 말이죠.

en.text: Greetings, brothers and sisters!
And welcome to this update
on the global COVID-19 pandemic.
On behalf of the Governing Body,
I want to tell you how encouraged we are
when we hear about your endurance through these difficult times.
In this update, I’d like to speak to you parents
who are raising children.
Although all of us have had to stay vigilant
to protect ourselves and others,
you dear parents have carried a particularly heavy load.
We can only imagine the deep concern you’ve had
for your young children and teens during the pandemic.
You worry about their physical safety
and their education.
You’ve also been concerned
about the emotional impact of physical distancing
for many months from other children,
grandparents, relatives, and the congregation.
And you’ve handled all of this
while you work to provide for them
and keep up your family’s spiritual routine.
That’s a lot on your shoulders.
Remember that the prophecy
in 2 Timothy chapter 3 tells us
tells us that “in the last days”
there would be “critical times hard to deal with.”
So the fact that Satan is attacking the family unit
is no surprise to you parents.
The surprise, however, may be
when the attack takes an unexpected form
or perhaps feels like many attacks coming all at once.
That’s what the pandemic has been for many of you.
Now I’m going to say something that you already know:
Jehovah God and Jesus know how you feel.
Their own example leaves no doubt.
For instance, there were times when Jehovah stepped in to protect his Son
when he was on the earth.
He first carefully entrusted Jesus
to the care of loving parents.
And when Herod wanted to kill Jesus as a child,
Jehovah told Joseph and Mary to “flee to Egypt”
until the threat passed.
You could say it was like an extended “lockdown”
that kept them away from family and friends for some time.
Jesus experienced what it’s really like
to grow up as a child in a wicked world.
He knows the pressures and the dangers.
It’s no wonder
that he took a special interest in children during his ministry,
and today he shares your deep concern for your children.
But you Christian parents have other good examples to look to.
It’s the example of our brothers and sisters
who live in areas that have been hit hard by the pandemic.
More recently, this has been the case
in India and Brazil.
We spoke to parents in those lands
and asked them how this has affected their families
and, in particular, their children.
For a child, it’s been a whole year
without being able to play
with other children.
So they really miss being with their friends.
A big challenge that parents have now
is coming up with something fun
for them to do as a family
so that their child
doesn’t feel upset or sad.
They feel anxious to go out,
and it’s very challenging for us
to keep them motivated to stay inside.
Our family was infected with COVID-19.
It was physically and emotionally
very stressful for all of us.
We’re not able to meet the friends
at the Kingdom Hall anymore.
Neither can we see our relatives,
so the kids are getting really bored.
Right after the pandemic began,
we got the news that Denise had cancer.
Of course, one of our main concerns was our daughter.
She really became anxious
about what was going to happen to her mom.
Perhaps you can sympathize
with some of the challenges parents in India and Brazil are facing.
We know it’s not been easy for parents and families during the pandemic.
But with every trial, there are also opportunities
to remain loyal to Jehovah and to grow spiritually.
For example, many parents have said
that they’ve had more time with their children
to do what it says at Deuteronomy 6:6, 7:
“These words that I am commanding you today
“must be on your heart, and you must inculcate them
“in your sons and speak of them
“when you sit in your house
“and when you walk on the road and when you lie down
and when you get up.”
Many of us have had more time
to “sit in [our] house” during the pandemic,
whether we wanted to or not.
But if this was your circumstance,
hopefully you made good use of the opportunity.
Jehovah gave the command to Israel
because he knew that spiritually strong families
would be happy families.
The same is true today.
When your family stays close to Jehovah,
you bring a blessing to yourself and your congregation.
But you parents are not just caring for your children’s spiritual needs.
You have spiritual needs too.
Jehovah’s command in Deuteronomy chapter 6
said that Israelite parents must have his words on their heart.
Notice the benefit you gain
when you make time for your spirituality.
Proverbs 20:7
explains it this way:
“The righteous one is walking in his integrity.
Happy are his children who come after him.”
So righteous parents make for happy children.
Parents, we know that you know these things.
We commend you for what you’re doing,
and we’re praying for Jehovah’s holy spirit
to give you strength, even when you feel tired out.
Our spiritual routine is even more important
when we’re being tested.
The families we met from India and Brazil were aware of this too.
They shared what they’ve done to adapt their spiritual routine
to meet the challenge of the pandemic.
We go out in the ministry together as a family
much more often than we did before.
Saturday is a special day for us.
We work together as a family every Saturday morning,
and we make plans with other families
who are also close friends of our children.
We always have a very enjoyable time.
When we conduct our Bible studies, we have them sit in.
The kids watch us closely, and they learn from us.
Family worship has played a very important role.
It’s a relaxed atmosphere in which we can have a good time.
One of the games we play is you name a Bible character,
and the next person has to come up with someone whose name starts
with the last letter of the name that was just said.
This way, the kids are getting to know new Bible characters
and they’re learning a lot about them.
One of our projects is a model of Noah’s ark.
Our kids have learned almost all of the original songs.
We’ve played a few games using some of the activities on jw.org.
We made some models of Bible accounts.
We enacted Bible scenes and role plays of Bible characters.
There was one time that we wrapped our son
in toilet paper and he was Lazarus.
And we have considered timely articles appearing on jw.org.
We also did a project on the metal image
of Daniel’s prophecy.
Our son enjoys family worship
because we do things that he likes
—something that holds his attention.
And it’s fun.
And seeing them happy, makes us happy.
All this has drawn us closer to each other.
And it also helped us to draw closer to Jehovah.
With Jehovah’s help, we can get through anything.
Perhaps something those families are doing can work
or is already working for your family.
Let’s review some suggestions
that can help your family’s spiritual routine.
For families with young children:
Dramatize Bible scenes.
Your children may like to dress up and make props
to bring the account to life and remember the lessons.
And the good thing is you don’t need expensive props
to make this interesting.
Play memory games.
This could be based on recent points from the meetings
or something they’ve been reading or watching on JW Broadcasting®.
Try a jw.org activity
for children together.
These are under the “Bible Teachings” section of the website.
But if you have young children,
I suspect you’ve been there before.
And here are some ideas for families with teens:
Practice “What if . . . ?” situations.
Perhaps let your teen choose a situation they’re concerned about.
Talk about goals.
These can be short-term or long-term goals.
Let your teen tell why they chose the goal,
and what steps they feel will help them reach it.
Read or watch a life story.
Again, let your teen choose a life story of someone they’re interested in.
Remember, though, that you don’t have to use every suggestion.
Talk to your family, pray about it,
and try what you think can make a difference for you.
And, of course, there’s nothing wrong with watching JW Broadcasting
during a family worship.
After all, that’s why we’re here.
But when you do,
try to make it more than just watching TV.
Take time to talk about the program as a family,
either at the end of the broadcast or after each segment.
Those are the suggestions.
Now here are the necessities for your family:
Pray together every day.
Try to include the feelings and concerns of each family member.
Keep attending the meetings.
Help each other to pay attention and participate.
Unlike being in the Kingdom Hall,
we may have many distractions when we attend from home.
Share in the ministry together.
As the pandemic continues to limit how we do our preaching work,
talk about the different forms of the ministry you can do
and how each family member feels about them.
Listen, and encourage everyone to do their best.
Finally, we urge you parents
to keep doing what you already know is vital:
Be alert for signs that your children
are struggling with negative emotions or stress.
If you sense that they are,
please read the article
“Help Your Children Cope With Stress.”
It’s in the Awake! of July 22, 1993,
pages 10 and 11.
There you’ll find wonderful suggestions on what you can do.
Jehovah loves your family.
He knows what you’re contending with,
and he wants to help you.
The pandemic has been just one of many tests
we’ll face in the last days.
That’s not meant to discourage you; it’s just reality.
But with Jehovah’s help,
your family can come out of each test spiritually stronger
and more prepared to face what’s ahead.
Jeremiah chapter 17
gives us this beautiful assurance in verse 7:
“Blessed is the man who puts his trust in Jehovah,
whose confidence is in Jehovah.”
And verse 8 concludes saying:
“And in the year of drought he will not be anxious,
nor will he quit producing fruit.”
Of course, we also want these tests to end.
And they will!
When you look back at the pandemic from the new world,
it will seem “momentary and light,”
even if it doesn’t seem so now.
In the meantime, we continue to pray for all of you
—parents, children, and all in our worldwide spiritual family.
May Jehovah bless your love and endurance.
From the World Headquarters of Jehovah’s Witnesses,
this is JW Broadcasting.

title: M. 스티븐 레트: 큰 그림을 보십시오 (사도 8:5)

ko.text: 문제의 세세한 부면에만 초점을 맞춘 나머지
상황을 전체적으로 보지 못하는 걸 가리키는 말이죠.
훌륭한 본을 보였습니다” 라고 알려 줍니다.
늘 여호와의 관점으로 상황을 보아야 합니다.
사실 보는 관점에 따라 차이가 생기는데,
초고층 건물 옆을 걸으면서 위를 올려다보면
복잡한 미로에서 길을 잃었다고 생각해 보십시오.
그런데 머리 위로 신뢰할 만한 친구가
그 친구는 우리가 어디로 가야 할지를
따라서 여호와의 생각과 같은 생각을 갖는다면,
그런데 항상 큰 그림을 보는 게
이처럼 우리 삶의 장면도 계속 변하고 있습니다.
마지막 날을 살면서 생길 수 있는
몇 가지 상황의 변화를 생각해 보고,
큰 그림을 볼 수 있는지 알아보겠습니다.
사는 곳에 있어서 가장 큰 변화를 겪은 분은
그분은 무수한 세월을 보낸 하늘을 떠나
사는 곳의 큰 변화를 겪은 훌륭한 본입니다.
더 필요한 곳으로 가서 섬기기로 할 수도 있고,
어쩔 수 없이 이사해야 할 수도 있습니다.
여호와를 섬길 수 있다는 걸 알았습니다.
상황이 변하게 만드는 또 다른 요인은
욥은 죽음에서 한 발짝 떨어져 있었죠.
무슨 일이 있어도 충절을 지키겠다고 결심했죠.
자신이 건강을 회복하게 될지 전혀 몰랐죠.
우리는 만성 질환이 생길 수도 있고,
이 제도가 끝나기 전에 죽게 될 수도 있습니다.
신세계에서 완벽한 건강을 영원히 누릴 것에 비하면
지금 질병을 앓는 것은 순간에 불과할 것입니다.
따라서 우리가 큰 그림을 보면서 충절을 지킨다면,
회중에서 불공정한 일이 일어났다고 느낄 때입니다.
우린 마음을 읽을 수 없고, 모든 사실을 알지 못하죠.
흔히 우리의 시각은 아주 넓은 집을
작은 문 틈 사이로 들여다보는 것처럼
사실을 다 알지 못한다는 걸 인정할 겁니다.
여호와께서만 사실을 다 아신다는 걸 인정할 겁니다.
일곱 금등잔대 사이를 거니는 이”로 묘사합니다.
상황의 변화에 직면하는 또 다른 예로
유혹을 받을 때 하와처럼 하면 안 되죠.
‘이 뱀은 날 위해 해 준 게 전혀 없어.
배우자가 아닌 사람에게 끌리는 유혹을 받을 때
그러면 사탄이 우리의 영적 갑옷 사이로
칼날을 집어넣으려 한다는 걸 알게 될 겁니다.
우리가 유혹을 받을 때 큰 그림을 본다면,
어떤 놀라운 축복이 있을지를 봐야 하죠.
생명의 위협을 받거나 죽임을 당한다 해도
여권을 준 것이나 다름이 없다는 것을
어떻게 큰 그림을 볼 수 있는지 살펴봤습니다.
어려운 상황에서 큰 그림을 보는 것이
여호와의 생각과 같은 생각을 하는 것입니다.

en.text: Now, the theme of my discussion is
“Despite Changing Circumstances,
Always See the Big Picture.”
Perhaps you’ve heard the expression,
“He can’t see the forest for the trees.”
This is referring to a person
who is too involved in the details of a problem
to see the situation as a whole.
Now, that’s a dangerous problem for anyone,
but especially one of Jehovah’s people.
No matter what the circumstances,
we want to always see the “big picture.”
The first sentence in today’s Watchtower  comments says this:
“Philip the evangelizer
“provides a fine example
“of one who stayed focused on [the] ministry
despite changing circumstances.”
And for us, just like Philip,
the big picture is always Jehovah’s thinking
—to see Jehovah’s view of the situation.
Jehovah’s thinking, or Jehovah’s viewpoint,
is so lofty—isn’t it?—so elevated.
Open up to Isaiah, please,
chapter 55,
and notice what is said here about the altitude
of Jehovah’s thinking.
Jehovah says in verse 9:
“For as the heavens are higher than the earth,
“so my ways are higher than your ways
and my thoughts than your thoughts.”
And if you think about it, viewpoint really does make a difference, doesn’t it?
It makes a huge difference.
For example, if you walk up to the World Trade Center building
on the sidewalk and look up,
it’s overwhelming—intimidating.
On the other hand, if you fly over the World Trade Center building
in an airplane and look out the window at it,
it looks like a matchstick stuck in the ground.
Well, viewpoint makes a difference.
Here’s another illustration:
Imagine that you’re lost in a complex maze.
Now, overhead, though,
is a trusted friend in a helicopter.
Now, that friend could easily direct you to safety, is that not true?
Well, in this illustration, our trusted friend
with the elevated view is, of course, Jehovah.
In fact, while you’re still looking at this picture,
let me read to you, please, Jehovah’s words
at Isaiah 30:21—his promise.
He says: “And your own ears will hear a word behind you saying,
“‘This is the way.
“‘Walk in it,’ in case you should go to the right
or in case you should go to the left.”
So if we make Jehovah’s thinking our thinking,
then Jehovah will safely guide us through any situation.
But now, what makes it challenging to always see the big picture?
Well, as we touched on —changing circumstances.
First Corinthians 7:31:
“The scene of this world is changing.”
Similarly, we could say the scene of our lives is constantly changing.
In fact, let’s talk about some changing circumstances
that could come our way before the end of this system
in which we want to always see the big picture.
Now, one is a change of residence.
As we touched on, that happened to Philip.
He was forced out of Jerusalem because of intense persecution.
He ended up in Samaria, but he saw the big picture there.
He knew he didn’t have to be in Jerusalem to preach.
He didn’t have to be in Jerusalem to serve Jehovah.
He could do it in Samaria, and he did so—powerfully.
Probably the most outstanding example
of a change of residence is Jesus.
He left his heavenly abode of billions of years
to live on this little tiny earth.
But obviously, he always saw the big picture
by making Jehovah’s thinking his thinking.
Abraham and Sarah were another excellent example
of a drastic change in residence.
Well, that may happen to us.
We may have a change of residence,
either by no choice of our own or by choice.
We may choose to move and serve where the need is greater.
We may have to move to care for family responsibilities.
I know of a Bethel couple who served at Bethel almost 25 years.
They had to leave to care for a father who had dementia,
but they continue to see the big picture.
They knew that you can preach, you can go to meetings,
you can read God’s Word, and you can serve Jehovah wherever you live.
Now, here’s another changing circumstance:
You develop chronic health problems,
perhaps problems that will only be corrected by Jehovah’s new world.
Now, in this vein, think for a moment about Job.
He was struck with cancerous boils
from the crown of his head to the soles of his feet
—brought to within one inch of death.
He wished that he was dead.
And yet, he saw the big picture, didn’t he?
‘I’ve got to keep my integrity to Jehovah no matter what.’
He even said at Job 27:5:
“Until I die, I will not renounce my integrity.”
Now, he had no idea that he would be restored to good health.
But he knew that if he kept his integrity, he would be resurrected.
Jehovah would call him, and he would answer from the grave.
Well, it’s the same with us.
We may develop chronic health problems.
We may even die before the end of this system.
But if we keep our integrity,
such an individual will take a quick nap
and, from his perspective,
instantaneously open his eyes in the new world
—if he keeps his integrity, like Job.
And if you think about this:
No matter how long we have to suffer some illness,
it’s momentary
compared to the permanency of perfect health in Jehovah’s new world.
That’s what 2 Corinthians 4:17 says:
“For though the tribulation is momentary and light,
[yet] it works out for us a glory that is . . . everlasting.”
So if we keep our eyes on the big picture
—maintain integrity— we can trade a moment of pain
for an eternity of perfect health.
You could say, “An ounce of suffering
for gigatons of pleasure.”
Think of that: A gigaton
—a billion tons compared to an ounce.
Here’s another changing circumstance:
We encounter perceived injustice in the congregation.
Now, you notice we said “perceived,”
because often things are not the way we see them to be.
We can’t read hearts.
We don’t have all the facts.
Often our view is like trying to look into a large house
through the front door that’s cracked open one inch (2.5 cm).
We have a very limited view.
So seeing the big picture,
we’ll recognize that we don’t have all the facts.
And seeing the big picture,
we’ll recognize who does have all the facts—Jehovah.
Everything is “naked and openly exposed” to him.
Jesus—Revelation 2:1 refers to him
as having “the seven stars [the elders] in his right hand
and [walking about] among the seven golden lampstands.”
So Jesus, the head of the congregation, has the facts.
So once we’ve done what’s in our jurisdiction
—perhaps reporting the matter—
seeing the big picture, we’ll leave it in the hands
of those who have all the facts,
confident that they will take care of this matter.
If it truly is an injustice,
they will take care of it in their time and their way.
Now, here’s another changing circumstance:
We come face-to-face with some temptation.
Now, in a case like this, we want to be nothing like Eve.
She obviously didn’t see the big picture, did she?
If she had, she would have realized,
‘This serpent has done nothing for me.
‘Jehovah has done everything for me.
‘In a contradictory situation, who, obviously,
would be telling me the truth?’
Instead, we want to be like Jesus.
When he was tempted by the Devil,
he saw the big picture —didn’t he?—
the issue of universal sovereignty.
So if we’re tempted to look at pornography,
listen to apostate ideas,
flirt with someone who’s not our mate (just a few examples),
let’s pause, elevate our thinking,
make Jehovah’s thinking our thinking,
and let’s see the big picture.
And the big picture is that Satan is trying to get the thin edge of a wedge
into our suit of armor.
Anything this world has to offer
cannot begin to equal the value of our relationship with Jehovah
and our place in his new world.
We’ll also be able to fast-forward if we see the big picture
and see the horrible consequences
of giving in to temptation.
Now, here’s one more changing circumstance: We’re persecuted.
And this can go from ridicule
to being threatened with execution or even being executed.
Think of David for just a moment.
He was ridiculed, and he was threatened with death by Goliath.
But even though David saw how big he was,
David saw the big picture, didn’t he?
He saw how puny, how wimpy
Goliath was compared to Jehovah, the Almighty.
So the big picture has to always include
the almighty God, Jehovah.
And again, we’ll be able to fast-forward to see the horrible consequences
of compromising if we’re persecuted.
On the other hand, we’ll see the wonderful blessings
if we keep our integrity.
We do not compromise.
In fact, even if we’re threatened with death or we’re executed,
if we see the big picture, we’ll realize
that Satan has just handed us a validated passport
right into the new world.
See, that is the big picture.
Well, we’ve talked about seeing the big picture
when you have a change of residence,
your health deteriorates,
you encounter a perceived injustice,
you come face-to-face with temptation,
or you are persecuted.
And these are just a few examples.
It may not always be easy
to see the big picture in challenging circumstances.
But the key is to make Jehovah’s thinking our thinking
—pause, elevate our thinking, view it from Jehovah’s standpoint.
The result will be protection and blessings coming our way
and praise going Jehovah’s way.

cn.text: 今天我想和大家讨论的内容是
虽然我们的情况不断改变，但总要看清全局
也许你听过这样的说法
“只见树木不见森林”
这指的是如果一个人太专注于问题本身
就很难看清全局
这对所有人来说都很危险
对上帝的子民来说就更是这样了
不管情况变得怎样，我们都总是要看清全局
今天《守望台》评论的第一句话这样说
“传福音者腓力是个好榜样
他虽然面对情况转变
却继续专注于传道工作。”
我们要像腓力一样
要看清全局就要有耶和华的想法
也就是用耶和华的观点来看待所有情况
耶和华的想法远远高于我们的想法，是吗？
请翻到以赛亚书第55章
这里提到耶和华的想法有多么高明
在第9节，耶和华说
“就像天比地高
我的道路也比你们的道路高超
我的思想也比你们的思想高明。”
想想看，人的想法真的很重要
会有很大的影响
比如你走到世贸中心大楼附近
向上看
会发现它高得让人生畏
但是如果你乘飞机飞过世贸大楼的上方
向外看
它小得就像一根火柴一样
的确，视角非常重要
再来看另外一个例子
想象一下，你在一个复杂的迷宫里迷路了
不过，有一个你信任的朋友
正坐在你头顶上方的直升机里
这个朋友很轻松地就能帮你走出迷宫
不是吗？
在这个比喻中我们信任的朋友就是耶和华
他可以从上面看到全貌
在你看这幅图片时，让我读一节经文给你
就是以赛亚书30:21
耶和华承诺道
“你们如果向左向右走偏了
就会听见后面有声音说
这才是正路，你们走这条路才对。”
所以，如果我们有耶和华的思想
那无论在任何情况下
都能受到他可靠的指引
但，是什么让我们很难看清全局呢？
就是不断变化的环境
哥林多前书7:31说
“这个世界的景象正在改变”
同样，可以说我们的生活也在不断改变
让我们来谈谈在这个制度终结前
我们可能会遇到什么样的改变
以及要怎么做才能继续看清全局
首先，是居住地点的改变
腓力就面对这样的改变
因为严重的迫害
腓力被迫离开耶路撒冷到撒马利亚
但他始终能看清全局
他知道
不是只在耶路撒冷才能传道和崇拜耶和华
在撒马利亚也可以
他这样做了，做得非常好
关于居住地点的改变
可能最杰出的榜样就是耶稣了
他离开天上居住了亿万年的居所
来到了小小的地球上
但是很明显
他总是让耶和华的思想指引自己
看事情的全局
在这方面
亚伯拉罕和撒拉也是很好的榜样
我们也一样
我们可能会改变居住的地方
无论这是我们自己的选择
还是不得不这样做
我们可能选择搬到需求更大的地区
也可能不得不搬家去照顾家人
我认识一对夫妇
他们在伯特利服务了将近25年
他们不得不离开伯特利去照顾失智的父亲
但他们继续看全局
他们知道无论在哪里都可以继续传道
参加聚会、阅读上帝的话语、崇拜耶和华
来看一下另一种情况的改变
你患了慢性疾病，可能这个问题
只有到了耶和华的新世界才可以解决
在这方面，想一想约伯的例子
当时约伯的情况是
从头顶到脚底都长满毒疮
差一点就死了
他非常痛苦，甚至想求死
然而他能够看清全局
无论怎样都对上帝保持忠义
在约伯记27:5，他说
“我到死也不会舍弃对上帝的忠义！”
虽然他当时不知道自己会恢复健康
但是他知道如果紧守忠义就会被复活
到时上帝会呼唤他，他就回答
我们也一样
我们可能有慢性的疾病
甚至可能在这个制度终结前死去
但如果我们保持忠义
就像一个人小睡了一会儿
对他来说，一睁开眼睛就看到新世界了
所以我们要像约伯一样紧守忠义
请你想一想，无论你患病多久
跟耶和华赐的新世界里永远完美的健康相比
这些都是暂时的
在哥林多后书4:17里说
“我们遭遇的患难是短暂而轻微的
为我们带来的荣耀却......永远长存。”
如果我们将目光放在全局上，保持忠义
就可以用短暂的痛苦换来永远完美的健康
所以说一丁点的苦楚可以换来巨大的福分
想想看
“一丁点的”和“巨大的”相比真的微不足道
还有一种情况的改变是
在会众里我们遇到了自己感觉不公平的事
这里说“感觉”
因为通常事实不是我们看到的那样
我们不能察看人心也不知道所有事实
我们看事情往往就好比
试图通过狭小的门缝去看一栋大房子
我们的视野非常有限
看清全局就要承认我们不知道全部事实
同样，看清全局
就是要承认耶和华知道全部事实
在他眼中“万物都是赤露敞开的”
耶稣呢？
在启示录2:1中提到他，说
他“右手拿着七颗星”，也就是长老
“走在七个金灯台之间”
所以耶稣是会众的头
他知道全部事实
我们只要做好自己能做的事情就好
比如告诉长老
要看清全局
就要把这件事情交给知道全部事实的人
要相信他们会处理好这件事
如果真的有不公正的情况
他们会以合适的时间和方式解决它
还会有另外一种情况就是
我们会受到引诱去做不对的事情
遇到这样的情况
我们肯定不想像夏娃那样
她一定没有看到全局
如果看到，她就会想
“这条蛇没为我做过什么呀
但耶和华给了我一切
撒但和上帝说的不一样
很显然我应该知道谁说的是事实。”
所以我们都想像耶稣一样
他受魔鬼引诱时，能看清全局
就是耶和华拥有宇宙至高统治权
所以如果我们受到引诱去看色情资讯
听叛道者的言论
或者和不是配偶的人调情等等
这时要暂停下来，从更高的视角来看
用耶和华的观点去看事情
也就是要看清全局
要清楚知道撒但正极力用尽各种方法
破坏我们跟上帝的关系
这个世界能够提供的任何东西
都比不上我们与耶和华的宝贵关系
以及能够进入新世界的福分

别人可能会嘲笑我们
扬言要杀死我们
或是真的把我们处决
想想大卫的经历
歌利亚嘲笑他，威胁要杀死他
即使大卫看到歌利亚有多么高大
他依然能看清全局
就是和全能的耶和华相比
歌利亚是多么地渺小和软弱
所以看清全局
就是要看出耶和华的观点是怎样的
这样被迫害时，我们就能预先看到
妥协会带来非常严重的后果
同时
也能看到保持忠义会带来美好的福分
我们绝不妥协
即使我们面对死亡的威胁或真的失去生命
能看清全局就会意识到
这其实是撒但亲手递给我们
进入新世界的通行证
你看，这就是全局！
所以当你面对各种考验以及难题时
比如需要搬家、有健康难题
觉得遇到不公的对待
又或者面对各种引诱、遭受迫害
都要记得看清全局
这可能并不容易
特别是遇到考验，身处逆境时
但如果我们暂停一下
把视角提升到耶和华的高度
以他的视角去看问题，就能看清全局
这样我们就能得到来自耶和华的保护和福分
也能为他带来赞美和荣耀
