코로나19에 더해 허리케인 샐리까지 온 겁니다.
여러 달 동안 집에만 있었기 때문에
형제 자매들이 너무나 신속하게 행동해 줘서
금요일에는 모든 게 다 조직되고 준비되어 있었죠.
얼마나 잘 돌보는지 볼 수 있었습니다.
‘나 혼자 할 수 있어, 난 할 수 있다고’ 하고 말하죠.
전화 한 통이면 여호와의 백성은 금방 달려오죠.
그 무엇도 여호와의 사랑을 막을 수 없습니다.
여호와의 사랑이 닿지 않는 곳은 없습니다.
여호와께서 우리를 계속 도우실 것이라고 확신합니다.
그 어떤 어려움도 이겨 낼 것입니다.
우리의 형제들이 승리를 거두고 있는 한 가지 이유는
위험을 무릅쓰면서까지 그렇게 한 분들도 있습니다.
이 모든 게 여러분의 관대함으로 인해 가능한 일이었습니다.
그들은 양심적 병역 거부 때문에 수감된 형제들이었죠.
2017년에 제가 러시아 대법원의 재판을 참관하러 갔을 때,
앞으로 어떤 일이 있을지 알 수 없었습니다.
그가 가석방 조건을 충족시킨 지도 1년이 넘었지만
당국이 어떤 사람들을 공격하고 있는지 유의해 보십시오.
정말 가슴이 무너져 내리는 것 같았죠.
우리 힘만으로는 견딜 수 없었을 거예요.
복면을 쓴 무장한 요원들이 집에 들이닥쳤죠.
아무 말도 할 수 없었고, 몸이 굳어버렸죠.
그 후 2020년에 저에 대한 재판이 시작되었죠.
여호와께선 우릴 돕고, 힘을 주고, 격려해 주셨죠.
우리 지역에 사는 수많은 형제 자매들이
그들은 늘 우리에게 힘이 되어 주었고
전화로 격려가 되는 말이나 성구를 읽어 주었죠.
사실 제가 고발될 거란 걸 이미 알고 있었죠.
하루하루가 여호와께서 주신 축복이라고 말하고 싶습니다.
마음으로 평화를 누리게 해 달라고 기도하죠.
‘하느님의 사랑에서 우릴 갈라놓을 수’ 있는 건
감옥 벽도 하느님의 사랑을 막을 수 없죠.
우리는 어디에서나 하느님의 사랑을 느낄 수 있습니다.
그 모든 역경을 이겨 낼 수 있었죠.
우린 반드시 이 시련도 이겨 낼 겁니다.
당국이 이렇게 연로한 형제 자매들을 공격하는 것은
어려움을 겪으면서도 박해에 용기 있게 맞서는
우리의 연로한 형제 자매들을 자랑스럽게 여깁니다.
오히려 믿음을 강하게 해 주었다고 말합니다.
여러분은 우리 모두에게 큰 격려를 줍니다.
현재 있는 것도 오게 될 것도 권세도
높음도 깊음도 그 밖의 어떤 피조물도
우리 주 그리스도 예수 안에 있는 하느님의 사랑에서
여호와의 사랑에서 우리를 갈라놓을 수 없기 때문입니다.

en.text: At Romans 8:35, the apostle Paul asked:
“Who will separate us
“from the love of the Christ?
“Will tribulation or distress or persecution
or hunger or nakedness or danger or sword?”
Notice how Paul answered that question in verse 37:
“On the contrary, in all these things
“we are coming off completely victorious
through the one who loved us.”
That’s a very fitting scripture
for this update.
Many of the things Paul mentioned
we’ve experienced in the past year.
There have been many challenges.
Yet, through the help we receive from Jehovah,
“we are coming off . . . victorious.”
Of course, we’re all contending with the pandemic.
Jehovah’s organization has been complying
with guidance from public health officials worldwide.
We’ve worked hard as an organization
to show deep respect for the sanctity of life.
And we’ve watched Jehovah bless these efforts
as our meetings and ministry have thrived.
However, we are not immune
to the effects of the virus.
As of May 15, we have now lost
over 17,000
of our dear brothers and sisters
to COVID-19.
No doubt most of us have lost someone we love.
How comforting to know that our loved ones
are safe in Jehovah’s memory!
Even death has not separated them from Jehovah.
There have been many recent news reports
about the pandemic in India and Brazil.
Many of you have been asking how our brothers there are doing.
In the past month in India,
there have been ten times
as many new cases and deaths among the brothers
than there were in the previous month.
The disaster relief committees
are actively monitoring the needs of our brothers
and, as needed, helping them locate hospitals
that have available beds.
In Brazil, the number of cases
and the number of deaths continue to be high.
Sadly, over 400 of our brothers in Brazil
have died from the virus in just the past month.
The responsible brothers are working hard
to help our brothers in these lands.
Please keep all of our brothers
in India and Brazil in your prayers.
In various parts of the world, the virus is resurging
in some cases because of new variants.
Clearly, this pandemic is not over.
Please continue to be careful.
You may find it helpful to review
the 2020 Governing Body Update #9,
which explains how COVID-19 spreads
and what we can do to protect ourselves.
What is our view on vaccination?
Jehovah’s Witnesses are not against vaccination.
We view it as a personal decision
for each Christian to make.
Already, in cooperation with public health officials,
many in our Bethel families have chosen to be vaccinated.
In 2020, we also faced
an unprecedented number of natural disasters.
Can you imagine that in the 2020 service year
we have had 204 disasters?
That’s more than double the number of disasters
that we had in 2018!
Of course, we’ve had to cope with many disasters during the pandemic.
Let me remind you of some of them.
Central America was struck by Hurricane Eta.
St. Vincent has had volcanic eruptions.
Croatia was shaken by earthquakes.
Lebanon was devastated by an explosion.
Nigeria suffered widespread flooding.
Mozambique was hit by Cyclone Eloise.
The Philippines was pummeled
by Super Typhoon Goni.
Australia had destructive bush fires.
These are just a few
of the disasters we have faced
during the pandemic.
This is exactly what Paul was talking about
when he mentioned tribulation, distress,
hunger, nakedness, danger, or sword.
Would any of these things
“be able to separate us from God’s love”?
What have we seen?
Let’s hear some expressions from our brothers in the United States.
When you have a disaster
on top of a disaster,
COVID-19 on top of Hurricane Sally,
it’s a challenge to get through and navigate both.
Being homebound for so many months,
everybody was already feeling
a little bit on edge.
Then you add the stress of the flood on top of it.
The speed of the brothers
and sisters responding
was probably the most heartwarming.
We called them on a Wednesday to start some of their work on Friday,
and by Friday, they were organized and ready to go.
I think it’s one of the most heartwarming
privileges I’ve ever seen
—how Jehovah’s organization
can take care of needs,
whereas the world around us is falling apart.
There are people who think:
‘I can handle this. I can handle this,’
you know, ‘I can do this.’
And you can’t do it on your own.
You need the friends. You need them.
When the call goes out, Jehovah’s people come running.
It’s an amazing thing to see.
There’s no way that Jehovah’s love can be blocked.
If you’re sheltered in place, wherever you are,
Jehovah’s love gets through.
We’ve been through a difficult situation,
but our confidence is solid
that he’ll continue to help us.
He got us through this problem;
he’ll get us through the next.
One of the reasons why our brothers are coming off victorious
is because of all of you.
You have been there to help.
Some of you have risked your own safety to provide relief.
Although most of us don’t have the circumstances to do that,
we’ve made donations.
As a result, we’ve been able to provide our brothers
with food, water, building materials, and medicine
—all because of your generosity and goodness.
Thank you for what you’ve done
to help our brothers who face these disasters.
That’s not the only thing that Paul talked about
in Romans 8:35.
He also mentioned persecution.
We certainly have had to face that.
It hasn’t gone away during the pandemic.
As of May 2021,
more than 155 brothers and sisters
are in prison for their faith.
Even so, there have been positive developments.
In recent months, we were so encouraged to learn
that 32 of our brothers in Eritrea
have been set free,
including Paulos, Isaac, and Negede,
who were imprisoned for 26 years.
We continue to pray
for the 20 brothers and sisters who are still in prison.
On May 8, we were delighted to learn
that the Turkmenistan government released from prison
all 16 of our brothers
who were imprisoned
for conscientious objection
to military service.
We thank Jehovah
for these positive developments.
When I went to Russia for the Supreme Court hearings in 2017,
it was a very sobering moment
when we heard the judge announce
that our legal entities were banned.
We knew Jehovah would look after our brothers,
but there were so many unknowns.
How would our brothers be affected?
Some, of course, have been arrested, like Brother Dennis Christensen.
He’s been in prison for four years
as of May 25, 2021.
Although Dennis has qualified for parole for over a year,
the authorities have “hardened their hearts.”
They have not let him go.
In spite of that,
Dennis and his wife, Irina, are in good spirits.
And we continue to remember our 10 brothers
who are in penal colonies in Russia
and the 48 who are in pretrial detention
as of May 14, 2021.
Now that four years have passed since the ban,
what do we see?
Our brothers have not cowered.
They have not backed down.
They continue to serve Jehovah faithfully.
As you watch this next video,
see who the authorities are attacking now.
our son, Igor, became ill,
and he got worse and worse.
Then, in 2014, our son died.
It was such a tragedy for us,
and words cannot describe it.
He was our only son and was deeply loved.
Then, two years later, my mother died.
And two years after that, my sister died.
Getting through all of that was beyond human strength.
We had just started to feel a little better
when on March 26,
. . . armed men in masks burst into our home.
It was such a shock! We went numb.
We couldn’t say anything.
We were paralyzed.
early in the morning at 5:45,
the doorbell rang.
I looked through the peephole and saw people
who showed me their identification.
Then those people came into my apartment,
made a search, and took me to the center
for fighting extremism.
It ended up with my being accused
of participating in extremist activity.
Then, in 2020,
the court hearings began for my case.
For example, for my criminal case,
they collected 17 volumes of evidence against me,
and they questioned over 200 witnesses.
Then the court hearings started.
First of all, there were Valentina’s hearings, then mine.
Of course, none of that is exactly pleasant,
but it somehow made us stronger,
and Jehovah supported us.
We even went to the court feeling joyful.
We felt that Jehovah was helping us, supporting us,
strengthening us, and encouraging us.
We are so grateful to him!
Our fellow worshippers constantly called on us
from all parts of the town.
They always supported us,
always called us and said strengthening things
and quotes from the Bible.
I understood that it would end up with my being a defendant.
It was as though inside I was already prepared for that
and, you know, I didn’t feel any kind of panic.
I just wanted to get through it in a dignified manner
and didn’t want to let anyone down
and under no circumstances
betray our God, Jehovah.
I want to say that each day for me
is a blessing from Jehovah.
I pray and ask for peace and calmness
in both my heart and my home.
And right now, the blessings far outweigh
all negative experiences.
This I value very highly.
The sentence might even involve time in prison
or it might be a suspended sentence.
But regardless of the outcome,
we need to remain faithful to God
and to stay on the way of truth
to the end.
No matter what happens,
whether I remain free
or they put me somewhere behind prison walls,
there is absolutely nothing
that can “separate us from God’s love.”
No prison walls can shut out God’s love.
It can penetrate everywhere
to all depths.
It was the strength that we received from God
that helped us to survive the death of our son
and many other misfortunes,
so we will get through this too.
We definitely will!
I have no doubt about it.
How shameful that the authorities are attacking
our elderly brothers and sisters!
And yet, isn’t it amazing
that, despite their own trials,
these dear older ones are not yielding to fear?
They say that the persecution
has only made them stronger in the faith.
You dear brothers and sisters in Russia
have done so well.
You are an inspiration to all of us.
We truly love you.
Doesn’t all of this convince us
of what Paul said in Romans 8:37?
“In all these things
“we are coming off completely victorious
through the one who loved us.”
That’s what we’ve seen with our brothers and sisters
facing the pandemic, natural disasters,
and persecution.
What conviction does this lead us to?
Paul continues in verses 38 and 39:
“For I am convinced
“that neither death nor life
“nor angels nor governments
“nor things now here nor things to come
“nor powers nor height nor depth
“nor any other creation
“will be able to separate us from God’s love
that is in Christ Jesus our Lord.”
Brothers and sisters,
we are convinced that you too
will continue to “[come] off completely victorious”
no matter what trials you face.
Why?
Because nothing can separate us
from Jehovah’s love.
Please know
that we love you all very much.
From the World Headquarters of Jehovah’s Witnesses,
this is JW Broadcasting®.

cn.text: 在罗马书8:35
使徒保罗问道
请注意，保罗在第37节怎么回答
本次的报导就和这两节经文有关
保罗在经文里提到的很多事
我们在过去1年都经历了
我们遇到了很多挑战
但靠着耶和华的帮助
我们战胜了这些挑战
当然疫情对所有人都是一场考验
各个国家的耶和华见证人都一直遵守当地
公共卫生部门的指示
我们无论在哪里都努力配合政府的防疫要求
因为我们珍视生命
耶和华也因此赐福给我们
让我们的聚会顺利进行
传道工作也不断发展
然而，我们每个人都会受到疫情的影响
截至5月15号
因为这次疫情
已经有超过1万7000个
我们亲爱的弟兄姐妹失去了生命
我们当中很多人都失去了挚爱的亲友
但令我们感到安慰的是
他们都安全地留在耶和华的记忆中！
即使死亡
也不能将他们和耶和华上帝分开
最近有很多关于印度和巴西
这两个国家的疫情报导
很多人都想知道那里的弟兄姐妹的情况
过去一个月
在印度，弟兄姐妹的死亡人数
和新增的确诊病例数上升了很多
是前一个月的10倍
救灾委员会的弟兄们
一直和当地的弟兄保持联系
了解他们的需要
帮助他们找到那些可以提供床位的医院
在巴西
确诊病例数和死亡人数也在不断攀升
难过的是，仅在过去一个月
那里就有400多个弟兄姐妹
因为感染这个病毒而去世
负责的弟兄们
正竭尽全力帮助那里的弟兄姐妹
请大家
为我们所有在印度和巴西的弟兄姐妹
向上帝祷告
在世界很多地方出现了新的变异病毒
所以疫情又严重起来
显然
这场疫情还没有结束
请继续保持警惕
大家可以复习一下
《2020来自中央长老团的报导（九）》
里面解释了冠状病毒是如何传播的
也告诉我们怎样做就能保护自己
我们怎么看待注射疫苗呢？
耶和华见证人不反对注射疫苗
打不打疫苗
我们认为这是每个基督徒个人的决定
当然为了和公共卫生部门配合
很多伯特利家庭成员已经选择注射了疫苗
在2020年，我们遭遇的自然灾害的数目
是有史以来最多的
你能想象吗？
在2020工作年度
我们已经遭受了204场自然灾害
这个数字是
2018工作年度的两倍还要多！
所以
我们还要在疫情期间应对这些灾害
让我们来看看其中的一些吧
中美洲被飓风埃塔袭击
圣文森特遭遇了火山爆发
克罗地亚发生了强烈地震
黎巴嫩发生了大爆炸
尼日利亚受到洪水重创
莫桑比克遭受气旋埃洛伊丝肆虐
菲律宾受到超强台风天鹅侵袭
澳大利亚遭遇丛林大火
这些只是我们在疫情期间
遭遇的自然灾害中的一小部分
这正是保罗在罗马书第8章的经文所提到的
患难、痛苦
饥饿、赤身
危险或刀剑
但这些难题
能否“隔绝上帝对我们的爱”呢？
让我们听一听
来自美国的一些弟兄姐妹的亲身经历
灾难一个接一个爆发
2019冠状病毒病还没结束
又来一个飓风莎莉真的很不容易
大家关在家里已经好几个月
心情都开始有一点烦躁了
然后又碰上洪水泛滥
真的觉得快受不了了
对我来说最让我感动的是
看到弟兄姐妹马上就来帮忙
我们星期三打电话给弟兄
请他们星期五来帮忙，到了星期五
他们就什么都准备好，可以出发了
我觉得，最让我受到鼓励和安慰的就是
看到耶和华的组织这么关心我们、照顾我们
但外面的世界就很不一样，四分五裂的
有些人觉得
“我，我应付得来，不用帮忙！”
但其实我们不能靠自己
我们需要朋友，真的很需要
弟兄姐妹知道哪里需要帮忙，就马上去了
我觉得很感动，真的
什么都不能隔绝耶和华对我们的爱
无论你在世界的哪一个角落
上帝都能表达他对你的爱
我们面对非常艰难的处境
但是我们很有信心
耶和华会继续帮助我们
这一次，他帮助我们渡过难关
下一次也一定会陪在我们身边
我们的弟兄之所以能战胜困难
其中一个原因就是你们
你们一直提供帮助
其中一些人甚至冒着危险提供救援
尽管我们大多数人不能亲临现场
但我们通过捐款支持他们
因此我们可以为受灾的弟兄姐妹提供食物
水、建筑材料和药品
所有这一切都是因为你们的慷慨和良善
非常感谢你们
为了帮助受灾的弟兄姐妹所做的一切
保罗在罗马书8:35
提到的难题不止这些
他还提到了迫害
这是我们必须面对的
迫害没有因为疫情而停止
截至2021年5月
有超过155个弟兄姐妹
因为信仰被政府关在监狱里
不过
还是有一些好的情况出现
不久之前
我们得到了非常鼓舞人心的消息
在厄立特里亚的32位弟兄被释放了
其中就包括波洛、以撒和尼格德
他们整整被囚禁了26年
我们会继续
为那里依然被囚禁的20位弟兄姐妹祷告
在5月8日，我们很高兴地得知
土库曼斯坦政府释放了所有被囚禁的弟兄
一共16位
他们都是因良心的缘故
拒服兵役而被囚
我们感谢耶和华成就的这些美好的事情
我去俄罗斯参加了最高法院的听审
当我听到法官作出判决
禁止我们的法人团体时
我的心情无比沉重
我们知道耶和华会照顾弟兄们
但未知数还有很多
他们会受到怎样的影响呢？
有一些人被囚
比如丹尼斯·克里斯滕森弟兄
到这个月的25号为止
他被关在监狱就满4年了
尽管他在1年多前就已经满足假释条件了
但俄罗斯政府“硬着心”
不让他离开监狱
虽然如此，丹尼斯和他的太太伊琳娜
依然保持冷静，充满信心
截至本月14日
在俄罗斯依然有10位弟兄被关在监狱
48位弟兄姐妹被审前羁押
我们会继续为他们祷告
我们的活动在当地被禁止已经4年了
我们看到了什么？
我们的弟兄没有失去勇气
没有停止传道工作
他们依然忠贞地崇拜耶和华
请观看接下来的短片
看看俄罗斯政府现在正在攻击谁
2013年，我们的儿子伊戈尔生病了
后来病情越来越严重
在2014年，他去世了，我们快崩溃了
那种痛苦是无法形容的
我们就这么一个儿子，真的很爱他
之后过了两年，我妈妈也去世了
又过了两年
我的姐姐也去世了
如果没有耶和华的帮助
我们根本承受不了这些打击
我们的心情刚刚好了一点
没想到，3月26号
带着面罩的武装分子冲进我家
我们都吓呆了！
根本不知道怎么反应
身体都动不了了，完全说不出话来
早上5点45分
我家的门铃响了
于是我从门口看出去
一些人就把证件举起来给我看
之后他们进了我家到处搜查
然后把我带到打击极端主义的部门
结果他们控告我参与极端主义活动
后来在2020年
法庭就开始审理我的案件了
比如说当局为了控告我
收集了17份证据
还查问了200多个证人
后来法庭开审了
他们先开庭审理我太太的案子
然后就是我的
这是个考验当然不好受
不过这个经历让我们更坚强
耶和华一直支持我们
我们去法庭的时候，心里甚至有点高兴
我们觉得耶和华在帮助我们、支持我们
给我们力量鼓励我们，我们非常感激他！
弟兄姐妹常常从不同的地方来看我们
或者打电话给我们
他们一直支持我们、鼓励我们
还引用圣经来强化我们的信心
我知道当局会以刑事罪名控告我
我觉得自己心里早就做了准备
所以我一点都没有害怕
我只想有尊严地面对这一切
不要让我的弟兄姐妹失望
也绝对不能背叛我的上帝耶和华

en.text: My theme is “‘The King of the North’ in the Time of the End.”
In recent years, the Russian government
has persecuted our brothers and sisters
who live in that country.
You’ve heard reports about the police invading Kingdom Halls
and breaking up meetings.
The government has labeled Jehovah’s Witnesses
as an “extremist group.”
It has seized our properties and imprisoned our brothers.
Please watch a brief video
that reviews some of the trials
Jehovah’s people in Russia have faced.
On April 20, 2017,
the Supreme Court of the Russian Federation criminalized
the activity of Jehovah’s Witnesses.
As of July 4, 2019,
authorities have progressively seized 131 of the properties
owned by Jehovah’s Witnesses,
with an additional 60 properties subject to confiscation.
One of the seized properties
was the former Russia branch complex in Solnechnoye.
At the time of filming, the Russian authorities continue
their aggressive attack on Jehovah’s Witnesses.
As of August 17, 2020,
there were 42 Witnesses who were in pretrial detention
or sentenced to prison,
32 who were under house arrest,
and 169 who were not allowed to leave their hometown.
All have been charged with organizing,
participating in, or financing the activity
of a so-called “extremist” organization.
At least 380 Witnesses were, at the time, under investigation
—ranging in age from 19 to 89 years old.
What has this meant for the individuals affected?
As an example,
on June 3, 2018,
Brother Sergey Klimov was arrested.
Local authorities initiated
criminal charges against him,
placing him in pretrial detention for two months.
This detention was extended seven times,
separating him from his wife and family
for a year and five months,
before he was finally tried and sentenced.
On November 5, 2019,
he was sentenced to six years in prison.
Two of our dear young people in Russia,
Brother Yegor Baranov and Sister Darya Dulova,
are courageously facing criminal conviction
and potential long-term imprisonment.
Brother Baranov is only 19 years old.
When the authorities raided her home, Sister Dulova was only 18 years old.
By means of the Newsroom on jw.org,
we are informed of updated news events.
This page includes links to name lists
of Witnesses currently imprisoned for their faith,
which can help us include them specifically in our prayers.
Our brothers and sisters in Russia are resolved to remain loyal to Jehovah
despite any opposition,
and they put their confidence in him in the assurance
that Jehovah is on their side!
It shouldn’t surprise us
that this powerful government has been persecuting
our peaceful, law-abiding brothers and sisters.
Why not?
Because that government is fulfilling Bible prophecy!
Please find Daniel chapter 11.
In verse 40, it refers to what the Bible calls
“the king of the north.”
Of that “king,” Daniel 11:41 says:
“He will also enter into the land of the Decoration,
and many lands will be made to stumble.”
Today, Russia and its allies
are filling the role of the king of the north.
Daniel foretold that this king would enter
“the land of the Decoration,”
meaning that he would interfere in a significant way
with the activities of God’s people.
As discussed in the May 2020 Watchtower,
Russia and its allies are not the first political power
to act as the king of the north,
but they may well be the last.
In this program, we will do three things:
First,
we’ll briefly trace the fulfillment of the prophecy
recorded in Daniel chapter 11.
Second, we’ll look at how that prophecy
is being fulfilled today.
And third, we’ll discuss how knowing this information
should affect the decisions that we make.
Brother Herman van Selm, a helper to the Writing Committee,
will help us review some of the key points of the prophecy
recorded in Daniel chapter 11.
Thank you, Herman, for helping me with this presentation.
It’s a pleasure to be with you, Ken.
Thank you for inviting me.
First, let’s briefly trace
how the prophecy has been fulfilled so far.
The prophecy in Daniel chapter 11 mentions
“the king of the north” and “the king of the south.”
Now, why are they described like that?
Well, initially,
these powers were located north and south
of the literal land of Israel,
thus the names king of the north
and king of the south.
These powers could be viewed as two thrones.
Over time, those thrones have been occupied
by various political powers
and these rival kings compete for world domination.
And what about Jehovah’s people?
They are right at the center of this conflict.
But let’s start at the beginning.
Ken,
what is the origin of the kings of the north and of the south?
The kings of the north and of the south
both rose from the empire
established by Alexander the Great.
One line of kings ruled over Egypt,
which is south of Israel.
And that dynasty was the first
to fill the role of king of the south.
During this period, another line of kings
ruled an area north of Israel
and those kings filled the role
of king of the north.
Then the Roman Empire took over
as king of the north.
As discussed in the May 2020 Watchtower,
God’s people are the focal point
of the prophecy recorded in Daniel chapter 11.
The angel who spoke with Daniel said that the prophecy
would help him “understand what will befall your people”
—that is, the nation of Israel.
And what, in fact, happened?
Well, the Jewish nation was God’s people until 33 C.E.
But after that, a change occurred.
Jehovah poured out his holy spirit
on Christ’s followers.
And from then on,
the congregation of true Christians
became God’s people.
Galatians 6:16 refers to them
as “the Israel of God.”
That point is significant
because the kings of the north and south can only be identified
when there is a clearly defined group of God’s people on earth.
Why is that the case?
Because, as we just considered,
the angel had told Daniel
that the prophecy centers on God’s people.
In the second century C.E.,
true Christians were overgrown
by weedlike false Christians.
In his illustration of the wheat and the weeds,
Jesus foretold that this would happen.
That illustration is recorded
at Matthew 13:36-43.
So from the second century onward,
we can no longer identify an organized group of true Christians.
And, as we considered, for that same reason,
we also cannot identify
the king of the north and the king of the south.
But in the 1870’s, a group of Bible students
began to separate itself from false Christians.
This group,
which included Charles T. Russell,
rejected teachings
that were not based on the Bible.
And like the first-century Christians,
they promoted the truths
taught in God’s Word.
Now this group underwent a development
that is foretold at Malachi 3:1.
They were the “messenger”
who would “clear up a way” before Jehovah.
And as events that followed prove,
this group clearly had God’s backing.
So from the 1870’s onward,
when true Christians began to organize themselves as a group,
we can again identify the political powers
that fill the roles of the king of the north
and king of the south.
At that time in history,
Britain was the dominant political force
and it filled the role
of the king of the south.
Amazingly, it was also in the 1870’s
that the German Empire emerged
and soon began to challenge Britain
for world domination.
This political power now filled the role
of the king of the north.
Daniel 11:25, 26 indicate
that the two kings would clash
and that the king of the north would lose many soldiers in the battle.
And that is exactly what happened
during World War I.
And it was during that war
that Britain and its close ally,
the United States,
forged a special bond.
So from this point on,
during these last days,
the Anglo-American power
has been the king of the south.
That brings us to our second point:
How has Daniel chapter 11 been fulfilled
from that time onward
until recent times?
During World War I,
the king of the north and the king of the south
persecuted those of God’s people who refused to fight in the war.
The king of the south even threw into jail
those who were taking the lead in the preaching work.
But let’s take a closer look at the king of the north.
Has the political power filling that role
changed during the last days?
And how has it treated God’s people?
The identity of the king of the north
has changed three times during the last days.
Starting in the 1870’s through to the end of the second world war,
the German Empire
filled the role of the king of the north.
In the period leading up to and including World War II,
it persecuted God’s people without mercy,
imprisoning thousands of our brothers
and killing hundreds of them.
Who replaced the German Empire as the king of the north?
That’s an important question, Herman.
After World War II,
the Soviet Union took on that role.
It also attacked God’s people,
imprisoning them or sending them into exile.
But, Ken, Daniel 11:34 says
that they—that is, God’s people—
would be “given a little help.”
What’s the significance of that statement?
This passage points forward to the time
when the Soviet Union collapsed.
Although God’s people suffered terribly under that government,
they were “given a little help.”
In what way?
After the USSR collapsed,
God’s people there could worship freely for a number of years.
In time, though, Russia and its allies
took on the role of the king of the north.
And like the other powers that filled the role of king of the north,
this government has continued to oppress God’s people.
How are our brothers and sisters coping with the current persecution?
Let’s take a look.
And what you’re going to see will break your heart
but also strengthen your faith.
my husband and I were woken up
by a loud bang on the door.
As soon as my husband had opened the door,
people burst in shouting,
“Everyone on the floor!”
I saw them taking my husband into the kitchen
and heard them
very aggressively ordering him to do something.
Then I heard some noise, and I realized
that he was being beaten.
My husband, Feliks, and I
were on our way back from the shopping mall
to the car park.
A jeep with tinted windows
blocked our path, and people
with weapons jumped out, shouting:
“On the ground! Don’t move!”
We were thrown against the vehicle.
Feliks was sent to a pretrial detention facility,
where he spent a year.
From the very first bang on the door,
I began praying to Jehovah for wisdom, calmness,
and for holy spirit so that I could make the right decisions
and act in the right way.
And for the whole day, I was praying.
Jehovah answered all my prayers,
and I felt that he was close at my side.
Before each court hearing when I was very afraid
and felt overwhelmed by emotion and couldn’t calm myself down,
it was prayer
that helped me to settle down.
When they took us for interrogation,
I started panicking and, at that moment,
I realized that I needed to meditate on something positive.
So I thought,
‘I need to sing our songs.’
And just one song came into my mind:
“He Will Make You Strong.”
It really strengthened me.
Those words about how Jehovah gave his Son for us
show he loves us and will never leave us.
Brothers and sisters
pray and tell me
that they are praying for me.
It gives me the feeling that I am part
of a large family.
After the interrogation,
he was sent home.
My husband and I
continue to stick to our spiritual routine.
We continue to conduct family worship, and we are always in the ministry.
Our brothers and sisters constantly support us.
They write kind words;
they commend us;
they send us encouraging scriptures from the Bible.
In September 2019, Feliks was found guilty
and sentenced to three years in a general regime colony.
When he and the other brothers arrived there,
they were beaten up by officers from the colony.
Feliks told me
that he prayed while he was being beaten,
and he noticed that at that moment, he stopped feeling the pain.
While he is behind bars,
Feliks tries to conduct family worship with me by letters.
He picks certain themes and some specific questions.
Then I do research
in the publications and send back what I find.
The scripture at Isaiah chapter 30 really strengthens me,
where it says that “your strength will be
in keeping calm and showing trust.”
Although I tend to worry,
I understand that calmness is expressed
by fully trusting in Jehovah.
I have become stronger because thanks to Jehovah,
in a way, I have developed almost a shell
against the difficulties
that used to scare me.
That confidence and faith help me.
Jehovah was with me,
and he will remain
close by me,
and we will be made stronger thanks to him,
and we will get through these trials.
How can we develop courage
like our brothers and sisters in Russia?
Well, we must be convinced
that the prophecies in the Bible are trustworthy.
As we’ve discussed,
each detail of the prophecy recorded at Daniel chapter 11
has come true so far.
We must have confidence
that the remaining events described in that prophecy
will also come true.
We are living in the last days of the time of the end.
Soon, the nations will fulfill the prophecy
at 1 Thessalonians 5:3:
“Whenever it is that they are saying,
“‘Peace and security!’
“then sudden destruction is to be instantly on them,
“just like birth pains on a pregnant woman,
and they will by no means escape.”
Then “sudden destruction”
comes upon all parts of Satan’s system.
As you can see on the screen,
Daniel 12:1 says:
“During that time Michael will stand up,
“the great prince who is standing in behalf of your people.
“And there will occur a time of distress such as has not occurred
“since there came to be a nation until that time.
“And during that time your people will escape,
everyone who is found written down in the book.”
That leads us into our third point:
How should knowing the information
that we have just discussed
affect the decisions that we make?
Well, what we have reviewed is not just interesting history;
it’s a dramatic prelude
to what will soon happen here on earth.
Jehovah has given his people this knowledge
so that we can act on it.
It should influence the choices we make.

en.text: That was my best friend, Lucas,
when we were kids.
And that was me, Oscar.
We knew exactly what we wanted to do
when we grew up:
Pioneer!
Go to Bethel!
Build Kingdom Halls!
We kept those goals.
And when graduation came,
we were ready.
Our little business needed just a few more accounts.
Then we’d have enough for us and to help our families.
Finally!
Day one of the service year
—and two new pioneers!
Where we live, . . .
Please don’t call me ever again!
. . . finding spiritual interest is tough.
We already have cleaners. Thanks.
And finding enough work was harder than we thought.
A few months in, I was sure
Jehovah would help if we just stuck it out.
Sorry, Oscar. Can’t make it today.
Something came up. Lucas.
What came up was an opportunity for more money,
but at what cost?
Are you quitting, or what?
No, I’m not quitting.
Pioneering or our business?
Neither, but you know the struggle here.
Most brothers can afford to pioneer for a year, two tops.
Look, it’s not full-time while I’m training.
It’s a backup plan.
So Lucas stopped pioneering?
Maybe he’s right.
He’s just being practical.
I mean, is it wrong to quit if you think it’s not working?
I struggled with the same question when I pioneered.
Whatever you decide,
if you can tell Jehovah your reason
with a clean conscience,
then it’s the right decision for you.
Why would I keep going when it’s so difficult?
“Since all these things are to be dissolved in this way,
“consider what sort of people you ought to be
in holy acts of conduct and deeds of godly devotion.”
It really is “the last days,”
and people need “the good news.”
And they’ll only hear it
if we keep up our “deeds of godly devotion”
as best we can.
I prayed to endure and only stop pioneering
if my circumstances left no other choice.
And I prayed to see the blessings.
And after a while,
I learned that a little perseverance,
with Jehovah’s spirit, can be contagious.
So, what do you want to do when you grow up?
Pioneer.
And go to Bethel?
Yep!
And then maybe build Kingdom Halls.
You in?
Yeah.

남편이 연구할 주제와 구체적인 질문을 써서 보내면

신뢰하는 데 있을 것이다” 라고 알려 주죠.
제가 아직 걱정할 때가 있긴 하지만,

여호와의 도움 덕분에 저는 더 강해졌습니다.
이제 더는 두렵지 않을 만큼 강해진 거죠.
여호와께서 함께하셨고, 계속 제 곁에 계실 거예요.

en.text: my husband and I were woken up
by a loud bang on the door.
As soon as my husband had opened the door,

“Everyone on the floor!”
I saw them taking my husband into the kitchen
and heard them
very aggressively ordering him to do something.
Then I heard some noise, and I realized
that he was being beaten.
My husband, Feliks, and I
were on our way back from the shopping mall
to the car park.
A jeep with tinted windows
blocked our path, and people
with weapons jumped out, shouting:
“On the ground! Don’t move!”
We were thrown against the vehicle.
Feliks was sent to a pretrial detention facility,
where he spent a year.
From the very first bang on the door,
I began praying to Jehovah for wisdom, calmness,
and for holy spirit so that I could make the right decisions
and act in the right way.
And for the whole day, I was praying.
Jehovah answered all my prayers,
and I felt that he was close at my side.
Before each court hearing when I was very afraid
and felt overwhelmed by emotion and couldn’t calm myself down,
it was prayer
that helped me to settle down.
When they took us for interrogation,
I started panicking and, at that moment,
I realized that I needed to meditate on something positive.
So I thought,
‘I need to sing our songs.’
And just one song came into my mind:
“He Will Make You Strong.”
It really strengthened me.
Those words about how Jehovah gave his Son for us
show he loves us and will never leave us.
Brothers and sisters
pray and tell me
that they are praying for me.
It gives me the feeling that I am part
of a large family.
After the interrogation,
he was sent home.
My husband and I
continue to stick to our spiritual routine.
We continue to conduct family worship, and we are always in the ministry.
Our brothers and sisters constantly support us.
They write kind words;
they commend us;
they send us encouraging scriptures from the Bible.
In September 2019, Feliks was found guilty
and sentenced to three years in a general regime colony.
When he and the other brothers arrived there, they were beaten up by officers
from the colony.
Feliks told me
that he prayed while he was being beaten,
and he noticed that at that moment, he stopped feeling the pain.
While he is behind bars,
Feliks tries to conduct family worship with me by letters.
He picks certain themes and some specific questions.
Then I do research
in the publications and send back what I find.
The scripture at Isaiah chapter 30 really strengthens me,
where it says that “your strength will be in keeping calm
and showing trust.”
Although I tend to worry,
I understand that calmness is expressed
by fully trusting in Jehovah.
I have become stronger because thanks to Jehovah,
in a way, I have developed almost a shell
against the difficulties
that used to scare me.
That confidence and faith help me.
Jehovah was with me,
and he will remain
close by me,
and we will be made stronger thanks to him,
and we will get through these trials.

en.text: On April 20, 2017,
the Supreme Court of the Russian Federation criminalized
the activity of Jehovah’s Witnesses.
As of July 4, 2019,
authorities have progressively seized 131 of the properties
owned by Jehovah’s Witnesses,
with an additional 60 properties subject to confiscation.
One of the seized properties
was the former Russia branch complex in Solnechnoye.
At the time of filming, the Russian authorities continue
their aggressive attack on Jehovah’s Witnesses.
As of August 17, 2020,
there were 42 Witnesses who were in pretrial detention
or sentenced to prison,
32 who were under house arrest,
and 169 who were not allowed to leave their hometown.
All have been charged with organizing,
participating in, or financing the activity
of a so-called “extremist” organization.
At least 380 Witnesses were, at the time, under investigation
—ranging in age from 19 to 89 years old.
What has this meant for the individuals affected?
As an example,
on June 3, 2018,
Brother Sergey Klimov was arrested.
Local authorities initiated
criminal charges against him,
placing him in pretrial detention for two months.
This detention was extended seven times,
separating him from his wife and family
for a year and five months,
before he was finally tried and sentenced.
On November 5, 2019,
he was sentenced to six years in prison.
Two of our dear young people in Russia,
Brother Yegor Baranov and Sister Darya Dulova,
are courageously facing criminal conviction
and potential long-term imprisonment.
Brother Baranov is only 19 years old.
When the authorities raided her home, Sister Dulova was only 18 years old.
By means of the Newsroom on jw.org,
we are informed of updated news events.
This page includes links to name lists
of Witnesses currently imprisoned for their faith,
which can help us include them specifically in our prayers.
Our brothers and sisters in Russia are resolved to remain loyal to Jehovah
despite any opposition,
and they put their confidence in him in the assurance
that Jehovah is on their side!

ko.text: 어떤 것에 관해 직접 알고 있는 사람을 가리킵니다.
우린 어떻게 여호와의 증인이 될 수 있습니까?
여호와께서 미래를 내다보실 수 있다는 사실을
두 번째로 우린 그분이 예언을 성취시키는 것을
아무도 막을 수 없다는 걸 알고 있습니다.
두 개의 놀라운 예언을 생각해 보겠습니다.
지속되지 않을 것이라는 점도 알려 주셨습니다.
여기를 두 부분으로 나누어서 읽어 볼 텐데요.
예루살렘과 그 성전이 두 번째로 멸망될 것이고,
그 도시와 거룩한 곳을 파괴할 것이며”
예루살렘과 그 성전은 이미 폐허 상태였습니다.
‘오고 있는 한 지도자의 백성이 파괴’할 거라고 했죠.
그런데 왜 이런 일이 있어야 했습니까?
이것이 예루살렘과 그 성전이 예언된 대로
기원 70년 전에 왔다는 걸 알 수 있습니다.
예수께서 하신 놀라운 예언 한 가지가
이 예언의 의미에 대해 생각해 보겠습니다.
주의 이름으로 기적을 많이 행하지 않았습니까?’
별로 놀라울 것도 없다는 생각이 들지 모릅니다.
시온 산에 어린양과 함께 있을 거라고 하셨죠.
이제 그 다음으로, 두 번째 요점은
아무도 예언이 성취되는 것을 막을 수 없다는 것입니다.
마귀는 예언이 성취되는 걸 막고 싶어 합니다.
한 명이라도 부족하게 만들 수 있다면
여호와의 예언이 틀렸다는 걸 보여주는 게 되니까요.
또 한 가지 예로, 미국과 영국이
영국은 세계 강국이 되지 못했을 겁니다.
영국이 세계 강국이 되지 못하게 막을 수 있는
모든 것이 영국에게 불리한 상황이었기 때문이죠.
그 밖의 여러 요인으로 프랑스는 패배했습니다.
그렇게 영국이 세계 강국이 된 것이죠.
그래서 19세기 후반에 영국, 즉 대영 제국은
미국과 권력을 나눠 가질 생각이 전혀 없었습니다.
아무도 예언 성취를 막을 수 없습니다.

en.text: Now, if you’d just
take a look at today’s text,
it says: “Come and witness
the activities of Jehovah”—witness.
Now, according to a dictionary,
a witness is someone who has personal knowledge of something.
So how can we be Witnesses of Jehovah?
What personal knowledge
do we have of his activities?
Well, first of all, we can testify to the fact
that Jehovah can see into the future.
And when he does that, he is right 100 percent of the time.
And second, we know that no one can prevent
what Jehovah foresees from coming true.
All of Jehovah’s prophecies come true.
Now, to illustrate the first point,
that Jehovah can see into the future,
let’s consider two remarkable prophecies
concerning the destruction of Jerusalem and its temple.
Now, we know that through the prophet Jeremiah,
Jehovah foretold that Jerusalem and the temple
would be destroyed by the Babylonians.
Did it come true?
Absolutely—in 607 B.C.E.
But Jehovah went further.
He said that Jerusalem would be rebuilt.
“They will rebuild the ancient ruins;
“they will raise up the desolated places of the past,
and they will restore the devastated cities.”
And true worship would also be restored.
So that was quite a level of knowledge.
But there’s more.
Jehovah went further.
Jehovah also indicated
that the spiritual revival wouldn’t last.
Now, that is remarkable.
And it’s implied by what we read in the second part
of Daniel 9:26.
I’d like you to have a look at this.
We’re going to be reading
two parts of this verse,
and it’s quite interesting
—Daniel 9:26.
So now, what’s our objective here?
It’s to see that Jerusalem and its temple
would be destroyed a second time
and that true worship would not last.
It says in the second part of verse 26:
“And the people of a leader who is coming
will destroy the city and the holy place.”
Now, when these words were written,
Jerusalem and the temple were already in ruins.
But Jehovah doesn’t say,
‘Nebuchadnezzar has destroyed the city and its temple.’
He says: “The people of a leader who is coming.”
The Roman general Titus in 70 C.E.
“will destroy the city and the holy place.”
In order for that prophecy to be fulfilled,
Jerusalem and the temple would have to be rebuilt
and then destroyed a second time.
Now, that is quite a level of knowledge —quite a level of information.
But what would make this necessary?
Why, when the Jews came back to the Promised Land
and they were intent on restoring true worship,
why would this fail?
And why would Jerusalem and the temple be destroyed a second time?
Part of it is due to what we find in the first part of verse 26:
“Messiah will be cut off.”
So Jehovah foretold, foresaw,
that when the Messiah came,
the Jews would reject him.
He would be cut off.
And because of that, partly because of that,
Jerusalem and the temple would be destroyed,
as it happens, in 70 C.E.
Now, wait a minute, wait a minute.
Let’s think about that a minute.
The Messiah comes first and Jerusalem and the temple
are destroyed after that in 70 C.E.
What does that mean?
It means that the Messiah comes before 70 C.E.
So we might ask our Jewish friends,
why are you still waiting for the Messiah?
70 C.E. has come and gone.
Well, the Messiah came, and he too proved to be a true prophet.
And a remarkable prophecy of Jesus is found in the Sermon on the Mount.
Let’s have a look at it and consider the implications of this prophecy.
This is Matthew chapter 7,
and we’ll read verses 22 and 23,
an amazing prophecy.
Now, imagine: At this point, Jesus’ teachings
have not spread beyond Israel.
But notice verses 22 and 23:
“Many will say to me on that day:
“‘Lord, Lord, did we not prophesy in your name,
“‘and expel demons in your name,
“and perform many powerful works in your name?’
“And then I will declare to them: ‘I never knew you!
Get away from me, you workers of lawlessness!’”
Now, isn’t that amazing?
If Jesus had simply predicted
that his teachings would spread throughout the earth,
you might say, “Well, there’s nothing remarkable about that.”
But Jesus is saying something different.
Jesus is foretelling
a great apostasy from his teachings.
Jesus is foretelling the birth of Christendom
300 years before the event.
So Jesus foresees that many
are going to turn away from the truth.
And by the end of the first century,
that apostasy was already at work, wasn’t it?
There were sects
—the sect of Nicolaus, for example, and other sects.
And now they’re on the cusp of the great darkness,
the great apostasy, that’s going to set in from the second century on.
And with this in mind, what does Jehovah do?
He makes an amazing statement
—Revelation 14—
‘144,00 will be on Mount Zion with the Lamb.’
There were nowhere near 144,000 in the truth in the first century.
And here Jehovah is saying there are going to be 144,000 in heaven
with the Lamb at the end.
But not only that, he goes further.
There’s going to be a ‘great crowd that no man can number.’
How could that ever come true?
Ours is the God of true prophecy.
Well, that’s prophecy.
What about the second point?
And that is that no one can prevent prophecy from being fulfilled.
The Devil would love to prevent that from taking place.
Think about Revelation 14.
If the Devil could make the number
one short of 144,000,
he’d be happy because he would show
that Jehovah was inaccurate in what he foretold.
And so that’s one of the reasons why the Devil
has made war on the remnant of the seed of the woman,
if at all possible, to prevent that number
of 144,000 from coming to pass.
But, of course, he’s going to fail.
And what about the prophecy in the Bible
that America and Britain would become a dual world power?
Now, Britain wouldn’t become a world power
at all if France had anything to say about it.
France and Britain were sworn enemies.
And for many, many, years,
France was much richer and much more powerful
than Britain was.
And finally, at the Battle of Waterloo in 1815,
France had one last chance
to prevent Britain from becoming a world power.
And France should have won that battle.
Everything was stacked against the British.
But there was a driving rain,
a fatal miscalculation on the part of Napoleon,
and a few other factors that foiled their attempt.
And Britain did become a world power.
And at the end of the 19th century,
it’s quite true that the sun never set on the British Empire.
But now, America and Britain were supposed to become a dual world power,
and Britain wasn’t the least bit interested in sharing its power with America.
It tried to prevent America from separating as a colony.
There was a long war,
and there were mistakes made on both sides.
But finally, America gained its independence from Britain.
Well, what do we find?
Some years after that,
Britain is sharing its power with America.
They are a dual world power.
Fighters against God will never prevail.
We serve “the God of true prophecy.”
And “what he foretells comes to be.”

cn.text: 今天的经文是诗篇46:8
经文说
“你们来见证耶和华的作为”
谈到“见证”
一本词典解释
“见证人”是指了解某件事并能作证的人
那么我们怎么成为耶和华的见证人呢？
关于耶和华的作为
我们自己都了解了哪些呢？
那首先我们可以作证的是
耶和华可以预知未来
他说出预言时，从来不会出错
其次，我们知道没有什么能阻止
耶和华实现他的预言
所有耶和华的预言都会实现
为了说明第一个要点
耶和华能预知未来
我们来看看两个令人印象深刻的预言
它们跟耶路撒冷以及圣殿的毁灭有关
我们知道，通过耶利米先知
耶和华预言
耶路撒冷和圣殿会被巴比伦大军毁灭
预言实现了吗？
没错
就是在公元前607年
但预言不止如此
他说，耶路撒冷会被重建
以赛亚书61:4说
“他们要重建旧日的废墟
修复昔日的荒地
他们要重建荒废的城镇”
另外，正确的崇拜也会复兴
耶和华给了非常具体的信息
而且他还给了更多细节
耶和华还预告
以色列人不会一直坚持正确的崇拜
这非同寻常
我们能够从但以理书9:26的后半部分
看出一点线索
请大家跟我一起看看这节经文
我们会读出这节经文的两个部分
这很有意思
但以理书9:26
那么，我们可以从这节经文看出什么呢？
耶路撒冷和圣殿会再次被毁灭
对耶和华的正确崇拜也会在此中断
9:26的后半部分说
“一个领袖会率领人
来毁灭这座城和圣地。”
当这节经文被记下时
耶路撒冷和圣殿就已经是废墟了
但经文不是说
尼布甲尼撒已经毁灭了这座城和圣殿
而是说
一个领袖会率领人来毁灭这座城和圣地
这个领袖就是公元70年的
罗马将军提图斯
耶路撒冷和圣殿要先被重建
然后第二次被毁灭
但以理书这个预言才会实现
这个预言很清楚也很具体
但是，事情为什么要这样发生呢？
本来
犹太人回到那片上帝承诺赐予的土地
是要恢复正确的崇拜
为什么却失败了呢？
耶路撒冷和圣殿为什么又一次被毁灭了呢？
部分原因是
26节的前半部分，经文说
“弥赛亚会被处死”
然后耶和华预告
当弥赛亚来到时
犹太人会弃绝他
然后把他处死
因为这个原因
或者这是部分的原因
耶路撒冷和圣殿在公元70年被毁灭了
等一下
让我们仔细想一想
弥赛亚要先来
然后耶路撒冷和圣殿
才会在公元70年被毁灭
这说明
弥赛亚在公元70年之前就已经来了
如果你遇到一些有犹太教背景的人
可以问问他们
“为什么你还在等待弥赛亚呢？”
弥赛亚来到后
他说的预言也非常准确
耶稣在登山宝训中说了这样一个预言
我们一起读读这个预言
考虑一下，他的意思是什么？
马太福音第7章
我们来读一读22和23节
有意思的是
在那个时候耶稣教导的对象
仍然只限于以色列人
“到那个日子，很多人会对我说
主啊，主啊，我们不是奉你的名说过预言
奉你的名赶过邪灵
奉你的名施行过很多奇迹吗？
到时我就要向他们声明说
我从来不认识你们！
走开，你们这些不守上帝法律的人！”
这个预言出人意料
如果耶稣只是说他的教导会传遍全球
你可能会说
“这个预言也没有什么特别之处啊！”
但耶稣其实是在预告
会有很多人背弃他的教导
在耶稣说完这个预言300年后
假基督教出现了
所以耶稣预料将会有很多人离弃真理
其实到了1世纪末
已经有人开始叛道了
当时出现了一些教派
比如尼哥拉派，还有其他的
从那时起，一段黑暗时期即将开始
就是大规模的叛道，而且会持续很多年
再来考虑耶和华的一个预言
在上帝的启示下，启示录14章提到
会有14万4000人
和绵羊羔站在锡安山上
1世纪的基督徒的人数
远远少于14万4000人
但耶和华说
最终会有14万4000人
和绵羊羔一起在天上
上帝还预告
将会有“一大群人
没有人能数得过来”
这会怎样实现呢？
我们的上帝是说预言的上帝
他说的一定会实现
第二点是什么呢？
没有什么可以阻止耶和华实现他的预言
魔鬼巴不得能阻止预言发生
想一下启示录14章
如果魔鬼可以让14万4000人少一个
他会很高兴
因为这样他就可以证明
耶和华的预言是不准确的
这就是为什么魔鬼要跟女人的后代中
余下的人作战
魔鬼一定会
尽全力阻止14万4000人到天上去
但毫无疑问，他终将失败
圣经中另外一个预言
是关于英国、美国会成为联合的世界霸权
但如果法国能阻止的话
英国就不会成为世界霸权了
法国和英国向来是宿敌
很多很多年以来
法国都比英国
要富有得多
也强大得多
但最终在1815年的滑铁卢战役中
法国本来有机会
可以最后阻止英国成为世界强权
而且看上去能够赢得这场战争
因为法国占尽了优势
不过一场突然的暴雨
拿破仑犯的一个致命的错误
还有其他一些因素
让法国最终失败了
英国也成为了世界强权
最后到了十九世纪的末期
英国真正成为了日不落帝国
可是预言说美国和英国会成为联合的霸权
不过英国一点儿也不想和美国分享势力
还试图阻止美国从殖民地脱离，独立出来
经过一场漫长的战争
双方都犯了不少的错误
但最终美国成为了独立的国家
后来呢，过了一些年
英国跟美国分享了势力
而且成为了联合的世界霸权
没有人能阻止上帝预言的应验
我们崇拜的是说预言的上帝
“他的预言必实现”

titles.ko: 데이비드 H. 스플레인: 우리는 참된 예언의 하느님을 섬깁니다 (시 46:8)

title: 나의 십 대 이야기—부모님과 어떻게 대화를 잘할 수 있을까?

ko.text: 또 저는 빨리 어른이 되고 싶었는데
사람들이 절 어른으로 대해 주길 원했거든요.
엄마는 학교로 저를 데리러 오곤 하셨어요.
하지만 전 너무 캐묻는 것처럼 느껴졌어요.
이어폰을 끼고 아무런 대꾸도 하지 않았어요.
다른 모국어를 사용하는 사람과 대화를 하면,
전 부모님이 제 마음을 모르신다고 느꼈죠.
여호와의 특성에 관해 많은 걸 배웠어요.
한 가지로 그분은 다가가기 쉬운 분이시죠.
그리고 집에서 제가 어떻게 행동하는지 돌아봤죠.
집에서 부모님을 대할 때 고칠 게 많더라고요.
전 두 개의 세상에서 사는 것 같았어요.
학교에서는 친구들이 절 잘 이해해 주는 것 같았죠.
전 여러 나쁜 습관에 빠지게 됐는데,
지금 상황이 훨씬 더 좋았을 거예요.
예수는 완전하셨고 완벽한 판단력을 갖고 계셨지만
전 가족들에게 더 은혜롭게 말할 필요가 있었죠.
제가 부모님께 날카롭게 말하는 경향이 있었기 때문에,
처음에 부모님과 대화를 하려고 했을 땐
부모님께 더 많은 관심을 가지려고 노력했어요.
부모님이 절 이해 못하는 것에만 초점을 맞추다 보니
이해하려는 노력조차 하지 않았던 것 같아요.
제가 아기였을 때부터, 오랜 시간 동안
그래서 저는 제가 누군가를 위해 열심히 일했는데
그 사람이 감사하다는 말을 하지 않으면 어떨지,
또 그 사람이 절 가까운 사이로 여기지 않으면 어떨지
부모님과 대화하는 게 훨씬 더 쉬워졌어요.
부모님이 하시는 말씀과 조언을 잘 받아들이고,
어디에 가는지 부모님께 알려 드리는 게
마음 가는 대로 행동하게 되기가 쉽죠.
종종 해를 입게 되는 경우가 있어요.
마음 가는 대로 행동하지 말라고 말씀하시는 거예요.
십 대 시절의 저와 이야기할 수 있다면,
하지만 사실은 저를 도와주려고 하셨던 거죠.

en.text: Well, when I was a teenager,
I didn’t see any benefit
in talking to my parents
because they liked different things than I liked.
So I thought, ‘Well, what’s the point?’
And I also wanted to be an adult.
I wanted to feel like an adult and be treated like an adult.
I remember when my mom used to pick me up from school.
She wanted to show personal interest in me,
so she’d ask me: “Oh, how are your friends doing?
“How was school today?
Do you have a lot of homework?”
But I just thought that she was being nosy.
I always had my earphones on.
And whenever my parents were trying to talk to me,
that was my chance to just pop them in and ignore them.
The way my parents grew up wasn’t
the same way that I grew up.
They grew up in a different country;
they spoke a different language; they grew up in a different time.
When you’re talking to somebody who doesn’t speak your language natively,
oftentimes you won’t be able to explain things from your heart.
And so I had that challenge.
I wasn’t able to talk directly to my parents heart to heart.
And so there was always this frustration
in trying to really convey how I felt.
And I felt like I wasn’t really getting through to my parents.
When I went to my first pioneer school, I learned a lot about Jehovah’s qualities.
And one of them was how he was a very approachable Person.
And I thought to myself, ‘Am I an approachable person?’
And I thought about how I acted in the ministry
and then at the meetings and then at home.
And I realized that at home I had a lot of things I needed to fix.
I felt like it was two different worlds I was living in.
One was when I was at school with my peers;
I felt like I was understood.
And at home, I kind of just withdrew to myself.
I wouldn’t try to communicate with them because it didn’t seem worth the effort.
I tried to figure out problems in my own way.
It was kind of trial and error.
I developed a lot of bad habits
that today I’m still trying to overcome.
If I’d been able to communicate with them more,
if I’d been able to connect with them and ask for their help
and get their support and have them on my team,
things would have gone a lot better.
And I really wish I had.
Jesus, who was a perfect human being
and who had perfect judgment, didn’t make decisions on his own.
He always looked to his Father for guidance.
And that got me thinking,
‘Well, if Jesus did that,
‘there has to be something good
in it for me too.’
What really helped me was Colossians 4:6.
I knew I needed to speak more graciously in the family.
And I realized that I was speaking very defensively
and that I needed to be more approachable to my parents.
When I first tried to talk with them, of course,
it was awkward and I didn’t want to talk about anything personal
because I wasn’t used to it.
So I thought I could maybe ask them about themselves
—ask them how their day was or what they liked from the meetings.
So I just tried to show more interest in them
instead of focusing on myself.
And I think that’s what got
the conversations going
and got me comfortable
to really talk with them.
I was so focused on how my parents weren’t understanding me
that I wasn’t really trying to understand them.
When I thought about my parents,
I thought about how much work it takes to be a parent.
From when I was a baby, for many years,
they were working day and night to try to care for me.
They never demanded a thank you or anything from me.
They were really self-sacrificing.
And I imagined: ‘If I had to work that much for somebody,
‘how would I feel if they didn’t really say thank you?
‘Or how would I feel
‘if this person whom I worked so hard for
didn’t really view me as their friend?’
Later on, as I got older and started
that communication going with my parents,
I realized that taking their advice and really listening to their opinions
and always letting them know
what I’m going to do and where I’m going to go
was a mature thing to do.
Our heart oftentimes
takes the driver’s seat, and it directs us
to where it thinks it should go.
And oftentimes it goes in the wrong direction,
and we sometimes get hurt.
Then we look back and say, “I wish I hadn’t done that.”
And our parents have been there.
What they’re trying to do for us now is to tell us,
“Don’t let your heart take the driver’s seat.”
If I could talk to my teenage self,
I would tell myself to see my mom and dad more like coaches,
because I used to think they were always trying to criticize me
and point out my faults.
But, really, they’re just trying to help me,
and they want me to have a happy life.
I really wish I knew that as a teenager.
But I’m glad I learned that now.

cn.text: 我十几岁时
觉得和爸妈说话对我没什么帮助
因为我们喜欢的东西完全不一样
所以我想有什么必要和他们沟通呢？
我想做个大人
也希望别人对待我就像对待大人一样
以前我妈妈来接我放学时
她很关心我就问我
你的朋友们好吗？
你今天在学校过得怎么样呢？
你的作业多不多啊？
但是我觉得她很烦
所以就总是戴上耳机
每一次我爸妈想跟我说话
我都会戴上耳机、堵住耳朵不理他们
我爸妈成长的背景跟我完全不一样
他们在另外一个国家长大
说不一样的语言
年轻时候的生活也跟我完全不一样
如果你跟一个人说话
他的母语跟你的不一样
你就没办法让他了解你心里真实的感受
我就有这种难题
我没办法让父母亲知道
我心里在想什么
所以每一次我跟他们说话的时候
心里都充满挫败感
我觉得他们真的不能完全了解我
我第一次参加先驱训练班时
学到了很多关于耶和华的特质
其中一个就是他很平易近人
所以我就问问自己，我平易近人吗？
在传道时、在聚会里、在家里
我给人什么感觉呢？
然后我意识到
在家里我需要改善对父母的态度
我觉得自己生活在两个不同的世界
一个是在学校里跟同学在一起的时候
我觉得他们了解我
另外一个是在家里，我把自己封闭起来
我不想跟父母亲说话
因为我觉得这样做也没有用
我用自己的方法解决问题
但却是一场灾难
我养成了很多坏习惯
现在还在努力克服当中
如果我能跟他们有更好的沟通
就能够向他们求助
他们就会帮助我支持我
现在我就不会有那么多难题了
如果是这样就好了
耶稣在地上时是完美的
他有完美的判断力
但他没有依靠自己做决定
而总是向父亲寻求帮助
这让我思考
如果耶稣这样做，那我也应该这样做
歌罗西书4:6给了我很大帮助
我知道对家人说话时要更仁慈体贴
我意识到自己和父母说话时
好像把他们当作敌人
我应该更亲近他们一些
我刚开始尝试和他们交谈时
总觉得有点奇怪
我不想谈太多个人的事情
因为我还不习惯
所以我想可以问问关于他们的事情
他们的一天过得好不好？
喜欢聚会里的什么内容？
我试着多关心他们，而不是只关注自己
这样我跟他们的沟通就更多了
也就更容易表达自己的感受了
我太关心自己的感受
觉得他们为什么不了解我
但是，我却没有尝试过去了解他们
我开始站在父母亲的角度去想
他们要花多少精力去照顾孩子
在我很小的时候
那么多年，父母都没日没夜地照顾我
他们没有要求我跟他们说谢谢
但他们却真的为我牺牲了很多
我试着想象，如果我为一个人做了很多事
但他却没有表示感谢，我会有什么感觉呢？
或是
他甚至根本没有把我当作是他的好朋友
那我又会怎么想呢？
后来，随着我不断长大
我和父母的沟通变得越来越好了
我意识到听他们的建议
接受他们的意见
并且总是让他们知道
我要做什么，我要去哪里
才是一种真正成熟的表现
不要让情绪控制人生方向盘
因为它会带我们去自以为是对的地方
但通常都是不对的方向
最后让我们受伤
这时我们才说
“如果我没有那样做就好了。”
其实父母一直在身边
他们一直提醒我们
千万不要让情绪掌控你的一生
如果可以对青少年时期的自己说话
我想对自己说
我以前想的是不对的
应该把父母看作我们的教练
尽管他们会批评我，指正我的错误
但其实他们一直想帮助我
希望我有一个幸福的人生
真希望青少年时我就懂得这一点
但现在能明白我也很高兴

titles.ko: 나의 십 대 이야기—부모님과 어떻게 대화를 잘할 수 있을까?
titles.en: My Teen Life—How Can I Talk to My Parents?
titles.cn: 年少时的我——怎样和父母沟通？

ko.text: “내가 이런 말을 한 것은 나를 통해 여러분이
대속과 관련이 있다고 말할 수 있죠.
예수를 통해 우리가 얻게 되는 평화란 무엇입니까?
승인받고 있다는 걸 알 때 느끼게 됩니다.
원래대로 여호와와 좋은 관계를 누리게 됩니다.
따라서 예수를 통해 얻게 되는 “하느님의 평화”가
우리 마음이 움츠러들지 않게 막아 줍니다.
그럼 우리는 평화와 용기를 얻기 위해
어떤 것에 의해 마음이 북돋아진다는 뜻입니다.
바다 위를 걸으시는 예수를 보고 놀란 사도들에게도
그런데 이 다섯 경우를 좀 더 자세히 살펴보면,
예수께서는 “용기를 내라”고 명령만 하신 것이 아니라
왜 용기를 낼 수 있는지 알려 주셨습니다.
네, 바울이 그 이유를 이해할 수 있도록
예수께서는 바울이 왜 용기를 낼 수 있는지
그럼 성구의 그 부분을 읽어 보죠.
“네가 예루살렘에서 나에 대해 철저히 증거한 것처럼
각 경우에 예수께서 덧붙여 말씀하신 이유가
사적인 대화에서 다른 사람들을 격려할 때,
방금 살펴본 세 가지 예에서 그 점을 볼 수 있습니다.
그저 “용기를 내십시오!” 라고 하신 게 아니라
그 사람은 아버지 품에 안긴 아이처럼
그저 “용기를 내십시오!” 라고 하신 게 아니라
이전에는 여자에게 한 번도 사용하신 적이 없는
분명 예수의 말씀은 그 여자의 마음을
사도들과 함께 예루살렘의 위층 방에 계셨습니다.
또 안드레는 예수의 첫 제자 중 하나로
정든 제자들을 보고 가슴이 뭉클하신 그분은
우리는 어려움도 시련도 겪을 수 있지만,
평화가 있으면 용기를 낼 수 있다는 겁니다.
마음을 감동시키려고 하면서 이렇게 말할 수 있죠.

en.text: We will consider two questions:
What is the link between peace and courage,
and how can we help others to take courage?
Let’s begin with reading John 16:33.
On the evening before his death,
Jesus told his apostles at John 16:33:
“I have said these things to you
“so that by means of me you may have peace.
“In the world you will have tribulation,
“but take courage!
I have conquered the world.”
The key words are “peace” and “courage.”
Now, The Watchtower from which our comments are taken
uses the same verse in connection with the ransom arrangement.
The article states that the ransom
is an expression of courage.
Indeed, we can say that courage
is connected to the ransom in two ways:
For Jesus, paying the ransom required courage.
For us, receiving the ransom gives us courage.
Now, before we thus consider the expression “take courage,”
let’s first look at the word “peace.”
What is the peace that we receive by means of Jesus?
Well, it’s the inner calmness, the tranquility, that we feel
when we perceive that we are approved and loved
by Jehovah and by Jesus.
And what is the reason why we have such inner peace?
It is because of the ransom arrangement.
The ransom makes it possible for us
to be reconciled to God,
to be brought back into a relationship with Jehovah.
Now, what results from having peace?
Well, look at John 14:27.
Earlier that same evening, Jesus told his apostles:
“I leave you peace; I give you my peace. . . .
“Do not let your hearts be troubled
nor let them shrink out of fear.”
So “the peace of God” that we receive by means of Jesus
prevents our heart from shrinking out of fear.
In other words, having peace will give us courage.
Now, to illustrate the link between peace and courage,
think of a flower —let’s say a tulip.
A tulip has a bulb and a flower.
Let’s compare the bulb with peace
and the flower with courage.
Now, just as a tulip grows out of a bulb
that a gardener placed in the soil,
so courage grows out of inner peace
that Jehovah put in our heart.
Without a bulb, there is no flower.
Without inner peace, there is no godly courage.
So, what do we need to do in order to obtain
peace and courage?
Well, there is a saying that points in the right direction.
The saying is that a Bible that is falling apart
usually belongs to a person who is not.
Indeed, we need to use the Bible often.
We need to study it; we need to meditate upon it.
The more we do so, the more courageous we will be.
Now let’s return to John 16:33,
and consider the two words of our daily text:
“Take courage!”
What is the meaning?
Well, “take courage” has the same meaning as “take heart.”
In fact, the word “heart” and the word “courage”
come from the same Latin word, “cor.”
So “take courage” means
to be encouraged because of something.
Now as you can see on the monitor,
the Bible records five instances
where Jesus used the expression
“Take courage!”
In speaking to a paralyzed man,
Jesus said: “Take courage . . . !”
In speaking to a woman
who suffered from a flow of blood,
Jesus said: “Take courage . . . !”
In speaking to the frightened apostles
who saw him walking on the sea,
Jesus said: “Take courage!”
In speaking to his apostles
during the evening before his death,
Jesus said: “Take courage!”
In appearing to the apostle Paul,
Jesus said: “Take courage!”
Now, when we take a closer look at these five instances,
we note that Jesus followed a pattern
whenever he used that expression.
Each time after saying “take courage,”
what did Jesus do?
He added a reason.
Jesus did not only give a command
but also a reason that helped his listeners to understand
why  they could be encouraged.
For example, look at Acts 23:11,
where Jesus spoke to Paul.
Now, at the end of the first sentence, we see the words: “Take courage!”
Then, what is the next word that Jesus said?
“For” —meaning, for the reason that, or because.
So the word for  introduces the reason
why Paul could take courage.
Thus, we could read that part of the verse as follows: “Take courage!”
Why?
‘For [the reason that] just as you have given a thorough witness about me in Jerusalem,
so you must also bear witness in Rome.’
The clear reason that Jesus added to his commands
no doubt encouraged Paul.
Now, in the other instances where Jesus said “take courage,”
the word for  is implied.
The monitor shows the reasons
that Jesus added in the other instances.
Matthew 9:2: “Take courage . . . !”
Why?
“Your sins are forgiven.”
Matthew 9:22: “Take courage!”
Why?
“Your faith has made you well.”
Matthew 14:27: “Take courage . . . !”
Why?
“It is I; do not be afraid.”
John 16:33: “Take courage!”
Why?
“I have conquered the world.”
Now, how can we imitate the pattern that Jesus set?
When encouraging others from the platform
or in a private conversation,
we tell them not only what to do
but also why  they should do so.
We try to persuade their mind
by giving reasons for their actions.
Now, what else do we see in the pattern that Jesus followed?
In encouraging others, he tried
not only to persuade the mind
but also to move the heart.
We can see that in three of the examples that we just considered.
As you see on the monitor, here is example 1:
At Matthew 9:2,
Jesus did not just say “Take courage . . . !”
But he said to the paralyzed man:
“Take courage, child!”
What a touching way
to address that paralyzed man!
He must have felt secure like a child in the arms of his father.
No doubt Jesus’ words
moved the man’s heart.
Example 2: At Matthew 9:22,
Jesus did not just say “Take courage . . . !”
But he said to the woman suffering
from a flow of blood:
“Take courage, daughter!”
How tenderly Jesus treated the ailing woman
by calling her “daughter!”
It was a word of affection that Jesus had never used before
when addressing a woman.
No doubt Jesus’ words
moved the woman’s heart.
Example 3: On the last evening before Jesus death,
he was together with his apostles in the upper room in Jerusalem.
Now, let’s imagine what happened shortly before Jesus told them:
“Take courage!”
After instituting the Memorial,
Jesus looked around at these 11 faithful friends.
There they were.
Peter —Jesus couldn’t help but love him—
so impulsive but so sincere.
There was James and his younger brother John,
once “sons of thunder,” but how they had changed for the better!
—still zealous but also compassionate.
And there was Andrew, one of the first disciples he talked to,
still going strong.
As Jesus looked from face to face,
a feeling of deep affection must have welled up in him.
At that moment, he felt so close to them
that he was moved to address them in a way
he had never addressed them before.
He called them “little children.”
No doubt Jesus’ words
moved the hearts of the apostles.
Shortly thereafter, he told them:
“Take courage!”
Now, what lesson do we learn from Jesus in these three examples?
As we try to encourage others in the congregation,
at Bethel, or in other locations where we serve,
we want to convey to them
our warm and sincere feelings of friendship.
We want to move their hearts.
So, what are the two main points of our brief discussion?
We have challenges; we have trials,
but because of having peace, we can be courageous.
And when encouraging others,
we try to persuade their mind and move their heart
as we tell them: “Take courage!” my friend,
for Jehovah is our Helper.

cn.text: 我们会来谈谈两个问题
一个是安宁和勇气有什么关联
另一个是我们可以怎样帮助别人鼓起勇气
我们先来看约翰福音16:33
耶稣在死前的晚上对使徒说的话
就记载在这节经文里
他说:“我把这些事告诉你们
是要让你们可以靠着我得到安宁
你们在世上会经历患难
可是要鼓起勇气！
我已经战胜了世界。”
今天要谈的关键词是“安宁”和“勇气”
今天的评论所根据的《守望台》文章
在讨论赎价这个安排时
引用了这节经文
文章说明耶稣的赎价是勇气的表现
可以说，勇气跟赎价在两方面有关联
对耶稣来说，献出赎价需要有勇气
对我们来说，接受赎价给了我们勇气
在讨论“鼓起勇气”之前
我们会先来谈一谈“安宁”这个词
我们通过耶稣得到的安宁是什么呢？
这是一种内心的平静、安心的感觉
是当我们知道耶和华和耶稣
爱我们、认可我们的时候会有的
为什么我们能够有这种内心的安宁呢？
就是因为有赎价这个安排
赎价让全人类
让每一个人都有机会跟上帝和好
恢复原本跟耶和华的良好关系
享有安宁会带来什么结果呢？
请看约翰福音14:27
当天晚上稍早时
耶稣对使徒们说
“我把我的安宁赐给你们
我留下这种安宁给你们
你们心里不要难过，也不要畏缩。”
所以，上帝通过耶稣基督赐下的安宁
会使我们不因害怕而畏缩
也就是说，这种安宁会给我们勇气
我们可以用一种花来说明安宁和勇气的关系
那就是郁金香
郁金香有球茎和花朵
现在我们把球茎比作安宁
花朵比作勇气
就像郁金香的花朵从球茎长出来
而球茎是园丁埋在土里的
勇气是从内心的安宁产生的
而这种安宁是耶和华放在我们心里的
所以没有球茎就没有花朵
没有内心安宁就没有来自上帝的勇气
那么，我们必须怎样做
才能得到安宁和勇气呢？
有一个很有趣的说法能帮助我们明白这点
一本圣经被翻到旧了，都快要散了
通常它的主人却过得很幸福
所以，我们必须经常用圣经
要阅读，并且沉思
我们越常这样做就会越有勇气
我们回到约翰福音16:33
讨论一下今天经文的关键词“鼓起勇气”
这个词是什么意思？
“勇气”和“心”是有关联的
在某些语言
“心”和“勇气”来自同一个拉丁语词
所以“鼓起勇气”的意思是内心受到鼓励
现在，画面上有5节经文
都有同一个希腊语词
圣经中翻译成“放心”或“鼓起勇气”
耶稣对一个瘫痪的人说
耶稣对一个患了流血病症的女人说
使徒们看到耶稣在海上行走而感到害怕
耶稣就说
耶稣在死前的晚上
对使徒们说
耶稣向使徒保罗显现
对他说
现在我们会仔细了解这五个记载
请留意
耶稣在说这些话的时候都用了同一套模式
耶稣每次说完“鼓起勇气”或“放心”之后
都怎么做呢？
他都会说理由
耶稣不是只说安慰的话
还说明原因
让听到的人能清楚了解为什么不必害怕
一起来看使徒行传23:11耶稣说的话
耶稣对保罗说“你要鼓起勇气”
耶稣接下来说了什么呢？
他说明原因
他向使徒保罗清楚解释
为什么使徒保罗是可以鼓起勇气的
我们可以读一下这部分的经文
“你要鼓起勇气”原因是
你在耶路撒冷为我作了彻底的见证
也要在罗马为我作证
耶稣说完“鼓起勇气”后
清楚地解释原因
这无疑鼓励了保罗
在其他的四个地方
耶稣也没有说“因为”这个词
不过
在画面上你可以看出耶稣接着说明的理由
马太福音9:2说
马太福音9:22说
耶稣说
约翰福音16:33说
我们可以怎样效法耶稣立下的榜样呢？
不论是在台上或是私下聊天的时候
我们鼓励人，不只是告诉人要做什么
还会告诉他为什么应该要这样做
我们会跟对方推理
方法是向他说明理由
我们还能从耶稣说话的这个模式学到什么呢？
在鼓励别人时
耶稣不只是努力跟他们推理
还想办法打动他们的心
从我们刚刚谈的三个例子就能看得出来
就像你在画面上看到的第一个例子
耶稣不只是说:“放心吧。”
而是对那个瘫痪的人说
这样称呼这个瘫痪的男子
多么感人
他一定感觉像在爸爸的怀里那样安全
耶稣的话肯定打动了这个男子的心
第二个例子
耶稣不只是说:“放心吧。”
而是对这个患了流血病症的女人说
耶稣把这个生病的女人称为“女儿”
多么暖人心窝啊！
这是耶稣第一次把一个女人称为“女儿”
他这个充满温情的称呼
深深打动了这个女人的心
第三个例子
耶稣在去世前的晚上
跟使徒们聚在耶路撒冷一个楼上的房间里
现在我们来想象一下
耶稣对他们说“鼓起勇气”之前
发生了什么事
耶稣在创立纪念仪式后
看着身边这11位忠心的朋友
包括彼得
他虽然冲动，却很真诚
耶稣非常爱他
还有雅各和他的弟弟约翰
曾经的“雷霆之子”
后来却变得越来越好
依旧热心，但多了份怜悯
还有安德烈，他很早就跟随耶稣
而且一直保持忠心
耶稣看着他们每一个人
一定对他们有很深的感情
当下，他觉得自己跟他们非常地亲近
所以他用了一个他从未用过的称呼
他说:“孩子们。”
耶稣的话深深地打动了使徒们的心
不久后
耶稣告诉他们:“要鼓起勇气！”
这三个例子让我们从耶稣的身上学到什么呢？
当我们鼓励别人时，也许是在会众
在伯特利或在服务的其他地方
我们都很想向他们表达
我们的温暖的爱和真诚的关心
希望能打动他们的心
今天我们学到哪两个要点呢？
我们有难题，我们有考验
但因为内心有安宁
我们可以勇气十足
当我们鼓励别人时
要努力跟他们推理，打动他们的心
并对他们说
要鼓起勇气，我的朋友
因为耶和华一定会帮助你

ko.text: 여호와께선 “내 생각은 너희 생각과 다르다”고 하시죠.
하루 중 제가 지쳐 있을 만한 시간대를 피해서 연구를 해요.
이 내용이 절 위한 조언임을 깨닫게 해 주시고,
여호와께서 사람들을 어떻게 도와주셨는지 알려 주는 기록에,
또 어떤 색깔은 경고가 되는 본에 표시하죠.
묵상을 하면 그 지식을 실천할 힘이 생기죠.
어떤 상황이고, 몇 명이 나오는지 알아보면,
그 구절의 진짜 의미를 알게 되실 겁니다.
그때부터 아버지와 함께 하늘에 계셨던 거예요.
여호와와 좋은 관계를 누릴 때 얻죠.
또 하느님의 평화는 어떻게 ‘마음을 지켜’ 줄까요?
그 덕분에 여호와와의 관계가 가능해진 거죠.
이 원칙은 제가 성별, 인종, 국적에 상관없이
모든 사람에게 전파하는 데 도움이 됐어요.
거기서 배운 연구 방법 한 가지는
한쪽에서만 보면 전체 그림을 못 보죠.
전 공부한 점을 연구생에게 말해 줘요.
그럼 연구생이 여호와를 더 잘 알고,
실용적이란 걸 깨닫는 데 도움이 되죠.
“저는 전 시간 봉사를 그만두기로 결정을 다 해 놨었어요.

제게 아이가 생긴 걸 알고 기도했죠.
전 이 아이를 영원히 지킬 수 있을 거예요.”
전 배운 걸 아이에게 전부 가르쳐 줬어요.
강한 믿음을 유지하는 게 여기에 달렸죠.
우리가 매번 올바른 연구와 묵상을 할 때마다,
우리 믿음을 튼튼하게 해 주는 기둥이
위층 방으로 달려가 모든 걸 차단하면
살면서 예상치 못한 일을 많이 겪지만,

en.text: The more you study,
the more you understand Jehovah.
The more you understand Jehovah,
the more you love him.
Jehovah clearly tells us:
“My thoughts are not your thoughts.”
So if we want to understand Jehovah’s thinking better,
we need to dig deep in our study,
and then we share those thoughts with others.
Personal study is like fuel
that keeps you going.
Personally, I’m not a good student,
but I really learned how to study the Bible.
The Bible came alive during Gilead.
Self-discipline is involved —very much.
I overcome the tiredness aspect
of Bible study by not doing it
at a time of day when I know I’m going to be tired.
I can be tired for other things later on —but not for that.
Each session of my Bible study begins with a prayer,
“Please help me recognize it is counsel for me,
and then give me the strength to work on it.”
I have a color-coded system,
so I know what certain things stand for.
I have a particular color
for Jehovah’s good hand in people’s lives;
I have another color for warning examples;
I have another for fine examples to imitate.
You have to get behind the information,
not just focus on one verse or one chapter.
See who’s involved, the time,
the conditions, how many people are there,
and then you’ll get the true meaning of the verse.
John 1:1,
who is “the Word”?
We can go to verse 18.
“Begotten” meant
he had a beginning, a time when he started
—when he began—
in heaven with his Father.
That’s where he was.
Philippians 4:6, 7 is a scripture that I’ve read many times over.
“The peace of God that excels all thought.”
OK, how do you get that?
It’s from having a good relationship with Jehovah.
How is it that God’s peace ‘guards your heart’?
“By means of Christ Jesus” our Lord.
And I said: “Why by Jesus?
“Because Jesus paid the ransom;
that ransom is what makes possible a relationship with Jehovah.”
So it almost goes full circle.
I attended a School for Congregation Elders
that had Gilead graduates as instructors.
One of the methods is to analyze
a certain Bible account from different perspectives.
We can’t see the whole picture from one angle.
I share my research results with Bible students,
and that helps them to know Jehovah better,
and it helps them to see that what they’re studying
is of practical value.
I had studied up on Jacob;
he wrestled all night
with an angel.
And I wanted to share it with some of my friends.
One of the brothers that happened to sit around
when this discussion was going on came back to me, and he said to me:
“I had concluded my arrangements
“to quit full-time service.
“But after listening to that discussion,
I’ve decided that I’m no longer stopping.”
And that was such a wonderful moment for me.
I thanked Jehovah.
When I learned that I was going to become a mom,
I said, “Jehovah, if this little one
could love you, then I’ll get to keep him forever.”
And I began to teach everything I was learning to him.
So it’s a matter
of keeping my faith strong,
and there’s no shortcut.
Every session of study that is properly done with good meditation
adds a new pillar
to the strength of our faith.
I look forward to those times when I can, you know,
run upstairs by myself and just shut everything off,
and it’s just me and Jehovah.
Life today is very unpredictable,
but I’ve come to see that as long as I keep a tight grip on God’s Word,
nothing can “separate [me] from God’s love.”

cn.text: 我们越研读  就越了解耶和华的想法

耶和华说
“我的思想跟你们的思想不同”
如果想清楚了解耶和华的想法
研读时就需要深入挖掘
然后把学到的和别人分享

但在基列学校
我学到了该怎样研读圣经
也看出上帝的话语是活的
研读需要自律  这非常重要
我会在自己精力最充沛的时候研读
而不是在已经感觉累的时候才开始
要把精力充沛的时间留给研读

求耶和华帮我理解研读的内容

还有一种是值得我们效法的好榜样

研读帮助我们吸收知识
而沉思会让我们更有动力
把学到的实践出来

还要深入挖掘
考察一下经文背景
比如时间  地点  事件
