约翰福音1:1
这里提到的“话语”是谁呢?
接着看第18节
这里说“独生的”
看来他是有开始的
那他最开始在哪里呢?
在天上  和他的父亲在一起
找到答案了!
腓立比书4:6,7
这段经文我读过很多遍
上帝会“赐下超越人能理解的安宁”
我怎样才能得到这种安宁呢?
就是要和耶和华有良好的关系
那这种安宁会怎样守护我的内心？
“通过基督耶稣”
我就继续问
为什么要通过耶稣？
因为耶稣付出了赎价
而赎价让我有机会亲近天父耶和华
这样，前后就全都联系起来了
我个人研读时
会努力找出律法和诫命背后有什么原则
比如  在马太福音28:19,20
耶稣吩咐我们
“要去  使所有国族的人做我的门徒”
背后的原则是什么呢?
就是“要爱人如己”
这个原则会让我
更愿意向各种各样的人传道
无论对方来自哪里  有什么背景
我参加会众长老训练班的时候
有一位导师是基列毕业生
他跟我们分享了一个研读方法
就是从不同的角度分析一个圣经记载
因为单从一个角度
你无法了解事情的全貌
我和圣经学生
分享了我研读时查到的资料
这帮助他们更加认识耶和华
看出自己所学的具有实用价值
有一次
我研读了有关雅各
整夜和天使摔跤的记载
我很想和几个朋友分享我的收获
我记得
当时有一位弟兄听到了我的分享
事后他过来找我  对我说
我本来打算停止全时服务
但是听了你的分享以后
我决定继续留在全时服务的岗位上
听到他这么说  我真的很感动
我也真的非常感谢耶和华
当我知道自己快要做妈妈的时候
我就跟耶和华说
真希望这个小家伙也会爱你
这样我和他就能永远在一起了
所以  我努力把学到的一切都教给他
想保持坚强的信心
就必须研读和沉思  没有捷径
每次认真研读  好好沉思
都会巩固我们的信心
就好像把房子立在更牢固的根基上
每次我都很期待  放下所有的事情
一个人跑进房间  不受任何干扰
享受和耶和华独处的时光
生活中总有许多不确定因素
但可以确定的是
只要我紧握上帝的话语
就什么都不能隔断上帝对我的爱

titles.cn: 改进你的个人研读

ko.text: 우리 활동이 금지된 구역에서 봉사해 왔습니다.
지금은 둘이 함께 특별 파이오니아로 봉사하고 있어요.
그분은 “내가 너를 강하게 하고 너를 도와주겠다”라고 하셨죠.
경찰들이 우리 집에 찾아온 적이 있었어요.
기운을 내도록 힘을 주시는 걸 느낄 수 있었어요.
한 경찰은 우리에게 이런 말을 하기도 했어요.
“당신들은 우리가 하는 질문에 명확하게 답을 잘하는데?
다른 종교인들은 우리가 뭘 물어도 제대로 답을 못하던데 말이야.
또 경찰들에게 진리를 전할 좋은 기회가 되었죠.
질문을 하면서 관심을 보이는 경찰들이 있어서
연구생들도 우리 경험을 듣고 격려를 받아요.
오히려 더 열심히 형제 자매들과 함께
그렇게 하면 형제 자매들이 격려를 받아요.
그분은 실제로 제 편이 되어 주셨고,
사람은 제게 아무것도 할 수 없다는 걸 보여 주셨습니다.
우린 이 왕국회관을 처음 지을 때 공사에 참여했습니다.
그 후에 왕국회관이 두 번째로 지어질 때도 참여하게 됐습니다.
공사가 막바지에 이르렀을 때쯤 건축 현장에 갔는데,
우리를 반대하는 이웃들이 매일같이 찾아와서는 공사를 방해하면서 이렇게 말했어요.
이전 공사 때 겪었던 어려움들이나 이웃들이 우리한테 돌을 던졌던 일이 생생하게 떠올랐거든요.
하지만 이사야 41:10의 이 말씀이 힘이 되었습니다.
‘내가 너와 함께 있으니 두려워하지 마라. 내가 너의 하느님이니 걱정하지 마라.
내가 너를 강하게 하겠다. 내가 참으로 내 오른손으로 너를 붙들어 주겠다.’
이 말씀을 읽을 때마다 늘 힘이 났습니다.
“이제 예루살렘 성벽을 재건하여, 더 이상 이런 수치를 당하지 않도록 합시다.”
여호와의 뜻은 왕국회관이 건축되는 것이고, 그건 그곳 사람들에게도 필요한 일이었죠.
전 여호와께 다시 찬양이 돌아가길 바랐어요.
여호와께서 지원하신다는 걸 분명히 느낄 수 있었습니다.
우린 세 번째로 건축을 시작했고 45일 만에 공사를 마칠 수 있었습니다.
우린 여러 장로들 그리고 봉사의 종들과 잘 협조하면서 일했습니다.
여호와의 손길이 느껴졌어요. 우리의 힘을 북돋아 주셨죠.
그분이 우리를 격려해 주시는 걸 느낄 수 있었습니다.
우리는 잠잠히 있을 수 없습니다. 하느님을 찬양해야죠.
그분을 볼 수 있고 또 알고 있으니까요.
우린 그분이 곁에서 늘 우리를 도와주신다는 걸 확신할 수 있었어요.
그분은 사랑 많은 아버지처럼 우리 손을 꼭 붙잡고 계시죠.
잘 인내한 덕분에 현재 많은 축복을 누리고 있습니다.
우리가 받은 모든 축복에 대해 여호와께 진심으로 감사드려요.
여호와께서 자신의 이름을 위해 원하는 무엇이든 되실 수 있다는 걸 분명히 깨달았습니다.

en.text: Since my dedication and baptism,
I have been serving in a territory
where our work is under ban.
When I was serving
in the full-time ministry,
I was assigned as a special pioneer to the territory
where my future husband had been serving.
Then we got married, and now we are sharing
in this special avenue of service together.
We are persecuted, put on probation,
and confronted by government officials.
In difficult times, Jehovah personally assures me
with the words from Isaiah:
“I will fortify you, yes, I will help you.”
The last time government officials came to our place,
they took us to their office for questioning.
They said they had no choice, and we went in their car.
At that moment, I felt that Jehovah
was not only giving me his holy spirit and wisdom
but also giving me the physical strength to go.
I was so thankful to him.
Indeed, on that day when we were taken in the car,
I prayed to Jehovah,
“Please help us to be able to give a witness about you.”
A government official even said these words:
“It’s very interesting for us to talk with you.
“When we talk with people of other faiths,
“we never have our questions fully answered.
“But you know the correct answers to our questions
and are capable of giving them.”
Isaiah 31:5 is a big help
because there Jehovah is described
as being “like swooping birds.”
After all, Jehovah is above me.
In this verse he also promises that he will defend and save.
Encounters with government officials and discussions with them
have brought many blessings for our brothers,
for our Bible students, and for us.
But it has been a good opportunity for policemen too,
because there are sincere ones among them who have a lot of questions.
We have had good discussions,
and I began to view them as my return visits.
We have shared with our students how Jehovah is giving us strength,
and how he is blessing us when we are talking with government officials.
As a result, they are able to stay strong in the faith.
After meeting with the police, we never sit at home trembling in fear.
On the contrary, we try to share in field service with our brothers and sisters
even more because it’s also an encouragement for them.
We spend a lot of time sharing with them
how Jehovah glorifies his name.
In certain situations, through his words in the Psalms,
Jehovah shows me that he is on my side,
and I fully believe it.
Jehovah indeed is on my side,
and he has shown me that people can do nothing to me.
We participated in the construction when the Kingdom Hall was
built the first time.
Everything was finished very nicely.
Then we were involved in the construction
of the same Kingdom Hall the second time.
And when we were close to the end of the construction
and came to the construction site and saw everything burned-out and ruined,
we cried.
So almost every day, unfriendly neighbors stopped us
and continued to say to us: “Stop your work.
Go out from our village.”
In those moments, I just used to pray silently to Jehovah.
I was a bit afraid since I still had fresh in my mind all the memories,
the difficulties, and how the neighbors threw stones at us.
But the words in Isaiah 41:10 gave me strength:
“Do not be afraid, for I am with you.
“Do not be anxious, for I am your God.
I will fortify you, . . . I will really hold on to you with my right hand.”
Reading these words
always gave us power to continue in our service.
I reflected on the words in Nehemiah 2:17:
“Come, let us rebuild the walls of Jerusalem,
so that this disgrace will not continue.”
Jehovah wants this Kingdom Hall to be.
This is important to the people there,
so I wanted the praise for Jehovah, again.
It was more than clear that Jehovah was backing us.
We finished construction of that same
Kingdom Hall for the third time from the floor to the roof in 45 days.
From a human standpoint, this was not possible.
We worked closely with many elders and ministerial servants.
It was an enjoyable experience.
We felt Jehovah’s hand.
Jehovah strengthened our spirit.
He encouraged us, and we felt it.
We cannot be silent; we have to praise God.
We see him.
We know him.
Jehovah poured out his holy spirit,
and we gained confidence that Jehovah
is always near and ready to help.
He is like a loving Father holding us by our hands.
Endurance helped us to receive
all the blessings we are experiencing now.
I am very grateful to Jehovah God for all these blessings.
I realize more fully that
for his name, Jehovah becomes anything he wants.

cn.text: 我受浸后
一直在受禁止的地区服务
做正规先驱一段时间后
我被委派做特别先驱
那时候我认识了我的丈夫
当时他也在那里服务
结婚后我们一起做特别先驱
我们受到过迫害
被判过缓刑
也面对过政府官员的盘问
在那些艰难的时候
耶和华通过以赛亚书的话
亲自向我保证
“我要使你坚强”
“我一定会帮助你”
政府官员最近一次来我家的时候
要把我们带去盘问
他们说他们也是执行任务
让我们跟他们上车
那时
我感受到耶和华
不仅赐给我神圣力量和智慧
也让我有力气跟他们走
我真的很感谢他
那天我们被带走的时候
我向耶和华祷告说
请帮助我们
让我们能为你作见证
有位政府官员甚至说
我很喜欢和你们聊天
其他宗教的人
都不能完全解答我们的疑问
但你们不仅可以回答我们
还解释得很清楚
以赛亚书31:5
把耶和华比作展翅护雏的飞鸟
这很鼓励我
让我感觉耶和华就在身边
这节经文还保证
他一定会保护我
一定施行拯救
和政府官员接触带来很大益处
这样的经历不仅让弟兄姐妹
圣经学生和我们自己得到鼓励
也给那些警察提供了很好的机会
他们当中有些人对真理很感兴趣
提出了不少问题
我们讨论得很愉快
其中有些人可以算是我的续访了
我们会给圣经学生讲
在和政府官员交谈时
耶和华怎样赐我们力量
怎样赐福给我们
这强化了他们的信心
遇到安全问题后
我们没有吓得躲在家里
反而更加积极地和弟兄姐妹一起传道
这对他们来说也是一种鼓励
我们也花不少时间跟他们相处
分享耶和华怎样使自己的名得到荣耀
耶和华通过诗篇里的话告诉我
他在我身边
我也确信这一点
这些经历让我体会到
耶和华确实在我身边
世人的确不能把我怎么样
第一次建这个王国聚会所的时候
我们都参与了
整个工程非常顺利
第二次重建的时候我们又去了
就在快完工的时候
聚会所又被人放火烧了
我们看到眼前的一切就哭了
那时候邻居几乎天天来反对我们
一直说:停工!
我们村不欢迎你们!
遇到这种情况
我就会在心里向耶和华祷告
我们遇到的那些困难
那些邻居向我们扔石头的样子
我还记得很清楚
所以我当时有点害怕
但我从以赛亚书41:10得到力量
经文说
“你不要怕，因为我与你同在”
“你不要忧虑”
“因为我是你的上帝”
“我要使你坚强”
“我一定会帮助你”
“一定会用我伸张正义的右手扶持你”
读到这些话总是让我充满力量
继续我们的工作
我沉思尼希米记2:17的话
“来吧，让我们重建耶路撒冷的城墙”
“不要再这么没尊严了！”
耶和华希望这里有聚会所
因为当地人很需要
我想要重建聚会所，赞美耶和华
很显然耶和华在背后支持我们
我们在原地第三次重建了聚会所
从地面到房顶
整个工程只用了45天
这在人看来是不可能的
我们和很多长老、助理仆人一起工作
大家关系都很亲密
那真是段愉快的时光
我们体会到耶和华的手在帮助我们
让我们振作起来
耶和华在鼓励我们
我们能感受到
我们不能沉默
我们必须赞美上帝
我们能看到他的作为
我们认识他
耶和华赐给我们充足的神圣力量
我们确信他总是在我们身边
随时帮助我们
他就像一位仁爱的父亲
时刻牵着我们的手
我们的忍耐是值得的
现在我们得到了很多福分
我非常感激耶和华所赐的一切福分
现在我更清楚明白耶和华名字的含义
他要做什么都能成功

titles.cn: 遭受迫害仍显出勇气

ko.text: 전 중립을 지킨다는 이유로 체포돼서 2년 6개월 형을 선고받았습니다.
감옥에 들어서자 모든 게 낯설고 겁이 났죠.
아는 사람도 없었고 감옥 생활이 어떤 건지도 몰랐어요.
어떤 문제든 평화롭게 해결하고 어떤 어려움이든 견딜 수 있게
능력과 힘을 달라고 여호와께 계속 기도했습니다.
그 안에서 제게 위로가 된 건 기도와 하느님의 말씀뿐이었죠.
출판물도 볼 수 있었는데, 조건이 있었어요.
근데 그렇다고 해서 말도 하면 안 되는 건 아니잖아요?
전 무슨 일이 있어도 충실을 유지하겠다고 결심했습니다.
제 행실을 보고 다른 수감자들이 좋은 인상을 받았어요.
제가 읽을 차례에 성경을 돌려받지 못한 적도 많았어요.
전 욕을 안 했고 청결을 유지했는데,
하루는 절 부르더니, 제가 청결하고 행실이 바르니까
봉사도 정말 즐거웠는데, 120시간을 봉사한 달도 있었어요.
여호와 덕분에, 수감되어 있는 동안 계속 정규 파이오니아를 할 수 있었습니다.
연합된 형제들 모두가 저와 같은 고난을 겪고 있다는
베드로 전서 5장 9절의 말씀이 제게 큰 힘이 되었어요.
앞으로 어떤 상황에 처하게 되든, 누가 우리를 위협하든
여호와께서 우릴 절대 버리지 않으실 거라고 확신합니다.
마침내 출소일이 되어 집에 갔을 때 어머니가 정말 깜짝 놀라셨죠.
어머니를 다시 만난 그날을 절대 잊지 못할 겁니다.

en.text: I was arrested and sentenced to two and a half years
in prison for my neutrality.
The surroundings in prison were unfamiliar and overwhelming.
I didn’t know anyone, and I didn’t know what to expect from them.
I was the only Witness.
I was continually praying to Jehovah for power and strength
to be able to resolve any problems in a peaceful manner
and withstand any difficulties.
In that situation, only prayer and God’s Word brought me comfort.
But then my Bible was taken away from me.
It was returned to me, though, some time later.
I was allowed to have literature on one condition:
that I would not preach.
True, preaching wasn’t allowed, but that didn’t
mean I wasn’t allowed to speak, did it?
I was determined that no matter what happened,
I would remain faithful.
My good conduct had a positive effect on the other prisoners.
Some of them started reading the Bible.
Quite often, I couldn’t even get my turn to read it.
I didn’t swear, and I kept myself physically clean.
This didn’t go unnoticed by the prison officials.
One day, they said to me,
“Because you are morally and physically clean,
we want you to be our head cook.”
That’s how I became their chef.
I constantly saw evidence of Jehovah’s hand.
The ministry was amazing.
There were months when I served up to 120 hours.
I placed more than 100 pieces of literature.
Thanks to Jehovah, I was able to stay in the full-time ministry
the whole time I was in prison.
This filled my heart with joy.
The thought at 1 Peter 5:9,
which says that the entire association of brothers
is experiencing the same kind of suffering I was, strengthened me.
I am confident that no matter what circumstances we find ourselves in,
no matter who is around us, Jehovah will never abandon us.
The day for my release finally arrived.
It was a complete surprise for my mother.
I hadn’t told her.
I will never forget that moment when we were reunited.

cn.text: 我因为严守中立，拒服兵役
被判入狱两年半
我从来没有进过监狱
一切都很陌生，我感到很无助
我是监狱里唯一的耶和华见证人
我不认识任何人
不知道他们会怎么对我
我不断祷告
求耶和华给我力量
冷静地处理问题
并帮助我忍受逆境
祷告和研读圣经给我很大的安慰
但后来他们拿走了我的圣经
虽然之后又还我
但是他们说
如果我想要其他书刊
就不准再传道
没错，他们不让我传道
但没禁止我说话啊！
我早就下定决心
不管发生什么事，都要忠贞到底
我的好行为也对其他囚犯产生好影响
有些人开始拿我的圣经去阅读
有时候我想看，还轮不到呢！
因为我不说脏话
而且总是保持干净
这些监狱的长官都看在眼里
有一天，他们跟我说
因为你表现良好，又注重卫生
我们决定派你去当主厨
就这样，我开始做厨师的工作
我一直清楚看见耶和华的手在扶持我
没想到我能在监狱里
得到这么丰硕的成果
好几个月，我传道120小时
分发了100多份圣经书刊
我很感谢耶和华
让我在监狱里全时为他服务
这让我非常快乐
彼得前书5：9说
整个弟兄团体都跟我经历同样的苦难
这给我很大的力量
我有信心
不管我们处于什么困境
周遭有什么人
耶和华都不会离弃我们
终于，我被释放了
我没有事先告诉妈妈
所以她看到我回家时
高兴得不得了
我永远忘不了
见到妈妈的那一刻！

titles.cn: 在迫害下保持忍耐

title: 여호와 하느님께서 제게 힘을 주실 겁니다

ko.text: 집을 수색해서 물건을 다 압수하고는 우리를 감옥에 가뒀지요.
저 혼자 감옥에 수감돼서 정말 무서웠어요.
그분만이 절 지켜 주실 수 있으니까요.
힘을 주실 거라는 사실을 생각한 게 도움이 됐어요.
영적으로 약해지는 것 같다는 느낌을 받은 적은 한 번도 없었습니다.
“내 딸아, 내가 함께 있으니 걱정하지 말아라!”
자유, 건강이나 경제적 이득을 더 사랑했다면은
하지만 저는 이 모든 것들보다 여호와 하느님을 더 사랑했기 때문에
가족들과 함께 집회에 가고 봉사도 할 수 있죠.
여호와의 손이 저와 함께한다는 걸 느꼈어요.
분명 여호와께서 저처럼 축복해 주실 겁니다.
여호와께서 지금 우리의 충절을 영원히 잊지 않으실 거라는 사실과
그분을 영원히 충성스럽게 섬기겠다고 다짐하게 합니다.

en.text: I was imprisoned for a year and three months
for upholding Christian neutrality.
I was in a cell with all types of hardened criminals.
I was sitting at home.
My whole family had been arrested.
They burned down the villages.
We had to go live in the bush.
That was difficult because we had a baby.
The police came in with guns,
pointed them at us and handcuffed us,
searched all our house, took everything away,
and took us to the detention center.
And that was the beginning of our imprisonment.
I was taken to prison
all alone and scared,
but I trusted in Jehovah
—that only he could protect me.
During that entire time, what helped me was the thought
that Jehovah God would strengthen me
and that he was by my side.
Every day, I would review all those scriptures
in my mind and go over them;
that was the first thing I did in the day.
So never at any time, although I didn’t have a Bible,
did I feel any spiritual loss or weakness.
During the difficult moments with the baby,
we always prayed to Jehovah.
I saw Jehovah as my Father, as a real Person.
It was like I was hearing Jehovah’s voice saying to me:
“My daughter, don’t worry. I am with you!”
So I never shrunk back.
I remained firm!
If I had valued myself, my freedom,
my health, or material gain
more than my relationship with Jehovah,
I might not have chosen to serve him.
But because I loved Jehovah more than all these things,
I was able to choose Jehovah
even if that meant that I had to serve time in prison.
Now I can freely serve God,
attend religious meetings,
and go in the ministry with my family.
I felt that Jehovah’s hand was with me
and that fear disappeared.
The one who gave me so much strength was Jehovah.
If you love Jehovah, love has no fear;
love banishes fear.
And I can only say that my life,
despite everything, has been pleasant,
and I’ve been so happy.
In fact, there have been so many occasions
when it’s been positive joy.
So I feel that that is because I’ve always kept Jehovah
right in front of my mind,
and I’m confident
that brothers and sisters who do the same
will find Jehovah will bless them
as he’s blessed me.
The fact that Jehovah
will never forget the loyalty that we show him
and the hope of Paradise that he has given us
help me to feel his love,
overcome my fear,
and become determined to serve him loyally forever.

cn.text: 我因为坚守基督徒的中立立场
被关在监狱里一年3个月
我跟那些重刑犯被关在同一个牢房里
当时我坐在家里
我全家人都被逮捕了
他们放火把村子全烧了
我们只能住在树林里
而且最困难的是我们还带着一个小宝宝
武装警察闯进来
拿枪指着我们
把我们铐上手铐
又搜查我们的房子
带走所有东西
把我们关在拘留所
后来我们就被关进监狱里了
我被单独监禁，觉得很害怕
但我信赖耶和华
只有他才能保护我！
那段时间
我知道耶和华上帝在我身边
给我力量
所以我才能撑过来
我每天起床后第一件事
就是沉思我想到的经文
虽然当时我没有圣经
但却不觉得跟耶和华疏远
或是对他失去信心
我们带着小宝宝逃难
实在很辛苦
我们一直跟耶和华祷告
我觉得耶和华非常真实
就像我的爸爸一样
我好像听到耶和华对我说
“女儿，我就在你身边，不要害怕！”
所以我从来都没有害怕退缩
我一直很坚定！
要是我在乎的是自己、自由
健康、金钱而不是跟耶和华的友谊
我可能就不会崇拜上帝了
但因为我爱的是耶和华而不是那些东西
所以我才会选择事奉耶和华
即使要坐牢我也在所不惜！
现在我可以自由地崇拜上帝
参加聚会
跟家人一起去传道
我觉得耶和华的手一直在帮助我
我一点都不害怕！
耶和华给我很大的力量
“爱里没有恐惧”
只要你爱耶和华
你什么都不用害怕！
我虽然经历过不少患难
但我可以说
我这一生是充满喜乐的
有很多事都让我感到非常地快乐
我把耶和华看得很真实
他就好像站在我面前一样
我相信只要弟兄姐妹对上帝忠贞
耶和华也会赐福给他们
就像他赐福给我一样
我们对耶和华忠贞
他绝对不会忘记
上帝给我们乐园的希望
让我感受到他的爱
帮助我克服恐惧
也使我决心永远都要忠贞地崇拜他！

ko.text: 교회에서 경리 일을 하는 일자리를 얻게 되었어요.
교회로 들어오는 돈을 다 관리하는 일이었죠.
과연 나만 빠질 수 있을까?’ 하는 생각이 들었죠.
그런 축일들은 가족 간에 정을 나누고
즐거운 시간을 보낼 수 있는 좋은 기회니까요.
학생 과제를 할 수 없다고 하셨죠.
그분을 위해 아무것도 해 드리는 게 없다는 생각이 들었죠.
이 일을 그만두면 당장 돈이 없는데’
가족들은 아예 저와 말을 하지 않았어요.
나만 이렇게 혼자 있구나’ 하는 생각이 들었습니다.
그분은 저를 그분의 자녀로 받아 주겠다고 약속하셨죠.
제가 마음을 굳게 먹는 데 도움이 되었습니다.
그리고 여호와께서 우리 모두의 아버지시라는 걸
수확 철이 되면 3, 4일씩 휴가를 내고 가서
성경을 펴서 여호와께서 어떤 행동을 좋아하시는지 알려 준 덕분에
제가 결정을 내려야 한다는 걸 깨달았습니다.
그분을 기쁘게 해 드리기를 원한다는 것을 알게 됐어요.
여호와 앞에서 제 양심이 깨끗하지 못했죠.
여호와 앞에서 깨끗한 양심을 갖게 되었습니다.
제가 경험을 통해 분명히 알게 된 건
그 말을 듣고 얼마나 기뻤는지 모릅니다.
저와 함께 여호와를 섬길 수 있게 되기를 바랍니다.

en.text: Right about the time
I started studying the Bible,
an opportunity came up for me
to start doing secretarial work
at a church.
I was the one who cared for all
of the money that the church would receive.
But at that moment, I didn’t see any problem
with staying where I worked.
I studied the Bible and learned that the festivals
I used to participate in
were displeasing to Jehovah.
But it did not seem possible
that I would be the only one not participating
in those festivals.
These opportunities brought families closer together,
and they were fun too.
One night at a meeting,
I was talking with an elder,
and he told me that I wouldn’t even be able
to give student parts at the Kingdom Hall,
since I was still working
as a secretary at the church.
That made me very sad
because I found myself just receiving guidance from Jehovah
and learning his truths,
but I was not giving back anything to him
despite what he was doing for me.
However, I have to admit
that I still hadn’t
completely made up my mind,
since my husband had back surgery
and wasn’t able to work at the time.
We had our little daughter to care for,
so I kept thinking: ‘What should I do?
‘Right now,
this is the only money we have coming in.’
I prayed a lot to Jehovah
for help with this issue.
I thought about Jehovah’s feelings.
I didn’t want to do anything that hurt Jehovah.
When I stopped participating in religious festivals,
my family stopped speaking to me.
When it was time for the festivals,
it made me think that they were together
and I was by myself.
So at times, I cried.
I meditated
on God’s promise at Psalm 27:10.
Jehovah promised me that if my parents abandoned me,
he would receive me as his child.
It helped me to stand firm.
Personally, I tried to attend the meetings
and participate in the ministry too.
All of these activities
made me feel that the congregation is like a family
and that Jehovah
is the Father of all of us.
But I never forgot my parents.
So I tried to help them in whatever ways I could.
I took about three or four days of vacation
to go help them harvest rice.
I had great help from my instructor.
Just as Jehovah doesn’t force us, she didn’t force me.
As she told experiences and showed me
in the Bible what really pleases Jehovah,
it made me realize that I had to make a decision.
As my Bible study got deeper,
I began to realize that I really was already loving Jehovah
and wanted to please him.
Before Jehovah, my conscience
was already affecting me.
I had to make a decision on his side.
That’s exactly what I did.
Two weeks later, I got a job,
and it was close to my home.
I was able to gain a clean conscience before Jehovah.
I have seen this in my life:
Anyone who trusts in Jehovah is not helpless.
When I told my parents that although I changed my religion,
I still loved them,
they started to open up and talk to me gradually.
So I invited them to attend a meeting.
When my father attended the meeting, he said:
“Oh! You made a good decision, my son.”
Then I was very happy.
I still hope
that my family will one day study the Bible
and worship Jehovah along with me.

cn.text: 我开始学习圣经的时候
刚好找到了一份工作
是在教会里做秘书
我负责管理教会里的所有收入
可是那个时候
我不觉得这有什么问题
还是留在那里继续工作
我学习圣经后才知道
从小到大过的那些节日
都是耶和华不喜欢的
可是大家都在过节
只有我一个人不过
这怎么可能啊！
我以前觉得
过节是跟家人团聚的好机会
而且也很有趣
一天晚上我去参加聚会
我跟长老聊天的时候
他说我还不能在台上做学生练习
原因就是
我还在教会里做秘书工作
这让我非常难过
因为我觉得自己
一直在接受耶和华的教导
他给了我很多的帮助
可是我却没有办法做些事来报答他
不过坦白说
我还没有下定决心辞掉工作
因为我丈夫的腰部做了手术
他那时根本没办法工作
我们还有一个小女儿
所以我一直在心里想
我到底该怎么做呢？
我们家就只剩这一份收入了
我向耶和华祷告
求了很多次
请他帮助我
我也想想耶和华有什么感受
我真的不想做让耶和华伤心的事
我决定不庆祝宗教节日后
我的家人都不跟我说话了
每次到了节日的时候
我就会想
家人都开心地团聚
我却孤零零的一个人
所以有时候我会躲起来
偷偷地哭
我沉思上帝在诗篇27:10的保证
就算我的父母离弃我
耶和华也会收留我
让我做他的孩子
这段经文帮助我
可以站稳立场
继续坚持下去
而且我也努力参加聚会
也经常跟弟兄姐妹一起传道
参加这些活动让我觉得
会众就像是一个大家庭一样
耶和华是我们所有人的爸爸
不过我也没有忘记自己的父母
所以我努力用各种方式帮助他们
照顾他们的需要
有一次到了水稻收割的时候
我请了三四天的假回家帮忙
圣经老师给了我很大的帮助
就像耶和华不会强迫我们
圣经老师也没有强迫我做决定
她给我讲了一些经历
也用圣经告诉我
耶和华希望我怎样做
我看出自己真的要作出决定了
我越深入学习圣经
就越爱耶和华
越想让他高兴
可是这份工作
总让我觉得在上帝面前良心不安
我真的需要按照上帝的想法做决定
于是我辞掉了教会的工作
两周后
我找到了另一份工作
离家很近
我终于可以良心清白地面对上帝了
我亲身体验到
只要信赖耶和华
他就会给我们打开出路
我告诉爸爸妈妈
自己虽然改变了宗教信仰
但还是很爱他们
慢慢地
他们的态度改变了
他们愿意跟我说话了
后来我也邀请他们参加聚会
爸爸来参加聚会的时候说
儿子，你做了一个很好的决定
听到爸爸这样说
我真的很高兴
我真的很希望我的家人
有一天会开始学习圣经
跟我一起崇拜耶和华

ko.text: 많은 사람에게 “종”이란 단어는 별로 기분 좋은 말은 아닙니다
또는 모든 자유와 개인적인 권리를 빼앗긴 채 속박된 하인.”
“종”이라는 단어를 들으면 노예를 사고 파는 일
흑인을 사고 팔았던 일이 떠오를지 모릅니다
그처럼 씁쓸한 기분이 아니라 오히려 좋은 기분이 들게 합니다
우린 완전한 인간 즉 예수의 귀중한 피로 값이 치러졌습니다
함께 성경을 펴서 계시록 5:9절을 읽어 보시죠
‘당신은 두루마리를 받으시고 그 봉인들을 떼시기에 합당합니다.
당신의 피로 모든 종족과 언어와 민족과 나라 가운데서 사람들을 사서
이런 일이 있었다는 사실에 우린 기뻐합니다
우리 주인이신 여호와와 예수를 위해 열심히 일하죠
여호와의 종이 되는 건 소중한 특권입니다
하느님의 소유가 되고 그분께 속하는 것만큼 좋은 것은 아무것도 없죠
“충실하고 슬기로운 종”이 집안 일꾼들을 매일 먹이는 일을 할 때
이곳 미국에 있는 베델 시설 이곳 저곳을 돌아다니는 걸 종종 보실 겁니다
세계 여러 지역을 다니고 있는 걸 보실 때도 있죠
충실한 종이 시간과 주의를 쏟고 있는 일들에는 어떤 것들이 있을까요?
전 세계에 있는 전도인, 보조, 정규, 특별 파이오니아
선교인, 순회 감독자, 베델 성원의 삶에 영향을 미치는 결정을 내립니다
세계 여러 나라에 새 지부 시설이 필요한지 결정합니다
이 분야는 하루가 다르게 계속해서 커지고 있습니다
자연 재해로 피해를 입은 형제 자매들을 어떻게 도울지
자금을 얼마나 할당할 수 있는지 등을 결정합니다
순회 대회와 지역 대회 프로그램의 주제, 드라마
모든 학교 마련에도 관여하는데, 사실 이 일에는 끝이 없죠
출판될 모든 자료들을 읽고 확인하고 승인하는 일도 합니다
출판물에 실릴 삽화도 모두 보고 승인하죠
그리고 정말 귀중한 보석과도 같은 jw.org 웹사이트
그리고 「JW 라이브러리」에 무슨 내용을 실을지도 결정합니다
전 세계 지부 봉헌식과 대회 회관 봉헌식도 조직하죠
양 떼를 돌보는 일에 여호와의 인도를 구하면서 계속 기도합니다
“충실하고 슬기로운 종”이 하는 일의 반 밖에 안 될 겁니다
하느님의 성령과 회중의 머리이신 예수의 인도가 있기에 가능한 거죠
중요한 결정과 승인은 모두 “충실하고 슬기로운 종”이 내리지만
여호와의 양을 먹이고 돌보는 우리의 책임을 지원하기 위해
요리로 치면 우리가 주방장처럼 보일 수도 있겠지만
아시다시피 주방에 주방장만 있는 건 아니죠
여러분이 정기적으로 우릴 위해 기도하는 걸 듣습니다
각주를 보면 “여호와의 종이 되십시오”라는 말로 끝맺습니다
하느님과 예수께 충성스럽게 순종하고 섬기면 그분들의 친구가 됩니다
“나는 여러분을 더 이상 종이라고 부르지 않습니다.
종은 주인이 하는 일을 모르기 때문입니다.
내가 아버지에게서 들은 것을 모두 여러분에게 알려 주었기 때문입니다.”
그분이 우리를 위해 하시는 일에 대해 우리는
예수를 따르는 사람은 그분의 종이자 친구입니다
예수의 친구가 되는 것보다 더 좋은 게 또 있을까요?
예수의 친구가 되면, 여호와의 친구도 되는 것이죠
오히려 입에 꿀처럼 기분 좋은 말입니다

en.text: For many people, just to hear
the word “slave”
leaves a bitter taste in their mouth.
They associate the word
with the following definition.
Listen carefully to it, please:
“A human being who is owned as property
“by another and is absolutely subject to his will,
“or a bond servant divested of all freedom
and personal rights.”
The word “slave” may bring to mind
the trafficking in slaves,
especially the buying and selling of blacks for profit
prior to the American Civil War.
Well, that having been said,
the Bible’s use of the word “slave”
does not leave a bad taste in our mouths
but a sweet taste.
Yes, we were bought with the precious blood of another human
—a perfect one— we all know to be Jesus.
And Paul told the early Christians in Corinth:
“You do not belong to yourselves,
for you were bought with a price.”
The 24 elders too in Revelation 5:9
sing to Jesus, “the Lamb of God.”
Open your Bibles, please, to this
—that’s the ninth verse
of the fifth chapter
of Revelation,
and it reads this way:
“And they sing a new song, saying:
“‘You are worthy to take the scroll and open its seals,
“‘for you were slaughtered and with your blood you bought people
“‘for God out of every tribe and tongue
and people and nation.’”
Well, that’s true.
That’s what has happened, and we are all happy for that.
But we all know that we are slaves of God.
We have been bought and paid for.
But we’re happy slaves, aren’t we?
We work diligently to please our owners, Jehovah and Jesus.
And that’s what Bethel is all about too.
We work hard as slaves.
To be a slave of Jehovah is a cherished privilege.
Just to be owned by God —to belong to him—
is the best thing that could happen to any one of us.
That is how “the faithful and discreet slave” feels
as the feeding of the domestics is accomplished each day.
Now, you see members of the Governing Body walking here and there
in the various complexes here in the United States
from time to time.
Every now and then, we’ll go up to Canada,
go other places throughout the world,
and you see a few of us walking around too.
What are some things that occupy
the time of the faithful slave and their attention?
I just jotted down a few things.
Now, I’m going to go through them very fast
because we don’t have a lot of time, but you just think about them:
making decisions that affect the lives of all sheep​
—​publishers, auxiliary, regular, special pioneers, missionaries,
circuit overseers, Bethel family members​—​ all over the world;
deciding whether new branch facilities
are needed in various countries throughout the world;
deciding on the needs in the field of computers,
a field that just keeps growing and growing with each passing week;
looking into legal fights we’re having all over the world;
deciding the best approach to helping brothers and sisters
who have been struck by natural disasters,
how much money can be allotted, and so forth;
deciding on assembly and convention program themes,
dramas, broadcast programs, videos,
new songs, Morning Worship programs;
involvement with all the schools being taught,
and there’s no end to them;
reading and checking and approving all material that will be printed;
looking and approving all artwork that will be used in our publications;
what new languages to start translating;
decide on what will appear
on jw.org and JW Library®
(and, of course, that has really been a jewel, and still is);
final approval on all audio recordings of the Bible;
organizes international and special conventions;
organizes branch dedications and Assembly Hall dedications worldwide;
involved with all teaching; constantly looking to
and praying to Jehovah for direction in shepherding his sheep.
Now, what has been said is probably only half
of what is done by “the faithful and discreet slave.”
What is accomplished is not by human effort alone,
but it is by means of God’s holy spirit and direction given by Jesus,
the head of the congregation.
While all major decisions
and approvals are made by “the faithful and discreet slave,”
we have 30 most qualified helpers
and several other brothers
who work hard in assisting us to accomplish our responsibility
of feeding and caring for Jehovah’s sheep.
Their work does not go unnoticed.
Now, some of us may be viewed as “Iron Chefs,”
but we’re not the only ones in the kitchen; you better believe that.
The entire Bethel family helps as well.
We hear you praying in our behalf on a regular basis,
and we thank you for your prayers.
Is it any wonder that the apostle Paul
is found admonishing sheep to “be industrious,
not lazy”?
“Be aglow with the spirit,” he says,
and then he ends up by saying: “Slave for Jehovah.”
That’s Romans 12:11.
By becoming loyally obedient slaves of God and Jesus,
we become their friends.
Let’s look at something here in our Bibles, John 15:15.
It reads this way: “I no longer call you slaves,
“because a slave does not know what his master does.
“But I have called you friends, because I have made known to you
all the things I have heard from my Father.”
Isn’t that beautiful?
That’s Jesus.
That’s what he does.
And we appreciate it so much —what he does for us.
So those who follow Jesus,
while slaves, are also his friends.
That’s a blessing.
Can you think of a better position
to be in than being a friend of Jesus?
If we have Jesus’ friendship,
then we automatically have Jehovah’s friendship.
So don’t let the word “slave”
put a bad taste in your mouth.
It’s a sweet thing.
It’s honey to the palate.

ko.text: 여호와의 증인은 이 세상 제도가 마지막 날 깊숙이 들어와 있다고 확신합니다.
가능한 한 많은 사람에게 전해 주겠다는 결의를 다지고 있습니다.
우리는 계속해서 전파 활동을 감독하고 그 활동에 박차를 가하길 원합니다.
끝이 오기 전에 해야 할 일이기 때문입니다.
“좋은 소식이 먼저 모든 나라 사람들에게 전파되어야 한다”고 말합니다.
예수께선 해가 뜨는 것보다 성서 예언이 더 확실하다고 하셨죠.
인간은 여호와께서 이루신 일을 해낼 수 없죠.
우린 모든 일에 대한 영예를 오직 그분에게만 돌려야 합니다.
그리고 우리에겐 완수해야 할 일이 있다는 것도 잊어선 안 되죠.
바로 이 시기에 여호와께서 원하시는 일을 하는 데 집중하도록
온 땅에 좋은 소식을 전하고 있는 형제들을 온전히 지원하고 싶습니다.

en.text: Jehovah’s Witnesses are convinced
that this system of things is deep
into its last days,
and the Governing Body is intent
on reaching as many people as possible
with the knowledge of God.
We want to continue to oversee
and give impetus to the preaching work
because this has to be done
before the end comes.
Mark 13:10:
“In all the nations,
the good news has to be preached first.”
Jesus said that we can have more confidence
in the fulfillment of the Bible
than the sun coming up.
And so with that kind of faith, we can do the work that’s involved.
We just pour ourselves into that.
It would be impossible
for humans to do
what Jehovah accomplished.
We have to give him full credit for things that have transpired.
And we also realize that we’ve got a work to complete.
So keeping our brothers and sisters focused
on what Jehovah wants us to do
at this particular time,
seeing how close the end is —that is our main focus—
and giving full support to the brotherhood,
as they continue to show their love for Jehovah
to preach that “good news . . . in all the inhabited earth.”

ko.text: 두 가지에 대해 소개할 수 있어 기쁩니다.
다음으로, 평일 집회에서 어떤 기대할 만한 변화가 있을 것입니까?
우선 교습 위원회는 베델의 모든 부서들에 대해 매우 고맙게 생각합니다.
대회와 평일 집회에서 즐기는 영적인 프로그램을 위해
베델에서 일하는 여러분 각자가 어떤 식으로든 기여하고 있기 때문입니다.
1889년 이래로 지역 대회는 많은 발전을 거듭해 왔습니다.
이제 살펴보겠지만, 여호와께서 그런 발전을 이루게 해 주셨죠.
이번 지역 대회는 아주 훌륭합니다. 정말 큰 감동을 주죠.
지역 대회 덕분에 우리 모두 영적으로 강해졌어요.
지난 100여 년 동안 수많은 사람이 비슷하게 느꼈습니다.
오랜 세월 진리 안에 계셨던 분들이 지역 대회가 열릴 때마다
이번 대회가 가장 좋았다고 말씀하시는 이유는 무엇입니까?
그런 이야기를 들으면 대회 프로그램을 준비하는 형제들은 어떤 느낌이 들까요?
그 형제들은 2017 지역 대회 영상에 나왔던 준이처럼 느낄지 모릅니다.
하지만 이 일은 사람의 일이 아닙니다.
우리는 시기적절한 대회들에 대해 여호와께 찬양을 돌려야 하죠.
그분의 영은 기꺼이 자원하는 많은 사람들을 통해 작용하고 있습니다.
이제 지역 대회를 어떻게 준비하는지 간단히 살펴보겠습니다.
한 단어로 된 주제를 여러 해 전에 미리 선정하죠.
그 단어에 근거해서 대회 프로그램을 준비하게 됩니다.
교습 위원회는 대본을 만들기 위해 드라마를 검토하는 팀과 함께 작업하면서
경험 많은 집필자들이 대회 주제에 꼭 맞는 교훈이 담긴 성경에 근거한 이야기를 만듭니다.
그러고 나서 대본을 폭넓게 연구 조사한 뒤,
드라마 제작을 위해 오디오/비디오 봉사부로 보냅니다.
이 모든 작업은 여러 해 전에 시작해야 합니다.
그러면 나머지 대회 프로그램은 어떻게 준비합니까?
전 세계의 지부 위원회와 본부 대표자들이 보내온 보고를 주의 깊이 검토합니다.
그러한 보고들을 보면 대회에서 어떤 점을 다루면 좋을지 알게 되기도 하죠.
전 세계 형제들의 필요에 맞게 대회 주제를 더 구체적으로 정합니다.
그리고 그 주제를 중앙장로회의 모든 성원에게 보내서 승인을 받습니다.
그러고 나서 지역 대회의 각 날에 맞는 주제 성구를 정하게 됩니다.
금요일 프로그램은 대회 전체의 기초를 놓습니다.
그 점이 지금 왜 우리에게 중요한지를 다룹니다.
토요일에는 개인 행실, 야외 봉사, 가정생활과 관련된 교훈이 베풀어지죠.
일요일에는 성경이 미래에 관해 무엇이라고 알려 주고,
우리가 계속 희망을 갖도록 어떻게 도와주는지를 다룹니다.
이렇게 기본적인 구성을 마치면 각 날에 어떤 연설들을 할지,
연설에 어떤 사상과 내용을 포함시킬지 정합니다.
또한 사상을 잘 전달하기 위해 다양한 방법을 생각해 보는데요.
성경의 교훈이 마음에 더 잘 이를 수 있도록 인터뷰나 동영상을 활용하기도 합니다.
교습 위원회는 이러한 세부적인 작업을 다 마무리한 후
오디오/비디오 봉사부는 집필자들과 협력하여 짧은 동영상들을 제작합니다.
미술부는 대회를 소개하고 광고하기 위한 아이디어를 구상합니다.
편집자는 집필된 내용에 대한 조사, 사실 확인, 교정 등
그렇게 해서 모든 골자와 대본이 완성되면
이제 지역 대회가 열리는 343개 언어로 번역 작업이 진행됩니다.
번역 봉사부는 전 세계의 번역 팀들이 번역을 수월하게 할 수 있도록 도와주죠.
작곡가와 편곡자들은 대회 때 부를 18개의 노래와 6개의 음악 영상에 사용될 곡을 만듭니다.
그리고 영화와 음성 드라마, 또 연설에 포함되는
약 40개의 짧은 동영상에 사용될 음악을 제작하고 녹음하는 작업도 음악 팀에서 진행하죠.
교습 위원회가 주관하는 일은 이 밖에도 더 있습니다.
교습 위원회는 연사를 임명하고 음향 장비를 설치하고
숙박업소나 대회 시설을 계약하고 대회와 관련된 부서들을 운영하고
자원봉사자들을 훈련하는 일에 관한 지침을 제공하죠.
이처럼 대회를 준비하기 위해 많은 사람이 기꺼이 자원하여 일합니다.
모두 하느님의 영감받은 말씀과 성령의 인도를 따르며 일하죠.
이런 협력이 가져오는 유익한 결과는 지역 대회에서만 볼 수 있는 게 아닙니다.
「그리스도인 생활과 봉사」 집회가 시작된 지도 2년이 됐는데요.
집회 때 더 열심히 참여하려고 하죠.
전 세계의 형제 자매들이랑 더 친해진 것 같아요.
이젠 예습할 때 그냥 밑줄만 치지 않고 어떤 보물이 있는지 찾아봐요.
성경을 깊이 파 들어가면서 정말 많은 걸 배우죠.
집회가 끝난 뒤에도 자신이 찾은 영적 보물에 대해 서로 이야기합니다.
집회 때마다 주말에 바로 실천할 수 있는 실용적인 점들을 배워요.
이제 우리 가족은 성경을 읽을 때 여호와의 특성에 더 많은 주의를 기울이죠.
청소년이나 새로운 전도인들이 호별 봉사에 더 자신감을 갖게 됐습니다.
집회 때 배운 걸 그대로 따라 하면 되니까요.
평일 집회의 구성 방식도 생각해 볼 수 있는데요.
길르앗 학교에서 공부하는 방식을 집회에 도입했습니다.
길르앗 학교에서는 성구의 문맥, 설명, 적용에 초점을 맞춥니다.
문맥을 분석하려면 시대적 상황, 역사적 배경, 필자의 의도가 무엇인지를 알아야 합니다.
평일 집회 때 살펴보는 성경에 담긴 보물 부분이나
「성경 소개 동영상」을 만들 때 바로 그런 점들을 염두에 두죠.
성구에 대한 설명은 모두 “충실하고 슬기로운 종”이 발행한 출판물에 근거해 있기 때문에
성구를 정확하게 올바로 이해할 수 있습니다.
사실, 길르앗 학생들도 추측에 근거해 성구를 설명해선 안 된다고 배우죠.
성구가 정확하게 설명되면 그 내용을 올바로 적용할 수 있습니다.
이런 식으로 문맥과 설명과 적용에 초점을 맞추면
성경을 의미 있게 연구할 수 있죠.
대화 방법과 그리스도인 생활 부분에 관해 제안합니다.
집필부는 봉사와 집회에서 출판물을 활용하는 방법에 관한 지침을 줍니다.
배부용 「파수대」가 1년에 6개 호가 아니라 3개 호만 발행될 것입니다.
또한 제공할 출판물을 미리 정해 놓는 마련도 중단되었습니다.
따라서 야외 봉사 때 사용할 대화 방법 제안에 변화가 생길 것입니다.
이제부터는 출판물을 전하는 것보다는 대화를 나누는 데 더 중점을 둘 것입니다.
분명, 평일 집회와 지역 대회를 준비하는 데는 엄청난 노력이 듭니다.
베델의 여러 부서에서 많은 사람들이 주의 깊이 계획하고 협력해야 하죠.
하지만 그 덕분에 전 세계 형제들이 유익을 얻습니다.
이런 집회를 보게 해 주셔서 여호와께 정말 감사해요.
베델에 보내 주신 편지들을 보면 때때로 이런 말이 나옵니다.
사실 이 모든 일을 하는 형제 자매들은 지칠 때가 분명히 있습니다.
하지만 그들은 결코 지치지 않는 분인 여호와를 늘 신뢰하며 그분과 협력해 일하고 있죠.
우리가 받는 모든 교육은 하느님이 베푸시는 것입니다.
오직 그분만이 구리를 금으로 바꾸실 수 있죠.
따라서 우리 앞에는 언제나 최상의 교육이 펼쳐질 것입니다.

en.text: It’s a pleasure to relate to you two aspects
of the Teaching Committee’s work.
First, what does it take
to put a regional convention together these days?
And second, what can we expect with regard to our midweek meetings?
The Teaching Committee is very grateful to every Bethel department.
Each of you has contributed in some way
to the spiritually festive events
that we enjoy at our conventions and our midweek meetings.
Our conventions have come a long way since 1889.
But as you’ll see, the improvements must be attributed to Jehovah.
This convention is so beautiful.
It moves you to the core.
It’s a very spiritually enriching experience for all of us.
We really see the Governing Body is caring for us.
It’s amazing!
This sentiment has been echoed for over a century.
How is it that year after year people who have been in the truth for decades
can say that the most recent convention
has surpassed all preceding ones?
And how do the brothers who prepare convention programs feel
when they hear comments like that?
If this were merely the work of humans,
they might feel like Caleb as depicted in the 2017 regional conventions.
Thankfully, this is not the work of one man.
All praise goes to Jehovah for the timely conventions we enjoy.
His spirit is working through many willing volunteers.
Let’s take a brief look at how our conventions are made.
It all begins with the theme.
As Brother Morris pointed out at the 2017 regional convention,
one-word themes are determined years in advance.
That one word will guide those preparing the program.
Dramas —the most labor-intensive part of a program—
are developed five years in advance.
To prepare scripts, the Teaching Committee cooperates closely
with the Writing Department in working with a team
known as the Drama Review Group.
These experienced writers
develop Scriptural plots that teach lessons in harmony
with the convention theme.
Scripts are extensively researched
and then sent to Audio/Video Services,
or AVS, for production.
All of this work has to begin early.
But how is the rest of a convention program developed?
Each year, the Teaching Committee carefully considers reports
from around the world from Branch Committees
and world headquarters representatives.
Often, such reports indicate topics that could be addressed on a convention.
The Teaching Committee then selects a more specific theme
that will serve as the basis for addressing the needs
of our worldwide brotherhood.
The theme is submitted to the entire Governing Body for approval.
Then, work begins on Scripture themes for each day of the convention.
The Friday program lays the foundation:
What is the central truth under discussion?
Why should we give attention to it now?
Saturday brings admonition on personal conduct,
field ministry, and family life.
Sunday often highlights what the Bible says
about our future and encourages us to maintain our hope.
Once this general framework is established,
talks are conceived
and additional lines of reasoning are chosen.
Attention is given to how to present ideas
in a variety of ways:
Could a Scriptural discussion reach the heart more effectively
by means of an interview or a video?
This detailed sketch is all worked out
before the Teaching Committee assigns teams of writers.
AVS collaborates with the writers in the development of brief videos.
The Art Department brainstorms ideas
for convention branding.
The compiler follows the written content through 70 steps
of research, fact-checking, and proofreading.
Then, all of these outlines and scripts have to be translated
into the 343 languages in which we hold regional conventions.
Translation Services helps teams around the world
to overcome challenges with the text.
Composers and arrangers
make music tracks for the 18 songs
that have been selected and the 6 music-video preludes.
Music services also produces and records
musical scores for the feature film, the audio drama,
and some 40 other brief videos that are used on the program.
But the Teaching Committee’s involvement
doesn’t end here.
It provides direction regarding the assigning of speakers,
the design of sound systems,
the securing of contracts for hotels and venues,
the operation of convention departments,
and the training of volunteers.
Thousands of willing workers are involved,
each submitting to the inspired direction
in God’s Word and the influence
of his holy spirit.
The benefits of such collaboration are felt
not only at our annual conventions
but also at our weekly meetings.
It’s been two years since the inception
of the Our Christian Life and Ministry  midweek meeting.
How have things been going on that front?
Everything got better: how the brothers and sisters feel
about the meeting and how they participate.
There are more videos at the meetings,
so I feel closer to the worldwide brotherhood.
I really enjoy what it does for young ones,
especially the two-minute parts.
You see young ones, even very young children, do a demonstration.
Instead of just underlining to prepare,
now I get excited looking for gems.
We really dig into a Bible account.
I learn a whole lot more.
After the meeting,
we enjoy discussing the gems we discovered.
Every meeting gives you something practical
that you can apply the next weekend right away.
Now we don’t just read the Bible as a family,
but we pay more attention to Jehovah’s qualities.
Young ones and new publishers are now less hesitant
about sharing their beliefs at the door
because they simply do what they learned at the meetings.
Regarding production of the meeting,
methods of the Gilead School are employed
in the approach to study.
The Gilead approach to study
considers context, explanation,
and application.
Analyzing the context considers the time period,
the historical setting, and the writer’s intent.
These are built into the Treasures From God’s Word
and the Bible Book Introduction Videos
we see at the midweek meetings.
The explanations for the verses are all based on the publications
of “the faithful and discreet slave”
to ensure accuracy and correct understanding.
After all, at Gilead School, students aren’t allowed to guess.
Once a scripture is explained accurately,
then it can be applied properly.
This method of context and explanation
followed by application leads to meaningful Bible study.
The Service Committee Office
provides input on field service presentations and Living as Christians.
The Writing Department gives insight on how to feature our publications.
What will change after January?
As announced at the 2017 annual meeting,
the public edition of The Watchtower will be published
three times a year instead of six.
The same will be true for Awake!
Also, specific monthly literature offers have been discontinued.
Thus, we will enjoy some adjustments in our field service presentations.
As you will see, the new focus will be
not so much on publications
but on conversations.
Clearly, the production of our midweek meetings
and regional conventions takes a lot of planning
and the cooperation of many willing workers
in a variety of Bethel departments.
But the positive effects are felt around the world.
All I can say to Jehovah is, “Thank you, Jehovah, for letting me be here.”
I feel very grateful to Jehovah for the meetings.
Thank you, Jehovah.
Sometimes Bethel receives letters that go something like this:
“Thank you for your tireless efforts.”
Actually, the brothers and sisters working on all these projects are tired.
But they never tire
of trusting in and cooperating with the One who truly is tireless:
the Source of all divine instruction, Jehovah.
He alone can replace copper with gold,
so that each segment of divine education
truly is the best ever.

en.text: With so much to do in our life
—not just in the ministry
but also with secular work,
family responsibilities, for some, even health issues
—we can get into a rut.
It’s not always easy to detect at first,
because in this age of technology,
we always feel busy.
But what consumes our day?
Watch this one-minute video,
and try to detect what’s going on in the life of one brother.
His life is in a rut.
Try to figure out why.
Would you say that this brother’s life is in a rut?
Oh, he’s active all day —he always has something to do.
But it’s as if his mind has been kidnapped by his devices.
Have you ever had the experience of reading an e-mail
while someone is trying to tell you something?
It can be embarrassing when you realize that they’ve asked you a question,
and they’re waiting for an answer, but you have no idea what they asked.
It’s embarrassing, right?
But what if the person
who is trying to speak to you is Jehovah?
Even though we aren’t doing anything wrong,
our daily routine can occupy our attention so much
that we are not able to hear the refreshing words of Jehovah.

아이가 관심 있어 하는 주제를 선택해요.
자연스럽게 성에 대한 이야기를 시작하는 데 도움이 되죠.
아이들이 사탄의 세상에서 성을 배우기 전에
우리가 먼저 성교육을 시켜 줄 수 있어요.
또 이미 알고 있는 게 뭔지 이해하게 도와줍니다.
어렸을 때부터 성에 대해 이야기했기 때문에

en.text: At times, it can be difficult to talk to Emilien about sex
because Emilien is a young boy, and I am a single mother.
I’ve been a widow for nine years.
And I find sexual education a difficult topic to talk about.
In our culture, talking about sex is taboo,
so much so that our parents do not talk to us about it.
It is hard to know how much information we should give to our children.
Children are naturally curious.
Our fear is: What if they get wrong thoughts?
It is not easy to bring up children
in the last days of this system of things.
It is very difficult to train children in a blended family,
but with the help of Jehovah,
it is Jehovah who has helped us to train them.
It’s true that Jehovah has given us an incredible task
to raise our children in the truth, but I am calm and confident
because thanks to his organization,
we always have what we need,
in due time, to successfully carry out this task.
I use the videos provided by “the faithful and discreet slave”
that relate to the topics Emilien wants to talk about,
in particular, the video Protect Your Children,
which speaks about sexual predators,
is a good starting point for a discussion on this.
Even before Satan’s world can teach our children about sex,
we can teach them.
Learn From the Great Teacher, chapter 32,
has beautiful questions.
It helps us to understand what is in their hearts
and how much information they already know.
Since we have already spoken to them about sex at this age,
we can talk about any serious matters
in the future without feeling awkward.
We lean on the counsel from the Bible regarding sexuality,
and this has helped the children to fear Jehovah.
Every time that we go out to the fields to do our work,
we are talking all the time with the children.
I see that Jehovah has blessed these efforts.
We do not have any problems among the children or with others.

title: 가족 숭배—어려움이 있지만 보람 있는 일

ko.text: 다섯 식구가 하루 저녁을 온전히 함께 보내려고
제가 사회하는 가족 연구는 과연 그렇게 알찰까,
자신감도 좀 없었다고 볼 수 있고.
가족 숭배에 대한 제 태도가 문제였죠.
관심을 쏟고 시간도 함께 보내 주면
기운도 없을 때가 있다는 게 문제예요.
특히 가장으로서 일을 해야 하는 일이 많다 보니까,
아무리 해도 안 될 때가 있습니다.
힘이 넘쳐 나는 어린 아들도 있죠.
가족하고 다른 일을 하고 싶어 할 때가 있어요.
가족 숭배는 그 마련이 생길 때부터
우리가 회중 집회에 빠지지 않는 것처럼
가족 숭배는 정기적으로 하는 게 중요합니다.
정말 자기 징계가 필요한 거 같아요.
가족 숭배가 먼저라는 걸 알기 때문에
막 요일 요일 달라지는 가족 숭배가 아니고,
그 수요일 날 밤에 운동하자고 부르는 전화는
가족 숭배 있어서 운동을 할 수 없다고 말하기가 좀 더 편했어요.
서로 힘을 합쳐서 열심히 해 보자고 말해요.
그런 느낌을 갖게 된 거 같습니다.
그 마음 때문에 계속해 나갈 수 있다고 생각해요.
아이도 진리를 가장 중요하게 여기도록 말예요.
예기치 않은 일이 생길 수 있죠.
그런 때는 상황에 맞게 조정할 필요가 있습니다.
애들이 나이가 들면서 방법을 바꿔야 했죠.
특히 회중에 새로 이사 온 분들이랑
봉사할 때 어떻게 할 수 있는지 생각해 보거나
그에 맞춰 가족 숭배를 계획해야 합니다.
애들의 믿음이 현재 어떤 상태인지 알아야 하죠.
아이들의 영적 목표에 초점을 맞추려고 노력합니다.
괜찮을 것 같아서 아빠한테 여쭤 봤죠.
아빤 역할을 바꿔 생각해 보자고 하셨어요.
제가 아빠가 되고 아빠가 제 역할을 했죠.
그치만 가족 숭배가 큰 도움이 되요!
저 혼자만이 안고 있는 게 아니라
또 엄마가 그 점을 잘 알아주시고
노력을 같이 해서 극복할 수 있었어요.
예수 시대에는 성구 찾는 게 힘들었을 텐데,
우리가 정말 편하게 성구를 찾을 수 있게 해 줬다는 걸 느꼈어요.
좀 더 솔직한 말들을 할 수 있어서
가족 숭배가 저한테 유익이 있는 것 같습니다.
가장의 책임을 잘 이행할 수 있게 도와주신 여호와께
집회 때 해설도 더 많이 합니다.
네게는 이렇게 많은 자녀가 있잖니’라고 주신 거였기 때문에,
이들을 제가 그동안 눈여겨보지 않았던 거죠.
가족 숭배는 우리 가족을 보호해 주고
여러가지 어려움에 대비할 수 있게 도와줍니다.
서로가 마음을 훨씬 더 잘 터놓게 되었어요.
정말 하나도 없다는 것을 알게 되었어요.

en.text: Finding a way to get everybody —five people at the same time—

I wondered whether I would be able to make our family worship
interesting and beneficial.
I was not very confident.

I would hang out with my friends from the congregation.

but you don’t always have the time and energy needed.
I had to provide financially for the family.
I was always tired and worn out,
so it was very hard to have family worship regularly.
Kenzie, of course, is a child with special needs,
and she has her challenges.

when I actually wanted to go to bed.
It is quite annoying.

the consistency of having family worship is very important.

because sometimes there are things that we want to do,

so we have to give that up.
My friends and the brothers in the congregation
often call me to exercise or play sports.

doesn’t change each week,
it becomes easier to turn them down.

Let’s try to encourage each other,” because it’s not easy.

and effort to leave work on time
in order to be able to honor our family worship.
I became confident that this can really be successful.
I think the most important thing is the love we have for Jehovah.
That keeps us going, I think.
That’s our motivation.
We are determined
to teach her as much as we possibly can
so that she’ll possibly understand,
so that the truth will mean everything to her too.
We’ll get there.
We’ll get there.
We’re a family,
and things pop up,
and something can come up unexpectedly.

We make it relaxing.
The children look forward to getting cake or fruit or something else

you feel that you have to make small, short sessions
so that they can concentrate on the subject being discussed.
As they got older, we had to change the methods.
At times, we invite brothers in our congregation.

so they can interview the brother or sister that is coming over,
especially if they’re new in the congregation.
So sometimes family worship might be about issues that our family is facing;
sometimes it might be about things in the ministry
that we want to try to accomplish;
sometimes it might be about games.
So we’ve stretched out all over the floor
and done all sorts of wonderful things for family worship
because it keeps people engaged.
It’s all about asking the family what they would like to talk about.
If the family is involved, it is a family worship
rather than Dad, or myself, setting out the agenda for family worship.
Well, then, it would be Dad’s family worship and not for the whole family.
But if we get the feedback from the whole family
—from everyone, everyone gets to put in ideas—
then we just plan that accordingly.
The reality of what we need now for relevance is that we need to make sure
they are grounded in their faith and belief.
At every family study,
we always try to focus on the kids’ spiritual goals.
Once, a kid at school came and asked me if I could play for the football team.
And I thought it was a good idea, so I went to Dad and asked him.
And then he said, “Oh, why don’t we do something called role reversal?”
I would play the dad, and he would play the son.
In my case, the biggest pressure I have to face
is dating in school,
and family worship helps me a lot!
Instead of allowing my problems
and negative emotions to fester within me,
I shared these feelings with my family during family worship.
Mom was very understanding,
and she made an effort to come up with themes during family worship
to address those issues.
We decided to make a scroll out of the book of Isaiah.
It really helps me to realize
that Jehovah’s organization makes it easier for us
to find the scriptures that we’re looking for
and not to make it so complicated, like in Jesus’ days.
But for me,
the best thing is to have an opportunity
to express myself.
It’s good sometimes to break it up a bit, so it’s not always Dad talking.
When I see how happy all the family members are after our family worship,
I silently thank Jehovah
for helping me fulfill my responsibility as the head of the household.
Our children have learned to be more outgoing
and participate more in the meetings.
It was Jehovah’s way of telling me:
‘You are not alone. You have these precious children with you.’
It’s just that I wasn’t paying enough attention to them.
We open with prayer, and then right after that, it’s just amazing.
It’s really fun.
So getting there is the hard part,
but once we get into it, that’s when it starts
—that’s when we start having fun.
Family worship has been protecting my family,
and it has been preparing my family
for the difficulties we face.
We actually are more open with each other
now than we ever were before.
And we can discuss just about anything and everything, which is actually good.
Family worship made me realize how happy I am to have Jehovah as my God
and that I have many reasons to be happy.
And it feels like I can just let go of what was making me sad
or what was making me a bit angry, and I can just be like,
‘It’s fine’ because I know everything will be OK and Jehovah has blessed our evening.

ko.text: 아타가 진리를 갈구하고 있다는 걸 알았지만,
두 사람은 이라크의 정치 상황 때문에 헤어지게 되었고
각기 유럽의 서로 다른 나라에 정착했습니다.
하지만 두 사람 사이의 거리가 문제가 되었을까요?
그래서 우린 창세기부터 성경을 읽기 시작했어요.
그 사고로 두 다리를 다 잃었어요.
다른 난민들처럼 이라크를 떠나고 싶진 않았지만
여호와의 증인과 성경 공부를 하고 있다고 하더군요.
네가 옳다는 게 말이 된다고 생각해?”
제 인생 최대의 실수를 저지르는 거라면서요.
아타에 관해 제게 말했던 게 생각납니다.
지아드가 그 형제에게 제 연락처를 준 거죠.
증인들 말을 한 번 들어보기로 한 거죠.
그래서 아무 방해도 받고 싶지 않으니까
아타가 언젠간 형제가 될 거라는 걸
마지드 형제 부부가 베풀어 준 도움이
“제가 침례를 받아야 하는 이유를 설명해 줄 수 있나요?”
제 결심에 가장 큰 영향을 미친 건
우리에게 미래에 대한 희망을 제시할 의무가 있으신 건 아니죠.
인터넷 화상 통화로 아타와 얘길 했는데,
이젠 침례를 받지 말아야 할 이유를
성경을 이해해 보려고 애쓰던 기억이 났습니다.
여호와의 증인이 되어 함께 앉아 있다는 사실이
제가 정말 이 모든 축복을 받을 자격이 되나요?’
이런 제가 성경을 이해할 수 있게 되었습니다.
진리를 들어본 적이 없는 사람이 있다고
개인적으로 신세계에서의 희망에 대해 생각할 때,
제가 두 다리를 되찾아 사슴처럼 뛸 수 있다는 건
그보다 더 중요한 문제들이 있기 때문이죠.
다른 누가 아닌 하느님께서 다스리실 때 오게 될

en.text: This story is about Brother Ataa Yaldiko.
He is an Assyrian man from Iraq
and was raised as a Christian.
Ataa’s childhood friend had noticed that Ataa had a thirst for the truth,
but because of the political situation in Iraq,
the two friends got separated and moved to different countries in Europe.
But was the geographical distance a problem?
No.
This is their story.
I was about 18 years old when one of my friends named Ziad asked me,
“Ataa, have you read the Bible?”
We started to read the Bible from Genesis.
I remember one time when we read the Sermon on the Mount,
we decided to go up to the mountain to read.
Our hometown, Alqosh, has many mountains.
In June 1998,
I was in an accident.
In this accident, I lost both my legs.
It was a difficult time
because I was so young.
I was 22 years old.
So it was very hard.
I remember I was at that time in Holland,
and I heard the news
from family in Iraq.
And I went somewhere alone,
and I started to cry.
I came to Sweden, and like many refugees,
I had no desire to leave Iraq.
I was talking to Ziad all the time.
And one day in 2006,
he called me and told me
that he was studying with Jehovah’s Witnesses.
So I said to him,
“Is it logical that two billion Christians are wrong
and that you are right?”
And after a few months, I told him that
I was going to be baptized.
When he said that, I thought I was going to have a heart attack.
And he tried to convince me
that it was not the truth.
That it was maybe the biggest mistake that I was going to make in my life.
I remember it was in 2006;
a brother (his name was Ziad)
talked to me about Ataa.
So I talked to Brother Majeed.
Ziad had left the number with him,
and we agreed to meet in my apartment.
I decided I would give the Witnesses a chance.
We started to study for a few months,
and after that, he told me
that he didn’t want to have a study.
I had a lot of things to deal with.
It was not the right time.
I was too tired to listen.
So I told him, “Leave me for now
because I cannot be bothered with anything.”
So, what we did was that we just stopped the study,
but I still continued to phone him, to visit him from time to time,
to invite him to the Memorial and the convention.
And that’s what we did for several years.
He was very patient with me
and let it be up to me when and how we should study.
But he kept in contact with me to check how I was doing.
For me, I knew very early
that Ataa would be a brother one day.
He was so honest.
He loved Jehovah,
he loved Jesus Christ,
and he loved the truth.
He was of great help to me.
When my mother died,
he and his wife really helped me in a way that changed my life.
He invited me to his home, and he asked me:
“Can you just explain that for me?
Why should I get baptized?”
I told Majeed and Ziad that I had come to this conclusion:
“Yes, I must be baptized!
It is important.”
What convinced me was the way Jehovah
and his organization treat people.
Jehovah is not obligated to provide us with a hope for the future,
but he does so out of love.
He shows us more respect than we show ourselves.
And the way the organization is united
cannot come from men.
So when I was home, we called each other through Skype,
and he told me,
“I can’t find any reason anymore not to be baptized.”
At the regional convention, August 9, 2014,
it was a beautiful day.
It was one of the biggest days in my life.
So it was just a very warm feeling
to be beside one of your best friends
and remember that one day, years ago,
we were trying to understand the Bible
without having any chance to understand it.
And now we are sitting here as Jehovah’s Witnesses.
I often think: ‘God, is it true?
‘Is it real?
Do I really deserve to have all these blessings?’
I don’t have anything—no talents.
I do not understand everything yet.
But still, thanks to God,
I can understand the Bible.
I think we don’t need to be afraid
that some people will never hear about the truth.
If they really want to know that, Jehovah will take care of it.
So Jehovah was actually waiting
for Ataa for many, many, many years.
For me, when I think of the hope of the new world,
I’ll be honest and say that it is
not a question about having my legs back
and being able to jump like a gazelle.
No, that is not what I think about,
because there are problems in this world,
both for me and for others, that make my legs not that important.
No, let me have a good conscience.
Let there be justice.
By that I mean that it is God who governs and no one else.
True love—that is what I long for.

cn.text: 这是关于雅他·尧迪克的故事
他是来自伊拉克的亚述人
在基督教会的家庭里长大
雅他童年的伙伴留意到他非常渴望了解真理
由于伊拉克的政治情况
他们两人不得不搬到欧洲不同的国家
但距离会是问题吗？
不，以下是他们的故事
当我18岁的时候，我的朋友齐亚德问我
“雅他，你读过圣经吗？”
于是，我们就从创世记开始一起读
我记得有一次我们读到登山宝训
我们决定去山上读这段记载
我们的家乡有许多山
我遇到了一场意外
在这场意外中我失去了双腿
当时我很年轻，才22岁
所以对我来说
那段日子非常痛苦
我记得那个时候我在荷兰
我从来自伊拉克的家人那里
听到了雅他的消息
呃
那时，我找到了一个没有人的地方
哭了起来
我去了瑞典
像许多难民一样
我并不想要离开伊拉克
我常常和齐亚德谈心
在2006年的某一天
他打电话告诉我
他正在和耶和华见证人学习
我问他
“难道你认为20亿的基督徒都是错的
只有你是对的吗？
这样合理吗？”
几个月后，我告诉他
“雅他，我要受浸了。”
他告诉我这件事的时候
我当时差点要得心脏病了
然后，他尝试说服我
“这不是真理
这可能会是你一生中犯的最大的错误。”
我记得在2006年
齐亚德弟兄告诉了我关于雅他的事
所以我和马吉德弟兄谈谈
齐亚德把我的电话给了他
我们同意在我的公寓碰面
我决定给耶和华见证人一次机会
就跟他们一起学习了
我们开始学了几个月
之后，他告诉了我他不想再学习了
我要面对许多事情，当时的时机不对
我很累，根本听不进去
所以我告诉他
“让我静一静，我不想被任何事打扰。”
所以我们停止了学习
但我还是继续打电话给他
有时去拜访他
邀请他参加耶稣牺牲纪念聚会
和大会这样的安排
有好几年我们都是这样做的
他对我非常有耐心
让我决定什么时候恢复圣经课程
以及如何学习
但他经常和我联络
看看我的情况如何
对我来说
我早就知道有一天雅他会成为弟兄
他非常真诚
而且爱耶和华和耶稣
也喜爱真理
他真的给我很大的帮助
我的妈妈去世时
他和他的妻子给我的帮助
真的改变了我的一生
他邀请我到他的家
然后问我
“你可以告诉我吗？我为什么要受浸呢？”
我告诉马吉德和齐亚德
我做出了决定
我一定要受浸
这非常重要
耶和华和他的组织对待人的方式
让我确信这是真理
耶和华给了我们未来的希望
不是出于义务，而是出于爱心
他对我们的尊重远超过我们对自己的尊重
这个组织的团结也绝不是人能做到的
当时我是在家里
我们两个用Skype通话
他告诉我
“我再也没有理由不受浸了。”
2014年8月9日的区域大会
那一天，多么美好！
那是我人生中非常重要的一天
那种感觉非常温暖
当你在你最好的朋友身边
一起回想几年前的某天
我们没有机会了解圣经
却试着去了解
而现在我们已经坐在这里
是耶和华见证人了
我常常想，这是真的吗？
我真的配得到这些福分吗？
其实我
什么都没有
我没有任何天赋
了解的事情也不多
但是
在上帝的帮助下
我可以
了解圣经
我想，我们不需要担心
有些人永远不会听到真理
如果他们真的渴望了解真理
耶和华一定会帮助他们
事实上
耶和华等了雅他
很多、很多、很多年
对我来说
当我想到新世界的希望时
老实说
我的双腿是否能恢复像鹿一样跳跃
并不是问题
这不是我最关心的
因为这个世界上有许多更严重的问题
相比之下
我失去双腿真的算不了什么
我更盼望的是可以拥有清白的良心
由上帝而不是人来统治地球
正义得以伸张
人间充满真爱

titles.ko: 제가 이 모든 축복을 받을 자격이 되나요?
titles.cn: 我真的配得这些福分吗？

ko.text: 우리가 꼭 생각해 봐야 할 주제입니다.
여호와께선 우리가 생명의 선물을 즐기게 해 주십니다.
첫 조상이 우리에게서 그 선물을 앗아 갈 뻔했지만요.
그분과 그분의 목적도 알 수 있게 하셨죠.
또한 여호와의 “완전한 선물” 중 가장 탁월한 선물은 대속입니다.
곧 하느님께서 자신의 독생자를 세상에 보내셔서,
우리가 그를 통해 생명을 얻게 해 주신 것입니다.”
기대치 않게 값진 선물을 받아 본 경험이 있으실 겁니다.
우리도 무엇으로 보답할 수 있을까 생각하게 되죠.
여호와께서 기쁘게 받으실 만한 예물 몇 가지를 살펴보겠습니다.
아직 이 중요한 단계를 밟지 않으셨습니다.
“형제 여러분, 나는 하느님의 동정심으로 여러분에게 호소합니다.
여러분의 몸을 거룩하고 하느님께서 받아들이실 만한
그것이 여러분이 이지력으로 드리는 신성한 봉사입니다.”
그분께 드릴 수 있는 최고의 예물 중 하나입니다.

en.text: This month I’d like to talk about “Presenting Your Gifts to God.”
We certainly have every reason to consider this topic.
Well, why is that?
It’s because Jehovah gives us so much.
James 1:17 says:
“Every good gift and every perfect present
“is from above,
coming down from the Father of the celestial lights.”
For example, Jehovah allows us to enjoy the gift of life,
even though our first parents
tried to take that from us.
He’s provided us with a variety of foods.
The environment is just right to support life.
He’s given us his precious Word, the Bible,
so that we can come to know him and his purposes.
And the greatest “perfect present” Jehovah has given us
is the ransom.
Jehovah sacrificed a great deal
to arrange for Jesus to buy back for us
the hope of everlasting life.
This was at no obligation on Jehovah’s part.
It was totally a gift of love.
Please read with me 1 John 4:9:
“By this the love of God was revealed in our case,
“that God sent his only-begotten Son into the world
so that we might gain life through him.”
What a gift of love from Jehovah, our God!
What does that move us to do?
Maybe you’ve had the experience of a close friend or family member
unexpectedly giving you a valuable gift.
Immediately, what are you thinking?
You are probably trying to think of what you can give in return.
How much more so would we want to ‘present our gifts to God’
so as to show our sincere appreciation
for all he’s done!
Let’s consider some possible gifts
that Jehovah would be pleased to receive from us.
Many of you in our viewing audience
have been moved to give your life to Jehovah,
dedicating yourself to do his will.
That’s commendable!
That’s what Romans 12 urges us to do.
However, there are some of you listening
who have thought about this way of giving back to Jehovah,
but you haven’t yet taken this vital step.
Notice the appeal the apostle Paul makes
at Romans 12:1:
“Therefore, I appeal to you by the compassions of God, brothers,
“to present your bodies as a living sacrifice,
“holy and acceptable to God,
a sacred service with your power of reason.”
Your life is precious.
Presenting your body, your whole soul, to God
is one of the best gifts you can give to him.

cn.text: 这个月我想谈谈
怎样把礼物献给耶和华
我们为什么要谈这个话题呢？
因为耶和华赐给我们很多礼物
雅各书1:17说
各种美好的礼物
各种完美的赏赐
都是从上头来的
是从天上亮光之父那里降下来的
比如耶和华赐给我们生命
即使人类的祖先让我们失去了完美的生命
耶和华也赐给我们各种各样的食物
还有适合人类居住的地球
他赐给我们宝贵的话语圣经
有了圣经，我们就可以认识他
了解他的旨意
此外，在各样完美的赏赐中
最宝贵的礼物就是赎价的安排
为了让我们得享永生
耶和华献出了最宝贵的儿子耶稣作为赎价
耶和华没有义务这样做
他完全是出于对我们的爱
请读一下约翰一书4:9
这是多么有爱心的礼物！
知道耶和华爱我们
这会激励我们怎么做呢？
也许你有过这样的经历
一个好朋友或者家人
送给你一份宝贵的礼物
这份礼物完全出乎你的意料
为了表达感谢
你可能马上想
我有什么礼物可以送给他呢？
我们会这样对待别人
不是更想送礼物给上帝
来表达我们的感激之心吗？
接下来让我们一起考虑
我们可以献给耶和华哪些礼物
使他高兴
收看这期电视网的很多人已经决定
献身给耶和华并遵行他的旨意
你们很值得称赞！
这也是罗马书12章鼓励我们做的
也可能有些人正在考虑献身给耶和华
但是还没有迈出这重要的一步
我们一起看看使徒保罗鼓励我们怎么做
罗马书12:1说
你的生命十分宝贵
因此，你把整个身体
以及整个生命献给耶和华
就是你献上的最好的礼物

titles.cn: 要把礼物献给耶和华

ko.text: 우리 가족은 저와 아내와 세 딸,
먹을 거 걱정은 해 본 적이 없었습니다.
우리 회사의 경영진이 새로 바뀌었다는 걸 알게 됐습니다.
그는 손에 제 이력서를 들고 있었는데,
제가 정직하고 업무 성과가 좋다고 하면서
그런데 한 가지 빠진 게 있다고 하더군요.
오늘이 마지막 출근이 될 거라고 협박했죠.
하지만 전 정당에 가입하겠다고 서명하지 않았습니다.
그건 성적 부도덕을 저지르고 숨기는 것이나 마찬가지고
그냥 서명을 하고 계속 직장에 다닐 수도 있었겠지만,
그렇게 했으면 평생 양심의 가책을 느꼈을 겁니다.
집회에 나가고 회중에서 장로로 섬길 수는 없었죠.
또 우리가 견딜 수 있는 것 이상으로 유혹받지 않게 해 달라고 간청했어요.
이겨 낼 수 있을 거라고 확신했습니다.
직장을 잃은 뒤 여러 가지 일을 했습니다.
두 딸은 자주 보조 파이오니아를 하고 있고,
여호와께서는 항상 우리 가족을 잘 돌봐 주셨습니다.

en.text: I had a comfortable economic situation.
For 20 years I worked as the supervisor of a firm contracted by the oil industry.
My family of five
—made up of my wife,
my three daughters, and myself—
never had to worry about food.
One afternoon, as I watched the news on television,
I learned that the company I worked for had come under new management.
That Monday, when I went to work, I arrived at my office
and found the new supervisor sitting in my chair
that I had occupied for 20 years.
I saw my résumé in his hand.
He congratulated me for being a hard worker who was honest and productive,
but he said there was just one thing missing:
I needed to join a political party.
I replied as tactfully as I could that my wife and I were Jehovah’s Witnesses
and that we were neutral in political matters.
The mood quickly deteriorated.
Visibly angered, the supervisor’s facial expression
and tone of voice changed, and he threatened me,
saying that if I did not join the political party,
then that would be my last day at work.
I did not sign it or join the political party,
because that would be like committing adultery and keeping quiet about it.
I would feel as if I had betrayed Jehovah.
I could have signed it and kept my old job,
but I knew my conscience would bother me for the rest of my life.
I would never be able to go to the congregation
and serve as an elder knowing that I had let Jehovah down.
Suddenly, I was unemployed.
I lost 20 years of work
and the severance and seniority pay I was due.
My wife and my daughters were waiting for me.
And right then and there, we prayed together
and asked Jehovah to please provide for us,
to please not let us be tempted beyond what we could bear.
We knew that we were facing a huge test,
but that we would prevail
because we had been obedient to Jehovah.
Since losing my job, I’ve done several different odd jobs
like gardening and painting houses, and at present,
I work with public transportation.
My daughter, Genesaret, the second oldest, paints pictures, and we sell them.
My wife makes food and homemade sweets,
and we have learned other skills as well.
We have greatly simplified our life.
My wife and I were even invited to pioneer school in 2014.
Our two older daughters auxiliary pioneer from time to time,
and our youngest daughter, who is 13, was baptized.
Jehovah has never let us down.

cn.text: 我的经济状况一直很稳定
我在一家与石油工业有关的公司
做了20年的主管
我们全家
我  妻子还有三个女儿
从来没有为吃喝担心过
一天下午
我在电视上看到一则新闻
说到我们公司的管理层发生了变动
接着的星期一早上
我一到公司
就看见那位新主管已经坐在我的座位上了
他手上拿着我的简历
他称赞我工作很努力

en.text: What if the demands of the State conflict with the commands of Jesus?
There’s a Bible principle for that.
Are you thinking of what it says at Acts 5:28, 29
—that “we must obey God as ruler rather than men”?
This is not disregard for the State
but, rather, reverence for God.
If the State demands that we do what God forbids
or refrain from doing what God commands,
then we believe God would consider that an invalid request.
Now, one might say,
‘I can imagine some situations
where that viewpoint could get you into trouble.’
Jesus foretold as much at Matthew 24:9,
where he said: “You will be hated by all the nations
on account of my name.”
More specifically, at Revelation 2:10,
Jesus said that some of his disciples would be thrown into prison
—not all of us but some.
So we’re not disappointed if we don’t get thrown into prison,
but neither are we discouraged if we do.

en.text: So as Christians, what is our position
where political matters are concerned?
We are neutral.
Sometimes people misunderstand this viewpoint.
Some have concluded that because we don’t promote one human government,
that we must be promoting another human government.
In the 1950’s, in what is now the Republic of Congo,
authorities falsely accused Jehovah’s Witnesses of being Communists.
But during the 1970’s,
when Congo adopted a Communist form of government,
the new authorities found fault with us for not being Communists!
Today, however, and for nearly three decades,
Jehovah’s Witnesses have enjoyed legal status in the Republic of Congo.
And whereas some have perceived our Christian neutrality
as sheer apathy,
others construe our position as a threat.
Let’s address both of these viewpoints.
First, there is a big difference between Christian neutrality and apathy.
Apathy is defined
as “a lack of interest, enthusiasm, or concern.”
We certainly don’t lack interest in people,
nor are we insensitive to their feelings.
Like Jesus, we strive to alleviate people’s suffering
by helping them in practical ways
while teaching them about the only Kingdom
that can eliminate injustice.
By teaching people from God’s Word,
we endeavor to change hearts,
not political institutions.
We feel this approach is realistic
because mankind’s main problems are not political but moral.
But why can it be said that Jehovah’s Witnesses
are not a threat but, rather, an asset?
We conscientiously obey the laws,
we support our communities through volunteer service
or compulsory civilian service where that exists,
and we pay our taxes.
It’s true, we don’t vote for political parties or candidates,
but neither do we disrupt elections or interfere with those who choose to vote.
It’s true, we don’t lobby, campaign, or run for government office,
but neither do we criticize those in power,
undermine their policies, or demonstrate for political change.
It’s true, we won’t salute a flag,
but neither will we burn a flag, spit on a flag,
or disparage the nation that a flag represents
—even in lands where these are considered protected expressions of freedom.
It’s true, we don’t sing national anthems,
but neither do we discourage others from singing,
nor do we make a public spectacle of not singing;
we simply don’t participate.
It’s true, we wouldn’t kill people in war,
but neither would we attack people at home.
So while we don’t promote any political position,
neither do we condemn any political position —even in our heart.
That is what neutrality means.
We don’t take sides.

en.text: Our theme this month is
“Christian Neutrality—What It Means,
What It Takes, and Why We Choose It.”
What is your opinion?
Where do you stand?
Can one person make a difference in countering injustice?
When we hear people discussing political topics,
we might at first think their conversation is purely philosophical;
but when injustice threatens our loved ones,
it can seem personal.
We expect that people will be divided over political ideology.
Revelation chapters 8-13 foretold that in the last days,
government would be the burning issue among mankind
and that people would feel pressured to take sides.
The question each of us needs to ask himself is,
How do I respond when people debate solutions to serious injustices?
As Christians, we’re most interested
in the example of Christ.
Satan was pleased to offer him
“all the kingdoms of the inhabited earth”
in an exchange for one act of worship.
But Jesus wouldn’t accept it.
Neither did he assert that Satan had no authority to make such an offer.
Later, Jesus’ own countrymen tried to make him king,
but he rejected that too.
Later still, someone asked him
whether it was lawful to pay taxes to the Roman government.
Again, Jesus didn’t take sides.
He refused to become a world ruler,
a national leader, or a political activist.
Did that mean that Jesus didn’t care?
that he had no opinion?
To the contrary!
Jesus cared more deeply than we can fathom.
And by treating people fairly,
Jesus promoted justice at the most fundamental level.
Still, his principal focus
was on teaching people about the Kingdom of God,
which would eliminate injustice for all time.
So, what did Jesus indicate should be our position
regarding human governments?
We learn from Jesus’ response
to the question about Roman taxation
as recorded at Mark 12:15-17:
“‘Bring me a denarius to look at.’
“They brought one, and he said to them:
“‘Whose image and inscription is this?’
“They said to him: ‘Caesar’s.’
“Jesus then said:
“‘Pay back Caesar’s things to Caesar,
but God’s things to God.’”
What are Caesar’s things?
At Romans 13:1-7,
the apostle Paul lists tax, tribute,
fear, and honor.
Notice, too, that Jesus said
to “pay back Caesar’s things.”
What does that imply?
That Caesar, the ruling authority of the day,
had issued valuable things
—coins, for example.
Thus, Caesar had the right to ask for some of those coins back.
This enabled the State to continue rendering necessary services.
Jesus acknowledged that.
On the other hand,
our most valuable possessions are grants from God himself
—such gifts as our heart, our life, our mind, and our strength.
We can’t give those things back to Caesar
because Caesar didn’t grant them to us in the first place.
We rightly give those things back to God
in the form of our dedication and our love.
Regarding our love for God,
Jesus said at Mark 12:30:
“You must love Jehovah your God
“with your whole heart
“and with your whole soul
“and with your whole mind
and with your whole strength.”
So the love we give back to God is total
—no bodily part, function, capacity, or desire being left out.
Those who love God take the side of Jesus,
whom Jehovah has appointed as King.

en.text: I started studying the Bible with Jehovah’s Witnesses when I was 14.
The moment I realized that God did exist,
I was so happy and prayed, saying:
“I just assumed you didn’t exist.
Please forgive me.”
Right away, I told my family that I wouldn’t be able to join
the Christmas and birthday parties that we cherished.
My mother called all our relatives
and spoke to them in tears as she told them that her daughter had joined
a terrible religion.
She even told my study conductor to give back her daughter.
She felt like I was taken from her.
When I observed those things, at times,
I felt as if I was doing something wrong.
But then, I knew
that if I compromised, Jehovah would be sad.
Jehovah had kindly let me know the truth.
I strongly felt that in order to please him, I should not give up.
It would have been easier if I had given up, then.
Yet, I knew that if I did,
I wouldn’t be able to draw my parents to the truth.
I knew I would get emotional if I tried to talk with them face-to-face,
so I wrote them letters instead.
I prayed and prayed and kept telling my mother
how much I appreciated her.
Gradually, she realized that she hadn’t lost her daughter,
and she was relieved.
Now someone is calling on her, and we have
a very peaceful and pleasant relationship.

en.text: What Bible principles
could help a couple to decide
whether to serve alcohol at their wedding?
What principles and scriptures
do you think would help them make a balanced decision?
Again, you’re welcome to pause the program
if you’d like to write down what comes to mind
or to research something.
Now, your list probably has some of these principles.
At John 2:9, Jesus made wine for a wedding.
However, 1 Corinthians 6:10 says
that ‘drunkards will not inherit the Kingdom.’
And 1 Corinthians 10:31, 32 says:
“Whether you are eating or drinking . . . ,
do all things for God’s glory”
and to “keep from becoming causes for stumbling.”
Now, it doesn’t seem that any one principle provides the answer.
The couple could simply say:
“Well, Jesus served wine at a wedding, so we can too.”
However, there’s really more to it than that, isn’t there?
It’s clear that a balance of all these Bible principles is needed.
Will relatives or others be there who might be prone to overdrinking?
Would serving alcohol bother the conscience of many present
because of local customs and feelings about alcohol?
It’s often the case when making decisions
that we need to balance several Bible principles,
not taking any one principle solely on its own merit.
Jehovah expects us to use our “power of reason”
to balance Bible principles and make good decisions.
Ecclesiastes 7:16-18
gives us good advice about being balanced.
“Do not be overly righteous, nor show yourself excessively wise.
“Why should you bring ruin to yourself?
“Do not be excessively wicked, nor be foolish.
“Why should you die before your time?
“It is best to grasp one warning without letting go of the other;
for the one who fears God will heed them both.”
How true.
Such balance between extremes
is often necessary when we apply Bible principles.
We need to heed them both, so to speak.
We need to balance all the Bible principles
so we can come to the decision
that would show love of God and love of neighbor.

en.text: Uhh, yours?
Yeah, thanks.
You’re Lily, right?
Yeah. And you’re Sean.

he is  a Witness.

the more I liked him.
“If only I knew where to find God!”
Like I said, “I had a problem.”
Every day I see couples my age at school.
To me, they look happy.
Honestly, I wanted that happiness too.
My parents noticed my problem too
and talked about it that night.
And pretty soon I didn’t feel alone anymore.
The next day, my mom invited me to go with her to run an errand.
Afterward, we went to a little café.
She asked me how things were going.
At first, I didn’t want to tell her,
but she made me feel really comfortable.
So I told her my feelings for Sean,
expecting her to think badly of me.
But she didn’t.
Everything you’re feeling is natural, Lily.
I remember having these same feelings
when I was your age too.
Really?
It’s true.
That’s just how Jehovah created us, Honey.
And because he created us, he knows the best way
for us to be happy.
And that’s all he wants for us.
And that’s all Daddy and I want for you too.
She didn’t scold me;
she didn’t make me feel embarrassed.
And most importantly, she didn’t seem to be in a rush.
My mom wasn’t the only one helping me.
My dad was preparing to help me with my problem too.
That evening, we had family worship.
And once again,
they just let me talk.
They told me I didn’t have to hold back, so I didn’t.
I just don’t know what to do.
Lily, thank you for telling us how you feel.
Let me ask you something:
Why do you think Jehovah created us with these
natural feelings toward the opposite sex?
So that one day a man and woman could marry.
That’s right!
In fact, a good marriage is like two skaters on the ice.
A beautiful performance
can seem effortless, but is it really?
No.
No one would even attempt that without practice,
a capable partner, or the right kind of guidance.
Right?
Yeah.
Well, it’s the same with a good marriage, Sweetie.
It doesn’t just happen.
It too depends on a good partner,
coordinated effort, but most importantly,
wise counsel from Jehovah.
In fact,
could you please turn with me to Psalm 32
and verse 8 and read that for us?
Sure.
It says:
“I will give you insight and instruct you in the way you should go.
I will give you advice with my eye upon you.”
Lily, Jehovah loves us very much.
And if we listen to him, we’ll make good decisions in our life
with absolutely no regrets.
We talked some more, and then I got some homework.
My dad gave me some articles he printed out for me to read,
so I did.
And as I read the words and started
meditating on them, I realized something.
By holding off dating a little longer, I wasn’t missing out.
Rather, I was preparing myself.
I could use the time now to focus on something
much more important
—my relationship with Jehovah.
I could also gain Christian qualities
and experience that will help me later
if I ever do get married.
Well, the big day finally arrived.
After all those months of preparation,
it was just as I imagined.
Oh wait!
That’s not me.
That’s me.
As I watched my sister get married that day,
I couldn’t help but think about my own future.
When I began dating Shane,
everything was perfect.
We spent a lot of time talking on the phone.
Everything just naturally seemed to click.
I was convinced he was the one.
But over time, I started to notice some things.
I was starting to see patterns.
And they didn’t seem to be getting better.
I wasn’t even sure our goals were the same anymore.
I felt alone.
But thankfully, I wasn’t.
My mom kindly asked how things were going,
so I told her.
“Maybe he’s not the one,” I told her.
I thought she was going to tell me
which way I should go, but she didn’t.
Instead, she reassured me
that if he wasn’t the one, I was going to be OK.
They reminded me about what Jesus said when building a tower.
“For example, who of you wanting to build a tower
“does not first sit down and calculate the expense
to see if he has enough to complete it?”
I realized that I was about to enter
into a building project of my own
—my relationship with Shane—
and I too needed to “calculate the expense”
before I committed to it.
They encouraged me to talk to Shane
and tell him about the things that were concerning me.
So I did.
And my mom was right.
I was OK, more than OK, really.
Shane and I decided it was best to break off the relationship.
And some years later,
I found someone that loves Jehovah as much as I do,
and I love him with my whole heart.

en.text: I didn’t have a problem with polygamy
because I too was in a polygamous marriage.
And I viewed myself as a good wife;
I was the second wife.
I used to work at the mines in Carletonville, South Africa.
My family lived in Botswana, in Gaborone.
I had a girlfriend, and we had three children.
My church didn’t see anything wrong with what I was doing
because that was a common practice.
We were just married according to Cambodian tradition.
But we never legally registered our marriage.
I got a Bible.
What I learned from it really touched me.
I realized that I
was wrong to be in a polygamous marriage.
The brother who was studying the Bible with me
saw a picture of my family.
He asked me about the picture,
and I told him that it was my girlfriend and my kids.
We then studied the lesson which talks about family life,
and I realized that I had to make changes in my life.
When I wanted to start preaching,
I realized that Jehovah requires
that we legalize our marriage.
I had prayed,
“O Jehovah, if you really have drawn me
“and are pleased with me,
“please help me get the birth certificate
and the money needed to make the trip.”
This really troubled me
for a very long time.
Another thing that made it difficult
to leave him was the fact
that I had ten children.
But I saw that loving this man shouldn’t prevent me
from becoming someone worthy to God.
So I said, “I’m leaving.”
As for the local community,
they would comment about me:
“This lady is a rebel. She stole a man’s children.”
But once I did leave, I felt as if something
was being lifted off of me.
I went back home
and got married to my wife.
This enabled me and my family to be together
in one place where we could serve Jehovah
as a family.
After I quit my job, I spent a whole year unemployed.
We planted some vegetables
in our yard, and that helped us
to get by.
To my surprise,
my Bible study conductor called me
and invited me to go to Takeo.
It’s very far away, really far!
When I mentioned the names of my parents,
