en.text: Being single—you can focus more on other people
rather than concentrating on yourself.
Being single, having more time, more flexibility
really helped me to attain this goal
which was regular pioneering.
I view singleness as a gift
because it opens up opportunities
to serve in a more focused
and more flexible way.
You can study more
and have more time in the field ministry.
You have more time for the friends.
You’re more available.
Singleness definitely is a gift
if it’s used in the right way for Jehovah.
Singleness has not always been easy.
Sometimes there comes a period in life,
a certain age, when people start to ask,
“Anja, did you find somebody?
Are you not yet married?”
And that’s not always easy.
Sometimes
people look at you, even brothers and sisters,
and feel a bit of pity for you
maybe because you’re still single.
That sort of draws your attention away
from what you are doing.
That sometimes can be difficult.
I think I guard my singleness in the sense
that I look out for what kind of movies I watch
—not too romantic because it’s easy to fall
into this type of thinking.
So I’ve also always made sure
that I associate with a range
of brothers and sisters from different age groups
but ones that have similar sorts of goals
and they have a very positive outlook.
Following Jesus closely as a single person,
I think, is easier than as a couple because
if we reflect on Jesus’ life
—early to rise, late to bed,
fully focused on the ministry, on his Father—
that, I think, is easier for a single person.
He was available to help others,
he was available to teach others,
even for children
he was available for them to give comfort.
Jesus was so busy in his ministry and was focused.
And when you’re single, you’re able to do that.
You’re able to concentrate more of your energy
and effort into the ministry,
into serving Jehovah more fully.
It’s not a matter of just being single;
it’s a matter of how you use it
to support Jehovah’s arrangement.
It doesn’t matter whatever age we are,
if we are single, use the circumstances
that you’ve got at the moment
to do whatever you can
because we’re just living in a momentous time.
There is so much work for us to do.
Just go and pioneer
or do something for Jehovah,
and wait for him to surprise you.
You can use this time
to do all sorts of different things
in Jehovah’s service at the moment.
There are so many opportunities
opened up for single ones,
including single sisters, now
—going where the need is greater,
moving to different countries, serving in Bethel.
So while you’ve got these circumstances,
use the time now because it’s wonderful.

en.text: In 1998, I started dating a girl, and we dated for two years.
During that time, I also started studying the Bible.
Our relationship was going well.
We didn’t have any big issues; we got along well; we rarely argued.
So, then, how do you go to someone when you’re dating
and everything is going well and say:
“Listen, I can see you don’t feel the same as I do.
“I don’t want to date you anymore because now I’m studying the Bible.
I want to be one of Jehovah’s Witnesses”?
I really had to muster up a lot of courage
to tell her that.
But there are moments when you start to ask yourself,
‘Did I really make the right decision?’
And up to around the time when I got baptized,
I was still hoping that she would learn the truth.
But, unfortunately, that didn’t happen.
I was also involved in something else that I really loved, which was sports.
When I was younger, I was part of the track and field team,
and I participated in many local 5K and 10K competitions.
Some who trained with me at the time went on to become professional athletes.
Some even competed in the Olympics.
I knew I had a decision to make.
It wouldn’t be possible for me to keep training for track and field
while trying to serve Jehovah.
So I had to have enough courage to speak to my coach.
And after that, I gave up being an athlete.
Looking back now, it wasn’t easy to leave those things behind,
but what Jehovah has given me today
is much more valuable than anything I gave up.
I have the privilege of serving
in Bethel together with my wife, who also gives her all in Jehovah’s service.
I can honestly say that I am
truly happy serving Jehovah with all my heart.

en.text: “You must be holy, because I am holy.”
—1 Peter 1:16.
Handwashing.
Harmful microbes are the cause of many illnesses.
Microbes are tiny organisms
that live all around us,
but they are too small to be seen with the naked eye.
The microbes that we come into contact with most often
include bacteria, parasites, and viruses.
Bacteria and parasites
cause serious illnesses
that can lead to death.
Diarrhea,
cholera, amoebas, malaria,
flu, diphtheria,
and many other sicknesses
are all caused by microbes.
The hand—it’s the body part
that’s most exposed to microbes.
It touches everywhere.
We really need to learn to wash our hands regularly
under running water.
If you set up an inclined tap system
like the one here,
it is possible to wash your hands
with just a small amount of water.
It is very important to use something to remove microbes.
Soap removes microbes.
Ashes remove microbes.
After removing excrement from a child,
it is important to wash your hands.
If you have to touch an open wound,
eyes, or mouth,
remember to wash your hands.
We need to be clean.
We must have the habit of washing our hands
each time we come from the toilet
and each time we want to eat.
Some have the habit of taking
a small bottle of water and soap with them everywhere they go.
That way they can wash their hands whenever they need to.
Wash hands with soap or ash and water.
Wash hands before eating.
Wash hands after using the toilet
and after removing excrement from yourself or a child.
Wash hands before and after
touching an open wound, eyes, or mouth.

title: 피가 관련된 치료법—어떻게 결정할 수 있습니까?

ko.text: 의사들이 설명해 주는 치료법이 생소하게 느껴졌어요.
‘전에 이 치료법에 대해 들어 본 적이 있나?
어디서 읽어 본 적이 있나?’ 하고 계속 생각했죠.
의사는 제가 받게 될 수술이 복잡한 수술이라고 말했어요.
수혈을 받지 않기 때문에 더 어려울 거라고 했죠.
건강을 회복시켜 주는 치료를 받기를 원합니다.
피에 관한 그분의 법을 존중하기를 원합니다.
그분은 동물을 먹어도 된다고 하시면서 이렇게 말씀하셨습니다.
“다만 고기를 그 생명 즉 피가 있는 채로 먹어서는 안 된다.”
하느님께서는 고대 이스라엘 사람들에게도 동일한 법을 주셨습니다.
“피를 먹어서는 안 됩니다. 피는 물처럼 땅에 쏟아야 합니다.”
초기 그리스도인들도 다음과 같은 명령을 받았습니다.
오늘날 여호와의 증인도 그 명령을 따릅니다.
그 명령을 어떻게 따라야 할지 판단하기가
많은 경우 네 가지 주요 성분으로 분리되어 사용됩니다.
우리는 전혈이나 그 네 가지 주요 성분 중 어떤 것도 받아들이지 않음으로
어떻게 그렇게 할 힘을 낼 수 있었는지 들어 보시기 바랍니다.
여호와께 그분의 생각을 잘 알고 따를 수 있게 도와 달라고 기도했습니다.
그리고 제가 결정한 것을 적어 두었죠.
제가 그렇게 끔찍한 사고를 당하리라곤 생각도 못 했습니다.
그분은 제가 필요한 점들을 다 이해할 수 있게 도와주셨죠.
피의 네 가지 주요 성분에서 추출한
그러한 분획은 더는 피가 아니라고 생각하는 사람들도 있고
피에서 나온 것은 무엇이든 받아들일 수 없다고 생각하는 사람들도 있습니다.
한 자매가 어떻게 관련된 사실들을 다 이해한 다음
내가 정말 어떻게 느끼는지를 알아내는 게 어려웠어요.
그분 앞에서의 깨끗한 양심이 달려 있었으니까
다른 사람이 대신 결정을 내릴 수 없는 문제였지요.
제가 피와 네 가지 주요 성분을
환자 자신의 피를 사용하는 시술의 경우
내 피의 일부가 몸 밖으로 나오고
피의 흐름이 잠시 중단될 수 있다면
그 피를 여전히 나의 일부로 여기고
“땅에 쏟을” 필요가 없다고 생각할 수 있을 것인가?
시술 중에 내 피의 일부를 몸 밖으로 빼 내어
다시 내 몸에 주입하거나 사용하는 경우는 어떠한가?
내 피를 사용하는 모든 시술을 거부하는 것이
인공 심폐기의 사용까지 거부하는 것임을 알고 있는가?
한 자매가 어떻게 양심에 거리낌이 없는 결정을 내릴 수 있었는지 들어 보십시오.
의사 선생님이 저에게 효과가 있을 만한 대체 치료법을 제안해 주셨어요.
그런 다음 개인적으로 조사도 해 보고
어떻게 올바른 결정을 내릴 수 있습니까?

en.text: Everything happened so fast.
Everyone thought that because so much blood was lost,
my life was in danger and I would need a blood transfusion.
The medical professionals
were describing treatments
that I wasn’t familiar with.
I was (in my mind) trying to think: ‘Have I heard of this?
‘Do I know what this is?
Have I read about it?’
She explained that it was
a complicated surgery
and that because I didn’t take blood,
it would be obviously more serious.
We love life, and in any medical situation,
we want treatments that preserve or restore our health.
But more important, we want to respect the Creator of life and his law on blood.
God first spoke that law to Noah’s family.
After the Flood, God told them
that the animals could serve as food, but he added:
“Only flesh with its life —its blood—you must not eat.”
Blood represents the life of a creature and should not be misused.
God repeated this law to ancient Israel with clear instructions:
“You must not eat it.
You should pour it out on the ground like water.”
It was the same for early Christians.
They received written direction to
“keep abstaining . .. from blood.”
Jehovah’s Witnesses still obey that command today,
even though it can be a challenge to understand
how that command should be applied
to the numerous medical treatments now available.
Donated whole blood is often separated
into its four main components
—red cells, white cells,
platelets, and plasma.
We abstain from blood by refusing to accept
a transfusion of whole blood
or of any of those four main components.
How did one brother demonstrate the strength necessary
to abstain from blood during an emergency?
When it comes to blood,
we have to be prepared.
So that’s what I did.
I researched it, and I prayed to Jehovah
so that I could understand his thoughts
and follow them.
And then I wrote down my wishes.
I never thought that I would have such an accident.
I am very thankful to Jehovah
that he helped me understand all of these things,
and because of that,
I was able to make and stick to a decision that pleases him.
Blood fractions are things that are extracted from any one
of the four main blood components.
But the Bible does not provide
specific direction
about using these fractions.
So to accept them or not
is a personal decision.
Some believe that a small, isolated fraction is no longer blood.
Others feel they can’t use anything that came from blood.
How did one sister make an informed decision
about which medications containing blood fractions to accept?
When it came to fractions, for me, the challenge
was figuring out what I really felt about it and deciding for myself
what I would or wouldn’t accept and why.
At stake is our relationship with Jehovah
and having a clean conscience before him.
So it’s something that no one else could have done for me.
I had to make clear to my doctor
that I absolutely would not accept blood
or any of the four main components.
And I also explained to him
what medications and other treatments I was willing to accept.
What questions should Christians ask themselves
about medical procedures involving their own blood?
What if during the course
of a therapy or procedure
some of my blood will be diverted
outside my body
and the flow might be interrupted for a time?
Does my conscience allow me
to view this blood as still part of me,
thus not requiring
that it be poured “out on the ground”?
What if during a medical procedure
some of my own blood will be withdrawn,
modified, and directed back
into (or onto) my body?
Does it trouble my Bible-trained conscience?
Or could I accept such a procedure?
Am I aware that refusing
all medical procedures involving the use of my own blood
means that I would not accept a blood test,
hemodialysis, or the use of a heart-lung bypass machine?
What did one sister do to ensure she made a decision
that would not disturb her conscience?
So my doctor presented me with an effective, alternative procedure.
It was something that I knew about,
but I asked her to clarify the details to make sure
that what she was talking about was OK with my conscience.
So I made it a personal study project,
and I also asked a mature friend
to help me go through all the information.
I made my decision with a clean conscience,
and I knew it would make Jehovah’s heart glad.
How can you make informed decisions about the medical use of blood?
Pray for God’s wisdom and holy spirit.
Meditate on what the Bible teaches,
and learn about the medical treatments that may be offered to you.
If needed, ask for help to understand the options.
And finally, put your decisions in writing.
Jehovah God knows what is best for us.
And when our resolve to obey him is tested,
he doesn’t want us to feel alone.
He wants to help us.
When we accept this help and show respect for life that comes from him,
we can look forward to a paradise with perfect health and everlasting life.

ko.text: 우리가 안전에 유의해야 할 중요한 이유가

안전과 생명의 신성함을 우선순위로 삼아야 합니다.
여호와와 형제 자매들에 대한 사랑의 깊이를 보여 줍니다.
이제 세계 여러 곳에서 제작한 다음 영상을 통해
우리가 어떻게 안전에 더 유의할 수 있는지 보시겠습니다.
그 순간, 제 행동 때문에 다른 사람이 다칠 수도 있었단 걸 깨달았어요.
전 한 번도 교통사고를 낸 적이 없었고,

다른 활동을 할 때에도 조심하려고 합니다.

전 몇 백 번도 더 다녔던 도로를 건너고 있었어요.

“For by him we have life and move and exist.”
Since life is such a precious gift from Jehovah,
safety and the sanctity of life must be a priority in our daily lives.
Our organization has a goal of zero accidents
—and not just on construction projects.
Being safety conscious is a lifestyle
that affects all we do
—whether we are at home, on the road, or on theocratic projects.
Our attitude toward safety is really a reflection of our spirituality
and our love for Jehovah and the brothers and sisters.
Let’s see a few dramatizations from around the world
to help us see how we all can be more safety conscious.
That day changed everything.
In that moment,
I realized that my actions could have injured someone.
I could even have become bloodguilty.
My problem was overconfidence.
I’d never had a car accident,
and I thought it could never happen to me.
But just a second of distracted driving can kill.
I meditated on Psalm 36:9:
“With you is the source of life;
by your light we can see light.”
My love for Jehovah, “the Source of life,”
now affects how I drive
and even my approach to other activities.
For example, I love sports.
But I stopped playing those with a high potential for serious injury.
And even relatively safe ones
I’m committed to enjoying in the safest way possible.
I thank Jehovah every day that I’m still alive.
It was such a close call.
It was a street I’ve walked across hundreds of times.
No one has ever been hurt there before, so I felt safe.
Besides, I was preoccupied with what I had to do that day.
I didn’t see the car until I heard the screeching tires.
I wish it hadn’t taken this to become more safety conscious.
Now we continually train our children to stop,
think, and evaluate even familiar surroundings before proceeding.
Acting safely is one way we show Jehovah
how much we appreciate life.
Whether at home or elsewhere, being safe
has become a lifestyle for us.
As a body of elders,
we take Proverbs 22:3 seriously:
“The shrewd one sees the danger
“and conceals himself,
“but the inexperienced keep right on going
and suffer the consequences.”
If we take shortcuts or permit something unsafe
and an accident happens,
we bear a measure of responsibility for the results.
We love Jehovah and our brothers and sisters too much to allow that.
With good direction
and training from the LDC Maintenance Training Team,
we’ve learned to apply the principle of Proverbs 22:3.
We identify potential risks
before we start working and make a plan to complete it safely.
We always assign the right person to a task,
being aware of everyone’s knowledge,
limitations, and abilities.
And while it’s wonderful to have young ones with us,
we make sure they’re always supervised
and work with either their parents or another responsible person.
Life is a gift from Jehovah,
and I want to train my children to value it.
The smallest actions can save lives.
My conscience is clean now.
Understanding that making safety a priority is an expression of my love
for Jehovah and my brothers and sisters
—I’m happier now.
Could it be that some of our actions
reveal a lack of appreciation for the gift of life?
As was mentioned, safety is a part of being spiritual people.
That understanding motivates us
to develop safer routines and ways of doing things.
Our minds will be focused on keeping us safe
by identifying risks and adjusting how we do things.
In this way, we stay safe by eliminating or controlling the risk.
The world focuses on speed and cutting corners to get things done.
In contrast, we want our theocratic and personal activities
to show that safety is a priority.
This can be accomplished if we view safety
as a reflection of our love for Jehovah
and his precious gift of life.

ko.text: 직접 선택해서 결정할 수 있다는 것에
하나도 직접 결정할 수 있는 게 없다고 상상해 보세요.
우리가 잘못된 선택을 할 수 있다는 걸 아시면서도
어떻게 우릴 믿고 자유 의지를 주셨을까요?
오후 두 시마다 이렇게 말하게 한다면 어떨까요?
그리곤 이렇게 생각한다면 전 문제가 있는 거죠.
사랑은 자유 의지에서 우러나온 것일 때에만 의미가 있죠.
여호와께서는 자유 의지에 어떤 경계를 마련해 주셨습니까?
이스라엘에 주신 율법에 그 점이 나와 있죠.
‘“네 마음을 다하고 영혼을 다하고 정신을 다해 너의 하느님 여호와를 사랑해야 한다.”
이 두 계명이 율법 전체와 예언서의 바탕이 됩니다.’”
이웃에 대한 사랑이라는 경계 안에 있습니다.
여기 화면에 나온 사람들이 하고 있는 일들을 보시죠.
여기 나온 어떤 행동이라도 할 수 있죠.
이러한 경계 안에 머물 수 있도록 여호와께선 우리에게
우리에게 도움이 더 필요하단 걸 아시죠.
즉 우리가 좋은 결정을 내리게 도와주는
충분히 성경 원칙의 인도를 받을 수 있습니다.
창조주이신 여호와께선 우리에게 가장 좋은 걸 아시죠.
또 그분은 우리가 성경 원칙에 따라 결정할 것이라고 믿으시는데,
우리가 그렇게 할 때 진정으로 행복하고 만족을 느끼며,
하느님과 그리고 사람들과 평화를 이룰 수 있음을 아시기 때문입니다.
즉 직접 선택할 수 있는 선물을 주셨으며,
성경 원칙을 식별하고 적용하는 훈련이 필요합니다.
“형제 여러분, 나는 하느님의 동정심으로 여러분에게 호소합니다.
여러분의 몸을 거룩하고 하느님께서 받아들이실 만한 산 희생 제물로 바치십시오.
그것이 여러분이 이지력으로 드리는 신성한 봉사입니다.”
“뭘 떨어뜨리면 어떻게 돼요? 공이나 연필 같은 거요.”
네, 아이들은 각각의 물건에 대한 규칙이 아니라,
“이 볼펜 떨어뜨리면 어떻게 돼요?” 라고 묻는다면 어떨까요?
아주 기본적인 원칙들에 주의를 기울이지 않은 거죠.
따라서 우리는 성경 원칙들에 주의를 기울임으로,
이웃에 대한 사랑이 어떤 것인지를 이해하고,
모든 상황에 대한 긴 규칙 없이도 무엇이 올바른 일인지 알 수 있습니다.
깊이 주의를 기울이면서 성경을 읽고 공부함으로 훈련할 수 있죠.
그러면 긴 규칙 없이도 그러한 결정을 내릴 수 있습니다.

en.text: You and I make a lot of decisions every day.
Now, some have a little impact on our lives;
others have a very big impact.
And we can appreciate that we can make choices and decisions for ourselves.
Think of how life would be if you made no decisions for yourself
—someone tells you when to go to bed,
they pick out your clothes, and they tell you what to do for work.
Well, none of us would like that!
Jehovah gave each of us free will,
and that’s the precious gift of making choices for ourselves.
Now, have you ever thought about why Jehovah gave us this gift?
I mean, why trust us with free will
when he knew that we could make bad choices or decisions?
Well, one powerful reason is love.
The only way to give us the gift of love
is also to give us the gift of free will.
The two are tied together.
You really can’t have one without the other.
For example, if I programmed my computer
to give me a message every day at 2:00 p.m.: “John, I love you.
I think you’re a wonderful guy,”
I think there’d be a little something wrong with me
if I thought: ‘Aw, isn’t that nice?
My computer, it loves me.’
Yeah, love only exists
if it comes truly from a free-will expression.
Now, did Jehovah place any boundaries on free will?
Yes.
They were stated in the Law to the nation of Israel.
And Jesus later repeated them
at Matthew 22:37-40:
“He said to him: ‘“You must love Jehovah your God
“‘“with your whole heart and with your whole soul
“‘and with your whole mind.”
“‘This is the greatest and first commandment.
“‘The second, like it, is this:
“‘“You must love your neighbor as yourself.”
“‘On these two commandments the whole Law hangs,
and the Prophets.’”
So our use of free will
has love of God and love of neighbor as its boundaries.
Notice, for example, what people are doing in this picture,
both inside the circle boundary
and outside.
See, free will allows us to do any of the things
we see in the picture.
But love of God and love of neighbor
move us to reject what’s outside the circle
and choose to do the kinds of things that we see inside the circle.
Now, to stay within those boundaries,
Jehovah gave us a marvelous brain
and a built-in conscience,
but he also knows we need more help.
And that’s why he also gave us Bible principles
—basic truths from the Bible
that can help us to make good decisions.
And it can safely be said that any decision we face
can be guided by Bible principles.
Now, our Creator, Jehovah, knows what’s best for us.
And he also trusts us to make decisions
based on Bible principles
because he knows that when we do that,
then we’re really, truly going to be happy, content,
and at peace with him and with others.
So in review so far: Jehovah gave us free will
—that’s the privilege to make choices for ourselves—
and he also gave us Bible principles
as the boundaries to our choices.
But making difficult decisions requires that we train ourselves
to recognize Bible principles and apply them.
Now let’s read Romans 12:1,
and let’s see how this verse describes
the decision-making process.
“Therefore, I appeal to you
“by the compassions of God, brothers,
“to present your bodies as a living sacrifice,
“holy and acceptable to God,
“a sacred service
with your power of reason.”
So are we using our “power of reason”
to understand Bible principles?
For example, young children ask lots of questions.
But has a child ever asked you: “What happens when I drop a ball?
a pencil? a book?”
No, they don’t ask that.
They know what happens to anything they drop.
It falls down!
See, the child doesn’t need rules for every object
but has quickly grasped the principle.
Anything he drops falls down.
Now, what if an 18-year-old asked you,
“What’s going to happen when I drop this pen?”
Well, it’s obvious he’s not been paying attention
to basic principles of life.
So by us paying attention to Bible principles,
we can very quickly see the pattern
of love of God and love of neighbor
and know the right thing to do
without a long list of rules for every situation.
Well, how can we train our “power of reason”?
We train it by paying attention
as we read and study the Bible.
Now, we don’t need rules for which movies to watch,
which songs to listen to,
or what clothes we can wear.
If we’re paying attention when we’re reading the Bible,
we train our conscience with Bible principles
so we can make such decisions without needing a long list of rules.

모든 생물의 소원을 만족시켜 주실 것입니다.
하느님께서는 자신을 충실히 섬기는 모든 사람에게
우리가 이처럼 아름다운 미래를 누리는 것이
예수께서 우리를 위해 하신 일 덕분입니다.
우리는 더 이상 길을 잃고 헤매지 않을 것입니다.
아버지께로 가는 길을 알려 주실 것입니다.

en.text: With one act of defiance,
mankind became lost,
“alienated from the life that belongs to God.”
Sin and death have become inescapable
for every human born on earth,
with the exception of one—Jesus Christ.
He used his God-given powers to heal sicknesses,
feed thousands
—he even resurrected people back to life.
Jesus performed many miracles while on earth.
But are they simply a collection of stories from the past
or clues to something far grander
—a glimpse into a wondrous future,
a future where God will “satisfy the desire of every living thing,”
the “real life” that God promises
to each of his faithful servants?
But how can this beautiful future be possible?
Because of what Jesus did for us.
He came to earth for a purpose.
He gave his life for those he loved.
The curse of inherited sin and death could now be lifted
from each one of us.
If we look intently to Jesus, we will no longer be lost.
He will show us the way “to the Father.”

cn.text: 由于一个反叛的行动
人类迷失了方向
跟上帝所赐的生命疏远
从此地上的每个人
都摆脱不了罪和死亡

耶稣基督
他用上帝给他的力量
医治病人

耶稣在地上施行了许多奇迹

还是预示着一个极其美好的前景
一个奇妙的未来？
上帝会满足众生的愿望
上帝会实现应许
赐给他的忠仆真正的生命
怎么可能有这么美好的未来呢？
因为耶稣为我们所做的一切
他肩负使命来到地上
他为自己所爱的人献出生命
我们每个人
就可以从遗传的罪和死亡中
解救出来
我们定睛注视耶稣
就不再迷失方向
他会指明道路
领我们到父亲那里去

titles.en: A Glimpse Into a Wonderful Future
titles.cn: 一睹美好的未来

title: 예수께서는 왕국이 무슨 일을 이룰지 보여 주셨습니다

ko.text: 왕국은 국민에게 어떤 유익을 줄 것입니까?
기적을 통해 하느님의 왕국이 무슨 일을 이룰지 보여 주셨습니다.
자신이 왕으로서 지구의 자연 현상을 통제하고
환경 문제를 해결할 것임을 보여 주셨습니다.
기적으로 수천 명에게 먹을 것을 주심으로
왕국이 굶주림을 없앨 것임을 보여 주셨습니다.
왕국을 통해 죽음도 없애실 것임을 보여 주셨습니다.

en.text: How will the Kingdom benefit its citizens?
When on earth, Jesus showed
through his miracles what God’s Kingdom would do.
When Jesus calmed a storm,
he showed that as King
he will control earth’s natural forces,
solving environmental problems.
By miraculously feeding thousands,
he demonstrated that the Kingdom
will eliminate world hunger.
When Jesus healed the sick,
lame, deaf, and blind,
he gave us a preview
of the perfect health
that all will enjoy under his rule.
And by resurrecting people,
he showed that through the Kingdom
he will reverse death itself.

cn.text: 这个王国会怎样造福人民呢？
从耶稣在地上施行的奇迹
就能知道上帝的王国能为人民做些什么

跛脚和患病的人

耶稣也曾复活死去的人
表明未来他会永远消灭死亡

여호와와 그분의 아들 예수 그리스도도 마찬가지이시죠.
어떤 명분을 지지할 것인가 하는 문제에서

en.text: When World War II erupted in 1939,
nearly every organized religion
sent its members into the battle.
French and American Catholics
killed German and Italian Catholics;
British and American Protestants killed German Protestants.
Jehovah’s Witnesses wanted to make it clear
that they were no part of this controversy.
The Watchtower of November 1, 1939, reasoned:
“How could a person who is devoted to God’s Kingdom
“favor one side or the other
in a conflict between factions of the world?”
It defined what neutrality meant.
We’re not pacifists.
Jehovah is not a pacifist;
neither is his Son, Jesus Christ.
And when it comes to being in support of some cause,
we were 100 percent in support of the Kingdom.
And so we could not engage in any of the world’s controversies
or share in their war efforts.
This stand would lead to their persecution by dictatorships
and democracies around the world.
This is something that is so fundamental
to Jehovah’s people.
They are absolutely “no part of the world.”
They must be strictly neutral
when it comes to any conflict between the nations.
There are no other people
that are entirely neutral with regard to the world,
but Jehovah’s people are.

cn.text: 1939年，第二次世界大战爆发
几乎所有教会都叫信徒参军
法国、美国的天主教徒
杀害德国、意大利的天主教徒

一个效忠上帝王国的人

文章清楚解释中立的意思
我们不是反战主义者
耶和华和他儿子耶稣基督也不是

ko.text: 예수께서 땅에서 봉사하시는 동안 가장 많이 말씀하신 주제는

en.text: Throughout Jesus’ ministry,
he taught about God’s Kingdom
more than any other subject.
For centuries, his followers have prayed
for that Kingdom to come.
But what is the Kingdom?
A kingdom is a type of government.
A government includes a ruler,
a seat of government,
a territory that is ruled over,
laws,
and citizens.
Sadly, many human governments
fail to meet the needs of their people,
advancing their own interests instead.
In contrast, God’s Kingdom
has the perfect Ruler —Jesus—
someone God himself chose to be King.
God also selects
others to be associate rulers with Jesus.
This Kingdom rules from heaven.
It receives its power and authority from God.
Its domain will include the whole earth,
eliminating problems caused by nationalism.
And anyone
who obeys its laws can be a citizen.

cn.text: 耶稣在地上传道时

国家领土

上帝也挑选了一群人跟耶稣一起统治
这个王国政府从天上施行统治
权力来自上帝
这个王国的领土包括整个地球

en.text: Just as a person can be awakened from a deep sleep,
the Bible shows that it is possible to be awakened from death.
Jesus did just that
for his friend Lazarus.
Lazarus had been dead for four days.
If some part of Lazarus
had survived his death and gone to heaven,
would Jesus take him out of heaven
and force him to live on earth again?
No.
Lazarus was asleep in the grave.
Jesus gave him back his life
and reunited him with his family.
The Bible promises a time
when many people will be resurrected from the dead,
just as Lazarus was.
Jesus spoke of this wonderful hope when he said:
“The one who exercises faith in me,
“even though he dies,
will come to life.”

cn.text: 就像一个熟睡的人可以被叫醒
圣经说

只是在坟墓里沉睡
耶稣使拉撒路复活过来
让他跟家人团聚
圣经保证未来有一天
很多死去的人会复活过来

耶稣说

title: 죽은 사람은 어떤 상태에 있습니까?—발췌 영상

ko.text: 사람이 죽어도 그 일부가 살아남는다고 가르칩니다.
하느님은 첫 인간 아담을 흙으로 만드셨습니다.
하지만 그가 하느님께 고의로 불순종했을 때
즉 더는 존재하지 않게 될 거라고 말씀하셨습니다.
예수께선 친구 나사로가 죽었다는 말을 들었을 때
깊이 잠든 사람은 아무 일도 하지 않으며

en.text: Nearly all religions teach
that part of a person survives death.
But what does the Bible teach?
God created the first man, Adam, from the dust.
He had the opportunity to live forever.
But when he deliberately disobeyed God,
he was told that he would return to the dust
—ceasing to exist.
What about others who died after Adam?
When Jesus was told that his friend Lazarus died,
Jesus did not say that Lazarus had gone to heaven.
Rather, he said:
“Our friend has fallen asleep.”
What did he mean?
Just as someone in a deep sleep
is inactive and unaware of his surroundings,
the dead are not conscious of anything at all.

cn.text: 大部分的宗教
都说人死后有灵魂继续存在
但是圣经怎么说呢？
上帝用尘土创造了第一个人亚当

这样他就不再存在了
那亚当的后代死后又怎样呢？

而是说
“我们的朋友拉撒路睡着了。”
他的话是什么意思呢？
一个睡得很熟的人
处于不活动的状态
不会知道周围发生什么事
死去的人也一样
完全没有知觉

ko.text: “자기 생명을 많은 사람과 교환하는 대속물로 주”실 수 있었습니다.
하지만 어떻게 한 사람의 죽음이 모든 인류에게 유익을 줄 수 있습니까?
어떤 큰 회사의 사장이 회삿돈을 훔친다고 생각해 보십시오.
그의 행동 때문에 회사는 큰 빚을 지고

en.text: Jesus was a perfect man,
just as Adam had been.
However, unlike Adam,
Jesus remained obedient.
This allowed him
“to give his life as a ransom
in exchange for many.”
But how could the death of one man
benefit all of mankind?
Well, imagine that the manager of a large factory
steals money from the company.
His actions plunge the company into debt,
forcing it to shut down.
The workers lose their jobs
and cannot pay their bills.
Many suffer because of that one man’s corruption.
Now suppose a kind and generous man feels sorry
for all those who are suffering.
He is moved to pay off the debt and reopen the company.
By canceling that one debt,
he brings relief to all the employees and their families.
Adam is like that corrupt manager.
When he rebelled,
he incurred a large debt of sin
and passed it on to his children.
Jesus is like the generous man.
When he gave up his perfect human life,
he paid off the debt of sin
and reopened the prospect of living forever
for each of us.

cn.text: 跟亚当一样
耶稣是个完美的人

耶稣却一直服从上帝

可以“作为救赎许多人的代价”

让工厂可以恢复运作
由于他还清了一个人欠下的债务

都摆脱了困境

还把债留给了子孙后代
耶稣就像那个慷慨的好心人

ko.text: 인간 역사 초기에 무슨 일이 있었는지 알아야 합니다.

아담은 에덴동산에 있는 모든 나무의 열매를 먹을 수 있었지만,

그분의 완전한 천사 아들 하나를 땅으로 보내

en.text: Billions of people have died
throughout history.
But the death of one person stands alone
—that of Jesus Christ.
Why did he die?
Did his death have a purpose?
To find the answer,
we need to go back to the beginning of human history.
The Bible explains that God created the man Adam perfect,
without sin.
He was free to eat from all the trees in the garden of Eden
—except one.
God gave the simple command
not to eat from that particular tree.
This tree symbolized God’s right
to set the standards of good and bad.
As long as Adam remained obedient to Jehovah,
he had the prospect of living forever
on a paradise earth.
But Adam did not appreciate
all the good things God had done for him.
He chose to disobey God.
As a result,
he lost the opportunity to live forever.
But he was not the only one affected.
All of his descendants
have inherited the fatal effects of sin.
By themselves,
humans could not break free from sin and death.
They needed someone to rescue them.
For this reason, Jehovah miraculously caused
one of his perfect spirit sons
to come to earth as a human.

cn.text: 从古到今有亿万人死去

他就是耶稣基督

就要从人类历史的开始说起

挣脱罪和死亡的枷锁

titles.cn: 耶稣因为什么而死？（上）

ko.text: 그런 환경에서 자라길 바라는 아이는 없죠.
돈 걱정도 없이 사는 것 같았습니다.
저 사람들은 어떻게 저렇게 잘 살까?’
저는 범죄와 폭력이 많은 동네에서 살았어요.
늘 좋은 충고를 해 주려고 하셨죠.
몇 년 동안 도장 사람들과 지내면서
그들은 제게 가족 같은 존재가 됐습니다.
저는 레이먼드를 어느 정도 동경하게 되었는데,
시간이 지나면서 저도 마약을 팔기 시작했죠.
저도 그렇게 될 수 있다는 생각이 들었죠.
‘내가 필요한 것도 바로 이거구나’ 하는 생각이 들었죠.
우리 삶에 왜 이렇게 문제가 많은지
그 친구들도 알았으면 좋겠다는 마음이 들어서
제게 더 이상 마약을 팔지 않아도 된다고 했어요.
프로 복서가 되게 해 줄 테니까
그분은 제가 진정한 위로와 평화를 찾도록 도와주셨습니다.
여호와께서 제가 삶의 진정한 의미와 목적을 찾게 해 주셨어요.

en.text: When you’re little, you just want to be happy.
But sadly, my father had a problem with alcohol,
and no child wants to live through that.
One day, my family from the United States came to visit us.
They looked so happy!
The way they talked, it was as though they only had fun
—a good life
with no economic problems.
I was shocked.
I asked myself, ‘How can we live
in such poverty while their life is so great?’
That was the life I wanted for my family.
So when I was nine years old,
I left my mother and the rest of my family
to cross the border into the United States.
I lived in a pretty rough neighborhood.
So I joined a local gym to learn how to defend myself.
The trainer, Leo, was like a father to me.
He always tried to give us good advice.
Raymond was part of the boxing team.
He was a good friend.
We got along really well.
He respected me, and he looked after me.
After several years of being around Raymond
and the other members of the team, I felt really comfortable.
To some extent, I admired him
because I could see that he was really doing well,
because Raymond was selling drugs.
I knew that it wasn’t right.
But in time,
I began to sell drugs as well.
Raymond was in a drug deal gone wrong,
and he was murdered.
I said to myself, ‘This could happen to me too.’
It had been six years since I had seen my mom and my siblings.
My mother was studying the Bible with Jehovah’s Witnesses.
It helped her to cope with a lot of suffering.
It brought her peace.
She was so happy.
I began to realize that this was what I really needed.
I also thought about my friends at the gym.
I wanted them to understand why life was so hard for all of us,
so I returned to the United States.
But they weren’t interested.
My trainer, Leo, told me that I didn’t need to sell drugs anymore;
he could make me a professional boxer,
and I could help out my family in that way.
He even gave me the nickname The Bible Boy.
But I realized that that was just a temporary solution.
What I was learning was going to help me forever.
I was determined to serve Jehovah.
I returned to Mexico.
I started to study the Bible and take it seriously.
I began to view Jehovah as my Father
because he helped me to find real relief from my pain,
to have peace—a tranquility that makes you feel
accepted, loved, and wanted.
I have enjoyed an incredible life serving Jehovah.
Decades later, my father was baptized as one of Jehovah’s Witnesses.
Jehovah has been so kind to me,
my family, and my siblings.
Truly, I have no way to repay Jehovah for the life he’s given me.
I’ve had so many blessings in my life: a wonderful wife
and great friends,
including those that I serve
alongside of in Bethel.
I’m not on my own anymore.
Jehovah has given me a life full of real meaning,
purpose,
and so much happiness.

cn.text: 每个人都想要有一个快乐的童年
但我没有
因为我爸爸有酗酒的习惯
没有人喜欢
这样的童年
有一天，我们的亲戚从美国来看我们
他们看起来好快乐
他们之间的互动充满欢笑
好像
没有经济压力，过着幸福的生活
我们家过得好辛苦
但是他们看起来好快乐
我希望跟他们一样，也可以有快乐的生活
后来我9岁的时候
我离开了我的妈妈
和其他的家人
越过边境去了美国
我那时住的地方，环境很不好
所以我加入了一个拳击社，学习保护自己
我的训练员叫做李奥
他就像我爸爸一样
他教了我们很多事情
雷蒙德也是拳击社的
他是我的好朋友
我们相处得非常好
他很尊重我，也很照顾我
跟拳击社这些朋友在一起的这几年
我感觉他们就像我的家人一样
其实，我还蛮羡慕雷蒙德的
他因为贩毒赚了很多钱，生活过得很好
我知道这样是不对的
不过后来我也跟他一样开始贩毒
有一天
雷蒙德去交货的时候
他被人谋杀了
我心想，下一个被杀的可能是我
那时，我已经有6年没见到妈妈和弟弟妹妹了
我妈妈正在跟耶和华见证人学习圣经
这帮助她应付很多难题
学习圣经带给她内心安宁
她变得好快乐
我现在知道，这才是我真正需要的
我想起了我那些拳击社的朋友
我觉得
他们也需要认识圣经
知道为什么生活有那么多难题
所以我回到美国去找他们
但是他们都不感兴趣
我的训练员李奥
他告诉我，我不用再卖毒品了
他会帮助我成为一个职业拳击手
这样我就能赚钱，照顾我的家人了
他甚至给我起了个别名，叫做
圣经小子
但我知道这不会真正解决问题
圣经才能够帮助我
所以我下定决心
我要崇拜耶和华
我回到墨西哥
我开始学习圣经，改变我的生活
我把耶和华看作是我的爸爸
因为他帮助我、安慰我，让我不再感到痛苦
有真正的内心安宁
我感觉自己被认可、被爱、被重视
崇拜耶和华让我的生活更有意义，也更快乐
许多年后
我的爸爸受浸，成为耶和华见证人
耶和华一直很照顾我
也照顾我的父母和弟弟妹妹
真的，耶和华给我太多，我永远也报答不完
耶和华赐给我很多福分
一个非常好的妻子，很棒的朋友
包括那些跟我一起在伯特利服务的弟兄姐妹
我再也不是孤单一个人了
耶和华给了我一个人生目标
让我过有意义的生活
我现在真的很快乐

titles.en: I'm Not on My Own Anymore
titles.cn: 我再也不孤单了

ko.text: 여호와 하느님은 인간이 고난을 겪기를 바라지 않으셨습니다.
그분은 첫 인간 부부가 행복하게 사는 데 필요한 모든 것을 주셨습니다.
첫 인간 부부가 하느님이 가지신 권위에 의문을 품게 만들었습니다.
무엇이 옳고 그른지 스스로 결정하는 길을 택했습니다.
인간은 하느님의 통치를 받지 않고도 스스로 잘 살아갈 수 있습니까?
하느님께 반역한 자들이 제기한 이 중요한 의문들이 해결되려면
교사가 문제를 푸는 방법이 틀렸다고 하면서,
자기가 맞는 방법을 알고 있다고 주장합니다.
물론 반항적인 학생들을 그냥 혼낼 수도 있습니다.
하지만 그렇게 하면 다른 학생들은 어떻게 생각하겠습니까?
교사가 자기가 틀렸다는 게 드러날까 봐 그런다고 생각하면서
교사를 더는 존경하지 않을 수도 있습니다.
하지만 교사가 그 학생이  원하는 방법대로 문제를 풀어 보게 하면 어떻게 될까요?
누가 가르칠 자격이 있는지를 모두가 알게 될 것입니다.
사탄이 여호와께 도전했을 때 수많은 천사가 지켜보고 있었습니다.
천사들을 비롯해 지성을 가진 모든 창조물에게
여호와께서는 그 점을 알고 계셨기 때문에
사탄이 이 세상을 통치해 보도록 시간을 주셨습니다.
사탄의 통치는 이루 말할 수 없는 고통을 가져왔습니다.
하지만 여호와께서 인간을 통치할 권리와 능력을 갖고 계시다는 것이 분명히 증명되고 나면,
그분은 사탄의 반역으로 인한 모든 피해를

en.text: Why does God allow suffering?
Jehovah God didn’t intend for humans to suffer.
On the contrary,
he gave the first human couple
a wonderful start.
But Satan, a rebel angel,
called God a liar
and influenced the first humans
to reject God’s authority.
When Adam and Eve disobeyed God,
they chose to follow Satan.
They rebelled against Jehovah
and decided for themselves
what was right and wrong.
Was Satan correct?
Could humans rule themselves successfully
without help from God?
Time would be needed to settle
the crucial issues raised by the rebels.
To illustrate:
A rebellious student claims
that the teacher’s method of instruction is wrong.
He insists that he knows a much better way.
Some students think that he is right,
and they also become rebellious.
What should the teacher do?
He has the authority to reprimand the rebellious students.
But what effect would that choice have on the other students?
They may lose respect for the teacher,
thinking that he is afraid of being proved wrong.
But suppose the teacher allows the student
to show the class his  method.
Then it would be proved to all present
who is qualified to teach.
Jehovah has done something similar
to what the teacher does.
When Satan challenged Jehovah,
millions of angels were watching.
How Jehovah handled the rebellion
would greatly affect all those angels
and eventually all intelligent creation.
Knowing this,
Jehovah allowed Satan
to rule this world for a time.
Satan’s rule has caused
untold pain and suffering.
However, once Jehovah’s right and ability to rule
is established beyond any doubt,
Jehovah will undo
all the damage caused by Satan’s rebellion.
At that time,
only people who choose
to follow God’s standards
will inhabit the earth.

cn.text: 上帝为什么容许苦难存在？
耶和华上帝并没有想过要人经历苦难
他让人类的祖先有一个完美的开始
可是
撒但这个反叛上帝的天使声称上帝说谎
并引诱亚当和夏娃拒绝上帝的统治
亚当和夏娃不听从上帝
其实等于选择跟随撒但
他们反叛耶和华
按自己的标准决定什么是对、什么是错
撒但说的是真的吗？
人真的不需要上帝的统治
也能管理好自己吗？
要解决这些叛徒挑起的重大争议
是需要时间的
打个比方
有一个叛逆的学生声称老师教错了
他自认为懂得更好的解题方法
有些学生认为他说得对
也表现出叛逆的态度
这位老师该怎么做呢？
他当然有权训斥那些叛逆的学生
但如果他这样做
其他学生会怎么想呢？
他们也许会认为老师真的教错了
怕被人揭穿
这些学生可能就不再尊重老师了
但如果老师让这个学生
给同学演示他自己的解题方法
那么所有人就能看出
谁才有资格当老师了
耶和华处理问题的方法
跟这位老师很类似
撒但挑战耶和华的权威时
千千万万的天使都在看着
耶和华怎么处理这个反叛事件
将会深深影响所有天使以及全人类
所以
耶和华容许撒但暂时统治这个世界
撒但的统治使这个世界
充满灾难和痛苦
不过，一旦事实证明
只有耶和华才有权力和能力施行统治
耶和华就会采取行动
彻底消除撒但造成的所有苦难
到时
只有选择按照上帝标准生活的人
才会永远居住在地球上

titles.cn: 上帝为什么容许苦难存在？（节选片段）

ko.text: 사람들은 성경에서 하느님이 세상을 다스린다고 말하는 것으로 생각합니다.
세상은 전혀 통제가 안 되고 있습니다!
세상 문제의 배후에는 보이지 않는 곳에서 모든 것을 조종하는
세상의 문제들을 해결할 수 없는 것입니다.
성경에서는 앞으로 세상이 완전히 달라질 것이라고 알려 줍니다!
그때까지 우리가 어떻게 살아야 하는지도 알려 줍니다.

en.text: People think the Bible says
that God controls the world.
But how could that be?
This world is out of control!
It’s full of pain and suffering,
sickness and death,
poverty and disaster.
How could a loving God
be responsible for all of this?
What the Bible says may surprise you.
It says:
“The Evil One controls the whole world.”
In other words,
there’s an evil power
behind the world’s problems,
someone who’s pulling the strings
behind the scenes.
That’s why, no matter how hard we try,
humans just cannot solve
the world’s problems.
The good news is:
The Bible says things
will not always be like this!
It tells us why we’re in this situation,
how God will fix it,
and how we can deal with it in the meantime.

cn.text: 很多人都以为圣经说
这个世界是由上帝掌控的
但这可能吗？
这个世界好像失控了！
这世界充满了痛苦
疾病、死亡
贫穷、灾难
上帝这么有爱心
他怎么可能做出这些事呢？
圣经的答案也许会让你感到意外
圣经说
“全世界都受那恶者控制”
也就是说这世界的问题
都是由一个邪恶的势力在幕后操纵的
这就是为什么
不管人类多么努力解决问题
都无法成功
但有个好消息就是
圣经说这些问题一定会解决的！
圣经告诉我们
为什么世上有这么多问题
上帝会怎样解决
还有目前我们可以怎样应付

titles.cn: 这个世界由谁掌控？

ko.text: 일본에서 열린 거의 모든 경기에서 우승했죠.
끝이 보이지 않는 길을 달리고 있었어요.
그 무렵에 제게 「행복」 책을 한 권 주었습니다.
그런데 후에 신장암에 걸렸다는 진단을 받았어요.
13년 동안 즐겁게 해 온 파이오니아 봉사를
더 이상 할 수 없게 되었거든요.
장로 분들의 격려가 절 지탱해 줬습니다.
할 수 있는 일에서 기쁨을 찾으려고 노력했어요.
후에 기력을 어느 정도 회복하고 나서,
파이오니아 봉사 학교에 다시 참석했을 땐
여호와께선 제가 이 길을 계속 갈 수 있게 도와주셨어요.
인생에서 정말 중요한 게 뭔지 생각해야 하죠.
물론 경험을 통해서도 배울 수 있어요.
그리고 창조주와의 관계를 통해 배우는 거죠.

en.text: A road for racing
—bicycle racing against my rivals down a road;
a road I traveled just for myself.
That was my life course.
I started road bicycle racing when I was a university student.
I won practically every race in Japan.
I won the Japan National Championship twice
and even participated in the Asian Games
and the 1988 Seoul Olympics.
Of course, I was always happy when I won.
But that happiness didn’t last very long.
Every time I won a race,
I would be expected to win the next one,
and I was overwhelmed with tremendous pressure.
That frightened me.
So I immersed myself in training.
Train, race, train, race
—I was racing down a road with no end in sight.
After the Seoul Olympics, I was devoted to practice.
It was then that my younger sister Rie,
who had become one of Jehovah’s Witnesses,
gave me the Happiness  book.
I really agreed with what that book said.
In 1989, I started to study the Bible seriously.
Even so, I just wasn’t able to believe in the existence of a Creator.
So I studied the Creation  book.
When I read about the structure of birds’ wings,
my eyes were opened.
I thought: ‘There is a Creator!
The Creator made this!’
When I was convinced of the existence of the Creator,
I was able to understand the purpose of life.
It’s just as Ecclesiastes chapter 12 says;
the purpose of life
is to know the Creator and to live for him.
I was so relieved.
In 1991, I dedicated my life to Jehovah
and started on the Creator’s road.
The following year, I started pioneering
and my sister and I moved to a congregation
where the need was greater.
But later, I was found to have kidney cancer.
And in 2005,
I had to quit pioneering after 13 wonderful years.
I was really discouraged.
I could no longer do the things I had always done,
and it was difficult to keep my self-respect.
However, at that time, timely publications
and encouragement from the elders gave me good support.
So I tried to find joy in what I could do.
Later, I got my strength back to some extent
and I started pioneering again in 2012.
I was overjoyed to attend
Pioneer Service School again.
Jehovah really helped me to continue on this road.
In this system,
we think we have a lot of time in our lives,
but in reality, we don’t.
People should live
thinking about what is really important in life
—in the time they have.
Of course, we can learn from the things we experience.
But the wise course is to learn from the truth
and from our relationship with our Creator.
I really want young people to learn that lesson.
The road with real value
is not the one we take for ourselves.
It is the road we take for the Creator.

cn.text: 我曾经只为自己而活
我的人生道路就是
在自行车赛道上超越所有对手
那曾经是我生活的全部
我是在读大学的时候
开始参加公路自行车比赛的
我几乎屡战屡胜
曾经两次拿下了全国冠军
我也有幸参加亚运会
以及1988年的首尔奥运会
说真的，每一次得奖我都特别高兴
但是，我发现这种喜悦很短暂
我赢了一次，就想要赢第二次
这让我压力很大
我几乎都要受不了了
我非常焦虑，只好疯狂地加紧训练
我不断地训练、比赛
再训练、再比赛
看起来根本没有尽头
首尔奥运会后，我又再次投入了训练
那时，我妹妹已经是一个耶和华见证人
她给了我一本书叫做
《快乐——怎样才能获致》
我非常认同这本书里的内容
1989年的时候
我开始认真地学习圣经
不过，我还是很难相信有造物主存在
所以我开始研读《创造》书
我读到关于鸟类翅膀的构造时
我感到很惊讶
我想:真的有造物主
这就是他的杰作啊！
我相信造物主存在后
就能明白人生的意义了
就像传道书12章说的一样
人生的意义就在于
认识造物主，为他而活
我感到很快乐
1991年，我决定献身给耶和华
踏上一条全新的人生路
为造物主而活
第二年，我开始做先驱
并和我的妹妹搬到需求较大的会众服务
但是后来，我得了肾癌
所以在2005年
我不得不停止13年快乐的先驱生活
我感到很灰心
生病以后，很多事情都做不了了
这也让我变得没有自信
不过，当时组织的出版物
和会众的长老的鼓励
给了我很大的帮助
于是我试着在
自己能做到的事情上找到喜乐
后来，我的状态好了一些
于是我在2012年重新开始做先驱
能够再次参加先驱训练班
我真的特别开心
耶和华真的帮助了我
让我能继续行走他的道路
在现在这个制度
我们可能觉得自己的人生还有很多时间
但其实不一定
人人都应该在有生之年思考
人生最重要的是什么
当然，我们可以从自己以往的经验学习
但更明智的做法是向造物主学习
认识他的真理
跟他培养亲密的友谊
我真的希望年轻人能够走这条正确的路
人生真正的价值
不是为自己而活
而是为造物主而活

titles.en: I Learned the Purpose of Life

ko.text: 엄청난 소음과 속도가 나도록 개조했고, 크롬 장식도 달았죠.
하고 싶은 건 다 해 본 것 같아요!
부족한 게 없었지만, 마음 한구석은 늘 공허했습니다.
내가 여섯 살 때 막 증인이 된 이모가 보여 준 이 책엔 이런 그림이 있었죠.
하지만 몇 장 뒤엔 낙원 그림이 나왔는데,
그런 곳에서 살고 싶단 생각을 늘 하게 됐죠.
밑져야 본전인데 이모가 뭘 믿는지 알아봐야겠다는 생각에
형제와 두어 번 연구를 했지만, 별로 마음에 와 닿지 않았어요.
그 덕에 이젠 이걸 끼고 걸어야 하죠.
이틀 전에 증인들이 집에 들렀을 때
샌프란시스코에서 하는 특별 강연에 날 초대했어요.
그 당시에는 마약이 유행이었고 나도 마약을 했어요.
파티에 갔다 새벽 두 시가 넘어 왔는데,
내일 아침 절 깨워 주십시오” 하고 여호와께 기도했어요.
다음 날 아침 6시에 눈을 떴는데 잠이 오지 않는 거예요.
‘참 이상한데’ 하는 생각에 모임에 가 보기로 했죠.
‘별거 없으면 예쁜 여자애들 구경이나 하자!’ 하고 생각했죠.
형제가 성구를 찾으라고 하면 다 그 성구를 찾더군요.
그래서 지체 없이 생활 방식을 바꿨습니다.
얼마 후 공개 전도 활동을 할 자격도 갖추었죠.
사람들에게 성경을 가르치는 일을 즐겁게 하고 있습니다.
1998년에는 사도 바울이 수행했던 과분한 임무를 맡게 되었어요.
회중들을 방문해 격려하는 일을 하게 된 거죠.
여행하는 감독자로 미국 여러 지역에서 봉사했습니다.
인생을 살면서 행복을 쫓아다녔지만 찾지 못했습니다.
직접 행복을 이뤄 보려고도 했지만 되지 않았죠.
하지만 이젠 목적 있는 삶을 살고 있고,

en.text: American motorcycles were my passion.
We’d make them louder,
faster,
and lots of chrome.
It wasn’t just the bike.
I had a great American sports car;
I had a brand new house; I had a good job.
Really, I had the American dream,
and I had a great life!
I was always looking for fun,
and I always seemed to find it!
Even though I thought I had everything,
there was still something missing.
The Vietnam War was brewing, was raging.
People were dying, and it really bothered me.
When I was six years old,
my aunt, who’d just become a Witness,
she showed me this book,
and there’s a picture inside I remember so well.
It’s of Armageddon.
And that scares a little kid!
I thought, ‘I don’t want to be there,’
but a few pages later there’s a picture
of the Paradise.
I never forgot it, and I always thought,
‘I wanted to be there someday.’
So I thought, ‘Maybe my aunt has something.
What have I got to lose?’
So I called her and said, “Send over some Witnesses.”
So I had a couple of studies with the brother,
but it didn’t really make sense yet,
and my lifestyle hadn’t changed.
I was 21, riding my motorcycle,
doing about 75 miles an hour,
because speed limits were for wimps,
and I hit a parked truck.
I nearly died
and, as a result, I now use this to walk.
Two days prior I actually had Witnesses over,
but then my aunt invited me to a special talk
given by the Watch Tower Society’s president
in San Francisco,
and I said, “OK, I’ll see.”
Well you gotta remember, at this time,
the drug culture was in full swing
and was part of my life too.
And so I partied,
got home after 2:00 a.m.,
but I tried something—I prayed to Jehovah.
I said, “If you’re real,
if this is true, get me up in the morning.”
Well, at 6:00 a.m. I woke up.
I could not sleep, and I thought,
‘This is really weird,’
and so I thought, ‘I better go!’
So I went with my aunt to this function,
and I thought, ‘If nothing else,
I’ll just check out the chicks!’
Hey, I was 21.
But you know what I found when I got there?
Everybody paid attention.
When the brother said turn to a scripture,
they all turned to that scripture.
It was such a unified group of harmony;
something that I always wanted.
So I made rapid changes in my life.
I soon qualified
to go out in the public preaching.
Soon after that I was baptized,
and six months later
I started in the full-time ministry.
And so for over 40 years now,
my wife and I have enjoyed this work
of going door to door
and teaching others the Bible.
I was dignified with the opportunity
to serve as the apostle Paul did
—visiting and encouraging congregations.
I’ve had the chance to do that
in different parts of the United States
as a traveling overseer.
So really I’ve gone from a life
of pursuit of happiness
and never found it.
I tried to make it happen, but it wasn’t there.
Now I have a life of purpose,
I have a family worldwide,
and I have a secure future.
What’s better than that?

cn.text: 我以前对重型摩托车很着迷
我们追求的是
把车弄得更吵、更快、更炫

我还有一辆超帅的跑车
一栋新房子

看起来我做到了！

了解一下也没什么问题

请她找耶和华见证人来

天不怕地不怕

时速120公里

耶和华见证人才来过我家

是守望台社社长发表的
我说好哇，到时再看看

演讲前一晚
我狂欢到凌晨两点多才回到家
但我做了一件事

我说

再也睡不着了

我还是去听演讲吧

要是没意思

ko.text: 하느님께서 지구를 이토록 특별하게 만드신 이유는 무엇입니까?

en.text: Our world is filled with breathtaking beauty.
Why did God create the earth
in such a special way?
Even from space,
it stands alone as wonderfully unique.
God created the earth
with an abundance of water.
He placed it
at just the right distance from the sun
and set its rotation at just the right speed.
He gave it a moon
to stabilize the earth’s tilt,
contributing to consistent seasons.
And he created an amazing variety
of living creatures to share the earth with.
Why did God put forth so much effort
to create this beautiful earth?
Because he wanted to give
the first human couple, Adam and Eve,
a wonderful home.
As long as they obeyed God,
they and their children would live forever
and expand the Paradise garden
to cover the entire globe.
This was God’s purpose for the earth.

cn.text: 地球是我们美丽的家园
上帝为什么把地球设计得这么特别呢？
在浩瀚的宇宙中
地球的确独一无二
上帝使地球有丰富的水资源
上帝使地球离太阳的距离刚刚好
上帝也使地球自转的速度
不会太快或者太慢
上帝创造了月球
使地球保持一定的倾斜角度
使地上有春夏秋冬
四季不断更替
上帝还在地球上
创造了种类繁多的生物
令人赞叹
为什么上帝这么用心
把地球创造得如此美丽呢？
因为
他想要给人类的祖先亚当和夏娃
一个漂亮舒适的家
只要他们听从上帝
他们和后代就可以永远活下去
使伊甸园不断扩大
直到整个地球都成为乐园
这就是上帝创造地球的目的

en.text: Our relationship with Jehovah can  start when we’re young.
For me, it was the example that others set of putting Jehovah first
and the happiness that came as a result
as well as being in that sort of environment
that really helped me to want to reach out
as well as be available for those opportunities.
And once we do give our life to Jehovah, it’s amazing to see the blessings
that he has in store for us.
But in order to build that relationship,
we need to read God’s Word;
we also need to pray to him.
The more you get to know him,
the more appealing things
you learn about him.
That makes you not want to lose him as your Friend.
I always knew it was the truth and that I wanted to serve Jehovah forever.
But I needed to reassure myself of certain aspects,
so I did some research projects with my parents,
using the Creator  book and some items from the Bible Teach  book.
After that, it only became more obvious.
And I was certain that I wanted it and that I was ready to get baptized.

en.text: I didn’t identify myself
as one of Jehovah’s Witnesses
because I was scared of what kids
at school would say about me.
Peer pressure is probably the worst challenge
because you don’t just get
peer pressure from friends,
but you also get it from your teachers.
Some of my friends
who joined this new Christian group
started spreading false rumors
about Jehovah’s Witnesses.
Many of them said we were led
by some unknown leader at the top.
At first, I wanted
to stand up and say, “Well, that’s not true!”
However,
I started to become fearful.
I was hanging out with the wrong crowd,
and girls invited me to go play
in the park after school.
Something kind of told me
that I shouldn’t have gone with them,
but I still went.
Out of nowhere, I see two young men come,
and they tried to steal our backpacks.
They started arguing with the boys in our group,
and they started fighting too.
The police came,
and when I saw the police,
I thought I was going to get into a lot of trouble,
so I just ran away.
One time, the teacher at school was mocking
all religions saying: “The Bible is outdated,”
and “How can you know that God exists?
“People have rewritten it so many times.
How can you know it’s the truth?”
And I remember thinking to myself,
‘I should say something.’
I did this the night before, ‘I should say something.’
And then my friend next to me said,
“Bianca is a Jehovah’s Witness.”
The teacher looked at me wide-eyed
and said, “Do you have anything to say?”
And I just stood there.
I didn’t know what to say, and then the bell rang,
and I was just relieved.
I felt how I imagine
Peter would have felt.
My conscience kept bothering me,
and I knew that Jehovah
didn’t approve of my association.
The fact that I had to open my mouth
and kind of prove myself
made me just cramp up inside,
and I felt very disappointed in myself.
I said a prayer to Jehovah,
and I asked him to give me courage
to stand up and say
that I was one of Jehovah’s Witnesses.
I remember a brother who gave a talk once,
and he cited from the words
of Mark 8:38, where it says
that we shouldn’t be ashamed of following Jesus
because he would be ashamed of us.
Those words really touched my heart,
and I knew that I had to make changes soon.
After I had considered the example of Jesus,
I prayed to Jehovah
for courage and also for another opportunity
to defend his name.
Talking to Mum was probably the biggest help.
Her experience
and her knowledge kind of helped
to give me the courage to keep going.
Identifying myself as one of Jehovah’s Witnesses
has served as a protection.
In biology class,
we were talking about the topic of blood,
and my teacher made the comment
that those JW people will let their kids die.
I said a really quick prayer to Jehovah
because I knew that was not the truth.
So I stood up, and I said,
“We’re called Jehovah’s Witnesses,
and we don’t allow our kids to die.”
I was so happy after that moment.
I was able to give a witness
when my schoolmates started asking me
about what we really believe and practice.
I was able to give them
a much more accurate understanding
of how our organization functions.
Now that I’m able to stand firm in my beliefs,
I feel much better.
You’re doing it for Jehovah,
and you’re doing it for yourself.
You’re not doing it to make them happy;
you’re doing it to make Jehovah happy.
When I feel scared or afraid,
I say a quick prayer to Jehovah,
and he gives me the courage
to defend my faith and keep going.
I have gained the respect
and admiration of my schoolmates.
I’m not ashamed anymore of identifying myself
as one of Jehovah’s Witnesses.
Now I’m proud to represent Jehovah.

cn.text: 我没有告诉人我是耶和华见证人

想偷我们的背包

还开始打架

这次麻烦大了

在取笑不同的宗教，说
圣经过时了
谁知道真的有上帝？
圣经被抄写过很多次了
谁知道是真的假的？
我当时对自己说
快说出来啊！
昨天晚上才练习过

我知道耶和华不喜欢我跟这些朋友来往
一想到要开口说话，要为自己辩护
我心里就非常紧张
我对自己真的很失望
我向耶和华祷告，求他给我勇气
可以告诉别人我是耶和华见证人
我记得一个弟兄
在演讲里提到马可福音8:38
经文说

en.text: Under the direction of the Governing Body and the United States Branch Committee,
the Legal Department works
to protect our legal rights to worship.
When restrictions are placed on our activities,
we work to ‘defend and legally establish the good news.’
Let’s examine a case that was taken all the way
to the United States Supreme Court.
The town of Stratton, Ohio
passed an ordinance requiring
that anyone wanting to engage
in door-to-door activity had to obtain a permit from the mayor.
The ordinances that were enacted
were specifically designed
to restrict the activity
of Jehovah’s Witnesses.
The Witnesses tried to work the matter out
with the municipality, with the village,
but the village was insistent that our brothers and sisters
obtain permits prior to going from door to door.
This permit scheme was upheld in the lower courts in Ohio.
Thus, the case was appealed to the United States Supreme Court.
The Supreme Court ruled in our favor
and held that such ordinances
are unconstitutional
as applied to the public ministry of Jehovah’s Witnesses.
Even now, we still have some municipalities
that would like to enforce their permit regulation
against our brothers and sisters.
We turn their attention to the Stratton  decision,
and the issue is resolved.
Since 1919, Jehovah’s Witnesses
have obtained 50 victories
before the United States Supreme Court.
Just as extraordinary, we have prevailed
in the European Court of Human Rights over 50 times.
Jehovah’s Witnesses
do not seek confrontation.
They prefer to quietly serve God.
But when events unfold
that force them to stand up
and say: ‘I won’t do this’
or ‘I have to do that
because my faith compels me to do so’
—it is remarkable to see
the steel-like determination
of these individuals
who have looked into the eyes of judges,
magistrates, and police officers
and have simply said: ‘I have to obey God.’

en.text: I was serving at the Austria branch
from about the mid-1970’s to 1990.
We had a small department
that was assigned to help certain countries in Eastern Europe.
And that included visiting the brothers under ban,
bringing them spiritual food,
having secret meetings with them,
and also strengthening
the local organization
that was exposed to persecution and ban.
We would print books on Bible paper
in miniature size.
This way,
more books or literature could be taken to these countries.
The couriers transported literature to these countries
in their own private cars.
This way, hundreds of books could be transported.
At the border, if a courier would be found transporting literature,
they would interrogate the driver.
But these brothers were trained;
they knew what to say to protect the work
and to not give away any secrets.
Usually, after a day or two days,
the officials would let them go back home to their home country
but not with their car;
they had to use public transportation
because their cars would be confiscated.
But the brothers had the spirit of sacrifice; they were willing to risk that.
But the majority got through, and actually every year
thousands of miniature books
were transported secretly to Eastern Europe.
So it was not just a matter
of us being so clever in hiding things
and getting it to the brothers,
but we were always fully convinced
and had evidence that it was Jehovah’s holy spirit that helped us.
Also, we transported stencils for local production
so that in their countries
they could reproduce the same material
with mimeographing machines.
In most cases,
the mimeographing machines
were transported secretly
by the couriers.
The other method was to build it within the country.
I remember that there was a brother
who was a very skilled engineer,
and under his direction,
they decided to build it themselves.
So there were self-made offset printing presses.
The brothers had a number
of underground printeries
that they had dug out under their own homes.
In many cases, the brothers had to do
what they did during the night
because in Communist countries,
they had to go during the day to a factory
or whatever else and do some secular work.
But it testifies to the great spirit of sacrifice that the brothers showed
—to forfeit so much of their private life as a family
to do at night the printing
of the spiritual food.
Some had only a few hours of sleep,
but they loved Jehovah
and the brothers so much
that they did it.
There was no Kingdom Hall.
The brothers had secret meetings
in private homes,
and they would not all come at the same time
because if the neighbors would see certain persons
all the time going to a specific house,
there could be suspicions.
And every week,
they had the meetings in a different home of the brothers.
And this helped to protect the work
so that it could be kept secret.
Singing was very important for the brothers,
and they didn’t have to have a songbook in hand.
They knew the text of the song by heart,
and immediately after saying a number,
they could sing the song.
That affected the heart —the emotions of the brothers—
so they were strengthened in their determination to be faithful.

en.text: Nepal is home to the tallest peak in the world
—Mount Everest.
Located in the Himalayas,
it is bordered by China and India.
As of today, Nepal is home to over 2,200
of our brothers and sisters
who zealously preach the Kingdom good news
to its more than 27 million residents.
Tragically, on April 25,
everyday life for the people of Nepal changed.
A 7.8-magnitude earthquake shook the region
of Nepal’s capital, Kathmandu.
Nepal’s residents were now suffering the effects of the most powerful earthquake
to hit that region in over 80 years.
We were caught by surprise
by this event.
We were not prepared
for destruction of this scale.
But I am happy to say
that our dear brothers and sisters are coping with this situation
with calm spirit and with true faith in Jehovah.
One hundred sixty-three homes of our brothers were damaged,
91 of which were completely destroyed.
As a result of the devastation, there was an acute shortage
of food, water,
and sanitary shelter.
Within 24 hours,
local brothers in less affected areas
and neighboring branch offices
coordinated and began
the distribution of relief supplies.
A local disaster relief committee was formed,
and a medical team was dispatched
to care for the physical and emotional needs
of those affected.
Simultaneously, attention was given to providing
much-needed spiritual comfort and encouragement.
Immediately after the first tremor,
elders of each congregation
started to contact
each member of their congregation.
Although there were frequent aftershocks,
elders and other brothers personally went to the house
of each member who could not be reached over the phone.
Since the first tremor hit us on Saturday afternoon,
we were staying in the tents.
The very next day, elders visited us.
They spoke with us, inquired about our situation.
We are very encouraged.
But we are not worried about clothing and food.
A sister helped us.
Within an hour, elders came to help and encourage us.
They are visiting us daily;
it’s beautiful; we are happy.
Thank you.
On May 1,
Brother Gary Breaux, a representative of world headquarters,
arrived to build up those who had suffered losses.
A highlight of the visit was a special meeting held on May 4,
which was streamed via the Internet
from a Kingdom Hall to other congregations around the country.
All of this was only nine days after the earthquake.
It is very clear
that Jehovah has provided the needed help
spiritually,
mentally,
and physically
through his organization and through his holy spirit.

ko.text: 사도 베드로가 오늘의 성구를 기록할 당시에는
즉 하느님의 영적 이스라엘을 이루고 있었습니다.
거룩한 나라이고, 특별한 소유가 된 백성’입니다.
그것은 여러분을 어둠에서 불러내어 자신의 놀라운 빛으로 들어가게 하신 분의
전에는 여러분이 백성이 아니었지만, 이제는 하느님의 백성입니다.”
여호와의 증인으로서 그분의 이름을 영광스럽게 할 책임이 있는
영으로 기름부음받은 회중 성원들을 가리켜 말한 것입니다.
또 이것은 베드로가 여러 해 전에
1세기 중앙장로회 모임에서 한 것으로 보고된 말과도 일치합니다.
“하느님께서 처음으로 이방 사람들 가운데서 자신의 이름을 위한 백성을 모으시려고
어떻게 그들에게 주의를 돌리셨는지 시므온이 자세히 이야기했습니다.
‘그 후에 내가 돌아와서 다윗의 무너진 천막을 다시 일으킬 것이며
그것은 남은 자들이 내 이름으로 불리는 모든 이방 사람들과 함께
이 일들을 행하고 있는 여호와가 말한다.’”
다른 종교들은 맡고 싶어하지 않는 책임인데요,
그분을 잘못 알리는 거짓 가르침들을 폭로할 의무 아래 있습니다.
가장 극적인 사기극을 벌인 사람일 겁니다.
비평가들이 자기 작품의 가치를 몰라본다고 생각하고
그들을 다 속여 자신의 재능을 알릴 작정이었죠.
잘 알려지지 않은 17세기의 그림을 가져다 그림을 지웠죠.
가장 큰 문제는 유화를 완전히 굳히는 것이었는데,
그는 물감에 기름 대신 합성수지를 섞고,
「엠마우스의 예수와 사도들」 (Christ and the Disciples at Emmaus)이란 그림이죠.
사도들이 죽은 뒤, 배교의 시기에도 있었습니다.
“하늘에 아버지와 말씀과 성신이 계시니, 이 셋은 하나이니라.”
가장 오래된 그리스어 사본들에서는 찾을 수 없는 표현입니다.
“결국 삼위일체 교의는 4세기 후반에 가서야 고안된 것이다.
그러한 경향이나 사조에 조금이라도 닮은 것조차 전혀 없었다.”
성경과 모순되는 교리를 가르치는 것의 어리석음을 폭로했습니다.
참으로 모순 투성이와 혼란에 빠져 있는 것이다!
그것은 그분이 지상에 있을 때 위선자였고
하느님께 기도한 것은 시늉에 불과했다는 뜻이 될 것이다.
••• 아버지는 언제나 불멸이셨으므로 죽으실 수 없었다.
••• 예수가 죽었음을 인정한다면, 또 다른 딜레마에 빠진다.
예수가 죽었을 때 셋 모두가 죽은 것이다.
어둡고 미신적인 과거로부터 우리에게 물려준 교의를 옹호하기 위해,
오직 한 분인 참하느님에 관한 진리를 계속해서 옹호합니다.

en.text: By the time the apostle Peter
wrote the words of today’s text,
individuals who were Jews, proselytes,
Samaritans, and Gentiles had been brought
into the Christian congregation
as God’s people,
the spiritual Israel of God.
In the verse before today’s text,
Peter outlined what their mission was.
Let’s open to 1 Peter chapter 2 and read that.
It’s in verses 9 and 10 of 1 Peter 2.
He wrote:
“But you are ‘a chosen race, a royal priesthood,
“‘a holy nation, a people for special possession,
“that you should declare abroad the excellencies’
“of the One who called you out of darkness into his wonderful light.
“For you were once not a people,
but now you are God’s people.”
And, of course, this refers
to the spirit-anointed members of the congregation
who would be responsible
for glorifying Jehovah’s name as his Witnesses.
And this harmonizes with what Peter had said years earlier
in the first-century governing body meeting,
as reported in Acts chapter 15.
So let’s turn there, Acts 15,
and we will begin with verse 14.
It says: “Symeon has related thoroughly
“how God for the first time turned his attention to the nations
“to take out of them a people for his name.
“And with this the words of the Prophets agree,
“just as it is written: ‘After these things I will return
“‘and raise up again the tent of David that is fallen down;
“‘I will rebuild its ruins and restore it,
“‘so that the men who remain may earnestly seek Jehovah,
“‘together with people of all the nations,
“‘people who are called by my name,
says Jehovah, who is doing these things.’”
Now, what about the rest of us who are not anointed Christians
but who call ourselves Jehovah’s Witnesses?
Are we also God’s people?
Well, most certainly!
And what a proud honor it is for us
to bear the name of the only true God.
But with that name comes responsibility,
one that other religious groups do not want to take on.
You see, we are under obligation to bear witness to Jehovah,
to tell the truth about him,
and to expose false teachings that misrepresent Jehovah.
And a classic example of an unscriptural dogma
that God’s people have exposed is the Trinity,
which reminds me of another hoax
that fooled many people who should have known better.
It’s the true story about a man named van Meegeren,
a Dutch artist, born in 1889,
who perpetrated what may have been
the most sensational art hoax of all time.
You see, he never won the critical acclaim
that he thought he was due as an artist.
So to get back at the art critics,
he decided to demonstrate his talent
by producing a painting that would fool them all,
and he set out to imitate the famous 17th-century Dutch impressionist,
Johannes Vermeer.
Well, van Meegeren spent 4 years
figuring out how to make a new painting look 300 years old.
The canvas was the easy part.
He just took a lesser-known painting from the 17th century
and removed the picture.
His biggest problem was getting oil paint to harden thoroughly,
which usually takes 50 years.
He solved it by mixing his pigments
with a synthetic resin instead of oil
and then baking the canvas.
Well, van Meegeren produced six paintings
that were passed off as Vermeers.
His greatest sold in 1937.
It was entitled Christ and the Disciples at Emmaus.
The most authoritative art historian of the day
said it was a genuine Vermeer masterpiece,
untouched, on the original canvas,
and that it had no restoration done to it.
But in reality, it was a fake.
The critic’s opinion was taken as gospel in the art world,
so much so that this critic had been nicknamed “The Pope.”
Eventually, though, a chemical analysis proved
that the paint contained an ingredient that had not been discovered
until two centuries after Vermeer died,
and that’s what exposed van Meegeren as a fraud.
Well, something similar went on during the apostasy
that took place after the death of the apostles.
Less than 300 years after the Bible was completed,
a Trinitarian added to 1 John 5:7 the words
“in heaven, the Father, the Word, and the Holy Ghost:
and these three are one.”
However, this addition does not appear in the oldest Greek manuscripts,
proving it’s a fake; it’s a corruption of God’s Word.
And yet for centuries, the churches propagated the Trinity doctrine.
As recently as the 19th century,
almost all Bible translations had this spurious addition.
As late as 1897,
Pope Leo XIII upheld the corrupted text of the Latin Vulgate.
Interestingly, the New Catholic Encyclopedia  comments on this and says:
“The Trinitarian dogma is in the last analysis
“a late 4th century invention.
“Among the Apostolic Fathers,
“there had been nothing even remotely approaching
such a mentality or perspective.”
Well, Jehovah’s anointed Witnesses
firmly rejected Christendom’s Trinity dogma.
In 1915, The Watch Tower  exposed the foolishness
of teaching a doctrine that contradicts the Bible.
The Watch Tower  said:
“In what a jumble of contradictions and confusion
“do they find themselves who say
“that Jesus and the Father are one God!
“This would involve the idea
“that our Lord Jesus acted the hypocrite when on earth
“and only pretended to address God in prayer,
“when He Himself was the same God.
“. . . The Father has always been immortal, hence could not die.
“How then, could Jesus have died?
“. . . The Scriptures declare, however, that He did die.
“. . . If they admit that Jesus really died, they take the other horn of the dilemma;
“for believing that their three Gods are all one person as many do,
“when Jesus died they must all three have died.
“If they all died, who raised them to life?
“How foolish all this sounds!
“. . . Shall we thus contradict the Apostles and Prophets and Jesus Himself,
“and ignore reason and common sense,
“in order to hold to a dogma handed to us
“from the dark, superstitious past,
“by a corrupt apostate Church?
Nay!” says The Watch Tower.
Well, Jehovah’s people continue to uphold
the excellencies of the only true God.

cn.text: 今天的经文出自使徒彼得
写给基督徒会众的信
当时会众里有犹太人
归信犹太教的人
撒马利亚人和外族人
他们都已经成为上帝的子民
也就是“上帝的以色列”
在彼得前书2:9
彼得概述了他们有什么使命
请打开彼得前书第2章
读这里的经文
彼得前书2:9,10这样说:
“你们‘是上帝挑选的一族人
是有王权的祭司
是圣洁的国族
是专属于他的子民
应该宣扬他的美德’
因为他已经呼召你们从黑暗出来
进入他奇妙的光里
你们以往不是上帝的子民
现在却是他的子民”
当然，经文的说话对象
是会众里受神圣力量任命的人
他们有责任颂扬耶和华的名
为他作见证
这跟多年前彼得在公元1世纪的
中央长老团会议上说的一致
这些话记在使徒行传15章
让我们一起翻到使徒行传15章
我们会从第14节开始读
“西门刚才详述了上帝第一次眷顾外族人时
怎样从他们当中选出一群归他名下的子民
这件事跟先知书上的话完全吻合
圣经上写着:‘这些事以后
我要回来重新建起大卫倒塌的帐篷
重建废墟，把帐篷再次竖立起来
让余下的人跟所有国族中称为我名下的人
一起恳切寻求耶和华
这是耶和华说的’”
那么我们呢？
我们也为耶和华作见证
但不是受任命到天上
我们也是上帝的子民吗？
当然是！
我们很荣幸能够成为
独一真神名下的子民
可是，这也意味着我们有一项责任
这是其他宗教团体不愿意承担的
这项责任就是
为耶和华作见证
告诉别人跟上帝有关的真理
并且揭露那些曲解耶和华的错误教义
在不符合圣经的教义当中
三位一体是个典型的例子
说到这里，我想到了一个骗局
当时，连许多专家也上当了
这是个真实的故事
有一位荷兰画家
名叫汉·凡·米格伦
生于1889年
他曾经制造了艺术史上
可以说是最轰动的一场骗局
米格伦觉得自己很有才华
但从未得到艺术评论家的认可
为了报复他们，证明自己的才华
他决定画一幅作品愚弄他们
他就伪造了17世纪著名的荷兰印象派画家
约翰内斯·维米尔的画作
米格伦花了4年的时间研究
如何使油画看起来像300年前画的
旧的画布不难找
只要找一幅17世纪不出名的油画
把上面的颜料去掉就行
最难的是让颜料干透
因为这通常需要50年
他没有用油
而是用合成树脂跟颜料混合
然后把画布拿去烘干
他用这样的方式仿制了维米尔的画作
一共6幅
最著名的一幅在1937年出售
名为《耶稣与他的门徒》
当时一位最权威的艺术史学家说
这是一幅真迹，是维米尔本人的杰作
没有任何破损和修复的痕迹
画布也是当年的画布
但其实这就是一幅赝品
这位专家的话在艺术界相当受重视
他甚至被称为艺术界的“教皇”
后来有化学分析证实
这幅油画中有一种成分
是维米尔去世两个世纪后才有人使用的
人们这才知道米格伦是个大骗子
其实在使徒们去世之后
叛道者也做了类似的事情
圣经写成后不到300年
鼓吹三位一体的人
在约翰一书5:7加了这句话:
“在天上有父，有道，有圣灵
这三位是合一的”
但圣经最古老的希腊语抄本没有这段话
可见这是伪造的
歪曲了上帝的话语
多个世纪以来
教会一直传播三位一体的教义
在19世纪
几乎所有的圣经译本都还是保留着
这节杜撰的经文
1897年，教皇利奥十三世
坚持在《通俗拉丁文本圣经》里保留这句话
值得留意的是
根据《新天主教百科全书》
三位一体这个教义
其实是在公元4世纪末才出现的
1世纪末到2世纪中叶的宗教作家
都没提过三位一体
或者任何相关的主张
受任命到天上的基督徒
坚决不认同一般教会主张的三位一体教义
在1915年，《守望台》指出
教导人跟圣经矛盾的教义是愚不可及的
《守望台》说:
“有些人声称耶稣和天父是同一位
他们的这种说法
是多么矛盾、多么混乱！
这样的说法会让人以为
主耶稣是个虚伪的人
他如果是上帝，他祷告就是装出来的
既然天父是永远不死的
耶稣又怎么会死去呢？
圣经说耶稣确实曾经死去
如果他们承认耶稣真的死了
又会陷入另一个困境
因为上帝如果是三位一体的
那么当耶稣死去时，三位就都死了
要是这样，谁来复活耶稣呢？
这个教义多么荒唐！
这个教义来自腐化叛道的教会
从黑暗的迷信时期流传下来
不符合使徒、先知和耶稣的教导
也违背常识
我们该相信这个主张吗？
怎么可能！”
一直以来
耶和华的子民不断告诉人
有关上帝的真理

ko.text: 우린 늘 그저 성경 연구생이라고 불렸고,
러셀 형제도 그걸 어느 정도 권장했죠.
다른 고유한 이름으로 알려지길 바라지 않는다고 말했고
사람들이 우리를 러셀파나 러더퍼드파라고 부르기 시작한 겁니다.
그리스도인이 된다는 것이 무슨 뜻인지도 모르면서
그들의 신분에 관한 점이 다루어질 것이었습니다.
우리는 찰스 T. 러셀 형제를 깊이 사랑하며,
그의 활동을 크게 축복하셨음을 기꺼이 인정합니다.
하지만 우리는 “러셀파”라고 불리는 것을 받아들일 수 없습니다.
또한 워치 타워 성서 책자 협회와
초기에 발행된 「시온의 파수대」지를 보면 알 수 있듯이,
성경 연구생들은 이미 하느님의 이름을 알고 있었습니다.
지식에는 증거할 책임이 따른다는 점을 상기시켜 줄 것이었습니다.

en.text: We were always just called the Bible Students,
and Brother Russell kind of encouraged that.
He said we didn’t want to be known
by any distinctive name
but just Bible Students,
and I appreciated his viewpoint on that.
But the trouble was that people
began to call us Russellites and Rutherfordites,
and not only that
but the term “Christian” itself became a misnomer.
Many people said they were Christians,
and they didn’t have any idea as to what being a Christian meant.
Their identity would be considered
at a seven-day convention
held in Columbus, Ohio, in 1931.
Attendees received programs
with the puzzling letters “JW” on the cover.
Speaking on Isaiah 43:10,
J. F. Rutherford presented a resolution.
We have great love for Brother Charles T. Russell,
and we gladly acknowledge
that the Lord used him and greatly blessed his work,
yet we cannot consent
to be called by the name “Russellites.”
The Watch Tower Bible and Tract Society
and the International Bible Students Association
are merely names of corporations.
We are servants of Jehovah God
commissioned to do a work in his name.
Henceforth, may it be known
that we are Jehovah’s Witnesses.
Early editions of Zion’s Watch Tower
reveal that the Bible Students
had already known God’s name.
But now, their new designation
would remind these Christians
that knowledge brings responsibility to bear witness.
So at that particular time,
we went from being a vague group of persons
who were joined together
by a common interest in studying the Scriptures
to being a Scriptural identity
that we could stand up and be proud of.

cn.text: 我们一直叫做圣经研究者
罗素弟兄喜欢这个名称
他说我们不需要什么特别名称
叫做圣经研究者就好了
我尊重他的看法
但问题是
有人开始叫我们做
“罗素派”“卢述福派”
后来连“基督徒”这个名称也不合用
因为许多人自称基督徒
却不知道做基督徒是怎么一回事
1931年的大会就谈到这个问题
这个大会在美国俄亥俄州哥伦布举行
为期七天
大会节目表的第一页
印着两个令人费解的字母“JW”
卢述福根据以赛亚书43:10
提出一个决议
我们敬爱查尔斯·罗素弟兄
乐于承认他蒙主任用
承认他的努力蒙主大大赐福
但我们绝不想被称为“罗素派”
至于守望台圣经书社
或者万国圣经研究会
都只是法人团体的名称
我们是耶和华上帝的仆人
奉他的名去执行他交托的任务
所以，我们要告诉人
我们是“耶和华见证人”
早期出版的《锡安的守望台》显示
圣经研究者早已认识上帝的名
“耶和华见证人”这个新名称
提醒这些基督徒
他们认识上帝的名
就有责任为他作见证
从那时起
我们不再只是一群
因喜欢研究圣经而聚集起来的人
“耶和华见证人”
这个有圣经根据的新名称
让我们引以为荣

titles.cn: 一个能表明我们身份的名称

ko.text: 조지프 러셀과 앤 일라이자 러셀 부부는
그들은 다섯 명의 자녀를 두게 되었는데
찰스의 형 토머스는 다섯 살 때 사망했습니다.
찰스가 아홉 살이 되기 전에 사망했습니다.
전쟁이 사람들에게 입히는 끔찍한 피해와 고통
그리고 죽음을 직접 목격할 수 있었을 것입니다.
모두 지옥불에서 영원히 고초를 당하게 하셨다고 가르쳤습니다.
러셀은 그러한 가르침에 대한 자신의 생각을 이렇게 기술했습니다.
영원한 고초를 받을 것을 미리 예정해 놓고서
인간을 창조하는 데 자기 능력을 사용하시는 그런 하느님이라면
그 표준은 많은 인간의 표준보다도 낮은 것이다.
악한 자들이 ‘영원한 고초’를 받는다고 교회들에서 가르치는 것을 보고는
하느님이 복수의 하느님이시라는 믿음이 널리 퍼져 있었죠.
어떻게 그런 일을 하실 수 있겠습니까?
선을 베푸는 가장 좋은 방법이라고 생각했습니다.
그는 십 대 초부터 아버지와 함께
그가 믿음을 회복하는 데 도움이 된 일이 있었습니다.
나는 먼지투성이의 어떤 음침한 방에 들어가 보았다.
큰 교회의 신조보다 더 지각 있는
어떤 점이 있지나 않을까 알아보기 위해서였다.
그의 성경 해설이 아주 명확한 것은 아니었지만
그 설교는 성서가 하느님의 영감을 받은 것이라는 점에 대한
나의 흔들리는 믿음을 다시 회복시켜 주기에 충분하였다.
러셀이 당시에 무신론자였던 것은 아님을 기억해야 합니다.
그는 어디에서도 진리를 찾을 수 없다고 느꼈습니다.
자신의 닳고 닳은 성서를 책장에서 꺼내
다시 조사하려는 마음을 갖게 된 것입니다.
열심으로 불타오른 찰스 러셀과 아버지 조지프 러셀,
그 주제와 관련 있는 모든 성구를 일일이 찾아보았습니다.
당시 널리 퍼져 있던 종교적 견해와는 상충되는 중요한 결론들에 이르게 되었습니다.
대부분의 종교에서는 사람이 영혼을 가지고 있다고 가르친 데 반해,
사람이 곧 영혼이며 영혼이 죽을 수 있다고 결론 내렸습니다.
아버지와 아들과 성령이 한 인격체라고 가르치지만,
그리스도께서 육체로 돌아오시고 땅이 멸망될 것이라고 가르쳤던 반면,
순종하는 인류를 축복하기 위해 돌아오실 것임을 이해했습니다.
그러니까 그들은 탁상공론만 하면서 온갖 가정과 추측을 늘어놓은 것이 아니라
실제로 진리를 찾는 데 몰두한 것입니다.
진리를 찾을 수 있다고 믿었음을 알 수 있습니다.
우리는 여호와께서 빛을 드러내시는 때가 돼야만 빛을 볼 수 있습니다.
그런데 여호와께서 자신의 백성을 어둠에서 찬란한 빛으로 인도하실 때가

en.text: It was in 1845
that Joseph and Ann Eliza Russell emigrated
from Ireland to Pennsylvania, U.S.A.
They would have five children,
among them Charles Taze.
But times were hard.
His brother Thomas died at age five.
Before Charles turned nine,
two more of his siblings died.
Then his mother died.
It’s OK, Son.
Everything is going to be all right.
That same year —1861—
the United States became embroiled in a civil war
that would send 618,000 to their graves.
Thousands perished on battlefields
not far from where the Russells lived and worked.
They would be able to see firsthand
the havoc that war wreaks on people
—the suffering, the death.
Young Charles Russell thought often about what happens to the dead.
Most religions held that God created man immortal
and that He made a fiery hell in which to torment people forever
—except for those predestined for salvation.
Russell’s feelings about such teachings came through in what he wrote.
A God that would use his power to create human beings
whom he foreknew and predestinated should be eternally tormented,
could be neither wise, just,
nor loving.
His standard would be lower than that of many men.
He could never reconcile
the teaching of eternal torment
with the description in the Bible of a loving God.
As he examined the creeds of the great churches,
when he saw that they taught that the wicked are tormented eternally,
why, he just could not accept that!
The whole culture, the religious culture,
at that time was a matter of believing
that God was a God of vengeance.
And Russell knew that the Bible said,
as it does at 1 John 4:8:
“God is love.”
How could a God of love do this?
And so his faith wavered.
He felt that he could do the most good for people
through business and philanthropy.
As a preteen, he became his father’s partner
in a growing chain of clothing stores.
Charles Russell enlarged the business,
eventually operating a number of stores by himself.
Here’s your change. Thank you for coming.
By age 25, he possessed over three hundred thousand dollars,
the equivalent of seven million dollars today.
Yet, his search for truth continued.
something happened that would help reestablish his faith.
Seemingly by accident,
one evening, I dropped into a dusty, dingy hall
to see if the handful who met there
had anything more sensible to offer than the creeds of the great churches.
Let us take note of the words
of our Lord and Saviour, Jesus himself, to the apostles . . .
There, for the first time,
I heard something of the views of Second Adventists
from the preacher Mr. Jonas Wendell.
“And he said unto them, . . .”
Though his Scripture exposition was not entirely clear,
it was sufficient, under God,
to reestablish my wavering faith
in the divine inspiration of the Bible.
Now, remember at this point, Russell is not an atheist;
he’s just discouraged.
He doesn’t feel the truth can be found anywhere.
And that sermon by a Second Adventist
was enough to get him to take his well-worn Bible off the shelf
and to start digging again.
As we’ve already seen,
the word “Trinity” doesn’t appear anywhere in the Bible.
Fired with enthusiasm, Charles;
his father, Joseph;
and a few acquaintances in Pittsburgh and Allegheny
formed a class for Bible study.
They would take a subject.
They would get a Bible concordance.
They would look up every single scripture that had a bearing on the subject.
And then they would write down their conclusions.
And then they would say: ‘All right. This is what the Bible teaches.
We are going to believe this.’
Yes, and God’s Word is clear.
After five years of study,
the religious thinking of these men had undergone remarkable change.
Christ’s return will mean great blessings . . .
Their study of the Bible led them to major conclusions
that challenged the prevailing religious views of the day.
For example,
while most religions taught that man has a soul,
Russell and his associates concluded
that man is a soul
and that the soul can die.
And, whereas Christendom’s churches teach
that the Father, the Son, and the holy ghost are one person,
these students held that Jehovah is one God
and not part of a Trinity.
In addition, while some churches
were teaching that Christ would return in the flesh
and that the earth would be destroyed,
this small group came to understand
that Christ would return invisibly
—in the spirit—
with the purpose of blessing obedient mankind.
So it wasn’t just philosophizing,
just talking about ‘what if’ or ‘perhaps this way,’
but they were focused on actually trying to find the truth.
And, the fact that they decided to write down those conclusions
showed that they had a belief that there is some truth to be found.
We see light only when it’s Jehovah’s time to reveal light.
And so this was the beginning of Jehovah’s time
to lead his people out of darkness into the wonderful light.

cn.text: 早在1845年
约瑟夫·罗素和妻子安·伊丽莎
从爱尔兰移居美国宾夕法尼亚州
他们先后生了五个儿女
其中一个叫查尔斯·泰兹
但人生无常
他哥哥托马斯五岁就夭折
查尔斯还没到九岁
一个弟弟和一个妹妹也都夭折了
没多久连他的母亲也去世了
（孩子，别难过）
（一切都会好转过来的）
就在他母亲去世那年
美国爆发内战
最后导致61万8000人丧生
在罗素一家居住和工作的地方附近
阵亡人数成千上万
他们亲眼看见战争造成的祸害
看见很多人受苦，很多人死亡
查尔斯·罗素年轻时就常常想到
人死后会怎样
大多数教会都声称
上帝把人创造成有不死的灵魂
又说上帝造了烈火熊熊的地狱
去永远折磨人
只有上帝预定可以得救的人才能幸免
对于这种主张，罗素把自己的看法写了下来
假如上帝一方面用大能创造人
一方面又预知并预定人会永远受折磨
这样的上帝既没有智慧
也没有爱心，而且做事不公
他的标准比许多人还不如
查尔斯·罗素觉得
地狱永刑跟圣经谈到上帝是仁爱的有矛盾
他查考过一些主流教会的教条
发觉这些教会都主张恶人会永远受折磨
这样的教条他简直无法接受
当时一般教会普遍认为
上帝是个施行报应的上帝
罗素知道圣经，比如约翰一书4:8说
“上帝就是爱”
但仁爱的上帝又怎么会做这种事呢？
结果他的信心动摇了
他觉得自己最能帮助人的
就是做生意和做善事
查尔斯11岁就跟父亲一起经营服装店
商店开了很多家
查尔斯扩充业务
最后有好几家商店都由他自己经营
罗素25岁就拥有家财30多万美元
相当于今天700万美元
但他继续寻找真理
有一件事令他恢复对圣经的信心
一天晚上
我凑巧经过一所昏暗肮脏的礼堂
那里聚集的人不多
我走了进去
要看看那里的人所说的
是不是比主流教会的教条合理
在那里我第一次听见基督复临会的主张
当时发表讲话的是乔纳斯·温德尔
虽然温德尔在解释圣经方面并不十分清晰
但在上帝的指引下
他的话已足以帮助我
再次相信圣经是上帝启示的
我们要记得
当时罗素并不是无神论者
他不过是感到灰心而已
他觉得哪里也找不到真理
但听过那个基督复临会的人演讲后
他决心把书架上那本旧圣经取下来
再次钻研
（三位一体这个词从没有在圣经里出现过）
由于热心钻研圣经
查尔斯和他父亲约瑟夫
连同匹兹堡和阿勒格尼的几个朋友
成立了一个圣经研究班
他们会提出一个课题
然后看看圣经词语索引
查考每一节跟课题有关的经文
再把结论写下来
之后会说
好，圣经是这样说的
我们应该相信
（对，圣经说得很清楚）
经过五年的仔细研究后
他们对圣经的理解有了重大的改变
他们从钻研圣经所得的重大发现
跟当时流行的宗教主张截然不同
例如，大多数宗教都说人有不死的灵魂
但罗素和同伴却认为人死后
身体没有任何部分继续生存
此外，一般教会说圣父、圣子和圣灵
是同一位个体
但这群研究圣经的人却说
耶和华是一位上帝
而不是三位一体神中的一位
还有，有些教会主张
基督复临时是个血肉之躯
而到时地球会被毁灭
但这小群研究圣经的人明白
基督复临时是灵体，是隐形的
而他复临是要造福顺服上帝的人
他们并不是做什么哲学研究
一味假设和猜测
而是集中探求真理
切实地找出真相
他们决定把得出的结论写下
可见他们相信真理是可以找到的
只有耶和华认为是时候显露光
我们才会看见光
因此，当时就是耶和华开始带领子民
脱离黑暗、进入奇妙之光的时候

ko.text: 남편이 혼자 가는 게 걱정됐기 때문에

그래서 제가 요한손 형제와 함께 방문을 하게 됐죠.
군인들은 요한손 형제한테 내리라고 한 다음
“너는 가도 되는데, 이 백인은 쏴 죽일 거야.”
“친구를 위해 자기 생명을 내놓는 것보다 더 큰 사랑은 없다”는 말씀을 떠올렸고,
“이 사람이 무슨 잘못을 했다고 이러는 거예요?
그때 기도가 정말 큰 힘을 발휘했습니다.
요한손 형제를 죽이려던 군인들의 태도가 완전히 바뀌었거든요.
그대로 액셀을 밟고 달린 덕분에 살았습니다.
자신의 백성을 구해 주신다는 걸 느낄 수 있었어요.
여호와께서는 틀림없이 자신의 백성을 구출해 주실 겁니다.
