en.text: The persecution spread throughout Malawi
soon after the announcement was made
that the Witnesses were banned in the country.
Their houses were burned,
and their maize crops were confiscated
because they refused to participate in the country’s politics.
The regular visits that Brother Johansson
was doing as a branch representative at that time
really encouraged the brothers from various parts of the country
who were affected by the persecution.
His wife, Linda,
suggested that he should ask someone to accompany him
so that he did not have to do the work alone.
And she suggested that I accompany him.
This was because of the fear of what might happen.
When we got to the ferry crossing,
the soldiers told Brother Johansson to get out and stand in front of the jeep.
They said to me, “You can pass,
but we first have to shoot the white man.”
Because the Scriptures say:
“No one has greater love than this,
that someone should surrender his life in behalf of his friends,”
I said:
“Shoot me instead!
What did this man do?”
Yes, it happened without me giving it a second thought.
It just happened spontaneously.
I stood between him and the soldiers.
Prayer helped very much
because the people that we thought were going to harm us
had a complete change of heart.
On the way back, Brother Johansson also saved my life.
We were stopped by a youth mob at a roadblock.
They asked for the political cards.
They would have killed me.
So Brother Johansson just sped off with his vehicle.
Yes, it was very exciting to see
that Jehovah God has many ways of saving his people.
Elisha said:
“For there are more who are with us
than those who are with them.”
In the end, Jehovah will rescue his people.
So in countries where our brothers are banned,
I encourage them to stand firm,
trusting in God —the God who never fails, Jehovah.

cn.text: 马拉维政府宣布
针对耶和华见证人的禁令后不久
遍及全国的迫害就开始了
弟兄姐妹因为拒绝参与政治事务
他们的房屋被烧毁
玉米地被充公
那段时间
杰克·约翰松弟兄
经常以分部代表的身份探访弟兄们
这鼓励了马拉维各地受迫害的弟兄姐妹
他的妻子琳达
希望有人可以陪杰克一起去探访
她推荐我陪她丈夫去
因为她担心会有危险
我们到渡口时
士兵命令杰克下车
让他站在吉普车前
他们对我说
你可以过去
但我们要先枪毙了这个白人
圣经说
“人为朋友捐弃生命”
“人的爱心没有比这更大的了”
于是我说
要杀就杀我吧!
这个人有什么错!
当时我根本来不及多想
就挡在了杰克的前面
我想也没想就这么做了
祷告起了很大作用
我们以为那些士兵会害我们
但没想到他们的态度完全转变了
回去的时候  杰克也救了我一命
有一群青年暴徒拦住我们的车
要我出示党员证
要是他们知道我不是党员
肯定会杀了我
杰克直接踩油门把他们甩在后面
看到耶和华通过各种方法拯救他的子民
真令人振奋
以利沙说
“与我们同在的比与他们同在的还多”
耶和华一定会拯救他的子民
我想鼓励受禁止国家的弟兄姐妹
要站稳
信赖我们的上帝耶和华
他绝不会失败

ko.text: 지부 구역에서의 확장에 따라 이루어지긴 하지만,
우리 조직은 피해 지역의 형제 자매들을 돕기 위해
여기에는 구호 물자를 전달하는 일이 포함됩니다.
형제들이 집과 왕국회관을 수리하거나 새로 짓는 일을 돕기도 합니다.
재해 구호 데스크가 복구 활동을 조직합니다.
비좁은 공간이나 왕국회관에서 함께 일해 본 경험이 많기 때문이죠.
“돈을 드릴 테니 우리 집 차고도 고쳐 주시겠어요?” 하고 물었죠.
원래 있던 곳에서 떨어져 나가 있었어요.
직접 보니 심하게 파손된 건 아니었죠.
“돈은 안 주셔도 되요. 다 여호와의 증인 자원봉사자들이거든요”
여기서 뭘 하시는 거죠?” 하고 물었죠.
안정을 찾게 도와주고 있어요” 하고 대답했죠.
잠시 후에 돈을 들고 다시 왔죠.
“그런데 여러분은 우리 집에 와서 돈도 안 받고 이렇게 도와주셨어요.
꼭 이 돈을 여러분의 헌금함에 넣어 주시기 바랍니다.”
재해 구호 활동에 직접 참여해 본 사람은
우리 조직에서 볼 수 있는 이러한 사랑은
정말 믿음을 강하게 해 주지 않습니까!

en.text: Although many of our construction projects
are the result of growth in a branch territory,
our donations also are put to good use
when disasters strike.
The organization is quick to respond
to the needs of our brothers and sisters in affected areas.
This includes the distribution of relief supplies.
It also involves helping our brothers
repair or rebuild their homes and Kingdom Halls.
This was the case in 2011
when a large tornado
ripped through the state of Missouri
in the United States.
When a disaster strikes,
the Disaster Relief Desk takes the lead in caring for the needs of the field.
This is done by using volunteers.
Our brothers know how to work together.
We’re using volunteers that are
used to crawling over each other
and working in a Kingdom Hall.
So they have the ability
to get into a disaster situation
and take direction and just take care of it.
It’s an evaluation process to see what’s needed.
The Purchasing Department
locally will then go ahead
and start buying materials,
those will be delivered,
and volunteers will come to get the home back to livable conditions
so that our brothers and sisters can get back into their homes.
So if we stabilize the friends and we stabilize the houses,
we can stabilize the congregation.
We had a group of brothers that went into Joplin, Missouri,
after the tornado destroyed 30 percent of the city.
We had probably 30 to 40 volunteers working on the house,
and a woman came down the street from the neighborhood.
She sees all the volunteers working; she thinks it’s a construction organization;
she says, “Can I pay you to come over and fix my garage?”
It was basically a shed
that had been picked up off the slab, turned upside down,
and moved a few feet away from the slab.
So the brothers said, “Well, let’s go take a look at it.”
So they went over and took a look at it.
It wasn’t that hard.
The shed was still intact.
They said, “We could do this in a few minutes.”
So they went and got all of their volunteers.
They went over there; they picked the shed up;
they got about 30 brothers on it,
and they turned it over and put it on the slab.
And the woman was so thankful.
She said, “OK, so, what do I owe you?”
They said, “No, we’re all volunteers; we’re Jehovah’s Witnesses.
“We’re working through the local Kingdom Hall here
—relief center.”
And she said, “You’re kidding me.
You’re all volunteers?”
He said, “Yeah, and we’re out . . . ,”
and she said, “What are you doing here?”
And he said, “We’re out working on our brothers’ and sisters’ homes
and trying to help them get stabilized.”
She was in tears.
She came back down the street a few minutes later
with a wad of money in her hand.
She said, “I want to tell you a story.”
She said: “I called my church after this happened,
“and I asked them to come work —to do this work for me,
“to put this shed back on its slab.
“They said: ‘We can do that.
We’ll be there in about three weeks, and it’s going to cost you this much.’”
She said, “And here you folks come over to my house,
“you don’t charge me, you don’t even know who I am,
and you put my home back together —what I needed to have done.”
She said, “Here’s the money; you have this;
you put it in your contribution box.”
When someone helps in building a Kingdom Hall,
when someone helps in building an Assembly Hall,
when someone aids in caring for a natural disaster,
their lives are changed forever.
When someone is benefited by one of these programs,
their lives are changed forever.
The love demonstrated in the organization
is truly faith-strengthening to see!
The same arrangement to respond to disasters
is in place all around the world.

cn.text: 由于传道工作的扩展
我们的捐款用在了许多建筑工程上
但当灾难发生的时候
我们的捐款还用在救灾工作上
上帝的组织很快就采取行动
帮助那些受灾的弟兄姐妹
这包括向弟兄姐妹分发救援物资
也包括修复或重建王国聚会所
还有弟兄姐妹的家
2011年，我们有一项救灾工作
当时一场强烈的龙卷风
吹袭了美国的密苏里州
造成了严重的破坏
每当有天灾发生
救灾事务处就会统筹救灾工作
他们会请很多志愿人员帮忙
弟兄们都知道怎样互相合作
不少志愿人员都有建筑聚会所的经验
习惯在狭窄的空间一起工作
所以能马上适应灾区的情况
按照指示完成任务
我们会先评估灾区需要哪些物资
然后采购部就会开始购买这些需要的东西
当物资送到灾区之后
志愿人员也会赶到现场
帮助弟兄姐妹修复他们的房子
好让他们可以尽快回家去住
我们让大家的心情稳定
有安稳的住处
就会使会众更稳固
我们有一群志愿人员
他们到了密苏里州的乔普林市
那里大概有30%的建筑物被龙卷风摧毁
有一次
有三四十个志愿人员在整修一所房子
一个住在附近的女士
以为他们是建筑公司的人，就说:
我可以付钱请你们来修我的车棚吗？
她的棚子整个被大风吹翻了
倒在一旁
弟兄们就跟她说:
我们先过去看看
到了那里，他们发现情况不难处理
车棚还很完整，就说:
几分钟就能搞定
后来有30个弟兄
合力把车棚翻过来放回原处
这位女士很感激，想要付我们钱
弟兄拒绝了，说:
我们是义工，是耶和华见证人
从附近的王国聚会所来的
这位女士很惊讶地说:
不会吧？你们都是义工？
你们来这里做什么？
弟兄说:我们来整修弟兄姐妹的房子

en.text: Who are Jehovah’s Witnesses?
We come from hundreds of ethnic and language backgrounds,
yet we share common beliefs and goals.
We worship Jehovah,
the God of the Bible and the Creator of all things.
We are Christians,
so we follow the teachings and example of Christ Jesus.
Like Jesus, we strive to be honest, peaceful, law-abiding citizens
of the land where we live.
Even more important,
we all follow Jesus’ example
by regularly spending time
helping people learn about the Bible and God’s Kingdom.
Because we witness, or talk, about Jehovah God and his Kingdom,
we are known as Jehovah’s Witnesses.
Each week, we meet together at Kingdom Halls
to learn about God and his Word, the Bible.
Our meetings are free and open to the public.
We welcome you to visit us.

en.text: All who truly followed Jesus reflected the light he radiated.
But Jesus foretold that after the death of his apostles,
there would be a falling away from pure worship.
That apostasy would be so extensive
that genuine disciples would practically disappear
until “the conclusion
of the system of things.”
At the same time,
a counterfeit form of Christianity would flourish.
And so it happened.
So-called Christian churches deviated from Christ’s teachings.
The result was the abuse of power
and untold suffering.
This was a period of deep darkness.
In the centuries after the establishment of the Christian congregation,
we see how many of those who were taking
the lead in the Christian church
(or, the Christian congregation)
likewise started to love worldly wisdom.
These ideas that came from Plato
and other Greek philosophers
started to infiltrate the so-called Christian thinking.
And so the apostates wished to blend
Christian teaching and Christian tradition
with pagan religious ideas.
The idea was to make these things
more acceptable to other pagans
so that pagans could be drawn into the Christian religion.
As the centuries passed,
apostate religious leaders obscured the light even further
by keeping the Bible in Latin,
a language no longer understood by most people.
Yet, at certain points during this darkness,
there were still individuals who felt keenly
the need to read and understand God’s Word.
For example, in the 1100’s,
a French merchant known as Vaudès
commissioned a translation of Bible books
into the language of the common people.
Two centuries later,
Catholic priest John Wycliffe wrote powerfully
against unbiblical practices of the church.
By 1382, Wycliffe’s team
released the first translation of the Bible into English.
His students, known as Lollards,
preached the Bible’s message to anyone who would listen.
By 1495, the invention of movable type
made it possible to print all or part of the Bible in 12 languages.
“Our Father which art in heaven, . . .”
Soon, people were reading it for themselves.
And some who did began to discern
that the church had gone off course.
In the 1500’s, such men as Huldrych Zwingli,
Martin Luther,
and John Calvin
preached the need to return to the original principles of Christianity.
These men and others tried to expose hypocritical practices
and uphold Bible teachings
even though this put them at odds
with powerful religious authorities.
You can see ones that were willing to stand out as being different
even though they didn’t have a full knowledge of the truth.
But standing out led to persecution,
and persecution often led to compromise,
especially when it came to preaching.
Nevertheless, in many lands,
the 16 and 1700’s were marked
by a strong upsurge in Bible study.
In England,
many learned men refuted the Trinity doctrine as unscriptural.
Among them, scientist Sir Isaac Newton,
poet John Milton,
and chemist Joseph Priestley.
Besides rejecting the Trinity doctrine,
Priestley declared that the teaching
of the inherent immortality of the soul was false.
He held that the first-century Christians had the true faith
and that any change to that pattern of belief was a corruption.

茨温利

加尔文

en.text: I love my family very much.
Even though we don’t have a lot, we’re glad we have each other.
Mom works really hard to provide for us.
It’s just the four of us.
We’ve all been feeling just a little sad lately.
I can tell she’s really tired and worries a lot.
I try to help out.
Sometimes I help to get everyone ready for the meeting.
We seem to manage all right.
But things are really hard.
At our next family worship,
Mom read to us 2 Corinthians 8:1-4.
That story is about the Macedonians.
Mom had us close our eyes so we could imagine the scene.
Even though the Macedonians were very poor,
they found happiness by giving what they could to others.
They even begged
the apostles for the opportunity to give.
Then we read Acts 20:35,
where it says:
“There is more happiness
in giving than there is in receiving.”
My sister said,
“But we don’t have anything to give.”
Mom said: “But we do.
We have ourselves.”
It got us all thinking.
Mom had a great idea.
We spent the rest of our family worship
making special gifts for the friends in our congregation.
It was pretty amazing!
Even though we don’t have a lot materially,
there is still so much we can give,
like putting a little in the contribution box
each week and helping to clean.
And, of course, sharing in the ministry
is the very best way we can give to others.
Now we are even closer as a family.
And we have learned that there truly
“is more happiness in giving.”

en.text: Pardon me, good women.
I heard that Jesus the Nazarene is somewhere in the area.
Have you seen him?
Why are you seeking him out?
Are you one of his disciples?
Are you one of his servants?
My dear woman, from what I hear,
the size of the crowds will not allow you to come near Jesus.
Do not even dream of meeting him!
Sisters, sisters!
Where is your love of strangers?
Please, excuse their rudeness.
How can we be of assistance?
Come, sit here with us.
Thank you.
I have an urgent need to meet the Lord Jesus.
Well, I’m not sure he’s any kind of “lord,”
but I can tell you I’ve heard no reports about Jesus being around here.
Are you related to him?
No.
But I heard that he’s curing the sick,
and I am a very sick woman.
I’ve suffered from a flow of blood for some 12 years.
I’ve been unable
to get a cure from anyone.
And I have suffered so much
at the hands of many physicians.
All of my money has been spent on this dreadful condition.
And after all these efforts, am I better?
No!
I have become worse!
When I heard about Jesus
and the miracles that he has performed,
I knew he must be from God.
I have faith in his power.
He can heal me.
Even if I could touch
just the fringes of his outer garment,
I will get well.
Otherwise,
I will surely die.
Teacher!
Teacher, again I plead with you!
My little daughter is extremely ill.
Please, come and put your hands on her so that she may get well and live.
Please! Come to my house.
Jesus, this is Jairus,
one of the presiding officers of the synagogue.
He has been begging for your help.
Jairus, where is your daughter?
Please, take me to her.
She is a beautiful girl.
She is my only daughter.
She is only 12 years old, and she is dying.
Please! Come quickly!
I will come.
Please lead the way.
Who touched my outer garments?
Who touched me?
Not me, my Lord!
Peter, James, did one of you touch me?
No, my Lord.
Jesus, surely you can see the crowds pressing in on you.
And you ask, “Who touched me?”
Someone touched me, for I know that power went out of me.
Woman, did you touch the Lord?
Please, please forgive me, my Lord.
It was I who touched you.
I merely touched the fringes of his outer garments.
Have no fear.
You’ve done nothing wrong.
Tell me, why did you touch my garment?
My Lord,
I have been very ill for 12 years!
Many physicians have treated me.
I have spent all that I had trying
to find a cure, but my condition got no better.
Rather, I got worse!
I’ve heard about you.
I have faith in you.
I knew that if I could just touch
the fringes of your outer garment,
I could get well.
Forgive me! I just wanted to get well.
Take courage, daughter!
Your faith has made you well.
Go in peace, and be healed from your grievous sickness.

예루살렘을 재건하라는 명령이 있은 지 483년 후에
12장에선 그분의 몸이 찔릴 것이라고 알려 줍니다.
또한 메시아가 우리의 죄를 위해 희생적인 죽음을 겪고
부자의 무덤에 매장될 것이라는 예언도 있습니다.
예수께서 자신의 생애 중의 사건들이 그 모든 예언에 들어맞도록
그리고 다윗이 출생한 베들레헴에서 태어나게 할 수 있었을까요?
성경에 제가 거기서 태어난다고 나와요’라고 하실 수 있었을까요?
분명 예수는 자신의 출생과 관련된 일을 제어할 수 없었습니다.
또한 그분은 제사장들이 유다에게 은 30닢을 주어
유다가 그분을 배반하게 해 놓으실 수 있었을까요?
적들이 그분의 얼굴에 침을 뱉도록 해 놓으실 수 있었을까요?
로마 당국이 그분을 형주에 못 박으라고 선고한 것은 어떻습니까?
군인들이 그분의 옷을 놓고 제비를 뽑은 것은요?
뼈를 꺾는 관습을 따르지 않은 것은 또 어떻습니까?
그럼 이 모든 예언이 그저 우연히 이루어질 수 있었을까요?

en.text: Let’s consider some
outstanding prophecies about Jesus
and their fulfillment.
One was that he would be born
of the tribe of Judah from the family of David the son of Jesse.
More than 700 years before Jesus was born,
Micah foretold in chapter 5
that he would be born in Bethlehem.
The prophecy speaks of “Bethlehem Ephrathah.”
Why is the designation “Ephrathah” important?
Because there existed another Bethlehem
in the territory of Zebulun.
It has been identified with Beit Lahm
about 7 miles, or 11 kilometers,
west-northwest of Nazareth.
Again, the prophecy was extremely specific.
And amazingly,
Isaiah prophesied he would be born of a virgin.
What human would ever think of such a thing?
Daniel chapter 9 foretold that the Messiah would arrive
483 years after the command to rebuild Jerusalem.
This proved to be true in the year 29 of our Common Era
when Jesus was baptized.
Zechariah chapter 11 foretold that the Messiah
would be betrayed for “30 pieces of silver.”
Chapter 12 says that his body would be pierced.
It was foretold that the Messiah would die a sacrificial death
for our sins and be buried in the tomb of a rich man.
Furthermore, prophecy proclaimed that he
would be in the grave for parts of three days
and then be resurrected.
What about the argument that Jesus deliberately arranged matters
so that the events in his life would fit all these prophecies?
What do you think?
Could Jesus have arranged to be born of the tribe of Judah
in the town of David’s birth in Bethlehem?
His mother, Mary, lived in Nazareth.
Could he tell her while in the womb,
‘Please take me to Bethlehem because the Scriptures say
I must be born there’?
Obviously, the very start of his life on earth
was beyond his control.
Furthermore, could Jesus have arranged for the priests
to pay Judas the 30 pieces of silver to betray him?
Could he have arranged that his enemies spit in his face?
that the Roman authorities sentence him to be nailed to a stake?
that the soldiers cast lots for his garments?
or that while piercing his side with a spear,
they not follow the custom of breaking any of his bones?
Could the prophecies just mentioned have been fulfilled by mere chance?

cn.text: 我们来看看跟耶稣有关的重大预言是如何应验的
其中一个提到耶稣会出于犹大部族
成为耶西的儿子大卫的后代
另外，在耶稣出生前700多年
弥迦书第5章就预告他会在伯利恒诞生
预言说“伯利恒，以法他”
为什么要特别提到“以法他”呢？
因为在西布伦部族境内
还有另一个城也叫做“伯利恒”
位于拿撒勒西北方约11公里的地方
的确，我们再次看出圣经预言是多么精确
让人惊讶的是
以赛亚也曾预告耶稣会由一个处女所生
一般人怎么可能会想到这样的事呢？
但以理书第9章预言
在修复耶路撒冷的谕旨颁布483年后
弥赛亚就会出现
后来，耶稣在公元29年受浸
这个预言就准确地应验了！
撒迦利亚书第11章预告
弥赛亚会因“三十块银子”被出卖
第12章提到他的身体会被“刺”
弥赛亚将会为人类的罪而牺牲生命
也会被埋葬在一个富翁所买的墓穴里
此外，其他预言也提到
他被葬在墓穴后三天
就会被复活
有些人说发生在耶稣身上的事情
都是他事先安排好的
好让自己可以符合圣经预言
你觉得呢？
耶稣能够安排自己生在犹大部族
也跟大卫一样生在伯利恒吗？
耶稣的母亲马利亚原本住在拿撒勒
难道耶稣能够在妈妈的肚子里跟妈妈说
“你要去伯利恒生我
我才能应验圣经预言”吗？
毫无疑问
耶稣根本不能控制他自己在哪里出生
要怎么出生
另外，耶稣有办法控制祭司们
要付30块银子给犹大
让犹大来出卖他吗？
他能控制仇敌吐口水在他脸上吗？
他能叫罗马总督将他钉在柱上吗？
他能控制罗马士兵
以抽签的方式平分他的外衣吗？
还有，耶稣有办法告诉士兵
只可以刺他的肋旁
而不照惯例把他的骨头打断吗？
这些预言全都应验了
难道只是巧合吗？

titles.cn: 耶稣应验了预言

en.text: At a tender age, I had a troubled mind
as to how I would be pleasing to God
and also at the same time be pleasing in the eyes of the voodoo.
Two of my siblings died before I was born,
so my mother was seeking protection
all through her pregnancy with me.
My mother was made
to believe that when she goes
to the voodoo shrine regularly,
she will be protected from the witches.
This meant she had to walk about four miles (6 km)
to the shrine regularly, barefoot.
After my birth,
I was sent to the voodoo shrine to be protected
from the attack of the witches.
I was kept there.
I got baptized into the Catholic Church.
There we were taught
that those who worship idols, the voodoos,
would be burned in an everlasting hellfire.
I was terrified.
One day, I asked my father,
“Won’t the priest be angry if he knows that we,
“after going in for the communion,
still go into the shrine?”
My father came back with the news
that the priest said I could still go ahead
being an idol worshipper
and at the same time being a Catholic.
I became disturbed.
I became confused.
I came across Jehovah’s Witnesses
when I was of age and left the village.
I bombarded them with questions.
So I demanded a book.
I read the book
before daybreak.
So that night,
in my heart I broke away from the voodoo worship
and also from the Catholic religion.
I was afraid to confront my father over the issue.
In our culture, it’s not easy for a young man
to take such a crucial decision.
Before I could be aware,
there was the news in the village that now
Donkor has joined a new religion.
So any time I’d go home,
relatives would knock on my door —at dawn—
to advise me to rescind my decision.
My worry was how to inform my father.
And one day,
my father invited me
and then inquired of me
what was really happening.
And it became a very strong confrontation.
I told him: “I’ll worship Jehovah.
Jehovah is the only God I’ll worship.”
So he flared up,
left me, and then went into his room.
So I also entered my room and started singing:
“Once with confusion our sad hearts were filled,
drinking the cup false religion distilled.”
I was singing so vigorously —as is somebody who has been liberated.
Because initially I was in prison,
but now I am a freedman.
So since then, I’ve been serving Jehovah.
The fear of man has been overcome.
I am no longer a captive
of the fear of death or even the dead.
I no longer engage myself
in any practices that are contrary to Bible standards.
I feel liberated.
It makes me happy when I see my children
also serving the only true God, Jehovah.
Now I live a very happy family life.

cn.text: 从小我就一直在想
我怎样做可以同时让上帝喜悦
又让巫毒的神灵喜悦
我的两个哥哥姐姐
在我出生前就过世了
所以我母亲在怀着我的期间
到处寻求庇佑
我的母亲相信
如果她常常到巫毒庙
她就会得到保护
而不会受到女巫骚扰
这意味着她要经常
赤脚走上大约四英里的路
去巫毒庙
我出生后
被送到了巫毒庙
以免受女巫攻击
我被留在那里
我受洗加入天主教会
我们被教导
崇拜偶像和巫毒教的人
都将永远在地狱里被火焚烧
我非常害怕
有一天我问父亲
如果神父知道我们用过圣餐后
仍然去巫毒庙
难道他不会生气吗？
我父亲回来告诉我
神父说
我还是可以一边继续崇拜偶像
一边做一个天主教徒
我感到不安
我感到困惑
当我遇到耶和华见证人时
我已成年，也离开村子了
我问了他们一大堆问题
所以我要了一本书
我读那本书直到天亮
那天晚上，在我的心里
我脱离了巫毒教
也脱离了天主教
我不敢向父亲表明这件事
在我们的文化
年轻男子要做这样的决定是很艰难的
不知不觉中
村庄就传来消息说
唐科加入了一个新宗教
每当我回到家
天刚亮时
亲戚们就会来敲我的门
劝我放弃这个决定
我担心的是如何向父亲开口
有一天
我父亲邀我谈谈
然后问我
到底发生了什么事
结果变成很严重的冲突
我告诉他
我只崇拜耶和华
耶和华是我唯一崇拜的神
于是他非常生气
然后离开我，走进他的房间
而我也走进房间，开始唱诗歌
错误主张蒙蔽人的思想
使人困惑惆怅
失去方向
我很大声地唱着
就像一个被释放的人
因为我仿佛曾在牢里
现在却获得自由
从那时起
我一直事奉耶和华
我克服了惧怕人的心理
我不再恐惧死亡
或死去的人
我不再从事任何违反圣经标准的行为
我觉得自己自由了
我很高兴
看到我的孩子
也事奉唯一的真神耶和华
现在我有很幸福的家庭生活

titles.cn: 真理叫我自由

en.text: My name is Steing Dott.
I was born in 1988 in Darwin, Northern Territory.
When I was eight years old,
I realized that life was getting very difficult for me.
I was diagnosed with ADHD,
obsessive-compulsive disorder, and Tourette syndrome.
And on top of all of that, I was diagnosed with severe anxiety as well.
My mum said this affected the entire family
because I would repeatedly yell out “Good night!”
to each individual person in the family.
And on top of that, I used to constantly go around
the house, checking the locks and the windows.
My school life was the hardest thing I’ve ever had to deal with.
My school was approximately 500 meters (1,600 ft) from my home.
It would take me at least two hours to get to school
because one of my obsessions was that if there were cracks on the footpath
and if I stepped on one,
I’d have to go all the way back home and start again.
Well, I found life to be a constant struggle,
and as I got older, it only got worse.
Even at ten years old,
I decided that I wanted to end my life
so that it would make everyone in the family’s life a lot easier.
But then we decided to use some medication,
which eased my problems a little bit.
Despite having medication,
life was still completely unbearable for me.
I had a constant struggle every day within myself.
I used to wash my hands hundreds of times a day.
I couldn’t leave the home;
I couldn’t get a driver’s license; I couldn’t even get a job.
A major turning point in my life
was my mum’s unwavering faith in Jehovah.
She used to iron my clothes for the meeting
and hang them on the doorknob,
even though I wasn’t ready to attend the meeting.
But what she didn’t know was that when
my mum went to the meeting with my sister,
I’d get a Bible and I’d try and start to read it.
I also began to pray to Jehovah.
And then one day, I thought, ‘I’m going to give this a shot.’
So I put my suit on, I got ready, and I went to the meeting.
When I went to the Kingdom Hall, I was absolutely terrified.
I was so nervous.
But when I got there, I saw
an elder who used to come and visit me,
and he made me feel very relaxed.
And then the amazing welcome by the brothers and sisters
—it made me feel like I was part of Jehovah’s organization again.
The scripture that really helped me
was 1 Peter 5:7 because it says,
“while you throw all your anxiety on him,
because he cares for you.”
So this made me feel like I had a very powerful Friend,
and Jehovah wanted me to throw my anxieties on him because he loved me.

cn.text: 我叫施泰因·多特
我在澳大利亚北部地区的达尔文市出生
8岁的时候

强迫症和抽动症

这让我的病情稍微缓解了一点
尽管这样
生活对我来说还是非常不容易
每天我的内心都在不停地交战
我一天要洗好几百次手
我出不了门，拿不到驾照
也找不到工作
妈妈对上帝有坚强的信心

彼得前书5:7的经文

经文说

就是耶和华

因为他很爱我

en.text: Jehovah’s Witnesses were proclaiming that the solution to the world’s problems
rests with God’s government.
On the other hand,
the churches repeatedly voiced support for human governments.
Jehovah’s Witnesses felt a responsibility to make people aware
of the position being taken by their religious leaders.
In 1938, more than 10,000 people
jammed into London’s Royal Albert Hall
to hear a pointed lecture by Joseph Rutherford,
while millions more heard this stinging message by radio.
Always outspoken,
Rutherford invited his listeners
to “Face the Facts.”
The dictator of the totalitarian rule of Germany
has entered into an alliance with the pope.
The indisputable facts are that the Roman Catholic hierarchy
has stooped wholly to political methods
to gain control of the world.
Rutherford pointed to the church’s role in the rise
of Adolph Hitler, its alliances with Fascist regimes,
and its push in many nations to make Catholicism
the state religion.
When World War II erupted in 1939,
nearly every organized religion
sent its members into the battle.
French and American Catholics
killed German and Italian Catholics;
British and American Protestants
killed German Protestants.
Jehovah’s Witnesses wanted to make it
clear that they were no part of this controversy.
The Watchtower of November 1, 1939, reasoned,
“How could a person who is devoted to God’s Kingdom
“favor one side or the other
in a conflict between factions of the world?”

cn.text: 耶和华见证人说

向来敢言的卢述福促请听众“面对事实”

事实证明
罗马天主教廷对政客百般逢迎
想借此统管天下
卢述福指出
天主教会协助希特勒上台
又跟法西斯政权结盟
并极力促使许多国家以天主教为国教
1939年，第二次世界大战爆发
几乎所有教会都叫信徒参军
法国、美国的天主教徒

ko.text: 길은 달라도 같은 목적지로 갈 수 있듯이,
하느님이 축복해 주실 거라고 여기는 것입니다.
한 길은 널찍하고 많은 사람이 다닙니다.
다른 길은 비좁고 찾아내는 사람이 적습니다.
올바른 숭배는 그 비좁은 길과도 같습니다.
하느님의 축복을 받을 수 있는 길을 알려 줍니다.
사람이 죽어도 영혼은 어딘가에서 영원히 산다고 가르칩니다.
의로운 자들은 땅에서 영원히 살 것입니다.
우리의 숭배는 아무 의미가 없게 될 것입니다.
단 하나의 종교만이 하느님을 기쁘게 해 드린다고 말합니다.

en.text: Many people believe that it doesn’t matter which religion you choose,
that religions are like different roads that lead
to the same destination
—lasting blessings from God.
But can that be true?
Does God accept all forms of worship?
The Bible itself describes worship as two roads:
One is spacious with many people on it.
The other is cramped
with only a few finding it.
Only the cramped road represents
acceptable worship, leading to life
and blessings from God.
How can we tell if we are on the correct path?
Imagine that you’re lost.
You stop someone to ask for directions.
One person says to head east;
another says to go west.
Finally, someone with a map shows you
that the destination is actually north.
Which one would you believe?
The Bible is like that map,
leading us to blessings from God.
So why are there so many conflicting beliefs?
For example,
many religions teach that the human soul
lives eternally in a spiritual realm,
while others believe that they are reborn in another body or form.
This is just one example of the many
religious beliefs in conflict with one another.
Could all religions really be teaching the truth?
According to the map,
the dead know nothing at all.
In due time, God will restore them to life
and righteous ones will live forever on earth.
If the Bible is clear on this teaching,
what about other matters, such as our personal conduct?
We may belong to a religion,
but if our conduct offends God, our worship may be futile.
The Bible teaches that many people today
would be “without self-control,
fierce, without love of goodness.”
However, it also says
that true worshippers of God
would be peaceable,
controlling their speech
and actions.
Rather than saying
there are many religions that please God,
the Bible says there is only one faith.
True worship leads a person
to a good relationship with God
and everlasting life.

cn.text: 很多人觉得信什么宗教都可以
所有宗教都劝人向善
最终是殊途同归
让人得到神明保佑

所有宗教都是真神认可的吗？
圣经把宗教比喻为两条路
一条是宽阔的，走的人多
另一条是狭窄的，找到的人少
而狭窄的路才代表上帝认可的宗教
可以让人得到真正的生命
以及上帝赐的种种福分
我们怎么知道自己走对了路呢？
假设你迷路了
你向不同的人问路
有人说该往东走
有人说该往西走
最后，有个人拿地图给你看
告诉你目的地其实在北边
你会相信谁呢？
圣经就像那张地图
告诉我们该怎么做才能得到上帝赐福
既然如此
为什么会有那么多互相矛盾的宗教道理呢？
举个例
有些宗教说
人死后灵魂会在某个灵界永远存在
另一些宗教则说
人死后会转世投胎
变成另一个人或其他生物
这只是一个例子而已
很多宗教相信的道理都互相矛盾
想想看
所有宗教
真的有可能都是在教人真理吗？
根据圣经这张地图
死人什么都不知道
时候一到
上帝就会使死去的人复活
让正义的人永远生活在地球上
圣经把人死后的情况解释得很清楚
那么
关于人的品行一类的问题又怎样呢？
我们可能属于某个宗教
但如果我们的行为态度是真神不喜欢的
我们的崇拜就可能没有价值了
圣经说，今天很多人
“缺乏自制，凶悍，不爱良善”
但是真正崇拜上帝的人会待人友善
也会约束自己的言谈
还会有良好的行为
圣经没有说
所有宗教都是上帝认可的
而是说上帝认可的宗教只有一个
正确的宗教
帮助人跟上帝建立亲密的关系
让人得到永远的生命

ko.text: 부모님 한 분이 집을 떠나셨을까 봐 불안했죠.
제 기억으로 두 분은 항상 다투셨거든요.
우린 그런 가치관과 사고방식을 갖고 성장했고
마약에 빠져 폭력적이고 부도덕한 생활을 했어요.
우리 집은 친구들끼리 함께 모이는 아지트가 됐죠.
그때 여호와의 증인 두 자매가 벨을 눌렀습니다.
그래서 들어오라고 했는데, 한번 놀려 줄 생각이었죠.
놀랍게도, 조롱하는 투로 말해도 그 자매들은 정말 친절했어요.
전 그날 대화에 깊은 감명을 받았습니다.
하지만 그분을 다시 못 볼 거라고 생각했죠.
누가 우리 같은 사람한테 다시 오겠어요?
한 연로한 파이오니아 형제와 다시 왔는데,
그 형제는 우릴 겁내지 않고 용기 있게 전파하셨어요.
전 실제로 생활을 변화시키고 발전하기 시작했습니다.
제가 배우고 있는 걸 말해 주기 시작했죠.
우리가 얼마나 친한 사이인지를 일깨워 주려고
이제부터 더는 함께 어울릴 수 없다고 그들에게 말했습니다.
저도 그 결심을 보고 생각해 봤어요.
또 진리의 길을 가려는 프란체스코의 강한 의지와
우리 모두는 프란체스코가 전해 준 소식에
종교에 빼앗긴 거 같아서 화가 났습니다.
하지만 겉으로는 그 친구가 미쳤다고 말하면서도
속으로는 분명 뭔가 중요한 이유가 있을 거라 생각했어요.
그래서 저는 진짜 뭔가 있다는 걸 알았죠.
놀랍게도, 친구들이 한 사람 한 사람 전부
연구를 하면서, 이게 진리란 걸 깨달았어요.
전에는 늘 증오심이 동기가 되어 행동했지만,
진리는, 제가 평화와 기쁨이라는 특성을 기를 수 있게 해 줬습니다.
그 덕분에 전엔 가져 보지 못했던
제게 가장 큰 만족감을 주는 건 여호와와 누리는 관계입니다.
진리를 전해 주고 싶은 마음이 생겨요.
마리아 자매가 보여 준 참을성을 생각하면서 저도 노력하게 되죠.
여호와의 눈에 변화가 불가능한 사람은 아무도 없습니다.

en.text: Our parents loved us,
but they did it in the wrong way.
They would often turn violent, so we learned that way of life.
I remember that ever since I was young,
I was afraid of coming home one day and not finding my parents together.
Because as far back as I remember, they have always argued with each other.
So we grew up with those values and those ways of thinking
that led us to become a group that was known and feared
in the area because of our violent, immoral lifestyle
that was devoted to drugs.
We had no rules!
We were people that you should stay away from.
It was one of those regular mornings when we were home alone.
And it became our hideout —the place we would meet.
We had skipped school,
and our parents didn’t know.
I was with Federico and Raffaele when two sisters,
two of Jehovah’s Witnesses, rang the doorbell.
So we had them come in, so we could make fun of them.
And as a matter of fact, that’s what we did.
I remember that Maria and the sister that was with her
were two very sincere and genuine people.
They showed courage as they brought us the truth.
I was surprised that they were so kind, despite that my tone of voice was mocking.
And I really appreciated their kindness.
She didn’t let anything stop her, not even the way we looked.
I was really touched by the conversation with Maria,
but I thought I would never see her again.
Who would ever come back to people like us?
Maria didn’t give up.
She came back with an older pioneer brother who wasn’t scared of us
and with courage started to preach.
I really started to change my life and make progress.
Immediately, I started to speak
about what I was learning with all my friends.
What surprised me was my mother’s reaction.
She wasn’t happy at all.
She reacted really violently.
They thought that I was going mad
—that I was being brainwashed.
I remember that they would do everything to remind me
of the strong friendship that was between us.
So they would put pressure on me emotionally.
I had to make a choice.
Although I did love them and was close to them,
I made the drastic decision to tell them
that from then on I would no longer be staying in their company.
This situation made me really intrigued.
In fact, I ended up studying with Francesco.
His determination really made me think.
It was obvious that the things he was telling us
were actually real—it was the truth.
And also, the strength it took to go forward with this
—his determination to leave his friends— was surely what made
all of us seriously interested in the message he was preaching.
I would blame it on the truth because it was taking my friend away from me
—a friend with whom I used to do the things I liked.
However, inside I knew that even though I told him he had gone mad,
I knew that inside there must have been something powerful
because he was so convinced,
and we could all sense his conviction.
So I realized that there was really something there.
To my surprise, one after the other,
all of my friends started studying the Bible.
As I studied, I realized that it was the truth.
It used to be hatred that always motivated my choices.
Now I act according to love, and this makes me feel good.
I can now say that thanks to Maria
and Francesco, Jehovah tried to draw me to Him.
I believe it’s been a miracle from Jehovah.
The truth helped me cultivate the qualities
of peace and joy
—the personality that has made it possible
for me to have the family I never had.
The greatest satisfaction I have in life is to have a relationship with Jehovah.
When I see someone
like we used to be, I feel motivated to speak to them.
The patience that Maria showed motivates me to be patient.
Despite our reputation, Maria did not give up.
She showed us
that in Jehovah’s eyes, no one is beyond recovery
—no one.

这真的让我们对他的新信仰

아내가 저한테 와서 할 말이 있다고 하더군요.
얼마 동안 여호와의 증인과 성경을 공부했고,

남편에게 성서 연구를 한단 말을 꺼내게 된 건

남편은 짐을 싸 떠나 버리려고도 했죠.

법이나 소송 사건에 대해, 연구하듯이 말이에요.”

en.text: I was the youngest of a family of three.
We lived in a little bitty town in Louisiana.
It was predominately Catholic.
In the Catholic Church,
the way that we were taught to pray was a set of repetitive prayers.
Really, it was easy to pray like that because you really didn’t have to think.
Once you had those prayers memorized
(which, you know, was at a very early age), it was just rote.
Around the time that I was
just about out of college and going into law school,
there was something missing.
I wanted to be close to God, but I didn’t know how.
I met Sharon in 1986,
and we ended up getting married the following year.
Sharon and I, because she had been divorced,
were not allowed to have our marriage
be conducted in a Catholic church with a priest.
And that didn’t bother me at first, but over time, it did.
I asked them what it would take for us to be able to bless our marriage.
She would have to undergo
a period of sessions of religious training.
When he asked me that, I said, “Yeah,
I’ll study with them.”
We never, ever opened up a Bible.
It was a little disappointing.
Around that same time,
there was a zealous sister and I would study with her.
And it was all Bible.
As I continued learning about the Bible,
the reasoning from the Scriptures was so great.
It was something that I knew
I wasn’t going to be able to brush off.
So she came forward and said: “I have something to tell you.
“I have been studying with the Jehovah’s Witnesses
“for a period of time.
“I am convinced that this is the true religion.
“And I do not want to participate anymore
in the Catholic faith, the Catholic Church.”
What moved me to tell Mike about my Bible study
was Genesis 6:6.
It matters what we do
—how we can affect Jehovah and that He can feel hurt in His heart—
and it crushed me.
It crushed me
because of the love that He has for us.
I consider it to be the dark years
because there was so much animosity on my part.
He was trying to do anything he could
to get me to stop.
I even talked about divorce, thinking that, you know,
the shock and awe treatment might bring her to her senses.
He would actually pack up a suitcase and leave.
She, in fact, was becoming
a better wife and a better mother.
The sister, my teacher, she’d say,
“This is good that he is being so zealous about his faith,
because he loves God.”
Like Paul, you know, he thought that was the right thing to do.
I was trained as a lawyer.
I get a case.
I usually know nothing about it.
I do an investigation.
I retain experts to help me understand what I don’t understand.
So, naturally, I’m going to go to my church; I’m going to go—
I’m going to go to my religious leaders, my spiritual leaders,
and get them to help me with this.
I made an appointment with a very, very high-ranking priest.
I told him that my wife was studying with the Jehovah’s Witnesses,
and I was seeking some help.
And the first thing that he told me (and I’ll never forget this)—
He looked straight at me
and said it would take nothing short of a miracle
for me to pull my wife away from the Jehovah’s Witnesses
because they knew the Bible so well.
In my life at that point,
where I’m struggling and I’m trying to win over my family,
that was a devastating day.
So I said: “Michael, the Bible,
“the book from God—you don’t know.
“Why not study it?
“Why not study that like you study
the law books or the cases?”
I decided that I would go with her on Sunday,
on Sunday only, and only for the first half hour.
I’d say it was at least a year
that I went to meetings with the aim
of learning and refuting it.
You read that the earth will stay forever;
there is no Trinity; there is a name for God, the Father;
there is no hellfire; there is no purgatory.
These things were refreshing.
I was totally convinced.
By October 1996, I wrote my letter
to the same priest who thought it was going to be a miracle for me to get my wife out
and informed him that I was withdrawing from the Catholic faith.
A large part of the transition that I made
was because of the friends in the congregation.
I was not a person that you’d want to approach.
But then when I decided to make the change (and it was fast),
these people never treated me any differently.
Their arms were always open.
Jesus tells us that no one
can come to the Father unless Jehovah draws that person.
What he saw, I don’t know.
I oftentimes pray to Him,
and I don’t know what to say.
But I’m deeply appreciative
of what He’s done for me.

cn.text: 我是我们家三个孩子中最小的
我们住在路易斯安那州一个小镇
大部分人都信天主教
我们在教会学到的祷告方法
就是背诵一套祷文
这种祷告方式真的非常容易
因为你根本就不需要思考
如果一个人小时候就背过这些祷文
那么他以后只要不断重复就好了
我大学快毕业，准备攻读法律的时候
觉得人生少了点什么
我很想亲近上帝
但我不知道该怎么做
我在1986年认识了莎伦
第二年我们决定结婚
天主教会不允许我们
在教堂里请神父主持婚礼
因为莎伦离过婚
我本来没那么介意
但后来觉得心里很不舒服
我问他们
我们的婚姻怎样才能受到祝福

en.text: I’m 53 years old.
I was known as a troublemaker.
I was fighting in the bars.
It comes to a point to where you begin to enjoy it.
He was flat-out scary.
He was a very mean and violent man,
so everybody
kind of kept their distance from him.
My language was detestable.
I would make grown men blush by the things
that I would say and things that I would do.
I was involved with some bikers,
and they were trying to prospect me into getting into their club.
Things were escalating.
We got married very young, and we were 17.
And we had my oldest daughter.
I was the mom,
and he lived a life of being out
with his friends and partying.
About that time, my wife started studying the Bible with Jehovah’s Witnesses.
It was a big change for her, but she explained the reasoning behind it.
I couldn’t argue with it.
She talked me into studying.
I studied from 20 years old to 30.
I had always seen it.
I had always seen that it was good.
I knew that this was where I needed to be.
Somehow, I just could never break free of the person that I was.
My mom always raised us in the truth,
growing up, and that’s what we knew.
So, then, to see my dad, where he was
so different but yet believed it to be the truth,
and then to see that his lifestyle didn’t do him any good
was kind of a good example of a bad example, if that makes sense.
I was afraid of the change.
People accepted me for who I was,
being the tough guy,
being Jimmy Brown.
The scripture comes to mind:
“I planted, Apollos watered, but God kept making it grow.”
Many brothers have studied with Jim from time to time over the years.
I just happened to be the one
at the time in his life when he was taking the truth and running with it.
I wanted to be a better person.
I truly knew that this was just not the way of life that I wanted anymore.
He changed his friends; he changed his life; he changed his dress and grooming;
he changed his speech patterns;
he changed the way he was a grandfather;
he changed the way he was a father; he changed the way he was a husband.
Everything changed about him.
I knew the work that Witnesses do
—going out door to door talking to people.
I thought I could never do that.
Whoa! Me, going door to door?
I’m going to run into people that I know,
that I drank with for years and years.
How can I face them now?
I had always told my wife,
“It would be much easier for me to become a Witness if I didn’t live here.”
But how wrong I was because what a witness
my changes have been to so many people in town.
I love life now.
I have true friends.
I know that I have hope for the future.
Jehovah has seen something in me,
and he’s brought it to light
that I am a good person.
I can be a good human being; I can help other people;
I can be loved by Him.
It’s priceless.

en.text: The more you study,
the more you understand Jehovah.
The more you understand Jehovah, the more you love him.
Jehovah clearly tells us:
“My thoughts are not your thoughts.”
So if we want to understand Jehovah’s thinking better,
we need to dig deep in our study,
and then we share those thoughts with others.
Personal study is like fuel that keeps you going.
Personally, I’m not a good student,
but I really learned how to study the Bible.
The Bible came alive during Gilead.
Self-discipline is involved—very much.
I overcome the tiredness aspect
of Bible study by not doing it at a time of day when I know I’m going to be tired.
I can be tired for other things later on —but not for that.
Each session of my Bible study begins with a prayer,
“Please help me recognize it is counsel for me,
and then give me the strength to work on it.”
I have a color-coded system, so I know what certain things stand for.
I have a particular color
for Jehovah’s good hand in people’s lives;
I have another color for warning examples;
I have another for fine examples to imitate.
Study and meditation work together.
Study helps us to acquire information,
and meditation empowers us to put that information into practice.
You have to get behind the information,
not just focus on one verse or one chapter.
See who’s involved, the time,
the conditions, how many people are there,
and then you’ll get the true meaning of the verse.

en.text: I was born 1993 into a Mennonite family.
And from childhood on, I learned that God created us to suffer,
to work the fields, and to try to be worthy to go to heaven.
But from infancy,
I desired to do what God wanted for me.
I wanted him to be pleased with me.
That was the desire of my heart.
Years back, I started to get the feeling
that the memorized prayers
that I would recite from my German prayer book
just weren’t enough.
They were not the prayers that I felt in my heart.
I didn’t even understand them.
I wanted to tell God how I really felt,
and that’s what I did.
All of a sudden, I couldn’t resist praying
in my own language.
I told God everything;
I opened my heart to Him.
One thing I asked for was that he might help my family
so that we could do the right thing and be saved.
When I finished, I felt much calmer,
and from then on, I always prayed that way.
Later, my mother bought a Bible in our language,
and that just happened to be when Jehovah’s Witnesses started to visit us.
Jehovah heard my prayer.
They came on a regular basis, and it was so remarkable.
We were amazed at how they answered all our questions in our own language
and with our own Bible.
It impressed me very much.
Then, when I was a teenager, I finished school.
Soon afterward, I started working at a job
that was three and a half hours away from home.
At the same time, I started to go out,
like the other young people
—looking for a girlfriend and drinking.
But later, my conscience tormented me.
My family was taking their Bible study very seriously,
but I didn’t.
But suddenly, things changed.
In January 2010, our family
attended a district convention,
and that was very special for me.
It was so different from what I was used to.
The brothers came and welcomed me
and treated me so kindly.
It was just amazing!
I could hardly believe it.
And the music they had —that was what touched my heart.
I liked it so much.
That was something I never forgot in all my life.
In July 2010,
I started to regularly attend the meetings as well.
Then a brother asked me if I would like to study the Bible with him
using the book What Does the Bible Really Teach?
I then realized that I had to do more if I wanted to please God.
It would have been good to attend every meeting.
But since I worked far away, I could not.
I could only attend the meetings on Sundays.
So I decided to ask my boss
if he could give me a different job, but that didn’t work.
He didn’t want to make the change, so I waited for a little while.
I thought I would try asking again.
This time, I asked him if I could attend the meetings in a congregation
that was near my work,
but he didn’t want to let me do that either.
And there was something else.
He wanted to give me a large bonus
if I would work for him until the end of the year.
But I thought to myself: ‘If I go on working,
‘what will this show regarding my decision-making?
‘If Jehovah’s day comes, what will I show is more important to me
—Jehovah or my work?’
And so the decision was made.
After I resigned my work, I brought all my things home,
and I felt free, relieved, and ready to serve Jehovah.
One week after I quit my job,
I was approved to preach with the congregation.
And what a great pleasure
it was for me when, four months later,
I could dedicate myself to Jehovah and get baptized.
That made me so happy.

我很想参加每一个聚会

我只能参加每个星期日的聚会

我等了一段时间，决定再试一次

如果聚会所在工作的地点附近
我能不能参加

但是我问自己，假如我继续为他工作
这代表什么呢？
耶和华的日子来到时
我的决定表明，耶和华比较重要
还是工作呢？
所以我决定辞掉工作
我回到家时，我感到自在和轻松
我准备好要事奉耶和华了
辞掉工作后的一个礼拜
我符合资格与会众一起传道
而四个月后，我决心献身受浸给耶和华
这带给我很大的喜乐

ko.text: 나무 위에서 놀다가 가지가 부러지는 바람에
목 아래로 온 몸이 마비가 되어 버린 겁니다.
다시 혼자서도 살아갈 수 있게 되었습니다.
제 삶이 또다시 크게 바뀐 거예요.
결국 저 같은 사람은 지옥에 가게 될 거라는 생각이 들었습니다.
나쁜 영향에서 벗어나야 한다는 걸 알았습니다.
어느 날 혼자 공원에 앉아 있었어요.
우리 두 사람 다 하느님을 섬기고 싶은데
저한테 지상 낙원에 대해 말하기 시작했어요.
아내와 전 37년 전 그 첫 집회를
전 긴 머리에 구멍 난 청바지를 입고 있었죠.
아마 신발도 안 신고 있었을 거예요.
연단에서 사회하는 나이든 형제가 우릴 보고
자기 가족과 함께 시간을 보내자고 초대했습니다.
그때 들은 건 하나도 기억이 안 나지만
우리가 받은 환대는 결코 잊지 못할 거예요.
생활 방식이 하루 아침에 바뀐 건 아니었죠.
우리 부부는 여호와께 헌신하고 침례를 받았습니다.

en.text: I grew up in a small town,
and I had a good childhood.
My parents instilled in me
from a young age a love for God
and a respect for the Bible.
We were regular church attenders
and I went to a private school
and I had Bible classes each and every day.
Despite all of this, however,
I felt like something was missing.
When I was 15,
my life changed in a moment’s notice.
I was playing high up in a tree,
the branch broke, I fell to the ground,
and I was paralyzed.
At that moment, I went from an active kid who could run
to one who was paralyzed from his neck down.
I couldn’t feel anything.
By the time I was 18,
I gained enough physical strength in my arms
that I once again had my independence.
At that point, I attended a university
and lived on campus.
My life changed dramatically once again.
Here I was exposed to drugs, alcohol,
immorality, and I fell into that lifestyle.
Every night, though, I still read the Bible;
I still had this strong faith in God.
But when I prayed and went to sleep at night,
I just knew I was going to end up
in that hellfire that I had been taught
from an early age.
During this time, I met a girl named Julie,
and we were married shortly after.
She was in the same hippie lifestyle that I was in,
and we knew that if we were going to stay married,
we had to move away from our bad influence.
We were looking for God, and we wanted him in our lives.
One day, I was in the park by myself.
It was a beautiful setting
—there was a lake in front of me, a mountain in the background—
and at that point, I said a prayer to God.
I told him that we wanted to serve him,
but we just didn’t know how.
About 10 minutes later, a guy walked up,
and he started talking to me about a paradise earth.
Everything he said made sense; I had read it before.
The thing that really stood out to me
was his explanation on hellfire.
It was so clear, it was so logical!
It just made sense to me.
He invited us to the Kingdom Hall the next day and we went.
My wife and I will never forget that first meeting
37 years ago.
I had my long hair, holes in my jeans.
I don’t think I even wore shoes that first time.
As we’re sitting there,
I’m thinking that the older brother who is conducting on stage
is going to find us so disgusting.
But to our surprise, right after the meeting
he came up, he greeted us,
and he invited us to spend time with his family.
We don’t remember anything that was said at that meeting,
but we’ll never forget the greeting.
We immediately started attending all the meetings at the Kingdom Hall
and also began a Bible study with the brother we met in the park.
The changes in our lifestyle did not come overnight,
but the brothers were so loving and patient with us.
We now had a purpose in life.
The emptiness that I had felt for so long was no longer there.
We no longer had to live in that self-centered lifestyle.
Now we had Jehovah, we had the brothers, and we had the ministry.
We made our dedication to Jehovah and we were baptized.

cn.text: 我在一个小镇长大
有很美好的童年
从小我父母就教导我
要爱上帝和尊重圣经
我们经常去教会
我所读的私立学校每天都有圣经课程
尽管这样
我还是觉得自己好像缺少什么
在15岁时，我的生活一瞬间改变了
我爬到树上玩
树枝突然断掉
我就掉在地上从此瘫痪了
在那一刻，我从一个活泼的孩子
变成一个脖子以下瘫痪的人
我没有任何知觉
到了18岁，我的手臂恢复了足够的力量
让我再次可以独立
当时，我上大学也住在学校里
我的生活又发生了巨大的改变
在那里，我跟其他人一样
开始吸毒、醉酒，过着不道德的生活
不过，我每天晚上还是读圣经
我仍然对上帝有坚强的信心
但我晚上祷告完要睡觉时
我想我最终还是会下地狱
就像我小时候学的一样
这期间，我认识了一个叫朱莉的女孩
不久后我们结婚了
她跟我一样过着嬉皮的生活方式
我们知道如果要维持这段婚姻
就必须远离不良的影响
我们一直寻找上帝
希望他能指引我们的生活
有一天，我独自在公园里
那是一个美丽的画面
我前面有一个湖，后面有山
我向上帝祷告
我告诉他，我们想事奉他
但不知道该怎么做
大约10分钟后
一个人走了过来
他开始向我谈论地上的乐园
他所说的都很合理
都是我在圣经里读过的
最吸引我的是
他对地狱永火的解释
非常清楚也合乎逻辑！
我觉得很有道理
他邀请我们隔天到王国聚会所去
我们就去了
我和太太永远不会忘记
37年前的第一次聚会
我留着长头发，穿着有洞的牛仔裤
我想我可能连鞋子都没有穿
我们坐在那里时
我心想
讲台上主持节目的年长弟兄
一定觉得我们很讨厌
但没想到
聚会结束后他立刻来找我们
问候我们
还邀请我们认识他的家人
我们不记得那次聚会的内容
但我们绝不会忘记那份问候
很快地，我们出席所有的聚会
并且和我在公园里遇到的弟兄
开始一个圣经讨论
虽然我们的生活方式没有马上改变
但弟兄对我们还是很有爱心和耐心
现在我们的生活有目标了
我长久以来的空虚感不见了
我们不再过着以自我为中心的生活
现在，我们有耶和华
有弟兄姐妹，也有传道工作
我们献身给耶和华后也受浸了

en.text: All around the world,
people come together every week
at places of worship called Kingdom Halls.
Have you ever wondered what happens inside
a Kingdom Hall of Jehovah’s Witnesses?
It’s a place where Bible study programs and lectures
are held each week.
The first time I attended a meeting, I felt very happy.
The atmosphere was so good;
I’ve never seen anything like it anywhere else.
The people are loving, orderly,
and show an interest in people.
Every meeting is open to the public.
Seats are free and no collections are ever taken.
Families are invited to attend and learn together.
All meetings begin and end with song and prayer.
One meeting, usually held on the weekend,
includes a 30-minute Bible discourse
especially designed for the general public.
After that, there’s a question-and-answer discussion
based on an article in the study edition
of the Watchtower  magazine.
Participation is always voluntary.
At one of the meetings during the week,
we not only study the Bible
but also receive training in public speaking.
Everyone is invited to the Christian meetings,
including those who are not Jehovah’s Witnesses.
You can go into any Kingdom Hall
and receive the same program
of Bible instruction.
Bible education, upbuilding association,
and the opportunity to praise God await you
at Christian meetings of Jehovah’s Witnesses.

所有人都可以参加这些聚会

我们除了深入探讨圣经外

这些基督徒聚会 欢迎所有人来参加

en.text: I’ve been suffering
from a very rare type of cancer
since I was eight years old.
I have a tumor growing along my spine next to my heart.
It causes heart problems and very violent back pains.
I begged Jehovah not to fall apart.
I was going to break down,
and before I had even finished my prayer,
I felt a veil of peace and serenity envelope me.
Jehovah was holding my hand,
and I could almost hear him saying,
‘I’m with you.’
Experiencing such extreme trials
allowed me really to taste Jehovah’s undeserved kindness,
and that’s wonderful.
There are a lot of things I’d like to do,
but I am unable to because of my sickness.
I’ve had many feelings since my childhood:
frustration, anger,
even denial.
But Jehovah really helped me accept my situation.
My parents always taught me
to cherish my relationship with Jehovah.
Today, I just need to know that Jehovah loves me.
When I don’t feel well,
I pray to him very intensely for very precise things.
Each time, he answers my prayer.

靠近心脏的位置

经历这个严峻的考验
让我深深感受到
耶和华是赐人分外恩典的上帝
这种感觉真的很好
因为生了这个病
我有好多想做的事都不能做
那段时间，我的内心充满了沮丧、愤怒
我甚至变得自暴自弃
不过，耶和华确实帮助了我
让我能面对现实
小时候爸妈就一直教我
要珍惜跟耶和华的关系
现在我确信耶和华是爱我的
只要不舒服，我就会向耶和华求助
清楚地告诉他我的感受
每一次他都回应我！

en.text: The Bible describes God
as the “Hearer of prayer.”
He can even hear your silent prayers.
How is that possible?
The Hearer of prayer is also the Creator of all life.
He understands how the human mind works.
He designed it.
So he can read the thoughts of your mind
and hear your silent prayers.
Jehovah God is interested in you
no matter where you live.
Whatever language you speak, he understands it.
But does he accept and listen to all  prayers?
Imagine a manager who sees an employee stealing.
The manager confronts him,
but the employee first lies about his stealing
and then tries to justify his actions.
Although the manager hears the employee’s lies and excuses,
he refuses to accept them.
Similarly, God does not accept all prayers.
For example,
what if a person’s prayer is selfish?
What if a man mistreats his wife at home,
and the next day he asks
for God’s blessings?
What if soldiers pray to God for help
to destroy their enemy,
while the opposing army prays
for the same thing?
Will God accept such prayers?
Clearly, God is not pleased with prayers
that conflict with his moral principles.
On the other hand,
God eagerly accepts your prayers,
even if you have done bad things,
if you sincerely want to draw close to him
and seek his wisdom and forgiveness.
Being heard by God is indeed possible
for those who strive to please him.

cn.text: 圣经说
上帝是“听祷告的主”
就算你在心中默默祷告
他也听得到
怎么可能呢？
因为听祷告的主
也是创造一切的造物主
人的大脑就是他设计的
他很清楚大脑怎样运作
所以他能知道你在想什么
能听到你在心里说的祷告
不论你住在什么地方
耶和华上帝都很关心你
无论你说什么语言
他都听得懂你的祷告
但所有祷告他都会听，都会接纳吗？
假设有个老板看到员工偷钱
老板质问他
但这个员工先是说谎
不承认自己偷钱
后来又为自己的行为辩解
虽然老板听到员工的解释
但这些谎言和辩解他是不会接受的
同样，不是所有祷告上帝都会接纳
举个例
一个人祷告是出于自私的理由
再比如
一个丈夫在家里恶待妻子
第二天却祈求神明赐福
又或者
一支军队求上帝帮助他们打败敌人
与此同时敌军也求上帝赐他们胜利
你觉得这样的祷告上帝会接纳吗？
显然，如果人的行为态度或祷告内容
不符合上帝的道德标准
祷告就不会得到接纳
另一方面，就算你做过一些错事

寻求他的智慧，祈求他的宽恕
他也会接纳你的祷告

title: 하느님의 친구가 되면 어떤 유익이 있습니까?

ko.text: 어렸을 땐 여호와께서 실제적인 분으로 느껴지지 않았죠.
어떻게 하느님과 친구가 될 수 있는지

여호와를 잘 알고 그분과 친구가 되려면 노력을 해야 하죠.
여호와께 그분과 친구가 되고 싶다는 걸 보여 드리는 행동을 해야 해요.

여호와께 염려를 맡기면 그분이 도와주신다는 겁니다.
그래서 그분과 정말 가까운 친구가 되었어요.
친구란 내가 어떻게 느끼는지를 마음 놓고 이야기할 수 있는 사람이라고 생각해요.
여호와께는 언제나 무엇이든지 말씀드릴 수 있죠.
여호와께서 항상 제 곁에서 도와주시는 걸 느꼈어요.
제가 무슨 이야기를 하든 잘 들어 주십니다.

en.text: When I was younger, I did not really think about Jehovah as a Person that much.
I definitely think that having a friendship with God
is a hard concept to understand.
I like the scripture that says: “Taste and see that Jehovah is good”
because if you want to get to know Jehovah as a Friend
and develop a relationship with him, you do have to put forth effort.
You have to take the first step, you could say.
You have to see Jehovah as a Person and know that he is real,
and when you pray, you know that he is hearing you.
When I’m all alone,
I take advantage of the opportunity to talk to him.
I talk to him all the time.
There is no greater feeling
than having Jehovah as your Friend, and it’s worth the effort.
Friends in your life come and go,
but the only Person who will truly never leave you is Jehovah.
He can be your Friend forever if you want him to be.
Our family went through some hard times.

en.text: From the moment we are born,
we experience the world through our senses.
Touch lets us feel safe and loved.
We use it to explore and learn.
The sounds we hear convey meaning.
With two ears, we can locate a sound’s direction.
Different wavelengths of light
are perceived as a range of vivid colors.
Images from each eye combine in 3-D
so that we can better judge depth and distance.
We can detect over ten thousand smells
by using a small group of cells
that detect microscopic materials in the air.
We taste,
see, smell,
touch, and hear
in one enjoyable experience,
with all the senses converging in one place
—our brain.
Some two hundred billion nerve cells
are connected by trillions of tiny contacts.
The brain interprets chemical signals from each sense,
connects new information to what we already know,
and stores lasting memories.
Life is a precious gift from our loving Creator.
King David was inspired to write:
“I praise you because in an awe-inspiring way
“I am wonderfully made.
“Your works are wonderful,
I know this very well.”

en.text: The universe is vast and awe-inspiring.
Earth and life on it are amazingly complex.
How did it all get here?
The Bible book of Genesis says that there is a Creator.
But the account is often misunderstood
or even dismissed as a myth.
Is what the Bible says about the origin of the universe plausible?
Scientists estimate
that the universe is 14 billion years old.
This implies that the universe,
including earth, had a beginning.
The Bible agrees.
Genesis 1:1 reads:
“In the beginning God created the heavens and the earth.”
The account does not say when or how the universe began.
Rather, it focuses on the creative process
that took place on earth over six periods of time,
which the Bible calls days.
Were these six 24-hour days, as many believe?
No.
The Hebrew word used in the Bible for “day”
can refer to various lengths of time.
Genesis even summarizes
the six days of creation as one day
—“the day that Jehovah God made earth and heaven.”
Each “day” in Genesis chapter 1
must have spanned extremely long periods of time.
The account’s perspective is also important.
The writer describes the creative periods
as they would have appeared to an observer on the earth.
Had someone been there,
he would have seen events that started in one period
and then progressed into the following periods.
Light penetrated the atmosphere
to reveal alternating day and night.
Earth was covered with water,
and vapor filled the air.
The dense clouds lifted from the waters that covered the earth,
forming an expansive sky between them.
Water receded to uncover dry ground,
and the first plants appeared.
The atmosphere cleared further
to reveal the sun and the moon.
God created living creatures in the sea
and flying creatures above.
And in the last period,
God created land animals
and humans.
In harmony with the Genesis account,
the Bible says:
“Of course, every house is constructed by someone,
but the one who constructed all things is God.”
The Bible does not speak in scientific detail,
but its account of creation is logical and reasonable.

en.text: Who is the Author of the Bible?
The Bible is a collection of 66 small books.
Over 3,500 years ago,
Moses began writing the first of those books.
During the next 1,600 years,
some 40 different men
wrote the remaining books that make up the Bible.
If men wrote the text,
why is the Bible called “the word of God”?
Consider this:
When a businessman wants to send an important message,
he might use a secretary to write a letter or an e-mail.
The employer tells his secretary the thoughts he wants to convey,
and the secretary compiles those thoughts into the e-mail.
Although the secretary types the e-mail,
he is not the author.
In a similar way,
the Bible writers expressed thoughts
and feelings in their own style,
but the message did not originate with them.
So where did it come from?
The Bible says: “All Scripture is inspired of God.”
Jehovah God used his power to guide their minds,
transmitting his thoughts to them.
How did he do this?
While the prophet Daniel was asleep,
Jehovah caused him to have dreams.
Others, like the prophet Ezekiel,
were awake when God caused them
to see incredible visions.
Sometimes, Jehovah used angels
to communicate his thoughts,
such as when he spoke with the apostle John.
But could Jehovah God really transmit his message in these ways?
Today,
people can communicate their thoughts
over great distances.
They can even communicate
with astronauts in outer space.
If humans can do this,
is it not reasonable to conclude
that their Creator can do far more?
We can trust the Bible
because it was authored, not by man,
but by our loving Creator, Jehovah God.

en.text: Does God have a name?
The Bible mentions the names of many gods.
The nations surrounding ancient Israel
worshipped deities named
Ashtoreth, Baal, and Molech.
The first-century Christians lived
among people who worshipped such deities
as Artemis, Hermes, and Zeus,
and the names of those gods
are recorded in the Bible.
The Bible acknowledges that there are “many ‘gods.’”
But the name of one God appears
in ancient manuscripts of the Bible
far more times than the names of all the other gods combined.
If you read modern Bibles,
you will still find the names of the other gods.
However, many Bibles have removed the name
of the most frequently mentioned God.
The name of that God appears some 7,000 times
in the oldest versions of the Bible.
Who is the God whose name has been removed from the Bible?
The first part of the Bible,
often called the Old Testament,
was written in Hebrew and a related language, Aramaic.
In Hebrew, God’s name is represented by four letters.
Hebrew is read from right to left.
In English, those four letters
are rendered by the consonants YHWH.
The original vowel sounds
used in God’s name are unknown,
but the four letters representing God’s name
appeared throughout
ancient Bible manuscripts
and have been inscribed in many other locations.
In English, a popular rendering of God’s name is Jehovah;
another rendering is Yahweh.
Some Bibles use one of these forms of God’s name
at Psalm 83:18
and in several other places.
A number of other translations,
such as the New World Translation  of the Holy Scriptures,
restore God’s name to the locations
in which it originally appeared.
Since God had his personal name
included in the Bible some 7,000 times,
he no doubt wants us to know and use that name.
In the Law God gave to Israel, he told Moses to write:
“Listen, O Israel:
Jehovah our God is one Jehovah.”
Jesus quoted that passage from the Law,
so he obviously knew and used
God’s personal name.
In one of his final prayers before his death,
Jesus said to Jehovah God:
“I have made your name known.”

cn.text: 上帝有没有名字呢？
圣经提到很多神的名字
古代以色列国周围的民族
崇拜不同的神
包括亚斯他禄、巴力，还有摩洛
公元1世纪
基督徒四周的人也崇拜不同的神
例如阿耳忒弥斯、赫耳墨斯、宙斯
这些神的名字也在圣经里
圣经不否认世上有很多的“神”
可是，在很多圣经古抄本里
有一位神的名字经常出现
比其他神名字出现的次数
加起来还要多得多
在现代的圣经译本里
你仍然可以看到其他神的名字
可是
圣经最常提到的那位神就是上帝
很多译本却把他的名字删去了
在很多古老的圣经抄本中
这位上帝的名字
出现了大约7000次
名字被人删掉的这位上帝是谁呢？
圣经的前半部分一般称为《旧约》
这个部分的原文
是用希伯来语和阿拉米语写成的
在希伯来语里
上帝的名字由四个字母组成
希伯来语是从右边读到左边的
这四个希伯来语字母
相当于英语字母YHWH
上帝名字的原本读法已经失传
但这个名字的四个希伯来语字母
却一直保留在圣经的古抄本里
甚至在很多地方都看得到
在中文里
上帝名字最普遍的译法是耶和华
另一个译法是雅威
有些圣经译本在诗篇83:18
和其他地方也采用这些译法
还有些圣经译本
例如《圣经新世界译本》
在原文中上帝名字出现的地方
恢复使用这个名字
既然上帝把他的名字记录在圣经里
大约7000次
他一定很希望我们知道他的名字
并用耶和华这个名字称呼他
上帝通过摩西向以色列人颁布的法典说
耶稣曾经引用这句话
显然他知道上帝的名字
也用这个名字来称呼上帝
耶稣去世前曾向耶和华上帝祷告说

ko.text: 혹은 영적으로 진보하기 위해 노력하라는 격려는
왕국회관 건축 자원봉사를 하기 원하는 형제 자매들은
어떤 직분이나 지위를 위해 야심을 품고 노력하라고
파이오니아나 베델 봉사자, 대회 회관의 종,
왕국회관 건축 자원 봉사자의 임명에 관한 것도 아닙니다.
여호와의 조직에서 책임 있는 일을 할 자격을 갖추도록
또 자매들에게는 이루기 위해 힘쓸 수 있는 목표가
왕국 전파자 학교나 길르앗 같은 목표죠.
예수께서는 빛을 내는 등불의 비유를 사용하십니다.
“이와 같이 여러분의 빛을 사람들 앞에 비추어,
영적 진보를 이루려고 열심히 노력하는 가장 중요한 이유는
여호와를 영광스럽게 하거나 찬양하고 싶기 때문입니다.

그러므로 이 점을 생각할 때 과연 우리는

봉사의 종이나 장로로 섬길 수 있도록
영적인 특성들을 기르려고 하는 형제들이 유익을 얻죠.
다른 사람들이 보고 유익을 얻게 됩니다.
왕국회관 건축이나 개축 공사에서 일하는 것을 보고
우리 한 사람 한 사람이 줄 수 있는
이제 영적 목표를 이루기 위해 노력할
우리가 힘들게 노력하고 힘쓰라고 권고받기 때문에
이 말은 모순처럼 보일 수 있죠.
그런데 어떻게 우리 자신이 유익을 얻게 된다는 겁니까?
우리가 어떤 방법으로 유익을 얻는지 알아보시죠.
바울은 여기서 영적으로 진보하는 과정을 설명합니다.
바울이 장성한 사람들에 관해 무엇이라고 했는지
옳고 그른 것을 구별할 줄 아는 이들의 것입니다.
“옳고 그른 것을 구별할 줄” 알게 됩니다.
좋은 결정을 내릴 수 있게 되죠.
우리 자신에게 또 다른 유익이 있는데요.
영적 목표를 이루기 위해 열심히 노력하면
요약해 보면, 형제든 자매든 우리 각자는
몸을 앞으로 내뻗치듯이 계속 힘써야 합니다.
다른 사람들이 유익을 얻게 되기 때문입니다.
또한 그렇게 한다면 우리 자신도 장성하게 되고

en.text: Now, our text for today
introduces a number of qualifications
for an overseer in the congregation.
However, by extension,
the encouragement to reach out
or to set our heart
on making spiritual progress
applies to all of us.
The Watchtower  comment at the end says this:
“In like manner, brothers and sisters
“who desire to serve as pioneers, as Bethelites,
“or as Kingdom Hall construction volunteers
do well to stretch forward to attain their goals.”
We all know that the apostle Paul here
did not encourage anyone to ambitiously strive
for a certain office or a certain status.
It is not about the appointments
or the office as a ministerial servant or an elder.
And it’s not about the appointment as a pioneer,
Bethelite, Assembly Hall servant, or Kingdom Hall construction volunteer.
Paul here encouraged all to reach out in an effort
to qualify for responsible work in Jehovah’s organization.
Today, we want to talk about the “why.”
Why would brothers want to work hard (as The Watchtower  comment says)
to qualify for assignments in the congregation?
And sisters now have more spiritual goals than ever
that they can reach out for, such as SKE, Gilead,
and other spiritual goals.
Why would we all, regardless of whether we are brothers or sisters,
stretch forward to attain spiritual goals?
We’d like to highlight three main reasons.
Let us open, first of all, to Matthew chapter 5.
Here at Matthew 5:14, 15,
Jesus uses the illustration of a lamp that gives light.
Now let’s look at verse 16, as we want to see his conclusion:
“Likewise, let your light shine before men,
“so that they may see your fine works
and give glory to your Father who is in the heavens.”
So the most important reason
for working hard to make spiritual progress
is our desire to glorify or praise Jehovah.
Is not the way Jehovah administers his sovereignty and love
a great motivating force to reach out?
Additionally, consider Jehovah’s mercy
with us imperfect humans,
his patience in helping us,
and his promise to protect us in these troublesome times.
So Jesus had good reasons to tell us:
“My Father is glorified in this,
“that you keep bearing much fruit
and prove yourselves my disciples,”
according to John 15:8.
So in this sense,
who of us can rightfully say it’s enough,
it’s time to relax, let’s just maintain the status quo?
The contrary is the case.
We work hard, for example, cultivating “the fruitage of the spirit”
in order to reflect Jehovah’s wonderful personality.
And, in fact, the apostle Paul uses the illustration
of a ‘mirror reflecting Jehovah’s glory,’
according to 2 Corinthians 3:18.
So making spiritual progress
is like polishing our mirror
in order to praise Jehovah better.
Can we see the smile of approval from Jehovah as he watches us
and as he sees the efforts of each one of us?
Now, what is reason number two
for our efforts in attaining spiritual goals
for reaching out to improve our qualifications?
Let us please turn to 1 Timothy chapter 4.
The young Timothy
must have displayed a maturity beyond his years.
According to chapter 4, verse 14,
Paul reminded Timothy that he had been appointed
to carry responsibilities in the congregation.
Why would Timothy need to continue making spiritual progress?
Let us read chapter 4, verse 15:
“Ponder over these things; be absorbed in them,
“so that your advancement may be plainly seen
by all people.”
So Timothy’s advancements in connection with his spiritual qualities
would be “seen by all people.”
So the second reason for reaching out, or forward,
to attain our spiritual goals is that others benefit.
For example, if we reach our goals in the ministry
when it comes to the amount of time that we spend there
or the quality of our conversations,
then others will benefit
—the people in the territory and our brothers—
brothers who are working on their spiritual qualities
so that one day they can serve as a ministerial servant or an elder.
All of this can be seen by others, and they benefit from their efforts.
Others will benefit from ones serving at an Assembly Hall
or working in Kingdom Hall construction or on a renovation project.
Our brothers and sisters need every help
and every word of encouragement from each one of us.
Therefore, we all work hard to continue making spiritual progress.
Since we have not stopped doing exactly this,
we might say that we have been able to inspire others to do the very same.
It is contagious, and we all continue to grow.
Now let’s look at the third reason
for our earnest efforts in attaining spiritual goals.
Reason number three is that we ourselves benefit from it.
Now, this seems to be a contradiction
because we are encouraged to reach out, to work hard.
How can we, ourselves, benefit from it?
Now let’s turn to Hebrews chapter 5
in order to find out in what way we benefit ourselves.
Paul here describes this process of making spiritual progress.
And here in chapter 5, verses 11 to 13,
he describes the brothers as little children
—small children constantly needing help
and guidance even in very basic things.
Otherwise, they are confused and helpless and frustrated.
But now let’s see what Paul describes here
about mature people in verse 14,
and we’ll continue reading until chapter 6, verse 1.
He says here: “But solid food belongs to mature people,
“to those who through use have their powers of discernment trained
“to distinguish both right and wrong.
“Therefore, now that we have moved
“beyond the primary doctrine about the Christ,
“let us press on to maturity,
not laying a foundation again,” and so on.
So Paul here tells us
to make spiritual progress.
This is something that does not happen automatically.
He says, “press on” —go forward.
So, what is the benefit for us?
As Paul here describes,
it will allow us “to distinguish both right and wrong.”
In other words, we can make good decisions.
And there is another benefit in this connection
—making spiritual advancement brings contentment.
It makes us happy.
As long as we work hard to attain our spiritual goals,
we will see progress —sometimes just baby steps—
sometimes two steps ahead,
and then sometimes one step back.
But anyway,
by doing this we ensure that we are
content and happy servants of Jehovah.
Now, in summary, each one of us
—whether we are a brother or sister—
needs to continue reaching out
and stretching forward to attain spiritual goals.
Why?
Because Jehovah deserves it,
and because others will benefit from it.
But, then, also, it’s a key for us to succeed
as a mature, content, and happy servant of Jehovah.

cn.text: 今天的经文告诉我们
弟兄们需要符合一些资格
才能成为会众的监督
但从广义来说
竭力符合资格这句话
也就是下定决心不断进步
对我们每个人都适用
《守望台》评论的结尾这样说
“类似地，弟兄姐妹都需要付出努力
才能达到自己的目标
成为先驱、伯特利成员
或王国聚会所志愿建筑人员。”
我们都知道，使徒保罗在经文中
并没有鼓励人野心勃勃地去追求某个头衔或者身份
保罗并不是说长老或助理仆人
这样的头衔有多重要
也不是说先驱、伯特利成员
大会堂仆人、王国聚会所建筑志愿人员
这样的身份有多重要
而是鼓励所有人竭力符合资格
可以多在耶和华的组织里负起责任
做更多工作
现在我们聊一下“为什么”
为什么弟兄们想要像《守望台》评论中说的那样
竭力符合资格，胜任会众的委派呢？
现在姐妹们也比以往有更多目标可以追求
例如SKE、基列学校
还有其他为耶和华服务的机会
为什么无论是弟兄还是姐妹
我们所有人都要竭力追求更多服务机会呢？
我们想强调三个主要原因
首先，请大家一起打开马太福音第5章
请翻开马太福音5章的14,15节
耶稣在这里用了一个“灯发出亮光”的比喻
在经文的第16节，耶稣这样解释
“你们的光也该在人前照耀
这样他们就能看见你们的好行为
把荣耀归于你们的天父。”
所以，我们竭力追求目标的最主要原因是
我们渴望尊崇和赞美耶和华
耶和华深爱我们，并且以爱心施行统治
这推动我们很想为他做得更多
另外，我们要想想耶和华对不完美的人表现的怜悯
在帮助我们的时候显出的耐心
以及在我们遇到困境时保护我们的承诺
所以，耶稣才会这样告诉我们
“你们不断多结果实
表明自己是我的门徒
我的父亲就因此得到荣耀了。”
根据约翰福音15:8
所以我们可以看出
我们没有人可以说自己做的已经够多了
是时候该放松一下了，保持现状就可以了
其实，刚好相反
我们要不断努力培养“神圣力量的果实”
反映耶和华的美好品格
就像使徒保罗在哥林多后书3:18说的比喻那样
我们“能像镜子一样反映出耶和华的荣耀”
所以，我们在真理中不断进步
就好像擦亮我们的镜子一样
可以更好地反映耶和华的荣耀
你能看到耶和华赞许的微笑吗？
因为他看到你正不断付出努力效法他
接下来，我们看看第二个原因
为什么我们要不断竭力符合资格，达到目标
请跟我一起打开提摩太前书的第4章
年轻的提摩太肯定已经表现出超越他年龄的成熟
在第4章的14节，保罗提醒提摩太
他已经受上帝委任在会众中担负职责
为什么提摩太需要在真理中继续进步呢？
请大家一起翻开第4章的15节，经文说
“这些事你要思考，要全神贯注
好让人人都清楚看到你的长进。”
提摩太的基督徒特质是有目共睹的
他的长进“人人”都看得到
所以，第二个竭力符合资格
努力达成目标的理由就是，让别人获得益处
如果我们在传道方面竭力达成目标
例如增加传道时间或者改善教导技巧
别人就能获得益处，包括传道对象和弟兄们
因为弟兄们正在不断改善品格
这样有一天就能符合资格成为助理仆人或长老
我们的长进，别人都看得见，也能从中得益
有些弟兄姐妹参与大会堂或王国聚会所的建筑
或翻新工程，让很多人获得益处
我们的弟兄姐妹需要从我们每一个人得到各方面的帮助
也需要听到鼓励的话
所以我们所有人都需要不断进步
我们一直在努力为耶和华做得更多
所以我们也能够鼓励其他人这样做
这是有感染力的
我们所有人都能不断进步
下面讨论一下
我们不断努力达成目标的第三个原因
第三个理由是，我们也能从中获益
但这看起来好像有点矛盾
因为我们需要竭尽全力、付出辛劳
那么，我们自己怎样从中获益呢？
现在请打开希伯来书第5章
我们来找一找我们自己能从中怎样得益
保罗在经文中描述了一个人成为成熟基督徒的过程
在第5章，从11节到13节
他把弟兄比作小孩
需要持续不断地得到帮助和指导
甚至是在一些非常基本的事情上
否则他们就会感到困惑、不知所措
甚至非常沮丧
现在请看看，保罗在经文中怎样描述成熟的人
我们从5章的14节一直读到6章的1节
经文说:“成熟的人才能吃固体食物
他们的辨识力因常常运用而锻炼纯熟，能明辨是非
所以，我们既然学过关于基督的初步教义
就该迈向成熟的阶段，不用再打基础。”
我们读到这里
保罗在这里告诉我们怎样成为成熟的基督徒
这件事并不是自然而然发生的
他说“迈向”，也就是前进
这样做有什么益处呢？
正如保罗描述的那样
这个过程帮助我们能“明辨是非”
换句话说，我们能做出明智的决定
我们在真理中不断进步，还有另一个好处
那就是带来满足感
我们也会感到喜乐
只要我们向着目标不断努力
就会看到自己的进步
好像婴儿走路一样
有时我们向前进两步，然后又往后退一步
不管怎样，我们继续付出努力
就能在崇拜耶和华的时候，感到快乐满足
我们来总结一下演讲的要点
我们每个人，无论是弟兄还是姐妹
都需要继续竭力为耶和华作更多服务
为什么呢？
因为耶和华配得这一切
因为别人也能从中获得益处
另外，这样的努力可以帮助我们变得更成熟、更满足
也能更喜乐地崇拜耶和华

집회를 중단시킨 보도들을 들어 보셨을 것입니다.

마치기 전에 보여 드릴 영상이 있는데요.
꿈을 꾸셨는데, 아무도 그 꿈이 뭔지 몰라.
저의 하느님 여호와께서 폐하의 꿈과 그 의미를

깊고 어두운 구덩이가 그대를 삼키려 하고 있어요.
빠져나갈 길이 지금은 없어 보일지도 몰라요.
그럴 때면, 고개를 숙여 기도를 드리세요.
그 즉시 여호와께서 가까이 계심을 느낄 수 있을 거예요.
그대의 마음 속에서 여호와에 대한 사랑이 불타오를 거예요.

그대를 꼭 붙들고 인도해 주실 거예요.
용기를 내고 앞에 놓인 축복을 바라보아요.
언제나 여호와의 손을 놓지 않도록 해요.
항상 여호와께서 우리 편이시니 두려워 말아요.
