en.text: Welcome, brothers and sisters.
In this month’s program,
we’ll review who the May 2020 Watchtower
identified as “the king of the north,”
and we’ll learn how knowing this
affects each one of us.
We’ll also see how perseverance helps us
reach our spiritual goals.
And we’ll debut an exciting new series
made especially for teenagers.
This is JW Broadcasting for May 2021.
My theme is “‘The King of the North’ in the Time of the End.”
In recent years, the Russian government
has persecuted our brothers and sisters
who live in that country.
You’ve heard reports about the police invading Kingdom Halls
and breaking up meetings.
The government has labeled Jehovah’s Witnesses
as an “extremist group.”
It has seized our properties and imprisoned our brothers.
Please watch a brief video
that reviews some of the trials
Jehovah’s people in Russia have faced.
On April 20, 2017,
the Supreme Court of the Russian Federation criminalized
the activity of Jehovah’s Witnesses.
As of July 4, 2019,
authorities have progressively seized 131 of the properties
owned by Jehovah’s Witnesses,
with an additional 60 properties subject to confiscation.
One of the seized properties
was the former Russia branch complex in Solnechnoye.
At the time of filming, the Russian authorities continue
their aggressive attack on Jehovah’s Witnesses.
As of August 17, 2020,
there were 42 Witnesses who were in pretrial detention
or sentenced to prison,
32 who were under house arrest,
and 169 who were not allowed to leave their hometown.
All have been charged with organizing,
participating in, or financing the activity
of a so-called “extremist” organization.
At least 380 Witnesses were, at the time, under investigation
—ranging in age from 19 to 89 years old.
What has this meant for the individuals affected?
As an example,
on June 3, 2018,
Brother Sergey Klimov was arrested.
Local authorities initiated
criminal charges against him,
placing him in pretrial detention for two months.
This detention was extended seven times,
separating him from his wife and family
for a year and five months,
before he was finally tried and sentenced.
On November 5, 2019,
he was sentenced to six years in prison.
Two of our dear young people in Russia,
Brother Yegor Baranov and Sister Darya Dulova,
are courageously facing criminal conviction
and potential long-term imprisonment.
Brother Baranov is only 19 years old.
When the authorities raided her home, Sister Dulova was only 18 years old.
By means of the Newsroom on jw.org,
we are informed of updated news events.
This page includes links to name lists
of Witnesses currently imprisoned for their faith,
which can help us include them specifically in our prayers.
Our brothers and sisters in Russia are resolved to remain loyal to Jehovah
despite any opposition,
and they put their confidence in him in the assurance
that Jehovah is on their side!
It shouldn’t surprise us
that this powerful government has been persecuting
our peaceful, law-abiding brothers and sisters.
Why not?
Because that government is fulfilling Bible prophecy!
Please find Daniel chapter 11.
In verse 40, it refers to what the Bible calls
“the king of the north.”
Of that “king,” Daniel 11:41 says:
“He will also enter into the land of the Decoration,
and many lands will be made to stumble.”
Today, Russia and its allies
are filling the role of the king of the north.
Daniel foretold that this king would enter
“the land of the Decoration,”
meaning that he would interfere in a significant way
with the activities of God’s people.
As discussed in the May 2020 Watchtower,
Russia and its allies are not the first political power
to act as the king of the north,
but they may well be the last.
In this program, we will do three things:
First,
we’ll briefly trace the fulfillment of the prophecy
recorded in Daniel chapter 11.
Second, we’ll look at how that prophecy
is being fulfilled today.
And third, we’ll discuss how knowing this information
should affect the decisions that we make.
Brother Herman van Selm, a helper to the Writing Committee,
will help us review some of the key points of the prophecy
recorded in Daniel chapter 11.
Thank you, Herman, for helping me with this presentation.
It’s a pleasure to be with you, Ken.
Thank you for inviting me.
First, let’s briefly trace
how the prophecy has been fulfilled so far.
The prophecy in Daniel chapter 11 mentions
“the king of the north” and “the king of the south.”
Now, why are they described like that?
Well, initially,
these powers were located north and south
of the literal land of Israel,
thus the names king of the north
and king of the south.
These powers could be viewed as two thrones.
Over time, those thrones have been occupied
by various political powers
and these rival kings compete for world domination.
And what about Jehovah’s people?
They are right at the center of this conflict.
But let’s start at the beginning.
Ken,
what is the origin of the kings of the north and of the south?
The kings of the north and of the south
both rose from the empire
established by Alexander the Great.
One line of kings ruled over Egypt,
which is south of Israel.
And that dynasty was the first
to fill the role of king of the south.
During this period, another line of kings
ruled an area north of Israel
and those kings filled the role
of king of the north.
Then the Roman Empire took over
as king of the north.
As discussed in the May 2020 Watchtower,
God’s people are the focal point
of the prophecy recorded in Daniel chapter 11.
The angel who spoke with Daniel said that the prophecy
would help him “understand what will befall your people”
—that is, the nation of Israel.
And what, in fact, happened?
Well, the Jewish nation was God’s people until 33 C.E.
But after that, a change occurred.
Jehovah poured out his holy spirit
on Christ’s followers.
And from then on,
the congregation of true Christians
became God’s people.
Galatians 6:16 refers to them
as “the Israel of God.”
That point is significant
because the kings of the north and south can only be identified
when there is a clearly defined group of God’s people on earth.
Why is that the case?
Because, as we just considered,
the angel had told Daniel
that the prophecy centers on God’s people.
In the second century C.E.,
true Christians were overgrown
by weedlike false Christians.
In his illustration of the wheat and the weeds,
Jesus foretold that this would happen.
That illustration is recorded
at Matthew 13:36-43.
So from the second century onward,
we can no longer identify an organized group of true Christians.
And, as we considered, for that same reason,
we also cannot identify
the king of the north and the king of the south.
But in the 1870’s, a group of Bible students
began to separate itself from false Christians.
This group,
which included Charles T. Russell,
rejected teachings
that were not based on the Bible.
And like the first-century Christians,
they promoted the truths
taught in God’s Word.
Now this group underwent a development
that is foretold at Malachi 3:1.
They were the “messenger”
who would “clear up a way” before Jehovah.
And as events that followed prove,
this group clearly had God’s backing.
So from the 1870’s onward,
when true Christians began to organize themselves as a group,
we can again identify the political powers
that fill the roles of the king of the north
and king of the south.
At that time in history,
Britain was the dominant political force
and it filled the role
of the king of the south.
Amazingly, it was also in the 1870’s
that the German Empire emerged
and soon began to challenge Britain
for world domination.
This political power now filled the role
of the king of the north.
Daniel 11:25, 26 indicate
that the two kings would clash
and that the king of the north would lose many soldiers in the battle.
And that is exactly what happened
during World War I.
And it was during that war
that Britain and its close ally,
the United States,
forged a special bond.
So from this point on,
during these last days,
the Anglo-American power
has been the king of the south.
That brings us to our second point:
How has Daniel chapter 11 been fulfilled
from that time onward
until recent times?
During World War I,
the king of the north and the king of the south
persecuted those of God’s people who refused to fight in the war.
The king of the south even threw into jail
those who were taking the lead in the preaching work.
But let’s take a closer look at the king of the north.
Has the political power filling that role
changed during the last days?
And how has it treated God’s people?
The identity of the king of the north
has changed three times during the last days.
Starting in the 1870’s through to the end of the second world war,
the German Empire
filled the role of the king of the north.
In the period leading up to and including World War II,
it persecuted God’s people without mercy,
imprisoning thousands of our brothers
and killing hundreds of them.
Who replaced the German Empire as the king of the north?
That’s an important question, Herman.
After World War II,
the Soviet Union took on that role.
It also attacked God’s people,
imprisoning them or sending them into exile.
But, Ken, Daniel 11:34 says
that they—that is, God’s people—
would be “given a little help.”
What’s the significance of that statement?
This passage points forward to the time
when the Soviet Union collapsed.
Although God’s people suffered terribly under that government,
they were “given a little help.”
In what way?
After the USSR collapsed,
God’s people there could worship freely for a number of years.
In time, though, Russia and its allies
took on the role of the king of the north.
And like the other powers that filled the role of king of the north,
this government has continued to oppress God’s people.
Let’s watch the following video
that outlines what has happened.
Daniel received a prophecy
about the coming of two rivals:
“the king of the north”
and “the king of the south.”
How has it been fulfilled?
In the late 1800’s, the German Empire
became the king of the north.
That government brought
its “power and . . . heart
“against the king of the south
with a large army.”
In fact, its navy was
the second largest on earth.
Who became the king of the south?
The alliance between Britain
and the United States.
He fought during World War I
“with an exceedingly large
and mighty army.”
He “swept away” and “humbled”
the king of the north.
But that was not the end
of the king of the north.
He turned his attention to and then hurled
“denunciations against the holy covenant.”
He removed “the constant feature”
by limiting the freedom of God’s people
to preach,
imprisoning many,
and even killing hundreds
of God’s anointed ones
and their fellow workers.
After Germany was defeated in World War II,
the Soviet Union
became the king of the north.
It worked with the king of the south
to “put in place the disgusting thing
that causes desolation”
—the United Nations.
Beginning in the early 1900’s,
the Soviet government tried to eliminate
religion in the lands under its control,
fulfilling the words
that he would “show no regard
for the God of his fathers.”
He gave glory, not to the God of heaven,
but “to the god of fortresses.”
As prophesied,
he used this military might
against the king of the south
by engaging “with him in a pushing.”
Anglo-America competed
with the Soviet Union
for world domination,
fighting in and supporting wars
and political struggles around the globe.
After the Soviet Union collapsed in 1991,
it was unclear who would fill the role of the king of the north.
For a time, God’s people there
had been able to preach and worship peacefully.
But in recent years, Russia and its allies
have pushed back at the king of the south.
Both kings have accused each other
of destructive cyber and economic attacks.
But the king of the north has not limited
his attacks to the king of the south.
As foretold, he also entered
“into the land of the Decoration”
—our realm of spiritual activity.
Today, Russian authorities continue
to attack true worship.
We expect such persecution,
but we also expect it to end.
Our King, Jesus Christ,
is more powerful than any human government.
Soon he will destroy not only the kings of the north and the south
but all of his enemies,
and he will deliver God’s loyal people.
That was a powerful and touching video!
How are our brothers and sisters coping with the current persecution?
Let’s take a look.
And what you’re going to see will break your heart
but also strengthen your faith.
my husband and I were woken up
by a loud bang on the door.
As soon as my husband had opened the door,
people burst in shouting,
“Everyone on the floor!”
I saw them taking my husband into the kitchen
and heard them
very aggressively ordering him to do something.
Then I heard some noise, and I realized
that he was being beaten.
My husband, Feliks, and I
were on our way back from the shopping mall
to the car park.
A jeep with tinted windows
blocked our path, and people
with weapons jumped out, shouting:
“On the ground! Don’t move!”
We were thrown against the vehicle.
Feliks was sent to a pretrial detention facility,
where he spent a year.
From the very first bang on the door,
I began praying to Jehovah for wisdom, calmness,
and for holy spirit so that I could make the right decisions
and act in the right way.
And for the whole day, I was praying.
Jehovah answered all my prayers,
and I felt that he was close at my side.
Before each court hearing when I was very afraid
and felt overwhelmed by emotion and couldn’t calm myself down,
it was prayer
that helped me to settle down.
When they took us for interrogation,
I started panicking and, at that moment,
I realized that I needed to meditate on something positive.
So I thought,
‘I need to sing our songs.’
And just one song came into my mind:
“He Will Make You Strong.”
It really strengthened me.
Those words about how Jehovah gave his Son for us
show he loves us and will never leave us.
Brothers and sisters
pray and tell me
that they are praying for me.
It gives me the feeling that I am part
of a large family.
After the interrogation,
he was sent home.
My husband and I
continue to stick to our spiritual routine.
We continue to conduct family worship, and we are always in the ministry.
Our brothers and sisters constantly support us.
They write kind words;
they commend us;
they send us encouraging scriptures from the Bible.
In September 2019, Feliks was found guilty
and sentenced to three years in a general regime colony.
When he and the other brothers arrived there,
they were beaten up by officers from the colony.
Feliks told me
that he prayed while he was being beaten,
and he noticed that at that moment, he stopped feeling the pain.
While he is behind bars,
Feliks tries to conduct family worship with me by letters.
He picks certain themes and some specific questions.
Then I do research
in the publications and send back what I find.
The scripture at Isaiah chapter 30 really strengthens me,
where it says that “your strength will be
in keeping calm and showing trust.”
Although I tend to worry,
I understand that calmness is expressed
by fully trusting in Jehovah.
I have become stronger because thanks to Jehovah,
in a way, I have developed almost a shell
against the difficulties
that used to scare me.
That confidence and faith help me.
Jehovah was with me,
and he will remain
close by me,
and we will be made stronger thanks to him,
and we will get through these trials.
How can we develop courage
like our brothers and sisters in Russia?
Well, we must be convinced
that the prophecies in the Bible are trustworthy.
That was a topic discussed
by Brother David Splane of the Governing Body
in the following Morning Worship program.
Now, if you’d just
take a look at today’s text,
it says: “Come and witness
the activities of Jehovah”—witness.
Now, according to a dictionary,
a witness is someone who has personal knowledge of something.
So how can we be Witnesses of Jehovah?
What personal knowledge
do we have of his activities?
Well, first of all, we can testify to the fact
that Jehovah can see into the future.
And when he does that, he is right 100 percent of the time.
And second, we know that no one can prevent
what Jehovah foresees from coming true.
All of Jehovah’s prophecies come true.
Now, to illustrate the first point,
that Jehovah can see into the future,
let’s consider two remarkable prophecies
concerning the destruction of Jerusalem and its temple.
Now, we know that through the prophet Jeremiah,
Jehovah foretold that Jerusalem and the temple
would be destroyed by the Babylonians.
Did it come true?
Absolutely—in 607 B.C.E.
But Jehovah went further.
He said that Jerusalem would be rebuilt.
“They will rebuild the ancient ruins;
“they will raise up the desolated places of the past,
and they will restore the devastated cities.”
And true worship would also be restored.
So that was quite a level of knowledge.
But there’s more.
Jehovah went further.
Jehovah also indicated
that the spiritual revival wouldn’t last.
Now, that is remarkable.
And it’s implied by what we read in the second part
of Daniel 9:26.
I’d like you to have a look at this.
We’re going to be reading
two parts of this verse,
and it’s quite interesting
—Daniel 9:26.
So now, what’s our objective here?
It’s to see that Jerusalem and its temple
would be destroyed a second time
and that true worship would not last.
It says in the second part of verse 26:
“And the people of a leader who is coming
will destroy the city and the holy place.”
Now, when these words were written,
Jerusalem and the temple were already in ruins.
But Jehovah doesn’t say,
‘Nebuchadnezzar has destroyed the city and its temple.’
He says: “The people of a leader who is coming.”
The Roman general Titus in 70 C.E.
“will destroy the city and the holy place.”
In order for that prophecy to be fulfilled,
Jerusalem and the temple would have to be rebuilt
and then destroyed a second time.
Now, that is quite a level of knowledge —quite a level of information.
But what would make this necessary?
Why, when the Jews came back to the Promised Land
and they were intent on restoring true worship,
why would this fail?
And why would Jerusalem and the temple be destroyed a second time?
Part of it is due to what we find in the first part of verse 26:
“Messiah will be cut off.”
So Jehovah foretold, foresaw,
that when the Messiah came,
the Jews would reject him.
He would be cut off.
And because of that, partly because of that,
Jerusalem and the temple would be destroyed,
as it happens, in 70 C.E.
Now, wait a minute, wait a minute.
Let’s think about that a minute.
The Messiah comes first and Jerusalem and the temple
are destroyed after that in 70 C.E.
What does that mean?
It means that the Messiah comes before 70 C.E.
So we might ask our Jewish friends,
why are you still waiting for the Messiah?
70 C.E. has come and gone.
Well, the Messiah came, and he too proved to be a true prophet.
And a remarkable prophecy of Jesus is found in the Sermon on the Mount.
Let’s have a look at it and consider the implications of this prophecy.
This is Matthew chapter 7,
and we’ll read verses 22 and 23,
an amazing prophecy.
Now, imagine: At this point, Jesus’ teachings
have not spread beyond Israel.
But notice verses 22 and 23:
“Many will say to me on that day:
“‘Lord, Lord, did we not prophesy in your name,
“‘and expel demons in your name,
“and perform many powerful works in your name?’
“And then I will declare to them: ‘I never knew you!
Get away from me, you workers of lawlessness!’”
Now, isn’t that amazing?
If Jesus had simply predicted
that his teachings would spread throughout the earth,
you might say, “Well, there’s nothing remarkable about that.”
But Jesus is saying something different.
Jesus is foretelling
a great apostasy from his teachings.
Jesus is foretelling the birth of Christendom
300 years before the event.
So Jesus foresees that many
are going to turn away from the truth.
And by the end of the first century,
that apostasy was already at work, wasn’t it?
There were sects
—the sect of Nicolaus, for example, and other sects.
And now they’re on the cusp of the great darkness,
the great apostasy, that’s going to set in from the second century on.
And with this in mind, what does Jehovah do?
He makes an amazing statement
—Revelation 14—
‘144,00 will be on Mount Zion with the Lamb.’
There were nowhere near 144,000 in the truth in the first century.
And here Jehovah is saying there are going to be 144,000 in heaven
with the Lamb at the end.
But not only that, he goes further.
There’s going to be a ‘great crowd that no man can number.’
How could that ever come true?
Ours is the God of true prophecy.
Well, that’s prophecy.
What about the second point?
And that is that no one can prevent prophecy from being fulfilled.
The Devil would love to prevent that from taking place.
Think about Revelation 14.
If the Devil could make the number
one short of 144,000,
he’d be happy because he would show
that Jehovah was inaccurate in what he foretold.
And so that’s one of the reasons why the Devil
has made war on the remnant of the seed of the woman,
if at all possible, to prevent that number
of 144,000 from coming to pass.
But, of course, he’s going to fail.
And what about the prophecy in the Bible
that America and Britain would become a dual world power?
Now, Britain wouldn’t become a world power
at all if France had anything to say about it.
France and Britain were sworn enemies.
And for many, many, years,
France was much richer and much more powerful
than Britain was.
And finally, at the Battle of Waterloo in 1815,
France had one last chance
to prevent Britain from becoming a world power.
And France should have won that battle.
Everything was stacked against the British.
But there was a driving rain,
a fatal miscalculation on the part of Napoleon,
and a few other factors that foiled their attempt.
And Britain did become a world power.
And at the end of the 19th century,
it’s quite true that the sun never set on the British Empire.
But now, America and Britain were supposed to become a dual world power,
and Britain wasn’t the least bit interested in sharing its power with America.
It tried to prevent America from separating as a colony.
There was a long war,
and there were mistakes made on both sides.
But finally, America gained its independence from Britain.
Well, what do we find?
Some years after that,
Britain is sharing its power with America.
They are a dual world power.
Fighters against God will never prevail.
We serve “the God of true prophecy.”
And “what he foretells comes to be.”
As we’ve discussed,
each detail of the prophecy recorded at Daniel chapter 11
has come true so far.
We must have confidence
that the remaining events described in that prophecy
will also come true.
We are living in the last days of the time of the end.
Soon, the nations will fulfill the prophecy
at 1 Thessalonians 5:3:
“Whenever it is that they are saying,
“‘Peace and security!’
“then sudden destruction is to be instantly on them,
“just like birth pains on a pregnant woman,
and they will by no means escape.”
Then “sudden destruction”
comes upon all parts of Satan’s system.
As you can see on the screen,
Daniel 12:1 says:
“During that time Michael will stand up,
“the great prince who is standing in behalf of your people.
“And there will occur a time of distress such as has not occurred
“since there came to be a nation until that time.
“And during that time your people will escape,
everyone who is found written down in the book.”
That leads us into our third point:
How should knowing the information
that we have just discussed
affect the decisions that we make?
Well, what we have reviewed is not just interesting history;
it’s a dramatic prelude
to what will soon happen here on earth.
Jehovah has given his people this knowledge
so that we can act on it.
It should influence the choices we make.
In the following dramatization,
notice how one young brother makes decisions
based on his understanding of Daniel’s prophecy.
That was my best friend, Lucas,
when we were kids.
And that was me, Oscar.
We knew exactly what we wanted to do
when we grew up:
Pioneer!
Go to Bethel!
Build Kingdom Halls!
We kept those goals.
And when graduation came,
we were ready.
Our little business needed just a few more accounts.
Then we’d have enough for us and to help our families.
Finally!
Day one of the service year
—and two new pioneers!
Where we live, . . .
Please don’t call me ever again!
. . . finding spiritual interest is tough.
We already have cleaners. Thanks.
And finding enough work was harder than we thought.
A few months in, I was sure
Jehovah would help if we just stuck it out.
Sorry, Oscar. Can’t make it today.
Something came up. Lucas.
What came up was an opportunity for more money,
but at what cost?
Are you quitting, or what?
No, I’m not quitting.
Pioneering or our business?
Neither, but you know the struggle here.
Most brothers can afford to pioneer for a year, two tops.
Look, it’s not full-time while I’m training.
It’s a backup plan.
So Lucas stopped pioneering?
Maybe he’s right.
He’s just being practical.
I mean, is it wrong to quit if you think it’s not working?
I struggled with the same question when I pioneered.
Whatever you decide,
if you can tell Jehovah your reason
with a clean conscience,
then it’s the right decision for you.
Why would I keep going when it’s so difficult?
“Since all these things are to be dissolved in this way,
“consider what sort of people you ought to be
in holy acts of conduct and deeds of godly devotion.”
It really is “the last days,”
and people need “the good news.”
And they’ll only hear it
if we keep up our “deeds of godly devotion”
as best we can.
I prayed to endure and only stop pioneering
if my circumstances left no other choice.
And I prayed to see the blessings.
And after a while,
I learned that a little perseverance,
with Jehovah’s spirit, can be contagious.
So, what do you want to do when you grow up?
Pioneer.
And go to Bethel?
Yep!
And then maybe build Kingdom Halls.
You in?
Yeah.
That young brother was trying to figure out
what to do with his life.
He made a good decision because he allowed Bible prophecy
to influence his thinking.
We know that teens everywhere
face many challenges, and we feel for you.
Of course, I was once a teenager,
but I can’t even imagine some of the situations
that you find yourselves in.
But the Governing Body loves you,
and we want to help.
So I’m very happy to announce a new series
—“My Teen Life.”
You’ll hear from Witnesses
who share the challenges they faced in their teens
and how they overcame them with Jehovah’s help.
The interviews are candid;
the issues are real.
Here’s the first episode.
Well, when I was a teenager,
I didn’t see any benefit
in talking to my parents
because they liked different things than I liked.
So I thought, ‘Well, what’s the point?’
And I also wanted to be an adult.
I wanted to feel like an adult and be treated like an adult.
I remember when my mom used to pick me up from school.
She wanted to show personal interest in me,
so she’d ask me: “Oh, how are your friends doing?
“How was school today?
Do you have a lot of homework?”
But I just thought that she was being nosy.
I always had my earphones on.
And whenever my parents were trying to talk to me,
that was my chance to just pop them in and ignore them.
The way my parents grew up wasn’t
the same way that I grew up.
They grew up in a different country;
they spoke a different language; they grew up in a different time.
When you’re talking to somebody who doesn’t speak your language natively,
oftentimes you won’t be able to explain things from your heart.
And so I had that challenge.
I wasn’t able to talk directly to my parents heart to heart.
And so there was always this frustration
in trying to really convey how I felt.
And I felt like I wasn’t really getting through to my parents.
When I went to my first pioneer school, I learned a lot about Jehovah’s qualities.
And one of them was how he was a very approachable Person.
And I thought to myself, ‘Am I an approachable person?’
And I thought about how I acted in the ministry
and then at the meetings and then at home.
And I realized that at home I had a lot of things I needed to fix.
I felt like it was two different worlds I was living in.
One was when I was at school with my peers;
I felt like I was understood.
And at home, I kind of just withdrew to myself.
I wouldn’t try to communicate with them because it didn’t seem worth the effort.
I tried to figure out problems in my own way.
It was kind of trial and error.
I developed a lot of bad habits
that today I’m still trying to overcome.
If I’d been able to communicate with them more,
if I’d been able to connect with them and ask for their help
and get their support and have them on my team,
things would have gone a lot better.
And I really wish I had.
Jesus, who was a perfect human being
and who had perfect judgment, didn’t make decisions on his own.
He always looked to his Father for guidance.
And that got me thinking,
‘Well, if Jesus did that,
‘there has to be something good
in it for me too.’
What really helped me was Colossians 4:6.
I knew I needed to speak more graciously in the family.
And I realized that I was speaking very defensively
and that I needed to be more approachable to my parents.
When I first tried to talk with them, of course,
it was awkward and I didn’t want to talk about anything personal
because I wasn’t used to it.
So I thought I could maybe ask them about themselves
—ask them how their day was or what they liked from the meetings.
So I just tried to show more interest in them
instead of focusing on myself.
And I think that’s what got
the conversations going
and got me comfortable
to really talk with them.
I was so focused on how my parents weren’t understanding me
that I wasn’t really trying to understand them.
When I thought about my parents,
I thought about how much work it takes to be a parent.
From when I was a baby, for many years,
they were working day and night to try to care for me.
They never demanded a thank you or anything from me.
They were really self-sacrificing.
And I imagined: ‘If I had to work that much for somebody,
‘how would I feel if they didn’t really say thank you?
‘Or how would I feel
‘if this person whom I worked so hard for
didn’t really view me as their friend?’
Later on, as I got older and started
that communication going with my parents,
I realized that taking their advice and really listening to their opinions
and always letting them know
what I’m going to do and where I’m going to go
was a mature thing to do.
Our heart oftentimes
takes the driver’s seat, and it directs us
to where it thinks it should go.
And oftentimes it goes in the wrong direction,
and we sometimes get hurt.
Then we look back and say, “I wish I hadn’t done that.”
And our parents have been there.
What they’re trying to do for us now is to tell us,
“Don’t let your heart take the driver’s seat.”
If I could talk to my teenage self,
I would tell myself to see my mom and dad more like coaches,
because I used to think they were always trying to criticize me
and point out my faults.
But, really, they’re just trying to help me,
and they want me to have a happy life.
I really wish I knew that as a teenager.
But I’m glad I learned that now.
We hope that you’ll enjoy and benefit
from future episodes of “My Teen Life.”
This new series is another way
the Governing Body prepares Jehovah’s people
to cope with today’s challenges
and to be ready for what’s coming.
Bible prophecy shows that in the near future,
the nations will turn on all false religions and wipe them out.
Then, they will launch a final attack on God’s people.
And what a mistake that will be!
As discussed in the Pure Worship book,
Jehovah will respond to that attack
by unleashing his rage on the nations.
After the dust of Armageddon settles,
those with the earthly hope can look forward
to a thousand years of genuine peace and security,
working under the rule of God’s Kingdom.
Before that time comes,
we will continue to face trials and opposition,
but we can endure.
We have many modern-day examples
that we can imitate right now.
Those examples can help all of us
to be prepared, to stand firm,
and to remain fully united in the faith.
This month’s original song
entitled “One United People”
encourages us to do just that.
We watch the storm clouds gather. We’ve seen the signs before.
The wind of persecution Is no stranger to our door.
We will face each test with courage, With Jehovah standing near.
And ‘no weapon formed against us’ Will give any cause for fear.
We are one united people,
Though we come from ev’ry land.
We are standing firm together,
For Jehovah makes us stand,
For Jehovah makes us stand.
We wait with calm assurance For Jehovah, the Most High—
The God of our salvation Whose love will never die.
He will never leave his people, And his spirit makes us strong.
No, our enemies won’t break us. To Jehovah we belong!
We are one united people,
Though we come from ev’ry land.
We are standing firm together,
For Jehovah makes us stand.
We stand firm together; Unafraid we face the crowd.
And these hearts that beat within us We have given to our God.
We are one united people,
Though we come from ev’ry land.
We are standing firm together,
For Jehovah makes us stand,
For Jehovah makes us stand.
The stirring theme of this year’s convention
is “Powerful By Faith!”
We will learn what faith is,
why it is essential,
and how we can acquire it.
Here is a preview.
It can be hard to put faith in something you cannot see.
But real faith is not blind.
Real faith is based on facts,
on realities,
on truth.
It gives us courage and strength,
and it helps us to endure.
When life gets hard, it provides peace.
It reminds us of our purpose,
and it brings us real joy.
Learn how to build and strengthen your faith
at the 2021 “Powerful by Faith!” Convention of Jehovah’s Witnesses.
Now it’s time for our video postcard, which comes to us
from our brothers and sisters in Belarus.
Belarus is an Eastern European nation that borders Russia.
It’s known as
the “blue-eyed” country because it is dotted
with more than 10,000 lakes.
Some of Europe’s most ancient trees, as well as
its largest mammal —the European bison—
can be found here.
Castles, some dating
from the 16th century, are popular sites.
This is Nesvizh Castle.
If you look up at the ceiling of its chapel, you’ll see Jehovah’s name
in the form of the Tetragrammaton.
When Belarus was part of the Soviet Union,
Jehovah’s Witnesses faced strong government opposition.
Some of our brothers were exiled to far-away Siberia.
Today, more than 6,000 publishers
in 84 congregations boldly declare the good news
in Belarus.
There is a zealous pioneer spirit here.
Twenty percent of the publishers
are in full-time service.
This is how our brothers share the good news
in the city of Brest.
They enjoy many aspects
of public witnessing.
Here are our brothers and sisters in the city of Kobryn.
Their territory includes both urban and rural areas.
The 78 publishers here conduct an average
of 74 Bible studies each month.
Our brothers and sisters in Belarus
send you their warm love and greetings.
Herman, it’s been a pleasure reviewing this exciting material
about the “king of the north” with you.
Thank you, Ken.
This information is so important.
It helps all of us
to face the future with confidence.
Before we say goodbye, we have a treat for you.
Here’s a preview of the video drama from this year’s convention.
Please enjoy.
You will receive training
in the house of the great King Nebuchadnezzar.
Wait!
Daniel!
Be strong, my son.
This is a new land with new laws.
Soon they’ll want us to worship their gods.
Jehovah is in Israel.
We’re in Babylon now.
What’s going to happen to us?
He had a dream,
and no one can tell him what it is.
Everyone is to be executed by dawn.
We have until morning.
To do what?
It’s Jerusalem.
They burned down Jehovah’s house!
As long as Jehovah exists,
we have hope.
Interpretations belong to my God, Jehovah.
He knows your dream and what it means.
Where is your God?
Kill them!
O Jehovah,
surely you didn’t bring us here to die.
Please, vindicate yourself.
As we’ve discussed in our program,
Daniel played an important role as Jehovah’s prophet.
And as we’ll see in our video drama,
there’s much we can learn from his life and example.
And now, before we sign off,
we have a special musical gift video
that closely relates to our monthly program theme.
You will be encouraged and inspired.
Please keep our brothers in Russia in your prayers.
Learn from their example of faith and courage.
See these events for what they are
—the fulfillment of Bible prophecy.
Let this knowledge move you to make wise decisions.
Stay faithful, and stay busy
as the end of this system draws close.
From the World Headquarters of Jehovah’s Witnesses,
this is JW Broadcasting.

en.text: An introduction to the book of Deuteronomy.
Deuteronomy was written by Moses
on the plains of Moab in 1473 B.C.E.
just before the Israelites
entered the Promised Land.
The name Deuteronomy means “Second Law,”
or “Repetition of the Law.”
However, the book is also an explanation of the Law.
Deuteronomy urges the Israelites
to love and obey Jehovah
in the land he is about to give them.
The book consists primarily
of four discourses,
a song, and a blessing by Moses.
In the first discourse, found in chapters 1-4,
Moses reviews Israel’s history after the Exodus
and urges the people to remember
what Jehovah has done for them.
For example, Moses reminds them
that Jehovah eliminated the faithless and cowardly generation
that, 40 years earlier, feared the inhabitants of Canaan.
In the second discourse,
contained in chapters 5-26,
Moses exhorts the people
to obey God’s commandments,
not out of mere duty,
but because they love him
with all their heart, soul, and strength.
Did you know?
In the ancient world,
foreigners often had no legal rights
and widows and fatherless children
faced many difficulties.
In Israel, however, Jehovah’s Law
applied to and benefited all,
including foreigners, widows,
and fatherless children.
Jehovah loves these individuals,
and his people should love them too.
In chapter 7, Moses tells the Israelites
that Jehovah will clear away the nations in the Promised Land,
which are more populous and mightier than Israel.
In chapter 8, Moses describes Israel’s inheritance
as “a good land” with streams of water,
wheat, barley, grapevines, fig trees,
pomegranates, olive oil, and honey.
But it is a land filled with false worship.
So in chapter 12, the Israelites
are commanded to pull down the altars to false gods,
to shatter the sacred pillars,
to burn the sacred poles,
and to cut down the graven images.
In chapter 16, Moses reminds God’s people
to celebrate the Passover
as well as the three great festivals:
the Festival of Unleavened Bread,
the Festival of Weeks,
and the Festival of Booths.
Chapter 18 contains a prophecy about a future great prophet.
Moses says: “Jehovah your God will raise up for you
“from among your brothers a prophet like me.
You must listen to him.”
The third discourse, in chapters 27 and 28,
sets out the cursings for disobedience
and the blessings for obedience.
After the nation crosses the Jordan River,
the cursings are to be recited on Mount Ebal,
where half of the tribes are to stand.
The other tribes are to stand on Mount Gerizim
and bless the people.
Chapters 29 and 30 contain Moses’ fourth discourse,
in which he makes a covenant with the people,
telling them to choose life
by obeying Jehovah.
In chapter 31,
Jehovah commissions Joshua as Moses’ successor.
Joshua should “be courageous and strong”
as he leads the nation into its God-given land.
Chapter 32 records the song of Moses,
which powerfully extols God’s faithfulness
in contrast with the Israelites’ unfaithfulness.
In chapter 33,
we read “the blessing that Moses . . .
pronounced on the Israelites before his death.”
In the final chapter,
Moses ascends Mount Nebo,
where he is shown the Promised Land.
Jehovah says:
“I have let you see it with your own eyes,
but you will not cross over there.”
Moses then dies at 120 years of age,
and Jehovah buries him in a secret location in Moab.
As you read the book of Deuteronomy,
see how Jehovah blesses those who love him,
note how he withholds his blessing
from those who disobey him,
and discern how the principles behind God’s Law
are reflected in the teachings of Jesus
—the Prophet like Moses,
who is also the King of God’s Kingdom.

ko.text: 배교로 인해 연합이 깨져 버린 것입니다.
이스라엘은 순결한 숭배를 더럽혔고 하느님의 이름을 모독했으며
이제 그 결과로 고통을 겪고 있습니다.
여호와께서는 희망을 주는 여러 가지 예언을 에스겔이 선포하게 하십니다.
「순결한 숭배」 책 제3부에서는 그러한 예언들을 다룹니다.
메시아에 관한 예언들은 여호와의 목적과 관련하여
매우 가슴 설레는 내용을 담고 있습니다.
우리가 가진 희망의 기초이기도 한 그 예언들이 8장에서 다루어집니다.
“내가 그들 위에 한 목자를 세워 그들을 먹이게 하겠다.
그가 그들을 먹이고 그들의 목자가 될 것이다.”
이 장을 연구하면서 다음 요점들을 찾아 보십시오.
예언적 의미가 담긴 큰 독수리들에 관한 수수께끼에서 어떤 점을 배울 수 있습니까?
에스겔서에 들어 있는 메시아에 관한 예언들을 통해,
왕 예수 그리스도를 신뢰할 수 있는 어떤 이유들을 알 수 있습니까?
우리 각자는 어떻게 영적 낙원의 평화와 연합에 기여할 수 있습니까?
이 장에 나오는 삽화와 삽화 설명문을 주의 깊이 살펴보고
그러한 자료들은 이 장에서 다루는 예언들을
더 깊이 이해하는 데 도움이 될 것입니다.
이 장의 내용을 더 깊이 이해할수록
여호와께 순결한 숭배를 드리려는 결심이 더욱 강해질 것입니다.

en.text: The city is in devastation.
It’s in chaos.
Bridges have collapsed.
Many houses on the edge of the river
were swept away.
Our main concern
was the health of our brothers
and their well-being.
We got in contact with some of the local elders,
who reassured us that everyone was safe.
So immediately we started getting in contact
with brothers from the circuit,
and in a few hours, almost one and a half tons of food
was received at the support center.
We had an experience with an older lady.
Because she had seen so many people
at our house cleaning up, she asked us:
“Why are there so many people at your house?
Do they all live in your house?”
“No, they’re brothers and sisters from our congregation.
We’re Jehovah’s Witnesses.”
“Ah, but nobody came from my church to help me,
“not even to assist me to get out of the house
and certainly not to clean up my house.”
So we really see what a privilege it is to have our brotherhood.
Even though our city is in this state,
we as Jehovah’s people
are together and united, and we’re all right.
Without a doubt, Jehovah is helping us and he’s with us.

title: 새뮤얼 F. 허드: 정말 최선을 다하고 있습니까?

ko.text: 자기 자신과 관련해서만 기뻐할 이유가 있을 것입니다.”
집회에서 의미 있는 해설을 하기 위해 노력하고 있는가?
최선을 다해 전파 활동에 참여하고 있는가?
재방문을 준비하는 면에서 더 개선할 점이 있는가?
그렇다면 최선을 다해 연구생을 돕고 있는가?’
자신이 정말 최선을 다하고 있는지 확인할 수 있죠.
우리보다 더 잘하는 사람을 보게 될지 모릅니다.
우리 자신과 다른 사람을 비교해서는 안 된다고
지금 자신이 할 수 있는 일을 다하고 있으니까
충분히 잘하고 있다는 생각이 들 수 있죠.
그런데 이 성구의 첫 부분을 기억해야 합니다.
우리는 자신이 지금 하고 있는 것과
개인적으로 최대한 할 수 있는 것을 비교해 봐야 합니다.
‘난 최선을 다하고 있는데, 뭘 더 하란 말이지?’
그래도 잘 살펴보고 검토해 봐야 합니다.
시간을 내서 여러분이 하고 있는 모든 일을
신권 활동을 더 할 수 있습니까?
그럴 수도 있고 아닐 수도 있죠.
연습하고, 훈련하고, 몸에 좋은 음식을 먹고,
제일 좋은 운동화를 신는 등 최선을 다하죠.
더 빠른 선수가 있으면 경기에 지고 맙니다.
최선을 다했지만 소용이 없게 된 거죠.
더 빠른 선수와 비교해서 그보다 느렸기 때문입니다.
딸이 학교에서 그린 그림을 집으로 가져옵니다.
엄마는 B-를 지우고 A+라고 써 줍니다.
그런 다음 그림을 냉장고에 붙여 놓습니다.
선생님은 그 아이를 같은 학년의 친구들과 비교했지만,
딸이 최선을 다한 것에 따라 점수를 매겼습니다.
우리가 영적으로 얼마나 잘하고 있는지를 판단하실 때
절대 할 수 있는 것 이상을 요구하지 않으시죠.
하지만 그분은 우리가 할 수 있는 최선을 다해
우리가 가진 모든 것을 다해야 한다는 것이죠.
봉사에 나가서 온 힘을 다해 전파합니다.
그렇게 온 힘을 다해 전파 활동에 참여한다고 해도
우리의 정신을 다해 올바른 것을 말하지 않는다면,
아무도 내가 하는 서론을 듣지 않는단 말이지.’
그 서론은 구역에 가장 알맞은 서론이었나요?
얼마나 오랫동안 그 서론을 사용해 오셨나요?
우리의 정신을 다해 서론을 미리 준비함으로
평일 집회 때 소개된 서론들을 사용해 보려고 노력합니까?
집주인은 여러분의 친절하고 밝은 표정을 볼 수 있습니까?
좋은 소식을 가지고 왔다는 게 얼굴에 나타납니까?
가까운 미래에 그 소식은 바뀌게 될 겁니다.
개선할 점을 찾으면 더 잘하게 될 것입니다.
정신을 기울여 주의 깊이 듣고 있다면
우리는 여호와 하느님께 가까이 가기 위해
그분이 가까이 오실 것’ 이라고 말합니다.
집회에 참석해서 얻는 유익 한 가지가 바로 그것입니다.
정기적인 집회 참석의 또 다른 유익인데요,
집회에 참석해서 우리는 서로 격려를 주고받죠.
“그리고 서로 생각해 주어 사랑과 훌륭한 일을 고무하며,
일부 사람들의 습관처럼 함께 모이는 일을 그만두지 말고,
오히려 서로 격려하며 그날이 다가오는 것을 볼수록
그렇다면 여러분은 정말 잘하고 계신 것입니다.
개인 연구를 할 때나 가족 숭배를 할 때는 어떤가요?
여호와에 대한 사랑과 감사가 더 커지게 해 주고
그분께 더 가까이 가게 도와주는 어떤 내용을 발견하셨습니까?
그 내용을 정신을 다해 묵상하고 계속 생각합니까?
그래서 마음 깊숙한 곳까지 이르게 합니까?
어떤 내용들은 배운 즉시 적용할 수는 없을지 모르지만,
나중에 꼭 필요할 때 떠올려서 적용할 수 있을 것입니다.
거의 매주 가족 숭배를 하고 계시죠?
아내가 매일 저녁을 아무렇게나 차린다면 어떨까요?
오늘 우리는 정말 최선을 다하고 있는지 고려해 봤습니다.
그 이유는 남과 비교하려는 게 아니라
단지 자신을 직접 검토해 보기 위해서였습니다.
자신을 위해, 가족을 위해, 영적 형제 자매들을 위해
다른 사람의 최선을 비교할 수 없다는 겁니다.
자기 자신을 분명히 보지 못할 수 있습니다.

en.text: In addressing our theme
“Is Your Best Good Enough?”
I’d like to start by reading Galatians 6:4.
It says: “But let each one
“examine his own actions,
“and then he will have cause for rejoicing
“in regard to himself alone,
and not in comparison with the other person.”
We’re told to “examine [our] own actions.”
So ask yourself: ‘How am I doing spiritually?
‘Am I happy with my attendance at Christian meetings?
‘Do I participate by sharing meaningful comments as able?
‘How about my personal study of the Bible?
‘Let me examine my involvement in the ministry.
‘Could I do better in preparing for my return visits?
‘Do I conduct any Bible studies with interested ones?
If so, am I content with what I am doing?’
In effect, you’re asking yourself,
‘Is my best good enough?’
We might see others in the congregation that are doing more than we are.
But then we look back at Galatians 6:4 again,
and it clearly said
that I should not compare myself with the other person.
So we could quickly assume that we’re doing what we can,
reasoning that it’s good enough.
But let’s not forget the first part of the verse.
We are to “examine [our] own actions.”
We need to compare what we are doing
with what we personally could be doing.
We need to be active
and not become self-satisfied and overconfident.
First Corinthians 10:12 provides this warning:
“So let the one who thinks he is standing
beware that he does not fall.”
But you may say: ‘I’m doing my best!
What more can I do?’
Take a good look at your best—scrutinize it.
Examine very closely all you’re doing with the time that you have.
Can mundane activity be replaced with theocratic activity?
What do you see?
Is your best good enough?
It may be; it may not be.
It depends on one’s outlook.
What are some examples?
A runner in a race—he practices; trains;
eats the right things; keeps a lean, healthy body;
wears the best running shoes; and so forth.
He gives his best
but loses the race to someone faster.
His best was not good enough.
Why?
It was compared to whether he was faster than his competitors.
Yohan Blake lost to Usain Bolt
in a 100-meter event in 2012
by just a fraction of a second.
He did his best, but his best wasn’t good enough.
A mother and daughter
—the daughter is in the second grade at school.
She brings home a picture she drew in class.
The teacher had put a B- on the picture.
The daughter shows it to her mother,
and the mother crosses out the B-
and puts an A+ on it.
She then tapes the picture on the refrigerator.
What is the difference between the teacher and the mother?
The teacher compares the student to other classmates of her age.
The mother grades her according to her best,
not in comparison with others.
Jehovah does not compare your best with the best of others.
Let’s look at Psalm 103:14.
When Jehovah examines our spiritual accomplishments,
what’s one of his measuring sticks?
Psalm 103:14:
“For he well knows how we are formed,
remembering that we are dust.”
“Dust” is used figuratively,
indicating mankind’s frailty and lowliness.
By “remembering that we are dust,”
Jehovah never asks more of us than we can give.
However, he expects us to obey his commands
to the best of our own ability.
Mark 12:30 —you can likely quote it from memory.
Verse 30 says:
“You must love Jehovah your God
“with your whole heart
“and with your whole soul
“and with your whole mind
and with your whole strength.”
This embraces everything we have —all that we are.
You go in service;
you use “your whole strength” to accomplish it.
That’s commendable.
But what good is it to use our whole strength
to go in service if our mind
cannot direct our tongue
to say the right things when we talk to a person?
‘I used a lot
‘of my strength walking
‘from door to door, climbing stairs, and so forth.
‘And yet, no one let me get past
my introduction.’
Question: Was that the best introduction you could give?
How long have you been using that introduction?
Would a new one help?
Would using “your whole mind”
by means of advance preparation
result in making your best even better?
Have you tried to use some of the introductions
demonstrated at our midweek meetings
or some of those found in the Reasoning From the Scriptures  book,
pages 9-15?
What does the householder see
in your face
when she opens the door?
Is your countenance
radiating pleasantness and kindness?
Does she see good news or bad news?
Do you look happy or sad?
The message we’re commissioned to deliver today
is the “good news of the Kingdom.”
We expect it to change sometime in the near future.
Do the best you can until you know better.
Then when you know better, you can do better.
You attend all congregation meetings
and pay rapt attention with your mind.
You’re to be commended.
But is that all that’s required
to love Jehovah with our whole mind?
Are we meditating on the knowledge
that we receive at our meetings
in order to draw close to Jehovah?
James 4:8 says:
“Draw close to God, and he will draw close to you.”
That’s one benefit we receive from our meeting attendance.
Let’s read Hebrews 10:24, 25.
This is another benefit of regular meeting attendance.
In this way, we give and receive encouragement.
Verses 24 and 25 read:
“And let us consider one another
“so as to incite to love and fine works,
“not forsaking our meeting together,
“as some have the custom,
“but encouraging one another,
“and all the more so
as you see the day drawing near.”
Do you give comments at meetings?
Are they well-prepared?
Do they encourage your brothers and sisters?
Are you giving your best?
If so, then your best is good enough.
What about your personal study
or family worship?
Are you doing your best?
Is your best good enough?
“I read all The Watchtowers  and Awakes!  when they come out,” you say.
It goes without saying that that’s good.
What did you find in what you read
that will deepen your love and appreciation for Jehovah
and draw you closer to him?
Do you use your whole mind
to meditate and continue to think about it,
thus spiking it down deep into your heart?
Some things we learn
may not be immediately applicable
but can be regurgitated
and applied later as needed.
Are you giving serious attention
to the spiritual needs of your wife and children?
Yes, you have family worship most weeks.
That’s commendable.
Do you prepare well for it
or just throw something together at the last minute?
What if your wife just threw something on the table
for dinner each evening
without giving any thought to the health needs of the family?
Think: Is your best good enough?
We can slop a pig, and he’ll enjoy it.
But give the same garbage to a cow, and she’ll ignore it.
Why are we considering
“Is Your Best Good Enough?”
It’s only as a reminder
to look at what we think to be our best
in what we’re doing for ourselves, our families,
and our spiritual brothers and sisters.
And remember, our best is not compared
with the best of another brother or sister.
Only Jehovah knows
when we’re doing our best.
He is a righteous and fair Judge.
Our knowledge, even of ourself,
can be faulty because of inherited sin.
Therefore, it’s wisdom on our part
to keep examining ourselves
to see where we might improve.
So is your best good enough?
I’d like to think it is.
What do you think?

cn.text: 这个演讲的题目是
《你的最好，足够好吗？》
我想先读出加拉太书6:4
经文说
要“察验自己所做的事”
所以你可以问问自己
“我和耶和华的关系好吗？
我经常参加基督徒的聚会吗？
参加聚会时
我努力举手发表评论，鼓励别人吗？
我的个人研读做得怎么样？
我尽力参与各种形式的传道工作吗？
在去续访别人之前，我认真准备吗？
我和感兴趣的人研读圣经吗？
开始讨论后，我尽力帮助圣经学生吗？”
事实上，这些问题都是在问
“我的最好，足够好吗？”
我们可能看到会众里的其他人
比我们做得更多
但当再一次看加拉太书6:4时
经文明确说我们不应该跟别人比较
所以我们很快就认定
自己已经尽力了
然后对自己说
我做的已经足够多，足够好了
但不要忘记经文的前半部分
经文说
我们要“察验自己所做的事”
我们需要把自己实际做的
和能够做的，做个比较
不要觉得我们做的已经够了
没有进步的空间了
我们应该尽力做到最好
哥林多前书10:12劝告我们说
也许你会说
“我已经尽力了，我还需要改善吗？”
你真的尽力了吗？
要好好察验一下自己
你所做的事有没有一些是不太重要的呢？
你可以把这些时间
用来做跟崇拜上帝有关的事吗？
你觉得怎么样？
你的最好，足够好吗？
可能是，也可能不是
这取决于和谁比较
我们来看几个例子
比如赛跑选手
他要努力训练，吃有营养的食物
控制体重，保持健康
也要有最好的装备，比如运动鞋
他尽了自己最大的努力
但还是输给了其他选手
他的最好，还不够好
为什么呢？
因为他想要赢得比赛
就要跑得比其他选手快
2012年，约翰·布莱克在100米赛跑中
只以零点几秒之差输给了尤塞恩·博尔特
他做到了自己的最好，但他的最好还不够好
再看一个例子
有一个女孩上小学二年级
她把自己在课上画的画带回家
老师给她的打分是B，就是良好
她把画拿给妈妈看
妈妈把老师打的B划掉了，在旁边改成了A+
然后她把女儿的画贴在冰箱上
为什么老师和妈妈的打分不同呢？
老师把这个女孩的画和其他同学作比较
而妈妈则知道她的女儿已经做到了她的最好
耶和华上帝不会把你的最好跟别人的比较
来看看诗篇103:14
当耶和华衡量我们为他做的服务时
他会用什么标准来看我们呢？
这里的“尘土”是一种比喻
指人类的脆弱和渺小
他记得我们是尘土
所以他从来不会对我们有过度的要求
但是他也希望我们能够遵守他的诫命
努力做到自己的最好
你也许记得
马可福音12:30
经文说
经文提到，我们要用自己的一切崇拜上帝
去传道时，你可能付出了很多的体力
这值得称赞
不过，虽然我们这样努力出去传道
但如果我们没有全神贯注、全心全意
就不能说出合适的话，打动别人的心
“我花了很多力气，挨家挨户地拜访
爬了很多楼梯
不过，我说完介绍词后
没有人愿意继续聊下去。”
问题来了
你确定这是你能做的最好的介绍词吗？
这个介绍词你已经用了多长的时间了呢？
可以换个新的吗？
即使你认为你已经做到了最好
但你能不能够更加全心全意地投入
准备更好的介绍词呢？
你用过周中聚会提到的对话建议吗？
或者你用过
《根据圣经而推理》这本书9-15页
《传道可用的引言》吗？
住户开门时会看到你脸上有什么表情呢？
你的表情是亲切又友善的吗?
他会觉得
你是带给他好消息还是坏消息呢？
你看起来是开心还是伤心呢？
我们现在和别人分享的
是“上帝王国的好消息”
但我们知道，我们传的消息将会改变
现在就要尽力做到最好
不过，当你发现自己的确需要作出调整
那就努力调整吧
会众的聚会，你全都参加并留心认真听吗？
你做得很好
但这是不是代表
你对耶和华上帝的爱是全心全意的呢？
我们有没有花时间好好沉思
在聚会中学到的内容，从而更亲近上帝呢？
雅各书4:8说
“你们要亲近上帝，上帝就会亲近你们。”
这就是我们参加聚会能够得到的一大益处
我们再看看希伯来书10:24,25
参加聚会还有一个益处
也就是我们可以互相鼓励
你在聚会时发表评论吗？
你是认真准备的吗？
你的评论鼓励到弟兄姐妹了吗？
你努力做到最好了吗？
如果是的话，那你的最好，就够好了
你的个人研读或家庭崇拜做得怎么样呢？
你尽力做到最好吗？
你的最好，够好吗？
你可能会说
“最新的《守望台》和《警醒！》我都读了。”
毫无疑问，你做得很好
你所读到的这些内容
是否帮助你加深对耶和华的爱和感激
从而更亲近他呢？
你是否全心全意沉思学到的内容
内心受到激励
愿意为耶和华做得更多呢？
我们学到的一些内容可能不会马上应用
但可以花时间慢慢咀嚼，在需要时实践出来
作为丈夫和父亲
你尽力帮助妻子和孩子亲近耶和华吗？
你可能经常举行家庭崇拜，这值得称赞
但你认真准备了吗？
还是在开始前才决定学习的内容呢？
如果妻子只是随便做做晚餐
而且每次都这样
完全不考虑家人的健康需要
你觉得怎么样呢？
想一想
你的最好，够好吗？
如果把我们吃剩不要的东西给猪吃
它吃得很开心
但给牛吃，它连理都不理
为什么我们要讨论今天这个主题呢？
这只是一个提醒，帮助我们可以仔细想想
怎样尽全力崇拜耶和华，照顾家人
以及帮助会众里的弟兄姐妹
请记住
不要拿我们的最好
跟其他弟兄姐妹的最好作比较
只有耶和华知道
我们是否已经尽力做到了最好
他是公平正义的审判官
因为我们都不完美
不能总是清楚地了解自己
所以我们不断察验自己
看看有哪一些需要改进的地方
是非常明智的
那么你的最好足够好吗？
我相信是的
你觉得呢？

titles.ko: 새뮤얼 F. 허드: 정말 최선을 다하고 있습니까?
titles.en: Samuel F. Herd: Is Your Best Good Enough?
titles.cn: 塞缪尔·赫德：你的最好，足够好吗？

ko.text: 길르앗 제145기 학급을 졸업한 두 분은
가족이 모두 큰 위험에 처하셨을 텐데요.
갑자기 이웃 사람들을 죽이기 시작하는 걸 보면서
여호와의 증인이었던 고모와 함께 살게 되었습니다.
「영원히 살 수 있다」 책으로 연구를 했는데,
전쟁에 나가는 군인들을 축복하는 삽화가 있었어요.
하지만 회중 형제 자매들은 서로 사랑하고 격려했어요.
심지어는 생명을 무릅쓰고 서로를 보호해 주었습니다.
형제 가족은 학살의 직접적인 피해를 입진 않았지만,
돈이 하나도 없어서 먹을 걸 사지 못했습니다.
어머니가 우리 자녀들에게 해 줄 수 있는 게 없어서
장로 형제들은 외국에 있는 우리 형제 자매들이
이 돈을 보내 주었다고 말해 주었습니다.
여전히 자리에 누워 계신 어머니께 돈을 드렸습니다.
비관적이 되지 않는 데 무엇이 도움이 되셨나요?
예를 들어, 부활 희망과 죽은 자의 상태에 관해 말할 때,
사랑하는 사망한 가족이 고통을 겪고 있지 않고,
앞으로 부활될 것이라는 확신이 더 강해집니다.
서로 사랑하라는 예수의 명령을 반복해서 말하고 있죠.
당시 그리스도인들은 박해를 받고 있었기 때문에,
그들의 삶에서 새롭게 실천할 필요가 있었습니다.
예수께서 서로 사랑하라고 하신 이 명령을
그 점을 다시 한 번 깨닫게 해 주었습니다.
우리 형제 자매들을 사랑해야 한다는 사실을 말이죠.
우리가 여러분 모두를 사랑한다는 걸 기억해 주세요.

en.text: With us today, we have Eugene and Odile Nteziryayo.
They’ve graduated from the 145th class of Gilead,
and they lived through this mayhem.
Odile, now, your family is Tutsi,
and this must have certainly put them in danger.
The killing was happening all over the country,
so my parents and my brother were killed.
I saw that some religious leaders were involved
in killing people in the genocide.
I couldn’t believe how friendly people
who were previously living together
now started killing their neighbors.
How did you get contact with the truth?
So after the genocide, I was taken in by my aunt
whose family were Jehovah’s Witnesses,
so I began studying the Bible with them.
I was in the Live Forever  book.
I saw a picture of a priest blessing people in the church,
and then he was blessing troops who were going to kill.
But also I could see how brothers and sisters in the congregation
would love and encourage.
And they risked their lives to take care of one another.
Oh, that’s touching.
Now, Eugene,
your family was not a direct target of the violence,
but what other hardships did you face?
The economic situation was very difficult.
My family had no money,
and they could not buy food.
I remember my mom
—I can still see her lying on the bed in complete despair,
not knowing what she could do for us children.
The elders asked me to go to the Kingdom Hall,
and when I arrived,
they handed me 18,000 Rwandan francs.
The elders told me that my brothers and sisters from abroad
offered us this gift.
So I immediately ran back home,
found my mom still lying on the bed,
and gave her the money.
I can still see my mom crying
because of the joy
and thankfulness of what the brothers had done.
Excellent.
Now, looking back at all the injustices you and your family have suffered,
Odile, what has helped you to not become a bitter person?
The preaching work is very important to me
because the more I talk about the Bible’s promises,
the more they become real to me.
For example, when I talk about the resurrection hope
and the condition of the dead,
this helps me to feel
that my loved ones are not suffering anymore
and they are waiting to be resurrected.
So this makes me feel happy.
The scripture that comes to mind is
where the apostle John repeated Jesus’ command
of loving one another just as Jesus loved us.
Christians during that time were facing persecution,
and now they needed a fresh application of that scripture in their lives.
We all love one another,
but during difficult moments
like the ones our brothers in Rwanda went through,
they needed that fresh application
of this very commandment of Jesus:
loving one another to the point
of risking our lives for our brothers.
Being here in Gilead has reminded me of that fact
—that I really need to love my brothers and sisters
as Jesus loved us.
You brothers and sisters in Rwanda
have given us a wonderful example
of courage and faith and love.
Please know that we love you all very much.
Thank you.
Thank you for joining us
on this edition of Extraordinary Experiences.

cn.text: 今天我们邀请到一对夫妻，尤金和欧黛儿
他们是基列学校145届的毕业生
曾经经历过一段非常可怕的时期
欧黛儿，你的家人是图西族
他们当时一定非常危险，是吗？
当时，全国境内发生了大屠杀
我的父母和我的弟弟都被杀害了
在这场屠杀中
我看到一些宗教领袖也参与其中
我不敢相信
曾经那么友好，生活在一起的人们
竟然开始彼此杀害
你是怎么开始认识真理的？
大屠杀结束后，我就开始跟我的姑姑一起住
他们一家人都是耶和华见证人
于是我就开始学习圣经了
《永远生活》是我当时学的书
我看到一张图片是牧师在教堂为人们祷告
然后他也为准备上战场杀人的军队祷告
但是我却看到在会众里的弟兄姐妹
彼此相爱、互相鼓励
他们甚至冒着生命危险去照顾彼此
真的很感动
那……尤金
你的家人虽然没有被直接伤害
但你面对了什么其他难题呢？
当时的经济状况非常差
我们没有钱
所以没有办法买食物
我还记得
我看着我的妈妈躺在床上
非常绝望的那个样子
她心里可能想着
她能够做些什么
才能够为我们孩子们买到东西吃
有一天，长老们要我到王国聚会所
我到了以后
他们给了我1万8000卢旺达法郎
他们告诉我
这笔钱是国外的弟兄姐妹给我们的礼物
我拿了钱，马上就跑回家
看到我的妈妈仍然躺在床上
然后我给了她这笔钱
她就感动得流下眼泪来
因为弟兄姐妹的爱心
让她感到喜悦又充满感激
很鼓励人
那……欧黛儿
你和你的家人经历到一些不公正的事
是什么帮助你没有成为一个充满仇恨的人？
传道工作对我非常重要
因为我提到越多次上帝的承诺
这些承诺就对我越真实
比如，当我谈论到
复活的希望和人死后的情况时
就让我明白，我的亲人现在没有经历痛苦
他们正在等待复活
这些真理都让我感到很欣慰
我想起约翰一书2:6,7说的话
在那里，使徒约翰重复了耶稣的命令
要我们彼此相爱，就像耶稣爱我们一样
我们基督徒在面对迫害的时候
我们就必须把这条圣经的原则实际运用出来
我们爱弟兄姐妹
不过，像卢旺达的弟兄姐妹所经历的一样
他们必须用另一种方式
实践这条圣经的原则
耶稣的命令就是我们要彼此相爱
甚至甘愿冒生命危险，保护我们的弟兄姐妹
在这里，基列学校的课程提醒我
真正爱弟兄姐妹是什么意思
我真的要爱我的弟兄姐妹
就像耶稣基督爱我们所有人一样
卢旺达的弟兄姐妹真的非常有勇气
也充满信心和爱心，立下了很好的榜样
我们很感动
-谢谢      -谢谢
谢谢大家收看这一集的非常访谈

ko.text: 이런 날이 올 줄은 상상도 못했어요.
오늘은 우리 모두가 고대하던 특별한 날입니다.
이야기는 몇 년 전으로 거슬러 올라가죠.
순회 감독자 형제 부부를 식사에 초대하고 싶으신 분들은 ...
순회 방문과 이 연설 주제가 계기가 되었죠.
화요일에 순회 감독자가 할 연설 주제는
음, 빌립에게서 뭘 배울 수 있을까?
우리 가족은 이미 영적으로 잘하고 있다고 생각했어요.
아내와 딸들도 회중 일을 잘 돕고 있었죠.
전 왕국회관 유지 보수 작업에도 참여했습니다.
가족 숭배 때 빌립에 관해 조사해 보기로 했습니다.
하지만 그는 훨씬 더 많은 일을 했죠.
박해 때문에 빌립은 예루살렘에서 사마리아로 가야 했네요.
사마리아는 그때까지 여호와의 말씀을 받아들이지 않았어요.
하지만 빌립은 자신이 겪은 시련을 영적인 기회로 보았죠.
많은 사람이 그 소식을 믿고 침례를 받았죠.
빌립은 필요한 곳이 어디든 기꺼이 봉사했네요.
또 늘 열심 있는 태도를 유지했죠.
20년 후에도, 여전히 복음 전파자로 알려져 있었어요.
그때쯤엔 빌립의 삶에 큰 변화가 있었네요.
딸 넷을 둔 가장이 되어 있었으니까요.
해 볼 수 있는 몇 가지 것들을 생각해 봤습니다.
순회 감독자를 점심에 초대하는 것부터 시작했어요.
빌립처럼, 저에게도 예상치 못한 변화가 찾아왔어요.
몇 달 동안, 직업을 잃게 됐거든요.
다양한 시간대에 사람들을 찾아갈 수 있었죠.
왕국 전파자 학교를 졸업하는 모습을 보고 있습니다.
더 열심 있는 복음 전파자가 되게 해 주었습니다.

en.text: Please find your seats.
It’s time to start our graduation program.
We never dreamed this would happen.
This is a very special day all of us have been anxiously waiting for.
We’re happy to see all of you here.
It all started a few years ago.
If you’d like to have the circuit overseer and his wife for a meal . . .
It was during that visit and this question.
His theme on Tuesday is
“What Lessons Can We Learn
From Philip the Evangelizer?”
Hmm.
What could we learn from Philip?
Honestly, we were already busy with the right things.
Lilly and the girls helped out wherever they could.
I worked on Kingdom Hall maintenance projects.
And we had a regular schedule for the ministry.
But like in a lot of places,
when someone showed interest,
it was tough to find them again.
I wondered if our spiritual routine needed an update.
Looking forward to that talk,
I decided we’d research Philip for family worship
—Acts chapter 6.
Philip was one of seven brothers
selected to distribute food to Christian widows in Jerusalem.
That was an important assignment,
but he did so much more than that.
Hmm, this is interesting.
Because of the persecution,
Philip had to flee from Jerusalem to Samaria.
Samaria hadn’t accepted the word of Jehovah yet.
But Philip saw that trial as a spiritual opportunity.
Samaria was largely untouched by the preaching work.
Philip declared the good news zealously,
and many believed and got baptized.
But sometime later,
an angel spoke with him.
He told Philip to “get up and go to the south.”
That led him to find the Ethiopian eunuch and preach in other cities.
Philip was willing to serve wherever there was a need.
And he always kept that evangelizing spirit.
Some twenty years later, he was still known as “the evangelizer.”
By that time, his life had changed.
He was a family man with four daughters.
But that didn’t stop him from showing hospitality
when Paul and his companions came to visit.
Visits like that must have been
full of spiritual lessons for his daughters.
That night, we came up with a few things we wanted to do.
We started by having the circuit overseer to lunch.
We hadn’t made time for that in a while.
Alex and Carla’s experiences
made the girls excited to reach their own spiritual goals.
But like Philip, changes came that we didn’t expect.
I was out of work for a few months.
It was a stressful time
but also a spiritual opportunity.
I could visit people at different times of the day.
We tried to make the most of the situation and preach zealously
like Philip.
And here we are,
watching our girls graduate from the School for Kingdom Evangelizers.
Those few lessons
made a big difference for this family
of evangelizers.

cn.text: 请各位就座
毕业典礼即将开始
我们从没想过会参加这个毕业典礼
今天是很特别的一天
我们都期待已久
我们很高兴看到你们所有人
-这要从几年前说起 -都出席今天的毕业典礼
如果你想请分区监督和他的太太吃饭
-改变都是因为那次的探访和当时的演讲 -请跟王弟兄联络......
分区监督星期二的演讲题目是
《我们从传福音者腓力身上学到什么？》
嗯，我们能从腓力身上学到什么呢？
老实说，我们已经很努力地为上帝服务了
哪里有需要，莉莉和女儿们都会去帮忙的
我呢
就负责聚会所的维修保养工作
我们都会在固定的时间出去传道
但像很多地方一样
每次我们找到感兴趣的人
下一次就很难再见到他们了
我在想
我们出来传道的时间是不是该调整了？
因为很期待分区监督的演讲
我决定在家庭崇拜的时候，研读腓力的记载
在使徒行传第6章
在耶路撒冷
有7位弟兄被委派分配食物给基督徒的寡妇
腓力也是其中一位
那是一个很重要的任务
但腓力做的还不止这些
嗯，这很有意思
因为被迫害
他必须从耶路撒冷逃到撒马利亚
当时撒马利亚人
大多没听过上帝话语的好消息
但腓力却把这个考验
看作是为耶和华做更多服务的机会
那时撒马利亚地区大部分还没有人去传道
腓力热心地传讲好消息
很多人都相信，而且还受浸了
但过了一段时间之后
有一位天使来跟他说话
天使对他说，你要往南走
腓力顺着指引就找到了埃塞俄比亚的内臣
之后又去其他城镇传道
不管哪里有需要，腓力都很愿意去
他总是热心地传道
大约20年后
大家还是称他为“传福音者”
那个时候，他的生活已经改变了
他已经结婚了，而且有4个女儿
但他非常热情好客
把握机会招待保罗和他的同伴
这样的场合一定加强了他的女儿
对耶和华的信心
那天晚上我们就列出了几件我们想做的事
首先，我们请分区监督吃午餐
我们已经很久没这样做了
志明跟嘉玲的经验让女儿们很想立下目标
为耶和华做更多服务
但就像腓力一样
我们也碰到了意想不到的事
我失业了，而且好几个月都找不到工作
那段时间我的压力不小
但我把握机会为耶和华做更多服务
我可以在不同的时间去拜访别人
我们利用失业的这段时间更热心地传道
就像腓力一样
就这样，我们来到了这里
参加女儿们王国传福音者训练班的毕业典礼
从腓力身上学到的事
真的彻底地改变了我们这一家

ko.text: 늘 제게 여호와에 대한 사랑을 심어 주려고 노력하셨어요.
하지만 전 자라면서 외로움을 많이 느꼈는데,
친구들 중에 생활 방식이나, 말하는 방식이나,
듣는 음악이 저와 맞는 사람이 없는 것 같았거든요.
어떤 표준을 따라야 할까?’ 하고 늘 고민했죠.
친구가 생길 수도, 혼자가 될 수도 있었으니까요.
안타깝게도 그중에는 저와 친한 사람들도 있었어요.
저는 그리스도인 가정에서 태어나 자랐기 때문에,
하고 끊임없이 자신을 다잡는 게 정말 힘들었어요.
기도를 하고 집에 가서 엄마한테 말씀드렸더니
그 순간 여호와께서 제게 이렇게 말씀하시는 것 같았어요.
네 앞에는 많은 축복이 기다리고 있어.
정말 멋진 삶을 살게 될 거야.
친한 친구 한 명은 저와 비슷한 유혹을 뿌리치지 못하고
얼마 후 그 친구는 여호와께 돌아왔습니다.
하루는 그 친구와 영상 통화를 하는데,
“엄마는 왜 여호와를 안 믿는 사람하고 결혼했어요?”
그 어린 딸은 여호와의 표준을 따라야 한다는 걸 이해한 거죠.
사람들이 생명의 길로 돌아오게 도울 수 있다는 건
그는 선한 마음을 가졌기 때문에 여호와께 용서받았지만,
자신의 행동에 따른 결과를 감당해야 했죠.
저는 여호와를 떠나지 않았기 때문에 많은 축복을 받았어요.
중요한 건 여호와 곁에 계속 머무르는 거예요.
이보다 더 행복한 삶은 없다는 확신이 들 거예요.
진리를 떠난 사람들을 보면 돌아왔다 해도,
힘든 짐을 안고 살아가는 경우를 종종 볼 수 있죠.
진리를 떠나는 건 아무 유익이 없다는 걸
저희 가족은 많은 축복을 누리고 있어요.
가장으로서 저는 네 자녀를 모두 진리 안에서 양육했죠.
저는 여호와의 방식을 따른 덕분에 큰 축복을 누리고 있어요.
사탄은 처음에는 여러분을 즐겁게 해 줄지 몰라요.
제가 받은 가장 아름다운 선물 중 하나는
저는 여호와께서 많은 축복을 주실 뿐만
아니라 각자에게 꼭 맞는 선물을 주신다고 확신합니다.
가장 좋은 선생님은 경험이 아니라 여호와이십니다.

en.text: I was born to two Christian parents;
they always tried to instill in us a love for Jehovah.
But I felt quite lonely growing up,
and I felt like I didn’t have people who wanted to do the same things
—the lifestyle, the way they spoke, the music they were listening to—
and so for me, the real struggle was where do I stand?
Where are my boundaries going to be set?
It’s really hard because it could mean
the difference between having a friend and not having a friend.
Over the years, I have talked to several
who’ve perhaps drifted a little bit in the truth.
And that unfortunately happened to some of my friends.
Nobody is immune to the pressures of the world.
I was born and raised by Christian parents,
so all through my childhood and teenage years,
I was happy serving Jehovah,
but it got a little bit harder when I started to work.
People at work would ask me
to do social activities with them, go for a drink and things,
but there were men who would ask me to go out with them.
It’s flattering when someone shows interest in you, so it was nice,
but it was hard to have to constantly remind myself,
‘Well, you know that this is not going to be successful;
you know this person doesn’t love Jehovah.’
I remember one day I drove into a parking lot,
and I just prayed to Jehovah with tears in my eyes, and I said:
“This is too hard. This is just too hard.
“The people that are my friends are starting to leave the truth.
I feel quite lonely, but I want to serve you.”
After that prayer I went home, I spoke to my mom,
and she got really quiet, and she just looked at me and said,
“Anything Jehovah tells you is to benefit yourself.”
And it clicked in that moment that Jehovah was saying to me: “I love you.
“I will carry you through this time, and you’ll see
“that there will be all these blessings that’ll open up to you,
“and you’ll have a really wonderful, colorful life,
but you have to hang in there.”
Even though it was hard, I resisted the temptation,
but someone close to me who faced the same pressure
gave in and ended up leaving Jehovah.
When I heard
that she was disfellowshipped,
it just completely hit me so hard
because you really are just worried
about what is going to happen with their future.
After a while, she did come back to Jehovah.
She’s raising a child on her own.
One day we were having a video chat
with the little one just playing in the background,
and she suddenly turned around and said,
“Mummy, why did you marry someone who doesn’t love Jehovah?”
She understood that we need to live according to Jehovah’s standards.
As elders, we can help people to get up and get back on the path to life,
and it’s a real pleasure.
I’m reminded about the account of David.
Eventually he was forgiven by Jehovah because he had a good heart;
however, there were consequences all through his life.
I’ve received so many blessings for sticking to Jehovah.
I found a lovely brother to marry in the Christian congregation,
and we’re very happy together.
The thing to do is to just stick with Jehovah.
“Taste and see that Jehovah is good,”
and when you do that, you will appreciate
that there is absolutely no need
to go anywhere else.
Having observed what has happened to people who have left the truth
and the baggage they sometimes end up carrying
when they come back in the truth makes me feel that it’s just not worth it.
Really, Jehovah is like a parent; he wants to protect us and care for us.
Things will always work out for the best if you do things Jehovah’s way.
I feel my family has had many blessings.
As a husband and a father,
I’ve got four children who have all grown up in the truth.
They’ve all gone on to have good theocratic lives,
where they’ve enjoyed many privileges of service.
So for me, it’s been a real blessing to do things Jehovah’s way.
I think when you test out the world,
Satan will give you immediate satisfaction,
but when you serve no purpose to him anymore, that’s it.
One of the most beautiful blessings I’ve received is people
—people around you who love Jehovah
and who want to serve him the way you do.
I really strongly believe that Jehovah
not only gives us a lot of blessings
but gives us blessings that he’s handpicked for us.
My observation would be
that experience is not the best teacher; Jehovah is the best Teacher.

cn.text: 我出生时
父母就是耶和华见证人
从小，他们就教导我们要爱耶和华
但我在长大的过程中觉得非常孤单
因为周围同学的生活方式、说话方式
还有他们喜欢听的音乐
都跟我很不一样
但真正困难的是
我要选择成为一个怎样的人
我的界线要在哪里
因为这关系到
以后会不会有人跟我做朋友
多年来
我一直试着帮助几个信心软弱的人
可惜的是
我有一些朋友
情况也是这样
我们每个人
都可能受到这个世界的影响
我在耶和华见证人的家庭长大
所以我在童年和青少年时期
都一直快乐地崇拜耶和华
但我开始工作以后
情况就有一点改变了
我的同事约我出去一起玩
一起吃点东西
也开始有男生约我出去
当有人开始关注你
对你有意思
这种感觉真的很好
我觉得很挣扎
需要不断提醒自己
让自己知道这样做不会快乐的
这个人他不爱耶和华
我记得有一天
我在车里哭着跟耶和华祷告说
“这太难了！真的太难了
我尽力只跟爱你的人做朋友
但他们也渐渐远离你了
我觉得好孤单
但我想继续崇拜你。”
我回家后也把心里的感觉跟妈妈说了
她静静地听，然后看着我说
“耶和华定下这些要求是因为他很爱你。”
那一刻
我好像听到耶和华在跟我说
“我会帮助你渡过难关
有很多美好的福分正等着你
你的人生将会非常精彩
但你必须坚持下去。”
虽然很不容易
但我还是成功抵抗住了引诱
不过，我的一个好朋友却向压力屈服了
最终离开了耶和华
当我听说她被会众开除的时候
我的心里
真的非常
非常难过
她将来的生活会怎么样
我真的很担心
一段时间后
她回到耶和华的身边
但她成了一个单亲妈妈
有一天，我打电话给她，和她聊天
我看到她的孩子在后边玩

en.text: In Nehemiah’s day, the Jews joyfully embarked
on a massive building project.
With Jehovah’s direction and help,
they were able to finish the work
in just 52 days.
You look like you’ve been working.
During the production of the film
Nehemiah: “The Joy of Jehovah Is Your Stronghold,”
the walls of Jerusalem were built once again,
but this time at the Mount Ebo studios in Brewster, New York.
A variety of skills were needed to produce this drama
with many volunteers coming together,
using their time, energy, and abilities
to create an accurate teaching tool.
And they found great joy in their work.
Good planning was needed right at the start of production.
Every day began with a Scriptural discussion
and prayer.
The costume and makeup departments
prepared the actors to appear on set.
Assistance was provided to help actors
feel more comfortable in front of the cameras.
And action!
Brothers, please.
Have they attacked anyone yet?
They must have.
No! But they will.
While the production team was filming in one studio,
sets were being prepared in another.
To add to the realism, detailed props were made
—many using 3D printing.
With all of these researched and crafted costumes,
sets, and props combined,
environments were designed to accurately recreate the time period.
But even more was needed to convey what it was like
to live in Jerusalem during Nehemiah’s day.
For example, there were many animals on set.
Even after principal filming was completed,
sets built in the studio were extended
using advanced visual effects.
Digital construction work was done
by the visual effects team.
Yes, building is a legacy of God’s people.
Nehemiah was one of many who throughout history
devoted their energies to supporting the work of building.
In a similar way, the production team that made
Nehemiah: “The Joy of Jehovah Is Your Stronghold,”
joyfully worked hard to produce a film
that helps build love and appreciation
in the hearts of God’s people.

title: 게리 브로: 여호와께서 우리를 틀 잡으시게 하십시오 (이사야 64:8)

ko.text: 오늘의 성구 이사야 64:8에서 분명히 알려 주듯이,
여호와 하느님은 도공이시고, 사실 위대한 도공이시고,
그럼 그분은 어떤 식으로 우리를 빚고 틀 잡으십니까?
이제 우리는 여호와께서 우리의 성품을 틀 잡기 위해
이 세 가지 방법을 어떻게 사용하시는지
첫 번째로 여호와께서는 그분의 말씀인 성경을 사용해
하느님의 말씀에 엄청난 힘이 있다고 했습니다.
자신의 성품을 점검하면서 이런 자문을 해 볼 수 있죠.
‘이걸 보면 나에 대해 뭘 알 수 있지?
이 성구가 얼마나 도움이 되는지 보시죠.
남을 자기보다 더 나은 사람으로 여기십시오.
여러분 자신의 일에만 관심을 갖지 말고
자신을 살펴보면서 이렇게 자문해 볼 수 있죠.
특히 이 부면에서 과거에 어려움이 있었다면 어떠한가?
겸손에 대해 이렇게 또 자문해 보십시오.
‘나는 늘 중요한 위치에 있는 사람처럼 행동하는가?
이런 식으로 생각해 볼 수도 있죠.
‘저 자매는 정말 나보다 참을성이 더 많아.
저 형제는 진짜 나보다 더 잘 가르쳐.’
우리의 생각을 틀 잡아 주실 수 있습니다.
‘뭘 배울 수 있지? 그분은 어떻게 하셨지?
어떻게 적용할 수 있나?’ 하고 자문해 보세요.
“그런데 그들 중에 누구를 가장 큰 자로 볼 것인가에 대해
네, 여기 겸손에 문제가 있다는 걸 바로 보실 수 있죠.
도리어 여러분 중에서 가장 큰 자는
인도하는 자는 섬기는 자와 같이 되어야 합니다.
식사를 하는 사람입니까, 아니면 시중드는 사람입니까?
그러나 나는 시중드는 사람으로 여러분 가운데 있습니다.”
그저 말씀만 그렇게 하신 게 아니었죠.
그분이 남기신 겸손의 본을 보고 따를 수 있습니다.
따라서 이렇게 자문해 보는 것이 좋습니다.
다른 사람들에게 그런 인상을 주고 있는가?
나 자신을 “식사를 하는 사람”으로 여기는가 아니면
여호와께서는 우리의 그리스도인 성품을 틀 잡기 위해
어떤 사람이 어떤 행동을 해서 생긴 결과입니다.
혹은 인간 불완전성의 결과로 생기는 것들입니다.
그런 다음 바울은 그와는 달리 “영의 열매”를 언급하는데,
이를 통해 알 수 있는 점은 “영의 열매”로 열거된 특성들은
우리가 더 나은 사람이 되기 위해
우리 마음을 특정한 방향으로 이끌어 줍니다.
성구를 적용하거나 조언에 귀 기울이게 해 줄 수 있죠.
이 그리스도인 특성들을 기를 수 있도록
22절을 보면, 그 특성 중 하나는 친절입니다.
바로잡을 필요가 있다고 느끼실 수 있을까요?
“여호와여, 이 영의 열매를 기르게 꼭 도와주세요”
친절에 관해서도 훌륭한 본이 들어 있습니다.
물론 가장 뛰어난 본이 되는 분은 여호와 하느님이십니다.
7절을 보면 아담과 하와가 열매를 먹은 뒤
자기들이 벌거벗고 있다는 것을 깨닫고 어떻게 했나요?
가시나무와 엉겅퀴가 있는 땅으로 내보내시기 전에
친절한 사람은 좋은 친구들을 쉽게 사귀고
말하거나 행동하는 방식이 부드럽”다고 알려 줍니다.
말하는 방법도 사람들에게 큰 영향을 줍니다.
겸손과 친절 같은 그리스도인 성품을 나타내도록 도우실 때
여호와 하느님께서는 우리를 틀 잡기 위해
따라서 우리 모두는 이런 면에서 발전하기 위해
이사야 64:8에 기록된 것처럼 말할 수 있을 것입니다.
우리는 모두 당신이 손수 만드신 것입니다.”

en.text: Our scripture here, Isaiah 64:8,
clearly establishes
that Jehovah God is the Potter
—the Great Potter, in fact—
and we are the clay.
Now, in what way is he molding us?
Well, one way is through adjusting
our Christian personality.
Now, how does he do that?
Well, he uses his Word —the Bible—
his holy spirit,
and the Christian congregation.
So, what we’re going to do is talk
about how Jehovah helps to mold our personality.
What’s the process that’s used?
We’re going to talk about two aspects of the Christian personality
—humility and kindness.
So we said one way Jehovah uses
to mold our personality is his Word, the Bible.
And Hebrews 4:12 says
that God’s Word has tremendous power.
So we take individual scriptures as we are reading it;
we look at our own personality:
‘What does it say about me?
How can I improve?’
Let’s take an example: humility.
We are going to go to Philippians chapter 2,
verses 3 and 4.
We see how this is a powerful aid to us.
Here’s what we should do,
Philippians 2:3, 4:
“Do nothing out of contentiousness or out of egotism,
“but with humility
“consider others superior to you,
“as you look not only for your own interests,
but also for the interests of others.”
So when we read this scripture, we look at ourselves and say:
‘Well, how am I doing with this?
‘Do I see that I have made progress,
‘especially if this has been an issue in the past?
‘Is Jehovah somehow nudging me, adjusting me,
molding me by means of this powerful scripture?’
Ask yourself about humility:
‘Am I the person that always seems to be in charge?
‘Do I give that attitude across to others?
Or, as it says here, Do I view others as superior?’
Maybe even we’re saying,
“I admit that that sister has more patience than I have,”
or “That brother is really a better teacher than I am.”
So, you see, by means of individual scriptures,
Jehovah God can help to mold our thinking.
Now, in addition to the individual scripture,
the Bible also provides examples
of that quality in action.
And so the Watchtower  comment for today
uses Christ Jesus as an example of humility.
So let’s open to that scripture (it’s referred to)
in Luke chapter 22.
And as we read the account,
we think: ‘What can I learn?
‘How did he handle it?
How can I apply it?’
So Luke 22:24
—this took place the evening before his death.
It says: “However, there also arose a heated dispute among them
over which one of them was considered to be the greatest.”
Well, automatically we see there’s a problem of humility here.
Well, so, let’s move down now
to verses 26 and 27.
He says: “You, though, are not to be that way.
“But let the one who is the greatest among you
“become as the youngest,
“and the one taking the lead as the one ministering.
“For which one is greater,
“the one dining or the one serving?
“Is it not the one dining?
But I am among you as the one serving.”
Now, these were not just words, because the apostles had seen
three and a half years of a beautiful example
of Jesus serving others —truly a humble man.
And through our Bible reading too,
we have seen this example of humility that we can apply.
So it’s good for us to ask ourselves:
‘Am I a proud person?
‘Do I give off that impression to others?
‘Do I view myself as “one dining”
or as “one serving”?’
Well, now, another way that Jehovah uses
to mold our Christian personality
is the holy spirit.
Now, how does that work?
Well, if you look at Galatians 5:19,
it talks about “the works of the flesh.”
And then in verse 22,
it refers to “the fruitage of the spirit”
—“works of the flesh,” “fruitage of the spirit.”
Now, work
is a result of what one does.
It’s the product of your actions.
And so the apostle Paul lists, as you see there, under “works of the flesh,”
various results that come
as a result of a conscious effort on an individual’s part
or possibly because of human imperfection.
But, on the other hand, Paul talks about “the fruitage of the spirit”
—not work, but the fruitage it results in.
And this is implying
that qualities that are listed there as fruitage of the spirit
are not the result of some sort of program we get into
to adjust our character,
but it’s the operation of God’s spirit
upon the individual.
It’s this tremendous force and power from Jehovah God
that moves us in certain ways.
It may be to recognize scripture or to listen to counsel.
Yes, we need to pray for his holy spirit
so that we can develop those Christian qualities that Paul mentions.
So when you look at verse 22, one of those qualities is kindness.
How important is that for the Christian personality?
So when the Great Potter looks at us,
does he see a need for adjustments
in the way we display kindness to others?
See, are we praying to Jehovah God,
“Please, Jehovah, help me develop
this fruitage of the spirit”?
Here, again, the Bible gives examples
of individuals who had kindness.
It’s the quality in action, so to speak.
And in this case, Jehovah God, of course, is the greatest example.
Here it is.
In Genesis chapter 3, it describes in verse 7
that after Adam and Eve ate the fruit, then they recognized their nakedness.
So what did they do?
“They sewed fig leaves together” as clothing.
But, now, in verse 21,
before putting them out of the garden of Eden
into the thorns and thistles, what did Jehovah do?
Well, it says he ‘made long garments
out of skins to clothe them.’
Now, that’s the ultimate kindness.
See, we want to allow these examples to touch us in ways
that move us to be kind to others.
Now, one benefit of kindness is
that people are drawn to that kind of person.
Proverbs 11:17 says this:
“A kind man benefits himself.”
It’s enjoyable being around a kind person, isn’t it?
A kind person easily finds
and keeps good friends.
Now, the Ministry School  textbook says
that “one who is kind and mild-tempered
is gentle in his way of doing things.”
Now, under the chapter “Voice Quality,” here’s what it says:
“People are greatly influenced
“not only by what is said
“but also by how it is said.
“If a person speaking to you has a voice
“that is pleasant, warm, friendly, and kind,
is it not true that you are more inclined to listen favorably?”
Most certainly it is.
And I might say that the November study edition
of The Watchtower  we just received
has a beautiful article in it entitled
“Kindness—A Quality Expressed in Word and Action.”
So when it comes to our Christian personality
—especially involving humility and kindness, as we’ve talked about today—
may each of us respond to the molding of Jehovah God.
He uses his Word —the Bible—
and he uses his holy spirit.
Now, we also said Jehovah uses the congregation.
So may we all be responsive to counsel
that we receive either from the platform
or maybe individual counsel
to improve in these areas.
And if we respond correctly,
then we can say
as recorded at Isaiah 64:8:
“But now, O Jehovah, you are our Father.
“We are the clay, and you are our Potter;
we are all the work of your hand.”
