在路加福音第22章
读的时候，我们可以问问自己
耶稣，他是怎么做的？
我可以怎样学习他？
路加福音22:24
事情发生在耶稣死前的那个晚上
经文说
“可是，他们又激烈地争论
他们哪一个算最大。”
我们清楚地看到使徒们没有表现谦卑
那我们看看接着的经文
在第26和27节
耶稣说
“可是你们不要这样
你们中间最大的，应该像最年轻的
带头的，应该像为人服务的
用餐的和在旁边服务的，哪一个大呢？
不是用餐的吗？
但我在你们中间是为你们服务的。”
耶稣不只是说说而已
在这3年半期间
门徒亲眼看到耶稣怎样为别人服务
他是一个真正谦卑的人
我们也可以亲自从圣经读到这些记载
向耶稣的好榜样学习
所以我们可以问问自己一些问题
我是一个骄傲的人吗？
别人怎么看我？
别人对我有这样的印象吗？
我又是怎么看自己呢？
我觉得自己是用餐的
还是在旁边服务的呢？
接着我们谈另一个方法
耶和华也会运用他的神圣力量来塑造我吗？
耶和华怎么做呢？
在加拉太书5:19提到了
“顺应罪性的行为”
接着在第22节提到了
“神圣力量的果实”
“顺应罪性的行为”和
“神圣力量的果实”
我们都知道，一个人无论做什么事情
有怎样的行为，都会带来某种结果
在加拉太书的第5章
使徒保罗提到了
一些“顺应罪性的行为”
有时，人们自己选择去做这些不对的事
有时，这些行为是因为人的不完美造成的
在另一方面
保罗提到了“神圣力量的果实”
也就是那些因神圣力量而有的品质
不过，我们不能靠着自己的力量
培养这些品质
改变自己的性格
从而变成更好的人
而是要通过耶和华的神圣力量
我们才能培养出这些特质
神圣力量非常强大
是来自耶和华的
它能够帮助我们做任何事
它能够帮助我们
听从或实践圣经的原则
所以我们要求上帝赐给我们神圣力量
帮助我们培养这些美好的基督徒特质
在22节里提到的一个特质是仁慈
对我们来说，仁慈这个特质特别重要
当伟大的陶匠耶和华看我们的时候
他会看出我们需要作出调整
在某方面对人更加仁慈吗？
我们有没有这样祷告呢？
耶和华啊
求你帮助我培养神圣力量的果实
在圣经里
记录了很多待人仁慈的好榜样
现在，让我们看看其中一个好榜样
就是耶和华上帝，他是最好的榜样
创世记3:7提到
亚当夏娃吃了决定善恶之树的果子之后
意识到自己赤身露体
接着，他们做了什么呢？
用无花果树的叶子做了衣服
但在21节
耶和华从伊甸园把他们赶到
长满荆棘和蒺藜的地方之前
他做了什么呢？
他用兽皮给亚当和夏娃做了衣服
你看，这就是真正的仁慈
我们要让圣经里的好榜样触动我们的心
推动我们也向人表现真正的仁慈
一个仁慈的人总是能吸引人亲近他
“仁慈的人让自己得益。”
我想大家都喜欢跟仁慈的人在一起
仁慈的人容易交到好朋友
而且能够维持长久的友谊
在《传道训练班课本》里
有一句话是这样说的
“仁慈而温和的人，待人接物和蔼可亲。”
另外，在同一本书的另一章
《改善音质》这一章里也这样说
“一段话的影响力不但在于内容
也在于说话的方式
你自己不也是喜欢别人用悦耳、亲切
友善、和蔼的声音跟你说话吗？”
一定是的
我邀请你们看看
2018年11月份的研读版《守望台》
里头有一篇文章，题目是
《仁慈——以言语和行动显出的特质》
今天我们提到了两个基督徒的品质
这两个品质分别是谦卑和仁慈
愿我们都接受
上帝通过他的话语圣经
和神圣力量给我们的塑造
培养出这些美好的品质
耶和华也会运用会众来塑造我们
所以
无论是在聚会时弟兄们发表的演讲
还是在私底下某个弟兄姐妹给我们的劝告
愿我们都乐意接受
如果我们这样做
我们就有以赛亚先知那样的精神
他在以赛亚书64:8说
“但耶和华啊，你是我们的父亲
你是陶匠，我们是陶泥
我们全都是你亲手造的。”

ko.text: 이번 보고에서는 가장 중요한 일인 제자 삼는 일에 대해 이야기해 보겠습니다.
중앙장로회는 우리의 봉사를 더 효과적으로 수행할 방법을 계속 찾고 있습니다.
2017 연례 총회에서 소개된 지침과 방향을 발전시키는 것입니다.
그 총회에서 중앙장로회는 고린도 전서 9:26에 근거해
몇 가지 조정된 마련에 대해 발표했죠.
“영원한 생명[에] 합당한 성향을 가진 사람들”을 찾는 데 집중하는 겁니다.
그렇게 하는 데 무엇이 도움이 되었습니까?
지난해에 있었던 일을 몇 가지 살펴보죠.
새로운 사람들이 발전하여 침례를 받도록 돕는 데 집중하고
발전하지 않는 성서 연구는 중단하도록 제안을 받았습니다.
제자 삼는 일과 성서 연구생이 침례받도록 돕는 일에 대해 살펴보았습니다.
정부 관리들에게 하느님의 왕국에 대해 알리기 위해
“합당한 성향을 가진” 사람들을 더 많이 찾기 위해서요.
더 효과적으로 가르치는 데 도움이 될 것입니다.
외국어 및 원주민 토착어 구역을 평가할 것임을 광고했죠.
왜 그와 같은 평가를 하게 되었습니까?
그때 중앙장로회가 장로들에게 전달한 지침은 이렇습니다.
다른 언어를 배워 봉사의 직무를 확장하라는 요청에 호응해 왔습니다.
이 면에서 자기희생적인 노력을 기울이는 전도인들은
발전의 증거가 거의 없다는 점에 유의하였습니다.
잘 발전하는 성서 연구가 거의 없고,
있다고 해도 침례받을 정도로 발전하는 연구생이 매우 드물었습니다.
중앙장로회는 우리가 “허공을 치는 일” 없이 효과적으로 노력을 기울이기 원합니다.’
어떤 방법으로 이러한 언어 집단들과 회중들을 평가했습니까?
바울과 그의 동료들은 봉사를 더 확장하고 싶어 했죠.
‘마케도니아로 건너와서 우리를 도와주십시오’ 하고 그에게 청했다.”
하느님께서 우리를 부르신 것이라는 결론을 내렸기 때문이다.”
물론 우리가 환상을 보는 것은 아니지만
구역 내의 증거를 볼 수 있습니다.
일부 외국어 및 토착어 집단이나 회중의 경우
거의 혹은 전혀 없다는 것을 알게 되었습니다.
해당 언어를 사용하는 사람들을 찾기 위해
먼 거리를 이동해야 하는 경우도 있었죠.
우리의 노력을 다른 곳에 사용하는 것이 더 낫다는 겁니다.
단지 16개 지부 구역의 평가 결과만 살펴보아도
다른 구역에서 섬길 수 있도록 조정되었습니다.
하지만 상황을 더 주의 깊이 조사한 결과,
많은 나라에서 새로 침례받은 사람들의 수가
그 나라의 주요 언어를 쓰는 회중들인 것으로 보입니다.
주요 언어를 사용하는 회중으로 다시 돌아가게 되신다면,
그곳에서 할 일이 정말 많으실 겁니다!
많은 회중은 봉사 구역이 너무 커서 어려움을 겪고 있죠.
수백만 명 이상의 사람들이 살고 있지만
그들에게 전파할 전도인과 파이오니아들의 수는 매우 적습니다.
이러한 구역에서 생산적인 재방문과 성서 연구를 보고하고 있습니다.
또한 많은 장성한 그리스도인들이 회중에 오면서
여러 가지 일을 도울 수 있게 되었죠.
몇몇 지부 위원들의 말을 들어 보겠습니다.
더 많은 수의 전도인들, 유능한 파이오니아들, 임명된 형제들이
가장 생산적인 언어 구역이나 성장 잠재력이 더 큰 구역에
생산성이 더 높은 구역에서 봉사할 수 있도록
왕국 전파자 학교를 졸업한 학생들을 임명할 수 있게 되었습니다.
그 결과 파이오니아들이 봉사에 더 큰 열정이 생겼고
그중 다수가 발전적인 성서 연구를 사회하고 있죠.
많은 형제 자매들이 이러한 변화에 순응하고
기꺼이 조정을 받아들이는 걸 보면 큰 격려가 되죠.
이러한 변화에 감사한다는 말을 수도 없이 한다고 합니다.
새로운 언어를 배우던 많은 형제 자매들은
그들은 새로운 회중에서 더 생산적인 봉사에 전념하게 되었고
영성도 더 잘 돌볼 수 있게 되었죠.
한 형제는 다른 언어를 배우고 있었는데,
그가 속해 있던 회중이 이번 변화로 집단으로 조정되었죠.
그 형제는 묵은 체증이 싹 가시는 느낌이 들었다고 했습니다.
이번 평가 결과로 직접 영향을 받은 몇 사람의 말을 들어 보시죠.
전 지금 포르투갈어 회중에서 섬기고 있는데,
현재 회중으로 옮긴 지 몇 주 만에 연구가 5건이 생겼죠.
전에는 여러 시간 운전해야 겨우 몇 사람 찾을 수 있었죠.
외국인을 만나면 만나는 대로 봉사를 할 수도 있죠.
시간을 알차게 보내는 것 같아서 봉사가 더 즐거워졌습니다.
외국어 봉사가 즐겁긴 했지만 솔직히 시간이 정말 많이 들었어요.
그런데 지금은 집회 프로나 과제를 준비하고
우리가 적용할 점을 함께 이야기할 시간이 더 생겨서 정말 좋아요.
전 개인적으로 여호와와 친밀한 관계를 발전시킬 시간을
더 가질 수 있어서 정말 좋았어요.
다른 집단에서 온 한 형제가 이런 재밌는 말을 했는데요.
“아, 이제 여호와의 계산법이 어떤 건지 알겠네.
그러니까 15명이 새로운 언어를 배워서 한 사람을 돕는 것보다,
그 한 사람이 새로운 언어를 배워서
100명이 넘는 회중 형제 자매들 전체로부터 도움을 받는 게
처음엔 그 언어밖에 할 줄 모르는 사람들이 좀 걱정됐어요.
그런데 결과적으론 그 형제들이 회중과 연합하게 되면서,
이제는 훨씬 더 많은 형제 자매들로부터 돌봄을 받게 된 거죠.
우리 회중 기념식에는 거의 항상 전도인들만 참석했어요.
올해 기념식에 전도인 수의 거의 두 배나 되는 사람들이 참석한 거예요.
그걸 보며 큰 기쁨과 감동을 얻었어요.
우리의 시간과 활력을 쏟고 있다고 느낍니다.
여러분도 이 형제 자매들과 비슷한 상황이라면,
그분이 원하시는 방향으로 노력을 기울여야 합니다.
물론 외국어를 배우는 것도 봉사를 확장하는 한 가지 방법이지만
전파자가 가장 많이 필요한 곳은 어딘가요?
주요 언어를 쓰는 회중 구역일 수 있죠.
여러분의 힘과 역량을 가장 필요로 하는 곳이 어디인지 알아보려면,
순회 감독자에게 문의하거나 지부 사무실에 편지할 수 있습니다.
전염병을 비롯해 그 무엇도 우리의 조직을 막을 수 없습니다!
훨씬 더 큰 성장이 있게 될까요?
한 지부에서는 열 달 연속 전도인 수 신기록을 달성했다고 보고했고,
그 어느 때보다 빠르게 증가하고 있다고 말했습니다.
즉 계속 생산적으로 봉사할 수 있도록 도와주실 것임을 확신합니다.

en.text: For this update, we’re going to focus
on our all-important disciple-making work.
Despite the pandemic,
the Governing Body continues to look for ways
to make our ministry even more effective.
How?
By continuing to build on the direction
provided at the 2017 annual meeting.
At that meeting, the Governing Body
announced organizational adjustments
based on 1 Corinthians 9:26.
That verse says:
“Therefore, the way I am running
“is not aimlessly;
“the way I am aiming my blows is
so as not to be striking the air.”
How do we make our “blows” count?
We focus on what Acts 13:48 mentions
—searching for “those who [are] rightly disposed
for everlasting life.”
How have we been helped to do that?
Consider a few examples from the past year.
We reviewed Watchtower  study articles
that focused on helping new ones progress to baptism
and that reminded us to discontinue unproductive studies.
The 2020 regional convention program
devoted an entire day to the disciple-making work
and to helping Bible students progress to baptism.
Who could forget Neeta and Jade?
Our November campaign included a special effort
to provide government officials with information
about God’s Kingdom,
with the goal of reaching even more
“rightly disposed” ones.
And aren’t we excited to use the new Bible study tool,
Enjoy Life Forever!,
which features a more effective teaching style?
But 2020 saw another significant effort
to make our blows count.
In June 2020,
it was announced that all branches would evaluate
their foreign-language and indigenous-language pregroups,
groups, and congregations.
What was the reason for this evaluation?
Notice what the Governing Body conveyed
to the elders at that time:
“In recent years,
“Jehovah’s people have responded to the call to expand their ministry
“by learning another language in order to reach honesthearted ones,
“and publishers should be commended
“for their self-sacrificing efforts in this regard.
“Nevertheless,
“it has been noted that in some cases
“pregroups or groups show little evidence of growth,
“with few progressive Bible studies
“and few, if any, progressing to baptism.
“In harmony with 1 Corinthians 9:26,
“the Governing Body wants to be certain
that we are making our blows count.”
How were these language groups
and congregations evaluated?
Notice what happened in the first century
when Paul and his companions
wanted to expand their ministry.
Acts 16:6-10 explains
that they traveled many miles
and made concerted efforts to preach in various territories.
However, Jehovah, through his holy spirit,
directed them to the right area.
Let’s read this at Acts 16:9:
“And during the night
“a vision appeared to Paul
“—a Macedonian man was standing there
“urging him and saying:
‘Step over into Macedonia and help us.’”
How did they respond?
Verse 10 says:
“As soon as he had seen the vision,
“we tried to go into Macedonia,
“drawing the conclusion
“that God had summoned us
to declare the good news to them.”
When they discerned Jehovah’s direction,
the brothers immediately followed
the leading of the holy spirit.
Likewise, we follow the spirit’s lead.
Of course, it’s not provided through visions
but through evidence in the field.
The recent evaluation showed
that some foreign-language and indigenous-language groups
and congregations had existed for years
and yet had few or no publishers
who were dependent on the language.
In other cases, the territory was very scattered,
so publishers and pioneers had to travel long distances
to find someone who could speak the language.
Despite all of this effort,
there were few Bible studies
and few interested ones, if any,
who attended meetings.
What was Jehovah’s spirit telling us?
It would be better to use our efforts in other fields.
Thus, such pregroups, groups, and congregations
were dissolved.
Have you been personally impacted
by this evaluation?
If so, you’re not alone.
For example, as a result of the evaluation
in just 16 branch territories,
some 4,700 elders,
2,800 ministerial servants,
and 11,000 regular pioneers
have been made available to serve in other fields.
At one time, we may have thought
that the largest increase was taking place
in foreign-language or indigenous-language fields.
But as we’ve considered the matter more carefully,
it seems that congregations in the main languages of many countries
are experiencing the largest numbers
of newly baptized disciples.
So if you’re now returning
to a congregation in one of the main languages of your country,
remember that you are needed there!
Many congregations are struggling
to cover their large territories.
In major cities,
there may be millions of people to reach
but few publishers and pioneers available to preach.
Many pioneers and publishers are finding
progressive return visits and Bible studies in these fields.
And think of how the congregations are being strengthened
as so many mature ones join them!
More appointed brothers are now available
to help with shepherding,
to deliver meeting parts,
and to assist in many other ways.
What practical blessings are resulting
from this evaluation?
Let’s hear the thoughts of a few Branch Committee members.
Thanks to the wise direction
of the Governing Body,
the way we accomplish our ministry
has improved.
More publishers, qualified pioneers, and appointed brothers
will be able to rapidly help other congregations
and concentrate their efforts in the most productive language fields
or fields with a greater potential.
This evaluation has allowed us
to assign graduates
from the School for Kingdom Evangelizers,
and special pioneers as well,
to more productive territories.
But what we’re hearing is that this has energized
the ministry of these pioneers.
In fact, many of them are conducting progressive Bible studies now.
None of us find adjustments easy,
so it has been so encouraging
to see how many have been willing
to adapt to these changes,
in fact, embracing them.
In one language field,
some brothers were a little hesitant at first,
but they were loyal.
So, of course, they went along with the changes.
Now the circuit overseer tells us
that these ones have sent so many expressions of appreciation
thanking them for these loving adjustments.
Many learners have informed us
that it has greatly reduced their stress level.
This has allowed them now to be in a congregation
that they can concentrate more on a productive ministry
and take care of their own spirituality as well.
There’s one brother who is learning another language.
And he was in a congregation, and this changed
from being a congregation to a group.
And he said, “It’s as if finally someone has just released the pressure valve.”
Truly, our Branch Committee saw Jehovah’s spirit act
and is convinced he blessed this evaluation.
What about our pioneers and publishers?
Let’s hear from some who have experienced
these adjustments firsthand.
In the congregation
where I’m serving now in Portuguese,
the territory is very productive.
People are so receptive.
I had the goal of starting one Bible study when I was in the foreign language group.
When the adjustment came, in just a few weeks I had five studies.
We would drive around for hours
looking for just a few specific individuals.
Now we just preach to people,
and if we find foreign-language speakers,
we can still preach to them too.
I have more joy in my ministry because I feel like I’m making good use of my time.
Well, we loved being in foreign language,
but realistically it takes a lot of time.
So we’ve really enjoyed having more time
to prepare for our meeting parts and discuss the points and our application.
It’s been a really nice blessing.
I personally have really benefited from having the extra time
just to spend on cultivating my relationship with Jehovah.
Something really, really interesting
is what one brother said from another group.
He said: “OK,
“now I think I understand better the way that Jehovah does math.
“So instead of having 15 people learn a language to help one person,
“now just one person needs to learn a language
“to be able to benefit from an entire congregation
—100 brothers or more.”
The first concern that I think we all had
was for those who depended on the language.
But as it’s turned out
and as they’ve become part of the congregation,
now they have an even bigger family of brothers and sisters who care about them.
So in our small congregation,
the attendance to the Memorial
was usually just the publishers.
Now, being in this new congregation,
it’s very exciting because this year
we had almost double the amount of the publishers
in our congregation for the attendance.
So that’s very encouraging to see.
We feel that now we are putting our time and energy
into a territory that is actually productive,
and like 1 Corinthians 9:26 says,
we feel like we are making our “blows” count.
If you’re in the same situation as these publishers,
what will you do now?
Like Paul,
we need to be willing to redirect our efforts
based on the leadings of God’s spirit.
Learning another language may be one way
that we can expand our ministry.
But it’s not the only way.
Where is the greatest need for preachers?
Where is there evidence of growth?
It might be in the field of your primary language.
For practical advice on where your efforts and abilities
are most needed,
speak to your circuit overseer
or write to your local branch office.
Jehovah’s organization is on the move,
and it will not be stopped by the pandemic
or anything else!
Will this recent adjustment in priorities
lead to even greater increases?
Perhaps.
It’s too soon to say.
But we’re receiving positive reports.
One branch reported that they’ve had
ten consecutive peaks in the number of publishers.
And another branch said
that the number of new regular pioneers and new Bible studies
is growing at a pace never seen before.
The Governing Body has every confidence
that Jehovah will strengthen each of you
so that we can truly make our blows count.
We love all of you very much!
From the World Headquarters of Jehovah’s Witnesses,
this is JW Broadcasting®.

우리를 변호하고, 증인들에 대한 잘못된 생각을
바로잡아 주어야 한다는 생각이 들 수 있죠.
여호와께 기도로 자제를 나타내게 해 달라고
예를 들어, 베델 가족이나 회중 형제 자매들에게
불평할 만한 타당한 이유가 있을 수 있습니다.
온유한 태도로 문제를 해결하려 하지 않는다면,
정당한 불평이 선을 넘게 될 수 있고
쉽게 투덜거림으로 발전하게 될 수 있습니다.
따라서 우리가 계속 하느님께 가까이 가고
우리 속에 있을지 모르는 교만, 질투, 야심, 앙심을
완전히 뿌리 뽑기 위해 힘써 노력해야 합니다.
온유한 사람들은 구원을 받게 될 것입니다.
따라서 우리 모두 계속 온유를 찾기 위해
이 땅을 상속받을 온유한 사람들 가운데

en.text: Our text for today deals with the quality
of meekness.
Interestingly, one Watchtower  article stated
that “meekness is [actually]
a difficult quality to cultivate”
—difficult but certainly not impossible.
We can say this because just think of the number of scriptures
that mention the quality of meekness
as being essential for salvation.
For example: Psalm 37:11:
“The meek will possess the earth.”
Psalm 76:9:
“[God will] save all the meek of the earth.”
Psalm 149:4:
“[Jehovah] adorns the meek with salvation.”
And then our text comments mention Zephaniah 2:3.
I invite you to take out your Bibles.
Let’s read that from God’s Word.
Zephaniah chapter 2
verse 3 says:
“Seek Jehovah, all you meek ones of the earth,
“who observe his righteous decrees.
“Seek righteousness, seek meekness.
“Probably you will be concealed
on the day of Jehovah’s anger.”
So all these scriptures show the connection
between meekness and our salvation.
So let’s take a moment then and examine
how this quality relates to each of us.
The Insight  book defines meekness
as “a mildness of temper, without haughtiness or vanity.
“[It is] the mental disposition that enables one
“to endure injury with patience
“and without irritation, resentment,
or vindictive retaliation.”
And as was mentioned earlier, how well this is illustrated
in the Bible example of Moses!
Let’s go back to the Bible —this time to Numbers chapter 12.
We’ll read a particular account and see
how the Bible describes the man Moses.
Numbers 12:1 says:
“Now Miriam and Aaron began to speak against Moses
“because of the Cushite wife he had married,
“for he had taken a Cushite wife.
“They were saying: ‘Is it only by Moses that Jehovah has spoken?
“Has he not also spoken through us?’
“And Jehovah was listening.
“Now the man Moses was by far the meekest of all the men
on the face of the earth.”
Well, we learn some interesting things in these verses
to help establish why Moses is described
as “the meekest of all the men on the face of the earth.”
Notice in verse 1 that Miriam and Aaron
—Moses’ older brother and sister—
It says they “began to speak against Moses.”
Their speaking against him meant
they were likely spreading their complaints about Moses
throughout the Israelite camp.
Miriam had a measure of influence in the camp.
She was a prophetess.
The Bible says that she led the women in singing and dancing
when Jehovah defeated Pharaoh and the Egyptians at the Red Sea.
So now that Moses’ wife, Zipporah,
was going to rejoin them in the wilderness,
is it possible that Miriam may have feared
that she would no longer be the leading lady in the camp?
Perhaps she felt that she would lose some of her prominence to Moses’ wife
—a non-Israelite at that.
Now, although Zipporah was not an Israelite, if we look in Exodus chapter 4,
it shows that she demonstrated her willingness to adhere to God’s laws.
So the root of Miriam’s complaints and murmuring
had nothing to do with true worship or the protection of God’s people.
Instead, the root cause appears to be jealousy
—an improper desire for authority and recognition.
And she, along with her brother Aaron,
used this as an excuse to murmur against Moses.
But if we look back in this account,
how is the meekness of Moses made apparent?
Well, despite the resentment and murmuring on the part of Miriam and Aaron,
Moses patiently and quietly
endured the abuse.
And if we look in verse 2, Moses did not have to defend himself
because “Jehovah was listening,”
and He took action.
If you look in verses 6-8, Jehovah rebukes Miriam and Aaron.
And Miriam, evidently the apparent instigator,
is stricken with leprosy.
And when this happens, if you look in verses 11 and 12 (how interesting),
Aaron asks Moses
to intercede on her behalf.
Now for just a moment, let’s just put ourselves in Moses’ sandals.
Could we blame Moses if he were upset?
Here it is, his older siblings have disrespected Jehovah,
they’ve disrespected Moses as God’s representative,
and now they’re talking about Moses’ wife,
even when there was no just cause to do so.
So could Moses have now felt about Miriam:
‘You know what? You had this coming to you.
‘You brought this upon yourself.
You are getting exactly what you deserve’?
Well, even though Moses could have been justified,
when he was given the opportunity,
notice what he does in verse 13:
“[He begins] to cry out to Jehovah, saying:
“‘O God, please heal her!
Please!’”
What a beautiful example of meekness displayed by Moses!
Now, how can his example benefit us?
Well, think about this: When is the next time you and I
might need to show meekness?
Could it be later today if we find that our work is being delayed
by someone else or another department?
Could it be at our meeting this week
if we receive counsel on a meeting part?
Could it be if we find that we’ve lost or that we’ve been passed over
for a privilege of service?
You see, because of our imperfect state, any number of circumstances could arise
where we might need to look back on Moses’ example
of displaying meekness.
Now for just a moment, let’s go back to Zephaniah 2:3.
If you notice in verse 3, we are told
to “seek meekness.”
That means that none of us are born with this quality,
so we have to seek it
by asking, by searching, by praying for Jehovah’s help
to exercise restraint and represent him properly,
even under difficult circumstances.
Perhaps we’ve had the experience in the ministry where we’ve been ridiculed
or we’ve encountered unreasonable individuals
who state all sorts of misconceptions about Jehovah’s Witnesses,
and we’ve heard them.
We don’t believe in Jesus; we break up families;
we don’t believe in helping the community.
And maybe when we hear them, it may bother us.
Frankly, it might even upset us
to the point where we just feel we need to give a reply.
We must defend ourselves.
We have to get the last word in in order to set the householder straight
on our beliefs.
But might that be the very time to seek meekness
—to pray to Jehovah to exercise restraint?
Or perhaps, on a more personal level,
it may be that we experience an injustice.
Perhaps we have a misunderstanding with a member of our family here
or with a brother or sister in the congregation.
And whatever the issue is,
we may have a legitimate complaint.
But isn’t it true that if we’re not careful,
if we don’t seek meekness,
if we don’t seek to resolve the matter in a spirit of meekness,
well, wouldn’t you agree that voicing our legitimate complaint
could very easily cross the line into murmuring?
And we know how Jehovah feels about that.
So certainly, we would never want to do anything to disappoint him.
Moses was meek —the meekest man who ever lived.
But even he reached a point on one occasion
where he did not show meekness and exercise restraint,
and he suffered the consequences.
So if you and I are to continue to draw close to God
and remain acceptable to him,
we must strive to uproot any traces
of pride, jealousy, ambition, or vindictiveness
that we may see in ourselves.
Yes, Jehovah loves those who are meek.
Those who are meek will inherit salvation.
So may each of us continue to seek this quality
by asking, praying,
and then cultivating a submissive attitude that will allow us
to be among the meek who will inherit the earth.

cn.text: 我们今天的经文跟谦和这个特质有关
《守望台》的一篇文章曾经提到
“要培养谦和这个特质的确不容易”
虽然是不容易，但不是不可能
因为在圣经里有很多节经文
都提到谦和这个特质是得救的基本条件
例如诗篇37:11
“谦和的人必拥有大地”
上帝“要拯救地上所有谦和的人”
耶和华“以救恩作为谦和人的装饰”
在今天的《守望台》评论里提到了
西番雅书2:3
我们一起来读读上帝说的话
“地上为人谦和、遵守上帝正义法令的人啊
你们都要寻求耶和华
追求正义，力求谦和
这样，你们就很可能会在耶和华发怒的日子
被隐藏起来。”
刚才提到的这些经文
都说明谦和跟得救有关系
那么现在让我们花点时间来看看
要怎样变得更加谦和
关于谦和
在《洞悉圣经》里，有一段话是这样说的
“性情温和，不高傲，不自负
谦和的人就算被人伤害，也能耐心忍受
不含怒，不怨恨，不报复。”
我们都知道，在这方面
摩西为我们立下了优良的榜样
现在我们再来看看民数记第12章
经文提到了摩西
请大家留意一下圣经怎样描述他
“摩西的妻子是古实人
米利暗和亚伦因为摩西娶了古实人做妻子
就批评他
他们说
难道耶和华只通过摩西一个人说话吗？
他不也通过我们说话吗？
这些话耶和华都听见了
摩西比地上任何人都要谦和。”
我们可以很清楚地从这些经文里看出
为什么圣经说
“摩西比地上任何人都要谦和”
在第1节里圣经告诉我们
摩西的姐姐米利暗以及他的哥哥
也就是亚伦开始“批评他”
批评的意思是
他们很有可能在以色列人当中多次埋怨摩西
米利暗在以色列人当中有一定的影响力
她是个女先知
当耶和华在红海击败法老大军的时候
她带领妇女们唱歌跳舞
可现在摩西的妻子西坡拉
到旷野重新加入了他们
这样米利暗会不会担心
她不再是以色列人当中最重要的女性了呢？
米利暗也许担心
摩西的妻子，这个外族人
反倒会变得比她更重要
虽然西坡拉不是以色列人
但是在出埃及记的第4章我们看到
她很乐意服从上帝的法律
米利暗发牢骚和埋怨
跟正确的崇拜没有关系
也不是为了保护上帝的子民
其实根本的原因是嫉妒的心理
她对权力和地位有不恰当的欲望
米利暗和他的兄弟亚伦找了个借口
批评、埋怨摩西
我们回头再看看圣经的记载
摩西怎样显出谦和呢？
尽管米利暗和亚伦怨恨摩西
但摩西仍然耐心、温和地忍受这样的指责
在第2节提到摩西甚至没有为自己辩护
因为上帝都“听见了”
并采取了行动
第6到第8节提到，上帝斥责米利暗和亚伦
而最早开始埋怨的，很可能是米利暗
所以她被惩罚染上了麻风
之后在第11和12节提到
亚伦请摩西替米利暗向上帝求情
现在让我们试着去体会摩西的感觉
如果摩西很生气，我们可以责怪他吗？
事实是，他的姐姐和哥哥不尊重上帝
也不尊重摩西这位上帝的代表
现在他们还批评摩西的妻子
其实他们这么做并没有正当的理由
那么摩西本可以怎样看待米利暗呢？
“米利暗，你知道吗？
这个后果是你自己造成的
是你咎由自取。”
即使摩西没有帮助米利暗也是合理的
但当他有了这个机会，我们看13节他怎么做
“摩西向耶和华呼喊
上帝啊，求求你！
求你治好她！”
摩西表现出这么美好的谦和的品质
我们可以从摩西的榜样学到什么？
让我们想想看
下一次在什么时候
你和我需要表现谦和呢？
也许就是等一下
因为别的部门或某个人
我们的工作被延误了
有可能是本周的聚会
我们从聚会得到劝告
又或者是
我们失去了或没有得到我们很想得到的委派
因为我们都不完美，所以要经常提醒自己
不断回想并努力效法
摩西表现出的谦和的榜样
让我们再次翻回西番雅书2:3
在第3节，你留意到经文说什么吗？
要“力求谦和”
这句话的意思就是
我们没有任何一个人生来就有这个特质
所以，身为上帝的子民
我们要通过祷告向耶和华寻求帮助
即使面对困难，也能表现自制
也许我们曾经在传道时被别人嘲笑
或是我们遇到一个无礼的人
他提到了关于我们的各种说法
但是都是不对的
他们说我们不相信耶稣，我们拆散家庭
也对社会没有贡献
我们听了心里也许不舒服
我们可能很生气，心里想着
我们一定要作出一些回应
认为一定要为自己辩护
要让住户知道我们相信的到底是什么
但这不是一个很好的机会
让我们力求谦和吗？
要祈求耶和华帮助我们表现自制
也许对我们来说
我们是受到了不公平的对待
也许我们的家人
或是会众里的某个弟兄或姐妹误解了我们
无论是哪种情况
我们都有理由心里觉得不舒服
要留意，在这些情况下
如果我们没有力求谦和
没有用谦和的精神来解决问题
我相信你会同意
原来只是心里不舒服
后来可能会变成埋怨
我们知道上帝对发怨言的看法
我们绝不想让他失望
摩西是谦和的，是世上最谦和的人
但我们知道
有一次他没有表现谦和，保持自制
所以受到了惩罚
如果我们想要继续亲近上帝，让他高兴
我们就必须努力从心里根除骄傲、嫉妒
以及野心，或想要报复的心理
没错，耶和华喜欢那些谦和的人
谦和的人会获得拯救
让我们继续祈求上帝，帮助我们表现谦和
同时，我们也要培养顺服的态度
这样就能成为谦和的人，得着大地

ko.text: 이번 달은 메이버 형제와 함께 진행하겠습니다.
먼저, 복음 전파자 빌립의 훌륭한 본에 대해
또, 여호와께서 오늘날에도 최고의 선생님이신 이유를
새로운 노래는 우리가 마음과 정신을 지킬 때,
여호와의 축복에 초점을 맞출 수 있다는 걸 보여 줄 겁니다.
자기 자신과 관련해서만 기뻐할 이유가 있을 것입니다.”
집회에서 의미 있는 해설을 하기 위해 노력하고 있는가?
최선을 다해 전파 활동에 참여하고 있는가?
재방문을 준비하는 면에서 더 개선할 점이 있는가?
그렇다면 최선을 다해 연구생을 돕고 있는가?’
자신이 정말 최선을 다하고 있는지 확인할 수 있죠.
우리보다 더 잘하는 사람을 보게 될지 모릅니다.
우리 자신과 다른 사람을 비교해서는 안 된다고
지금 자신이 할 수 있는 일을 다하고 있으니까
충분히 잘하고 있다는 생각이 들 수 있죠.
그런데 이 성구의 첫 부분을 기억해야 합니다.
우리는 자신이 지금 하고 있는 것과
개인적으로 최대한 할 수 있는 것을 비교해 봐야 합니다.
‘난 최선을 다하고 있는데, 뭘 더 하란 말이지?’
그래도 잘 살펴보고 검토해 봐야 합니다.
시간을 내서 여러분이 하고 있는 모든 일을
신권 활동을 더 할 수 있습니까?
그럴 수도 있고 아닐 수도 있죠.
연습하고, 훈련하고, 몸에 좋은 음식을 먹고,
제일 좋은 운동화를 신는 등 최선을 다하죠.
더 빠른 선수가 있으면 경기에 지고 맙니다.
최선을 다했지만 소용이 없게 된 거죠.
더 빠른 선수와 비교해서 그보다 느렸기 때문입니다.
딸이 학교에서 그린 그림을 집으로 가져옵니다.
엄마는 B-를 지우고 A+라고 써 줍니다.
그런 다음 그림을 냉장고에 붙여 놓습니다.
선생님은 그 아이를 같은 학년의 친구들과 비교했지만,
딸이 최선을 다한 것에 따라 점수를 매겼습니다.
우리가 영적으로 얼마나 잘하고 있는지를 판단하실 때
절대 할 수 있는 것 이상을 요구하지 않으시죠.
하지만 그분은 우리가 할 수 있는 최선을 다해
우리가 가진 모든 것을 다해야 한다는 것이죠.
봉사에 나가서 온 힘을 다해 전파합니다.
그렇게 온 힘을 다해 전파 활동에 참여한다고 해도
우리의 정신을 다해 올바른 것을 말하지 않는다면,
아무도 내가 하는 서론을 듣지 않는단 말이지.’
그 서론은 구역에 가장 알맞은 서론이었나요?
얼마나 오랫동안 그 서론을 사용해 오셨나요?
우리의 정신을 다해 서론을 미리 준비함으로
평일 집회 때 소개된 서론들을 사용해 보려고 노력합니까?
집주인은 여러분의 친절하고 밝은 표정을 볼 수 있습니까?
좋은 소식을 가지고 왔다는 게 얼굴에 나타납니까?
가까운 미래에 그 소식은 바뀌게 될 겁니다.
개선할 점을 찾으면 더 잘하게 될 것입니다.
정신을 기울여 주의 깊이 듣고 있다면
우리는 여호와 하느님께 가까이 가기 위해
그분이 가까이 오실 것’ 이라고 말합니다.
집회에 참석해서 얻는 유익 한 가지가 바로 그것입니다.
정기적인 집회 참석의 또 다른 유익인데요,
집회에 참석해서 우리는 서로 격려를 주고받죠.
“그리고 서로 생각해 주어 사랑과 훌륭한 일을 고무하며,
일부 사람들의 습관처럼 함께 모이는 일을 그만두지 말고,
오히려 서로 격려하며 그날이 다가오는 것을 볼수록
그렇다면 여러분은 정말 잘하고 계신 것입니다.
개인 연구를 할 때나 가족 숭배를 할 때는 어떤가요?
여호와에 대한 사랑과 감사가 더 커지게 해 주고
그분께 더 가까이 가게 도와주는 어떤 내용을 발견하셨습니까?
그 내용을 정신을 다해 묵상하고 계속 생각합니까?
그래서 마음 깊숙한 곳까지 이르게 합니까?

en.text: Welcome!
I’m here with my good friend and cohost, Chris Mavor.
Chris, what’s in store for this month’s program?
Thanks, Brother Herd.
We’ll see the value of learning
from the good example of Philip the evangelizer.
We’ll also learn why Jehovah is still the best Teacher today.
And our new song shows how,
by safeguarding our heart and mind,
we can focus on Jehovah’s blessings.
This is JW Broadcasting® for April 2021!
In addressing our theme
“Is Your Best Good Enough?”
I’d like to start by reading Galatians 6:4.
It says: “But let each one
“examine his own actions,
“and then he will have cause for rejoicing
“in regard to himself alone,
and not in comparison with the other person.”
We’re told to “examine [our] own actions.”
So ask yourself: ‘How am I doing spiritually?
‘Am I happy with my attendance at Christian meetings?
‘Do I participate by sharing meaningful comments as able?
‘How about my personal study of the Bible?
‘Let me examine my involvement in the ministry.
‘Could I do better in preparing for my return visits?
‘Do I conduct any Bible studies with interested ones?
If so, am I content with what I am doing?’
In effect, you’re asking yourself,
‘Is my best good enough?’
We might see others in the congregation that are doing more than we are.
But then we look back at Galatians 6:4 again,
and it clearly said
that I should not compare myself with the other person.
So we could quickly assume that we’re doing what we can,
reasoning that it’s good enough.
But let’s not forget the first part of the verse.
We are to “examine [our] own actions.”
We need to compare what we are doing
with what we personally could be doing.
We need to be active
and not become self-satisfied and overconfident.
First Corinthians 10:12 provides this warning:
“So let the one who thinks he is standing
beware that he does not fall.”
But you may say: ‘I’m doing my best!
What more can I do?’
Take a good look at your best—scrutinize it.
Examine very closely all you’re doing with the time that you have.
Can mundane activity be replaced with theocratic activity?
What do you see?
Is your best good enough?
It may be; it may not be.
It depends on one’s outlook.
What are some examples?
A runner in a race—he practices; trains;
eats the right things; keeps a lean, healthy body;
wears the best running shoes; and so forth.
He gives his best
but loses the race to someone faster.
His best was not good enough.
Why?
It was compared to whether he was faster than his competitors.
Yohan Blake lost to Usain Bolt
in a 100-meter event in 2012
by just a fraction of a second.
He did his best, but his best wasn’t good enough.
A mother and daughter
—the daughter is in the second grade at school.
She brings home a picture she drew in class.
The teacher had put a B- on the picture.
The daughter shows it to her mother,
and the mother crosses out the B-
and puts an A+ on it.
She then tapes the picture on the refrigerator.
What is the difference between the teacher and the mother?
The teacher compares the student to other classmates of her age.
The mother grades her according to her best,
not in comparison with others.
Jehovah does not compare your best with the best of others.
Let’s look at Psalm 103:14.
When Jehovah examines our spiritual accomplishments,
what’s one of his measuring sticks?
Psalm 103:14:
“For he well knows how we are formed,
remembering that we are dust.”
“Dust” is used figuratively,
indicating mankind’s frailty and lowliness.
By “remembering that we are dust,”
Jehovah never asks more of us than we can give.
However, he expects us to obey his commands
to the best of our own ability.
Mark 12:30 —you can likely quote it from memory.
Verse 30 says:
“You must love Jehovah your God
“with your whole heart
“and with your whole soul
“and with your whole mind
and with your whole strength.”
This embraces everything we have —all that we are.
You go in service;
you use “your whole strength” to accomplish it.
That’s commendable.
But what good is it to use our whole strength
to go in service if our mind
cannot direct our tongue
to say the right things when we talk to a person?
‘I used a lot
‘of my strength walking
‘from door to door, climbing stairs, and so forth.
‘And yet, no one let me get past
my introduction.’
Question: Was that the best introduction you could give?
How long have you been using that introduction?
Would a new one help?
Would using “your whole mind”
by means of advance preparation
result in making your best even better?
Have you tried to use some of the introductions
demonstrated at our midweek meetings
or some of those found in the Reasoning From the Scriptures  book,
pages 9-15?
What does the householder see
in your face
when she opens the door?
Is your countenance
radiating pleasantness and kindness?
Does she see good news or bad news?
Do you look happy or sad?
The message we’re commissioned to deliver today
is the “good news of the Kingdom.”
We expect it to change sometime in the near future.
Do the best you can until you know better.
Then when you know better, you can do better.
You attend all congregation meetings
and pay rapt attention with your mind.
You’re to be commended.
But is that all that’s required
to love Jehovah with our whole mind?
Are we meditating on the knowledge
that we receive at our meetings
in order to draw close to Jehovah?
James 4:8 says:
“Draw close to God, and he will draw close to you.”
That’s one benefit we receive from our meeting attendance.
Let’s read Hebrews 10:24, 25.
This is another benefit of regular meeting attendance.
In this way, we give and receive encouragement.
Verses 24 and 25 read:
“And let us consider one another
“so as to incite to love and fine works,
“not forsaking our meeting together,
“as some have the custom,
“but encouraging one another,
“and all the more so
as you see the day drawing near.”
Do you give comments at meetings?
Are they well-prepared?
Do they encourage your brothers and sisters?
Are you giving your best?
If so, then your best is good enough.
What about your personal study
or family worship?
Are you doing your best?
Is your best good enough?
“I read all The Watchtowers  and Awakes!  when they come out,” you say.
It goes without saying that that’s good.
What did you find in what you read
that will deepen your love and appreciation for Jehovah
and draw you closer to him?
Do you use your whole mind
to meditate and continue to think about it,
thus spiking it down deep into your heart?
Some things we learn
may not be immediately applicable
but can be regurgitated
and applied later as needed.
Are you giving serious attention
to the spiritual needs of your wife and children?
Yes, you have family worship most weeks.
That’s commendable.
Do you prepare well for it
or just throw something together at the last minute?
What if your wife just threw something on the table
for dinner each evening
without giving any thought to the health needs of the family?
Think: Is your best good enough?
We can slop a pig, and he’ll enjoy it.
But give the same garbage to a cow, and she’ll ignore it.
Why are we considering
“Is Your Best Good Enough?”
It’s only as a reminder
to look at what we think to be our best
in what we’re doing for ourselves, our families,
and our spiritual brothers and sisters.
And remember, our best is not compared
with the best of another brother or sister.
Only Jehovah knows
when we’re doing our best.
He is a righteous and fair Judge.
Our knowledge, even of ourself,
can be faulty because of inherited sin.
Therefore, it’s wisdom on our part
to keep examining ourselves
to see where we might improve.
So is your best good enough?
I’d like to think it is.
What do you think?
What would you like to be known for?
In the first century,
a servant of Jehovah named Philip
was known as “the evangelizer.”
In the following dramatization,
we’ll learn how Philip earned this reputation
and what we can apply from his good example.
Please find your seats.
It’s time to start our graduation program.
We never dreamed this would happen.
This is a very special day all of us have been anxiously waiting for.
We’re happy to see all of you here.
It all started a few years ago.
If you’d like to have the circuit overseer and his wife for a meal . . .
It was during that visit and this question.
His theme on Tuesday is
“What Lessons Can We Learn
From Philip the Evangelizer?”
Hmm.
What could we learn from Philip?
Honestly, we were already busy with the right things.
Lilly and the girls helped out wherever they could.
I worked on Kingdom Hall maintenance projects.
And we had a regular schedule for the ministry.
But like in a lot of places,
when someone showed interest,
it was tough to find them again.
I wondered if our spiritual routine needed an update.
Looking forward to that talk,
I decided we’d research Philip for family worship
—Acts chapter 6.
Philip was one of seven brothers
selected to distribute food to Christian widows in Jerusalem.
That was an important assignment,
but he did so much more than that.
Hmm, this is interesting.
Because of the persecution,
Philip had to flee from Jerusalem to Samaria.
Samaria hadn’t accepted the word of Jehovah yet.
But Philip saw that trial as a spiritual opportunity.
Samaria was largely untouched by the preaching work.
Philip declared the good news zealously,
and many believed and got baptized.
But sometime later,
an angel spoke with him.
He told Philip to “get up and go to the south.”
That led him to find the Ethiopian eunuch and preach in other cities.
Philip was willing to serve wherever there was a need.
And he always kept that evangelizing spirit.
Some twenty years later, he was still known as “the evangelizer.”
By that time, his life had changed.
He was a family man with four daughters.
But that didn’t stop him from showing hospitality
when Paul and his companions came to visit.
Visits like that must have been
full of spiritual lessons for his daughters.
That night, we came up with a few things we wanted to do.
We started by having the circuit overseer to lunch.
We hadn’t made time for that in a while.
Alex and Carla’s experiences
made the girls excited to reach their own spiritual goals.
But like Philip, changes came that we didn’t expect.
I was out of work for a few months.
It was a stressful time
but also a spiritual opportunity.
I could visit people at different times of the day.
We tried to make the most of the situation and preach zealously
like Philip.
And here we are,
watching our girls graduate from the School for Kingdom Evangelizers.
Those few lessons
made a big difference for this family
of evangelizers.
The Bible is rich with examples like Philip.
And we have many fine examples among Jehovah’s people in our day.
Learning from them helps us make good decisions
and manage serious issues.
Let’s pay attention to this interview
with Eugene and Odile Nteziryayo,
who attended the 145th class of Gilead.
What can we learn from their example of faith and endurance?
With us today, we have Eugene and Odile Nteziryayo.
They’ve graduated from the 145th class of Gilead,
and they lived through this mayhem.
Odile, now, your family is Tutsi,
and this must have certainly put them in danger.
The killing was happening all over the country,
so my parents and my brother were killed.
I saw that some religious leaders were involved
in killing people in the genocide.
I couldn’t believe how friendly people
who were previously living together
now started killing their neighbors.
How did you get contact with the truth?
So after the genocide, I was taken in by my aunt
whose family were Jehovah’s Witnesses,
so I began studying the Bible with them.
I was in the Live Forever  book.
I saw a picture of a priest blessing people in the church,
and then he was blessing troops who were going to kill.
But also I could see how brothers and sisters in the congregation
would love and encourage.
And they risked their lives to take care of one another.
Oh, that’s touching.
Now, Eugene,
your family was not a direct target of the violence,
but what other hardships did you face?
The economic situation was very difficult.
My family had no money,
and they could not buy food.
I remember my mom
—I can still see her lying on the bed in complete despair,
not knowing what she could do for us children.
The elders asked me to go to the Kingdom Hall,
and when I arrived,
they handed me 18,000 Rwandan francs.
The elders told me that my brothers and sisters from abroad
offered us this gift.
So I immediately ran back home,
found my mom still lying on the bed,
and gave her the money.
I can still see my mom crying
because of the joy
and thankfulness of what the brothers had done.
Excellent.
Now, looking back at all the injustices you and your family have suffered,
Odile, what has helped you to not become a bitter person?
The preaching work is very important to me
because the more I talk about the Bible’s promises,
the more they become real to me.
For example, when I talk about the resurrection hope
and the condition of the dead,
this helps me to feel
that my loved ones are not suffering anymore
and they are waiting to be resurrected.
So this makes me feel happy.
The scripture that comes to mind is
where the apostle John repeated Jesus’ command
of loving one another just as Jesus loved us.
Christians during that time were facing persecution,
and now they needed a fresh application of that scripture in their lives.
We all love one another,
but during difficult moments
like the ones our brothers in Rwanda went through,
they needed that fresh application
of this very commandment of Jesus:
loving one another to the point
of risking our lives for our brothers.
Being here in Gilead has reminded me of that fact
—that I really need to love my brothers and sisters
as Jesus loved us.
You brothers and sisters in Rwanda
have given us a wonderful example
of courage and faith and love.
Please know that we love you all very much.
Thank you.
Thank you for joining us
on this edition of Extraordinary Experiences.
That was a very moving experience.
We can imitate the good example of our brothers in Rwanda
by taking care of brothers and sisters when they’re in need.
In recent years, our video dramas have brought to life
Jonah, Josiah, and other examples of faith.
Have you wondered how our brothers ensure
that these dramas are both vivid and accurate?
Well, let’s go behind the scenes of one of our latest dramas:
Nehemiah: “The Joy of Jehovah Is Your Stronghold.”
In Nehemiah’s day, the Jews joyfully embarked
on a massive building project.
With Jehovah’s direction and help,
they were able to finish the work
in just 52 days.
You look like you’ve been working.
During the production of the film
Nehemiah: “The Joy of Jehovah Is Your Stronghold,”
the walls of Jerusalem were built once again,
but this time at the Mount Ebo studios in Brewster, New York.
A variety of skills were needed to produce this drama
with many volunteers coming together,
using their time, energy, and abilities
to create an accurate teaching tool.
And they found great joy in their work.
Good planning was needed right at the start of production.
Every day began with a Scriptural discussion
and prayer.
The costume and makeup departments
prepared the actors to appear on set.
Assistance was provided to help actors
feel more comfortable in front of the cameras.
And action!
Brothers, please.
Have they attacked anyone yet?
They must have.
No! But they will.
While the production team was filming in one studio,
sets were being prepared in another.
To add to the realism, detailed props were made
—many using 3D printing.
With all of these researched and crafted costumes,
sets, and props combined,
environments were designed to accurately recreate the time period.
But even more was needed to convey what it was like
to live in Jerusalem during Nehemiah’s day.
For example, there were many animals on set.
Even after principal filming was completed,
sets built in the studio were extended
using advanced visual effects.
Digital construction work was done
by the visual effects team.
Yes, building is a legacy of God’s people.
Nehemiah was one of many who throughout history
devoted their energies to supporting the work of building.
In a similar way, the production team that made
Nehemiah: “The Joy of Jehovah Is Your Stronghold,”
joyfully worked hard to produce a film
that helps build love and appreciation
in the hearts of God’s people.
We learn from good examples like Nehemiah and many others.
But, as we’ll see in our next video,
we also learn important lessons from those who made poor decisions.
I was born to two Christian parents;
they always tried to instill in us a love for Jehovah.
But I felt quite lonely growing up,
and I felt like I didn’t have people who wanted to do the same things
—the lifestyle, the way they spoke, the music they were listening to—
and so for me, the real struggle was where do I stand?
Where are my boundaries going to be set?
It’s really hard because it could mean
the difference between having a friend and not having a friend.
Over the years, I have talked to several
who’ve perhaps drifted a little bit in the truth.
And that unfortunately happened to some of my friends.
Nobody is immune to the pressures of the world.
I was born and raised by Christian parents,
so all through my childhood and teenage years,
I was happy serving Jehovah,
but it got a little bit harder when I started to work.
People at work would ask me
to do social activities with them, go for a drink and things,
but there were men who would ask me to go out with them.
It’s flattering when someone shows interest in you, so it was nice,
but it was hard to have to constantly remind myself,
‘Well, you know that this is not going to be successful;
you know this person doesn’t love Jehovah.’
I remember one day I drove into a parking lot,
and I just prayed to Jehovah with tears in my eyes, and I said:
“This is too hard. This is just too hard.
“The people that are my friends are starting to leave the truth.
I feel quite lonely, but I want to serve you.”
After that prayer I went home, I spoke to my mom,
and she got really quiet, and she just looked at me and said,
“Anything Jehovah tells you is to benefit yourself.”
And it clicked in that moment that Jehovah was saying to me: “I love you.
“I will carry you through this time, and you’ll see
“that there will be all these blessings that’ll open up to you,
“and you’ll have a really wonderful, colorful life,
but you have to hang in there.”
Even though it was hard, I resisted the temptation,
but someone close to me who faced the same pressure
gave in and ended up leaving Jehovah.
When I heard
that she was disfellowshipped,
it just completely hit me so hard
because you really are just worried
about what is going to happen with their future.
After a while, she did come back to Jehovah.
She’s raising a child on her own.
One day we were having a video chat
with the little one just playing in the background,
and she suddenly turned around and said,
“Mummy, why did you marry someone who doesn’t love Jehovah?”
She understood that we need to live according to Jehovah’s standards.
As elders, we can help people to get up and get back on the path to life,
and it’s a real pleasure.
I’m reminded about the account of David.
Eventually he was forgiven by Jehovah because he had a good heart;
however, there were consequences all through his life.
I’ve received so many blessings for sticking to Jehovah.
I found a lovely brother to marry in the Christian congregation,
and we’re very happy together.
The thing to do is to just stick with Jehovah.
“Taste and see that Jehovah is good,”
and when you do that, you will appreciate
that there is absolutely no need
to go anywhere else.
Having observed what has happened to people who have left the truth
and the baggage they sometimes end up carrying
when they come back in the truth makes me feel that it’s just not worth it.
Really, Jehovah is like a parent; he wants to protect us and care for us.
Things will always work out for the best if you do things Jehovah’s way.
I feel my family has had many blessings.
As a husband and a father,
I’ve got four children who have all grown up in the truth.
They’ve all gone on to have good theocratic lives,
where they’ve enjoyed many privileges of service.
So for me, it’s been a real blessing to do things Jehovah’s way.
I think when you test out the world,
Satan will give you immediate satisfaction,
but when you serve no purpose to him anymore, that’s it.
One of the most beautiful blessings I’ve received is people
—people around you who love Jehovah
and who want to serve him the way you do.
I really strongly believe that Jehovah
not only gives us a lot of blessings
but gives us blessings that he’s handpicked for us.
My observation would be
that experience is not the best teacher; Jehovah is the best Teacher.
Jehovah wants us to be happy
and avoid the painful consequences of bad decisions.
If you’re facing a test of integrity in some way,
remember that, as our brother said,
“Jehovah is [our] best Teacher.”
Of course, if we’re to learn from Jehovah,
we have to allow him to teach us.
We must let him mold us.
This was the topic of a recent morning worship
by Brother Gary Breaux.
Our scripture here, Isaiah 64:8,
clearly establishes
that Jehovah God is the Potter
—the Great Potter, in fact—
and we are the clay.
Now, in what way is he molding us?
Well, one way is through adjusting
our Christian personality.
Now, how does he do that?
Well, he uses his Word —the Bible—
his holy spirit,
and the Christian congregation.
So, what we’re going to do is talk
about how Jehovah helps to mold our personality.
What’s the process that’s used?
We’re going to talk about two aspects of the Christian personality
—humility and kindness.
So we said one way Jehovah uses
to mold our personality is his Word, the Bible.
And Hebrews 4:12 says
that God’s Word has tremendous power.
So we take individual scriptures as we are reading it;
we look at our own personality:
‘What does it say about me?
How can I improve?’
Let’s take an example: humility.
We are going to go to Philippians chapter 2,
verses 3 and 4.
We see how this is a powerful aid to us.
Here’s what we should do,
Philippians 2:3, 4:
“Do nothing out of contentiousness or out of egotism,
“but with humility
“consider others superior to you,
“as you look not only for your own interests,
but also for the interests of others.”
So when we read this scripture, we look at ourselves and say:
‘Well, how am I doing with this?
‘Do I see that I have made progress,
‘especially if this has been an issue in the past?
‘Is Jehovah somehow nudging me, adjusting me,
molding me by means of this powerful scripture?’
Ask yourself about humility:
‘Am I the person that always seems to be in charge?
‘Do I give that attitude across to others?
Or, as it says here, Do I view others as superior?’
Maybe even we’re saying,
“I admit that that sister has more patience than I have,”
or “That brother is really a better teacher than I am.”
So, you see, by means of individual scriptures,
Jehovah God can help to mold our thinking.
Now, in addition to the individual scripture,
the Bible also provides examples
of that quality in action.
And so the Watchtower  comment for today
uses Christ Jesus as an example of humility.
So let’s open to that scripture (it’s referred to)
in Luke chapter 22.
And as we read the account,
we think: ‘What can I learn?
‘How did he handle it?
How can I apply it?’
So Luke 22:24
—this took place the evening before his death.
It says: “However, there also arose a heated dispute among them
over which one of them was considered to be the greatest.”
Well, automatically we see there’s a problem of humility here.
Well, so, let’s move down now
to verses 26 and 27.
He says: “You, though, are not to be that way.
“But let the one who is the greatest among you
“become as the youngest,
“and the one taking the lead as the one ministering.
“For which one is greater,
“the one dining or the one serving?
“Is it not the one dining?
But I am among you as the one serving.”
Now, these were not just words, because the apostles had seen
three and a half years of a beautiful example
of Jesus serving others —truly a humble man.
And through our Bible reading too,
we have seen this example of humility that we can apply.
So it’s good for us to ask ourselves:
‘Am I a proud person?
‘Do I give off that impression to others?
‘Do I view myself as “one dining”
or as “one serving”?’
Well, now, another way that Jehovah uses
to mold our Christian personality
is the holy spirit.
Now, how does that work?
Well, if you look at Galatians 5:19,
it talks about “the works of the flesh.”
And then in verse 22,
it refers to “the fruitage of the spirit”
—“works of the flesh,” “fruitage of the spirit.”
Now, work
is a result of what one does.
It’s the product of your actions.
And so the apostle Paul lists, as you see there, under “works of the flesh,”
various results that come
as a result of a conscious effort on an individual’s part
or possibly because of human imperfection.
But, on the other hand, Paul talks about “the fruitage of the spirit”
—not work, but the fruitage it results in.
And this is implying
that qualities that are listed there as fruitage of the spirit
are not the result of some sort of program we get into
to adjust our character,
but it’s the operation of God’s spirit
upon the individual.
It’s this tremendous force and power from Jehovah God
that moves us in certain ways.
It may be to recognize scripture or to listen to counsel.
Yes, we need to pray for his holy spirit
so that we can develop those Christian qualities that Paul mentions.
So when you look at verse 22, one of those qualities is kindness.
How important is that for the Christian personality?
So when the Great Potter looks at us,
does he see a need for adjustments
in the way we display kindness to others?
See, are we praying to Jehovah God,
“Please, Jehovah, help me develop
this fruitage of the spirit”?
Here, again, the Bible gives examples
of individuals who had kindness.
It’s the quality in action, so to speak.
And in this case, Jehovah God, of course, is the greatest example.
Here it is.
In Genesis chapter 3, it describes in verse 7
that after Adam and Eve ate the fruit, then they recognized their nakedness.
So what did they do?
“They sewed fig leaves together” as clothing.
But, now, in verse 21,
before putting them out of the garden of Eden
into the thorns and thistles, what did Jehovah do?
Well, it says he ‘made long garments
out of skins to clothe them.’
Now, that’s the ultimate kindness.
See, we want to allow these examples to touch us in ways
that move us to be kind to others.
Now, one benefit of kindness is
that people are drawn to that kind of person.
Proverbs 11:17 says this:
“A kind man benefits himself.”
It’s enjoyable being around a kind person, isn’t it?
A kind person easily finds
and keeps good friends.
Now, the Ministry School  textbook says
that “one who is kind and mild-tempered
is gentle in his way of doing things.”
Now, under the chapter “Voice Quality,” here’s what it says:
“People are greatly influenced
“not only by what is said
“but also by how it is said.
“If a person speaking to you has a voice
“that is pleasant, warm, friendly, and kind,
is it not true that you are more inclined to listen favorably?”
Most certainly it is.
And I might say that the November study edition
of The Watchtower  we just received
has a beautiful article in it entitled
“Kindness—A Quality Expressed in Word and Action.”
So when it comes to our Christian personality
—especially involving humility and kindness, as we’ve talked about today—
may each of us respond to the molding of Jehovah God.
He uses his Word —the Bible—
and he uses his holy spirit.
Now, we also said Jehovah uses the congregation.
So may we all be responsive to counsel
that we receive either from the platform
or maybe individual counsel
to improve in these areas.
And if we respond correctly,
then we can say
as recorded at Isaiah 64:8:
“But now, O Jehovah, you are our Father.
“We are the clay, and you are our Potter;
we are all the work of your hand.”

en.text: Few things in life are more painful
than the death of someone we love.
When my dad was diagnosed with Alzheimer’s,
I felt incredibly worried and anxious.
When he finally passed away,
I had spent so much time worrying about him
and thinking about him
that I felt a huge emptiness.
I didn’t really know what to do with myself.
Shiho, our daughter,
died from a sickness
when she was 16 years old.
She had a disability,
so she was always with us.
Losing someone who was always there,
you know, right here in front of you
—that loss can’t be expressed in words.
If you’ve experienced the loss of someone you love,
is there anything that can help ease the pain?
No two people experience grief in the same way.
But there are some practical suggestions
that may help you.
These are frequently cited by grief counselors as being effective.
Number one: Accept support from your friends and family.
I found it difficult to accept help from others
because I felt like what I was going through
was so difficult that I felt like my friends wouldn’t understand.
But when I reached out to my friends,
they could do some of the things
that I maybe had enjoyed with my dad.
And so it gave me the confidence
that I wasn’t going to be alone
—that I had friends that could fill that hole for me.
Our friends sent us upbuilding messages
and lots of flowers,
enough to fill up this room.
Friends are a big help.
They truly were there for us.
Number two: Take care of your health.
Maintain a balanced diet,
stay physically active,
drink plenty of water,
and try to get enough sleep.
This is especially important when you are grieving,
because grief can be exhausting.
I found that if I didn’t get good enough sleep,
it made things a lot harder.
I try to avoid being on my phone
too much before bed, and I try and do things that relax me.
Number three: Be balanced.
Many find it helpful to alternate
periods of grieving with breaks in their routine.
You might consider spending time with new friends,
learning new skills, or just enjoying some time off.
While at home, I was a bit down and maybe a little pessimistic.
But when I stepped outside, I noticed how nice
the breeze was and I felt so much better.
Taking moments to relax works.
Number four: Help others.
Many find it helpful to use some of their time
to help others, including friends and relatives
who are also grieving the loss of your loved one.
Acts 20:35, where it says
“there is more happiness in giving than there is
in receiving,” really helped me.
So I tried every day, even if it was reaching out
on the phone, to do something for someone else.
And I found that really helped
with not just making me happy but it helped control my anxiety too.
Number five: Remember your loved one.
Many find it comforting to do things
that help keep alive the memory of the person they’ve lost.
We sometimes talk about her,
saying, “Shiho used to laugh if we said this”
or “Do you remember she liked this?”,
and remembering those moments
warms our hearts.
None of these things can
completely erase the pain of grief,
but they may provide you with at least a measure of relief.
The advice offered in this video is in perfect harmony
with principles found in the Bible.
Many who have lost someone they love have found
that turning to the Bible gives them peace of mind and comfort.
For more information
on how the Bible can help you cope with the pain of grief,
please visit our website, jw.org.

cn.text: 亲友去世

我爸爸被诊断出
得了阿尔茨海默病（阿兹海默症）的时候
我感到很担心，也很害怕
我爸爸生病的时候
我脑子里想的都是他的事
后来他去世了

我们的女儿志穗16岁的时候
生病去世了
她行动不便

但她不在了
这种感觉就是
原本一直在你眼前的这个人
就这样没了，我真的不能接受
如果你失去亲人或朋友

他们也会安排时间
跟我做一些
我跟爸爸在一起时喜欢做的事情

找个时间让自己休息一下
对于缓解悲伤的情绪会有帮助
你可以花点时间认识新朋友
学习新技能

我要是一直在家里
情绪就很低落
当我走到户外

花时间放松一下，真的很有帮助

en.text: Many religions teach that God condemns
the wicked to eternal torment after they die
and hope that this fear of torment
prevents them from doing bad.
Does God really punish people after they die?
The Bible reassures us
that the dead are unconscious
and that “[they] know nothing at all.”
If the dead are unconscious,
they cannot suffer.
Does that mean God does not
punish wicked people at all?
No.
God explained to the first human couple
how they would be punished if they rebelled against him.
God said nothing about torment or hell.
He simply said:
“You will certainly die.”
And after being expelled from the garden of Eden,
that is exactly what happened to wicked Adam and Eve
—they passed away and became dust.
The Bible says that after death,
one is no longer accountable for past mistakes
because “the one who has died
has been acquitted from his sin.”
But there is an even greater reason
why a hell of torment could never exist.
The Bible tells us: “God is love.”
Would a loving God command that sinners be tormented,
not just for minutes, but for all eternity?
Consider the following:
In Bible times, God condemned the practice
of sacrificing children in the fire to false gods.
He said that such a cruel deed
‘never even entered his heart.’
We hate the idea of such brutality
because we are made in the image
of a loving, merciful God.
Clearly, we do not need to worry that our dead loved ones
might be suffering punishment somewhere.
The Bible tells us that they are at peace, at rest.
But why do good people die?
What happens to them when they die?
What hope is there for our dead loved ones?
To learn more, go to jw.org
and search for these topics
or fill in the online request
for one of Jehovah’s Witnesses to contact you.

en.text: So when reading today’s text,
maybe two questions came to your mind.
One is, What are these
body members on the earth?
And the other one is,
How do we deaden
our body members?
Our text reminds us of the words of Jesus, when he said,
‘It is better to cut off your hand, your foot, throw your eye away
rather than being destroyed.’
In Bible language,
the hand, the foot, the eye
often are used to illustrate
what we do with our life.
The hand represents things we do, or make, with our hands.
The foot represents walking or running
—often connecting it with where we go in life.
The eye represents our viewpoint, our opinion
—how we look at things, whether we like them or not.
So, what do the body members mean?
They do not refer to literal parts of our body
like the hand, the foot, or the eye.
It illustrates our tendencies
as imperfect people.
In our text for today at Colossians 3:5,
Paul lists some of these tendencies.
He said they are “immorality, uncleanness,
“uncontrolled . . . passion, hurtful desire,
(Some translations say “evil desires.”) and greediness.”
The bad inclinations we have within us
we have from birth.
Greed and bad desires
come quite easily to most of us.
If you put a ball
on a table that is not perfectly level,
the ball will roll down to the lower end.
All humans
are born with that inclination to go down.
So how do we deaden,
or stop, our inclination
toward evil desires and greed?
Simply put, remove them from our life.
But that is not so easy to do
because that inclination is very strong.
So how can we stop our inclinations
from starting to roll?
Well, we’ll discuss five things
that we can do
to keep that ball of wicked inclinations in place.
Number one: Control our mind.
Jehovah gave us this wonderful tool,
powerful tool —our mind—
and we can keep our inclinations under control.
But how do we do that?
Here at Colossians 3:2
it says: “Keep your minds fixed
on the things above.”
So when the mind wants to go where it should not,
immediately bring it under control.
Stop it from going where it is bad.
We have a choice in what we think about.
Don’t allow that ball
of wicked reasoning to start rolling.
Don’t even think about it.
The more time spent thinking about something
means that it is much more likely that we will do it.
So the second one:
Control our emotions.
How do we do that?
Well, don’t let our emotions control us.
See our imperfect inclinations for what they really are.
They are imperfect and they are selfish
—like naughty little children.
When we don’t get our way,
our emotions can become like a screaming child.
It wants something. It wants it now.
It does not understand reason,
and the good mother refuses to give in to the child.
Now, if we’re not careful, our emotions will take over,
screaming blue murder,
demanding that we get it now.
Let’s read here 1 Corinthians 6:12,
and we’ll read the second part of verse 12:
“All things are lawful for me,
“but I will not let myself
be controlled by anything.”
Number three
(to control our inclinations, to keep that ball from rolling):
Recognize the danger of greed.
The last part of our text today at Colossians 3:5 says:
“. . . and greediness, which is idolatry.”
When we fall prey to greed,
our desires become our master, our god,
and we surrender our will,
and we actually become idolaters —self-worshippers.
Now, that does not mean that all desires are bad.
‘Jehovah opens his hand
and satisfies the desire of every living thing.’
The difference between normal desire and greed
might be likened to the difference between the small campfire
that cooks food and the blazing inferno
that consumes a forest.
Number four (to control our inclinations):
Do not be naive.
Let us read here Proverbs 14:15, 16
—Proverbs 14:15, 16:
“The naive person believes every word,
“but the shrewd one ponders each step.
“The wise one is cautious and turns away from evil,
but the stupid one is reckless and overconfident.”
Do not for a moment think,
‘Well, this is not going to happen to me.’
Don’t be fooled by your own desires.
Greed can never be satisfied.
It never says, “Enough!”
A brother who was addicted
said this about every time that he gave in;
he said, “I was drawn by a force so powerful
that I did not turn back until it was too late.”
Once that ball starts rolling, very little can stop it.
Number five (to stop that inclination):
Be honest with yourself.
Let us read here Romans 7:22, 23
—Romans 7:22, 23.
It says: “I really delight in the law of God
“according to the man I am within,
“but I see in my body another law
“warring against the law of my mind
and leading me captive to sin’s law that is in my body.”
So it speaks there about a war.
This is war!
Paul was in this war; we are in this war,
and there will be painful injuries.
A soldier, for example,
may damage a limb badly during battle,
and it has to be amputated.
At some point, he has to accept the fact
that he is going to lose a limb
and agree for it to be cut off.
Now, we’re not talking about literally cutting off members.
But at some point,
we need to face the facts.
We must agree in our heart
that we will give up a habit or a custom
that we feel is as precious
as a hand or a foot or an eye.
This is not a game.
Life depends on this.
Two things: Admit that we have a problem.
And number two:
Do whatever it takes to root it out of our life.
So in summary,
yes, obey the command
to “deaden . . . your body members.”
The battleground is our own heart.
If we discover an inclination that is bad,
stop it immediately.
Cut it off. Throw it away.
No harm will come to us.
When we do this, we really begin to live.
It is exactly as the psalmist says
at Psalm 63:
“Your loyal love is better than life.”

cn.text: 今天的经文
可能会让你想到两个问题
一个是地上的肢体到底是指什么？
还有
我们怎样才能处死这些地上的肢体？
这节经文让我们想到耶稣说的话
失去我们的手，我们的脚或者眼睛
也比整个人被毁灭来得好
在圣经里
手、脚或眼睛常常用来比喻
在生活中我们所做或者所想的事情
手，常常指我们做的东西或成就的事
脚，可以走路或跑步
通常跟我们怎样生活联系在一起
眼睛，指的是我们怎样看事情
跟我们的想法有关，反映我们的喜好
不过地上的肢体指的又是什么呢？
他指的不是我们实际身体的某个部位
例如手、脚或眼睛
他指的是
我们不完美的倾向或错误的欲望
保罗在歌罗西书3:5
就提到了一些错误的欲望
包括淫乱、不洁、放纵的性欲、不当的渴求
或者有些译本说是邪恶的渴求和贪婪
我们生来就不完美，很容易有犯罪的倾向
所以我们很容易变得贪婪
或产生错误的欲望
如果你把一个球，放在一个倾斜的桌子上
那么球自然会往比较低的那一边滚去
我们人人生来都不完美
所以会有一种倾向做错误的事
那么我们要怎样处死或制止
这种贪婪或邪恶的欲望呢？
就是要去除这些想法
不过要这样做非常不容易
因为错误的欲望有时是非常强烈的
那么我们怎样阻止这个球往下滚
抵抗我们错误的欲望呢？
接下来，我们一起考虑五个方法
可以帮助我们克制这些错误的欲望
第一，要控制我们的思想
耶和华给我们一个美好而强大的工具
就是我们的思考能力
好好运用这个工具
可以帮助我们克制错误的欲望
我们可以怎样做呢？
在歌罗西书3:2，经文说
“你们的思想要专注于天上的事。”
所以当我们的头脑出现错误欲望的时候
要立刻控制它
不要让它继续往坏的方向倾斜
我们的头脑要想什么
是自己可以控制的
不要允许自己一直想着不对的事情
要控制自己
我们花越多时间想着一件事
通常就越有可能真的采取行动
第二个方法
要控制我们的情绪
可以怎么做呢？
不要让我们的情绪控制我们
要认清我们不完美的倾向
我们的情绪和感情都是不完美的
可能像个淘气的小孩
我们得不到我们想要的东西时
情绪可以像个抓狂的孩子一样
他想要的东西，他现在就要，完全不讲理
可是一个明理的妈妈不会对孩子有求必应
如果我们不小心，情绪可能会控制我们
让我们有一种错觉
认为自己理应得到想要的一切
我们看看哥林多前书6:12
我们会读读这个经文的后半部分
经文说
“什么事我都可以做
但我不会让任何事控制我。”
第三个帮助我们克服错误的欲望
阻止我们内心错误倾向的方法
就是要认清贪婪带来的危险
歌罗西书3:5
经文的最后部分说“贪婪就等于拜偶像”
当我们成为贪婪的猎物
错误的欲望就变成了我们的主人、我们的神
我们向贪婪屈服，崇拜他
结果成了拜偶像的人
我们不是说所有的欲望都是错误的
耶和华也说，他会张手满足众生的愿望
不过如果我们把正当的愿望
比作野炊时煮饭用的营火
那么错误的欲望
就是摧毁整个森林的熊熊烈火
两者是截然不同的
第四个克服错误欲望的方法是
不要做天真无知的人
让我们一起读读箴言14:15,16
“天真无知的人，凡话都信
精明审慎的人，步步留心
明智的人小心谨慎，远离恶事
愚昧的人行事鲁莽，过度自信。”
我们一定不要这样想
我一定不会做这些事
千万不要被你的欲望骗了
贪婪的心是永远无法被满足的
它永远不会说：“够了！”
有一个弟兄，他曾经被错误的欲望控制
他分享他的感受，说
“错误的欲望就像一股强大的力量控制着我
迫使我向他屈服。”
如果让欲望控制了我们
就像球开始往下滚，就很难停下来了
第五个克制欲望的方法
是要对自己诚实
让我们一起看看罗马书7:22,23
经文说
“我的内心确实喜欢上帝的法律
但我看出身体里有另一种法律
跟我思想的法律交战，要俘掳我
使我受制于身体里罪的法律。”
经文提到了交战
这是一场战争
保罗曾经参与这场战争
我们也正在打这场仗
受伤或感到疼痛是在所难免的
举例来说，一个士兵可能受了重伤
后来必须失去身体的一部分
对他来说，他需要理解医生的做法
也不得不接受现实，他可能需要被截肢
我们现在
不是在讨论实际砍掉身体的某个部分
但我们需要认真想想以下的问题
有一些爱好或习惯
对我们来说，就像手、脚或眼睛一样宝贵
我真的从心底里接受，甘心放弃它吗？
这不是儿戏，这关系到我们的生命
我们学到
第一，要看出自己的问题
第二，要尽全力把它从我们的生活中除去
总结一下
是的，我们要听从劝告
努力治死地上的肢体
这是一场内心的战争
如果我们发现内心有错误的欲望和想法
要立刻制止它，要把它砍下来，扔掉
这一定会帮助我们
我们努力这样做，就会得到真正的快乐
就像诗篇执笔者在诗篇第63篇所说的一样
“你的忠贞之爱比生命更美好。”

en.text: Welcome to your Bible study!
Millions around the world enjoy
this interactive Bible course,
and we hope you will too.
What will you learn?
How to have a happy family life,
how to cope with anxiety,
how to draw closer to God,
and why you can hope for a better future.
What can you expect during a study session?
Your teacher may begin the study with a brief prayer.
Next, you will discuss
the first page of the lesson,
read a paragraph,
and then discuss the question for that paragraph
before reading the next.
Most paragraphs have key Bible verses highlighted.
Your teacher will also read and discuss with you other verses,
especially those marked “Read.”
Next, read and discuss the section “Dig Deeper.”
By reading scriptures,
discussing questions,
and watching videos that are available to you,
you will learn more about how the topic of the lesson
can help you personally.
Finally, after reviewing the lesson,
your teacher may say a prayer to end the study session.
How often do you need to have a study session?
And how long should each session last?
This is flexible.
But to maximize the benefits of this course,
we recommend covering at least one lesson per week.
The Bible is the world’s best guide to a happy life.
Discover how it can help you in this interactive Bible course.

都很喜欢我们的互动式圣经课程
希望你也会喜欢

怎样克服忧虑？

你也会学到

为什么这些希望一定会实现？

接着，讨论每一课第一页的内容
