titles.ko: 아렌시비아 가족: 삼 형제가 세 자매와 결혼해 고난의 때에 여호와를 신뢰하다
titles.en: The Arencibias: Three Brothers Married to Three Sisters Lean on Jehovah in Times of Distress
titles.cn: 阿伦西维亚一家：信赖耶和华，克服难题

title: 로버트 시렌코: “그들이 한 몸이 될 것이다” (창세 2:24)

ko.text: 남자와 여자가 결혼하면 ‘한 몸이 된다’고 했습니다.
어떻게 그 말처럼 살 수 있습니까?
그런 좋은 본을 보인 부부가 성경에 나옵니까?
‘사람이 계속 혼자 있는 것이 좋지 않으니,
내가 그를 위해 그의 보완자가 될 돕는 자를 만들겠다.’”
“그래서 여호와 하느님께서 사람을 깊이 잠들게 하셨고,
그가 자고 있을 때에 그의 갈빗대 하나를 빼낸 다음
‘드디어 내 뼈 중의 뼈, 내 살 중의 살이 나타났구나.
남자가 아버지와 어머니를 떠나 아내에게 고착할 것이며
그럼 첫 번째 질문으로, 누가 이 말을 했습니까?
아담이 한 말은 23절에 나오는 시적인 표현뿐입니다.
그 성구를 보면 아담의 말이 따옴표 안에 들어 있습니다.
창세기를 모세가 썼으니까 모세가 한 말일까요?
모세는 아담과 하와의 결혼을 보지도 못했죠.
또 약 2500년 후에야 창세기를 쓰기 시작했고,
그것도 자기 생각이 아닌 영감받은 말을 썼습니다.
“한 몸”이라는 이 표현을 쓴 성서 필자는
누가 그 말을 했는지 알 수 있습니다.
마태는 이 내용을 기록하면서 예수의 말씀을 인용했죠.
남자가 아버지와 어머니를 떠나 아내에게 고착할 것이며,
따라서 그들은 더 이상 둘이 아니라 한 몸입니다.
네, 마태는 이 말을 한 분이 여호와라고 밝혀 줍니다.
이 사실을 보면 결혼이 얼마나 신성한 마련인지
결혼으로 짝지어 주셔서 한 몸이 되게’ 하셨습니다.
흥미롭게도 한 성서 해설서는 이 점에 관해 이렇게 알려 줍니다.
그분만이 결혼이 무엇인지 결정하실 수 있다. ...
결혼이란 한 남자와 한 여자의 결합이다.
하느님은 두 남자와 한 여자를, 두 여자와 한 남자를 창조하지도,
두 남자 또는 두 여자를 창조하지도 않으셨다.
일부 전문가들이 어떻게 말하든 하느님의 뜻에 어긋난다.”
“어떤 법정도 하느님이 제정하신 것을 바꿀 수 없다.”
“한 몸이 될 것이다”라는 말은 무슨 뜻입니까?
물론 한 몸이 된다는 것에는 성적인 결합도 포함되지만,
그 말은 더 많은 것을 의미합니다.
정신적으로, 감정적으로, 영적으로 연합되는 것이 포함됩니다.
두 사람은 삶에서 바라는 것들과 목표에서 하나가 되어야 하죠.
“남편은 아내와 떨어질 수 없게 합쳐질 것이다.”
서로 인생에서 가장 가까운 짝이 되는 것이죠.
“한 몸”이라는 것은 언제나 자기 자신보다 상대방을 더 생각하고,
모든 일을 할 때 상대방을 고려해야 한다는 뜻입니다.
그러므로 독신인 사람이 결혼하면 생각을 내 것에서 우리 것으로,
단지 서류 상이 아니라 마음으로 독신 생활은 끝났고
세 번째 질문으로, 어떻게 그 말처럼 살 수 있습니까?
안타깝게도 요즘 많은 사람은 결혼을 아주 가볍게 여기고,
무고한 배우자가 간음한 배우자를 용서하지 않을 때뿐이라고
그럼 이 점에 관해 바울이 한 말을
매춘부와 한 몸이 된다는 것을 모릅니까?
‘둘이 한 몸이 될 것이다’라고 그분이 말씀하셨습니다.”
자기 배우자에게서 떨어져서 제3자와 한 몸이 되는 것입니다.
한 몸인 남편과 아내의 결합을 끊는 것은
몸을 두 동강으로 자르는 것과 같습니다.
결혼한 두 사람이 아무튼 더는 서로를 좋아하지 않는다면
두 사람은 서로 어떤 점에 끌렸는지 떠올려 보고
그 감정을 되살려 보려고 노력해야 합니다.
동시에 부부 사이뿐 아니라 두 사람의 영성도
부부는 한 몸이라는 여호와의 견해대로 살았던
남편과 아내가 한 몸이 되어야 한다는
그의 충실한 아내의 내조를 떠올리지 않을 수 없었습니다.
그리스도인 그리스어 성경에 여섯 번 언급되는데,
그 모든 경우에 부부가 함께 일하고
또 한 사람만 언급된 적이 없죠.
그들은 집에서, 세속 일에서, 봉사에서 늘 함께 일했습니다.
그들의 결혼 생활이 영적으로 높은 수준을 유지한 건
왕국을 위해 나란히 그리스도인 활동을 하면서
우리는 각자 하는 일과 책임이 달라서
하루에 많은 시간 배우자와 떨어져 있을지 모릅니다.
부부가 참숭배와 관련된 활동을 함께 할 때
결혼 생활이 튼튼해진다는 걸 알 수 있습니다.
함께 그리스도인 집회에 참여하고, 함께 봉사하고, 함께 기도하고,
점점 더 한 몸으로 생각하고 느끼고 행동하게 됩니다.
이제 우린 누가 그 말을 했는지 압니다.
배우자와 늘 가까이 지내고 결혼의 띠를 잘 유지해야 합니다.
그리고 아굴라와 브리스길라의 훌륭한 본을 따라야겠습니다.

en.text: Genesis 2:24 says of a man and a woman
who marry that they are
to “become one flesh.”
Now, that raises some questions:
Whose words are those?
What do they mean?
How can we show that we believe them?
And is there a good example in the Bible of a couple who did?
Let’s start with looking at the context.
If you’d open your Bibles, please, to Genesis chapter 2,
and we’ll start with verse 18—Genesis 2.
It reports: “Then Jehovah God said:
“‘It is not good for the man to continue to be alone.
I am going to make a helper for him, as a complement of him.’”
Continuing in verse 21:
“So Jehovah God caused the man to fall into a deep sleep, and while he was sleeping,
“he took one of his ribs and then closed up the flesh over its place.
“And Jehovah God built the rib that he had taken from the man into a woman,
“and he brought her to the man.
“Then the man said:
“‘This is at last bone of my bones and flesh of my flesh.
“This one will be called Woman, because from man she was taken.’
“That is why a man will leave his father and his mother
and he will stick to his wife, and they will become one flesh.”
So our first question is, Whose words are these?
Adam’s?
No.
The only words attributed to Adam are when he waxed poetic in verse 23.
And you can see that from the opening and closing quotation marks in that verse.
Well, then it must have been Moses’ words because,
after all, he wrote the Bible book of Genesis.
No.
He was not present at the time of the first marriage.
He did not start writing until some 2,500 years later,
and even then, he was writing what he was inspired to write.
Three Bible writers use this expression, “one flesh”
—Matthew, Mark, and Paul.
And it’s Matthew who gives us the clue as to whose words they are.
So let’s turn to Matthew chapter 19,
Matthew 19
beginning with verse 4.
And here Matthew writes and quotes Jesus;
it says: “In reply he [Jesus] said:
“‘Have you not read that the one who created them
“‘from the beginning made them male and female and said:
“‘“For this reason a man will leave his father and his mother
“‘and will stick to his wife, and the two will be one flesh”?
“‘So that they are no longer two, but one flesh.
Therefore, what God has yoked together, let no man put apart.’”
So Matthew makes it clear that Jehovah said those words.
And shouldn’t that elevate in everyone’s mind
the sanctity of the marital union?
As Jesus said, ‘God created male and female’ —two complementary genders—
and he ‘yoked them together in marriage as one flesh.’
Now, it’s interesting what The Bible Exposition Commentary
says about this: “God established marriage,
“and therefore only God can control its character . . .
“It is a union between one man and one woman.
“God did not create two men and one woman,
“two women and one man, two men, or two women.
“‘Group marriages,’ ‘gay marriages,’
“and other variations are contrary to the will of God,
no matter what some psychologists and jurists may say.”
“No court of law can change what God has established.”
And those are comments we can agree with.
Now, our second question is, What do these words mean: “They will become one flesh”?
Well, of course, the one-flesh relationship certainly involves sexual union,
but it goes beyond that because it includes a husband and wife
who have achieved mental, emotional, and spiritual harmony.
They are to have a oneness in their purpose and desires.
As Bible translator William Barclay renders it at Matthew 19:5:
“The husband will be joined inseparably to his wife.”
So in marriage, a man and a woman
are to become each other’s closest partner in life.
Being “one flesh” means that they must always
be thinking more of each other than of themselves,
that they must consider each other in everything they do.
So when single people marry, they need to shift
their thinking from mine to ours,
from me to we.
And so they must stop being single at heart
and come to be married at heart, not just on paper.
Now, our third question is,
How can we show that we believe these words?
Well, sad to say, many people these days
take a very casual attitude toward marriage,
and when the relationship becomes strained,
they just give up and walk out on their mate.
But that is not the Christian way.
Marriage is to be a lifelong relationship.
Just a few verses later on at Matthew 19:9,
Jesus taught that the only Scriptural ground for dissolving marriage
is when an innocent mate
chooses not to forgive an adulterous partner.
And that is because sexual relations outside the marriage bond
are a gross perversion of the one-flesh union.
Now, let’s read Paul’s words about this
at 1 Corinthians chapter 6
—1 Corinthians 6:16;
he said: “Do you not know that anyone who is joined to a prostitute
“is one body with her?
For ‘the two,’ says he, ‘will be one flesh.’”
So the adulterer pulls away from his marriage mate
and makes himself one flesh with a third person.
That, then, is the only Scriptural basis for divorce.
But divorce is a very painful experience.
As one sociologist put it, “Divorce is drastic surgery.”
To sever the one-flesh bond between husband and wife
would be like sawing oneself asunder.
What, though, if no adultery has been committed?
What if, for some reason, two people who are married to each other
just don’t like each other any longer?
Divorce is not an option.
Instead, they need to remind themselves of what attracted them to each other
and work at rekindling those feelings,
while at the same time looking to Jehovah for help
in not only strengthening their marriage
but also their spirituality.
Our fourth question is,
What Scriptural example is there of a married couple
who believed this one-flesh idea?
Turn to Romans 16:3, please,
Romans 16:3; here Paul writes:
“Give my greetings to Prisca [or Priscilla] and Aquila,
my fellow workers in Christ Jesus.”
So, yes, Aquila and Priscilla —what a model of a close and united couple
living up to what Jehovah meant when he said that a husband or wife
should become one flesh!
And Paul, who worked closely with them,
could not think of that dear brother
without recalling the faithful cooperation of his wife.
So it’s a fine example for Christian couples today.
And in every one of the six references to this couple
in the Christian Greek Scriptures, we find them working together,
cooperating without competition or strife.
And never is one mentioned without the other.
They constantly worked together in their home,
in their secular work, in the ministry.
And surely it was the time spent together in Christian activities
that kept their marriage on a high spiritual plane,
working side by side to further the Kingdom work.
Now, you and your marriage mate may be apart
for much of the day due to different work and responsibilities.
But can you find time each day to eat meals together,
to do household chores together, to take walks together,
to be together to get caught up
on what has gone on in your lives during the day?
Aquila and Priscilla proved that being united
in activities related to true worship
can keep a couple’s thinking and goals aligned,
and that does strengthen a marriage.
For example, studying together,
participating in congregation meetings together,
sharing in the ministry together, praying together,
in doing all of that,
a person’s interests, priorities, and habits
will harmonize with those of one’s spouse until,
like Aquila and Priscilla,
we increasingly think, feel,
and act as one flesh.
So now we know who said the words.
It was Jehovah.
We understand what they mean —achieving harmony
in one’s relationship with one’s mate.
And we can certainly prove that we believe these words
by staying close to our mate and maintaining our marriage bond.
And then we have that excellent example of Aquila and Priscilla to abide by.

cn.text: 创世记2:24说
结婚的男女应该“合为一体”
这让我们想到几个问题
这段话是谁说的呢？
他的话是什么意思呢？
我们同意这段话吗？
圣经里有没有这样的好榜样呢？
我们先看看经文的上下文
请打开你的圣经到创世记第二章
我们先看看第18节
经文说
耶和华上帝说
“那个人独自生活不好
我要为他造一个合适的伴侣帮助他。”
第21节接着说
“耶和华上帝就使他沉睡
他睡着的时候
上帝取了他的一根肋骨
然后把那里的肉合起来
耶和华上帝用那个人的肋骨造了一个女人
把她带到那个人面前。”
那个人说［这是亚当说的］
“我骨中的骨、肉中的肉终于出现了
她要叫做‘女人’
因为她是从男人身上取出来的。”
亚当说完了
然后24节说
“所以人要离开父母，与妻子长相厮守
二人合为一体。”
这段话是谁说的呢？是亚当吗？
不是
圣经里唯一记录亚当说的话
是在第23节的诗
你可以从经文当中的引号看出这点
你可能会认为
这段话是摩西说的
因为创世记是他写的
也不是
亚当夏娃结婚的时候，摩西并不在场
他在2500多年之后才开始执笔写圣经
而且他所写的是耶和华指引他所写下的
有三个执笔者都用了“合为一体”这个词
包括马太、马可和保罗
而马太给我们一些线索
让我们知道这段话是谁说的
我们一起看看马太福音
第19章
从第4节开始
这里马太记录了耶稣说的话
第4节，耶稣回答
“你们没有读过吗？
最初上帝创造人，造了男人和女人
［然后耶稣引用了上帝的话］说
‘因此人要离开父母，与妻子长相厮守
二人合为一体。’
［耶稣继续说］
所以夫妻不再是两个人，而是一体了
上帝结合的，人就不可分开。”
马太的记载让我们清楚看出
这段话是耶和华说的
这帮助我们明白婚姻是多么神圣的
像耶稣说的
耶和华造了男人和女人，这两个互补的性别
通过婚姻的安排，耶和华使两个人成为一体
在英语的《圣经注释与评论》这本书里
这样说
“婚姻是上帝创造的
只有他有权力为婚姻制定标准
婚姻是一个男人跟一个女人的结合
上帝不是创造了两个男人一个女人
两个女人一个男人
两个男人或两个女人
所以多夫多妻、同性婚姻
或任何其他形式的婚姻
不管其他专家怎么说
都不是上帝认可的
上帝建立的婚姻安排是不可能改变的。”
我们很同意这段话，对吗？
我们的第二个问题是
“合为一体”到底是什么意思呢？
当然，“合为一体”包括在性方面彼此结合
但不仅是这样
这句话的意思也包括
夫妻两个人要在思想、感情和信仰上合一
他们需要在生活上追求共同的理想和目标
我们的《圣经新世界译本》
在马太福音19:5说
“人要与妻子长相厮守。”
所以结婚后
丈夫和妻子就成为彼此生命中最亲密的伙伴
“合为一体”表示他们总是为对方着想
他们做任何事总是考虑对方的感受
而不是自己
所以，一个单身的人结婚之后
就必须调整他的想法
不再只是想着“我”，而是“我们”
结婚不只是一张证书
而是从此两个人要一起生活
第三个问题
我们认同上帝对婚姻的看法吗？
很遗憾的是
现在很多人对婚姻都怀有随便的态度
当他们的关系出现问题时
很多人选择放弃或结束这段婚姻
但基督徒不应该这样
婚姻应该是一种永久的结合
就像在接着的经文
马太福音19:9，耶稣提到
圣经认可人可以离婚的唯一理由
就是当清白的一方决定不原谅
犯了淫乱的配偶
人要是犯了淫乱，就破坏了
耶和华原本要两个人合为一体的安排
我们看看保罗对这件事有怎样的看法
哥林多前书6:16
这节经文说
“你们不知道跟妓女结合的
就是跟她合为一体吗？
因为上帝说：‘二人合为一体’”
一个人犯了淫乱
就是把自己和配偶分开
跟另外一个人合为一体
所以，圣经认可人离婚的唯一理由
就是人犯了淫乱
不过，离婚非常痛苦
一个社会学家说
“离婚就好像动了一场大手术。”
要把合为一体的丈夫和妻子分开
就像把一个身体用锯子锯开一样
不过，如果问题不是淫乱呢？
只是因为某些理由
不再像以前一样喜欢对方了，那怎么办？
这不是离婚的借口
夫妻应该努力回想当初为什么爱上对方
而且付出努力再次燃起对对方的爱
同时寻求耶和华的帮助
求耶和华巩固他们的婚姻
并努力做耶和华看为对的事
我们的第四个问题是
圣经里有没有一些值得学习的好榜样？
他们对婚姻有耶和华的看法吗？
请跟我一起翻开罗马书16:3
保罗写道
“请代我向百姬拉和亚居拉问好
他们是我的伙伴，一起为基督耶稣工作。”
百姬拉和亚居拉是多么好的榜样
他们亲密无间
就像耶和华对婚姻定下的安排一样
两人成为一体
保罗每次想到他亲爱的弟兄亚居拉时
一定也会想到他忠贞的妻子百姬拉
他们是今天所有基督徒夫妻的好榜样
《希腊语经卷》有6次提到这对夫妻
他们总是一起工作
他们互相合作，而不是彼此竞争
而且他们的名字每一次都是同时出现
他们总是互相扶持
不管是在家、在工作时
或是一起传道
我们相信他们拨出时间一起聚会
一起推广王国的工作
一定让他们之间的关系更紧密了

en.text: Before, we had the written Watchtower,
but I couldn’t understand it.
At the meeting,
I couldn’t really grasp everything either,
so I didn’t feel confident to raise my hand and comment.
I tried to study the magazine,
but I couldn’t understand it,
and neither could the other deaf brothers.
At the meetings, it was frustrating
not being able to understand.
From the very beginning,
we saw Jehovah’s hand in matters.
In 1996, we went from being a small group
to a congregation,
and then more groups were formed in different parts of the country.
And later, even assemblies were interpreted in Peruvian Sign Language.
However, we realized
that our deaf brothers and sisters couldn’t progress any further,
and this was because they didn’t have
an official translation of the Watchtower  magazine
in their own language.
The deaf wanted
to participate in the meetings,
but they always had to rely on us
to understand the publications.
It was just so frustrating for them.
A lot of them didn’t even want a copy of the publication
because they felt powerless to understand it.
For many years, the deaf brothers begged:
“Please, we want The Watchtower.
We need to prepare in our own language!”
We even received videos from different parts of the country saying,
“Ask the Branch Committee, the Governing Body
—we need The Watchtower, please!”
When the letter arrived saying, “Yes, you can translate The Watchtower,”
we were jumping with joy!
We wanted to shout out loud and tell them,
“Brothers, here is your Watchtower!”
But we had to control ourselves and wait for the moment of the official announcement
when Jehovah would say, ‘Here is your gift, The Watchtower!’
When they made the announcement about the new Watchtower  in sign language,
the brothers were jumping out of their seats!
The whole place was just electrified!
Everyone was cheering!
The Watchtower in Peruvian Sign Language?
Wow!
I was so happy that I started to cry.
There are many benefits to having The Watchtower  in Peruvian Sign Language.
The brothers can download it from the website
two months ahead of time and prepare without stress.
Another excellent benefit is that now the elders who are deaf
can study and understand the Watchtower
and prepare it in order to conduct at the meeting
because it’s in their own language.
Now, not only can our deaf brothers and sisters
receive their own spiritual food
directly from the official translation of the Watchtower  magazine,
but even better, they receive the spiritual food
at the same time as any other language group in the world.
When I view The Watchtower,
I can understand everything!
My heart is overflowing with happiness.
I’m so thankful to Jehovah for this support.
What I’m learning now
is helping me to progress spiritually.
I am very happy that now
I can deepen my friendship with Jehovah!
Now that we have The Watchtower
in Peruvian Sign Language,
I’m so excited and it touches my heart.
It’s the best feeling in the world
that all my deaf brothers and sisters can understand just like I can.
The spiritual light is progressively getting “brighter and brighter” for us.
It’s obvious that Jehovah’s spirit is guiding the work.
At last, this light is reaching our hearts.
Now all  the deaf in Peru are benefiting from this blessing.
We are so, so thankful to you, Jehovah!

she spoke up.

I needed to tell him how I felt,
but I needed to do it the right way.
That night we spoke,
and little by little things started to improve.
Imitating Sarah really worked.

한편 아내는 남편의 활동과 일에 관심을 가짐으로
남편이 자신의 일상을 공유하도록 격려할 수 있습니다.
아내가 남편에게 일 얘기는 하지 말라고 한다면,
그러면 아내는 남편의 중요한 일상을 모르게 됩니다.
남편이 가족 부양을 위해 하는 일에 감사를 표현하고,
남편이 하는 일 얘기가 재밌지 않을 수 있지만,
두 번째 예를 고려해 보죠, 문제를 해결할 때입니다.
남편과 아내가 차를 타고 목적지를 향해 가다가
아내는 지나가는 사람에게 길을 물어보자고 합니다.
남편은 ‘내가 찾을 수 있는데 왜 그러지?’
낯선 사람에게 길을 잃은 것처럼 보이기를 원하지 않습니다.
다른 사람의 도움 없이도 찾아갈 수 있다는 걸
단지 다른 사람에게 물어봐서 도움을 얻고
어떻게 하면 아내를 기쁘게 할까 하고 ... 염려합니다.”
남편은 아내를 기쁘게 하고, 아내의 존경을 얻고 싶어 합니다.
남편은 존경을 바라는 면에서 균형 잡힌 시각을 가져야 합니다.
가끔 길을 묻거나 도움을 청하는 것도 괜찮습니다.
한편, 아내는 남편이 어떤 문제를 해결하려고 할 때
말이나 어조로 조급한 태도를 나타내지 않도록
가족의 문제를 해결하고 싶어 하는 남편의 마음을 잘 아는 아내는
그러한 사소한 일에서 지원을 받게 되면,
더 큰 문제가 있을 때 자신감을 갖고
가정을 잘 이끌어 나갈 수 있습니다.
부부 중 한 사람이 말을 하는데, 다른 한쪽이
아내가 그러면 안 된다고 하는 경우도 있죠.
아내의 기분을 상하게 하는 얘기를 하는 경우도 있습니다.
아내가 다른 사람들 앞에서 하는 말에
남편은 큰 상처를 받을 수 있습니다.
악한 것이 아니라 선한 것으로 보답한다.”
따라서 다른 사람과 함께 있을 때,
심지어 가족이나 자녀와 함께 있을 때도,
남편이 하던 걸 가로채려 하지 마십시오.
아내는 다른 사람 앞에서 남편에게 말하는 방식을 통해
에베소 5:33이 어떻게 도움이 될 수 있습니까?
하지만 아내에겐 우정이나 좋은 관계가 중요하기 때문에,
남편이 자신을 깎아내리는 농담을 할 때
아내는 남편 여러분을 모든 걸 나눌 수 있는
서로의 문제를 말하기에 가장 좋은 때는
다른 사람이 듣지 못하게 이야기할 수 있습니다.
남편은 아내에게 사랑을 보일 수 있습니다.
지금까지 다음의 세 가지 예를 통해,
사랑과 존경이 행복한 결혼 생활에 도움이 된다는 걸 보았습니다.
다른 사람들 앞에서 행동할 때를 살펴봤죠.
배우자를 대하는 면에서 좋은 습관을 갖고 계십니까?
불완전한 두 사람의 결혼 생활에 도움을 줍니다.
이 구절의 단 몇 마디 말로 여호와께선
결혼 마련에 대한 핵심 원칙을 알려 주십니다.
각자에게 무엇이 필요한지, 무엇이 중요한지 알려 주시죠.
하느님을 기쁘시게 하는 결혼 생활의 비결입니다.
여호와께서 마련하신 대로 행복한 결혼 생활을 해 나가기 위해,
최선을 다해 결혼 생활에 적용하도록 합시다.

en.text: Jehovah designed marriage
as a beautiful and rewarding relationship
between a husband and a wife.
When a husband and wife
fulfill their God-given roles
and they treat each other
with love and respect,
their marriage is a wonderful and intimate friendship.
A marriage that has good patterns
shaped by Jehovah’s principles
looks like this well-balanced family circle.
But if a married couple over time
has set bad patterns in how they deal with each other,
this is often the result.
Life is going to be a bit rough for them.
Let’s consider what Jehovah says
about the roles of husband and wife
and then discuss how love and respect
are real keys to a happy marriage.
So, what roles did Jehovah give
to the man and woman in marriage?
Well, Jehovah places the husband as head of the family.
Ephesians 5:23 says:
“A husband is head of his wife.”
So that means that the husband makes final decisions for the family.
And his decisions will reflect his love for his wife,
his children, and his understanding of their spiritual,
physical, and emotional needs.
At 1 Corinthians 11:3,
we get a sense, though, of how Jehovah feels about the husband’s role.
And as we read this together, I want you to imagine
Jehovah saying to husbands: ‘Yes, you’re head of the family.’
“But I want you to know that the head
“of every man is the Christ;
in turn, the head of a woman is the man.”
Sounds a lot like a father-in-law speaking to the groom:
“You can marry my daughter,
but you’d better treat her good because you’re responsible to me.”
Well, Jehovah is giving a very clear message for husbands.
Jehovah will hold you accountable to him
for how you treat your wife.
It’s something for us husbands to think about, isn’t it?
Well, what about the role of a wife?
Jehovah assigned wives as a beloved partner to her husband.
And as partners, they can discuss important family matters
and work together to make their marriage a success.
Jehovah placed the woman under the headship of the man,
and as such, her role is to be in subjection to him.
At Ephesians 5:22,
it says: “Let wives be in subjection to their husbands as to the Lord.”
Subjection —said a certain way, it almost sounds bad:
“You have to be in subjection!”
But is the subjection of a Christian wife to a Christian husband a bad thing?
No.
See, subjection as described in the Bible
is not about being subservient;
it’s about her role in the marriage.
You’re partners, each with a beautiful role to fulfill.
We could illustrate it with watching a couple ice skating.
As they move gracefully across the ice, do you think to yourself,
‘How come they never let her hold him over her head?’
Well, no.
You look at him; you look at her.
It’s obvious who should hold who over their head.
Well, just as we admire and respect a woman’s role as an ice skating partner,
a husband deeply loves and appreciates
his wife’s role as his partner
as they work gracefully together to make their marriage a success.
Well, now that we’ve briefly reviewed the roles for husbands and wives,
let’s read together a key Scriptural principle
at Ephesians 5:33
that shows how Jehovah wants husbands and wives
to fulfill their roles in marriage.
Ephesians 5:33:
“Each one of you must love his wife as he does himself;
on the other hand, the wife should have deep respect for her husband.”
Well, the obvious message in this scripture
is that husbands should love their wives
and wives should respect their husbands.
However, there’s another way to look at this scripture
and learn something about husbands and wives.
Jehovah God is telling us what each mate needs.
Men need respect, and women need love.
Now, this is not to say that men don’t need love
and women don’t need to be respected.
However, it does mean that men
tend to emphasize respect and status
and women often emphasize
intimacy, connection, and love.
This perfect principle can help us to understand
why our husband or wife may act or feel a certain way.
Now, this difference in emphasis affects many areas of married life.
Let’s consider three examples
of how this powerful Scriptural principle of love and respect
can give us insight into how a husband and wife
talk to each other,
how they solve problems,
and how they act in the company of others.
Let’s consider our first example:
how they talk to each other.
Now, since a wife’s emphasis
is on being loved,
her conversations often stress friendship
and connection when she talks to her husband.
She’s eager to share the details of her life with him
and in this way become closer to him.
She wants him, in turn, to share with her the details of his day and life.
Husbands, your wife
feels loved when you learn to communicate with her
in a way that tells her you truly care about her.
She places great emphasis on conversation and sharing her life with you
and likewise you sharing your life with her.
For example, a wife
tells her husband about something
that happened to her that day.
He grows impatient with the story and interrupts
or changes the subject or offers a quick solution.
How does she feel?
‘Why can’t he listen to the whole story?
Has he lost interest in me?’
It’s important that husbands give their wives
their full attention as they speak.
After a long day at work,
his mind may be focused on events that happened to him that day.
And he may without realizing it
feel that the events or conversation of his wife
aren’t on important subjects.
So he may be inclined to play down the events in her life
as unimportant, or trivial,
while events he talks about are substantial and important
because they happened to him.
Well, such a feeling over time can truly discourage a wife.
A husband’s disinterest in her stories
and events of her life feels a lot like disinterest in her.
The advice of Proverbs 20:5 is good for husbands.
It says: “The thoughts of a man’s [or we could say in this case, woman’s] heart
“are like deep waters,
but the discerning man draws them out.”
That’s great advice for husbands.
Husbands, when you draw
your wife out, let her speak from her heart.
That’s an indication of great love
and affection for your dear wife.
Men, on the other hand, often view conversation differently.
A husband comes home, and his wife asks, “How was your day?”
He says: “It was OK. Nothing special.”
But later that night when they’re with a group of friends,
he tells a story about what happened at work.
And she wonders,
‘Well, why didn’t he tell me that when I asked about his day?’
Well, since a man’s emphasis is on respect,
they often use conversation
to establish respect and status with others.
A husband may feel that his wife already respects him,
so there’s no need to tell her the story.
Wives, you can encourage your husband to share his life with you
by being interested in his work and activities.
If you tell him, “Don’t talk to me
about all that work stuff with me,” he won’t
and you’ll cut yourself off from a part of his life.
Show him that you’re proud of what he does to support the family.
Be interested in what happened to him,
how he feels about things, or challenges that he overcame.
While you may not find his work all that interesting,
remember, it is important to him.
Let’s consider our second example:
how they solve problems.
Now I want you to imagine a husband and wife.
They’re in a car, they’re looking for an address,
and they’re lost.
And the wife suggests that they ask someone for directions.
She’s thinking, ‘Why won’t he ask?’
He’s thinking, ‘Why can’t she just let me find it?’
You see, since the man’s emphasis is on respect,
he’s trying to avoid looking lost to a stranger.
The act of asking someone else for directions
may make him feel like he’s in a lower position.
Finding their way is a challenge to him,
and he wants to show his wife that he can find it on his own.
For the woman, such an idea may not come to mind.
She may view it as a simple interchange between them and a stranger.
They get help and directions, and they find out where they’re going.
At 1 Corinthians 7:33, Jehovah tells us:
“But the married man is anxious . . . ,
how he may gain the approval of his wife.”
Wives, your husband is anxious to have your approval and respect.
But on balance, husbands have to be careful
that an emphasis on respect doesn’t become unreasonable.
It won’t hurt us to ask for directions or help at times.
On the other hand, a wife needs to be careful
that she doesn’t show impatience by her words or tone
as her husband works his way through a problem.
A wife who clearly understands her husband’s desire
to solve problems for the family
will understand his actions and will do her part to support him,
even in the little things around the home.
Now, this support in the little areas of life
builds his confidence in her support
and can be a major factor
in whether a husband takes the lead in larger matters.
Our third and final example:
how they act in front of others.
Have you ever seen a couple where one of them is telling a story
and the other is constantly correcting the details?
or the husband is trying to give some direction
and the wife corrects or challenges the direction?
or the husband is telling others some unflattering story
that hurts his wife’s feelings?
How can Ephesians 5:33
help a wife in these situations?
Well, since a husband’s emphasis is on respect,
he’ll be much more sensitive
to comments his wife may make in front of others.
It can hurt a husband deeply
when his wife openly challenges him in front of others.
Proverbs 31:12
has this advice for wives:
“She rewards him with good, not bad,
all the days of her life.”
So when in public or when others are around
—even close family and children—
try not to openly disagree with him, correct him,
or attempt to take over what he’s doing.
How you speak to your husband in front of others
is a great way to show your deep respect for him.
It also builds respect for him in others, including any children in the family.
Well, how can Ephesians 5:33
help a husband act in front of others?
Well, when in public, husbands will want to act
like the husband at Proverbs 31:28.
It says: “Her husband rises up and praises her.”
It’s common today for husbands to make fun of
or even say demeaning things about their wives.
But since a wife places so much emphasis
on connection and friendship,
she can really be hurt when demeaning remarks are said
to get a laugh; it makes her feel awful.
Husbands, your wife considers you her best friend,
the one she shares everything with.
If you break that trust, she feels unloved and hurt.
Now, the best time to bring matters to each other’s attention
is when you’re in private or, if needed, when you can talk in such a way
that others cannot hear what’s being said.
In this way, a wife shows deep respect for her husband
and the husband shows his love for his wife.
So in review, we’ve considered just three situations
that the principle of love and respect
can help us to have a successful marriage:
how a husband and wife talk to each other,
how they solve problems,
and how they act in the company of others.
A good marriage is hard work.
How is your marriage?
Would you say that you’ve developed good patterns
or bad patterns in dealing with each other?
When was the last time you talked as a couple
about love and respect for each other?
Jehovah’s perfect advice at Ephesians 5:33
can help the marriage of two imperfect people.
In just a few words in this verse,
Jehovah is sharing with us a key principle
of how he designed marriage.
He’s telling us what each needs and places emphasis on.
Husbands put emphasis on being respected,
and wives put emphasis on being loved.
And this principle forms a key part
of the divine pattern for marriage.
If you want your marriage to operate as Jehovah designed,
then work hard to apply his perfect principle
of love and respect in your marriage.

cn.text: 耶和华设立婚姻
让夫妻双方享有幸福又有意义的关系
如果夫妻俩都按照上帝的原则生活
以爱和尊重彼此相待
那他们的夫妻关系就会是美满亲密的
如果他们总是按照上帝的原则对待彼此
那家庭就会像这个能平衡转动的车轮一样
但如果随着时间过去
夫妻不再像之前那样相处
那就会变成我手上的这个车轮一样
关系变得很紧张
首先看看上帝如何看待丈夫和妻子的角色
然后再来谈谈爱和尊重
为什么对幸福婚姻那么重要
那么耶和华让丈夫和妻子扮演什么角色呢？
耶和华让丈夫做家庭的头
以弗所书5:23说
“丈夫是妻子的头”
这意味着丈夫会为家庭做最终决定
他的决定会反映出他爱妻子和孩子
也表明他重视家人的健康、幸福
和与耶和华的关系
在哥林多前书11:3
我们可以知道耶和华怎样看待丈夫的角色
让我们一起来读经文
我希望你们可以想象
耶和华正在对丈夫们说话
听起来像岳父对女婿说话
“你可以娶我的女儿
但是你必须好好对待她
因为这是你要负起的责任。”
耶和华给了丈夫一条明确的信息
他要求你要好好照顾自己的妻子
我们做丈夫的
确实要好好思考这一点，不是吗？
那妻子的角色呢？
上帝让妻子做丈夫亲密的伴侣
他们一起商量家里的大小事
也共同努力经营幸福的婚姻
耶和华让女人在男人的领导之下
也就是说女人需要顺服男人
以弗所书5:22说
顺服
有些人听起来可能不太舒服
“你必须要顺服！”
但妻子对丈夫表现顺服是一件坏事吗？
不是的
圣经中提到的顺服不是要人盲目地服从
这指的是妻子该有的态度
夫妻双方要扮演好各自的角色
让我们用双人滑冰做个比喻
当他们在冰上优雅地滑行时，你会不会想
“为什么不让女选手把男选手举到肩上呢？”
当然不会
你看看他们的身型就知道谁该这样做了
就像男选手要尊重和保护自己的同伴一样
丈夫也要深深地爱护和珍惜自己的妻子
他们共同建立一个美满的家庭
我们已经简单回顾了丈夫和妻子的角色
现在让我们来一起读一节非常重要的经文
在以弗所书5:33
经文告诉我们
耶和华希望丈夫和妻子怎样履行自己的角色
以弗所书5:33
这节经文很明确地告诉我们
丈夫应该爱妻子，而妻子应该尊重丈夫
然而，我们可以换个角度看看这节经文
想想可以从中学到什么？
上帝告诉我们夫妻双方的需要
男人需要的是尊重，女人则需要爱
这并不是说男人不需要爱
或女人不需要被尊重
这是指男人更在乎的是被尊重和认可
而女人更在乎的
是亲密的关系、和人交流以及爱
这条完美的原则帮助我们理解
为什么丈夫和妻子的感受和反应
有时是不同的
男女之间的差异可以影响婚姻生活的很多方面
让我们来考虑三个例子
看看这节经文中爱与尊重的原则
如何发挥作用
这三个例子分别是
丈夫和妻子怎样沟通
怎样解决问题
怎样在别人面前互动
第一个例子是夫妻怎样沟通
通常妻子都想确认自己是被爱的
所以当她们和丈夫交谈时
特别看重感情和互动
生活中大大小小的事
她们都想和丈夫分享，以此变得亲密
她们也希望丈夫分享自己工作中发生的事
丈夫们，在和妻子交流时
如果你们能显出对她们的真正关心
她们就能确认自己是被爱的
妻子很重视沟通
也很喜欢和你分享她的生活
同样，你的心情要和她分享
举个例子
妻子告诉自己的丈夫，今天发生了什么事
丈夫很快就变得不耐烦
他打断妻子的话，然后改变话题
或直接说怎么解决，妻子会怎么想呢？
“他为什么不听我说完呢？
他不爱我了吗？”
妻子说话时，丈夫用心听这很重要
一整天的工作后
丈夫满脑子想的可能都还是工作的事
他可能并没有意识到，自己没有留心听
也没有重视妻子对他说的话
他可能下意识地认为
妻子说的事都是小事，没什么大不了的
而自己想的事才重要，因为和工作有关
久而久之，丈夫这样的想法会伤害到妻子
丈夫不再关心她说的话做的事
妻子就会觉得丈夫可能是不再爱她了
箴言20:5给丈夫们非常好的建议
经文说
“人［在这里我们就把她当作是女人吧］
心里的思想好像深处的水
明辨事理的人却能汲引出来。”
这是很棒的建议
丈夫们，如果你想了解妻子的想法
就要仔细聆听她的心里话
那你就能向你心爱的妻子表达爱了
另一方面，关于沟通，男人有不同的看法
丈夫回到家，他的妻子问他
“今天过得好吗？”
他回答
“很好，没事。”
但晚上和朋友在一起时
他就谈很多工作上的事
妻子就想
“今天我问你的时候，你为什么不告诉我呢？”
男人特别需要得到别人的认可
为了得到别人的认可和尊重
他们就愿意跟这些人说很多话
丈夫可能觉得妻子已经很认可他了
所以就没必要多说什么了
妻子们
如果你们对丈夫的工作表现出兴趣
他们就更愿意多和你们说说话了
但如果你对他说
“不要和我说你工作的事情。”
他就真的不会说了
而你，也就真的不能了解你的丈夫了
所以你要让他知道
你很感谢他为了努力养家而做的一切
你很爱他
即使你对丈夫的工作并不感兴趣
但也要尽力了解和关心他
让我们来考虑第二个例子
怎样解决问题
现在请你想象一对夫妻坐在车里
他们在找个地方，但是迷路了
妻子建议他们可以找人问路
她想
“为什么不问呢？”
但丈夫想
“为什么不让我自己找呢？”
既然男人在乎的，是别人的认可

아주 멋진 건물을 지을 수 있게 해 줍니다.
많은 촬영과 녹음 작업이 진행될 것이므로,
부지 중앙에서 가장 가까운 숙소 건물의
따라서 단기간 촬영 작업을 지원하기 위해 오는 형제 자매들이나
사무 공간으로 활용할 수 있을 것입니다.
이 새로운 시설에서 가장 중요한 부분인
이것은 우리가 짓는 가장 큰 건물이 될 것입니다.
여러 곳에 뿔뿔이 흩어져 열심히 일하던 우리의 형제 자매들이
이곳에 모여 한 지붕 아래 일하게 됩니다.
여호와께서 뜻하신 것은 그 무엇도 불가능하지 않다는 것을
앞으로 그분이 우리에게 또 어떤 식으로 보여 주실지
라마포 공사가 어떻게 놀랍게 진척되어 왔는지 살펴보면
여호와께서 우리가 라마포에 “집을 세우도록” 도와주고 계심이 분명합니다!
앞으로도 라마포 공사가 어떻게 진척되고 있는지
다른 보고들을 통해서도 계속 알려 드릴 것입니다.
지난 한 해 동안 이루어진 모든 일을 생각해 보면
여호와께서 전 세계 베델 가족의 희생을 축복해 주고 계심이 분명합니다.
그들은 시편 110:3에 묘사되어 있는 태도를 나타내고 있죠.
따라서 베델 가족과 라마포 공사를 위해
이 팬데믹 기간에 여러분의 수고와 인내를
여러분이 다가오는 특별 강연과 그리스도의 죽음의 기념식에
가능한 한 많은 사람을 초대하기 위해
최선을 다하실 것이라는 점도 잘 알고 있습니다.

en.text: In this update, I’d like to talk with you
about something very close to my heart
—Bethel.
When I learned the truth as a teenager,
I made Bethel service a goal.
After I was baptized, I pioneered for two years
and then I came to Bethel.
And I’ve been here for 36 years now.
So I’m happy to talk to you about how things are going at Bethel
and how the worldwide Bethel family is coping with the pandemic.
No doubt you’ll be encouraged to hear
what helps them to remain joyful in their service.
Many of you have expressed appreciation,
saying that during this pandemic,
we have continued to receive spiritual food.
This includes our weekly meetings,
news articles on jw.org,
new publications, monthly broadcasts,
convention programs, and more.
All of this is possible because of the willing spirit
and hard work of our Bethel family
under challenging circumstances.
Around the world, the Bethel family has been sheltering in place,
in most cases, for about one year.
Our Bethelites have sacrificed opportunities
to spend time in person with family and dear friends,
and they’ve done this with a cooperative and willing spirit.
Why?
Because they love Jehovah and Jesus,
and because they love you.
They want to serve the needs of our worldwide brotherhood.
That’s been a sacrifice for them,
but we know that’s also been a sacrifice for all of you
who have family and friends at Bethel
because you haven’t been able to see them in person
during these difficult times.
In a sense, you’ve made a contribution to the work
by helping members of your family who are at Bethel
to be able to stay and concentrate on their work.
What a beautiful gift your support has been!
Of course, when this all began,
few imagined it would stretch on for so long.
In the following video,
you’ll see what some of our hardworking Bethelites have been doing
to maintain their joy
and keep the Kingdom work going without interruption.
Three things that I miss are traveling,
playing sports,
and taco stands.
I really miss my family.
Well, as I’m living on my own,
the most difficult thing for me
is that I miss the brothers.
I don’t have as much contact with them as I did before.
Most of all, I miss my two young nieces.
I am very close to them.
I really miss hugging the sisters
and the kids in the congregation.
Everything changed overnight
and very suddenly.
The brothers from outside Bethel who came to help us with the recordings
could not do this anymore, so the work increased considerably,
especially for the regional convention.
We had more work than ever.
Right before the pandemic, I was assigned to a new branch.
That means learning a brand-new culture
and starting again, developing friendships.
I didn’t feel as busy as before
or as busy as I would have liked to have been.
And I have to admit, I sometimes have the feeling
that I’m just not as useful as I was before.
My dad had to be admitted to a hospital because he became very ill,
and I felt helpless and guilty
because I couldn’t do what I really wanted to do
—to be with my family.
Because we live in an apartment right in the city center,
we can’t go out.
When you’re lonely and trapped inside four walls,
it’s very easy to get lost in negative thoughts.
I like to think
about the Biblical example of Joseph.
He did not concentrate
on the negative aspects of his situation,
but, rather, he always thought of doing his best
with all the assignments he was given.
Of course, the Bible has helped me a lot.
I think about Bible texts such as Psalm 94:18, 19,
where it says:
“Your loyal love, O Jehovah, kept supporting me.
When anxieties overwhelmed me, you comforted and soothed me.”
Thinking about the Paradise,
I picture myself with my Mom
and my sister Carol, walking along the beach
and watching a beautiful sunset.
We’ll have all eternity to be together.
I do exercise every day,
and I also connect with the congregation for the preaching work.
Increasing the time I spend in the preaching work
has allowed me to focus on helping other people.
Auxiliary pioneering has been my window into the world outside.
When my friends and family ask me how I’m doing, I tell them that I’m OK.
We don’t try to paint an unrealistic picture
that all is fine
and that there are no challenges,
but we try always to be positive.
My wife and I tell them to remain calm
because at Bethel, they take good care of us.
But they still know that it’s not easy.
And every time I see them smile in a video call,
it’s as if they were giving my heart a big hug.
Also, by doing practical things for our parents,
for example, we would connect with them
and read the daily text together.
Being at Bethel during the pandemic is a great privilege
because it gives me the circumstances to be a source of encouragement
for those at Bethel who are going through a rough time
but especially for the friends who are out in the front lines of this battle.
Being at Bethel makes me feel deeply indebted to Jehovah.
He’s been taking care of us spiritually, emotionally, and physically.
And we are here serving at Bethel
(as it has been said) as the “supply line” to support the brothers.
I’m doing this at the most crucial moment of history.
And I’m seeing all of this up close.
That’s why every sacrifice I make for this privilege is worth it.
We deeply appreciate our Bethelites
along with their families and their congregations
for all the sacrifices they’re making in support of the Kingdom work.
We keep all of you dear brothers and sisters in our prayers.
As you saw from the video,
like you, our Bethelites deal with anxieties during the pandemic.
It’s normal to have these feelings.
We know that the trials that we’re experiencing are going to end.
But in the meantime, we’re dealing with very real human emotions.
So, what can we do to cope?
First, be honest about it with Jehovah
and express to him what you’re dealing with.
When David prayed to Jehovah in a time of crisis,
he said at Psalm 142:2:
“Before him I pour out my concern;
before him I tell about my distress.”
We can do the same.
Pour out your concerns and anxieties to Jehovah.
He promises to help us cope if we have faith.
Pray for faith each day.
Along with this, keep in mind
that today’s problems are only temporary.
The last days had a beginning,
and the last days will have an end.
This pandemic had a beginning,
and this pandemic will have an end.
The apostle Paul called such trials “momentary.”
And this is the case even more so
as we move toward the end of this system of things.
At 2 Corinthians 4:17, 18, he said:
“For though the tribulation is momentary and light,
“it works out for us a glory
“that is of more and more surpassing greatness
“and is everlasting;
“while we keep our eyes,
“not on the things seen,
“but on the things unseen.
“For the things seen are temporary,
but the things unseen are everlasting.”
That inspired advice benefited the early Christians,
and it can benefit all of God’s people today.
We commend all of you for your faithful endurance
and for remaining busy in your service to Jehovah.
Through your efforts along with the power of Jehovah’s spirit
not only has the Kingdom work continued
but it’s also moving forward and expanding in exciting ways.
One example of that
is the world headquarters project at Ramapo, New York,
announced at the 2019 annual meeting.
Have you been wondering how the Ramapo project
has been affected by the pandemic?
We’re happy to share this behind-the-scenes report
on how things have been progressing.
On the January 2020 monthly broadcast,
our brothers around the world learned
that the Governing Body had determined
it was Jehovah’s direction
and approval had been given for a site dedicated primarily
to media production in Ramapo.
Well, just three months later,
a once-in-a-generation event, COVID-19,
brought grinding to a halt
the plans that large institutions, even nations,
had in mind.
How were the plans for Ramapo affected?
Was it really the right time for Jehovah’s organization
to start a major construction project?
As we review the events of 2020, look out
not only for clear evidence of Jehovah’s direction and blessing
but also the conclusion that Job once came to
when he said to Jehovah,
‘Nothing you have in mind is impossible for you to do.’
For a period here in New York,
nonessential construction activities
were restricted.
However, at the exact time
our project schedule required it,
the town of Ramapo started holding town board meetings
over (you guessed it) Zoom.
That meant that even though we were in the midst of the unfolding global chaos,
we were still able to meet a milestone on July 8, 2020,
when we had our first project meeting with the town board.
And we have clearly seen Jehovah’s blessing
in the meetings we have had with them since then.
We hit a second
and much more significant milestone
on December 9, 2020,
when the town approved
our scoping document.
Like the homework a teacher assigns a student
in order to pass an important grade,
we now know the information we should provide the town
in order to obtain permission to start construction.
When will that be?
Currently, we are on course for the end of 2021.
That is a number of months earlier than had originally been planned for,
even before the pandemic.
So just as Job said,
‘Nothing Jehovah has in mind is impossible.’
Since April 2019,
when the Construction Project Committee
was appointed,
the design of the site and the first buildings to be constructed
has advanced tremendously.
Many key lessons taken from recent large projects
have influenced the direction
that the Worldwide Design/Construction Department,
under the direction of the Publishing Committee,
have given.
The Ramapo site is 249 acres.
The buildings are about 160 feet
above Sterling Mine Road.
The primary interests off Sterling Mine Road
bring you first to the visitors’ center,
which will accommodate
1,200 visitors per day.
The studio building with its soundstages
is in the center of the site
and adjacent to the studios are workshops.
Over the ridgeline is the back lot
for outdoor sets and filming.
Next to the studios are the offices,
reception,
and the events building.
This building can be configured
as either a large assembly space
for 1,300 attendees,
a large dining room for 1,200 people,
or some yet-to-be-defined function.
On the west of the site are residences
for 1,290 volunteers.
Much time and energy have been invested
in the research of the best energy options for the site.
This led to the decision to use electricity
as the primary energy source.
A vast geothermal well field located beneath the studios
will heat and cool the entire complex,
and 120,000 square feet
of photovoltaic panels
will create electricity,
which is then stored
in an industrial-grade battery bank
and can thus be used at any time.
The result is that the site has its own microgrid
with the ability to make, to store,
and then to redirect energy
around the site where it is needed.
Many of us who generally work
in an office environment
have gotten used to working from home
during the pandemic.
Will that affect the need for office space on the Ramapo project?
Frankly, it’s impossible to predict
what the configuration of office space will be in the future.
Therefore, flexibility in the layout of future office space
is the most important design criteria.
The building is divided
into 10-foot by 15-foot modules.
Each module has a ceiling cloud above it
containing a heating and cooling unit and lighting.
Power and data wiring are in a raised floor
to allow for a variety of configurations
and reconfigurations.
Demountable partitions extend from the floor
to the deck above.
They can transform one module
into a single office
or small conference room.
Partitions can group several modules together
to form a larger conference room,
or the floor can be free of partitions
to work as an open-plan work area.
More important,
as these demountable partitions have no services in them,
these changes can be made at any time before
or after moving into the facility,
as office needs are better understood.
Maximizing the glass on the facades
and then the use of glass partitions inside the offices
ensures that all offices have plenty of natural light.
The ten residence buildings are oriented
in a north-south direction
so that all rooms will have
either morning or afternoon sun.
They are clustered around existing wetlands.
Careful research led to the decision
to pursue a different structural system
known as mass timber
—something we’ve not done on previous projects of this scale.
Timber is bonded in crossed directional layers
to form the structural elements of the building.
This is an increasingly familiar system.
Robust and safe
—that means that the beams, the columns, and the floors
can be prefabricated off-site,
making the structure of the building
faster to put up.
And apart from being economical, time-saving,
and reducing the carbon footprint of the project,
it should also make for some very attractive buildings.
As many filming
and recording projects
will be produced at the new Ramapo facility,
50 rooms in the residence building closest to the center of the site
have been designed to be smaller hotellike rooms
that will allow for comfortable
short-term stays
for those here to assist
as cast members
or other visitors.
As mentioned, many have worked from home during the pandemic,
and some prefer it.
Will it be the wave of the future?
We cannot say.
However, the majority of the residence rooms
will have a separate room
—many with a window—
that can be used
either as an additional storage room
or home office.
Future updates will feature the central focus of this new facility
—the new AVS studios building.
Although it will be the biggest we have ever constructed,
more important,
it will bring what is presently done in many different areas
—and, of course, our hardworking brothers and sisters—
all under one roof.
Despite a number of challenges in 2020,
the Ramapo project kept moving forward.
As we look ahead, we eagerly await
even further evidence
that nothing Jehovah has in mind
is impossible for him to do.
The amazing progress we’re making with Ramapo
—even in the middle of such challenging circumstances—
reminds us of Psalm chapter 127
and verse 1:
“Unless Jehovah builds the house,
it is in vain that its builders work hard on it.”
There’s no doubt that Jehovah is helping us
“[build] the house” at Ramapo!
You may have noted that the video mentioned future updates.
So, in time, you can look forward
to more reports about the Ramapo project.
When we reflect on all that’s been accomplished this past year,
it’s clear that Jehovah is blessing
the self-sacrifice of our worldwide Bethel family.
They’re like the ones described at Psalm 110:3,
where it says:
“Your people will offer themselves willingly.”
These brothers and sisters
are truly “[offering] themselves willingly” to Jehovah
day after day.
So please keep the Bethel family
and the Ramapo project in your prayers.
We’re confident that Jehovah will bless your hard work
and your endurance during this pandemic,
whether you’re serving in Bethel or in the field.
And we know that you’ll show the same zeal
during the campaign to invite as many as possible
to the special talk and Memorial of Christ’s death.
It’s our earnest prayer
that Jehovah continue to guide and strengthen you
in the days ahead.
From the World Headquarters of Jehovah’s Witnesses,
this is JW Broadcasting®.

ko.text: 기억해야 할 네 가지 점이 무엇인지 알아보겠습니다.
과거에 그리스도인이 되었을 때의 일이 떠오르기도 하지만,
한 번 일어나고 그걸로 끝나 버리는 게 아니죠.
다 나비가 되어야 한다는 말은 아니고요.
이것은 마치 옷을 갈아입듯 피상적인 변화가 아니라
그렇다고 우리가 언제나 나아지기만 한다는 것은 아닌데요.
그 다음에 조금 더 발전하곤 하죠.
한 번으로 완전히 끝나 버리는 것이 아닙니다.
그런데 얼마 동안 군 복무를 한 뒤에
이 변화가 어떤 것인지 알 수 있죠.
“난 활짝 깨어 있어서 그런 너절한 잡지는 필요 없소.”
다행히도 그 남자가 멀리 달아난 걸 보고
“그랬다면 여호와 이름에 얼마나 모욕이 돌아갈지 생각해 보세요.
아직 철저한 변화를 하지 못했던 겁니다.
이 몸집이 큰 형제의 이야기를 들으면
아주 두드러진 변화가 생길 수 있습니다.
하지만 그 일이 어려운 이유는 무엇입니까?
그릇된 일을 하려는 경향이 있기 때문입니다.
이런 것들은 정원에 있는 잡초에 비할 수 있습니다.
그것으로 다 끝나는 게 아니라는 걸 아실 겁니다.
우리는 사탄과 그의 세상에 둘러싸여 있습니다.
사탄의 세상은 늘 우리에게 영향을 주려고 하죠.
여기서 사탄의 세상을 어떻게 묘사하고 있는지 보시죠.
네, 사탄은 마치 물을 흐려 놓듯이 우리의 정신을 둔하게 만들어서
하느님의 말씀을 받아들이지 못하게 만들려고 애씁니다.
우리는 계속 “정신을 새롭게 함으로 변화”되어야 합니다.
더 영구적이 된다고 할 수 있습니다.
이런 예로도 그걸 설명할 수 있는데요.
우리가 어떤 새로운 것을 배우는 것은
마치 정글을 헤쳐 나가는 것과 같습니다.
아마 새로운 언어를 배우는 것과도 같을 겁니다.
정글의 수풀을 쳐 내며 나아갈 때처럼 말이죠.
어떤 것을 더 자주 하면 할수록
더 걷기 쉬운 길이 된다는 것입니다.
우리가 어떤 것을 한 번만 하고 계속 하지 않으면 어떻게 되죠?
여기서 어떤 점을 배울 수 있습니까?
우리가 개인 연구나 묵상을 할 때,
또는 배운 것을 적용하려고 할 때
항상 새로운 점만 찾으려고 해서는 안 됩니다.
우리의 정신에 길을 한 번 냈다고 해서
그 길이 언제나 다니기 쉬운 길로 남아 있는 것은 아니기 때문입니다.
같은 것을 몇 번이고 계속해서 반복해야 합니다.
우리 정신 속에 있는 비유적인 통로가
“정신을 새롭게 함으로 변화”되었다고 말하게 될 것입니다.

en.text: “Be transformed by making your mind over”
—what really is involved with this process?
Well, when we analyze this verse
at Romans 12:2,
perhaps there are four things initially that we need to remember.
First of all, to whom was Paul writing under inspiration?
Well, he was writing to Christians
who were anointed, who were faithful,
and yet he used an imperative form,
saying: “Be  transformed.”
He didn’t say, “You were already transformed.”
So that’s an interesting point for us because when we read these words,
it’s not just a matter of us remembering what happened to us in the past
when we became Christians,
but it’s something that we need to focus on now.
And that’s highlighted by the second point:
that in the original language, the verbs used here
indicate a continual process,
not just something that happens once and that’s it.
And the third point:
that it indicates a complete change.
Now, many of us remember that the Greek word here
involves a complete change.
“Metamorphosis” is the word that comes from that.
And that reminds us of a caterpillar changing into a butterfly.
Now, by this, we’re not inferring that we all have to become butterflies.
But the point highlighted is that it’s a complete change
from something that is one form to another.
So in a similar way,
with regard to our personality,
this is not just a superficial change,
as if we were changing our clothing
but, rather, a deep-down change that involves our personality.
So we change from one person to another.
Of course, this takes time.
And that’s the fourth point we need to keep in mind:
It’s a gradual process.
Not always is it just completely progressing in a positive sense.
Sometimes, for many of us,
we make some progress and then slip back a little,
and then we make some further progress.
But the main thing is that we’re making progress.
Yes, this is not just something that you do one time, and that’s it forever.
That’s highlighted by an experience
in The Watchtower  back in 1977
of a brother, Harry Yoshikawa, from Hawaii.
He was a very large Japanese brother.
But before coming into the truth, he was a street brawler.
And, in fact, the article (his life experience) was
“From Street Brawler to Christian Minister.”
Now, Harry was trained in the martial arts.
He was trained in boxing, and he just enjoyed fighting other people.
But after serving in the military for a while,
eventually he came in contact with the truth,
and he started to make changes.
And his life story perhaps helps us to realize
what’s involved with these changes.
So, of course, he stopped drinking; he stopped fighting.
But Harry goes on to tell us about the first day that he went witnessing.
He was in a market area, holding up the Awake!  magazine.
And he was calling out, “Read the Awake!”
Well, all of a sudden, some smart person said to him:
“I’m wide awake so I don’t need that trashy magazine.”
Well, Harry says that at that point,
his old personality returned to him.
He yelled out: “You’re wide awake, huh?
“Well, you won’t be for long.
You’ll be sleeping shortly.”
So Harry took a blow at this man,
who promptly ran,
and Harry chased him for two blocks.
Now, the other brother who was with Harry chased after him,
and fortunately the first man was a fast runner.
And when the other brother caught up with Harry, he said,
“Harry, what would you have done if you caught the man?”
He said, “I would have beat him up.”
And the brother tried to reason with Harry,
“Well, just imagine what a reproach this would be on Jehovah’s name,
I mean, if the police came.”
And Harry said: “No, it wouldn’t be.
“I wouldn’t tell him I was a Witness.
I’d say I was a Pentecostal.”
Well, Harry hadn’t quite made
that complete change.
But later, you see in this picture, as it appeared in The Watchtower,
here’s Harry working with his wife,
doing something that many Asian men would find very hard to do,
helping her in the kitchen.
And for many years, Harry and his wife served very faithfully in the circuit work.
And the change was so different
that many of the brothers and sisters who heard this story about Harry
—who was called, by the way, Tiny the Bruiser—
didn’t really believe that he was such a violent man previously.
So, what do we learn from this?
That this transformation process
may involve some drastic changes in the beginning
that outwardly appear to make someone different.
But gradually over the years,
we have to continue on making these changes,
transforming our thinking and our desires.
Now, why is that such a challenge?
Well, we know for a start
that we have a tendency to do what’s wrong because we’re sinful.
There are all sorts of wrong attitudes and thoughts
that are perhaps lying dormant in our personality.
It could be a matter of prejudice;
it could be a racial viewpoint,
hatred, pride, greed.
And these things we could liken to weeds in a garden.
Any of us who have done gardening realize
that just because you took the weeds out one time,
doesn’t mean that’s a onetime effort, does it?
They tend to grow back.
So we constantly need to be on the watch to make sure
that these weedlike tendencies, or traits, that we may have
don’t grow back.
And, of course, the other thing is we’re surrounded by Satan and his world.
And Satan’s world is always trying to influence us.
Let’s take our Bibles and turn together, please,
to the book of Ephesians
—Ephesians 4:18.
And notice here how it describes Satan’s world.
It’s the opposite to what we should be doing.
It says: “They are in darkness mentally
“and alienated from the life that belongs to God,
“because of the ignorance that is in them,
because of the insensitivity [or, the “dulling,” ftn.] of their hearts.”
So Satan is trying to muddy the waters, we might say,
trying to get us mentally to be dull
—to not be receptive to God’s Word.
So that’s why we need to continue
to “be transformed by making [our] mind over.”
But how can we do that?
Well, we’re not going to discuss at depth
the physical explanation with regard to neurons and synapses
(this is early in the morning for that),
but we do need to understand
a little bit of how the mind works.
You see, basically we can say
that when we have new thoughts,
or new concepts, that come into our mind,
it’s as if symbolically there are little pathways
that are formed in our mind.
And the more that we think about certain things,
the more solid, we might say, or more permanent,
these pathways become.
So maybe we could illustrate it this way:
You see, as we’re starting to learn new things,
it’s as if we’re going through the jungle.
And as we’re cutting our way through the jungle,
at first, it is very difficult.
Perhaps, we could say, it’s like learning a new language.
We all know (if we’ve tried to do that) that at first, it is very, very difficult.
It’s like cutting your way through a jungle path.
Or if you’re trying to learn something new, like driving an automobile,
it can seem very difficult.
But what do we realize?
The more often we do something, then what happens?
These symbolic pathways in our minds
become easier to walk along.
On the other hand, of course, if we do something once
but we don’t continue to do it, what happens?
It’s as if the jungle grows back,
and it becomes difficult to do things again.
So, what’s the point for us to get from this?
Well, in our personal study, our meditation,
and when we try to apply the things that we learn,
we shouldn’t always look for new things.
You see, sometimes we might say: “Well, I’ve read that publication already.
I don’t need to reread it.”
Yes, you do.
Why?
Because just because you cut a path in your mind through the jungle
doesn’t mean to say that that path
is always going to remain easy to pass through.
No, it’s good for us to go back again
and go over and over the same things.
And what happens?
That symbolic pathway in our mind
becomes easier for us to go along,
and we can truly say
that we have been “transformed by making [our] mind over.”

cn.text: “要更新思想而改变自己”
这个改变的过程是怎样的呢？
我们在分析罗马书12:2的时候
有四件事情非常值得我们留意
首先，这是保罗受启示写给谁的话呢？
保罗写信的对象是那些受任命的基督徒
他们都很忠贞，但请留意
保罗用了命令的语气，说“要改变自己”
而没说“你们已经改变了”
这一点很值得我们留意
因为这节经文不是要告诉我们
我们在成为基督徒时已经作出了哪些改变
而是要提醒我们继续付出努力
这也是我们要留意的第二件事情
在希腊语原文里
这个动词指一个持续不断的过程
而不是指只进行一次就结束了
第三件事
这里说的改变是非常彻底的改变
很多人都知道
在原语里的希腊语词指的是一种彻底的改变
这让我们想到毛毛虫蜕变成蝴蝶的过程
这是一个彻底的改变
当然，我不是说大家都要变成蝴蝶
但要点就是
从一种形态完完全全地转变成另一种形态
同样的道理
在谈到基督徒要作出的改变时
我们不是只作出表面的改变，好像换件衣服
实际上，这是一种发生在内心深处的改变
牵涉到品格，仿佛变成另一个人
当然，这需要时间
这也是我们要考虑的第四件事
这是一个逐渐的过程
我们不是一直处于在进步的状态
有时，我们很多人都是先进步
之后退步一点点，然后再继续进步
但总体来说我们是在进步的
我们要一直付出努力
而不是只努力一次就够了
一个弟兄的经历可以说明这一点
这个经历登载在1977年的《守望台》里
这位弟兄名字叫哈里，出生在夏威夷
他是日本裔的，身强力壮
在认识真理之前，他是个街头混混
实际上，这篇《守望台》文章的题目就是
《从街头混混变成王国传道员》
哈里，他练习过武术，也学过拳击
他特别喜欢跟别人打架
哈里在部队当了一段时间的兵
后来他接触到了真理
他就开始在生活上作出很多改变
我们看看他的经历就可以知道
改变牵涉到什么
一开始哈里戒了酒，也不再与人打斗
后来文章讲述了哈里第一次传道时发生的事
他在一个市场传道
手里举着《警醒！》杂志
他大声喊“警醒！警醒！”
突然之间，有个男人走过来对他说
“我清醒得很，谁会想看你们这些烂杂志”
哈里一听这个男人这么说
他的旧脾气就又爆出来了
哈里喊道
“你很清醒是吧？
好，你给我等着
等一下你躺在地上就不会这么说了”
说着，哈里就一个拳头打了过去
那个人转身就跑
哈里就在后面追他，追了两条街
跟哈里一起传道的弟兄也赶快去追哈里
幸亏那个男人跑得快，没被哈里追上
那个弟兄追上哈里问他
“哈里，你追上他想做什么？”
哈里说“我要揍他一顿”
弟兄努力和哈里推理，说
“想想看，要是警察来了
你这么做会对耶和华的圣名
造成什么影响呢？”
哈里说“我不会说我是耶和华见证人
我会说我是五旬节派的”
看来，哈里也还没有完全改变过来
但是后来，哈里不一样了
你看《守望台》的这张图片
哈里正在帮太太做家务
在亚洲的文化里
一个大男人跟妻子一起下厨房
这是非常难得的
后来，他们夫妻做分区探访的工作很多年
哈里的改变非常大
很多弟兄姐妹都不能相信
哈里以前是个非常暴力的人
对了，顺便提一下
哈里学习圣经前有个外号
叫“街头小霸王”
所以，我们学到什么呢？
就是，一个人刚刚开始学习圣经时
他可能作出非常大的改变
在别人看来，他好像变了一个人
但我们还需要很长时间
一步一步地，继续作出改变
不断地调整我们的思想和动机
为什么作出改变这么不容易呢？
一个原因是
我们每个人都不完美，都有不良的倾向
我们每个人难免多多少少都有一些
根深蒂固的错误想法和观念
例如我们抱有偏见
或者心里充满种族歧视、仇恨、骄傲、贪婪
我们可以把这些错误的观念
比作花园里的杂草
我们除过杂草的人都知道
杂草除了一次之后
并不表示以后不用再管它了，对吗？
它们会再长出来
所以我们需要不断留意
避免让自己身上那些
像杂草一样的错误观念再次冒出来
另一个原因就是
我们生活在撒但控制的世界里
而撒但总是千方百计地想要影响我们
现在我们一起打开以弗所书
看看以弗所书4:18
让我们看看撒但世界希望我们怎么做
这跟我们应该做的正好背道而驰
以弗所书4:18说
“他们思想昏暗，远离上帝所赐的生命
因为他们不想认识上帝，心里麻木”
可以说，撒但就是想让人看不清楚
使我们变得思想昏暗，心里麻木
结果对上帝的话充耳不闻
这就是为什么
要不断“更新思想而改变自己”
怎样才能做到呢？
嗯，我不想这么一大早
就跟大家详细讨论跟神经元或突触有关的
这么高深的科学问题
但我们可以稍微了解一下
人的大脑是怎么运作的
简单来说，每当我们有了新的想法
或者学到新的概念时
这时，我们的大脑中
就仿佛有一条新的路径形成
我们越是经常按照这个新的模式去思考
这条小路就会变得越清晰，越来越好走
也许我们可以这么理解
其实，我们在学习新的东西时
就好像在穿越一片丛林
想要在丛林中开出一条路来
刚开始可能很难
学习另一种语言，情况也类似
学过另一种语言的人都知道
刚开始有多么不容易
就好像在丛林中开辟一条新路一样
又比如，你学习一门新的技能
比如学开车，刚开始很难
但你会发现
如果我们经常练习，就不一样了
我们脑中的路径就会变得更清晰、更好走
但是，如果我们只做了一次
就停下来不再做了
又会怎样呢？
丛林就会再长起来
那条新开的小路就又走不通了
我们从中可以学到什么呢？
我们在做个人研读、沉思
或者思考怎么应用学到的内容时
不需要总是寻找新的要点
有时候你可能会想
我不需要再读这个，因为我已经读过了
但你需要的！
为什么呢？
因为你在大脑的丛林里开辟出来的这条新路
如果你只走过一次
它就不会那么清晰、那么好走
我们需要重复走这条路，一遍又一遍
在这条路上多走几次
这样，我们大脑中的这条路就会越来越好走
这时候我们才可以说
我们已经“更新思想而改变自己”了

en.text: The last time we spoke, I left you with the question,
Why did Jesus die?
How would you answer that question?
I’ve been thinking about it.
I don’t really know.
That’s OK.
It’s a question that has puzzled a lot of people throughout history.
Thankfully, the Bible can help us find the answer.
Notice what it says here at Matthew 20:28.
Would you like to read that out loud?
Sure.
“Just as the Son of man came, not to be ministered to,
“but to minister and to give his life
as a ransom in exchange for many.”
Thank you.
Looking at the end of the verse,
do you notice the reason Jesus gave his life?
“As a ransom”?
Exactly.
Jesus gave his life to buy back the lives of others
—and not just a few but many.
Really, Jesus gave his life for everyone
who sincerely wants to benefit from that sacrifice,
including you and me.
He also taught us how we can show our appreciation for it.
Let’s consider what he said about that the next time I’m here.
That sounds great.

en.text: Today, I’ve been discussing with people the identity of Jesus Christ.
What are your thoughts about Jesus?
I think he was a good man.
He certainly was.
In fact, he was the greatest man who ever lived.
But the Bible identifies him as being much more than that.
Consider what we read here at Matthew 16:16.
Jesus has just asked his disciples who they believe he is.
Notice their response:
“Simon Peter answered: ‘You are the Christ,
the Son of the living God.’”
So according to this verse, who was Jesus?
Was Jesus just a good man, or more?
More.
It says he was the Son of God.
That’s right.
Of course, we might wonder,
‘Since Jesus is the Son of God
—and a perfect Son at that— why did he die?’
Maybe we can discuss the Bible’s answer the next time we talk.
Yes, I’d like that.

ko.text: 부부가 사랑과 존경을 나타내는 데 도움이 될 겁니다.
어떻게 변화하는 상황에 적응했는지도 알게 될 것입니다.
성경 원칙에 따를 때 얻게 되는

두 사람은 아주 가까운 좋은 친구가 되죠.
부부가 여호와의 원칙에 따라 서로를 대하는 습관을 기른다면

부부가 서로를 대하는 면에서 나쁜 습관을 들인다면,

여호와께선 남편과 아내에게 어떤 역할을 주셨습니까?
따라서 남편이 가정에서 최종 결정을 하죠.

모든 남자의 머리는 그리스도이고 여자의 머리는 남자이며.”

여호와께선 아내가 남편의 소중한 짝이 되게 하셨습니다.

그날 있었던 어떤 일에 대해 말합니다.

아내가 겪은 일이나 아내가 하는 말이
대수롭지 않게 여기는 경향이 있을지 모릅니다.

남편에게 꼭 필요한 조언이 잠언 20:5에 나옵니다.
분별력 있는 사람은 그것을 길어 낸다.”
아내의 마음속에 있는 말을 길어 내십시오.
아내에 대한 사랑과 애정을 나타내는 것입니다.
반면에 남자는 흔히 대화를 다른 각도로 봅니다.
집에 온 남편에게 아내가 오늘 어땠냐고 묻습니다.

자신의 입지를 다지기 위해 대화를 하는 경향이 있습니다.
아내의 존경을 이미 받고 있다고 생각해

아내가 남편에게 일 얘기는 하지 말라고 한다면,
그러면 아내는 남편의 중요한 일상을 모르게 됩니다.
남편이 가족 부양을 위해 하는 일에 감사를 표현하고,
남편이 하는 일 얘기가 재밌지 않을 수 있지만,
두 번째 예를 고려해 보죠, 문제를 해결할 때입니다.
남편과 아내가 차를 타고 목적지를 향해 가다가
아내는 지나가는 사람에게 길을 물어보자고 합니다.
남편은 ‘내가 찾을 수 있는데 왜 그러지?’
낯선 사람에게 길을 잃은 것처럼 보이기를 원하지 않습니다.
