또 약 2500년 후에야 창세기를 쓰기 시작했고,
그것도 자기 생각이 아닌 영감받은 말을 썼습니다.
“한 몸”이라는 이 표현을 쓴 성서 필자는
누가 그 말을 했는지 알 수 있습니다.
마태는 이 내용을 기록하면서 예수의 말씀을 인용했죠.
남자가 아버지와 어머니를 떠나 아내에게 고착할 것이며,
따라서 그들은 더 이상 둘이 아니라 한 몸입니다.
네, 마태는 이 말을 한 분이 여호와라고 밝혀 줍니다.
이 사실을 보면 결혼이 얼마나 신성한 마련인지
결혼으로 짝지어 주셔서 한 몸이 되게’ 하셨습니다.
흥미롭게도 한 성서 해설서는 이 점에 관해 이렇게 알려 줍니다.
그분만이 결혼이 무엇인지 결정하실 수 있다. ...
결혼이란 한 남자와 한 여자의 결합이다.
하느님은 두 남자와 한 여자를, 두 여자와 한 남자를 창조하지도,
두 남자 또는 두 여자를 창조하지도 않으셨다.
일부 전문가들이 어떻게 말하든 하느님의 뜻에 어긋난다.”
“어떤 법정도 하느님이 제정하신 것을 바꿀 수 없다.”
“한 몸이 될 것이다”라는 말은 무슨 뜻입니까?
물론 한 몸이 된다는 것에는 성적인 결합도 포함되지만,
그 말은 더 많은 것을 의미합니다.
정신적으로, 감정적으로, 영적으로 연합되는 것이 포함됩니다.
두 사람은 삶에서 바라는 것들과 목표에서 하나가 되어야 하죠.
“남편은 아내와 떨어질 수 없게 합쳐질 것이다.”
서로 인생에서 가장 가까운 짝이 되는 것이죠.
“한 몸”이라는 것은 언제나 자기 자신보다 상대방을 더 생각하고,
모든 일을 할 때 상대방을 고려해야 한다는 뜻입니다.
그러므로 독신인 사람이 결혼하면 생각을 내 것에서 우리 것으로,
단지 서류 상이 아니라 마음으로 독신 생활은 끝났고
세 번째 질문으로, 어떻게 그 말처럼 살 수 있습니까?
안타깝게도 요즘 많은 사람은 결혼을 아주 가볍게 여기고,
무고한 배우자가 간음한 배우자를 용서하지 않을 때뿐이라고
그럼 이 점에 관해 바울이 한 말을
매춘부와 한 몸이 된다는 것을 모릅니까?
‘둘이 한 몸이 될 것이다’라고 그분이 말씀하셨습니다.”
자기 배우자에게서 떨어져서 제3자와 한 몸이 되는 것입니다.
한 몸인 남편과 아내의 결합을 끊는 것은
몸을 두 동강으로 자르는 것과 같습니다.
결혼한 두 사람이 아무튼 더는 서로를 좋아하지 않는다면
두 사람은 서로 어떤 점에 끌렸는지 떠올려 보고
그 감정을 되살려 보려고 노력해야 합니다.
동시에 부부 사이뿐 아니라 두 사람의 영성도
부부는 한 몸이라는 여호와의 견해대로 살았던
남편과 아내가 한 몸이 되어야 한다는
그의 충실한 아내의 내조를 떠올리지 않을 수 없었습니다.
그리스도인 그리스어 성경에 여섯 번 언급되는데,
그 모든 경우에 부부가 함께 일하고
또 한 사람만 언급된 적이 없죠.
그들은 집에서, 세속 일에서, 봉사에서 늘 함께 일했습니다.
그들의 결혼 생활이 영적으로 높은 수준을 유지한 건
왕국을 위해 나란히 그리스도인 활동을 하면서
우리는 각자 하는 일과 책임이 달라서
하루에 많은 시간 배우자와 떨어져 있을지 모릅니다.
부부가 참숭배와 관련된 활동을 함께 할 때
결혼 생활이 튼튼해진다는 걸 알 수 있습니다.
함께 그리스도인 집회에 참여하고, 함께 봉사하고, 함께 기도하고,
점점 더 한 몸으로 생각하고 느끼고 행동하게 됩니다.
이제 우린 누가 그 말을 했는지 압니다.
배우자와 늘 가까이 지내고 결혼의 띠를 잘 유지해야 합니다.
그리고 아굴라와 브리스길라의 훌륭한 본을 따라야겠습니다.
남편과 아내는 성경 원칙을 적용할 때
성공적인 결혼 생활을 할 수 있습니다.
늘 내 곁에 서서 날 믿어 준 그대.
그 깊은 존경심, 난 매일 느끼죠.
날 아끼는 그 눈빛 좋은 걸.
서로 손 꼭 잡고 여호와 섬기죠.
결혼 생활에서 사랑과 존경심을 보이라는 것이었죠.
사라의 본은 아내가 남편에게 어떻게 제안을 해야 하고,
남편이 아내를 어떻게 소중히 여길 수 있는지
아내가 여호와를 섬기게 된 예도 보았습니다.
여호와께서 결혼 생활에 함께하시게 할 때
부부가 함께 어려움을 극복하고 여호와를 섬길 수 있죠.
그럼 이번 달 프로그램을 마치기 전에
가이아나의 우리 형제 자매들을 만나 보겠습니다.
75만 명이 넘는 사람들이 살고 있는 이 나라는
사탕수수 농장, 드넓은 초원 지대가 있습니다.
기온이 높고 습하며 비가 많이 내립니다.
이 구역에서는 강을 따라 봉사를 많이 합니다.
가이아나 인구 반 이상이 시골에 살고 있고,
대부분의 사람이 해안 지역 마을에 삽니다.
금 채취로 유명한 카리브어 공동체 마을입니다.
매달 평균 228건의 성서 연구를 사회하고 있습니다.
그래서 구역 사람을 만나려면 여러 시간을 걸어가야 합니다.
형제 자매들은 포기하지 않고 봉사하고 있습니다.
형제들은 농부를 만나든 금을 캐는 광부를 만나든,
여호와의 증인의 세계 본부에서 JW 방송이었습니다.

en.text: Welcome!
This month’s program will help us show love and respect in marriage.
Here are a few highlights.
Is your marriage strained
because your spouse opposes the truth?
We’ll see how Alexandru’s love and patience
promoted peace in his marriage
and ultimately moved his wife, Dorina, to serve Jehovah.
We’ll learn how Claudius Johnson dealt with changing circumstances.
And our new original song reminds us of the joys of marriage
based on Bible principles.
This is JW Broadcasting® for March 2021!
Jehovah designed marriage
as a beautiful and rewarding relationship
between a husband and a wife.
When a husband and wife
fulfill their God-given roles
and they treat each other
with love and respect,
their marriage is a wonderful and intimate friendship.
A marriage that has good patterns
shaped by Jehovah’s principles
looks like this well-balanced family circle.
But if a married couple over time
has set bad patterns in how they deal with each other,
this is often the result.
Life is going to be a bit rough for them.
Let’s consider what Jehovah says
about the roles of husband and wife
and then discuss how love and respect
are real keys to a happy marriage.
So, what roles did Jehovah give
to the man and woman in marriage?
Well, Jehovah places the husband as head of the family.
Ephesians 5:23 says:
“A husband is head of his wife.”
So that means that the husband makes final decisions for the family.
And his decisions will reflect his love for his wife,
his children, and his understanding of their spiritual,
physical, and emotional needs.
At 1 Corinthians 11:3,
we get a sense, though, of how Jehovah feels about the husband’s role.
And as we read this together, I want you to imagine
Jehovah saying to husbands: ‘Yes, you’re head of the family.’
“But I want you to know that the head
“of every man is the Christ;
in turn, the head of a woman is the man.”
Sounds a lot like a father-in-law speaking to the groom:
“You can marry my daughter,
but you’d better treat her good because you’re responsible to me.”
Well, Jehovah is giving a very clear message for husbands.
Jehovah will hold you accountable to him
for how you treat your wife.
It’s something for us husbands to think about, isn’t it?
Well, what about the role of a wife?
Jehovah assigned wives as a beloved partner to her husband.
And as partners, they can discuss important family matters
and work together to make their marriage a success.
Jehovah placed the woman under the headship of the man,
and as such, her role is to be in subjection to him.
At Ephesians 5:22,
it says: “Let wives be in subjection to their husbands as to the Lord.”
Subjection —said a certain way, it almost sounds bad:
“You have to be in subjection!”
But is the subjection of a Christian wife to a Christian husband a bad thing?
No.
See, subjection as described in the Bible
is not about being subservient;
it’s about her role in the marriage.
You’re partners, each with a beautiful role to fulfill.
We could illustrate it with watching a couple ice skating.
As they move gracefully across the ice, do you think to yourself,
‘How come they never let her hold him over her head?’
Well, no.
You look at him; you look at her.
It’s obvious who should hold who over their head.
Well, just as we admire and respect a woman’s role as an ice skating partner,
a husband deeply loves and appreciates
his wife’s role as his partner
as they work gracefully together to make their marriage a success.
Well, now that we’ve briefly reviewed the roles for husbands and wives,
let’s read together a key Scriptural principle
at Ephesians 5:33
that shows how Jehovah wants husbands and wives
to fulfill their roles in marriage.
Ephesians 5:33:
“Each one of you must love his wife as he does himself;
on the other hand, the wife should have deep respect for her husband.”
Well, the obvious message in this scripture
is that husbands should love their wives
and wives should respect their husbands.
However, there’s another way to look at this scripture
and learn something about husbands and wives.
Jehovah God is telling us what each mate needs.
Men need respect, and women need love.
Now, this is not to say that men don’t need love
and women don’t need to be respected.
However, it does mean that men
tend to emphasize respect and status
and women often emphasize
intimacy, connection, and love.
This perfect principle can help us to understand
why our husband or wife may act or feel a certain way.
Now, this difference in emphasis affects many areas of married life.
Let’s consider three examples
of how this powerful Scriptural principle of love and respect
can give us insight into how a husband and wife
talk to each other,
how they solve problems,
and how they act in the company of others.
Let’s consider our first example:
how they talk to each other.
Now, since a wife’s emphasis
is on being loved,
her conversations often stress friendship
and connection when she talks to her husband.
She’s eager to share the details of her life with him
and in this way become closer to him.
She wants him, in turn, to share with her the details of his day and life.
Husbands, your wife
feels loved when you learn to communicate with her
in a way that tells her you truly care about her.
She places great emphasis on conversation and sharing her life with you
and likewise you sharing your life with her.
For example, a wife
tells her husband about something
that happened to her that day.
He grows impatient with the story and interrupts
or changes the subject or offers a quick solution.
How does she feel?
‘Why can’t he listen to the whole story?
Has he lost interest in me?’
It’s important that husbands give their wives
their full attention as they speak.
After a long day at work,
his mind may be focused on events that happened to him that day.
And he may without realizing it
feel that the events or conversation of his wife
aren’t on important subjects.
So he may be inclined to play down the events in her life
as unimportant, or trivial,
while events he talks about are substantial and important
because they happened to him.
Well, such a feeling over time can truly discourage a wife.
A husband’s disinterest in her stories
and events of her life feels a lot like disinterest in her.
The advice of Proverbs 20:5 is good for husbands.
It says: “The thoughts of a man’s [or we could say in this case, woman’s] heart
“are like deep waters,
but the discerning man draws them out.”
That’s great advice for husbands.
Husbands, when you draw
your wife out, let her speak from her heart.
That’s an indication of great love
and affection for your dear wife.
Men, on the other hand, often view conversation differently.
A husband comes home, and his wife asks, “How was your day?”
He says: “It was OK. Nothing special.”
But later that night when they’re with a group of friends,
he tells a story about what happened at work.
And she wonders,
‘Well, why didn’t he tell me that when I asked about his day?’
Well, since a man’s emphasis is on respect,
they often use conversation
to establish respect and status with others.
A husband may feel that his wife already respects him,
so there’s no need to tell her the story.
Wives, you can encourage your husband to share his life with you
by being interested in his work and activities.
If you tell him, “Don’t talk to me
about all that work stuff with me,” he won’t
and you’ll cut yourself off from a part of his life.
Show him that you’re proud of what he does to support the family.
Be interested in what happened to him,
how he feels about things, or challenges that he overcame.
While you may not find his work all that interesting,
remember, it is important to him.
Let’s consider our second example:
how they solve problems.
Now I want you to imagine a husband and wife.
They’re in a car, they’re looking for an address,
and they’re lost.
And the wife suggests that they ask someone for directions.
She’s thinking, ‘Why won’t he ask?’
He’s thinking, ‘Why can’t she just let me find it?’
You see, since the man’s emphasis is on respect,
he’s trying to avoid looking lost to a stranger.
The act of asking someone else for directions
may make him feel like he’s in a lower position.
Finding their way is a challenge to him,
and he wants to show his wife that he can find it on his own.
For the woman, such an idea may not come to mind.
She may view it as a simple interchange between them and a stranger.
They get help and directions, and they find out where they’re going.
At 1 Corinthians 7:33, Jehovah tells us:
“But the married man is anxious . . . ,
how he may gain the approval of his wife.”
Wives, your husband is anxious to have your approval and respect.
But on balance, husbands have to be careful
that an emphasis on respect doesn’t become unreasonable.
It won’t hurt us to ask for directions or help at times.
On the other hand, a wife needs to be careful
that she doesn’t show impatience by her words or tone
as her husband works his way through a problem.
A wife who clearly understands her husband’s desire
to solve problems for the family
will understand his actions and will do her part to support him,
even in the little things around the home.
Now, this support in the little areas of life
builds his confidence in her support
and can be a major factor
in whether a husband takes the lead in larger matters.
Our third and final example:
how they act in front of others.
Have you ever seen a couple where one of them is telling a story
and the other is constantly correcting the details?
or the husband is trying to give some direction
and the wife corrects or challenges the direction?
or the husband is telling others some unflattering story
that hurts his wife’s feelings?
How can Ephesians 5:33
help a wife in these situations?
Well, since a husband’s emphasis is on respect,
he’ll be much more sensitive
to comments his wife may make in front of others.
It can hurt a husband deeply
when his wife openly challenges him in front of others.
Proverbs 31:12
has this advice for wives:
“She rewards him with good, not bad,
all the days of her life.”
So when in public or when others are around
—even close family and children—
try not to openly disagree with him, correct him,
or attempt to take over what he’s doing.
How you speak to your husband in front of others
is a great way to show your deep respect for him.
It also builds respect for him in others, including any children in the family.
Well, how can Ephesians 5:33
help a husband act in front of others?
Well, when in public, husbands will want to act
like the husband at Proverbs 31:28.
It says: “Her husband rises up and praises her.”
It’s common today for husbands to make fun of
or even say demeaning things about their wives.
But since a wife places so much emphasis
on connection and friendship,
she can really be hurt when demeaning remarks are said
to get a laugh; it makes her feel awful.
Husbands, your wife considers you her best friend,
the one she shares everything with.
If you break that trust, she feels unloved and hurt.
Now, the best time to bring matters to each other’s attention
is when you’re in private or, if needed, when you can talk in such a way
that others cannot hear what’s being said.
In this way, a wife shows deep respect for her husband
and the husband shows his love for his wife.
So in review, we’ve considered just three situations
that the principle of love and respect
can help us to have a successful marriage:
how a husband and wife talk to each other,
how they solve problems,
and how they act in the company of others.
A good marriage is hard work.
How is your marriage?
Would you say that you’ve developed good patterns
or bad patterns in dealing with each other?
When was the last time you talked as a couple
about love and respect for each other?
Jehovah’s perfect advice at Ephesians 5:33
can help the marriage of two imperfect people.
In just a few words in this verse,
Jehovah is sharing with us a key principle
of how he designed marriage.
He’s telling us what each needs and places emphasis on.
Husbands put emphasis on being respected,
and wives put emphasis on being loved.
And this principle forms a key part
of the divine pattern for marriage.
If you want your marriage to operate as Jehovah designed,
then work hard to apply his perfect principle
of love and respect in your marriage.
Why can we be confident
that Bible principles for husbands and wives work?
Because they’ve worked for Jehovah’s people in the past.
In the following dramatization,
notice what wives and husbands
can learn from the example of Sarah.
Pioneering where the need is greater wasn’t easy.
After a long day in service, I had a part to work on.
Thankfully, Jess took care of everything,
so I could focus on my part.
She’s the best!
Poor thing, she was exhausted.
Good thing we were turning in early.
William and I couldn’t agree on much lately.
We couldn’t afford this!
There had to be something cheaper,
but he wouldn’t listen.
Sometimes, I feel that my husband doesn’t make the best decisions.
I just wish he’d value my suggestions.
Frankly, I’ve given up trying.
“Just as Sarah obeyed Abraham,
calling him lord.”
Hebrews chapter 11 and Isaiah chapter 51
also cite Sarah as a fine example for Christian wives.
But Christian husbands
can also learn much from carefully examining . . .
Hmm.
Sarah’s example: for me.
“Sarah was willing to move to parts unknown
A life fraught with danger and hardship.”
She unselfishly supported Abraham
no matter what
—just like my Jessica.
She does without, never complains
—what a gem!
I can do better letting her know
just how precious she is to me.
Sarah submissively obeyed her husband,
but she also spoke up.
She loved her son,
and she knew what was at stake
—God’s promises through Isaac.
Even though she knew it would upset Abraham,
she spoke up.
She must have thought carefully
before speaking to him.
After all, she called him “lord.”
Jehovah blessed her
for her loyal support of Abraham,
even reminding him to listen to her.
I knew I couldn’t expect Jehovah
to whisper in my husband’s ear.
But did my speech show respect like Sarah’s?
I needed to tell him how I felt,
but I needed to do it the right way.
That night we spoke,
and little by little things started to improve.
Imitating Sarah really worked.
In our next video, we’ll get to know Claudius Johnson.
Even though his wife died over 20 years ago,
I think you’ll see from his interview
that his spiritual qualities and focus on Kingdom interests
enhanced his over four decades of marriage.
Prayer is an important thing.
With everything I do,
I always go to Jehovah in prayer
and ask for his guidance.
I was born on the 26th of March, 1923
in Panama.
I was baptized in August 1946
in Cleveland, Ohio.
I started pioneering
in January of 1947.
There are a couple of scriptures that have been most influential in my life.
One is Psalm 55:22,
which says: “Throw your burden on Jehovah,
“and he will sustain you.
Never will he allow the righteous one to fall.”
One of the most trying experiences of my life
was facing the Selective Service Board.
I registered as was required by law,
and I received the classification of 1-A
—fit for military service.
I then spoke
with the Society’s Legal Department,
and I was instructed to appeal the decision
because I was a regular pioneer.
I had to go to the draft board,
and there I was severely questioned.
One of the problems they had
was that I had a part-time job,
and they felt that
that interfered with my being classified as a full-time minister.
However, because I was conducting
about 12 Bible studies at that time,
I took copies
of all those records and presented them to the board.
The chairman said to me,
“Are you saying that if we were
“to talk to all of these people, they would tell us
that you are conducting Bible studies with them every week?”
And I said, “Yes, Sir.”
While they are deliberating,
I am praying hard, “Jehovah, help them
to make a proper decision.”
In a few days’ time,
the classification card came as 4-D.
I was classified as a Religious Minister,
and I lifted my thoughts to Jehovah and said, “Thank you, Jehovah, very much!”
When I was in the circuit work in Cuba,
I had a few encounters with soldiers.
It’s difficult to understand
the tense atmosphere
that existed back in those days
and the freedom that those rebels had
with shooting people—even Batista’s people.
They didn’t give it a second thought.
I had just got through serving a congregation in the hills,
and we took the local bus
that ran around that area.
And on the highway,
two soldiers stopped the bus
and ordered all the men to get off.
They started looking at each of us one by one,
sending everybody back on the bus.
They looked at me and said: “You! Stay there!”
They pointed a rifle at me and said, “Who are you?”
And I explained myself,
but they kept pointing the rifle.
One of the soldiers said to the driver, “Take off!”
That’s when you pray hard,
and you remember the scripture at Proverbs 29:25:
“Trembling at men is a snare,
but the one trusting in Jehovah will be protected.”
The driver said: “No! He’s a circuit overseer!
He rides with me all the time.”
And he really defended me and made me believe
that Jehovah’s angels intervened.
And that’s why I say that I am a slave to prayer.
It’s the most important thing in my life.
When I came back to the United States,
I was being used
by the Service Department in the full-time work.
A few years later,
I had to give up the full-time work
and take care of my family.
The adjustment I had to make
to be a family man was hard
because most of my life was occupied in full-time service.
But I had to leave matters
in Jehovah’s hands.
We started the prison ministry
around May of 1974.
It gives you a measure of satisfaction
in seeing how the Bible
has a very strong influence
on individuals —to see criminals
turn their life completely around.
The Bible changes lives,
and that’s why pioneering has always been in my heart.
And so after my wife died,
I felt that the proper thing to do
was to get back into the full-time service.
As a result of that,
I started pioneering again in 1998.
Jehovah God has been good to me, and at my age of 96,
I thank Jehovah every day
for the health and strength that he permits me to enjoy
—and I keep on going.
Did you notice that it was prayer
that helped Brother Johnson and his family
to face a variety of changing circumstances?
He continues to display the same spirit
at nearly 98 years of age.
Are you married to someone who doesn’t serve Jehovah
or is even opposed to the truth?
You’ll appreciate the experience of Alexandru and Dorina Văcar.
I started to study the Bible in 1993.
At that time, I was 43 years old.
I was married for 19 years, and I had two children.
At that time, I didn’t know if I would become
one of Jehovah’s Witnesses or not.
But I accepted a Bible study.
At my husband’s request, I started studying the Bible at the same time,
but I only studied for about a year.
Then I decided, ‘I’m going to stop.’
I asked him to stop studying too.
I told him: “Let’s stop studying.
“This is not for us.
We don’t understand it.”
But in a very diplomatic and calm way,
he said he would continue.
When I realized he would continue studying, I said to myself:
‘Well, all right then.
‘Just you wait and see.
‘If you really want to continue, I will somehow make you stop studying
(in a subtle way), but I will do it.’
Just seeing him get ready to go in field service annoyed me so much.
I started burying him with household chores,
asking him to help me more and more around the house.
But calmly and gently every time,
he would ask me if he could prepare for meetings.
And one time when he asked me if he could prepare for the meeting,
yet again I got irritated and said:
“You’re not going to prepare now.
We’re going to clean the whole apartment thoroughly.”
After we were finally finished at midnight,
he asked me very calmly
if there was anything else he could help me with.
It was not easy for him to deal with my efforts
to force him to stop studying.
And after he got baptized,
I tried even harder.
But he never retaliated; he stayed calm and endured it.
In this period, I was trying to understand her reactions.
But it wasn’t easy for me.
Hearing her criticisms, those harsh replies, I thought sometimes:
‘I think I’ll just give up.
It makes no sense to go on like this.’
I said to the brother who was studying with me about this,
“I want to stop.”
And he encouraged me.
He said: “No, no, no, don’t stop.
“Don’t quit.
“Continue, continue.
Probably your wife will follow you.”
These conversations always encouraged me,
and when we finished our study,
I would see things from a different perspective.
I always loved my wife,
and I wanted her to be by my side.
During this period, he often told me how much he loved me
—many times, yes, very often.
And sometimes he would ask me if I loved him too.
There were times when I would answer him,
and there were times when I just smiled and said nothing.
And I even thought, ‘Hey, this guy really cares about me.’
I was impressed by his kindness.
I was very impressed.
Many times, I was musing: ‘Well, as a man, he could hit me.
He could be demanding, “You will sit down,”’ you know.
But no, he never did that.
He never raised his voice, never spoke a mean word
—never.
When she saw that I did not retaliate
—as in I would not reply harshly and I would not talk badly to her—
then eventually
she would calm down.
In his calm and mild way, he began inviting me to the meetings.
He kept on inviting me, and sometimes I was willing to accept.
Slowly, I started to attend the meetings.
I was happy.
I was very happy when she said she wanted to resume her study.
In August 2006,
I started studying the Bible again.
And in March 2007, I became an unbaptized publisher.
And in July 2007, I decided to get baptized.
I served in the Baptism Department,
and I had the privilege
to personally baptize my dear wife.
First Corinthians 13:4 says
that “love is patient and kind.”
Patience means,
first of all, being patient for months,
years, or maybe even decades.
Never give up.
Never consider someone as a lost cause.
Even though Alexandru and Dorina’s marriage
was far from ideal for a long time,
Alexandru didn’t lose his patience.
He was calm and loving.
That promoted peace, and eventually
it moved Dorina to embrace the truth.
If you have an unbelieving mate,
remember Alexandru’s example
and, as he said, “Never give up.”
Ecclesiastes 4:12 speaks of “a threefold cord”
that “cannot quickly be torn apart.”
That’s often applied to Christian marriage.
But what does that “threefold cord” mean,
and how does it make a marriage successful?
We’ll learn the answers in our next segment.
It was summertime, and a group
of brothers and sisters made arrangements
during vacation time to go to the beach.
And so during that time,
heading to the beach is where I met her.
I had met her sisters, but I had not met her.
My grandparents and my aunt
were a very important part
in raising me and my sisters.
They learned the truth first, in Ecuador.
We always lived close by.
I always went to visit them.
And they helped my parents in guiding me into the truth.
The first three or four years of our marriage,
we were about an hour and a half away from our family.
That was really hard on me because I’m close to my sisters.
So it was kind of hard being so far— To me that was really far.
I knew early on that one of the most important things
that I needed in a mate is someone who loves Jehovah.
And they always say—
I remember my parents (and at the meetings) always said,
“Find someone who loves Jehovah more than they love you.”
And it’s easy to say that,
but then you find someone
and you realize that she loves Jehovah more than she loves you.
She has demonstrated it through our entire marriage.
When it comes to Jehovah, he’s first.
I think that is the key to a successful marriage.
I think the biggest challenge we went through in our marriage
was our first year in the circuit work.
It was hard enough moving 3,000 miles away from everyone
and starting a new type of life.
Two months later, my grandfather dies;
six months right after that, my mother dies.
So after her mom died, my mom passed away.
It was one right after the other.
That was a difficult time for us
—all the pain and suffering
from losing our moms and loved ones.
Many times we felt that we could not continue.
It was overwhelming.
The period of time was eight months
and ten days between the death of Mimi’s mom and my mom.
The threefold cord is a routine in which Jehovah is included
in the marriage
—from reading the Bible together,
to going in the ministry together,
to doing everyday things together.
And as you do this, Jehovah is present in your marriage.
We always think that it’s our Bible reading.
Actually, we don’t think—we realize
that our Bible reading is very important for us.
We pick a book; we start reading it, and we know
that is what keeps us together.
We were both already pioneering before we got married.
And when we got married,
we just figured out a way to continue pioneering together
to make sure to start our spiritual careers together.
So we have to always depend on Jehovah,
which is the best Person to always depend on.
We spent a lot of time by ourselves,
driving from city to city and from state to state.
We had plenty of time to reflect, to talk,
and to draw close to each other
—to not only rely on Jehovah but also to be closer between us
and to spend more time
talking about the visits,
talking about the friends, and talking about how we feel.
I think that at the end it was the toughest assignment,
but it was the most rewarding
of all the assignments we had had
in all these years in the traveling work.
Because it’s the three of us and Jehovah’s an equal part of our marriage,
it doesn’t matter what we go through
—whether it’s Peter or I that’s having a little bit of a struggle—
because Jehovah is there.
He’s going to keep us united and strong.
And also, it’s not just in the things we do while we worship.
Yes, we worship together,
but it’s also all the other things that we do Jehovah’s way.
We’re best friends, and we enjoy spending time together
outside of service and the meetings.
We like doing fun things outside. We like the outdoors.
When we’re facing a difficult challenge, we will go to Jehovah in prayer together
and specifically pray, “Jehovah, help us with this challenge.”
Our assignments have helped us
to always be with each other because we have the same goals in mind.
We’re working together
for the same purpose.
So the same schedule —spiritual schedule—
has really helped us to go through these challenging periods in our life.
Knowing that Jehovah is our Creator, the Sovereign Being
—he’s the one who should tell us what to do.
And there is an arrangement, and when you follow his arrangement,
there’s happiness; there’s success.
We’re in an imperfect world,
but his arrangement works, and we have felt it.
When husbands and wives are united with Jehovah,
their marriage is as strong as that threefold cord.
The Bible uses another term to describe the unity of husband and wife:
“They . . . become one flesh.”
This was the topic of a Morning Worship program
presented by Brother Robert Ciranko.
Genesis 2:24 says of a man and a woman
who marry that they are
to “become one flesh.”
Now, that raises some questions:
Whose words are those?
What do they mean?
How can we show that we believe them?
And is there a good example in the Bible of a couple who did?
Let’s start with looking at the context.
If you’d open your Bibles, please, to Genesis chapter 2,
and we’ll start with verse 18—Genesis 2.
It reports: “Then Jehovah God said:
“‘It is not good for the man to continue to be alone.
I am going to make a helper for him, as a complement of him.’”
Continuing in verse 21:
“So Jehovah God caused the man to fall into a deep sleep, and while he was sleeping,
“he took one of his ribs and then closed up the flesh over its place.
“And Jehovah God built the rib that he had taken from the man into a woman,
“and he brought her to the man.
“Then the man said:
“‘This is at last bone of my bones and flesh of my flesh.
“This one will be called Woman, because from man she was taken.’
“That is why a man will leave his father and his mother
and he will stick to his wife, and they will become one flesh.”
So our first question is, Whose words are these?
Adam’s?
No.
The only words attributed to Adam are when he waxed poetic in verse 23.
And you can see that from the opening and closing quotation marks in that verse.
Well, then it must have been Moses’ words because,
after all, he wrote the Bible book of Genesis.
No.
He was not present at the time of the first marriage.
He did not start writing until some 2,500 years later,
and even then, he was writing what he was inspired to write.
Three Bible writers use this expression, “one flesh”
—Matthew, Mark, and Paul.
And it’s Matthew who gives us the clue as to whose words they are.
So let’s turn to Matthew chapter 19,
Matthew 19
beginning with verse 4.
And here Matthew writes and quotes Jesus;
it says: “In reply he [Jesus] said:
“‘Have you not read that the one who created them
“‘from the beginning made them male and female and said:
“‘“For this reason a man will leave his father and his mother
“‘and will stick to his wife, and the two will be one flesh”?
“‘So that they are no longer two, but one flesh.
Therefore, what God has yoked together, let no man put apart.’”
So Matthew makes it clear that Jehovah said those words.
And shouldn’t that elevate in everyone’s mind
the sanctity of the marital union?
As Jesus said, ‘God created male and female’ —two complementary genders—
and he ‘yoked them together in marriage as one flesh.’
Now, it’s interesting what The Bible Exposition Commentary
says about this: “God established marriage,
“and therefore only God can control its character . . .
“It is a union between one man and one woman.
“God did not create two men and one woman,
“two women and one man, two men, or two women.
“‘Group marriages,’ ‘gay marriages,’
“and other variations are contrary to the will of God,
no matter what some psychologists and jurists may say.”
“No court of law can change what God has established.”
And those are comments we can agree with.
Now, our second question is, What do these words mean: “They will become one flesh”?
Well, of course, the one-flesh relationship certainly involves sexual union,
but it goes beyond that because it includes a husband and wife
who have achieved mental, emotional, and spiritual harmony.
They are to have a oneness in their purpose and desires.
As Bible translator William Barclay renders it at Matthew 19:5:
“The husband will be joined inseparably to his wife.”
So in marriage, a man and a woman
are to become each other’s closest partner in life.
Being “one flesh” means that they must always
be thinking more of each other than of themselves,
that they must consider each other in everything they do.
So when single people marry, they need to shift
their thinking from mine to ours,
from me to we.
And so they must stop being single at heart
and come to be married at heart, not just on paper.
Now, our third question is,
How can we show that we believe these words?
Well, sad to say, many people these days
take a very casual attitude toward marriage,
and when the relationship becomes strained,
they just give up and walk out on their mate.
But that is not the Christian way.
Marriage is to be a lifelong relationship.
Just a few verses later on at Matthew 19:9,
Jesus taught that the only Scriptural ground for dissolving marriage
is when an innocent mate
chooses not to forgive an adulterous partner.
And that is because sexual relations outside the marriage bond
are a gross perversion of the one-flesh union.
Now, let’s read Paul’s words about this
at 1 Corinthians chapter 6
—1 Corinthians 6:16;
he said: “Do you not know that anyone who is joined to a prostitute
“is one body with her?
For ‘the two,’ says he, ‘will be one flesh.’”
So the adulterer pulls away from his marriage mate
and makes himself one flesh with a third person.
That, then, is the only Scriptural basis for divorce.
But divorce is a very painful experience.
As one sociologist put it, “Divorce is drastic surgery.”
To sever the one-flesh bond between husband and wife
would be like sawing oneself asunder.
What, though, if no adultery has been committed?
What if, for some reason, two people who are married to each other
just don’t like each other any longer?
Divorce is not an option.
Instead, they need to remind themselves of what attracted them to each other
and work at rekindling those feelings,
while at the same time looking to Jehovah for help
in not only strengthening their marriage
but also their spirituality.
Our fourth question is,
What Scriptural example is there of a married couple
who believed this one-flesh idea?
Turn to Romans 16:3, please,
Romans 16:3; here Paul writes:
“Give my greetings to Prisca [or Priscilla] and Aquila,
my fellow workers in Christ Jesus.”
So, yes, Aquila and Priscilla —what a model of a close and united couple
living up to what Jehovah meant when he said that a husband or wife
should become one flesh!
And Paul, who worked closely with them,
could not think of that dear brother
without recalling the faithful cooperation of his wife.
So it’s a fine example for Christian couples today.
And in every one of the six references to this couple
in the Christian Greek Scriptures, we find them working together,
cooperating without competition or strife.
And never is one mentioned without the other.
They constantly worked together in their home,
in their secular work, in the ministry.
And surely it was the time spent together in Christian activities
that kept their marriage on a high spiritual plane,
working side by side to further the Kingdom work.
Now, you and your marriage mate may be apart
for much of the day due to different work and responsibilities.
But can you find time each day to eat meals together,
to do household chores together, to take walks together,
to be together to get caught up
on what has gone on in your lives during the day?
Aquila and Priscilla proved that being united
in activities related to true worship
can keep a couple’s thinking and goals aligned,
and that does strengthen a marriage.
For example, studying together,
participating in congregation meetings together,
sharing in the ministry together, praying together,
in doing all of that,
a person’s interests, priorities, and habits
will harmonize with those of one’s spouse until,
like Aquila and Priscilla,
we increasingly think, feel,
and act as one flesh.
So now we know who said the words.
It was Jehovah.
We understand what they mean —achieving harmony
in one’s relationship with one’s mate.
And we can certainly prove that we believe these words
by staying close to our mate and maintaining our marriage bond.
And then we have that excellent example of Aquila and Priscilla to abide by.
“One flesh,” “a threefold cord”
—when a husband and wife apply Bible principles,
their marriage endures and is successful.
And we’ll see that in our new music video.
You’re the one, The only one for me.
You’re my love, My one and only.
Your qualities, your faith— They bring me such delight.
And with God’s help, I know our future’s bright.
It fills my heart with love To know you stand by me.
I feel your deep respect; I know you’re proud of me.
Together we can be strong; Together’s where we belong.
Jehovah helps us stay more in love each day— My only one.
You’re the one for me; You listen to my thoughts.
And as a team, We work hard for our God.
Yes, in my heart I feel You cherish me, my love.
You’ll always be the one— The one I’m so proud of.
Together we can be strong; Together’s where we belong.
Jehovah helps us stay more in love each day— My only one.
Together we can be strong; Together’s where we belong.
Jehovah helps us stay more in love each day— My only one,
My only one, My love.
The theme of this month’s program was
“Show Love and Respect in Your Marriage.”
Sarah’s example shows wives
how to give their husbands suggestions
and husbands how to show
appreciation for their wives.
We learned the importance of prayer when we face changing circumstances.
And Alexandru’s love and patience
helped his wife serve Jehovah.
By integrating Jehovah into their marriage,
couples can overcome challenges and serve Jehovah together.
Now let’s enjoy our video postcard.
This month we visit our brothers and sisters in Guyana.
This country of more than 750,000 people
is in the northeastern corner of South America.
This is a land of lush rain forests,
sugarcane plantations, and open grasslands.
Temperatures and humidity are high, and the rainfall is heavy.
In fact, Guyana means “land of water.”
These brothers are with the congregation in Charity,
a part of Guyana known for extensive preaching done along the river.
More than half of Guyana’s population is rural,
and most people live in villages in the coastal region.
This is Baramita, a Carib-language-speaking community
known for gold mining.
The congregation’s 119 publishers
conduct an average of 228 Bible studies every month.
Baramita is also home to a remote translation office.
Many people live scattered throughout the surrounding dense jungle.
And reaching them requires hours and hours of walking.
Because the rainy season is over half of the year,
travel can be very difficult.
But our brothers and sisters —they’re not deterred by the terrain.
Now, these are typical dwellings of the Carib community in Baramita.
And, our brothers —they preach to everyone they encounter,
from cassava farmers to gold miners.
Our brothers and sisters in the Baramita Congregation
send you their warm love and greetings.
From the World Headquarters of Jehovah’s Witnesses,
this is JW Broadcasting.

我们做丈夫的

顺服

当然不会

丈夫也要深深地爱护和珍惜自己的妻子

在以弗所书5:33
经文告诉我们

是亲密的关系、和人交流以及爱
这条完美的原则帮助我们理解
为什么丈夫和妻子的感受和反应
有时是不同的
男女之间的差异可以影响婚姻生活的很多方面
让我们来考虑三个例子
看看这节经文中爱与尊重的原则
如何发挥作用
这三个例子分别是
丈夫和妻子怎样沟通
怎样解决问题
怎样在别人面前互动
第一个例子是夫妻怎样沟通
通常妻子都想确认自己是被爱的
所以当她们和丈夫交谈时
特别看重感情和互动
生活中大大小小的事
她们都想和丈夫分享，以此变得亲密
她们也希望丈夫分享自己工作中发生的事
丈夫们，在和妻子交流时
如果你们能显出对她们的真正关心
她们就能确认自己是被爱的
妻子很重视沟通
也很喜欢和你分享她的生活
同样，你的心情要和她分享
举个例子
妻子告诉自己的丈夫，今天发生了什么事
丈夫很快就变得不耐烦
他打断妻子的话，然后改变话题
或直接说怎么解决，妻子会怎么想呢？
“他为什么不听我说完呢？
他不爱我了吗？”

他们的婚姻就会像三股拧成的绳子一样牢固
圣经还用了另外一个词来描述夫妻两人的关系
就是“二人合为一体”
接下来
罗伯特·斯朗科弟兄会谈谈这个主题
创世记2:24说
结婚的男女应该“合为一体”
这让我们想到几个问题
这段话是谁说的呢？
他的话是什么意思呢？
我们同意这段话吗？
圣经里有没有这样的好榜样呢？
我们先看看经文的上下文
请打开你的圣经到创世记第二章
我们先看看第18节
经文说
耶和华上帝说
“那个人独自生活不好
我要为他造一个合适的伴侣帮助他。”
第21节接着说
“耶和华上帝就使他沉睡
他睡着的时候
上帝取了他的一根肋骨
然后把那里的肉合起来

那个人说［这是亚当说的］
“我骨中的骨、肉中的肉终于出现了
她要叫做‘女人’
因为她是从男人身上取出来的。”
亚当说完了
然后24节说
“所以人要离开父母，与妻子长相厮守
二人合为一体。”
这段话是谁说的呢？是亚当吗？
不是
圣经里唯一记录亚当说的话
是在第23节的诗
你可以从经文当中的引号看出这点
你可能会认为
这段话是摩西说的

也不是
亚当夏娃结婚的时候，摩西并不在场
他在2500多年之后才开始执笔写圣经
而且他所写的是耶和华指引他所写下的
有三个执笔者都用了“合为一体”这个词

让我们知道这段话是谁说的
我们一起看看马太福音
第19章

［耶稣继续说］

这段话是耶和华说的

我们很同意这段话，对吗？
我们的第二个问题是

ko.text: 그러한 열망을 갖는 것은 좋은 것입니다.

en.text: Since ancient times,
humans have wanted to feel close to God.
This is a noble desire.
The Bible says that if we “seek God,”
we can “really find him” and “draw close” to him.
Yet, God is invisible.
So how can we feel close
to a God whom we cannot see?
Would it help if we venerated physical objects
as a means to feel closer to God?
Some people use statues in their worship.
Others venerate icons and other religious images
as part of their worship.
But is it possible that those who try to get closer to God in this way
are actually drawing farther away from him?
Consider what the Bible says happened when the ancient Israelites
made a statue of a calf and tried to use it to worship God
and they called it “a festival to Jehovah,” the God of the Bible.
Did God accept this kind of worship?
No.
He said that he was not pleased
with what they had done.
Just think:
Instead of helping them to get closer to God,
this object actually pushed them away.
In fact, contrary to ancient rulers
who were often viewed as gods and had images of themselves made,
the “great King over all”
—Jehovah God—
told his people not to create
or use images for worship.
He said:
“You must not make for yourself a carved image . . .
“You must not bow down to them . . .
I . . . am a God who requires exclusive devotion.”
Centuries later, the same command applied to Jesus’ followers.
The apostle John wrote to early Christians, saying:
“Guard yourselves from idols.”
God explains why his worship should always be free of images:
“I give my glory to no one else,
nor my praise to graven images.”
He invites people to draw close to him personally
and to pray to him directly without the use of images.
Is it really wrong to use images,
idols, or icons merely as aids in our worship?
How can we feel close to God if we cannot see him?
To learn more, search for these topics at jw.org
or fill out the online request for one of Jehovah’s Witnesses
to visit at a time and place convenient for you.

ko.text: 예언자 에스겔은 여호와의 지시에 따라 이상한 행동을 했습니다.
예를 들어, 그는 일주일 동안 아무 말 없이 앉아 있었습니다.
그러더니 갑자기 일어나 문을 닫고 집 안으로 들어가 버렸습니다.
그는 다시 밖으로 나와 벽돌 한 장을 가져다 무언가를 새겼습니다.
그러한 행동들에는 오늘날 우리에게도 의미가 있는
이 장의 제목은 “지금 네게 끝이 이르렀다”입니다.
이 장의 주제 성구인 에스겔 7:3에서 인용한 것이죠.
“지금 네게 끝이 이르렀으니, 내가 너에게 내 분노를 쏟아,
네가 걸어온 길에 따라 너를 심판하고
너의 모든 혐오스러운 행위에 대해 너에게 책임을 묻겠다.”
다음 세 가지 질문에 대한 답을 찾아 보시기 바랍니다.
하느님의 말씀에 예언된 미래의 어떤 중요한 사건들을 떠올리게 합니까?
에스겔이 여호와의 경고의 소식을 전파하는 임무를
우리의 봉사에 대해 어떤 견해를 갖게 됩니까?
자신의 우선순위를 다시 검토해 보아야겠다는 마음이 들게 합니까?
이 장에서 배우게 되는 점들을 바탕으로
여호와께 순결한 숭배를 드리는 데 도움이 되기 바랍니다.

en.text: ‎Jehovah asked the prophet Ezekiel to do some strange things.
‎For example, on one occasion
‎Ezekiel sat speechless for a week.
‎Then he suddenly got up and shut himself in his house.
‎When he came out again,
‎he picked up a brick and etched it with a drawing.
‎Ezekiel’s actions were unusual,
‎but they conveyed an important message
‎that has meaning for us today.
‎Chapter 6 of the Pure Worship book
‎discusses Ezekiel’s unusual actions.
‎It is entitled “The End Is Now Upon You.”
‎That statement is found at Ezekiel 7:3,
‎the theme scripture for this chapter:
‎“The end is now upon you,
‎“and I will unleash my anger against you,
‎“and I will judge you according to your ways
‎and call you to account for all your detestable deeds.”
‎As you study this material,
‎look for the answers to these three questions:
‎The events that Ezekiel acted out
‎remind us of what momentous events that God’s Word foretold for our future?
‎How does the way Ezekiel carried out
‎his commission to preach Jehovah’s warnings
‎affect your view of the ministry?
‎Why might the prophecies that we consider in this chapter
‎move you to reexamine your priorities?
‎Allow what you learn in this chapter to affect you
‎as you set priorities for yourself.
‎May the choices you make help you to give Jehovah
‎the pure worship he so richly deserves.

title: 우리의 조직이 이루고 있는 일들—현지 번역 사무실을 위한 간소화된 마련

ko.text: 영적 양식을 1000개 이상의 언어로 번역하는 일은
그리고 출판위원회도 번역 작업을 지원하고 있는데,
RTO라고 하는 현지 번역 사무실을 짓고
번역 팀에게 필요한 도구들을 공급해 줍니다.
실제로 그 언어가 사용되는 지역에 세워집니다.
헌금이 지혜롭게 사용되는 모습을 보게 되실 것입니다.
사람들이 모국어로 여호와에 대해 배울 때
어떤 좋은 결과가 있는지 볼 것입니다.
우리가 번역하는 언어를 사용하는 지역에 살고 있으니까
매일 RTO 일을 지원하는 출퇴근 봉사자들이
바로 이곳에서 태어나서 자란 사람들이라는 거죠.
헌금을 최대한 절약하는 데 도움이 됩니다.
빨간 벽돌로 된 번역 사무실 건물이
이처럼 빠른 시간 안에 지어질 거라곤
지원 업무를 하는 RTO로 사용하고 있습니다.
지원 업무를 하는 이러한 RTO 덕분에
번역만 하는 RTO를 더 간소화할 수 있습니다.
이처럼 크게 증가한 이유 중 한 가지는
“보라! 나의 종들은 먹겠지만 너희는 굶주릴 것이다.
보라! 나의 종들은 마시겠지만 너희는 목마를 것이다.”
자신의 백성을 먹이겠다는 약속을 지키실 것입니다.
그 일을 지원하는 것을 특권으로 여깁니다.

en.text: In November 2019,
the Governing Body of Jehovah’s Witnesses
reported an amazing milestone.
Content on jw.org
was now available in 1,000 languages.
We thank Jehovah for this accomplishment.
He guides us with his holy spirit
to “make disciples of people of all the nations.”
But it didn’t stop at 1,000.
More than 20 languages have been added
since that 2019 report.
Translating media into over 1,000 languages
is an incredible amount of work,
and it requires close cooperation
across many parts of our organization.
Translation teams work under the direction
of the Writing Committee of the Governing Body.
Additionally, the Publishing Committee of the Governing Body supports their work
by building remote translation offices
and equipping them with the tools they need.
These remote translation offices are established
where people speak the language being translated.
In this video report, we’ll see how this is done
using adaptable methods
that make wise use of our donations.
But most important, we’ll see the good results
when people are able to learn about Jehovah
in their own language.
Living where the language we translate
is spoken
has helped us to improve
the way we translate our publications.
We are now able to interact directly with the native speakers
when we go in the ministry and attend meetings and assemblies.
The other benefit is
that the commuter volunteers
who come and help daily at the RTO
were born and raised right here.
This fact makes these brothers and sisters
a precious part of the translation team
because they write in a way that is clear and easy to understand.
The remote translation offices arrangement
has proved to be very effective.
Over time, the Worldwide Design/Construction Department,
working under the direction of the Publishing Committee,
worked to simplify new RTOs
and adjust existing ones.
A small RTO can be established
in a Kingdom Hall,
like this one in Easter Island,
or at an Assembly Hall,
like here in Guatemala.
These flexible solutions make the best use of dedicated funds.
The translation office was built very quickly
with red bricks,
which made it possible for us to move in within four months.
We never expected that we could be given
such a beautiful place as this
—constructed in record time!
In about six months, they constructed
the residence building,
the offices,
and the recording studio.
In Bangalore, India, rented space in this commercial building
is used as a support RTO.
As a result,
support for translation-only RTOs can be fairly simple.
This also means that the space requirements
for a translation-only RTO reduces significantly.
The team takes the translated text from the translators
and then they can work it into a design format
that can be used for printing or for distribution over the Web
and can also be read on the  JW Library® app
or can be heard as an audio recording.
For a number of years, there were just a handful of RTOs;
today, there are over 400 worldwide.
That tremendous growth is possible
in part because of the way we now build
and equip RTOs.
Isn’t it wonderful to be part of Jehovah’s people
who make such great efforts
to reach as many people as possible, regardless of language?
Since the language used in the publications is
easy to understand,
I really enjoy doing my personal study.
This has made it possible
to know our Father, Jehovah, better,
and it has also helped me to teach others about Jehovah,
who are also making Jehovah their Friend.
At Isaiah 65:13, Jehovah says:
“Look!
“My servants will eat,
“but you will go hungry.
“Look!
“My servants will drink,
but you will go thirsty.”
Jehovah’s promise to feed his people
will not go unfulfilled.
It’s the Publishing Committee’s privilege to assist in that feeding.
We pray for Jehovah’s blessings on our efforts to provide
remote translation offices wherever they are needed
to support God’s people.

cn.text: 耶和华见证人中央长老团宣布
我们的组织来到了一个新的里程碑
jw.org网站的语言总数达到了1000种
我们非常感激耶和华
他用神圣力量指引我们
“使所有国族的人”做耶稣的门徒
但1000不是个终点
从2019年的报告以来
我们又增加了20多种语言
要翻译超过1000种语言的内容
牵涉到巨量的工作
各部门要紧密合作，与组织同步并进
翻译小组在写作委员会的督导下一起工作
另外，出版委员会会协助设置
并建立远程翻译处（RTO）
也会提供他们所需的一切
这些远程翻译处会设立在说这种语言的地区
接下来我们会看看
组织如何善用捐款
用灵活的方法建造RTO
更重要的是
我们会看到人们用自己的语言
认识耶和华带来的美好结果
我们生活的地区使用的语言
就是我们翻译的语言
这对翻译工作很有帮助
我们现在去传道、参加聚会和大会时
就可以直接跟说这种语言的人交流
还有一个好处是
每天来RTO协助我们的通勤人员
都是土生土长的本地人
所以这些通勤弟兄姐妹的翻译
既清楚又容易明白
对翻译小组很有帮助
他们真的很宝贵
我们看出远程翻译处是非常有效的安排
全球设计及建筑部在出版委员会的指引下
以简易的方式设立了新的RTO
并且调整了现有的RTO
一个小的RTO可以设立在王国聚会所
例如在复活节岛的这个
也可以设立在大会堂
例如在危地马拉的这个
这种灵活的安排可以大大善用弟兄姐妹的捐款
远程翻译处很快就盖好了
它是由红砖建的
我们不到四个月就搬进去了
我们从来没有想过
能够有这么美观、舒适的远程翻译处
而且是以超快的速度建成的
他们差不多花了6个月
就盖好了宿舍、办公室和录音室
在印度的班加罗尔
我们在商业大厦里租了一个地方
用来做支援型RTO
有了这些支援型RTO
只负责翻译的RTO就简单多了
而且这样一来
只负责翻译的RTO就不用那么大的空间了
翻译员翻译好的资料会被制作成不同的版式
可以用来印刷或发布到我们的网站上
大家也可以在JW Library® app上
读到或听到这些出版物的内容
有很多年的时间
我们只有数量很少的RTO
但今天，全球已经有超过400个了
能有这样大的增长
一个原因是我们改进了RTO建造和配置的方法
我们多么高兴
能够成为耶和华子民中的一员
竭尽全力帮助更多说不同语言的人认识真理
因为我们的出版物翻译得很容易明白
所以我研读的时候真的能乐在其中
这让我能更认识天父耶和华
这也帮助我能教导别人去认识耶和华
并帮助他们成为耶和华的朋友
在以赛亚书65:13，耶和华说
耶和华承诺喂养他的子民
这个承诺绝不会落空
出版委员会很荣幸能为此尽一分力
愿耶和华继续赐福给我们
让我们在所有需要的地方设立远程翻译处
全力支持上帝的子民

ko.text: 훌륭한 본을 세울 수 있었던 이유는 무엇입니까?
그는 이주할 당시 30세 정도 되었을 것입니다.
그는 에스더와 모르드개와 동시대에 살았을 것입니다.
하만이 유대인들을 전부 없애려고 했던 때였죠.
여호와께서 자신의 민족을 어떻게 보호하고 돌보시는지
젊은 에스라의 마음과 정신에 깊은 인상을 남겼을 겁니다.
순결한 숭배를 위해 힘쓰겠다고 결심했을 겁니다.
예루살렘으로 이주하는 게 쉬운 일은 아니었습니다.
“에스라는 여호와의 율법을 조사[하려고] 마음을 준비해 두었다.”
가족과 친구들을 떠나서 예루살렘으로 가는 걸
편안하게 생활하고 있는데 그걸 다 뒤로한 채
먼 곳으로 떠나서 기꺼이 어려운 환경 속에서 생활할 것인가?’
그리고 기꺼이 여호와의 일을 첫째 자리에 두었습니다.
그는 여호와의 법을 깊이 존중하는 사람이었습니다.
“내 눈을 열어 주시어 당신의 법의 놀라운 것을 뚜렷이 보게 해 주십시오.”
그는 조사한 내용을 깊이 있게 묵상했습니다.
그는 유다의 왕들과 제사직에 대해 조사했습니다.
하지만 그는 조사만 한 게 아닙니다.
그는 마음이 감동받아 배운 걸 적용했죠.
이처럼 에스라는 배운 것을 기꺼이 실천했습니다.
그가 배운 내용은 그의 감정에 영향을 미쳤고
그가 여호와 하느님과 더욱 가까워지게 했습니다.
그리고 그는 자신의 동족을 돕기 위해
연구를 통해 지식만 얻은 게 아니라
마음이 움직였다는 걸 알 수 있습니다.
“나는 돌아가는 길에 적에게서 우리를 보호할 군인과 기병을 달라고 왕에게 청하기가 부끄러웠다.”
‘하느님의 선한 손은 그분을 찾는 모든 자 위에 있지만,
그분을 대적하는 자에게는 그분이 힘과 분노를 내리신다’고 말했기 때문이죠.
그가 어떤 묵상을 했을지 상상해 보십시오.
모압, 에돔, 암몬 등의 민족이 연합하여 여호사밧을 대적했지만
그래서 여호와를 신뢰하고 보호를 요청하지 않았죠.
충실한 종이 공급하는 양식을 섭취하는 거죠.
여호와와 가까워지다 보면 답을 찾게 되죠.
그가 하느님의 말씀을 깊이 연구한 것이
‘거룩한 자손이 이방 민족들과 섞’인 것을 보았습니다.
거룩한 자손이 이방 여자들과 섞이게 될 것이었습니다.
결국 민족 전체가 이교에 동화될 수 있었죠.
순결한 숭배가 지상에서 사라질 수 있었습니다.
메시아의 가계를 식별하는 것도 불가능해질 것이었습니다.
그가 정말 다윗의 자손이고 유다의 가계인지 알 수 없게 될 것이었죠.
에스라가 지닌 아름다운 성품을 엿볼 수 있습니다.
예루살렘 가운데서 “남자와 여자와 아이들의 큰 무리”가 그에게 모여 함께 웁니다.

en.text: What made Ezra such a sterling example
of faith and trust in God?
And more important, how can you and I
—how can we—
imitate the total reliance
that Ezra put on Jehovah God
and in His Word?
Well, let’s find out.
Let’s examine Ezra chapter 7.
Let’s open our Bibles to Ezra chapter 7,
and we’re going to look at verses 6 and 7.
Now, verse 6, it says:
“Ezra came up from Babylon.”
So that’s where he lived.
Remember, he was under the Medo-Persian Empire at the time,
and he lived there.
And he was “well-versed in the Law” and “a skilled copyist.”
But verse 7, it says
that he “went up to Jerusalem
in the seventh year of King Artaxerxes.”
Now, the seventh year of King Artaxerxes
would be the year 468 B.C.E.
So as a reference point,
we have 607 B.C.E., when Jerusalem was destroyed;
537 B.C.E., when the Jews returned to their homeland in Jerusalem;
and 515 B.C.E., when, under the encouragement
of Haggai and Zechariah,
the Jews rebuilt the temple of Jehovah.
Now, at that time, Ezra probably wasn’t even born yet.
So he enters into the picture here
in the year 468 B.C.E.
But the question is, What would have moved Ezra
to want to move to Jerusalem?
He was probably around 30 years old when he made this move.
And he wanted to advance pure worship,
even that, as it mentions in verse 10,
he wanted “to teach [the] regulations and judgments in Israel.”
But what would have moved him to do that?
Well, Ezra would have lived during the time period
of Esther and Mordecai.
And that was the time period when Haman tried to exterminate the Jews.
Now, that was in the year 484 B.C.E.,
and Ezra was a teenager at that time.
So he would have seen firsthand
how Jehovah defended his people
and how Jehovah strengthened and cared for his people.
This event —this national crisis—
would have made an indelible impression, an imprint,
on that young man’s mind and heart.
And no doubt he said to himself: ‘When I get of age,
‘I want to go to Jerusalem.
I want to be there to help and advance pure worship.’
So that’s what he decides to do.
However, it wasn’t easy for Ezra to make this move to Jerusalem,
and that’s where we come to verse 10:
“Ezra had prepared his heart
to consult the Law of Jehovah.”
So to prepare his heart, what did Ezra have to do?
How did he prepare his heart?
He must have asked himself questions:
‘Why do I want to go to Jerusalem?
‘Is it just to make a name for myself, or is it to honor Jehovah?
‘How do I feel about going there?
‘How do I feel about leaving my family and my friends
‘and this comfortable way of life that I have here in Babylon
‘—I’m going to leave it all behind; I’m going to move to this distant land
and to live under circumstances that would be difficult?’
So he’s preparing his heart by asking himself these questions.
But he was desirous
of putting Jehovah’s work first.
Now, notice here in verse 10, it says
that then he wanted “to consult
the Law of Jehovah.”
That’s why we love Ezra.
He consults the Law of Jehovah.
That was his love; that was his first priority.
He didn’t consult the arithmetic, the astronomy,
the history, the chronology, and the geography of Babylon.
No, it was the Law of Jehovah.
In fact, Ezra had deep respect for that Law of Jehovah.
He is the one who wrote First and Second Chronicles.
It shows that he was a deep student of God’s Word
and familiar with Psalm 119:18.
You can imagine him saying before studying:
“Open my eyes so that I may see clearly
the wonderful things of your law.”
That’s Ezra.
And when we think about him
and how he meditated deeply on the information that he gathered—
He gathered information about the kings of Judah and about the priesthood.
That was his interest —to track the line leading to the Messiah.
But he did more than just gather facts,
he applied what he learned.
It touched his heart.
How do we know?
Notice in verse 10, it said,
after “consult[ing] the Law of Jehovah,”
“and to practice it.”
“To practice it” —Ezra was ready to act upon what he studied.
What he learned stirred his feelings, touched his emotions,
and moved him to draw closer to Jehovah God.
That was his whole goal of studying.
And then he acted to help his brothers.
He did move to Jerusalem; he acted.
He did it in spite of the inconveniences
and the problems that he would be facing.
But now let’s look at chapter 8,
verse 22,
just to highlight again how he was moved by what he read.
It’s just not a fact-finding mission.
In chapter 8, verse 22,
it says here that as he was ready to leave Babylon
and move to Jerusalem,
in speaking to the king, he said: “I was ashamed
“to ask the king for soldiers and horsemen
“to protect us against the enemies along the way,
“[I’m ashamed to do that]
“because we had said to the king: ‘The good hand of our God
“‘is over all those seeking him, . . .
his strength . . . [is] against all those [who are against] him.’”
“I was ashamed.”
What’s the point?
Well, as he again tracked those Judean kings
(because that’s what First and Second Chronicles do,
track the Judean kings leading to the Messiah),
imagine how he meditated when he got to David
or Hezekiah
—185,000 Assyrians killed in one night.
What about Josiah?
What about Asa —a million Ethiopians killed?
What about Jehoshaphat?
The combined enemies of Moab, Edom, Ammon, and so forth
came up against Jehoshaphat,
and yet Jehovah defended them.
He had this in his mind,
and that’s why he said: ‘I’m ashamed because of what I’ve studied.
‘No, I don’t need an escort, dear king.
Jehovah is going to be with us.’
So it just shows the same point for us when we study.
It’s part of our worship.
And we study to draw close to Jehovah God, not simply to gather facts,
but to allow our attachment to Jehovah God to get stronger.
For example, the Watchtower  Study.
Yes, we study The Watchtower,
but is it just to find an answer?
Is it that ‘Oh, I need to make a comment’?
That’s not why we study the Watchtower  magazine.
It’s part of pure worship.
It’s being fed by “the faithful and discreet slave.”
We read The Watchtower  and we open the Scriptures to draw close to Jehovah God.
And in the meantime: ‘Yes, I found an answer.
I can make a comment.’
But our primary goal is to feed our hearts.
How do I feel about what I’m reading?
We prepare our hearts.
What is my motive in studying the lesson?
Each time we open up God’s Word,
our attitude should be like Samuel, who was told to say:
“Speak, Jehovah, for your servant is listening.”
Ezra also was given insight and understanding,
and that enabled him to be a blessing to the nation
as he dug deep into God’s Word.
For example, in chapter 9, verse 2,
he recognized, when he got there to Jerusalem,
that ‘the holy offspring was being mingled with the pagan nations.’
The men were marrying these pagan women.
Ezra saw the disastrous consequences:
“You’re going to mingle the holy seed along with pagan women?
“You’re going to assimilate the whole nation into a pagan environment?
“You’re going to merge true worship?
“It could vanish from the earth in time if not careful.
“You wouldn’t be able to locate the Messiah, the lineage.
“Is he of the line of David? We don’t know.
Is he of the tribe of Judah? We don’t know.”
Ezra saw that, and he acted
because of the insight that Jehovah God gave him.
Now notice chapter 10, verse 1
(because it again gives us insight into the beauty of Ezra’s personality),
when he did act on it
and got rid of those foreign wives
(chapter 10, verse 1),
his humble confession before Jehovah God
and what happens when he humbly prays to Jehovah:
“A large crowd of men, women, and children of [Jerusalem]
gathered around him . . . [and] were weeping.”
That’s Ezra.
They did not cringe and retreat before a tyrant.
Rather, they were drawn to a loving shepherd.

cn.text: 是什么让以斯拉
成为一个表现信心的杰出榜样？
还有更重要的
你和我
我们可以怎样效法以斯拉的好榜样
全心信赖耶和华和他的话语呢？
我们一起来看看
我们一起打开圣经到以斯拉记第7章
我们先看看第6,7节
第6节，经文说
“以斯拉从巴比伦回到故乡。”
他生活在米底亚－波斯统治的时代
那时候他住在巴比伦
经文说他是个抄经士，精通摩西法典
但在第7节，经文说
亚达薛西王在位第7年
以斯拉和一些人一起回到了耶路撒冷
亚达薛西王在位第7年就是公元前468年
我们现在有几个参考年份
公元前607年，耶路撒冷被毁灭
公元前537年，犹太人返回故乡耶路撒冷
还有公元前515年，先知哈该和撒迦利亚
鼓励犹太人重建耶路撒冷的圣殿
那个时候，以斯拉可能还没有出生
以斯拉这个名字第一次出现在圣经里
是在公元前468年
你想过是什么原因
让以斯拉想要回耶路撒冷吗？
他回耶路撒冷的时候可能是30岁左右
他想推广正确崇拜
第10节还说，他“要在以色列
教导人认识其中的条例和判决。”
是什么原因推使他这样做呢？
以斯拉跟末底改和以斯帖
生活在同一个时代
那段时期，哈曼试图消灭犹太人
在公元前484年
当时以斯拉还是一个十几岁的青少年
他亲眼看到耶和华怎样保护
照顾和帮助他的子民
整个事件的发展
犹太民族的危机
一定在这个年轻人的脑海里
留下一个无法磨灭的记忆
他一定这样对自己说过
“当我长大以后，我要回耶路撒冷
我要在那里帮助人
以正确的方式崇拜上帝。”
但对以斯拉来说
要回耶路撒冷也不是那么容易
在第10节，经文说
“以斯拉心里做好准备
要查考耶和华的法律”
经文说“以斯拉心里做好准备”
他要做什么准备呢？
他一定问过自己一些问题
“我为什么要去耶路撒冷
只是要为了出人头地吗？还是为了耶和华？
真的去到那里，我会有什么感觉？
要离开家人、朋友
还有在巴比伦这里舒适的生活
要抛下这一切
我真的要搬去那么远的地方吗？
那里的居住环境又很不好。”
为了准备他的心
他一定问过自己这些问题
但对以斯拉来说
最重要的是耶和华的工作
再请大家留意经文第10节接着怎么说
以斯拉“查考耶和华的法律”
以斯拉就是这么好的榜样
以斯拉查考耶和华的法律
他最爱耶和华的法律，这是最重要的
他有查考巴比伦的数学、天文
历史、年代、地理学吗？
没有！他查考的是耶和华的法律
他珍视并认真查考上帝的法律
也执笔写了历代志上下
他很熟悉诗篇119:18
在他读圣经之前，他也许这样说
“求你使我张开眼睛
让我清楚看出你法律的绝妙之处。”
我们可以想一想
以斯拉怎样深入沉思他收集到的资料
就是那些有关于犹大国的国王
和祭司们的资料
他对弥赛亚的家系非常感兴趣
但他不只是收集资料而已
他还实践自己所学到的
这些资料打动了他的内心
我们怎么知道呢？
请留意第10节
在“查考耶和华的法律”
后面说“加以遵守”
意思是他会把学到的运用出来
他学到的内容触动了他的感情
让他很想跟耶和华有更进一步的关系
这就是他查考的目标
在此之后
他就去了耶路撒冷帮助他的同胞
他确实采取行动了
尽管有很多不便和困难
我们来看看8:22
这里再次说明他怎么被读到的内容打动
他这样做，不单为了吸收知识
“我觉得请国王派军队和骑兵护送我们
以免被敌人攻击
是很丢脸的事［我没脸这样做］
因为我们曾经对国王说
我们的上帝
一定会向所有寻求他的人伸出援手”
却要施展能力打击所有离弃他的人
他为什么觉得丢脸呢？
他执笔写了历代志上下
里面记录了
关于弥赛亚家谱当中的那些犹大君王们
他怎么看大卫和希西家王的经历呢？
当他读到关于18万5000个亚述士兵
在一夜之间被杀的时候，他会怎么想呢？
那么约西亚呢？亚撒呢？
100万埃塞俄比亚大军被杀呢？
敌人集合起来攻打约沙法时
耶和华怎么保护他们呢？
他把这些事铭记在心
所以他说
“耶和华会跟我们同在，我不需要护送
我看了那么多上帝怎样保护他子民的历史
如果有人护送，我会很丢脸的！”
我们研读的时候也应该像以斯拉
研读是崇拜的一部分
目的是亲近耶和华，巩固我们跟他的关系
而不只是吸收知识
比如
我们研读《守望台》文章的时候
只是为了找答案吗？
为了评论吗？都不是！
研读也是一种崇拜
资料是忠信睿智的奴隶提供的
我们研读《守望台》、查考圣经
是为了亲近耶和华
当然，研读时我们可以找到答案
在聚会时可以评论
但是，研读是为了巩固我们跟耶和华的关系
你研读时有什么感受呢？
要准备自己的心
我的动机是什么呢？
每次我们打开圣经
我们都应该像撒母耳一样，他说
“耶和华啊，请说，仆人在听。”
耶和华也赐给以斯拉
洞悉事理的能力和理解力
让他能够在深入查考上帝的话语后
实际去帮助以色列人
比如在9:2
他发现圣洁的后代跟四周的民族混杂起来
很多男子娶了外族女子
以斯拉深知这将会带来灾难
“你们竟然娶外族的女子！
你们想要被同化吗？
你们竟然把正确崇拜跟异教混在一起吗？
如果不小心
正确崇拜很可能会从地上消失
这样你们就认不出谁是弥赛亚了！
这个人是出自大卫家系吗？
出自犹大部族吗？
我们不知道！”
在上帝帮助下，以斯拉看出问题并纠正事态
现在我们看看10:1
这节经文再次透露以斯拉的美好品格
以斯拉谦卑地在上帝面前祷告、认罪
帮助犹太人送走他们的外族妻子
那时，有一大群以色列人
“包括男女和小孩，都聚集在他周围痛哭”
这就是以斯拉
他不像专制的暴君，没有人害怕他
以斯拉就像一个仁爱的牧人
把许多人吸引到他身边

titles.en: Mark Noumair: “Ezra Had Prepared His Heart” (Ezra 7:10)
titles.cn: 马克·努玛尔：以斯拉心里做好准备（拉7:10）

title: 알렉스 라인뮬러: “우리 하느님 여호와는 한 분인 여호와이십니다” (신명 6:4, 5)

ko.text: 그들은 성경에서 하느님이 때때로 분노하시는 것에 불편해하죠.
이 세상의 비평가들 때문일 수 있습니다.
가장 불쾌한 주인공이라고 할 수 있다.”
그 뒤 내용은 차마 말할 수가 없습니다.
사람들은 그와 같은 주장을 자주 들을수록
전 이런 악몽 같은 일을 매일 겪었죠.”
먼저 비평가들의 주장에 대한 성경의 가르침을 살펴본 뒤
여호와는 한 분이시라는 강력한 진리를 옹호하셨습니다.
한 서기관이 가장 큰 계명이 무엇인지 물어보았을 때
우리 하느님 여호와는 한 분인 여호와이시니,
네 마음을 다하고 영혼을 다하고 정신을 다하고 힘을 다해
바알 신을 예로 들 수 있죠.
다른 종교들에서도 비슷한 상황을 볼 수 있습니다.
하느님께서 하나의 인격만을 가지신 분임을 떠올렸을 것입니다.
그러면 사랑의 하느님이 왜 때때로 분노하십니까?
그분은 자신의 이름과 표준을 변호하셔야 했습니다.
여호와께서는 ‘분노하기를 더디 하고 사랑의 친절이 풍부하신’ 분입니다.
사랑 그 자체이시라고 요한1서 4:8은 알려 줍니다.
‘그에게 믿음을 나타내는 사람이 누구나 멸망되지 않고
영원한 생명을 얻게 하려는 것’이라고 하셨죠.
그분이 마치 예전보다 더 부드러운 분이 되셔서
다른 성품을 갖게 되신 게 아니죠.
그리고 그분의 사랑이 전보다 더 커진 것도 아니죠.
그를 사랑 많은 아버지로 볼지 모릅니다.
그의 성품의 다른 부면이 나타나는 것입니다.
그분을 사랑하는 사람들에 대한 목적과 관련해 특히 그러시죠.
그분의 입체적이고 아름답고 변하지 않는 성품 전체에 대한
그분이 언제나 우리를 부드럽게 대하시기 때문에
자신의 종들이 언제나 잘되기를 바라신다는 것을
“‘내가 너희에 대해 갖고 있는 생각을 나는 잘 알고 있다.’
너희가 미래와 희망을 갖게 하려는 것이다.’”
그분이 언제나 주변 상황과 자기 자신에 대한 온전한 통제력을 행사하시기 때문에
그리고 예수께서 우리 죄를 위해 죽으셨기 때문에
우린 언제나 여호와의 품 안에서 안전감을 느낍니다.
“그날에는 여호와가 하나일 것이며 그 이름도 하나일 것이다.”

en.text: A newspaper in Japan
once quoted a Catholic priest.
He said, ‘The God of the Old Testament,
‘Yahweh,
‘is a God of anger,
and I can’t feel close to him.’
And then he added,
‘But he developed and transformed
‘into what is the God of the New Testament,
that is, the God of love whom Jesus taught.’
Have you ever heard that?
A lot of people still think like this,
as if God has a split personality.
They are uncomfortable when they read in the Bible
that God gets angry sometimes.
Why is that?
Well, it may be for one of two reasons.
First, there are outspoken critics in this world
who constantly try to discredit Jehovah.
A prominent biologist, for example, made headlines a few years ago.
He said in his book: “The God of the Old Testament
is arguably the most unpleasant character in all fiction.”
I stopped the quote there because it gets much worse.
How blasphemous a viewpoint that is!
The more often people hear statements like this,
the more they tend to believe them.
There’s a second reason, though, why some struggle with God’s anger.
They have suffered in abusive relationships,
and now they’re sensitive to any perceived abuse.
Take Carolyn for example, she said:
“When my drunken father used to explode in anger,
“his appearance changed.
He became like a wolf baring its teeth before attacking.”
She said, “I lived this nightmare every day.”
Well, abuse like this can scar people for a long time.
So how can we help sincere persons
get past their fears about God’s anger
and draw closer to Jehovah?
Well, let’s address the critics first
and then see how we can reassure those who may be feeling insecure.
First, let’s make one thing clear:
Jehovah does not have multiple personalities.
When Jesus was on earth, he advocated
the powerful truth that Jehovah is one.
When a Jewish scribe asked him
what was the greatest of all commandments, what did he say?
Let’s read Mark 12:29, 30
and see what his reply was in his own words.
He answered by quoting today’s text
“Jesus answered: ‘The first is,
“‘“Hear, O Israel, Jehovah our God is one Jehovah,
“‘“and you must love Jehovah your God
“‘“with your whole heart and with your whole soul
and with your whole mind and with your whole strength.”’”
So for Jesus, loving Jehovah for who he is
(not for who we want him to be),
is really the most important decision any of us could make.
Now, the pagan nations had all sorts of gods for different purposes.
And they would worship different aspects
of even the same God in different localities,
like the god Baal, for example.
And something similar happened in other religions.
Say, for example, the Catholic Church
with its different manifestations of the worship of Mary.
But things were very different in Israel.
They learned that there was only one God, Jehovah,
who was responsible for everything.
And each time they read Deuteronomy 6:4,
they were reminded that God had one personality.
So why does a God of love get angry sometimes?
Well, the answer is quite simple.
When rebels challenged Jehovah’s sovereignty,
he had to defend his name and standards.
Rebellion did make him angry and rightly so,
but Jehovah’s anger is always under control
and guided by right principles.
As a Father, he had to protect his household.
Respect for his own name and his love for his children
compelled him to act.
At the same time,
Jehovah is “slow to anger
and abundant in loving-kindness.”
His fundamental mood is not anger, but joy.
And Jesus said that “God loved the world so much
that he gave his only-begotten Son.”
Jehovah has been, is, and always will be
a God of unchangeable love.
First John 4:8 says: “God is love.”
It identifies who he is.
But Jesus also said that God gave his Son
in order that “everyone exercising faith in him
“might not be destroyed
but have everlasting life.”
Did you notice that Jesus said
those not exercising faith will be destroyed?
So Jehovah’s personality didn’t mellow over the years,
as if it needed mellowing.
It didn’t transform from one personality to another.
His severity today against the wicked is no less
nor his love any greater than it was in the past.
Jehovah does not change.
We can illustrate it like this, perhaps:
Criminals may know that a police officer
is an arm of the law.
His children may see him
as a loving father that he is.
And his close friends may value him
for his good sense of humor.
Now, the police officer, the father, and the friend
are all the same person.
In each situation, a different aspect of his personality stands out.
And it’s the same with Jehovah.
In harmony with his name,
“He Causes to Become”
or becomes whatever he needs to in every situation
in order to fulfill his purpose,
especially his purpose toward those who love him.
So if we want to get closer to Jehovah,
we have to accept the full range
of his beautiful, multifaceted,
and unchanging personality.
For those who love God, we don’t fear his anger.
We learn to trust him because he’s always kind
and tender toward us.
Why can we say that?
Well, open your Bibles with me
to Jeremiah 29:11,
and notice why we can be sure
that Jehovah always wants the best for us
as he did for his servants in the past.
In his own words:
“‘For I well know the thoughts that I am thinking toward you,’
“declares Jehovah,
“‘thoughts of peace, and not of calamity,
to give you a future and a hope.’”
Because Jehovah loves us,
because he is always in full control of himself
and circumstances around him,
and because Jesus has already died for our sins,
we can always feel safe with Jehovah.
We do not ever need to fear approaching him.
Very soon now, as Zechariah 14:9 predicts,
Jehovah must become “King over all the earth.
“In that day [the prophet said]
“Jehovah will [prove to] be one,
and his name one.”
Everyone in heaven and on earth will agree at that time
that Jehovah our God is the Universal Sovereign,
and you and I will gladly join our voices
with that happy chorus.
What a beautiful prospect that is!

cn.text: 日本的一份报纸引用一个天主教教士的话
他说旧约的上帝雅威是个愤怒的上帝
我很难与他亲近，他继续说
这位上帝后来演变成新约充满爱心的上帝
也就是耶稣教导人认识的上帝
你也听说过吗？
有不少人认为
上帝有两种截然不同的性格
当他们读到圣经说上帝有时会生气
这让他们很不舒服
为什么呢？
这可能有以下两个原因
首先，世上的一些批评家一直攻击上帝
试图破坏耶和华的名声
例如
在几年前一个非常有名的生物学家在自己的书里说
“毫无疑问
旧约的上帝是所有小说中最不受欢迎的角色。”
他接下来讲得太难听，我就不说了
这样的说法真的亵渎上帝！
人越常听到这样的说法就越容易相信
有些人无法接受上帝会发怒还有一个原因
这些人曾被人以暴力对待
所以他们很容易觉得别人也受到了一样的对待
我们看凯罗琳的例子，她说
“每次爸爸喝醉时，他的样子就变了
他像一只凶暴的狼
露出尖锐的牙齿，准备攻击猎物。”
她说这场噩梦每天都在重演
这类暴力会对人造成长久的伤害
那么，我们可以怎样帮助诚恳的人
不再对上帝的愤怒感到害怕
并亲近上帝呢？
我们先来回应一下批评
看看怎样安慰那些可能觉得不安的人
首先，要澄清一件事
上帝的性格从未改变
耶稣在地上时，向人强调一个重要的真理
就是上帝始终如一
当一个抄经士问耶稣诫命中哪一条最重要的时候
他怎么回答呢？
我们来读马可福音12:29,30
看看耶稣怎么回答抄经士的这个问题
今天的经文引用了耶稣的回答
马可福音12:29,30，耶稣回答说
“最重要的是，‘以色列啊，听吧！
耶和华我们的上帝是独一的耶和华
你要全心，全意，全力
用全部生命爱耶和华你的上帝’。”
所以，跟耶稣一样
我们要全心爱耶和华
而不是只爱上帝的某些部分
这是我们每一个人都要做的重要决定
异教的国族为了不同的目的崇拜不同的神
即使这些异教国族崇拜同一个神
但在不同的地方
人们可能也崇拜他的不同部分
巴力崇拜就是个例子
其他宗教也有类似的情况
举个例
各地的天主教会也以不同的方式崇拜马利亚的不同方面
但古代以色列却完全不一样
他们知道只有一位上帝耶和华
他统管天地万物
每当以色列人读到申命记6:4的经文都受到提醒
耶和华是始终如一的
那么，为什么充满爱心的上帝有时会生气呢？
答案其实很简单
叛徒挑战耶和华的至高统治权时
他就需要捍卫自己的名声和标准
叛徒让他生气，而他也确实有理由生气
但耶和华的怒气总是受到控制
也受他的公正原则支配
身为父亲，他要捍卫自己的家
基于维护自己的名声和对孩子的爱
他采取行动
在这种情况，耶和华仍然不轻易发怒
也表现出忠贞的厚爱
上帝是一个快乐的上帝
不是愤怒的上帝
而耶稣也说
“上帝深爱世人，甚至赐下自己的独生子。”
耶和华的爱
不管是过去、现在，还是未来都不会改变
约翰一书4:8说:“上帝就是爱。”
经文说出了他的特质
耶稣也说上帝赐下儿子
是为了“让所有信从他的人都不致灭亡
反而得到永远的生命”
你留意到耶稣说所有不信从他的人都会灭亡吗？
所以，耶和华的性格并没有随着时间过去而改变
好像他需要进步一样
他也没有从一种性格变成另外一种性格
现在，他对恶人的判决并没有减轻
他也不是后来变得更爱人类
我们的上帝耶和华从来没改变
我们可以打个比方来说明
对一个罪犯来说
警察是一个法律的执行者
对警察的孩子来说
他却是一个仁爱的父亲
对警察的朋友来说
他又是一个幽默的人
你看，警察、父亲还有朋友都是同一个人
在不同的情况下
他的不同特质就表现出来
耶和华也类似
耶和华名字的意思是成事者
也就是他能按需要
想成为什么就成为什么
以求实现自己的旨意
特别是实现对那些爱他的人的旨意
所以，如果我们要亲近耶和华
我们就必须爱他的所有特质
也就是他不会改变的每一种美好特质
对爱上帝的人来说
我们并不害怕他的愤怒
我们可以信赖他
因为他一直仁慈体贴地对待我们
为什么这样说呢？
我们一起打开圣经到耶利米书29:11
请留意为什么我们可以确信
耶和华总是为我们的最大益处着想
就像他对待古代的仆人那样
经文说:“耶和华说
‘我很清楚我想要为你们做什么
我要赐安宁，不是降灾祸
要让你们有前途有希望。’”
因为耶和华很爱我们
因为耶和华能完全控制自己和他身边的所有情况
也因为耶稣已经为我们的罪而死
我们跟耶和华在一起时总是有安全感
不用害怕亲近他
不久后，撒迦利亚书14:9预告的就会实现
“耶和华会成为统治整个大地的君王
那一天，唯独耶和华会受人崇拜
唯独他的名字会受人尊崇”
到时，天地众生都会同意
我们的上帝耶和华是宇宙的至高主宰
你和我会一起快乐地高声赞美上帝
这是多么美好的前景！

titles.ko: 알렉스 라인뮬러: “우리 하느님 여호와는 한 분인 여호와이십니다” (신명 6:4, 5)
titles.en: Alex Reinmueller: "Jehovah Our God Is One Jehovah" (Deut. 6:4, 5)
titles.cn: 亚历克斯·赖因米勒：“耶和华我们的上帝是独一的耶和华”（申6:4,5）

ko.text: 하지만 그들은 하느님의 사랑에 어떤 반응을 보였습니까?
바로 그 성전에서 거짓 신들을 숭배했습니다!
예루살렘의 멸망에 대한 에스겔의 예언을 통해
그 질문들에 대한 답을 알아볼 것입니다.
배교한 유다의 영적, 도덕적 몰락에 대해 다룹니다.
에스겔은 모세 율법에 대해 잘 알고 있었습니다.
여호와께 순결한 숭배를 드리는 데 무엇이 요구되는지도 알고 있었죠.
그런데 그는 예루살렘 성전에서 여호와의 충실한 숭배자라면
누구나 경악할 만한 일이 벌어지는 것을 보게 됩니다.
이제 에스겔 8:9을 펴서, 함께 읽어 보시죠.
‘들어가서 그들이 거기서 행하고 있는 악하고 혐오스러운 일들을 보아라.’”
5장에서는 에스겔이 본 그러한 장면들에 대해 다루며,
이 장을 연구하면서 다음 질문들에 대한 답을 찾아 보시기 바랍니다.
우리는 어떻게 그 기대와 일치하게 행동할 수 있습니까?
이스라엘 백성은 영적으로 타락했음을 보여 주는 어떤 행동들을 했으며,
우리는 어떻게 영적으로 깨끗한 상태를 유지할 수 있습니까?
우리가 도덕적으로 깨끗한 상태를 유지하기로 결심하는 이유는 무엇입니까?
‘영적으로 깨끗한 상태를 유지하기 위해 나는 어떤 유혹들을 물리쳐야 할까?’
어떤 불결한 습관이든 극복할 수 있게 해 주실 것입니다.
여호와께 그분이 마땅히 받으셔야 할 순결한 숭배를 드릴 수 있습니다.

en.text: ‎Jehovah loved and cared for the Israelites
‎as his “treasured possession.”
‎But how did they respond to God’s love?
‎By worshipping false gods
‎in the very temple that bore his name!
‎They broke Jehovah’s heart
‎and brought reproach upon his name.
‎Why did Israel sink so low?
‎What can we learn from Ezekiel’s prophecy
‎about Jerusalem’s destruction?
‎Those questions are answered
‎in section 2 of the book
‎Pure Worship of Jehovah —Restored At Last!
‎This section is based
‎on Ezekiel 5:11 and is entitled
‎“It Was My Sanctuary That You Defiled.”
‎The first chapter of this section focuses
‎on apostate Judah’s spiritual and moral decline.
‎Ezekiel knew the Mosaic Law well.
‎He knew what was involved in giving Jehovah pure worship,
‎but he saw things happening at the temple in Jerusalem
‎that would shock any faithful worshipper of Jehovah.
‎Turn, please, to Ezekiel 8:9,
‎and read along with me:
‎“He said to me: ‘Go in and see
‎the evil, detestable things that they are doing here.’”
‎This passage sets the scene for chapter 5,
‎“See the Evil, Detestable Things That They Are Doing.”
‎As you study this chapter,
‎look for the answers to the following questions:
‎What does Jehovah rightly expect of his worshippers,
‎and how can you live up to his expectation?
‎In what ways did the Israelites
‎become spiritually unclean,
‎but how can you keep spiritually clean?
‎And why are you determined
‎to stay morally clean?
‎As you consider this material, ask yourself,
‎‘What temptations must I resist
‎if I’m to remain spiritually clean?’
‎Please be assured
‎that Jehovah will give you the strength you need
‎to reject any temptation
‎or to overcome any unclean habit.
‎Only if we remain clean
‎can we give Jehovah what he deserves
‎—our pure worship.

cn.text: 耶和华深爱以色列人，照顾他们
把他们视为自己“珍爱的产业”
但他们怎样回报上帝的爱呢？
他们竟然在耶和华名下的圣殿里崇拜假神！
他们让耶和华非常伤心，也使他蒙受耻辱
以色列人怎么沦落到这样的地步？
以西结预言耶路撒冷会被毁灭
我们从中可以学到什么？
《正确的崇拜终于复兴了！》
这本书的第二部分会回答这些问题
这个部分的标题是
“我的圣殿被玷污了”
主题经文是以西结书5:11
这个部分的头一章重点讲述
叛道的犹大国在宗教和道德上的堕落
以西结精通摩西法典
也知道对耶和华的正确崇拜应该是怎样的
但他在耶路撒冷圣殿里看到的事
却会让任何忠心崇拜耶和华的人感到震惊
请跟我一起翻到以西结书8:9
这句话把我们带进第5章的场景
这一章的标题是
“看看他们......做的可憎的恶事”
学习这一章时，请找找以下问题的答案
耶和华对崇拜他的人有哪些合理的要求？
你可以怎样达到这些要求？
什么显示以色列人在崇拜方面变得不洁？
你可以怎样确保自己对上帝的崇拜不受玷污？
为什么你决心要在道德方面保持洁净？
你学习这一章时，请问问自己
我要确保自己对上帝的崇拜不受玷污
就必须拒绝哪些引诱呢？
请放心
耶和华一定会给你需要的力量去拒绝任何引诱
克服任何不洁的习惯
我们必须保持洁净
才能参与正确的崇拜，敬奉耶和华
这是他配得的

titles.cn: 第5章简介

title: 우리 시대를 위한 경고의 본보기—발췌 영상

ko.text: 삽디, 진짜 가나안 사람을 만났을 때
절대로 그런 일은 없을 거야, 벨라!
우리 앞에서 이스라엘의 모든 적이 쓰러질 테니까.
우리도 못 봤지만, 재미있는 소문이 돌더군.
왜 여자들이 우리 진영으로 오는 걸까?
우리가 군사력이 훨씬 더 강한 아모리 사람들을
지므리는 그 외국 여자들하고 이야기해 봤다던데.
방금 모압 여자 얘기를 하던 참인데.
이 정보의 대가로 뭘 줄 텐가?
우리가 젖과 꿀이 흐르는 땅으로 들어가고 있다면,
이게 바로 그 첫 꿀맛이라고만 말해 주지.
먼지 폭풍 속의 낙타처럼 눈이 먼 거지.
그러니 우리도 관대하고 합리적이어야 하지 않겠어?
미디안 제사장 이드로의 딸과 결혼하지 않았나?
거기는 호화롭고 음식과 술과 음악이 있지.
우리 할아버지들은 모세와 아론의 말을 들었지.
아론도 죽었고, 모세도 곧 뒤따를 테고.
나는 뭔가 더 나은 삶을 원해,
형, 우리 조상은 여호와께 반역했기 때문에
아모리, 가나안, 히위, 브리스, 여부스 사람들이야.
그런데 비느하스가 모압에 대해 험담을 한단 말이지.
모압 사람들이 사귀기에 그토록 위험하고 악하다면,
지므리는 마치 뭐든지 다 아는 것처럼
하지만 저는 그의 태도가 마음에 걸렸는데,
그 덕분에 제가 목숨을 건졌을 겁니다.
그들과 싸우지 말라고 하신 이유 말인데요.
여호와께서 우리가 모압과 전쟁을 하면 안 된다고
땅의 상속 재산을 갖도록 정하셨기 때문이야.
그들에게 주신 땅을 우리가 차지하면 안 되지.
하지만 벗이 되는 게 뭐 잘못입니까?
그 대답을 알고 있을 텐데, 야민.
율법에 들어 있는 높은 표준에 따라 살고 있나?
그들의 벗이 되기를 원하실 거라고 생각하지?
저, 어쩌면 그들에게서 배울 수도 있잖아요.
그들이 어떤 면으로 우리를 도울 수 있을 테고.
그리고 아마 우리도 여호와에 관해 배우도록
야민, 여호와께서 어떻게 인도하시는지 두고 봐야겠지.
모압이 들어 있지 않은 건 사실이지.
만일 우리가 그 땅의 주민들과 벗이 되고자 한다면,

cn.text: 你们这些胆小的迦南军队，赶快逃命吧！
撒底，真的遇上迦南人
- 说不定要逃命的是你呢！ - 怎么可能，比拉
- 所有敌人都会倒在我们面前！ - 说得对！
- 雅悯，你觉得那些女人怎么样？ - 什么女人？
摩押女人啊，你一定听说过！
我是听说这几晚有外族女人到我们营地来
但是我没见过她们
- 我们也只听过一些传闻 - 什么传闻？
听人家说，那些女人很漂亮
跟我们的“旷野”女人完全不一样
那些女人更有魅力
听说，她们也非常善解人意！
- 为什么只有女人来到我们营地，男人却没来？ - 唉，雅悯！
你这样问，证明你不了解女人，原因很简单
所有人都听说了我们怎么打败亚摩利人
虽然他们兵力比我们强大，西宏和噩那么强大
不是都被我们轻松击败了吗？
迦南人都很害怕我们
在我看来，那些女人就是好奇
她们想见识一下真男人！
强壮勇猛的男人，这不就是我们吗？
撒底，别忘了是耶和华让我们得胜的
也许吧，但上阵杀敌的是我们啊！
我们所向无敌
看！你的表哥心利
- 听说，他认识那些外族女人 - 愿你们平安，弟兄们！
- 心利 - 愿你平安
心利，我们刚才在聊摩押女人
听说你见过她们，快说说！
你们也对新邻居感兴趣
但我说了，你们会给我什么好处？
要是你都告诉我们
我们就把我们最贵的东西都给你，比如......
- 两杯吗哪，怎么样 ？ - 这么难吃的东西，自己留着吧！
- 你们想知道什么？ - 全部！她们长得怎么样？
这样说吧！如果我们要进入流奶流蜜的土地
- 这就是我们的第一滴蜜！ - 营里有人说，这些女人别有用心
这样说的人就像风暴中的骆驼，什么也看不清！
摩押人是我们的亲戚
也是亚伯拉罕家族的后人，跟我们一样
- 我们也可以向他们学习嘛！ - 赶紧说说那些女人！
心利，他们不崇拜耶和华！
他们反对我们的崇拜吗？没有
他们是通情达理的人
不但尊重我们的民族，也尊重我们的宗教
我们不是也应该对他们通情达理吗？
他们很乐意帮助我们，给了我们食物和水
其他民族却拒绝了我们，你忘了吗？
- 他们是卖给我们的，那是买卖，不是帮助 - 快说说那些女人吧！
不管怎样，他们给了我们食物和水
这说明他们很友善
说不定耶和华要我们合作呢！
我们帮助他们，他们帮助我们！
我告诉你们，如果拒绝他们的好意
我们就是傻子
- 其实我看过，他们过得可舒服了！ - 什么？你看过......？
你什么时候去的？怎么去的？
歌斯比带我去的，她是个米甸女人
她的父亲是个大人物
什么！你是说连米甸女人也到我们营地来了吗？
摩押人和米甸人的关系很好
- 你经常跟那个米甸女人来往吗？ - 怎么了？
摩西不也娶了个米甸女人吗？
他的岳父叶特罗不是米甸祭司吗？
摩押的城镇是什么样的？你看到了什么？
各位弟兄，我告诉你们，他们很懂得享受生活
美酒、佳肴、音乐、珠宝，样样都有
我想我们祖先在埃及的生活也是这样
难怪他们讨厌吗哪！
每天吃这么难吃的东西真让人恶心！
想不想跟我到摩押那边逛一逛、开开眼界？
我告诉你们，摩押人很热情
一定会好好招待你们
这样做不太好吧
- 非尼哈和其他导师不是常常警告我们 - 啊！别，别跟我提非尼哈！
他仗着父亲以利亚撒是新任大祭司
就以为自己可以发号施令！
我们是新时代的人
我可不想像上一代人那样浪费生命！
- 你的意思是？ - 我的意思是
我们祖先听从摩西、亚伦，结果怎样？
他们放弃了埃及的享受，到旷野来受苦
到头来还不是死在旷野了！
亚伦死了，摩西也活不了多久了
我可要过好日子，现在就要！
- 我也要！ - 我也是。我要加入你们！
等一下，我们的祖先是因为反叛耶和华
所以才死在旷野的
心利，你跟这些不崇拜真神的民族来往
真的不会有问题吗？
雅悯，你脑子里进沙子了！
我怎么会有你这么蠢的表弟？
我问问你:耶和华有没有吩咐摩西赶走摩押人？
- 嗯，没有 - 耶和华有没有说过，要赶走米甸人？
- 好像没有 - 耶和华命令我们要赶走的是亚摩利人、迦南人
希未人、比利洗人和耶布斯人
当时，我的思绪很混乱
心利说的关于摩押人的话似乎有点道理
不是摩押人，也不是米甸人
你说非尼哈那个顽固的笨蛋要我们小心摩押人
那你就去问问他这个问题
如果摩押人那么邪恶和危险
为什么耶和华特别吩咐摩西不让我们攻击他们？
拿这个问题去请教你的好朋友非尼哈吧！
我不知道，也许你是对的
心利对自己的话那么有自信，仿佛什么都知道
但他那不满、固执的态度却让我很不舒服
我决定去找非尼哈
心利肯定没想到我会这么做
但这是我做过最明智的决定
因为这个决定救了我一命
不好意思，非尼哈，可以跟你聊一下吗？
当然可以，小伙子。请坐！
- 你叫什么名字？ - 我叫雅悯，是西缅部族的
雅悯，很高兴认识你，一切都好吗？
我很好。但我有个问题想不通
既然你是我们的祭司和导师
- 我就想请教你一下 - 什么问题呢？
呃，我很想知道你对摩押人的看法
- 你的意思是？ - 为什么耶和华吩咐摩西不要与他们交战呢？
你觉得，上帝是要我们跟他们来往吗？
耶和华是对摩西说过，不要跟摩押人交战
但他也说明了原因
他让摩押人可以拥有自己的土地
而我们不可以占据他们的土地
但上帝没有说过我们可以跟他们来往
那跟他们来往有问题吗？
我想你知道答案，雅悯
摩押人崇拜真神吗？
不，他们有自己的神
他们有没有按照耶和华40年前赐下的法典里
崇高的标准生活呢？
没有
那你为什么觉得耶和华想要我们跟他们来往呢？
呃，也许我们可以向他们学习啊
也许他们能帮助我们
说不定我们也可以帮助他们认识耶和华呢
这就得看日后耶和华有什么指引了，雅悯
可是，在选择跟谁来往方面，我们必须小心谨慎
虽然耶和华没有吩咐我们去攻打摩押人
但他们崇拜假神巴力，跟迦南人一样
