ko.text: 여호와 보시기엔 둘 다 심각한 문제죠.
오늘은 걸려 넘어지는 문제에 대해 생각해 보죠.
우리는 이 말을 오해해서는 안 되는 게,
걸려 넘어져도 된다고 정당화하는 말이 아닙니다.
우리가 걸림돌이 될 만한 문제에 부딪혔을 때
“의로운 자는 일곱 번 쓰러져도 다시 일어나지만”.
이제 무엇이 걸림돌이 될 수 있는지,
어떻게 걸려 넘어지는 일을 피할 수 있는지 살펴보죠.
동료 신자들이 우리를 부당하게 대하는 것이 걸림돌이 될 수가 있죠.
우리도 이런 장애물 중 하나에 발이 부딪혀
이러한 장애물이 우리를 가로막는 벽이 되어
우리를 완전히 가로막는 일이 없게 하려면
이 성구는 앞에 나온 질문에 대한
우리가 걸려 넘어지지 않을 수 있다는
“당신의 법을 사랑하는 이들에게는 풍부한 평화가 있으니,
그들을 걸려 넘어지게 하는 것이 아무것도 없습니다.”
가장 자주 부딪히는 걸림돌 중 하나는
여호와를 섬기는 일을 중단하지 않을 수 있는지 살펴보겠습니다.
어떻게 균형을 되찾을 수 있었는지 설명했습니다.
골디 자매도 러더퍼드 형제가 잘못했다고 생각한 것이죠.
여동생 부부가 골디 자매의 집에 왔습니다.
골디가 러더퍼드 형제 때문에 이제 집회에 안 갈 거라고 하자
골디는 루마니아에서 침례를 받아서 그때는 몰랐다고 했죠.
“러더퍼드 형제가 진리를 떠나면 처형도 떠날 건가요?”
그 순간 골디는 정신이 번쩍 들어 말했습니다.
딸 베스가 길르앗 14기 학급에 초대되기도 했습니다.
왜 이름이 골디인지도 알게 되실 겁니다.
하느님의 말씀의 깊은 진리를 배우게 되었습니다.
프랑스어로 발간되는 종교 신문들에 광고를 실었고
많은 사람들이 그 광고에 큰 관심을 보였습니다.
웨버 형제는 여름에는 스위스에서 벌목공과 정원사로 일했고
유럽에 있는 프랑스어 밭의 활동을 전반적으로 감독했습니다.
아 글쎄, 웨버 형제보다 세속 교육을 더 받은 다른 형제를
왕국을 위해 자신이 할 수 있는 일을 기꺼이 했습니다.
세속 교육을 더 받은 그 형제,
그 뒤를 이어 임명된 네 사람도 진리를 떠났죠.
웨버 형제는 자신이 해 오던 일을
그 특성이 가져오는 결과에 주목해 보시죠.
웨버 형제에게 정말 딱 들어맞는 말이죠!
그는 한 번도 사람들의 인정을 받으려 하지 않았지만
웨버 형제의 삶을 이렇게 아름답게 요약합니다.
‘지나치게 자기 자신을 중요시하는 감정에 빠져 버린 사람도 있었으나
자신에 대해 겸손하고 겸허한 시각을 유지하면서
여호와와의 친밀한 관계를 길러 나가는 데

en.text: Which is worse?
To stumble others or to be stumbled?
From Jehovah’s viewpoint,
both are serious matters
that can affect our lives
and also the lives of others.
But today, we’re going to focus on the matter of being stumbled
because our text urges us: “Do not be quick to take offense.”
James 3:2 warns us
that “we all stumble many times.”
We don’t want to misunderstand these words
and say that it’s OK to be stumbled.
It’s not providing an excuse.
Rather, James simply stated a reality
of our imperfect lives.
The important thing, then, is,
What do we do when we run into a potential stumbling block?
Proverbs 24:16 tells us:
“The righteous one may fall even seven times,
and he will certainly get up.”
Let’s consider what might cause us to stumble
and how we can avoid being stumbled.
Some causes of stumbling are injustices
on the part of our fellow believers.
It could be persecution, tribulation,
or it may be the imperfections of others.
Any one of these obstacles could cause us
to trip, to stumble, or even to fall down.
How can we prevent these stumbling blocks
from turning into roadblocks that stop our forward movement
in Jehovah’s service?
Please open your Bibles to Psalm 119.
We’ll read verse 165.
This scripture provides a simple answer to that question,
and it also assures us that we can avoid being stumbled
“Abundant peace belongs to those who love your law;
nothing can make them stumble.”
Why not?
Because if we love Jehovah’s law,
Jehovah will not allow us to be stumbled.
Our deep love for him and for his law
will prevent that from happening.
Some of the most common stumbling blocks
result from the imperfections of others.
I’d like to reflect on two experiences
that illustrate how we can avoid letting such problems
become a permanent stumbling block.
The first experience is
of Sister Goldie Romocean.
She was born in Romania in 1903.
She was baptized in 1918.
In 1921, she immigrated to the United States,
and that same year she married a Romanian brother from her hometown.
They settled in Akron, Ohio, and had four daughters.
In the mid-1930’s, Goldie and her husband were stumbled.
Listen to Goldie as she explains why they were stumbled
and what helped them to regain their balance.
She related:
‘I became angry with Brother Rutherford.
‘A new Witness felt that Brother Rutherford
‘had dealt unjustly with him, not hearing him out.
‘I felt that Brother Rutherford was wrong.
‘Well, one Sunday my sister Mary and her husband, Dan, came to visit us.
‘After dinner Dan said: “Let’s get ready to go to the meeting.”
‘“We don’t go to the meetings anymore,” I said.
‘“We’re mad at Brother Rutherford.”
‘Dan asked: “Did you know Brother Rutherford when you got baptized?”
‘“Of course not,” I replied.
‘“You know I got baptized in Romania.”
‘“Well, why did you get baptized?” he asked.
‘“Because I learned that Jehovah is the true God,
‘and I wanted to dedicate my life to serve him,” I answered.
‘“Never forget that! ” Dan replied.
‘“What if Brother Rutherford left the truth, would you leave too?”
‘“Never, never!” I said.
‘That brought me to my senses, and I said:
‘“Everybody get ready for the meeting.”
And we haven’t stopped since.’
Jehovah continued to bless Goldie and her family.
For example, her daughter Beth graduated from the 14th class of Gilead.
The moving account of Goldie’s life story
can be found in the April 1, 1997,
issue of The Watchtower.
By all means, go back and read it.
You will not only be encouraged
but you’ll also learn how she got the name Goldie.
Is there a lesson here for us?
Yes.
Goldie and her family avoided permanent stumbling
by staying focused on the big picture
—that is, Jehovah’s sovereignty
and their personal relationship with him.
Now let’s consider a second experience.
When I read the text for today,
I immediately thought of Brother Adolf Weber.
I first read his experience 38 years ago
in the 1980 Yearbook.
Obviously, his experience made a lasting impression
on my mind and heart.
Adolf Weber was a Swiss woodcutter.
His job was cutting down trees.
In the mid-1890’s, he traveled to the United States.
He worked as a part-time gardener for Brother Russell,
and that’s how he came to learn the deep truths of God’s Word.
Brother Weber was fluent in English, German, and French.
He volunteered to return to Europe
to cultivate the French-speaking field, and Brother Russell agreed.
Brother Weber went to his hometown in Switzerland,
and there he placed ads in French religious newspapers
and found an excellent response to those ads.
Then in 1903,
Brother Russell visited Europe and arranged with Brother Weber
to publish an eight-page French edition of the Watch Tower.
And like a zealous regular pioneer,
in the summer, Brother Weber worked as a woodcutter and a gardener in Switzerland
and then he would travel to France and to Belgium
to follow up on interested ones
who had responded to his newspaper ads.
He traveled extensively and gave general oversight to the work
in this French-speaking field in Europe
for over 12 years.
Then in 1912, Brother Russell visited Europe again
and he appointed a new brother who was better educated than Brother Weber
to be in charge of the work.
Do you see a potential stumbling block?
Absolutely.
But Brother Weber didn’t even flinch.
He humbly stepped down and was happy to do whatever he could
to advance Kingdom interests.
Interestingly, that better-educated brother
who replaced Brother Weber eventually left the truth
and so did four others who succeeded him.
But through all of this,
Brother Weber humbly kept on doing what he had done for years
—spreading seeds of truth to honesthearted ones in the field.
Is there a lesson here for us?
Certainly.
Please open your Bibles to Matthew chapter 23,
and we’ll read verse 12.
This scripture identifies an outstanding quality of Brother Weber.
Notice the results of showing this quality
—Matthew 23:12:
“Whoever exalts himself will be humbled,
and whoever humbles himself will be exalted.”
How true this proved to be in Brother Weber’s case!
Brother Weber was never looking for recognition,
and yet his experience appears in the Proclaimers  book,
the 1980 Yearbook, the 1984 Yearbook,
and the 1987 Yearbook  because of all that good work he did in Europe.
The 1987 Yearbook  gave this meaningful summary
of Brother Weber’s life.
It said: “Though some had allowed feelings
“of self-importance to overreach them,
“Brother Weber had continued to serve Jehovah loyally and humbly. . . .
“His modesty, strong faith, and zealous service
“left a deep impression on all who knew him.
“Finally, at the age of 85,
he finished his earthly course in February 1948.”
What a fitting tribute to this humble servant of Jehovah
who was not quick to take offense!
So may we be like Brother Weber and Sister Romocean.
Let’s maintain a humble, modest view of ourselves
and stay focused on building
a close relationship with Jehovah.
If we do this, we will not be quick to take offense
and nothing will make us stumble.

cn.text: 什么更糟糕呢？
是绊倒别人还是被绊倒呢？
从耶和华的观点来看
这两种情况都很糟糕
因为这关系到我们和其他人的生命
今天我们会集中谈谈
被绊倒的情况
今天的经文是“你不要轻易动怒”
雅各书3:2提醒我们说
“我们人人都难免多次犯错。”
我们不想误解这节经文，说
“被绊倒很正常啊！”
这不是一个借口
雅各只是在陈述不完美可能造成的一种情况
重要的是
当我们遇到可能会绊倒我们的情况时
我们如何去做？
箴言24:16告诉我们
“义人跌倒七次，也会再次起来”
让我们考虑一下，什么是我们绊倒的原因
以及我们如何不被绊倒
一些原因可能是弟兄姐妹对我们不公平
也可能是迫害、患难
或是其他人的不完美造成的
这些原因都可能导致我们被绊倒、跌倒
甚至一蹶不振
我们如何避免让这些事
成为我们崇拜耶和华路上的障碍
让我们不再崇拜他呢？
请打开你的圣经，翻开诗篇119篇
我们会读165节
这节经文回答了我们刚才的问题
并且告诉我们怎样做就不会被绊倒
“爱你法律的人饱享安宁
什么都不能使他们失足。”
为什么呢？
因为我们爱耶和华的法律
耶和华就会帮助我们不会被绊倒
我们深深地爱他和他的法律
就不会有这样的事发生
经常使人绊倒的一个理由是
其他人的不完美
我想说说两个经验
它们说明如何不让别人的不完美
成为我们永久的绊脚石
首先我们来听听
戈尔迪·罗莫塞安姐妹的经历
1903年，她在罗马尼亚出生
在1918年受浸
1921年她移民来美国
在同一年
她嫁给来自她同乡罗马尼亚的一位弟兄
他们有4个女儿，住在俄亥俄州的阿克伦
在30年代中期，戈尔迪和她丈夫被绊倒了
戈尔迪说明为什么他们会被绊倒
以及是什么帮助他们调整观点
她说
“我对卢述福弟兄很不满意
因为一个刚受浸的传道员觉得
卢述福弟兄对他不公平
我觉得卢述福弟兄确实做得不对
一个星期日，我的妹妹玛丽和妹夫来看我们
晚餐过后，妹夫说
‘我们去聚会吧！’
但我说：‘我们不会再去聚会了
我们对卢述福弟兄很不满意。’
妹夫问
‘你受浸的时候认识卢述福弟兄吗？’
我回答：‘当然不认识！
我是在罗马尼亚受浸的。’
他问：‘那你为什么要受浸呢？’
我回答
‘因为我知道耶和华是真神
我想把一生都奉献给他，我要崇拜他。’
他说：‘不要忘记你说的话！’
他继续问
‘如果卢述福弟兄离开真理
你也会离开吗？’
‘我当然不会离开！’我这样回答
我马上就清醒过来了
对大家说：‘准备去聚会吧。’
从那天起
我们就再也没有错过一次聚会了。”
耶和华不断赐福给戈尔迪和她一家
比如
她女儿贝思毕业于第14届的基列学校
戈尔迪姐妹的经历非常鼓励人
她的生平故事就记载在
《守望台》1997年4月1日刊里
你可以去读一下
你不仅会得到鼓励，也会知道
她为什么会叫做戈尔迪
我们学到什么呢？
戈尔迪和她的家人没有被绊倒的原因是
把目光集中于真正重要的事
也就是耶和华的至高统治权
和他们和耶和华之间的个人关系
我们再看看一个弟兄的经历
今天的经文让我马上想到一位弟兄
他是阿道夫·韦伯弟兄
38年前
我在1980年的《年鉴》里读到了他的经历
在我心里留下了非常深刻的印象
阿道夫·韦伯原本在瑞士做伐木工人
19世纪90年代中期
他到了美国找到了一份兼职的工作
就是为罗素弟兄做园丁
在那里他认识了真理
韦伯弟兄可以流利地说英语、德语和法语
他志愿回到欧洲向说法语的人传道
罗素弟兄同意了
韦伯弟兄就回到家乡瑞士
在那里
他在一份法文的报纸上刊登了广告
结果有许多人有很好的反应
罗素弟兄探访了欧洲
和韦伯弟兄一起发行了
只有八页的法语版《守望台》杂志
就像一个热心的正规先驱
夏天的时候
韦伯弟兄在瑞士砍树木
做园丁
然后他会去法国、比利时
拜访那些对他刊登的广告感兴趣的人
他到过好多个国家
照顾那些在欧洲说法语的地区
超过12年
但在1912年
当罗素弟兄再次探访欧洲的时候
他委任了另外一个教育程度比较高的弟兄
照顾当地的传道工作
这会是韦伯弟兄的绊脚石吗？
有可能
不过他完全没有受到任何影响
他谦卑地接受了这个安排
而且非常快乐
继续支持王国传道的工作
很可惜，那位教育程度更高的弟兄
以及接替他的另外4位弟兄
都离开了真理
尽管发生了这些事
韦伯弟兄多年来
一直谦卑地撒播真理的种子
继续帮助有正确态度的人认识真理
我们学习到什么？
请打开你的圣经，我们看马太福音23章
我们一起读12节
在这节经文里
我们看到了韦伯弟兄的一个宝贵特质
也请留意经文提到
拥有这个特质的人会怎么样？
“谁抬高自己，就会被贬低
谁谦卑下来，就会被抬高。”
韦伯弟兄的经历就证明了这节经文说得没错
他关心的不是自己拥有什么职位
但因为他热心传道
他的经历就刊登在1980
1984以及1987年的《年鉴》里
也刊登在《宣扬者》书里
1987年的《年鉴》里有一段有意思的话
总结了韦伯弟兄的一生
“虽然有些人变得骄傲自大
认为自己非常重要
但韦伯弟兄继续忠贞、谦卑地崇拜上帝
后来在1948年的2月
在他85岁的时候
他走完了地上的一生
他的谦虚、热心以及坚强的信心
都给认识他的所有人留下了深刻的印象。”
这样的称赞多么地恰当！
因为他非常谦卑，从不轻易动怒
让我们向韦伯弟兄和罗莫塞安姐妹学习
谦卑、谦虚地看待自己
并且把目光专注于
增进自己跟耶和华的关系
如果我们这样做
我们就不会很容易动怒
而且没有任何事情可以轻易地把我们绊倒

ko.text: 부모라면, 분명히 자녀들에게 여호와에 대해 가르치기를 좋아할 겁니다.
많은 부모는 충실한 종이 마련한 삽화와 동영상을 활용하여
사랑 많으신 우리 하느님에 대한 기본적인 진리를 가르치죠.
그런데 삽화는 여호와에 대한 깊은 진리를 이해하는 데도 도움이 됩니다.
“또 그 가운데 네 생물처럼 보이는 것이 있었는데,
그들의 얼굴 모양으로 말하자면, 넷 다 사람의 얼굴을 하고 있는데
오른쪽은 사자의 얼굴이고 왼쪽은 수소의 얼굴이었다.
또 넷 다 독수리의 얼굴도 하고 있었다.”
“‘네 얼굴을 가진 생물들’은 누구인가” 라는 이 책 4장에서
이 장을 살펴보면서 이러한 요점에 유의해 보시기 바랍니다.
여호와의 힘과 위력을 나타낸다고 할 수 있는 이유는 무엇입니까?
우리는 여호와께서 나타내시는 탁월한 특성들을 통해
그룹의 네 얼굴이, 전체를 함께 보면,
여호와의 특성 모두를 상징한다고 결론 내릴 수 있는 이유는 무엇입니까?
우리를 여호와의 사랑에서 멀어지게 할 수 없음을
해설을 하면, 형제 자매들을 격려할 수 있고,
또 자신이 여호와에 대해 어떻게 느끼는지 그분께 표현할 수 있죠.
그리고 여호와께 순결한 숭배를 드리겠다는 결심도 강화될 것입니다.

en.text: ‎Parents, you no doubt love
‎to teach your children about Jehovah.
‎Many of you likely use the pictures and videos supplied
‎by the faithful slave to help you teach basic truths
‎about our loving God.
‎But pictures can also help us understand deeper truths about Jehovah.
‎Please read with me
‎Ezekiel 1:5, 6, and 10:
‎“Within it were what looked like four living creatures,
‎“and the appearance of each one was like that of a human.
‎“Each one had four faces and four wings.
‎“Their faces had this appearance:
‎“Each of the four had a man’s face
‎“with a lion’s face on the right,
‎“a bull’s face on the left,
‎and each of the four had an eagle’s face.”
‎These verses are discussed in the chapter entitled
‎“Who Are ‘the Living Creatures With Four Faces’?”
‎As you consider this material, look for these key points:
‎Why do the faces of a man, a lion,
‎a bull, and an eagle
‎especially reflect Jehovah’s strength and mightiness?
‎In what ways are you already benefiting
‎from expressions of Jehovah’s outstanding attributes?
‎Why can we conclude that the four faces of the cherubs
‎when viewed together represent all of Jehovah’s attributes?
‎How does this vision of Ezekiel assure you
‎that you are never beyond the reach of Jehovah’s love?
‎If possible, answer as often as you can during the study.
‎Your answers will encourage your brothers and sisters.
‎But they’ll do more.
‎They’ll tell Jehovah how you feel about him,
‎and they’ll strengthen your resolve
‎to give Jehovah pure worship.

ko.text: 여러 가지 시련과 어려움을 겪었을지 모릅니다.
제가 이 연설을 위해 선택한 주제 성구입니다.
확실히 우리의 속사람은 날마다 새로워지고 있습니다.”
유혹을 당해도 여호와를 섬기기를 중단하지 않죠.
산상 수훈에서 예수께서는 우리가 포기하는 일이 없도록
여호와께 “유혹에 빠지지 않게” 해 달라는 기도를 해야 한다고
우리가 귀를 기울여 좋은 조언을 잘 듣고,
그 조언을 깊이 생각해 보면 포기하지 않는 데 도움이 됩니다.
그럼 함께 고린도 후서 4:1을 찾아 보실까요?
이 봉사의 직무를 가지고 있으니 포기하지 않습니다.”
자신과 고린도 회중 사람들이 ‘자격을 갖추는 일이
적합한 자격을 갖추게 해 주셨”다는 점을
“우리는 ... 이 봉사의 직무를 가지고 있”다고 한 말은
그럼 제가 고린도 후서 3:5, 6을 읽을 때
우리에게서 무엇이 나온다고 생각하는 것은 아닙니다.
그분은 참으로 우리가 새 계약의 봉사자로,
영의 봉사자로 적합한 자격을 갖추게 해 주셨습니다.”
이 봉사의 직무를 가지고 있”다고 했는데,
바로 앞 구절에서 말한 기름부음받은 자들이
하늘에 들어갈 때 받는 영광에 이르기까지
“점점 더 영광스럽게 ... 변화되어 갑니다”라고 알려 주죠.
강한 동기를 가지고 포기하지 않고 견딥니다.
그들 앞에는 아주 값진 상이 놓여 있기 때문이죠.
그런 이유로 바울은 4:1에서 이렇게 말한 겁니다.
‘영광을 빼앗긴’ 옛 계약과 새 계약을 대조하면서
그 영광이 더 크고 계속 남아 있을 것이라고 했습니다.
“우리는 그러한 희망을 가지고 있기 때문에”라고 했죠.
거기선 ‘우리는 이 봉사의 직무를 가지고 있으니’라고 했죠.
일반적인 야외 봉사를 말하고 있는 것입니까?
새 계약의 봉사의 직무를 말하는 것입니다.
바울이 새 계약으로 가능해진 하늘의 부르심에 관해
쓰고 있다는 걸 알 수 있습니다.
오늘날 기름부음받은 자들에게도 강한 동기를 주어
하느님께서는 또한 우리에게 인장을 찍으시고”라고 했죠.
새 계약의 봉사의 직무를 통해 놀라운 축복을 받습니다.
새 계약과 그 봉사의 직무라는 보물을 가지고 있는 것처럼,
큰 무리도 자신의 봉사의 직무를 보물로 여깁니다.
큰 무리도 결코 포기하지 않겠다고 결심합니다.
이 땅 낙원에서 영원히 살 놀라운 희망이 있으니까요.
우리 모두는 어떤 희망을 갖고 있든 인내해야 합니다.
심한 압박을 받아 낙심하는 일을 피할 수는 없습니다.
하지만 하느님께선 우리가 이 낡은 제도에서
“창백한 말”에 앉은 상징적 말 탄 자가
이 일은 1차 세계 대전이 끝날 무렵 발생한
스페인 독감을 시작으로 100년이 넘게 일어나고 있습니다.
당시 세계 인구의 3분의 1인 5억 명이 감염된 것으로 추산되며
사탄은 우리가 낙담해 있을 때 공격합니다.
누가 우리를 실망시켜도 포기하지 않을 겁니다.
성서 시대에 여호와의 매우 충실한 종들조차도
그는 “나를 괴롭히는 모든 자 때문에”라고 했습니다.
다윗은 자신에 대한 사람들의 악한 행동 때문에
그렇지만 동료 인간들이 자신에게 한 행동 때문에
우리도 다른 사람의 말이나 행동 때문에
“생각 없이 하는 말은 칼로 찌르는 것과 같”다고
그리스도인 형제나 자매라면 더 깊이 찔릴 수 있죠.
상처를 준 사람과 말하기가 어려울지 모르죠.
그 사람을 고의로 피하기까지 할 수 있습니다.
분을 삭이지 못한 어떤 사람들은 그만 포기하고
사람들이 우리를 실망시키거나 감정을 상하게 할 때
어떻게 마귀의 덫을 피할 수 있습니까?
우리는 분을 품지 않으려고 해야 합니다.
분을 품으면 마음이 너무 상해서 우울해질 수 있죠.
우린 사탄의 먹잇감이 되지 말아야 합니다.
인내할 힘을 어디서 얻을 수 있을까요?
여호와께선 낙심한 이들에게 깊은 관심이 있으시죠.
여호와께서는 사랑 많은 형제들과 그분의 영과 말씀을 통해
그 내용을 묵상하는 것은 도움이 됩니다.
기름부음받은 형제인 나쇼 도리는 이렇게 말했습니다.
‘내 목표는 매일 적어도 한 시간씩 성경을 읽는 것이었는데,
시력이 약해지기 전까지 거의 60년 간 그렇게 했습니다.’
극단적인 공산주의 독재 하에서 견딜 수 있었죠.
매일 성경을 꼭 한 시간씩 읽으시라는 건 아닙니다.
하지만 일 년 안에 성경을 통독해 보시기 바랍니다.
시간을 들여 천천히 읽는다면 묵상할 수 있을 것입니다.
읽고 내용을 묵상하는 데 충분할 것입니다.
소리 내어 읽어서 자기 목소리를 듣는다면,
읽는 속도를 늦추고 묵상할 수 있습니다.
우리는 또한 그분의 조직을 통해 힘을 얻습니다.
많은 사람이 인내하는 데 큰 도움을 줍니다.
회중의 전도인들도 우리에게 큰 힘을 줍니다.
하느님의 뜻은 우리가 계속 “서로 격려”하는 것이며
이 일은 그 어느 때보다 긴급히 지금 해야 할 일입니다.
주제 성구인 고린도 후서 4:16의 말씀처럼 해야겠습니다.

en.text: Some of us have been in the truth for 40 years,
50 years, 60 years, or more.
During our life, we may have been confronted
with various tests, or challenges.
Still, we did not and “we do not give up”
the truth and our precious relationship with our heavenly Father.
Also, we do not give up preaching the Word of God.
Second Corinthians 4:16
is the theme scripture I’ve selected for this talk.
Please locate that with me
—2 Corinthians 4:16.
It says: “Therefore, we do not give up,
“but even if the man we are outside is wasting away,
certainly the man we are inside is being renewed from day to day.”
As it said, “we do not give up,”
and we do not give in when it comes to temptations.
First Peter 3:6 encourages us
to “not give in to fear.”
Deuteronomy 13:6-8 tells the Israelites
that when a false prophet becomes active,
“you must not give in to him or listen to him.”
In the Sermon on the Mount, according to an alternate rendering,
Jesus told his listeners to pray to Jehovah
to “not allow us to give in to temptation.”
On one occasion, Peter encouraged others
—1 Peter 3:6: “Do not give in to fear.”
We do give ear when somebody gives us good counsel;
we give serious thought
when somebody wants to help us;
we give comfort to those in need.
In the first century, Paul gave comfort
to the congregation in Corinth.
Please find 2 Corinthians 4:1 with me,
and we can read it together.
And it says there:
“Therefore,
“since we have this ministry through the mercy that was shown us,
we do not give up.”
So who were the “we”?
The anointed.
Second Corinthians 3:3
tells the Corinthians
(they are the words of Paul)
that they are like “a letter of Christ
“written by [him and his friends] as ministers,
inscribed . . . with the spirit of [our] living God.”
The apostle, then, in verse 5, humbly acknowledges
that the fact that he and the Corinthians
‘were qualified came from God’
and, in verse 6,
that he “has . . . adequately qualified [Christians]
to be ministers of a new covenant.”
What did Paul refer to when he said in verse 1
“since we have this ministry”?
He referred to the ministry of that “new covenant”
of which he was just talking about.
Please follow the reading
of 2 Corinthians 3:5, 6,
where it says:
“Not that we of ourselves are adequately qualified
“to consider that anything comes from us,
“but our being adequately qualified comes from God,
“who has indeed adequately qualified us
“to be ministers of a new covenant,
not of a written code, but of spirit.”
At 2 Corinthians 3:18, he says
“and all of us, while we . . . reflect like mirrors
the glory of Jehovah.”
Well, who did he refer to when he wrote “all of us”?
He meant all of the anointed.
In chapter 4, verse 1, he says
“therefore, since we have this ministry
through the mercy that was shown us.”
The expression “therefore”
refers back to the reason and motivation
for the anointed not to give up.
In chapter 3, verse 18, he refers to the anointed
as being “transformed . . .
from one degree of glory to another,”
culminating in the glory they receive when entering heaven.
Since the anointed are progressing “from glory to glory,”
until going to heaven,
they have a strong motivation
not to give up but to endure,
since there is such a precious prize, or reward, ahead of them.
Understandably, Paul said in chapter 4, verse 1:
“Therefore, . . . we do not give up.”
Also in 2 Corinthians 4:16, Paul wrote:
“Therefore, we do not give up.”
In the third chapter, Paul contrasts
the old covenant that was “stripped of glory”
with the new covenant that would (like verses 10 and 11 say)
excel with greater glory
—a glory that would remain.
And 2 Corinthians 3:12 says
“since we have such a hope.”
What hope?
The heavenly hope.
Did you note the similarity with chapter 4, verse 1?
It said “since we have this ministry.”
What ministry was Paul referring to?
Was he referring to the field ministry in a general sense?
No.
He referred to the ministry of the new covenant.
In chapter 4, verse 7,
he then calls the ministry of the new covenant
a “treasure.”
“Since we have this [treasure],” he said.
It’s not just any treasure.
It was a great incentive for the anointed in the first century
not to give up in view of this treasure of the new covenant
that involves progressive glory.
Paul wrote: “Therefore, we do not give up.”
Also, the context of the next verses
shows that Paul was writing about the heavenly calling
that the new covenant made possible.
What Paul wrote is a strong incentive for the anointed today
not to give up.
What about the “great crowd” of “other sheep”?
Paul did not have the great crowd in mind
when he wrote the words of 2 Corinthians chapters 3 and 4.
In the introduction to his letter,
he referred to “all the holy ones.”
In 2 Corinthians 1:21, 22, he says:
“Who anointed us is God.
He has also put his seal on us.”
However, the great crowd is a recipient
of the radiant blessings of the ministry of the new covenant.
Some time ago, The Watchtower
made a general application in principle to the great crowd.
Just like the anointed have
the treasure of the new covenant and its ministry,
the great crowd also considers
their ministry a treasure.
The great crowd is also determined not to give up
in view of the beautiful hope
to live forever in Paradise on earth.
And all of us, no matter what hope,
have to endure.
Paul wrote at 2 Corinthians 4:8
that “we are hard-pressed”
—some more than others.
Please find Psalm 90:10.
None of us are exempt from the pressures
that can cause discouragement.
And it says there:
“The span of our life is 70 years,
“or 80 if one is especially strong.
“But they are filled with trouble and sorrow;
they quickly pass by, and away we fly.”
Because of the pressures of life and disappointments,
most of us grow weary at times.
But we must remember that God never promised
that we would have a problem-free life in this old system.
Even in the first century, God’s servants faced adversities,
including persecution and poverty.
Jehovah does allow his servants
to be tempted and tested.
For the time of the end, he also foretold
“earthquakes,” wars,
increased lawlessness, and “pestilences”
according to Luke 21:11.
In Revelation, he foretold
that a figurative horseman on the “pale horse”
would kill a large amount of people.
This has happened for decades
but started with the Spanish flu at the end of World War I,
where an estimated 500 million were affected
—one third of mankind of that time—
and about 50 million died.
Satan exploits our moments of discouragement
just as a lion takes advantage of an animal when it is most vulnerable.
But we will not give up!
We will not give up if others disappoint us.
In Bible times, even the most faithful servants of Jehovah
may have felt weighed down at times.
“I have grown weary with my sighing,”
wrote David.
“All night long I make my couch swim;
with my tears I make my own divan overflow.”
Why did David feel that way?
“Because of all those showing hostility to me,”
he explained.
The hurtful actions of others caused David such pain of heart
that his tears flowed freely.
Still, David did not draw away from Jehovah
because of what fellow humans had done to him
—and neither do we!
Similarly, the words or actions of others
may cause us much pain of heart.
“There exists the one speaking thoughtlessly
as with the stabs of a sword,” says Proverbs 12:18.
When the thoughtless one is a Christian brother or sister,
the stab wound can go deep.
The human tendency may be to take offense,
perhaps harboring resentment.
This is especially true if we feel
that we have been treated unkindly or unjustly.
We may find it hard to talk to the offender.
We might even deliberately avoid him or her.
Weighed down with resentment, some have given up
and have stopped coming to Christian meetings.
How can we avoid playing into the Devil’s hands
when others disappoint or hurt us?
We must try not to harbor resentment.
It can hurt us so much that we start suffering from depression.
Instead of giving in to depression or aggression,
take the initiative to make peace
or settle matters as quickly as possible.
Colossians 3:13 urges us:
“Continue . . . forgiving one another freely
. . . if anyone has a cause for complaint against another.”
We do not have to fall prey to Satan.
Jehovah and Jesus are on our  side.
How can we find encouragement to endure?
Jehovah deeply cares about those who may be discouraged.
Acts 17:27 shows
that “he is not far off from each one of us.”
Jehovah comforts and strengthens us
through loving brothers and through his spirit and his Word.
Reading the Bible daily
and meditating upon it helps.
The publications have encouraged us
to read the Bible through once a year.
Why not make it your resolve to try such a program?
Nasho Dori, an anointed brother from Albania
who persevered under ban, said:
‘My goal was to read the Bible
‘for at least one hour each day,
‘which I did for some 60 years
before my eyesight failed.’
Was he bragging when saying this?
No.
It helped him not to give up
under the extreme Communist dictatorship.
We do not necessarily expect you
to read the Bible for one hour each day,
but we encourage you to read it through in one year
and to read it slowly enough that you can meditate on it.
About 20 minutes a day provides ample opportunity
to read and meditate on what you read.
If you read so you hear your own voice,
it will help you to read slower and to meditate.
We also find encouragement through his organization
—things we read in the literature or magazines.
And we greatly benefit from the congregation meetings.
We also benefit from sweet association with our brothers
—be it live or via television.
So do not give up!
Elders, when they shepherd,
are also a big help for many to persevere.
Publishers in our congregation do a lot to strengthen us.
According to Hebrews 10:25, it is God’s will
that we keep “encouraging one another,”
and doing so is more urgent now than ever before.
Let us always keep in mind the inspired words
of 2 Thessalonians 3:13:
“For your part, brothers,
do not give up in doing good.”
Galatians 6:9 similarly says:
“Let us not give up in doing what is fine,
for in due time we will reap.”
What do we conclude from this?
It is in the words of our theme text,
2 Corinthians 4:16:
“We do not give up”!

cn.text: 我们一些人在真理中已经40年
50年、60年或是更久
在一生的岁月中
我们可能碰到了很多的挑战和困难
尽管如此
我们没有放弃，也不会放弃真理
以及我们和天父的宝贵关系
我们也不会放弃传讲上帝的话语
哥林多后书4:16是这个演讲的主题经文
现在请大家打开这节经文
哥林多后书4:16
经文说
“所以，我们不会放弃
我们外在的人虽然渐渐衰败
内在的人却天天更新。”
就像经文说的，我们不会放弃
面对引诱的时候
我们也不会放弃崇拜上帝
彼得前书3:6鼓励我们
不要“因恐惧而放弃”
申命记13:6-8告诉以色列人
如果有假先知要他们崇拜别的神
“千万不要依从他，也不可听他的话”
在登山宝训中，耶稣对群众说话
教导他的门徒怎样向上帝祷告的时候
也说求耶和华“不要让我们陷入引诱”
的确，有些事是我们不要做的
但有一些事，是我们应该要做的
我们要仔细聆听别人给我们的劝告
我们也要认真想想
别人为了帮助我们而说的话
我们要安慰其他人
在一世纪
保罗就安慰在哥林多会众的弟兄姐妹
请跟我一起翻开哥林多后书4:1
我们一起读读这段经文
经文说
“我们既然得到上帝的怜悯
领受了这个职务，就不会放弃。”
这里说的“我们”是谁呢？
有希望去天上的基督徒
在哥林多后书3:3
保罗告诉哥林多会众的人
他们是“基督的信”
由保罗和其他上帝的仆人写成
是用“真神的神圣力量写的”
保罗接着在第5节谦卑地承认
他和哥林多会众的人
能胜任工作，全靠上帝
接着，保罗说
上帝“使我们胜任，能够为新约做仆人”
4:1说我们“领受了这个职务”
那么，职务指的究竟是什么呢？
这个职务，指的就是
我们刚刚提到的“为新约做仆人”
我们再回到哥林多后书3:5,6
经文说
“这不是说我们靠自己就能胜任什么工作
其实我们胜任，全靠上帝
他使我们胜任，能够为新约做仆人
不是为法典做仆人
而是为神圣力量做仆人”
在哥林多后书3:18，保罗说
我们“能像镜子一样反映出耶和华的荣耀”
那么
他这里提到的“我们”指的是谁呢？
所有有希望到天上去的基督徒
在3章第18节
经文提到他们为什么不会放弃的理由
经文说，他们会反映耶和华的荣耀
而且这样的荣耀会越来越大
当他们到天上去的时候
就能完全反映上帝的荣耀
这就是为什么在接着的4章第1节
经文提到，既然他们得到了“上帝的怜悯
领受了这个职务，就不会放弃”
既然他们能越来越反映上帝的荣耀
直到进入天上
那么，他们就有强烈的动机
不会放弃，而会保持忍耐
摆在他们前面的，是多么宝贵的奖赏
怪不得，使徒保罗在4:1说
我们不会放弃
在哥林多后书4:16，保罗也说
“所以，我们不会放弃。”
保罗做了对比
他说在旧约条文里
有荣耀的就“光彩尽失”
新约则有更大的荣耀
这是一种可以长存的荣耀
接着，哥林多后书3:12提到
“我们既然有这样的希望”，什么希望呢？
到天上去的希望
你有注意到这和4:1的相似之处吗？
1节说，我们既然领受了这个职务
保罗说的职务是什么呢？
他说的是我们通常理解的传道工作吗？
不是
这里，保罗指的是新约的职务
之后，他在4:7中
将新约的职务称为“珍宝”
经文说我们“有这个珍宝”
但这不是一般的珍宝
对于一世纪有希望到天上去的基督徒来说
新约的职务像“珍宝”一样
大大鼓励了他们不要放弃
在16节，保罗说
“所以，我们不会放弃。”
保罗在之后的经文中写到了来自天上的呼召
而正是新约，让这样的希望成为可能
保罗的话也大大鼓励了
今天有希望到天上的基督徒不要放弃！
那“另外的绵羊”中的“大群人”呢？
保罗在写哥林多后书第3章和第4章的时候
想到的并不是大群人
在信的开头，他写到
信是写给“所有圣民”的
在哥林多后书1:21,22，保罗说
“任命我们的正是上帝
他在我们身上盖了他的印”
然而，大群人也因为新约的职务
而得到美好的福分
不久前，《守望台》的文章解释了
原则上这些经文也适用于大群人
就像有希望到天上去的基督徒
将新约的职务视为珍宝
大群人也一样，将传道工作视为珍宝
能在地上乐园里永远生活的美好希望
也让大群人下定决心，决不放弃
我们所有人，无论有什么希望
都必须忍耐到底
保罗在哥林多后书4:8写道
“我们四面受压”
有些人承受更多
让我们一起来看看诗篇90:10
我们每个人都会碰到困难
也都会因此变得失望沮丧
像经文说的一样
“我们一生的岁月不过七十年
特别强壮的可能活到八十岁
劳碌终生，不过是烦恼痛苦
一生匆匆，我们就如飞而逝。”
因为生活的压力和不如意
我们大多数人都常常感到身心疲惫
不过，上帝其实没有保证
现在的生活就会一帆风顺
在一世纪，上帝的忠仆就面对不少逆境
包括迫害和贫穷
耶和华容许他们面对引诱和挑战
耶和华也预告，在末后的日子会有“地震”
战争、不法的事增多
还有像路加福音21:11说的“瘟疫”
在启示录，耶和华也预告会有一匹
象征性的“苍白的马”，杀死很多人
这个预言在超过100年前
已经开始影响全人类
从第一次世界大战结束时
西班牙流行性感冒开始
那时，全世界1/3的人口
大约5亿人都受到感染
其中有5000万人死去
撒但总是在我们最灰心的时候攻击我们
就像狮子总是在动物最软弱的时候攻击它们
但是，我们不会放弃
就算别人令我们失望，也不会放弃
在圣经的时代
就算是耶和华最忠心的仆人
有的时候也会觉得灰心沮丧
大卫说
“我因叹息而疲惫，彻夜哭泣
泪流成河，床榻湿透。”
大卫为什么会有这种感觉？
他说，他的眼睛因所有侵扰他的人而模糊
有些人的行为伤害了大卫
所以他非常伤心，以至于“泪流成河”
虽然这样
他没有因为别人的行为而离弃耶和华
我们也不该离弃耶和华
类似地，别人说的话或做的事
也可能会伤害我们
“说话不慎的如刀刺人”
如果说话不小心的是我们的弟兄或姐妹
那可能就更痛了
不完美的人，可能很容易因为别人的冒犯
而感到不满或生气
特别是觉得受到不公正的对待时
我们可能很难跟冒犯我们的人说话
甚至可能会刻意避开他
这种怨恨的感觉可能会压垮我们
让有些人想要放弃，不再参加基督徒聚会
当别人冒犯我们的时候
我们怎样才不会掉进撒但的陷阱里呢？
我们不要一直想着那些让我们伤心的事
这些事可能会让我们变得抑郁沮丧
与其一直想着这些让人沮丧的事
不如主动地尽快解决问题
促进彼此之间的和睦
在歌罗西书3:13里
经文鼓励我们就算“有理由对人不满”
还是要“继续……彼此甘心宽恕”
我们千万不要掉进撒但的陷阱里
耶和华和耶稣跟我们在一起
我们可以怎样得到鼓励，继续保持忍耐呢？
耶和华非常关心那些灰心的人
使徒行传17:27说
“他离我们各人都不远。”
耶和华会用他的神圣力量
他的话语圣经，还有弟兄姐妹来安慰我们
天天阅读和沉思圣经也会给我们很大的帮助
我们的出版物鼓励我们
每年把圣经读过一次
何不下定决心，试着这样做呢？
阿尔巴尼亚的内斯奥·多里
是个有希望去天上的基督徒
他曾受到严峻地迫害
他说
“我立下目标，每天至少阅读圣经1小时
60年来，我一直保持这个习惯
直到我的视力不行为止。”
他是在吹嘘自己吗？
不是
阅读圣经，帮助他在独裁政府的压迫下
继续保持忠贞
我们不是要求你们每天都要读圣经1个小时
但是，我们鼓励你试着在1年内
把圣经从头到尾读一遍，而且要慢慢地读
让你可以好好沉思
每天只要20分钟
就有足够的时间阅读和沉思你所读的内容
把看到的经文读出来
也可以帮助你仔细阅读，好好地沉思
我们也从上帝的组织得到很大的鼓励
包括我们从书籍、杂志读到的资料
还有我们从聚会学到的一切
我们也很喜欢跟我们的弟兄姐妹来往
彼此鼓励
不管是面对面的，或者是通过连线的方式
所以我们不会放弃
长老们的牧养探访
也可以帮助我们继续保持坚忍
会众的弟兄姐妹也可以鼓励我们
希伯来书10:25告诉我们
耶和华希望我们继续“彼此鼓励”
我们现在比以往任何时候更需要这样做
让我们谨记上帝启示的话语
在帖撒罗尼迦后书3:13
“弟兄们，你们不要放弃行善。”
加拉太书6:9也鼓励我们
“不要放弃做美好的事……
时候到了就有收成。”
我们学到什么呢？
像主题经文哥林多后书4:16说的
“我们不会放弃”

titles.en: Gerrit Lösch: “We Do Not Give Up”
titles.cn: 格里特·勒施：我们不会放弃

ko.text: 한 충실한 그리스도인 자매에 관해 말합니다.
그는 ‘바울을 비롯해 많은 사람을 보호해’ 주었습니다.
독특한 상황에 있는 세 분의 충실한 자매의 경험을 들어 볼 것입니다.
세 분 다 미국 지부 위원회에서 봉사하는 형제들의 아내입니다.
우선 어떻게 진리를 받으셨는지 말씀해 주실까요?
회중의 연로한 분들의 따뜻한 사랑을 통해
저는 십 대 후반에 힘든 일을 겪었는데,
왜 죽게 놔두셨는지 이해가 안 됐죠.
우주 주권 쟁점에 대해 더 깊이 조사해 보라고 격려해 주셨습니다.
또, 우선순위를 다시 검토해 보게 되었는데,
그리고 워릭과 턱시도 건축 공사에도 참여했습니다.
지부 위원의 아내로서 바쁜 생활을 하고 계실 텐데요,
우리가 영적 전쟁을 하고 있다는 걸 되새깁니다.
그러니까 모든 게 바라는 대로 될 순 없죠.
지금은 순결한 숭배를 가장 앞자리에 두어야 합니다.
남편과 행복하고 친밀하게 지내는 것도 중요하지만,
가장 큰 기쁨은 여호와 안에서 찾아야 합니다.
다른 분들이 저를 위해 해 준 희생을 생각하는 겁니다.
여호와께선 저를 위해 예수와 보낼 33년을 희생하셨죠.
그리고 제가 독신으로 파이오니아를 할 때,
몇몇 자매들이 저를 식사에 자주 초대해 주고
추운 겨울 밤에 제 차를 고쳐 주기 위해
그 훌륭한 본들을 따르는 것이라고 생각합니다.
더 큰 내적인 평화를 누리고 있습니다.
지부 위원 형제들이 얼마나 여호와의 영에 의존하는지,
얼마나 많은 시간을 기도하고 또 기도하는지,
조직의 결정을 지원하고, 잘 듣고, 순종하는 것이 훨씬 쉬워졌어요.
좋은 경험을 하나 말씀해 주실 수 있을까요?
저희 부부는 수십 년간의 내전으로 황폐된
한 나라의 작은 지부를 방문한 적이 있는데요,
이 형제도 아직 못 먹은 상태였는데,
굶어야 할 수도 있게 된 거죠.
하지만 이 형제가 너무나 밝은 표정으로
자신의 임명에 대해 이야기하는 걸 보면서,
물질적인 것에 좌우되지 않는다는 걸 알 수 있었어요.
더 중요한 것에 초점을 맞추게 해 주었기 때문입니다.
「낙원을 잃은 때부터 낙원을 찾을 때까지」 책으로 연구를 했습니다.
십 대 시절에, 임시 파이오니아를 했는데,
한 파이오니아 부부가 저희를 많이 도와주었어요.
하지만 졸업하면서 전 시간 직장을 다니게 됐어요.
그런데 지역 대회에서 한 연사가 이렇게 말했어요.
‘파이오니아가 아니라면, 여호와께 그 이유를 설명해 보세요.’
이젠 자매들도 출퇴근을 할 수 있다는 거였어요.
잠깐 동안 브루클린 창고에서 일한 적도 있죠.
지금은 월킬에 있는 봉사부에서 일하고 있습니다.
형제 자매들에게 알리는 게 도움이 됐어요.
그럼 형제 자매들과 가까운 느낌이 들어요.
형제 자매들이 계속 방문할 수 있죠.
가진 것을 나눠 주도록 가르쳐 주셨어요.
또 여호와와 그분의 사랑에 대해 배운 것이
또 저와는 다른 개성이나 성격을 가진
다양한 특성과 성품에 대해 배울 기회로 여기려고 노력합니다.
좋은 경험을 하나 말씀해 주실 수 있을까요?
“여호와의 축복은 사람을 부유하게 해 준다”고 말하죠.
사실, 저는 영적인 일을 하면서 얻은
그곳의 형제 자매들과 함께 일한 것은
여호와께 믿음과 충성을 나타내는 것을 보면서
이제 서니 치키 자매와 얘기를 나눠 보죠.
한동안 조경부 일을 같이 하기도 했지만,
저는 카드와 편지를 써서 보내는 걸 좋아해요.
첫 번째는 자신의 축복을 헤아려 보는 건데,
가장 의미 있는 일을 수행하는 조직에 속해 있죠.
두 번째는 더 큰 그림을 보는 거예요.
세 번째는 충분한 휴식을 취하는 건데,
말씀해 주실 경험이 하나 있다고 들었는데요.
남편은 몇 년 후에 배교자가 되었고,
하지만 여러 면으로 여호와의 도움을 느꼈어요.
후에 톰과 결혼하고 베델 봉사를 시작하면서
뵈베를 언급한 로마서 16:2을 근거로 한 노래입니다.
오늘 나오신 세 분의 자매도 마찬가지죠.
확신 잃지 않아 상을 곧 받으리.”

en.text: The accounts of faithful women are found throughout the Bible.
One faithful Christian sister is mentioned by the apostle Paul
at Romans 16:1, 2.
There he mentions Phoebe,
who ‘proved herself to be a defender of many, including Paul.’
Today, we’re blessed to be able to get to know
faithful Christian sisters who share something unique.
All of them are wives of brothers
who serve as members of the United States Branch Committee.
Sister Snyder, we’d like to get to know more about you.
Can you, please, first tell us how you got the truth?
I was introduced to the truth by my parents.
And Jehovah used the example of my sister
and the nurturing love of older ones
in the congregations to draw me to him.
Then how did you start in the full-time ministry
and then into Bethel service?
Well, it was a bit of a test.
When I was in my late teens, a friend of mine died,
and I couldn’t understand why Jehovah would allow this
to happen to such a kind person.
So an elderly pioneer sister encouraged me
to do deeper research on the issue of universal sovereignty.
And this not only comforted me,
but it caused me to reevaluate my priorities
and to see if I
truly believed Jehovah would take care of me
if I really put him first.
So I started pioneering and put college on hold.
And it wasn’t long before I was broke
and the rent was coming due.
And so the next meeting,
I quietly put my last $50 in the contribution box
and thought: ‘That’s it, done, doesn’t work.
I’m going back to school.’
But that evening,
I learned that Matthew 6:33 is undeniably true.
Jehovah surprised me
and cared for all my needs from the most unlikely sources,
and he hasn’t stopped caring for me since.
And then you joined Troy in Bethel service later on, right?
Now, what assignments have you enjoyed at Bethel?
I’ve enjoyed housekeeping.
I’ve really enjoyed a lot of assignments within Transportation Department,
and I was one of the thousands who worked
on the Warwick and Tuxedo construction projects.
Now, as the wife of a Branch Committee member,
you have a demanding schedule.
Can you explain one challenge?
Well, like most wives of good shepherds,
I would love to have more time with my husband.
That’s understandable.
So, what practical things have you done to deal with that challenge?
Well, prayer, study, and meditation
have reminded me that we’re at spiritual war.
And we’re at war, so our priorities have to change.
So I can’t long for ideal circumstances,
although they’re coming quickly.
Right now, it’s about advancing pure worship.
And while it’s important to maintain
a healthy and close relationship with Troy,
my primary joy should be in Jehovah.
And, then, second is remembering the sacrifices that were made for me.
Of course, Jehovah gave up 33 years with his best friend for me.
And also there were sisters when I was single and pioneering
who would invite me over for lots of meals
and to go out in service.
They would even send their husband
out on freezing cold, dark nights to fix my car,
which broke down often.
So I’m grateful,
and the main way I can show this appreciation
is to imitate their examples.
Now, with challenges come blessings.
What’s one blessing you enjoy as the wife of a Branch Committee member?
Increased peace
that comes from having complete confidence
in how Jehovah directs and blesses the decisions
his organization makes through the Governing Body.
If I were not married to a Branch Committee member,
I may never have known
just how much the brothers rely on Jehovah’s spirit
and how much time they spend
—long periods of time— in prayer
and how much they deeply, deeply love the friends.
So I’m embarrassed
about how much worrying I’ve done in the past about these things.
But now it’s a lot easier to just be supportive
and listen, obey, and be blessed.
Very nice.
Now, as you look back
on your rich spiritual life in Jehovah’s service,
is there an experience you can share with us?
We were visiting a small branch in a developing country
that had been ravaged by decades of civil war.
I’d never seen poverty like that before.
And one evening, I went into the dining room
to gather dinner for us.
But before getting the dinner,
I stopped and talked to a lovely young brother.
At one point, I turned around and noticed that all the food had been taken.
And I said, “There’s no more food.”
Now, this young brother hadn’t eaten either.
But he just shrugged and said, “It’s just hunger,”
and he continued zealously talking about his assignment.
Now, this brother was a commuter and very thin,
and so it was likely that he might not eat that night
or maybe even the next morning.
But the way his face glowed when he talked about his assignment,
it was clear that his joy was not based on anything physical
or the lack of anything physical.
So I really treasure this lesson
because it’s made me want to appreciate more what I do have currently
and to imitate his example in focusing on what’s truly important.
And I think you told me that he did get some food that night,
so we’re happy about that.
Thanks for letting us get to know you and for sharing that experience.
Now we’d like to get to know Sister Shirrell Georges.
Sister Georges, can you tell us how you got the truth?
When I was 11, my mother started to study.
Another sister studied with my two sisters and me
out of the book From Paradise Lost to Paradise Regained.
Two years later, on November 13, 1971,
my mother, my oldest sister, and I were baptized.
How did you start in the full-time ministry?
As teenagers, a pioneer couple assisted us
when we temporary, or vacation, pioneered, as it was called then.
That led me to want to regular pioneer after high school.
However, after graduating, I started working full-time.
It was at a district convention where the point was made,
‘If you’re not pioneering, tell Jehovah why.’
Well, I really didn’t have a good reason.
So I started making plans to work part-time.
It was in September of 1980
when I realized my goal of regular pioneering.
And how did that lead to Bethel service?
While pioneering,
I had the opportunity to assist
with the Brooklyn Assembly Hall renovation project on Thursdays.
It was one Thursday that I learned
of an announcement made at Bethel:
Sisters could now commute.
So after a while, I turned in my application
and started commuting in November of 1987.
But before commuting, I had met Luther.
We started to court, and then later,
we were married and accepted as a couple to Bethel.
And what assignments have you enjoyed at Bethel?
While commuting, I worked in the Dry Cleaning Department
and continued there after marriage.
For a short time, I worked with the Brooklyn Warehouse Department.
Then Luther and I received a surprise assignment.
We were asked to assist at the Jamaica branch,
starting in March of 1995.
There I worked in alterations,
laundry, kitchen, housekeeping,
shipping, and the Bethel Office.
Then in 2014, the Jamaica branch merged with the United States branch.
We were invited to serve back in the United States
—first at Patterson, where I worked in Audio/Video Services,
and now at Wallkill, in the Service Department.
Now, you too have a demanding schedule.
Can you explain one challenge?
Well, many of the assignments that Luther has involve traveling.
So that means that we are away from our congregation,
sometimes for weeks.
It also means that we’re not able to get back
to our return visits and Bible studies on a weekly basis.
So, what practical things have you done to deal with that challenge?
We’ve found it helpful to let the friends know
whenever we will be away.
Many times we would receive a text from them:
“Just saying hi. Checking on you.
Hope you’re doing well.”
This really has helped us to stay connected.
Something else we did was to invite publishers
to go with us on our return visits and Bible studies.
This way, whenever we were away, they could keep the interest going.
That’s a good idea.
What good habits did you form early in life
that help you now as you support your husband?
Growing up, my mother taught us to be content
and to share whatever we had.
One Watchtower  article stated:
“True contentment comes from loving and being loved.”
We grew up in a loving family,
and then learning about Jehovah and his love as I grew older
helped me to find contentment in Jehovah’s service.
So whatever assignment I have, I try to be content
and view any differences as an opportunity for me to learn
about the various aspects, unique personalities,
and qualities of my brothers and sisters.
Now, as you look back on your rich spiritual life,
is there a memory you can share with us?
Proverbs 10:22 says:
“The blessing of Jehovah —that is what makes [one] rich.”
I feel as if I have been enriched
in so many ways with so many memories.
One memory is being able to assist
in the former Jamaica branch for over 19 years.
Working together with the brothers
was such a unique privilege
and was really encouraging.
To see the brothers exhibit their faith and loyalty to Jehovah
despite various challenging circumstances
was a true encouragement for us.
We made many friends in that assignment,
and we continue to keep in touch to this day.
That is a nice memory.
Thanks for sharing that with us.
Finally, we’d like to talk to Sister Sunny Cheiky.
Sister Cheiky, can you tell us how you got the truth
and then entered the full-time ministry?
My mother raised me and my two brothers to serve Jehovah.
It was difficult for her because my father left the truth
and our family when we were very young.
But she set a very good example for us.
And then because of the encouragement of young pioneers in our congregation,
I began regular pioneering in the Pasadena, California, Congregation
after I graduated from high school in 1962.
And how did that lead to Bethel service?
I served in a few other areas where the need was great
in New Mexico, northern California,
a special pioneer assignment in Iowa,
and then a small congregation in Mississippi.
Tom was a Brooklyn Bethelite,
and he came down to Mississippi to dedicate a Kingdom Hall.
In May 1981, we met;
seven months later, we were married,
and we were accepted to serve as a couple at Bethel.
Nice.
What assignments have you enjoyed at Bethel?
I was a housekeeper for my first three years,
and now I’ve been in laundry for 35 years.
I did have a part-time assignment in grounds maintenance for a while,
but now I joyfully serve full-time in the Wallkill laundry.
Now, you too have a demanding schedule.
Can you explain one challenge?
Meeting so many wonderful friends in our assignments,
I like to keep in touch with them.
But time is so limited,
so I feel that that can be overwhelming at times.
So, what practical thing have you done to deal with that challenge?
Well, I love to write cards and send letters,
so that’s how I deal with this.
To be able to keep in touch with my friends —that really helps a lot.
So, what has helped you to be balanced despite your busy schedule?
I loved the March 2016 broadcast that stressed three things.
The first is count your blessings.
We are a part of an amazing organization
that is carrying on the most meaningful work of preaching and teaching.
The second is look at the big picture.
When I feel stressed out,
I try to put things in the right perspective
—Jehovah’s sovereignty first, foremost, and not focusing on myself—
and that helps me to keep calm.
And third is get enough rest.
Without enough rest, I can’t think straight
and even ordinary activities in my routine
seem overwhelming, or too much.
That’s very practical.
Now, is there a particular experience you’d like to share with us?
When I was special pioneering in Iowa,
I married a brother who was a pioneer
and then became an elder,
and so I continued in the congregation as a regular pioneer.
After several years, he became an apostate,
and he tried to encourage me to go with him; but I refused.
The elders made great efforts to help him to recover,
but he was persistent in carrying out his course.
So in time, he separated from me and ended the marriage.
But I felt Jehovah’s support in so many ways.
One in particular was a couple who would call me often,
and they would have me to their home,
and they never wanted me to feel alone.
Then another blessing came later when I moved to Mississippi,
and I became partners with a sister who was 20 years older than me.
She had been in the seventh class of Gilead,
and she had been special pioneering for 30 years.
So you can imagine she was a tremendous help to me.
More blessings came later
when I married Tom and began serving at Bethel.
So feeling Jehovah’s support in a difficult time
and experiencing his blessings is unforgettable.
Sister Cheiky, thank you so much for sharing that experience with us.
In the introduction, we referenced the example of Phoebe,
that faithful Christian sister.
Interestingly, our Kingdom song number 137,
entitled “Faithful Women, Christian Sisters,”
is based on the description of Phoebe at Romans 16:2.
The lyrics of that song remind us that our Christian sisters
show a faithful spirit we all can imitate,
and that’s true of the sisters we interviewed today.
The song concludes with the words:
“Christian sisters, may Jehovah keep you  firm in your conviction,
your prize is drawing near.”
How we appreciate the example set by all of our faithful Christian sisters!

cn.text: 圣经中记载了很多忠心女子的好榜样
其中一个是保罗在罗马书16:1,2提到的
菲比姐妹
经文说，她“维护过许多人”
包括保罗
今天我们很高兴可以认识几位忠贞的姐妹
她们都有一个共同点
她们的丈夫都是美国分部委员会的成员
斯奈德姐妹，我们想听听你的经历
请问你是怎么认识真理的？
是我的父母教导我真理的
我的姐姐
还有会众中年长的弟兄姐妹对我的爱
帮助我亲近耶和华
你是怎么开始全时服务和伯特利的工作的？

我不能理解
耶和华为什么让这么好的一个人死去？
一位年长的姐妹鼓励我
在宇宙至高统治权这个问题上作深入的研究
这样做不仅安慰了我，也让我重新想想
什么在我生活中是最重要的
我真的相信如果我把上帝放在第一位
他会一直照顾我吗？
后来我没有去大学，开始做正规先驱
但没过多久钱就用完了，没办法付房租
不过，在参加聚会的时候
我把最后剩下的50块钱全部都捐出去了
然后想
“就这样吧，大不了不做先驱了
回去上大学。”
但是那个晚上
我亲身体会到马太福音6:33说得千真万确
耶和华给了我一个惊喜
用我完全没想到的方法，满足了我所有的需要
从那时起，他一直在照顾我
后来你和丈夫就加入了伯特利的服务，对吗？
在伯特利，你做过哪些工作呢？
我喜欢家务部的工作
也真的非常喜欢在运输部的工作
也很荣幸参与了沃威克
和塔克西多的建筑工程
身为分部委员会成员的妻子，你一定很忙
可以告诉我们其中一个挑战吗？
嗯，和大多长老的妻子一样
希望丈夫多陪陪我
嗯，我可以理解
那你要做哪些具体的事来应对这个挑战呢？
祷告、研读和沉思都时刻提醒我
我们正在和撒但打一场战争
我们在打仗的时候，什么是最重要的呢？
现在我们不可能期待有完美的生活
对我们最重要的是拥护正确的崇拜
尽管和丈夫有亲密的关系非常重要
但耶和华才是我真正喜乐的来源
还有就是要记住，其他人为我作出的牺牲
耶和华跟他最好的朋友分开33年，为了我
我结婚之前做先驱的那段时间
很多姐妹常常约我去她们家
跟她们一起吃饭，一起传道
姐妹们常常让她们的丈夫冒着严寒
在晚上出去帮我修车
那时我的车常常坏掉
我非常感激他们
嗯，我表达感谢的一个主要方式就是
向他们学习
但一定也有福分
现在你是分部委员会成员的妻子
你喜欢哪个福分？
我的内心越来越安宁了
因为我现在完全相信
耶和华正通过中央长老团
指引和赐福给他的组织
如果没有嫁给分部委员会成员
我可能永远都不会知道
他们是那么地依赖神圣力量
不会知道他们花了那么多时间祷告
更不会知道他们是那么
那么地深爱弟兄姐妹
现在想来有点惭愧
以前我总是担心他们的决定
现在听从组织的指引就容易多了
我也从中得到很多福分
很好，你为耶和华服务这么多年
有什么特别的经历可以跟我们分享吗？
我们以前探访过一个发展中国家的小分部
这个国家曾经经历过几十年的内战
我从来没见过那么穷的国家
有一天晚上，我到餐厅去拿晚餐
就在快拿到食物之前
我看到一个年轻的弟兄
就停下来跟他聊了起来
突然我转身过去发现，食物都被拿光了
我就说:“没有食物了！”
这位年轻的弟兄其实也还没有吃饭
但他耸了耸肩说
“那就饿一顿吧。”
然后他就继续热情地跟我谈他的委派
他是个通勤人员，非常瘦
很可能他那天晚上没饭吃
第二天早上也没有饭吃
但他谈到委派时，脸在发光
他看起来非常快乐
很明显
他没有因为没有食物吃而愁眉苦脸
他的快乐不在于物质财富
我从他身上学到很多
因为，是他让我更珍惜我目前所拥有的东西
我要向他学习，把目光集中于真正重要的事
但我们很高兴听说
他那天晚上还是拿到了食物
非常感谢你和我们分享你的经历
现在我们来认识一下雪丽·乔治姐妹
乔治姐妹，你是怎样认识真理的？
我11岁时，我妈妈开始学习圣经
还有一位姐妹用
《从乐园的失落到乐园的复得》这本书
跟我的两个姐姐和我讨论圣经
两年后，在1971年11月13号
我妈妈和两个姐姐还有我都受浸了
你是怎么开始全时服务的？
我和姐姐十几岁的时候就会利用假期做先驱
那时一对夫妻帮助我们
他们鼓励我们，高中毕业后就做正规先驱
可是，我毕业之后就开始做全职的工作
有一次，在区域大会上我听到了一个要点
“如果你现在没有做先驱
就告诉耶和华为什么？”
我想不出什么好理由
所以我就开始计划做兼职工作
在1980年9月，我就开始做正规先驱了
你是怎么开始伯特利服务的？
我做先驱时，有一段时间每周四
都有机会协助布鲁克林大会堂的整修工程
有一次我在伯特利听到一个宣布
姐妹们现在可以做通勤服务了
过了几天我就递交了申请表
在1987年11月开始做通勤人员
不过在那之前，我就跟路德弟兄谈恋爱了
我们结婚以后就一起在伯特利服务
你在伯特利做过哪些工作？
我做通勤服务时在干洗部工作
结婚后也继续在那里工作
后来我在仓储部短暂工作过一段时间
接着我们就收到一个意想不到的委派
组织要我们从1995年3月开始
在牙买加分部服务
我在那里的很多部门工作过
裁缝部、洗衣部、厨房部、家务部
装运部以及伯特利办公室
在2014年牙买加分部并入了美国分部
我们又回到美国分部服务
首先在帕特森的影音服务部服务
现在在华基尔的传道部服务
那你现在一定很忙
你能讲讲其中一个挑战吗？
路德常常要出差
所以我们不得不常常跟会众分开
有时候长达几个星期
这样我们就不能回去拜访
那些对圣经感兴趣的人
不能每周跟圣经学生学习
那你有什么方法应对这个挑战呢？
我们发现出差的时候跟朋友们讲一声非常好
有时我们会收到他们的短信
“你们好，只是问候一下
希望你们旅途愉快”
这让我们跟弟兄姐妹很亲近
我们出去续访或是跟学生讨论圣经的时候
都会邀请别的传道员一起
这样我们出差的时候
他们就可以继续帮助学生
好主意
你以前养成了哪些好习惯
有助于你现在支持丈夫的工作呢？
小时候，我妈妈教我们学会知足
也学会跟人分享
一篇《守望台》文章提到
我们爱别人也受别人所爱
内心就会真正感到满足
我在一个充满爱心的家庭长大
大一点时，开始了解耶和华和他的爱心
这帮助我在服务的时候能够保持知足
我也学到无论接获什么委派都能感到快乐
把它们看作是学习的好机会
我可以学习不同的知识
了解不同弟兄姐妹的个性和好品格
回顾以往
你有没有什么特别美好的经历想跟我们分享？
“耶和华所赐的福使人富足”
我觉得这么多年来
耶和华赐给我很多美好的福分
其中的一个福分就是
我能够在以前的牙买加分部服务超过19年
和那里的弟兄姐妹一起工作
是一个很难得的机会
我们受到很大的鼓励
因为他们虽然面对很多考验和难题
但依然显出信心忠于耶和华
这真的很鼓励我们
我们交到很多好朋友，到现在还经常联系
真是美好的经历，谢谢你的分享
最后我们认识一下珊妮·谢奇姐妹
谢奇姐妹，你可以说说你是怎么认识真理
怎么开始全时服务的吗？
妈妈教导我和两个哥哥从小崇拜耶和华
这对她来说其实很不容易
因为，我们还小的时候
爸爸就离开了真理，抛弃了我们
但妈妈做得真的很好
当时会众里有一些年轻的先驱
他们给我很大的鼓励
我在1962年高中毕业以后
就开始在加州的帕萨迪纳会众做先驱了
你是怎么去伯特利服务的？
我曾在新墨西哥州和加州北部
一些需要大的地区服务
后来被委派到爱荷华州做特别先驱
后来又到了密西西比州一个小会众服务
汤姆是布鲁克林的伯特利成员
他来密西西比州参加一个聚会所的呈献礼
我们是在1981年5月认识的
7个月以后我们结婚了
然后组织就邀请我们一起在伯特利服务
嗯，那你在伯特利做过哪些工作？
前3年，我在家务部工作
然后就在洗衣部工作了35年直到现在
中间有一段时间我在庭园保养部做兼职工作
现在我在华基尔洗衣部快乐地服务
你肯定非常忙
你可以说说其中一个挑战吗？
我认识了很多非常好的弟兄姐妹
很想跟他们保持联系，但时间非常有限
有时候很多事情想做但却做不到
那你是怎么应付这个挑战的？
我喜欢给朋友写信、写卡片
通过这个方法我可以跟朋友保持联系
这真的给我很大的帮助
你这么忙，什么帮助你保持平衡呢？
我很喜欢2016年3月份的每月节目
强调的三件事
第一，数算你的福分
我们的组织正做着最有意义的传道教人的工作
而我们是其中的一分子
第二，着眼于大局
我感到压力很大的时候
就会试着换个角度看问题
我会把焦点放在耶和华的至高统治权上
而不是自己身上
这真的帮助我保持冷静
第三，好好休息
如果休息得不够，我就不能好好思考
就连一些普通的事情
我做起来都觉得压力很大
这个方法不错
你想分享什么比较特别的经历呢？
我在爱荷华州做特别先驱的时候
跟一个做正规先驱的弟兄结了婚
后来他成为长老
我也继续在那群会众做正规先驱
没过几年，他成了一个叛道者
也想让我跟他一起离开组织，但我拒绝了
长老们付出很大努力，想要帮助他恢复过来
但他坚持自己的看法，拒绝作出改变
很快我们就分开了，我们的婚姻也结束了
我觉得耶和华给了我很多很多的支持
当时有一对夫妻，他们常常来看我
他们也会邀请我去他们家
他们不想让我觉得孤单
我搬到密西西比州的时候
耶和华给了我另外一个福分
我跟一个比我大20岁的先驱姐妹一起住
她参加过第七届基列学校
已经做特别先驱30年了
所以你能想象她对我的帮助有多大！
我跟汤姆结婚，开始在伯特利服务以后
就得到了更多的福分
耶和华在困难的时候支持我
赐给我很多福分，我永远也忘不了
谢奇姐妹，谢谢你跟我们分享宝贵的经历
在采访开头，我们提到了菲比
就是那个忠心的基督徒姐妹
我们的王国诗歌第137首
《忠心的女子，基督徒姐妹》
参考经文就是提到菲比的罗马书16:2
这首歌的歌词提醒我们
我们的基督徒姐妹非常忠贞，值得我们学习
这三位姐妹就是这样的榜样
诗歌第137首的结尾这样说
“你是耶和华所关爱的人
他必定帮助你，赐你未来福乐。”
我们多么珍视
这些忠心的基督徒姐妹立下的好榜样

ko.text: 연례 총회 프로그램에서 다시 뵙게 되어 기쁩니다.
이제 집필 위원회 보조자인 레너드 마이어스 형제가
한 충실한 그리스도인 자매에 관해 말합니다.
그는 ‘바울을 비롯해 많은 사람을 보호해’ 주었습니다.
독특한 상황에 있는 세 분의 충실한 자매의 경험을 들어 볼 것입니다.
세 분 다 미국 지부 위원회에서 봉사하는 형제들의 아내입니다.
우선 어떻게 진리를 받으셨는지 말씀해 주실까요?
회중의 연로한 분들의 따뜻한 사랑을 통해
저는 십 대 후반에 힘든 일을 겪었는데,
왜 죽게 놔두셨는지 이해가 안 됐죠.
우주 주권 쟁점에 대해 더 깊이 조사해 보라고 격려해 주셨습니다.
또, 우선순위를 다시 검토해 보게 되었는데,
그리고 워릭과 턱시도 건축 공사에도 참여했습니다.
지부 위원의 아내로서 바쁜 생활을 하고 계실 텐데요,
우리가 영적 전쟁을 하고 있다는 걸 되새깁니다.
그러니까 모든 게 바라는 대로 될 순 없죠.
지금은 순결한 숭배를 가장 앞자리에 두어야 합니다.
남편과 행복하고 친밀하게 지내는 것도 중요하지만,
가장 큰 기쁨은 여호와 안에서 찾아야 합니다.
다른 분들이 저를 위해 해 준 희생을 생각하는 겁니다.
여호와께선 저를 위해 예수와 보낼 33년을 희생하셨죠.
그리고 제가 독신으로 파이오니아를 할 때,
몇몇 자매들이 저를 식사에 자주 초대해 주고
추운 겨울 밤에 제 차를 고쳐 주기 위해
그 훌륭한 본들을 따르는 것이라고 생각합니다.
더 큰 내적인 평화를 누리고 있습니다.
지부 위원 형제들이 얼마나 여호와의 영에 의존하는지,
얼마나 많은 시간을 기도하고 또 기도하는지,
조직의 결정을 지원하고, 잘 듣고, 순종하는 것이 훨씬 쉬워졌어요.
좋은 경험을 하나 말씀해 주실 수 있을까요?
저희 부부는 수십 년간의 내전으로 황폐된
한 나라의 작은 지부를 방문한 적이 있는데요,
이 형제도 아직 못 먹은 상태였는데,
굶어야 할 수도 있게 된 거죠.
하지만 이 형제가 너무나 밝은 표정으로
자신의 임명에 대해 이야기하는 걸 보면서,
물질적인 것에 좌우되지 않는다는 걸 알 수 있었어요.
더 중요한 것에 초점을 맞추게 해 주었기 때문입니다.
「낙원을 잃은 때부터 낙원을 찾을 때까지」 책으로 연구를 했습니다.
십 대 시절에, 임시 파이오니아를 했는데,
한 파이오니아 부부가 저희를 많이 도와주었어요.
하지만 졸업하면서 전 시간 직장을 다니게 됐어요.
그런데 지역 대회에서 한 연사가 이렇게 말했어요.
‘파이오니아가 아니라면, 여호와께 그 이유를 설명해 보세요.’
이젠 자매들도 출퇴근을 할 수 있다는 거였어요.
잠깐 동안 브루클린 창고에서 일한 적도 있죠.
지금은 월킬에 있는 봉사부에서 일하고 있습니다.
형제 자매들에게 알리는 게 도움이 됐어요.
그럼 형제 자매들과 가까운 느낌이 들어요.
형제 자매들이 계속 방문할 수 있죠.
가진 것을 나눠 주도록 가르쳐 주셨어요.
또 여호와와 그분의 사랑에 대해 배운 것이
또 저와는 다른 개성이나 성격을 가진
다양한 특성과 성품에 대해 배울 기회로 여기려고 노력합니다.
좋은 경험을 하나 말씀해 주실 수 있을까요?
“여호와의 축복은 사람을 부유하게 해 준다”고 말하죠.
사실, 저는 영적인 일을 하면서 얻은
그곳의 형제 자매들과 함께 일한 것은
여호와께 믿음과 충성을 나타내는 것을 보면서
이제 서니 치키 자매와 얘기를 나눠 보죠.
한동안 조경부 일을 같이 하기도 했지만,
저는 카드와 편지를 써서 보내는 걸 좋아해요.
첫 번째는 자신의 축복을 헤아려 보는 건데,
가장 의미 있는 일을 수행하는 조직에 속해 있죠.
두 번째는 더 큰 그림을 보는 거예요.
세 번째는 충분한 휴식을 취하는 건데,
말씀해 주실 경험이 하나 있다고 들었는데요.
남편은 몇 년 후에 배교자가 되었고,
하지만 여러 면으로 여호와의 도움을 느꼈어요.
후에 톰과 결혼하고 베델 봉사를 시작하면서
뵈베를 언급한 로마서 16:2을 근거로 한 노래입니다.
오늘 나오신 세 분의 자매도 마찬가지죠.
확신 잃지 않아 상을 곧 받으리.”
마이어스 형제와 나와 주신 자매들께 감사합니다.
전 세계에는 왕국을 첫째로 구하는 남편들을 지원하는
이제 중앙장로회 성원 한 분의 연설을 들어 보겠습니다.
여러 가지 시련과 어려움을 겪었을지 모릅니다.
제가 이 연설을 위해 선택한 주제 성구입니다.
확실히 우리의 속사람은 날마다 새로워지고 있습니다.”
유혹을 당해도 여호와를 섬기기를 중단하지 않죠.
산상 수훈에서 예수께서는 우리가 포기하는 일이 없도록
여호와께 “유혹에 빠지지 않게” 해 달라는 기도를 해야 한다고
우리가 귀를 기울여 좋은 조언을 잘 듣고,
그 조언을 깊이 생각해 보면 포기하지 않는 데 도움이 됩니다.
그럼 함께 고린도 후서 4:1을 찾아 보실까요?
이 봉사의 직무를 가지고 있으니 포기하지 않습니다.”
자신과 고린도 회중 사람들이 ‘자격을 갖추는 일이
적합한 자격을 갖추게 해 주셨”다는 점을
“우리는 ... 이 봉사의 직무를 가지고 있”다고 한 말은
그럼 제가 고린도 후서 3:5, 6을 읽을 때
우리에게서 무엇이 나온다고 생각하는 것은 아닙니다.
그분은 참으로 우리가 새 계약의 봉사자로,
영의 봉사자로 적합한 자격을 갖추게 해 주셨습니다.”
이 봉사의 직무를 가지고 있”다고 했는데,
바로 앞 구절에서 말한 기름부음받은 자들이
하늘에 들어갈 때 받는 영광에 이르기까지
“점점 더 영광스럽게 ... 변화되어 갑니다”라고 알려 주죠.
강한 동기를 가지고 포기하지 않고 견딥니다.
그들 앞에는 아주 값진 상이 놓여 있기 때문이죠.
그런 이유로 바울은 4:1에서 이렇게 말한 겁니다.
‘영광을 빼앗긴’ 옛 계약과 새 계약을 대조하면서
그 영광이 더 크고 계속 남아 있을 것이라고 했습니다.
“우리는 그러한 희망을 가지고 있기 때문에”라고 했죠.
거기선 ‘우리는 이 봉사의 직무를 가지고 있으니’라고 했죠.
일반적인 야외 봉사를 말하고 있는 것입니까?
새 계약의 봉사의 직무를 말하는 것입니다.
바울이 새 계약으로 가능해진 하늘의 부르심에 관해
쓰고 있다는 걸 알 수 있습니다.
오늘날 기름부음받은 자들에게도 강한 동기를 주어
하느님께서는 또한 우리에게 인장을 찍으시고”라고 했죠.
새 계약의 봉사의 직무를 통해 놀라운 축복을 받습니다.
새 계약과 그 봉사의 직무라는 보물을 가지고 있는 것처럼,
큰 무리도 자신의 봉사의 직무를 보물로 여깁니다.
큰 무리도 결코 포기하지 않겠다고 결심합니다.
이 땅 낙원에서 영원히 살 놀라운 희망이 있으니까요.
우리 모두는 어떤 희망을 갖고 있든 인내해야 합니다.
심한 압박을 받아 낙심하는 일을 피할 수는 없습니다.
하지만 하느님께선 우리가 이 낡은 제도에서
“창백한 말”에 앉은 상징적 말 탄 자가
이 일은 1차 세계 대전이 끝날 무렵 발생한
스페인 독감을 시작으로 100년이 넘게 일어나고 있습니다.
당시 세계 인구의 3분의 1인 5억 명이 감염된 것으로 추산되며
사탄은 우리가 낙담해 있을 때 공격합니다.
누가 우리를 실망시켜도 포기하지 않을 겁니다.
성서 시대에 여호와의 매우 충실한 종들조차도
그는 “나를 괴롭히는 모든 자 때문에”라고 했습니다.
다윗은 자신에 대한 사람들의 악한 행동 때문에
그렇지만 동료 인간들이 자신에게 한 행동 때문에
우리도 다른 사람의 말이나 행동 때문에
“생각 없이 하는 말은 칼로 찌르는 것과 같”다고
그리스도인 형제나 자매라면 더 깊이 찔릴 수 있죠.
상처를 준 사람과 말하기가 어려울지 모르죠.
그 사람을 고의로 피하기까지 할 수 있습니다.
분을 삭이지 못한 어떤 사람들은 그만 포기하고
사람들이 우리를 실망시키거나 감정을 상하게 할 때
어떻게 마귀의 덫을 피할 수 있습니까?
우리는 분을 품지 않으려고 해야 합니다.
분을 품으면 마음이 너무 상해서 우울해질 수 있죠.
우린 사탄의 먹잇감이 되지 말아야 합니다.
인내할 힘을 어디서 얻을 수 있을까요?
여호와께선 낙심한 이들에게 깊은 관심이 있으시죠.
여호와께서는 사랑 많은 형제들과 그분의 영과 말씀을 통해
그 내용을 묵상하는 것은 도움이 됩니다.
기름부음받은 형제인 나쇼 도리는 이렇게 말했습니다.
‘내 목표는 매일 적어도 한 시간씩 성경을 읽는 것이었는데,
시력이 약해지기 전까지 거의 60년 간 그렇게 했습니다.’
극단적인 공산주의 독재 하에서 견딜 수 있었죠.
매일 성경을 꼭 한 시간씩 읽으시라는 건 아닙니다.
하지만 일 년 안에 성경을 통독해 보시기 바랍니다.
시간을 들여 천천히 읽는다면 묵상할 수 있을 것입니다.
읽고 내용을 묵상하는 데 충분할 것입니다.
소리 내어 읽어서 자기 목소리를 듣는다면,
읽는 속도를 늦추고 묵상할 수 있습니다.
우리는 또한 그분의 조직을 통해 힘을 얻습니다.
많은 사람이 인내하는 데 큰 도움을 줍니다.
회중의 전도인들도 우리에게 큰 힘을 줍니다.
하느님의 뜻은 우리가 계속 “서로 격려”하는 것이며
이 일은 그 어느 때보다 긴급히 지금 해야 할 일입니다.
주제 성구인 고린도 후서 4:16의 말씀처럼 해야겠습니다.
앞으로 마지막 날에 어떤 일을 겪든,

en.text: We are happy to continue
with the annual meeting program.
We now have with us Brother Len Myers,
a helper to the Writing Committee,
who will conduct an interview with wives of Branch Committee members
in the United States.
Brother Myers, please.
The accounts of faithful women are found throughout the Bible.
One faithful Christian sister is mentioned by the apostle Paul
at Romans 16:1, 2.
There he mentions Phoebe,
who ‘proved herself to be a defender of many, including Paul.’
Today, we’re blessed to be able to get to know
faithful Christian sisters who share something unique.
All of them are wives of brothers
who serve as members of the United States Branch Committee.
Sister Snyder, we’d like to get to know more about you.
Can you, please, first tell us how you got the truth?
I was introduced to the truth by my parents.
And Jehovah used the example of my sister
and the nurturing love of older ones
in the congregations to draw me to him.
Then how did you start in the full-time ministry
and then into Bethel service?
Well, it was a bit of a test.
When I was in my late teens, a friend of mine died,
and I couldn’t understand why Jehovah would allow this
to happen to such a kind person.
So an elderly pioneer sister encouraged me
to do deeper research on the issue of universal sovereignty.
And this not only comforted me,
but it caused me to reevaluate my priorities
and to see if I
truly believed Jehovah would take care of me
if I really put him first.
So I started pioneering and put college on hold.
And it wasn’t long before I was broke
and the rent was coming due.
And so the next meeting,
I quietly put my last $50 in the contribution box
and thought: ‘That’s it, done, doesn’t work.
I’m going back to school.’
But that evening,
I learned that Matthew 6:33 is undeniably true.
Jehovah surprised me
and cared for all my needs from the most unlikely sources,
and he hasn’t stopped caring for me since.
And then you joined Troy in Bethel service later on, right?
Now, what assignments have you enjoyed at Bethel?
I’ve enjoyed housekeeping.
I’ve really enjoyed a lot of assignments within Transportation Department,
and I was one of the thousands who worked
on the Warwick and Tuxedo construction projects.
Now, as the wife of a Branch Committee member,
you have a demanding schedule.
Can you explain one challenge?
Well, like most wives of good shepherds,
I would love to have more time with my husband.
That’s understandable.
So, what practical things have you done to deal with that challenge?
Well, prayer, study, and meditation
have reminded me that we’re at spiritual war.
And we’re at war, so our priorities have to change.
So I can’t long for ideal circumstances,
although they’re coming quickly.
Right now, it’s about advancing pure worship.
And while it’s important to maintain
a healthy and close relationship with Troy,
my primary joy should be in Jehovah.
And, then, second is remembering the sacrifices that were made for me.
Of course, Jehovah gave up 33 years with his best friend for me.
And also there were sisters when I was single and pioneering
who would invite me over for lots of meals
and to go out in service.
They would even send their husband
out on freezing cold, dark nights to fix my car,
which broke down often.
So I’m grateful,
and the main way I can show this appreciation
is to imitate their examples.
Now, with challenges come blessings.
What’s one blessing you enjoy as the wife of a Branch Committee member?
Increased peace
that comes from having complete confidence
in how Jehovah directs and blesses the decisions
his organization makes through the Governing Body.
If I were not married to a Branch Committee member,
I may never have known
just how much the brothers rely on Jehovah’s spirit
and how much time they spend
—long periods of time— in prayer
and how much they deeply, deeply love the friends.
So I’m embarrassed
about how much worrying I’ve done in the past about these things.
But now it’s a lot easier to just be supportive
and listen, obey, and be blessed.
Very nice.
Now, as you look back
on your rich spiritual life in Jehovah’s service,
is there an experience you can share with us?
We were visiting a small branch in a developing country
that had been ravaged by decades of civil war.
I’d never seen poverty like that before.
And one evening, I went into the dining room
to gather dinner for us.
But before getting the dinner,
I stopped and talked to a lovely young brother.
At one point, I turned around and noticed that all the food had been taken.
And I said, “There’s no more food.”
Now, this young brother hadn’t eaten either.
But he just shrugged and said, “It’s just hunger,”
and he continued zealously talking about his assignment.
Now, this brother was a commuter and very thin,
and so it was likely that he might not eat that night
or maybe even the next morning.
But the way his face glowed when he talked about his assignment,
it was clear that his joy was not based on anything physical
or the lack of anything physical.
So I really treasure this lesson
because it’s made me want to appreciate more what I do have currently
and to imitate his example in focusing on what’s truly important.
And I think you told me that he did get some food that night,
so we’re happy about that.
Thanks for letting us get to know you and for sharing that experience.
Now we’d like to get to know Sister Shirrell Georges.
Sister Georges, can you tell us how you got the truth?
When I was 11, my mother started to study.
Another sister studied with my two sisters and me
out of the book From Paradise Lost to Paradise Regained.
Two years later, on November 13, 1971,
my mother, my oldest sister, and I were baptized.
How did you start in the full-time ministry?
As teenagers, a pioneer couple assisted us
when we temporary, or vacation, pioneered, as it was called then.
That led me to want to regular pioneer after high school.
However, after graduating, I started working full-time.
It was at a district convention where the point was made,
‘If you’re not pioneering, tell Jehovah why.’
Well, I really didn’t have a good reason.
So I started making plans to work part-time.
It was in September of 1980
when I realized my goal of regular pioneering.
And how did that lead to Bethel service?
While pioneering,
I had the opportunity to assist
with the Brooklyn Assembly Hall renovation project on Thursdays.
It was one Thursday that I learned
of an announcement made at Bethel:
Sisters could now commute.
So after a while, I turned in my application
and started commuting in November of 1987.
But before commuting, I had met Luther.
We started to court, and then later,
we were married and accepted as a couple to Bethel.
And what assignments have you enjoyed at Bethel?
While commuting, I worked in the Dry Cleaning Department
and continued there after marriage.
For a short time, I worked with the Brooklyn Warehouse Department.
Then Luther and I received a surprise assignment.
We were asked to assist at the Jamaica branch,
starting in March of 1995.
There I worked in alterations,
laundry, kitchen, housekeeping,
shipping, and the Bethel Office.
Then in 2014, the Jamaica branch merged with the United States branch.
We were invited to serve back in the United States
—first at Patterson, where I worked in Audio/Video Services,
and now at Wallkill, in the Service Department.
Now, you too have a demanding schedule.
Can you explain one challenge?
Well, many of the assignments that Luther has involve traveling.
So that means that we are away from our congregation,
sometimes for weeks.
It also means that we’re not able to get back
to our return visits and Bible studies on a weekly basis.
So, what practical things have you done to deal with that challenge?
We’ve found it helpful to let the friends know
whenever we will be away.
Many times we would receive a text from them:
“Just saying hi. Checking on you.
Hope you’re doing well.”
This really has helped us to stay connected.
Something else we did was to invite publishers
to go with us on our return visits and Bible studies.
This way, whenever we were away, they could keep the interest going.
That’s a good idea.
What good habits did you form early in life
that help you now as you support your husband?
Growing up, my mother taught us to be content
and to share whatever we had.
One Watchtower  article stated:
“True contentment comes from loving and being loved.”
We grew up in a loving family,
and then learning about Jehovah and his love as I grew older
helped me to find contentment in Jehovah’s service.
So whatever assignment I have, I try to be content
and view any differences as an opportunity for me to learn
about the various aspects, unique personalities,
and qualities of my brothers and sisters.
Now, as you look back on your rich spiritual life,
is there a memory you can share with us?
Proverbs 10:22 says:
“The blessing of Jehovah —that is what makes [one] rich.”
I feel as if I have been enriched
in so many ways with so many memories.
One memory is being able to assist
in the former Jamaica branch for over 19 years.
Working together with the brothers
was such a unique privilege
and was really encouraging.
To see the brothers exhibit their faith and loyalty to Jehovah
despite various challenging circumstances
was a true encouragement for us.
We made many friends in that assignment,
and we continue to keep in touch to this day.
That is a nice memory.
Thanks for sharing that with us.
Finally, we’d like to talk to Sister Sunny Cheiky.
Sister Cheiky, can you tell us how you got the truth
and then entered the full-time ministry?
My mother raised me and my two brothers to serve Jehovah.
It was difficult for her because my father left the truth
and our family when we were very young.
But she set a very good example for us.
And then because of the encouragement of young pioneers in our congregation,
I began regular pioneering in the Pasadena, California, Congregation
after I graduated from high school in 1962.
And how did that lead to Bethel service?
I served in a few other areas where the need was great
in New Mexico, northern California,
a special pioneer assignment in Iowa,
and then a small congregation in Mississippi.
Tom was a Brooklyn Bethelite,
and he came down to Mississippi to dedicate a Kingdom Hall.
In May 1981, we met;
seven months later, we were married,
and we were accepted to serve as a couple at Bethel.
Nice.
What assignments have you enjoyed at Bethel?
I was a housekeeper for my first three years,
and now I’ve been in laundry for 35 years.
I did have a part-time assignment in grounds maintenance for a while,
but now I joyfully serve full-time in the Wallkill laundry.
Now, you too have a demanding schedule.
Can you explain one challenge?
Meeting so many wonderful friends in our assignments,
I like to keep in touch with them.
But time is so limited,
so I feel that that can be overwhelming at times.
So, what practical thing have you done to deal with that challenge?
Well, I love to write cards and send letters,
so that’s how I deal with this.
To be able to keep in touch with my friends —that really helps a lot.
So, what has helped you to be balanced despite your busy schedule?
I loved the March 2016 broadcast that stressed three things.
The first is count your blessings.
We are a part of an amazing organization
that is carrying on the most meaningful work of preaching and teaching.
The second is look at the big picture.
When I feel stressed out,
I try to put things in the right perspective
—Jehovah’s sovereignty first, foremost, and not focusing on myself—
and that helps me to keep calm.
And third is get enough rest.
Without enough rest, I can’t think straight
and even ordinary activities in my routine
seem overwhelming, or too much.
That’s very practical.
Now, is there a particular experience you’d like to share with us?
When I was special pioneering in Iowa,
I married a brother who was a pioneer
and then became an elder,
and so I continued in the congregation as a regular pioneer.
After several years, he became an apostate,
and he tried to encourage me to go with him; but I refused.
The elders made great efforts to help him to recover,
but he was persistent in carrying out his course.
So in time, he separated from me and ended the marriage.
But I felt Jehovah’s support in so many ways.
One in particular was a couple who would call me often,
and they would have me to their home,
and they never wanted me to feel alone.
Then another blessing came later when I moved to Mississippi,
and I became partners with a sister who was 20 years older than me.
She had been in the seventh class of Gilead,
and she had been special pioneering for 30 years.
So you can imagine she was a tremendous help to me.
More blessings came later
when I married Tom and began serving at Bethel.
So feeling Jehovah’s support in a difficult time
and experiencing his blessings is unforgettable.
Sister Cheiky, thank you so much for sharing that experience with us.
In the introduction, we referenced the example of Phoebe,
that faithful Christian sister.
Interestingly, our Kingdom song number 137,
entitled “Faithful Women, Christian Sisters,”
is based on the description of Phoebe at Romans 16:2.
The lyrics of that song remind us that our Christian sisters
show a faithful spirit we all can imitate,
and that’s true of the sisters we interviewed today.
The song concludes with the words:
“Christian sisters, may Jehovah keep you  firm in your conviction,
your prize is drawing near.”
How we appreciate the example set by all of our faithful Christian sisters!
Thank you, Brother Myers.
We thank you sisters as well.
There are so many faithful wives around the world who support their husbands
who are putting Kingdom interests first.
We thank you and pray for all of you.
Now we have the pleasure of hearing
from another member of the Governing Body,
Brother Gerrit Lösch.
He will speak on the subject “We Do Not Give Up.”
Brother Lösch, we look forward to your discussion.
Some of us have been in the truth for 40 years,
50 years, 60 years, or more.
During our life, we may have been confronted
with various tests, or challenges.
Still, we did not and “we do not give up”
the truth and our precious relationship with our heavenly Father.
Also, we do not give up preaching the Word of God.
Second Corinthians 4:16
is the theme scripture I’ve selected for this talk.
Please locate that with me
—2 Corinthians 4:16.
It says: “Therefore, we do not give up,
“but even if the man we are outside is wasting away,
certainly the man we are inside is being renewed from day to day.”
As it said, “we do not give up,”
and we do not give in when it comes to temptations.
First Peter 3:6 encourages us
to “not give in to fear.”
Deuteronomy 13:6-8 tells the Israelites
that when a false prophet becomes active,
“you must not give in to him or listen to him.”
In the Sermon on the Mount, according to an alternate rendering,
Jesus told his listeners to pray to Jehovah
to “not allow us to give in to temptation.”
On one occasion, Peter encouraged others
—1 Peter 3:6: “Do not give in to fear.”
We do give ear when somebody gives us good counsel;
we give serious thought
when somebody wants to help us;
we give comfort to those in need.
In the first century, Paul gave comfort
to the congregation in Corinth.
Please find 2 Corinthians 4:1
with me, and we can read it together.
And it says there:
“Therefore,
“since we have this ministry through the mercy that was shown us,
we do not give up.”
So who were the “we”?
The anointed.
Second Corinthians 3:3
tells the Corinthians
(they are the words of Paul)
that they are like “a letter of Christ
“written by [him and his friends] as ministers,
inscribed . . . with the spirit of [our] living God.”
The apostle, then, in verse 5, humbly acknowledges
that the fact that he and the Corinthians
‘were qualified came from God’
and, in verse 6,
that he “has . . . adequately qualified [Christians]
to be ministers of a new covenant.”
What did Paul refer to when he said in verse 1
“since we have this ministry”?
He referred to the ministry of that “new covenant”
of which he was just talking about.
Please follow the reading
of 2 Corinthians 3:5, 6,
where it says:
“Not that we of ourselves are adequately qualified
“to consider that anything comes from us,
“but our being adequately qualified comes from God,
“who has indeed adequately qualified us
“to be ministers of a new covenant,
not of a written code, but of spirit.”
At 2 Corinthians 3:18, he says
“and all of us, while we . . . reflect like mirrors
the glory of Jehovah.”
Well, who did he refer to when he wrote “all of us”?
He meant all of the anointed.
In chapter 4, verse 1, he says
“therefore, since we have this ministry
through the mercy that was shown us.”
The expression “therefore”
refers back to the reason and motivation
for the anointed not to give up.
In chapter 3, verse 18, he refers to the anointed
as being “transformed . . .
from one degree of glory to another,”
culminating in the glory they receive when entering heaven.
Since the anointed are progressing “from glory to glory,”
until going to heaven,
they have a strong motivation
not to give up but to endure,
since there is such a precious prize, or reward, ahead of them.
Understandably, Paul said in chapter 4, verse 1:
“Therefore, . . . we do not give up.”
Also in 2 Corinthians 4:16, Paul wrote:
“Therefore, we do not give up.”
In the third chapter, Paul contrasts
the old covenant that was “stripped of glory”
with the new covenant that would (like verses 10 and 11 say)
excel with greater glory
—a glory that would remain.
And 2 Corinthians 3:12 says
“since we have such a hope.”
What hope?
The heavenly hope.
Did you note the similarity with chapter 4, verse 1?
It said “since we have this ministry.”
What ministry was Paul referring to?
Was he referring to the field ministry in a general sense?
No.
He referred to the ministry of the new covenant.
In chapter 4, verse 7,
he then calls the ministry of the new covenant
a “treasure.”
“Since we have this [treasure],” he said.
It’s not just any treasure.
It was a great incentive for the anointed in the first century
not to give up in view of this treasure of the new covenant
that involves progressive glory.
Paul wrote: “Therefore, we do not give up.”
Also, the context of the next verses
shows that Paul was writing about the heavenly calling
that the new covenant made possible.
What Paul wrote is a strong incentive for the anointed today
not to give up.
What about the “great crowd” of “other sheep”?
Paul did not have the great crowd in mind
when he wrote the words of 2 Corinthians chapters 3 and 4.
In the introduction to his letter,
he referred to “all the holy ones.”
In 2 Corinthians 1:21, 22, he says:
“Who anointed us is God.
He has also put his seal on us.”
However, the great crowd is a recipient
of the radiant blessings of the ministry of the new covenant.
Some time ago, The Watchtower
made a general application in principle to the great crowd.
Just like the anointed have
the treasure of the new covenant and its ministry,
the great crowd also considers
their ministry a treasure.
The great crowd is also determined not to give up
in view of the beautiful hope
to live forever in Paradise on earth.
And all of us, no matter what hope,
have to endure.
Paul wrote at 2 Corinthians 4:8
that “we are hard-pressed”
—some more than others.
Please find Psalm 90:10.
None of us are exempt from the pressures
that can cause discouragement.
And it says there:
“The span of our life is 70 years,
“or 80 if one is especially strong.
“But they are filled with trouble and sorrow;
they quickly pass by, and away we fly.”
Because of the pressures of life and disappointments,
most of us grow weary at times.
But we must remember that God never promised
that we would have a problem-free life in this old system.
Even in the first century, God’s servants faced adversities,
including persecution and poverty.
Jehovah does allow his servants
to be tempted and tested.
For the time of the end, he also foretold
“earthquakes,” wars,
increased lawlessness, and “pestilences”
according to Luke 21:11.
In Revelation, he foretold
that a figurative horseman on the “pale horse”
would kill a large amount of people.
This has happened for decades
but started with the Spanish flu at the end of World War I,
where an estimated 500 million were affected
—one third of mankind of that time—
and about 50 million died.
Satan exploits our moments of discouragement
just as a lion takes advantage of an animal when it is most vulnerable.
But we will not give up!
We will not give up if others disappoint us.
In Bible times, even the most faithful servants of Jehovah
may have felt weighed down at times.
“I have grown weary with my sighing,”
wrote David.
“All night long I make my couch swim;
with my tears I make my own divan overflow.”
Why did David feel that way?
“Because of all those showing hostility to me,”
he explained.
The hurtful actions of others caused David such pain of heart
that his tears flowed freely.
Still, David did not draw away from Jehovah
because of what fellow humans had done to him
—and neither do we!
Similarly, the words or actions of others
may cause us much pain of heart.
“There exists the one speaking thoughtlessly
as with the stabs of a sword,” says Proverbs 12:18.
When the thoughtless one is a Christian brother or sister,
the stab wound can go deep.
The human tendency may be to take offense,
perhaps harboring resentment.
This is especially true if we feel
that we have been treated unkindly or unjustly.
We may find it hard to talk to the offender.
We might even deliberately avoid him or her.
Weighed down with resentment, some have given up
and have stopped coming to Christian meetings.
How can we avoid playing into the Devil’s hands
when others disappoint or hurt us?
We must try not to harbor resentment.
It can hurt us so much that we start suffering from depression.
Instead of giving in to depression or aggression,
take the initiative to make peace
or settle matters as quickly as possible.
Colossians 3:13 urges us:
“Continue . . . forgiving one another freely
. . . if anyone has a cause for complaint against another.”
We do not have to fall prey to Satan.
Jehovah and Jesus are on our  side.
How can we find encouragement to endure?
Jehovah deeply cares about those who may be discouraged.
Acts 17:27 shows
that “he is not far off from each one of us.”
Jehovah comforts and strengthens us
through loving brothers and through his spirit and his Word.
Reading the Bible daily
and meditating upon it helps.
The publications have encouraged us
to read the Bible through once a year.
Why not make it your resolve to try such a program?
Nasho Dori, an anointed brother from Albania
who persevered under ban, said:
‘My goal was to read the Bible
‘for at least one hour each day,
‘which I did for some 60 years
before my eyesight failed.’
Was he bragging when saying this?
No.
It helped him not to give up
under the extreme Communist dictatorship.
We do not necessarily expect you
to read the Bible for one hour each day,
but we encourage you to read it through in one year
and to read it slowly enough that you can meditate on it.
About 20 minutes a day provides ample opportunity
to read and meditate on what you read.
If you read so you hear your own voice,
it will help you to read slower and to meditate.
We also find encouragement through his organization
—things we read in the literature or magazines.
And we greatly benefit from the congregation meetings.
We also benefit from sweet association with our brothers
—be it live or via television.
So do not give up!
Elders, when they shepherd,
are also a big help for many to persevere.
Publishers in our congregation do a lot to strengthen us.
According to Hebrews 10:25, it is God’s will
that we keep “encouraging one another,”
and doing so is more urgent now than ever before.
Let us always keep in mind the inspired words
of 2 Thessalonians 3:13:
“For your part, brothers,
do not give up in doing good.”
Galatians 6:9 similarly says:
“Let us not give up in doing what is fine,
for in due time we will reap.”
What do we conclude from this?
It is in the words of our theme text,
2 Corinthians 4:16:
“We do not give up”!
Thank you, Brother Lösch.
May we all be determined to follow
that Scriptural advice and not give up,
no matter what we face ahead during these last days.
And we’d like to remind all of you
that the concluding segment of the annual meeting
will be posted on February 1, 2021,
right here on JW Broadcasting®.

我的姐姐

我亲身体会到马太福音6:33说得千真万确
耶和华给了我一个惊喜

从那时起，他一直在照顾我

我喜欢家务部的工作
也真的非常喜欢在运输部的工作
也很荣幸参与了沃威克
和塔克西多的建筑工程

嗯，和大多长老的妻子一样
希望丈夫多陪陪我

祷告、研读和沉思都时刻提醒我

现在我们不可能期待有完美的生活
对我们最重要的是拥护正确的崇拜

还有就是要记住，其他人为我作出的牺牲
耶和华跟他最好的朋友分开33年，为了我
我结婚之前做先驱的那段时间
很多姐妹常常约我去她们家
跟她们一起吃饭，一起传道

在晚上出去帮我修车

我非常感激他们

向他们学习

我的内心越来越安宁了
因为我现在完全相信
耶和华正通过中央长老团
指引和赐福给他的组织
如果没有嫁给分部委员会成员

我们以前探访过一个发展中国家的小分部

我从来没见过那么穷的国家

他看起来非常快乐

因为，是他让我更珍惜我目前所拥有的东西

我和姐姐十几岁的时候就会利用假期做先驱

我做先驱时，有一段时间每周四

姐妹们现在可以做通勤服务了

在1987年11月开始做通勤人员
不过在那之前，我就跟路德弟兄谈恋爱了
我们结婚以后就一起在伯特利服务

我做通勤服务时在干洗部工作
结婚后也继续在那里工作
后来我在仓储部短暂工作过一段时间

在牙买加分部服务
我在那里的很多部门工作过
裁缝部、洗衣部、厨房部、家务部
装运部以及伯特利办公室
在2014年牙买加分部并入了美国分部
我们又回到美国分部服务
首先在帕特森的影音服务部服务
现在在华基尔的传道部服务

路德常常要出差
所以我们不得不常常跟会众分开

那些对圣经感兴趣的人

我们出去续访或是跟学生讨论圣经的时候

好主意

一篇《守望台》文章提到
我们爱别人也受别人所爱

我在一个充满爱心的家庭长大

这帮助我在服务的时候能够保持知足
我也学到无论接获什么委派都能感到快乐
把它们看作是学习的好机会
我可以学习不同的知识
了解不同弟兄姐妹的个性和好品格
回顾以往

和那里的弟兄姐妹一起工作

我们受到很大的鼓励
因为他们虽然面对很多考验和难题

这真的很鼓励我们
我们交到很多好朋友，到现在还经常联系

当时会众里有一些年轻的先驱
他们给我很大的鼓励
我在1962年高中毕业以后

我曾在新墨西哥州和加州北部
一些需要大的地区服务
后来被委派到爱荷华州做特别先驱
后来又到了密西西比州一个小会众服务
汤姆是布鲁克林的伯特利成员
他来密西西比州参加一个聚会所的呈献礼
我们是在1981年5月认识的
7个月以后我们结婚了

前3年，我在家务部工作

中间有一段时间我在庭园保养部做兼职工作
现在我在华基尔洗衣部快乐地服务
你肯定非常忙

有时候很多事情想做但却做不到
