세계적으로 전염병 때문에 많은 것이 중단되었지만
여호와와 그분의 조직에는 전혀 장애물이 되지 않았죠.
이 대회 프로그램을 즐기는 걸 보면서 정말 감동을 받았습니다!
현재 좋지 않은 세상 상태에도 불구하고
우리는 정말 말라기 3:18의 성취를 보고 있는데,
섬기지 않는 자의 차이를 보게 될 것’이라고 했죠.
우리 모두가 지역 대회를 즐길 수 있도록
전 세계의 많은 형제 자매들이 이 큰 작업에 참여했습니다.
이 형제 자매들은 모두 여러분이나 저처럼 보통 사람들이죠.
인도와 전 세계의 형제 자매들을 위해
무엇이든 되실 수 있다는 것을 보여 준
여호와의 이름에 큰 영예가 돌아갔기 때문이죠.
네, 여호와의 성령은 많은 어려움에도 불구하고
우리가 일을 완수할 수 있게 해 주었습니다.
그 결과, 어떤 축복들을 맛볼 수 있었습니까?
잘 이해가 안 되는 곳이 있으면 다시 돌아가서 볼 수가 있죠.
또 프로그램에 집중이 안 될 때에도
앞으로 돌아가서 다시 볼 수 있습니다.
그래서 이번 대회를 통해 더 많은 유익을 얻을 수 있었습니다.
이번 대회는 그 어떤 대회보다 국제적이었던 것 같습니다.
어떻게 잘 이겨 내고 있는지 볼 수 있었습니다.
우린 몸은 따로 떨어져 있어도 하나로 연합되어 있죠.
이 대회를 통해 더 연합된 느낌입니다.
저희가 사는 마을에는 인터넷이 안 됩니다.
새벽같이 출발하거나 밤 늦게 출발한 적도 있었습니다.
그 모든 어려움을 극복할 수 있었습니다.
아내는 여호와를 함께 섬긴 정말 훌륭한 동반자였습니다.
대회 내내, 여호와께서 모든 중앙장로회 성원과 보조자들을
저를 위해 개인적으로 보내 주신 것 같은 느낌이 들었어요.
이보다 더 좋은 선물은 없을 겁니다.
말로 설명해 주는 기능이 정말 좋았어요.
이 기능 덕분에 이전보다 대회를 훨씬 더 잘 즐길 수 있었어요.
벤이 사무실에서 나오자 동료들이 고개를 가로젓는다.
영상을 말로 설명해 줘서 정말 놀랐어요.
실제로 보는 것 같은 느낌이 들었습니다.
예전에는 궁금하지만 알 수 없었던 것들이나,
다른 사람들한테 설명해 달라고 하던 것들을
그래서 국제 대회 때 하는 것처럼
또 대회를 시작할 때 동시에 듣기 위해서
같이 노래하고 같이 대회를 볼 수 있었습니다.
정말 국제 대회에 온 것 같았어요.
다 함께 왕국 노래를 부르지 못한다는 거였어요.
청중이 다 같이 노래를 부르면 참 좋을 텐데,
집에서 대회를 보니까 그럴 수가 없어서 아쉬웠죠.
그래서 가족이 함께 노래를 크게 부르기로 했어요.
저희는 자녀가 셋이고, 다섯 식구 모두가 코로나에 걸렸어요.
대회를 보는 내내 모두 다 증상이 나타나고 있었죠.
우리 가족은 이번 대회 프로그램으로 많은 격려를 받았습니다.
마치 같은 방에 와 있는 친한 친구가
바로 옆에 앉아서 따뜻하게 말해 주는 것 같았다고 했습니다.
이번 대회는 우리 모두에게 정말 긍정적인 영향을 주었습니다.
부모님은 현재 두 분 다 심한 병으로 투병 중이세요.
하지만 이번에 가족이 함께 집에서 대회를 볼 때
두 분도 저와 남동생과 올케와 같이
함께 노래를 부르고 대회를 같이 봤는데,
대회장에서 대회가 열렸다면 이렇게 할 수 없었을 거예요.
그 어떤 것도 여호와께서 저희 가족에게
도움의 손길을 베푸시는 걸 막을 수 없었죠.
우린 모두 같은 중앙장로회 성원들이 연설한
동일한 영적 프로그램을 같은 시기에 보고 있습니다.
이런 기회가 생길 줄은 생각도 못했죠.
첫 회기에 함께하게 되어 참으로 기쁩니다.
주변의 모든 게 한순간에 무너져 내릴 때가 있죠.
그럴 때 우리가 의지할 수 있는 건 여호와밖에 없습니다.
당신의 이름을 두려워하도록 내 마음을 하나로 모아 주십시오.”
어떤 두려운 일이나 어떤 시련이 닥쳐도,
2020년 지역 대회는 우리가 어떤 상황에 있든지
여호와께서 계속 우리에게 영적 양식을 공급하실 것이고,
우리는 그분을 계속 섬길 것임을 보여 주었습니다.
우리는 빌립보서 4:4의 말씀이 참되다는 것을 경험했습니다.
급변하는 상황 속에서도 우린 무엇을 알 수 있었죠?
연례 총회의 이어지는 두 번째 부분도
JW 방송을 통해 즐기실 수 있을 것입니다.
다음 달 JW 방송에서 소개해 드리겠습니다.
우리 형제 자매들을 만나 보도록 하겠습니다.
아프리카 대륙의 거의 정중앙에 위치해 있습니다.
그 밖에도 여러 부족 언어들이 사용됩니다.
다이아몬드, 금, 목재와 같은 천연 자원이 풍부합니다.
표범과 같은 많은 동물들을 흔히 볼 수 있습니다.
안타깝게도 이 나라에서는 여러 해 동안
우리 형제들은 성경의 희망을 전하는 일을 지치지 않고
보줌 회중이 회중 구역을 돌보는 것에 더해,
형제들이 그 집단들까지 가는 것은 쉬운 일이 아닌데,
이 나라의 도로 중 3퍼센트만이 포장되어 있기 때문입니다.
보줌 회중에서는 보카랑가에 정기적으로 장로들을 보내
공개 강연을 하고 「파수대」 연구를 사회하도록 마련합니다.
그 집단은 약 30건의 성서 연구를 사회하고 있습니다.
전 세계에 있는 여러분 모두에게 사랑과 안부를 전합니다.
우리도 중앙아프리카 공화국의 모든 형제 자매들에게

en.text: Welcome!
This is JW Broadcasting®
for January 2021.
On Saturday, October 3,
the Watch Tower Bible and Tract Society
of Pennsylvania
held its annual business meeting
via videoconferencing.
In normal times, after we care for that necessary business,
we share spiritual encouragement in a larger meeting.
However, we’re not living in normal times.
Because of the COVID-19 pandemic,
we had to readjust our plans.
However, the good news is,
we did not cancel the spiritual portion of the program.
You likely already enjoyed Brother Herd’s talk
in October about the 2021 yeartext.
If not, we encourage you to do so.
In addition, the Governing Body assigned me
to be the chairman for the 2020 annual meeting,
and I’ll also be the anchor for this month’s and next month’s
JW Broadcasting programs.
We’re happy that in this month’s broadcast,
you’ll see the first part
of that spiritual portion of the annual meeting.
It begins with a special musical prelude.
Please enjoy!
Annual meetings of the Watch Tower Bible and Tract Society of Pennsylvania
have been held for many years
—in fact, since January 1885.
They have been held in different states in the United States
and, in 1983, in Britain.
This year, 2020, the corporate meeting
is being held by videoconference.
The spiritual program has been recorded
for the benefit of the brothers all over the earth.
This is a historic annual meeting.
In the past, we have had some historic annual meetings.
For example,
at the annual meeting held on October 2, 1944, in Pittsburgh,
the members of the Pennsylvania corporation
adopted six resolutions amending its charter.
The charter had provided that voting shares be issued
to contributors of funds to the Society’s work,
but the third amendment eliminated that provision.
Thereafter, directors of the Society were to be voted into office
by individuals who were fully devoted to Jehovah,
irrespective of the amount of money that they contributed
to advance the Kingdom work.
After the historic annual meeting in 1944,
a vital question remained.
Since the Governing Body was then closely identified
with the Pennsylvania corporation’s seven-member board of directors,
did this mean that the Governing Body
could never be made up of more than seven anointed Christians?
Moreover, since the directors
are elected by the members of the corporation,
were the corporation members electing members of the Governing Body
at the annual meeting each year?
Are the directors and officers
of the Watch Tower Bible and Tract Society of Pennsylvania
and the members of the Governing Body
one and the same, or are they different?
These questions were answered years later.
They were answered at the annual meeting held
on October 1, 1971
—another historic annual meeting.
On that occasion, one of the speakers pointed out
that the governing body preceded
the Watch Tower Bible and Tract Society of Pennsylvania
by hundreds of years.
Now, despite some who opposed Jehovah
and the earthly part of his organization
and who claimed there was no governing body in the first century
and hence saw no need for a Governing Body today,
a governing body was formed at Pentecost of 33 C.E.,
more than 18 centuries
before the Pennsylvania corporation came into existence.
At first, the governing body consisted of 12 apostles.
Its number was enlarged later,
for “the apostles and older men in Jerusalem” were taking the lead.
Now notice what happened later
here in the Bible book of Acts
in chapter 15.
So other issues had been handled by the 12 apostles,
but now with this circumcision issue
that came up among the congregations,
notice what we read here in verse 2 of Acts 15:
“But after quite a bit of dissension and disputing
“by Paul and Barnabas with them,
“it was arranged for Paul, Barnabas, and some of the others
“to go up to the apostles
“and elders in Jerusalem
regarding this issue.”
So the issue was going to be settled by the first-century governing body.
And now it’s larger than the apostles;
it included the elders and the apostles
in Jerusalem.
Now, what is the benefit
of following the direction from the governing body in the first century
and, by extension, today?
Notice that at Acts 16:4, 5,
they’re carrying the decree there.
And it mentions: “As they traveled on through the cities,
“they would deliver to them for observance
“the decrees that had been decided on
“by the apostles and the elders who were in Jerusalem.
“[Now notice.]
“Then, indeed, the congregations
“continued to be made firm in the faith
and to increase in number day by day.”
Isn’t that beautiful?
There was a governing body.
They didn’t have a need for legal entities
to advance the Kingdom work in the first century,
but they did indeed need a governing body.
As long as conditions in this world permit,
the Governing Body will make use of legal entities.
If a legal entity is dissolved by government decree,
the preaching work will still go on.
Even now, in lands where restrictions are in effect
and no legal entities are used,
the Kingdom message is being proclaimed,
disciples are being made,
and theocracy’s increase continues.
In the midst of this pandemic, the preaching continues.
Many experiences are happening globally.
Now, one I received and confirmed
from two elders serving at Warwick Bethel,
I think you’ll appreciate.
So much is going on and so many nice experiences.
A health-care system that operates
dozens of hospitals across the United States,
and many of them were COVID hot spots,
wanted to publish a video interview
featuring two frontline health-care workers in one of the hospitals.
Well, it happened that the two nurses they chose for the interviews
were our brothers.
They were asked to supply pictures of their families.
One of the pictures had been taken before the pandemic
in front of a paradise scene in one of our Assembly Halls.
Now, the woman coordinating the video interviews
told the brother that she recognized that scene.
So he asked her if she was a Witness.
She replied: “No, but I studied with the Witnesses,
“and I know it’s the truth.
I can see how close we are to the end.”
The brother then told her that she’d be happy to know
that the second nurse whom she had interviewed the day before
was also a Witness.
Then the woman burst into tears.
She said it made sense that the two nurses selected for this interview
would both be Witnesses.
“I can see it in your approach
and in the belief in something bigger than this.”
And she said she planned to resume her Bible study.
So we pray for this woman and all the wonderful experiences happening
as the preaching goes on during this pandemic.
So this is all happening because Jehovah’s Witnesses
plant and water
and “God [keeps] making it grow.”
All glory goes to Jehovah.
At this meeting, as was pointed out last year
with the announcement about the Ramapo project,
you will learn that the faithful slave is not slowing down.
We have more work to do until Jehovah says
the preaching work is finished.
As we look to the future, we are confident
that Jehovah will care for the spiritual and material needs of his people.
He and his Son, Jesus Christ, will continue to provide
the heavenly direction and support needed
to complete the Kingdom preaching work.
We therefore beg Jehovah for his spirit
to finish the work he has given us.
While Jehovah’s organization here on earth
is legally established and abides by governmental requirements
for its business meetings,
this organization is bound by a higher power.
Before he left the earth, Jesus told his followers:
“Go . . . make disciples . . . , teaching them.”
But he did even more.
Jesus promised that during the time of the end,
we would also receive “food at the proper time”
to help us fulfill that commission.
Has Jesus kept his promise?
Please watch the following video.
It is entitled “Go, . . . Teaching Them.”
Everyone who claims to be a Christian
and has dedicated himself to Jehovah God
must not only preach
but he must be able to teach.
We must go into the homes of the people
and teach them what the Bible says.
We needed a book that could be used
effectively in conducting Bible studies,
one that would cover
the basic doctrines and truths.
Many years ago
in the Bethel dining room
after the noon meal,
Brother Knorr read off a list of 15 to 20 brothers’ names
who were to report at his office immediately.
And they were told to write
a new study book using simple, everyday language,
just as they would present basic Bible truths
to someone at the door.
Well, within months, that book was written,
printed, and released
as “Let God Be True.”
That book made even
a new publisher feel confident.
It was like having a ‘bombshell’ in our hands,
capable of blowing to bits all of the false doctrines.
At one house, I conducted studies in that book
for 15 years with different people!
First, a woman;
next, a family;
then, some young people;
finally, another woman —six people in all
got baptized using that book.
Still, some struggled to finish this
and the even more detailed ‘Impossible to Lie ’ book
and to make progress.
By the late 1960’s,
a book was needed that got right to the point.
They called it the “blue bomb.”
And it was a game changer
—a game changer.
It was written in a simple, clear,
and pointed way so that any sincere reader
could understand it.
I used to deal drugs.
I wanted to change, but I didn’t know how.
Then, my manager gave me the Truth  book.
I was immediately convinced
I had found the truth and the real meaning of life.
From then on,
everyone who came looking for drugs
got a Truth  book instead!
By the early 1980’s,
the field needed something new.
Could a book be produced at the same level as the Bible Stories  book
but with the information presented in the Truth  book?
I had no Bible studies at all.
Now, I have three,
and a fourth one is ready to start.
Thank you!
I was studying with a man who had been smoking for 17 years.
Then he started to read the Live Forever  book.
That did it.
Any book that powerful shouldn’t go to waste sitting on the shelf.
Only a decade later, the world had changed.
In some lands, so many wanted to study
that they were put on a waiting list.
Other lands faced a different problem.
Somehow, we dillydally with some of our students.
[It] takes us years to bring some into the truth,
and we wonder why.
Maybe this book,
with its pointed truths,
will open their minds
and their hearts to see.
The Live Forever  book helped me to love Jehovah,
but the Knowledge  book
helped me to make the decision to serve him.
My husband studied the Knowledge  book
while he was working in Poland.
He loved it so much that he translated it
into Mongolian and sent it to us.
Soon we were all baptized.
My husband then joined
the real Mongolian translation team.
Still, we needed a book
that not only sped up disciple-making
but also touched the heart.
This book has an instant appeal
that quickly draws householders
into a conversation.
Some are calling it the Gold Nugget!
I was searching for something to fill
the emptiness that we both felt in our lives.
I was being trained by one of Jehovah’s Witnesses,
and she said, “Feel free to read whatever I have in my toolbox.”
I opened it, and immediately a little yellow book,
What Does the Bible Really Teach?, caught my eye.
The scriptures at the beginning of the book,
they touched my heart immediately,
and I felt like,
‘These answer all the questions
I’ve been searching for my entire life!’
. . . publication entitled What Can the Bible Teach Us?
It was like having a ‘bombshell’ in our hands.
It really touched the heart,
and it helped bring many into the truth.
I found answers to all my questions
in just one book.
This book was sent from God.
The best teaching tool
I’ve ever been privileged to use.
We thought this was the book
—the only book—
and that there never could be another.
Many of you have used every one
of those publications over the years.
Like me, you have felt that each one was a great instrument for its time.
But we’re not stuck in the past.
We look to the future.
What is the future of disciple-making?
Listen as Brother David Splane delivers the talk
“Wouldn’t It Be Great . . .?”
The yeartext for 2020 was about the preaching work:
“Go . . . make disciples . . . , baptizing them.”
Now, in harmony with that theme, the Governing Body directed
that a number of study articles should be prepared
for the study edition of The Watchtower
about the ministry and particularly about conducting Bible studies.
Then at the regional convention this summer,
why, almost the entirety of Saturday
was dedicated to the disciple-making work.
Why?
We don’t just want to report Bible studies;
we want to make disciples.
That’s what Jesus told us to do:
“Go . . . make disciples . . . ,
baptizing them.”
Now, when it comes to reporting Bible studies, we’re doing very well.
Worldwide, we’re reporting about ten million Bible studies.
And when you think of it, in many cases,
more than one person is sitting in on that study.
So it could be that between 12 and 15 million people
are studying the Bible with us.
But now, what about the “make disciples” part of it?
Well, every year, between 200 and 300 thousand people
are baptized.
So you can see that the “make disciples” part
is lagging behind the reporting Bible studies part.
Now, this trend has been a concern of the Governing Body for a number of years.
And we wondered,
‘Why is it that so many people are not taking a stand for the truth?’
You can probably think of a number of reasons yourself.
Some people, for example, are quite happy to learn what the Bible teaches,
but they’re not willing to act on what the Bible teaches.
They’re not willing to make drastic changes in their life.
Some may have studied through a whole book or maybe two,
but they haven’t been to a single meeting
—maybe one, maybe the Memorial once.
Well, they make us think of something
that Jehovah told the Israelites
back in the days of Ezekiel.
I’d like you to turn to Ezekiel chapter 33,
and we’re going to read verse 32.
Now, this was a description of the Israelites in Ezekiel’s day,
but I think you’ll find that the description fits pretty well
a few of our Bible students.
Ezekiel chapter 33 (I’ll give you a moment),
and we’re going to read verse 32:
“Look! You are to them like a romantic love song,
“sung with a beautiful voice
“and skillfully played on a stringed instrument.
“[But then notice this.]
“They will hear your words,
but no one will act on them.”
Doesn’t that describe some of our Bible students?
Or maybe the study isn’t regular; maybe it isn’t consistent.
Maybe the student often cancels
or maybe the publisher often cancels.
Well, if a study isn’t regular,
it’s pretty hard for the person to make progress, isn’t it?
And in many cases, kindhearted publishers
just can’t bring themselves to stop the study
when no progress is being made.
Or they may say: ‘If I stop the study, I won’t have a study.
I like having a Bible study.’
Well, we’re talking about progressive Bible studies, and that’s a challenge.
It’s not easy to conduct a progressive Bible study.
There are so many factors to consider.
For example: ‘How early do I bring in prayer?
‘How do I direct interest to the organization?
‘How early should I mention the meetings?
And what do I do if my Bible student doesn’t show up at the meeting?’
What about opposition?
That can be tricky.
Bring it up too soon, and you might scare him off.
Wait too long, and it may be too late.
And what about the ministry?
‘How do I encourage my Bible student
‘to share what he is learning with others?
‘These are a lot of challenges,
‘and don’t even mention helping my Bible student
to break a bad habit like smoking.’
Wouldn’t it be great if we could get some help
with some of these things?
Here’s more food for thought:
‘How do I make sure that the material
‘is really touching the student’s heart?

Well, the reaction, initially, was that we were very excited.

and this was a huge opportunity
to do just that.
But then as we had more meetings about it,
we found out what was going to be involved.
We suddenly got very nervous
because we found out about all the translation
and how soon everything had to be finished.
What impact did that have?
Audio/Video Services had never produced
an online program of this size before.
You’re talking
an 18-hour online regional convention that had to be produced
in a very short time.
Most years,
we just translate the outlines,
which are relatively easy,
and then we translate
all the convention videos and dramas.
But this year,
the translators not only had to do that work of translating the videos
but they had to translate the scripts for each talk and then arrange
for recording all of those talks.
It was a tremendous amount of work.
Some of us were saying:
“Can we postpone it?
“Can we ask
“to write back and say,
‘Brothers, please, can we do it later?’”
because we just thought
it was impossible to do.
The government in India
had announced a complete lockdown,
so overnight
we were without our offices,
our computer equipment,
our recording studios,
the level of connectivity we enjoyed.
We felt like a carpenter who’s asked to produce furniture
but has no access to his toolbox or his workshop.
That is a lot to contend with.
What are some unique solutions
that the teams came up with to meet those various challenges?
Well, there were amazing solutions.
One of the things that impressed me
was the recording studios that were made.
Normally the translators go into the RTO
or the branch to do the recording,
but now they had to make hundreds of makeshift studios in their homes.
How would translators accomplish the work
outside the branch with the power coming in and out?
Well, the brothers would wait,
and as soon as the power came, they would start working,
no matter what time it was in the day.
Our brothers are so dedicated that they accomplished the work.
Very touching.
Our brothers who do sign language recordings
had to record
in front of a camera,
but they also ideally needed
to have a background behind them
that was bright green or bright blue
so that their signing could be superimposed
onto another video.
And so some brothers were able to get a cloth.
Many of our brothers painted a wall in their house
this bright chartreuse color.
Admirable ingenuity—thank you.
One of the most interesting solutions
was that many of the translators around the world
in different branches would go
into their car late at night
when all the noise had subsided
in the neighborhood, and they would do the recording
inside the car.
Thank you and everyone working with you for being so willing to adapt.
In your opinion,
what made all of this possible?
Despite a global pandemic,
despite a lockdown
—none of those things
mattered to Jehovah’s organization.
What has shut down various other things throughout the world
proved to be no obstacle for Jehovah and his earthly organization.
And what a beautiful thing it is
to see this program be something that’s enjoyed by everyone worldwide!
Here, despite the conditions going on in the world around us,
Jehovah’s people are moving forward.
And you really see the fulfillment of Malachi 3:18,
where it says that ‘you will see a distinction
between those serving Jehovah and those who don’t.’

—the thousands of brothers and sisters around the world
who had a part in bringing these convention programs
to our brothers and sisters—
they’re just normal people like you and me,
but Jehovah uses normal people
to accomplish incredible things.
This convention has been a landmark convention
because of the content and the beautiful theme,
but we’ll also remember it for the way Jehovah helped us
to produce it in so many languages
for our brothers and sisters in the country and around the world.
Well, in translation, we like verbs,
and in Jehovah’s name, there’s a verb:
“He Causes to Become.”
This 2020 convention was proof
that Jehovah causes whatever he wants
to become to accomplish his purpose,
because if there’s a convention that Jehovah used
to give glory to his name, this is it.
What beautiful conviction!
Thank you, brothers.
Yes, Jehovah’s spirit helped ensure
that the work was accomplished in spite of many challenges,
but what were some of the blessings experienced once the work was done?

that maybe we didn’t quite get.
And maybe even because sometimes our minds drift,
it’s good, because we can go back and rewatch it.

a convention more international than this one.

to make a difficult situation turn out well
—that is, we’re together,

in order to obtain the videos.

all of these challenges.

about two months before the convention started.
It was cancer.
We had been married for 14 years,
and she was only 47.

so this left me with a gaping hole.

came just at the right time for me.

all the members of the Governing Body and its helpers to me personally.

because I am someone who is legally blind,

what was happening.

are things that I normally would have been curious about
and would have been asking somebody to help me understand.

knowing that the Governing Body loves us this much.

I speak Japanese.

like what we would have at international conventions.

one, two, three and start playing our videos at the same time.
This way we were able to watch and sing together.
It really felt like an international convention.

So then I wondered: ‘How is this going to work at home?
‘There won’t be a crowd, everyone singing together.
How’s it going to be?’
I thought I would really miss it, but then my family and I agreed
to sing the Kingdom melodies loudly, and it worked!
I have never seen my family sing so loudly.

And all during the time that the convention was being shown,
we were all exhibiting symptoms.
It was a really hard time.

it was as if the talks the brothers gave
were like hearing advice from a close friend
who was sitting right next to you
like they were right in the same room with us.
The convention is very positive;
it’s contagious.
It has really touched our hearts.
I truly feel the convention has touched my heart deeply.
Both my mom and my dad, who are right now struggling
with very serious illnesses,
were able to join me,
my brother, and my sister-in-law,
and we were together as a family in our living room.
We got to sing together and watch the assembly together,
which otherwise just would not have been possible.
Despite the struggles,
despite the limitations
that we may be facing,
none of that has stopped Jehovah from reaching out
and even being in our own living rooms during this convention.
Jehovah transforms something
that Satan is using right now to take away our joy
into something that gives us joy.
Think about it:
We’re watching the same spiritual program
at the same time with the same speakers, brothers from the Governing Body.
We never imagined that we would have this opportunity.
OK, are we all set?
OK, we’re ready whenever you are if you want to go ahead.
We are delighted that you could join us for this opening session
of the “Always Rejoice”! Convention of Jehovah’s Witnesses.
And when everything around you is chaotic,
the one thing you have is your relationship with Jehovah.
“I will walk in your truth.
Unify my heart to fear your name.”
But we discovered something we had lost
—joy.

or in the future, we will be able to continue to rejoice

that no matter what the circumstance we are in,
Jehovah will continue to feed us,
and we will continue to worship him.

we will “always rejoice in the Lord.”

Jehovah lived up to the meaning of his name:
“He Causes to Become.”

How encouraging!

will be released on January 18
in the Video on Demand section of JW Broadcasting.
Then I’ll be back in the studio next month
to introduce the last part of the program.
To conclude our January monthly program,
we’ll get to know brothers in the Central African Republic
during our video postcard.
As its name suggests, the Central African Republic
is near the exact center of the African continent.
Landlocked, it shares its border with six neighboring countries
and is comparable in size to France.
While it has two official languages —French and Sango—
there are also several other tribal languages spoken.
The Central African Republic is rich in natural resources,
such as diamonds, gold, and timber,
not to mention beautiful wildlife, such as antelope,
elephants,
baboons,
leopards, and many others that roam freely.
Sadly, this country has endured many years
of armed conflicts and civil unrest,
which has resulted in severe hardship for the people living there.
Despite these hardships, our brothers are working tirelessly
to provide spiritual relief.
For example, in the Bozoum Congregation,
there are some 70 publishers
and several pioneers.
Together, they’re conducting about 150 Bible studies!
Besides caring for their local territory,
the branch office has assigned the congregation
the care of three isolated groups.
These groups are up to 125 kilometers, or 78 miles,
away from Bozoum.
Reaching these groups is challenging for our brothers,
since there is no public transportation
and only 3 percent of the roads in the country
are paved.
Nevertheless, the Bozoum Congregation
regularly sends elders to give public talks
and conduct the Watchtower  Study in Bocaranga,
since there are no appointed brothers in that group of ten publishers.
Although there is civil unrest in Bocaranga,
the group is conducting some 30 Bible studies.
The Bocaranga brothers and sisters and the Bozoum Congregation
send their greetings to all of you
fellow Witnesses worldwide.
And we send our greetings back to all of our brothers
in the Central African Republic.
From the World Headquarters of Jehovah’s Witnesses,
this is JW Broadcasting!

en.text: Infectious diseases
have been around for a long time.
In the past, you may have just heard
about outbreaks in other places.
But what can you do
when a disease spreads close to home?
So much is out of your control.
It can be scary.
But there’s a lot you can do
to protect yourself and stay healthy.
Some of the most effective steps
are also the simplest,
like washing your hands often.
If you wash for at least 20 seconds,
soap and water can break up the virus
or bacteria and rinse it away.
A strong alcohol-based hand sanitizer
can work too.
Cough and sneeze into a tissue
or the inside of your elbow.
And avoid touching your face,
especially after you touch something else.
Follow instructions from the authorities.
That might mean staying home for a while,
wearing a mask when you go out,
or keeping the recommended safe distance
from other people.
And if you do get sick,
call a doctor right away.
Your emotional health is important too!
Too much bad news, unverified rumors,
even conflicting reports can cause anxiety.
Stay informed, but set limits
so you don’t feel overwhelmed.
Keep yourself occupied,
and stay connected with friends and family.
You might cheer them up
and feel a little better yourself.
There’s another aspect
of your health that’s important.
In the Bible, Jesus sought time alone
to pray and meditate.
Use some of your time
to take care of your spiritual health.
If you focus on a hope for a better future,
it’ll be easier to cope with challenges today.
Jehovah’s Witnesses keep their hope strong
by sharing it with others in whatever ways are safe.
They show people what the Bible teaches.
They invite them to their meetings too.
If possible, they meet in person.
If not, they have video meetings.
The Bible says at Isaiah 33:24
that someday no one will say: “I am sick.”
Until then, it says at Isaiah 30:15
that “your strength will be in keeping calm
and showing trust.”
So when things like this happen,
do your best to stay calm,
stay informed,
and stay healthy.

ko.text: 성경에 나오는 충실한 종들에 관한 기록은

성경 교리를 거짓으로 여긴다고 되어 있었죠.
여호와의 증인을 유아나 임산부 할 것 없이
유배를 면할 수 있는 방법을 제안받았습니다.
우리 가족을 유배하는 일을 맡은 담당관은
아버지가 여호와의 증인 조직을 탈퇴한다는 서류에 서명하게 하려고 설득했습니다.
그 제안을 받아들인 증인은 거의 없었습니다.
철도 인근에 있는 촌락들에서 지내게 되었습니다.

여호와의 증인을 불신하도록 제작된 선전 영화들이
저는 여호와의 증인을 염탐하라는 지시를 받았습니다.
그 질문에 대한 답을 찾을 수 있었습니다.
하지만 증인들에 대한 검찰의 전면 공격은
여호와께서 주시는 특별한 힘을 경험하게 됩니다.
그분은 늘 그 요청에 응답해 주십니다.
하느님의 백성은 끔찍한 신체적 학대에 더해
선전 영화 등을 통해 박해를 받았습니다.
하지만 니콜라이 비치코프의 예를 통해 확인할 수 있듯이,

en.text: At John 15:20, Jesus said:
“A slave is not greater than his master.
If they have persecuted me, they will also persecute you.”
How will we react when we are mistreated?
How will we find the strength to endure?
We have a record of faithful servants of old.
We know that Jehovah’s people can endure.
But we also have the record
of Jehovah’s Witnesses in modern times.
The following video draws on footage
from two previously released videos by the organization.
It highlights two outstanding examples:
our brothers in Germany during World War II
and our brothers in the former Soviet Union
in the years that followed the war.
It also reveals the tactics
that enemies of the truth consistently use
—to no avail—against Jehovah’s people.
Reviewing and meditating on the examples
of these faithful brothers and sisters
will prepare us for what lies ahead,
will fill us with courage, and will strengthen our faith.
On January 30, 1933,
Adolf Hitler comes to power.
Hitler gave the people jobs.
He restored their faith
in the fatherland.
He is hailed as their savior.
But the Witnesses could not give to a man what they believed belonged to God.
Thus, a battle line
was drawn over a simple greeting —“Heil Hitler.”
Jehovah’s Witnesses refused to say “Heil Hitler”
because it meant “Salvation comes from Hitler.”
At his job in a steel mill,
one Witness faced this test.
I was the only one among 2,000
who did not raise my hand
and did not return the German salute
—every day running the gauntlet, since I was required
to give the German salute, and I simply said,
“Good day.”
Children were drawn into the battle.
Six-year-old Paul Gerhard Kusserow,
like other Witness children, was pressured
by students and teachers.
As soon as I entered school,
the head teacher and the pupils confronted me
and tried to make me say, “Heil Hitler.”
More than 800 children were taken away from their Witness parents by the Gestapo.
In one German state after another, the police shut down meetings
of the Witnesses and prohibit their door-to-door preaching.
At first, there were nasty words,
sometimes a beating,
but soon enough, it led to the first arrests.
Starting in 1937, Jehovah’s Witnesses were given a purple triangle
as a sign.
Jehovah’s Witnesses
were the only religious group
that made up a separate category of inmates.
The Jehovah’s Witnesses received especially severe treatment.
The goal was to destroy this religious group;
there were to be no more Witnesses in Germany.
The Nazis, obsessed with breaking the Witnesses’ stubborn commitment,
made them an extraordinary offer.
Each Witness could buy
his freedom for a price: his signature
and his faith.
Witnesses in prisons and camps
were repeatedly handed a piece of paper and a pen.
Very few signed.
When I was to be released from prison,
I was given a paper to sign.
It required that I give up my faith
and recognize the German government as the highest authority,
place myself under the Hitler government,
and consider the Bible as a false doctrine.
I said, “That’s out of the question!”
The unity among the sisters and the brothers
—that gave us so much strength.
It was our aim to endure under all circumstances.
We never prayed to be set free.
We prayed for strength to endure.
Everything else was unimportant.
What mattered was standing up for Jehovah’s name.
On February 19, 1951,
the head of the security police presented a secret plan to Stalin.
All of Jehovah’s Witnesses
—including infants and pregnant women— would be exiled.
The plan was code-named “Operation North.”
Stalin approved it.
Interestingly, the Witnesses were offered a way to avoid deportation.
The man in charge of the deportation of our family
tried to persuade Father to sign a paper
renouncing the organization
of Jehovah’s Witnesses.
Few Witnesses, if any, accepted this offer.
Once in Siberia, the Witnesses were dropped off
at settlements along the rail lines.
The majority of the Witnesses
were forced to cut trees.
We recalled the time when the Israelites
lived in Egypt
and how they were forced to work.
We prayed, “God, make our faith stronger so that this work,
which is beyond our strength, will not shake us.”
Stalin’s death in 1953
brought hope of relief.
But relief would be a long time
in coming.
The new regime went on in the same course.
They arrested and sentenced us.
Most arrested Witnesses were sentenced to labor camps.
In court, they could not expect a fair trial.
Guilty verdicts had already been decided upon.
Under the Khrushchev administration,
special “reeducation” camps were set up,
designed to turn inmates from their beliefs.
During this period, propaganda films designed to discredit Jehovah’s Witnesses
were distributed throughout the USSR.
Whoever has studied persecution in the past
has seen that in one way or another,
persecution is always built on a lie.
The victim is slandered.
Besides using propaganda, for many years,
the KGB recruited informers to infiltrate Witness congregations.
For instance, in 1968, the KGB district director
offered Nikolai Bychkov an assignment.
He requested me
to spy on Jehovah’s Witnesses.
One Witness booklet that compared the teaching of evolution with the Bible
changed the KGB informer’s viewpoint.
No one could answer that question:
how life appeared.
In the Bible,
I could find answers to those questions.
In Khabarovsk in 1984, Nikolai Bychkov,
now a baptized Witness, and several fellow believers
were accused of anti-Soviet activities.
But the all-out attack on the Witnesses’ faith backfired
on the persecutors.
In Germany and in Soviet times,
they thought that you could get rid
of an idea by using extreme violence.
But it turned out that when an idea is strong,
it makes people strong.
So the outcome was just the opposite of what was expected.
In March 1991,
Jehovah’s Witnesses were legally registered in Russia.
I think it is frightening
only if you’ve never faced difficulties.
But once you face them, you know that special strength.
When we rely on Jehovah
—we ask for his guidance; we ask for his help—
we will always get it.
In addition to horrible physical treatment,
God’s people faced slander,
outright lies, and fabrications,
even in the form of propaganda films.
Opposers attempted to infiltrate our brotherhood with informants.
But as we saw in the example of Nikolai Bychkov,
such devious plans are in vain
when pitted against the truth from God’s Word.
As Professor Nikolai Gordienko noted,
“When an idea is strong, it makes people strong.”
What idea can be stronger
than the reality of our Father, Jehovah;
his reigning King, Jesus Christ;
and his Kingdom, now poised to thwart all opposition?
And so, what people can possibly be stronger
than Jehovah’s people?
As our brothers in Russia and other areas of the earth
face renewed opposition
and as we all face the prospect of being mistreated
just as our Master, Jesus, was,
we are determined to stand firm
and remain faithful no matter what the enemies of truth attempt.

cn.text: 在约翰福音15:20，耶稣说
“奴隶不比主人大
他们要是迫害了我，也会迫害你们。”
面对不公平的对待时
我们会有什么反应呢？
怎样才能得到力量能继续忍耐？
圣经里记载了很多
以往忠心崇拜耶和华的仆人
表现忍耐的例子
他们是我们的好榜样
不过，我们也有很多现代的好榜样可以学习
接下来的短片
节选了以往组织发行过的两部影片
影片里
讲述了两段令人印象深刻的经历
包括德国的弟兄在二战期间的一些经历
以及二战之后苏联的弟兄面对的情况
从影片我们可以看到
攻击耶和华子民的敌人
一直以来用的这些伎俩是没有用的
回顾和沉思这些弟兄姐妹忠心的好榜样
可以帮助我们做好准备
应付前头可能面对的考验
也可以强化我们的信心
1933年1月30日，希特勒开始掌权
希特勒使人民有工作做
使他们对祖国恢复信心
他被人民视为救主
但是耶和华见证人
不能把他们深信属于上帝的东西
给一个凡人
结果他们因为不愿意说“希特勒是救星”
就被纳粹党攻击
耶和华见证人拒绝说“希特勒是救星”
因为这样说就等于承认救恩来自希特勒了
一个弟兄在他工作的炼钢厂
就面对这样的考验
工厂里有2000个工人
只有我不愿意做德国式的敬礼
我因此受到别人的恶意批评
每逢要敬礼的时候
我只是说“希望你今天过得好”
孩子也受到了牵连
像其他耶和华见证人的孩子一样
6岁大的保罗·格哈德·库斯罗
也受到了来自同学和老师的很大压力
我一到学校
班主任和同学就强迫我说“希特勒是救星”
有800多个耶和华见证人的孩子
被盖世太保带走，跟他们的父母分离
在德国很多地方
警察纷纷禁止耶和华见证人举行聚会
也不准他们挨家挨户传道
起初他们只是恶言恐吓，有时出手打人
但不久后，他们就开始逮捕耶和华见证人了
从1937年开始
当局发给耶和华见证人
一个紫色的三角作为记号
在囚犯当中
他们是唯一一个收到这个记号的宗教团体
耶和华见证人受到了非常残酷的对待
政府决心要把这个宗教团体彻底消灭
他们不希望德国有任何耶和华见证人
纳粹党决心让耶和华见证人变得不忠
所以给他们一个特别的机会
让他们可以重获自由
这个机会就是只要他们在一份文件上签名
声明自己放弃信仰，他们就会重获自由
他们常常受到这样的引诱
但很少有人签名
我快要出狱的时候
官员让我在一张纸上签名
这是一份声明，说我会放弃自己的信仰
承认德国政府是最高的权威
我会听从希特勒政府的领导
承认圣经的道理是虚假的
我告诉他们
“我绝对不会签名！我连考虑都不需要。”
弟兄姐妹的团结，给我们非常大的力量
我们决心要在任何情况下，都保持忍耐
我们从没有祷告求上帝给我们自由
而是求上帝给我们力量，忍耐下去
其他事都不重要，重要的是拥护上帝的圣名
秘密警察的头子向斯大林献计
要放逐所有耶和华见证人，包括婴儿和孕妇
这个计划的代号是“北方行动”
斯大林批准了这个计划
不过
政府给耶和华见证人一个不被放逐的机会
负责放逐我们的那个军官
不断试图说服我爸爸签署文件
脱离耶和华见证人的组织
只有极少的耶和华见证人签署了文件
到了西伯利亚
耶和华见证人在铁路沿线的不同地方住了下来
大部分耶和华见证人都被迫以砍树为生
我们想起以色列人在埃及做苦工时的情况
我们祷告说
“上帝啊，求你使我们的信心更加坚定
不要让这些苦难动摇我们的信心。”
斯大林在1953年去世
这给耶和华见证人重获自由的希望
但这个希望还遥遥无期
新政权也用同样的方式对待我们
他们逮捕我们，把我们关在监狱里
耶和华见证人被捕后，大都被囚在劳改营里
在法庭上，他们得不到公平的审讯
因为他们早就被定罪了
在赫鲁晓夫执政时期
政府设立了一些改造营
专门用来改变囚犯的思想
在这段期间
丑化、污蔑耶和华见证人的宣传电影
在全苏联播放
任何研究过迫害史的人都会看出
迫害的理由往往都是人捏造出来的
受害人被恶意中伤
除了宣传手段，多年来
秘密警察也派人混进耶和华见证人的会众里
例如，在1968年
尼古拉·比奇科夫就被派去执行这个任务
我的任务是监视耶和华见证人的一举一动
这个间谍看了耶和华见证人的一本册子
比较了进化论和圣经，后来改变了观点
没有人能够解答
“生命从何而来？”这个问题
不过，这个看来没有人知道答案的问题
我在圣经里找到了答案
受了浸的尼古拉·比奇科夫和几个弟兄姐妹
被指控在哈巴罗夫斯克进行反政府的活动
不过，对耶和华见证人发动的全面攻击
最后却没有得逞
德国纳粹党和苏联政府都认为
使用暴力就可以叫人屈服
事实证明
如果你的信念够坚定，你就可以保持忍耐
因此，当局的迫害丝毫没有动摇他们的信心
耶和华见证人在俄罗斯合法注册了
如果你从未面对过困难
逼迫来的时候，你会害怕
但如果你勇敢面对困难
你就会体验到那种非凡的力量
我们只要依赖耶和华
求他指引我们，帮助我们
我们总会得到力量
政府不仅在身体上虐待和折磨上帝的子民
也撒谎捏造事实
甚至用一些宣传电影来丑化上帝的子民
那些反对者还派出间谍
混进我们的会众里
但是，就像尼古拉·比奇科夫的例子那样
那些跟耶和华对抗的阴谋和伎俩
是绝对不会成功的
正如尼古拉·戈尔季延科教授所说的
如果一个人的信念很坚定，他就会很坚强
我们相信天父耶和华
也相信君王耶稣基督以及他的王国
很快会摧毁所有敌人
还有什么信念比这更强的吗？
那么
有什么人能比耶和华的子民更坚强呢？
今天我们在俄罗斯和其他地方的弟兄姐妹
再一次受到迫害
将来我们所有人
都有可能像主耶稣那样受到不公的对待
不管我们受到怎样的迫害
我们都决心对耶和华保持忠贞，毫不动摇

en.text: Our text comments contain this thought
(if you look about halfway down,
there’s a sentence that says):
“Feeling tender compassion
will move us to acts of kindness.”
It’s interesting that the Bible
in different places
links those two qualities together.
For example, Ephesians 4:32 states:
“Become kind to one another, tenderly compassionate.”
Insight on the Scriptures  defines compassion this way:
“A sympathetic awareness of another’s suffering or adversity
coupled with a desire to alleviate it.”
So we have the awareness —we have the feeling—
along with that desire to act kindly.
But sadly, as The Watchtower  once mentioned:
“The moral climate of our time . . .
has killed compassion in the hearts of so many.”
A “Watching the World” item highlighted that some years ago in the Awake!
In Italy, a six-year-old girl and her father were driving to the beach.
As they entered a tunnel, the father,
who was only in his 30’s, suddenly suffered a heart attack.
Before he died, he told his little girl to find her way home.
She struggled out of the tunnel,
repeatedly blown over by gusts of wind
from cars that zipped by without slowing.
Scratched, bleeding, and in tears,
she walked along the highway for half an hour,
ignored by hundreds of passing cars filled with vacationers
until finally one car stopped to help.
Newspaper editorials around the country asked searching questions,
such as whether the country’s affluence had made it lose
some of the warmth and compassion
for which it had long been famous.
One newspaper mentioned:
“Along the happy road of vacation,
“there were no scheduled stops
for attending to the pain of others.”
Well, that account sadly illustrates the world that we live in.
Let’s talk a little bit more about this quality of compassion.
We’ll consider when compassion should not be shown,
we’ll look at an example of Jehovah’s compassion,
and then we’ll consider some practical ways
that we can show compassion.
First, there are times when compassion should not be shown.
For example, if someone deliberately persists in sin,
it would be wrong to feel that we
should compassionately shield them from discipline.
See, that would be misplaced compassion.
Let’s notice an example in ancient Israel.
Please turn with me to Deuteronomy chapter 13 —Deuteronomy 13.
If you look at verse 6,
the Israelites were commanded that if a brother, child,
and you’ll notice there some expressions such as “cherished wife”
or “closest companion,”
if any of those were to urge a person to “serve other gods,”
notice the instruction in verse 8:
“You must not give in to him or listen to him, nor should you show pity
“or feel compassion or protect him;
instead, you should kill him without fail.”
Now, why was that so important?
Why was it important not to show compassion?
Well, verse 11: “Then all Israel will hear and become afraid,
“and they will never again
do anything bad like this among you.”
So it was for a protection for the nation.
If someone tried to turn an Israelite from serving Jehovah,
that was not the time to show compassion.
Yielding to pressure to show compassion when it’s contrary to God’s will
can have serious consequences.
So we certainly need to avoid misplaced compassion.
Now let’s consider an example of Jehovah’s compassion.
Turn with me to Exodus chapter 3 —Exodus chapter 3.
While tending to his father-in-law’s sheep,
Moses saw something he’d never seen before.
And I daresay none of us have ever seen it either.
Moses saw a thornbush on fire,
but it wasn’t being consumed.
So Moses decided to go and investigate.
By means of an angel, Jehovah spoke to Moses from the midst of the fire.
And notice what he said in verse 5:
“Do not come any nearer.
“Remove your sandals from your feet,
because the place where you are standing is holy ground.”
So just think: Because the holy God was present representatively,
the ground itself became holy.
Now, keep that thought in mind; we’re going to come back to it.
Let’s focus now on Jehovah’s compassion for his people who were suffering in Egypt.
Notice verse 7: “Jehovah added:
“‘I have certainly seen the affliction of my people who are in Egypt,
“‘and I have heard their outcry because of those who force them to work;
I well know the pains they suffer.’”
So Jehovah wasn’t blind to the misery of his people.
He wasn’t deaf to their cries for help.
Their anguish became his own.
Did you notice the expression at the end of the verse?
“I well know the pains they suffer.”
Regarding the phrase “I well know,” one reference work states:
“The expression implies personal feeling,
tenderness, and compassion.”
So Jehovah’s words here reveal a deeply concerned,
caring, and compassionate God.
And what would Jehovah do?
Would he act kindly on that compassion?
Well, we know he was going to.
In verse 10, in part, Jehovah commissioned Moses:
“Bring my people . . . out of Egypt.”
You know, this account should be encouraging to us.
We can be sure that Jehovah sees our adversities.
He hears our cries for help.
He knows the pain that we suffer at times.
But Jehovah just doesn’t feel  compassion for us.
No, he’s moved to act kindly.
Why?
First Peter 5:7 —he cares for each one of us.
God’s compassion also gives us reason for hope.
One sister who struggled with depression and discouragement
found comfort in this account about Moses and the thornbush.
Remember the holy ground that we read about in verse 5.
The sister said:
“If Jehovah can make even the dirt holy,
then maybe there is a little hope for me.”
See, she’d benefited from Jehovah’s compassion.
Well, so far we’ve seen the need to avoid misplaced compassion.
We’ve considered Jehovah’s example of not only feeling  compassion
but acting  kindly on it.
How can we imitate him?
One quality that can help is love
—unselfish love— of neighbor.
Let’s consider two practical ways that can help us
—that we can show this type of compassion.
First, compassion will help us to avoid
reacting harshly when others make mistakes.
Remember that earlier we quoted Ephesians 4:32,
linking kindness and compassion.
Well, let’s turn to the verse just previous to it
—Ephesians 4 and let’s read verse 31— Ephesians 4:31.
Keep that thought in mind: Compassion will help us
to avoid reacting harshly when others make mistakes.
Verse 31: “Put away from yourselves every kind of malicious bitterness,
“anger, wrath, screaming, and abusive speech,
as well as everything injurious.”
And then verse 32 says: “But [there’s the connector, but]
“become kind to one another,
tenderly compassionate.”
So whether at home, in the congregation,
at Bethel, on construction sites —wherever we may be—
let’s allow love, this unselfish love of neighbor,
to cause us to show compassion
and avoid reacting harshly when others make mistakes.
A second way that love can help us to be compassionate
is that it will help us to avoid the imperfect tendency
to abuse power.
Colossians 3:12 states:
“Clothe yourselves with the tender affections of compassion, kindness.”
There are the two linked together again,
and then the verse adds “humility [or “lowliness of mind,” ftn.].”
The Watchtower  once made this point about that verse:
“Lowliness of mind enables us to put ourselves
“in the position of those under our supervision.
“To be compassionate involves being humble and reasonable
“rather than hard to please.
“Efficiency should not be an excuse
for treating people as mere parts of a machine”
—good points to keep in mind.
So those are two ways that love can help us to be compassionate:
Avoid reacting harshly when others make mistakes,
and avoid the imperfect tendency to abuse power.
So while the moral climate has killed compassion
in the hearts of so many today,
we want to be known for our compassion.
Of course, never would we want to display misplaced compassion
if someone deliberately persists in sin.
Rather, we want to imitate Jehovah
and kindly act on our feelings of compassion for those in need.
So as we go about our day, let’s look for ways
that we can heed the admonition there at Ephesians 4:32:
“Become kind to one another, tenderly compassionate.”

cn.text: 今天引述的《守望台》资料提到了一句话
“慈怜的心会推动我们待人仁慈”
圣经经常把“怜恤之心”
跟“仁慈”联系在一起
例如以弗所书4:32
“要以仁慈相待，也要怀着温情体恤别人”
关于怜恤之心，《洞悉圣经》说
“有怜恤之心的人会关注和同情困苦的人
渴望为他们解困。”
所以我们不单只是同情别人
我们还会渴望付出行动去帮助别人
但很可惜，《守望台》曾经提到
“当今世风日下
......许多人的怜恤之心都被扼杀了。”
《警醒！》杂志的“世闻点滴”专栏里
提到了一件事
在意大利有一个爸爸
开车带着六岁的女儿要到海边
他们开车，经过一个隧道
当时才三十几岁的爸爸突然心脏病发作
在他去世前，他告诉女儿要想办法回家
这小女孩艰难地走出隧道
好多车子呼啸而过，没有人停下来帮助她
她受了伤，流着血
她沿着高速公路满脸都是眼泪
她走了半个小时
很多要去玩的人开车匆匆经过她
最后总算有一辆车停下来
当地的报纸向民众发问
“是不是因为人民变得有钱了
就失去了本来有的温情和怜恤之心呢？”
一份报纸说
“奔向快乐假期的人
根本没空停下来去理会别人的伤痛。”
这个新闻其实就是现在冷漠世界的写照
现在让我们谈谈怜恤之心
首先，什么时候不该表现怜恤之心？
然后是耶和华怎样表现怜恤之心？
最后是，我们要怎样向人表现怜恤之心？
在有些情况下，我们不应该表现怜恤之心
例如，一个人经常故意做不对的事
如果我们同情他，不让他受到惩罚
这样就不对了，怜恤之心就用错地方了
让我们看看古代以色列人的例子
申命记第13章
在第6节，耶和华吩咐以色列人
“假如你的亲兄弟，或是你的儿女
［请你留意接下来圣经说］或是你的爱妻
或是你最亲密的朋友”
如果他们引诱你去崇拜其他神
请你看第8节说什么
“你都千万不要依从他，也不可听他的话
你不可同情他，也不要可怜或包庇他
一定要把他处死。”
为什么在这个场合
我们不应该表现怜恤之心呢？
11节说
“全以色列听见了就会害怕
再也不敢在你那里做这种坏事。”
所以目的是为了保护以色列人
如果有人企图让以色列人崇拜别神
以色列人就不该对他表现怜恤之心
如果我们迫于压力对他表现怜恤之心
就会损坏自己跟耶和华的关系
所以我们不要把怜恤之心用错了地方
现在我们看看耶和华怎样表现怜恤之心
在出埃及记的第3章
当摩西正在牧放他岳父的羊群的时候
他看到了一件异乎寻常的事
我相信我们没有任何人看过这样的事
摩西看到荆棘丛着了火却没有烧掉
所以他决定走向前去查看
在烧着的荆棘丛中
耶和华通过天使向摩西说话
在第5节说
“不要再走近了
把你的鞋脱下来
因为你站的地方是神圣的。”
仅是因为代表上帝的天使在这里
这里就变成神圣的
请你们记住这个要点
我们一会儿再来谈谈
先来谈谈
上帝怎样对受苦的子民表现怜恤之心
在第7节，耶和华说
“我的子民在埃及的苦况，我确实看见了
他们被监工压迫而发出的哀号，我也听见了
我清楚知道他们的痛苦。”
耶和华没有对他们的苦况
视而不见，充耳不闻
耶和华感同身受
你留意到经文的后半部怎么说吗？
“我清楚知道他们的痛苦。”
经文说“我清楚知道”
一本参考书说
“这个短语流露出一种个人的关怀
和怜恤之心。”
耶和华说的话，显示他深深关注自己的子民
耶和华会做什么呢？
他会帮助以色列人吗？
耶和华会帮助以色列人
第10节，耶和华对摩西说
“带我的子民......离开埃及。”
耶和华说的话让我们很感动
我们可以确信耶和华看得见我们的痛苦
他听得到我们的呼求，他知道我们身处逆境
耶和华不仅仅同情我们
他还会采取行动帮助我们
为什么呢？
彼得前书5:7说，他关心我们
上帝的怜恤之心给我们希望
一个姐妹曾受抑郁沮丧的情绪困扰
她读了摩西在荆棘丛的那段记载后
从中得到了不少鼓励
她说
“如果耶和华能够使泥土也变得圣洁
那么看来我还是有希望的。”
她从上帝的怜恤之心得到了安慰
我们学习了不该把怜恤之心用错地方
我们也看到了耶和华的榜样
不仅仅同情人，还会付诸行动
我们怎么效法他呢？
就是要表现无私的爱
来看看两种情况
有怜恤之心的人会怎么做？
首先，当别人犯错的时候
有怜恤之心的人不会严厉数落他
你还记得吗？
以弗所书4:32
把仁慈和怜恤之心放在一起谈
现在我们看看前一节经文
以弗所书4:31
请大家记得，当别人犯错的时候
有怜恤之心的人会避免严厉地数落他
31节说
“你们要除掉一切恶毒、怒气、愤恨
叫骂、伤人的话，以及一切有害的事。”
请留意32节说什么
“要以仁慈相待，也要怀着温情体恤别人”
无论是在家里、会众、伯特利、建筑工地
无论任何地方，我们都要有无私的爱
这样我们就能表现怜恤之心
当别人犯错的时候
我们就不会严厉地数落他
我们来谈谈第二个情况
爱让人有怜恤之心
这样的人会避免滥用权力
歌罗西书3:12说
“就要穿上温暖的怜恤之情、仁慈”
这两种特质又放在一起谈
还加上“谦卑”，就是“卑微”的意思
《守望台》曾经有以下的评论
“如果我们有权监管别人
谦卑的思想可以帮助我们设身处地
体贴别人的处境
富于怜恤的人会虚怀若谷、通情达理
而不是难以讨好
人不该以讲求效率为借口
把别人视作机器的零件。”
所以两个表现怜恤之心的情况是
一，别人犯错时，不要严厉数落他
二，也要避免滥用权力
虽然现在世风日下
很多人的怜恤之心都被扼杀了
但我们却要满怀怜恤之心
当然，如果有人常常故意犯罪
我们绝不想向他表现怜恤之心
而对于那些需要帮助的人
我们则要效法耶和华，对他们表现怜恤之心
所以
今天让我们把以弗所书4:32的劝告用出来
“要以仁慈相待，也要怀着温情体恤别人”

ko.text: 사람들을 직접 만나고 싶다는 생각도 드실 겁니다.
조금 덜 지키고 싶은 마음이 생길 수도 있습니다.
전 세계적으로 그 어느 때보다도 많은 사람이
마음을 완고하게 하는 자는 재앙에 빠진다.”
우리가 계속 조심해야 하는 이유가 무엇인지,
또 어떻게 그렇게 할 수 있는지 살펴볼 것입니다.
또 계속 조심하는 것이 유익하다는 것을 잘 보여 주는
우선, 우리가 자신과 다른 사람들을 보호해야 하는 이유에 대해 생각해 보겠습니다.
바이러스에 걸리지 않을 거야’라고 생각하기가 쉽습니다.
우리가 조심하고 계속 유의해야 할 충분한 이유가 있습니다.
소중한 가족과 친구를 잃은 형제 자매들을 생각하면
지난 한 달 동안 감염된 형제들의 수가
그 이전 기간을 모두 합한 것보다
계속 조심하며 경계를 늦추지 않는 것이
형제들의 안전을 지키는 데 어떻게 도움이 되었는지
피터 캐닝 형제의 말을 들어 보겠습니다.
그래서 사업장과 식당이 다시 문을 열었고,
‘공개 증거와 같은 봉사를 다시 할 수 있지 않을까’ 하고 생각했죠.
공개 증거를 할 수 있을 만큼
몇 주 만에 크로아티아의 감염자 수는
지금은 매일 수천 명씩 늘어나고 있습니다.
세 가지 주요 원칙을 설명해 주었습니다.
현재의 방역 수칙이 불편할 수 있지만
이웃을 진심으로 사랑한다는 것을 보여 줄 수 있습니다.
셋째, 안일한 태도를 가져서는 안 됩니다.
따라서 우리는 이렇게 자문해 보아야 합니다.
안일한 태도를 피한다는 걸 보여 주는가?’
감염을 피할 수 있는 방법을 기억하십시오.
다른 사람들에게 바이러스를 퍼뜨릴 수 있습니다.
다른 사람과 밀접 접촉을 할 경우에는
코로나바이러스 감염을 예방할 수 있는 가장 좋은 방법은
jw.org 웹사이트에서 영어로 볼 수 있고
곧 다른 언어들로도 볼 수 있을 겁니다.
미국의 한 현지 번역 사무실의 업무를 원격으로 지원하고 있는
그런데 가족 중 많은 사람이 감염됐어요.
그 후 가족 몇 명이 병원에 입원했어요.
아직도 일부 가족들이 아파서 병원에 입원해 있지요.
가족들과 정말 오랜 세월을 함께 보냈는데
바이러스에 감염되어 있을 수 있다고 생각해요.
그렇게 해야 한다는 걸 알 수 있죠.
좋은 사람들의 생명을 많이 앗아 갔습니다.
그들의 밭을 돌볼 사람도 아무도 없지요.
계속 조심하는 것이 중요하다는 걸 알 수 있습니다.
우리 가족은 바이러스에 걸리지 않을 거라고 안심하지 마십시오.
우리는 여러분과 여러분의 가족을 위해 기도합니다.
우리는 “아무도 ‘내가 병들었다’고 말하지 않을” 때가 올 것이라는
어떠한 어려움도 이겨 낼 수 있을 것이라고 확신합니다.
여러분께 중앙장로회의 따뜻한 인사를 전해 드립니다.

en.text: It’s my great pleasure
to speak for a few minutes
to you dear, beloved servants of Jehovah.
As you well know, we’ve been dealing
with the effects of this pandemic for a long time.
Are you tired of wearing a mask?
tired of physical distancing?
No doubt you miss getting together in person.
Because this is lasting so long,
it may be tempting to lower your guard
and ease up on the precautions we’ve been taking.
But as you’re probably aware,
case numbers have risen sharply
in one country after another.
In fact, case numbers and deaths worldwide
are higher than they have ever been
at any point during the pandemic.
This is not a time to let down our guard.
Proverbs 28:14 says:
“Happy is the man
“who is always on guard,
“but whoever hardens his heart
will fall into calamity.”
If we’re “always on guard” like a watchman at his post,
that can help us avoid the calamity.
In this update, we’d like to discuss
why we need to stay safe
and how we can do so.
And we’ll hear some experiences
that highlight the benefits of keeping on guard.
First, let’s talk about why we need
to protect ourselves and others.
As the months have gone by
and if we or our family have not contracted COVID-19,
it can be easy to think,
‘My family and I won’t get the virus.’
The Bible warns us, though,
about being overconfident.
First Corinthians 10:12 says:
“So let the one who thinks he is standing
beware that he does not fall.”
In line with that principle, rather than being overconfident
when it comes to our safety and thinking, ‘It can’t happen to me,’
we have good reason to “beware”
and remain cautious.
Sadly, as of December 20,
more than 7,500
of our brothers and sisters worldwide
have died from COVID-19.
Our hearts go out to those
who have lost dear family members and friends.
And, unfortunately,
the tragic effects of this pandemic
are not over.
Some branches have reported two to three times more cases
among the brothers in just the last month
than they’ve had this entire year!
So we need to stay safe.
In the following video,
note how Brother Peter Canning
from the Croatia branch
explains how vigilance
is helping our brothers stay as safe as possible.
At the beginning of June, life in Croatia
seemed to be getting back to normal.
Some days, there were no new reported cases
of the virus in the entire country.
So businesses and restaurants reopened,
and tourists flooded back into Croatia.
Some brothers wondered,
‘Can we restart certain activities such as public witnessing?’
Well, shortly after that, as a safety precaution,
the Governing Body directed all branches
not to resume public witnessing until further notice.
At first, this level of caution was not easy to understand,
as conditions seemed relatively safe for public witnessing.
But what a wise decision it proved to be!
Within weeks, the number of cases in Croatia began to rise.
And now there are thousands being infected every day.
Our experience has made us even more determined
to pay close attention to the direction coming from the organization
and to be ready to follow it.
We cannot let our guard down.
As Brother Canning said,
we should not let down our guard.
So, what will help us stay safe?
Well, back in June, in Governing Body Update #4,
Brother Morris stated
three key principles
to serve as a guide.
It was good advice then
and, with the infection rates rising,
it’s really good advice now.
Let’s review those principles.
Number one:
Place a high value on life.
Although the precautions you are taking
may be inconvenient, remember,
they protect you and your family’s lives.
Number two: Listen to the authorities.
When we follow their safety guidelines,
we show respect for Jehovah’s arrangement
and demonstrate that we really care about our neighbors.
Number three: Do not develop a casual attitude.
As this situation stretches on,
please don’t lower your guard.
Those are three excellent principles.
But now, here’s a question to ask yourself:
‘Do my decisions show
‘that I place a high value on life,
‘listen to the authorities,
and have not developed a casual attitude?’
Whatever decisions you make, consider this:
Your decisions affect not just yourself
but your household,
your brothers and sisters, and your community.
That’s a sobering thought, isn’t it?
As you consider how you and your family
will handle activities in the coming months,
we urge you
to keep following
the basic safety guidelines.
Remember how COVID-19 is spread
and what you can do to protect yourself.
Here’s a brief overview.
Health experts agree
that the main way the virus spreads
is through the air.
So when someone infected coughs, sneezes,
speaks, or even breathes,
they can spread the virus.
Even if someone infected with the virus
doesn’t have symptoms,
he or she can still spread the virus to others.
There’s an even higher risk
if we’re in close contact with others,
in crowded places,
or indoors.
One of the best ways to prevent the spread of COVID-19
is to wear a mask
and maintain physical distancing.
To review other precautions you can take to protect yourself,
we’ve created a new whiteboard animation
entitled Virus Outbreaks
—What You Can Do.
This video is now available in English
on jw.org
and will be available in other languages soon.
Please take the time to watch it.
No doubt you’d agree
that it takes effort to remain vigilant,
but how can that benefit us?
Do you recall what we read earlier
in Proverbs 28:14?
“Happy is the man who is always on guard.”
In this video interview,
notice how Sister Louise Slender,
who is a remote volunteer
with a remote translation office in the United States,
has benefited by remaining on guard.
You’ll also see
the tragic impact
that COVID-19 has had
on her non-Witness relatives.
I live on the Navajo land,
a place called Tuba City, Arizona.
When it came (the pandemic),

ko.text: 지난 여름에 누매어 부부와 저희 부부는
특별 지역 대회에 참석할 수 있었습니다.
중계로 보신 분들을 포함하여 총 참석자 수는 2만 1914명이며
형제들의 연합이 이 대회에서 얼마나 잘 나타났는지
조지아에서 특별 지역 대회를 열도록 승인됐다고
교습 위원회가 알려 줬을 때 정말 기뻤죠.
자세한 지침이 주어졌고, 책임 있는 형제들이 임명되어
열심 있는 형제 자매들이 전국 각지에서 돕기 위해
많은 자원봉사자가 교육을 받기 위해 기꺼이 여러 시간씩 여행했습니다.
그 일을 하는’ 사람들의 태도와 연합을 축복하셨죠.
이 자원봉사자들은 특별 지역 대회 준비를 돕기 위해
자원하는 태도 덕분에 모든 게 제때에 마련되었죠.
거기 가면 어떻게 사랑하는지 보게 될 거라고 말했는데,
우리는 용감하게 여호와 하느님과 그 백성 편에 섭니다.
스페인, 그 밖의 여러 나라에서 온 형제들을 만난 건
형제들을 평생 알고 지낸 것 같았죠.
우리의 편이 우리의 적보다 많다는 확신이 더욱더 강해집니다.
우릴 집에 데려가서 먹여 주고 함께 봉사도 나가고요.
현지 문화를 맛보게 해 주는 것뿐 아니라
여러 달 동안 열심히 준비한 현지 전도인들이
사랑을 나타낼 기회를 갖게 하는 것이었습니다.
우린 사랑 많은 형제들로 이루어진 세계적인 가족입니다.
분열도 없고 차별도 없는 진짜 가족이죠.
이 경험으로 신세계를 조금 맛본 것 같다고들 합니다.
한 아버지 아래 같은 가족이 되고
우린 진짜 형제 자매들이 되는 것입니다.
우리 모두에게는 한 아버지, 여호와께서 계십니다.

en.text: This past summer,
the Noumairs and Susan and I
had the privilege to attend
the special convention in Tbilisi, Georgia.
We had delegates from 18 different countries.
Our total attendance, including those tied in,
with 208 baptized.
The unity of our brotherhood
was on display as you will see in this brief video.
When the Teaching Committee informed us that we had been approved to hold
a special convention in Georgia, we were thrilled.
They provided detailed direction,
and responsible brothers were appointed
to oversee the daunting task
of caring for nearly 2,500 delegates from more than ten countries.
Local brothers and sisters from all over the country
eagerly volunteered to assist.
Many volunteers were willing to travel several hours each way for training.
Jehovah blessed the unity
and willing spirit of those who were
‘courageous and strong and went to work.’
These hardworking brothers and sisters were
often willing to use their own material resources
to support the special convention preparations.
Because of their willing spirit,
everything was ready on time.
A brother told me when we got on the plane
that you’re taught to love, but when you get there,
you’re going to be shown how to love —and that happened.
We landed at midnight, and they were there ready to hug us.
It was awesome!
With Jehovah’s help, I can fight!
With Jehovah’s help, I can win!
We are the victors.
We win.
We courageously stay with Jehovah God and his people.
It’s absolutely amazing to have brothers from Azerbaijan, Armenia,
Turkmenistan, Poland, United States,
Spain, and many others countries.
And it’s like we’ve known our brothers all our life,
but yet we’re just now meeting them.
Our united brotherhood gives us yet
another reason for confidence
that there are more with us than against us.
No matter where you go, the friends are there.
They’ll take you home; they’ll feed you;
they’ll go out in service with you.
The purpose of the evening-gathering program
was not only to give a taste of the local culture
but was also an opportunity
for local publishers who worked on the program for months
to demonstrate their love toward their visiting brothers and sisters.
It’s amazing!
We don’t want to go back home.
No!
The love of the brothers and the way
that we’re an international, complete family
—it’s not separate; it’s not segregated; it is a family.
And that experience is like nothing ever.
It’s very touching.
We kept hearing that this experience is a little taste of what the new world
will be like when everyone on the planet Earth
will be of the same family,
will truly love each other, have the same Father
—and that’s absolutely what makes us brothers and sisters.
We all have the same Father —our Father, Jehovah.

亚美尼亚、土库曼斯坦、波兰、美国

ko.text: 우린 이미 첫째 딸 레니타가 있었는데,
쌍둥이가 태어나게 될 거라는 말을 들었어요.
그때 우린 진리에 막 들어왔고 경험도 부족했습니다.
무엇보다 영적으로 튼튼하게 기를 수 있을까?
어떻게 여호와를 사랑하고 그분을 섬기도록 가르칠 수 있을까?’
그 성구는 좋은 재료로 가정을 세우는 것이
가족이 영적 일과를 잘 따르는 게 자녀들에게는 참 중요해요.
아내와 제가 영적으로 튼튼한 기초를 놓아야 했습니다.
자녀들에게 좋은 본을 보여 주어야 했어요.
부모님이 늘 개인 연구를 하시던 모습이 생각이 나요.
한 번은 아버지께서 거실로 나오셔서 이렇게 말씀하셨어요.
밤낮으로 그분의 법을 낮은 소리로 읽으라’고 나오잖아.
가족이 매일 소리를 내서 성경을 읽는 거지.
부모님은 단순한 생활을 하셨고, 저희 집엔 값비싼 물건들이 없었어요.
부모님은 늘 시간제 일을 하셨고 아버진 파이오니아를 하셨죠.
차가 말썽을 부릴 때가 자주 있었는데,
집회 가기 직전에 고장이 나기도 했죠.
처음엔 ‘집회에 안 가도 되겠구나’ 하고 생각했죠.
그래서 우리 다섯 명은, 아버진 정장을 입고,
치마 입은 여자 네 명은 집회 가방을 들고 걸어갔죠.
집회에 빠져서는 안 된다는 걸 배웠어요.
부모님은 가족이 함께 즐거운 시간을 보내는 걸
오늘 하루는 어땠는지, 집회는 어땠는지 이야기했죠.
그런 시간들 덕분에 우리 가족은 더 가까워졌어요.
아무리 바빠도 하던 일을 멈추시고 저와 이야기할 시간을 내셨어요.
하던 일보다 절 더 중요하게 생각하신다는 걸 느꼈죠.
다른 문제들도 편안하게 말씀드릴 수 있었어요.
왜냐면 부모님이 제 감정을 이해해 주시고
제가 하는 말을 화내지 않고 잘 들어 주신다는 걸 알게 됐거든요.
성경에 근거해서 생각하고 묵상하는 방법을 가르쳐 주신 건
파이오니아 같은 전 시간 봉사를 목표로 삼도록 격려해 주셨습니다.
우리 셋 다 시간제 일을 하고 있었어요.
그런데 우리 가족과 가까운 한 자매가 이런 말을 해 줬어요.
딸인 네가 전 시간 직장을 구해야 하지 않겠니?
그래야 부모님이 좀 더 안정적인 생활을 할 수 있지.”
그런 대화를 나눈 후에 저는 파이오니아를 중단하려고 했어요.
하지만 부모님이 그렇게 하는 걸 좋아하지 않으실 거란 걸 알고 있었죠.
우리가 여호와를 섬기는 데 젊은 시절을 사용하길 바라셨으니까요.
남편과 저는 제145기 길르앗 학교에 초대받았습니다.
그 감사함을 말로 다 표현할 수가 없네요.
부모님은 저희 세 자매를 영적으로 좋은 환경에서 키워 주셨습니다.
저는 많은 문제들을 겪지 않을 수 있었습니다.
그리고 여호와의 방식으로 양육해 주셔서 감사해요.

en.text: We already had our firstborn, Renita.
And then I was told that we were going to have twins.
We were new in the truth and inexperienced.
So I was saying to myself:
‘How can I take care of my children, not only physically but more so spiritually?
‘How will I be able to teach them to love Jehovah,
to worship Jehovah?’
And 1 Corinthians 3:10
shows us the importance
of raising a family
by using good quality materials.
So having a spiritual routine is very important for the children.
My wife and I would have to lay a good spiritual foundation.
We would have to set a good example for our children.
As long as I could remember, I would always see my parents studying,
doing personal Bible study.
I remember Dad—one time, he came to us in the living room,
and he said, “You know, I was reading Psalm 1:2,
“where it said we should find ‘delight in the law of Jehovah
and read in an undertone day and night.’”
He said, “What if we do this as a family project,
like, we read the Bible every day out loud together?”
And my parents were very simple, you know.
They didn’t require a lot of fancy things.
They were content.
Mom and Dad always worked part-time.
Dad pioneered, so money was limited.
Sometimes the car we had wasn’t the most reliable,
and it would break down right before the meeting.
I remember when our car broke down.
Initially I thought, ‘Oh, we’re not going to go to the meeting.’
Mom and Dad would say: “Well, the car broke down.
There’s a meeting tonight, so let’s walk.”
So there are the five of us —my dad in his suit,
the four women would be in our dresses with our book bags.
And so that taught me not to let obstacles
and anxieties prevent me from going to my meetings.
Spending quality time was very important to my parents,
especially after the meetings.
We would change into our pajamas, grab a snack,
go to the living room, and just start talking
about how our day went and how the meeting went.
Just those special moments
—they brought us closer together.
I saw that Dad,
no matter how busy he was,
would drop what he was doing and look at me and talk.
I knew I was more important to him than what he was doing.
I remember a time when I had a crush on a boy.
My parents reasoned with me.
I felt very comfortable, you know, after that point, to maybe talk
about other things because I could see that my parents
were not going to be angry at me.
You know, they were going to listen to me and what I was feeling.
One of the blessings that Mom and Dad gave me
was teaching me how to think
and meditate on scriptures.
They encouraged us to set full-time service,
or pioneering, as a goal.
We all worked part-time, me and my siblings.
And I remember one close family friend
said to me: “You know, your parents are getting older.
“You know, you’re their daughter, and you should probably work full-time.
That way they’d have more of an easy life.”
After that sister’s conversation, I almost gave up
on pioneering, but I knew deep down
that my parents would not be happy about that.
They wanted us to spend our youth serving Jehovah.
My husband and I were invited to attend
the 145th class of Gilead, and that was like a dream come true.
I have to thank my parents for that
because they always supported me through the years.
I couldn’t have done it without them,
and for that I’ll be forever grateful.
I really do thank my parents
for the upbringing that they gave me.
I have a very happy life.
I’m thankful that I was able
to avoid a lot of heartache,
and that’s because my parents raised me
in the truth and in Jehovah’s way.
Children are born imitators,
and they’re going to imitate our example.
I want to thank Jehovah for what our family is now.
To see all of us in the pioneer work
—all five of us are pioneering— thank you, Jehovah.

cn.text: 我们已经有一个女儿叫雷妮塔

如何崇拜他

之后我们会聊聊

让我们全家人更亲密了

他都会放下手边的事跟我说说话，聊一聊
这让我知道
我比他手上正在做的事还重要

爸妈就花时间跟我谈了一下

之后我有什么事都很愿意跟他们说

跟我们家很熟的一个朋友对我说
你看你爸妈都越来越老了

这样他们的生活才会舒服一点

因为他们希望我在年轻的时候
就全心为耶和华服务

成为基列学校第145届的学生

没有他们，我一定做不到

我真的很感谢爸爸妈妈
用上帝的方式养育我，让我一生充满快乐
我很感谢爸爸妈妈
用耶和华的方式养育我
让我在真理中长大，避开了烦恼和痛苦
孩子天生就喜欢模仿别人
他们会学习我们所做的一切
我想感谢耶和华，让我们有这么好的家庭
看到我们一家五口都全时为耶和华服务
我真的很高兴
谢谢你，耶和华

title: 윌리엄 맬렌폰트: 새로운 언어를 배우는 일 (느헤미야 13:24)

ko.text: 그 사람의 마음에 가장 잘 와닿는 언어가 됩니다.
우리는 보통 집에서 자라면서 모국어를 배우는데,
우리가 배우는 언어에 가장 큰 영향을 미치는 사람은 어머니이죠.
하지만 당시 많은 어머니들은 이방 여자였고
자녀에게 언어뿐만 아니라 이방 신에 대해서도 가르쳤을 겁니다.
심지어 탁월한 사람들까지 그 이방 여자들과 결혼했죠.
아스돗, 암몬, 모압 여자와 결혼한 유대인들이 있었다.
그들의 아들들은 절반이 아스돗 말을 했고
유대 말을 할 줄 아는 사람은 아무도 없었다.”
언급된 것처럼 그 이방 어머니들은 자녀들에게
자기 나라와 문화와 종교와 이방 신들에 대해 가르쳤을 겁니다.
그래서 에스라와 느헤미야는 조언과 지침을 베풀었습니다.
이방 아내들과 자녀들을 내보내기로 결정한 것입니다.
하지만 그 자녀들은 히브리어나 여호와에 대해 전혀 모르고
이방 나라들의 언어만 할 수 있었죠.
따라서 그 자녀들을 내보낸 것은 유대인들의 정체성을 보호하고,
그들이 주변 나라들의 문화와 종교에 서서히 동화되는 것을
지금은 히브리어를 꼭 배울 필요는 없으니
지혜로우신 여호와께서는 우리가 어떤 언어를 하든,
“순결한 언어”, 즉 그분과 그분의 목적에 대한
바벨에서 있었던 일과 정반대의 일을 하시는 것인데요,
그래서 그들은 함께 일할 수 없었고 흩어지게 되었죠.
오늘날 사람들은 아주 다양한 언어를 사용하지만,
여호와께서는 큰 지혜를 나타내셔서 사람들을 모으십니다.
“그때에 내가 민족들의 언어를 순결한 언어로 바꾸어서,
그러니까 다른 언어를 말하는 민족들이 우리가 진리를 전하면
그들이 ‘어깨를 나란히 하여 하느님을 섬길 것’이라고 말하니까요.
모국을 떠나 다른 곳에 살고 있죠.
그들도 마음에 이르는 언어로 진리를 배워야 합니다.
사람들에게 진리를 가르치기 위해 외국어를 배우고 있습니다.
따라서 출퇴근 봉사자들을 포함한 많은 베델 봉사자들이
진리를 가르치기 위해 열심히 수고하고 있습니다.
우리가 아이처럼 언어를 배울 수 있다면 얼마나 좋을까요?
노력 없이도 금방 말을 하기 시작합니다.
언어를 습득하도록 프로그램이 되어 있는 것 같다.
어린아이의 뇌는 말을 할 수 있는 생물학적 역량을
미리 갖춘 채 태어나는 것 같다.”
뇌는 언어를 배우는 기능이 탑재된 컴퓨터와 같다고 말합니다.
안타까운 건 저를 비롯한 많은 분들이 나이가 들면서
이 기능에 문제가 생기기 시작한다는 것이죠.
그 언어를 사용하는 회중으로 옮기기로 한다면,
이걸 기억하는 게 도움이 될 수 있습니다.
그 외국어 회중에 있는 어린아이들이 좋은 선생님이 될 수 있다는 것이죠.
모국어가 머릿속에 너무나 깊이 뿌리 박혀서
익숙하지 않은 새로운 언어의 자음과 모음을
억양이나 발음에 지나치게 신경 쓰지 마십시오.
물론 어떤 사람들의 억양이 다른 사람들보다 더 듣기 좋을 수는 있죠.
인정하기 싫은 사람도 있겠지만, 누구나 억양은 있습니다.
심지어 같은 언어를 쓰더라도 어디에서 왔는지,
단어를 발음하는 억양이나 강세의 차이에 따라서 말이죠.
예전에 선교인들이 임지에 임명이 되었을 때는
새로운 언어를 배우는 특별한 프로그램이 있었습니다.
바벨탑에 와 있는 것 같은 기분이 들었습니다.
두 번째 달에는 하루에 4시간씩 언어를 공부하고
세 번째 달에는 150시간을 봉사하고 할 수 있는 만큼 공부했습니다.
외국어를 배우려고 하는 사람들을 위한 훌륭한 몇 가지 제안이
네 가지 점을 들 수 있는데요.
의욕이 강할수록 더 잘 배울 수 있기 때문입니다.
처음부터 자신에게 너무 많은 기대를 하지 마십시오.
아마겟돈 후에야 그 목표를 이룰 수 있을 테니까요.
따라서 실수를 두려워하지 말고 새로운 언어를 계속 배우십시오.
한 형제는 “첫 두 해는 힘이 들었고, 때때로 포기하고 싶었다”고 말했습니다.
하지만 이 형제는 갈수록 더 쉬워졌다고도 했습니다.
새로운 언어에 유창해지는 데 도움이 됩니다.
단 몇 분이라도, 매일 연습해야 합니다.
따라서 새로운 언어를 짧은 시간이라도 꾸준히 연습하십시오.
사실 우리 지부의 베델 봉사자들은 대부분 영어 구역에서 섬기고 있습니다.
그들은 회중에 큰 축복이 되고 있습니다.
회중을 격려하기 위해 열심히 노력하는 베델 봉사자들에게
우리 모두가 기억해야 할 중요한 점은,
베델 임명에 최선을 다해야 한다는 것입니다.
우리는 무엇보다 가장 중요한 언어인 순결한 언어,
이 언어를 계속 배워 나가야 하겠습니다.

en.text: Usually,
the language that we learned
from infancy becomes
the language of the heart,
and we learn it at home.
In most cases, the dominant influence
in our life in connection with our language of the heart,
or the first language, is our mother.
And that’s precisely what took place
in Israel in the days of Nehemiah.
But the mothers in this case were pagans
sharing their language and probably their beliefs with their children.
And a lot of Jewish men —prominent Jewish men—
had married pagan women.
Let’s read the scripture together
at Nehemiah 13:23, 24
—Nehemiah 13:23, 24.
It says: “In those days I also saw Jews
“who had married Ashdodite, Ammonite,
“and Moabite women.
“Half of their sons were speaking Ashdodite
“and half spoke the language of the different peoples,
“but none of them
knew how to speak the language of the Jews.”
And as was stated, it’s very likely that those mothers
would be teaching the children
about their land, their culture,
their worship, and the pagan gods they worshipped.
And so the decision was made
by the Jews themselves,
when they were counseled and given direction
from Ezra and from Nehemiah,
to send those wives away along with the children.
And that’s an interesting thing.
It must have been a bit difficult
for some husbands to see their children sent away.
But all they knew were the languages of the pagan wives
—nothing about Hebrew and the worship of Jehovah God.
And the problem was that they were sent away to keep the Jews
from losing their identity by a gradual assimilation into the cultures
and the religions of the surrounding nations that those wives belonged to.
In Nehemiah’s day, speaking Hebrew was vital,
and we’re grateful it’s not necessary today.
We all don’t have to learn Hebrew.
But in his wisdom, Jehovah invites people who speak any language
to learn the “pure language,” the truth about him and his purposes.
And, you know, it’s a bit like the opposite
of what took place at the Tower of Babel,
where Jehovah intervened and confused the builders of the Tower of Babel,
imposing upon them different languages, including different ways of thinking.
And so they went off disorganized and separated from one another.
And today, we have people from all over the world
who speak many, many different languages,
but in Jehovah’s wisdom,
he’s bringing them all together
—those who love the truth and love him— in unity.
And this is what Zephaniah says —Zephaniah 3:9.
It speaks of the “pure language”:
“I shall give to peoples the change to a pure language,
in order for them all to call upon the name of Jehovah.”
And that’s what these people do who speak other languages.
We reach them with the truth, but then they’re unified
with Jehovah’s organization,
because it goes on to say “in order to serve him
shoulder to shoulder.”
So isn’t that interesting—the way Jehovah has used the “pure language”
to bring people of many diverse backgrounds
and languages together in his worship?
In our day, people of many different languages
are leaving their home countries to live elsewhere.
And it’s really quite amazing when you consider:
Large cities are filled with people
of different languages, and even in little villages,
we find people speaking different languages.
They need help to learn the truth
in the language of their heart.
It’s interesting to note how many Bethelites
have learned other languages in order to teach the truth to people.
In the United States Bethel, in our branch,
there are over 2,500 Bethelites
who are engaged
in 24 different language groups and congregations.
So a lot of Bethelites (and commuters are included in those numbers)
are doing a very fine work
in helping people in the territory to learn the truth.
And wouldn’t it be nice— I know some of us would love to learn some other languages
—wouldn’t it be lovely if we could learn the way a child does?
They just absorb it —no effort—
and they start speaking it.
A researcher, Dr. John Brierley, says this:
“‘Clearly the young brain seems
“to be programmed almost like a computer’
“for language development.
“He notes that even ‘brain anatomy’ suggests
“‘that an infant is born
with a pre-programmed biological capacity to speak.’”
And then the comment in Awake!  said
that it’s as though the brain is hardwired
to learn language.
I’m sorry to say that as the years go by,
the hardwiring starts to fray a bit in many of us.
But if we make the effort
and we do make a switch to a congregation where they speak the language
that you would like to learn, remember this:
Children can be a big help in the congregation
that you attend in a foreign language.
They can also be very startling and frank:
“You speak funny.
“Why can’t you pronounce that word properly?
It’s so easy.”
‘Well, yes, to you  it’s easy.
You were raised with it.’
But that’s how kids are.
They don’t realize the difficulties we have
as we get older, with the grooves being so deep
and so thick in the brain with our original language
that it’s hard to get out of those grooves the vowels and consonants
that we’re not used to saying in a certain order.
Keep a sense of humor; listen to the kids.
They’ll help you.
And don’t be overly concerned
about speaking a new language without an accent.
Everybody has an accent one way or another.
Some are more agreeable than others, but everyone has that.
And some don’t want to admit it, but they really do.
They have an accent.
Even when we all speak the same language, you can tell where a person is from
—whether it’s east, north, west (whatever it may be), south.
There are accents or intonations in the way words are pronounced.
I remember, in years gone by, for missionaries
who were sent out into the field,
we had to follow a special program in learning a new language.
Your first month in your new assignment,
you had to study 11 hours a day
for 30 days your new language.
Well, you felt like you were in the Tower of Babel
on those occasions because it was very difficult.
The second month, you had to study your new language
four hours a day and be out preaching 130 hours.
Your third month was 150 hours in the field ministry,
and you’d study the language as you could.
For those who are striving to learn a new language,
here are a few suggestions I gleaned from the Awake!  of March 2007
and the January issue of 2000.
There are four points:
(1) motivation,
(2) humility,
(3) patience,
(4) practice.
“Motivation.
You need an incentive —a reason to pursue your goal.”
Because if you have a high level of motivation,
you’re going to be more successful.
Well, we have the best motivation there is:
teach people the truth; praise our God, Jehovah;
build up the congregation we’ve chosen to attend.
What about humility?
Well, “don’t expect too much of yourself” when you start learning a new language.
“Mistakes are inevitable.”
And if you wait until you can speak it perfectly
before you start making comments or give a talk,
you may be waiting quite a while.
Be prepared, because it may not be
until after Armageddon that you achieve that goal.
So don’t be afraid to make mistakes and carry on with your new language.
‘Patience.
‘A brother stated: “For me, the first two years were difficult,
‘and at times I felt like giving up.”
‘Still, he acknowledges
that it does get easier as time goes by.’
And it gets enjoyable.
And number four: “Practice.
“A regular routine will help you to become fluent in [your] new language.
“Try to practice every day, even if it’s for just a few minutes.
“[There’s an interesting saying] As one textbook puts it,
“‘“A little and often”
is preferable to “a lot but seldom.”’”
So be steady,
even for short periods of time, in practicing the new language.
Now, the fact is that most Bethelites in our branch
are serving in the English-language field,
and they are truly a blessing to their congregations.
The brothers are happy to have Bethelites who take the lead,
who give of themselves, and who work hard to build up the congregation.
So the decision to serve in an English congregation
or with a different language group is highly personal.
Whatever the decision may be, there’s a key factor
that we all have to keep in mind
to maintain our spirituality at a high level
and give our Bethel assignment our best.
And that key factor that we have to keep in mind
is to focus on the one language that counts the most
—the “pure language” that Jehovah God has given to his people.

cn.text: 通常，我们从婴儿的时候开始学习的语言
也就是在家里学习的语言
是最能打动我们的心的
对大部分人来说
教我们说这个语言的
而且影响我们一生最深的就是我们的母亲
这正是尼希米的时代
很多犹太人家庭的情况
不过当时很多做母亲的是外族人
她们教孩子说她们的语言
甚至包括她们的信仰
当时很多犹太男子
甚至那些带头的都娶了外族人
我们一起读读尼希米记13:23,24
“那段日子，我也发现有些犹太人
娶了亚实突、亚扪、摩押的妻子
他们的儿女有一半说亚实突话
一半说其他民族的语言
没有一个会说犹太话。”
像我们刚才说的
这些外族母亲很可能会教导自己的孩子
认识自己的家乡和文化
还有他们崇拜的外族神
后来，当时的犹太人
他们接受了以斯拉和尼希米的劝告和指示
作出了这样的决定
要把这些外族妻子和他们的孩子送走
这件事真的值得我们想想
对一些犹太丈夫来说
要把他们的孩子送走，一定很不容易
可是这些孩子只会说外族的语言
完全不会说希伯来语，也不崇拜耶和华
把这些孩子送走，是为了保护犹太人
不让他们被这些外族妻子的文化
和信仰渐渐同化
当时犹太人都应该学会说希伯来语
我们很高兴
还好今天我们不需要学习说希伯来语
不过耶和华也邀请说不同语言的人
学习一个共同的语言，纯洁的语言
也就是认识他和他的旨意
这跟人们在建造巴别塔的时候
发生的情况很不一样
耶和华使他们突然说起不同的语言
有不同的思维方式
因此他们没有办法组织起来完成建造的工作
后来他们就分散到全地了
但今天耶和华用他的方法
让世界各地说许多不同语言的人
也就是那些爱真理、爱耶和华上帝的人
可以团结起来
这就是西番雅说的
在西番雅书3:9
经文也提到“纯洁的语言”
“那时候，我要教导所有民族的人
改说纯洁的语言
让他们都可以呼求耶和华的名”
所以，这些人都会学习
说一个纯洁的语言
他们认识了真理
和耶和华的组织团结在一起
然后就像经文接着说的
可以和我们并肩敬奉耶和华
这很有意思，对吗？
耶和华用纯洁的语言
让说不同语言的人团结崇拜他
今天有许多人离开自己的家乡
住在其他的国家
这件事情其实很有趣
你想想，在一些大城市里
住着许多说不同语言的人
甚至在一些小地方也有这样的人
我们要用能打动他们的语言，向他们传道
我们很高兴看到
为了帮助人学习圣经
有许多伯特利成员学习其他的语言
在美国伯特利
我们的分部有超过2500个伯特利成员
他们分别在
24个不同语言的小组和会众里服务
所以有很多伯特利成员
包括那些通勤人员
都在自己的地区里热心地帮助人学习圣经
这真的是很好，是不是？
我们当中有一些人喜欢学习语言
很多人都希望自己能像孩子一样
轻松地学会一个语言
他们就是自然地学习，毫不费力
约翰·布莱尔利博士说
年轻人的头脑就像一台电脑
安装了可以学习语言的程序
他也说，根据大脑解剖学
婴儿一出生就有学习说话的能力
《警醒！》杂志也提到
人的大脑好像有一个可以学习语言的装置
不过很可惜，随着人的年纪越来越大
这个装置也越来越磨损
学习语言就不容易了
如果我们想学习一个语言
也付出努力学习并且决定
搬去说这个语言的会众
要记得
这个会众的孩子可以帮助你学好这个语言
他们可能直率得让你很惊讶
“你发音很奇怪欸！”
“这个发音很简单！”
是啊，这对你来说很简单
你从小就说这个语言
孩子就是孩子
他们不知道我们大人学习语言有多困难
头脑里那个像电脑的装置
随着年纪越来越大也就老化了
所以大人很难发出这个新的语言的发音
要保持幽默
听孩子们的，他们会帮助你
学习一个语言
不用太过担心自己的口音太重
每个人或多或少都有口音
只是有些人的口音比较好听
有些人不想承认他们有口音
但其实他们真的有
即使我们说同一个语言
你也能从口音听得出
他们从东南西北哪个地方来
同一个单词在不同的地方可能有不同的发音
我记得多年前，我们做特派传道员的时候
为了学习一个新的语言
我们参加了一个特别的课程
在新的委派的第一个月
每天必须用11个小时学习这个新语言
我觉得自己好像在建造巴别塔的那个时候
我都听不懂别人在说什么
第二个月，每天学习语言4个小时
要传道130个小时
在第三个月要传道150个小时
然后尽可能学习这个语言
如果你想学习一个新语言
以下有四个要点
来自《警醒！》2007年3月刊
以及2000年1月刊
第一，学习动机
第二，虚心学习
第三，要有耐心
第四，勤于练习
学习动机
你需要一个理由帮助你学好其他语言
你的动机越强烈就越能学好这个语言
我们有最好的动机
就是要教导人圣经、赞美耶和华上帝
鼓励会众里的弟兄姐妹
那么虚心学习呢？
嗯，当你学习一个新语言的时候
不要对自己的要求过高
错误百出是在所难免的
如果你想等到把这个语言说得完美
再发表评论或演讲
你可能会等很久
那就要等到哈米吉多顿之后才能做到了
不要害怕说错，要继续使用这个新语言
