자녀에게 언어뿐만 아니라 이방 신에 대해서도 가르쳤을 겁니다.
심지어 탁월한 사람들까지 그 이방 여자들과 결혼했죠.
아스돗, 암몬, 모압 여자와 결혼한 유대인들이 있었다.
그들의 아들들은 절반이 아스돗 말을 했고
유대 말을 할 줄 아는 사람은 아무도 없었다.”
언급된 것처럼 그 이방 어머니들은 자녀들에게
자기 나라와 문화와 종교와 이방 신들에 대해 가르쳤을 겁니다.
그래서 에스라와 느헤미야는 조언과 지침을 베풀었습니다.
이방 아내들과 자녀들을 내보내기로 결정한 것입니다.
하지만 그 자녀들은 히브리어나 여호와에 대해 전혀 모르고
이방 나라들의 언어만 할 수 있었죠.
따라서 그 자녀들을 내보낸 것은 유대인들의 정체성을 보호하고,
그들이 주변 나라들의 문화와 종교에 서서히 동화되는 것을
지금은 히브리어를 꼭 배울 필요는 없으니
지혜로우신 여호와께서는 우리가 어떤 언어를 하든,
“순결한 언어”, 즉 그분과 그분의 목적에 대한
바벨에서 있었던 일과 정반대의 일을 하시는 것인데요,
그래서 그들은 함께 일할 수 없었고 흩어지게 되었죠.
오늘날 사람들은 아주 다양한 언어를 사용하지만,
여호와께서는 큰 지혜를 나타내셔서 사람들을 모으십니다.
“그때에 내가 민족들의 언어를 순결한 언어로 바꾸어서,
그러니까 다른 언어를 말하는 민족들이 우리가 진리를 전하면
그들이 ‘어깨를 나란히 하여 하느님을 섬길 것’이라고 말하니까요.
모국을 떠나 다른 곳에 살고 있죠.
그들도 마음에 이르는 언어로 진리를 배워야 합니다.
사람들에게 진리를 가르치기 위해 외국어를 배우고 있습니다.
따라서 출퇴근 봉사자들을 포함한 많은 베델 봉사자들이
진리를 가르치기 위해 열심히 수고하고 있습니다.
우리가 아이처럼 언어를 배울 수 있다면 얼마나 좋을까요?
노력 없이도 금방 말을 하기 시작합니다.
언어를 습득하도록 프로그램이 되어 있는 것 같다.
어린아이의 뇌는 말을 할 수 있는 생물학적 역량을
미리 갖춘 채 태어나는 것 같다.”
뇌는 언어를 배우는 기능이 탑재된 컴퓨터와 같다고 말합니다.
안타까운 건 저를 비롯한 많은 분들이 나이가 들면서
이 기능에 문제가 생기기 시작한다는 것이죠.
그 언어를 사용하는 회중으로 옮기기로 한다면,
이걸 기억하는 게 도움이 될 수 있습니다.
그 외국어 회중에 있는 어린아이들이 좋은 선생님이 될 수 있다는 것이죠.
모국어가 머릿속에 너무나 깊이 뿌리 박혀서
익숙하지 않은 새로운 언어의 자음과 모음을
억양이나 발음에 지나치게 신경 쓰지 마십시오.
물론 어떤 사람들의 억양이 다른 사람들보다 더 듣기 좋을 수는 있죠.
인정하기 싫은 사람도 있겠지만, 누구나 억양은 있습니다.
심지어 같은 언어를 쓰더라도 어디에서 왔는지,
단어를 발음하는 억양이나 강세의 차이에 따라서 말이죠.
예전에 선교인들이 임지에 임명이 되었을 때는
새로운 언어를 배우는 특별한 프로그램이 있었습니다.
바벨탑에 와 있는 것 같은 기분이 들었습니다.
두 번째 달에는 하루에 4시간씩 언어를 공부하고
세 번째 달에는 150시간을 봉사하고 할 수 있는 만큼 공부했습니다.
외국어를 배우려고 하는 사람들을 위한 훌륭한 몇 가지 제안이
네 가지 점을 들 수 있는데요.
의욕이 강할수록 더 잘 배울 수 있기 때문입니다.
처음부터 자신에게 너무 많은 기대를 하지 마십시오.
아마겟돈 후에야 그 목표를 이룰 수 있을 테니까요.
따라서 실수를 두려워하지 말고 새로운 언어를 계속 배우십시오.
한 형제는 “첫 두 해는 힘이 들었고, 때때로 포기하고 싶었다”고 말했습니다.
하지만 이 형제는 갈수록 더 쉬워졌다고도 했습니다.
새로운 언어에 유창해지는 데 도움이 됩니다.
단 몇 분이라도, 매일 연습해야 합니다.
따라서 새로운 언어를 짧은 시간이라도 꾸준히 연습하십시오.
사실 우리 지부의 베델 봉사자들은 대부분 영어 구역에서 섬기고 있습니다.
그들은 회중에 큰 축복이 되고 있습니다.
회중을 격려하기 위해 열심히 노력하는 베델 봉사자들에게
우리 모두가 기억해야 할 중요한 점은,
베델 임명에 최선을 다해야 한다는 것입니다.
우리는 무엇보다 가장 중요한 언어인 순결한 언어,
이 언어를 계속 배워 나가야 하겠습니다.
우리는 폭풍과도 같은 시련이 닥칠 것을 예상해야 합니다.
계속 강한 믿음 키워 갈 거야.
절대 포기 안 해, 내 믿음을.
절대 포기 안 해, 우리 믿음.
절대 포기 안 해, 우리 믿음.
여러분이 시련에도 확고함을 유지할 수 있도록
이달 말에 새로운 동영상이 나올 것입니다.
「시련 아래서도 충실을 유지한 소련 치하의 여호와의 증인들」입니다.
과거 그 두 비디오의 감동적인 내용이 들어 있는
‘각 사람은 자기가 어떻게 짓고 있는지 계속 살펴야 합니다’였죠.
루디와 네니타가 어떻게 좋은 본을 보여
세 딸이 의미 있는 영적 목표를
블랜턴 자매가 영적으로 만족스런 삶을 사는 데
어떻게 도움이 됐는지 볼 수 있었습니다.
매달 87만 건이 넘는 성서 연구가 사회되고 있죠.
어떤 구역은 걸어서만 갈 수 있는데,

en.text: Welcome!
Usually, our December program
features the Gilead graduation program
held in September of each year.
However, the 149th class of Gilead
was scheduled to arrive in the United States
when the COVID-19 pandemic was underway.
Therefore, that class was postponed.
So this month, we’ll focus on being
the best Bible teachers we can be!
Here are a few highlights:
Cecilio and Schera made many sacrifices
to help their students become
dedicated worshippers of Jehovah.
We’ll see the impact
they had on Mercedes and Abel.
The arrival of a baby brings
great joy as well as new challenges.
We’ll learn how Jehovah helps
first-time parents adjust to their new responsibilities.
And we’ll learn how Louise Blanton’s parents
prepared her for a satisfying life
in Jehovah’s service.
This is JW Broadcasting®
for December 2020!
My comments this month
are drawn from 1 Corinthians 3:10:
“Let each one keep watching
how he is building.”
Building
—are we talking about the upcoming construction
of a facility for headquarters departments in Ramapo, New York?
Or are we referring to the building of new Kingdom Halls in your country?
Well, as important as those building projects are,
my comments are directed to an even more important building work.
Let’s look at the context
at 1 Corinthians 3:5.
Apollos and Paul are mentioned by name.
And what was their specific role identified to be?
Verse 5 says
“ministers through whom you became believers.”
Apollos and Paul had taught the Scriptures to many in Corinth.
In verses 6 through 9,
Paul likens this teaching activity to the planting of a field.
Seeds of truth are planted in the heart of a person.
By means of return visits and Bible studies,
the seeds are watered.
But if the person is receptive,
then with Jehovah’s spirit and blessing,
the truth will blossom
and grow to the point of dedication and baptism.
Did you notice in verse 9
that Bible teachers are described as “God’s fellow workers”?
What an awesome privilege we have to assist Jehovah
in gathering “the precious things of all the nations”!
So we now know the topic of these verses
in 1 Corinthians chapter 3.
It’s discussing Bible teachers
who help others to become believers.
But did you also notice that in verse 9,
Paul changes illustrations?
He said: “You are God’s field under cultivation”
—that’s agricultural.
But then he changes the analogy,
saying “God’s building”
—that’s architectural; that’s construction.
Why the change in illustrations?
The building analogy highlights a specific point.
You see, the illustration of the farmer
doesn’t focus on the farmer’s impact on the growth of a plant.
In that illustration, the farmer waters the seedling,
but it’s God that makes the plant grow.
However, the illustration of building, or construction,
focuses on the builder’s involvement,
or the Bible teacher’s involvement.
The one constructing a building has considerable influence
over the quality of the end product.
What kind of materials does he select?
Is he thorough in his work,
or does he cut corners to get the job done faster
or with less effort?
Now let’s read the 10th verse
of 1 Corinthians chapter 3:
“According to the undeserved kindness of God that was given to me,
“I laid a foundation as a skilled master builder,
“but someone else is building on it.
“But let each one keep watching
how he is building on it.”
There in Corinth, Paul, as a “master builder,”
had initially acquainted many with the truth.
In effect, he “laid a foundation”
for others to build on.
But what was that foundation?
Verse 11 says:
“For no one can lay any other foundation
“than what is laid, which is Jesus Christ.”
Paul had helped establish the congregation there in Corinth
based on the teachings of Jesus,
the foundation of the truth.
Building on that foundation,
others would become Bible teachers
and help still others to progress toward baptism.
That is why Paul cautioned in verse 10
to “keep watching how” we build.
We can affect the outcome.
So to all of us Bible teachers, including parents,
we ask the question,
How are we building on the foundation?
Why does it really matter?
Let’s read verses 12 and 13:
“Now if anyone builds on the foundation
“gold, silver, precious stones,
“wood, hay, or straw,
“each one’s work will be shown for what it is,
“for the day will show it up,
“because it will be revealed by means of fire,
“and the fire itself will prove
what sort of work each one has built.”
Do we understand how important it is
to analyze our teaching techniques?
Will we use the best techniques possible
to reach our student’s or our child’s heart?
Or do we just try to get by with the bare essentials,
in effect, a halfhearted effort,
using hay or straw, as it were?
Some years ago in one developing country
during an economic boom,
it became a priority
to build more and more schools.
Unfortunately, building requirements and materials
were substandard.
Well, what happened when a 7.9-magnitude earthquake
hit one of the areas?
Many schools in the earthquake zone crumbled
while buildings around them remained standing.
An official report indicated
that over 5,000 students died.
Think about it.
Prior to the earthquake, schools were in session
and everything seemed fine.
Students and faculty
were coming and going on a daily basis.
But the unforeseen earthquake proved
that the building methods used
were not of the quality needed to prevent collapse
and terrible carnage.
First Corinthians 3:13 makes clear
that how we build spiritually when teaching Bible students
or our children
is just as important.
Now notice the sobering point
made in verses 14 and 15:
“If anyone’s work that he has built on it remains,
“he will receive a reward;
“if anyone’s work is burned up, he will suffer loss,
“but he himself will be saved;
yet, if so, it will be as through fire.”
The point in verse 14 is that if we’re conscientious
and reach the hearts of our Bible students,
that may be what gives them the needed fortitude
to withstand unexpected trials.
In that case, our diligent work “remains.”
Then verse 15 makes the point
that if our teaching techniques were inconsistent
or were in some way slipshod,
our student may not successfully weather a “fire,”
or stormy trial in his life.
We personally may survive,
but we might suffer the loss of the one we studied with,
whether a Bible student
or our own child.
That’s why Paul is highlighting the need
to be the best Bible teacher
we personally can be.
However, we should mention
that if a person who progresses to dedication and baptism
later leaves the truth,
it’s not necessarily the responsibility of the Bible teacher.
The teacher may have been very diligent
and used the best of spiritual building materials.
But the student or child may not have responded from his heart.
Or possibly he allowed human imperfection or temptation
to cause him to deviate from the way.
But the takeaway point from 1 Corinthians chapter 3
is to do our best to build in our students or children
fire-resistant materials.
We want them to remain
—to endure the tests that are sure to come their way.
What might be likened to building with inferior materials
when studying the Bible with someone?
Possibly, we initially aroused a person’s interest
by telling him about the hope of everlasting life in Paradise.
That’s indeed Scriptural.
But is that in itself building in such a way
that the person will survive
a fiery trial of faith in the future?
What if our teaching consisted solely of saying,
“If you want to live forever in Paradise,
“you must study, go to the meetings,
and share in the preaching work”?
If so, we are not building
in a way to ensure
that the student or child
will resist the fire of trials
or stand the test of time.
In effect, we’re using wood, hay, or straw.
Do you remember that Paul said we are to build “on the foundation”?
He said the foundation “is Jesus Christ.”
That is solid.
Ephesians 3:16, 17
help us to understand what it means
to build with quality materials
such as gold, silver, and precious stones.
In verse 16, it makes clear that there’s a way
that we can “be made mighty in the [person we] are inside.”
Let’s read verse 17:
“And that through your faith
“you may have the Christ dwell in your hearts with love.
May you be rooted and established on the foundation.”
How can we help our child or Bible student
become strong, or mighty, spiritually?
Interestingly, verse 17 said
that it’s by having “the Christ dwell in your hearts,”
not just knowing Jesus in the head
but sounding his teachings and personality down
into our student’s heart.
It means to know Jesus so well
that it’s as if he lives, or dwells, inside of us
and motivates us as Christians.
The result?
Verse 17 concluded by saying
that the student would become
“rooted and established on the foundation.”
Yes, solidly grounded
on Jesus Christ.
And Hebrews 1:3
says that “[Jesus] is the reflection of God’s glory
and the exact representation of his very being.”
Jesus himself said:
“No one comes to the Father except through me.”
So building with fire-resistant materials means
helping the student to love Jesus, yes,
but also to have a close, loving relationship
with Jehovah God himself.
But why are we considering the theme
‘Keep Watching How You Are Building’ now?
Why is this more urgent than ever before?
It’s because all indications,
Scripturally and circumstantially,
point to Satan’s evil system of things coming to an abrupt end.
The physical indications of Matthew chapter 24
and the bizarre temperament described
at 2 Timothy 3:1-5
become more and more precise
as we watch “the scene of this world” unfold.
We can expect even more opposition and persecution
from those who are opposed to our resolve
to stand on the side of Jehovah.
Our brothers in Russia and other lands
are experiencing this now.
Some have been beaten
and brutalized in other ways.
As we’ve heard,
others have been sentenced to years in prison.
In recent years, the organization has reminded us of what we can expect
as the great tribulation begins.
Do you remember this video clip
from the Pursue What Builds Loyalty video series
shown at the 2016 regional convention?
Be reminded.
And your faith has led you here
as loyal servants of Jehovah,
confident that Psalm 97:10
applies to you personally:
“[Jehovah] is guarding the lives of his loyal ones.”
Where are they?
Try the basement!
Check that door!
That video series has been affectionately called
the basement video.
It was depicting one possible scenario
that could be considered a “fire”
according to 1 Corinthians 3:13.
The serious question we want to ask ourselves is,
‘Would my Bible student or child
be in the basement with those other faithful brothers and sisters?’
If not, would the reason be
because of his own lack of faith?
Or might it, at least in part, be
because we did not take our responsibility as a teacher
seriously enough?
Did we build with fire-resistant materials
or, in effect, with hay or straw?
The same verse said:
“For the day will show it up . . .
“the fire itself will prove
what sort of work each one has built.”
It’s a sobering thought, isn’t it?
If you recall in the May 2020
JW Broadcasting® monthly program,
Brother Lett addressed the concern a few parents have expressed
about some of our videos that depict
Biblical or modern-day situations.
In these, at times, true worshippers are depicted
as having their faith tested
as if by fire.
The concern expressed is that some scenes
could have an effect on children
who’ve been protected from all negative circumstances on TV,
including daily news reports of catastrophes
being faced by real people.
The basement scene we just reviewed
was one of our videos
that produced such a reaction.
Another one was the reenactment of the Bible account
depicting Jehovah’s saving acts in the time of King Hezekiah.
It was shown at the 2016 regional convention,
and the video is entitled
“O Jehovah, . . . I Trust in You.”
Let’s look again at that portrayal of Jehovah’s saving acts.
My lord!
If a parent has shielded his child
from viewing all scenes on the news
or other visual images depicting negative realities,
it’s understandable that there may be a concern.
However, as Brother Lett stated:
‘Parents need to give their children a realistic idea
‘of what we will face in the near future.
‘Many parents choose to help their children appreciate
‘the graphic visual imagery of a Bible-based account
‘while at the same time building trust in Jehovah,
who will be with them in times of distress.’
The point is, friends,
the Bible warns us, young and old alike,
that a time of fiery testing looms on the horizon.
We want to be realistic and face these events
with faith and courage.
Our videos depict such circumstances
in a tasteful and sanitized way,
not showing any actual acts of bloodshed or violence.
Be assured that the Governing Body
is not trying to scare anyone.
Instead, we are trying
to prepare everyone.
We feel responsible to fortify the brotherhood
by using fire-resistant building materials
in the spirit of 1 Corinthians chapter 3.
As teachers of the Word of God,
may we all give prayerful thought to the methods,
techniques, and the diligence we display
when conducting Bible studies.
We’re motivated by the very spirit of Jehovah God.
The words at 2 Peter 3:9 come to mind.
Of Jehovah, it says:
“He does not desire anyone to be destroyed
but desires all to attain to repentance.”
May that be our resolve
as we take to heart the inspired words of 1 Corinthians 3:10:
“Let each one keep watching how he is building”!
Having children is one of the greatest joys in life
and one of the greatest responsibilities
Jehovah entrusts to a husband and wife.
In the following dramatization,
notice how the arrival of a baby changes a marriage
and how Jehovah helps first-time parents.
Jehovah has been so good to us.
We enjoy a busy life full of blessings . . .
. . . including one we didn’t expect.
We love our little Emma so much!
But child-rearing was harder than we thought.
Most days went well
—others, not so much.
I just need some rest.
When will things be back to normal?
I wake with every little cry!
I wake when she’s silent.
Am I doing this right?
I should check on them.
Any time to ourselves was time to do nothing.
Fatigue was affecting our relationship with Jehovah . . .
. . . and each other.
We were so relieved when David, a father himself,
offered to visit with another elder.
We read Isaiah 40:29:
“He gives power to the tired one
and full might to those lacking strength.”
As a loving Father,
Jehovah wants parents to succeed.
So he gives us what we need to recharge us.
Things might never be like they were before.
But his suggestions helped us create
a practical and consistent spiritual routine.
David said it’s normal for new parents to feel anxious,
and anxiety is tiring.
So we pray for a calm heart . . .
. . . and extra kindness when tired,
so we can keep working as a team.
I so appreciate Zack’s help.
And I’m sacrificing some unnecessary things
to put spiritual things first.
There will always be a lot to do.
But when Emma sleeps,
I feed my faith
and rest.
Our new spiritual routine is invigorating.
Hey, Daddy!
Look!
Hey.
Jehovah helped us to understand.
While life in this system may have many challenges,
putting spiritual things first
will give us the strength to meet them.
That new father wanted life to get “back to normal.”
But all parents realize
that having children creates a “new normal.”
If you are first-time parents, please remember,
one of the most important adjustments you’ll make
is to establish a new spiritual routine
for yourselves and your precious little child.
Of course, children grow,
and when they cross into their teenage years,
suddenly, everything seems to change.
In the following video, notice how Rudy and Nenita Garcia
were determined to teach their daughters Jehovah’s ways
and the results they experienced.
We already had our firstborn, Renita.
And then I was told that we were going to have twins.
We were new in the truth and inexperienced.
So I was saying to myself:
‘How can I take care of my children, not only physically but more so spiritually?
‘How will I be able to teach them to love Jehovah,
to worship Jehovah?’
And 1 Corinthians 3:10
shows us the importance
of raising a family
by using good quality materials.
So having a spiritual routine is very important for the children.
My wife and I would have to lay a good spiritual foundation.
We would have to set a good example for our children.
As long as I could remember, I would always see my parents studying,
doing personal Bible study.
I remember Dad—one time, he came to us in the living room,
and he said, “You know, I was reading Psalm 1:2,
“where it said we should find ‘delight in the law of Jehovah
and read in an undertone day and night.’”
He said, “What if we do this as a family project,
like, we read the Bible every day out loud together?”
And my parents were very simple, you know.
They didn’t require a lot of fancy things.
They were content.
Mom and Dad always worked part-time.
Dad pioneered, so money was limited.
Sometimes the car we had wasn’t the most reliable,
and it would break down right before the meeting.
I remember when our car broke down.
Initially I thought, ‘Oh, we’re not going to go to the meeting.’
Mom and Dad would say: “Well, the car broke down.
There’s a meeting tonight, so let’s walk.”
So there are the five of us —my dad in his suit,
the four women would be in our dresses with our book bags.
And so that taught me not to let obstacles
and anxieties prevent me from going to my meetings.
Spending quality time was very important to my parents,
especially after the meetings.
We would change into our pajamas, grab a snack,
go to the living room, and just start talking
about how our day went and how the meeting went.
Just those special moments
—they brought us closer together.
I saw that Dad,
no matter how busy he was,
would drop what he was doing and look at me and talk.
I knew I was more important to him than what he was doing.
I remember a time when I had a crush on a boy.
My parents reasoned with me.
I felt very comfortable, you know, after that point, to maybe talk
about other things because I could see that my parents
were not going to be angry at me.
You know, they were going to listen to me and what I was feeling.
One of the blessings that Mom and Dad gave me
was teaching me how to think
and meditate on scriptures.
They encouraged us to set full-time service,
or pioneering, as a goal.
We all worked part-time, me and my siblings.
And I remember one close family friend
said to me: “You know, your parents are getting older.
“You know, you’re their daughter, and you should probably work full-time.
That way they’d have more of an easy life.”
After that sister’s conversation, I almost gave up
on pioneering, but I knew deep down
that my parents would not be happy about that.
They wanted us to spend our youth serving Jehovah.
My husband and I were invited to attend
the 145th class of Gilead, and that was like a dream come true.
I have to thank my parents for that
because they always supported me through the years.
I couldn’t have done it without them,
and for that I’ll be forever grateful.
I really do thank my parents
for the upbringing that they gave me.
I have a very happy life.
I’m thankful that I was able
to avoid a lot of heartache,
and that’s because my parents raised me
in the truth and in Jehovah’s way.
Children are born imitators,
and they’re going to imitate our example.
I want to thank Jehovah for what our family is now.
To see all of us in the pioneer work
—all five of us are pioneering— thank you, Jehovah.
Raising three daughters
took years of work and sacrifice.
But Rudy and Nenita are joyful,
knowing their daughters are happily serving Jehovah full-time.
Likewise, if we build in our children
fire-resistant materials,
then we give them everything they need
to make wise decisions themselves.
This was the case for Louise Blanton.
Notice how her parents’ building techniques
helped her to choose a fulfilling life.
My family started studying with Witnesses in New Jersey.
My parents had been very diligent in helping us to appreciate
not only Bible principles
but also characters in the Bible
who could be a role model for us.
It helped us to know that Jehovah cared
not only for adult publishers
but also for the children
that were serving him.
When you went out in the ministry,
it became such a common thing
—the police would come and pick you up.
If they couldn’t track down the parents, they would put the children in jail,
knowing that eventually the parents would have to come looking for them.
The police would use scare tactics.
They’d say: “There are rats in the cell.
Is that where you want to be?”
—anything to make you fearful,
to intimidate you to tell them where your parents were.
They’d put us in the jail,
and in order to build our faith, we would sing.
We didn’t have Kingdom melodies back then,
so we used to make up songs,
and that would keep us focused
on what we were doing there.
After I reached the age of 18,
my parents were agreeable to my accepting an assignment.
And in those years,
because of the racial issue in the south,
there were so many areas in the south
where they didn’t have Kingdom Halls
that the colored could attend.
So if you were free and you would accept an assignment,
the Society usually sent you to the south.
My parents were both born in the south,
so they were able to tell us what to expect
to keep the culture shock from being so great.
I was assigned to pioneer in Andalusia, Alabama.
Based on all of the matters that pertain
to integration and segregation,
this was a hotbed
for testing those issues.
And so I was concerned
about whether I had the fiber
to work under those circumstances.
The field was wide open.
There were so many in the area
that had no knowledge of Jehovah’s Witnesses
and were very receptive to the message.
That part of our ministry was very rewarding.
We had some very strong
and helpful brothers
that Jehovah was using
to get his people
—no matter what color—
to appreciate Him and his purpose.
When you focused on these things
—the suggestions and the ideas—
the brothers would help you to appreciate
how to deal with the issues.
They taught us, for one thing,
that the whole purpose of the Ku Klux Klan
is to intimidate.
They feel that if they frighten you enough,
you will leave.
Satan has always used
methods to try to intimidate.
But we would make it a practice to stay, to hold our place.
When we were in street work, we’d stay right there.
And of course, as they passed,
they had their remarks to make,
but we just stood there.
When I think back on my youth,
there isn’t anything that I was able to participate in
that I came to regret.
There were always blessings that went along with it.
If you make yourself available,
Jehovah will use you.
Jehovah is always there as a support.
There isn’t anything that he directs his organization to do
that doesn’t receive his support.
So if we are challenged with a new assignment
or if we feel inadequate about it,
if we look to Jehovah
—with Jehovah, you can’t fail.
Louise’s parents taught her to appreciate principles
and characters in the Bible.
That reached her heart
and aided Louise to endure difficult trials.
She has now spent over 50 years
of her life in the full-time service,
including over 40 years in Bethel service.
Hard work and sacrifice
may also be needed to help our Bible students
to become disciples.
We’ll see that in our next video.
A teacher should always help his or her student
to develop love for Jehovah.
That’s the best foundation to build on.
For me, it’s important that they see Jehovah
as a real Person.
In order to help them build a good foundation, they need to know
that Jehovah gave us the Bible so that we can receive his guidance
for the future and for eternity.
I’m so thankful for my Bible teacher.
She always helped me see Jehovah’s point of view
on things from the Bible.
I’ll never stop thanking Jehovah
for what he’s done for me.
He drew me to the truth.
He gave me a teacher that didn’t just teach me about the Bible,
but by his example, the brother taught me
how to really be one of Jehovah’s Witnesses.
When I started studying,
my parents told me that they didn’t consider me their daughter anymore.
During the study, my teacher helped
me see from the Bible that Jehovah had a lot of really good things in store for me.
My environment was very hostile before.
My problem was that my wife and I argued a lot,
and I had a bad temper.
The brother’s advice really helped us to keep calm when we had problems.
When a person starts getting to know Jehovah and they learn
and apply Bible truths in their lives,
the people who were their friends before are going to disappear.
We need to give them that friendship they’re losing.
We’ve had to make some sacrifices for our students.
But when we think about the blessings,
we can barely remember the sacrifices.
I worked full-time,
but I had to adapt to the student’s needs,
not the other way around.
Sometimes I’d be up at six o’clock in the morning
conducting a Bible study.
Sometimes things come up, and you can’t make it.
But the study should still happen.
Another brother can study with them if we’re not going to be there.
When someone starts studying, it can feel like a lot.
The Bible itself has 66 books.
So for example, you can suggest that the student start reading
a few verses every day
and then add a little more every week.
So that is how we see them progress.
You get to see them practice what they’re learning
—really following the Bible’s counsel in their lives.
We don’t just conduct a study,
see them progress, get baptized,
and then say, “OK, see you later.”
It doesn’t work like that. They become part of our life.
He’s been my friend since before I got baptized.
It’s been about 28 years now.
Years ago, my former student Abel had a really difficult time.
His wife got sick.
Although we were far away when we heard about it,
we kept in touch with him.
“Thank you, Livingston family,
“for calling Jessica during these hard times.
It’s very encouraging to us.”
“I know that you love us, and we also love you very much.
“You are an example in true worship for us.
May Jehovah continue caring for you and blessing you.”
I got baptized 34 years ago
and have been pioneering for 33 years.
My Bible teacher was Schera.
She was diagnosed with cancer.
When I got sick, Jehovah used Mercedes to help me.
After all this time, since I helped
her learn the truth, now she comforts me.
It’s a father-son relationship.
At some point,
maybe this student will help me.
And we can say that ‘we are good-for-nothing slaves,
and we have done what we ought to have done.’
And they keep loving and serving Jehovah.
What’s better than that?
To expand their ministry,
many of Jehovah’s Witnesses have learned a new language.
Have you?
Teaching someone the truth
in the language of their heart can be rewarding.
But learning to speak and think
in a new language can also be tough.
In a recent morning worship,
Brother William Malenfant offered some practical suggestions.
Usually,
the language that we learned
from infancy becomes
the language of the heart,
and we learn it at home.
In most cases, the dominant influence
in our life in connection with our language of the heart,
or the first language, is our mother.
And that’s precisely what took place
in Israel in the days of Nehemiah.
But the mothers in this case were pagans
sharing their language and probably their beliefs with their children.
And a lot of Jewish men —prominent Jewish men—
had married pagan women.
Let’s read the scripture together
at Nehemiah 13:23, 24
—Nehemiah 13:23, 24.
It says: “In those days I also saw Jews
“who had married Ashdodite, Ammonite,
“and Moabite women.
“Half of their sons were speaking Ashdodite
“and half spoke the language of the different peoples,
“but none of them
knew how to speak the language of the Jews.”
And as was stated, it’s very likely that those mothers
would be teaching the children
about their land, their culture,
their worship, and the pagan gods they worshipped.
And so the decision was made
by the Jews themselves,
when they were counseled and given direction
from Ezra and from Nehemiah,
to send those wives away along with the children.
And that’s an interesting thing.
It must have been a bit difficult
for some husbands to see their children sent away.
But all they knew were the languages of the pagan wives
—nothing about Hebrew and the worship of Jehovah God.
And the problem was that they were sent away to keep the Jews
from losing their identity by a gradual assimilation into the cultures
and the religions of the surrounding nations that those wives belonged to.
In Nehemiah’s day, speaking Hebrew was vital,
and we’re grateful it’s not necessary today.
We all don’t have to learn Hebrew.
But in his wisdom, Jehovah invites people who speak any language
to learn the “pure language,” the truth about him and his purposes.
And, you know, it’s a bit like the opposite
of what took place at the Tower of Babel,
where Jehovah intervened and confused the builders of the Tower of Babel,
imposing upon them different languages, including different ways of thinking.
And so they went off disorganized and separated from one another.
And today, we have people from all over the world
who speak many, many different languages,
but in Jehovah’s wisdom,
he’s bringing them all together
—those who love the truth and love him— in unity.
And this is what Zephaniah says —Zephaniah 3:9.
It speaks of the “pure language”:
“I shall give to peoples the change to a pure language,
in order for them all to call upon the name of Jehovah.”
And that’s what these people do who speak other languages.
We reach them with the truth, but then they’re unified
with Jehovah’s organization,
because it goes on to say “in order to serve him
shoulder to shoulder.”
So isn’t that interesting—the way Jehovah has used the “pure language”
to bring people of many diverse backgrounds
and languages together in his worship?
In our day, people of many different languages
are leaving their home countries to live elsewhere.
And it’s really quite amazing when you consider:
Large cities are filled with people
of different languages, and even in little villages,
we find people speaking different languages.
They need help to learn the truth
in the language of their heart.
It’s interesting to note how many Bethelites
have learned other languages in order to teach the truth to people.
In the United States Bethel, in our branch,
there are over 2,500 Bethelites
who are engaged
in 24 different language groups and congregations.
So a lot of Bethelites (and commuters are included in those numbers)
are doing a very fine work
in helping people in the territory to learn the truth.
And wouldn’t it be nice— I know some of us would love to learn some other languages
—wouldn’t it be lovely if we could learn the way a child does?
They just absorb it —no effort—
and they start speaking it.
A researcher, Dr. John Brierley, says this:
“‘Clearly the young brain seems
“to be programmed almost like a computer’
“for language development.
“He notes that even ‘brain anatomy’ suggests
“‘that an infant is born
with a pre-programmed biological capacity to speak.’”
And then the comment in Awake!  said
that it’s as though the brain is hardwired
to learn language.
I’m sorry to say that as the years go by,
the hardwiring starts to fray a bit in many of us.
But if we make the effort
and we do make a switch to a congregation where they speak the language
that you would like to learn, remember this:
Children can be a big help in the congregation
that you attend in a foreign language.
They can also be very startling and frank:
“You speak funny.
“Why can’t you pronounce that word properly?
It’s so easy.”
‘Well, yes, to you  it’s easy.
You were raised with it.’
But that’s how kids are.
They don’t realize the difficulties we have
as we get older, with the grooves being so deep
and so thick in the brain with our original language
that it’s hard to get out of those grooves the vowels and consonants
that we’re not used to saying in a certain order.
Keep a sense of humor; listen to the kids.
They’ll help you.
And don’t be overly concerned
about speaking a new language without an accent.
Everybody has an accent one way or another.
Some are more agreeable than others, but everyone has that.
And some don’t want to admit it, but they really do.
They have an accent.
Even when we all speak the same language, you can tell where a person is from
—whether it’s east, north, west (whatever it may be), south.
There are accents or intonations in the way words are pronounced.
I remember, in years gone by, for missionaries
who were sent out into the field,
we had to follow a special program in learning a new language.
Your first month in your new assignment,
you had to study 11 hours a day
for 30 days your new language.
Well, you felt like you were in the Tower of Babel
on those occasions because it was very difficult.
The second month, you had to study your new language
four hours a day and be out preaching 130 hours.
Your third month was 150 hours in the field ministry,
and you’d study the language as you could.
For those who are striving to learn a new language,
here are a few suggestions I gleaned from the Awake!  of March 2007
and the January issue of 2000.
There are four points:
(1) motivation,
(2) humility,
(3) patience,
(4) practice.
“Motivation.
You need an incentive —a reason to pursue your goal.”
Because if you have a high level of motivation,
you’re going to be more successful.
Well, we have the best motivation there is:
teach people the truth; praise our God, Jehovah;
build up the congregation we’ve chosen to attend.
What about humility?
Well, “don’t expect too much of yourself” when you start learning a new language.
“Mistakes are inevitable.”
And if you wait until you can speak it perfectly
before you start making comments or give a talk,
you may be waiting quite a while.
Be prepared, because it may not be
until after Armageddon that you achieve that goal.
So don’t be afraid to make mistakes and carry on with your new language.
‘Patience.
‘A brother stated: “For me, the first two years were difficult,
‘and at times I felt like giving up.”
‘Still, he acknowledges
that it does get easier as time goes by.’
And it gets enjoyable.
And number four: “Practice.
“A regular routine will help you to become fluent in [your] new language.
“Try to practice every day, even if it’s for just a few minutes.
“[There’s an interesting saying] As one textbook puts it,
“‘“A little and often”
is preferable to “a lot but seldom.”’”
So be steady,
even for short periods of time, in practicing the new language.
Now, the fact is that most Bethelites in our branch
are serving in the English-language field,
and they are truly a blessing to their congregations.
The brothers are happy to have Bethelites who take the lead,
who give of themselves, and who work hard to build up the congregation.
So the decision to serve in an English congregation
or with a different language group is highly personal.
Whatever the decision may be, there’s a key factor
that we all have to keep in mind
to maintain our spirituality at a high level
and give our Bethel assignment our best.
And that key factor that we have to keep in mind
is to focus on the one language that counts the most
—the “pure language” that Jehovah God has given to his people.
As we noted earlier,
we can expect stormy tests
and trials to come our way.
But if we’ve built fire-resistant materials
in our children, our students, and ourselves
—we will stand firm.
We’ll see that in our beautiful new music video.
The first time I heard the word of truth
About Jehovah and a world that is new,
Love grew in my heart right up to this day.
But I know this world wants to pull me away.
I cannot lose sight.
I want to do what is right.
I’ll keep building my faith so I can be strong.
I will not give up or give in.
His Word as my guide I’ll follow each day.
I’ll pray to stand firm on the ground.
I’ll keep building my faith; I won’t stop now.
So we have to choose where we will stand:
A life built on rock or one built on sand.
This world around us wants us to believe
It will stand forever, so live and be free.
But we know the truth,
What the Kingdom will do.
Let’s keep building our faith so we can be strong.
We will not give up or give in.
His Word as our guide we’ll follow each day.
We’ll pray to stand firm on the ground.
Let’s keep building our faith; we won’t stop now.
Let’s keep building our faith so we can be strong.
We will not give up or give in.
His Word as our guide we’ll follow each day.
We’ll pray to stand firm on the ground.
Let’s keep building our faith; we won’t stop now.
We won’t stop now.
We won’t stop now.
What an encouraging song!
And to further help you stand firm against trials,
a new video will be released
later this month entitled
Firm Under Opposition.
This 10-minute video consists of segments
from two previous documentaries
that touched the hearts of many:
Jehovah’s Witnesses Stand Firm Against Nazi Assault
and Faithful Under Trials
—Jehovah’s Witnesses in the Soviet Union.
So please look for this video that combines the highlights
of the two previous programs.
It will strengthen
and help you remain faithful to Jehovah.
The theme of this month’s program was
“Let Each One Keep Watching How He Is Building.”
We saw how first-time parents
can successfully embrace their new responsibilities.
By setting a good example, Rudy and Nenita
helped their three daughters reach meaningful, spiritual goals.
Louise received fine training from her parents,
which has helped her to enjoy a fulfilling life.
Cecilio and Schera
made sacrifices to be effective
Bible teachers, and their efforts made
a real difference in the lives of their students.
Before we close,
let’s visit our brothers and sisters in Nigeria.
Nigeria is the most populous country in Africa.
Its some 200 million people
speak over 500 languages.
More than 400,000 Jehovah’s Witnesses
live and preach there.
Many publishers come from other lands to share in the ministry.
The response to the good news is very encouraging.
More than 870,000 Bible studies
are conducted every month.
On average, about 40 people are baptized every day,
and seven new congregations
are formed every month.
This is the Obudu Ranch Congregation.
Their territory is beautiful, vast, and mountainous
—literally in the clouds.
Twenty-three publishers,
including two special pioneers, serve here.
To reach areas only accessible by foot,
the publishers sometimes walk for eight hours.
The terrain is challenging, but the long walk
provides opportunities for upbuilding association.
After working the territory, our brothers
stay overnight and walk back
another eight hours.
Our brothers and sisters in the Obudu Ranch Congregation
send their warm love and greetings!
From the World Headquarters of Jehovah’s Witnesses,
this is JW Broadcasting.

cn.text: 大家好！
通常12月份的电视节目
都会播放每年9月份举行的
基列学校毕业典礼
可是
就在今年的第149届基列学生
快要来到美国开始上课之前
疫情就爆发了
所以这届学生的课就延期了
因此这个月我们会集中谈一谈
怎样才能成为最好的圣经老师！
这个月的节目有
利文斯顿夫妇
为了帮助学生献身受浸崇拜耶和华
作出了很多牺牲
我们会看看他们夫妇
对圣经学生有怎样的影响
孩子的到来会带来很多快乐
但也会带来很多挑战
我们会了解
耶和华怎样帮助新手爸妈调整生活
负起新的责任
也会看看路薏丝·布兰顿的父母
怎样帮助她一生都快乐地崇拜耶和华
这是2020年12月份的JW电视！
这个月
我想谈谈的主题是根据哥林多前书3:10
《人人都要不断留意自己怎样建造》
建造
我们要谈的是总部即将在纽约拉马波
开始的建筑工程吗？
还是在你的国家一些正在建筑的
新王国聚会所呢？
当然，这些建筑工程也非常重要
不过我们今天会谈的建造
比这些建筑物还要更重要
让我们一起来看看
哥林多前书3:5的上下文
这里提到了亚波罗和保罗
他们扮演着怎么样的角色呢？
第5节
亚波罗和保罗帮助很多哥林多人认识真理
在第6到第9节
保罗把这种教导的工作比喻成栽种田地
一开始真理的种子撒在一个人的心里
借着续访和圣经课程
这些种子开始受到浇灌
一个人如果对真理有良好的反应
耶和华的神圣力量就会赐福给他
使真理的种子发芽
后来他会采取行动献身受浸，崇拜耶和华
你留意到吗？
第9节说
圣经老师是跟上帝一起工作的伙伴
对我们所有人来说
这是多么大的荣幸！
可以协助耶和华搜集来自万国的珍宝
现在我们知道
哥林多前书第3章这几节经文
在讨论的是什么了
它在说明圣经老师怎样帮助人成为门徒
但你有没有留意到在第9节
保罗换了一个比喻
他说
这个比喻跟农业有关
但下一句却说
他换了一个比喻
跟建筑有关
为什么他要换一个比喻呢？
建筑的比喻强调一个特别的要点
在耕种的比喻里
没有刻意强调
农夫对种子的生长产生多大的影响
因为农夫的工作只是负责浇水而已
使农作物生长的却是耶和华
不过
在建筑或建造的比喻里
却强调了参与建筑的人
也就是圣经老师需要付出的努力
建造房屋的人
对于建筑物最后的品质会有非常大的影响
他选择用怎样的建筑材料呢？
他施工仔细吗？
还是偷工减料
希望可以轻轻松松赶快完成呢？
现在我们一起看看哥林多前书第3章
我们读读第10节
在哥林多
保罗像一个工程主管一样
帮助很多人认识真理
保罗打下了良好根基
让其他人继续建造
那么根基是指什么呢？
第11节经文说
保罗根据真理的根基
也就是来自耶稣基督的教导
在哥林多建立了会众
根基建立之后
会有更多人成为圣经老师
帮助别人认识真理成为门徒
所以保罗在第10节提醒人
要留意自己怎样建造
因为这跟学生的生命有关
那么各位圣经老师
也包括父母们
我们想问问你
“我们可以怎样为别人打好根基呢？”
这样做很重要吗？

en.text: ‎Abel was an imperfect man, born to sinful parents.
‎Even so,
‎when he offered God a sacrifice as an act of worship,
‎Jehovah accepted his gift.
‎However, when Abel’s brother Cain offered God a gift,
‎Jehovah rejected his worship.
‎Why?
‎Please read with me Hebrews 11:4:
‎“By faith Abel offered God a sacrifice
‎“of greater worth than that of Cain,
‎“and through that faith he received the witness that he was righteous,
‎“for God approved his gifts,
‎“and although he died,
‎he still speaks through his faith.”
‎That scripture states the theme for the chapter
‎“‘God Approved’ Their Gifts.”
‎In this chapter, we’ll discuss four elements that are essential
‎if our worship is to be acceptable to God.
‎You’ll learn why Jehovah accepted worship from Abel
‎but not from Cain.
‎You’ll also consider what we can learn
‎from the examples of others mentioned in Hebrews chapter 11.
‎As you review the history of pure worship,
‎take time to meditate on the example set
‎by such faithful men as Noah, Abraham, and Jacob.
‎If you do so,
‎you will gain a deeper understanding
‎of what we need to do to give Jehovah
‎the pure worship he deserves.

en.text: We have 2,500 delegates coming in.
For us, we want to give them our absolute best.
What we want them to feel is the love of the true brotherhood.
The commission was to make it a life-changing experience.
In order to do that, we thought we had to put together more than just,
‘Come and have some dinner with us.’
Overwhelming —I don’t know how to express how I feel.
We had to first of all come up with and create the acts.
So I went in a room for two days and cried and prayed.
This is where the trust that Jehovah is directing us
through his organization has helped us.
There was so much more involved
in showing hospitality to our delegates than we originally thought.
We have an original, authentic, 1892 chuck wagon,
real Texas cowboys, real horse trainers,
roping lessons, and Texas Longhorns.
We’re making buttermilk biscuits just like they did on the trail
—in a Dutch oven with coals.
We have four different casts that we’re using
(each somewhere in the range of 80-90 per cast),
three different locations we’re going to be performing at,
and this spans over four days.
The evening programs include providing some food
to the friends that are here,
some spiritual entertainment with music, some interviews, some videos.
We haven’t had field service as part of our conventions as in the past.
However, it’s so apparent that Jehovah is behind this
—the example set by the slave;
it’s so evident that this should be done.
They’re facing similar challenges in the ministry,
but they’re still working hard while dealing with these challenges.
Hearing that was very encouraging,
and it gave me the renewed motivation to keep preaching with zeal.
We also needed volunteers to come to the Assembly Hall
and greet the delegates as they came in off the buses.
At first, I wasn’t sure why there were so many people outside
when I saw them from the bus.
When I found out that they were there to welcome us,
it brought me to tears.
When we found out that the tours were coming to the Assembly Hall,
we knew that we were going to have an extra special blessing.
We had well over 3,600 volunteers
and probably more like 5,000 that were willing to help.
We contacted probably a little bit over 200 congregations
to participate in these activities.
We are from Cheyenne, Wyoming —about 850 miles (1,367 km) away.
We started about two or three weeks ago
getting all the wagons ready,
and it took a couple of days to get here.
One of the things
I had to do was to ask permission at my job
—ask for a week off in order to be here.
I prayed a lot to Jehovah.
And through him, they gave me permission,
and I was able to be here.
I’m so energized and pumped,
and I really just see us walking into the new world
and feeling all of this every day.
My job has been to come up with drawings
and paintings for note cards
of things that are indigenous to Washington.
I had the privilege of designing the logo
that went on the gift bags for the international convention.
We’re going to sing for the delegates.
I want to sing for the delegates
because I want to make God happy and the delegates too.
The singing at the airports
—it was touching to see them waiting for us
at night, because we arrived around 10:00 p.m.
I think that they’ll be happy to see all of us welcoming them
and the things that we’re preparing for them
—something to take back with them to remember
this opportunity that they have had.
This part, the top part—the large JW
was actually from The Messenger,
which was back in 1931
at the international convention in Columbus, Ohio.
As you see with all the brothers and sisters
—everyone wanting to contribute, everyone wanting to have a part,
everyone wanting to be called, everyone wanting to participate
in whatever way they can.
Welcome to Seattle!
Just seeing it being used and enjoyed by the delegates
was a great feeling.
I was a little bit tired from the flight.
But when you (kind of like) saw all the smiles
and the cheers and the big banners and all the gifts,
it was just like, “Oh, my goodness!”
You felt loved, didn’t you? You felt loved straightaway.
You felt loved.
It was love.
We don’t know where they’re from.
We don’t know their names.
But they just smile and wave, and seeing that unity
—I mean it’s genuine love, and you just—
you just almost want to cry.
We want them to know
that they have brothers here that will support them
and who love them and are willing
to do whatever we can to make them enjoy their stay here.
Yes.
We just want them to feel
like our arms have been around them the whole time they’ve been here.
It really shows that Jehovah is behind the work.
But it also shows the loving brotherhood because it’s so evident
by what you see with all the happy faces —the zeal, the enthusiasm.
Everything that is being spent is all so that we can praise Jehovah
but also to welcome his sheep, the delegates,
coming from all the different parts of the world.
I hope that 2,000-3,000 years from now
somebody walks up to me and says: “I remember you!
You were at the cowboy deal in Texas!”
That, to me, would be fantastic.
I know cowboys aren’t supposed to cry, but trust us,
we do when it comes to this.
I’m so happy!
It moves me to tears.
They came here
to let us sing, and they watched us,
so they take our song with them.
We want the delegates to be happy!

en.text: Are you making full use of JW Library®?
Let’s learn how some are using it,
and then practice together.
I create notes in my Bible for many different reasons.
It could be a good point from a talk,
an illustration to help me to explain something to a Bible student,
or something for my own meditation.
I highlight the key phrase and create a note.
Let’s practice together.
If you have JW Library,
find 1 Timothy 2:6 in the Bible.
Now highlight the word “ransom,”
and tap the “Add a note” button.
Then type your comment.
Tapping the note marker in the margin
brings your comment into view.
I’ve created a lot of notes.
I use tags to help me find them again.
For example, whenever I hear a point that I want to use in the ministry,
I create a note and add a tag
like “prayer,” “ransom,” or “last days.”
Then when I’m in the ministry, I can quickly find my note.
Let’s practice together.
On the note you just created,
tap the three dots
and then “Edit.”
Now tap the button “Add a tag,”
and enter a tag name.
In this case, type “ransom.”
You can add as many tags as you like.
To find your notes again,
go to the Personal Study tab.
You can type in the Search box,
or you can just tap the tag.
As I read the Bible chapters for the midweek meeting,
I often come across verses that I want to understand better.
So I check the Research Guide.
Sometimes I use the points I find in a comment at the meeting.
Let’s practice together.
Are you still at 1 Timothy chapter 2?
Tap on the number for verse 6,
then tap the Research Guide button on the menu.
Now you can read information that explains this verse.
You can even copy a portion of the research and paste it into your note.

然后添加标签

title: 로버트 루시오니: 영적인 코어 근육을 강화하십시오 (디모데 후서 3:13)

ko.text: 우리가 강화해야 할 아주 중요한 근육이라고 말합니다.
뭔가에 부딪혀도 제대로 서 있을 수 있죠.
또 코어 근육이 튼튼하면 무거운 걸 들 수 있습니다.
그리고 넘어지더라도 다시 일어나는 것이 쉽습니다.
중심 근육인 코어를 강화시키는 운동은 매우 중요하며
그런데 오늘 실제로 하고 싶은 질문은 이것입니다.
우리의 영적인 코어 근육, 영적인 중심 근육들은 얼마나 강합니까?
그럼 강한 영적인 코어 근육이 얼마나 중요한지 오늘의 성구를 보시죠.
사도 바울은 악한 사람들이 “남의 집안에 슬그머니 들어가”
모세의 모든 말과 행동에 불신을 조장하려고 했죠.
마지막 날에 “악한 사람들과 속이는 사람들”이 나타날 것이고
그래서 바울은 디모데에게 무엇이 필요하다고 했습니까?
“그러나 그대는 배워서 확신하게 된 것에 머무르십시오.
그대는 그것을 누구에게서 배웠는지 알고 있으며,
그 기록들은 그리스도 예수에 대한 믿음을 통해
그대를 지혜롭게 하여 구원을 얻게 해 줄 수 있습니다.”
누구에게서 배웠는지 잊지 않고 기억할 필요가 있었습니다.
그것이 악한 사람들과 속이는 사람들에게 저항하는 데
강한 코어 근육과도 같은 이러한 믿음은
악하고 속이는 사람들이 예수께 사용한 수법들을 생각해 보십시오.
또 우리가 거기 있었다면 우리에게도 영향을 주었을 겁니다.
그들이 예수께 사용한 네 가지 수법을 살펴보시죠.
첫 번째로 거짓말과 허위 주장을 했습니다.
한 가지 예로 마태복음 11장을 함께 보실까요?
세금 징수원과 죄인들의 친구다’ 하고 말합니다.”
실제로 세금 징수원과 죄인들과 함께 드셨나요?
그분과 24시간 붙어 있는 게 아니라 모르겠네.
네, 거짓말로 의심이 싹트고 신뢰심이 흔들릴 수 있습니다.
악하고 속이는 사람들은 예수의 말씀을 왜곡했습니다.
“이 때문에 유대인들은 더욱 그분을 죽이려 했다.
사실 그러한 말을 하신 적이 없죠.
하지만 그들은 계속 예수의 말씀을 바꾸고 왜곡해서
그분이 하느님과 동등하다고 주장하는 것처럼 만들었죠.
만약 우리가 그 왜곡된 이야기를 전해 들었다면 어떠할까요?
왜곡된 이야기의 그 대목만 들은 거죠.
제자들이 소년에게서 악귀를 쫓아내지 못한 일이 있었죠.
내가 언제까지 여러분과 함께 있으면서 여러분에 대해 참아야 합니까?
우리가 알다시피 서기관들은 소년을 고치지 못한다고
우리가 그 자리에 있으면서 그 사건을 직접 봤다면 어땠을까요?
이게 그들의 임무고 해야 할 일인데 말이야.
사람들이 이해하지 못하는 말을 들었을 때
요한복음 6:54에서 예수께선 이런 말씀을 하신 적이 있죠.
“누구든지 내 살을 먹고 내 피를 마시는 사람에게는 영원한 생명이 있으며,
나는 마지막 날에 그를 부활시킬 것입니다.”
누가 저 말을 듣고 있을 수 있겠는가?’ 하고 말했다.”
“[그들은] 떠나가고 더 이상 그분과 함께 다니지 않았다.”
그들은 시간을 들여 그 말씀을 이해하려 하거나
예수께서 분명히 설명해 주시길 기다리지 않고
그 결과 많은 사람이 예수를 떠났습니다.
그 말씀을 감당할 수 없었던 것이죠.
이번에는 예수의 말씀을 직접 들었다면 어떨까요?
이 말씀은 도저히 이해가 안 되네.
갈수록 더 이상한 얘기를 하시는 것 같아.’
사실 이 무리는 예수를 따르기를 좋아했고
수천 명이 와서 그분께 와서 먹고
결국에는 대부분이 예수 곁에 남아 있지 않았습니다.
기적을 보는 것만 아니라, 그런 부가적인 것들만 아니라
바로 하느님의 아들이라는 믿음이 꼭 필요했기 때문입니다.
그들의 영적 코어 근육은 강하지 않았습니다.
하지만 예수의 제자들은 코어 근육이 강했죠.
때때로 넘어져 혼란을 느낄 때가 있었지만
하느님의 아들의 말씀을 듣고 있다는 확신을 가졌기 때문입니다.
오늘날에도 악하고 속이는 사람들은 똑같은 수법을 사용하고 있습니다.
그들은 거짓말을 하고 허위 주장을 합니다.
그들은 우리가 아동 학대의 가해자를 다루고
피해자를 돌보는 방법에 관해 거짓말을 하죠.
제명 처분에 대해 우리가 한 말을 왜곡합니다.
그리고 실수로 보이는 것들을 이용해 공격합니다.
마지막 때에 관한 우리의 이해에 관해
단정적으로 말했다가 나중에 바꿨다는 식으로 말이죠.
또 그들은 이해하지 못하는 변화에 대해 반감을 갖게 만듭니다.
그 결과 어떤 사람들은 마음이 흔들리죠.
우리 각자는 성경을 깊이 있게 정기적으로 연구해야 합니다.
또한 여호와께서 우리에게 좋은 것을 베푸시기 위해
중앙장로회를 사용하고 계시다는 사실을 기억해야 합니다.
우리가 영적으로 누리고 있는 부가적인 것들이
모두 사라질 때가 올 수 있기 때문입니다.
JW 방송을 더는 볼 수 없다면 어떠합니까?
흥미진진한 연례 총회를 더는 즐길 수 없다면 어떠합니까?
지금도 일부 형제 자매들은 이런 걸 즐기지 못하고 있습니다.
디모데 후서 3:14, 15에 있는 사도 바울의 조언을 따라야겠습니다.
우리가 아는 모든 좋은 것들을 누구에게서 배웠는지 기억합시다.
이 영적인 코어 근육을 강하게 유지한다면
앞으로 있을 일도 헤쳐 나가게 될 것입니다.

en.text: How strong is your core?
Now, health experts will tell you
that the core is
one of the most important groups
of muscles that you can strengthen.
These are the muscles
that are in the trunk of the body
from somewhere around the neck to the waist.
And a strong core will keep you standing if something knocks against you.
Having a strong core will allow you to carry a heavy weight.
And if you fall, a strong core
will help you to get back up on your feet.
So thus, experts say that exercises that strengthen the core,
these foundational muscles, are so important,
especially for older people.
So how strong is your core?
But the real question we want to consider today is,
How strong is your spiritual core
—our spiritual foundational muscles?
Now, we see the importance of having a strong spiritual core
when we look at today’s text in 2 Timothy chapter 3.
If you look up verse 6, here the apostle Paul is talking
about wicked “men who slyly work their way
into households” and deceive many.
At verse 8, he talks about “Jannes and Jambres [who] opposed Moses.”
These were wicked men, “completely corrupted in mind,”
who tried to discredit everything that Moses said and did.
And then, as we see in today’s text, Paul said that “wicked men and impostors”
would arise in the last days and they would “advance from bad to worse.”
Well, what did Paul say would help Timothy?
What did he need to do?
He needed a strong spiritual core.
What was that?
Well, look what he says in verses 14 and 15—2 Timothy 3.
He says: “You, however, continue in the things that you learned
“and were persuaded to believe, knowing from whom you learned them
“and that from infancy you have known the holy writings,
which are able to make you wise for salvation through faith in Christ Jesus.”
Do you see the two things?
Number one: He needed to have a deep understanding
and trust of “the holy writings,” the Scriptures.
And two: He needed to never forget, to remember,
from whom he learned all the good things that he knew.
See, he needed to make sure that was solid.
That would help him to deal with the wicked men
and impostors.
Now, this solid, spiritual foundation
is what also helped Jesus’ apostles.
Think about the tactics that the wicked men and imposters
used against Jesus and how this could have affected the apostles
or affected us, if we had been there.
Let’s consider four tactics that they used against Jesus.
Number one: They used lies and misrepresentation.
Turn back, if you will, to Matthew 11:9 as an example
—Matthew 11:19, excuse me.
Matthew 11:19—it says:
“The Son of man did come eating and drinking, but people say,
“‘Look! A man who is a glutton and is given to drinking wine,
a friend of tax collectors and sinners.’”
Now, did Jesus like to eat and drink?
Yes.
Did he, in fact, eat with tax collectors and sinners?
Yes.
But you know what the wicked men and imposters did?
They stretched it to say, ‘Well, you see, he’s a glutton;
he’s a drunkard; he is a friend of tax collectors and sinners.’
Look at Luke 15:2;
it even kind of insinuates that he condones their behavior
or maybe even shares in their sins.
What if you were there?
‘Now, we know he likes to eat and drink,
‘but I’m not with him 24 hours a day.
I hope that’s not true.’
Can you see how that could plant seeds of doubt?
how it could rock somebody?
A second tactic: Wicked men and imposters would also twist Jesus’ words.
Look at John 5:18 as an example.
John 5:18—it says:
“This is why the Jews began seeking all the more to kill him,
“because not only was he breaking the Sabbath
“but he was also calling God his own Father,
making himself equal to God.”
So here they twist Jesus’ words,
saying that Jesus was saying that he was “equal to God.”
Jesus never said that he was equal to God.
He said that he was God’s Son; he said: “The Father is greater than I am.”
But they constantly took Jesus’ words and repackaged them,
twisting them to make it sound like Jesus was off on his own.
Now, what if you heard that story told and retold?
You didn’t hear the conversation,
but you heard the story; you heard the sound bite.
‘Wow! Did he really say that?
‘Now, that would be out of line if he had,
because nobody is equal to God.’
They also capitalized on errors that were made.
Look over to Luke chapter 9.
You remember, this is the account when the disciples
could not cast out the demon in the young man.
And you look at verse 40.
Here the father says —Luke 9:40—
he says: “‘I begged your disciples to expel it, but they could not.’
“In response Jesus said: ‘O faithless and twisted generation,
“‘how long must I continue with you and put up with you?
Bring your son over here.’”
Now, as we know, apparently the scribes were criticizing
the disciples because of their failure to heal the boy.
Now, again, what if you were standing there?
What if you saw this one with your own eyes?
‘Wait a minute, those are Jesus’ disciples.
‘That’s their commission.
‘That’s what they’re supposed to do.
Perhaps these people aren’t as special as I thought they were.’
Wicked men and impostors
would also inflame statements that people did not understand.
Look at John 6:54.
You remember here when Jesus said:
“Whoever feeds on my flesh and drinks my blood has everlasting life,
and I will resurrect him on the last day.”
What was the reaction?
You look at verse 60:
“When they heard this, many of the disciples said:
‘This speech is shocking; who can listen to it?’”
Verse 66: “[They] went off to the things behind
and would no longer [follow] him.”
See, rather than giving it time to see if they understood it correctly
or waiting to see if maybe Jesus clarified the statement, it knocked them.
And you notice (in verse 52) the Jews further stirred this up,
and because of that, many stopped following him.
It was too heavy for them to carry.
Now, what if you were there, and this time you heard Jesus say that?
‘Whoa! Man, that’s odd!
‘I don’t think I can explain that teaching.
He seems to be getting more and more extreme.’
Well, how did many react to these attacks?
Well, the crowds loved to follow Jesus.
They loved to hear his winsome words.
‘No man has ever spoken like this.’
Thousands would come to be fed by him and to be healed by him,
but in the end, most did not stick with Jesus.
Why?
Well, because when you strip all the other peripherals away,
all the other extras away,
it came down to their faith in Bible prophecy
and that this man that was speaking to them
was the Son of God.
Their spiritual core was not strong enough.
Now, Jesus’ disciples had a strong spiritual core.
See, even though they did get knocked down
—they got confused at times— they stayed solid.
They were able to get back up. Why?
Because they recalled the Scriptures,
and they were convinced that they were listening to the Son of God.
Well, today, wicked men and imposters use exactly the same techniques.
And it’s only going to get worse.
They use lies and misrepresentation.
They lie about how we deal with child abusers
and how we care for the victims of child abuse.
They twist statements that are made regarding our stand on blood,
loyalty to families, disfellowshipping.
They capitalize on what they perceive as errors
—perhaps dogmatic statements we made in the past
regarding a Bible prophecy or our understanding of the time of the end,
and then we later changed it.
They also put a negative spin on changes that they do not understand
—why we simplified and did reassignments in 2015,
new explanations of the generation, or changes at world headquarters.
What’s the result? Well, some are swayed by these things.
They’re stumbled; they’re knocked down.
It’s too heavy for them to carry.
How about us?
How strong is our spiritual core?
See, that’s why we hear repeatedly
that we must personally have a regular,
deep study of the Scriptures.
That’s why we’re reminded repeatedly that Jehovah
is using the Governing Body to give us the good things that we have.
Now, why is that so important?
Well, because one day we may hit a time,
whether personally (in our personal life) or as an organization,
when all the other spiritual peripherals are gone—all the extras.
What do we do then?
What do we do, for example, if the lights go out on JW Broadcasting®?
What happens, perhaps, when we don’t have the incredible conventions,
the touching videos, the catchy music,
the beautifully-written (well-written) Watchtower  articles,
the exciting annual meetings?
They’re gone.
See, some of our brothers and sisters do not have access
to those things right now.
Well, you see, at that time, it will come down to our faith
that this is God’s Word
and that the Governing Body is the channel that Jehovah has been using.
So during this period of relative calm,
may we follow the advice of the apostle Paul
at 2 Timothy 3:14, 15
and know “the holy writings” inside and out
and remember from whom we’ve learned all the good things that we know.
That’s our spiritual core —strengthen it; maintain it.
It will stabilize us, and it will help us
to get through the things that are yet to come.

cn.text: 你的核心肌群有多强壮？
有些医学专家说
核心肌群是我们特别需要训练的肌肉
这些肌肉位于脖子以下，腰部以上
如果核心肌群够强壮
我们受到撞击时就不那么容易跌倒
强壮的核心肌群能够让你搬运重物
如果你跌倒了
强壮的核心肌群也可以帮助你站起来
难怪有些专家说，要训练我们的核心肌群
这些核心肌群特别重要，尤其是对老年人
那你的核心肌群有多强壮呢？
其实，我们要讨论的是
你的比喻性的核心肌群有多强壮呢？
也就是，你有多信赖耶和华和他的组织呢？
从提摩太后书3章我们可以学到
不断增强对耶和华的信心有多重要
在3:6保罗提到
有些邪恶的人潜入别人家里去迷惑人
在第8节他也说，雅尼和杨布反对摩西
这些邪恶的人思想完全腐败
他们想方设法破坏人们对摩西的信任
接着在13节里，保罗说
在最后的日子
邪恶的人和骗子会越来越坏
保罗给提摩太什么提醒呢？
他需要怎样做呢？
他需要有强壮的核心肌群
这是什么呢？
在提摩太后书3:14,15
保罗对他说
“你却要持守你学到的道理
因为你是经过学习
受到劝导才确信这些事的
而且你知道是跟谁学的
也知道你从婴儿时期就认识圣经
你认识圣经，相信基督耶稣
就有智慧可以得救。”
保罗提到两件事
第一，提摩太需要深入学习
并确信他从圣经学到的这些话
第二，他要记得，这些道理是跟谁学的
所以，提摩太需要加强对耶和华
以及对圣经的信心
也要信赖那些教他真理的人
就能抵抗邪恶的人和骗子
这种坚强的信心也曾帮助过使徒们
邪恶的人和骗子曾用过哪些伎俩反对耶稣？
这可能对使徒们有什么影响？
如果我们在场的话
我们又会受到什么影响？
来看看他们用过的四个伎俩
第一，他们说谎，歪曲事实
我们来看看马太福音11:19里面的一个例子
马太福音11:19
经文说
“人子来到，也吃也喝，人们却说
‘看！这个人贪食好酒
跟收税人和罪人做朋友。’”
那么，耶稣喜欢吃喝吗？
喜欢
他跟收税人和罪人一起吃饭了吗？
对
但是，邪恶的人和骗子
他们加油添醋地说
你们看，这个人贪食好酒
跟收税人和罪人做朋友
在路加福音15:2，那些邪恶的人暗示
耶稣纵容罪行， 甚至自己也犯了罪
如果你在场，也许会这样想
我不是24小时都跟耶稣在一起
谁知道他会不会贪食好酒呢？
你看出，怀疑和不信任是怎么开始的吗？
第二个伎俩
邪恶的人和骗子也歪曲耶稣的话
约翰福音5:18就是一个例子
约翰福音5:18说
“于是犹太人更想要杀他
因为他不只触犯了安息日的规定
还把上帝称为自己的父亲
自命跟上帝平等。”
他们歪曲耶稣的话
说耶稣“自命跟上帝平等”
耶稣从没有这样说过
他说，他是上帝的儿子
也说:“父亲是比我大的。”
但他们不断歪曲耶稣的话，以讹传讹
让人觉得耶稣自命与上帝平等
如果你听到这个被歪曲的故事
你没有听到耶稣这样说
但是你听到别人讲到的只言片语
啊！他真的这么说吗？
他这样说的话就大错特错了
因为没有人和上帝平等
他们也利用耶稣门徒的错误攻击他
我们再来看一段经文
在路加福音第9章有一段记载
门徒不能帮一个孩子驱走邪灵
路加福音9:40，孩子的父亲说
“我求过你的门徒把邪灵赶出去
但他们办不到
耶稣回应说
‘这一代又不信又歪邪的人啊
我要跟你们在一起到什么时候
要容忍你们多久呢？
把你的儿子带到这里来吧。’”
显然，抄经士批评门徒
因为他们不能治好这个男孩
这一次，如果你在场
亲眼见到这一切，会怎么想呢？
等等，他们不是耶稣的门徒吗？
不是应该给人治病吗？
难道，耶稣没给他们这个能力吗？
看来没有
民众不理解耶稣说的话
邪恶的人和骗子就利用这一点激怒他们
来看约翰福音6:54，耶稣说
“谁吃我的肉，喝我的血
谁就会有永远的生命
在最后的日子，我会使他复活。”
民众有什么反应呢？
请看第60节
“他门徒中有很多人听到就说
这样的话骇人听闻，谁听得进去呢？”
第66节，他们就离开了
“回去照料已经撇下的事务
不再与他同行。”
他们没有找答案
也没有等耶稣解释，就离开了
52节说
他们听了耶稣的话之后，激动地争论起来
后来有些人不再跟从耶稣了
他们没办法接受耶稣说的话
如果当时你在场
也听到耶稣亲自说这些话
啊！
一定会觉得很奇怪
他到底在说什么啊？
他说的话太夸张了！
那人们有什么反应呢？
很多人很想跟随耶稣
耶稣说的话非常吸引他们
因为从来没有人像他那样讲话的！
耶稣喂饱也医好了很多的人
但到最后，大部分人都没有跟随耶稣
为什么呢？
如果我们抽丝剥茧
就会发现他们根本的问题在哪里
他们对圣经的预言没有信心
他们没有看出
这位正在跟他们说话的人就是上帝的儿子
这就好比他们的核心肌群不够强壮
耶稣的门徒拥有非常强壮的核心肌群
虽然有的时候他们的确不明白耶稣的意思
但是他们信心坚强
他们继续跟随耶稣
因为他们相信圣经
他们知道耶稣就是上帝的儿子
今天，邪恶的人和骗子
他们也用同样的手法
而且他们的做法更加邪恶
他们说谎， 而且歪曲事实
比如，在关于处理侵犯儿童这件事上
他们诬蔑我们
关于不输血、家庭关系，以及开除的安排
他们也歪曲了我们说过的话
他们找到了一些我们以往的错误
虽然我们现在都调整过来了
例如，我们对一些圣经预言的理解错误
对最后的日子的不合理期待
他们还质疑我们的动机
例如，在2015年
为什么要简化工作以及调整人事安排
质疑我们对“这一代人”的新的解释
还有搬迁世界总部等等
结果有些人的信心动摇了
有些人不再崇拜耶和华了
他们没办法接受这些改变
那我们呢？
我们的比喻性的核心肌群够强壮吗？
这就是为什么我们不断受到提醒
我们一定要经常深入地研读圣经
这也是为什么我们不断受到提醒
耶和华现在正运用中央长老团
给我们指引以及保护
为什么这些事那么重要呢？
因为也许有一天，可能我们的环境改变了
或是中央长老团不再能提供给我们这些
加强信心的东西
很多额外的资料和安排都没有了
我们该怎么办呢？
例如，如果有一天
我们不再能收看JW电视
不再有令人难忘的大会，让人感动的影片
悦耳的音乐，深入人心的《守望台》文章
以及令人振奋的年会
这些东西都没了，我们会怎么样呢？
其实现在有很多弟兄姐妹都没有这些东西
所以到时，最重要的
是我们要对上帝的话语有信心
也要相信
上帝任用中央长老团来保护以及帮助我们
在现在相对平静的时期
我们要留意保罗在提摩太后书3:14,15的话
要透彻地认识圣经
也要记得
我们是跟谁学习到这些宝贵的真理
要加强我们比喻性的核心肌群
也就是信心
这样，我们就能应付将来的任何挑战

titles.ko: 로버트 루시오니: 영적인 코어 근육을 강화하십시오 (디모데 후서 3:13)

ko.text: 예수께서는 마지막 날에 일어날 일에 대해 설명하시면서
여러분은 얼마나 오랫동안 깨어 살펴 오셨나요?
우리는 참으로 “대처하기 어려운 위급한 때”에 살고 있습니다.
우리는 여러 해 동안 오늘날의 세상 상태에 대해 전파해 왔죠.
현재 성취되고 있는 몇 가지 성경 예언을 살펴보고,
11월에 하느님의 왕국을 알리는 특별 운동이 얼마나 시기 적절한지 검토할 것입니다.
우선, 예수께서 제자들에게 알려 주신 표징에 대해 생각해 볼까요?
예수께서는 “곳곳에 식량 부족과 역병이 있을 것”이라고 말씀하셨습니다.
우리는 마지막 날의 표징의 이 부분이
매우 두드러지게 성취되고 있는 것을 보고 있습니다.
바빌론 제국부터 우리 시대까지 이어져 온
그러면 단단한 철과 부드러운 진흙이 섞여 있다는 것은 무엇을 상징합니까?
진흙은 영미 세계 강국의 영역 안에서 급진적인 성향을 나타내는 일반 사람들을 상징하는데,
그들은 철 같은 힘을 발휘할 수 있는 영미 세계 강국의 능력을 약화시킵니다.
그들이 철과 진흙처럼 “서로 달라붙지 않을 것”이라고 알려 주죠.
철과 진흙에 관한 내용의 분명한 증거를 다음과 같이 지적했습니다.
근소한 차이밖에 나지 않는 선거 결과 때문에,
오늘날의 상황에 더 잘 들어맞지 않습니까?
성경 예언이 바로 지금 어떻게 성취되고 있는지 곰곰이 생각해 보면
말들에게 물을 주는 큰 통에서 침례를 받았어요.
연단 앞에 특별히 마련된 좌석에 앉으라는 요청을 받았죠.
여러분 모두 무료로 한 부씩 받게 될 겁니다.’
여호와를 더 열심히 섬겨야겠다는 마음을 갖게 됐죠.
그 이전부터 보조 파이오니아 봉사를 해 와서
전 시간 봉사에 대한 열망을 키울 수 있었죠.
여러 해 동안 충실하게 봉사해 온
연로한 형제 자매들도 낙담할 수 있죠.
친밀한 관계를 누리는 게 정말 중요합니다.
모든 문제를 해결해 줄 것이라고 기대합니다.
특별 전파 활동이 있을 거라는 말을 듣고
앞으로 다른 예언들도 성취될 것이라는 확신이 강해집니다.
영원히 사라질 것이라고 알려 주는 예언들 말이죠.
땅을 영원히 통치할 유일한 정부가 될 것입니다.
인류의 문제의 유일하고 진정한 해결책인 하느님의 왕국을 알리고 있다는 것은
과거에 여호와를 섬겼다가 그분의 조직을 떠난 사람들 가운데 일부는
다시 여호와의 조직으로 돌아와야겠다는 마음을 갖게 되었습니다.
현재 무활동이거나 제명된 상태에 있는 분들이라면
인근 회중의 장로들에게 도움을 요청하시도록 권해 드립니다.
또한 이 잡지를 읽어 보고 싶다면
자매는 그의 말을 잘 들어 주고
오늘날 세상에서 일어나는 일에 대해 어떻게 생각하는지 물어보았습니다.
자매는 예수께서 이런 일이 있을 것을 모두 예언하셨고
조만간 하느님의 왕국이 모든 문제를 해결해 줄 것이라고 말해 주었죠.
일이 끝난 다음 남편과 함께 다시 전화해서 대화를 계속할 수 있는지 물어보았습니다.
그 여자는 약속한 대로 남편과 함께 다시 전화를 걸었습니다.
자매는 지금 전하고 있는 「파수대」 제2호를 사용하여
성경을 알아보는 게 중요함을 깨달았다고 말했죠.
자료를 자신들의 모국어로 볼 수 있다는 것에 감동을 받았죠.
성경에 관해 계속 토의하고 싶어 하며
그들을 계속 돕기 위한 마련을 하고 있습니다.
네, 프랑스를 비롯하여 전 세계에 있는
수개월 전만 해도 우리의 삶은 지금과 많이 달랐죠.
급변할 수 있다는 중요한 교훈을 배웠습니다.
그때 우리가 어떤 반응을 보여야 하는지를 이렇게 알려 주셨습니다.
도둑이 밤 몇 시에 올지 집주인이 알았더라면,
집에 도둑이 침입하지 못하게 했을 것입니다.
준비하고 있어야겠다는 마음이 더 강해지지 않습니까?
우리의 주의를 산만하게 하는 것들로 인해
우리는 이전 어느 때보다도 열심히 기도하고 연구하고
집회에 참석하고 꾸준히 봉사에 참여해야 합니다.
왕국에 대해 알리는 이번 특별 활동에
이 활동에 아직 참여해 보지 않은 분이 있다면 꼭 참여해 보십시오.
인류가 겪고 있는 모든 문제에 대한 해결책인 왕국에 대해 알리는 것은
우리가 “깨어 살피”고 “준비하고 있는” 데 도움이 될 것입니다.

en.text: “Keep on the watch.”
That’s what Jesus told his disciples
after describing the events
of the last days.
How long have you been keeping on the watch?
We’re certainly experiencing
“critical times hard to deal with.”
These are the conditions
we’ve been preaching about for years.
In this update, let’s review
some of the prophecies being fulfilled
right before our eyes
and reflect on the timeliness
of the November campaign publicizing God’s Kingdom.
First, think about the sign Jesus gave his disciples.
At Luke 21:11, Jesus said
we would see “food shortages and pestilences”
“in one place after another.”
Well, we are now experiencing
the fulfillment of this part of the sign
in a very pronounced way.
A second prophecy to consider
is recorded in Daniel chapter 2.
There we read about an immense image representing
a succession of human kingdoms
from the Babylonian Empire down to today.
The feet and toes at the bottom of that image
represent the Anglo-American World Power,
and Daniel tells us
they are “partly of iron and partly of clay.”
Do you remember what this mix of hard iron
and soft clay represents?
The clay pictures the radical and popular elements
within the sphere of the United States and Britain
that weaken its ability to act
with ironlike strength.
Daniel 2:43 says:
“They will not stick together, one to the other.”
The Watchtower  of June 15, 2012,
pointed out clear evidence
of the iron and clay when it said:
“Opposing ideologies
“and close election results
“that do not end up in a clear majority
“have weakened the power base
“of even popular leaders,
“so that they have no clear mandate
to implement their policies.”
Would you agree that this is more evident now
than eight years ago when this was published?
Reflecting on the fulfillment of Bible prophecy
that we are seeing right now can fortify our faith.
In the following interview,
Brother Richard Kelsey, who was baptized in 1941,
shares his thoughts about what’s helped him
to keep on the watch for some 80 years.
I was baptized in June 1941
in Des Moines, Iowa,
at the same time as Peggy,
and we were baptized in a horse watering tank there.
And this was shortly before the international convention
in St. Louis, Missouri.
We, as youngsters and children,
were all asked to sit in the first rows
in front of the stage, and Brother Rutherford
gave the talk “Children of the King.”
And during this talk
at the conclusion, he said,
‘There is a new book, the Children  book,
and you will all get a free copy.’
That motivated me greatly.
And, of course, when it was studied later,
that was even a greater motivation to serve Jehovah.
I started pioneering in September 1948,
but I had already auxiliary pioneered and, of course, that whetted
my appetite for full-time service.
We see world conditions worsening, and that could frighten us.
It could be that faithful older ones could become discouraged
after many years, and it’s very important
to have a close relationship with Jehovah
—an intimate relationship.
We look forward to his Kingdom rule
as a solution for all problems.
Young ones will see the faithfulness
of the older ones and will want
to imitate their faith.
And, of course, that’s pleasing to Jehovah.
Well, when we heard that there was going
to be a special campaign now,
Peggy and I—my wife and I—applied
for auxiliary pioneer service.
We have been preaching God’s Kingdom for many years,
and now there is a special campaign
devoted to that subject, God’s Kingdom.
And it’s going to be a highlight
in our many years of service to Jehovah.
Like Brother Kelsey,
has your confidence in Jehovah’s promises
been strengthened by what you see happening today?
People around the world realize
how unusual it is to have a pandemic,
food shortages, civil unrest, earthquakes,
and other disasters all occur at the same time.
Watching the fulfillment of Bible prophecies builds our confidence
in other prophecies yet to be fulfilled
—prophecies that promise permanent relief
from the problems we’re dealing with.
For example, as Daniel 2:44 tells us,
soon God’s Kingdom will become the only government
ruling over the earth—forever!
Isn’t it exciting that, amidst these critical times,
we’re participating in a special campaign
clearly pointing people to the only real solution,
God’s Kingdom?
Some who were once associated with Jehovah’s organization
are also recognizing the fulfillment of Bible prophecy
and have been motivated to come back.
If you are inactive or disfellowshipped,
we encourage you to speak to the elders in your local congregation;
they’ll be happy to assist you.
If you’d like a copy of this magazine,
please go to our website, jw.org,
and download it or ask any one of Jehovah’s Witnesses for a copy.
Just a few days into the November campaign,
a sister in France got a call from a telemarketer.
Let’s listen as Brother Bruno Faure
explains how she took advantage
of the opportunity to advertise the Kingdom.
Clearly, the zealous efforts of our brothers in France
and around the world are resulting in a great witness.
Many people are surprised to see
how quickly things have changed in 2020.
Just a few months ago, life was very different.
This is a very good lesson for us
on how fast things can change in the future.
After saying the words “keep on the watch”
at Matthew 24:42,
notice what Jesus said about the suddenness
of these events that would occur and how we should react.
Matthew 24:42-44 says:
“Keep on the watch, therefore,
“because you do not know ‏
“on what day your Lord is coming.
“But know one thing:
“If the householder had known
“in what watch the thief was coming,
“he would have kept awake
“and not allowed his house to be broken into.
“On this account,
“you too prove yourselves ready,
“because the Son of man [Jesus]
“is coming at an hour that you
do not think to be it.”
Hasn’t the fast-changing world situation
heightened your appreciation
for the need to “prove yourselves ready”?
Rather than allowing distractions to diminish
our spiritual alertness,
now more than ever we need to pray,
study, attend meetings,
and stay active in the ministry.
Thank you to all of you who have worked tirelessly
on this Kingdom campaign.
If you haven’t participated in the campaign yet,
be sure to do so.
What a privilege it is to advertise the Kingdom
—the solution to all of mankind’s problems!
By doing so, we can “keep on the watch”
and ‘prove ourselves ready.’
Please be assured of our constant prayers in your behalf
and our warmest love.
From the World Headquarters of Jehovah’s Witnesses,
this is JW Broadcasting®.

cn.text: “要不断守望”
耶稣告诉他的门徒
“最后的日子”会发生什么事之后
要他们不断守望
而你已经不断守望多久了呢？
毫无疑问
我们正生活在“难以应付的非常时期”
而这个信息我们已经传讲了很多年了
在这个报告里
我们会看看一些正在应验的圣经预言
我们也可以从中看出
在11月进行宣扬上帝王国的特别活动
是多么恰当的时候！
我们先看看
耶稣告诉门徒有关“最后的日子”的征象
在路加福音21:11，耶稣说
我们会看到“一处接一处有粮荒和瘟疫”
我们现在比以往任何时候更清楚看到
这个预言正在大规模地应验，不是吗？
我们会考虑的第二个预言
记录在但以理书第2章
在那里我们读到一个巨像
它代表着不断改变的世界霸权
从巴比伦帝国的时代一直到我们今天
巨像最底部的脚和脚趾
代表着英美世界霸权
而但以理告诉我们
这个部分是由“铁和陶泥”相混而成的
你还记得
强硬的铁和柔软的陶泥代表什么吗？
陶泥代表美国和英国
这个世界霸权统治下那些激进的人民
他们的反对和抗议
削弱了政府钢铁般强硬的统治力量
但以理书2:43说
铁和陶泥相混却不能黏合
《守望台》2012年6月15日刊提到
我们可以清楚看出
是哪两个部分代表“铁和陶泥”

ko.text: 형제들이 연합하여 함께 거하는 것이 얼마나 좋으며 얼마나 즐거운가!”
이 성구가 참되다는 것을 분명히 볼 수 있었습니다.
저는 2018년 5월에 본부 대표자로 아내 수잔과 함께
이 두 지부를 방문할 기회가 있었습니다.
이 두 지부는 최근 몇 년간 큰 변화를 겪었습니다.
언어와 문화가 다른 몇몇 지부들과 통합된 것이죠.
형제들이 이러한 상황에 어떻게 대처하고 있는지 직접 보는 것은
이전에 덴마크, 아이슬란드, 노르웨이, 스웨덴에 있던 지부들이
스칸디나비아 지부는 코펜하겐에서 한 시간 정도 떨어진 홀베크에 있습니다.
도시 외곽의 멋진 곳에 자리 잡은 지부 시설 주변은
방문 기간 내내 날씨가 정말 화창했는데
그래서 모두가 따뜻한 날씨와 햇살을 즐겼습니다.
하지만 지부에서 일하는 형제들이 나타낸 사랑은 그보다 더 따뜻했죠.
이 지부에는 총 92명의 정규 베델 봉사자가 있습니다.
저는 이곳 형제들이 어떻게 작업을 하는지,
특히 영적 프로그램을 어떻게 즐기는지 궁금했는데요.
형제들은 세 가지 언어를 모두 사용하고 있었습니다.
예를 들어, 아침 숭배 때 사회는 덴마크어로,
시작 기도는 노르웨이어로, 해설은 스웨덴어로 제공되기도 했습니다.
또 그린란드와 페로 제도에 있는 현지 번역 사무실에서
세 가지 언어가 다르긴 해도 서로 비슷한 점이 많아서
형제들은 서로의 말을 이해하는 데 크게 어려움이 없습니다.
하지만 원활한 의사소통을 위해 형제들은 안내 책자를 만들었습니다.
그 책자에는 자주 사용하는 단어들과 그 의미가 언어별로 나와 있습니다.
또한 그 책자는 “다섯 가지 계명”을 소개하는데,
그 덕분에 서로 오해하는 일을 크게 줄일 수 있습니다.
하지만 다섯 가지 계명을 잘 적용한다면
노르웨이 형제는 덴마크 형제에게서 “참 특이하시네요”라는 말을 듣더라도
이 언어들로 번역하는 일은 현지 번역 사무실 즉 RTO에서 진행됩니다.
모든 RTO는 각각의 언어가 사용되는 나라에 있죠.
RTO가 운영되는 방식은 베델과 매우 비슷합니다.
보통 식사는 제공되지만 세탁과 교통편 마련은 각자가 합니다.
우리는 스웨덴 말뫼에 있는 RTO에 방문할 기회가 있었습니다.
덴마크에서 차를 타고 조금만 가면 되는 곳이죠.
스웨덴의 RTO에서 일하는 형제 자매들은 근처에 있는 아파트를 숙소로 사용합니다.
형제들은 영적 양식을 스웨덴어와 스웨덴 수화로 번역하는 작업과
오디오 파일로 제작하는 작업을 하느라 바쁘게 일하고 있습니다.
공간이 다소 비좁긴 해도 이곳에는 기쁨이 가득합니다.
형제들은 서로 협력하며 즐겁게 일하고 있죠.
베델 업무를 수행하고 지부 구역 전체를 돌보는 데
최신 기술이 큰 도움이 되고 있습니다.
스칸디나비아 지역에 있는 모든 회중에 특별 강연을 제공할 때
그 점을 분명히 볼 수 있었습니다.
스트리밍을 통해 이 연설을 들을 수 있었습니다.
핀란드 지부를 방문했을 때도 같은 연설을 했는데
스트리밍을 통해 관할 구역 내의 모든 왕국회관들로 송출되었습니다.
에스토니아, 라트비아, 리투아니아 세 지부에서 돌보던 구역들이 포함되었습니다.
현재 현지 번역 사무실이나 왕국 전파자 학교,
순회 감독자 부부 학교를 위한 시설로 잘 사용되고 있습니다.
스칸디나비아 지부와 핀란드 지부는 개축 작업을 통해
사무 공간이나 안락한 휴식 공간으로 바꾸었죠.
또한 방문객들에게 이 지역들에서 수행된 왕국 활동의 역사에 대해 알려 주는
저는 이전에 각 지부에서 여러 해 동안 지부 위원으로 일해 온 형제들이
이러한 통합에 대해 어떻게 느끼는지 궁금했습니다.
그들의 말을 통해 그들이 영성이 얼마나 강한지,
여호와와 그분이 조직을 통해 베푸시는 인도를 얼마나 신뢰하는지 알 수 있었습니다.
라르스-에리크 에릭손 형제는 스웨덴에서 14년간 지부 위원으로 일했습니다.
그는 지부 통합에 관한 중앙장로회의 결정에 대해 듣고 어떻게 느꼈습니까?
놀라기는 했지만 생각해 보면 그리 놀라워할 일은 아니었습니다.
전 세계의 다른 지역들에서 몇몇 지부들이 이미 통합되고 있었기 때문이죠.
예전에 스웨덴의 지부 위원으로 일한 형제들이
재미 삼아 이렇게 얘기하던 기억이 납니다.
통합된 지부가 있을 곳은 스웨덴일 거라고 말이죠.
또 우리는 노르웨이와 스웨덴 지부만 통합될 줄 알았습니다.
당시에 노르웨이의 지부 위원으로 일하던 한 형제가 제게 전화를 했습니다.
새로 통합될 지부가 왜 덴마크에 있어야 하는지
숙소를 비롯한 다른 시설들이 이미 충분히 갖추어져 있고
그에 비해 덴마크 지부는 규모가 작지 않냐고 말했습니다.
그분의 길이 우리의 길보다 높다’는 중요한 교훈을 배웠습니다.
시작 단계부터 베델 가족들이 아주 잘 협조해 주었습니다.
특히 초반에 우리는 이 지부가 덴마크 지부나
그와 비슷한 일을 겪은 핀란드 지부에서 지부 위원으로 일하는
국적과 문화와 언어가 다른 형제 자매들이 한 지부에서 함께 일한다는 것이
우리가 할 일은 그 결정을 성공적으로 실행할 방법을 찾는 것임을 알고 있었죠.
여호와께서는 지부 통합 마련을 축복해 주셨습니다.
지금 우리는 여호와의 백성이 하나로 연합되어 있고
우리 지부 구역 내의 형제 자매들이 여러 나라에 살고 있지만
또한 지금 우리가 이처럼 훌륭한 행실을 나타내고 연합을 이루는 것이
앞으로 신세계에서 더 많은 축복을 누리며 살게 될 때를 준비하는 과정이라고
이번 지부 통합 마련을 통해 우리는 하느님의 왕국이 통치하고 있으며
그 왕국의 왕이신 예수 그리스도께서 중앙장로회를 인도하고 계시다는 것을
방문 기간 동안 베델 성원들과 야외에서 열심히 일하는 분들로부터
지부 통합이 정말 좋은 결정이었다는 말을 많이 들었습니다.
여호와에 대한 믿음이 강해지고 형제들에 대한 사랑이 더 깊어졌습니다.
핀란드 지부 위원인 테무 콘스티 형제는
지부 통합으로 누리게 된 한 가지 큰 축복은
형제 자매들이 서로 더 가까워졌다는 것입니다.
베드로가 예수께 그분을 따르면 어떤 상을 받게 될지 물었을 때
그분은 “영원한 생명”을 얻게 될 것이라고 대답하셨습니다.
영적 ‘형제와 자매와 아버지와 어머니’를 받게 될 것이라는 말씀도 하셨죠.
우리는 정말 많은 형제와 자매와 아버지와 어머니를 얻게 되었습니다.
이 지부들을 방문하면서 믿음이 크게 강화되었습니다.
형제들은 사람의 관점으로는 극복할 수 없어 보이는 문제들을
하나로 연합되어 하느님의 뜻을 행하고 있었습니다.
많은 수의 이민자들과 난민들을 도울 기회가 생겼습니다.
