en.text: At Psalm 133:1, we read:
“Look! How good and how pleasant it is
for brothers to dwell together in unity!”
This scripture was vividly seen when visiting
the Scandinavia and Finland branches.
I had the privilege of serving these two branches
as a headquarters representative
during the month of May 2018 along with my wife, Susan.
We knew that these branches had undergone major changes
in their territory assignments in recent years.
Both were merged with other branches that have different languages and cultures.
I was very anxious to see firsthand
how the brothers were handling these challenges.
The former branches in Denmark,
Iceland,
Norway,
and Sweden
were merged to form the Scandinavia branch.
The branch facilities are located in Holbæk,
which is about an hour outside of Copenhagen.
It is beautifully situated in a suburban community,
and the grounds of the branch form a lovely garden.
During our visit, the weather was exceptionally fine,
which is not typical for Scandinavia.
So all took advantage of the sunshine and warm weather.
But the warmth of the sunshine could not outdo
the love shown by our brothers at the branch.
The Bethel family totals 92 full-time members.
Forty-seven are Danish-speaking,
17 speak Norwegian,
and 28 speak Swedish.
I wondered how they carried out their work
and especially their spiritual programs.
As it turns out, they use a mixture
of all three languages.
For instance, at morning worship, the chairman might speak in Danish,
the opening prayer might be in Norwegian,
and the commentors might give their comments in Swedish.
And every week, there are prerecorded comments
from one of the Remote Translation Offices,
such as Greenland and the Faroe Islands.
In addition, the branch alternates conducting
the Monday night Watchtower  Study between Danish, Norwegian, or Swedish,
and the brothers are free to comment in their mother tongue.
Though all these languages are different from each other,
there are similarities and, so for the most part,
they all can understand each other.
But to help the brothers communicate with each other,
the brothers came up with a language manual
that contains lists of common words and their meanings in each language.
In addition, the manual contains “Five commandments” such as:
“Do not speak fast,”
“Use good articulation,”
and “Smile while you speak.”
This greatly helps in smoothing over any miscommunications.
For instance, the Danish word for “kind”
is the Norwegian word for “peculiar.”
So by following these commandments,
a Norwegian brother would not feel bad
if his Danish brother were to tell him,
“You are a peculiar person.”
The translation work for these languages
takes place at Remote Translation Offices, or RTOs.
Each language RTO is located in their respective countries.
The RTOs function much like a Bethel facility.
For the most part, meals are provided,
but each cares for their own laundry and transportation.
We were grateful for the opportunity to visit the RTO in Malmo, Sweden,
which is a short car ride from Denmark.
At the Swedish RTO, the workers live
at a nearby apartment complex.
It’s a busy place, since they not only translate into Swedish
but also translate into Swedish Sign Language
and produce audio recordings.
The facilities are well used and a bit cramped for space.
Nevertheless, there is a joyful spirit at the RTO,
and the brothers there enjoy working with one another.
The use of technology plays a major role in caring for the work at Bethel
as well as in communicating
throughout the branch territory.
This was well-illustrated when giving a special talk
to all congregations in Scandinavia.
The talk was streamed to congregations as far away
as the north of Norway, to the south and the Faroe Islands,
as well as to Greenland.
All throughout Scandinavia, the brothers came together
to hear and see the talk
“Sing Out Joyfully to Jehovah.”
Likewise in Finland,
when visiting that country, I gave the same talk.
It too was streamed to Kingdom Halls all throughout their territory,
including the former branch territories of Estonia, Latvia, and Lithuania.
These three branches had been merged with Finland in recent times.
The former branch facilities in Estonia, Latvia, and Lithuania
are being well used as RTOs
and to hold classes for the School for Kingdom Evangelizers
and the School for Circuit Overseers and Their Wives.
Both branch facilities underwent some renovations to convert
their former printeries into office space
and a comfortable family lounge.
This space also provides a place for historical museums
where tours can visit and learn about the history
of the Kingdom work in these lands.
While visiting these branches,
I wondered how those who had served for a number of years
on their respective Branch Committees felt about the mergers.
The comments I received showed a tremendous depth
of spirituality and faith in Jehovah
and the direction he provides through his organization.
Consider Brother Lars-Erik Eriksson.
He served on the Branch Committee in Sweden for 14 years.
How did he feel when the Governing Body informed the branch about the merger?
In one way, it came as a surprise for us.
But in another way, it was not
—because the merging of branches
had already started in other parts of the world.
And I remember that we brothers
on the former Swedish Branch Committee joked
and said that if something will take place in Scandinavia,
the new branch office will be located in Sweden.
And we also thought
that only Norway and Sweden
should be merged —but not so.
One brother from the former Norwegian Branch Committee
called me, and he couldn’t understand
why the new branch should be located in Denmark.
He said that you already have the needed space in Sweden
—rooms and other things—
and Denmark is small in comparison.
I had to admit, I was surprised too.
We have learned an important lesson
that ‘Jehovah’s ways are not our ways,
and his ways are higher than our ways.’
Everything turned out very well.
Right from the beginning,
there has been a wonderful cooperation in the family.
And we work together in peace and unity.
A few times, especially in the beginning,
we reminded each other that it is not a Danish branch,
it is not a Norwegian branch or a Swedish branch,
it is a Scandinavian branch office.
In a similar vein, consider what Brother Jouni Palmu,
a member of the Finland Branch Committee, noted about their merger:
Combining different countries,
cultures, and languages
under one branch office
seemed impossible five years ago when this project started.
However, we were confident
that if the Governing Body had started such a project,
our task was to figure out
how to make it work well.
We started working, and we can see that Jehovah
has blessed this project.
We can now see how Jehovah’s people
are a united group and how we are like a big family
in a territory that covers several countries.
It has also made us confident of the fact
that if we are already a united, fine people,
when the new world comes,
we are prepared to live there and receive more blessings.
This project has clearly shown us
that God’s Kingdom rules
and that the Governing Body is under Christ’s direction.
During my visit, it was common to hear comments from Bethelites
and those working hard in the field
that the mergers were the best thing that could have happened.
It has been a spiritually enriching experience for all.
It has strengthened their faith in Jehovah
and has increased their love for their brothers.
Along this line, consider what Brother Teemu Konsti,
a member of the Finland Branch Committee, said:
Well, a great spiritual blessing
has been that this merger
has brought us closer as a brotherhood.
Peter once asked Jesus
what the reward would be for following Jesus Christ,
and Jesus answered: “everlasting life.”
But in this period of time, the reward is ‘brothers and sisters
and fathers and mothers,’ spiritually speaking.
So after this merger,
we have gained so many brothers and sisters and fathers and mothers.
So we have been richly rewarded.
Our trip to these branches was truly faith-strengthening.
It was a joy to see that despite the challenges
that from a human standpoint are insurmountable,
with Jehovah’s help our brothers joyfully overcame them
and are united in doing God’s will.
Because of such unity, Jehovah has opened the door
for large numbers of immigrants and refugees
that speak a variety of languages.
Therefore, the brotherhood in both Scandinavia and Finland
has become quite diverse in languages as well as cultures.
Yes, it was truly a delight
to see our brothers “dwelling together in unity.”
No matter where we went, all the brothers
wanted you to be sure of their warm love and brotherly affection.

en.text: The prophet Isaiah foretold
that ‘in the final part of the days,
‘nations would stream
‘to the mountain of Jehovah
‘[his elevated pure worship]
to be instructed about his ways.’
In God’s organization,
we can all benefit from that divine education.
We also see the results
of Proverbs 4:18:
“The path of the righteous is like the bright morning light
that grows brighter and brighter.”
Naturally, what we learn
through the program of divine education
has to keep pace with our refined understanding
of Bible teachings.
To accomplish this,
the Teaching Committee of the Governing Body
oversees the work of the Theocratic Schools Department
in Patterson, New York.
How do they keep the curriculums of our theocratic schools
up-to-date and effective
in training God’s people to do his will?
In the fall of 1942,
Brother Nathan Knorr wondered
if 1,000 pioneers could be found
who would be willing to go through Gilead
to ensure the school’s operation
for at least five years.
Nearly 80 years later,
Gilead School is still going strong,
and it’s not alone.
The Theocratic Schools Department
develops and maintains seven schools
under the direction of the Teaching Committee.
Together, these schools train God’s people
for theocratic assignments around the world.
But each school’s curriculum
needs continual review and updating.
Why?
We may receive new direction for a school from the Governing Body
or need to integrate Bible teachings
from new or updated publications.
Thanks to Jehovah’s rich blessing,
theocratic schools are being conducted
in 93 branch territories in 293 languages.
The amazing growth of these schools produces
a mammoth amount of work behind the scenes.
There are more than 2,000 documents that need to be put through a robust process
of formatting, proofreading,
editing, cross-checking for redundancy, and internal indexing.
Additionally, thousands of reference checks
that include scripture citations and publication references are made.
The schools are dynamic, so this work is continuous
to keep them up-to-date, accurate, and harmonious.
Once revisions are identified, the affected teaching outlines are adjusted.
Often, when a school is revised, a pilot class is taught.
Brothers from the Schools Department can observe
and listen to comments and suggestions from the instructors.
They can then make further adjustments
before the updated school is taught worldwide.
The theocratic schools are having a far-reaching effect.
How did the students feel about their training?
The training I received at Gilead was a big help
for my new assignment as a member of the Branch Committee.
It helped me not to be rule oriented or position oriented.
It helped me to understand how Jehovah
wants me to use authority
—to treat our brothers and sisters
in a humble and a friendly and a loving way,
to really take care of his sheep.
In October 2018, a special announcement was made.
We are pleased to inform you
that the Governing Body has given approval
for all field missionaries with an FMF enrollment
who have been serving for at least five years
to attend the School for Kingdom Evangelizers, SKE.
SKE was very much a refresher course for us.
It helped us to be able to bring back to mind
things that we had learned from Gilead
and then improve upon them.
Going to SKE was just Jehovah’s way
of giving us that encouragement (that hug)
telling us that he loves us and giving us
the needed training to keep on going.
Brother Knorr may have wondered in 1942
if we’d ever find 1,000 students,
but by the tenth class of Gilead,
the 1,000th student had graduated.
In just the United States branch territory,
more than 1,000 students are being trained
in theocratic schools each week!
In our times, we see Isaiah 60:22 coming true:
“The little one will become a thousand and the small one a mighty nation.”
Jehovah has blessed the use of theocratic schools
to contribute to this amazing growth.
And with such training,
he’s strengthening his people from the inside out
as he prepares us all for “the real life” to come.

title: 조엘 델링거: 분별력 있는 학생이 되십시오 (잠언 3:13)

ko.text: 어떻게 하느님의 말씀이 힘을 발휘하게 할 수 있는지 알려줍니다.
‘자신과 자신의 가르침에 한결같이 주의를 기울여야’ 합니다.
그리고 나이가 많든 적든 우리 모두는
사람들은 하느님의 말씀이 줄 수 있는
지혜와 분별력을 얻을 기회를 갖게 됩니다.
도움이 되는 조언을 해 주고 나서
그 말을 결코 잊을 수 없습니다.
가르칠 때 우리가 본받아야 할 분이
위대한 선생님이신 예수라는 걸 일깨워 주었습니다.
겸손하고 부지런한 학생이 되어야 한다는 점을 깨닫게 됩니다.
거의 대부분의 영적 프로그램에서 우리가 하는 역할은
얼마나 많은 시간을 보내는지 생각해 보십시오.
가족 숭배나 개인 연구를 하기 위해 시간을 냅니다.
이 귀중한 교훈과 격려와 조언의 일부
또는 많은 부분을 흘려보낼 수 있습니다.
따라서 오늘 아침 숭배 나머지 시간에는
여기 “마음을 준비해 두었다” 옆에 별표가 있죠?
그는 율법을 통해 가르쳐 주실 분이
자신이 우선 실천해야 한다는 것을 인정했습니다.
다른 사람을 효과적으로 가르칠 자격을 갖출 수 있었죠.
우리가 아까 살펴본 점을 강조하지 않습니까?
우리는 늘 하느님의 말씀을 배우는 학생입니다.
베델이나 회중에서 영적 프로그램에 참석하기 전이나
겸손한 태도로 잘 듣게 해 달라고 기도할 수 있습니다.
우리는 얼마나 오랫동안 여호와께 배워 왔든지 잘 들어야 합니다.
모든 걸 다 아는 사람은 아무도 없고,
“지혜로운 사람은 잘 들어서 더 많은 교훈을 얻”는다고 알려 줍니다.
좀 부정적인 태도를 갖고 있다면 어떠합니까?
어쩌면 그 주제에 대해 흥미가 없거나
썩 마음에 들지 않을 수 있죠.
여호와로부터 온 것임을 인정하고 기억할 수 있게 도와 달라고
“보통 이상의 주의를 기울이십시오” 라는 기사가 실렸는데요.
거기에 나오는 내용을 좀 읽어 드리죠.
프로를 다루는 사람의 가르치는 능력을 기준으로
프로를 다루는 사람의 가르치는 기술이 중요하기는 하지만,
그것이 집회의 성공을 좌우하는 유일한 요인은 아닙니다.
연사가 연설을 얼마나 잘 하느냐가 아니라
우리가 귀를 기울여 얼마나 잘 듣느냐가 되어야 하지 않겠습니까?
제공되고 있는 내용에 주의를 기울일 때,
우리는 하느님의 뜻과 일치하게 그분을 숭배하는 것입니다.
연사의 능력에 관계없이, 집회로부터 유익을 얻을 것입니다.”
우리 모두가 꼭 기억해야 할 점이죠!
언제나 받아들이고 적용하려고 결심한 학생들로서 말이죠.
아침 숭배를 베델 식당이 아닌 다른 곳에서 시청하게 될 경우,
우리의 주의를 산만하게 하는 것이 얼마나 많은지 아마 잘 아실 겁니다.
그런가 하면 질병이나 통증 때문에 집중하기 어려운 경우도 있습니다.
오랫동안 심한 편두통에 시달려 왔다고 말했습니다.
편두통에 시달리며 집회를 본다고 상상해 보니
주의를 산만하게 하는 요인이 많은 건 사실입니다.
우리가 어디에 집중하는지에 큰 영향을 주기 때문에,
집중하는 데 도움이 되는 방식으로 눈을 사용하십시오.
연사가 읽을 때 눈으로 따라 읽으십시오.
소리가 나는 쪽으로 고개를 돌리고 싶은 마음을 억제하도록 하십시오.
주의를 산만하게 만드는 정보가 눈을 통해 머릿속에 몰려들면,
연단에서 제공되는 내용의 상당 부분을 놓치게 될 것입니다.”
이제 전자 기기를 사용하는 문제도 생각해 보죠.
알림이 오거나 문자나 이메일을 받은 적이 있으신가요?
차단하는 모드로 바꾸는 것이 지혜로울 것입니다.
그럼 염려나 불안한 생각이 있을 때는 어떻게 해야 합니까?
그분이 가까이 계신다는 점을 기억할 수 있습니다.
시편 필자가 여호와께 무엇이라고 말했는지 살펴보시죠.
집회에서 우리가 그분께 배우는 것에 집중할 수 있도록
우리를 달래 주고 위로해 주실 수 있습니다.
네, 집회는 영적으로 살아 있게 해 주는 여호와의 마련입니다.
우리도 ‘여호와의 법을 조사하고 실천하고 가르치겠다고’ 결심합시다.
또한 주의를 빼앗는 것이 많기 때문에,
여호와께서 가르치시는 선한 것들에 온전히 집중하도록 합시다.

en.text: Our focus in the Watchtower study article
is on how we can unleash
the power of God’s Word
when teaching from the platform.
But, you know, whether we’re teaching
in a congregation setting,
on a Bible study, or in the family,
isn’t it true that all of us, brothers and sisters,
need to ‘pay constant attention to ourselves and to our teaching’?
And we know why that’s so important —because lives are at stake.
And all of us, younger or older,
touch the lives of other people.
So when we teach effectively,
we are giving opportunity to others
to attain the wisdom and the discernment that God’s Word can give them.
That’s why we need to approach any teaching opportunity
seriously and prayerfully.
Over 20 years ago, a kind elder gave me
some constructive counsel after a public talk.
And then, with a warm smile, he said this,
“Remember, none of us teach like Jesus did.”
Well, I’ll never forget that counsel.
Why were those observations so helpful?
Well, it reminded me that when teaching,
our model needs to be Jesus, the Great Teacher.
There’s more to learn from him.
And Jesus’ example reminds us of the need
to remain humble and diligent students of Jehovah
—the Grand Instructor.
Though all of us are teachers on occasion,
isn’t it true that most often
the role we play during spiritual programs
is that of students?
Just for a moment, think about the many hours
we spend as students —not teachers—
when we’re in the audience at congregation meetings,
at assemblies, and at conventions.
Add to that the time we are students
when we buy out time to watch the monthly broadcast,
to prepare for meetings, to engage in family and personal study.
And then think of the added privilege that many of us here have
—to enjoy morning worship five days a week.
You know, a typical program of morning worship
lasts between 20 to 25 minutes.
If you multiply that by 5 days a week and then by 52 weeks,
at a minimum, we are exposed
to at least 86 hours
of divine instruction each year.
But if we’re not careful,
some or much of that valuable instruction,
encouragement, and counsel could just wash over us.
So for the remaining time for our program this morning,
let’s consider some things all of us can do
to listen more effectively
at spiritual programs.
Please, for our first point, open your Bible
to Ezra 7:10,
and let’s consider Ezra’s example.
That’s Ezra 7:10,
and notice the reading carefully:
“Ezra had prepared his heart
“to consult the Law of Jehovah
“and to practice it,
“and to teach its regulations
and judgments in Israel.”
Now, if you have the Bible with the asterisk
next to “prepared his heart,”
if you tap on that, you’ll notice that that could be rendered as
“had determined in his heart.”
Well, what do we learn from Ezra?
He had the right attitude going into a period of study.
He had the right approach to study and learning.
He recognized that it was Jehovah
who would be teaching him through His Law.
And as the verse goes on to say, he first recognized
that he needed to personally practice what he was learning.
Only then would he be in a rightful position
to effectively teach others.
Well, this scripture emphasizes the point we’ve already made, doesn’t it?
Though we are teachers on occasion,
we are always first and foremost
students of God’s Word.
How can we imitate Ezra’s example
and prepare our hearts before study,
before attending a spiritual program
(whether here at Bethel or in the congregation),
before watching a monthly broadcast?
Well, we need to prepare our hearts by specifically praying to Jehovah,
recognizing him as the Source of the teaching.
What should we pray specifically about?
Well, for one, we want to pray that we remain humble
while listening to theocratic instruction.
We need to listen
—no matter how long we’ve been in Jehovah’s classroom—
because none of us know it all,
nor will we ever know it all.
Proverbs 1:5 reminds us
that “a wise person listens and takes in more instruction.”
Well, this leads to another question:
What if we find we have a somewhat negative attitude
toward a certain presentation
—perhaps the material doesn’t interest us,
or we have a negative attitude toward a certain brother
and his teaching ability?
What should we do?
Prepare our heart.
Pray to Jehovah to recognize and appreciate
that the instruction is from him.
Pray to have a thankful spirit.
You know, back in 2002, The Watchtower  made this helpful point
in an article that was entitled “Pay More Than the Usual Attention.”
I quote: “Some may tend to gauge the quality of a meeting
“by the teaching abilities of the participants. . . .
“Though the teaching ability of participants is important,
“it is not the sole factor contributing to a meeting’s success.
“Do you not agree that our prime concern should be,
“not how well the speaker delivers his talk,
“but how well we incline our ear?
When we attend meetings,” the article continues,
“and pay attention to what is being presented,
“we are worshiping God in harmony with his will.
“That is what makes the meeting a success.
“If we are eager to take in the knowledge of God,
“we will benefit from meetings,
regardless of a speaker’s abilities.”
What a beautiful reminder for all of us!
So our first point: Like Ezra,
let’s prepare our hearts with prayer,
as students who are determined to always
accept and apply what Jehovah has to teach us.
Let’s consider a second point:
the need to focus our attention.
Have you faced the challenge of staying focused
during spiritual programs?
Our minds may be distracted
with anxieties and many other things.
Noise and movements around us could distract us.
If we’re watching morning worship
at a location other than the Bethel dining room,
likely we well know the numerous distractions
that fight for our attention.
Some of us have ailments and physical discomforts
that may make it difficult to concentrate.
Recently, a sister in our congregation
told us about her long-term battle with migraine headaches.
I tried to put myself in her shoes,
having a migraine headache while attending a spiritual program
—difficult to concentrate.
Well, whatever the case may be, we know —we admit—
that there are many challenges and distractions.
What can we do about it?
Well, since the eyes strongly influence
where we focus our attention,
the Benefit  book provides this suggestion:
“Use your eyes to help you concentrate by keeping them on the speaker.
“When he cites a Bible text —even a familiar one—
look it up, and follow along as he reads it.”
And then it said this: “Resist the temptation to turn your head
“in the direction of every noise or movement.
“If the eyes are flooding your mind with distracting information,
you will miss much of what is presented from the platform.”
And think about, too, the use of electronic devices.
Have you ever been alerted, messaged, or e-mailed
while looking at the Bible on your device?
How wise it is when we turn those devices to a mode
that eliminates unnecessary distractions!
Well, what about anxieties or disquieting thoughts?
What could we do about that?
Well, here, again, is where we can remember
who the Grand Instructor is and how close he can be to us
when we’re in a teaching environment.
Open, please, your Bible to Psalm 94:19
to recall what the psalmist said to Jehovah.
At Psalm 94:19,
we read:
“When anxieties overwhelmed me,
you [Jehovah] comforted and soothed me.”
What a beautiful reminder!
Jehovah can soothe and comfort us
when attending spiritual programs
so that we can focus on what he’s teaching us.
Yes, spiritual programs are a provision from him
—a spiritual lifeline.
So as needed during a spiritual program,
we should pray to Jehovah to help us stay focused.
Pray repeatedly as needed.
Well, in summary, what have we learned?
All of us are teachers from time to time,
but first and foremost, we are students
in the classroom of the Great Teacher and the Grand Instructor.
Like Ezra, humility and appreciation
should move us to ‘prepare our hearts’ before every spiritual program.
We don’t want to miss anything
that Jehovah has for us.
We’re determined ‘to consult that Law
so that we can practice it and then teach it.’
And in view of all the potential distractions,
let’s make it our aim to use our eyes, our mind, and our heart
to focus attention on the goodness of Jehovah’s spiritual provisions.

cn.text: 一篇《守望台》文章提到
弟兄们在发表演讲时
可以怎样使用上帝的话语打动听者的心
不过，其实不管我们是在聚会时发表演讲
主持圣经课程或家庭崇拜
我们所有人不管弟兄或姐妹
都需要时刻留意自己和自己的教导
我们知道为什么这样做很重要
因为这关系到别人的生命
我们所有人不管年纪大小
都会对别人的生活产生影响
所以，如果我们好好施行教导
就会让别人有机会从上帝的话语
得到智慧和明辨事理的能力
这就是为什么
我们要认真看待每一个教导人的机会
并为此向上帝祷告
20多年前，一位长老在我发表演讲后
给了我一些实用的建议
然后他亲切地笑着对我说

en.text: How will you feel when all we came here to do
is finally completed?
No doubt, we will find a moment to reflect
on the words of Philippians 2:13.
Yes, Jehovah energized us
and gave each and every one of us “both the desire
and the power to act.”
How has sharing on this project affected your life?
It all started over seven years ago.
Can you imagine how excited you’re going to be
when we hear that the new branch facility at Chelmsford
has been approved by the City Council?
Well, guess what?
Yesterday afternoon we received the approval.
Whilst the buildings are beautiful,
at the end of the day, they are just buildings.
The really special part of this project
has been the people;
even non-Witnesses saw that something special
was taking place on our site.
It’s a very friendly site to work on.
It’s just how friendly everyone is.
You walk in, and it just— I find it mind-blowing.
In a negative (sometimes) society,
when you come here, it just puts a smile on your face.
A truly unexpected success
was the visitors’ center.
How we underestimated the appreciation
Jehovah’s people have
for theocratic activities.
Visitors from all around the globe witnessed
the activities of Jehovah for themselves.
This is partly why
I’m actually studying the Bible to get baptized,
because when I came here, it just hit me somewhere, you know?
Me and Alicia can’t see,
so everyone has been so encouraging and thoughtful.
We really feel like Jehovah is with us and he’s supported us.
I really liked the ladies driving tractors.
Everyone wanted to have a part in the project.
Every single contribution warmed our hearts
and sometimes our heads too.
Another beautiful project highlight
was the day-volunteer program.
The effort and expense brothers and sisters
sacrificed reminded all of us
of what a privilege it is to work for Jehovah.
And how about the commuters who helped on the project?
Would the BRD family have had
the same spirit without our commuters?
Don’t you just love being a part of this amazing family?
We were regularly reminded that spirituality
is of the utmost importance.
Did you ever say that a monthly meeting
was the best one yet?
What lies outside the comfort zone
is the faith zone.
Don’t cry because it’s over;
smile because it happened.
What is your story?
The center of all of our stories is Jehovah.
He is the one who energized us;
he is the one who gave us both the desire
and the power to act.
He is the one we can thank
for the lifelong friendships we have formed,
the training we have received,
and the challenges we have been able to overcome.
Remember your story.
Really, it’s only just beginning.

en.text: Our family had been learning Chinese for over a year.
It wasn’t easy.
God has many titles.
Did you know he has only one name?
[Speaking Chinese]
I was ready, or at least I thought so.
Matthew!
Yeah, I’ll be right there.
We were making progress,
and we weren’t giving up.
It seemed like most people just weren’t interested.
We were not having a good morning.
What happened?
Mom and Liz weren’t having a good morning either.
Brother and Sister Lin joined us.
They’ve been a big help to us.
We told them about our morning.
We were finally able to converse a little and give presentations,
but everything seemed to fall flat.
You ask good questions at the door
—but not always the right one.
You see, when you learn the language,
do not forget to learn about people.
He was right.
Our questions started conversations in our old territory, but not here.
Your pronunciation is very good, see.
Thanks, Brother Lin.
We needed a different approach
where we didn’t just learn the language
but also how to reach the heart of someone who speaks it.
In the July 2019 Watchtower,
we read about “Reaching the Hearts of Nonreligious People.”
Did you notice in paragraph 7,
how do you think that we could be more like the apostle Paul?
Well, Paul was a Jew,
but when he was talking to other people,
he had to adapt his presentation.
I like what 1 Corinthians 9:20-23 says:
“To the Jews I became as a Jew in order to gain Jews;
to those under law I became . . .”
Liz was right.
When Paul spoke to fellow Jews in Athens,
he reasoned from the Scriptures.
But when he spoke to the Greeks at the Areopagus, he adapted,
reasoning with them first without the Bible.
He later wrote:
“I have become all things to people of all sorts,
so that I might by all possible means save some.”
That’s what we needed to do.
We learned more about the people.
We started to listen more and talk about things
that interested them.
We found different ways to start conversations.
And we kept learning more about the culture.
Part of a Chinese proverb I found says:
“He who comes near ink is stained black.”
It’s been a great way to introduce
Proverbs 13:20:
“The one walking with the wise will become wise.”
It all comes down to showing love.
The more we paid attention to how we were teaching,
the more we were able to show people the God who loves them.

전 오락을 선택하는 면에서 변화가 좀 필요했어요.

하지만 요즘엔 우리가 볼 만한 건전한 프로를 찾기가
그렇다고 나쁜 프로를 보는 건 아니에요.
과연 영적으로 나에게 도움이 될까 하는 생각이 듭니다.
대학교에 다니다 보니 물질적인 것을 통해
안정된 삶을 추구하라는 사고방식에 영향을 받게 됐어요.
내가 살 집도 갖고 경제적 안정도 누리고요.
사탄은 부를 쌓아야 안정된 삶을 누릴 수 있다는 생각을 조장하죠.
하지만 그렇게 하려면 많은 걸 희생하게 됩니다.
그 기사는 우리에게 꼭 필요한 거였어요.
경고를 발해서 도시를 보호하는 파수꾼에 대해 말하죠.
경고를 발할 때는 도시를 보호하기 위해 성문을 닫아야 했습니다.
이 세상의 그 어떤 친구에 대한 충성보다
여호와에 대한 충성이 먼저 와야 합니다.
그저 재미만 느끼는 게 아니라고 했어요.
어머니들이 아이들에게 재미있는 이야기를 들려주곤 하죠.
어머니가 해 주신 이야기가 지금까지 계속 저에게 영향을 주고 있어요.
그러니까 지금 내가 TV에서 보고 있는 흥미로운 이야기도
저는 즐겨 보던 여러 프로를 아예 보지 않기로 결정했습니다.
전 지금 전 시간 봉사를 하고 있는데, 너무 좋아요!
여호와께서 저를 잘 돌봐 주고 계시죠.
하지만 저는 그 기사에서 배운 훌륭한 원칙들을 잊지 않을 거예요.
최선을 다해 아버지 여호와를 섬기고 싶습니다.
우리 마음에 떠오르지 않는 날이 하루도 없어요.
친구들이 돌아와서 함께 어깨를 나란히 하여 여호와를 섬기길 간절히 바랍니다.
우리의 파수꾼인 양심을 확인하라는 것도 배웠어요.
경고를 발하고 성문을 닫는 일을 잘하고 있는지 말이에요.
물론 말만큼 쉽진 않지만 그렇게 하는 게 우리의 몫이죠.

en.text: Well, very good friends of ours
decided they wanted to go their own way and leave Jehovah.
And in the interim, they became bad association for us.
We had many good times together.
We drove to isolated territory together;
we even visited a brother who was sick in the hospital to encourage him.
I feel heartbroken
that they’re no longer serving Jehovah.
It’s really hard to lose a friend spiritually —very hard.
I was about to enter into full-time service,
but I still needed reassurance.
I was raised by my mother as a Witness.
Even though I had very little contact with my father,
he still tried to oppose my spiritual progress.
I kept fighting for the truth,
and I got baptized when I was 11.
I guess I felt like I was doing OK.
And after high school, I went to university.
I had to make some changes in my choice of entertainment.
We really never stop learning.
I do enjoy relaxing and watching television.
But I must admit that it is more and more difficult
to find something decent to watch these days.
Well, I’m not saying that I watch bad programs.
I would never do that,
but still I wonder
if what I watch is spiritually healthy for me.
The way of thinking I was exposed to in university
was pressuring me to find security in my life through material things
—like having my own place to live and economic stability.
But at what cost?
I remember that paragraph.
It said that Satan promotes making money
as the only way
you can find security in this world.
But one could sacrifice
so much to achieve it.
You could even lose
your friendship with Jehovah.
That article—it was just what we needed.
It described a watchman
who would protect the city
by sounding out an alarm on impending danger.
And at sounding that alarm,
he would shut the gates to the city to protect the city.
And I needed to do that.
We both needed to do that.
It’s true.
And it’s not even a question.
Our loyalty to Jehovah comes first
—before we’re loyal to any friends we have in this world.
The Watchtower  said
that storytelling
does more than entertain us.
In Bana, the city of Cameroon where I was born,
mothers spend their evenings with their children, telling them stories.
And even though I was young,
the stories my mother told me
continue to influence me even today.
So I said to myself: ‘Oh, no. Wait a minute, Happy!
‘It means that the stories that I watch on television
‘will also affect me sooner or later,
and the Devil knows that too.’
So I decided to completely cut out a number
of programs that I used to watch.
Now I’m serving in full-time service,
and I love it!
Jehovah is really taking care of me,
but I don’t want to forget
the beautiful principles I’ve learned from that article.
I still have to safeguard my heart.
I want to give my best to my Father, Jehovah.
Not a day goes by where we don’t think about these friends of ours.
And it’s certainly our hope that they come back to Jehovah
and that we can serve Jehovah together shoulder to shoulder.
But we’ve also learned
to keep our “little watchman” in check.
We need to make sure he does his job to “sound the alarm” and “shut those gates.”
Hmm, we never stop learning.
Well, true, it’s easier said than done,
but it is up to us.
It’s so important to safeguard your heart!

cn.text: 我们的好朋友决定离开耶和华，不再崇拜他
如果我们继续跟他们来往
就会影响到我们跟耶和华的关系
我们以前在一起的时候很快乐
我们曾一起到偏远的地方传道
也一起到医院探望一位生病的弟兄
所以当他们不再崇拜耶和华时，我很心痛
好朋友不再爱上帝，真的很难过
在我决定做先驱之前
我还是要继续加强自己的信心
在我小的时候
妈妈就已经是一位耶和华见证人
虽然我跟爸爸很少联络
但他不喜欢我崇拜上帝
我一直努力
后来我就在11岁的时候受浸了
我觉得自己做得还可以
高中毕业后，我就去念大学了
在选择娱乐方面
我真的需要作出一些调整
我们看到的，都会影响到我们的思想
我很喜欢看看电视轻松一下
不过我必须承认
现在适合我们看的电视节目越来越少了
我不是说我会去看那些不好的节目
我绝不会去看那些节目
不过我在想
我看的这些节目
真的可以让我跟耶和华有好的关系吗？
大学提倡的思想影响了我
要我追求物质财富才能有安全感
比如说
一定要买一个房子或是经济一定要很稳定
但这要付出什么代价呢？
我记得一篇文章说
撒但散播一种思想
就是人要得到财富，才会有安全感
但却要因此牺牲很多东西
包括跟耶和华的友谊
我找到一篇文章，刚好是我们需要的
这篇文章提到
城墙上的守望人看到危险逼近时
就会发出警告
发出警报时
他也会去赶快把城门关起来
保护城里的人
我也要这样做
我们两个都要这样做
对
在这件事上
答案是很清楚的
我们对耶和华的忠贞
比世上任何友谊都还来得重要
《守望台》说
休闲娱乐有了故事情节
就会牵动我们的思考和感受
我出生在喀麦隆的巴纳
在那里
妈妈们都会在晚上的时候跟孩子说故事
我小的时候，妈妈也告诉我很多故事
那些故事到现在都还深深地影响着我
所以我对自己说
“哦，等等！
我看的电视节目，里面的故事情节
迟早也会对我自己有影响。”
撒但也知道这一点
所以我决定
不再看一些我平常爱看的电视节目了
现在我是一个先驱
我很喜欢这个工作
耶和华真的很照顾我
我不会忘记那些有智慧的圣经原则
我还是必须保护自己的心
我会把自己最好的献给天父耶和华
我们每天都很想念我们的朋友
希望他们可以重新回到上帝的组织
这样我们就可以再一次一起敬奉耶和华了
我学到
要确定我们的“小小守望人”
就是良心会“发出警告”
也会“关上城门”
我们永远都在学习
不过说的比做的容易
但是决定是在我们自己
最重要的就是要保护自己的心！

ko.text: 우리 결혼 생활에 아무런 문제가 없다고 생각했어요.
한달이 채 안 되어 우리는 이혼하게 되었죠.
이혼한 뒤 저는 딸들을 부양할 방법을 찾아야 했습니다.
또 딸들을 영적으로도 돌봐 주어야 했어요.
하지만 너무 낙담이 되고 피곤할 때가 자주 있어서
거기다가 마음속에 차오르는 부정적인 감정과도 싸워야 했습니다.
계속 기도하는 것 외에는 할 수 있는 게 없었죠.
걸을 수도 없었고, 집회에 갈 수도 없었습니다.
장로들은 제가 집회에 못 나온다는 것을 알게 되었습니다.
장로 분들이 저희 집에 찾아와서 성구를 읽어 줬을 때
“내가 길을 가고 누울 때에 나를 보시고 내 모든 길을 잘 아십니다.”
여호와께 제가 소중한 존재라는 걸 깨달았습니다.
여호와께서 제 마음을 치료해 주시는 것 같았습니다.
그분이 제게 관심이 있으시고, 저를 돌보신다는 확신이 들었어요.
또 감사한 기억이 있는데요, 집회가 끝나고 있었던 일이에요.
장로 한 분이 오셔서 집에 가서 읽어 보라고 성구를 몇 개 적어 주셨어요.
그리고 도움이 필요하면 장로들이 언제든 도와주겠다고 말씀하셨죠.
여호와께서 목자로 사용하시는 두 장로가 사랑 많게도 절 보러 왔어요.
제가 회관에서 멀리 떨어진 곳에 살기 때문에,
두 형제는 대중교통을 타고 큰 길까지 온 다음에
형제들이 와 주지 않았다면 견디기 힘들었을 거예요.
장로들은 제 얘기를 잘 들어 주고 함께 울어 줬습니다.
저는 몸이 좀 나아져서 다시 집회에 나갈 수 있었어요.
형제들과 다시 함께할 수 있어서 정말 행복했습니다.
우리 가족은 다양한 도움을 받은 덕분에, 지금은 잘 지내고 있습니다.
우리 가족에게 회중은 집처럼 편안한 안식처가 되었어요.
형제 자매들과 장로들의 도움이 없었다면 우리 가족이 지금처럼 될 수 없었을 거예요.
우리 가족에 대한 여호와의 큰 사랑을 분명히 느낄 수 있었습니다.
장로 형제들도 양 치는 방문을 하려면 쉽지는 않을 거예요.
하지만 그 방문이 정말 도움이 된다는 걸 체험했어요.
장로 분들도 그 모든 수고와 노력이 가치가 있다는 걸 느끼실 거예요.
장로들의 도움을 결코 잊지 못할 겁니다.

en.text: Everything was going fine in my marriage
—or so I thought.
My ex-husband was disfellowshipped,
left home
and, in less than a month, we divorced.
Right after the divorce, I had to figure out
how I would provide for the girls,
so I began working as a cleaner.
I also had to provide for them spiritually.
But many times, because of discouragement and tiredness,
I couldn’t be there for them as much as they needed me to be.
Besides all of this,
I also had to deal with very negative feelings.
It was a very difficult time in my life.
I had never been so sick.
I couldn’t even get up to go to the hospital.
To cope with this problem, I just kept praying.
I was not able to walk, and I was not able to get to the meetings.
The elders realized that I was missing from the meetings.
The elders quickly came to my aid.
I remember that one of the things
that touched me the most
was when the elders read a scripture.
Psalm 139:3:
“You observe me when I travel and when I lie down;
you are familiar with all my ways.”
I realized that I am precious to Jehovah.
It was as if Jehovah was healing me.
I now knew that Jehovah was interested in me
and that he was looking after me.
He was making sure that I knew it.
Something else that I remember fondly
was after a meeting at the Kingdom Hall.
One of the elders gave me some scriptures to read at home
and said that if we needed any help,
the elders were there for us.
Two elders lovingly came to see me,
because Jehovah uses them as shepherds.
I live very far from the Kingdom Hall.
But the brothers made the sacrifice to get public transport,
get off at the main road,
and from there they walked 40 minutes
to reach my house.
I don’t know what I would have done.
When the elders arrived, they listened to me,
they cried with me, and they read the Bible with me.
Jehovah loves me.
When I started to feel better,
I went back to the group.
I was really happy to be back with my brothers.
Now, after all the help we have received, we are doing well.
The congregation is our second home, and we feel very good there.
Everything I have today, I owe to the brothers and sisters,
especially the elders.
I see shepherding calls as a very evident way
in which Jehovah demonstrates his full love for us.
I understand that at times
these visits might be a challenge for the elders,
but the results are really good.
Without a doubt, they can see that all the work
and all the effort is worthwhile.
I will never forget the help that I received from the elders.
This situation taught me that Jehovah will not let his sheep get lost,
not even one.
Jeremiah 23:4 says:
“‘And I will raise up over them shepherds
“‘who will really shepherd them.
“‘They will no longer be afraid or be terrified,
and none will be missing,’ declares Jehovah.”

cn.text: 之前，我认为我的婚姻很幸福
至少我这么认为
我的前夫被开除了，离开了家
在一个月内，我们离婚了
离婚后，我必须想办法抚养两个女儿
所以我开始当清洁工
同时，我必须要帮助她们亲近耶和华
很多时候，我感到灰心沮丧也很疲累
我不能给她们所需要的一切帮助
除此之外，我还要面对自己消极的想法
这是我生命中非常艰难的一段时期
我从来没有病得这么严重过
甚至站起来，自己去趟医院都非常费力
为了面对这个难题，我只能不停地祷告
我不能走路，也不能去参加聚会
长老们留意到我错过了一些聚会
长老们很快就过来帮助我
他们做了很多事
其中最让我感动的
就是长老们为我读了一节经文
在诗篇139:3，经文说
我感受到耶和华真的很爱我
他正在医治我的伤口
现在我知道耶和华非常关心我
也非常照顾我
耶和华希望我知道这一点
还有一件事
我记得很清楚，也给我很大的鼓励
就是有一次在聚会后
一个长老给我几节经文，让我回家自己看
他还说，如果我们需要帮助的话
长老们都非常乐意帮助我们
有两位长老很好心地过来看我
因为耶和华任用他们来牧养我
我的家离聚会所很远
但他们很愿意辛苦地搭车
再走路40分钟来我家看我
如果他们没有来
我真不知道自己会变得怎样
长老来了之后，他们就听我说话
跟我一起哭，也跟我一起看圣经
耶和华真的很爱我
当我觉得身体好一点之后
我就回去开始参加聚会
我真的很高兴可以跟弟兄们在一起
弟兄们给我们很大的帮助
我们的情况就变得比较好了
弟兄姐妹就是我们的家人
跟他们在一起，我们觉得很舒服
因为有弟兄姐妹们，我们才能坚持到现在
特别是长老们
我看出长老们的牧养探访
就是耶和华爱我们的明显证据
我知道对长老们来说
要做牧养探访有的时候不是那么容易
但成果却非常地好
我确定长老们都能看出
他们所做的努力是非常有价值的
我绝不会忘记长老们给我的帮助
我学到，耶和华绝不会让他的绵羊走失
连一只都不会
就像耶利米书23:4说的

title: 세스 하이엇: 여러분은 주의를 기울이고 있습니까?

ko.text: 주의를 집중하라는 말을 들어 본 적이 있을 겁니다.
사실, 우리 모두가 생각해 봐야 할 점입니다.
특별히 주의를 기울여야 할 어떤 경우들이 있을까요?
장로라면 양 치는 방문을 할 때,
자녀라면 부모의 교훈을 들을 때 그래야 합니다.
주의를 산만하게 하는 것들이 너무나 많죠.
정말, 주의를 기울인다는 것은 쉽지 않습니다.
수십 차례 이상 나온다는 걸 알고 계셨습니까?
여호와께서 자신의 백성을 교훈하실 때 그 말씀을 하셨습니다.
그리고 우리가 여호와께 주의를 기울이는 것은
그들이 가진 모든 것을 완전히 멸망시키라고 명령하십니다.
사울이 자신이 불순종한 일에 대해 어떤 변명을 하는지 보겠습니다.
‘그러면 내 귀에 들려오는 이 양 떼의 소리와
내가 듣고 있는 소 떼의 소리는 대체 무엇입니까?’
백성이 당신의 하느님 여호와께 희생을 바치려고
양 떼와 소 떼의 제일 좋은 것을 남겨 두었습니다.
여호와께 희생을 바치려고 동물들을 남겨 뒀다고 했습니다.
주의를 기울이는 것과 순종이 어떻게 관련되는지 살펴보겠습니다.
사울이 불순종하게 된 한 가지 원인은 무엇이었습니까?
여호와의 지시에 주의를 기울이지 않았기 때문이죠.
사울은 주의를 기울이지 않았기 때문에 불순종하게 됐고
우리의 숭배가 여호와께 받아들여지지 않을 수 있습니다!
주의를 기울이는 것이 왜 중요한지 알아봤습니다.
여러분은 사람이 아니라 여호와를 위해 재판하는 것이기 때문입니다.
여러분이 판결을 내릴 때 그분이 여러분과 함께하십니다.’”
그 재판관들은 맡은 일에 주의를 기울여야 할 중요한 이유가 있었습니다.
바로 여호와 앞에 책임을 져야 했기 때문입니다.
그들의 결정은 동료 숭배자들에게 큰 영향을 미쳤습니다.
그들은 여호와의 생각을 잘 알아야 했고,
그들이 맡은 일에 주의를 기울일 수 있기 때문이죠.
장로들은 여호와를 대표해 문제들을 다룰 때
맡은 일을 주의를 기울여 잘 해낼 수 있습니다.
네, 장로들은 여호와의 생각을 잘 안 다음에
그분의 지침을 주의 깊이 따라야 합니다.
자신이 맡은 일에 주의를 잘 기울이는 것입니다.
여호와께서 계속해서 베푸시는 교육 마련을 보면
그분이 장로들을 돕고 싶어 하신다는 걸 알 수 있죠.
장로들을 위해 특별히 준비된 내용을 알려 줍니다.
장로들이 그러한 지침에 온전한 주의를 기울이고
정확한 지침을 전달할 수 있을 것입니다.
우리가 주의를 기울여야 할 두 번째 점을 살펴보겠습니다.
누구든지 가진 사람은 더 받을 것이지만,
가지고 있다고 생각하는 것마저 빼앗길 것입니다.”
하지만 복음서를 통해 그분의 말씀을 읽고
그분이 하신 일로부터 교훈을 얻을 수 있습니다.
우리는 누구의 말을 귀담아 잘 들어야 할까요?
배우자, 자녀들의 말을 잘 들을 수 있죠.
사울이 아말렉 사람들에 대한 여호와의 지시를 주의 깊이 잘 들었다면,
자신이 받은 지시의 중요성을 깨달았을 것이고,
따라서 여호와께서 우리를 교훈하시고 인도하실 때,
어떻게 듣는 일에 주의를 기울이고 있다는 것을
땅에서 오래 살 것이다’라고 약속되어 있습니다.”
청소년들은 이 말씀에 주의를 기울이고 있다는 것을
부모님은 저에게 이런저런 심부름을 시키곤 하셨는데요.
부모님이 시킨 일을 하기가 너무 싫어서
여호와의 마음도 기쁘게 해 드릴 수 있습니다.
기꺼이 잘 듣고 순종하는 데 달려 있다는 걸 기억해야 합니다.
주의를 기울이는 것은 우리 모두에게 중요합니다.
“그러나 여러분의 마음이 과식과 과음과 생활의 염려로 짓눌려,
갑자기 그 날이 올무와 같이 순식간에 여러분에게 닥치는 일이 없도록
자기 자신에게 주의를 기울이라고 하셨을 때,
그분은 사울왕이 나타낸 이기적인 태도를 권장하신 것이 아닙니다.
오늘날에는 그런 태도가 널리 퍼져 있고 권장되기까지 하죠.
즉 자신의 마음에 무엇이 있는지 알아야 한다는 것입니다.

“나 여호와는 마음을 살피고 가장 깊은 생각을 조사한다.”

en.text: Are you paying attention?
Perhaps you’ve been asked that question
by your parents, a teacher,
or someone else in authority.
It’s a good question for each of us to ask ourselves.
Can you think of occasions associated with our worship
that require us to pay special attention?
For example, when reading the Bible, attending meetings,
elders when shepherding,
you children when being instructed by your parents.
We want to pay attention,
and yet there are so many distractions
—electronic gadgets,
the conversations and activities of those around us.
Truly, it can be a challenge to pay attention.
Did you know that the phrase “pay attention”
occurs dozens of times in the New World Translation?
In many of those occurrences,
Jehovah is instructing his people to pay attention.
What does it mean to “pay attention”?
And how important is it
that you and I pay attention to Jehovah?
The account in 1 Samuel chapter 15
will help us to answer those questions.
In verse 3, Jehovah instructs King Saul
to strike down the Amalekites
and to devote them and everything they have to destruction.
However, verses 8 and 9 tell us
that Saul did not obey.
He spared the king of Amalek
and the best of the animals.
How did Saul respond
when Samuel confronted him?
As we read verses 13-15,
note how Saul tried to justify his disobedience:
“When Samuel finally came to him,
“Saul said to him:
“‘May Jehovah bless you.
“I have carried out the word of Jehovah.’
“But Samuel said:
“‘Then what is this sound of the flock in my ears
“and the sound of the cattle that I hear?’
“To this Saul said:
“‘They were brought from the Amalekites,
“‘because the people spared the best of the flock and the herd
“‘for sacrificing them to Jehovah your God;
but what was left we devoted to destruction.’”
Did you notice?
Saul attempted to justify his disobedience,
claiming that the animals would be sacrificed to Jehovah.
Was Jehovah pleased with Saul?
As we read verse 22,
please note the connection between paying attention
and obedience:
“Samuel then said:
“‘Does Jehovah take as much pleasure in burnt offerings and sacrifices
“‘as in obeying the voice of Jehovah?
“‘Look!
“‘To obey is better than a sacrifice,
and to pay attention than the fat of rams.’”
What was one of the causes of Saul’s disobedience?
He didn’t pay attention to Jehovah’s instructions.
His failure to pay attention resulted in disobedience
and brought Jehovah’s disapproval.
What a powerful lesson for us!
As happened with Saul,
our worship could become unacceptable to Jehovah
if we fail to pay attention!
Now that we understand why it is important to pay attention,
let’s consider three aspects of paying attention
that are discussed in the Bible.
The first scripture we’ll consider
is 2 Chronicles 19:6:
“And he [Jehoshaphat] said to the judges:
“‘Pay attention to what you are doing,
“‘for you do not judge for man but for Jehovah,
and he is with you when you pass judgment.’”
This admonition to “pay attention”
was given by King Jehoshaphat
to appointed judges throughout the land of Judah.
What a sobering reminder!
Those judges had good reason
to pay attention to what they were doing.
Why?
They were responsible to Jehovah.
They represented him,
and their decisions affected the lives of fellow worshippers.
Thus, they needed to be familiar with Jehovah’s thinking on matters
and to hold to his unprejudiced viewpoint
when handling matters.
This is an excellent reminder for those who serve as elders.
Good elders are good students of the Bible
and Bible-based publications.
Why?
Their attentiveness to Jehovah
enables them to pay attention to what they are doing.
If they are going to represent Jehovah
and reflect his thinking accurately as they handle matters
—whether they’re shepherding the congregation,
delivering a part at a meeting,
caring for a challenging assignment,
or addressing wrongdoing
—they must pay attention to what they are doing.
That is why they must be familiar with Jehovah’s thinking
and then take care to follow his direction.
If they do, they show that they are paying attention
to what they are doing.
Jehovah’s interest in assisting the elders
is demonstrated in the ongoing education he provides.
Each time the circuit overseer visits the congregation,
he presents material prepared especially for the elders.
The Kingdom Ministry School and the School for Congregation Elders
provide more intensive instruction.
How important
that elders pay close attention to
and apply such instruction!
Their doing so protects, not just themselves
but also fellow worshippers.
By paying attention, elders will be able
to convey direction to the congregations accurately.
This can be especially important if our worship is banned
or restricted in the event of a natural disaster
or other catastrophic event.
This brings us to the second aspect of paying attention
that we’ll consider.
Let’s read Luke 8:18:
“Therefore,
“pay attention to how you listen,
“for whoever has will be given more,
“but whoever does not have,
even what he imagines he has will be taken away from him.”
What did Jesus mean when he said:
“Pay attention to how you listen”?
Those in Jesus’ audience in the first century
had the wonderful privilege of hearing Jesus’ literal voice
as he instructed them.
Of course, we can’t hear the voice of Jesus today,
but we can read his words and learn of his actions
as revealed in the Gospel accounts.
In fact, we have many opportunities to listen
to Jehovah, Jesus,
“the faithful and discreet slave,”
the elders in our congregation,
our marriage mate,
and our children.
No wonder the Bible writer James stated
that “everyone must be quick to listen.”
Think about it:
If Saul had truly listened receptively
to Jehovah’s direction regarding the Amalekites,
he would likely have grasped the importance of the direction he received
and would have been motivated to obey.
However, his lack of attentiveness
led to disobedience and Jehovah’s disapproval.
If we don’t pay attention to how we listen,
we could find ourselves becoming critical
or unappreciative
or even disobedient.
So as Jehovah instructs and directs us,
we need to think about what we are being told,
ponder over its meaning,
mull it over in our mind and, most important,
apply the instruction in our own lives.
If you’re a young person,
how can you show that you’re paying attention
to how you listen?
Consider the admonition at Ephesians 6:1-3:
“Children, be obedient to your parents
“in union with the Lord,
“for this is righteous.
“‘Honor your father and your mother’
“is the first command with a promise:
“‘That it may go well with you
and you may remain a long time on the earth.’”
You children, who do you think is the source of this direction?
We know that these words come from Jehovah.
Did you notice that the verses state not only
that children should “be obedient” to their parents
but also that they should “honor” their parents?
How can you show that you’re paying attention
to how you listen to this direction?
When I was a boy, I can remember occasions
when my parents would ask me to do something,
perhaps to take out the trash.
I would always obey.
But at times, I’d make it very clear
that I didn’t really want to do what was asked.
I think you young ones know what I mean.
However, if we’re truly paying attention
to how we listen to Jehovah’s words,
we’ll be careful to honor our parents,
which is an essential element of obedience.
In this way, we contribute to the peace of the family,
and we make Jehovah’s heart glad.
Additionally, as the promise in verse 3 indicates,
paying attention to how you listen will protect you
and contribute to your success in other ways
throughout your adult life.
Of course, all of us should remember
that our everlasting welfare will depend
on our willingness to listen and obey.
How important, then, that all of us
pay attention to how we listen.
The third aspect of paying attention is found
at Luke 21:34, 35:
“But pay attention to yourselves
“that your hearts never become weighed down
“with overeating and heavy drinking
“and anxieties of life,
and suddenly that day be instantly upon you as a snare.”
When Jesus admonished his followers
to pay attention to themselves,
he didn’t have in mind the selfish thinking that characterized King Saul
and that’s so common, even encouraged, in today’s world.
Rather, Jesus’ words reveal
that the key to paying attention to ourselves
is knowing ourselves
—knowing what’s in our figurative heart.
This is a challenge for all of us.
Why?
The Bible explains at Jeremiah 17:9:
“The heart is more treacherous than anything else
“and is desperate.
Who can know it?”
Verse 10 answers:
“I, Jehovah, am searching the heart,
examining the innermost thoughts.”
So Jehovah knows what is in our heart,
and he can help us to know.
He can help us to examine our motives and goals
and to discern why we do certain things.
Carefully and honestly looking at ourselves in the mirror of God’s Word
can reveal areas in our thinking, words,
and actions
that need attention.
For example, some of Jehovah’s people
—including those of retirement age
who have enjoyed very comfortable circumstances—
have concluded that they needed to make adjustments in their lifestyle,
simplifying their lives
so that they can serve Jehovah more fully.
Some who have done so have had the privilege
of attending the School for Kingdom Evangelizers.
Although it meant stepping out of their comfort zone,
perhaps moving to a new congregation,
they’ve experienced Jehovah’s blessing in ways that they couldn’t have anticipated
as they share the benefits of their experience
and theocratic education
in their new assignments.
How grateful we are
that Jehovah is providing ongoing, life-saving instruction
by means of his Word and organization.
May each of us be determined to “pay attention”
to what we are doing,
to how we listen,
and to ourselves.
By doing so, we’ll avoid falling into the trap of disobedience
as King Saul did.
Instead, as attentive and obedient servants,
we’ll enjoy Jehovah’s friendship forever.

cn.text: 你在听我说话吗？
很可能你的父母
老师或者上司曾经问过你这个问题
其实我们每个人都该问问自己这个问题
你能想到在哪些情况下
你需要特别留心听吗？
比如
在阅读圣经的时候
在参加聚会的时候
长老们在牧养探访的时候
还有你们孩子们在接受父母教导的时候
我们真的需要留心听
因为有电子产品
还有身边的人或事会让我们分心
要留心听真的不容易
你知道吗？
留意或留心
在《圣经新世界译本》里出现过很多次
而且，很多时候
都是耶和华用来提醒他的子民的
留意或留心是什么意思呢？
对我们来说留意耶和华的话有多重要呢？
我们可以在撒母耳记上15章
找到这些问题的答案
在第3节
耶和华吩咐扫罗王要消灭亚玛力人
亚玛力人所拥有的一切也全部要灭尽
很可惜
在第8和第9节我们看到
扫罗没有留心听耶和华的话
他放过了亚玛力王和他们上好的家畜
扫罗看到撒母耳后说了什么呢？
让我们一起看13到15节
扫罗怎样在这件事上
为自己的不服从找借口呢？
经文说
你留意到吗？
扫罗试着为自己的不服从找借口
他说，这些上好的牲畜
是为了用来给耶和华做祭物的
耶和华对扫罗说的话满意吗？
让我们继续看看第22节
请留意，留心听跟服从有什么关系呢？
第22节
是什么原因导致扫罗不服从上帝呢？
因为他没有听从耶和华的吩咐
他不服从上帝是因为没有留意上帝说的话
也因此得罪了上帝
这个教训让我们印象深刻
就像扫罗王一样
如果我们没有留意听耶和华说的话
我们也有可能会让耶和华不高兴
我们已经知道，留心听上帝的话是那么重要
接着我们从三个方面谈谈
圣经怎么帮助我们留心听
首先让我们打开圣经到历代志下19:6
经文说
约沙法王在委任审判官的时候
吩咐他们要留意自己怎样做
这个提醒的确发人深省
这些审判官必须这样做
因为他们要对耶和华负责
他们代表上帝
他们做的决定
会影响崇拜耶和华上帝的人的生活
因此
他们必须熟悉耶和华对一些事情的看法
在处理事情的时候要公平无私
对长老们来说，这是一个很好的提醒
好的长老会勤奋研读圣经以及圣经刊物
为什么呢？
因为，这样他们就能留心听耶和华的话
知道怎么样照顾弟兄姐妹
长老们要牧养弟兄姐妹
有时候也要执行一些不容易的委派
要主持会众的节目
要处理会众的难题
在这些时候，他们代表的是耶和华
要正确地反映出耶和华的思想
如果要做到这一点
他们就必须留心听耶和华的话
熟悉耶和华的思想
然后呢？
认真按照上帝的吩咐执行职务
耶和华希望长老们能够胜任他们的职务
所以不断教导他们
例如，每次分区探访的时候
分区监督都会提供一些资料培训长老们
另外，王国职务训练班以及会众长老训练班
也提供给长老们额外的培训
长老们留心听
并实践这些教导是非常重要的
因为他们这样做不但能保护自己
还能保护弟兄姐妹
长老们留心听
就能把组织的指引正确地传达给弟兄姐妹
当我们的传道活动受禁止
或因为天灾人祸受到限制的时候
留心听组织的指引就特别重要了
接着我们来谈谈第二方面
在路加福音的8:18
经文说
耶稣说要留心怎样听，是什么意思呢？
生活在公元1世纪的人
他们有非常大的殊荣
有机会亲自接受耶稣基督的教导
今天我们无法亲自听到耶稣说话
但是我们可以从福音书里
读到耶稣基督说过的话
以及学习他怎样处世待人
我们有很多机会可以留心听
耶和华、耶稣、忠信睿智的奴隶
会众中的长老
我们的配偶，以及孩子说话
难怪圣经执笔者雅各就说
人人都要乐于聆听
想想看
在处理亚玛力人的事上
如果扫罗留心听上帝的指引
他就会知道彻底听从是多么地重要
也会乐意服从上帝
很可惜，由于他没有留心听
导致他不服从上帝，得不到上帝的嘉许
如果我们没有留心怎样听
我们可能就会变得吹毛求疵
没有感激之心，甚至不服从上帝
所以当耶和华教导、指引我们的时候
我们要好好想想，耶和华想告诉我们什么
琢磨一下经文的含意
更重要的是，在日常生活中用出来
如果你是个年轻人
你要怎样做才能表明你留心听呢？
让我们看看一段经文
在以弗所书6:1-3
经文说
孩子们
你知道这个吩咐是谁给的吗？
这个吩咐是耶和华给的
你留意到吗？
在刚才读的经文里
不但提到孩子要服从父母
经文还提到孩子要尊敬父母
你怎样做就表示你真的留心听这个吩咐呢？
我记得小时候爸妈会要我去做某些事情
例如，他们要我把东西拿出去丢掉
基本上，我都会听话
但有的时候
我就是不想按他们的话去做，觉得很烦
我相信年轻人都知道我在说什么
如果我们留心听耶和华的话
我们就会尊敬自己的父母
而尊敬父母
是孩子们服从父母的最基本的要求
这样，我们就能尽一分力，使家庭更和睦
我们也能让耶和华高兴
另外，在第3节提到一个承诺
如果我们留心听，我们就会得到保护
在往后的一生中，无论做什么都会事事顺利
我们所有人都要记得
我们未来永生的希望
都取决于是否乐意聆听和服从
所以我们留心自己怎样听是非常重要的
接下来是第三方面
请打开圣经到路加福音21:34,35
耶稣劝勉门徒要当心
他的意思并不是要门徒像扫罗王一样
只关心自己
因为这个世界充满并鼓吹这种精神
耶稣劝勉门徒要当心，他的意思是
我们要真正认识自己
了解自己心里到底在想什么
这对我们来说都不容易，为什么呢？
因为耶利米书17:9就说
“人心比什么都诡诈
不顾一切， 谁能看透呢？”
那谁能看透呢？
第10节说
“我耶和华探察人的内心
察验人心底的想法。”

ko.text: 첫째, 부활에 관해 우리가 알고 있는 것은 무엇입니까?
둘째, 부활에 관해 우리가 모르는 것은 무엇입니까?
셋째, 부활에 관해 알고 있는 우리는
이 땅에 곧 있게 될 부활에 관해
우선 부활이 반드시 이루어질 약속이라는 점을 우리는 알고 있습니다.
그 점을 이렇게 분명히 알려 줍니다.
“의로운 사람들과 불의한 사람들의 부활이 있으리라는 것입니다.”
얼마나 놀라운 광경이 펼쳐질지 한번 상상해 보십시오.
파수대에서 발췌된 오늘 성구 해설의 첫 줄이 참 격려적인데요.
모든 인류에 대한 그분의 변치 않는 사랑을 분명히 보여 줍니다.
“기념 무덤에 있는 모든 사람이 그의 음성을 듣고 나올” 것입니다.
우린 그 무덤에 누가 묻혀 있는지도 모르지만
그분의 영원한 기억 속에 저장해 두셨습니다.
그러면 다시 살아날 의로운 사람들이란 누구입니까?
예수께서 대속 희생으로 죽으시기 전에 죽은 충실한 남녀들과
이 마지막 날 기간 중에 죽은 다른 양들을 말합니다.
성경 진리를 적용할 기회를 제대로 갖지 못한 채 죽은 사람들,
그분의 뜻을 행할 기회를 가질 겁니다.
“장례식 대신, 부활되는 사람들을 환영하는 행사가 있을지도 모릅니다.”
우리가 그때 실제로 그런 환영하는 행사에 참여하게 된다면
그 집회 교재에는 두 가지 질문이 나옵니다.
“가족이나 친구 중에 특히 누구를 다시 보고 싶습니까?”
아마 지금 머리에 떠오르는 분들이 있을 텐데,
“성경 인물 가운데 특히 누구를 만나서 이야기를 나누어 보고 싶습니까?”
죽은 사람들이 부활되는 방식에 대해 알려 주는 내용이 있습니까?
질서 있는 방식으로 이루어진다는 걸 알 수 있습니다.
그다음은 그리스도의 임재 중에 그분께 속한 사람들입니다.”
이와 같이 여호와께서는 질서의 하느님이시기 때문에
질서 있는 방식으로 이루어질 것이라고 결론 내리는 것이 합리적입니다.
수많은 사람들이 한 번에 부활되는 것이 아니라
우리는 각 사람이 부활되어 돌아올 때마다
부활된 사람들이 받게 될 물질적, 영적 돌봄에 관해
그들에겐 살 집과 입을 옷과 먹을 음식이 풍부하게 주어질 것입니다.
그럼 이 모든 걸 누가 마련하죠?
이 제도에서 신세계로 넘어갈 사람들이 마련할 겁니다.
예수께서 한 소녀를 부활시키신 때가 생각나시나요?
그때 그 놀라운 기적을 보고 있던 사람들에게
누군가를 부활시킬 때마다 이런 말씀을 하시진 않았는데
이번엔 그 소녀의 개인적인 필요를 아시고
신세계에서 부활된 사람들을 돌볼 기회를 갖게 될 것입니다.
또 우리가 지금까지 받은 모든 훈련을 생각해 보십시오.
LDC와 조직 여러 곳에서 받은 훈련을
영적인 가르침이 필요하다는 점도 생각해 보십시오.
그리고 대속에 대한 믿음을 어떻게 나타낼 수 있는지 배워야 하죠.
여호와와 예수와 여호와의 요구 조건에 대해 가르치기 위해
계시록 20:12에 나오는 요한의 환상에 힌트가 더 있습니다.
“또 나는 죽은 사람들이 큰 자나 작은 자나 왕좌 앞에 서 있는 것을 보았다.
죽은 사람들이 그 두루마리들에 기록된 대로 자기의 행위에 따라 심판을 받았다.”
죽기 전에 한 행동에 따라 받는 것이 아닙니다.
따라서 부활되어 다시 살아나는 사람들은 백지상태에서 새 출발을 하는 거죠.
죽기 전에 여호와를 섬기지 않았던 사람이 많기 때문입니다.
새 출발을 할 수 있어 참 다행이죠.
영원히 사는 데 필요한 요구 조건들이 더 베풀어질 것입니다.
우리는 천년 기간에 여호와께서 베푸실 이 요구 조건들과
또 밝혀 주실지 모르는 새로운 지침들을 배우고
그럼 부활에 관해 모르는 것은 무엇입니까?
그리스도의 천년 통치 기간 초기에 부활되어 돌아올 것입니까?
그들은 사랑하는 사람들의 환영을 받을 것입니까?
사람들은 자신이 죽은 지역에서 부활될 것입니까?
결혼한 상태로 죽은 사람들에게는 여호와께서 어떤 마련을 해 주실까요?
지도력이 있는 고대의 충실한 남자들이 부활되어
그리고 영적 양식은 어떻게 공급될 것입니까?
아니면 영적 양식을 공급할 또 다른 마련이 있을까요?
그때가 오기까지 지금 우리가 초점을 맞추어야 할
“여호와께서는 자신에게 희망을 두는 자에게, 자신을 계속 찾는 사람에게 선하시다.
여호와의 구원을 잠잠히[각주에 따르면, “참을성 있게”] 기다리는 것이 좋다.”
각 사람의 필요를 돌보실 것이라고 확신할 수 있습니다.
우리가 충실하도록 필요한 걸 늘 주시며,
이제는 우리 각자가 해야 할 일은
그 희망을 다른 사람들에게 알리는 것입니다.
과거를 돌아보며 이렇게 말할 수 있을 것입니다.

en.text: We would like to begin
by posing three questions
and then answering those three questions.
First, what do we know
about the resurrection?
Second, what don’t we know
about the resurrection?
And third, what should we do
with what we know about the resurrection?
Well, first, let’s go to that first question posed:
What do we know about the resurrection
that will soon take place here on earth?
Well, first of all, we know it’s a guarantee.
It’s a promise that will be fulfilled.
And based on today’s text
at Acts 24:15, it says:
“There is going to be a resurrection
of both the righteous [as well as] the unrighteous.”
And just imagine what it will be like when that begins,
when over 6,000 years of deaths are undone
and those who are sleeping in the graves will come back to life.
What an amazing prospect!
And as was pointed out,
the first line in our Watchtower  comments
was pretty awesome, and I’m sure you saw that too,
that Jehovah wants people to live, not die.
So this is really a manifestation of Jehovah’s power
as well as his unfailing love for all mankind.
And Jesus reflected his Father’s love.
In fact, he died in our behalf,
and he wanted to fulfill the promise he made
at John 5:28, 29,
where he said: “All those in the memorial tombs
will hear his voice and come out.”
“All” meaning
“all the righteous and the unrighteous.”
Those who are asleep will awaken.
They may have been long forgotten by humans,
but Jehovah has never forgotten them.
They are right in his memory.
Now, have you ever gone to an old cemetery
and looked at some of the gravestones?
Some of the engraving has been worn off over years of weathering.
We don’t even know who’s buried
in that burial plot, but Jehovah does.
And he has it filed away in his everlasting memory.
So when we’re talking about the righteous that will come back,
who are we talking about?
Well, the righteous are the faithful men and women
that have died before Jesus’ sacrificial death
and the other sheep who die during the last days.
And what about the unrighteous?
Well, the unrighteous are humans, billions of humans,
who died without really having an opportunity
to know Jehovah, to get to worship him
or even to apply Bible truths.
They will have the opportunity to get to know Jehovah,
to draw close to him, and to do his will.
The March 2016 meeting workbook
(you may recall this) had this scenario.
It said: “Instead of funerals,
there may be welcoming sessions for the resurrected.”
Wow!
That’s going to be so amazing for us to actually be there
and experience these welcoming-type of meetings.
And it posed two questions in that meeting workbook:
“Which of your friends and relatives
do you especially look forward to seeing again?”
Now, there are probably some people
going through your mind right now, like I am thinking about.
The second question:
“Which Bible characters do you especially want to meet and talk to?”
Again, a whole list is probably coming into our minds.
Well, stay tuned.
Well, here’s a question:
What indication do we have as to the manner
in which the resurrected ones will take their place?
How will they come back?
Well, based on 1 Corinthians 15:23,
we know that the heavenly resurrection
of the anointed is done in an orderly way.
As Paul said: “Each one in his own proper order:
“Christ the firstfruits,
afterward those who belong to the Christ during his presence.”
So it will be progressive during that time.
Now, since we know that Jehovah is a God of order,
it’s reasonable to conclude that the earthly resurrection
will take place in a logical and orderly way.
Instead of having billions come back to life all at once,
we know that it would make much more sense that it would be done progressively.
So as each one is resurrected —they come to life—
we can help them individually
with their needs and their circumstances.
Well, what do we know about the physical and spiritual care
resurrected ones will receive at that time?
Well, at the right time,
at Jehovah’s perfect timing, he will awaken them.
And what will they find?
They will find abundant housing, clothing,
and food all given to them.
By whom?
By those who will make it through this system and on into the next
—great tribulation survivors,
you and me.
And we have a precedent for that.
Remember when Jesus resurrected a little girl?
And all those who saw that amazing miracle
—what did he say to those who saw that?
He said: ‘Please give the little girl something to eat.’
So he didn’t say that every time he resurrected someone,
but he knew her individual needs, and he addressed those.
And likewise, we will have that privilege in this coming system.
Most of us will have that privilege.
And think about all the training
that we have received here at Bethel and LDC
and other areas of our organization
that will be put to use at that time.
And think about the billions of “unrighteous ones”
that will be resurrected that will need to have spiritual instruction.
They will need to learn about Jehovah;
they will need to learn about Jesus and the ransom sacrifice
and how they can exercise that faith in the ransom.
Who will teach them?
You will teach them, and hopefully I will teach them.
And what will we use as a basis
to teach these ones who need to learn
about Jehovah, Jesus, and Jehovah’s requirements?
Well, of course, the Bible will be something that we will use.
But John’s vision at Revelation 20:12 gives us another clue.
Let’s turn there and read this together,
Revelation 20:12;
it says:
“And I saw the dead, the great and the small,
“standing before the throne, and scrolls were opened.
“But another scroll was opened; it is the scroll of life.
“The dead were judged out of those things
written in the scrolls according to their deeds.”
Now, was this mentioning the “deeds”
of their past conduct, or past deeds?
No.
This judgment will not focus on what they did before they died.
But how do we know that?
Romans 6:7, as you recall, says:
“For the one who has died has been acquitted
“[or the footnote says: “released (pardoned)”]
from his sin.”
So those who come back to life,
those who are resurrected, will have a clean slate.
What a relief for them and for us,
because many of us do know many
who did not worship Jehovah before they passed away!
So that clean slate is such a relief.
So to live forever there will be further requirements
for those who survive the great tribulation
as well as those who are resurrected.
We need to learn and continue to obey those requirements
and any new ones that might be revealed by Jehovah
during the thousand years.
Well, what don’t we know about the resurrection?
A lot.
There are so many questions that we might have:
Will those who died recently be raised
near the start of Christ’s Thousand Year Reign?
Will the righteous be brought back first and then the unrighteous?
Will they be welcomed by loved ones who know them?
Will resurrections take place in the area where people died?
How will Jehovah arrange matters
for those who were married when they died?
Will faithful men of old with leadership abilities
come back to help to organize matters?
Well, how will theocratic spiritual food be given?
Will there be a Teaching Committee or Writing Committee,
or will another arrangement be made to provide spiritual food?
Will there be hard copies?
Will there be electronic copies? Will there be videos?
Will there be some sort of JW broadcast?
We just don’t know.
We need to stay tuned, and we need to be patient.
It’s good to heed Jeremiah’s advice.
If you turn to Lamentations chapter 3,
notice there in Lamentations 3:25, 26
something that we want to focus on today in the meantime.
It says: “Good is Jehovah to the one hoping in him,
“to the person who keeps seeking him.
“Good it is to wait in silence [or the footnote says: “to wait patiently”]
for the salvation of Jehovah.”
So we know that in due course,
all will be revealed by Jehovah.
And as we rest our hope on Jehovah
and those in the future come back,
they will know that the one who will “satisfy the desire of every living thing”
will have it all taken care for us.
All the answers will be given to us.
Jehovah has always given us what we need to be faithful now,
and he’ll do the same in the future.
And now it’s up to each and every one of us
to prove our faithfulness,
to put our hope in that resurrection hope, and to share it with others.
And hopefully some day, maybe a thousand years from now,
we’ll look back, and we’ll say:
“There [was ] a resurrection
of both the righteous and the unrighteous.”

cn.text: 在这个演讲里
我们会回答关于复活的三个问题
首先
关于复活，我们知道哪些事？
第二
有哪些事是我们目前不知道的？
还有第三
知道这些关于复活的事之后
我们可以做什么？
我们知道复活很快会在地上实现
那么我们来考虑第一个问题
关于复活，我们知道些什么？
我们知道
这是耶和华给我们的一个保证
当然，是一定会实现的
今天的经文是使徒行传24:15
经文说
正义的人
还有不正义的人都会复活
想象一下
当复活开始的时候会是怎样的景象？
6000多年来
所有死去的人
所有在死亡中沉睡的人都会复活过来
这是多么令人期待的景象
今天当日经文，守望台的评论
有一句话说得很好
它说
“耶和华
他希望人能永远活着，而不是死去。”
这让我们清楚看出耶和华的力量是多么强大
而且他对人类的爱是永远不会改变的
耶稣也表现出像耶和华那样的爱
事实上，他甚至愿意为我们而死
目的就是要兑现
他在约翰福音5:28,29的承诺
他说
“所有在坟墓里的人都会听到他的声音
就出来。”
所有人当然包括那些正义的和不正义的人
那些在死亡中沉睡的人都会再次活过来
他们可能已经被历史遗忘了
但耶和华从没有忘记他们
他们一直留在上帝的记忆里
你曾经去过一些旧的墓地或墓园
看到那里的墓碑吗？
有些墓碑上的文字因年久失修
都已经看不清楚
很多人已经忘记到底是谁埋在那里
但耶和华知道
而且他把他们一个一个都留在他的记忆里
谈到那些会复活过来
正义的人，这些人是谁呢？
包括那些
在耶稣牺牲生命之前去世的忠心男子和女子
同时也包括在最后的日子去世的另外的绵羊
不正义的人又是谁呢？
我们知道
不正义的人包括那些千千万万死去的人
他们在去世之前没有机会认识耶和华
崇拜耶和华
或按照圣经的真理而生活
复活的时候
他们会有机会认识耶和华
跟他建立个人的关系
按照他的旨意而生活
2016年3月的《聚会手册》
有一句话这样说
它说
“未来我们不用再悼念死者
而是要欢迎那些复活的人。”
哇！
你能想象到时的情况吗？
你可以在现场欢迎那些复活的人
你会有多么高兴！

title: 첫 번째 왕국 전파자 학교 졸업식

ko.text: 봉사 훈련 학교에서 그리스도인 부부 성서 학교,
학생들이 영적 유산의 가치를 더 깊이 이해할 수 있어요.
실제적으로 봉사를 잘할 수 있는 법을 배울 수 있습니다.
왕국 전파자로서 준비를 더 잘 갖추게 된 것 같습니다.
여호와께서 우리에게 직접 하나하나 가르쳐 주시는 것 같았죠.
저도 여호와처럼 사람들에게 진실한 관심과 참을성을 나타내면서
독신 자매도 이 학교에 참석할 수 있어서 정말 좋아요.
여호와의 성품의 다양한 부면에 대해 배울 수 있다는 건
복음 전파자로서 사람들에게 가서 전파해야 할 절실한 필요를 느끼게 됐어요.
학교 과정에 온전히 집중할 수 있도록
처음에는 좀 긴장도 되고 걱정도 됐어요.
우리 학생들은 서로 격려하고 지원하고 있죠.
학교가 진행되는 내내 여호와의 도움을 경험했습니다.
‘지혜와 이해력이 금과 은보다 낫다’고 알려 줍니다.
이미 금을 어느 정도 가지고 있었죠.
나름대로 성경을 연구해서 모은 학생들도 있죠.
깊이 파내려 가는 법을 가르쳐 줍니다.
깊이 있게 연구하는 법을 알게 되죠.
충실히 수행하는 데 도움이 될 것입니다.
학생들이 임지로 떠날 준비가 되어 있다고 확신합니다.
하루라도 빨리 야외에서 적용하고 싶어 합니다.
개정된 교과 과정의 첫 번째 학급의 졸업식에 오신 여러분을 환영합니다.
독신 형제 자매들도 참석할 수 있죠.
부부들과 독신 자매들이 몇 분 계시네요.
그보다 더 큰 축복을 베푸시는 분입니다.
우리 한 사람 한 사람을 축복하려는
여호와의 따뜻한 마음을 잘 보여 주죠.
이 학교를 모든 분들께 권해 드립니다.
이 특별한 교육에 대해 감사하는 마음을 유지하고,
여러분이 두 달 전에 이곳에 왔을 때보다
더 훌륭한 왕국 시민이 되었음을 보여 주십시오.
오늘날 이 세상 교육을 통해 얻게 되는 “지식은 우쭐대게” 하죠.
우리는 이 학교에서 그 점을 분명히 느꼈죠.

en.text: I’m Joy Allen, and I’m a single sister,
and I’m in the first class
of the School for Kingdom Evangelizers.
We’re just thrilled at the idea of being invited.
Now, when they raised the age limit
and allowed us to apply,
we were just so thrilled.
Well, with the schools, we’ve seen constant refinement
—from MTS
to BSCC to now the School
for Kingdom Evangelizers.
It’s become much more visual.
We have historic presentations to help them with their spiritual heritage.
We have workshops that help them to see
how to really carry out their ministry properly.
I feel better equipped
to be a Kingdom evangelizer.
Jehovah has really sat us down
and showed us how to do it.
So now I would like to express that genuine care for people as well,
and just be patient and, at the same time, be bold like Jehovah is.
I am so happy that single sisters
are being accepted to attend this school.
It is an amazing privilege
being able to see so many different aspects
of Jehovah’s personality with different class discussions.
Of course, this helped me as an evangelizer.
I feel the urgent need to really go and preach.
Being selected to the first class of SKE
was really, really amazing to me.
Jehovah was listening to my prayers,
and he said, “OK, you can come.”
Living with our host family has been like a home away from home.
It’s amazing how quickly
you can feel like you’re family
with somebody that you just met.
And they’ve gone out of their way to make us feel comfortable
and make sure that we have what we need
so we could study and get the most out of the course.
But it’s just been nice to also have a friendship along the way.
I was nervous and anxious
because of English
not being my first language.
But all those worries, you know,
went away immediately.
The instructors are really loving and caring;
and classmates are cheering for each other, supporting each other;
and Jehovah helped me through every step.
Proverbs 16:16
—the essence of it says
that wisdom and understanding are better than silver and gold.
And the students came to school rich;
they had gold.
Some of them got it because they were raised in the truth—it was handed to them.
Some gold they gleaned
from some surface study.
But what SKE did for the students
was that it taught them
how to mine for gold.
So when they leave the school,
they are delving into the Bible
as they have never dug into it before,
and that will sustain them in any assignment they are given.
Oh, the students are ready for their assignments, no doubt about that.
They are anxious to get to the field.
They really want to get out there and apply what they have learned.
They want to “do the work of an evangelizer”
and “fully accomplish [their] ministry.”
We welcome you to class number one
of the revised curriculum, and the name has been changed
to School for Kingdom Evangelizers,
which includes single brothers and sisters.
And this class has some single sisters along with the couples.
So this is some history here.
I would recommend this school to anyone
who is in a position to accept it.
It will strengthen your bond with Jehovah and with your brothers and sisters.
And it’s a beautiful gift
and provision that he has made for all of us.
A school like this is evidence
(and we have almost a dozen schools functioning
that are educating Jehovah’s Witnesses)
that we’re big about education, but it’s divine education.
One thing we’ve learned is
that Jehovah can bless more than we can sacrifice.
SKE is a beautiful manifestation of Jehovah’s desire
to bless each and every one of us.
I highly encourage it.
Stay grateful for the privilege you’ve enjoyed,
and set a good example.
Prove to yourselves that you’re better ministers
than when you got here a couple of months ago
and that you’re better citizens of the Kingdom now
because of your divine education.
First Corinthians 8:1 really helped us to see that this world today
may offer things, but “knowledge puffs up.”
“Love builds up” in this course.
We’re built up; we’re built up.
So I would say, “If you want, come be built up by Jehovah.”

ko.text: 방해가 될 수 있는 게 있더라도
어떻게 여호와께 계속 초점을 맞출 수 있는지 살펴볼 것입니다.
봉사에서 마음을 감동시키는 데 초점을 맞출 때
어떻게 더 효과적이 되는지도 볼 것입니다.
청소년들을 위해 특별히 만들어진 이번 달 새로운 노래는
여러분이 생명의 상에 눈을 계속 고정하는 데 도움이 될 것입니다.
주의를 집중하라는 말을 들어 본 적이 있을 겁니다.
사실, 우리 모두가 생각해 봐야 할 점입니다.
특별히 주의를 기울여야 할 어떤 경우들이 있을까요?
장로라면 양 치는 방문을 할 때,
자녀라면 부모의 교훈을 들을 때 그래야 합니다.
주의를 산만하게 하는 것들이 너무나 많죠.
정말, 주의를 기울인다는 것은 쉽지 않습니다.
수십 차례 이상 나온다는 걸 알고 계셨습니까?
여호와께서 자신의 백성을 교훈하실 때 그 말씀을 하셨습니다.
그리고 우리가 여호와께 주의를 기울이는 것은
그들이 가진 모든 것을 완전히 멸망시키라고 명령하십니다.
사울이 자신이 불순종한 일에 대해 어떤 변명을 하는지 보겠습니다.
‘그러면 내 귀에 들려오는 이 양 떼의 소리와
내가 듣고 있는 소 떼의 소리는 대체 무엇입니까?’
백성이 당신의 하느님 여호와께 희생을 바치려고
양 떼와 소 떼의 제일 좋은 것을 남겨 두었습니다.
여호와께 희생을 바치려고 동물들을 남겨 뒀다고 했습니다.
주의를 기울이는 것과 순종이 어떻게 관련되는지 살펴보겠습니다.
사울이 불순종하게 된 한 가지 원인은 무엇이었습니까?
여호와의 지시에 주의를 기울이지 않았기 때문이죠.
사울은 주의를 기울이지 않았기 때문에 불순종하게 됐고
우리의 숭배가 여호와께 받아들여지지 않을 수 있습니다!
