다른 사람을 효과적으로 가르칠 자격을 갖출 수 있었죠.
우리가 아까 살펴본 점을 강조하지 않습니까?
우리는 늘 하느님의 말씀을 배우는 학생입니다.
베델이나 회중에서 영적 프로그램에 참석하기 전이나
겸손한 태도로 잘 듣게 해 달라고 기도할 수 있습니다.
우리는 얼마나 오랫동안 여호와께 배워 왔든지 잘 들어야 합니다.
모든 걸 다 아는 사람은 아무도 없고,
“지혜로운 사람은 잘 들어서 더 많은 교훈을 얻”는다고 알려 줍니다.
좀 부정적인 태도를 갖고 있다면 어떠합니까?
어쩌면 그 주제에 대해 흥미가 없거나
썩 마음에 들지 않을 수 있죠.
여호와로부터 온 것임을 인정하고 기억할 수 있게 도와 달라고
거기에 나오는 내용을 좀 읽어 드리죠.
프로를 다루는 사람의 가르치는 능력을 기준으로
프로를 다루는 사람의 가르치는 기술이 중요하기는 하지만,
그것이 집회의 성공을 좌우하는 유일한 요인은 아닙니다.
연사가 연설을 얼마나 잘 하느냐가 아니라
우리가 귀를 기울여 얼마나 잘 듣느냐가 되어야 하지 않겠습니까?
제공되고 있는 내용에 주의를 기울일 때,
우리는 하느님의 뜻과 일치하게 그분을 숭배하는 것입니다.
연사의 능력에 관계없이, 집회로부터 유익을 얻을 것입니다.”
우리 모두가 꼭 기억해야 할 점이죠!
언제나 받아들이고 적용하려고 결심한 학생들로서 말이죠.
아침 숭배를 베델 식당이 아닌 다른 곳에서 시청하게 될 경우,
우리의 주의를 산만하게 하는 것이 얼마나 많은지 아마 잘 아실 겁니다.
그런가 하면 질병이나 통증 때문에 집중하기 어려운 경우도 있습니다.
오랫동안 심한 편두통에 시달려 왔다고 말했습니다.
편두통에 시달리며 집회를 본다고 상상해 보니
주의를 산만하게 하는 요인이 많은 건 사실입니다.
우리가 어디에 집중하는지에 큰 영향을 주기 때문에,
집중하는 데 도움이 되는 방식으로 눈을 사용하십시오.
연사가 성구를 언급할 때는 —잘 아는 성구라도—찾아보고,
연사가 읽을 때 눈으로 따라 읽으십시오.
소리가 나는 쪽으로 고개를 돌리고 싶은 마음을 억제하도록 하십시오.
주의를 산만하게 만드는 정보가 눈을 통해 머릿속에 몰려들면,
연단에서 제공되는 내용의 상당 부분을 놓치게 될 것입니다.”
이제 전자 기기를 사용하는 문제도 생각해 보죠.
알림이 오거나 문자나 이메일을 받은 적이 있으신가요?
차단하는 모드로 바꾸는 것이 지혜로울 것입니다.
그럼 염려나 불안한 생각이 있을 때는 어떻게 해야 합니까?
그분이 가까이 계신다는 점을 기억할 수 있습니다.
시편 필자가 여호와께 무엇이라고 말했는지 살펴보시죠.
집회에서 우리가 그분께 배우는 것에 집중할 수 있도록
우리를 달래 주고 위로해 주실 수 있습니다.
네, 집회는 영적으로 살아 있게 해 주는 여호와의 마련입니다.
우리도 ‘여호와의 법을 조사하고 실천하고 가르치겠다고’ 결심합시다.
또한 주의를 빼앗는 것이 많기 때문에,
여호와께서 가르치시는 선한 것들에 온전히 집중하도록 합시다.
미래에 영향을 줄 많은 결정들을 내려야 할 것입니다.
그렇다면 어떻게 결정을 잘 내려서 끝까지 생명의 경주를 달릴 수 있을까요?
많은 분들이 신권 건축 공사에 자원하려는 목표를 갖고 계시죠.
최근에 영국의 아름다운 새 지부 시설을 위한 건축 공사에
수많은 우리 형제 자매들이 시간과 활력을 바쳤습니다.
그들의 수고로 어떤 결과가 있었고 어떤 축복이 있었는지 알고 싶으십니까?
시 의회의 건축 허가를 받았다는 소식을 들으면
이 건물들이 아름답긴 하지만, 사실 그저 건물일 뿐이죠.
이 공사에서 정말 특별한 부면은 바로 사람들입니다.
이 현장에선 아주 사이 좋게 일하더군요.
모두 얼마나 친절한지 몰라요. 여기 와 보니, 정말 인상적입니다.
부정적인 사회에서 살다가 이곳에만 딱 오면
예상 밖의 인기를 끈 곳은 방문객 센터였습니다.
이토록 관심이 많을 줄은 미처 몰랐습니다.
사실 제가 침례를 받으려고 성경 공부를 하는 이유 한 가지가
그래서 다들 격려해 주고 배려해 주셨죠.
모든 분들이 이 공사를 돕고 싶어 했습니다.
보내 주신 기부와 선물들은 우리 마음을,
때로는 우리 머리까지 따뜻하게 해 주었습니다.
이 공사에서 두드러진 또 하나의 특징은
형제 자매들이 노력과 비용을 들여 희생하는 모습을 보고,
여호와를 위해 일하는 게 정말 특권임을 다들 느꼈습니다.
이 공사에서 그만한 열심과 열정을 느낄 수 없었을 겁니다.
이 훌륭한 분들과 한 가족이라는 게 행복하지 않으십니까?
월간 모임을 가질 때마다 이번이 최고라고 느꼈습니다.
자신의 한계를 넘어서는 일들도 믿음으로 할 수 있죠.
공사가 끝났다고 슬퍼하지 말고, 좋은 경험한 걸 기뻐해야죠.
평생 우정을 나눌 친구들을 갖게 해 주시고,
여호와께 주의를 기울인다는 것이 무슨 뜻인지 배웠습니다.
어떻게 여호와께 계속 초점을 맞출 수 있는지 살펴봤죠.
사람들의 마음을 감동시키는 데 초점을 맞추면
청소년들이 생명의 상에 계속 눈을 고정하도록 일깨워 줍니다.
이제 마치기 전에, 일본 남서쪽 끝에 위치해 있는
이시가키 회중의 형제 자매들을 만나 보겠습니다.
이 회중 구역에 있는 야에야마 제도는 12개의 크고 작은 섬들과
360여 종의 산호가 있는 산호초들로 이루어져 있습니다.
숲이 빽빽이 우거진 섬을 둘러싸고 있습니다.
여호와께서 만드신 아름다운 천체를 관찰하기에 이상적인 곳입니다.
섬들 사이의 거리가 멀기 때문에 봉사에 어려움이 따릅니다.
외딴 섬마을로 가기 위해 전도인들은 배나 작은 비행기를 탑니다.
그렇게 하는 덴 비용이 많이 들고, 이곳 경제 사정도 좋진 않죠.
섬에서 이동할 때는 자전거를 타기도 하고
물소가 끄는 수레나 마차를 이용하기도 합니다.
이곳에 오는 많은 관광객에게 좋은 소식을 전하는 데 효과적입니다.
최근 한 해에 백만 명이 넘는 관광객이 찾아왔죠.
이 회중에서는 매달 100건이 넘는 성서 연구를 사회하고 있습니다.
왕국회관은 중심이 되는 섬에 있는 이시가키시에 있습니다.
멀리 떨어진 이리오모테섬의 작은 집회 장소로 중계됩니다.
이곳에는 일곱 명의 형제 자매들이 살고 있죠.
전도인들은 함께 일하며 왕국회관을 잘 관리합니다.
또 이 아름다운 섬에서 격려적인 교제를 나누며 힘을 얻습니다.
이시가키 회중에 있는 우리의 형제 자매들이
지금까지 여호와의 증인 세계 본부에서 JW 방송이었습니다.

en.text: Welcome to our program!
This month’s theme is
“Are You Paying Attention?”
Strained relationships,
illnesses,
careers,
entertainment
—we’ll learn how to stay focused on Jehovah
despite these potential distractions.
We’ll see how our ministry is more effective
when we focus on reaching the hearts of people.
And our new song was written
especially for you young adults
to help you keep your eyes
on the prize of life.
This is JW Broadcasting®
for November 2020.
Are you paying attention?
Perhaps you’ve been asked that question
by your parents, a teacher,
or someone else in authority.
It’s a good question for each of us to ask ourselves.
Can you think of occasions associated with our worship
that require us to pay special attention?
For example, when reading the Bible, attending meetings,
elders when shepherding,
you children when being instructed by your parents.
We want to pay attention,
and yet there are so many distractions
—electronic gadgets,
the conversations and activities of those around us.
Truly, it can be a challenge to pay attention.
Did you know that the phrase “pay attention”
occurs dozens of times in the New World Translation?
In many of those occurrences,
Jehovah is instructing his people to pay attention.
What does it mean to “pay attention”?
And how important is it
that you and I pay attention to Jehovah?
The account in 1 Samuel chapter 15
will help us to answer those questions.
In verse 3, Jehovah instructs King Saul
to strike down the Amalekites
and to devote them and everything they have to destruction.
However, verses 8 and 9 tell us
that Saul did not obey.
He spared the king of Amalek
and the best of the animals.
How did Saul respond
when Samuel confronted him?
As we read verses 13-15,
note how Saul tried to justify his disobedience:
“When Samuel finally came to him,
“Saul said to him:
“‘May Jehovah bless you.
“I have carried out the word of Jehovah.’
“But Samuel said:
“‘Then what is this sound of the flock in my ears
“and the sound of the cattle that I hear?’
“To this Saul said:
“‘They were brought from the Amalekites,
“‘because the people spared the best of the flock and the herd
“‘for sacrificing them to Jehovah your God;
but what was left we devoted to destruction.’”
Did you notice?
Saul attempted to justify his disobedience,
claiming that the animals would be sacrificed to Jehovah.
Was Jehovah pleased with Saul?
As we read verse 22,
please note the connection between paying attention
and obedience:
“Samuel then said:
“‘Does Jehovah take as much pleasure in burnt offerings and sacrifices
“‘as in obeying the voice of Jehovah?
“‘Look!
“‘To obey is better than a sacrifice,
and to pay attention than the fat of rams.’”
What was one of the causes of Saul’s disobedience?
He didn’t pay attention to Jehovah’s instructions.
His failure to pay attention resulted in disobedience
and brought Jehovah’s disapproval.
What a powerful lesson for us!
As happened with Saul,
our worship could become unacceptable to Jehovah
if we fail to pay attention!
Now that we understand why it is important to pay attention,
let’s consider three aspects of paying attention
that are discussed in the Bible.
The first scripture we’ll consider
is 2 Chronicles 19:6:
“And he [Jehoshaphat] said to the judges:
“‘Pay attention to what you are doing,
“‘for you do not judge for man but for Jehovah,
and he is with you when you pass judgment.’”
This admonition to “pay attention”
was given by King Jehoshaphat
to appointed judges throughout the land of Judah.
What a sobering reminder!
Those judges had good reason
to pay attention to what they were doing.
Why?
They were responsible to Jehovah.
They represented him,
and their decisions affected the lives of fellow worshippers.
Thus, they needed to be familiar with Jehovah’s thinking on matters
and to hold to his unprejudiced viewpoint
when handling matters.
This is an excellent reminder for those who serve as elders.
Good elders are good students of the Bible
and Bible-based publications.
Why?
Their attentiveness to Jehovah
enables them to pay attention to what they are doing.
If they are going to represent Jehovah
and reflect his thinking accurately as they handle matters
—whether they’re shepherding the congregation,
delivering a part at a meeting,
caring for a challenging assignment,
or addressing wrongdoing
—they must pay attention to what they are doing.
That is why they must be familiar with Jehovah’s thinking
and then take care to follow his direction.
If they do, they show that they are paying attention
to what they are doing.
Jehovah’s interest in assisting the elders
is demonstrated in the ongoing education he provides.
Each time the circuit overseer visits the congregation,
he presents material prepared especially for the elders.
The Kingdom Ministry School and the School for Congregation Elders
provide more intensive instruction.
How important
that elders pay close attention to
and apply such instruction!
Their doing so protects, not just themselves
but also fellow worshippers.
By paying attention, elders will be able
to convey direction to the congregations accurately.
This can be especially important if our worship is banned
or restricted in the event of a natural disaster
or other catastrophic event.
This brings us to the second aspect of paying attention
that we’ll consider.
Let’s read Luke 8:18:
“Therefore,
“pay attention to how you listen,
“for whoever has will be given more,
“but whoever does not have,
even what he imagines he has will be taken away from him.”
What did Jesus mean when he said:
“Pay attention to how you listen”?
Those in Jesus’ audience in the first century
had the wonderful privilege of hearing Jesus’ literal voice
as he instructed them.
Of course, we can’t hear the voice of Jesus today,
but we can read his words and learn of his actions
as revealed in the Gospel accounts.
In fact, we have many opportunities to listen
to Jehovah, Jesus,
“the faithful and discreet slave,”
the elders in our congregation,
our marriage mate,
and our children.
No wonder the Bible writer James stated
that “everyone must be quick to listen.”
Think about it:
If Saul had truly listened receptively
to Jehovah’s direction regarding the Amalekites,
he would likely have grasped the importance of the direction he received
and would have been motivated to obey.
However, his lack of attentiveness
led to disobedience and Jehovah’s disapproval.
If we don’t pay attention to how we listen,
we could find ourselves becoming critical
or unappreciative
or even disobedient.
So as Jehovah instructs and directs us,
we need to think about what we are being told,
ponder over its meaning,
mull it over in our mind and, most important,
apply the instruction in our own lives.
If you’re a young person,
how can you show that you’re paying attention
to how you listen?
Consider the admonition at Ephesians 6:1-3:
“Children, be obedient to your parents
“in union with the Lord,
“for this is righteous.
“‘Honor your father and your mother’
“is the first command with a promise:
“‘That it may go well with you
and you may remain a long time on the earth.’”
You children, who do you think is the source of this direction?
We know that these words come from Jehovah.
Did you notice that the verses state not only
that children should “be obedient” to their parents
but also that they should “honor” their parents?
How can you show that you’re paying attention
to how you listen to this direction?
When I was a boy, I can remember occasions
when my parents would ask me to do something,
perhaps to take out the trash.
I would always obey.
But at times, I’d make it very clear
that I didn’t really want to do what was asked.
I think you young ones know what I mean.
However, if we’re truly paying attention
to how we listen to Jehovah’s words,
we’ll be careful to honor our parents,
which is an essential element of obedience.
In this way, we contribute to the peace of the family,
and we make Jehovah’s heart glad.
Additionally, as the promise in verse 3 indicates,
paying attention to how you listen will protect you
and contribute to your success in other ways
throughout your adult life.
Of course, all of us should remember
that our everlasting welfare will depend
on our willingness to listen and obey.
How important, then, that all of us
pay attention to how we listen.
The third aspect of paying attention is found
at Luke 21:34, 35:
“But pay attention to yourselves
“that your hearts never become weighed down
“with overeating and heavy drinking
“and anxieties of life,
and suddenly that day be instantly upon you as a snare.”
When Jesus admonished his followers
to pay attention to themselves,
he didn’t have in mind the selfish thinking that characterized King Saul
and that’s so common, even encouraged, in today’s world.
Rather, Jesus’ words reveal
that the key to paying attention to ourselves
is knowing ourselves
—knowing what’s in our figurative heart.
This is a challenge for all of us.
Why?
The Bible explains at Jeremiah 17:9:
“The heart is more treacherous than anything else
“and is desperate.
Who can know it?”
Verse 10 answers:
“I, Jehovah, am searching the heart,
examining the innermost thoughts.”
So Jehovah knows what is in our heart,
and he can help us to know.
He can help us to examine our motives and goals
and to discern why we do certain things.
Carefully and honestly looking at ourselves in the mirror of God’s Word
can reveal areas in our thinking, words,
and actions
that need attention.
For example, some of Jehovah’s people
—including those of retirement age
who have enjoyed very comfortable circumstances—
have concluded that they needed to make adjustments in their lifestyle,
simplifying their lives
so that they can serve Jehovah more fully.
Some who have done so have had the privilege
of attending the School for Kingdom Evangelizers.
Although it meant stepping out of their comfort zone,
perhaps moving to a new congregation,
they’ve experienced Jehovah’s blessing in ways that they couldn’t have anticipated
as they share the benefits of their experience
and theocratic education
in their new assignments.
How grateful we are
that Jehovah is providing ongoing, life-saving instruction
by means of his Word and organization.
May each of us be determined to “pay attention”
to what we are doing,
to how we listen,
and to ourselves.
By doing so, we’ll avoid falling into the trap of disobedience
as King Saul did.
Instead, as attentive and obedient servants,
we’ll enjoy Jehovah’s friendship forever.
Elders play an important role
in helping us stay focused on Jehovah,
particularly when we’re facing difficult problems.
In our first video,
notice how elders provide loving assistance.
Everything was going fine in my marriage
—or so I thought.
My ex-husband was disfellowshipped,
left home
and, in less than a month, we divorced.
Right after the divorce, I had to figure out
how I would provide for the girls,
so I began working as a cleaner.
I also had to provide for them spiritually.
But many times, because of discouragement and tiredness,
I couldn’t be there for them as much as they needed me to be.
Besides all of this,
I also had to deal with very negative feelings.
It was a very difficult time in my life.
I had never been so sick.
I couldn’t even get up to go to the hospital.
To cope with this problem, I just kept praying.
I was not able to walk, and I was not able to get to the meetings.
The elders realized that I was missing from the meetings.
The elders quickly came to my aid.
I remember that one of the things
that touched me the most
was when the elders read a scripture.
Psalm 139:3:
“You observe me when I travel and when I lie down;
you are familiar with all my ways.”
I realized that I am precious to Jehovah.
It was as if Jehovah was healing me.
I now knew that Jehovah was interested in me
and that he was looking after me.
He was making sure that I knew it.
Something else that I remember fondly
was after a meeting at the Kingdom Hall.
One of the elders gave me some scriptures to read at home
and said that if we needed any help,
the elders were there for us.
Two elders lovingly came to see me,
because Jehovah uses them as shepherds.
I live very far from the Kingdom Hall.
But the brothers made the sacrifice to get public transport,
get off at the main road,
and from there they walked 40 minutes
to reach my house.
I don’t know what I would have done.
When the elders arrived, they listened to me,
they cried with me, and they read the Bible with me.
Jehovah loves me.
When I started to feel better,
I went back to the group.
I was really happy to be back with my brothers.
Now, after all the help we have received, we are doing well.
The congregation is our second home, and we feel very good there.
Everything I have today, I owe to the brothers and sisters,
especially the elders.
I see shepherding calls as a very evident way
in which Jehovah demonstrates his full love for us.
I understand that at times
these visits might be a challenge for the elders,
but the results are really good.
Without a doubt, they can see that all the work
and all the effort is worthwhile.
I will never forget the help that I received from the elders.
This situation taught me that Jehovah will not let his sheep get lost,
not even one.
Jeremiah 23:4 says:
“‘And I will raise up over them shepherds
“‘who will really shepherd them.
“‘They will no longer be afraid or be terrified,
and none will be missing,’ declares Jehovah.”
How did the elders help Mariana and Elias?
As good shepherds,
they were attentive to Jehovah’s flock,
so they were quick to notice that help was needed.
They visited Mariana and Elias in their homes,
shared encouraging scriptures, and listened.
They showed that Jehovah cares for every one of his sheep.
Those brothers, like the elders in your congregation,
paid attention to the loving training and instruction
they’d received from Jehovah.
To expand their ministry,
many Witnesses have learned another language.
Have you?
If so, Jehovah knows your selfless effort and hard work
to preach and teach in that language.
But is preaching to people in their native language
sufficient to reach their heart?
Let’s see in this dramatization.
Our family had been learning Chinese for over a year.
It wasn’t easy.
God has many titles.
Did you know he has only one name?
[Speaking Chinese]
I was ready, or at least I thought so.
Matthew!
Yeah, I’ll be right there.
We were making progress,
and we weren’t giving up.
It seemed like most people just weren’t interested.
We were not having a good morning.
What happened?
Mom and Liz weren’t having a good morning either.
Brother and Sister Lin joined us.
They’ve been a big help to us.
We told them about our morning.
We were finally able to converse a little and give presentations,
but everything seemed to fall flat.
You ask good questions at the door
—but not always the right one.
You see, when you learn the language,
do not forget to learn about people.
He was right.
Our questions started conversations in our old territory, but not here.
Your pronunciation is very good, see.
Thanks, Brother Lin.
We needed a different approach
where we didn’t just learn the language
but also how to reach the heart of someone who speaks it.
In the July 2019 Watchtower,
we read about “Reaching the Hearts of Nonreligious People.”
Did you notice in paragraph 7,
how do you think that we could be more like the apostle Paul?
Well, Paul was a Jew,
but when he was talking to other people,
he had to adapt his presentation.
I like what 1 Corinthians 9:20-23 says:
“To the Jews I became as a Jew in order to gain Jews;
to those under law I became . . .”
Liz was right.
When Paul spoke to fellow Jews in Athens,
he reasoned from the Scriptures.
But when he spoke to the Greeks at the Areopagus, he adapted,
reasoning with them first without the Bible.
He later wrote:
“I have become all things to people of all sorts,
so that I might by all possible means save some.”
That’s what we needed to do.
We learned more about the people.
We started to listen more and talk about things
that interested them.
We found different ways to start conversations.
And we kept learning more about the culture.
Part of a Chinese proverb I found says:
“He who comes near ink is stained black.”
It’s been a great way to introduce
Proverbs 13:20:
“The one walking with the wise will become wise.”
It all comes down to showing love.
The more we paid attention to how we were teaching,
the more we were able to show people the God who loves them.
What a beautiful reminder that in the ministry,
we want to pay attention to people
—to what interests them and to what helps them!
And as we saw,
we may need to analyze and adapt our teaching methods,
just as Paul did.
Even as we endeavor to reach the hearts of people in the ministry,
we must safeguard our own heart.
A recent Watchtower article
offered practical suggestions to help us do that.
In our next video,
notice how our brothers benefited from applying what they learned.
Well, very good friends of ours
decided they wanted to go their own way and leave Jehovah.
And in the interim, they became bad association for us.
We had many good times together.
We drove to isolated territory together;
we even visited a brother who was sick in the hospital to encourage him.
I feel heartbroken
that they’re no longer serving Jehovah.
It’s really hard to lose a friend spiritually —very hard.
I was about to enter into full-time service,
but I still needed reassurance.
I was raised by my mother as a Witness.
Even though I had very little contact with my father,
he still tried to oppose my spiritual progress.
I kept fighting for the truth,
and I got baptized when I was 11.
I guess I felt like I was doing OK.
And after high school, I went to university.
I had to make some changes in my choice of entertainment.
We really never stop learning.
I do enjoy relaxing and watching television.
But I must admit that it is more and more difficult
to find something decent to watch these days.
Well, I’m not saying that I watch bad programs.
I would never do that,
but still I wonder
if what I watch is spiritually healthy for me.
The way of thinking I was exposed to in university
was pressuring me to find security in my life through material things
—like having my own place to live and economic stability.
But at what cost?
I remember that paragraph.
It said that Satan promotes making money
as the only way
you can find security in this world.
But one could sacrifice
so much to achieve it.
You could even lose
your friendship with Jehovah.
That article—it was just what we needed.
It described a watchman
who would protect the city
by sounding out an alarm on impending danger.
And at sounding that alarm,
he would shut the gates to the city to protect the city.
And I needed to do that.
We both needed to do that.
It’s true.
And it’s not even a question.
Our loyalty to Jehovah comes first
—before we’re loyal to any friends we have in this world.
The Watchtower  said
that storytelling
does more than entertain us.
In Bana, the city of Cameroon where I was born,
mothers spend their evenings with their children, telling them stories.
And even though I was young,
the stories my mother told me
continue to influence me even today.
So I said to myself: ‘Oh, no. Wait a minute, Happy!
‘It means that the stories that I watch on television
‘will also affect me sooner or later,
and the Devil knows that too.’
So I decided to completely cut out a number
of programs that I used to watch.
Now I’m serving in full-time service,
and I love it!
Jehovah is really taking care of me,
but I don’t want to forget
the beautiful principles I’ve learned from that article.
I still have to safeguard my heart.
I want to give my best to my Father, Jehovah.
Not a day goes by where we don’t think about these friends of ours.
And it’s certainly our hope that they come back to Jehovah
and that we can serve Jehovah together shoulder to shoulder.
But we’ve also learned
to keep our “little watchman” in check.
We need to make sure he does his job to “sound the alarm” and “shut those gates.”
Hmm, we never stop learning.
Well, true, it’s easier said than done,
but it is up to us.
It’s so important to safeguard your heart!
We all enjoy reading The Watchtower
and commenting at the Watchtower  Study.
But truly paying attention
means putting what we learn into action.
What else goes into being a discerning student?
That was the topic of a recent Morning Worship program
presented by Brother Joel Dellinger.
Our focus in the Watchtower study article
is on how we can unleash
the power of God’s Word
when teaching from the platform.
But, you know, whether we’re teaching
in a congregation setting,
on a Bible study, or in the family,
isn’t it true that all of us, brothers and sisters,
need to ‘pay constant attention to ourselves and to our teaching’?
And we know why that’s so important —because lives are at stake.
And all of us, younger or older,
touch the lives of other people.
So when we teach effectively,
we are giving opportunity to others
to attain the wisdom and the discernment that God’s Word can give them.
That’s why we need to approach any teaching opportunity
seriously and prayerfully.
Over 20 years ago, a kind elder gave me
some constructive counsel after a public talk.
And then, with a warm smile, he said this,
“Remember, none of us teach like Jesus did.”
Well, I’ll never forget that counsel.
Why were those observations so helpful?
Well, it reminded me that when teaching,
our model needs to be Jesus, the Great Teacher.
There’s more to learn from him.
And Jesus’ example reminds us of the need
to remain humble and diligent students of Jehovah
—the Grand Instructor.
Though all of us are teachers on occasion,
isn’t it true that most often
the role we play during spiritual programs
is that of students?
Just for a moment, think about the many hours
we spend as students —not teachers—
when we’re in the audience at congregation meetings,
at assemblies, and at conventions.
Add to that the time we are students
when we buy out time to watch the monthly broadcast,
to prepare for meetings, to engage in family and personal study.
And then think of the added privilege that many of us here have
—to enjoy morning worship five days a week.
You know, a typical program of morning worship
lasts between 20 to 25 minutes.
If you multiply that by 5 days a week and then by 52 weeks,
at a minimum, we are exposed
to at least 86 hours
of divine instruction each year.
But if we’re not careful,
some or much of that valuable instruction,
encouragement, and counsel could just wash over us.
So for the remaining time for our program this morning,
let’s consider some things all of us can do
to listen more effectively
at spiritual programs.
Please, for our first point, open your Bible
to Ezra 7:10,
and let’s consider Ezra’s example.
That’s Ezra 7:10,
and notice the reading carefully:
“Ezra had prepared his heart
“to consult the Law of Jehovah
“and to practice it,
“and to teach its regulations
and judgments in Israel.”
Now, if you have the Bible with the asterisk
next to “prepared his heart,”
if you tap on that, you’ll notice that that could be rendered as
“had determined in his heart.”
Well, what do we learn from Ezra?
He had the right attitude going into a period of study.
He had the right approach to study and learning.
He recognized that it was Jehovah
who would be teaching him through His Law.
And as the verse goes on to say, he first recognized
that he needed to personally practice what he was learning.
Only then would he be in a rightful position
to effectively teach others.
Well, this scripture emphasizes the point we’ve already made, doesn’t it?
Though we are teachers on occasion,
we are always first and foremost
students of God’s Word.
How can we imitate Ezra’s example
and prepare our hearts before study,
before attending a spiritual program
(whether here at Bethel or in the congregation),
before watching a monthly broadcast?
Well, we need to prepare our hearts by specifically praying to Jehovah,
recognizing him as the Source of the teaching.
What should we pray specifically about?
Well, for one, we want to pray that we remain humble
while listening to theocratic instruction.
We need to listen
—no matter how long we’ve been in Jehovah’s classroom—
because none of us know it all,
nor will we ever know it all.
Proverbs 1:5 reminds us
that “a wise person listens and takes in more instruction.”
Well, this leads to another question:
What if we find we have a somewhat negative attitude
toward a certain presentation
—perhaps the material doesn’t interest us,
or we have a negative attitude toward a certain brother
and his teaching ability?
What should we do?
Prepare our heart.
Pray to Jehovah to recognize and appreciate
that the instruction is from him.
Pray to have a thankful spirit.
You know, back in 2002, The Watchtower  made this helpful point
in an article that was entitled “Pay More Than the Usual Attention.”
I quote: “Some may tend to gauge the quality of a meeting
“by the teaching abilities of the participants. . . .
“Though the teaching ability of participants is important,
“it is not the sole factor contributing to a meeting’s success.
“Do you not agree that our prime concern should be,
“not how well the speaker delivers his talk,
“but how well we incline our ear?
When we attend meetings,” the article continues,
“and pay attention to what is being presented,
“we are worshiping God in harmony with his will.
“That is what makes the meeting a success.
“If we are eager to take in the knowledge of God,
“we will benefit from meetings,
regardless of a speaker’s abilities.”
What a beautiful reminder for all of us!
So our first point: Like Ezra,
let’s prepare our hearts with prayer,
as students who are determined to always
accept and apply what Jehovah has to teach us.
Let’s consider a second point:
the need to focus our attention.
Have you faced the challenge of staying focused
during spiritual programs?
Our minds may be distracted
with anxieties and many other things.
Noise and movements around us could distract us.
If we’re watching morning worship
at a location other than the Bethel dining room,
likely we well know the numerous distractions
that fight for our attention.
Some of us have ailments and physical discomforts
that may make it difficult to concentrate.
Recently, a sister in our congregation
told us about her long-term battle with migraine headaches.
I tried to put myself in her shoes,
having a migraine headache while attending a spiritual program
—difficult to concentrate.
Well, whatever the case may be, we know —we admit—
that there are many challenges and distractions.
What can we do about it?
Well, since the eyes strongly influence
where we focus our attention,
the Benefit  book provides this suggestion:
“Use your eyes to help you concentrate by keeping them on the speaker.
“When he cites a Bible text —even a familiar one—
look it up, and follow along as he reads it.”
And then it said this: “Resist the temptation to turn your head
“in the direction of every noise or movement.
“If the eyes are flooding your mind with distracting information,
you will miss much of what is presented from the platform.”
And think about, too, the use of electronic devices.
Have you ever been alerted, messaged, or e-mailed
while looking at the Bible on your device?
How wise it is when we turn those devices to a mode
that eliminates unnecessary distractions!
Well, what about anxieties or disquieting thoughts?
What could we do about that?
Well, here, again, is where we can remember
who the Grand Instructor is and how close he can be to us
when we’re in a teaching environment.
Open, please, your Bible to Psalm 94:19
to recall what the psalmist said to Jehovah.
At Psalm 94:19,
we read:
“When anxieties overwhelmed me,
you [Jehovah] comforted and soothed me.”
What a beautiful reminder!
Jehovah can soothe and comfort us
when attending spiritual programs
so that we can focus on what he’s teaching us.
Yes, spiritual programs are a provision from him
—a spiritual lifeline.
So as needed during a spiritual program,
we should pray to Jehovah to help us stay focused.
Pray repeatedly as needed.
Well, in summary, what have we learned?
All of us are teachers from time to time,
but first and foremost, we are students
in the classroom of the Great Teacher and the Grand Instructor.
Like Ezra, humility and appreciation
should move us to ‘prepare our hearts’ before every spiritual program.
We don’t want to miss anything
that Jehovah has for us.
We’re determined ‘to consult that Law
so that we can practice it and then teach it.’
And in view of all the potential distractions,
let’s make it our aim to use our eyes, our mind, and our heart
to focus attention on the goodness of Jehovah’s spiritual provisions.
If you are a young Christian who recently graduated from school
or will soon graduate,
you’ll make many decisions that will affect your future.
How, though, can you make decisions
that let you successfully run the race for life?
That’s the subject of our new music video.
Don’t look back To the things behind.
Keep your eyes straight ahead On that finish line.
Now’s the time to be strong. Keep building your faith.
Don’t let the world slow you down.
Put off ev’ry weight.
So let’s Run the race; run the race.
Run the race for life.

You’ve got to keep on going— Got to keep on moving.

The prize we gain— It’ll never fade away.
All the blessings in store— Soon we’ll see the day.

This world would like to have you turn around
And lose yourself in this life. But don’t let your hands drop down.

Run the race. Run the race for life!
Volunteering for theocratic construction projects
is a goal for many.
Recently, thousands of brothers and sisters
sacrificed their time and energy
to build a beautiful new branch facility in Britain.
Would you like to see the results of their hard work
and the blessings they received?
Please enjoy this report.
How will you feel when all we came here to do
is finally completed?
No doubt, we will find a moment to reflect
on the words of Philippians 2:13.
Yes, Jehovah energized us
and gave each and every one of us “both the desire
and the power to act.”
How has sharing on this project affected your life?
It all started over seven years ago.
Can you imagine how excited you’re going to be
when we hear that the new branch facility at Chelmsford
has been approved by the City Council?
Well, guess what?
Yesterday afternoon we received the approval.
Whilst the buildings are beautiful,
at the end of the day, they are just buildings.
The really special part of this project
has been the people;
even non-Witnesses saw that something special
was taking place on our site.
It’s a very friendly site to work on.
It’s just how friendly everyone is.
You walk in, and it just— I find it mind-blowing.
In a negative (sometimes) society,
when you come here, it just puts a smile on your face.
A truly unexpected success
was the visitors’ center.
How we underestimated the appreciation
Jehovah’s people have
for theocratic activities.
Visitors from all around the globe witnessed
the activities of Jehovah for themselves.
This is partly why
I’m actually studying the Bible to get baptized,
because when I came here, it just hit me somewhere, you know?
Me and Alicia can’t see,
so everyone has been so encouraging and thoughtful.
We really feel like Jehovah is with us and he’s supported us.
I really liked the ladies driving tractors.
Everyone wanted to have a part in the project.
Every single contribution warmed our hearts
and sometimes our heads too.
Another beautiful project highlight
was the day-volunteer program.
The effort and expense brothers and sisters
sacrificed reminded all of us
of what a privilege it is to work for Jehovah.
And how about the commuters who helped on the project?
Would the BRD family have had
the same spirit without our commuters?
Don’t you just love being a part of this amazing family?
We were regularly reminded that spirituality
is of the utmost importance.
Did you ever say that a monthly meeting
was the best one yet?
What lies outside the comfort zone
is the faith zone.
Don’t cry because it’s over;
smile because it happened.
What is your story?
The center of all of our stories is Jehovah.
He is the one who energized us;
he is the one who gave us both the desire
and the power to act.
He is the one we can thank
for the lifelong friendships we have formed,
the training we have received,
and the challenges we have been able to overcome.
Remember your story.
Really, it’s only just beginning.
In this month’s program,
we learned what it means to pay attention to Jehovah.
We saw how we can stay focused on Jehovah
despite potential distractions.
Elders are good shepherds
because they are attentive to Jehovah’s instruction.
Our ministry is more effective
when we focus on reaching the hearts of people.
And our new song
reminds our young adults to keep their eyes
on the prize of life.
Before we say goodbye,
let’s go to the southwest tip of Japan
and visit our brothers and sisters in the Ishigaki Congregation.
Their territory includes the Yaeyama Islands,
an archipelago
of 12 islands and more than 360 coral reefs.
Emerald-green waters surround these lush,
jungle-covered islands.
With almost no light pollution,
this is an ideal place to observe
Jehovah’s beautiful heavenly creation.
Vast distances between the islands make the ministry a challenge.
To reach remote communities,
publishers take ferries and small airplanes.
This is costly, and economic conditions here aren’t easy.
Transportation includes bicycles
as well as carts and wagons pulled by water buffalo.
Public witnessing is an effective way
to share the good news
with the many tourists who travel here.
More than one million
visited during one recent year.
Contact cards also produce good results.
The Ishigaki Congregation has 112 publishers,
including 35 regular pioneers.
They’re conducting more than 100 Bible studies every month.
The Kingdom Hall is in Ishigaki City on the main island.
Talks from this Kingdom Hall
are streamed to this small meeting place
for the seven brothers and sisters
who live on remote Iriomote Island.
The publishers work together to maintain the Kingdom Hall,
and they enjoy upbuilding association
in this beautiful land.
Our brothers and sisters in the Ishigaki Congregation
send their warm love and greetings.
From the World Headquarters
of Jehovah’s Witnesses,
this is JW Broadcasting.

工作

第22节

约沙法王在委任审判官的时候

会影响崇拜耶和华上帝的人的生活
因此

在处理事情的时候要公平无私
对长老们来说，这是一个很好的提醒
好的长老会勤奋研读圣经以及圣经刊物

因为，这样他们就能留心听耶和华的话
知道怎么样照顾弟兄姐妹

熟悉耶和华的思想

例如，每次分区探访的时候
分区监督都会提供一些资料培训长老们
另外，王国职务训练班以及会众长老训练班
也提供给长老们额外的培训
长老们留心听

ko.text: 그는 형법 제282조의 2 제1항을 어겼다는 이유로 기소되었습니다.
법원에서 해산한 단체의 활동을 조직했다는 것이었습니다.
안드레이 스투프니코프는 해당 단체의 발기인도 아니고
그 단체 산하 법인체의 회원이었던 적도 없습니다.
여호와의 증인 종교 자체는 금지되지 않았습니다.
법원도 해당 단체를 해산하면서 그 점을 분명히 밝혔죠.
그런데 그의 기소장에는 이렇게 돼 있습니다.
해당 종교 신자 수를 유지하고 증가시키는 조치를 취했다.”
이런 기소를 하는 건 터무니없는 일입니다.
저희 부부는 공항에 새벽 네 시에 도착했습니다.
탑승 수속을 밟고 있는데 보안국 요원들이 저희에게 다가왔어요.
그러면서 제가 수사를 받고 있다고 말했죠.
안드레이는 보안국에서 신문을 받고 법정에 섰는데,
그 후 여덟 달 동안 미결 구금되었습니다.
그동안 그는 아내를 볼 수 없었고
테러나 그 밖의 혐의를 추가할 수도 있다고 말했죠.
수사관들이 제가 협조하기로 하거나 죄를 인정하면
아내를 곧 만날 수 있게 될 거라고 말하더라고요.
자신을 격려하러 법원에 와 준 덕분에
안드레이가 그 어떤 극단주의 활동에도 연루되지 않았다는 건 분명합니다.
다른 누구에게 폭력이나 편견을 조장한 일이 전혀 없죠.
자기가 폭력을 행사한 적도 물론 없고요.
그가 한 일이라곤 동료 신자들과 만나고
자신의 종교적 견해를 다른 사람에게 이야기한 게 전부죠.
왜 이런 무고한 사람들에게 범죄자라는 누명을 씌워서
여러 가지 설이 있는데 그중 한 가지는
법 집행 당국에 할당된 극단주의자 검거 목표량이 있는데,
하지만 재판이 끝날 때까지 그의 활동에는 제약이 있습니다.
이 일을 겪으면서 안드레이의 삶은 크게 달라졌지만,
그는 무슨 일이 있어도 하느님에 대한 믿음을
그 무엇 하나 바꾸지 않을 겁니다.
저 때문에 피해를 입었다고 할 수 있는 사람은 한 명도 없죠.
저는 여호와를 아는 것에 대해 자부심을 느낍니다.
안드레이에 대한 재판 절차가 현재 진행 중에 있습니다.
조만간 재판 결과가 나올 것으로 기대됩니다.

en.text: The Krasnoyarsk Zheleznodorozhny District Court
has begun consideration of the criminal case
against Andrey Stupnikov, a peaceful believer
accused of extremism.
He is accused of a crime
under Article 282.2(1)
of the Criminal Code
—namely, organizing the activity of an organization
that has been liquidated by a court decision
for carrying out so-called extremist activity.
Andrey Stupnikov was not one of the founding members of such organizations
and was never a member of any of their agencies.
The religion was not banned.
This was specifically pointed out by the court
that ruled to liquidate the legal entities.
But the indictment states:
“Andrey Stupnikov took steps to maintain
“and increase the number of followers
of the said religious teaching.”
But a religion cannot exist without followers
who profess certain beliefs.
Andrey and Olga
have been married for 27 years.
They say that Bible knowledge makes their life strong and happy.
But on July 3, 2018,
their happy family life was disrupted
when Andrey was detained by the Federal Security Service (FSB).
My wife and I arrived at the airport
at four o’clock in the morning.
When we were at the check-in counter, the FSB officers
approached us
and said that I was under investigation.
Andrey was interrogated
by the FSB, appeared in court,
and then spent eight months in pretrial detention.
He was prevented from seeing his wife.
Officials tried to coerce him
into incriminating himself.
The authorities shouted and threatened
that they could, for example, increase the charges against me to include terrorism.
Then a difficult situation arose.
For some time, I stopped receiving letters from my wife
but I received letters from others.
Then a man came
and asked me:
“So, what happened to your wife? Do you know?”
Later, I realized why this was happening.
They told me that I could return to my wife very soon
if I agreed to cooperate or plead guilty.
Andrey acknowledges that the presence
of hundreds of fellow believers who came to court to encourage him
was a great support.
To the discerning mind,
it is obvious that law-enforcement agencies
have crossed all boundaries by labeling peaceful,
law-abiding citizens as “extremists.”
It’s clear that Andrey Stupnikov did not engage in any extremist activities.
He did not incite anyone to violence or discrimination,
much less employ violent means himself.
All he did was meet with fellow worshippers, participate in religious services,
and share his religious views with others.
Why are such peaceable individuals
being framed as criminals and imprisoned for six years?
There are many opinions on that question,
one of which is that they are an easy target for law-enforcement officers
who have quotas to meet in their battle against extremism.
At present, Andrey is home.
His current pretrial restrictions
prohibit certain activities.
And although Andrey’s life has changed a lot in the past year, he says
that persecution will not force him
to renounce his faith in God.
Reflecting on my life
since I dedicated myself to God,
I wouldn’t change anything.
Not one person can say
that I have ruined his life or done anything bad to him.
I’m proud to know Jehovah
and to have him by my side.
The judicial proceedings
against Andrey Stupnikov are well underway,
and we will likely find out very soon
if the judge will render a fair and independent decision
by acquitting a person who simply believes in God.

ko.text: 그리고 그 밖의 다른 일도 병행하고 있는데요.
실내 장식이나 시스템 관리 일도 하죠.
요원들이 우리 부부가 사는 집을 수색했습니다.
한 달 뒤에 법원은 저를 미결 구금하라고 지시했죠.
아내인 옐레나가 그 모습을 지켜보고 있었죠.
아내가 다시는 저를 보지 못할까 봐
걱정하고 있다는 걸 느낄 수 있었습니다.
저는 이바노보시에 있는 구금 시설에 수감되었죠.
동료 신자들에 대한 정보를 대라고 강요했어요.
그들의 이름, 주소 그리고 직업과 같은 것 말이죠.
또 이것은 형제 자매들에 대한 충성도 관련된 일이었죠.
다시 말해 사랑을 나타낼 것인가 하는 문제였어요.
제게는 여호와에 대한 충성이 그 무엇보다도 중요하며
무슨 일이 있더라도 하느님에 대한 충성을 지킬 것이라고
수사관들은 여러 달 동안 저를 가혹하게 대하고
저는 구금 시설의 도서관에 있는 성경 한 권을 받았습니다.
여호와께서 주시는 내적 평화와 안정감을 느낄 수 있었죠.
우리의 대해 생각하시고 우리에게 관심이 있으시다는
사랑하는 아내가 써 준 편지를 통해 절 격려해 주셨죠.
모든 걸 그분의 관점에서 바라보는 것이라는
수감자들 중에는 저를 힘들게 한 사람들도 있었는데
그런 사람들이 영적인 것에 관심을 보이고
제 신앙에 대해 질문을 하기도 했습니다.
어떤 수감자는 제가 정말 하느님을 믿는다면
십자가 같은 걸 지니고 다녀야 하는 것 아니냐고 물었습니다.
그래서 전 그에 대한 답을 성경에서 알려 주겠다고 했죠.
제가 읽어 준 내용을 듣고 그는 스스로 결론을 내렸습니다.
얼마 후 그 수감자는 제게 다가와
자기가 더는 십자가 목걸이를 하지 않는 걸 보여 주었죠.
수감되어 있을 때 제게 전도 봉사는
사람들에게 성경 진리를 전하는 것보다 더 큰 의미가 있었죠.
제가 긍정적인 시각과 기쁨을 유지하도록 돕기 위해
기쁨도 더 빨리 되찾을 수 있죠.
여호와를 섬기고 다른 사람을 도울 수 있습니다.
항소 법원은 저를 석방하라는 결정을 내렸죠.
사랑하는 아내와 형제 자매들이 함께 있었죠.
제가 살던 곳뿐 아니라 다른 도시들에서도
필요한 물건을 좀 전달해 주기로 했습니다.
그래서 물건을 사서 구금 시설을 방문했죠.
그리고 얼마 후 한 수감자에게서 감사 편지를 받았는데
사람들이 나를 사랑하고 소중히 여기고 그리워하는 게
얼마나 행복한 일일까 하고 상상해 보았어요.
그런 경험을 해 보지 못한 사람도 많이 있죠.
수감되어 있을 때 아내의 편지가 정말 큰 힘이 되었어요.
마치 여호와께서 아내를 통해 제게 말씀하시는 것처럼 느꼈죠.
지금 당신은 저의 사랑이나 가족과 벗들의 사랑을
온전히 느낄 수 없는 상황에 있지만
가장 중요한 건 당신이 하느님의 손 안에 있다는 거예요.
당신은 특별한 방법으로 그분의 사랑을 받고 있어요.
흔들리지 않고 안전감과 평온함을 누릴 수 있죠.
하느님과의 관계를 절대 깨지지 않도록 강하게 하세요.
하느님께서 주시는 힘으로 그 어떤 어려움도 이겨낼 수 있죠.

en.text: I work as a street cleaner;
either that or I do some other kind of work, like decorating
or system administration.
On April 20, they came to search
the home of my wife and me.
I was interrogated.
And after a month, a court ruled
to put me in pretrial detention.
When they lead me out of the courtroom in handcuffs . . .
. . . and put me into the vehicle,
Yelena (my wife) was at the exit.
From her words, I could sense
that she felt as though she was losing me.
They took me to the detention center in the city of Ivanovo.
They moved me from cell to cell.
And then they put me into what is known as the pressure cell.
They told me I had to admit my guilt
and tell them about my fellow worshippers
—give them names, addresses, what they do, etcetera.
For me, that would mean losing my loyalty to God.
And the second thing was that it involved my loyalty to my fellow worshippers.
In essence, it was about showing love.
I said that for me, loyalty to Jehovah is above everything else,
so whatever happens, I will remain loyal to God.
I told them openly, directly.
They pressured me physically and emotionally for several months.
They brought me a Bible from the detention center’s library.
Thanks to fervent prayers, I felt how Jehovah gave me
internal peace and calm.
It proves that Jehovah doesn’t just exist,
but he thinks about us; he cares for us.
Jehovah supported me through a letter from my dear wife.
In it was the thought that trusting in Jehovah
means seeing things the way he sees them.
The prisoners who put pressure on me
also expressed interest in spiritual things
and started asking questions relating to my beliefs.
Someone told me that if I am really a believer,
I should have objects to prove it, such as a cross, which all believers wear.
I told him that I could show him the Bible’s viewpoint.
From what I read, he made his own conclusions.
And after some time, this prisoner came up to me and showed me
that he wasn’t wearing a cross anymore.
When you are in prison,
the ministry isn’t just about opportunities
to tell people about the truth from the Bible.
It is more about Jehovah using it
to help you keep a positive outlook and maintain joy.
The more we concentrate on what we had before,
the more we suffer.
The quicker we accept the new circumstances,
the quicker our joy returns to us
along with the opportunity to make good use
of the new circumstances.
The appeal instance court ruled to release me.
It was, of course, quite an unexpected decision.
At the exit, my dear wife
and other fellow worshippers (brothers and sisters)
not just from my hometown but from other cities too met me.
Yelena and I thought it would be good to collect some essentials,
so we bought some things and went to the detention center.
And afterward, one of the prisoners
wrote me a letter of thanks:
“I heard how everyone came to meet you.
“I tried to imagine how cool it is
“to be loved, valued, and missed.
“For some, there’s not enough of that in life.
Take care of yourself, Dima!”
The letters from my wife were such a big support for me at that time.
To be honest, I saw her letters
as if it were Jehovah using her to speak to me.
“Nobody loves us as strongly as God.
“You can’t right now feel my love to the full extent
“or the love of your family and friends.
“But the main thing is that you are in God’s hands,
“and that is what’s more important.
“He loves you in a special way right now
“and very gently looks after you and cares for your feelings.
“By trusting in God,
“we can get a feeling of security, stability, and calmness.
“Our connection with God must be unbreakable.
“If our strength is in God,
“then we will overcome everything.
“Our suffering is just temporary,
and God will richly reward all who are loyal to him.”

cn.text: 我的工作是打扫街道
除此以外，我也做一些装修
还会做一些跟电脑有关的工作
4月20号那一天
执法人员闯进了我们的家
开始搜查
我被带到警局接受盘问
一个月后，法院决定将我审前羁押
他们给我铐上手铐
把我带出来
押进车里
我的妻子叶连娜站在法院门口
她对我说了一些话
我感觉她好像很担心
再也看不到我了
我首先被关在伊万诺沃市的拘留所
然后又从一个牢房搬到另一个牢房里
后来我被关进一个叫高压室的地方
他们要我认罪
还要我说出弟兄姐妹的名字、住址、工作
还有关于弟兄姐妹其他方面的信息
如果我真的说了，就是对耶和华不忠
也是对弟兄姐妹不忠
我意识到这是一个很好的机会
可以证明自己爱耶和华，也爱弟兄姐妹
对我来说，对上帝保持忠贞比什么事都重要
所以我很直接地告诉他们
不论情况怎样
我一定会对上帝忠心到底
一连几个月
他们向我施压，还虐待我
后来，他们从拘留所的图书室
给我拿了一本圣经
我恳切地向耶和华祷告
我能感受到耶和华赐给我内心的安宁
让我保持平静
这让我看出，耶和华不只是真实存在
还很关心我们，在乎我们
妻子给我写了一封信
让我感受到耶和华对我的扶持和帮助
信中提到
信赖耶和华
就是从耶和华的角度来看事情
对我不太友好的几个犯人
也开始对圣经表现出一些兴趣
而且开始问我一些问题
我记得有一次
一个犯人来问我
你既然是基督徒，为什么不戴十字架呢？
所有信上帝的人都戴十字架呀
后来，我让他直接看圣经怎么说
没想到的是，过了一段时间
这个犯人来见我
告诉我他不再戴十字架了
当你被关的时候
传道不仅让你有机会告诉人圣经真理
还是耶和华帮助你
保持乐观和快乐的一个方法
如果我们老是想着以前拥有什么
就会感到很痛苦
但如果我们尽快接受现状
并把眼前的这些考验
视为崇拜耶和华和帮助别人的机会
那么我们也会更快地重拾喜乐
后来，法院把我释放了
这个决定真的出乎我的意料
我出来的时候
看到我亲爱的妻子在外面等着我
还看到了其他的弟兄姐妹们
他们有的来自我的城市
有的甚至从其他城市赶过来欢迎我
获释后，我和妻子决定买一些必需品
去见那些在拘留所里的犯人
后来，一个囚犯给我写了一封感谢信
信中说
我听说有很多人过来接你
能够得到别人的爱、重视
还有思念
是多么快乐的一件事啊！
但有的人却得不到这样的爱
真的很羡慕你
德米，请多保重！
那个时候
妻子给我写的信真的给我很大的力量
我把这些信
看成是耶和华在通过我的妻子跟我说话
在信里她说
在这个世界上最爱我们的就是上帝
也许现在
你无法完全感受到我和亲朋好友的爱
因为我们不在你身边
但只要你知道耶和华正在看顾你，这就够了
他非常爱你
也在乎你的感受
只要我们信靠耶和华
就会享有内心的平静
还有安全感
我们必须和上帝建立牢不可破的关系
只要我们信赖耶和华
靠着他的力量
我们就可以克服任何考验
我们现在所受的苦是暂时的
但上帝一定会赐福给忠于他的人

titles.cn: 德米特里·米哈伊洛夫的访谈

title: 로버트 루시오니: 유혹할 기회를 노리는 사탄 (누가 4:6)

ko.text: 오늘 성구는 사탄이 예수를 유혹한 한 가지 경우를 언급하는데요,
사탄이 다른 기회 즉 예수를 유혹할 “또 다른 편리한 때까지”
이 점을 염두에 두고, 세 가지 질문을 생각해 보죠.
첫째, 사탄이 한 세 가지 유혹의 의도는 무엇이었습니까?
둘째, 사탄은 정말 또 다른 기회를 찾아 예수를 유혹하러 왔습니까?
셋째, 오늘날도 사탄은 그러한 유혹을 합니까?
세 번의 유혹이 나오는 마태의 기록을 통해 답을 찾아보겠습니다.
‘당신이 하느님의 아들이라면, 이 돌들에게 빵이 되라고 말해 보시오.’”
첫 질문으로, 이 유혹의 의도는 무엇이었을까요?
사탄은 예수가 여호와의 맏아들이란 걸 너무나 잘 알고 있었지만,
예수가 자신이 여호와의 아들이라는 사실에 의문을 품게 하려고 했습니다.
‘정말 당신이 하느님의 아들이라면, 왜 아버지가 먹을 걸 주지 않는 거요?
여호와가 당신을 돌보고 있다고 믿을 수 있소?’
네, 사탄은 예수가 여호와의 돌봄에 의문을 품고,
예수께선 이 유혹의 의도를 알아차리셨고, 속지 않으셨죠.
두 번째 질문은, 사탄이 정말 또 다른 기회를 찾아 유혹하러 왔는지였죠.
그는 예수가 체포됐을 때를 기회로 여겼을 겁니다.
“열두 군단이 넘는 천사들”이 자신을 구출하도록 요청할 수 있다고 하셨죠.
사탄은 그때를 기회로 생각했을 수 있습니다.
또는 예수께서 형주에 달려 계실 때,
‘당신이 하느님의 아들이라면 형주에서 내려와 보라’고 조롱했습니다.
흥미롭게도 그들은 사탄과 같은 말을 사용했죠.
하지만 예수께서는 여호와께서 자신을 돌보실 것임을 신뢰하셨습니다.
세 번째 질문으로, 사탄은 오늘날도 그러한 유혹을 합니까?
우리의 가족이나 벗이 어려움에 처한 상황에서,
여호와께서 그들을 돌보실 것을 신뢰하는 면에서
우리의 손으로 직접 문제를 해결해야겠다는 생각이 강하게 들 수 있을까요?
우리가 가진 봉사의 특권을 이용해 도움을 얻으려는 유혹을 받을 수 있을까요?
“그러자 마귀는 그분을 거룩한 도시로 데리고 들어가서
성전 흉벽 위에 세우고 그분에게 말했다.
“그분이 너에 대해 천사들에게 명령을 내리실 것이다”,
“그들이 손으로 너를 받들어 너의 발이 돌에 부딪히지 않게 할 것이다.”’”
이번에도 사탄은 예수의 신분에 의심을 불러일으켰습니다.
여호와가 실제로 당신을 돕고 소중히 여기는지 봅시다.
시편에도 진짜 하느님의 아들은 그분이 분명 도우신다고 나오지 않소?’
예수께선 유혹의 의도를 알아차리고 넘어가지 않으셨죠.
그럼 사탄은 또 그런 유혹을 한 적이 있습니까?
아마 마가복음 8:11의 경우가 바로 그런 상황이었을 수 있습니다.
기록을 보면 바리새인들이 와서 “그분과 논쟁을 벌이기 시작하며,
그분을 시험하려고 하늘에서 오는 표징을 요구했다”고 나옵니다.
바로 전에 예수께서 귀먹고 말 못하는 남자를 고치고
그들은 만족하지 않고 무언가 더 극적인 걸 원합니다.
당신이 하느님의 아들이란 걸 증명해 보시오.
그럼, 우리는 언제 비슷한 유혹을 받게 됩니까?
어떤 형제 자매들은 살면서 겪은 일 때문에
사탄은 지금이 공격하기 좋은 때라고 생각할 겁니다.
비성경적인 방법으로 자신의 가치를 인정받으려고 할 수 있습니다.
“마귀는 다시 그분을 매우 높은 산으로 데리고 가서
세상의 모든 왕국과 그 영광을 보여 주며 그분에게 말했다.
‘당신이 엎드려 내게 숭배 행위를 한다면, 이 모든 것을 당신에게 주겠소.’”
당신이 겪을 고통을 잘 알지 않소.
이번에도 예수께서는 사탄의 의도를 아시고 유혹을 물리치셨습니다.
사탄은 비슷한 유혹을 할 또 다른 기회를 찾았습니까?
아마도 요한복음 6:15의 상황이 사탄이 찾은 편리한 기회였을 수 있습니다.
사람들은 그때 예수를 왕으로 삼으려고 했습니다.
예수께선 이 유혹을 죽음의 고통 없이 자신의 왕국을 세울 좋은 기회로 보셨을까요?
그분은 사람들을 피해 혼자 산으로 들어가셨습니다.
우리는 여호와를 섬기기 위해 기꺼이 희생을 해 왔습니다.
그런데 다른 사람들이 갖고 있고 하고 있는 걸 보면,
지금 안정된 삶을 살 순 없을까?
여호와도 섬기고 돈도 더 벌어 갖고 싶은 걸 가질 순 없을까?’
여러분은 아버지께서 돌보실 것임을 정말 신뢰합니까?
여호와께서 여러분을 사랑하고 소중히 여긴다는 걸 확신합니까?
따라서 자문해 볼 질문은, 우리가 유혹받기 쉬운 때는 언제입니까?
사탄은 우리를 유혹할 또 다른 편리한 때를 찾아 돌아올 것입니다.
우리가 할 일은 사탄의 유혹을 저항하는 것이죠.
첫째로, 예수께서는 유혹을 받을 때 그것을 분별하셨습니다.
둘째로, 그 순간에 여호와께 초점을 맞추셨습니다.
그분은 사탄에게 대답하실 때마다 매번 여호와의 이름을 사용하셨습니다.
네, 여호와의 이름은 사탄의 공격에 대한 강력한 보호가 됩니다.
그래서 예수께서는 기도하는 방법을 가르치실 때
유혹을 물리치고 악한 자에게 저항할 힘을 주실 것을
같은 이유에서 예수께선 제자들에게 여호와의 이름을 알려 주신 것이죠.
우리가 보호를 받을 수 있는 “견고한 망대”라고 알려 줍니다.
네, 여호와께 말씀드리고, 그분의 이름을 사용하고,
그 이름에 담긴 모든 의미를 묵상하는 것은
사탄이 기회를 찾아 우리를 공격할 때 도움이 됩니다.
그렇게 할 때 어떤 결과가 있을까요?
시편 44:5에 나오는 이런 보증의 말씀에 유의해 보십시오.
우리를 대적하여 일어나는 자들을 당신의 이름으로 짓밟을 것입니다.”
네, 우리 모두는 사탄이 기회를 찾아 우리를 유혹할 것임을 알고 있습니다.
자신이 어떤 유혹을 받고 있는지 잘 분별하십시오.
그리고 여호와를 의지하고, 그분의 이름에 초점을 맞추십시오.
그렇게 한다면 우리는 시편 필자의 말에 공감하게 될 것입니다.
우리와 우리의 조직을 대적하는 자들을 물리치고 짓밟게 될 것입니다.

en.text: What are your convenient times?
Our text for today discusses
one of the temptations
that Satan presented to Jesus.
Luke 4:13 later says
that then Satan goes away
to return at “another convenient time” to tempt Jesus.
So with all that in mind, we’re going to consider three questions today:
(1) What were these three temptations really about?
(2) Did Satan ever find a convenient time
to come back and tempt Jesus?
(3) Does Satan try to use these temptations today?
We’re going to look at Matthew’s account of these three temptations
and try to answer those questions.
So let’s start first with Matthew 4:2, 3.
It says: “After he had fasted for 40 days and 40 nights,
“he felt hungry.
“And the Tempter approached and said to him:
“‘If you are a son of God,
tell these stones to become loaves of bread.’”
Now, our first question is, What was at the root of this temptation?
Well, Satan knew full well
that Jesus was Jehovah’s firstborn Son,
but he was trying to get Jesus to question
that he was who Jehovah said he was.
‘If you are a son of God,
‘why hasn’t your Father fed you?
Can you really trust Jehovah to take care of you?’
See, Satan wanted Jesus to begin to question Jehovah’s care
and use his position to benefit himself.
Well, Jesus recognized that this was a temptation,
and he did not fall for it.
Question two is, Did Satan ever come back
and try this trick again with Jesus?
Well, when Jesus was arrested, could that have been a convenient time?
Remember, Jesus said that he could have called on “12 legions of angels”
to come and save him.
Could that have been a temptation to save himself?
Or remember when he was on the stake,
the rulers and the soldiers taunted him and said,
‘If you are a son of God, come on down off the stake!’
It’s interesting that they used the same terminology.
Could that have been a temptation?
No.
Jesus trusted that Jehovah would take care of him.
Now, our third question is, Does Satan use that temptation today?
Well, we are living in unsettled times.
Are these convenient times for Satan?
Our families and our friends may be in need.
Could we be tempted to question
if we really trust that Jehovah is going to take care of them?
Could we be convinced or convince ourselves
that we may need to take matters into our own hands?
Are we ever tempted to use our privileges of service
to benefit ourselves?
Let’s look at the second temptation.
Matthew 4:5, 6 says:
“Then the Devil took him along into the holy city,
“and he stationed him on the battlement of the temple
“and said to him: ‘If you are a son of God,
“‘throw yourself down, for it is written:
“‘“He will give his angels a command concerning you,”
“‘and, “They will carry you on their hands,
so that you may not strike your foot against a stone.”’”
Again, what was the root here?
Well, Satan was again trying to cast doubt on who Jesus was.
‘If you are who you say you are, prove it.
‘Let’s see if Jehovah really is there for you.
‘He does value you.
‘He’ll save you because Psalms says
that’s what he’ll do for the real Son of God.’
Well, Jesus saw that this was a temptation and did not fall for it.
Now, did Satan ever try such a temptation again?
Well, perhaps another time
is what’s recorded at Mark 8:11,
where the Pharisees came, and the account says
they “started disputing with him,
demanding from him a sign from heaven, to put him to the test.”
Now, Jesus had just healed a deaf and speechless man
and miraculously fed over 4,000 people, but that wasn’t enough for them.
They wanted something spectacular.
‘Throw yourself off the temple or something.
‘Prove you are who you say you are.
Let’s see if Jehovah really values you.’
Now, when might we face a similar temptation?
Well, some of our brothers and sisters may feel unlovable
because of events in their life.
Times of isolation and depression may be convenient times
for Satan to attack them.
‘Am I sure Jehovah really loves me?
‘Am I sure I’m important to Jehovah?
Do I have value?’
Well, such feelings have caused ones to stop serving Jehovah
or to seek validation of their value
through unscriptural means.
Look at our third temptation.
Matthew 4:8, 9:
“Again the Devil took him along to an unusually high mountain
“and showed him all the kingdoms of the world and their glory.
“And he said to him: ‘All these things I will give you
if you fall down and do an act of worship to me.’”
So, what was Satan offering here?
‘Don’t wait! You can have it now.
‘You know what’s coming —the pain that’s coming.
My offer is better than Jehovah’s.’
Again, Jesus recognized what Satan was doing,
and he resisted that temptation.
Did Satan ever find a convenient time to try that again?
Well, perhaps the account at Luke 6:15 explains
what may have been another convenient time.
Remember, the people wanted Jesus to begin ruling right then.
Could that have been a temptation to get his Kingdom started
without the pain of being tortured to death?
Well, knowing that the people were coming for him,
Jesus withdrew.
Do we face similar temptations today?
Well, we willingly make sacrifices and have made sacrifices to serve Jehovah.
But we may see what others do and what others have and wonder:
‘Are our sacrifices really worth it?
‘Is there any way I can have it now?
‘Maybe if there’s a way I can make some more money, I could do both
and have the things I want.’
You see, three powerful temptations:
Can you trust that your Father will take care of you?
Are you sure Jehovah loves you and you have value?
Why wait when you can have it now?
So again, the question is,
What are your convenient times?
What are my convenient times?
Satan is going to find convenient times to tempt us—that’s a given.
First Peter 5:8 says that he’s out there
“like a roaring lion, seeking to devour [us].”
If he found convenient times to tempt Jesus,
we can be sure that he will do the same to us.
What do we need to do?
Our job is to resist his temptations.
How do we do that?
The same way that Jesus did.
Did you notice the two things he did?
(1) Jesus recognized
when he was being tempted,
and (2) at that moment, he focused on Jehovah.
It’s interesting that in every one of his responses to Satan,
he used Jehovah’s name.
See, Jehovah’s name is a powerful protection against Satan’s attacks.
That’s why Jesus listed praying to Jehovah
to resist temptation, to resist the wicked one,
as a fundamental part when he was teaching his disciples how to pray.
That’s why Jesus said that he made Jehovah’s name known to his followers.
That’s why Proverbs 18:10 tells us that Jehovah’s name
“is a strong tower” that we can run to for protection.
See, speaking with Jehovah, using his name,
and meditating on his name and everything that it means
can help us when we are being tempted by Satan
—when he finds convenient times to attack us.
And if we do that, what will be the result?
Well, notice the guarantee that we have
at Psalm 44:5
—Psalm 44:5.
It says: “By your power
“we will drive back our adversaries;
“in your name
“we will trample down
those who rise up against us.”
Yes, all of us are going to find times
that Satan finds convenient to tempt us.
When that happens, may we be sensitive to recognize
that it is a temptation
and then look to Jehovah and focus on his name.
And if we do, we can have the confidence
that as this psalm says, this will help—
Jehovah’s name will help us to drive back and trample
those who rise against us individually
and as an organization.

cn.text: 你什么时候会被撒但引诱呢？
今天的经文提到
撒但引诱耶稣的其中一个伎俩
路加福音4:13后半部分说
撒但就离开耶稣等候别的机会引诱他
让我们从三个方面来谈谈这件事
第一
耶稣面对的三个引诱牵涉到什么？
第二
撒但后来真的找别的机会引诱耶稣吗？
第三
撒但今天也用类似的伎俩引诱我们吗？
为了回答这三个问题
让我们看看马太福音中
关于撒但三次引诱耶稣的记载
马太福音4:2,3
“他禁食了40日40夜
就觉得饿了
那引诱人的来对他说
如果你是上帝的儿子
就叫这些石头变成食物吧。”
首先，这个引诱的真正目的是什么？
其实撒但非常清楚
耶稣就是耶和华的头生子
但是他还是想方设法
想要耶稣质疑自己的这个身份
“如果你是上帝的儿子
你的父亲耶和华为什么不给你食物吃呢？
你可以相信他会好好照顾你吗？”
你看，撒但想要耶稣怀疑
耶和华是否关心他
想要耶稣滥用自己的身份
来满足自己的需求
但耶稣看穿了撒但的伎俩
第二个问题是
撒但后来有没有用同一个伎俩
来引诱耶稣呢？
撒但有没有在耶稣被捕的时候
再次引诱耶稣呢？
耶稣说，他可以求上帝
派12个军团以上的天使来救他
所以对耶稣来说，这可能又是一个引诱吗？
另外
耶稣被挂在苦刑柱上时
当时的统治者和士兵都嘲笑他说
“如果你是上帝的儿子
就从苦刑柱上下来吧！”
他们也用了跟撒但一样的说法
但耶稣不会上当
因为他相信耶和华一定会帮助他
第三个问题是
今天撒但也会用同样的伎俩吗？
我们正生活在艰难的时期
这会成为撒但引诱我们的好机会吗？
如果我们的家人和朋友遇到难题
我们是否真的相信
耶和华很关心他们并会好好照顾他们呢？
遇到难题的时候
我们会不会想要依靠自己的力量去解决呢？
会不会想利用自己在组织中的职务
来满足私欲呢？
现在
我们来看看第二个引诱
马太福音4:5,6说
“接着，魔鬼带他进了圣城
让他站在圣殿的外墙上
对他说
如果你是上帝的儿子，就跳下去吧
因为圣经上写着
他会为你命令天使
又说
他们会用手托着你
不让你的脚碰到石头。”
这个引诱的目的又是什么呢？
撒但想要再次引起耶稣对自己身份的怀疑
“如果你是上帝的儿子
就给我们证明
看看耶和华是否真的关心你
他要是真的看重你，就会救你
因为诗篇执笔者说
上帝会救自己真正的儿子”
耶稣看出这是来自撒但的引诱
所以没有落入陷阱
那么撒但
后来还用同样的方式引诱过耶稣呢？
也许有
有一次，法利赛派的人来了
这是马可福音8:11提到的
他们跟耶稣“争论起来
叫他显个从天上来的神迹，想要试探他。”
那时，耶稣刚刚治好一个有言语障碍的聋人
也施行奇迹喂饱了4000多人
可是这些证据对他们来说都不够
他们想看更壮观的奇迹
“从圣殿的墙上跳下去吧
证明你就是上帝的儿子
让我们都看看耶和华是不是真的看重你”
今天
我们也可能受到类似的引诱吗？
有些弟兄姐妹因为曾经的往事
觉得自己没有人爱
如果他们孤立自己或看法消极
撒但就会趁虚而入，引诱他们
“耶和华真的爱我吗？
耶和华会看重我吗？
我有价值吗？”
这样的怀疑会让人停止崇拜耶和华
或者通过耶和华不喜欢的方式
去让自己看起来有价值
来看第三个引诱
马太福音4:8,9说
“魔鬼又带耶稣上了一座极高的山
向他展示世上的万国和万国的荣耀
然后对他说
只要你跪下来崇拜我，就这一次
我就把这一切都给你。”
这一次的诡计是什么呢？
“不用等了，你现在就能拥有这一切
我给你的比耶和华给你的好得多
再等下去，只会带来痛苦”
但耶稣又识破了撒但的诡计
那撒但后来放弃引诱耶稣了吗？
我们来看看约翰福音6:15
经文告诉我们耶稣可能又遇到了引诱
那时，人们想要耶稣马上做王
不用痛苦地死去就能开始做王
这对耶稣会是一个引诱吗？
然而 ，耶稣知道人们要来
就退到山上去了
今天我们也面对类似的引诱吗？
为了崇拜耶和华
我们很愿意作出牺牲，或已经作出了牺牲
但我们看到其他人做的事
或他们拥有的东西，就可能会想
“我付出的牺牲值得吗？
有没有一个方法，让我能够赚到更多钱
同时又崇拜耶和华呢？”
你看，这三个引诱多么厉害
“你确信耶和华真的会照顾你吗？
耶和华真的爱你吗？
你真的有价值吗？
既然现在就能拥有想要的一切
何必等到新世界呢？”
所以，再想想
撒但何时会引诱你呢？
何时会引诱我呢？
撒但会找时机引诱我们
这一点，确凿无疑
彼得前书5:8说
撒但像咆哮的狮子，设法吞噬人
撒但曾经找到机会引诱耶稣
我们可以肯定他也同样会引诱我们
我们该怎么做呢？
要抵抗他的引诱
而我们抵抗引诱的方法
耶稣已经教给我们了
有两个方法
第一，耶稣能看穿撒但的伎俩
第二，受到引诱时，他专注于耶和华
在每一次回应撒但的引诱时
耶稣都用了耶和华的名字
所以，耶和华的名字大有力量
可以帮助我们抵抗撒但的攻击
这就是为什么耶稣教门徒祷告时
要他的门徒求耶和华帮助他们抵抗引诱
抵抗那恶者
耶稣认为这是最重要的事之一
也是为什么耶稣说
他已经让他的门徒认识了耶和华的名
耶和华的圣名是坚固的塔楼
我们投奔就会得到保护
因此，当魔鬼撒但
利用某些机会引诱我们或攻击我们时
我们要向耶和华祷告
使用他的名字
并沉思他名字的所有含义
这样做，会带来什么结果呢？
我们就会体验诗篇44:5的保证
“靠着你的力量
我们会把敌人击退
奉你的名
我们会把攻击我们的人踩在脚下。”
我们所有人都有可能受撒但引诱
当引诱来到时
愿我们都能保持警觉
看穿撒但的伎俩
寻求耶和华
并把目光集中于耶和华上帝的名字之上
如果这样做
我们就能对诗篇执笔者所说过的话有信心
就像经文说的那样
相信耶和华的名会帮助我们
把那些攻击我们、引诱我们的个人和组织
一一击退并踩在脚下

titles.ko: 로버트 루시오니: 유혹할 기회를 노리는 사탄 (누가 4:6)
titles.cn: 罗伯特·卢乔尼：引诱会在何时出现？(路4:6)

ko.text: 한 가지 중요한 교훈을 생각나게 합니다.
우선 이 점을 먼저 생각해 보시죠.
여러분의 삼촌이 그 날에 맞아 죽었다면
생명의 신성함과 피가 관련된 문제이기 때문이죠.
도피 도시 마련을 생각해 볼 때
하느님께서 그리스도를 통해 여러분을 기꺼이 용서하신 것처럼
네, 여호와께서 용서해 주시는 분이라는 사실에는 의문의 여지가 없습니다.
하느님께서 죄를 잊어 주시는 분임을 이렇게 알려 줍니다.
그들의 죄를 더 이상 기억하지 않을 것이다.”
하느님께서는 실제로 잘못을 용서하고 잊어 주십니까?
다윗에 관한 기록을 한번 생각해 보겠습니다.
‘다윗은 마음의 충절로 올바르게 걸어 내가 그에게 명령한 것을 다 행했다.’
네, 하느님께서는 다윗을 분명히 용서해 주셨습니다.
그 기록을 성경에 남겨 두신 것을 보면
하느님께서 다윗의 죄를 잊으신 것은 아닙니다.
그분 앞에서 치워 버리신다는 의미에서 잊어 주셨다고 할 수 있습니다.
그의 죄를 다시 끄집어내지 않는다는 의미에서 그 죄를 기억하지 않으십니다.
하느님께서는 다윗의 죄를 그분 앞에서 치워 버리신 거죠.
그러면 우리는 어떻게 다른 사람의 잘못을 용서하고 잊어 줄 수 있습니까?
우리의 기분을 상하게 하거나 우리에게 상처를 주는 말을 합니다.
칼로 찌르는 것과 같은 말을 하기도 하죠.
그럴 때 우리는 어떻게 해야 할까요?
앞으로 다시는 그 형제나 자매를 상대하지 않을 것입니까?
“하느님께서 그리스도를 통해 여러분을 기꺼이 용서하신 것처럼
그 사람이 우리에게 저지른 잘못을 우리 앞에서 치워 버려야 합니다.
그러면 실제로 어떻게 그렇게 할 수 있습니까?
우리 몸에 난 상처를 예로 들어 설명해 보도록 하겠습니다.
더 심각하고 더 깊은 상처도 있습니다.
우리가 긴급하게 맹장 수술을 받아야 한다고 생각해 볼까요?
맹장이 있던 자리를 이리저리 휘저어 보는
상처가 난 부위를 계속 찔러 보는 게 도움이 되겠습니까?
상처를 그대로 두고 잊어버리는 게 낫지 않을까요?
이전에 맹장 수술을 받으신 분이 있다면
어쩌면 여러 해 동안 생각하지 않고 지내셨을 겁니다.
배에 작은 수술 자국은 남아 있겠죠.
몸에 상처가 났을 때와 비슷하게 반응할 수 있지 않을까요?
“누군가 다른 사람에 대해 불평할 이유가 있더라도
계속 서로 참고 서로 기꺼이 용서하십시오.
여호와께서 기꺼이 용서하시는 분임을 생각해 보면
우리도 기꺼이 용서하려는 마음이 생기지 않습니까?
예수께서 모범 기도를 알려 주시면서 하신 말씀
하느님께서도 우리의 잘못을 용서해 주실 것’이라는 말씀을
우리가 사람들의 잘못을 용서하려 하지 않는다면
하느님께서 우리의 잘못을 용서해 주실 것으로 기대할 수 없습니다.
다른 사람의 잘못을 용서하고 잊어 주라는 교훈을
우리는 어떻게 개인적으로 적용할 수 있습니까?
그 일에 대해 다른 사람들에게 이야기하는 것이 아니라
그냥 지나쳐 준다는 의미에서 용서해야 합니다.
그리 대수롭지 않은 문제일 수 있습니다.
다른 사람이 우리의 마음에 입힌 상처도 그렇게 여길 수 있습니다.
하지만 더 깊고 더 심각한 상처를 입었을 때는 어떠합니까?
신뢰를 저버리는 행동을 하게 될 때
그 사람이 여전히 우리의 형제나 자매라는 사실을 기억하면서
그 일들을 우리 앞에서 치워 버릴 수 있습니까?
여호와께서 우리의 잘못을 용서해 주시는 것처럼
우리도 그들의 잘못을 용서해 주고 잊어 주도록 합시다.

en.text: The cities of refuge
—that was a merciful provision of God.
But we might link it to something
that could involve all of us,
and that is the common expression
“Forgive and forget.”
I’m sure you’ve heard it, and maybe you have tried to apply it.
But maybe at the outset, ask yourself,
‘Were the cities of refuge
a provision to forgive and forget?’
Well, if you were there and some men were chopping a tree
and the ax head flew off
and bonked your uncle, killing him,
do you think you’d be in position to say:
“Oh, well, it was an accident. You didn’t mean it.
You feel sorry, so why don’t we just forgive and forget?”
No, that wasn’t possible
because the sanctity of life and blood
were involved in that case.
But do they suggest (the cities of refuge)
that God, though merciful,
does not forgive or forget?
Well, if you open to the fourth chapter of Ephesians,
there is a verse there that makes it clear what the answer is.
That is, Ephesians 4:32:
“But become kind to one another,
“tenderly compassionate, freely forgiving one another
“just as God also by Christ
freely forgave you.”
So, certainly, we wouldn’t disagree
that God is able to forgive.
As to forgetting, in Jeremiah chapter 31,
the comment (with regard to the new covenant) said:
“I will forgive their error,
and I will no longer remember their sin.”
So does God forgive and forget?
Think of the account of David.
We know of his grievous sin.
Still, afterward,
God said to Solomon (with regard to David)
that ‘David walked, with integrity of heart with uprightness,
by doing according to all that I commanded.’
So, clearly, God had forgiven David.
But how about forgetting?
Did God forget David’s sins?
We know about them because they’re recorded in the Bible.
We don’t forget them, and certainly by God recording them in the Bible,
it shows that he doesn’t forget them in the strictest sense of the word.
But with regard to David’s serious sins,
God was able to forget in the sense of putting behind Him
David’s sins and not remembering them
in the sense of calling them back
to punish David time and time again.
He—that is, God— put David’s sins behind Him.
Well, what about us and the encouragement
to forgive and forget?
We know that there are times, as mentioned earlier today,
when individuals may rub us the wrong way
or say something hurtful about us;
maybe it’s like a stab of a sword.
They may do something thoughtless;
they may even betray a confidence
and hurt us in that way.
So, what’s our reaction going to be? get angry?
say something harsh in return?
maybe simply avoid the brother or sister thereafter?
Well, we mentioned Ephesians 4:32,
read it, and it said:
“Freely forgiving one another
“just as God
also by Christ freely forgave you.”
So, clearly, if we want to imitate God,
then that involves being willing to forgive,
and that means
putting the individual’s trespasses
behind us.
Realistically, though, how can we go about that?
We might think of some physical wounds to illustrate the point.
Some wounds are small and light
and others more serious or deeper,
and they don’t all require the same reaction.
But let’s just imagine that we had an envelope
and we used our finger to open the envelope,
and in the process we got a paper cut.
“Ow! Wow, that hurt!”
We wished we had used a letter opener.
We didn’t. We used our finger, and it really hurt.
But isn’t it true that if you’ve done that,
a day or two later
you can’t even remember where the wound is?
I mean, you cut yourself, but you’ve forgotten it.
Some wounds, of course, are more serious or deeper.
Let’s just say that you needed
an emergency appendectomy,
and it wasn’t going to be done laparoscopically
with three small holes
but rather with an open incision.
Now, after that, would it be rational
to stick your finger through the incision
and kind of poke around inside where the appendix had been?
Would poking around in the wound help things?
Or, rather, do we let it go —forget about it?
It might be hurtful to walk for a few days,
but in time, it’s behind you.
And, in fact, now, if you’ve had an appendectomy,
you probably don’t think about it,
and maybe it’s been years since you thought about it.
Oh, granted, there may be a small scar on your abdomen,
but it’s been put behind you.
Can that same concept be applied
to unkind things that have been said about us
by someone who hurt us, perhaps betrayed a trust?
Now what?
Colossians chapter 3,
we might read the whole verse,
verse 13:
“Continue putting up with one another
“and forgiving one another freely
“even if anyone has
“a cause for complaint against another.
“Just as Jehovah freely forgave you,
you must also do the same.”
Now, we want to imitate Jehovah, do we not?
And if God freely forgives,
is that not an incentive for us to try to do the same?
Now, granted, that doesn’t mean
that Jehovah has forgotten the trespass against us.
Can we? Maybe, maybe not.
We do recall what Jesus said in the model prayer, however,
when he said that ‘as we forgive the trespasses of others
so God will accordingly forgive our trespasses.’
Conversely, if we are disinclined
to forgive the trespasses of others,
what can we expect of God for us?
So, then, what is the essence,
applied personally,
of this encouragement to forgive and forget?
It means to forgive
in the sense of letting go,
not holding on to the anger,
not feeling constant resentment thereafter,
or not even gossiping
about what was done that hurt us.
Maybe it really is quite immaterial.
Maybe it’s simply like a paper cut:
In a couple of days, we don’t even remember where the wound is.
Can we do that with regard to the offense,
or the hurt, personally?
But even with something more serious
—an offense that seems deeper—
can we be like Jehovah
by forgetting in the sense of putting it behind us?
Just as Jehovah didn’t thereafter
punish David time and time again,
can we put the fellow servant’s error,
offense,
perhaps a lack of trust—
Can we put those things behind us
just realizing that he or she is still our brother?
And it’s an imperfect brother just as we’re imperfect,
but put it behind and forgive the trespass
just as Jehovah forgives our trespasses.

cn.text: 古代以色列人的庇护城
是上帝出于怜悯而设置的
但这个安排跟我们每一个人都息息相关
我们用两个词来概括，就是
宽恕和忘记
大家也许已经努力在生活中实践过
不过开始讨论之前
请问问自己
庇护城这个安排
是为了帮助我们宽恕和忘记吗？
假如你和叔叔跟别人在树林里砍树
其中一个人的斧头飞了出去
砸中了你的叔叔，把他砸死了
你会不会对他说
唉，算了，都是意外
你也不是故意的，我看你也挺难过的
我原谅你了，这件事就过去了
相信你肯定不会这样说
因为人命关天
生命和血都是神圣的
这是不是说，上帝设立庇护城的安排
虽然有怜悯之心
却没有宽恕人、遗忘他们的过错呢？
那如果你打开以弗所书的第4章
有一节经文清楚地给出这个问题的答案
那就是以弗所书4:32
“要以仁慈相待，也要怀着温情体恤别人
彼此甘心宽恕
就像上帝通过基督甘心宽恕了你们一样。”
所以，当然我们都同意
上帝是会宽恕人的
但关于忘记，在耶利米书31章
一节经文跟新约有关
上帝说:“我要宽恕他们的罪过
不再记住他们的罪。”
所以上帝会宽恕人，忘记过错吗？
请想想看大卫的记载
我们知道他犯了严重的罪
不过在那之后
上帝跟所罗门提到大卫时说
大卫“怀着纯洁正直的心敬奉”他
照他吩咐的一切去做
所以很明显的
上帝宽恕了大卫
但忘记呢？
上帝忘了大卫犯的错吗？
我们知道这些事
因为它们都被记在圣经里
我们没有忘记，上帝肯定也没有忘记
因为他把这些事都记了下来
不过，大卫确实犯了严重的罪
上帝把大卫的罪抛在脑后
意思是，上帝宽恕他
上帝不再回想大卫犯下的严重的罪
因他的罪一次又一次地惩罚他
这就是上帝把大卫的罪抛诸脑后的意思
那我们呢？
什么激励我们要宽恕和忘记呢？
我们知道有时候就像演讲开始提到的那样
别人得罪了我们
或说了伤害我们的话
这种感觉好像被刺了一刀
他们可能做了些鲁莽的事
甚至辜负了我们的信任
结果让我们很受伤
所以，我们该有什么反应呢？
生气吗？
用尖酸刻薄的话回击？
还是从此以后就避开这个弟兄或者姐妹？
我们刚刚读了以弗所书4:32
经文说:“彼此甘心宽恕
就像上帝通过基督甘心宽恕了你们一样。”
由此可见，如果我们想要效法上帝
我们就要乐意宽恕别人
也就是说，要把别人的过错抛在脑后
不要一直去想
不过，我们实际要怎样才能做到呢？
我们可以拿身体的一些伤口来说明这一点
有些是轻微的伤口，比较小
有些是严重的，比较深
我们不需要用同样的方式来处理
我们来想象一下，我们有一个信封
我们用手指头打开信封的时候
不小心被纸割伤了
哎呀，好痛！
早知道就用小刀来开了
但我们却用手指来开，结果受伤了
不过，就算你被纸割伤了
是不是一两天之后
你就忘记伤口在哪里了呢？
意思是，你被割伤了
但你也忘记了
不过有些伤口却比较深
或比较严重
假如你突然需要接受紧急的阑尾切除手术
不是用腹腔镜开三个小洞
而是需要在肚子上开一个切口
不过，手术后
难道你会把手指探进切开的伤口
然后不停地戳阑尾切除的部位吗？
你觉得这样一直戳伤口
会有帮助吗？
还是你会先不想这个伤口，让它慢慢好呢？
头几天你走路时可能会有点疼
但好了，你就忘了
其实，如果你以前动过阑尾切除手术
你可能不会再想这件事
很多年你都不会再想
当然，你的肚子上
可能留下了一道小小的伤疤
但是你已经不会再去想它了
如果有人对我们不好
做了伤害我们的事
或者辜负了我们对他的信任
我们可以把这个原则运用出来吗？
是的，让我们来看看歌罗西书3:13
经文说:“无论谁有理由对人不满
都要继续彼此包容
彼此甘心宽恕
耶和华怎样甘心宽恕了你们
你们也要怎样甘心宽恕人。”
的确，我们都很想效法耶和华上帝
既然他甘心宽恕了我们
我们不是也受到激励
去甘心宽恕别人吗？
当然这不是说
耶和华真的会忘记得罪我们的人的过错
那我们能忘记吗？
也许能，也许不能
相信我们都记得耶稣在模范祷告中所说的话
他劝勉门徒
“要是你们宽恕别人的过错
你们天上的父亲也会宽恕你们。”
但是，如果我们不愿意宽恕别人的过错
我们天上的父亲还会宽恕我们的过错吗？
所以，对我们来说
我们自己
可以怎样实践宽恕并忘记这个原则呢？
就是要原谅对方，让事情过去
不再追想
不再一直生气、怀恨在心
也不再对别人的过错耿耿于怀
甚至不会说别人的闲话
到处谈论他们是怎样伤害我们的
也许别人对我们造成的伤害
就像被纸刮伤一样
其实很小，过了几天之后
我们甚至记不得伤口在哪里了
当别人冒犯或伤害我们的时候
我们也可以宽恕并忘记吗？
不过，即便有些弟兄姐妹
给我们造成了更严重的伤害
我们能不能效法耶和华
忘记他们的过错
把这些事抛在脑后呢？
就好像耶和华没有因为大卫的罪过
一次又一次地惩罚他
如果有弟兄姐妹冒犯了我们
得罪了我们
伤害了我们
或辜负了我们的信任
我们能不能也把这些事抛在脑后
仍然把他看作亲爱的弟兄姐妹呢？
弟兄姐妹是不完美的
就像我们也是不完美的一样
但是我们要宽恕并忘记他们的过错
就像耶和华宽恕了我们的过错一样

en.text: That’s a heavy one, Son.
Let me help you.
I can do it, Papa.
You’re going to hurt yourself, Son.
Now, I need someone to prepare the talking machine.
I can do it.
Off you go, then.
I was born on December 4, 1916,
at a place called Sharon, Pennsylvania.
I’m 102 years old.
My father took the “Photo-Drama of Creation” around.
I’m very appreciative of my parents, what they did.
In 1931, I attended the convention in Columbus, Ohio,
and I already knew my grand Helen.
And when Brother Rutherford announced
the new name of Jehovah’s Witnesses, she got real enthused about it.
So the first thing I did when I got into my pioneer work was write to Helen.
Such a letter she wrote!
She said, “You didn’t tell me the answer to the question I wanted to know.”
It was whether I was a pioneer or not.
I wrote, “I am a pioneer, and I hope I always will be.”
And then we got a letter from Brooklyn,
asking us if we were willing to go in the traveling work.
And we accepted, and so we went to west Kentucky.
Aubrey and Bertha Bivens were both from Kentucky too.
Do you know how it is when a couple of brothers
are good friends and their wives are good friends?
When we went to Gilead, we were already good friends.
But then a surprise came: We were assigned to Guatemala.
And would you believe it?
We were assigned with the Bivens in the missionary home!
So when they were assigned to Puerto Barrios, it was a sad thing.
It was a real heartbreaker to separate from the Bivens.
Then we were assigned back to Guatemala City
to the branch office.
We had an active life.
We had many years of blessings.
We were very good as husband and wife.
And when my wife was sick, it was very sad.
If I’ve come to the end of my life,
I beg Jehovah to take care of my David.
Thank you for him, Jehovah,
and for our marriage.
So wonderful and so happy!
The day Sister Helen passed away, I went to his room.
And I was thinking: ‘I want to tell David that he is not alone
‘—that I can accompany him if he wants me to.
And I’ll be his traveling companion whenever he needs me.’
I think he knew he’d had an incredibly good life with Sister Helen
—a wonderful life— but also that he had to keep on going.
He never isolated himself.
After Sister Helen died, Brother David kept on serving
on the Guatemala Branch Committee for another 18 years.
Then Brother David moved to the Assembly Hall in San Lucas.
I think living in the Assembly Hall has done Brother David a lot of good.
Every weekend he has the opportunity to associate with the brothers and sisters.
We have assemblies.
And they’re not my assemblies, but I know many of the people.
So I go down and say hello to them.
It’s like the Bible says about the Christians
—that is what made the difference— that they loved each other.
Well, it’s wonderful.
I have lots of friends too.
My precious one,
I ask you to put this text on your desk.
It applies to you and your long years of service to Jehovah.
Hebrews 6:10 says:
‘God is not unrighteous so as to forget your work
and the love you’ve shown for his name.’

亲爱的戴维

因为你多年来一直忠心地为耶和华服务

ko.text: 여러 가지 제물에 관한 법을 알려 줍니다.

en.text: An introduction to the book of Leviticus.
Leviticus was written by Moses
in the wilderness of Sinai.
The name Leviticus, later given to the book,
comes from a Greek word meaning
“pertaining to the Levites.”
Yet, the book was written, not for the Levites alone,
but for the entire nation of Israel.
Leviticus covers a period of about one month,
describing the events immediately following
the construction of the tabernacle.
Leviticus focuses on Jehovah’s holiness
and the holiness of his people by their obedience to his statutes.
Chapters 1 to 7
set out the various laws about offerings to Jehovah.
Chapters 8 and 9 cover the installation of the priesthood,
the anointing of Aaron as high priest,
and Aaron’s first offerings to God.
In chapter 10,
Jehovah puts to death two of Aaron’s sons
—the priests Nadab and Abihu—
for offering “unauthorized fire,” or incense.
Jehovah then issues the command
that priests must not drink alcohol
before entering the tent of meeting, or tabernacle.
Chapters 11 to 15
set out laws about cleanness and uncleanness.
In regard to food, Jehovah tells the Israelites
which creatures they may and may not eat.
Instructions regarding the Day of Atonement
are given in chapter 16.
Chapters 17 to 20 contain laws on holy conduct.
For example, God’s people must not eat blood
or engage in any form of idolatry or spiritism
as the nations around them were doing.
They should show consideration for the blind,
the deaf, and the foreign resident.
And they should treat the elderly with respect.
Did you know?
The arrangements mentioned in the book of Leviticus
were “a shadow of the good things to come,”
as explained in the book of Hebrews.
For example, the high priest typifies Jesus Christ;
the blood of the animal sacrifices
foreshadows the blood of Jesus;
the Most Holy of the tabernacle represents “heaven itself,”
where Jesus appeared “before God on our behalf.”
Chapters 21 and 22 set out rules for the priesthood.
For example, those serving as priests
must be sound in body, having no physical defects.
Chapters 23 and 24
have instructions about festivals and holy days.
Jehovah also provides directions
regarding the lamps in the tabernacle
and the ring-shaped loaves of showbread.
Chapter 24 also highlights the sacredness of God’s name.
At Jehovah’s command,
a man who cursed that name is stoned to death.
Chapter 25 contains laws about the Sabbath year,
the Jubilee year,
the restoration of property,
and the treatment of the poor.
Those who are sold into slavery must be treated kindly, as hired workers.
Chapter 26 spells out the blessings of obedience to Jehovah
and the punishments for disobedience.
Chapter 27 closes the book of Leviticus
with laws about things vowed to Jehovah
and things devoted to him.
As you read the book of Leviticus,
note how we should strive to be holy in imitation of Jehovah;
why we should deeply respect his holy name;
and why we can have confidence
that the entire earth will reflect God’s holiness
under the rule of his Son,
the great High Priest and King of God’s Kingdom.

cn.text: 利未记是由摩西于公元前1512年
在西奈旷野写成的
这卷书后来被称为利未记
这个名称来源于一个希腊语词
意思是“跟利未族有关的”
但这本书不单是写给利未族人的
也是写给整个以色列国族的
利未记的记载涵盖的时间不超过一个月
描述的是会幕设立后不久发生的事
利未记强调耶和华是圣洁的
只要人民服从他所定的法律就会是圣洁的
1到7章谈到了献祭给耶和华的各种指引
8到9章谈到了祭司的就职礼
亚伦被立为大祭司

第10章记录了亚伦的两个儿子
拿答和亚比户
因为违法献上香火被上帝处死
耶和华接着颁布法令
祭司在进入会幕的时候
任何酒都不可喝
第11到15章
耶和华就洁净和不洁净定下相关条例
比如在饮食方面哪些动物可以吃
哪些动物不可以吃
第16章谈到跟赎罪日有关的律例
17到20章谈到了跟圣洁品行有关的律例
举例来说
上帝的子民不可像周围的民族那样吃血
向偶像下拜或通灵
他们应该关心盲人和聋人
善待外族居民并尊重老人
你知道吗？
利未记中提到的各项安排
就是希伯来书谈到的将来美好事物的影子
举例来说
大祭司预表耶稣基督
动物祭牲的血预表耶稣基督流出的宝血
会幕的至圣所代表天上
耶稣基督在天上为我们出现在上帝面前
第21和22章
列出了做祭司必须符合什么条件
比如，做祭司的必须身体健全
没有缺陷
第23和24章谈到
耶和华就节期和圣日给出相关律例
也谈到如何照料会幕的油灯
以及桌上的圈饼
第24章
也强调了上帝的名字是神圣的
有一次一个人咒骂上帝的名字
后来上帝命令人用石头将他打死
第25章谈到了
耶和华颁布有关安息年、禧年、归还产业
以及如何对待穷人的各项规定
做主人的要像对待雇用的工人一样
善待那些卖身为奴的人
第26章说明了
服从耶和华会得到哪些福分
不服从会受到哪些惩罚
第27章谈到当人许下誓愿要献上东西
以及无条件献给耶和华东西时
需要遵守哪些诫命
当你阅读利未记时，请留意
我们要努力效法耶和华保持圣洁
要深深尊重他的圣名
我们也要确信
在上帝的爱子耶稣基督
我们伟大的大祭司
兼上帝王国的君王统治时
地上的一切都会是圣洁的

en.text: Do you smoke?
Are you tempted to?
maybe to fit in?
deal with stress?
Or maybe you’re just curious.
Whatever the reason, you should know
what smoking can do to you.
At Romans 12:1,
the Bible tells you to use “your power of reason.”
So instead of just following the crowd,
be smart enough and think for yourself.
Tobacco companies spend billions of dollars
trying to convince people to smoke.
And many people fall for it
without thinking of the consequences.
For example, smoking can ruin your health
and even the way you look.
The Bible says to “cleanse ourselves
of every defilement of flesh and spirit.”
But smoking does the opposite!
Smokers are more likely to die from cancer,
heart attacks, and other diseases.
And you know, it doesn’t just affect you.
Secondhand smoke hurts those around you.
But what about vaping?
Is it safer?
Not on your life!
After being promoted as a safe alternative to smoking,
vaping was implicated in dozens of deaths
and thousands of users got very sick.
And, just like smoking,
you could get addicted.
Who really benefits if you take up vaping?
So, what will you do if someone invites you to smoke?
Try simply saying: “No, thanks. I don’t smoke.”
If that doesn’t work, try something like,
“I checked out the risks, and it’s not for me.”
But what if you’re already addicted?
It might feel like there’s no way out.
But you can break the habit.
First, if you vape or smoke, ask for help,
if possible, from someone who has successfully quit smoking.
Second, avoid people and places that feed the urge.
And one more thing—pray.
If you pray intensely
for help before you give in,
you can quit with God’s help.
A Bible writer said at Psalm 18:29:
“By God’s power I can scale a wall.”
Yes, even if you struggle with addiction,
you can win the fight.
Resist the temptation to use tobacco in any form.
You’ll be healthier,
happier, and breathe easier,
knowing your life isn’t going up in smoke.
