title: 새뮤얼 F. 허드: 염려가 많은 때에 평온을 유지하기 위해 노력하십시오

ko.text: 우리는 스트레스가 아주 심한 때에 살고 있습니다.
베드로 전서 5:8에서는 사탄 마귀가 몹시 화가 나서
성경을 보면, 과거에 여호와를 두려워했던 그분의 숭배자들도
예를 들어, 시편 13:2에서 다윗왕은 이렇게 말했죠.
날마다 마음속에 슬픔을 안고 있어야 합니까?”
“아버지, 아버지께서 원하신다면 이 잔을 제게서 거두어 주십시오.
그렇지만 제 뜻이 아니라 아버지의 뜻이 이루어지게 하십시오.”
그 뒤에 무슨 일이 있었는지 43절을 보시죠.
“그때에 한 천사가 하늘에서 그분에게 나타나 힘을 북돋아 주었다.”
예수를 격려하기 위해 천사가 온 것입니다.
그로 인해 예수와 염려와 걱정이 즉시 사라졌습니까?
“그분이 몹시 괴로워서 더욱 간절히 계속 기도하시니,
여러분 중에 염려가 너무나 심해서 땀이 핏방울처럼 되신 분이 있나요?
사실, 여러분 중에 인류 전체의 구원을 어깨에 짊어진 분은 없죠!
크고 작은 염려를 겪고 있는 것도 사실입니다.
의식주에 들어가는 높은 비용 때문에 염려할지 모릅니다.
평소보다 더 많은 수의 형제 자매들이 염려와 걱정 속에 있습니다.
또 어떤 분들은 범죄와 폭력이 일상사가 된 지역에 살고 계실지 모릅니다.
부정직하거나 부도덕한 일을 하라는 유혹을 받는 분도 있습니다.
이 모든 것이 염려의 근원이 됩니다.
일부 형제 자매들은 아주 가혹한 대우를 받기도 하는데,
또는 증오와 편견을 조장하는 거짓 종교로부터 그런 대우를 받습니다.
“염려가 많은 때에 평온을 유지하기 위해 노력하십시오”입니다.
오늘날에도 우리가 염려와 압박감을 느낄 때
7절에서는 우리가 염려를 느낄 때 어떻게 해야 하는지 알려 줍니다.
“그러므로 하느님의 강력한 손 아래 자기를 낮추십시오.
때가 되면 그분이 여러분을 높이실 것입니다.
그분이 여러분에게 관심을 갖고 계시기 때문입니다.”
즉시 그렇게 되지는 않을 수 있습니다.
염려가 되는 상황이 생기면, 어떻게 할 수 있다고 했습니까?
7절에서는 그럴 때 염려를 어떻게 하라고 말했나요?
염려를 자기 속에 간직해서는 안 됩니다.
‘내 염려는 너무나 무거워서 들 수조차 없는데,
그분을 의지하면 그분이 너를 위해 행동하실 것이다.”
각주에 따르면 너의 길을 여호와께 “굴려 보내라”고도 번역할 수 있습니다.
따라서 염려가 너무 무거워서 내다 맡기기가 힘들다면,
여호와께 내맡기거나 굴려 보낼 수 있습니까?
기도와 간구로 여러분의 청원을 하느님께 알리십시오.
그러면 모든 이해를 뛰어넘는 하느님의 평화가
여러분의 마음과 정신력을 지켜 줄 것입니다.”
염려를 여호와께 굴려 보낼 수 있는 방법은 바로
부끄럽고 창피한 일도 얘기할 수 있습니다.
여호와께서는 여러분이 한 이야기를 아무에게도 말하지 않으실 것입니다.
7절에선 그렇게 기도하면 어떤 결과가 있다고 했습니까?
우리는 우리를 붙들어 주시는 여호와의 능력을 온전히 신뢰할 수 있습니다.
또 무엇이 우리를 평온하게 해 줄 수 있을까요?
회중에 신뢰할 만한 벗들에게 염려를 털어 놓으십시오.
편안하게 느끼는 장로 형제에게 말해 보십시오.
우리가 함께 모일 때에 격려를 받는다고 알려 줍니다.
또는 지금처럼 불확실한 시기에는 함께 모이는 대신에
사랑하는 형제 자매들이 보내 준 편지나
평온함을 유지하는 데 또 한 가지 도움이 되는 것은
자신에게 적용되는 하느님의 말씀의 일부분을 읽고 묵상하는 것입니다.
이 내용은 하느님과 손잡고 걷는 것을 묘사합니까?
역경과 염려에서 구해 주시는 걸 묘사하는 것입니까?
내가 너를 강하게 하고 너를 도와주겠다.
내가 참으로 내 의로운 오른손으로 너를 붙들어 주겠다.”
여호와께서는 여러분에게 두려워하거나 걱정하지 말라고 하셨습니다.
그분이 자신의 오른손으로 붙들어 주실 것이기 때문이죠.
우리가 살아 가면서 겪게 될지 모르는 어려운 상황들에 관해 말합니다.
“나 여호와 너의 하느님이 네 오른손을 붙잡고 있다.
이 기록은 단지 하느님과 손을 잡고
함께 걸어가는 모습을 묘사한 내용이 아닙니다.
이 내용은 하느님이 여러분을 구출하시는 장면입니다!
여러분의 왼손이 그분의 오른손을 잡고 있어야죠.
여호와께서 여러분의 오른손을 자신의 오른손으로 잡고 계십니다.
여호와께서 여러분을 마주 보고 계신 것이죠.
자신의 오른손을 뻗어 여러분의 오른손을 잡고
이렇게 특정한 성구들은 우리를 평온하게 해 주고 안심시켜 줍니다.
지금까지 살펴본 세 가지는 첫째, 기도,
유죄 판결을 받고 징역형을 선고받은 러시아의 네 형제도
러시아 연방 보안국 직원이 우리한테 와서 조사를 해야겠다고 말했습니다.
문 두드리는 소리가 났는데, 그들이 저를 찾으러 왔다는 걸 알아차렸죠.
우리를 체포했습니다. 수갑을 채우고 몸을 수색했어요.
안이 하나도 안 보이는 차가 제 차를 가로막더니,
그러더니 팔을 뒤로 꺾고 저를 차 위에 대고 짓눌렀어요.
다음 날, 저에 관한 법원 명령이 떨어졌고
저는 하바롭스크의 미결 구금 시설로 이송되었습니다.
저는 교도소의 어두운 감방 안에 수감되었습니다.
거기서 저는 무릎을 꿇고 여호와께 기도했습니다.
시련에도 굳건함을 유지하고 그분께 충실함을 지키고 싶다고요.
구치소에 수감되어 있을 때 매일 저녁 저는 기도했습니다.
그리고 제가 아는 모든 사람의 상황을 생각하면서 구체적으로 기도했습니다.
상황이 점점 안 좋아지고 있었기 때문에,
저는 여호와께 눈물을 흘리며 기도하기 시작했습니다.
여호와께서 이미 그날 아침부터 돕고 계셨던 것 같았습니다.
저는 담대함과 용기를 주시고 차분함을 잃지 않게 해 달라고 기도했어요.
앞으로 있을 일을 두려워하지 않고, 차분하게 대화할 수 있었습니다.
여호와께서 제 곁에서 절 돕고 계시고,
모든 상황을 통제하고 계신다는 걸 알 수 있게 해 달라고 기도했습니다.
그날 아침 제가 제일 처음 본 편지는 태양에 관한 것이었어요.
저는 예전에 태양에 관한 기사들을 읽어 보면서
그분의 엄청난 힘과 능력에 대해 생각했던 적이 많았습니다.
그런데 그날은 특히 더 마음에 와닿았죠.
하느님의 특성과 제가 처한 상황에서 나타내야 할 특성에 관한 것이 많았습니다.
그 편지들은 제게 격려가 되었을 뿐 아니라
교도관들은 이런 곳에도 아는 사람이 있냐고 하면서 놀랐어요.
또 프랑스나 미국 같은 외국에서 편지가 오니까 더 놀랐습니다.
이 편지들은 수많은 사람이 저에 대해 그리고 제가 처한 상황에 대해
잘 알고 있다는 걸 교도관들에게 보여 주었습니다.
교도관들은 자신들의 행동을 많은 사람들이 지켜보고 있다는 걸 알게 된 거죠.
연설과 집회 프로를 위한 아이디어를 얻을 수 있었습니다.
또 다른 편지에서는 공개 강연을 위한 재료를 얻을 수 있었습니다.
여러 편지에서 내용을 수집해서 하나의 자료집을 만들었어요.
그런 다음 그 안의 내용을 골라 비교하면서
아주 수준 높은 개인 연구를 할 수 있었습니다.
그 덕분에 조직과 계속 보조를 맞출 수 있었죠.
한 남자아이가 보내 준 그림에 이렇게 쓰여 있었어요.
“형제가 충실을 지키면 낙원에 갈 수 있어요.”
한 연로한 자매가 저를 아들같이 생각하고 따뜻한 편지를 써 주셨어요.
그 편지는 제가 가장 힘들 때 정말 큰 위로가 됐어요.
특별한 방법으로 위로해 주신다는 걸 느꼈습니다.
감방 안에 있는 모두가 자고 있는 조용한 시간이었기 때문에
저는 특정한 성구를 생각하고 또 생각했는데,
하루가 끝날 쯤에는 그 말씀이 마음 깊숙이 새겨졌어요.
얼마나 마음에 이르게 하는가가 중요하다는 것을 깨닫게 되었습니다.
구치소 감방 안에서 성경을 읽으면서 그 말씀이 새롭게 다가왔어요.
사도 행전을 읽을 때는 바울이 겪은 일들이 참 공감이 되었습니다.
그 기록은 저에게 큰 힘을 주었고
바울처럼 저도 이 시기를 인내할 수 있다는 걸 일깨워 줬습니다.
성경에 나오는 모르드개의 본이 특히 격려가 됐습니다.
왕을 만나 이스라엘 백성을 멸망시킬 법을 만들게 한 하만은
그때 모르드개는 ‘일어나지도 않고 떨지도 않았다’고 알려 줍니다.
모르드개가 그랬던 것처럼 지금 우리도 결코 떨지 않습니다.
형제들의 격려를 받고, 하느님의 말씀을 묵상한 결과,
평온을 유지하고 여호와를 신뢰할 수 있었습니다.
염려가 많은 이때에 기억해야 할 큰 힘이 되는 성구입니다!
이스라엘 백성은 여호와께서 주신 이 중요한 교훈을 들으려 하지 않았습니다.
“주권자인 주 여호와, 이스라엘의 거룩한 분이 이렇게 말씀하신다.
‘나에게 돌아오고 쉼을 얻어야 너희가 구원을 받을 것이다.
너희의 힘은 평온을 유지하고 신뢰하는 데 있을 것이다.’
그러나 너희는 그렇게 하려 하지 않고.”
그렇게 할 것입니까, 하지 않을 것입니까?
염려가 많은 이때에 그리고 앞으로 더 많은 고난이 있을 때,
우리는 여호와의 이 권고를 따를 것입니까?
어떻게 할 때 힘을 얻을 수 있다고 했는지 유의하셨습니까?
‘너희의 힘은 평온을 유지하고 나를 신뢰하는 데 있다.’
앞으로 더 어려운 때가 닥칠 겁니다!
우리가 기도하고, 서로 격려하고, 지혜가 담긴 하느님의 말씀에 의지할 때,
이 마지막 때에도 무엇을 경험할 수 있습니까?
우리의 위대한 하느님 여호와를 온전히 신뢰하게 될 것입니다!

en.text: We live in very stressful times.
First Peter 5:8 indicates that Satan the Devil
is bitterly angry
and “walks about like a roaring lion.”
Throughout the Bible,
we learn that God-fearing worshippers of Jehovah in the past
faced circumstances that produced anxiety.
For example, at Psalm 13:2, King David asked:
“How long will I have anxious concern,
with grief in my heart each day?”
Please find with me Luke 22:42-44.
Even Jesus, a perfect man, experienced the agony
of intense anxiety on the night of his betrayal.
Here is what he prayed at Luke 22:42:
“Father, if you want to,
“remove this cup from me.
“Nevertheless, let, not my will,
but yours take place.”
He knew what he was in for.
Well, what happened?
Verse 43:
“Then an angel from heaven
appeared to him and strengthened him.”
An angel was dispatched to encourage Jesus.
Did that instantly erase his anxious concerns?
No.
Let’s read verse 44:
“But he was in such agony
“that he kept praying more earnestly;
“and his sweat became as drops of blood
falling to the ground.”
Have you ever been that anxious about anything,
your sweat becoming drops of blood?
Probably not.
But you did not have the salvation
of the world of mankind on your shoulders!
The point is that all of Jehovah’s servants in these last days
will have bouts of anxiety.
For many around the world, it might be the high cost of food,
clothing, and shelter.
In the wake of the pandemic,
this anxiety is likely being experienced by more
of our brothers than would normally be the case.
Some of you live in neighborhoods with a high crime rate
and violence all around.
Others face temptation from workmates or schoolmates
to be dishonest or immoral.
Then there are family issues, health issues,
emotional issues, the death of loved ones.
All of these can be causes of anxiety.
Still others of our brothers and sisters
face mistreatment and abuse from family members,
governmental oppression,
and from false religious elements that foment hate and prejudice.
The title of this talk is
“Strive for Calm When Facing Anxious Times.”
Is “calm” even possible?
Jehovah came to the assistance of his servants in the past.
Today, he makes it possible for us to gain a measure of calm
when facing distress or anxiety.
Locate 1 Peter 5:6, 7, please.
Verse 7 describes an action we can take with our anxiety.
Let’s read verses 6 and 7:
“Humble yourselves, therefore,
“under the mighty hand of God,
“so that he may exalt you in due time,
“while you throw all your anxiety on him,
because he cares for you.”
Did you notice the time element in verse 6?
It said that Jehovah will “exalt you in due time.”
So not necessarily immediately.
If you are facing anxious moments,
what do you do in the meantime?
It is the action that’s described in verse 7:
“Throw all your anxiety on [Jehovah].”
If we throw something,
what are we left holding in our hand?
Nothing.
We don’t keep the anxiety bottled up inside ourselves.
We throw all of it on our God.
You might be thinking,
‘My anxiety is so heavy and burdensome that I can’t even pick it up,
let alone throw it anywhere!’
Let’s look at a related scripture
in the book of Psalms—Psalm 37:5.
Instead of “throw,” it uses the word “commit.”
Verse 5:
“Commit your way to Jehovah;
rely on him, and he will act in your behalf.”
It said: “Commit your way.”
The footnote says this could be translated:
“Roll your way upon” Jehovah.
So if your anxiety seems too heavy
to throw on Jehovah, give it a push.
Try rolling it on him.
How do we “throw,” “commit,”
or “roll” our anxious thoughts on Jehovah?
Let’s open our Bibles to Philippians 4:6, 7:
“Do not be anxious over anything,
“but in everything by prayer and supplication
“along with thanksgiving,
“let your petitions be made known to God;
“and the peace of God
“that surpasses all understanding
“will guard your hearts
“and your mental powers
by means of Christ Jesus.”
We throw
or roll our anxiety on Jehovah
by means of fervent prayer.
Pour your heart out to God.
You can tell Jehovah anything,
even if it is embarrassing to you.
Remember,
Jehovah is not going to tell anyone about it.
Throw or roll it on him.
And what did verse 7 say would be the result of such prayers?
It said that “the peace of God,”
yes, a calm tranquility comes over us
when we fully trust Jehovah’s power to sustain us.
How else can our heart calm down?
Share your anxiety with trusted friends in the congregation,
including an elder you feel comfortable with.
Hebrews 10:25 says
that when we meet together, we receive encouragement.
Or, in these uncertain times,
instead of meeting together, it might be that letters,
e-mails, or texts
from your concerned brothers and sisters
will have a similar effect.
What else can have a calming effect on us?
Reading applicable portions of God’s Word
and meditating on them.
For example, in Isaiah chapter 41,
is this describing walking hand in hand with God?
Or is this describing Jehovah reaching into your life
and saving you from calamity and anxiety?
Let’s compare two verses in Isaiah 41.
Notice his promise in verse 10:
“Do not be afraid, for I am with you.
“Do not be anxious, for I am your God.
“I will fortify you, yes, I will help you,
“I will really hold on to you
with my right hand of righteousness.”
Did you notice that Jehovah tells you
not to be afraid or anxious?
Why?
Because he will hold on to you with his right hand.
In verses 11 and 12,
it describes some tragic circumstances we might face in life.
Now, in verse 13:
“For I, Jehovah your God,
“am grasping your right hand,
“the One saying to you, ‘Do not be afraid.
I will help you.’”
Do you see the point?
This is not describing a stroll with God.
This is not describing walking hand in hand with God.
This is a rescue mission by God!
If it was a casual stroll with God,
your left hand would be in his right hand.
But the two verses say
that Jehovah grasps your right hand
with his right hand.
It is as if Jehovah is facing you.
He sees your dire plight.
He reaches out with his right hand and grasps your right hand
and pulls you up and out to safety.
Specific Bible verses calm us down and reassure us.
The three aspects we’ve considered:
(1) prayer,
(2) encouragement from our brothers,
and (3) meditating on the Scriptures
were mentioned by four brothers in Russia
who have been convicted to prison sentences.
Please watch the following video.
I was detained at the airport at four in the morning.
Right at the check-in desk, an FSB officer came up to us
and said that investigative measures were being taken against us.
There was a knock at the door,
and I understood that they had come for me.
It all happened very quickly.
First, they detained us,
then they handcuffed us, then they searched us.
A jeep with tinted windows blocked the road.
Then with shouts of “Stay where you are!”
they twisted my arms and threw me onto the hood of my automobile.
The next day, a court imposed preventive measures on me, and I was taken
to the pretrial detention facility in Khabarovsk.
I was taken to a dark room in the prison and shut in.
Then I got on my knees
and prayed to Jehovah
telling him that I wanted to stand firm
in the face of the trials and remain faithful to him.
When I was in the detention cell, every evening
I prayed for my friends, my wife,
my children —everyone I know—
and tried to think about their circumstances and pray specifically.
Once, I started praying to Jehovah for help with tears
because things were getting very difficult for me.
But then things started changing,
which (as I understood)
Jehovah had already arranged at the start of that day.
I prayed for boldness and to be courageous, calm, and kind.
And Jehovah gave me the strength for that.
I felt calm when I talked with them,
and I didn’t feel afraid of consequences or anything.
I prayed to Jehovah and asked him to show me
that he was close by, that he was doing something,
and that the whole situation was under his control.
And the first letter I received that morning was about the sun.
Interestingly, I had read a lot of articles about the sun and understood
that Jehovah’s immense strength and power are manifested in it.
But that day I especially felt it.
The first letters that I received were about God’s qualities
and about the qualities that I needed to display in that specific situation.
They weren’t just encouraging to me.
They were also a fine witness to the administration.
The guards were amazed.
They asked: “Vanya, who is writing to you from Krasnodar?
I’ve got friends there.”
And then about other places— They wrote to me from France, from America.
The letters enabled them to see that the situation is under control.
A huge number of people
know about me, about my circumstances.
Their actions are being carefully observed by many people.
Talks, topics for talks,
items for meetings—these are things I took
from the letters that I received each day.
From one letter, I would take, for example,
material for a ten-minute talk, and from another,
I could make a public talk.
Because I was able to collect quotes from various letters,
I eventually had an entire library.
I was able to compare and collect information
and then conduct high-quality, excellent personal study
that helped me keep in step with the organization at that time.
A boy drew a picture and sent it to me.
He wrote,
“If you remain faithful,
you will be in the new world.”
An elderly sister
began her letter
with these warm words: “Greetings, my son!”
She shared her feelings with me.
Her letter came
at one of the most difficult times for me.
I felt that Jehovah
comforts us in a special way through letters.
I made the following schedule:
I got up early in the morning at 5:30 a.m.
While everyone else in the cell was snoozing
and all was quiet,
I was able to read the Bible.
I would think a great deal about a particular verse.
The more I reflected on it, the more I saw how beautiful it was.
By the end of the day, the verse became
stunningly beautiful and unique to me.
Then I understood that a good heart is formed
not by the amount that you take in
but by the amount you can retain in your heart.
When you read the Bible in a pretrial detention cell,
it takes on new meaning.
When I read the book of Acts, the things that happened
to Paul became especially understandable.
It strengthened me
and showed me that I could get through these times just as he did.
Mordecai’s experience from the Bible went to my heart.
After Haman had made an agreement with the king
to destroy the Israelites, he went out and met Mordecai.
And it says that Mordecai
‘did not rise and did not tremble.’
The main point is that now
just as then as with Mordecai, we don’t tremble.
When applying the three elements
of prayer, encouragement from our brothers,
and meditating on God’s Word,
what did that produce?
It helped the brothers to be calm and trust in Jehovah.
Let’s look at the final scripture for this talk.
Please find Isaiah 30:15.
What a beautiful verse for us to keep in mind
when facing these anxious times!
Unfortunately, the Israelites were not willing
to listen to this profound directive from Jehovah.
Please read it with me, Isaiah 30:15:
“For this is what the Sovereign Lord Jehovah,
“the Holy One of Israel, says:
“‘By returning to me and resting,
“‘you will be saved;
“‘your strength will be in keeping calm
“and showing trust.’
But you were unwilling.”
What about us?
Will we be willing or unwilling?
As we face these anxious times and even more turbulent times ahead,
will we take to heart Jehovah’s admonition?
Did you notice where your strength of character and fortitude will come from?
It is by “keeping calm
and showing trust.”
And that, brothers and sisters,
is our 2021 yeartext!
“Your strength will be in keeping calm
and showing trust,” Isaiah 30:15.
We will face anxious times ahead!
By means of prayer, encouragement from each other,
and leaning on God’s insightful Word,
what can we experience during these last days?
We can keep a sense of calm
and fully trust in the Sovereign of the universe,
our great God, Jehovah!

cn.text: 我们正生活在一段充满压力的时期
彼得前书5:8说
我们的大仇敌魔鬼撒但
“好像咆哮的狮子
走来走去，设法吞噬人。”
在圣经里
我们读到许多敬畏耶和华、崇拜他的人
也曾面对不少情况，让他们感到忧虑
例如在诗篇13:2
大卫王问耶和华说
“我每天烦恼忧伤，要到什么时候呢？”
另外，请跟我一起打开圣经到
耶稣，他是一个完美的人
但是在他被出卖的那个晚上
他也感到非常非常忧虑
路加福音22:42，他向耶和华祷告说
耶稣知道他将会非常痛苦
接着有什么事发生呢？
43节说
耶和华派了一个天使去鼓励耶稣
然后，耶稣就因此不再感到忧虑了吗？
没有
接着请看第44节
你曾经感到非常担心
忧虑到流出来的汗珠像血滴一样吗？
大概没有
那是因为拯救全人类的重责大任不在你肩上
不过，所有崇拜耶和华的人
在这最后的日子都一定会有许多忧虑
很多人担心或忧虑没有钱买到食物
衣服或居住的地方
在这段疫情期间
很可能有更多的弟兄姐妹
需要面对不同的挑战和压力
有些人居住的地方犯罪率很高
身边充满了暴力
有些人的压力是他们的同学或同事
要他们说谎或做不道德的事
有些人面对家庭的问题、健康的问题
情绪的问题或是失去亲人的痛苦
这些事都会让人感到非常忧虑
还有一些弟兄姐妹面对来自家人的反对
嘲弄甚至虐待，政府的迫害
错误宗教也挑起人们对我们的仇恨与偏见
这个演讲的题目是
“面对令人忧虑的情况时，要保持冷静”
这有可能吗？
以往，耶和华曾经帮助他的忠仆
今天，当我们在面对忧虑的情况时
他也一定会帮助我们保持冷静
请打开彼得前书5:6,7
第7节告诉我们
如果我们感到忧虑的时候可以怎么做？
我们一起读第6,7节
第6节有一个跟时间有关的词
耶和华说，他会在适当的时候给你尊荣
帮助可能不是马上的
如果你正在经历让你忧虑的情况
你可以怎么做呢？
要把我们所有的忧虑
卸给耶和华
这是第7节说的
把手里的东西放下来
你手里还剩下什么呢？
什么都没有
我们千万不要把忧虑留在自己手里
要把它们全部都给上帝
你可能会想
我的忧虑实在是太重了
我连拿都拿不起来，要怎么拿给上帝？
我们来看看另一个经文
诗篇37篇
我们看看第5节
这里用的另一个动词是“交托”
而不是“卸给”
第5节说
要交托给耶和华
英语圣经的脚注说
“交托给”也可以翻译成滚过去
或推给耶和华
所以如果你的忧虑太重
没办法拿给耶和华的话
试着推它一下，或者滚过去给耶和华
我们怎样才能把忧虑
卸给、交托或滚过去给耶和华呢？
让我们打开圣经到腓立比书4:6,7
经文说
我们可以通过热切地祷告
把忧虑卸给或推给耶和华
要把你心里的话都告诉上帝
你可以告诉他任何事
就连那些很尴尬的事也可以说
要记得
耶和华绝不会把你的事告诉任何人
要把忧虑卸给或推给他
第7节说
我们这样祷告以后，会怎么样呢？
会有上帝赐下的安宁
没错，如果我们完全信赖上帝
相信他一定会帮助我们
我们就会感到非常平静
还有什么方法可以让你平静下来呢？
你可以把你的忧虑
跟会众里值得信任的朋友说说
或者是一位让你觉得没有压力的长老
希伯来书10:25说
我们聚会的时候就会得到鼓励
在疫情期间
虽然不能在一起聚会
但如果你收到弟兄姐妹的信、电邮或短信
你就会感到很平静
因为他们非常关心你
还有什么方法帮助我们冷静呢？
要看看跟我们的难题有关的经文
也要好好沉思这些经文
比如说，以赛亚书41章
可以想想
我们只是手牵手跟上帝一起走路吗？
还是耶和华会伸出援手
帮助我们应付灾难和生活中的忧虑呢？
我们来比较一下以赛亚书41章的两节经文
先看看第10节的保证
你留意到了吗？
耶和华要你不要害怕，也不要忧虑
为什么呢？
因为他会用他的右手紧紧握着你
第11节和第12节
提到了我们可能会碰到的一些艰难的处境
13节接着说
你看出要点了吗？
这里说的不是跟上帝一起闲逛
也不是跟耶和华上帝一起手牵手去散步
经文说的是上帝伸手去救你
如果你只是跟上帝一起去散步的话
你的左手就会被他的右手握着
这两节经文是说
耶和华用他的右手紧紧握着你的右手
就好像耶和华正面对着你
他能看到你现在需要帮助
他伸出他的右手
紧紧抓着你的右手把你给拉上来
拉到安全的地方
圣经的一些经文让我们保持冷静，加强信心
我们说过3个保持冷静的方法
第一是祷告
第二是弟兄姐妹的鼓励
第三，沉思一些经文
这些经文
一些俄罗斯的弟兄在监狱的时候也沉思过
接下来我们来看个短片
早上4点钟，我在机场被扣留了
我们正在办理登机手续
一位联邦安全局的人走过来对我们说
要我们配合调查
我听到敲门的声音
我知道他们一定是冲着我来的
事情发生得太快了
他们逮捕了我们
把我们铐起来，还搜我们的身
一辆黑色玻璃的吉普车停在路中间
他们大喊着:“站住！”
接着他们就把我压到汽车的引擎盖上
然后把我铐了起来
第二天法院决定拘留我
我就被带到哈巴罗夫斯克等候法院的审理
我被带到一个昏暗的囚室里
被关了起来
我就跪下来向耶和华祷告
我告诉他
我想要在考验中对他保持忠心，绝不动摇
我被关在监狱的时候
每天晚上
我都会为我的朋友们
我的妻子和孩子
还有我认识的每一个人祷告
我会努力想一想他们的处境
为他们具体地祷告
我流着眼泪向上帝祷告
情况越来越难
不过之后事情有所转机
因为我相信
耶和华在事情发生的第一天就安排好了一切
我求耶和华让我勇敢坚强
内心平静和对人友善
于是我跟他们谈话时感到很平静
我不害怕他们会对我怎样
我向耶和华祷告
求他让我看出他就在我身边
正在帮助我
而且整件事情都在他的掌控之下
那天早上
我收到的第一封信提到了太阳
有趣的是
我读过很多关于太阳的文章
明白太阳本身就显示了耶和华强大的力量
那天，我感触很深
还有一些信提到了上帝的特质
包括那些
我在这个特殊的情况下需要表现的特质
他们不仅仅鼓励了我
也向狱警作了很好的见证
狱警很惊讶地问我
“谁从克拉斯诺尔达给你写信呢？
我也有朋友在那里”
我也收到来自法国和美国的来信
这些信让狱警看出很多人关心这件事
也让狱警看出我有不少的朋友
他们非常关心狱警会对我们做什么
通过每天收到的信，我可以得到一些灵感
帮助我准备演讲，还有聚会的内容
比如说
有一封信帮助我准备一个10分钟的演讲
另一封信我甚至可以准备一个公众演讲
从众多的来信当中
我收集到鼓励我的内容
以至于最后我拥有了一个个人的图书馆
我比较、收集这些信息
然后可以作优质的个人研读
这样就可以继续跟上组织的脚步
一个小男孩画了一张画，然后寄给我
上面写着
“如果你保持忠贞，就可以在新世界里”
一位年长的姐妹给我写了一封信
信的开头非常温暖
“我亲爱的儿子”
她非常用心写这封信给我
我收到她的信时，是我最低落的时候
我能感受到
耶和华用书信这个特别的方式来安慰我们
我给自己定下了这样的时间表
早上5点半我就起床了
那个时候其他人还在呼呼大睡
周围很安静，所以我可以阅读圣经
我花很多时间沉思一节经文
就能感受到它的美妙之处
一天结束后
这节经文会在我的脑海里留下非常深的印象
对我特别有意义
我体会到要有一颗良善的心
不在于吸收多少圣经知识
而在于让多少知识影响自己
在我被审前羁押的时候阅读圣经
对经文有了新的理解
当我读使徒行传的时候
我就更能理解在保罗身上发生的事情
这加强了我的信心，让我知道
我也能够像他一样度过这个艰难的时期
末底改的经验让我体会很深
哈曼说服国王要灭绝犹太人
他走出王宫遇见末底改
经文说
末底改没有起身，也没有战兢
所以我们也可以向末底改学习
不要惧怕，也不要战兢
这些弟兄祷告
接受弟兄姐妹的鼓励
还沉思上帝的话语后，结果怎么样呢？
他们就冷静下来，也非常信赖耶和华
让我们看看最后一节经文
请翻开以赛亚书30:15
当我们面对令人忧虑的情况时
这节经文会鼓励我们
很可惜
以色列人不愿意听从
耶和华这个特别重要的指引
请跟我一起看这节经文
以赛亚书30:15
那我们呢？
我们愿意还是不愿意听从呢？
当我们面对令人忧虑的情况
或将来更加艰难的挑战时
我们会把耶和华的提醒谨记在心吗？
什么可以帮助你保持坚强并忍耐下去呢？
就是要保持冷静，全心信赖上帝
弟兄姐妹们
这就是我们2021年的全年经文
以赛亚书30:15
我们的情况将会更加艰难
所以在这最后的日子
我们要热切祷告
我们要跟弟兄姐妹互相鼓励
也要依靠上帝的话语圣经
这样，我们就能够保持冷静
全心信赖宇宙的至高主宰
我们伟大的上帝耶和华！

titles.ko: 새뮤얼 F. 허드: 염려가 많은 때에 평온을 유지하기 위해 노력하십시오
titles.en: Samuel F. Herd: Strive for Calm When Facing Anxious Times
titles.cn: 塞缪尔·赫德：面对令人忧虑的情况时，要保持冷静

ko.text: 이번에는 우리의 소중한 청소년들에 관해 살펴볼 것입니다.
여러분은 봉사에 정말 열심히 참여하고 있습니다.
집회 참석과 성경 읽기도 아주 잘하고 있죠.
전염병 기간에 침례를 받은 청소년들도 많이 있습니다!
무엇을 하며 시간을 보내야 할지 몰라 힘들어합니다.
지금은 학교 생활도 이전과 많이 달라졌죠.
여러분이 힘들 거라는 걸 잘 압니다.
많은 청소년들이 여러분과 동일한 문제를 겪고 있습니다.
여러분도 비슷하게 느낀 적이 있는지 생각해 보세요.
이런 적은 거의 없었던 것 같아요.
예전처럼 친구들과 놀고 싶다는 생각만 했어요.
저는 늦게 자고 늦게 일어나게 됐어요.
저는 친구들이랑 같이 못 노는 게
부모님도 감염이 되지는 않을까 하고 늘 걱정해요.
특히 할머니, 할아버지한테 병을 옮길까 봐 걱정이 됐어요.
늘 혼자 공부하는 게 정말 힘들었어요.
모든 게 다 너무 버겁게 느껴져서
편지 봉사보다 전화 봉사가 훨씬 더 두렵게 느껴져요.
예전처럼 함께 모여서 집회를 보지 못한다는 말을 들었을 때
가족과 헤어지는 것 같은 느낌이 들었어요.
혹시 여러분의 상황과 많이 비슷하다는 생각이 들었나요?
여러분을 가장 힘들게 하는 것은 무엇입니까?
내가 너를 강하게 하고 너를 도와주겠다.
이 전염병 기간에도 여러분의 손을 놓지 않으실 겁니다.
현재 상황에 잘 대처하는 데 필요한 힘을 주실 수 있습니다.
어려움을 극복하는 데 무엇이 도움이 되고 있는지 유의해 보세요.
할 수 없게 된 일들이 아니라
새로 생긴 기회들에 초점을 맞추라고 말해 주고 싶어요.
해야 할 일 목록을 만드는 게
무언가 새로운 걸 시도해 보는 게 도움이 돼요.
항상 친구들과 함께 시간을 보내야 하는 건 아니라는 걸 알게 됐죠.
자기 감정을 다른 사람에게 이야기하는 걸 두려워하지 마세요.
왜 그런 감정이 드는지 이해가 안 될 때도요.
여호와께선 늘 적절한 때에 도와주실 거예요.
부모님이 봉사를 더 많이 할 수 있는
여호와에 관해 말해 줄 기회가 있었어요.
그 애는 줌으로 열리는 집회에 참석해서
전 세계가 많은 변화를 겪고 있지만,
여러분에게 도움이 될 만한 점이 있었나요?
어떤 방법을 적용해 보면 좋겠다고 느꼈습니까?
이 힘든 시기를 극복할 수 있는
지금 여러분에게 도움이 될 만한 내용이 많이 있습니다.
그런 내용을 찾아 연구해 볼 수 있죠.
한 자매는 매일 하나씩 읽고 있죠.
그런 기사들을 많이 찾아 볼 수 있습니다.
또 한 가지 기억해야 할 점이 있습니다.
어떤 실용적인 조처를 취할 수 있습니까?
혼자라는 생각이 들 때 “실용적인 지혜”를 나타내는 방법은
회중의 형제 자매들과 즐겁게 대화를 나누고 함께 웃기만 해도
“실용적인 지혜”를 나타낼 수 있는 또 다른 방법은
다른 청소년들의 좋은 본을 살펴보는 것입니다.
저는 또 다른 형사 고발을 당했어요.
현재 그 사건들에 대한 재판이 진행 중이에요.
개인 연구를 더 많이 하려고 노력했어요.
여호와께 문제를 맡겨야 한다는 뜻이기도 하지만,
우리 집이 급습을 당하기 얼마 전에
물이 차오르는 사람의 모습만 보이는 거예요.
자신의 믿음을 변호한 둘로바 자매의 모습이
이제 부모 여러분들께 잠시 말씀을 드리죠.
원격 수업을 듣는 아이들도 챙겨 주어야 하니까요.
동시에 이 모든 일을 해내고 있죠.
이처럼 어려운 상황을 견디는 데 도움이 되는 건
영적인 활동을 소홀히 하지 않는 것입니다.
가족 숭배를 정기적으로 하시는 걸 칭찬해 드립니다.
여러분의 가족 숭배에 초대해 보는 건 어떨까요?
함께하는 모두에게 좋은 시간이 될 겁니다.
여호와와 가까운 관계를 유지하려고 노력하는 모습을 보면
여호와께서 여러분을 자랑스럽게 여기실 거라 확신합니다.

en.text: This is our seventh video update
since the start of the pandemic.
This one is about a very special topic
—you precious young ones.
How are you doing?
We want to commend you for being active in the ministry,
not only that but attending meetings and reading the Bible.
Many of you have even got baptized during the pandemic!
We are so proud of you.
But we’re also concerned about you.
We’ve heard that many of you are struggling
with only seeing your friends on a screen
and not in person.
Some of you are dealing with a lack of structure in your life.
And for many of you, even school is different now.
We know this must be a hard time for you.
You’re not alone.
Many young ones are facing the same challenges.
As you watch this video,
see if you can relate to how these young ones feel.
Sometimes I struggle
with a negative attitude,
thinking that the coronavirus will never end.
My normal routine has completely changed.
It’s a very unusual situation.
At first, I was kind of just sitting
around all day, being lazy,
wishing I could hang out
with my friends like I used to.
I would stay up late and sleep in,
and I was losing track of time.
Not being able to associate
with my friends has been a real challenge.
Now that I’m spending
more time with my family,
I’m much more likely
to get irritated quickly.
Kids my age are always anxious
when their parents go to work.
They keep thinking,
‘Are they going to get infected?’
One of my biggest concerns
was that I would infect my family
—especially my grandparents.
When homeschooling started,
I found it very difficult
to study all on my own.
I felt overwhelmed and ended up
not being able to do anything.
I struggled with telephone witnessing
because I was afraid of the reaction
I would get from people.
Phone witnessing is a lot scarier than letter writing for me.
My time in the ministry
has actually gone down.
This made me feel really sad.
When we were told
that we could no longer attend
meetings as usual,
it was like someone said,
“You may not see your family!”
I’ve really missed being able to hug my brothers and sisters
and friends from the congregation.
Did some of those comments hit home
with you and your family?
Why don’t you pause this video
and think about it or talk about it with your family?
For example, which of those challenges
did you identify with the most?
We hope you had a good chat about the challenges you’re dealing with.
We feel for you.
Jehovah does too.
He knows this is tough
and has promised to help us through difficult times.
Let’s read what he promised at Isaiah 41:10
—Isaiah 41:10:
“Do not be afraid, for I am with you.
“Do not be anxious, for I am your God.
“I will fortify you, yes, I will help you,
“I will really hold on to you
with my right hand of righteousness.”
Did you catch that?
Jehovah has got you by the hand,
and he is not going to let go during this pandemic.
He can give you the strength you need
to control your thinking
and to make the best of your circumstances.
In this next video,
listen to what is helping other young people
to deal with these challenges.
For those having a tough time,
I would encourage them
to not look back at what they can’t do
but to look at the new opportunities
they have now.
Making a plan helped me to be organized in my daily life.
I made a to-do list, for example, which was extremely helpful.
I decided I would study,
not because my parents told me to
but to be able to serve Jehovah.
That boosted my morale.
If I am frustrated or bored,
doing something creative helps.
Having creative outlets helped me to realize
that I don’t need to be with my friends all the time.
So I started painting, sewing,
learning a new language and a new instrument,
and cooking and baking a lot more.
Arguments with my brother —they happen.
But when we deliver food or do good for others,
we both feel good about it and we bond more.
Talk to your parents,
because the more you keep something inside,
the worse you’re going to feel.
Do not be afraid to talk about your feelings
with someone else.
It’s not a weakness but a sign of strength.
Whatever feelings you have
—even if sometimes
you don’t understand them yourself—
pour them out to Jehovah.
He will always help at the right time.
I talked to my parents.
They gave me some practical suggestions
on how I could spend more time in the ministry,
such as letter writing and sitting in on other people’s studies.
I was able to talk to a friend at school about Jehovah.
She joined one of our Zoom meetings
and even gave a comment during the Watchtower  Study,
which I was really happy about.
During this pandemic,
a lot of things have changed on this earth,
but we don’t have to be afraid.
You are not alone in this.
We are together in this.
Jehovah is by our side.
With Jehovah, we can succeed,
and we will be able to enjoy that beautiful life in Paradise.
Did you hear anything that those young ones said
that might help you?
Which solutions do you think could work for you?
Go ahead and pause this video
and think about it or talk about it with your family.
We’ll give you a moment now.
Did you come up with any good ideas?
I’m sure you did!
One of the keys to coping with this pandemic
is doing what it says at Philippians 1:10.
There we read:
“Make sure of the more important things.”
What are some of those “more important things”?
The basics
—the Bible reading,
prayer,
field service and, of course, family worship.
How about personal study?
That’s important too!
The Young People Ask  books are a great place to find topics
that may be affecting you right now.
Some young ones have started reading life stories.
One young sister reads a different one every day.
It’s like traveling the globe
and hearing firsthand how others have dealt with challenges.
You can find
those articles
on Watchtower ONLINE LIBRARY ™.
Just type in “life stories.”
Here’s something else to think about:
What practical steps can we take
when feeling alone, or lonely?
Remember what Proverbs 18:1 says.
Let’s read it:
“Whoever isolates himself
“[that is, keeps to himself] . . .
rejects all practical wisdom.”
If you’re feeling alone, it is “practical wisdom”
to reach out to others.
You may find that some good conversation or laughter
with your friends from the congregation
—even over the phone—
is just what the doctor ordered.
Another way we can show “practical wisdom” is
by learning from the good examples of other young ones.
You know, some young people are in prison for their faith;
others are awaiting trial.
What helps them to cope?
You’ll find out in this interview
with Sister Darya Dulova from Russia.
When she was just 18, her home was raided
and the government started a criminal investigation
against her and her mom.
They raided our home on August 1, 2018.
My feelings at the time were probably both fear and shock.
They told my mom that I needed to be rescued from the mire;
otherwise, I would have no future, no job, no family—nothing.
They opened a criminal case against me, and I was found guilty.
Mom was given a two-year conditional sentence,
and I received one year.
After a short time, they started another criminal case against me,
and now these court proceedings are ongoing.
I was afraid that they would send my mom and me to prison.
So to somehow allay the fear,
I tried to spend more time in personal study.
That way, even if they did imprison me,
I would have more to meditate on.
Second Chronicles 20:17 encouraged me.
It says: “Take your position,
stand still, and see the salvation of Jehovah in your behalf.”
That means not just entrusting Jehovah with your problems,
but it also means, you know, waiting for him to act.
At the convention that took place shortly before we were raided,
there was an interesting point made
about how humans are actually 80 percent water.
So when they took me into the interrogation room,
I sat down and looked at the interrogator.
And in my mind, I drew a dotted line
and filled him up with 80 percent water.
And when he started saying things like,
“Dasha, you’ve got no future,”
all I saw was him filling up with water.
In short, his threats didn’t bother me.
Because I felt Jehovah’s support during those trials,
I’m no longer afraid to face new ones.
I am sure that Jehovah will support me.
His care may not come in a way that I expect,
but I know that it will always be in a way that glorifies him.
And that’s a guarantee that everything will be OK for me.
Isn’t it encouraging to see
how Darya has kept her integrity and defended her faith?
Well, I’ve enjoyed talking to you young ones,
but I’d like to talk to the rest of the family for a moment,
since this pandemic has brought challenges to them too.
Parents, many of you have been busier than ever,
supporting your children with their remote schooling
while also working and maintaining your homes
and keeping up with your schedule of theocratic activities.
You’re trying to juggle it all.
We love you for it.
Jehovah does too.
What’s going to help us all get through this
is a good spiritual routine.
Parents, we commend you
for keeping family worship regular.
From time to time, can you include
some extended family members or friends
by videoconference or by telephone?
They’ll love that also, and so will you.
It warms our hearts to see all that you young ones
are doing to stay close to Jehovah during this time.
In spite of all that’s going on,
you’re continuing to grow spiritually.
We’re very proud of you,
and you can be sure that Jehovah is proud of you too.
We want to extend the warm love of the Governing Body
to every one of you.
From the World Headquarters of Jehovah’s Witnesses,
this is JW Broadcasting®!

en.text: When we talked a few days ago,
we said we’d discuss, What will God’s Kingdom accomplish?
Yeah, I remember.
I have a short video I’d like to show you.
As we watch it, see if you can identify
some of the things God’s Kingdom will accomplish.
OK.
Throughout Jesus’ ministry,
he taught about God’s Kingdom
more than any other subject.
For centuries, his followers have prayed
for that Kingdom to come.
But what is the Kingdom?
When on earth, Jesus showed through his miracles
what God’s Kingdom would do.
When Jesus calmed a storm,
he showed that as King
he will control earth’s natural forces,
solving environmental problems.
By miraculously feeding thousands,
he demonstrated that the Kingdom
will eliminate world hunger.
When Jesus healed the sick,
lame, deaf, and blind,
he gave us a preview of the perfect health
that all will enjoy under his rule.
And by resurrecting people,
he showed that through the Kingdom,
he will reverse death itself.
You may wonder,
‘When will God’s Kingdom rule the earth?’
How can you support God’s Kingdom now?

en.text: Now, my discussion is about
the miracle of prayer.
What is one of the foremost ways
we draw close to, we stay close to, Jehovah?
By means of prayer.
In prayer, we experience Jehovah’s love
in a truly intimate way.
The Watchtower some years ago made this comment:
“Be assured that through the miracle of prayer
Jehovah is able to listen to you.”
And that’s very appropriate —to describe prayer as a miracle.
Let’s think about it.
You can pray in any language,
even though according to some linguists
there are more than 6,800 languages spoken on the earth today.
Jehovah knows all those languages.
Now, we’re impressed if a person knows two or three languages.
Jehovah knows every language, and that includes
the, perhaps, 300 sign languages
being used on earth today, according to one encyclopedia.
Jehovah knows every sign language.
In fact, our prayer can be a silent prayer
uttered only in the privacy of our heart.
Amazingly, if a faithful servant of Jehovah
does not even know what to pray for
because of the perplexity of the situation
or his mental anguish,
according to Romans 8:26,
the holy spirit can, in effect,
formulate a prayer in his behalf.
Now, that is truly miraculous.
And as we know, Jehovah has not delegated
the hearing of a prayer to anyone —not even his Son.
Psalm 65:2 calls Jehovah
the “Hearer of prayer.”
And “Hearer” is singular.
But here’s a question: What is prayer?
Well, some have defined it as talking to Jehovah.
But is that really accurate?
Go to Genesis chapter 3, please.
Let’s use this scripture to answer that —if it’s just talking to Jehovah.
Genesis 3:9:
“And Jehovah God kept calling to the man and saying to him:
‘Where are you?’
“Finally, he [Adam] said:
“‘I heard your voice in the garden,
but I was afraid because I was naked so I hid myself.’”
Well, clearly, Adam was talking to Jehovah, but it was not prayer.
And we have numerous other examples in the Bible.
So, appropriately, the Insight  book defines prayer
as “worshipful address to the true God.”
And then it adds: “[It] involves devotion, trust, respect,
“and a sense of dependence
on the one to whom the prayer is directed.”
So that’s a very good point.
If we want Jehovah to view our prayer
as not just talking to him but truly prayer,
we’ve got to make sure it is worshipful address
and that we attach devotion, trust,
respect, a deep sense of dependence on Jehovah.
And, obviously, that would require that we prepare our hearts
before we pray to Jehovah.
Ezra 7:10—Ezra “prepared his heart.”
Well, we would do well to do the same.
But now, here’s another question, What are the different types of prayer?
Well, our publications have explained
that there are basically four types of prayer.
We have petition, supplication,
thanksgiving, and praise.
And if you boil it down even further,
you can say there are two types of prayer —petition and thanksgiving—
because supplication is really a form of petition
—just very deep petition, but petition.
And praise is a form of thanksgiving
—thanking Jehovah for being the God that he is.
But now, let’s briefly talk about these four categories of prayer
we can divide it into.
Take first, petition.
Just like it sounds, we’re asking —we’re requesting—of Jehovah.
And Jehovah encourages us to ask him for our needs.
At Matthew 7:7, Jesus said:
“Keep on asking, and it will be given you;
“keep on seeking, and you will find;
keep on knocking, and it will be opened to you.”
And, of course, Jesus gives us things we can pray for
—our daily bread, forgiveness of our sins,
deliverance from the evil one as a few examples.
But now, let’s take supplication.
The Watchtower explains
that “the word means ‘earnest entreaty,’ . . . ‘beseeching prayer.’”
It involves imploring God very earnestly
as in time of great stress or peril.
If you want to think of a modern example of supplication,
think of a wife’s prayer
the night before her husband is executed
for keeping his integrity
—that would truly be supplication.
Now, let’s go to thanksgiving.
As it sounds, it’s the rendering of thanks to Jehovah.
And how voluminous are the things
for which we should express gratitude to Jehovah!
We think about all the material, or physical, gifts
that not only make life possible
but make it enjoyable.
‘Every good gift and every perfect present comes from Jehovah.’
—James 1:17.
And then what about the spiritual gifts that Jehovah showers upon us
—the benefits of that ransom sacrifice,
the holy spirit, God’s Word,
the Christian congregation, our marvelous Kingdom hope,
just to mention a few things?
It is only right that we thank Jehovah
for the things he has done, is doing,
and will yet do in the future.
As Paul said at Ephesians 5:20,
we should be “always giving thanks to our God and Father
for everything.”
But now, let’s move to praise.
Praise is a noble, exalted form of prayer,
as we said before, closely related to thanksgiving.
We could look at it this way.
Thanksgiving—we thank Jehovah for the gifts he gives us;
praise—we thank Jehovah for being the God he is
and for the qualities he has that we appreciate so much.
See, one brother said that praise is “bragging on Jehovah.”
And that really harmonizes with what Paul said at 1 Corinthians 1:31:
“The one who boasts,
let him boast in Jehovah.”
Jehovah is above all others.
He is certainly deserving of praise.
Exodus 15:11 tells us this.
It says: “Who among the gods
“is like you, O Jehovah?
“Who is like you, showing yourself mighty in holiness?
“The One to be feared with songs of praise,
the One doing wonders.”
Yes, Jehovah is worthy
of our words in our songs of praise.
Well, there we have four types of prayer.
We mentioned petition, supplication,
thanksgiving, and praise.
And, obviously, we should endeavor to try to balance our prayers
using a combination of these different aspects of prayer.
Now, if we’re not especially careful, there’s a danger
that our prayers could become lopsided with petition.
Now that would not be good, would it?
In fact, I think of a survey
that the Awake! commented on in “Watching the World,”
a survey among people who prayed.
And among those who still pray, that survey showed
that for most of them, their prayers are only petitions.
And then it said that they view God
like a divine Santa Claus:
“Give me this. Give me that.
Help me with this. Do this for me.”
We wouldn’t want our prayers
to even slightly take on a selfish tenor like that.
And what probably is the weakest aspect of most prayers?
Probably praise.
If we’re not careful, our prayers
could lack sufficient praise for Jehovah.
And it would be sad because he is so deserving of praise.
Well, may we “persevere in prayer.” —Romans 12:12.
May we “pray constantly.” —1 Thessalonians 5:17.
And may we strive to keep our prayers balanced and heartfelt
—truly “worshipful address” to our heavenly Father.
And this will help us to draw close
and stay close
to our wonderful heavenly Father.

cn.text: 今天，我们会跟大家讨论祷告这个奇迹
我们亲近耶和华，跟他保持良好的关系
最重要的方法之一是什么呢？
就是祷告
通过祷告
我们可以亲身感受到耶和华对我们的爱
多年前的一篇《守望台》文章这样说
你可以确信，通过祷告这个奇迹
耶和华一定能够听到你说的话
把祷告称为奇迹，这再合适不过了
想想看，你可以用任何语言向上帝祷告
虽然一些语言学家说
世界上有超过6800种语言
可是耶和华都能听得懂这些语言
一个人会说两三种语言已经很厉害
耶和华却懂得所有的语言
另外，根据一本百科全书
世界上有大概300种手语
耶和华也懂得这些手语
事实上，我们也可以默祷
也就是没有发出声音
只在心里向上帝说话
令人惊讶的是
如果上帝的一个忠仆
因为情况复杂而不知所措
或心里非常痛苦而不知道要求什么的时候
罗马书8:26说
这时上帝的神圣力量就会为他祈求
这真的是一个奇迹
耶和华没有把听祷告这件事委派给任何人
包括耶稣
诗篇65:2说
耶和华是“听祷告的主”
“听祷告的主”，原文是个单数只有一个
那么祷告是什么呢？
有些人说
就是跟耶和华说话啊！
这样说够准确吗？
让我们来看看创世记第3章
我们可以在圣经里找到这个问题的答案
创世记第3章
第9节
“耶和华上帝一直呼唤他:你在哪里？”
然后
亚当回答说
“我在园子里听见了你的声音
但我很害怕
因为我赤身露体，就躲起来了。”
很明显地
亚当在跟耶和华说话
但这并不是祷告
其实圣经里还有很多类似的例子
关于祷告，《洞悉圣经》是这样说的
“怀着崇敬的态度，对真神说话。”
书里继续说
“祷告牵涉到爱戴
信任和尊重
也涉及对祷告对象的依赖。”
这里说的很清楚，是不是？
如果我们不希望耶和华认为
我们的祷告只是毫无意义地说话而已
我们就要怀着
尊重的态度向上帝祷告
也要表现出信任、尊重
爱戴以及深深的依赖
要好好思考祷告的内容
以斯拉记7:10说
以斯拉祷告时心里做好准备
我们也应该跟他一样
另一个问题是祷告包括哪些类型？
我们的出版物提到祷告基本上有四种类型
祷告有祈求、恳求、感谢和赞美
如果你仔细想想的话
祷告其实可以分为两大类
就是祈求和感谢
因为恳求也是祈求的一种
只是比较深的祈求
而赞美呢，就是感谢的一种
我们感谢耶和华是那么好的上帝
现在我们来讨论一下这四种不同类型的祷告
第一是祈求
祈求的意思是
我们向耶和华上帝提出请求
求他赐给我们需要的一切
马太福音7:7说
“你们不断恳求，就会给你们
不断寻找，就会找到
不断敲门，就会给你们开门。”
耶稣说过，我们可以为哪些事祷告
比如说
我们每天的食物
原谅我们的罪，或者救我们脱离那恶者
接下来说说恳求
《守望台》提到
这个词的意思是热切地恳请
或恳求的祷告
这意味着向上帝热切地恳求
就像人在遇到重大压力或危险时那样
我们来举一个关于恳求的现代例子
一位弟兄因为保持忠贞就要被处决了
前一天晚上，他的妻子为他祷告
这一定是一个恳求的祷告
现在来说说感谢
感谢的意思是
我们感谢耶和华
我们有太多的事
要向耶和华上帝表达我们的感激之情了
上帝赐给我们很多东西，很多礼物
让我们
不但能好好活着，还能享受人生
圣经说，各种美好的礼物
各种完美的赏赐都来自耶和华
上帝为了帮助人成为他的朋友
赐下很多礼物
比如赎价的益处
神圣力量
上帝的话语
基督徒会众
我们的美好希望
还有好多好多
我们唯一该做的事就是感谢耶和华
感谢他以前做过的事
现在正在做的事
以及将来要做的事
就像保罗在以弗所书5:20说的
我们凡事都要
“时刻感谢上帝我们的父亲。”
最后就是赞美
赞美是一种高尚的祷告
它跟感恩的祷告息息相关
我们可以这样看
感恩，我们感谢耶和华赐给我们礼物
赞美，我们感谢耶和华是这么好的上帝
有这么好的特质
我们都非常喜欢他的特质
有位弟兄说，赞美就是夸赞耶和华
这跟保罗说的一致
保罗在哥林多前书1:31说
“夸耀的人应该因耶和华而夸耀。”
耶和华比任何人都伟大
毫无疑问，他配得上我们的赞美
出埃及记15:11告诉我们这一点
经文说
“耶和华啊，众神当中谁比得上你？
谁比得上你，圣洁超凡
可颂可畏，施行奇事？”
没错
耶和华上帝的确值得我们用歌声赞美他
我们讨论了四种祷告
这包括祈求
恳求
感谢
还有赞美
我们祷告的时候要尽量保持平衡
这四种类型的祷告
都应该在我们的祷告里出现
如果不小心，就很可能会有一种危险
就是我们只会求上帝满足我们个人的愿望
这样做很不好，对不对？
我想起《警醒》杂志
在“世闻点滴”这个栏目
提过一个调查，是一个关于祷告的调查
调查显示
在现在还在祷告的人当中
大部分人的祷告都只是祈求
调查说他们把上帝看作是圣诞老人
给我这个，给我那个
帮我做这个，帮我做那个
我们绝不想我们的祷告变得这么自私
就连一点自私的倾向也不想
那么我们祷告时最容易忽略的是什么呢？
很可能是赞美
如果不小心
我们就可能很少在祷告中赞美耶和华
这真令人难过
因为耶和华值得我们常常赞美他
罗马书12:12说
“祷告要坚持不懈。”
帖撒罗尼迦前书5:17说
“不断祷告”
愿我们祷告时能够保持平衡
并怀着崇敬的态度
发自内心地向天父说话
这样做，我们就能够亲近耶和华
并跟他保持良好的关系

ko.text: 이번 달 프로그램의 주요 장면을 살펴보시죠.
유혹을 이겨 내는 데 기도는 어떻게 여러 가지로 도움이 됩니까?
한 가지 예로, 나르시소 형제가 성경 원칙과 어긋나는 행실을 그만두는 데
작년에 수백만 명이 스페인어 「신세계역」 개정판을 받고 기뻐했습니다.
형제들이 보이지 않는 곳에서 어떤 수고를 했는지 살펴보겠습니다.
여호와의 가장 아름다운 특성 한 가지는 기꺼이 용서하는 것입니다.
이번 달 뮤직비디오는 우리도 여호와의 도움으로
다른 사람을 용서할 수 있다는 걸 보여 줄 것입니다.
이번 달에는 이러한 주제를 다룰 것입니다.
예수께서 하신 이 말씀은 마태복음 26:41에 기록돼 있습니다.
오늘 우리가 살펴볼 세 가지 질문이 있습니다.
셋째, 예수의 본을 통해 어떤 교훈을 얻을 수 있습니까?
“유혹에 빠지지 않도록 깨어 살피고 계속 기도하십시오.
그분은 처형당하기 전 마지막 밤에 이 말씀을 하셨습니다.
그 밤은 분명 예수에게 이제껏 가장 힘든 밤이었을 것입니다.
앞선 구절들을 보면 “그분은 비통해하며 몹시 괴로워하기 시작하셨습니다.”
예수께서 그날 밤 느끼셨을 스트레스와 압박감은
그분은 사탄이 자신을 총공격할 것임을 알고 계셨습니다.
또 그분은 자신이 고통스럽게 죽게 될 것도 알고 계셨습니다.
하지만 그분에게 더 큰 시련은 따로 있었죠.
치욕스러운 죄로 유죄 판결을 받게 될 것을 아셨습니다.
마태복음 26:39의 연구 노트에는 이런 말이 나옵니다.
하느님께 모독이 돌아갈까 봐 매우 염려하셨을 것이다.
그래서 그분은 이 ‘잔’이 지나가게 해 달라고 기도하셨다.”
이 엄청난 압박감 속에 예수께서는 죽기까지 충실을 지킬 것입니까?
수많은 사람들의 생명이 그분에게 달려 있었습니다.
훨씬 더 중요한 점으로, 아버지의 이름이 관련되어 있었습니다.
그처럼 극심한 감정적 스트레스를 받을 때 그분은 무엇을 하셨나요?
한 번도 아니고 세 번이나 하셨습니다!
“그분이 몹시 괴로워서 더욱 간절히 계속 기도하시니,
생각해 보면, 예수는 사탄을 잘 알고 계셨죠.
하늘에 계실 때부터 사탄이 온갖 방법을 써서
하느님의 종들을 유혹하는 것을 다 지켜보셨습니다.
어떤 유혹을 하든 문제없다고 생각하지 않으셨습니다.
하느님의 도움과 힘을 얻기 위해 기도할 필요가 있었다면
따라서 그분의 이 조언은 참으로 적절합니다.
“우리는 사탄의 영향력 아래 있으면서 스스로 유혹을 받게 될 수 있습니다.
하느님의 뜻과 반대되는 무엇인가를 하거나 가지면 좋겠다고 생각하고,
이러한 부적절한 생각으로 인해 생긴 욕망을 버리지 않고
계속 품고 있을 때 스스로 유혹을 받게 됩니다.
하느님의 조언과 경고를 무시하게 될 수 있습니다.
기도는 유혹을 받을 때 도움이 됩니다.
기도는 여호와께서 원하시는 것에 초점을 맞추고
유혹에 빠지지 않도록 힘을 얻는 데 도움이 됩니다.
예수께서는 이 땅에 계실 때 어떤 유혹을 받으셨습니까?
마귀에게 세 번 유혹을 받았던 일이 떠오르실 것입니다.
그 세 가지 유혹을 잠깐 생각해 보겠습니다.
돌을 빵으로 만들어 보라는 유혹을 사탄에게 받으셨습니다.
사탄은 사람의 자연스러운 식욕을 이용하려고 했습니다.
사탄의 의도대로 부적절하게 식욕을 충족시키지 않으셨습니다.
둘째로, 사탄은 예수에게 성전 흉벽에서 뛰어내려 보라고 유혹했습니다.
왜냐하면, 그처럼 극적인 방법으로 과시하는 것이
교만하게 여호와를 시험하는 것과 같다는 것을 알고 계셨기 때문이죠.
마지막으로, 사탄은 예수에게 “세상의 모든 왕국과 그 영광”을 제시했습니다.
사탄은 그 대가로 자신에게 숭배 행위를 하라고 요구했습니다.
여러분도 비슷한 유혹을 받은 적이 있으신가요?
‘저한테 돌을 빵으로 만들라거나, 높은 데서 뛰어내리라고 한 사람은 없어요.
세상을 다스릴 권력을 주겠다고 한 사람도 물론 없고요.’
여러분은 비슷한 유혹을 받은 적이 있으신가요?
우리 대부분은 육적인 욕망을 자극하는 유혹을 받은 적이 있습니다.
우리는 부도덕한 일을 저지르게 만드는 유혹을 받을 수도 있고,
탐욕이나 물질에 대한 지나친 염려에 빠지게 하는 유혹을 받을 수도 있습니다.
그런가 하면 우리의 자존심이나 과시욕을 부추기거나,
겸손을 시험하는 유혹을 받을 수도 있습니다.
또한 우리는 누구나 사탄의 세상에서 살아가면서
부나 권력이나 명예를 추구하게 만드는 유혹을 받을 수 있습니다.
