적이 실제로 존재한다는 느낌을 전달하지 않습니다.
마귀가 실제로 존재하는 적이라는 걸 알고 계셨죠.
그는 사람을 자신의 덫과 유혹에 걸려들게 해서
여호와 보시기에 그릇된 일을 하게 만듭니다.
죄를 지은 사람은 죄책감에 사로잡히게 되고,
사나운 적인 마귀는 그를 더 짓밟습니다.
죄에 굴복했다는 비참한 느낌에 시달리게 만들죠.
그럼 어떻게 그처럼 강력한 적과 맞설 수 있습니까?
그럼 사도 바울이 우리의 상황을 묘사하기 위해
자기를 군인으로 모집한 사람의 승인을 얻기 위해
생계를 위한 영리 활동에 얽매이지 않습니다.”
그리스도 예수를 통한 여호와의 구원 마련을 받아들이고,
전쟁을 하는 이유에는 별로 관심이 없습니다.
여호와께 온전히 헌신하고 그리스도께 충성을 다합니다.
군인이 갖고 있는 또 다른 특징은
“하느님을 섬기는 자와 섬기지 않는 자” 사이에는 큰 차이가 있습니다.
여러분이 보초를 서고 있는 군인이라고 생각해 봅시다.
서로 밀접히 연합해서 평화롭게 일하는 것에 대해 설명합니다.
“다만 그리스도에 관한 좋은 소식에 합당하게 행동하십시오.
그리하여 내가 가서 여러분을 만나게 되든 떨어져 있든,
여러분이 한 영으로 굳건히 서 있고 한 영혼으로
좋은 소식에 대한 믿음을 위해 나란히 힘써 싸우고 있으며
어떤 면에서도 반대자들 때문에 두려워하지 않고 있다는 말을
네, 어깨를 나란히 해서 연합하는 것은 매우 중요합니다.
여호와께서도 적들에게 그렇게 하신 적이 있죠.
해가 질 때까지 화난 상태로 있지 마십시오.
우리 사이에 불화와 분열이 있을 때
우리는 진짜 적이 누구인지 잊지 말아야 합니다.
우리를 실망시키거나 상처를 줄 때가 있는 것은 사실이지만
그래야 형제들의 사기까지 꺾는 일이 없을 것입니다.”
여러분이 여호수아의 군대에 들어가 전투 준비를 하고 있는데
“여호수아는 모세만큼 여호와의 축복을 받지 못하는 거 같아.”
우리에겐 여호와를 신뢰하는 긍정적이고 용감한 형제들이 있어 기쁩니다.
사탄은 우리의 약점을 잘 알고 있습니다.
“사단의 궤계를 대항하여 굳게 서라”는 기사가 실렸는데,
마귀는 우리의 약점을 잘 알고 있다고 알려 줍니다.
우린 이 영적 전쟁에서 승리할 수 있습니다.
여호와께서 ‘우리의 훈련을 끝내시고 우리를 강하게 하실’ 겁니다.
우린 여호와의 도움으로 성공할 수 있습니다.
코컨 형제의 말처럼 사탄은 동정심이 전혀 없습니다.
그는 온갖 방법으로 우리가 죄를 짓도록 유혹합니다.
수많은 형제 자매들이 이 소식에 기뻐했습니다.
스페인어는 여호와의 증인들이 가장 많이 사용하는 언어이기 때문에
번역 작업을 할 때 고려해야 할
그 단어를 아예 사용하지 않는 곳도 있고
뢰시 형제가 개정판 성경을 발표했을 때
즉시 다운로드 받을 수 있었기 때문입니다.
성경을 다운로드 받도록 도움을 주기 위해
훨씬 더 마음에 와닿는 것 같아요.
표현이 많이 바뀌었다는 걸 알게 됐어요.
이번 달 주제는 ‘유혹에 빠지지 않도록 계속 기도하십시오’였습니다.
나르시소 형제는 열심히 기도한 덕분에, 생활에서 큰 변화들을 했고
그의 겸손을 시험했던 유혹들도 이겨 냈습니다.
사도 베드로의 본을 통해 어떻게 두려움을 극복하고
여호와와 형제들에게 더 사랑을 나타낼 수 있는지도 배웠습니다.
다케시 형제는 자신의 한계에 초점을 맞추지 않고
형제 자매들을 위해 매일 기도하면서 기쁨을 얻었습니다.
우리가 여호와의 특성을 본받아 기꺼이 용서한다면
사랑하는 사람에게 받은 상처가 치유될 수 있다는 걸 보여 주었습니다.
아르헨티나의 티에라델푸에고주에 사는 우리 형제 자매들을 만나 보겠습니다.
남아메리카 대륙의 최남단에 위치한 여러 섬으로 이루어져 있습니다.
그중 가장 큰 섬의 산들에는 빙하가 있고
이곳의 낮의 길이는 한 해 동안 크게 변하는데,
바람이 불고 눈과 얼음을 볼 수 있습니다.
이 섬의 도시인 우수아이아에는 세 개의 회중이 있습니다.
이곳의 형제 자매들이 대회에 참석하기 위해서는
약 200킬로미터나 되는 산악 지대를 가로질러 가야 합니다.
눈과 얼음 때문에 길을 다니는 것이 불가능할 때도 있습니다.
우리 형제들은 날씨가 어떻든 야외 봉사에 참여합니다.
겨울에는 해가 산 위로 충분히 높이 뜨지 않아
우수아이아 일부 지역에는 해가 잘 들지 않습니다.
날이 짧아지면 형제들은 가능한 해가 떠 있을 때 봉사하기 위해
형제들은 시골 지역이나 외딴 섬들에서 봉사하는 마련을 하기도 하는데,
이를테면 비글 해협 건너편에 있는 나바리노섬에 가기도 합니다.
최근에 일부 형제 자매들은 열심히 영어를 배워서
이 곳을 찾아오는 관광객들에게 훌륭한 증거를 하기도 했습니다.
우리 형제 자매들이 여러분께 따뜻한 사랑과 안부를 전합니다!
여호와의 증인 세계 본부에서 지금까지 JW 방송이었습니다.

en.text: Welcome, brothers and sisters.
Here are some highlights from this month’s program.
We’ll discuss the many ways
that prayer can help us resist temptations.
For example, we’ll see how prayer helped Narciso leave behind
practices that conflicted with Bible principles.
Last year, millions were delighted to receive
the revised New World Translation in Spanish.
We’ll go behind the scenes
and see what it took to produce this translation of God’s Word.
Among Jehovah’s most endearing qualities
is his willingness to forgive.
Our new music video reminds us that with Jehovah’s help,
we too can forgive others.
This is JW Broadcasting®.
This month, we’re going to discuss the theme
“Pray Continually,
So That You May Not Enter Into Temptation.”
Those words of Jesus
are recorded at Matthew 26:41.
In this discussion, we’ll answer three important questions:
(1) Why did Jesus pray?
(2) What temptations did he face?
and (3) What lessons can we learn from Jesus’ example?
Let’s start by reading that verse together.
That’s Matthew 26:41:
“Keep on the watch and pray continually,
“so that you may not enter into temptation.
“The spirit, of course, is eager [or, “willing,” ftn.],
but the flesh is weak.”
Why did Jesus pray?
Jesus uttered these words
on the final night before his execution.
No doubt this was the most difficult evening
that Jesus had ever faced.
The surrounding verses tell us
that “he began to feel grieved and to be greatly troubled.”
It’s hard for us to comprehend fully
the stress and pressure Jesus was facing on that night.
He knew that Satan was about to throw everything he could at him.
Jesus also knew that he’d soon die
an agonizing death.
But something else was even harder for him to handle.
He realized that he was about to be falsely charged
and convicted of the despicable crime
of blasphemy against Jehovah’s holy name.
The study note on Matthew 26:39 says:
“Jesus no doubt felt great concern
“over the reproach that his death
“as one charged with blasphemy and sedition
“could bring on God,
“moving him to pray
that this ‘cup’ pass away from him.”
In the face of all that pressure,
would Jesus remain faithful until death?
The lives of countless people hung in the balance.
Even more important,
his Father’s reputation was involved.
Under all that intense emotional stress,
what did Jesus do?
He prayed, not just once,
but three times!
Notice how Luke describes what happened,
as recorded at Luke 22:44:
“But he was in such agony
“that he kept praying more earnestly;
“and his sweat became as drops of blood
falling to the ground.”
What’s the lesson for us?
Well, think about it.
Jesus knew Satan well.
Jesus had observed from heaven
all the temptations that Satan uses
in his efforts to ensnare God’s servants.
Yet, Jesus did not feel that he could easily handle
whatever “the Tempter” might place before him.
So this is a clear lesson for us:
If the perfect Son of God
felt the need to pray for divine help and strength,
how much more so should we.
How appropriate then is the admonition:
“Pray continually,
so that you may not enter into temptation.”
But what does it mean to “enter into temptation”?
The Watchtower  back in 1951 explained:
“We ourselves under Satan’s influence
“create the temptation by thinking how nice it would be
“to do or to have something contrary to God’s will,
“and then not dismissing the desire created by this improper thinking,
“but considering it more and more.
“In this way we are drawn out
“and led to ignore God’s counsel and warning.
We enter into temptation.”
Prayer helps us when we face temptation.
It helps us to focus on what Jehovah wants us to do
and to ask him for the strength not to enter into temptation.
Our second question:
What temptations did Jesus face
while here on earth?
We probably immediately think of the occasion shortly after Jesus’ baptism
when he was tempted three times by the Devil.
Let’s quickly summarize those three temptations.
First, Jesus was asked to turn stones into bread
at a time when he was extremely hungry.
Basically, Satan appealed to Jesus’ desire for food.
However, Jesus immediately rejected the temptation
to satisfy that desire in an inappropriate way.
Second, Satan challenged Jesus
to throw himself off the temple battlement.
Jesus rejected this temptation as well.
Why?
Because he knew that such a spectacular display
would amount to a prideful testing of Jehovah.
Finally,
Satan offered Jesus
“all the kingdoms of the world and their glory.”
But at what price?
Satan demanded that Jesus offer him in return
an act of worship.
What was Jesus’ answer?
He flatly refused, saying: “Go away, Satan!”
Have you had to face similar temptations?
Well, you might quickly answer:
‘No one has asked me to turn stones into bread
‘or to jump off a tall building.
‘And certainly no one has offered me
the rulership of all the governments in the world!’
But notice, please, we said “similar,” not “the same.”
So have you faced similar temptations?
No doubt you have.
Most of us have faced temptations
involving fleshly desires.
It may have been temptations to commit immorality
or temptations that appealed to greed
or an unbalanced concern about material things.
Other temptations may have appealed to our pride or tested our humility
or our desire to impress others.
And who of us hasn’t been tempted by opportunities
offered to us by Satan’s world
for wealth, power, or position?
No matter what temptation comes our way, though,
remember Jesus’ words: “Pray continually,
so that you may not enter into temptation.”
But were those the only temptations that Jesus faced?
No.
How do we know?
Well, notice Luke’s words
found at Luke 4:13:
“So the Devil, having finished all the temptation,
departed from him until another convenient time.”
Did Satan ever come back again to tempt Jesus?
He must have because of what we’re told
at Hebrews 4:15.
Let’s read that:
“For we do not have a high priest
“who cannot sympathize with our weaknesses,
“but we have one who has been tested
“in all respects as we have,
but without sin.”
Have you ever wondered what other “convenient time”
Satan selected to test Jesus?
Well, let’s consider some possibilities.
One example occurred in 32 C.E.,
about two and a half years after the initial temptations.
Please turn to John 6:15:
“Then Jesus, knowing that they were about to come
“and seize him to make him king,
withdrew again to the mountain all alone.”
This seems like a similar temptation
to what Jesus had already faced.
But this time, the setting was different.
Satan didn’t directly offer the kingship to Jesus.
There was no demand for Jesus to worship the Devil.
Rather, those following Jesus wanted to make him their king.
This temptation was going to be by popular demand.
How did Jesus react?
Well, even before they could make their move,
Jesus withdrew from them to a mountain, just by himself.
And what did he do on the mountain?
We find the answer in a detail
added in the parallel account recorded by Matthew.
Let’s read it together.
It’s Matthew 14:23:
“After sending the crowds away,
he went up on the mountain by himself to pray.”
Yes, Jesus went there not just to avoid the crowds
but to pray.
The third question:
What lessons can we learn
from Jesus’ example?
Even though we may have passed a test,
or avoided entering into temptation, in the past,
we shouldn’t be surprised
if a similar temptation may arise again
but in a different form or situation
and at a convenient time.
For whom?
For Satan, not us.
Another occasion occurred when Jesus and his apostles
were in the vicinity of Mount Hermon,
near Caesarea Philippi.
Jesus’ apostles had just acknowledged him
as “the Christ, the Son of the living God.”
So Jesus took the opportunity to expand their thinking further.
Notice what’s recorded
at Matthew 16:21:
“From that time forward,
“Jesus began explaining to his disciples
“that he must go to Jerusalem
“and suffer many things
“from the elders and chief priests and scribes and be killed,
and on the third day be raised up.”
What was the reaction of his apostles to this information?
Let’s read on in verse 22:
“At this Peter took him aside
“and began to rebuke him, saying:
“‘Be kind to yourself, Lord;
you will not have this happen to you at all.’”
Although these words were uttered by a close friend,
Jesus immediately recognized
that they reflected Satan’s wishes, not Jehovah’s.
So he firmly responded:
“Get behind me, Satan!
“You are a stumbling block to me,
“because you think, not God’s thoughts,
but those of men.”
Although this account doesn’t specifically refer
to Jesus praying at that time,
we know that Jesus was a man of prayer.
The apostle Paul tells us at Hebrews 5:7:
“During his life on earth,
“Christ offered up supplications and also petitions,
with strong outcries and tears.”
So no doubt those prayers helped Jesus
to focus on the reason why he came to earth.
That clear focus helped him to see
that Peter’s misguided counsel
would only help to further the Tempter’s cause.
What does this teach us?
This shows us that temptations don’t always come
from those who are Jehovah’s enemies.
Some who are close to us
may even serve Satan’s ends unintentionally,
as was the case with Peter.
It could be an employer, a workmate, a schoolmate,
a friend, a relative, a parent,
a brother, or a marriage mate.
Let’s examine another example of how Satan returned to Jesus.
This time, it was by means of the religious leaders.
They attacked Jesus verbally,
misquoting Scripture and hurling senseless accusations at him.
But Jesus understood what they were up to and frankly told them:
“You are from your father the Devil.”
We shouldn’t be surprised if apostates and other opposers
use similar tactics today.
Just as Jesus was accused of blasphemy
and political sedition,
so too God’s people have been labeled as “extremists”
and have been the victims of all sorts of false accusations.
Like Jesus, we remember
who really is behind all these attacks
—Satan, the great Tempter!
What will help us to avoid the temptation
of giving up because of discouragement?
How can we successfully handle
all these types of attacks?
Paul tells us what to do.
We read at Ephesians 6:11:
“Put on the complete suit of armor from God
“so that you may be able to stand firm
against the crafty acts of the Devil.”
After speaking about the importance of putting on the spiritual suit of armor,
Paul goes on to say in verse 18
that this should be done together “with every form of prayer
“and supplication
[as we] carry on prayer on every occasion in spirit.”
So, what have we learned from our discussion?
It seems that Satan didn’t try again to tempt Jesus directly,
but he was persistent.
He kept coming back in different guises.
He used others to give Jesus wrong advice,
to oppose and ridicule him,
as well as to try to make him a king.
Perhaps we’ve rejected some serious temptations in the past,
but remember, Satan doesn’t give up on us
just because he failed in the past.
At a time convenient to him,
he may come back to tempt us with something completely different
or the same temptation
dressed up in a different form.
So, what’s the key to not entering into temptation?
We need to remember and apply Jesus’ admonition:
“Pray continually,
so that you may not enter into temptation.”
So far, we’ve discussed how we could “enter into temptation”
to do something wrong.
However, we may also be tempted
not to do something right.
For example,
although we know that we should forgive another person
for something they have done against us,
perhaps we may enter into the temptation
of avoiding that person and not forgiving them,
even though there may be a basis for doing so.
What can help us in such a situation?
Again, the answer is: Pray for Jehovah’s help.
This is the theme of our music video for this month.
It involves a very painful situation
between a mother and a daughter.
Let’s see the role of prayer
in starting to resolve
what might seem to be an impossible problem.
I’ve got this grudge. I’m holding it in.
But it’s so heavy; it pulls me down.
I wish I could turn this around.
I understand the need to forgive,
But it’s not easy if it’s not my fault.
These thoughts bring forgiveness to a halt.
It’s right about now that I have to pray.
Jehovah saw what happened; he knows my pain.
But most of all he gives me
Strength to let it go.
No, I can’t do this on my own.
I pray, “Jehovah, please help me; Help me forgive freely.”
He’ll help me to reflect The way he forgives, the way he forgets.
I pray, “Jehovah, please help me; Help me forgive freely.”
Forgive freely.
Trying my best to let it all go,
But at times, it comes back to mind.
I wish I could put all this behind.
I realize that I can’t hold on.
Forgiveness means you don’t bring it back up.
This only gets me in a rut.
It’s right about now that I have to pray.
Jehovah saw what happened; he knows my pain.
But most of all he gives me
Strength to let it go.
No, I can’t do this on my own.
I pray, “Jehovah, please help me; Help me forgive freely.”
He’ll help me to reflect The way he forgives, the way he forgets.
I pray, “Jehovah, please help me; Help me forgive freely.”
Forgive freely. Forgive freely.
Forgive freely. Forgive freely.
I’m sure this video touched our hearts.
What a difficult situation!
And, of course, such situations are not resolved overnight.
Some wounds take a long time to heal,
but it’s possible to start the process of healing
by trying to forgive.
But we can’t do it alone.
Remember what our song beautifully emphasized.
Keep praying, “Jehovah, please help me;
help me forgive freely.”
In our next video,
we’ll see another example of how prayer helps us today.
Narciso Garcia worked hard to bring his life
in harmony with Bible principles.
But it wasn’t easy.
Notice how he dealt with temptations similar to those Jesus faced.
I sweated blood to train myself in martial arts.
So when I joined a big competition, I won the fight.
My life changed.
I became the bodyguard of a well-known politician
and taught martial arts to some popular celebrities.
My students and my boss
and his family —they all became part of my life.
But I was still looking for something.
One day, some Jehovah’s Witnesses came by and gave me a tract.
I was surprised
and really happy to learn God’s name.
I thought, ‘This could be what I’ve been looking for.’
So I accepted a Bible study,
and I realized that I owed everything to God.
When I attended my first meeting,
I saw how humble and caring the Witnesses were.
But my neighbors made fun of me.
I wanted to beat them because I knew I could.
I was ashamed that I couldn’t do anything
to defend Jehovah’s name.
Then one morning before going to the meeting,
for the first time,
I approached Jehovah in prayer, asking him to give me courage.
I couldn’t do it alone.
After that prayer, I felt that Jehovah really strengthened me,
and I humbly told the neighbors
that I was going to the Kingdom Hall.
Since then,
I’ve always prayed to Jehovah when making decisions.
I needed to leave martial arts.
I had to quit my job as a bodyguard and stop carrying guns.
Doing his will wasn’t always easy,
but Jehovah gave me the courage to do so.
My boss asked me to visit him.
He offered me a new car
and double my salary.
His offer was very tempting.
So I went to the washroom and intensely
prayed again to Jehovah for courage.
“Jehovah, help me, please,” I said.
“I can’t do this on my own.”
In the end, I chose Jehovah.
Jehovah is more precious to me than anything this world could offer.
I told him,
“Sorry, but I am not accepting your offer.”
It felt like losing a family in death.
Eventually, I got baptized.
I realized that it didn’t matter what people thought about me.
It’s how Jehovah sees me that matters.
Now I am very grateful
to be with the brothers in serving Jehovah.
I am now serving as a regular pioneer.
And this is the life
that I had been looking for.
How was Narciso tempted?
When his neighbors made fun of him for going to the Kingdom Hall,
he thought about using these
and going back to using martial arts.
Yes, ridicule tested Narciso’s humility.
But through prayer,
he was able to speak calmly and confidently with his neighbors.
Narciso’s boss tempted him with a new car and a raise.
What did Narciso do?
He immediately went to a quiet place
and prayed intensely.
Jehovah gave him the courage to make the right decision.
When we face similar temptations,
we can be confident that through prayer,
Jehovah will help us to do the right thing.
One way Jehovah responds to prayer
is by directing us to the Scriptures.
There we find wonderful examples of faithful servants
who overcame all sorts of challenges.
In the following dramatization,
let’s see what we can learn from the apostle Peter.
After working unassigned territory,
I made up my mind to put in my application for regular pioneering.
However, things were going really well at work.
Is this the right time to make a drastic change?
A new foreign-language group is being formed in our congregation.
There’s no way I’m joining.
Do you know how difficult it is?
Maybe this isn’t right for me.
The culture and language are so different.
What do you think?
With our youngest now
in his own assignment,
maybe we could serve where the need is greater,
like we did before the kids.
But we’re not that energetic couple anymore.
Maybe it’s too much.
I shared my concerns about pioneering
with someone who’s been doing it for a long time.
He reminded me of the apostle Peter’s example.
He was a fisherman by trade,
but Jesus knew
he could be so much more.
Peter hadn’t caught anything all night,
but with Jesus next to him, things would be different.
But Peter felt overwhelmed.
Simon,
stop being afraid.
From now on you will be catching men alive.
The ministry would be his life’s work.
The apostle Peter faced a situation
similar to mine in Syrian Antioch.
Initially, he associated freely
with Gentile Christians.
But then some from the congregation in Jerusalem visited,
and his fear of their opinion closed his heart.
Jehovah used
the apostle Paul to help Peter put aside
his fear of man.
So I prayed to Jehovah to help me open my heart wide.
We turned to the wisdom
of older ones,
and they reminded us of Peter’s ministry.
He may have been our age when he moved
to where the need was greater in Babylon.
They must have had concerns like ours.
Could they make the trip?
adapt to a different place?
But they trusted in Jehovah to help them succeed.
We can do the same.
If we overcome our doubts
and open our hearts wide,
we can conquer fear
and receive Jehovah’s blessing
to the full.
Peter was like us.
He loved Jehovah.
He loved his brothers.
He also had doubts and fears that sometimes held him back.
But Peter relied on Jehovah to conquer fear.
We can do the same.
Our prayers are not limited to asking Jehovah
for help with our concerns and our needs.
We can also ask Jehovah to help others.
We’ll see that in action in our next video.
I pray for my brothers and sisters every day
because I know Jehovah is the Hearer of prayer.
Ever since our baptism,
we as a family were fully engaged in Christian activities.
It was a busy yet fulfilling life.
I really loved preaching.
I enjoyed conducting Bible studies
and talking to others about the truth.
At one point, I was the only elder in the congregation.
I tried to make shepherding calls on everyone,
but I just did not have the time,
so I developed the habit
of praying for them many times during the day.
I would mention them individually by name.
I wanted Jehovah to protect
his precious sheep from Satan’s attacks.
Some time later,
my wife fell seriously ill.
After being hospitalized for a while,
I decided to take care of her at home.
I needed to step down from pioneering.
Kuniko served Jehovah faithfully until her death.
After a while, I became sick as well.
One morning, I felt especially bad and couldn’t move.
Fortunately, I managed to survive somehow,
but now I’m confined to a wheelchair.
I can no longer walk in the ministry as I used to
or handle congregation responsibilities.
I need help to change clothes and take a shower.
I get really depressed
when I think of the times when I was able to move around freely.
But Jehovah never forgets the love we’ve shown.
He is pleased to see us doing our very best
in whatever circumstances we are in.
I am limited in what I can do, but I can still pray.
In my prayers, I mention
the names of those in my congregation
and my personal friends.
I make a list of their names so as not to forget anyone.
Through jw.org®,
I read about the brothers in Russia being arrested
and the situation in Eritrea,
so I make sure to include them in my prayers.
The Governing Body and its helpers and those in full-time service
also need Jehovah’s support.
Jehovah is without a doubt the Hearer of prayer.
When I was the only elder in the congregation
and when my wife was sick in bed,
he listened to my prayers.
So I am confident that the prayers that I offer
will help my fellow friends.
Now I do what I can in service,
such as witnessing to caregivers.
When I meet those whom I have not seen for a long time
and tell them “I’ve been praying for you,”
they often tell me how it has really helped them.
Some even shed tears out of gratitude.
I feel happy too.
Although I’m getting physically weaker every day,
my prayers are becoming
more and more meaningful.
I want to cherish this precious gift of prayer
that Jehovah has given us
as long as I live.
Takeshi could easily dwell on all the things he can’t do.
Instead, he focuses on his brothers and sisters.
He prays for them every day.
And they’re not generic prayers.
He makes lists so that he doesn’t miss anyone,
and he goes to jw.org®
to learn about our brothers in need.
Why does he make this effort?
Takeshi said,
“I know [that] Jehovah is the Hearer of prayer.”
Whether we’re dealing with the effects of old age and illness
or with persecution and unrest,
we face a common enemy, Satan the Devil.
How does Jehovah help us win this spiritual warfare?
Brother Harold Corkern explains how in this Bethel morning worship.
Our text highlights the fact
that we are at war with Satan.
War is defined
as “a state of hostility
“accompanied by actions
“to conquer or to destroy
those viewed as the enemy.”
And the context of our text today at 1 Peter 5:8
talks about the type of enemy we have
—“a roaring lion, seeking to devour someone.”
And that expression “roaring” denotes
“the howl of a beast in fierce hunger.”
So we have a real enemy.
And that’s why the words of Jesus
are so meaningful for us when he gave the model prayer.
He said at Matthew 6:13:
“Do not bring us into temptation,
“but deliver [or, the footnote, “rescue”] us
from the wicked one.”
Now, other Bible translations,
like the King James Version or the Revised Standard Version,
use an expression like, “Deliver us from evil.”
Or the Contemporary English Version says:
“Protect us from evil.”
But that doesn’t convey the real fierceness of a real enemy, does it?
It’s more generic.
And so Jesus knew the Devil was real,
and he is a real enemy.
And the Devil has no remorse.
He’s fierce. He has no pity.
He will take a person and, with his traps and lures,
get him to do something bad in Jehovah’s eyes,
and then the person is overcome with guilt.
And then, like a fierce enemy,
the Devil comes along and stomps on him
and makes him feel worse because he caved in and sinned.
So how do we deal with such a powerful enemy?
Well, in war, there are soldiers.
So let’s use an expression
that the apostle Paul used to describe our situation.
Let’s open our Bibles, please, to the book of 2 Timothy.
In 2 Timothy chapter 2, we’re going to read verses 3 and 4
and talk for a few moments about our being soldiers.
Second Timothy 2:3:
“As a fine soldier of Christ Jesus,
“take your part in suffering adversity.
“No man serving as a soldier
“involves himself in the commercial businesses of life,
in order to gain the approval of the one who enrolled him as a soldier.”
We become soldiers of Christ
when we accept Jehovah’s arrangements
for salvation through Christ Jesus
and we dedicate our lives to him unreservedly
for our entire life.
We become a soldier and, like a soldier,
we know that it’s not going to be easy.
There are going to be hardships and trials.
And yet, a fine soldier
—his main objective is to stay loyal to his commanding officers
and to those who are giving instructions.
And likewise we know it’s not going to be easy.
It’s not easy, but we have chosen to become a soldier of Christ.
Now, a soldier, like this loyal one being described,
is far different from a mercenary.
A mercenary is one who hires himself out to fight,
but he may not have any devotion, really, to the cause.
He’s a hired man, and he’s doing it for the reward only
or for something else that he may gain.
But we’re not mercenaries.
We’re those with godly devotion, wholly devoted to Jehovah
and loyal to Christ so that we can be fine soldiers,
loyal and true.
Now, another aspect of soldiers is that they are identified
by their distinctive uniforms
or their particular fighting equipment.
And that way, it helps to identify
who’s the friend and who’s the foe in the middle of the battle.
Their appearance makes that possible.
Well, today, there is a clear difference, isn’t there,
between the soldiers of Satan
and the soldiers of Christ?
There’s great enmity, but there’s a sharp contrast
in appearance and attitude and disposition
and motivation and conduct.
And that’s why when we think about that,
we think about the contrast between “the works of the flesh”
described in Galatians chapter 5
and those who have the fruitage of God’s spirit.
There is such a strong distinction
between “one serving God and one not serving him.”
And that’s why, too,
we think about the type of armor we bear.
Ephesians chapter 6 says:
“Put on the complete suit of armor from God.”
So our very armor is from God.
We do not use the tactics and the methods of the Devil,
but we are clearly identified as a soldier of Christ.
And there can be no gray area here;
we’re either on one side or the other, correct?
For example, suppose that you’re a soldier,
and you’re on guard duty, and it’s evening,
and you see someone approaching, and you cry out:
“Halt! Who goes there?
Friend or foe?”
and you hear back, “I’m both.”
There’s an enemy.
You can’t be on both sides.
Now, what is another aspect of being a good soldier in this fight?
Well, let’s open our Bibles to Philippians chapter 1,
Philippians chapter 1, and we get to the concept of unity
and working closely together in peace,
because an army needs to be unified.
Philippians 1:27 says:
“Only behave in a manner worthy of the good news about the Christ,
“so that whether I come and see you or I am absent,
“I may hear about you and learn
“that you are standing firm in one spirit,
“with one soul [and the footnote, or “with one accord”],
“striving side by side for the faith of the good news,
“and in no way being frightened by your opponents.
“This very thing is a proof of destruction for them,
but of salvation for you; and this is from God.”
Well, we have this matter of unity —don’t we?—
shoulder to shoulder, side by side.
And yet, one of the tactics of the Devil
is to get us divided and disjointed
and fighting among ourselves.
To turn the enemy on itself is a very effective war strategy.
Even Jehovah used that —remember?—
against his enemies.
At 2 Chronicles 20:20-23,
there was the attack “of Ammon, Moab,
and the mountainous region of Seir” against Judah.
What did Jehovah do?
He confused them.
They struck down each other; they helped destroy one another.
And the Devil, in a very sinister way, uses that same approach.
How?
Well, if he can get us to not get along with each other
and turn on one another,
then that’s a very effective tactic.
In fact, we remember the expression
at Ephesians 4:26, 27 about getting along:
“Be wrathful, but do not sin;
“do not let the sun set while you are still angry;
do not give the Devil an opportunity.”
So when he sees discord and disunity,
he can really amplify that.
So we have to remember who our real enemies are.
Now, our brothers may disappoint us; they may frustrate us;
they may hurt us at times because of imperfections.
But they’re not the enemy.
The Devil and his hordes —they are the enemies.
So we don’t get to fighting with the wrong person.
We keep in mind that our brothers are with us.
And, in this connection
(we just read it in that scripture in Philippians),
it talked about not being afraid.
And do you remember something about being afraid
when it related to a soldier in Israel’s army?
Deuteronomy 20:8 says:
“The officers should also ask the people,
“‘Who is fearful and fainthearted?
“‘He should return to his house,
so that he may not cause his brothers to lose heart as he has.’”
Well, we do have an effect on each other.
Can you imagine being in Joshua’s army,
getting ready to battle, and to your left is a soldier?
And as you’re about ready to leave for battle,
he says to you: “We’re going to die.
“We’re not going to come back.
Say goodbye to your family. This is it.”
Or he may say,
“I’m not sure Joshua has Jehovah’s backing like Moses did.”
All of that would be terrible.
And so anyone in that category was to go home
because they would have an effect on others.
How grateful, though, we are that we have positive, courageous brothers
who trust in Jehovah,
examples in the Bible, and also modern-day examples,
just like our brothers in Russia!
Well, as soldiers in this battle, we’re ‘not ignorant of Satan’s designs.’
And yet, he studies us very carefully, and he knows our weaknesses.
The September 1, 1988, Watchtower had an article
“Stand Firm Against Satan’s Machinations,”
and in that, it said the Devil knows what our weaknesses are.
But do we?
If we don’t identify them and then correct them,
we will be defenseless at times.
But it takes honesty and humility
and an earnest desire to address that which is bad.
Otherwise, we become a victim.
So we need to ask: ‘What are my weaknesses?
Do I identify them? Do I work on them?’
And yet, with Jehovah’s help, we can come off victorious in this battle.
First Peter 5:10 says that ‘Jehovah will finish our training;
he will make us firm; he will make us strong.’
So with Jehovah’s help, we can succeed.
So may we all continue as fine soldiers of Christ,
trusting in Jehovah,
and win the battle against the enemy—the Devil.
As Brother Corkern mentioned, Satan has no pity.
He’ll try everything to lure us to sin against Jehovah.
Last year, the revised New World Translation in Spanish was released.
This was exciting news for millions of our brothers and sisters.
Since Spanish is the most widely spoken language among Jehovah’s Witnesses,
this took special effort.
Enjoy the following report.
Soon after the Governing Body released
the revised English edition of the New World Translation,
they decided to revise the Spanish edition.
They wanted it to be a modern, understandable translation
for the entire Spanish-speaking world.
Spanish is the mother tongue of around 480 million people.
And it is also the most widely spoken language
among Jehovah’s Witnesses.
This translation project would be a unique challenge.
It eventually took four and a half years to complete.
Why did it take so long?
Apart from the translation process itself,
the work was complicated
by the wide geographic range
of these Hispanic countries
and their different cultures.
This diversity meant that in different countries
the same Spanish word could mean different things.
In other cases, the word may be unknown
in certain areas or even sound objectionable to some.
To overcome these difficulties,
the translators used 100 outside readers
from many different countries
to review the translated text progressively.
These readers were of different ages, cultures, and backgrounds.
These outside readers regularly received chapters of the Bible electronically,
and then they introduced their suggested revisions.
The translation teams took note of all their recommendations,
and in some cases, they also sent them specific inquiries.
Every verse was checked by 130 different people.
Naturally, all of this took time.
The work was finished in the spring of 2019.
But then another challenge arose.
We needed to print millions of Bibles
to satisfy the demand of the Spanish-speaking field.
This was a huge job
for our printing presses in the United States and Japan.
Despite working night and day,
the task would take a long time.
And naturally, everyone wanted to have the Bible right away.
Right at the Madrid international convention,
the Governing Body decided to release
the Bible in digital format.
This was several months before all the Bibles could be printed.
The highlight of the Friday morning convention program
was when Brother Lösch presented the newly revised Bible.
But there was another surprise!
Since at the convention
most brothers and sisters had their phones and tablets with them,
they were able to immediately download the revised Bible.
How was that possible?
Over 500 portable Wi-Fi devices were distributed
among each of the 11 convention venues
in Spain that were tied in with the Madrid stadium.
During the lunch break on Friday,
practically everyone in attendance could download
the revised Spanish edition of the New World Translation.
More than 1,200 volunteers were trained
to give technical support to those who needed it.
In this way, the brothers started to use the revised translation
right away during the afternoon program.
We laughed and cried with joy.
We knew it was a gift from Jehovah,
which he was giving us at that moment.
And also, we felt so happy because we’d been waiting a long time for it.
What I like most about this revision
is that it’s very easy to understand.
Sometimes I think,
‘But was this what we had before?’
It seems that it reaches my heart much quicker.
As you use it,
you realize that many scriptures
have been adjusted and that the faithful slave
has worked very hard to make it easier to understand.
Without a doubt, this revised edition of the New World Translation
is a wonderful gift for all our Spanish-speaking brothers.
The Word of God has power,
and this will be a powerful tool
to help many people get to know Jehovah.
This month’s theme was
“Pray Continually, So That You May Not Enter Into Temptation.”
By trusting in prayer,
Narciso made major changes
in his life and resisted temptations
that tested his humility.
The apostle Peter’s example showed us
how to overcome fear so that we can show more love
for Jehovah and our brothers.
Rather than dwell on his limitations,
Takeshi finds joy in praying
for his brothers and sisters every day.
And the song “Forgive Freely”
reminds us that we can imitate Jehovah’s quality of forgiveness
to heal the pain of being hurt
by someone we love.
Before we conclude, let’s visit our brothers and sisters
in the Tierra del Fuego province of Argentina.
Tierra del Fuego
is a group of islands off the southernmost tip
of the South American mainland.
The main island rises to mountain glaciers
and peaks of nearly 8,000 feet,
or 2,400 meters.
Here daylight varies greatly throughout the year
—from about 17 hours during summer
to some 7 hours during winter.
But no matter how much sunlight there is,
there can be wind, ice,
and snow every season of the year.
Three congregations are in the city of Ushuaia on the main island.
To attend assemblies, the brothers
have to cross a mountain range
—a trip of about 125 miles, or 200 kilometers.
Sometimes snow and ice make the roads impassable.
Our brothers are out in the ministry no matter what the weather has in store.
In the winter, the sun doesn’t rise high enough to be seen
above the mountains in some parts of Ushuaia.
When days are short, the brothers adapt
and start preaching later to make the best use of sunlight.
The brothers have organized a campaign
to preach in rural communities and on remote islands,
such as Navarino Island, across the Beagle Channel.
Recently, some made a special effort to learn English
so that a good witness
can be given to the many tourists who visit.
There are over 300 publishers
and some 47 regular pioneers
in Ushuaia’s three congregations.
They’re conducting 286 Bible studies.
Our brothers and sisters
in Ushuaia, Tierra del Fuego,
send their warm love and greetings!
From the World Headquarters of Jehovah’s Witnesses,
this is JW Broadcasting.

en.text: Sharks have skin
that protects them in a unique way.
Left unchecked,
microorganisms would establish colonies on the shark’s skin,
which in turn would attract larger parasites
to latch on to the shark.
If that happened,
the shark’s health and ability to swim would suffer.
But the fact is
that the shark’s skin remains virtually free of parasites.
How?
Sharkskin is covered in complex scales
called dermal denticles.
Though they look like tiny fish scales,
they are built more like mammal teeth
with a smooth enamel surface.
This very smooth surface,
together with a complex structure
of tiny ridges,
makes it very hard for microscopic organisms
to grab on to the shark’s skin.
If one does latch on,
those same ridges channel water
to flow faster and wash off the hitchhiker.
So this single design element
resists parasites in two different ways.
But that’s not all.
The denticles’ unique shape
creates small areas of suction
all along the shark’s body,
enhancing its ability to thrust itself forward as it swims.
These advantages allow sharks like the shortfin mako
to reach burst speeds
of 74 kilometers (46 mi) per hour!
Scientists are engineering artificial surfaces
that mimic sharkskin
to help boats and planes
to be more fuel efficient.
This nature-inspired technology could also prevent
harmful germs from growing on hospital surfaces
without having to use toxic disinfectants.
What do you think?
Did sharkskin simply evolve?
Or was it designed?

cn.text: 鲨鱼的皮是非常特殊的防护层
如果鲨鱼没有这层保护
身上就会滋生大量的微生物
还会引来其他寄生虫附着在鲨鱼身上
这不仅会影响鲨鱼的健康
还会降低它的游泳能力
但事实是
鲨鱼全身上下几乎都没有寄生虫
鲨鱼的皮为什么这么神奇呢？
鲨鱼的表皮
覆盖着一层结构复杂
锯齿状的小鳞片
通常称为盾鳞
盾鳞看起来
像小小的鱼鳞
但它在构造上
更像哺乳类动物的牙齿
盾鳞上覆盖着一层光滑的牙釉质
又称珐琅质
盾鳞除了表面光滑
还有微小的沟槽
这些都让微生物难以附着在鲨鱼皮上
这些沟槽可以加快水流的速度
冲走不速之客
盾鳞的这两个特点
让寄生虫难以附着在鲨鱼身上
不过盾鳞的作用还不只这样
盾鳞的特殊形状可以在鲨鱼的身体周围
产生小范围的吸力
让鲨鱼能游得更快
例如，灰鲭鲨的瞬间速度
就可达每小时74公里
科学家正在研发类似鲨鱼皮的材料
希望可以用在船只和飞机的外壳上
减少油耗
这样的材料或许也可以应用在
医疗器具的表面上
有效地抑制细菌滋生
也无须使用强效杀菌剂
你认为怎样？
鲨鱼的皮是进化或演化而来的
还是经过设计的呢？

titles.en: Was It Designed? The Shark’s Skin
titles.cn: 有设计者吗？鲨鱼的皮

ko.text: 느헤미야는 어떻게 그들이 온갖 어려움 속에서도
기쁨을 잃지 않게 도울 수 있었을까요?
성벽을 재건한 일은 많이 알려져 있지만,
사실 훨씬 더 많은 일들이 있었죠.
왕에게 술잔 올리는 일을 하고 있었습니다.
거기서 우리 백성이 여호와를 섬기는 모습을 떠올리면
우리랑 같이 가야 될 거 같아.
백성들이 여호와의 계명을 지키지 못해 죄를 지은 건 사실이지만,
도움이 필요한 그들을 돕지 않는 저 자신도
제 조상들이 묻혀 있는 도시가 황폐되고
성문들도 불에 탄 채 그대로 있습니다.
또 이 종에게 은혜를 베풀어 주신다면,
저와 함께 온 군대와 그 많은 목재들은
하지만 우리가 이스라엘 백성을 위해 온 것을
적들은 여호와의 백성을 계속 손에 쥐고
우리 백성 중에 저 사람 땅을
근데 왜 우리에게 도와 달라고 하지 않았소?
일단 저거부터 치워야 할 것 같은데.
이겨 내는 걸 보면서 큰 격려를 받았죠.
아 그리고, 집세 안 낼 거야?
아니, 그냥 와서 집안일 좀 돕고
뭐 정 싫으면 할 수 없고.
자기 딸처럼 잘 돌봐 주겠다고 했어.
거기 가면 더 잘 살 수 있어.
게셈, 자넨 사마리아 군대를 이끌고 이쪽으로 움직여.
계속 이렇게 두 손 놓고 있을 거예요?
아니 아직도 상황 파악이 안 되세요?
왜 우리가 이런 일을 당하는 거죠?
우리 하느님께서 우리를 위해 싸우실 겁니다.
여, 오늘 일 좀 했나 보다, 응?
우리가 뭘 어떻게 할 수 있겠습니까.
이 약속을 지키지 않는 모든 사람을
느헤미야는 우리가 아직도 팔팔한 줄 아나 봐.
그동안 뼈 빠지게 고생한 건 모르고.
이게 다 하늘에서 뚝 떨어진 줄 알어?
게셈, 이제 자네 계획대로 해 보지.
알아, 그냥 한번 찔러 보는 거겠지.
여호와여, 부디 제 손을 강하게 해 주소서.
내 말대로 하는 게 좋을 거요.
불가능해 보이는 일을 해낼 수 있었죠.

en.text: As we learned in our audio drama,
the Jews returned to Jerusalem
to rebuild the temple in 537 B.C.E.
And by 515 B.C.E., it was finally completed.
However, the city’s walls were still left in ruins.
Jehovah’s time had now come to rebuild the walls,
and he used the faithful man Nehemiah
to take the lead in this work.
This would be a massive undertaking for the Jews.
And once again, there were opposers.
Nehemiah told the nation of Israel
that “the joy of Jehovah is your stronghold.”
How could he encourage them to be joyful
despite all the opposition?
What lessons can we learn from their example?
There are many,
but here are three to think about as you watch:
What role did prayer play in helping Nehemiah
to be a courageous person for Jehovah?
In addition to direct attacks,
what schemes did the enemies employ
to oppose the work?
Despite setbacks,
what was Nehemiah’s main source of joy?
Got it?
All right, then, with that in mind, please sit back
and enjoy the following video presentation
“The Joy of Jehovah Is Your Stronghold.”
It was a privilege to have a share
in the restoration of Jehovah’s worship.
People know we rebuilt the wall,
but there is so much more to the story.
Let’s start at the beginning.
In the 20th year of King Artaxerxes Longimanus,
I was in Shushan the palace.
I was cupbearer to the king.
He trusted me with his life.
Although I was far from Jerusalem,
I found great joy just thinking
about our people there serving Jehovah
—until one day when I received a visit
from my brother Hanani.
That visit changed everything.
What’s going on, Hanani?
How are our people?
Not good.
The conditions are disgraceful.
The walls of Jerusalem are broken down,
and its gates have been burned with fire.
What about the temple?
It stands,
but the services are nothing but empty rituals.
Most of the people and the priests ignore God’s Law.
You have to return with us.
For days, my conscience plagued me.
Would the king even allow me to go?
Our people had sinned
by not keeping Jehovah’s commandments,
but now I felt as if I were sinning
by not helping them in their time of need.
I begged Jehovah to grant me success.
Nehemiah,
why are you so gloomy when you’re not sick?
This can be nothing but gloominess of heart.
Why should I not look gloomy
when the city,
the place where my forefathers are buried,
lies in ruins,
and its gates have been consumed by fire?
Nehemiah, what is this?
Speak frankly.
What are you seeking?
At once, I prayed to the God of the heavens.
If it pleases the king
and if your servant has found favor with you,
send me to Judah,
to the city where my forefathers are buried,
and let me rebuild it.
You may go.
Jehovah was with us.
The king gave me supplies,
an army,
and an appointment as governor.
We were on our way to help rebuild Jerusalem’s walls.
I had seen a portion of the city,
but it wasn’t until I rose
by night to inspect the walls
that I saw just how badly God’s city had been treated.
Wait here.
I couldn’t believe the destruction.
The time had come
to reveal Jehovah’s purpose for Jerusalem.
I gathered the leaders.
Who is this man?
I’m told he’s Nehemiah, cupbearer to the king.
What does he want from us?
Men!
The holy city is completely vulnerable.
Let us rebuild the walls of Jerusalem,
so that this disgrace will not continue.
But what will our neighbors think?
Yes, we have many powerful enemies.
Artaxerxes commissioned me
to rebuild the walls and the entire city.
Didn’t you see the horsemen he sent
and all the timber?
He gave it all!
Brothers, the good hand of our God was upon me.
He is the one to fear, not men.
He will give us success.
Not everyone was happy
that we had come to do something good
for the people of Israel.
So that’s what this Nehemiah is up to.
Geshem, do you see what I’m seeing?
Without a wall,
we can keep the Jews under control.
If they rebuild it,
the Jews won’t need our land or resources.
That means he’s planning to rebel.
We can’t let him.
We must act, and act together.
Are you with me?
You have my support.
And mine, as always.
Good!
We must go to Jerusalem to keep an eye on Nehemiah.
The opposers wanted to maintain control
and to profit from Jehovah’s people.
They wasted little time trying to intimidate us.
Who are these?
That’s Sanballat, governor of Samaria.
Next to him is Tobiah, an Ammonite official
and landowner to many of our people.
They all look up to him.
That’s Geshem;
he’s a very wealthy Arabian and close ally to Sanballat.
Nehemiah, are you rebelling against the king?
The king himself gave us the authority.
To rebuild the city and the wall?
To rebuild the city and the wall
is what the king expects us to do.
Why did you not consult with me?
I am the governor of Samaria.
Well, yes, but the king appointed
Nehemiah as governor of Judah.
So why have you not asked for our help?
We worship Jehovah too.
We’ve sacrificed to him for generations.
Along with sacrifices to all of your other gods.
The God of the heavens
is the One that will grant us success,
and we, his servants,
will get up and build.
No one should let his religious beliefs
come before national unity.
You have neither share
nor claim nor memorial in Jerusalem.
Sanballat,
could it be you
who is rebelling against the highest King of all?
Despite opposition,
the people worked strenuously.
Nehemiah, these things have to go somewhere.
Their struggles went far beyond building a wall.
Jehovah remembers brothers like Peleth.
Seeing how he dealt with personal challenges
strengthened my faith.
Peleth.
Raham.
We’ll never finish this work.
It’s nothing but rubble.
At least we’re trying to make a change.
Always an optimist.
By the way, you’re late on your rent
—again.
Raham, I’m sorry;
I need more time.
With the work on the wall, . . .
I have enough troubles.
Look, if I don’t get payment
by the end of the month,
you and your family are out.
Is there anything we can do?
Maybe I can work it off till we get caught up.
Seriously?
You don’t have time to work it off,
but maybe your daughter can help.
She can come stay with us.
As a slave?
No, I’ll hire her to help Azubah
—to pay off your debt.
Look, I’m trying to help,
but you don’t have many options here, my friend.
Think about it.
So Raham spoke to me today.
About what?
He wants to hire Simcha to help Azubah in the house.
He says he’ll care for her like his own daughter.
Imma, I’ve known Raham and Azubah
ever since I came here with Ezra.
Raham helped us.
Our house belongs to him.
I don’t trust him.
He wants our Simcha to live with him?
Imma, . . .
What about Jehovah’s command
that parents raise their own children?
Don’t you want her to have a better life?
I-I cannot agree
to having her live apart from us,
even if we have to survive on gleanings.
How do you know we’ll survive at all?
Because Jehovah always takes care
of those who love and obey him.
Men like Peleth threw their burden on Jehovah
and kept working.
Sanballat set up camp near Jerusalem
to keep an eye on our progress.
So, what is it?
My lord.
Yes?
The wall
—it’s up to half its height all around the city.
This has gone too far!
Geshem, how long will it take
to assemble an attack force?
Attack force?
My lord, Sanballat, an attack on the Jews
would be an attack on the king.
What are you talking about?
He’s right.
Nehemiah has authorization from Artaxerxes himself.
You saw how many horsemen the king sent with him.
Yes!
Would you be talking like this if those horsemen
were still here?
And they can come back.
Nonsense!
Never mind the horsemen.
This is my province!
Out here, I decide what to do.
Now, we need to threaten them.
Geshem, you bring Samaritan troops
and come in from this way.
They’re preparing to attack us!
How do you know that?
I heard them talking.
Brothers, please.
Have they attacked anyone yet?
They must have.
He saw something.
Are you going to wait until they start killing us?
Of course not!
Of course not!
Hanani,
post men by families at the lowest parts of the wall
—at all the exposed places.
Yes, Nehemiah.
That’s not going to work.
Brothers,
if we let mere threats frighten us into stopping,
they will have achieved their goal.
It’s no use. Don’t you see?
These people hate what we’re doing.
They hate us.
You don’t have to live and work around them like we do.
Brothers,
where is your faith?
It is Jehovah’s will that we build this wall.
If it is really Jehovah’s will,
then why are we getting all this opposition?
Maybe this isn’t the right time.
Besides, this work is too much for us.
We’re worn out.
Why do we need a wall anyway?
To protect Jehovah’s people.
Brothers,
do not be afraid of them.
Remember Jehovah,
who is great and awe-inspiring;
and fight for your brothers,
your sons and daughters,
your wives and homes.
So when you hear the sound of the horn,
gather together to where we are.
Our God will fight for us.
Listen for this signal.
The threats aren’t working.
The next sound they hear will be our battle cry.
Wait!
We already spoke about this.
A direct attack would be seditious.
Besides, they’ve armed themselves.
Wait!
My-my lord,
Geshem is right.
We’d never get away with this.
Don’t you recall who commissioned Nehemiah?
It was the king.
It was the king of Persia, let me remind you.
Nehemiah is setting himself up as a king.
I recommend we turn the accusation of sedition
against Nehemiah.
That’s brilliant!
Yes,
he will beg for our help.
Let’s go back to Samaria.
Hanani,
you look like you’ve been working.
I must smell like it too.
Yes!
Yes, you do.
Brothers!
Brothers, we are well on our way to completing the wall.
Jehovah is helping us,
but we must not let our hands drop.
From now on,
we will all spend the night inside Jerusalem.
We will take turns keeping watch.
Hanani will give out assignments.
Good work today.
Everyone was working hard on the wall.
But there were more issues to contend with.
My brothers, how can I help you?
Nehemiah, we, with our sons and daughters, are many.
We need food to stay alive.
We gave our fields and vineyards
and houses as security to get grain during
the food shortage.
We borrowed money
on our fields and our vineyards to pay the king’s tribute.
And we’ve had to sell some of our children into slavery.
We’re powerless to stop this
because our fields and vineyards belong to others.
Thank you for bringing this to my attention.
I must ponder all this.
Thank you, Nehemiah.
Thank you.
Hanani, please tell all the nobles
and deputy rulers to come to me
first thing tomorrow morning.
With God’s help, we can make this right.
Men of Judah,
each of you is demanding interest from your brother.
You should be ashamed of yourselves.
Should you not walk in the fear of our God
so that the nations, our enemies,
cannot reproach us?
Let us, please, stop this lending on interest.
Please restore to them their fields,
vineyards, olive groves, houses,
and the interest.
Nehemiah, I will restore the fields this day at sunset.
We all will restore these things to our brothers.
Before Jehovah,
do you swear to these promises?
We do!
May the true God shake out from his house
every man who does not carry out this promise.
Amen!
Meshullam,
we must inform Tobiah about this.
This will be successful.
Jehovah will bless it.
Raham!
I bring good news.
Is that so?
Yes.
We have your rent.
Oh?
Come by anytime and collect it.
But I thought we—
What about Simcha?
She’ll be staying with us.
Well, how were you able to put it together so quickly?
Jehovah always takes care of those
who love and obey him.
Ever since Nehemiah got here,
things have been getting better and better.
Nehemiah thinks we’re still as young
as when we came here with Ezra.
I’ve worked hard.
But now Nehemiah treats us like it all fell out of heaven,
and we just have to pick it up.
I worked hard for what I have, didn’t I?
Yes, you worked hard.
If I give back my fields,
what am I to eat?
What am I to drink?
What’s wrong with lending on interest?
You borrow, you pay with interest.
Raham, Jehovah just wants us
to treat our brothers fairly, doesn’t he?
Haven’t you heard a word I said?
I treat everyone fairly!
Then why are you so angry?
I’m not angry!
Why are you talking to me like this?
I just feel betrayed.
By whom?
By the people I’ve lent money to!
What can I do about it?
Only what a wife is supposed to do!
Give me a son!
If not a son, then a daughter.
I cannot give you what Jehovah does not give us.
One day,
it will be too late.
I say we write a letter to the king.
Well, let’s see what the boy reports when he returns.
My lord, Sanballat.
Now what?
The wall has no more gaps.
What?
How can they advance so quickly?
Also, there’s a letter for Tobiah.
Nehemiah is forcing
landlords to return their fields to the original owners.
We’re running out of time.
Enough!
Tell this to Nehemiah:
“Come, and let us set a time
to meet together in the Valley Plain of Ono.”
They’re trying to lure me away from Jerusalem
to do me harm.
Please, tell your master:
“I am engaged in a great work,
“and I am not able to go down.
“Why should the work stop
while I leave it to come to you?”
They sent me the same message several times.
Each time I gave them the same response.
My lord, he has rejected your offer a fourth time.
Geshem,
it’s time to implement your plan.
Tobiah,
write this down:
“Among the nations it has been heard,
“and Geshem is also saying it,
“that you and the Jews
“are scheming to rebel.
That is why you are building the wall.”
Yes?
Give this to Nehemiah.
Tell your master:
“None of the things you are saying have taken place.
You are making them up out of your own imagination.”
They’re bluffing.
They’re trying to frighten us into stopping the work.
Yes, they know that the king won’t change his decree.
But believe me, they won’t stop.
Jehovah, I pray,
strengthen my hands.
What can we do to stop him?
We don’t have much time.
The wall is almost complete.
Sanballat,
I think I know a way.
Shemaiah, you called for me.
Yes!
Quickly!
You are in great danger.
And so am I because I know about it.
Talk sense, man!
What danger?
They’re coming to kill you—by night!
We must go into the temple and close the doors.
Shemaiah,
should a man like me run away?
You don’t understand.
What would that do to the spirit of the entire nation?
It’s the only safe place.
Besides, I’m not a priest.
If I entered the temple,
that would be valid reason to kill me.
I will not go in.
That decision would be foolish, Nehemiah.
Oh, I see!
Tobiah and Sanballat put you up to this,
didn’t they, you hypocrite?
May Jehovah remember them
and all of you false prophets
who keep trying to frighten me.
Come, Hanani,
we have work to do.
Argh!
We just kept working day and night.
But before we knew it,
we were finishing the very last section of the wall.
Jehovah helped us to achieve the impossible.
We were tired,
but we discovered something we had lost
—joy.
Nehemiah, the wall is complete!
Yeah! Yes!
That’s it.
In just 52 days.
My lord, it’s from Shemaiah.
What does it say?
The wall is complete.
Only the doors are left to be put in.
Sanballat, we must act quickly.
Sanballat . . .
Stop it, Tobiah.
No, there’s still time.
Write that letter to the king.
Tobiah,
don’t you see?
God must be helping the Jews.
It’s over.
We’ll lose all control over them.
This isn’t over.
Rebuilding the walls was only the beginning.
We would definitely need God’s help
for what was coming next.
