title: 제자 삼는 일에서 기쁨을 얻고 있는 세계 전역의 우리 형제들

ko.text: 우리도 그와 같은 마음이 들지 않습니까!
세계에서 가장 인구가 많은 두 나라인
인구가 가장 많은 나라가 될 것입니다.
아직 진리를 접해 보지 못했기 때문에
임명되지 않은 구역에 사는 사람들에게 증거하기 위해
큰 기쁨을 얻을 수 있다는 점을
아시아와 아메리카 대륙 사이의 태평양에 위치한
우린 여호와를 첫째 자리에 둘 때에만
여호와께서 연구생의 마음을 보시고 축복해 주”신 겁니다.
그 비결 네 가지를 생각해 보죠.
형제들은 제자 삼는 일을 할 때
그는 증인들이 날이 덥든 비가 오든
오늘 살펴본 것과 같은 경험들을 보면
여러분이 전 세계의 형제 자매들과 함께
생명을 구하는 일을 하고 있다는 점을 기억하십시오.
그렇게 한다면 큰 기쁨을 얻게 될 것입니다.

en.text: If you were asked to think of two men
in the first century who were zealous disciple-makers,
who would come to your mind?
You may be thinking of Paul and Barnabas.
Together, they traveled extensively,
preaching the good news and helping many
to learn the wonderful truth about Jehovah.
This work brought joy not only to them but others too.
Acts 15:3 states:
“So after being escorted
“partway by the congregation,
“these men continued on
“through both Phoenicia and Samaria,
“relating in detail the conversion
“of people of the nations
and bringing great joy to all the brothers.”
Their shared experiences
were a great source of joy to the brotherhood.
They all felt encouraged
and united as one spiritual family.
So, too, today, we have many like Paul and Barnabas,
who are actively working to find honesthearted ones.
Let’s quickly review the numbers
and see what our spiritual family’s united efforts
have accomplished during the 2019 service year.
The good news was preached in 240 lands.
The average number of publishers
each month reached over 8.4 million!
More than two billion hours
were spent in the field.
Also, you’ll be pleased to know
that the number baptized
surpassed 300,000
for the first time in 20 years!
That’s, on average, 5,843 people
symbolizing their dedication
to Jehovah every weekend.
And there’s great potential
for millions more to embrace the truth.
On average, 9.6 million Bible studies
were conducted each month,
and almost 21 million attended the Memorial.
We praise Jehovah for this growth
and thank you for your share in this great increase.
The Governing Body received
some beautiful experiences and reports this past service year,
and they wanted to share that joy with all of you now.
Would you like to hear some of these reports
and meet some of our hardworking brothers and sisters?
Well, then, let’s go!
We’ll meet publishers from six regions of the earth
and hear in their own words the effect
that the disciple-making work has on them.
Here’s a quick peek.
We’ll see some of their unique challenges.
When it rains,
there is so much mud everywhere
that we need to remove our shoes and hold them in our hands.
We’ll meet ones who made personal sacrifices.
When I turned 60 and retired,
my wife and I decided to serve where the need is greater.
This brother can see, but he cannot walk,
and me, I can walk but cannot see.
We’ll see the impact the truth can have on new ones.
It made me happy.
Yet, can I really dare believe that?
I was actually sort of in shock,
and it really put a spotlight on who I really was.
What bad habits did some have at first?
What pressures did they face?
And how did they overcome them?
One day she asked her to choose
between family and Jehovah.
Hopefully that whets your appetite for what’s to come.
Now, as we take you around the world,
enjoy the stories of your brothers and sisters
and watch for clues to what contributed to their joy.
Let’s begin with Africa.
It stretches from the Mediterranean
past the golden Sahara
through mountains and savannas
to the Cape of Good Hope.
This continent is known for the enormous diversity
and richness of its wildlife.
Africa’s population, about 1.3 billion people,
is growing faster than any other part of the world.
More than 1,500 languages are spoken here.
The first Christian from Africa,
the Ethiopian eunuch mentioned in Acts chapter 8,
likely brought the good news back with him
to Ethiopia when he returned home.
Today, over 1.7 million publishers
are making disciples throughout this vast continent.
Let’s visit our brothers and sisters in Africa’s most populous country:
Nigeria.
More than 360,000 publishers
are sharing the good news with Nigeria’s over 200 million people.
The territory is highly diverse
—more than 500 languages and 250 ethnic groups.
It’s so encouraging to see the response to the good news!
Some 870,000 Bible studies
are being conducted and, on average,
273 are baptized each week.
This is the Utonkon Congregation in Benue state.
Here, 51 publishers and 4 regular pioneers
are having good results despite a challenging territory.
Preaching in the Utonkon territory
is enjoyable.
It is just that it is accompanied
by some problems.
One is that the territories are very far apart,
and two, the roads are not good.
It takes us three hours to get to some territories.
When it rains, there is so much mud everywhere
that we need to remove our shoes and hold them in our hands.
Whether householders are church-goers, Muslims,
or traditional healers, they listen.
Many even accept our invitation to attend the meetings
despite the travel challenges.
So it makes us very happy to see
that in spite of far territories and bad roads,
we see good results.
I am enjoying my life now,
but when I lost my sight,
I thought it was all over.
As a carpenter, I wondered how I would be able
to do my carpentry.
The thought of it worried me so much.
But as I began to learn about Jehovah from the Bible,
I came to realize that there was hope.
That negative thinking (that my life was over)
disappeared from my mind.
So I am very happy now.
I am joyful.
There is a brother named Joseph.
This brother can see, but he cannot walk,
and me, I can walk but cannot see.
I hold his wheelchair
and push while he directs it.
This has helped us to meet many of our Bible students.
Before now, we were few that went out in the field as pioneers,
but now we are many.
This shows that the example has helped other people,
because when they see someone who cannot walk
and someone who cannot see are pioneering,
they conclude that they can pioneer too.
This is the experience of one of my relatives.
His name is Cletus.
He was very kind to me.
He would hold my hand and assist me to the meetings at the Kingdom Hall.
When he got to the Kingdom Hall, he would leave for his church.
But as he noticed how I preached and attended meetings,
the joy I radiated,
the way we treated other people,
and our knowledge of the Scriptures,
he was impressed
and began asking many questions.
The answers he got were quite different from what he had learned,
what they told him in church.
They continued telling him to “get out of there”
and that he should not talk to me again.
He studied the Bible, concluded his study, and got baptized.
Now he serves as a ministerial servant.
Sometimes they used to assign talks to both
of us to handle as a symposium,
and this made me see Cletus as a spiritual brother
in the organization and the congregation.
This gives me joy and makes me very happy.
When people notice our activities,
they usually praise Jehovah and encourage us
to do more since they know that the work we do
is not by our power,
but it is Jehovah who empowers us.
It is true that I am blind,
but I can see Jehovah.
I am helping other people see Jehovah’s hand in our lives.
Even people who are disabled
can bring praise to Jehovah.
I have nothing to do other than to be joyful
and praise Jehovah for my life.
We share your joy, Brother Igbo!
Doesn’t it touch our hearts to see Gabriel and Joseph
helping each other in the pioneer work?
Their example encourages others to ask,
‘What prevents me from pioneering?’
Perhaps we’re moved to ask that question too.
And did you notice what spurred Cletus to action?
He observed the conduct of Gabriel
and other Witnesses in the congregation.
What do we learn?
That our Christian conduct often speaks louder
than even the most eloquent words.
Now we go to the largest continent in the world: Asia.
Asia is home to three fifths of the world’s people,
including some 760,000 Jehovah’s Witnesses.
The geography of Asia ranges
from tundra
to coral reefs
—from Earth’s tallest peak, Mt. Everest,
to its lowest land surface, the Dead Sea.
Asia’s cultural diversity is greater than any other continent.
The two most populated countries in the world
—China and India—
are here in Asia.
Let’s visit our brothers in India.
With a growing population of about 1.3 billion people,
India is on track to become the world’s most populous country
within a decade.
Imagine the potential for growth in India!
With 90 percent of the population
having not yet received a witness,
our 50,000 brothers and sisters have plenty of work to do.
The good news is being preached
in territory that includes mountain ranges, plains and plateaus,
villages, and some of the world’s largest cities.
Hyderabad is in south-central India.
This is the Hyderabad RTC Cross Roads Congregation
in the heart of the city.
Here, 94 publishers,
including 17 regular pioneers,
are conducting 95 Bible studies.
They were delighted to have 252 attend last year’s Memorial.
Let’s meet Sangram.
His story actually begins in another part of India,
where he learned the truth with the help of Alex and Anne Das.
My wife and I serve in the Pandharpur Sign-Language Group.
Currently, there are only three publishers
—me, my wife,
and another brother who is deaf.
We have contact with around 100 deaf ones in our territory.
Each week, 50 to 60 deaf ones attend the meetings.
When they come, they bring their deaf friends with them.
They also bring their relatives.
We are so happy to see them come regularly for the meetings
in spite of the opposition from their families
—sometimes even severe opposition.
They are progressing well spiritually.
We are really happy to see their spiritual advancement.
When I turned 60 and retired,
my wife and I decided to serve where the need is greater.
To our surprise, we were asked to support the sign-language field.
At that time,
we did not have any experience in sign language.
Then our circuit overseer asked us
if we were ready to move to where the need is greater.
He asked if we would move to Latur,
a city that was 521 miles (838 km) from our home.
Once we reached the city,
we were overjoyed to see the interest of the deaf ones.
So we decided to stay there.
Not long after we arrived there,
we met a priest whose name is Sangram.
He was the leader of a deaf association,
and he was short-tempered.
Since we wanted to meet him often,
we invited him to our home to discuss the daily text.
He came regularly at seven o’clock for daily text discussions.
When we moved here, we did not know how to sign very well;
both my wife and I knew almost nothing.
But after we met Sangram
and started to teach him the Bible, we, in turn,
started to learn sign language from him.
We were very happy.
We were really very happy.
As soon as we started studying the Bible with Sangram,
he made changes in his life in line with the Bible principles.
He changed his hairstyle.
He left the deaf association of which he was the leader.
And even his personality changed.
He stopped responding angrily to those who provoked him.
We are so happy
about the Bible discussions we had with him,
because with these his life changed completely.
Soon he broke almost all of his bad habits.
However,
he was still unable to stop his habit of chewing tobacco.
Now, since we loved him,
we took him to a dentist and had his teeth cleaned.
After that visit to the dentist, he completely stopped using tobacco.
Within six months from starting the Bible study,
Sangram became a qualified publisher,
and after that, he continued to progress well.
Latur now has a sign-language congregation.
My wife and I then moved to another group.
We are now serving in Pandharpur.
When we meet our old studies at the conventions
and see their progress, we are overjoyed.
The very thought that Jehovah has extended to us this privilege to serve him
makes us overwhelmed with happiness.
There are no words to express how we feel.
When Sangram showed us his big smile,
did a smile come to your face too?
That’s how the truth affects us.
And don’t we appreciate the sacrifices that Alex and Anne made
in order to serve where the need was greater?
They had to learn sign language and move far away from their home.
But how did it turn out?
Alex says they are “overwhelmed with happiness.”
Imagine that.
They were certainly rewarded for their sacrificing spirit.
We now move west to Europe.
Europe gave birth to the Greek and Roman Empires,
the Middle Ages, and the Renaissance.
With 160 culturally distinct groups,
Europe is immensely varied and densely populated.
Almost 1.6 million Jehovah’s Witnesses
are actively making disciples on this continent.
In southeastern Europe,
you’ll find Romania
—a country of nearly 20 million people.
Today, over 39,000 publishers
are conducting almost 22,000 Bible studies.
Eight out of ten people belong to the Romanian Orthodox Church.
The ratio of publishers to the population varies greatly,
from 1 to 4,000 in the southeast
to 1 to 7 in Transylvania in the northwest.
Last year, special preaching campaigns
were organized to reach those in unassigned territories.
As a result, 85 percent of these territories
have been given a witness.
Here are the 112 publishers and 4 regular pioneers
of the Jibou Centru Congregation.
They serve a territory that includes a small city, rural areas,
and large communities of Hungarians and Roma.
Let’s see what it’s like to make disciples there.
One of the challenges we face in our town
is that we have a small territory
compared to the number of brothers
—a ratio of 1 publisher to about 40 inhabitants.
So we put great emphasis on preaching in the villages around Jibou.
Jehovah blessed our efforts,
and we have more Bible studies who make good progress.
When I was still in elementary school,
not yet baptized myself,
I used to speak about Jehovah
to one of my classmates.
Her name was Oana.
She was very interested and even asked many questions.
We were both 12 at that time.
A little while later, after I got baptized,
Oana became my first Bible student.
I was able to show her how to prepare well for the study.
In the evening, we used to read the Bible together,
and we even wrote down in a notebook our favorite Bible texts.
At the same time, by means of different study projects,
I tried to help her see Jehovah as a real Person.
For example, we wrote down on a big sheet of paper
all of Jehovah’s qualities and the way we could imitate them.
Oana made good progress, attended the meetings,
and even started to participate.
I was so happy to see
how much joy Oana had in learning about the truth.
Not surprisingly, difficulties arose on the way.
Oana’s mother was not happy at all that I was studying with her daughter.
She forbade her to study, and one day she asked her
to choose between family and Jehovah
and put her out of the house.
Oana was 16 years old.
I encouraged Oana with the scripture
from Isaiah 41:10, 13,
which says that Jehovah is ‘grasping our hand’
and that he will ‘help us.’
We talked a lot together, and we prayed together.
And after only one week, Jehovah answered our prayers.
Oana’s mother calmed down and not only allowed her to return home
but also to attend meetings and to continue studying together.
I was so happy!
On the 21st of July, 2018,
Oana got baptized.
Now I can finally preach together with my spiritual sister.
Jehovah always gave me the joy I needed.
In fact, I can’t find
the words to describe the joy I experience now.
Did you notice where and when
Beatrice started talking to Oana about Jehovah?
In elementary school.
What a wonderful reminder
that you young ones can experience joy
by making school your personal territory!
If you haven’t tried it already,
look for someone with whom you can share the good news.
You may be surprised at the results.
Let’s go next to North America.
Now, this continent extends from the tiny islands near the Arctic
to the Isthmus of Panama in the south.
North America is home to almost 2.6 million Jehovah’s Witnesses.
The United States is by far the most populous country in North America,
with over 325 million people.
Here you can find metropolitan cities
as well as vast areas that are sparsely populated.
This territory is cared for
by more than 1.2 million publishers
and over 180,000 pioneers.
Meet the brothers and sisters
of the Juniata River Pennsylvania German Congregation
in Mifflintown, Pennsylvania.
As we’ll see in the following report,
their unique territory is rich with people
who sincerely respect God’s Word.
The challenge is our territory being so vast.
Sometimes you may drive an hour and a half to two hours
just to get to the territory.
One of my favorite joys
is getting to use the Bible constantly in this field.
They respect the Bible.
They all have one in their house.
Starting this language almost three years ago, from a pregroup
to now a congregation with four groups in the area, you can see the growth
and the excitement of everyone.
Honestly, I can say it’s been the happiest time in my life
since I started working in this field.
Out in service one day, just working from door to door,
I met a lady, and she accepted the Greatest Man  book.
Eventually, Memorial season came around.
I went and left an invitation with Jane.
We went back the day before the Memorial
and were surprised when Jane said,
“Yes, we’d love to come.”
So we talked about a Bible study,
and eventually Jerry agreed
to having one as a family.
But there was a contrast from what I’d been taught,
so I was willing to dig for more knowledge
to try and figure out what was going on here.
He read a scripture in Psalms
about the earth, and I said:
“Wow! Yes, all the things I pictured myself doing in heaven
are the things I enjoy on earth.”
It made me happy.
Yet, can I really dare believe that?
The more I studied about the Bible and looked up the scriptures,
the more I realized I never really knew a whole lot about the Bible.
I was actually sort of in shock,
and it really put a spotlight on who I really was.
At one point, Ben and I went over to make a return visit.
We had planned what we wanted to do with the family,
and it just did not lend to that at all,
and we ended up playing cards instead.
We didn’t get to share anything from the Bible.
The family was like, ‘Oh.’
It dawned on them; we’re real people too.
In the Pennsylvania German culture, people teach pretty strongly
obedience to parents to make God happy.
One day, Jerry let me know that his dad wanted to talk to me.
Although my dad meant well, he tried to stop the study.
But the information that he was bringing to me about the Witnesses
was not what I saw.
What we were being taught
was directly from my Bible that I had in my house.
How could it be wrong?
You could tell that they were just distraught as a family with what was going on.
They wanted to do the right thing, but they could feel all the pressure to stop.
We eventually had to cut ties
in order to continue spiritual growth.
After that, Jerry and Jane just progressed very fast.
They were making changes in their life,
and they got to really see the freedom that serving Jehovah gives you.
Seeing their joy grow
was irreplaceable; it was fantastic.
We have gained a hundredfold of what we could have ever lost.
And so as we share good news
with individuals and as they make progress,
we are very excited and happy.
I would just love for everyone to have
that opportunity to have that same joy.
What happened when Jerry and Jane
read for themselves the truths contained in the Bible?
It deeply affected their thoughts and emotions
and revealed who they really were on the inside.
As a result, they now joyfully serve Jehovah
along with their children.
Ben and Joanna used the Bible skillfully.
They let God’s Word speak for itself.
And the joy this experience brought them is,
as Ben said, “irreplaceable; . . . fantastic.”
That kind of joy is contagious.
We feel it too just watching them.
Next we go to Oceania.
This is the collective name for Australia
and for the more than 10,000 islands
in the Pacific Ocean between Asia and the Americas.
Some of Oceania’s islands,
are known as “high islands” because they were developed
as volcanic eruptions built up land over time.
“Low islands,” such as the country of Kiribati,
are made of coral and sometimes barely reach above sea level.
Over 100,000 Jehovah’s Witnesses are hard at work
in this beautiful territory.
Fiji is an archipelago of some 300 islands
scattered over 3 million square kilometers,
or about 1 million square miles.
This territory is cared for
by some 3,000 publishers and over 500 pioneers.
In the last service year,
they conducted over 4,700 Bible studies.
These brothers and sisters
are in the South Suva English Congregation.
Let’s see what unique challenges our brothers face there.
Many, if not all, in our territory know about God’s Word, the Bible.
However, they are taught false teachings.
The challenge arises
when customs and traditions
conflict with Bible teachings.
As they study and progress,
they face opposition from their family
and, of course, there’s the social pressure
that comes from their community.
Added to this are the materialistic goals that are put before them.
So all of this combined really poses a challenge with these ones progressing.
Despite these challenges,
some of them eventually do study the Bible with us.
Some have become Jehovah’s friend and made the truth their own.
So to be able to show these ones from God’s Word,
the Bible, that Jehovah is a God of love
and to see their reaction —that in itself is a wonderful blessing.
I used to study with this young girl.
She wanted to make progress in the truth.
But in order for her to do that,
she had to overcome these two big obstacles:
One was the career that she had,
and the other was the obstacle of her unbelieving family.
I really didn’t want to impose the truth on her,
so my goal was to help her understand what the Bible teaches,
help her see the big picture,
and let her draw her own conclusion.
I try to be a good example to her by enjoying
the ministry myself, you know,
and helping her to understand that as I’m out in the ministry,
I know I’m working along with Jehovah.
Although she had a high-paying job,
she wasn’t happy.
She was always stressed.
Then she sees Jehovah’s Witnesses.
Despite being out there in the ministry
on hot, sunny days or rainy days,
they’re happy.
She knew and was convinced
that she would be really happy
if she put Jehovah first in her life.
So eventually she had to tell her mother-in-law
that she had resigned from her employment.
So her mother-in-law said:
“And now you’ve resigned?
“So, what are you going to do?
Are you going to go preaching?”
And then she said:
“The decision that I have made is going to make me happy.
It’s going to make Jehovah happy as well.”
In seeing the big picture,
she was able to take a stand for true worship
and be on Jehovah’s side of universal sovereignty.
I attended the Pioneer Service School with her.
You know, what really made me happy
was seeing ones like her
being happy in doing the same work
of helping others come to serve Jehovah
and knowing the fact that Jehovah had actually used me
in helping others
find the truth and serve Jehovah as well.
To some, Fiji may seem like paradise.
But, as we learned, the people of that beautiful land
face the same issues as people everywhere
—stress, pressure-filled jobs, and an uncertain future.
As Makereta’s student learned, putting Jehovah first
is the only guarantee for true, lasting happiness.
Our final destination is South America.
South America is home to earth’s largest river, the Amazon,
as well as the driest place, the Atacama Desert.
Animal life on this continent is rich and diverse,
particularly its bird population.
With some 3,000 species of birds,
South America is sometimes called the bird continent.
More than 400 million people live here,
including over 1.7 million Jehovah’s Witnesses.
There is tremendous language diversity
in South America.
Let’s visit Bolivia,
a country of more than 11 million people
and a wide range of indigenous cultures.
Bolivia presents unique challenges
to our about 28,000 brothers and sisters who live here.
Their territory includes the towering Andes Mountains in the west
and rain forests in the north.
The publishers endure weather
that ranges from burning heat and tropical humidity
to freezing winds.
To reach remote territories,
they may have to cross rivers and drive for hours
on poorly maintained mountain roads
—sometimes just a few millimeters, or inches, from the precipice!
How Jehovah is blessing their courageous efforts!
In the last service year alone,
more than 42,000 Bible studies were conducted.
Here are the 35 publishers and 8 regular pioneers
of the Norte Quechua Congregation.
To reach and seek out those who speak Quechua,
the publishers travel long distances.
Sadly, many of the Quechua-speaking community
have been victims of prejudice
and do not receive basic education in their language.
Our brothers and sisters spend hours
helping interested ones learn to read
so they can comprehend basic Bible truths.
The response to the good news in Bolivia is very positive.
But, as we’ll learn in the following report,
Bible students frequently face opposition,
often from those closest to them.
When an interested person begins to learn
the truth from the Bible,
at first the family is happy for them,
and their friends are happy too.
But when the teachings of the Bible are in opposition to popular customs,
those family members and friends may become their main source of opposition.
However, we have also seen many, many blessings from Jehovah.
For example, although the challenges may be great,
we see Jehovah’s hand
working in the lives of each of these individuals,
because they make huge  changes.
They take hold of Jehovah, they see him as their God,
and they leave behind popular customs and start to make progress.
It is a beautiful blessing to see a Bible student
get baptized, filled with joy.
Lydia was a young woman
who was very interested in spiritual things.
But just like anyone who does not study the Bible,
she had habits that were not pleasing to Jehovah.
She liked to socialize with her workmates,
and at times, she went out drinking with her friends
—sometimes drinking a little too much.
However, despite that, she was very humble.
You could see that she was very sincere;
she appreciated good things.
After seeing these beautiful qualities in her,
I said, “Jehovah can make
other good qualities grow in her heart.”
So we set the date to start the study.
We always tried to be consistent
and to not miss a study.
When a publisher does not miss the day and time for the study,
the Devil is not given the opportunity to disrupt it.
Some teachings Lydia accepted immediately,
but others took more time.
Her manner of dress was not appropriate;
she wore tight clothing and very short skirts.
How did we correct that?
By showing her in the Bible
that women should dress “with modesty and soundness of mind.”
It was not easy, but she did it.
After that, when she attended meetings, she looked like one of Jehovah’s Witnesses.
When you plant a literal plant, you start to water it
and it keeps growing.
While you are sleeping, you don’t know how those changes happen.
It happens exactly the same way with a Bible student.
As time passed, Lydia expressed the desire to be baptized.
After that, she just kept making progress
and started to serve as a regular pioneer.
Later, she was invited to serve at Bethel.
She has been serving at Bethel for 16 years.
I am one of the 70 persons
who learned the truth from Edith.
Her example helped me
to be considerate, to be insightful,
and also to be consistent
in making disciples.
Over the years,
I have learned so much about disciple-making,
especially that this work is not ours.
When Bible students make progress,
it is thanks to the blessing of Jehovah,
because He sees their hearts.
So we’re not working for a man;
we’re working for the Most High God.
How encouraging to see ones like Lydia learn the truth
and with God’s help make the needed changes!
And what joy it continues to bring to her teacher, Edith,
to see her serving Jehovah today!
As Edith says, “When Bible students make progress,
“it is thanks to the blessing of Jehovah,
because He sees their hearts.”
Well, in our time together,
we’ve circled the earth to bring you these experiences.
Did you notice any patterns for joyful disciple-making?
Here are just four patterns that stood out to me.
We saw that the first step
is to seek out all those with the right heart condition.
Our brothers in Nigeria,
Fiji, and Bolivia
spread the good news despite the great distances,
poor roads, and extreme weather.
Gabriel and Joseph teamed up
to overcome their disabilities,
and their example inspires us to do more.
Alex and Anne Das learned sign language
and moved more than 500 miles
to serve where the need was greater.
Then we saw a second vital element
in disciple-making: the “art of teaching.”
We know, for example, that helping students
to reason on the Scriptures is very effective.
That was the case with Makereta.
Using the Scriptures, she helped her student
draw her own conclusions about the truth.
Benjamin and Joanna skillfully used the Bible
with Jerry and Jane.
The power of the Scriptures touched their hearts.
And when opposition came, they stood firm
because they were convinced that they were learning the truth
from God’s inspired Word.
A third element of disciple-making involves helping our students
to develop good study habits and a regular spiritual routine.
Edith and Lydia made it a goal never to miss a study.
Beatrice showed creativity, developing projects
like that big sheet of paper to help Oana know Jehovah as a real Person.
And fourth: In every experience,
we saw that disciple-making involves love
—showing genuine love.
Alex and Anne took Sangram to the dentist because they love him.
What motivated Cletus to study the Bible?
The joy radiated by Jehovah’s people
and the loving way we treat others.
Angeline gave up her stressful job and put Jehovah first.
Why?
Because she observed Jehovah’s Witnesses,
who out of self-sacrificing love
were motivated to preach the good news
on hot days and rainy days,
and she especially noted the joy it brought them.
As you can see, the joy of Jehovah
comes from sincere efforts to help people
and Jehovah’s blessing on those efforts.
When you see and hear your brothers’ and sisters’ heartfelt expressions,
how does it make you feel?
Like Paul and Barnabas,
we too may have challenges along the way, even some setbacks.
But nothing compares with the deep joy and happiness
that results from helping others come to know and love Jehovah.
There are still honesthearted ones out there,
and they desperately need the truth.
It’s experiences like the ones we’ve just listened to
that help us to see that Jehovah is truly speeding up the work.
The next time you go out in service,
picture yourself working side by side
with your brothers and sisters around the world.
Just as in a search and rescue effort,
we may feel we’re not finding survivors in our area.
But just one report of a rescue victim
being pulled out alive spurs on all the volunteers
to double their efforts.
Imagine the joy Jehovah feels
when he looks down and sees us
across the globe working “shoulder to shoulder”
in the greatest rescue mission of all time!
So keep calling out;
keep searching through the rubble of this dying system
to find those crying out for help.
And may your joy abound as you do so.

cn.text: 如果有人要你说出在一世纪
热心宣扬好消息的两个人
你会想到谁呢？
你可能会想到保罗和巴拿巴
他们为了宣扬好消息，长途跋涉
去过很多地方，帮助很多人认识耶和华
他们热心传道，给自己和别人都带来喜乐
使徒行传15:3说
他们讲述自己的传道经历
听到的弟兄姐妹都大受鼓励
这让他们更加团结地崇拜耶和华
彼此亲如一家
今天
也有很多人像保罗和巴拿巴一样
他们努力找出那些有正确态度的人
接下来让我们看看
在全球弟兄姐妹共同的努力下
2019年工作年度
我们取得了哪些成果呢？
我们在240个国家和地区宣扬好消息
平均每个月传道员总数超过840万
传道时间超过20亿小时
另外，我们也很高兴告诉大家
去年的受浸人数
是20年以来第一次超过30万
也就是说
每星期平均有5843人
公开表明他们献身给耶和华
另外还有许多人表明他们对圣经感兴趣

en.text: For  the last 45 years, I’ve been in the pioneer work,
traveling work,
and in Bethel here for a number of years.
My health was very good
—never had any problems at all.
One day, I had a headache.
It was severe.
I really couldn’t see clearly—anything.
We went to the Bethel doctor, and he referred us to a specialist,
and the specialist gave us the diagnosis
of a very aggressive brain tumor called glioblastoma.
He had surgery the next Thursday.
Then, after surgery, he had radiation
and chemotherapy at the same time.
A year later, he had to have another surgery.
And right now he is on his fourth type
of chemotherapy treatment.
From the very first time that he got sick, the hardest thing
was to see my husband become increasingly dependent
upon me and upon other people.
I didn’t want this
to define who we are.
The brothers played a pivotal role
and tried to help us.
One brother found out that I had to go in for surgery.
He gave me a scripture,
and we prayed together.
I’ll always remember that.
It was a beautiful example.
I also get a lot of encouragement from Sara,
who gets us prepared for meetings.
When we go out in service, I’ve gotten the opportunity
to go and help people
—just talk to them and encourage them.
In my Bethel assignment
in the Service Department, I have a brother or two
who will come over and review a case
that we’re considering, and I get a lot of joy in that way.
I’m very thankful that I can still do a little something
to help.
For me,
because he’s been humble through this whole thing, it’s been easier.
My hope is strong, and I’m going to keep
right on going this way and serve Jehovah
right on into the new world or whatever comes.

en.text: We knew when we first got married that we would enjoy having a family.
So when we first found out
that we were pregnant, we were overjoyed.
When Becky first told me she was pregnant,
it’s like a light switch went off in my heart.
Immediately, I felt like a dad.
Instantly, you begin to make plans.
It was like all this love
just flooded in.
One day, Becky was feeling a little off,
and a friend encouraged us, “Just go see the doctor.”
So we did.
And while we were there, they did an ultrasound.
The doctor came back
and they said there wasn’t a heartbeat anymore.
That was a very difficult moment
—something I can never forget.
Because all of a sudden, all of those hopes,
those dreams, those preparations you are making
—they’re gone.
This place in your heart that opened up to make room for this child
is now this huge, gaping, open hole
and there’s nothing to fill it.
It just is incredible emptiness.
We didn’t know what to do.
But it was a meeting night,
so we wanted to go to the meeting.
It felt like the place where Jehovah’s holy spirit is,
and we wanted to be there because we knew
we were not going to be able to survive this on our own strength.
We needed Jehovah.
After people learned that we had lost
the baby, so many people
shared a little bit of their experiences with me,
which made us feel not alone, for sure.
But Jehovah has also given us some incredible friends
—friends who have stuck closer to us
than a brother, friends who always seem to know
when we’re having a hard day, who have prayed with us,
who have taken walks with us, listened.
And I know those are expressions Jehovah has given us.
Regaining joy is a work in progress.
There was a particular scripture in my personal study
that I found very helpful, Psalm 139, where it talks
about how there’s nowhere
that Jehovah can’t find us.
There’s no darkness that is too dark for Jehovah.
And it felt like such a dark place.
Dwelling on that scripture was something that helped me a lot.
And gradually, bit by bit,
I felt like Jehovah did help me
to see beautiful things again.

孩子已经没有心跳了
这件事对我打击太大了
真的太大了
一时间
你所有的希望，所有的梦想
还有你做的所有的准备
一切都没了
我原本很幸福
满脑子想的都是我的孩子
可现在我的心像被掏空了一样
这种痛苦
真的没办法表达
我们真的无法接受这个事实
但刚好那天有聚会
所以我们都很想要参加
因为在那里有耶和华神圣力量发挥作用
也帮助我们
我们知道只靠自己是真的撑不下去
我们真的需要耶和华
弟兄姐妹知道这件事以后
都来安慰我们
也说了他们自己的经历
我们觉得并不孤单
耶和华赐给我们一些好朋友
他们甚至比家人更亲密
他们总是在我们最需要的时候出现
跟我们一起祷告，一起散步
听我们说话
我们能感受到
耶和华在通过他们表达对我们的爱
想走出悲伤
不是那么一件容易的事
我研读的时候
看到一节经文对我的帮助很大
在诗篇139篇
这里谈到
耶和华比我们自己还要了解我们
无论面对什么样的情况
耶和华都会把我们从幽暗的低谷拉出来
沉思这节经文给了我很大的安慰
渐渐地耶和华帮助我快乐起来
让我再次看到了希望

titles.ko: 시련을 겪을 때에도 기뻐할 수 있다—고난
titles.cn: 在考验下也能喜乐——痛苦

title: 시련을 겪을 때에도 기뻐할 수 있다—박해

ko.text: 이른 아침에 무장한 러시아 특수 경찰들이
이틀 뒤 법원은 저를 미결 구금하라고 지시했습니다.
감옥에서 어떤 일을 겪게 될지 몰랐기 때문에
죄를 자백하고 동료 형제 자매들의 이름을 대라고 했죠.
아내가 정말 보고 싶었고 너무 힘들었습니다.
두 달 동안 그 어떤 영적 양식도, 성경도 볼 수 없었습니다.
아내가 노트를 한 권 보내 줬는데
저는 거기다가 생각나는 성구들을 매일매일 적었습니다.
그 후 성경을 한 권 구했는데
영적으로 굶주렸던 저는 4개월 만에 다 읽었죠.
감옥에 있는 동안 아내와 친구들에게 편지를 썼는데
성경을 읽으면서 배운 흥미로운 점들을 알려 주곤 했습니다.
아내와 친구들이 보내 준 편지가 정말 큰 힘이 되었죠.
형제 자매들이 제게 아주 가까이 있다는 느낌이 들었어요.
마치 제 옆 방에 있는 것 같았죠.
형제 자매들이 바로 제 옆에 있었죠.
국가가 저를 사람들로부터 떼어 놓을 수는 있어도
저는 하루에도 여러 번 여호와께 기도했죠.
하지만 다른 사람들이 다 자고 있을 때가
감방에 아무도 없고 저 혼자만 있었던 적도 있었어요.
저는 그런 기회를 놓치지 않고 잘 활용했죠.
저는 여호와께 청한 것들을 종이에 적어 보았고
그분이 들어주실 때마다 하나씩 지워 나갔죠.
여호와께서 바로 제 옆에 계시다는 확신이 들었습니다.
저는 하루에도 여러 번 나지막한 목소리로 왕국 노래를 불렀죠.
하지만 혼자 있게 되면 목청껏 노래했어요.
몸에 문신을 하는 거나 “북방 왕”에 대해서도 얘기했죠.
‘내가 두려워할 필요가 없었구나’ 하는 생각이 들었습니다.
영적으로 발전하는 데 도움이 된 좋은 기회였죠.
여호와를 이렇게 가깝게 느꼈던 적이 없습니다.
하느님의 주권을 지지할 수 있어서 큰 영광입니다!

en.text: Early one morning, armed Russian special forces
broke into my home.
They handcuffed me and searched my place.
They took me
to the FSB office for interrogation.
Two days later, the court sentenced me to pretrial detention.
I was scared because I didn’t know
how I would be treated in prison.
Threatening that things would get worse for me, the officer demanded
that I incriminate myself, admit guilt, and give the names of my fellow believers.
I also really missed my dear wife.
It was so hard without her.
For two months, I didn’t have
any spiritual food or a Bible,
so I decided to make one.
My wife sent me a notebook,
and every day I wrote down verses
that I was able to remember.
After I had written about 500 verses,
I was given a Bible.
Because I was
so spiritually hungry, I read it through in four months.
During this time, I wrote letters
to my wife and friends and shared interesting things
that I learned from my reading.
But the letters I received
from my friends and my dear wife gave me the feeling
that the brothers and sisters were so close to me,
as if they were in the cells next to me.
I wasn’t lonely.
I felt as if my friends were right there with me.
Pretrial detention isolates a person from society.
But it’s impossible to isolate someone from Jehovah.
Throughout the day, I prayed to Jehovah many times,
but I especially waited for bedtime.
When everyone was in bed and only the night-light was on,
I could talk to Jehovah as much as I wanted.
There were times when I was all alone
in the cell and, of course, I took advantage of the situation.
I would get down on my knees and would literally cry
as I prayed to Jehovah.
I decided to write my requests to God
on a sheet of paper and then mark off the ones that he answered.
I was convinced that Jehovah was very close to me.
I also quietly sang our songs
throughout the day.
But when I was all alone, I sang at the top of my voice.
I also tried to give a witness whenever possible.
We discussed a variety of topics
—everything from tattoos to “the king of the north.”
All my fears and anxieties were for nothing.
I was in detention 343 days,
and “not even a hair” fell from my head.
This was the most interesting year of my life
—an excellent school to help refine my spiritual qualities.
I have never felt so close to Jehovah.
What a great honor to uphold God’s sovereignty in this way!

cn.text: 一天早上
有一群武装警察闯进我的家
他们给我戴上手铐
还搜查我的家
之后又把我带去警察局问话
两天后
我就被拘禁起来了
刚开始，我很害怕
因为我不知道当局会怎样对待我
他们要我认罪
也要我供出弟兄姐妹的名字
不然就要我好看
那时我真的非常想念我的妻子
真希望她就在我身边
接下来的两个月
我都没办法读到圣经和书刊
所以，我就决定自己做一本
我妻子寄来一个笔记本
我每天就把我想得到的经文写下来
我写了大约五百节经文以后
有人给了我一本圣经
因为我太久没读到圣经了
所以我四个月就把整本圣经读完了
拘禁期间
我写信给我的妻子和我的朋友
跟他们分享我的研读心得
他们也会回信给我
这些信让我觉得弟兄姐妹离我好近
他们仿佛就在隔壁的牢房
跟着我一起坐牢
我感觉他们就在我身边
我一点都不孤单
他们可以把我拘禁起来
不让我跟外界接触
却无法阻止我亲近耶和华
我一天会跟耶和华祷告很多次
但我特别期待睡觉的时间
因为那时候大家都睡了
我就可以尽情向耶和华祷告了
我也会有一个人在牢房里的时候
这时
我会抓紧机会
跪下来
向耶和华边哭边祷告
我会把我跟耶和华求的写在一张纸上
要是耶和华回应了
我就做个标记
这让我确信
耶和华就在我身边
我经常会在心里默默地唱着我们的歌曲
但是当我一个人的时候
我就会大声地唱出来
只要有机会
我就会向人作见证
我们会谈论各式各样的话题
比如说
纹身，还有“北方王”的预言
我被拘禁了343天
我之前担心的事都没有发生
就像耶稣对门徒说的一样
“你们连一根头发也不会受损”
过去这一年
我感觉自己好像上了一个特别的训练班
培养出更多美好的特质
我从来没有跟耶和华这么亲近过
能以这种方式支持耶和华的至高统治权
我感到非常荣幸！

title: 시련을 겪을 때에도 기뻐할 수 있다—굶주림

ko.text: 먹을 걸 원하는 만큼 살 수 있었고
기본적인 식품조차 전혀 구할 수 없었죠.
장로 형제 두 분이 거의 매일 찾아와서
저희에게 필요한 만큼 식품을 전달해 주셨죠.
그 정도만 먹어도 괜찮을 거라고 생각했는데
제가 다 먹을 때까지 곁에 있어 줬죠.
예전에 비해 지금은 살이 좀 빠진 편이에요.
장로 형제들은 항상 저를 잘 돌봐 주셨어요.

en.text: Well, here in Venezuela, long before the crisis,
there weren’t so many financial problems like we have today.
We could go to the stores, we could buy
the amount of food we wanted,
and life was peaceful.
For us, the situation started to get really bad
five years ago.
It was hard to get any food at all,
even basic items.
When it came time to buy something, well, it was all gone.
There were two elders that,
I can say, were checking on me almost daily
—always asking how much food I needed.
When I prepared it and served it, my main concern
was that my children would get enough.
I always gave them more food.
Even though my youngest boy would ask,
“Mommy, is that what you’re going to eat?”
I would tell him, “Yes, dear, I’m fine with this.”
Then he would say, “I don’t think so.”
I would think, ‘I can handle this,’
but the amount that I was eating just wasn’t enough for my body.
One Sunday morning, during the meeting, I wasn’t feeling very well but,
thanks to Jehovah, my daughter was nearby.
When I came to, she said,
“Mom, you fainted three times!”
I said, “That can’t be!”
So the brothers immediately took me to the doctor.
I was diagnosed as having severe malnutrition.
The brothers began a plan of action:
They brought food that was already prepared
and, in fact, they would sit by me until I finished my food.
I have not yet
fully recovered my body weight, because I was a little heavier.
But healthwise, I have felt very well.
The elders were always looking after me,
and that boosted my energy.
And definitely, I never lost my joy.
And it’s all thanks to Jehovah!
Thanks to him because he is the One who sustains me.
He clothes me, he feeds me, and he gives me great friends.
That is what Jehovah gives me.

cn.text: 在委内瑞拉爆发经济危机之前
大家遇到的经济难题
没有像现在这么多
我们可以到店里买需要的食物
生活还算安定
但五年前，情况变得很糟
我们根本买不到东西吃
连生活的必需品都没有
我们到店里去
发现东西都卖光了
有两个长老
几乎每天都来看我过得怎样
问我东西够不够吃
我做饭的时候
想的就是让我的两个孩子能吃饱
所以我会分给他们多一点
自己就少吃一点
结果我的小儿子问我
“妈妈，你怎么吃这么少？”
我就跟他说
“宝贝别担心
妈妈吃这些就够了。”
他说：“你也吃得太少了吧！”
我本来以为自己可以挺得住
但事实完全不是我想的那样
有一次聚会的时候
我觉得不太舒服
没想到我昏倒了
醒来的时候，女儿跟我说
“妈妈，你刚才昏过去三次！”
我说：“不会吧？”
弟兄们马上带我去看医生
医生说我严重营养不良
弟兄们马上做出安排
他们会带做好的食物来给我吃
而且他们会陪着我
等我把东西吃完他们才离开
我现在还是比以前瘦得多
但我已经恢复健康
身体还算不错
长老们一直关心我，给我安慰
这让我充满力量
我从来就没有失去过喜乐
这都要感谢耶和华！
因为他一直扶持我
我完全不用担心吃什么、穿什么
他还给我很多好朋友
耶和华让我一无所缺

title: 시련을 겪을 때에도 기뻐할 수 있다—헐벗음

ko.text: 그래서 늘 주위를 잘 살피고 다니죠.
이게 보통 일이 아니란 걸 직감했죠.
물이 집 안까지 들어올 줄 생각도 못 했어요.
근데 그 주에 순회 대회가 있었어요.
전 입고 갈 양복도 넥타이도 없었죠.
금요일에 노크 소리가 들려서 나가 보니까,
여호와께서 저흴 입혀 주신 거나 다름없죠.
그 약속이 제게 큰 기쁨을 줘요.
살다 보면 다양한 시련을 겪게 될 수 있죠.
우리와 여호와 사이를 갈라놓거나 멀어지게 할 수 없습니다.

en.text: Well, one thing you have to understand about living in New York City
is that it’s a very fast-paced life.
So you’ve got to keep up with that lifestyle.
We were doing pretty fine,
and we were happy pioneering, working
—just trying to survive in New York.
One of the things that you usually have to worry about
is your safety —being careful of your surroundings.
But hurricanes are just something we never considered;
it’s something we never had to worry about.
The day when we first heard the warning,
it was raining outside and kind of windy.
We saw the water coming into the parking lot where our apartment was
and that’s when I realized something was about to happen.
We got out with the clothes on our back.
It was just total devastation.
You lose everything
—one single night.
I never had any thought that water
would come into our place and destroy everything from our material possessions
to our clothes.
And I truly felt what it was like to be destitute.
It just broke my heart.
And all I could do
was wonder, ‘Where do my wife and I go from here?’
Our assembly was scheduled for that weekend.
I didn’t even have
a suit jacket or a tie.
I think I probably took for granted something as simple as clothing.
I always had it.
But the brothers and sisters stepped in to assist in so many different ways.
I heard a knock on the door that Friday
—three suits
and shoes!
They purchased clothing for us.
It was a most unbelievable experience.
These friends gave us big hugs and gave us envelopes.
We are fully convinced
we were clothed by Jehovah’s love.
We were able to go to our assembly and enjoy taking in spiritual food,
even though we were in that situation.
Even though we lost everything physically,
we were still able to keep on pioneering, which we have been doing up to this day.
Jehovah made a promise.
If we keep seeking first his Kingdom,
everything else he will take care of.
And that’s where my joy comes from.
No matter what type of tribulation you go through in your life,
and even if it’s to the point of nakedness,
it will never ever be able to stop
or cut off the relationship that we have with our God, Jehovah.

cn.text: 可能大家都知道
在纽约人们生活的步调非常快
我们的生活也是这样
我们过得还不错
我们能够快乐地做先驱
又有工作养活自己
在这里通常要留意的就是治安的问题
出门的时候要特别小心
但是我们从来没有想过有一天会遇到飓风
会受到这么大的影响
我记得政府发出飓风警报的那天
外面刮着大风，下着大雨
看着停车场的水渐渐涨上来
我就想
完了
大事不妙了
我们撤离的时候除了身上的衣服
什么都没有
我们完全不知道该怎么办
一夜之间
什么都没了
我万万没有想到水会淹进我们家
我们家的东西
家具
衣服
什么都毁了
我人生第一次感到什么叫一无所有
我当时非常迷茫
我就想我和妻子接下来该怎么办呢？
那个周末刚好有大会
可是我连一套西服和领带都没有
我以前从来不会
为了穿什么衣服这么简单的事情担心
没有想到会这样
弟兄姐妹给了我们很多实际的帮助
他们没有半点犹豫
星期五一大早有人敲门
我推门一看
三套西装
还有皮鞋
他们给我们新的衣服，还有一些钱
还热烈地拥抱我们
我们真的太感动了
我觉得我们穿上不只是新的衣服
还穿上耶和华的爱
正因为有他们的帮助
我们可以安心地参加整天的大会
享受所有的节目
虽然我们什么东西都没了
但我们还是继续做先驱
一直到现在
耶和华向我们保证
只要我们先追求上帝的王国
其他的，他都会照顾我们
一想到这个我就非常快乐
无论我们在生活中遇到什么患难
就算是没有衣服穿
这都不能妨碍我们继续崇拜上帝
也不能阻止我们继续亲近耶和华

title: 시련을 겪을 때에도 기뻐할 수 있다—위험

ko.text: 몇 년 전에는 한 파이오니아 자매가
아직도 아들이 쓰던 침대와 물건들이 있고,
아들이 자주 입던 양복도 제자리에 걸려 있는데,
가끔씩 혼자 있을 때 아들 생각이 많이 나요.
저는 나사로에 대한 기록을 정말 좋아하고
여호와께서 반드시 그렇게 해 주실 겁니다.
여호와께서 이렇게 위로해 주시는 것 같습니다.
꼭 아들을 다시 만나게 될 거야.”

en.text: I was born in Caracas and live
in an area of the city called Petare.
In Petare, I have to live
with violence and delinquency.
A few years ago, we lost a pioneer sister who,
sadly, was hit by a bullet.
Well, something like that also happened to my son.
There was a confrontation
in the neighborhood, and a stray bullet hit my son
and killed him instantly.
That left such a void.
It hurt me to go into his room and see his empty bed.
And then to see his things:
his shoes, his favorite clothes.
To see them in the wardrobe—
Crying was inevitable.
These situations were very difficult to deal with at the time.
But as soon as the congregation
found out about the situation,
right away they gave me support.
They were there to help care for all the things you need to do
when you lose a loved one.
After going through all that, I was very afraid
to continue going out in field service.
I feared for my life
and for the life of my family.
I prayed to Jehovah,
and Jehovah gave me practical wisdom to continue.
Sometimes when I’m alone meditating and thinking about my son,
those memories return and, of course, I have a setback,
so to speak,
and I begin to cry again.
But keeping clearly in mind the promise of the resurrection
is what motivates me to keep going.
An account that I really like
and that I always keep in mind is the account about Lazarus.
There, Martha uses an expression.
She says, ‘I know he’ll rise on the last day.’
And that is the same confidence that I have in Jehovah.
I know that my son will rise.
Jehovah will give him to me.
At the time that this terrible thing happened,
it’s true that I lost my joy for a time.
But later after the mourning passes,
the resurrection hope gives us joy.
It’s as if
Jehovah speaks to me, saying, ‘Keep calm.’
It’s as if he gives me a gentle pat,
telling me to ‘keep going and that’s what will happen to you.
Keep faithful, and continue loyal, and I will give him back to you.’

cn.text: 我在加拉加斯出生
现在住在佩塔雷
这里的治安一点儿都不好
常常会看到暴力事件
几年前
就有一位先驱姐妹不幸中枪，失去了生命
我儿子也有同样的遭遇
附近发生冲突的时候，他意外中枪
当场死亡
我实在伤心欲绝
每当我进到他的房间
看到他空荡荡的床
看到衣柜里挂着他喜爱的衣服、他的鞋
我就忍不住哭了起来
那段日子对我来说
简直是太难熬了！
会众的弟兄姐妹一听说我有这样的遭遇
就马上过来安慰我
他们给我实际的帮助
也帮我处理儿子的后事
这件事以后，我就不敢出去传道了
因为我担心我和家人会随时遭遇不测
我向耶和华祷告
后来耶和华真的帮助我
让我能够继续传道
我一个人的时候，还会想起我的儿子
想到他所遭遇的一切，我还是会很伤心
甚至有的时候还会流下泪来
但这时我会提醒自己
要记住耶和华的承诺，他会复活死去的人
这会给我力量，让我能够忍耐下去
我最喜欢的
就是在圣经里关于拉撒路复活的记载
我记得马大说过这样一句话
“在最后的日子复活的时候
拉撒路一定会活过来。”
我对耶和华也有同样的信心
相信他一定会复活我的儿子
儿子去世这件事
确实让我有一段时间失去了喜乐
但沉思复活的希望让我能重拾喜乐
我感觉
耶和华一边拍着我的肩膀，一边安慰我
对我说
“我一定会让你的儿子回到你身边。”

반군이 쿠데타를 일으키려 한다는 소문이 돌았어요.
그걸 듣고 사람들은 큰 혼란에 빠졌죠.

en.text: When everything falls apart
and when everything around you is chaotic,
the one thing you have is your relationship with Jehovah.
My name is Baite Michael Dugbe.
I was born in Monrovia, Liberia in 1980.
Growing up in Monrovia
before the war was an amazing time.
I had wonderful parents.
We grew up in a nice house, and we went to a great school.
When I was nine years old, everything changed overnight.
There were reports of rebels
trying to take over the government.
Those reports alone
made people panic.
Businesses started to close down.
Services were shut down
—the lights, the power, the water— everything stopped.
The next few years were really unstable.
In 1996, things again fell apart completely.
It was all-out war.
This time, the rebels were in the city.
There was a lot of looting going on.
There was a lot of shooting.
The rebels—they were known for torture
if people would not agree to fight with them.
In a situation like that,
there’s a lot of fear; there’s a lot of panic.
And when your fear level rises,
the best way to deal with it is prayer —prayer to Jehovah,
asking him specifically for direction
on what to do next.
As the fighting escalated
and it got closer to where we lived, it was no longer safe.
We had to flee, and we ended up at the branch office.
The brothers were very loving; they took really good care of us.
Our spiritual activities
—they made sure we kept up with that.
Looking back, I’m very grateful to have survived.
Two things helped us get through.
Number one: our relationship with Jehovah.
That’s the only thing that keeps you stable.
But then, also, we were able to survive
because of the help from the brothers and sisters.
Those moments of trial —that’s when you really realize
how much you need the brotherhood.
I have a lot of joy in my assignment at Bethel
in Audio/Video Services.
I love the brothers and sisters that I work with.
It’s all thanks to Jehovah
that I am alive and that I get to serve him every day.

cn.text: 当你的周围一片混乱
自己又不知道该做什么的时候
你唯一能做的就是倚靠耶和华
我叫巴伊特·杜贝
我1980年出生在
利比里亚（赖比瑞亚）的蒙罗维亚
战争爆发前这里的生活还算安稳
父母非常爱我
我记得那时我们住着大的房子
我也接受非常好的教育
就在我九岁那年
一切都变了
人们听说反叛分子要推翻政府
听到这样的消息
大家都感到非常害怕
商店都关门了
水电也停止了供应
这个城市彻底瘫痪了
接下来的几年
周围的情况也非常不稳定
1996年，情况再次完全失控
战争一触即发
反叛分子闯进了我住的城市
抢劫，枪击事件接二连三地发生
反叛分子希望有人站在他们那一边
如果有人拒绝
他们就会用残酷的手段对待他们
面对这样的情况
你可能会感到非常的害怕
不知道该做什么
但当你有这样的感觉时
最好的办法就是向耶和华祷告
具体地向他寻求指引
这样你就知道接下来该怎么做了
战争越来越激烈
就连我们住的地方也受到了影响
后来，我们不得不离开住所到分部避难
分部的弟兄姐妹们非常有爱心
他们不但在生活方面照顾我们
也确保我们能够参加所有崇拜耶和华的活动
回顾以往
我真的感谢耶和华让我活下来
我从这个经历当中学到两件事
第一就是要和耶和华培养亲密的关系
这可以帮助你在逆境时保持内心安宁
我学到的第二点就是
我们能够活下来
是因为身边有弟兄姐妹在帮助我们
只有经历考验时，你才知道他们有多重要
我现在在伯特利的影音服务部工作
我很爱跟我一起工作的弟兄姐妹们
我真的非常感激耶和华让我能够活下来
每天都可以为他服务

en.text: I thought happiness was all about money
and getting to buy whatever I wanted.
I was really into fashion.
I was always thinking about what I was going to get next,
and I didn’t mind putting in extra overtime to get it.
My day ended with me taking the last train home, eating,
and then going to bed at one or two o’clock in the morning.
But this affected me mentally and physically.
I’d wake up in the middle of the night with panic attacks.
I felt so lost and confused.
Everything I’d worked for was for nothing.
My motto for shopping was,
“When in doubt, buy!”
I bought a lot of things: powerful motorcycles, a house, cars.
I was totally absorbed in work and sometimes worked all night.
I somehow made it to meetings,
but after they ended, I’d leave right away.
I didn’t show interest in anyone, not even my wife.
All I ever talked about was work,
and I showed a real lack of consideration for my wife.
I was really blunt with her,
and there was a constant back and forth between us.
And we had a strained relationship.
We weren’t happy.
We just felt stress, stress, and more stress.
Everything seemed pointless.
I realized that I hadn’t been caring
for myself on the inside,
so I decided to read the Bible all over again.
I was especially moved
by how Jehovah repeatedly tried to help the Israelites
despite all their failures.
This reminded me that Jehovah had been expressing
his love for me all along.
I couldn’t hold back my tears.
I decided that I’d live the rest of my life for him.
I adjusted my work
and made the ministry the focal point in my life.
When I get to share a Bible scripture
with someone and see it make an impact on them,
I feel truly happy.
I saw some brothers from the congregation
playing soccer with a young boy who had just lost his father.
They were trying to comfort him by spending time with him.
When I saw them showing personal interest in someone
and considering others’ feelings,
it really impressed me and I thought,
‘I want to use my time like that as well.’
A scripture in the Bible says:
“There is more happiness in giving than there is in receiving.”
The more I practiced it, the happier I became.
I became convinced that this really is the truth.
Now when my wife and I spend time together,
I’m better able to really understand her,
and I’ve come to realize how much she means to me.
I am so thankful that Jehovah has taught me the truth.

cn.text: 我原以为
只要有钱，想买什么就买什么
这样才能快乐
我很喜欢追求时尚，老是想着购物
所以我就经常加班，工作到很晚
就是为了买那些自己喜欢的东西
我每天都坐末班车回家，然后吃点东西
睡觉的时候已经是一两点了
这种生活方式影响了我的健康
情绪也出了问题
我经常睡到半夜就突然醒过来
感到非常恐慌
赚钱并没有给我带来快乐
我感到很迷茫很失落
我原来觉得快乐就一个字
我买了很多东西
光是摩托车和轿车，我换了一辆又一辆
也买了一套房子
我那时脑子里想的都是工作
而且还经常加班
我是去聚会，但一结束我就马上离开
我对谁都漠不关心，对妻子也是这样
我唯一感兴趣的就是工作
我对待妻子也非常的冷漠
我动不动就向她发脾气
而且我们也常常吵架
我们的婚姻充满难题
说实话
那个时候我们一点也不开心
感觉做什么事都没有意义
我意识到
我忽略了跟耶和华的关系
所以我决定
把整本圣经从头到尾再读一遍
让我印象最深的就是
虽然以色列人经常犯错
但耶和华还是一次又一次地帮助他们
这让我想到了自己
耶和华也从来没有放弃过我
我感动地哭了起来
我决定从今以后
要全心全意地为耶和华而活
我调整了工作
把大部分的时间都放在传道工作上
每当我跟别人分享圣经真理
看到上帝的话语在他们身上发挥作用
我就感到非常开心
会众里有个男孩，他的父亲刚刚过世
我看到弟兄们愿意花时间陪在他身边
跟他一起踢足球
安慰他，鼓励他
当我看到他们那么关心别人
顾及别人的感受
我真的非常感动
我当时就想，我很想像他们那样
圣经里有句话说
“施与比接受更快乐。”
我把这个原则实践出来就感到更快乐了
所以我确信这就是真理
现在我和妻子在一起的时候
我更能理解她的感受了
也开始明白
原来她对我那么重要
我非常感激耶和华让我认识了真理

建于台伯河畔
一个有七座山丘的地区
随着帝国的发展
罗马城不断扩建
这是阿庇亚大道
保罗就是沿着这条路来到罗马城的
现在看到的是大竞技场
这是罗马城的第一个竞技场
在保罗的日子就已经存在了
有些基督徒很可能就是在这里殉道的
到了公元1世纪中叶

其中包括一个相当大的犹太社区

马塞卢斯剧场
巴尔布斯剧场
庞培剧场

ko.text: 좋은 관계를 맺는 데 꼭 필요한 특성입니다.
미가 6:8의 이런 말씀을 우리는 잘 알고 있습니다.
“사람아, 선한 것이 무엇인지를 그분이 네게 알려 주셨다.
겸허하게 네 하느님과 함께 걷는 것이 아니냐!”
겸허에 관한 이런 흥미로운 내용이 실렸는데 읽어 드리죠.
“겸허에는 여러 가지 의미가 있을 수 있습니다.
자랑하지 않으려는 태도를 의미할 수 있습니다.
겸허[는] ... ‘경계 내에 머무르는 것’을 의미하기도 합니다.
또한 자기가 해야 할 일과 할 수 있는 일에
그리고 자기에게는 권한이 없는 일이 있다는 것을 압니다.”
이것을 보면 겸허에는 아주 다양한 부면이 있다는 것을 알게 됩니다.
할 수 있는 일에 한계가 있다는 것을 인정”한다고 했습니다.
우리의 개인적인 한계를 인정하는 것이 포함됩니다.
때때로 우리는 신체적인 한계는 쉽게 인정합니다.
예를 들어, 우리가 수영을 잘 못한다면
해변에 갔을 때 곧바로 바다에 뛰어들진 않겠죠?
이처럼 우리가 신체적으로 할 수 없는 일이 있다는 것을 인정하기는 쉽습니다.
하지만 겸허는 단순히 신체적인 한계를 인정하는 것보다 더 많은 것을 의미합니다.
이 점을 분명하게 이해하는 데 도움이 되는
잠시 이 구절의 문맥을 생각해 보면,
다윗이 자신을 죽이려는 사울왕을 피해 숨어 다니던 때를 기억하시죠?
그런데 이제 다윗에게 절호의 기회가 찾아옵니다.
오랜 도피 생활을 끝낼 수 있는
“다윗과 아비새가 밤에 그 군사들에게 가 보니
사울은 진영 안에서 머리맡 땅바닥에 창을 꽂아 놓고
아브넬과 군사들은 사울 주위에 누워 있었다.
‘하느님께서 오늘 당신의 적을 당신의 손에 내주셨습니다.
내가 창으로 그를 단번에 땅에 박게 해 주십시오.
손을 들어 여호와의 기름부음받은 자를 치고도 결백할 수 있는 자가 누구이겠소?’
‘여호와께서 살아 계심을 두고 단언하는데, 여호와께서 친히 그를 치실 것이오.
내가 손을 들어 여호와의 기름부음받은 자를 치는 것은,
여호와의 관점에서 생각할 수 없는 일이오!
그러니 이제, 그의 머리맡에 있는 창과 물병만 가지고 떠납시다.’”
네, 다윗은 마음만 먹으면 사울을 쉽게 죽일 수 있었을 겁니다.
하지만 이 상황에서 다윗이 겸허하게 행동하는 데
다윗은 자신의 위치, 즉 자신의 권한을 생각해야 했습니다.
여호와께서는 다윗에게 그런 임무를 맡기신 적이 없습니다.
아무튼 사울은 여호와께서 기름부으신 이스라엘의 왕이었기 때문에,
다윗은 자신에게 사울을 죽일 권한이 전혀 없다는 것을 인정했습니다.
다윗은 자기 손으로 문제를 해결하려 하기보다는
이 상황을 처리해 주실 것을 확신했습니다.
하지만 그가 나중에 겸허하지 않게 행동한 때도 있었다는 걸
우리는 겸허란 특성을 기르기 위해 열심히 노력해야 하지만,
겸허를 유지하기 위해서도 열심히 노력해야 한다는 겁니다.
자기 자신을 과대평가하기 시작할 수 있습니다.
그렇게 되면 우리의 겸허가 사라지기 시작하면서
주제넘은 행동을 하게 될 수 있죠.
이렇게 된 성경의 유명한 예로 누가 있을까요?
아마 웃시야의 예가 바로 생각나셨을지 모릅니다.
그리고 그에게 무슨 일이 일어났는지 잠깐 살펴보시죠.
여호와의 눈에 옳은 일을 계속 행했다.
참하느님을 두려워하도록 그를 가르치던 스가랴의 날 동안에
그가 여호와를 찾던 동안에는 참하느님께서 그를 번영하게 해 주셨다.”
웃시야는 생애 가운데 그 시점에는 교만한 사람이 아니었습니다.
그는 자기 하느님 여호와께 불충실하게 행동하여,
여호와의 성전으로 들어가서 분향 제단에 분향하려고 했다.”
“웃시야 왕이여, 왕께서 여호와께 분향하시는 것은 옳지 않습니다!
성별된 제사장들만 할 수 있는 일입니다.
여호와 하느님에게서 영광을 받지 못하실 것입니다.”
우리 모두는 살아가면서 어려운 상황에 직면할 때가 있습니다.
우리의 생각대로 문제를 해결하고 싶은 마음이 들지 모릅니다.
심지어 “충실하고 슬기로운 종”이 베푼 출판물의 지침을
우리가 취할 수 있는 지혜로운 행동은
한 걸음 물러나서, 심호흡을 하고, 열까지 센 다음
‘나는 지금 하려는 일에 대한 권한을 실제로 가지고 있는가?
나에겐 지금 이 말을 할 권한이 실제로 있는가?
여호와께서 이 상황을 바로잡아 주실 때를
네, 우리 모두 자기 자신에 대해 합당한 견해를 갖고,
여호와와 “충실하고 슬기로운 종”이 베푸는 인도에 밀접히 고착하고,
또 여호와께서 어떤 문제든 필요하다면 시정해 주실 것이라는
겸허하게 걸을 수 있는 영예를 누리게 될 것입니다.

en.text: Modesty is absolutely essential
to having a good relationship
with our heavenly Father, Jehovah.
We remember what Micah 6:8 tells us:
“He has told you, O man, what is good.
“And what is Jehovah requiring of you?
“Only to exercise justice,
“to cherish loyalty,
and to walk in modesty with your God!”
Well now, what does modesty mean to you?
You probably, when you listened to the comments this morning,
heard a variety of different definitions.
All of them had a common theme,
but each one had a slightly different sense.
The Watchtower  of 2000 made some very interesting comments
about the definition of modesty.
It said: “Modesty can mean a number of things,
“such as a lack of conceit, or vanity,
“and a reluctance to boast about one’s abilities,
“achievements, and possessions.
“According to one reference work,
“modesty also means ‘keeping within bounds.’
“A modest person
“stays within the bounds of good behavior.
“He also acknowledges that there are limits
“to what he ought to do and is able to do.
“He knows that there are things
to which he is not entitled.”
That’s a very interesting definition, isn’t it?
And it kind of helps us to see
that there are many shades of meaning involved with this word.
But let’s center our discussion this morning on that last thought.
A modest person “acknowledges that there are limits
to what he ought to do and is able to do.”
Well now, to be modest, we understand,
involves recognizing our own personal limitations.
And sometimes it’s easier to be able to see our physical limitations.
For example, if you’re not a strong swimmer, probably when you go to the beach,
you won’t swim right out into the ocean, will you?
You’ll recognize your limitations.
Or if you’re not in good shape,
you probably won’t sign up for the New York marathon.
You see, we are able to see
that we’re not able to do some of these physical tasks.
But modesty goes far beyond
just simply acknowledging our own physical limitations.
Now let’s look at an example from the Scriptures
that can help us to see this, perhaps more clearly.
Let’s go to 1 Samuel chapter 26,
and we’re going to start reading here at verse 7,
so 1 Samuel 26:7.
Now, just to set the context for you here,
you’ll remember that David had been hiding from King Saul,
who was seeking to kill him.
Now, a golden opportunity came for David
to be able to put an end to Saul
and to all of this hiding that David had had to be doing for so long.
Now, let’s read what it says, verse 7:
“So David and Abishai made their way to the troops by night,
“and they found Saul lying asleep in the camp enclosure
“with his spear stuck to the ground next to his head;
“Abner and the troops were lying all around him.
“Abishai now said to David:
“‘Today God has surrendered your enemy into your hand.
“‘And now, please, let me pin him to the ground
“‘with the spear just once,
“and I will not need to do it twice.’
“However, David said to Abishai:
“‘Do not harm him,
“‘for who can lift his hand against the anointed of Jehovah
“and remain innocent?’
“David continued:
“‘As surely as Jehovah is living,
“‘Jehovah himself will strike him down,
“‘or his day will come and he will die,
“‘or he will go down into battle and perish.
“‘It is unthinkable from Jehovah’s standpoint
“‘for me to lift my hand against the anointed of Jehovah!
“‘So now take, please, the spear next to his head and the water jug,
and let us be on our way.’”
Well now, it would have been so easy
for David to kill Saul, right?
But what helped David
to act modestly in this situation?
Well, let’s consider the first factor:
David had to consider his own position,
or his own authority.
Now, had Jehovah instructed David to kill Saul?
No.
Jehovah had never assigned David to carry out that task.
After all, Saul was anointed by Jehovah
to be the king of Israel,
so David acknowledged
that he simply did not have the authority to kill Saul.
It was not his place.
But now, let’s consider a second factor.
Notice verse 10.
Do you remember what David said?
He said: “As surely as Jehovah is living,
“Jehovah himself will strike him down,
“or his day will come and he will die,
or he will go down into battle and perish.”
Well, what’s the point?
You see, David had complete confidence in Jehovah.
You see, instead of taking matters into his own hands,
he had the total confidence
that Jehovah was going to handle this situation
in his own way and in his own time
David modestly trusted in Jehovah.
Well, David acted modestly on that occasion.
But perhaps you can think of a few other occasions later in his life
when he didn’t act so modestly.
What’s the lesson?
Modesty is a quality
that we must work hard to develop,
but we must also work hard to maintain our modesty.
Otherwise, our minds can begin to focus
on our strengths, on our talents, and on our abilities
to such an extent
that we begin to get a very distorted view of self.
When that happens, our modesty can begin to disappear,
and we can begin to behave presumptuously.
Now, who is one of the greatest examples of this in the Bible?
Well, perhaps right away you think of the example of Uzziah.
And if you go in your Bible to 2 Chronicles chapter 26,
let’s just review for a minute
what we know about Uzziah and what happened to him.
You see in 2 Chronicles 26:4—
Do you see what it says?
“He [speaking of Uzziah]
“continued to do what was right in Jehovah’s eyes,
“just as his father Amaziah had done.
“And [you notice this] he kept searching for God
“in the days of Zechariah, who taught him to fear the true God.
“During the time he was searching for Jehovah,
the true God made him prosper.”
Now, do you hear the modesty there? Did you hear it?
Well, you see, it says Uzziah was not a self-satisfied person
at that point in his life.
He was searching for Jehovah.
He felt the need for Jehovah’s guidance
and wisdom and blessing in his life.
But what happened?
If you go down to verse 16, do you see?
“However, as soon as he was strong,
“his heart became haughty to his own ruin,
“and he acted unfaithfully against Jehovah his God
“by entering the temple of Jehovah
to burn incense on the altar of incense.”
Can you imagine?
He became so emboldened
that he actually went into Jehovah’s temple
and burned incense on the altar of incense.
Well, the priests came running.
And what did they say to him? Do you see verse 18?
“It is not proper for you, Uzziah, to burn incense to Jehovah!
“It is only the priest who should burn incense,
“for they are the descendants of Aaron, those who have been sanctified.
“Go out from the sanctuary,
“for you have acted unfaithfully
and you will receive no glory from Jehovah God for this.”
Well, Uzziah started out fearing God.
He started out searching for Jehovah,
but when he became powerful, what happened?
He quickly lost his modesty.
Well now, brothers, why is this an important discussion,
really, for all of us?
Well, all of us face trying situations in life.
And when we face those situations,
we may be tempted
to want to rush in and handle them.
We may be tempted to ignore Bible principles
and even published direction that we have
from “the faithful and discreet slave.”
How wise we are in those moments, in those situations,
to step back for a moment,
take a deep breath, count to ten,
and say to ourselves:
‘Do I really have the authority to do what I’m about to do?
‘Is it really my place to say what I’m about to say?
‘Instead, would it be better
to wait on Jehovah to correct this situation?’
You see, by having a proper view of self,
by sticking closely to the direction that we have from Jehovah
and from “the faithful and discreet slave,”
and by maintaining our full and complete confidence
that Jehovah will correct any matters
that need to be rectified,
we can have the privilege to walk
—not just for a short time but to walk eternally—
in modesty with our magnificent,
our wonderful God, Jehovah.

cn.text: 想要跟耶和华上帝
有很好的关系
我们就必须要有
谦虚这个特质
我们都记得
圣经在弥迦书6:8说
“世人啊，上帝已经告诉你什么是善
耶和华对你有什么要求呢？
他只是要你处事公正
喜爱忠贞
谦虚地
与你的上帝同行。”
那么，谦虚是什么意思呢？
刚才我们都听到了弟兄姐妹们的评论
他们都提到了关于谦虚的几种解释
他们提到的基本上都差不多
但还是有些微小的差异
关于谦虚
2000年的《守望台》
提到了一段很有意思的解释
文章是这样说的
谦虚这个特质
含有几个不同方面的意思
例如
一个谦虚的人
不自高自大
也不会夸耀自己的才能
成就或财富
据一本参考书说
谦虚也含有“留在限度之内”的意思
谦虚的人会说话、举止得体
不越权妄为
他们承认
自己应该做和能够做的事
都有适当的限度
他也知道
有些事是自己无权过问的
这个解释非常清楚，是不是
这帮助我们了解
谦虚可以表现在不同方面
今天
我们会重点讨论其中一个方面
也就是一个谦虚的人
承认自己应该做和能够做的事
都有适当的限度
一个谦虚的人会承认
自己在很多方面
是有能力和权利限度的
我们都知道
自己在身体上是有限度的
例如
如果你不擅长游泳
你到海边的时候
你大概不会直接跳到海里游泳
因为你知道自己做不到
如果你身体不舒服
你大概也不会参加纽约马拉松比赛
所以我们都知道
自己在身体上会有哪些局限
但是谦虚的人
不单单只会承认自己在身体上有所限制
圣经里有一个例子
可以帮助我们更清楚看出这点
我们看看撒母耳记上第26章
我们会从第7节开始读
26章第7节
你看看经文的上下文就会知道
这节经文的背景是
为了躲避扫罗王的追杀
大卫到处躲藏
对大卫来说
现在出现了一个绝佳的机会
他可以杀死扫罗王
并结束他一直以来
到处流浪的亡命生涯
我们从第7节开始读
“于是大卫和亚比筛在夜里潜入军营
看见扫罗在营里睡着了
他的矛插在他头旁边的地上
押尼珥和军兵都睡在他周围
亚比筛对大卫说
今天上帝把你的敌人交在你手里了
现在请让我用矛把他刺透在地上
一下就行了，不用刺两下
大卫对亚比筛说
不要伤害他
谁能动手伤害
耶和华任命的领袖而无罪呢？
大卫又说
永活的耶和华可以作证
他会被耶和华处决
或者有一天会寿终而死
或者会在战场上阵亡
在耶和华看来
我动手伤害耶和华任命的领袖
是万万不该的！
现在
请你把他头旁边的长矛
和水瓶拿来
我们走吧。”
你看，大卫要杀死扫罗
是不是轻而易举的事呢？
但是什么帮助大卫
在这种情况下
表现谦虚呢？
我们来谈谈第一个原因
大卫必须考虑到自己的身份
也就是他的权力限度
那，耶和华有指示大卫去杀死扫罗吗？
没有
耶和华从来没有吩咐大卫去做这件事
毕竟，扫罗是耶和华挑选的
以色列的君王
大卫的决定表明
他承认自己没有权力杀死扫罗
他无权这样做
现在来谈谈第二个原因
请留意第10节大卫说什么
他说
“永活的耶和华可以作证
他会被
耶和华处决
或者有一天会寿终而死
或者会在战场上阵亡。”
重点是什么？
就是大卫对耶和华有完全的信心
与其靠着自己的能力解决问题
不如把事情交给耶和华
按照耶和华的方法
在他指定的时间
来解决问题
我们看出
大卫谦虚地依靠耶和华
大卫在这件事上表现了谦虚
但其实，在他的一生中
有那么几次他没有表现谦虚
我们学到什么？
谦虚这个特质是我们必须努力培养的
但我们还要努力保有这个特质
要不然
很可能
我们的思想就会集中在自己的优势
自己的才干
和我们自己擅长做的事上
以至于我们开始过度关注自己
变得骄傲
这样，我们就会失去谦虚这个特质
我们会变得自负，不受约束
在这方面，你会想到圣经里的哪个例子呢？
你可能马上想到的
是犹大王乌西雅
我们一起翻开历代志下26章
我们来看看乌西雅王做了什么事情
以及在他身上发生了什么事
我从26章4节开始读
请弟兄姐妹留意经文怎么说
“乌西雅
一直做耶和华眼中正确的事
就像他父亲亚玛谢一样
撒迦利亚在世的时候
教导他敬畏上帝。”
请留意这里说什么
“他就一直敬奉上帝
在他敬奉耶和华的那段时期
上帝赐福给他。”
你觉得乌西雅王是谦虚的吗？
你看得出来吗？
经文说得很清楚
在那个时候，乌西雅王很谦虚
一点都不骄傲
他想让耶和华高兴
他寻求上帝的指引和智慧
上帝因此赐福给他
但后来呢？
我们继续看看第16节
第16节说
“可是
他一强大起来
就心高气傲
自取灭亡
他对耶和华他的上帝不忠
竟闯进耶和华的圣殿
要在香坛上烧香。”
他竟然变得骄傲自大
闯进耶和华的圣殿
想要在香坛上烧香
第18节，祭司对他说
“乌西雅
烧香给耶和华不是你该做的事！
只有祭司才可以烧香
因为他们是亚伦的子孙
上帝使他们成圣去担任这个工作
离开这个神圣的地方吧
你做了对上帝不忠的事
耶和华上帝
不会因为你烧香而给你尊荣。”
乌西雅王
敬畏过上帝
他寻求过耶和华
不过
当他变得强大的时候
就发生了什么事呢？
他就变得不再谦虚了
所以，弟兄姐妹们
为什么今天提到的事很重要呢？
因为
我们所有人都会面对艰难的处境
我们遇到难题的时候
可能很想立刻采取行动
想要用自己认为对的方式去处理问题
但我们可能会忽略圣经原则
或是忽略忠信睿智的奴隶
在圣经出版物中提出的指引
所以当难题发生时
怎么做才是明智的呢？
我们要停下来
深呼吸
从1数到10
然后问问自己
我真的有权力
这么做吗？
我真的有权力这么说吗？
还是
我把事情交托给耶和华
由耶和华来处理
会不会更好呢？
如果我们对自己有适当的看法
同时也仔细留意
耶和华
以及忠信睿智的奴隶提出的指引
并且
全心信赖耶和华
相信他一定会处理
任何必须受到纠正的事情
我们就有荣幸
可以谦虚地
与伟大的上帝耶和华同行
不是只有现在，而是永远与他同行

titles.en: Mark Sanderson: “Wisdom Is With the Modest Ones” (Prov. 11:2)

ko.text: 맡겨 주신 일 하며 승인을 얻을 때.”
바로 왕국을 전파하고 제자 삼는 일이죠.
그 상징으로 침례받는 단계까지 발전하는 모습을 보는 것은
정말 특별한 경험이 아닐 수 없습니다.
예수께서 어떻게 사랑과 관심을 나타내셨는지 보겠습니다.
사람들에 대한 사랑을 알 수 있죠.
그분은 이 땅에 계신 기간 내내
한 선교인 자매와 나눈 대화가 생각나는데요.
여섯 건은 다른 사람한테 인계할 수 있었죠.
하지만 이 네 건은 인계를 못 하겠어요.
하지만 사람들에 대한 사랑을 잘 보여 주죠?
전파 활동이 훌륭한 일인 건 사실이지만,
그 일을 실제로 하는 게 언제나 쉽지만은 않습니다.
“여호와의 말씀이 저에게 온종일 모욕과 놀림거리가 되었습니다.
그래서 ‘내가 그분에 대해 이야기하지 않고, 더 이상 그분의 이름으로 말하지 않으리라’ 했지만.”
이렇게 느낄 때가 있는 게 정상일까요?
“제 마음속에서 그 말씀이 마치 뼛속에 갇혀 타오르는 불같이 되었습니다.
제가 그것을 억누르기에 지쳐서 더 이상 견딜 수 없었습니다.”
그는 계속 마음을 쏟을 수 있었고,
하느님의 말씀을 연구하는 일을 대신할 수 없다는 걸 알게 됩니다.
무엇이 자신의 “뼛속에 갇혀 타오르는 불” 같다고 했나요?
그가 사람들에게  전해야 할 소식이 얼마나 중요한지
“영원한 생명을 얻기에 합당한 성향을 가진 사람들”을 찾기 위해
최선을 다해야 한다는 걸 늘 생각하게 됩니다.
여호와께선 기꺼이 우리에게 성령을 주실 것입니다.
효과적으로 봉사하는 데 필요한 것을 주실 것입니다.
충실하고 슬기로운 종이 베풀어 주는 제안을 적용하는 것입니다.
우리 자신에게 너무 많은 것을 기대했기 때문일 겁니다.
제공 연설을 아주 멋지게 해야 한다거나
일정량의 출판물을 꼭 전해야 한다고 느꼈을지 모릅니다.
하지만 봉사에서 여러 조정이 있게 된 것은
그래서 우리는 부담감을 덜 수 있게 되는데요.
잠깐 예수께서 보이신 본을 다시 생각해 보겠습니다.
나중에 믿게 된 그 모든 사람도 생각해 보십시오.
예수께서 물을 달라며 대화를 시작하신 것의 결과였습니다.
원하는 만큼 호별 봉사를 할 기회가 많지는 않지만,
대화를 시작할 기회가 생길 수 있습니다.
여호와께 감사하는 마음을 나타내는 좋은 방법입니다.
우리는 모든 기회를 활용하여 증거를 시작합니다.
오늘 감사함을 나타내는 여러 방법 중
우리의 봉사를 발전시킬 수 있는 제안을 적용하는 것,
다른 많은 충실한 여호와의 증인들을 본받도록 합시다.
하느님과 사람들에 대한 사랑을 나타내기 위해 최선을 다하면서
감사하는 마음으로 계속 좋은 소식을 전파해야겠습니다.

en.text: “How does it make you feel,
“knowing God’s support is real,
“and that he’s entrusted [us]
to do the work we do?”
We know that song.
We love that song.
But have you ever stopped to meditate on the lyrics?
How do we feel?
Because, really, it’s a tremendous, amazing privilege
that Jehovah has entrusted to his people
—the work of Kingdom preaching and disciple-making.
Now, while the work at Bethel contributes to the preaching work
in a very precious and unique way,
we still recognize it’s quite special
to be able to assist someone in the ministry
and watch them progress to the point of making a dedication
and symbolizing that by water baptism.
Our text comments mention the qualities
of gratitude and undeserved kindness.
And these are good qualities
because they’re qualities that motivate us,
that move us to action,
that touch our emotions.
Why is this emotional investment
so important when it comes to our ministry?
Well, think, for example,
of our greatest Teacher and Preacher
who ever walked the earth, and that is Jesus Christ.
Turn with me in your Bibles, please, to Luke chapter 19,
and we’ll just take a look at one instance
of how Jesus demonstrated this love and concern.
Luke 19:41
says: “And when he [that is, Jesus] got nearby,
“he viewed the city [Jerusalem]
and wept over it.”
How interesting!
Jesus’ heart was filled with so much emotion
that his eyes brimmed over with tears when he contemplated the people,
their rejection of the message,
the siege that was to follow.
Doesn’t that show his love for people?
And obviously, that love was made evident
the entire time that he was here on the earth.
Now, we may not give way to tears
every time we go into our territory and engage in the ministry,
but certainly we want to imitate Jesus’ example,
because it’s so vital that we have and demonstrate love for people.
It reminds me of a conversation I had with a missionary sister some time ago,
and at the time, she was revealing her personal circumstances.
And she felt that at that time
she could comfortably handle ten Bible studies.
So I asked her how things were going.
She said, “Well, actually I have 20.”
She said, “I was able to get rid of six.”
She said, “But I just can’t turn over these last four.”
She said, “They’re such a part of my life;
I just can’t let them go.”
Well, it sounds like a good problem to have.
But doesn’t it highlight her love for people?
She was emotionally invested.
Now, we also have to admit
that while preaching is a wonderful work,
actually carrying it out is not always easy to do.
Perhaps at times we may feel like the prophet Jeremiah.
You recall when he was commissioned as a prophet,
he gave Jehovah a number of reasons why he shouldn’t be selected.
He was too shy, too young, wasn’t able to speak well.
And then once he got into his assignment
and the opposition and the ridicule started
—well, let’s take note of his feelings.
Turn with me, please, to Jeremiah chapter 20,
Jeremiah chapter 20.
We’ll begin with the B  part of verse 8:
“For me the word of Jehovah
“has been the cause of insults and jeering all day long.
“So I said: ‘I am not going to make mention of him,
and I will speak no more in his name.’”
Have you ever had times when you felt like Jeremiah,
when you just didn’t have the desire
or feel like speaking to others about Jehovah?
And maybe it was for similar reasons:
We’re shy; we feel nervous;
people in the territory are indifferent.
Or could it just be that we’re just tired?
The energy that we feel we need, we just don’t have it.
Is it normal to feel this way at times?
Absolutely.
But let’s take note of what Jeremiah says next.
Let’s finish verse 9.
He says: “But in my heart
“it became like a burning fire shut up in my bones,
“and I was tired of holding it in;
I could no longer endure it.”
You notice, it was Jeremiah’s love for Jehovah,
his zeal for the truth, his strong spirituality
—all of these were things that were able to help him remain invested
and be able to overcome any temporary discouragement
that he might have been feeling at that time.
So, what can help us to stay invested
and to maintain our love for people?
Well, there are many ways, but we’ll discuss two.
First, Jeremiah’s example shows us
that there is never a substitute
for the study of God’s Word.
Did you notice,
What was that ‘burning fire shut up in his bones’?
Verse 8 tells us it was “the word of Jehovah.”
So it was Jeremiah’s appreciation
for the importance of his message
that made him responsive
to the encouragement he received when he read God’s Word.
And it works the same for us as well.
Study of God’s Word helps to reinforce our love for Jehovah.
It’s a constant reminder that we’re living in the last days,
that we’re deep in the time of the end,
and that we need to do all that we can to find
those who are “rightly disposed for everlasting life.”
Yes, it is natural that we are going to experience
discouragement from time to time,
but when we pray to Jehovah for help,
you see, if his Word is in our hearts,
then Jehovah can freely impart his holy spirit to us.
He can give us what we need
to be bold preachers of the good news
and be productive in our ministry.
Now, the second thing that can help us
is applying the suggestions that are given to us
by the slave to help us improve our ministry.
Now, perhaps in the past, preaching may have been difficult,
maybe just because of pressure we put upon ourselves.
Perhaps we may have felt that we had to have the perfect presentation
or we had to place a certain amount of literature.
But how loving it is that we see
that with the various adjustments that have been made in our ministry,
well, hopefully some of that anxiety has been lifted
because now we know our focus is on starting conversations!
And with the help of prayer and God’s spirit,
we can see how that just naturally progresses into a witness.
If we just think back for a moment to the example of Jesus,
we can only imagine how many preaching opportunities
Jesus must have had just from starting conversations.
Of course, the one we’re most familiar with is in John chapter 4
—the Samaritan woman at the well.
Not only was that a great witness
but just think about all of those who became believers afterward.
And all of that started simply from Jesus starting a conversation
—asking for water.
We may not always have as many opportunities at Bethel
to engage in the house-to-house work as we would like,
but certainly as we travel, as we move about,
this can present greater opportunities
to start conversations.
In last month’s meeting workbook, there was an article
“Starting Conversations That Can Lead to a Witness,”
and that article just provided many excellent, practical suggestions
that we can implement.
So if we follow these suggestions,
well, this is a nice way that we can show and demonstrate our gratitude.
We’re making the best use of our time to start a witness.
So, as we mentioned,
there are many ways that we can show our gratitude.
But certainly these two:
Our study of God’s Word and applying the suggestions to improve our ministry
are two ways that we can certainly implement.
So in imitation of Jesus, Jeremiah,
many other faithful Witnesses of Jehovah,
may we do what we can to show that we are invested,
that we show our love for God and our love for people
as we appreciatively carry out our commission to preach the good news.

cn.text: “传道感觉真好！
这项任务很重要
耶和华亲自托付
提供仁爱指导”
我们都知道这首歌，我们也都很喜欢这首歌
但你思考过这些歌词吗？
你觉得怎么样呢？
耶和华把传道教人
使人做门徒的工作交托给我们
这是多大的荣幸啊！
我们很珍惜伯特利的服务
因为在这里我们也能够
以一种特别的方式支持传道工作
但我们还是可以实际去传道
帮助别人进步，献身受浸给耶和华
今天的《守望台》段落
提到分外恩典和感激之心
这打动我们的内心
激励我们采取行动去关心别人
为什么在传道时
我们发自内心，真诚地关心别人
很重要呢？
为了说明这一点
让我们来想想耶稣基督的例子
他是我们的伟大导师，也是非常好的传道员
请大家打开圣经
路加福音19章
我们来看看
耶稣基督怎样表达对人的爱和关心
路加福音19:41 说
“快到耶路撒冷的时候
耶稣看着城，为城哭泣。”
就是为耶路撒冷哭泣
你看
当耶稣想到耶路撒冷的居民
想到日后敌军围困这座城的情景
也想到他们拒绝真理时
心里就充满感情，流下泪来
耶稣很爱别人
他的一生都在向人表明他的爱
当然我们向人传道的时候
不可能每次都流下眼泪
但我们很想效法耶稣的榜样
因为我们爱别人
向别人表明我们爱他们非常重要
这让我想到之前
我跟一个特派传道员姐妹的对话
当时她告诉我她的传道情况
她说如果学生超过10个
她教导起来就比较吃力了
所以我问她那你有几个学生？
她说:“其实我之前有20个
但其中的6个我已经交给了别人
剩下的4个我实在舍不得
他们是我生活的一部分。”
这是一个很好的难题，是吧
这表明她很爱别人
传道时总是对人怀着感情，对吗？
虽然传道工作非常美好
但我们不得不承认
实际做起来
并不总是那么容易
也许有时候
我们也觉得自己像耶利米
你还记得吗？
他告诉上帝很多他不想做先知的理由
他太害羞了，太年轻了
并且不擅长表达
他接受委派后就开始面对反对和嘲笑
我们来看看他内心的感受
耶利米书20章
我们从8节的后半部分开始读
“耶和华的话使我整天受人辱骂讥讽
于是我说
我不想再提起他
也不想再奉他的名说话了。”
你曾经也像耶利米先知一样吗？
那时你不想出去传道
也许原因跟耶利米的差不多
例如:我们很害羞
也很容易紧张
或者地区里的人对真理反应很冷淡
或者我们就是觉得自己好累
我们需要的那股力量现在没有了
这种感觉是正常的吗？
当然
但请留意耶利米在9节的后半部分怎么说
耶利米说
“可是他的话就像火，在我心里燃烧
困在我的骨头里，我再也忍不住
不能不说出来。”
你留意到了吗？
耶利米非常爱耶和华上帝
他也很爱真理
他也知道什么事最重要
这三个因素都推动他想要做好先知的工作
并帮助他成功克服之前灰心失望的感觉
什么能帮助我们保持传道的热心
继续爱地区里的人呢？
我们来讨论两个方法
首先
耶利米的榜样告诉我们
没有什么方法能够取代研读上帝的话语
是什么东西“像火一样燃烧
困在他的骨头里”呢？
8节告诉我们，就是“耶和华的话”
耶利米真的非常珍视耶和华上帝的话语
所以当他读到上帝的话语时
就很想告诉别人
我们也应该像耶利米一样
研读耶和华的话语会加强我们对他的爱
我们离终结很近了
所以我们需要尽一切努力
找到那些有正确态度
而可以得到永远生命的人
当然，我们有时候会灰心沮丧
但如果我们珍视上帝的话语
并且经常研读
也向他祷告，求他帮助我们
他就会赐给我们他的神圣力量
帮助我们成为勇敢的传道员
并且在传道工作上结出丰硕的果实
现在我们来看看
帮助我们保持热心的第二个方法
就是把忠信睿智奴隶的建议运用出来
以前，我们可能对自己的要求太高
所以觉得传道工作很困难
例如向人传道时，一定要说得很完美
或者一定要分发多少数量的书籍杂志
近年来，组织在传道工作上做了一些调整
我们更重视怎样跟人开始交谈
希望这样的调整可以减轻一些传道员的压力
靠着祷告和神圣力量
我们都可以很自然地展开交谈向人作见证
我们来想想耶稣的例子
有好几次
耶稣只是很自然地跟人交谈
就打开了一个向人作见证的机会
例如在约翰福音4章
他向一个在井边的撒马利亚妇人说话
这是多么好的一次交谈
后来很多人还因此成为耶稣的门徒
这样的好成果
仅仅是因为耶稣说了一句
请给我点水喝
在伯特利工作
我们可能没有很多机会挨家挨户地向人传道
但只要我们出门买东西
或去旅游
我们都有很多机会可以跟人展开交谈
上个月的《聚会手册》里
有篇文章
题目是《开始交谈就能为作见证创造机会》
文章提供了很多实用又有效的传道建议
如果我们把这些建议运用出来
这就表明我们感激耶和华
同时也表明我们正善用时间为王国作见证
就像我们刚刚提到的
我们有两个方法可以表明我们感激上帝
就是:研读上帝的话语
以及把组织的建议运用出来
改善自己的传道技巧
我们可以向耶稣
耶利米
还有耶和华的其他忠仆学习
我们要继续热心宣扬王国的好消息
这就表明我们爱上帝，以及爱其他人
