title: 제프리 W. 잭슨: 예상치 못한 일을 받아들이십시오

ko.text: 졸업식 프로그램이 이런 식으로 바뀔 것이라고는
우리 중 아무도 예상하지 못하셨을 것입니다.
곧 졸업생이 되실 길르앗 학생 여러분을
여러분이 이러한 변화를 훌륭하고 긍정적인 태도로 받아들였기 때문입니다.
이제 곧, 원래 계시던 곳이든 새로운 곳이든,
그곳에서도 여러분은 분명히 예상치 못한 일을 겪게 되실 겁니다.
이와 관련된 한 가지 부면을 함께 살펴보겠습니다.
이 성구는 한 가지 예상치 못한 일을 이렇게 묘사합니다.
“내가 보니 종들은 말을 타고 군왕들은 종처럼 걷는구나.”
어떻게 이러한 일이 생길 수 있을까요?
“능력이 뛰어난 사람이라고 해서 항상 인정받는 것은 아닙니다.
때로는 능력이 더 적은 사람이 더 많은 영예를 받기도 합니다.”
여러분은 어떤 새로운 특권이 주어지지 않을까 하는 마음이 생길 수도 있습니다.
여러분이 바라는 그 특권을 받게 될 수 있습니다.
이런 특권을 받을 줄은 상상도 못했어요!”
길르앗 훈련을 받은 건 바로 난데.
그분은 우리가 예상치 못한 방식으로 일하실 때가 있습니다.
예상치 못한 사람에게 특권을 주실 수 있죠.
여러분이 받은 초대가 예상치 못한 일일 수 있습니다.
네, 다른 사람들도 우리가 특권을 받을 때
다른 사람이 특권을 받는 예상치 못한 일이 생길 때,
어떻게 그 상황을 잘 받아들일 수 있습니까?
성경에 담긴 두 가지 원칙을 보시죠.
“눈에 보이는 것을 즐기는 것이 욕망을 쫓아 헤매는 것보다 나으나,
다른 특권을 더 가지려고 하지 마시기 바랍니다.
길르앗에 와서 훈련받은 것도 여러분이 지금 가진 특권입니다.
“내가 당신의 생각나게 하는 것들에 고착하니, 오 여호와여,
내가 당신의 계명의 길을 열렬히 추구하리니,
그것을 받아들이도록 내 마음을 넓혀 주시기 때문입니다.”
그분은 이렇게 말씀하고 계신 것일 수 있습니다.
너는 이미 많은 특권을 받지 않았니.
이제 내가 다른 사람에게 예상치 못한 특권을 줄 때 기뻐해라.’
이런 상황에서 도움이 되는 또 한 가지는
성경에 나오는 여러 가지 기록들을 기억하는 것입니다.
다윗이 거인 골리앗과 싸우겠다고 나서기 전이라면
누가 그 거대한 골리앗을 쓰러뜨릴 거라고 예상하셨겠습니까?
아마도 가장 먼저 떠오른 사람은 사울왕이었을 겁니다.
그는 보통 사람들보다 머리에서 어깨까지만큼 키가 더 컸고,
그의 아들인 요나단을 떠올릴 수도 있었을 것입니다.
사실, 요나단은 그 당시에 국가적인 영웅이었기 때문입니다.
요나단과 그의 수종은 용감하게 언덕 위로 올라가
요나단을 예상하는 사람들도 분명 있었을 것입니다.
무릿매를 사용하는 게 제일 좋은 방법이라고 생각했다고 합시다.
그렇다면 그렇게 할 사람이 누구라고 예상하시겠습니까?
사울의 형제들이 돌팔매질을 자유자재로 했다고 알려 줍니다.
여호와께서 어떤 일을 하실지 모르는 상황에서
분명 사울왕과 요나단이 적임자라고 생각했을 겁니다.
물론 사자와 곰을 죽인 적은 있지만,
골리앗은 이 어린 소년이 자신과 싸우러 오는 모습을 보고 깜짝 놀랐죠.
무릿매를 잘 쓰는 것으로 유명했던 사람들 가운데 포함되지 않았죠.
다윗은 베냐민 지파의 영토 근처에 살았기 때문에
그곳에서 무릿매 던지는 기술을 익혔을 수 있습니다.
그 누구도 어린 소년이었던 다윗이 사용될 거라고 예상하지는 않았을 것입니다.
사람들이 보인 반응에 대해 생각해 보겠습니다.
다윗을 죽이고 싶을 만큼 강한 질투로 바뀌었습니다.
그는 다윗과 아주 튼튼한 우정을 쌓았습니다.
이 기록을 통해 무엇을 배울 수 있습니까?
네, 다른 누군가가 어떤 훌륭한 특권을 받게 됐다면,
그런데 그 특권이 여러분이 오랫동안 사모해 왔고
어느 정도 받을 자격도 있다고 생각해 온 특권이라면,
예상치 못한 특권이 주어질 수 있다는 걸
여호와께서 다른 사람을 통해 자신의 이름을 영광스럽게 하실 때
네, 다른 사람이 예상치 못하게 사용될 때에도

en.text: Expect the unexpected.
Well, the unexpected has arrived, hasn’t it?
None of us expected that this graduation program
would need to be modified and changed as it is.
And yet, what have you had to do?
You’ve had to accept the unexpected.
There’s not much you can do.
And we’d like to commend you students,
soon-to-be graduates of this class of Gilead,
because you have accepted these changes
in a fine, positive attitude.
But it does highlight to us —doesn’t it?—
that sometimes it can be disappointing
when unexpected things occur.
Now soon, you’ll be going to your assignments,
whether back home or to a new assignment.
And, no doubt, you are going to face
some unexpected things as well.
And we’d just like to discuss one aspect of this theme.
If you’d like to take your Bibles
and turn with me to Ecclesiastes chapter 10,
Ecclesiastes 10:7,
and here it describes something that is unexpected:
“I have seen servants on horseback
but princes walking on foot just like servants.”
Well, you wouldn’t expect to see that, would you?
Now, how are you going to see that?
Well, The Watchtower made a very interesting comment
about this verse that said:
“Those who have great ability
“do not always receive the recognition.
“And those with less ability
sometimes receive more honor.”
So when you arrive back full of enthusiasm
—you’ve enjoyed your Gilead training,
and no doubt you’re thinking:
‘I’m a different person. I’ve changed.’
And we hope you have.
Maybe you might expect
that there will be certain privileges granted to you.
And yet, at the same time,
you may see that someone you don’t expect
is given those privileges.
They may even come up to you and say: “I’m so surprised!
I’m shocked they’ve given me this privilege!”
And outwardly you say, “Hmm,”
but inwardly you’re saying: “I’m shocked too,
“because I’m the one who is trained at Gilead.
Surely I should get this privilege.”
But when you think about it,
remember that Jehovah is the one
who is backing the work, and at times,
he does the unexpected and, in this case,
gives someone we don’t expect a privilege.
Think about it for a few moments.
When you first came here, we know and remember your introductions,
and quite a number of you made the comment:
“When we received that invitation to Gilead, we were shocked!
“We were humbled.
“We were amazed, numb all over,
thinking why we were selected.”
And maybe some of the people in your congregation and branch
were also saying, “Why were they accepted?”
You see, maybe that was an unexpected invitation.
But now, here you are about to graduate.
But it’s good to remember that sometimes others are surprised
about privileges that we’re given.
So, what can help us to accept the unexpected
when it comes to others getting privileges?
Well, let’s look at two principles in the Scriptures.
The first one is at Ecclesiastes 6:9,
Ecclesiastes 6:9:
“Better to enjoy what the eyes see
“than to wander after one’s desires.
This too is futility, a chasing after the wind.”
So, in other words, be satisfied with the privileges you do have.
Don’t be looking for other privileges,
just not satisfied with what you’ve already been given.
Treasure the privileges you already have.
Included in that is the privilege
of coming here to Gilead and being trained.
Now, the second principle we’d like to highlight
is found in the book of Psalms,
“I cling to your reminders.
“O Jehovah, do not let me be disappointed.
“I will eagerly pursue the way of your commandments
because you make room for it in my heart.”
What’s the point?
Don’t be disappointed.
Trust in Jehovah.
Trust in his arrangement.
It could be that Jehovah is saying to you:
‘Look, you’ve already had enough privileges.
‘You went to Gilead, remember?
‘Now be happy that I’m letting someone else
have an unexpected privilege.’
Well, that can be a test.
Another thing that will help us in a situation like that
is to remember many of the accounts in the Scriptures.
And one of those we like to refer to briefly
is that of David killing Goliath.
Let’s think for a few moments.
If you were an Israelite soldier
just before David offered himself to do this assignment,
who would you have expected
to take down this giant, Goliath?
Well, probably, first of all, you would have thought about King Saul
because, after all, he was head and shoulders taller
than the average person and he was a man experienced in warfare.
So you might have expected,
‘I think King Saul is the one who will take this on.’
Or maybe if you weren’t thinking of King Saul,
you might be thinking of his son Jonathan.
Why?
Well, remember Jonathan was a national hero by this time.
There was the case there at Michmash,
where he and his attendant climbed up
and boldly and bravely appeared before the Philistines.
They killed about 20 of them, and that was the turning point in the battle.
So if anyone is going to take on Goliath, probably you would expect
that Jonathan would be able to do that.
Now, let’s just assume that you were thinking,
‘Maybe the best way to do this would be with a sling and a stone.’
So now, who would you expect to actually do this?
Probably Saul and Jonathan.
Why?
They were from the tribe of Benjamin.
And what do you remember about the people from Benjamin?
They were experts with using the sling.
In fact, we’re told they could sling a stone
to a hairbreadth and would not miss.
And in fact, at 1 Chronicles 12:2,
it says that the brothers of Saul were experts with the sling.
So not knowing what Jehovah was going to do,
probably each one of us, if we were there back then,
would have thought that surely it would be King Saul or maybe Jonathan.
They were the most qualified.
But why wouldn’t you have expected David?
Well, for a start, David was just a boy.
He wasn’t a soldier.
He didn’t have experience in warfare.
Yes, he’d killed a lion and a bear,
but he really didn’t know about fighting people in a war.
Second, he wasn’t impressive in appearance.
In fact, Goliath was shocked
when he saw this young man coming toward him.
And third, he wasn’t from the tribe of Benjamin.
You see, he wasn’t one of these famous persons who could use the sling.
The Watchtower made the comment
that perhaps because David lived near where the tribe of Benjamin was,
maybe that’s where he learned how to use the sling.
But the bottom line is
none of us would have expected
that this young man David would have been used.
It was an unexpected event.
But now, let’s think for a moment about how others reacted.
How did King Saul react?
Well, initially, King Saul was very happy
with the fact that David killed Goliath.
But what happened later?
That turned into jealousy —didn’t it?—
even into a murderous desire to kill David.
But, on the other hand, what about Jonathan?
You see, Jonathan perhaps could have been jealous, but he wasn’t.
He built a strong relationship and friendship with David.
So, what can we learn from this account?
You see, if you come across someone
who gets that ideal privilege
—that assignment that you always secretly have wanted
and that you actually modestly think you deserve—
what will you be?
a Saul or a Jonathan?
Yes, brothers and sisters,
let’s always remember that Jehovah does the unexpected,
and sometimes the unexpected is giving someone else you don’t expect
a certain privilege.
Don’t stand in the way of Jehovah
when he uses someone else to glorify his name.
Yes, rejoice in the fact that others are used,
just like you are being used, in an unexpected way.

你们很快就要从基列学校毕业了

因为你们愿意
而且用积极的态度来接受这些改变
但从这件事我们学习到什么呢？
当意料之外的事发生的时候
我们可能会感觉到很失望
你们就要去执行你们的委派了
无论是回到原有的岗位，还是接获新的委派
很可能，你们会遇到一些你们意料之外的事
所以，我们很想跟你们谈谈
要怎么样应付这种情况
现在，请你跟我一起打开圣经
让我们一起看看传道书的第10章
传道书
第10章第7节
这里就提到了一个意料之外的事
“我看见仆人骑着马
领袖反而走路，像仆人一样。”
这种事很奇怪，很少见对不对？
那为什么会这样子呢？
关于这节经文
《守望台》曾经做了一个很有趣的评论
这里说
很有能力的人不一定受到重用
看来没有什么才华的人
有时却得到许多称赞和关注
现在你毕业了
你满腔热忱想要赶快把学到的用出来
你可能会这样想
我现在不一样了，我已经改变了！
我们希望你真的改变了
也许你期待毕业后
你会得到某些特别的服务
不过，同时你却看到
某个人竟然也得到
那些服务机会
他们甚至还跑过来跟你说
“我好惊讶，真是太不可思议了！
我竟然得到了这个服务机会！”
表面上你说：“嗯！”
但其实你心里却想
“我也很震惊啊！
我才是基列毕业生
应该是我得到这个服务机会才对。”
但请你想想
要记得
是耶和华在指挥他的组织
耶和华做了我们意想不到的事
例如
他赐给某个人特别的服务机会
请你回想一下
你还记得你刚到的时候
你们所有人都做了自我介绍
你们有很多人都这样说
“当我们收到邀请的时候
我们好惊讶
这怎么可能？
太不可思议了！我们都傻了！
然后想他们怎么可能选我们呢？”
可能你们的会众或分部的一些弟兄也说
“怎么会选他啊！”
你看，你来基列学校上课，就是一个意外
但现在，你们坐在这里，很快就要毕业了
所以我们最好记得
有时候别人也会很惊讶
我们得到某些服务机会
如果别人得到
我们很想得到的服务机会
什么能帮助我们接受这个事实呢？
让我们来看看圣经的两个原则
第一个，是在传道书6:9
传道书6:9
“满足于眼前有的
胜过徘徊于欲望之中
这也是空虚，也像捕风。”
所以要满足于我们现在拥有的服务机会
不要觉得自己应该得到更多
老想着其他的服务机会
要珍惜你现在拥有的
这包括你们有殊荣来这里
接受基列学校的培训
接着，我们来看看第二个原则
是记录在诗篇里
“我切实听从你的提醒
耶和华啊，求你不要让我失望
我要热切遵从你的诫命
因为你使我宽心。”
重点是什么？
不要感到失望
要信赖耶和华，相信他的安排
也许耶和华就在对你说
“嘿！你已经有很大的殊荣了！
你还去过基列学校呢！
所以我现在给别人这个意想不到的殊荣
你应该为他感到高兴才对！”
这就看你谦不谦卑了
一个可以帮助我们应付这种情况的方法是
要记得圣经里的许多好榜样
其中一个
我们想提到的是
大卫杀死歌利亚的事
你可以想想看
如果你是一个以色列的战士
就在大卫自告奋勇上战场之前
你觉得谁才有能力杀掉巨人歌利亚呢？
很可能你第一个想到的就是扫罗王
首先，他比所有人都高出一个头
而且他是个身经百战的战士
所以你可能会认为
能杀死歌利亚的非扫罗王莫属
或者，你想到的不是扫罗王
而是他的儿子约拿单
为什么呢？
我们都知道，当时约拿单是个有名的战士
在密抹
约拿单和他的侍卫手脚并用地爬了上去
勇敢无畏地出现在非利士人面前
他们杀了大约20个敌人
而这也是整场战役的转折点
所以
如果你还想到任何一个可以杀死歌利亚的人
那肯定就是约拿单了
也许你在想
“要打败歌利亚，最好用投石袋”
那么哪个人最会使用这个武器呢？
哪一个人最适合上战场呢？
可能还是扫罗和约拿单
为什么？
他们是出自便雅悯部族的
便雅悯部族的人最擅长什么武器呢？
他们都是使用投石带的高手
圣经就说
他们个个都擅长用投石带，能百发百中！
在历代志上12:2
圣经说，扫罗的弟兄也都是投石的高手
我们不知道耶和华会派谁上战场
但我们马上想到的人选
很可能就是扫罗王或是约拿单
他们是最有能力的
那么你为什么没有想到大卫呢？
首先，他当时非常年轻
他不是军人，而且没有任何作战经验
没错，他杀死过狮子和熊
但他肯定不知道怎样打仗
此外，大卫的身材并不魁梧
事实上
歌利亚看到这个小伙子走过来的时候
他非常惊讶
还有一点
他不是出自便雅悯部族的人
所以大卫不是被公认很会使用投石带的人
《守望台》曾经提过
也许因为大卫住的地方离便雅悯部族比较近
所以他有机会学习使用投石带
所以重点是
我们都不会想到
大卫这个年轻人会被上帝任用
这正是意料之外的事
那现在我们来看看别人有什么反应
扫罗有什么反应呢？
刚开始
他知道大卫杀死歌利亚的时候
他非常高兴
但后来呢？
他开始嫉妒大卫
严重到甚至想要杀了他
那约拿单又怎么样呢？
约拿单也有理由嫉妒大卫
但他并没有
约拿单反而跟大卫建立了深厚的友谊
那么，我们可以从这里学到什么呢？
就是
当你知道某个人
得到了一个特别的服务机会
而这个服务机会是你一直很想得到的
而且你觉得自己很有资格做这个服务
你会像谁一样呢？
是扫罗还是约拿单？
没错，弟兄姐妹们
我们要记得
耶和华的作为太奇妙，我们永远无法预料
有时候
他会把服务机会赐给我们意料不到的人
我们千万不要妨碍耶和华
任用某个人去达成他的旨意
是的
别人得到某些殊荣时，我们要为他高兴
就像你们一样
上帝也用出乎意料的方式任用了你们！

title: 마크 샌더슨: 다른 사람의 유익을 구하십시오 (고린도 전서 10:23)

ko.text: 오늘의 성구인 고린도 전서 10:23을 다시 한번 읽어 보실까요?
“모든 것이 허용되지만 모든 것이 세워 주는 것은 아닙니다.
각 사람은 자신의 유익이 아니라 다른 사람의 유익을 계속 구하십시오.”
네, 바울이 한 말의 의미는 무엇입니까?
제가 그 부분을 좀 읽어 드리죠.
행동을 할 수 있는 범위가 넓기 때문에
그리스도인은 그리스도인 양심에 따라 많은 문제들을 결정해야 한다.
그러나 그는 또한 다른 사람들의 양심도 고려해야 한다.
모든 것이 자신에게나 남에게 덕이 되는 것은 아니다.”
특정한 상황에서 우리가 그리스도인으로서 어떻게 행동해야 하는지
성경에 구체적인 법이 나오지 않는 경우가 참 많죠.
여호와께서 우리에게 주신 놀라운 선물인 양심을 사용해야 합니다.
나쁜 행동을 못하게 막아 주는 역할을 주로 떠올리게 될지 모릅니다.
양심을 마치 화재 경보기와 같다고 생각하는 거죠.
화재 경보기는 연기가 조금만 나도 경보음을 울려서
우리가 조처를 취할 수 있게 해 줍니다.
우리가 위험한 길로 들어서려고 할 때 우리에게 경고하는 역할을 합니다.
하늘의 아버지 여호와의 생각과 일치하게 정말로 잘 훈련되어 있다면,
양심은 위험을 경고하는 것보다 훨씬 더 많은 일을 할 수 있습니다.
함께 다윗왕에게 있었던 일을 생각해 보시죠.
다윗은 압살롬의 반역 때문에 예루살렘에서 피신해야 했습니다.
아마 여러분도 잘 아시는 내용일 텐데요,
다윗과 그의 부하들이 광야로 피신해 있다는 것을
충실한 세 명의 남자들이 듣게 되었죠.
암몬 사람들의 랍바에서 나하스의 아들 소비가,
또 밀, 보리, 곡식 가루, 볶은 곡식,
누에콩, 렌즈콩, 구운 곡식, 꿀, 버터, 양, 치즈를 가져왔다.
다윗과 그와 함께한 백성에게 먹으라고 준 것이다.”
빈손으로 광야까지 도망쳐 나왔다는 걸 알게 되었죠.
단지 한두 가지만 가져온 게 아니었습니다.
양심이 작동한 결과 그들은 다윗 일행을 돕기 위해
친절한 행동, 관대한 행동, 선한 행동을 실제로 하게 되었죠.
사실 다윗을 돕는 건 위험한 일이었는데,
그 사실이 알려지면 압살롬이 가만두지 않을 게 뻔했으니까요.
그러니까 자기 목숨을 걸고 도와준 거죠.
옳은 일, 선한 일, 관대한 일을 기꺼이 했던 겁니다.
단지 나쁜 행동을 하지 않도록 막아 주기만 하는 게 아닙니다.
올바르고 친절하고 관대하고 충성스러운 일을 하게 해 줍니다.
예수께서 가르치신 한 가지 비유를 함께 살펴보시겠습니다.
먼저 이 비유에 나오는 몇 가지 세부점을 함께 살펴보겠습니다.
어떤 남자가 예루살렘에서 예리코로 내려가던 중에
강도들은 “그를 때려 반쯤 죽게 된 채로 버려두고” 갑니다.
마침 한 제사장이 그 길로 내려가다가
반쯤 죽은 채 버려진 그 사람을 보게 됩니다.
처음부터 그 자리에 아무도 없었던 것처럼
한 레위 사람도 그를 보고 똑같이 행동합니다.
곤경에 처한 이 남자를 한번 거들떠보지도 않고 말이죠.
상처에 기름과 포도주를 붓고 싸매 주었습니다.
그러고는 그를 자기 짐승에 태워 여관으로 데리고 가서 돌봐 주었습니다.”
그는 여관 주인에게 돈을 주면서 이렇게 말하죠.
비용이 더 들면 내가 돌아올 때에 갚겠습니다.”
사마리아 사람이 이렇게 행동한 이유는 무엇입니까?
그리고 여호와 하느님의 생각과 일치하게 잘 훈련받게 되면,
그 선한 양심은 훨씬 더 많은 일을 하게 됩니다.
단지 나쁜 행동을 하지 않도록 막아 주는 것만이 아니라
올바르고 관대하고 친절한 일을 하도록 우리의 마음을 움직이죠.
어떻게 이 내용을 적용할 수 있을까요?
지금 우리 모두는 현재 사태로 인해
어쩔 수 없이 불안감과 스트레스를 겪고 있습니다.
방에서 갇혀 지내는 시간이 늘어나고 있죠.
유럽에서 코로나 사태로 인해 큰 피해를 입은 한 나라의 사례인데요,
한 자매가 암 치료차 병원에 입원해 있었죠.
자매의 딸과 사위는 베델에서 일하고 있었습니다.
이동 봉쇄령이 내려져 있어서 딸 부부는 자매를 만날 수 없었습니다.
이 자매에게는 한 가지 걱정이 생겼습니다.
병원에서 혼자 기념식을 지켜야 될까 봐 염려가 된 것이었죠.
병원에 와서 기념식을 같이 지켜 주기로 했습니다.
오로지 그 자매를 위해 그러한 친절을 나타내기로 한 것이죠.
자매는 필요한 보호 장비를 착용한 채로
병원에 혼자 있던 그 자매와 함께 기념식을 잘 지킬 수 있었습니다.
병원에서 근무하는 또 다른 젊은 형제가 있었습니다.
코로나 바이러스로 인한 피해가 매우 컸던 나라이기 때문에
우리 형제 자매들 중에도 사망자가 있었습니다.
죽음을 앞둔 여러 형제 자매들을 찾아가 위로를 베풀기로 마음먹었죠.
병원에 찾아와 임종을 지켜 줄 수 없었기 때문입니다.
그 가족들이 그처럼 힘든 시기에 이 형제가 자원하여
그들을 위로하고 사랑을 나타낸 것을 알게 되었을 때
이런 예들에서 무엇을 배울 수 있을까요?
지금 이 시기에 사람들은 스트레스와 불안감이 점점 더 커지고 있습니다.
우리 모두는 친절한 행동과 선한 행동을 통해
다른 사람들에게 도움을 주고 사랑과 관대함을 나타낼 수 있습니다.
따라서 우리의 양심이 선하고 친절하고 관대한 일을 하도록 마음을 움직일 때
하늘에 계신 아버지 여호와를 본받도록 합시다.
우리는 스트레스와 불안감이 줄어드는 것을 느끼게 되고,

en.text: Well, brothers, let’s open our Bibles,
and let’s read again our text for today
—1 Corinthians 10:23.
It says: “All things are lawful,
but not all things are advantageous.”
And then you notice it goes on to say:
“All things are lawful, but not all things build up.
“Let each one keep seeking, not his own advantage,
but that of the other person.”
Now, what is Paul trying to tell us here?
In the 1975 Watchtower, commenting on these two verses,
this is what The Watchtower  said:
“Within the framework of Christian law
“there is a wide latitude of action
“and the Christian has to decide many matters
“according to his Christian conscience.
“But he must consider also the consciences of others.
“Not all things build up
either himself or others.”
Well, now, what’s the point?
There are many, many areas of life
where there is not a specific law
that governs our action as Christians.
We have to use Bible principles
and the wonderful gift of the conscience that Jehovah God has given us.
But most often, we tend to think of the conscience
as something that prevents us
from doing what is wrong.
In fact, maybe we tend to think of it as being like the smoke alarm.
When there’s just that slightest hint of smoke,
that alarm goes off to protect us,
to signal that something is wrong
—something needs to be done.
Well, it’s true that our well-trained conscience can alert us
when we’re about to enter into a course that could cause us danger.
But if our conscience is really well-trained
according to the thinking of our heavenly Father, Jehovah,
it will be able to do even more than that.
Now, what do we have in mind?
Well, let’s consider an example of King David
when he had to flee from Jerusalem
at the time of the revolt of Absalom.
Now, let’s go to 2 Samuel chapter 17.
Now, as you’re looking this up,
2 Samuel chapter 17,
you’ll remember that down here in verse 27,
three faithful men came to know
that David and some of his men were out there in the wilderness.
Now, what did they do? Look at verse 27:
“As soon as David came to Mahanaim,
“Shobi the son of Nahash from Rabbah of the Ammonites,
“Machir the son of Ammiel from Lodebar,
“and Barzillai the Gileadite from Rogelim
“brought beds, basins, clay pots,
“wheat, barley, flour, roasted grain,
“broad beans, lentils, parched grain,
“honey, butter, sheep, and cheese.
“They brought all of this out for David and the people with him to eat,
“for they said [now, notice this]:
“‘The people are hungry and tired
and thirsty in the wilderness.’”
Now, what’s the point?
You see, these men came to know
about David and his men being out there in the wilderness with no supplies.
Now, how did that affect them?
Well, their conscience began to work,
and it showed them they needed to do something to help those men.
Now, when you look at that list of things,
it’s obvious they didn’t just send one or two things,
but their conscience moved them to really do something kind,
to do something generous, to do something good to help them.
Now, consider also that helping David was risky.
Absalom was more than willing to kill people
who were going to support David.
So it took a risk of even their own safety.
But these men, because of their good conscience,
were moved to do the right thing, the good thing, the generous thing.
Now, what do we learn from that?
Well, a well-trained conscience
will not just simply prevent us from doing the wrong thing,
but it has the power to move us to do what’s right,
to do what’s kind, what’s generous, what’s loyal
to our brothers and to Jehovah.
Well, now, Jesus also taught this lesson.
And let’s look at the example that Jesus taught in this parable.
Now, of course, we always used to call it the parable of the good Samaritan,
but now we call it the parable of the neighborly Samaritan.
I’m still getting used to that myself.
But Luke chapter 10—
And let’s just remind ourselves of some of the details about this.
So you remember, first of all, in verse 30:
“[This] man was going . . . from Jerusalem to Jericho
and [he] fell victim to robbers.”
And verse 30 says that they ‘beat him,
and they left him half-dead’ on the road.
Now look at verse 31.
It says here that a priest was going by on the road
and that he saw this man laying on the road half-dead.
And what did he do?
It says he crossed the street.
He went to the other side and passed by
as though that man was not even there.
But now look at verse 32.
Here comes a Levite, and he sees him also.
But what does he do?
Just exactly the same thing.
He crosses the road and passes by
to avoid having to even look at this man who was in distress.
What can you say about those two men?
Their conscience was not working at all, was it?
But now what about the Samaritan?
Verse 33 says that when he saw this man,
“he was moved with pity.”
And what did he do?
Verse 34 says: ‘He approached him,
‘he bandaged his wounds, he poured oil and wine on them,
‘he put the man on his own animal,
‘he brought him to an inn, he took care of him,
‘he took out money, and he gave it to the innkeeper.
‘He said: “Take care of him;
‘“whatever you spend besides this, I’ll come back and I’ll give it to you.
I’ll pay you.”’
Now, what do we know about this man who was a Samaritan?
Obviously, his conscience was working,
and it told him what was the right thing to do
—what was the good thing, the generous thing,
the helpful thing to do— for this man.
Well, what’s the point?
This good conscience
—if it’s well-trained by Bible principles
and by the thinking of our God, Jehovah—
will do so much more
than just prevent us from entering into a wrong course.
It will stimulate us to do the right thing,
the generous thing, the kind thing.
Now, how can we use this information
in the midst today of this coronavirus pandemic?
Well, of course, no doubt all of us right now
are feeling some measure of anxiety and stress
as this goes on week after week,
having to be in our room, sheltering in place, and so on.
It’s not an easy situation for any of us.
In one country in Europe that has been very hard hit
by the pandemic,
a sister was in the hospital for cancer treatment
when the lockdown was enforced.
Now, her daughter and son-in-law are at Bethel.
They’re very, very close to the hospital,
but they were not able to go and visit her because of the situation.
Now, as the Memorial was approaching,
this dear sister was so worried
that she was going to have to celebrate the Memorial
all by herself in the hospital.
But can you imagine how touched she was
when she found out that a sister who worked in the hospital
had very kindly decided to travel to the hospital
when it was not her shift
just for the sole purpose
of being with our sister and celebrating the Memorial?
She dressed up in all the appropriate protective gear
and then enjoyed the Memorial
with our sister who was alone at the hospital.
How beautiful!
In the same country in Europe,
the brothers told about a young brother who works also in a hospital
and, of course, because the country has been so hard hit
and some of our brothers and sisters have died
as a result of the pandemic,
this dear brother has made a point of going to visit
these various brothers and sisters who are dying
to offer them comfort
because their own family members are not able to come to the hospital
and be with them at that time.
Can you imagine how comforting it’s been
for those family members to know
that this young brother has taken the initiative to be with them,
to comfort them, to show them love in such a difficult time?
Well, brothers, what do we learn from all of this?
We are in a time of increased stress,
of increased anxiety.
We all have the power to help others
through acts of kindness and deeds of goodness
that show generosity and love.
Let’s be motivated by our good conscience
to do those good and kind and generous things
that really show that we’re imitators of our heavenly Father, Jehovah.
And as we do, we’re going to find
that our stress will be relieved,
and at the same time, we’ll show that we’re eager to do things
that are not only lawful
but also that are advantageous.

cn.text: 好，弟兄姐妹
我们来打开圣经
今天我们的当日经文是哥林多前书10:23
这里说
“凡事都可以做，但不是样样都有益处。”
接着你继续看，它说
“凡事都可以做
但不是样样都让人受到鼓励
每个人都要时常为别人着想
不要只顾自己。”
保罗在这里是要说什么呢？
关于这两节经文
1975年的《守望台》提到
在基督徒法律的范围之内
我们有很多自由
我们可以根据圣经原则
按照自己的良心做很多事
然而，我们也必须同时考虑到
别人的良心
因为不是所有事情都能鼓励人
那么
这段话的要点是什么呢？
就是在基督徒生活的很多方面
其实圣经并没有给我们很多明文规定
所以我们必须运用圣经原则
还有耶和华上帝赐给我们的
宝贵良心来做决定
通常一般人都觉得
人的良心是可以阻止人做坏事的
我们可以把我们的良心看成是一个警报器
只要侦测到有烟雾，它就会发出声音
告诉我们出问题了
良心也会这样提醒我们
不要再做某件事了
因为我们学习过圣经
当我们快要犯错或者遇到危险的时候
我们的良心就会发出警告
不过，如果我们的良心受过很好的训练
能反映出天父耶和华的想法
那我们的良心就不单只是会发出警告而已
我要说的是什么呢？
你还记得在押沙龙反叛后
大卫王逃离耶路撒冷时发生的一件事吗？
现在我们来看看撒母耳记下17章
请你打开圣经，撒母耳记下17章
27节提到三个忠心的人
他们知道大卫和他的手下来到了旷野
那么，他们做了什么呢？
请看27节
“大卫一到玛哈念
亚扪族的拉巴人拿辖的儿子朔比
罗底巴人亚米利的儿子玛吉
基列的罗基琳人巴西莱
送来床、盆子、陶罐
小麦、大麦、面粉
烘谷、蚕豆、小扁豆
烤谷、蜂蜜、奶油
绵羊、奶酪
他们把这些食物
送给大卫和跟随他的人吃”
请留意，这里他们怎么说
他们说
“大家在旷野一定很累
而且又渴又饿。”
你看出重点是什么吗？
当这三个人知道
大卫和他的手下来到旷野
没有人给他们食物和需要的生活用品时
他们怎么做呢？
他们的良心开始发挥作用
他们看出要做些事来帮助大卫他们
你看看经文里，他们所送的
很明显不是只有一两个东西而已
而是很多很多
所以他们的良心推使他们
做一些仁慈的事
慷慨地帮助大卫
那么你想想
要帮助大卫也是要冒风险的
因为任何人想帮助大卫
押沙龙一定都不会放过
所以，想帮助大卫的人
都是需要冒生命危险的
这三个人的良心推使他们做对的事
好的事、慷慨的事
那么，我们从这个记载学到什么呢？
如果我们的良心跟圣经原则一致
就不会只是不犯错
良心还会推使我们做对的
仁慈的、慷慨的事
也会对弟兄姐妹和耶和华表现忠贞
耶稣也说过一个类似的道理
我们来看看耶稣所说的一个比喻
这个比喻以前叫“良善的撒马利亚人”
现在我们说“有爱心的撒马利亚人”
我也还在慢慢适应
在路加福音第10章
我们来看看这个比喻里面的一些细节
你们还记得吗？
首先在30节
说“有一个人从耶路撒冷下耶利哥去
途中遇劫”
然后经文继续说
这些强盗
“把他打个半死，扔下他就走了。”
我们现在看第31节
这里说
后来
有一个祭司经过那条路
看到一个
被打个半死的人躺在路边
他怎么做呢？
他从另一边绕了过去
假装没看到这个人躺在路上
我们继续看32节
现在来了一个利未族人
他看到这个人，他怎么做呢？
他跟那个祭司一模一样
从另一边绕了过去
避开那个可怜的人
连看都不想看他一眼
你觉得他们怎么样呢？
他们的良心完全没有发挥作用
那个撒马利亚人又怎么样呢？
33节说
他看到这个人，“就十分可怜他”
他走上前去
拿了油和酒，倒在他的伤口上
然后又帮他包扎
又扶他上自己的牲口
带他到客店照顾他
还掏了钱给客店的老板
对他说，请照料他
还有什么花费，我一定会还你的
从这个撒马利亚人做的事
我们看出什么呢？
很明显的，他的良心发挥了很大的作用
任何对这个人有好处、有帮助的事
他都愿意去做
那么，我们从这个比喻学到什么呢？
如果我们按照圣经原则
还有耶和华上帝的思想
来锻炼自己的良心的话
良心就不单单只会阻止我们犯错
它还会推使我们去做对的事
慷慨的事、仁慈的事
面对现在的疫情
我们可以怎样把刚才学到的用出来呢？
当然，我们每一个人在这段时间
一定多多少少都会感到忧虑，有压力
因为我们已经好几个礼拜
都只能待在自己的房间，自己的家里
这对我们每一个人来说都很不容易
在欧洲一个疫情非常严重的国家里
有位姐妹因为癌症而住院
而医院因为疫情的缘故禁止人探病
她的女儿女婿都住在伯特利
虽然离医院很近
但他们还是没有办法去探望她
主的晚餐快到了
这位姐妹非常担心
她必须一个人在医院里面参加主的晚餐
有一位姐妹刚好在这家医院工作
主的晚餐当天虽然她不上班
但她决定特地到医院来
陪这位姐妹一起参加主的晚餐
你可以想象
这个生病的姐妹她有多感动吗？
这位在医院工作的姐妹
她穿上了全套的防护装备
跟这位姐妹一起参加了主的晚餐
这是多么感人的经历啊！
也是在这个国家
有一个年轻的弟兄也在医院里工作
由于疫情非常严重
我们有些弟兄姐妹都因为染病而去世了
这位弟兄发现，因为疫情的关系
这些病危的弟兄姐妹的家人
都没有办法来医院陪伴他们
这个弟兄就决定主动去探望这些弟兄姐妹
看到这位弟兄在疫情最严峻的时候
对弟兄姐妹所表现的爱心
你能想象
这些弟兄姐妹的家人知道了之后
会有多安慰，多感动吗？
那么，弟兄们
我们从这几件事学到什么呢？
现在我们正处于压力、忧虑
都越来越多的时期
但我们还是可以帮助别人
我们可以对别人表现仁慈
对别人表现慷慨
对别人表现爱心
我们可以效法我们的天父耶和华上帝
我们要按照圣经的原则
锻炼自己的良心
让我们的良心推动我们做对的事
如果我们这样做
自己的压力就会减少了
而且这样做也表明
我们不只是想要避免做不对的事
还会努力为别人着想

en.text: Please watch the following video
that contains heartfelt comments
from persecuted brothers
and sisters in Russia,
and see why we have no reason to fear persecution.
I was horrified when several masked officers
broke down two doors and burst into the home
where the meeting was being held.
Everything happened at once
—loud sounds, noise,
the order: “Everyone sit on the floor!”
I was overcome with fear when they put me
in handcuffs, placed me in the police van,
and took me to jail.
I was afraid
because I didn’t know how long
I would be there and what was awaiting me.
When I was being interrogated,
I was afraid that I might be unfaithful
to Jehovah and let my brothers down.
After being detained, I was mostly afraid
about what I would face in prison
—whom I would encounter, how to act, how others would treat me—
the unknown.
When one of the officers
began to describe how bad life is behind bars,
I imagined that behind the officer
stood an angel just like the one
who supported Daniel in the illustration.
This helped me to calm down
and not to panic or be afraid.
That’s how Jehovah supported me.
At the first court appearance,
when I was brought out, the brothers’ feelings
impelled them to show support somehow, and they began applauding.
How that encouraged me
that they were with me!
Fervent and sincere prayers to Jehovah
helped me to cope with these fears.
Isaiah 30:15
gave me much support.
I realized that tranquility
and trust in Jehovah
are now the most important things.
Understanding this
made things much easier for me.
We took the elevator down to the first floor,
the doors opened,
and there stood a large crowd
of our brothers and sisters
—and they all began clapping.
When I saw that, my emotions just welled up,
and I got a lump in my throat.
I felt as if I had wings;
I felt the “great cloud of witnesses.”
I prayed to Jehovah for calmness, courage, and wisdom
and that he help me not to bring reproach on his holy name.
Almost immediately, “the peace of God” came over me,
and I was calm.
The unpleasant sensations did not go away,
but I was no longer afraid.
While overcoming our fear,
my wife and I tried to go out
in service every day.
When you don’t concentrate on yourself
but focus on helping others, fear disappears.
Something that helped me to cope with my fears
is hope,
looking at the situation through Jehovah’s eyes,
seeing what will happen next
that this is not the end of the situation,
but only a difficult phase through which you can pass.
I was helped to cope with my fear
by the words of the song:
“Take one day at a time;
“leave tomorrow until tomorrow;
peace is what I find.”
I understood that it was important
to solve problems as they came up
and not to be troubled by what might never happen.
Fear is interesting;
that is, in principle, fear can be
inside a person, and if someone is afraid,
that is not shameful.
But the question is,
Can you overcome this fear?
Can you get the fear under your control?
Can you overcome this surge of negativity?
And when my heart persuaded me to get scared,
then I started to pray.
I prayed to Jehovah to give me courage
and not be afraid of anyone or anything.
I still say to myself,
‘Feliks, do not fear anybody or anything except Jehovah!’
Dear brothers and sisters, I really appreciate your support.
I’m very happy for all your letters,
for all your thoughts, for all your prayers.
I really appreciate it a lot.
I try to do my best,
and I try to serve Jehovah in the best way that I can.
I will do that forever!

遭受迫害的弟兄姐妹的心声

一些蒙面武装警察突然破门而入

仿佛云彩的见证人在我周围

感动地都快哭了
我觉得我好像鹰一样能展翅高飞
我求耶和华赐给我勇气和智慧
让我保持冷静
帮助我不做任何使他圣名蒙羞的事
就在那个时候，我感受到上帝把
“超越人能理解的安宁”赐给我
虽然情况没有转变，但我已经不再害怕了
这种情况的确不容易
我和妻子都很害怕
但我们还是决定每天出去传道
我们集中精神帮助别人
不是只关心自己，我们就不再害怕了
上帝赐下的希望帮助我不再恐惧
我学会从耶和华的角度来看事情
所以我知道未来会发生什么事
而现在的情况并不是事情最终的结局
只是一个片段而已
我们肯定会渡过这个艰难的时期
一首原创歌曲的歌词帮助我不再害怕
“信赖耶和华每一天
明天的事明天再挂念，心得享平安。”
我现在知道
难题发生的时候，就尽力去解决
但不要担心还没发生的事
“恐惧”很有意思
基本上每个人都会感到恐惧害怕
所以一个人感到害怕并不是什么丢脸的事
但问题是，你可以克服恐惧吗？
你可以控制它吗？
当满脑子都是消极的想法时，你能应付吗？
当我感到恐惧时，我就会向耶和华祷告
求他赐给我勇气
让我不再害怕任何人或任何事
我也告诉自己
不要畏惧任何人或任何事，要敬畏耶和华！
亲爱的弟兄姐妹，非常谢谢你们
你们写的信和为我做的祷告
都很鼓励我，我真的非常感动
我会继续努力，竭尽全力为耶和华服务
我会一直这么做
永远这么做！

titles.cn: 面对迫害，无所畏惧

ko.text: 그는 여호와께서 그들을 어떻게 보호하셨는지 설명한 후에
“그러니 여호와를 두려워하며 충절과 충실로 그분을 섬기고,
‘강’ 건너편과 이집트에서 섬기던 신들을 없애 버리고,
이제 여호와를 섬기는 것이 여러분에게 좋아 보이지 않으면,
아니면 여러분이 살고 있는 아모리 사람들의 땅의 신들이든,
그러나 나와 내 집안은 여호와를 섬기겠습니다.”

en.text: Toward the end of his life,
Joshua assembled all the tribes of Israel
and gave a moving farewell speech.
In it, he recounted how Jehovah protected them.
Listen to his conclusion
as recorded at Joshua 24:14, 15:
“Therefore, fear Jehovah
“and serve him with integrity and faithfulness,
“and remove the gods that your forefathers served
“on the other side of the River and in Egypt,
“and serve Jehovah.
“Now if it seems bad to you to serve Jehovah,
“choose for yourselves today whom you will serve,
“whether the gods that your forefathers served
“on the other side of the River
“or the gods of the Amorites in whose land you are dwelling.
“But as for me and my household,
we will serve Jehovah.”
Did Joshua motivate his listeners?
Verse 16 says:
“At this the people answered:
“‘It is unthinkable for us to abandon Jehovah
and to serve other gods.’”
Verse 31 adds
that “Israel continued to serve Jehovah
“all the days of Joshua
and all the days of the elders who outlived Joshua.”
This teaches us something
about how we can conclude a discussion effectively.
Our final words should connect to the overall topic,
motivate our listeners, and be simple and brief.
Let’s watch the following conclusion of a public talk.
So, brothers, during these “critical times hard to deal with,”
let’s follow the counsel in today’s talk,
because with Jehovah’s help, we can endure life’s challenges.
And when he brings an end to this world and all its problems,
we’ll survive to live forever in a beautiful Paradise.
What do you think?
Did the speaker connect his conclusion to the overall topic?
Could you identify the theme
of his talk from this conclusion?
And while it’s good that the speaker
tried to motivate his audience,
was he specific?
Did he speak with a note of finality?
Let’s give him another chance.
So, brothers, although we live “in times of distress,”
may we always remember how Jehovah helps us.
He offers us his powerful holy spirit,
he provides support through our loving Christian brotherhood,
and he gives us a hope.
Therefore, when facing trials,
let’s ‘throw our burdens on Jehovah,’
confident that ‘he will sustain us.’
This time, the speaker rephrased the theme
“Where Can You Get Help in Times of Distress?”
and he restated the talk’s three main points.
He motivated his listeners by reminding them
how to benefit from Jehovah’s provisions.
His conclusion was simple and brief.
How might we apply these principles in the ministry?
In the following example,
a brother named Aaron is talking to a workmate named Mark,
who recently attended his grandfather’s funeral.
Aaron sees an opportunity to witness informally,
so he tells Mark about the resurrection
and shows him John 5:28, 29.
Now, how might Aaron
effectively conclude their conversation?
So Jesus promises to resurrect those who’ve died.
Interesting.
Well, I guess we’d better get back to work.
Not much of a conclusion, was it?
Let’s watch him try again.
So Jesus promises to resurrect those who’ve died.
Interesting.
What do you think that promise means for your grandfather?
In his conclusion,
Aaron connected the topic of their conversation
to the death of Mark’s grandfather.
But a good conclusion should also motivate your listeners
and show them what to do with the information they learned.
Let’s watch the rest of Aaron’s conclusion.
So, Mark, during those times
when your grandfather’s death makes you especially sad,
think about Jesus’ promise that death is not the end.
Imagine what it’ll be like to see your grandfather again.
That helps me when I’m sad about relatives I’ve lost in death.
Thanks for sharing that.
Sure.
Maybe when we talk next time, I’ll show you what Jesus said about . . .
Well done!
After repeating the main point for Mark to remember,
Aaron motivated him to reflect
on the resurrection hope during times of sadness.
Aaron could have also tried
to motivate Mark to accept a Bible study,
to come with him to a congregation meeting,
or some other specific action.
When your conclusion is effective,
your audience will remember your theme and main points
and be motivated to apply what they learned.

title: 조엘 델링거: 두려움이 아니라 믿음을 가지고 앞으로 나아가십시오 (이사야 41:10)

ko.text: 사람들이 요즘 가장 많이 느끼는 감정은 무엇일까요?
“확실히 두려움은 오늘날 사람들의 생활에서 가장 큰 단일 감정인 것 같다”고 했습니다.
마지막 날의 표징에 관한 예수의 말씀에 근거한 것이었습니다.
알고 계신 것처럼, 전쟁, 지진, 식량 부족, 전염병에 더해,
하느님의 적들이 곧 닥칠 일을 생각하면서 ‘사람의 아들’의 표징을 보기 직전에
어떤 감정에 휩싸일 것이라고 예수께서 말씀하셨는지 기억나시나요?
“사람이 거주하는 땅에 닥칠 일들에 대한 두려움과 예상 때문에
앞으로 큰 환난이 가까이 오면서 상황이 더 나빠지더라도 그럴 것입니다.
이 세상이나 우리 삶에 어떤 나쁜 일이 일어나더라도
2020년 올해를 위해 여호와께선 우릴 어떻게 대비시켜 주셨나요?
한 가지 방법은 2019년의 성구로 이사야 41:10을 주신 것이었습니다.
이사야 41:10의 믿음을 강화하는 세 가지 약속을 묵상하는 것이 매우 중요함을 배웠습니다.
다시 한 번 함께 오늘의 성구를 읽어 보실까요?
우리가 이 세 가지 약속을 전적으로 신뢰할 수 있다는 걸 보여 주는
먼저, 안나라는 자매의 경험을 소개해 드리죠.
이 자매는 믿음 때문에 투옥되어 있습니다.
안나는 격려 편지가 너무 많이 와서 답장을 다 못하고 있었죠.
이 경험은 작년 11월에 보고됐는데, 그때까지 얼마나 많은 편지를 받았을까요?
그 재소자는 친절하게도 안나가 답장을 쓰는 걸 도와주겠다고 했습니다.
그 재소자는 편지를 하나하나 잘 읽어 보고 어떻게 답장할지 물어보았습니다.
재소자는 나중에는 아주 능숙해져서 묻지 않고도 혼자 답장을 써 주곤 했다고 합니다.
그런데 안나 자매의 수감 생활은 순탄치만은 않았습니다.
하루는 교도관이 감방을 검사하다가 안나 자매에게 성경을 압수하겠다고 했습니다.
자매는 성경을 가져가지 말라고 사정했지만 소용이 없었습니다.
놀랍게도, 자매와 한방을 쓰던 다른 재소자들이 소란을 피우고 감방 문을 두드리면서
안나 자매에게 성경을 당장 돌려주라고 요구했습니다.
그들은 교도관에게 “안나에겐 성경이 음식보다 더 중요해요”라고 했는데,
자매가 성경을 읽는 것을 수시로 봤기 때문이죠.
나중에, 자매는 또 다른 시험에 직면했습니다.
하루는 자매와 같은 방에 있던 재소자 중에
두 여자가 자신들이 저지른 범죄에 대해 집시어로 노래를 부르기 시작했습니다.
안나 자매는 그들이 사용하는 집시어를 다 이해하지는 못했지만,
노래 가사에 저속한 말이 들어 있다는 걸 알아차리게 되었습니다.
안나 자매는 여호와께 상황을 바로잡아 달라고 즉시 기도했습니다.
갑자기 집시 여자 한 사람이 왕국 노래를 부르기 시작한 겁니다.
“그 노래를 어떻게 아세요?” 그런 다음 노래를 함께 따라 불렀죠.
나중에 알고 보니, 그 집시 여자의 어머니가 여호와의 증인과 성서 연구를 했었고,
딸인 이 여자는 그때 외운 왕국 노래를 교도소에서 부른 것입니다.
이 경험으로 안나 자매는 여호와께서 기도에 신속히 응답하시고
심지어 증인이 아닌 사람을 통해서도 격려해 주신다는 걸 알게 됐죠.
형제 자매 여러분, 이사야 41:10에 있는 약속처럼,
현재 수감 중인 모든 형제 자매와 함께 계시다는 걸 확신할 수 있지 않습니까?
여호와께선 자신의 종들에게 온전한 애정과 관심을 보이십니다.
이사야 41:10의 두 번째 약속을 확신시켜 줍니다.
피터라는 형제가 쓴 글의 일부를 읽어 드리죠.
“투옥되고 처음 몇 달 동안은 독방에 갇혀 있었습니다.
낙심에 빠진 저는 양 치는 방문을 받는 상상을 하기 시작했습니다.
저를 격려해 주러 넥타이를 맨 두 형제가 찾아오면 얼마나 좋을까 하고요.
양 치는 방문을 받고 나서 ‘넥타이 맨 남자들’이 방문해 주었다고 말하곤 했죠.
저도 그런 방문을 받고 싶어서 이렇게 기도했습니다.
‘여호와여, 지금 그게 불가능하다는 걸 잘 알지만,
저도 “넥타이 맨 남자들”의 방문을 받고 싶어요.’”
“얼마 지나지 않아, 전 편지가 적힌 카드를 받았어요.
분홍색 셔츠에 노란색 넥타이를 맨 모양의 카드였습니다.”
피터가 그 순간 어떻게 느꼈을지 상상이 되십니까?
이 형제는 여호와에 대해 이렇게 느꼈다고 썼습니다.
“기도의 응답이었습니다. 진짜 양 치는 방문 같았죠.
상상하지 못할 만큼 큰 격려를 받았습니다.
그 어려운 시기에 정말 잊지 못할 날이었죠.
여호와께서 제 감정적 필요를 돌보신다는 실제적인 증거였죠.
이 소중한 경험을 카드와 함께 간직할 겁니다.”
네, 여호와께서 “내가 너의 하느님이다”라는 두 번째 약속을 어떻게 지키셨는지 알 수 있죠?
그분은 뜻밖의 방식으로 친절하게 피터 형제의 필요를 돌보셨습니다.
이 약속에 대해 「파수대」는 어떤 상황에서든 도와주실 수 있는 분을
그 어느 때보다 신뢰해야 한다고 했죠.
세상 사람들은 많은 문제를 해결할 길이 없기 때문에 두려워합니다.
우리도 다른 사람들과 동일한 문제를 겪고 있지만,
여호와의 약속이 있기 때문에 두려워할 필요가 없다는 걸 우린 알고 있습니다.
오늘날 사람들이 겪는 문제들은 비행기를 뒤흔드는 강풍과도 같습니다.
하지만 우린 왜 평온할 수 있나요?
세 번째 경험담은 이사야 41:10의 다음 약속에 관한 건데,
90세 된 이 자매는 바깥 출입을 못하고 휴대폰이나 인터넷도 없으십니다.
전염병 때문에 지난주 기념식 때 집에 혼자만 있게 될까 봐 무척 걱정하셨다고 합니다.
회중에서는 안토니아 자매가 다른 한 자매와 함께
안전하게 기념식을 지킬 수 있도록 계획을 세웠습니다.
그러자 안토니아 자매와 친한 사이인 패티 자매가 돕겠다고 나섰습니다.
그래서 의사와 상담을 했고 의사는 두 자매의 안전을 위해,
표상물을 담을 잔과 접시를 소독하는 것과 같은 세세한 지침을 알려 줬습니다.
안토니아 자매에게 이 계획을 알려 주면서 패티 자매가 도우러 가면 어떻겠냐고 물었더니,
그래서 두 자매는 지난주에 함께 기념식 연설을 들을 수 있었습니다.
안토니아 자매는 눈물을 글썽이며 표상물을 취했고,
“저는 계속 여호와를 충실히 섬기게 도와달라고 기도드립니다.”
이 형제 자매들의 생생한 경험을 들어 보니 정말 감동적이지 않습니까?
여호와께서 안나, 피터, 안토니아에게 하신 일은 파수대의 이 내용을 확증해 줍니다.
여호와께서 자신의 백성을 사랑하지 못하게 막을 수 없습니다.
우리를 향한 그분의 충성스러운 사랑은 결코 흔들리지 않습니다.”
우리 하느님 아버지 여호와께 대한 확신을 강하게 하고 싶으십니까?
오늘 이사야 41:10을 깊이 묵상해 보는 것은 어떨까요?
여호와를 더 잘 알려고 계속 노력하기 위해
정기적으로 성경을 주의 깊이 읽고 내용을 묵상하십시오.
여호와께서 함께하신다는 걸 온전히 확신하고 앞으로 나아갈 것입니다.

en.text: What would you say
is the biggest single emotion
gripping people today?
Well, many would readily agree
that it’s fear.
Interestingly, in 1982, the book
You Can Live Forever in Paradise on Earth said this:
“Fear is probably the biggest single emotion
in people’s lives today.”
And that comment by “the faithful and discreet slave”
was based on Jesus’ words
in giving us a sign about the last days.
You know that in addition to wars, earthquakes,
food shortages, and epidemics,
at Luke 21:11, the Bible tells us
that Jesus included “fearful sights,”
or “terrifying events,” as indicated in the Study Bible.
At Luke 21:26,
do you recall the emotion that Jesus said would overwhelm God’s enemies
as they looked ahead in the near future
to seeing the sign of “the Son of man”?
It would be fear.
Jesus said: “People will become faint out of fear
and expectation of the things coming upon the inhabited earth.”
Well, what about us as Jehovah’s people?
As a group, we are nowhere near
being “faint out of fear,”
nor will we be as things worsen
as we approach the great tribulation.
Why not?
Simply put, it’s because Jehovah has prepared us
to remain calm
when bad things happen in the world or in our personal lives.
Think about one way Jehovah prepared us
for the year 2020.
It was by giving us in the year 2019
the yeartext at Isaiah 41:10.
In our study of that yeartext last year,
we were reminded that a key to not giving way to fear
is to meditate on the three faith-building promises
contained in Isaiah 41:10.
Look at it again, please, in Examining the Scriptures.
Do you see the three promises?
First, Jehovah will be with us;
second, he is our God;
and third, he will help us.
This morning, to illustrate
the reliability of those three guarantees,
we’ll consider some delightful experiences.
To begin, consider, please,
the experience of a sister we’ll call Anna
who is in prison for her faith.
Anna’s cellmate noticed
that Anna was not able to reply
to all the letters of encouragement that she was receiving.
When this experience was compiled last November,
do you know how many letters our sister had received?
More than 1,700.
So her cellmate in a friendly way
offered to be Anna’s secretary.
According to Anna, this cellmate agreed
that she would read each letter very carefully
and then consult with Anna about how to respond.
She became so good at the job
that she even would respond to letters by herself.
Well, Anna’s circumstances in prison were not ideal.
One day, a prison guard conducted an inspection of the cell
and asked Anna to give him her Bible.
She begged him not to take it away,
but he did anyway.
Anna started to cry.
Then something unexpected happened.
Surprisingly, Anna’s other cellmates
started making a lot of noise and began beating on the cell doors
demanding that the Bible be returned immediately to Anna.
They told the guard, “To Anna the Bible
is more important than food”
because they had regularly seen her reading that Bible.
Eventually, the guard returned the Bible to our sister.
Later, Anna confronted another test in jail.
Two of the prisoners in her cell were in jail for criminal activity,
and they were singing Gypsy songs one day
about their criminal life.
Even though our sister did not completely understand
the language they were using,
she suspected that their singing
included some vulgar speech.
Immediately, Anna prayed to Jehovah
and asked that he correct the situation.
And again, something unexpected happened.
Suddenly, one of the Gypsy women began singing one of our Kingdom songs.
Anna was shocked.
She asked, “How do you know this song?”
And then Anna joined her in finishing the song.
As it turned out, this Gypsy woman’s mother
had studied the Bible with Jehovah’s Witnesses
and during that time her daughter who is now in prison
had memorized the Kingdom song.
Anna said that this experience was proof
that Jehovah responds very quickly to prayers
and that he can even use non-Witnesses to encourage his servants.
Well, brothers and sisters, in thinking about the promise
in Isaiah 41:10,
can there be any doubt
that Jehovah is with Anna
and with all of our imprisoned brothers and sisters at this time?
Even when cut off from family and friends,
Jehovah gives his servants his full affection
and attention.
A second experience received last July
highlights the fact that Jehovah is our God,
the second assurance in Isaiah 41:10.
A brother we will call Peter reported this, and I quote:
“During the first few months of imprisonment, I was placed in solitary confinement.
“I felt downhearted and began to dream of a shepherding visit.
“I thought about how good it would be
“to talk with two brothers in ties.
“I had heard that in some congregations when someone received a shepherding visit,
“they would say, after the fact, that ‘the ties’ came to visit me.
“I too wanted such a visit, so I prayed:
“‘Jehovah, I understand that this is practically impossible now,
but I want “the ties” to come visit me.’”
Peter goes on to state:
“After a short time, I received a letter with a card.
“The card was made in the form of
a pink shirt with a yellow tie.”
You’ll see it on the monitors.
“In the card,” Peter said,
“were the words from the song Shepherds—Gifts in Men,
our song 103.”
Brothers and sisters, can you imagine how Peter felt at that moment?
How did he view Jehovah?
He continues: “This was the answer to my prayer.
“A real shepherding visit.
“This encouraged me more than I could have imagined.
“It was one of the best days during that difficult time.
“With tears, I thanked Jehovah for his support.
“I saw tangible evidence of Jehovah’s care for my emotional needs.
I will keep this card as a treasured memento.”
Well, do we see how Jehovah proved true to that second assurance?
“I am your God.”
Jehovah answered Peter’s need
in an unexpected but very tender way.
In discussing this part of Isaiah 41:10,
The Watchtower acknowledged that now more than ever
we need to remember who is in control.
People around us are in fear because so many things seem out of control.
And while we’re affected by the same problems that affect other people,
we know, based on Jehovah’s assurances,
that there’s no need for us to be afraid.
The problems people face today
are like the strong winds that might rock an airplane during flight.
Some passengers naturally panic.
But why do we remain calm?
Because we know who our pilot is.
It is Jehovah our God.
Let’s consider one more experience that connects well with Isaiah 41:10,
where Jehovah says: “I will help you.”
In Illinois, we have a dear anointed sister
by the name of Antonia, who is 90 years old.
She is homebound and does not have a mobile device
nor access to the Internet.
Due to the pandemic, she was very nervous about
being home alone last week for the Memorial.
So how did Jehovah help Antonia?
The congregation worked out a plan
so that she could observe the Memorial with another sister present
without risking their health.
Patty, a close friend, offered to assist Antonia
if it would be safe to do so.
So a doctor was consulted, and he provided detailed instructions
that would keep both sisters safe,
which included the use of gloves and masks
and sanitizing the plate and the cup that would be used for the emblems.
When the plan was presented to our sister Antonia,
she was asked if she would like Patty to assist.
She replied, “With all my heart.”
So our two sisters listened together
to the Memorial talk last week.
Antonia partook of the emblems with tears in her eyes.
With heartfelt emotion she said,
“I pray to Jehovah to help me
stay worthy and faithful.”
Brothers and sisters, these true-to-life experiences
are heartwarming, aren’t they?
And what Jehovah has done for Anna, Peter, and Antonia
proves what The Watchtower said, and I quote:
“No force in the universe can make Jehovah abandon his love
for those who serve him; his loyalty to us is unshakable.”
Well, would you like to strengthen your confidence in Jehovah,
our God and our Father?
Today, why not meditate deeply on Isaiah 41:10?
If possible, commit those verses to memory.
And let’s keep working to get to know Jehovah better
by regularly reading
the Bible carefully and meditating on what we read.
Then, as we face trials together,
we’ll move ahead with full confidence that Jehovah is with us.
We’ll do so with faith, not fear.

cn.text: 你认为在今天
怎样的情绪对人影响最深呢？
很多人会觉得
是恐惧
1982年出版的
《你能够永远生活在地上的乐园里》
这本书说过
“恐惧很可能是今日
人们生活上最显著的情绪。”
“忠信睿智的奴隶” 在书里提到的这段话
是跟末世的征象有关
除了战争、地震
粮食短缺和瘟疫
在路加福音21:11
在这里耶稣说
在最后的日子
人们还会看见“恐怖的事”
你还记得耶稣在路加福音21:26说什么吗？
人子快要来到之前
上帝的敌人会有什么反应呢？
他们会非常非常害怕
在26节，耶稣说
“人们想到世上要发生的事
就会害怕得头晕目眩。”
那我们这些上帝的子民呢？
我们完全不会“害怕得头晕目眩”
虽然大患难来临前情况会越来越糟糕
我们也不会害怕
为什么呢？
因为耶和华帮助我们保持冷静
无论这个世界发生了什么坏事
还是我们遭遇了不幸，我们都不会害怕
请想想，耶和华怎样帮助我们
为2020年做好准备呢？
就是2019年的全年经文
以赛亚书的41章第10节
在跟这个全年经文有关的《守望台》文章里
我们学会了克服恐惧的方法
就是要沉思三个鼓舞人心的保证
记录在以赛亚书41:10里
让我们再看一次这节经文
你留意到经文里提到的三个保证吗？
第一，耶和华与我们同在
第二，他是我们的上帝
第三，他一定会帮助我们
为什么我们可以完全信赖这三个保证呢？
接下来
我想跟大家分享几个非常有意思的经历
第一个经历是一位姐妹，她叫安娜
她因为信仰的缘故而被关在监狱里
安娜的狱友发现，安娜收到非常多的鼓励信
多得没有办法一一回复
我们去年11月的时候听到这个经历
当时安娜已经收到了多少信呢？
超过1700封信！
安娜的狱友非常热心
主动提出要当她的秘书
安娜说，这个狱友会很认真地看完每一封信
之后再跟安娜讨论可以怎样回信
这个秘书非常称职
后来她不用跟安娜讨论就知道可以怎么回信了
但其实监狱里的环境还是非常不好的
有一天，一个狱警来检查她们的牢房
他想要没收安娜的圣经
安娜求狱警不要没收她的圣经
但狱警还是无动于衷
安娜就哭了起来
这时，意想不到的事发生了
突然间，安娜的狱友们大吼大叫
不断敲打牢房的门
要求狱警马上把圣经还给安娜
他们告诉狱警
对安娜来说，圣经比食物还重要
因为她们看到安娜经常在读圣经
最后狱警就把圣经还给安娜了
之后，安娜又遇到了另一个挑战
有一天，两个女囚犯
开始哼唱一些吉普赛语的歌
她们唱的歌里面的歌词都在描述
她们曾经犯过的罪行
虽然安娜并不完全明白她们到底在唱什么
但是她听得出来
歌词里面包含一些粗俗下流的内容
安娜马上向耶和华祷告，求上帝帮助她
又一次，意想不到的事发生了
突然，其中一个女囚犯开始唱我们的诗歌
安娜非常惊讶，问她
“你怎么会唱这首歌？”
然后就跟着她一起唱
原来，这个女囚犯的妈妈
之前跟耶和华见证人学习过圣经
她的妈妈在学习圣经的时候
她也学会了一些王国诗歌
安娜说，她从这个经历学到
耶和华会很快回应人的祷告
上帝甚至可以用不崇拜他的人
去鼓励他的子民
想想以赛亚书41:10的保证
我们就会看出，耶和华真的和安娜
以及所有在监狱里被囚的弟兄姐妹同在
耶和华的保证确实是可以信赖的！
即使我们跟亲朋好友分开了
耶和华还是会继续关心我们、照顾我们
第二个经历是我们在去年7月听到的
这个经历说明，耶和华确实是我们的上帝
就像第二个经文里的保证一样
有一个弟兄名叫彼得，他说
“我刚被关进监狱的时候
被单独监禁了几个月
我非常沮丧，很希望弟兄们来探访我
如果有两个弟兄来探访我就太好了
最好他们都打着领带
我听到有些弟兄姐妹说
他们被牧养探访后会说
“领带们”来看我了
我也很希望被探访
所以我向耶和华祷告，对他说
耶和华我知道现在的情势不太可能
但是我真的很希望“领带们”可以来看我
彼得继续说
“没过多久，我收到了一张卡片
这张卡片的造型
竟然是一个粉色衬衫配上黄色领带！”
就像你在萤幕上看到的那样
彼得说
“卡片里写的是诗歌第103首
《上帝赐下仁爱的牧人》的歌词。”
你们能够想象彼得那个时候的心情吗？
他对耶和华会有什么感觉呢？
他说
“耶和华回应了我的祷告
‘领带’真的来看我了
真没想到耶和华会用这样的方式来鼓励我
那一天实在是太美好了！
我热泪盈眶，感谢上帝
我好感动，耶和华真的关心我的感受
我会永永远远珍藏这张卡片。”
这个经历让我们看出
第二个保证“我是你的上帝”
也是值得信赖的
耶和华用意想不到的方式安慰彼得
体贴他的感受
关于以赛亚书41:10
《守望台》强调
耶和华能在任何情况下帮助我们
很多人看到这个世界失控了
都感到非常害怕
这个世界发生问题的时候
我们跟一般人一样都会受到影响
但因为有耶和华的保证
所以我们不会感到惊慌
今天的情况就好像我们坐飞机时遇到乱流
飞机会剧烈摇晃一样
很多乘客会因此很紧张
但我们不会，为什么呢？
因为我们知道我们的机长是谁
就是耶和华上帝
耶和华的第三个保证“我一定会帮助你”
为什么值得信赖呢？
我们再看一个经历
有一个90岁的姐妹叫做安东尼娅
她是有希望到天上的基督徒
她没有办法离开家，也没有手机电脑可以上网
因为疫情的关系
她非常担心没有人可以陪她参加主的晚餐
耶和华怎样帮助她呢？
会众作出安排
请一个姐妹到安东尼娅的家
陪她一起参加主的晚餐
佩蒂是安东尼娅的好朋友
她很乐意主动提供协助
长老们询问了医生
为了保护她们两个的健康
医生给她们详细的指引
包括要戴手套、戴口罩
还有装象征物的容器都要彻底消毒
之后长老们问安东尼娅姐妹
“你觉得让佩蒂姐妹

제 개인 경험에 비추어 볼 때

en.text: I always say that we should be grateful to those who have introduced us
—in this case, Jehovah’s Witnesses—
to bloodless surgery
because by means of the ongoing work on patients
who have refused transfusions over the past 30 years,
we have gained truly valuable information.
The first is that blood transfusions
are not associated with an altogether positive outcome.
The second is that
with a well-thought-out approach and with targeted strategies,
it is possible to perform even major surgeries
without transfusing allogeneic blood.
Well, I’ve been a doctor for 25 years,
so I have witnessed various forms of progress.
The first thing I can say is
that the concept of non-pharmacological therapies
has evolved
—for example, the use of machines to recycle
intraoperative blood.
Techniques of preoperative normovolemic hemodilution
have been developed.
There is medicine that reduces bleeding.
But, above all, surgery has evolved.
I witnessed the birth, so to say, of laparoscopic surgery,
which is an operative technique that enables major surgeries
with minimal, even zero, blood loss.
So we should thank
surgical technologies and developments in anaesthesiology
for the steady decrease in intraoperative bleeding
that we have seen over the years.
I would say the doctor has the absolute duty to respect a patient’s will.
This is also because the patient’s rightful consent is
the only act that authorizes the doctor,
or surgeon, to operate on him.
Otherwise, he would be guilty of an assault.
According to my experience
and what is clear according to international literature,
at least 80-90% of all elective surgeries
can safely be performed without allogeneic blood.

ko.text: 과거에는 의사들이 환자들에게 수혈을 너무 많이 했기 때문에

en.text: We have been working with Jehovah’s Witnesses for 30 years now
and have progressively grown together through this experience.
Jehovah’s Witnesses have led us to be
extremely cautious with the use of blood
through good patient preparation,
careful selection of the patient,
careful management in the operating room
with all the available blood conservation methods,
and correcting anemia prior to surgery.
This has resulted— And I have to say, of course,
thanks to a relationship that has become stronger over the years,
it has resulted in a committee within this hospital
entrusted with limiting the use of blood
even for those who are not bound by these restrictions.
So it has been a beneficial process.
It has also led to a global reduction in the use of blood,
which we know is harmful and can lead to complications, such as those
associated with recovery, as well as avoidable costs.
If anemia is a factor, we treat it beforehand
with all the pharmaceutical means we have available to correct it.
We have a committee in Verona for the best use of blood
that recommends all these procedures,
which we also apply to patients who are not Jehovah’s Witnesses.
This is a beneficial process that your presence has allowed us to make.
With this type of preparation, we can address
even complex cases of pancreatic resection and liver resections.
We do resections of liver tumors and resections of pancreatic tumors.
And we can do these with reasonable —reasonable—
risks and perform them safely.
In gastrointestinal oncology, we have come
from a rate of 50 percent of patients transfused to 15 percent.
So there has been a notable reduction in the use of blood
because we have, on the one hand,
applied more careful surgical techniques and,
on the other, used all the tools available to us for an efficient hemostasis.

참하느님의 집을 건축할 때 그들을 지원하도록 해 주셨기 때문이다.
“왕의 마음은 여호와의 손에 있는 물줄기와 같아서 그분이 어디로든 원하시는 대로 이끄신다.”
따라서 우리는 이 세상의 그 어떤 단체나 통치자에게
그중 무엇도 우리에게 영원한 구원을 주지 못합니다.
모든 나라가 여호와의 백성을 대적할 것입니다.
하지만 나라들은 닷드내보다 더 끔찍한 결과를 맞을 것입니다.
그분의 일을 계속 수행하기 위해 기울이는 노력을 축복하시고
이 사명을 물질보다 앞자리에 두고 있음을 나타냅니까?
즉 예수의 대속 희생을 근거로 여호와를 숭배하는 마련 안으로
꼭 필요하지 않은 것을 추구하는 데 정신을 쏟을 때가 아닙니다.
이제 곧 우리가 예상하지 않은 때에
주의를 빼앗기 위해 아무리 애쓴다 해도
여호와와 계속 함께 걸으며 평화로운 신세계로 들어가
그곳에서 영원토록 그분을 기쁨으로 섬기게 되기를 바랍니다.

en.text: “Serve Jehovah with rejoicing,”
says Psalm 100:2.
Yes, Jehovah wants us to be joyful.
And he’s given us many reasons to rejoice.
He gave us life with its many joys.
He gave us the Bible to teach us how to enjoy life.
And he guides us into countless joyful experiences.
Yes, Jehovah is the God who gives joy.
Satan, however, does not want us
to find joy in serving Jehovah.
Why not?
For one thing, he knows that joy helps us
to keep on preaching and teaching
—the very work he wants to stop.
So he tries to destroy our joy,
sometimes through official opposition
and at other times through family and community pressure.
Satan also wants us
to cut back our service to Jehovah
in order to obtain unnecessary material things.
He wants us to think that getting more and more material things
will bring us lasting joy.
It won’t.
Satan’s tactics are not new.
As we now read portions of the books
of Ezra, Haggai, and Zechariah,
look for lessons that can help us
to “serve Jehovah with rejoicing” today.
Note what brought Jehovah’s people joy back then
and what robbed them of their joy.
And consider why and how we  can experience
“the joy of Jehovah” today,
even under trying circumstances.
Ezra, a priest and a copyist of the Law of Moses,
is the writer of the book that bears his name.
The book of Ezra picks up the history of Israel
from the end of 2 Chronicles,
which likely Ezra also wrote.
It’s 537 B.C.E.,
and many Jews are about to return to Judah.
The nation has spent 70 years in captivity to Babylon
for practicing idol worship.
They’ve learned a hard lesson,
and never again does the entire nation
fall back into idolatry.
Now the time has come to get pure worship
back on its feet in Jerusalem.
The account spans the reigns
of several Persian kings,
starting with King Cyrus,
and it has a joyful beginning.
Please open to Ezra 1:1-6, and follow along.
“In the first year of King Cyrus of Persia,
“in order that Jehovah’s word spoken by Jeremiah would be fulfilled,
“Jehovah stirred the spirit of King Cyrus of Persia
“to make a proclamation throughout his kingdom,
which he also put in writing, saying:”
“This is what King Cyrus of Persia says,
“‘Jehovah the God of the heavens
“‘has given me all the kingdoms of the earth,
“‘and he has commissioned me to build him a house in Jerusalem,
“‘which is in Judah.
“‘Whoever there is among you of all his people,
“‘may his God be with him,
“‘and let him go up to Jerusalem, which is in Judah,
“‘and rebuild the house of Jehovah the God of Israel
“‘—he is the true God—
“‘whose house was in Jerusalem.
“‘Anyone who is residing as a foreigner,
“‘wherever he may be,
“‘let him be helped by his neighbors
“‘by their giving him silver and gold,
“‘goods and livestock,
“‘along with the voluntary offering for the house of the true God,
which was in Jerusalem.’”
“Then the heads of the paternal houses of Judah and of Benjamin
“and the priests and the Levites
“—everyone whose spirit the true God had stirred—
“prepared to go up and rebuild the house of Jehovah,
“which was in Jerusalem.
“All those around them supported them
“by giving them utensils of silver and of gold,
“goods, livestock, and valuable things,
besides all the voluntary offerings.”
Just imagine!
Jehovah returns the Jews to their land
with a commission from King Cyrus himself to rebuild the temple.
Many Jews joyfully take up this assignment.
However, those who for various reasons cannot return
give financial support to those who can.
Likely in the early spring of 537 B.C.E.,
nearly 50,000 Israelites depart Babylon.
Leading them are high priest Jeshua,
also called Joshua,
and the governor whom Cyrus appointed,
Zerubbabel.
In the early autumn, they arrive in Judah,
and they are joyful!
But how can they sustain that joy?
Note what they do as soon as they get settled.
Let’s read Ezra 3:1-6:
“When the seventh month arrived and the Israelites were in their cities,
“they gathered together with one accord in Jerusalem.
“Jeshua the son of Jehozadak and his fellow priests
“and Zerubbabel the son of Shealtiel and his brothers
“rose up and built the altar of the God of Israel,
“so that they could offer up burnt sacrifices on it,
“as it is written in the Law of Moses the man of the true God.
“So they set the altar up on its former site,
“despite their fear of the peoples of the surrounding lands,
“and they began offering up burnt sacrifices to Jehovah on it,
“the morning and the evening burnt sacrifices.
“Then they held the Festival of Booths according to what is written,
“and day by day they offered up the specified number of burnt sacrifices
“that were required each day.
“Afterward they offered up the regular burnt offering
“and the offerings for the new moons
“and those for all the sanctified festival seasons of Jehovah,
“as well as those from everyone
“who willingly offered a voluntary offering to Jehovah.
“From the first day of the seventh month
“they started to offer up burnt sacrifices to Jehovah,
“though the foundation of Jehovah’s temple
had not yet been laid.”
Did you notice that the Jews reinstitute Jehovah’s worship
“despite their fear of the peoples of the surrounding lands”?
Because of their courageous action,
this is a very joyful time.
It’s just as Moses said when he instructed the nation
to celebrate the Festival of Booths:
“You will become nothing but joyful”!
The next year, they courageously
and joyfully lay the foundation for the temple.
Let’s read about that at Ezra 3:10-13:
“When the builders laid the foundation of the temple of Jehovah,
“then the priests in official clothing, with the trumpets,
“and the Levites, the sons of Asaph, with the cymbals,
“stood up to praise Jehovah
“according to the direction of King David of Israel.
“And they began to sing in response
“by praising and giving thanks to Jehovah,
“‘for he is good; his loyal love toward Israel endures forever.’
“Then all the people shouted with a loud shout of praise to Jehovah
“because the foundation of the house of Jehovah had been laid.
“Many of the priests, the Levites, and the heads of the paternal houses
“—the old men who had seen the former house—
“wept with a loud voice when they saw the foundation of this house being laid,
“while many others shouted joyfully at the top of their voice.
“So the people could not distinguish
“the sound of the joyful shouts from the sound of the weeping,
“for the people were shouting so loudly
that the sound was heard from a great distance.”
Yes, some of the oldest members of the nation
cannot imagine how this temple could possibly match
the glory of Solomon’s temple.
But the others’ joyful shouting overpowers their weeping.
The people of the surrounding lands, however,
do not rejoice.
Instead, they cunningly target Israel’s joy.
Let’s see how in Ezra chapter 4:1-3:
“When the enemies of Judah and Benjamin heard
“that the returned exiles were building a temple to Jehovah the God of Israel,
“they immediately approached Zerubbabel and the heads of the paternal houses
and said to them:”
“Let us build along with you;
“for like you, we worship your God
“and we have been sacrificing to him
“since the days of King Esar-haddon of Assyria,
who brought us here.”
“However, Zerubbabel and Jeshua
“and the rest of the heads of the paternal houses of Israel
said to them:”
“You have no share with us in building a house to our God,
“for we alone will build it to Jehovah the God of Israel,
just as King Cyrus the king of Persia has commanded us.”
Zerubbabel discerns that behind their enemies’ offer to help
lurk bad motives.
When he rejects their offer,
they try to prevent the Jews from working on the temple.
Notice how verses 4 to 7 continue:
“Then the people of the land
“were continually discouraging the people of Judah
“and disheartening them from building.
“They hired advisers against them to frustrate their plans
“all the days of King Cyrus of Persia until the reign of King Darius of Persia.
“At the beginning of the reign of Ahasuerus,
“they wrote an accusation
“against the inhabitants of Judah and Jerusalem.
“And in the days of King Artaxerxes of Persia,
“Bishlam, Mithredath, Tabeel, and the rest of his colleagues
“wrote to Artaxerxes the king;
“they translated the letter into Aramaic,
writing it with Aramaic characters.”
Let’s read what Rehum, the chief government official,
and others of Israel’s enemies write to the king.
Consider what kind of false accusations they make,
as recorded at Ezra 4:11-16:
“This is a copy of the letter that they sent him.”
“To King Artaxerxes from your servants,
“the men of the region Beyond the River:
“And now let it be known to the king
“that the Jews who came up here from you to us have arrived at Jerusalem.
“They are rebuilding the rebellious and wicked city,
“and they are finishing the walls and repairing the foundations.
“Now let it be known to the king
“that if this city should be rebuilt and its walls finished,
“they will not give tax, tribute, or toll,
“and it will result in a loss to the treasuries of the kings.
“Since we eat the salt of the palace
“and it is not proper for us to see the king’s interests harmed,
“we have therefore sent to make this known to the king,
“so that there may be an investigation
“of the book of records of your ancestors.
“You will find in the book of records
“and learn that this city is a rebellious city,
“injurious to kings and provinces,
“and within it have been those stirring up sedition
“from ancient times.
“That is why this city was destroyed.
“We are making known to the king
“that if this city is rebuilt and its walls are finished,
you will have no control of the region Beyond the River.”
Do those false accusations sound familiar?
They are the same ones our enemies sometimes hurl against us today:
“They don’t pay taxes.
“They work against the government’s interests.
“They are rebellious and seditious.
They’re uncontrollable.”
All false charges, of course!
And back then, they had their effect.
The king orders the work halted,
and temple rebuilding comes to a standstill.
How sad!
When the Jews first returned,
they didn’t let fear of man
stop them from doing Jehovah’s work.
But now they do.
Many of us today
face increasing opposition to Jehovah’s work.
But compromising or giving up
has never brought anyone joy
—just the opposite.
Remaining faithful brings joy,
even in the face of violent persecution.
But how is that possible?
Consider a true-life example.
Picture a mother and daughter
surrounded by a mob of angry men
demanding that they buy political party cards.
What would the sisters do?
If they compromised and bought the cards,
their persecutors would rejoice.
But afterward the sisters would be miserable,
knowing they had denied their heavenly Father.
The sisters did not give in.
Of course, they didn’t enjoy being ridiculed and mistreated.
Later, however, their consciences were clean.
And they felt deep joy,
knowing they had remained faithful to Jehovah.
What about the Jews of Ezra’s day?
Many may have left a stable life in Babylon
to make the arduous trek to Judah.
Now, after about 14 years of constant opposition,
from the laying of the temple’s foundation up to the ban,
the Jews have lost their zeal for Jehovah’s work.
They go through the motions of offering sacrifices,
but they are not doing what Jehovah told  them to do
—finish rebuilding the temple!
When they meet resistance,
they rationalize that it must not be
Jehovah’s time to finish the work.
Apparently, even Governor Zerubbabel
and high priest Jeshua need encouragement.
To provide it, Jehovah sends the prophet Haggai.
Let’s turn now to the book of Haggai, chapter 1.
Haggai’s clear and powerful messages,
delivered during a period of about four months,
get right to the heart of the matter,
as we read at Haggai 1:2-11:
“This is what Jehovah of armies says,
“‘These people say,
“The time has not yet come for the house of Jehovah to be built.”’
“And the word of Jehovah again came through Haggai the prophet, saying:
“‘Is it the time for you to dwell in your paneled houses,
“‘while this house lies in ruins?
“‘Now this is what Jehovah of armies says,
“‘“Set your heart on your ways.
“‘“You have sown much seed, but you harvest little.
“‘“You eat, but it is not to satisfaction.
“‘“You drink, but you do not drink your fill.
“‘“You put on clothing, but no one gets warm.
“‘“The one who hires himself out
“puts his wages in a bag full of holes.”’
“This is what Jehovah of armies says,
“‘Set your heart on your ways.
“‘Go up to the mountain and bring in lumber.
“‘And build the house,
“so that I may take pleasure in it and I may be glorified,’ Jehovah says.
“‘You were expecting much and receiving little;
“‘and when you brought it into the house, I blew it away.
“For what reason?’ declares Jehovah of armies.
“‘Because my house is in ruins,
“‘while each of you runs around taking care of his own house.
“‘So the heavens above you withheld their dew,
“‘and the earth withheld its produce.
“‘And I kept calling for a drought on the earth,
“‘on the mountains, on the grain, on the new wine,
“‘on the oil, on what grows from the ground,
on humans and livestock, and on all the labor of your hands.’”
Jehovah compares the results of the Jews’ self-centered efforts
to those of a hired worker who puts
his wages into a moth-eaten sack.
Because the Jews are neglecting the house of Jehovah,
he holds back his blessing.
The results of the Jews’ labor are limited,
and their lives lack joy.
Evidently, some try to fill that void
by beautifying their own homes.
But material  things cannot satisfy spiritual needs.
Can we see the warning here for us?
It’s not wrong to enjoy nice things.
But material things cannot bring us true and lasting joy,
especially if we neglect Jehovah’s work to obtain them.
Remember the lesson of Psalm 127:1:
“Unless Jehovah builds the house,
“it is in vain
that its builders work hard on it.”
On the other hand, when we unselfishly ‘seek first
God’s Kingdom and his righteousness,’
he  provides what we really need
and at just the right time.
As Proverbs 10:22 tells us:
“It is the blessing of Jehovah
“that makes one rich,
and He adds no pain  with it.”
But now, will this rebuilt temple really not attain to its former glory,
as some believe?
Through Haggai, Jehovah guarantees
that the future glory of this house
will be even greater.
Let’s continue reading at Haggai 2:3-9.
“‘Who is left among you who saw this house in its former glory?
“‘How does it look to you now?
“‘Does it not seem like nothing in comparison?
“But now be strong, Zerubbabel,’ declares Jehovah,
“‘and be strong, Joshua son of Jehozadak, the high priest.
“And be strong, all you people of the land,’ declares Jehovah,
“‘and work.
“For I am with you,’ declares Jehovah of armies.
“‘Remember what I promised you when you came out of Egypt,
“‘and my spirit remains among you.
“Do not be afraid.’
“For this is what Jehovah of armies says,
“‘Yet once more —in a little while—
“‘and I will shake the heavens and the earth
“‘and the sea and the dry land.
“‘And I will shake all the nations,
“‘and the precious things of all the nations will come in;
“and I will fill this house with glory,’ says Jehovah of armies.
“‘The silver is mine,
“and the gold is mine,’ declares Jehovah of armies.
“‘The future glory of this house
will be greater than the former,’ says Jehovah of armies.”
Yes, when the Creator and Owner of the entire universe declares his purpose,
who or what could possibly prevent him from carrying it out?
Nothing and no one!
Jehovah’s straightforward message is unmistakable.
Still, the returnees need more encouragement.
Jehovah sends his angel
to another prophet, Zechariah.
Please turn to Zechariah 1:12-16,
and let’s read together the angel’s reassuring words for Israel.
That’s Zechariah 1:12-16.
“So the angel of Jehovah said:”
“O Jehovah of armies,
“how long will you withhold your mercy from Jerusalem and the cities of Judah,
with whom you have been indignant these 70 years?”
“Jehovah answered the angel who was speaking with me,
“with kind and comforting words.
Then the angel who was speaking with me told me:”
“Call out, ‘This is what Jehovah of armies says:
“‘“I am zealous for Jerusalem and for Zion with a great zeal.
“‘“With great indignation I am indignant with the nations that are at ease,
“‘“because I felt indignant to a small extent,
“‘but they added to the calamity.”
“‘Therefore this is what Jehovah says:
“‘“I will return to Jerusalem with mercy,
“‘and my own house will be built in her,” declares Jehovah of armies,
“and a measuring line will be stretched out over Jerusalem.”’”
To emphasize just how protective Jehovah will be,
the angel continues, at chapter 2, verses 7-9:
“Come, Zion!
“Make your escape, you who are dwelling with the daughter of Babylon.
“For this is what Jehovah of armies says,
“who after being glorified has sent me to the nations that were plundering you:
“‘Whoever touches you touches the pupil of my eye.
“‘For now I will wave my hand against them,
“and they will become plunder for their own slaves.’
And you will certainly know that Jehovah of armies has sent me.”
Would you let someone poke his finger in your eye?
Of course not!
Neither will Jehovah allow Israel’s opposers to harm them.
Then, in Zechariah 3:1, 2,
the angel reveals the greater enemy behind the opposition.
“And he showed me Joshua the high priest standing before the angel of Jehovah,
“and Satan was standing at his right hand to resist him.
Then the angel of Jehovah said to Satan:”
“May Jehovah rebuke you, O Satan,
“yes, may Jehovah, who has chosen Jerusalem, rebuke you!
Is not this one a burning log snatched out of the fire?”
Is all this intended simply to build up
Israel’s confidence in themselves?
On the contrary!
They need to remember that only with Jehovah’s help
can they accomplish anything.
Listen to the angel’s further words
to Zechariah in chapter 4, verses 6, 7:
“This is the word of Jehovah to Zerubbabel:
“‘Not by a military force, nor by power,
“but by my spirit,’ says Jehovah of armies.
“Who are you, O great mountain?
“Before Zerubbabel you will become a level land.
“And he will bring out the top stone amid shouts of:
‘How wonderful! How wonderful!’”
Energized by Jehovah’s motivating words
through his two prophets,
the Jews stop wavering in a lack of faith and resume
construction of the temple.
Predictably, Israel’s enemy neighbors,
led by Tattenai and Shethar-bozenai,
also spring into action.
Returning to the book of Ezra,
we read at chapter 5, verses 3-5:
“At that time Tattenai the governor of the region Beyond the River
and Shethar-bozenai and their colleagues came to them and asked them:”
“Who issued an order to you to build this house
and to finish this structure?”
“Then they asked them:”
“What are the names of the men who are working on this building?”
“But God was watching over the elders of the Jews,
“and they did not stop them until the report could be sent to Darius
and an official document could be sent back concerning this.”
So there is another lesson for us today:
When we courageously do Jehovah’s work despite opposition,
Jehovah blesses our efforts
and enables us to keep on serving him.
For now, though, the Jews must continue their work
on the temple under ban.
The king who issued  the ban, however,
was assassinated after reigning only seven months.
So Tattenai and his accomplices
are dealing with a new  king, Darius I.
In denouncing the Jews,
they try to use Zerubbabel’s own words against him,
including his statement that King Cyrus
issued the order to rebuild the temple.
They ask King Darius to investigate whether that’s really so.
Darius orders the investigation.
What will King Darius decide?
Will the Jews’ renewed faith and determination bring them joy?
or just more trouble?
Darius learns that Cyrus did indeed order that the temple be rebuilt.
At Ezra 6:6-12, we read
Darius’ stinging reply.
“So now Tattenai the governor of the region Beyond the River,
“Shethar-bozenai, and your colleagues,
“the lesser governors of the region Beyond the River
“—stay away from there.
“Do not interfere with the work on that house of God.
“The governor of the Jews and the elders of the Jews
“will rebuild that house of God in its former place.
“Furthermore, I am issuing an order
“as to what you are to do for these elders of the Jews
“for rebuilding that house of God:
“From the royal treasury,
“from the tax collected in the region Beyond the River,
“the expenses are to be promptly given to these men
“to continue without interruption.
“And whatever is needed
“—young bulls as well as rams and lambs
“for the burnt offerings to the God of heaven,
“wheat, salt, wine, and oil,
“just as the priests who are in Jerusalem say—
“is to be given them continually
“day by day without fail,
“so that they may continually present offerings
“that please the God of the heavens
“and pray for the life of the king and his sons.
“I have also issued an order that if anyone violates this decree,
“a timber will be pulled out of his house
“and he will be lifted up and fastened to it,
“and his house will be turned into a public latrine for this offense.
“And may the God who has caused his name to reside there
“overthrow any king and people who lift a hand
“to violate this order and destroy that house of God,
“which is in Jerusalem.
“I, Darius, issue this order.
Let it be done promptly.”
Upon receiving the king’s command, Tattenai and his colleagues have no choice.
Not only must they stop interfering with the work on the temple,
they must help finance it!
What a joyful outcome for the faithful Jews.
In 515 B.C.E.,
they hold the inauguration of the house of God with joy,
and as we read at verse 22:
“They also joyfully held
“the Festival of Unleavened Bread for seven days,
“for Jehovah caused them to rejoice
“and he had made the heart of the king of Assyria favorable toward them,
“so that he supported them in the work of the house of the true God,
the God of Israel.”
Today, when wise and just officials similarly intervene in our behalf,
we’re very grateful to them.
But we’re most grateful to Jehovah for directing matters.
As Proverbs 21:1 says:
“A king’s heart is like streams of water
“in Jehovah’s hand.
He directs it wherever He pleases.”
So we do not put our ultimate hope in any ruler
or institution of this world.
None of them can bring us permanent salvation.
In fact, before the end of Satan’s system,
all the nations will turn against Jehovah’s people.
But they’ll experience an outcome worse than that of Tattenai’s.
What lessons can we  draw
from these portions of Ezra, Haggai, and Zechariah?
First, Jehovah blesses our determined efforts
to keep on doing his work despite challenges,
but he frustrates the efforts of our opposers.
Second, when we put Jehovah’s work ahead of material comforts,
he gives us true joy.
What’s the work Jesus commissioned us to do today?
He made it very clear in his parting words to his followers:
“Go, therefore, and make disciples
of people of all the nations.”
Are we, with our hearts and hands,
putting this assignment ahead of material goals?
Haggai foretold that one day,
Jehovah’s temple would become far more glorious
than the one Solomon built.
That prophecy is being fulfilled today.
Jehovah is using our preaching to shake the nations.
Millions of “precious things” —new worshippers—
are coming to him.
These are joyfully flocking to the great spiritual temple
—Jehovah’s arrangement for worshipping him
on the basis of Jesus’ ransom sacrifice.
Now is not the time to focus our attention
on “paneled houses”
or on any other unnecessary pursuit.
Very soon, on a day we do not expect,
Satan’s world will end,
and we will enter Jehovah’s new world.
So no matter how Satan tries to discourage
or distract us now,
may we never let him rob us
of our joy in Jehovah!
May we, rather, walk with Jehovah
right into his peaceful new world,
where we will serve him forever with rejoicing.
Zerubbabel,
Jeshua,
Haggai,
and Zechariah have done much
to help Israel regain Jehovah’s favor.
Later, in 468 B.C.E.,
Ezra himself comes to Jerusalem to support true worship.
But the nation needs still more direction.
So Jehovah sends them another brave leader.
During the next two days of this convention,
we’ll learn about that faithful and powerful man
—Nehemiah.

cn.text: “要欢欢喜喜地敬奉耶和华。”
耶和华希望我们快乐
他赐给我们生命，让我们可以得享喜乐
他用圣经来教导我们可以怎样过快乐的生活
他让我们过富有意义的生活
没错，耶和华是赐人喜乐的上帝
可是，撒但不希望我们快乐地崇拜耶和华
为什么这么说呢？
如果我们失去喜乐
就不会热心地从事传道教人的工作
这是他很想看到的
所以，他想方设法夺走我们的喜乐
他可能会通过政府来打压我们
也会利用我们身边的人来反对我们
撒但希望我们为了不必要的东西而拼命工作
