居鲁士确实曾下令，让犹太人重建圣殿
请大家看看以斯拉记6:6-12
看看大流士做了什么决定
现在河西省长达特奈和示达波斯奈
以及你们的同僚，就是河西的副省长们
都要离开那里
不要干涉上帝圣殿的工程
要让犹太人的省长和犹太人的长老
在原处重建上帝的圣殿
关于犹太人的长老和重建上帝圣殿的工程
现在我下旨，要从王室宝库中
拨出河西的部分税收给他们作为工程款
拨款的事要尽快办理，免得工程中途停顿
他们需要的东西，不管是用来做全烧祭
献给天上上帝的公牛犊、公绵羊、绵羊羔
还是小麦、盐、酒、油
都要按照耶路撒冷祭司的要求
天天给他们，不得有误
这样，他们就可以经常献祭给天上的上帝
让他喜悦
也可以为国王和国王的子孙祈求长寿
我再下旨
谁违反这条法令
就要从他的房子拆出一根木头
把他举起来挂在上面
他的房子也会成为公厕
上帝为自己的圣名选了这座圣殿
任何君王或人民胆敢违抗我的谕旨
破坏上帝在耶路撒冷的圣殿
愿上帝消灭他们
我大流士亲自下旨，必须尽快执行
达特奈和他的同伙收到王的命令后
就只能遵照而行
他们不但不能干涉
还必须资助圣殿的重建工作
这个结果让忠心的犹太人喜出望外
公元前515年
犹太人欢欢喜喜地
为上帝的圣殿举行了启用礼
我们接下来看一看以斯拉记6:22
他们一起欢欢喜喜地过无酵节七天
因为耶和华使他们欢喜
又使亚述王善待他们
支持他们建造真神的圣殿
也就是以色列上帝的圣殿
今天，我们也会遇到一些开明公正的官员
愿意帮助我们，我们真的非常感激他们
但我们最感激的是耶和华
因为是他在指引事态的发展
就像箴言21:1所说的那样
我们不会把希望寄托在
统治者或者这个世界的任何机构上
因为他们并不能拯救我们
实际上，在撒但的制度终结前
所有国族还会攻击我们
但他们的结局会比达特奈的更糟
那么，我们从以斯拉记、哈该书
以及撒迦利亚书可以学到什么呢？
首先，哪怕面对各种挑战
只要我们坚持不懈地做好耶和华交托的工作
他就会帮助我们，不会让反对我们的人得逞
第二，我们把上帝的工作放在首位
不让物质享乐使我们分心
耶和华就会赐给我们真正的喜乐
上帝的工作指的是什么呢？
耶稣在回到天上前，明确地吩咐门徒
“你们要去，使所有国族的人做我的门徒。”
你把心思、时间、精力用在什么地方呢？
是传道工作，还是追求物质财富呢？
哈该预言，终有一天
耶和华圣殿的荣耀会比所罗门的更大
这个预言今天就应验了
耶和华正通过传道工作来震动万国
许许多多万国的珍宝
也就是越来越多的人，前来崇拜他
他们正汇集到这座
在比喻意义上的伟大圣殿
也就是耶和华根据耶稣的赎价
为正确崇拜所做的安排
现在绝不是我们住豪华房子
追求物质享乐的时候
再过不久，撒但的世界会突然被毁灭
我们会进入耶和华承诺的新世界
撒但一心想要夺走我们的喜乐
他用的方法就是使我们灰心
或者在崇拜的事上分心
千万不要让他得逞！
愿我们继续崇拜耶和华
希望有一天，我们可以在新世界里
永永远远喜乐地崇拜他
所罗巴伯、耶书亚、哈该、撒迦利亚
他们付出了很多努力
来帮助以色列人恢复和上帝的关系
在公元前468年
以斯拉来到耶路撒冷
帮助以色列人以正确的方式崇拜耶和华
但他们还需要更多的帮助
于是耶和华又派了一个信心坚定
勇敢无畏的人来带领他们
他就是尼希米
在接下来两天的大会里
我们会看看他的故事

titles.cn: “耶和华使他们欢喜”

title: 제148기 길르앗 졸업식—결론 연설 및 임명

ko.text: 그러면 이제 이 졸업식에서, 마지막 연설을 즐기실 차례입니다.
모리스 형제, 그 귀중한 “청사진”을 보여 주시죠.
세계 본부 건축을 위한 청사진의 일부입니다.
서비스를 제공하는 부서들과 여러 사무실이 있는 건물을 위한 청사진이죠.
그리고 저도 이번에 새로 알게 됐는데요,
요즘 업계에서는 이런 흰색 배경의 청사진도 많이들 쓰더군요.
「웹스터 사전」을 보면 설명이 잘 나와 있습니다.
“푸른 바탕 위에 흰색으로 또는 흰 바탕 위에 푸른색으로 나타나는 사진.
주로 지도와 기계 도면, 건축가의 설계도를 복사하는 데 쓰인다.”
예수는 건축가의 지시를 잘 따랐기 때문에 언제나 영적으로 성공하셨죠.
이제 곧 청사진이 어떻게 적용되는지 살펴볼 테니까요.
“청사진과 비슷한 어떤 것. (이를테면 본보기나 지침의 역할을 하는 것.)
[전 이 다음에 나오는 짧은 표현에 유의해 보았는데요.]
베드로의 두 번째 편지에 나오는 내용을 살펴보겠습니다.
제가 말하는 영적 성공을 위한 청사진이 무엇인지 함께 보시죠.
우리가 강조하려는 아홉 가지 점들이 여기 나옵니다. 5-7절.
경건한 정성에 형제 애정을, 형제 애정에 사랑을 더하십시오.”
물론 다른 것도 많죠. 성경 전체를 주셨으니까요.
하지만 이 아홉 가지는 기억하기 좋은 청사진과 같습니다.
이 청사진을 사용해 우리는 계속 영적으로 성공적인 사람이 될 수 있죠.
칭찬할 만하게도, 여러분은 진지한 노력을 다해
자격을 갖춰 길르앗에 초대받고, 열심히 수업을 받았죠.
주말에는 야외 봉사도 하셨고요. 진지한 노력이죠.
계속 그렇게 해야 합니다. 진지한 노력은 저절로 나오지 않죠.
우리는 진지한 노력을 기울일 겁니다. 그게 출발점이죠.
‘난 이 일에 진지한 노력을 기울일 거야. 그래서 성공해야지.’
아홉 가지를 하나하나 세세히 다룰 시간은 없지만,
그러면 우리 함께 히브리서를 펴서 11장의 내용을 읽으면서,
보이지 않는 실체에 대한 확실한 증거입니다.”
믿음이 필요하며 매우 중요하다는 점을 강조하는데,
“믿음이 없이는 하느님을 기쁘시게 할 수 없습니다.
하느님께 가까이 가는 사람은 그분이 계시다는 것과
그분이 자신을 진지하게 찾는 사람들에게 상 주시는 분이라는 것을 믿어야 합니다.”
우리가 바라는 것들에 대한 보증된 기대를 계속 가져야 한다는 겁니다.
믿음이 약해지면, 분명히 어떻게 된다고 했나요?
믿음 없이는 하느님을 기쁘시게 할 수 없습니다.
여러분이나 저나 하늘의 아버지 여호와를 기쁘시게 하는 데 남은 시간을 써야 합니다.
바울은 이 말을 쓰기 직전에 10장에서 이런 말을 했는데요.
“‘나의 의로운 사람은 믿음으로 인해 살 것이다’,
‘그가 뒤로 물러나면 내가 그를 기뻐하지 않는다’고 했습니다.
우리는 뒤로 물러나서 멸망할 사람들이 아니라 믿음으로 생명을 보존할 사람들입니다.”
우리가 영적으로 성공하고 영원한 생명을 얻게 된다는 것입니다.
독신이든, 기혼이든 여러분은 도덕적 탁월함인 덕을 갖추고 계십니다.
특히 이 세상의 마지막 날에는 정말 눈에 띕니다.
일부러 눈에 띄려고 하는 건 아니지만
여러분의 도덕적 탁월함, 좋은 행실은 하느님을 영광스럽게 합니다.
그분은 우리가 그분을 영광스럽게 하고 그분께 주의를 돌리기를 원하십니다.
많은 코미디언은 입만 열면 그런 얘기죠.
우리는 “세상의 영”을 단호히 저항해야 하고, 도덕적으로 탁월해야 합니다.
분명, 여러분은 지식을 소중히 여기고 계십니다.
하지만 우리 조직을 포함해서 얼마나 많은 사람이
여러분처럼 몇 달씩 성경을 깊이 공부할 수 있겠습니까?
여러분은 학교에 오시기 전에 성경을 다 읽으셨습니다.
사랑하는 신권 학교 강사들과 교습 위원회 덕분에
몇 달 전보다 훨씬 더 풍부한 지식을 갖게 되셨습니다.
여러분 앞에 쏟아진 이 모든 지식으로 만족해서는 안 됩니다.
여러분이 계속해서 지식을 얻어야만 영적으로 성공할 수 있습니다.
여호와께서는 지식을 얻으려는 여러분의 노력을 축복하실 겁니다.
배우는 덴 끝이 없죠. 멋진 일입니다.
제가 자주 하는 말인데, 배우면 배울수록, 얼마나 아는 게 없는지 깨닫게 됩니다.
이건 그냥 하는 말이 아니라, 사실입니다.
여호와에 관해 계속 배우다니 얼마나 멋집니까!
지금부터 그렇게 배우면, 영원히 배울 수 있죠.
자제는 여러분이 잘 아시는 “영의 열매”의 한 부면입니다.
영적으로 성공하고 영원한 생명을 얻기 위해서는 자제가 필요하죠.
특히 마지막 날에 사는 우리는 자제에 대해 기도해야 합니다.
고린도 전서 10장에는 이런 말이 나오는데, 그걸 보고 다시 베드로 후서를 보겠습니다.
“그러므로 서 있다고 생각하는 사람은 넘어지지 않도록 조심하십시오.”
우리의 생각을 보호하기 위해 자제를 달라고 기도해야 합니다.
시도 때도 없이 우리 생각에 영향을 주려고 하니까요.
마귀가 어떤 유혹을 하거나 어떤 어려움이 닥쳤을 때,
당신 편에 굳건히 서고 싶습니다” 하고 요청하십시오.
마귀가 우리의 성공을 막으려고 악한 시도를 하지만,
우리는 인내 하나만 갖고도 한참을 얘기할 수 있습니다.
여러분은 헌신한 후로 이미 많은 걸 인내해 오셨습니다.
이런 재난이나 모든 일들을 겪을 때면
제가 조정자 위원회 사무실의 형제들에게 이렇게 말했었는데요.
좋아할 일은 아니지만 사실 이건 현실입니다.
우리가 지금 겪고 있는 세계적인 전염병에 관해
전 어제 지부 학교에서 이런 말을 했습니다.
우린 이런 일이 일어날 줄 알고 있었죠.
여호와의 인도로 잘 대처하면서, 인내해야 합니다.
그럼 예수께서 마태복음 24장에서 하신 말씀을 함께 읽고,
우리가 성공할 수 있도록 이런 말씀으로 대비시켜 주셨습니다.
네, 끝까지 인내한 사람은] 구원을 받을 것입니다.”
우린 청사진의 일부인 인내를 끝까지 나타낼 겁니다.
어떤 일이 닥치든 우린 여호와의 도움으로 성공할 겁니다.
여러 해 전에 「파수대」에서 이 특성에 관해 해설했죠.
이 특성이 매우 중요한 이유를 기억한다면 좋을 것입니다.
저는 「신세계역」에서 경건한 정성이라고 표현한 것이 마음에 듭니다.
하지만 배우자 각자가 하느님께 개인적인 애착을 가져야 합니다.
그렇게 해야 둘 다 성공할 수 있죠.
경건한 정성은 여호와께 개인적인 애착을 갖는 것입니다.
누구나 단순한 정성이 아니라 그분에 대한 애착을 가져야 하죠.
우린 그분을 영혼을 다해 사랑합니다. 전적인 정성을 드리죠.
여러분은 보이지 않겠지만, 제 등에 소름이 돋습니다.
그분에 대한 사랑, 그분에 대한 애착을 생각하면요.
결혼하셨다면 배우자가 그런 애착을 가지고 있는 건 기쁜 일이죠.
우리가 그분께 드리는 정성, 그분이 해 주신 모든 것,
또 해 주실 것들에 대한 정성은 아주 개인적인 것입니다.
이제 경건한 정성 다음에 언급되는 것은
저는 이 말을 들으니까 누매어 형제가 한 말이 생각납니다.
강의가 진행되는 동안 여러분과 함께 있으면서 봤고,
마지막 수업이 끝난 후에도 여러분의 모습을 보았는데요.
누매어 형제는 여러분이 서로 함께 있는 걸 얼마나 좋아하는지 언급했죠.
서로에 대한 여러분의 형제 사랑을 잘 표현한 겁니다.
여러분은 진실한 형제 애정을 갖고 계십니다.
여러분은 그 애정을 나타내셨는데, 성공하려면 계속 나타내야 합니다.
여러분이 여기서 잘 해 오신 것을 칭찬해 드립니다.
임지에 돌아가서도 형제 애정을 계속 나타내셔야 합니다.
그런데 한 가지 생각할 점이 데살로니가 전서 4장에 나옵니다.
잘 기억해 두셨다가 임지로 가서도 계속 실천하셔야 할 점이죠.
“그러나 형제 사랑에 관해서는 여러분에게 쓸 필요가 없습니다.
여러분 자신이 하느님에게서 서로 사랑하라는 가르침을 받았기 때문입니다.
사실 여러분은 마케도니아 전역에 있는 모든 형제에게 그렇게 하고 있습니다.
그러나 형제 여러분, 우리는 여러분이 앞으로도 더욱 온전히 그렇게 할 것을 권고합니다.”
수업을 받는 동안 그 애정을 나타내셨지만,
영적으로 성공하려면 때때로 생각해 봐야 할 점이 있습니다.
특히 개인적으로, 원한다면 부부가 함께 이렇게 자문해 보십시오.
세상이 점점 더 위급해지기 때문에 이 점을 생각해 보는 게 중요합니다.
우리는 서로에게 계속해서 형제 사랑을 나타낼 필요가 있습니다.
하지만 더 온전히 그렇게 해야 합니다.
여러분이 잊지 않고 그렇게 하리라 믿습니다.

en.text: Continuing our excellent program,
we will now get to enjoy our final talk.
And Brother Anthony Morris of the Governing Body
will be giving this talk to us.
And he has an interesting theme also:
“A Blueprint for Spiritual Success.”
Brother Morris, please give us this valuable “blueprint.”
To introduce the information,
I thought I’d show you this here.
This is a blueprint.
Now, this one happens to be—
And I got it from a friend of mine.
This was part of the blueprint
for building world headquarters.
So this is connected with the Offices/Services Building,
and that’s the blueprint.
Now, what I did learn is that you also have,
in that business,
a lot of them on white background now.
And Webster’s Dictionary did capture that fact very nicely.
Here’s what it says
in defining a blueprint (that word):
“a photographic print in white on a bright blue ground
“or blue on a white ground
“used especially for copying maps,
mechanical drawings, and architects’ plans.”
Particularly thinking of the architects’ plans,
I couldn’t help but think about Proverbs chapter 8,
and we see there Jesus being referred to
as the “master worker” and Jehovah is really the Architect.
He’s the Creator.
Now, Jesus was a spiritual success with that
because he followed the Architect’s direction.
So that’s something I want you to keep in mind,
and we’ll get to the blueprint, as I’m calling it, in a moment.
The other definition in Webster’s Dictionary I thought was pertinent:
“something resembling a blueprint
“(as in serving as a model
“or providing guidance);
“[and I love the one little expression that appeared after that]
“especially: a detailed plan
or program of action.”
So that’s how I’m borrowing that word “blueprint”
with these following thoughts
in Peter’s second letter.
So if you could, we’re going to show you
what I’m referring to as a blueprint for spiritual success.
So in 2 Peter chapter 1,
there are nine things you’ll notice here
that we’re going to emphasize in verses 5 through 7.
So Peter writes: “For this very reason,
“put forth all earnest effort
“to supply to your faith virtue,
“to your virtue knowledge,
“to your knowledge self-control,
“to your self-control endurance,
“to your endurance godly devotion,
“to your godly devotion brotherly affection,
to your brotherly affection love.”
So there is the blueprint.
So there are nine thoughts that are expressed here.
Obviously, there are a lot of other things.
Jehovah gave us the whole Bible,
but this is just a nice memory aid, a good blueprint,
for you to continue
as spiritual, successful people.
Now, the first one there is “earnest effort.”
That’s basic.
Now, obviously, (and we commend you for it)
you’ve shown earnest effort just to come this far:
to be invited to Gilead (to qualify for that),
during your class,
and going out in the ministry on the weekends —earnest effort.
So you have to continue that.
You’re not born with earnest effort.
That’s a decision you make.
I have to make the same decision.
We’re going to put forth earnest effort.
It starts there.
No effort, no success.
So each individual has to decide,
‘I’m putting forth the earnest effort here,
and I’m going to be a success.’
And then you’ve got the earnest effort,
and then this is what’s involved here
—have the effort to have faith.
Now, time does not allow us
to go into detail on each one of these,
but faith obviously is essential.
Now notice in Hebrews chapter 12
(or, excuse me, 11—Hebrews chapter 11)
and the absolute necessity of faith
to be a spiritual success.
Here in chapter 11, verse 1:
“Faith is the assured expectation
“of what is hoped for, the evident demonstration
of realities that are not seen.”
So it goes on to emphasize the need for it
and how essential it is in verse 6 of the same chapter:
“Moreover, without faith it is impossible
“to please God well,
“for whoever approaches God must believe
“that he is and that he becomes the rewarder
of those earnestly seeking him.”
That’s pretty clear.
It’s not easy to misunderstand what’s being said here.
You have to keep your assured expectation
of what you’ve been hoping for.
That’s part of being a spiritual success.
It can’t weaken.
And how clear does it get?
You can’t please God and I can’t please God without faith.
That’s serious business.
And none of us want to go the remainder of the time
not pleasing our heavenly Father, Jehovah God.
We appreciate that.
In fact, right before he went into that,
in the previous (what we call chapter 10),
notice verse 38 and verse 39
of chapter 10:
“But my righteous one will live by reason of faith,
“and if he shrinks back, I have no pleasure in him.
“Now we are not the sort who shrink back to destruction,
but the sort who have faith for the preserving of our lives.”
Or, as we’re applying it now,
you’re going to be a spiritual success and have everlasting life.
But you have to have faith.
It’s crucial.
Now next he mentions “virtue.”
Now, that has to do with moral excellence.
So all of you have that.
Some are single; others of you are married.
You have virtue—that moral excellence.
And when you’re morally excellent,
especially in these last days in this world,
boy, do you stand out.
And what does that do?
It’s not that you’re trying to stand out,
but your moral excellence, your virtuous behavior,
glorifies God.
And Jehovah appreciates that.
He wants us to succeed at glorifying him.
Bring attention to it.
We don’t joke about immorality.
You know, I mean, the comedians are full of it.
We’re morally excellent.
We don’t have a thing to do
with “the spirit of the world”—with that.
Now next he mentions here
“knowledge”—“knowledge.”
Well, obviously you appreciate knowledge.
Now, you had a lot of knowledge before you got to Gilead.
But how many people, and including in this organization,
have a few months of studying like you have?
It is incredible, isn’t it?
I mean, it’s very hard for you to explain to others.
You were reading the Bible before you got here.
Don’t raise your hand if you didn’t quite get there.
God forgives you.
It depends on circumstances.
But once you were here, (and we love our instructors here
with theocratic schools, the Teaching Committee)
you have a whole lot more knowledge
than you did a few months ago.
Don’t you agree? It’s wonderful.
Now, part of you succeeding is
don’t be satisfied with this downpour
of all this knowledge.
Just take it as valuable.
Keep going, and get some new ideas
on how to research some things, and go with it.
But if you’re going to be a spiritual success,
you’ve got to keep taking in the knowledge.
That’s very clear and very simple.
And Jehovah will bless your intake
of knowledge.
There’s no end to it. It’s wonderful.
You know, it’s just that I’m always amazed.
I’ve always said,
“The more I learn, the more I realize how little I know.”
Now, that’s not just a statement. That’s a fact.
And imagine, with Jehovah, it’s just— But isn’t that great?
It will go on for eternity —taking in knowledge.
If you do it now, you’ll be able to do it forever.
What an honor for our heavenly Father!
And then he mentions here
“to your knowledge self-control.”
Now, that’s an aspect of “the fruitage of the spirit”
that you’re well aware of.
I have to have it.
You have to have it if you’re going to succeed spiritually
and gain everlasting life.
You need self-control.
And you have to pray about it, especially in these last days.
In fact, notice in 1 Corinthians chapter 10,
and we’ll come back here to Peter right after.
So here in verse 12
—1 Corinthians 10:12:
“So let the one who thinks he is standing
beware that he does not fall.”
So our thinking—
We need to pray for self-control with it
because the Devil and his wicked system
as well as he and his demons are always trying to affect our thinking.
So in this case here, you think you’re standing?
Guess what? You’re about ready to fall.
So by saying, “Jehovah, please give me self-control”
or you see when the Devil might try some sort of temptation or whatever
(something you face):
“Give me self-control.
I want to stand firm for you” —now you’re OK.
The holy spirit will do that.
You’ll have that self-control necessary
to oppose the Devil in his wicked effort
to make it so that we don’t succeed.
So it’s just crucial.
Now next he mentions with self-control
(the blueprint goes on) “endurance.”
We could spend considerable time
just talking about endurance.
It’s absolutely essential.
Some of the things you’ve endured already in your dedicated life.
And as I told the brothers
in the Coordinators’ Committee Office,
you know, when we’re facing these disasters and all these things,
and I’ve been telling them for some time now:
“Cheer up! It’s going to get worse.”
And so we keep a sense of humor with it.
But that’s a fact.
What we’re experiencing right now in this global pandemic,
I was telling the branch class yesterday:
“Doesn’t bother me. We’ve been waiting for this.
“We knew things like this were going to happen.
“Christ Jesus has prepared us.
Where’s the shock?”
Now, you got to think, and Jehovah directs us with how to deal with these things,
but we endure.
And that’s why Jesus— You remember this in Matthew chapter 24,
and then we’ll come back here —Matthew chapter 24.
And we’ve been so well-equipped.
It’s all here so that we can be a success.
Verse 13 of Matthew chapter 24:
“But the one who has endured to the end
“[not who showed some endurance,
“no, the one who has endured to the end]
will be saved.”
So that’s what we beg Jehovah: “Help us.”
It’s part of the blueprint.
We’re going to endure to the end.
That’s it.
Whatever we have to face,
with Jehovah’s support, we’re going to succeed.
Now after endurance,
he mentions “godly devotion.”
Now, The Watchtower has commented
on this in years past.
And it’s a beautiful thing to keep in mind
why this is so crucial to spiritual success.
It’s captured nicely here
in the revised translation—godly devotion.
So the thinking there and to try to convey
what was coming across here for all of us
is you’re devoted
or I’m devoted to Jehovah personally
—this attachment to him personally.
So some of you are married couples.
Well, you want your mate
to be attached to your God
that you worship together.
That’s what is going to make a success.
Godly devotion —being personally attached to Jehovah.
It affects every aspect of our life.
We’re attached to him. It’s personal.
It’s just something special,
and everyone should have that feeling
of not just devotion,
no, but attachment to him.
We love him. We’re whole-souled.
‘You get exclusive devotion.’
Right now, just thinking about him, and you can’t see them,
but I got goose bumps on my back,
thinking about the love for him —the attachment to him.
And how nice when, if you are married, your mate has that.
You’re going to succeed.
Devotion to Him personally
for all that he has shown and will show
—that’s just very personal.
Now next
he attaches after godly devotion,
“brotherly affection”
—“brotherly affection.”
So when you think about that now—
And I appreciated Brother Noumair’s comments.
I saw this yesterday while with you for a couple of lectures
and then saw some of you after your last class,
and Brother Noumair mentioned how you enjoy each other’s company.
Well, what he was describing was your brotherly affection for each other.
It’s real; it’s genuine.
You have that brotherly affection.
That should be true in all the congregations.
You’ve displayed it.
Well, to succeed, you’ve got to continue to do that.
So here’s something for you to think about, though,
because commendably you’ve done well with that.
I’m sure you are going to take it back with you
—this need for godly devotion.
You’re going to do that. I’m counting on it.
However, here’s a thought for you
from 1 Thessalonians chapter 4
—1 Thessalonians
chapter 4.
It’s just something to consider
(you soon-to-be graduates),
and take it with you to your assignments.
First Thessalonians 4:9
and then here in the 10th verse as well:
“However, concerning brotherly love,
“you do not need us to write to you,
“for you yourselves are taught by God to love one another.
“In fact, you are doing so
“toward all the brothers in all of Macedonia.
“[Now notice this. This is a thought-provoking point.]
“But we urge you, brothers,
to go on doing so in fuller measure.”
Whoa!
So that applies to you too.
You’ve shown it during your class.
But I want you to think about it from time to time
so that you’re a spiritual success.
You’ve got to ask yourself, individually particularly,
maybe as a couple if you wish,
are you doing it in fuller measure?
It’s a lot to think about, seeing as things get more and more critical.
Good point.
We need this godly expression here
of our brotherly affection.
We love our brothers.
We forgive each other, but we have this.
And it’s got to get fuller, and we know you’re going to do that.
You’ll think about it.
Just examine yourself from time to time with this blueprint.
Are you showing brotherly affection in fuller measure?
And you might get back— I know we’re all different.
I don’t know your circumstances,
obviously God does and Christ Jesus does,
but some might say:
‘Boy, she’s just filled with brotherly affection.
‘It’s amazing.
‘I don’t remember that about her
before (or him).’
Now sisters, I don’t want you to feel like I’m picking on you.
The same applies to the brothers.
But show love and brotherly affection in fuller measure.
It’s something to think about from time to time.
Now back here
in Peter’s second letter,
this is the last thought
that he puts into the blueprint:
“to your godly devotion brotherly affection,”
and then notice, “to your brotherly affection love.”
So that has reference to a·gaʹpe.
So brotherly affection
is a unique expression of brothers —that love for them.
But this is a principled love, as you know.
So it’s governed by principle.
And that’s the kind of love we need to keep on preaching
because people are going to get more and more
distinct with their contempt for us.
It’s growing in most countries.
Well, the a·gaʹpe is going to move us to keep on going.
No matter how they mistreat us and what they say or do,
we’re going to show love until Jehovah says:
“That’s it. No more preaching.”
And think about our time right now because of this threat.
There are these national security problems in different countries.
Metropolitan preaching in many countries is not happening.
Door-to-door preaching is a problem.
The Memorial campaign is—
Different things are going on.
Jehovah has given his spirit to the Governing Body
to try to do the right thing
—to respect Caesar and obey Him as our ruler.
It makes you think:
‘What are the inactive or others that have known about the truth—?
What are they thinking?’
Well, we hope the best for them.
“But you better move. This is serious business.”
Our a·gaʹpe love is going to help us to try to reach out to them.
Now is the time for action because the day is coming.
That’s it; it’s over.
Once that great tribulation breaks out, that’s it.
We can’t help. It’s over for them.
So those are the nine parts
of the blueprint for spiritual success.
Now notice the thought here
(and that’s what we want to conclude with)
in verse 8:
“For if these things exist in you
“[now notice] and overflow,
“they will prevent you from being either inactive
“or unfruitful regarding the accurate knowledge
of our Lord Jesus Christ.”
So there it is.
So we’re just exhorting you precious ones soon to graduate:
Don’t let it just exist (the blueprint).
Let all of this overflow,
and you are guaranteed to be a spiritual success.
Well, we appreciate that very much, Brother Morris.
Thank you for that blueprint
that guarantees success in building spirituality
in ourselves and others.
Now, you probably have noticed
that we have some envelopes here on our table.
Now, these are not ordinary envelopes.
They’re special envelopes containing some special items.
Now, in these envelopes are your diplomas.
There’s a class picture in the envelopes.
There’s a letter from the Teaching Committee.
And some of the envelopes contain additional letters
regarding world headquarters assignments.
And there’s a note indicating
that you will receive a modest monetary gift
deposited into your account on Monday.
So some good things are in these envelopes.
We’re confident that all of you
will appreciate receiving these special envelopes.
So one by one and couple by couple,
we’re going to have you come up and receive your envelopes.
Now, Brother David Schafer,
a helper to the Teaching Committee, is going to help me here.
And he’s got the hard job.
He has to pronounce all of these names,
and the pressure is on him.
The parents and relatives are listening, and they’ll know if he did it right.
But all I have to do is hand the envelopes to them
and give them an elbow bump.
That’s our modified handshake
as recommended by the Health Department.
So we’re going to have you come up and, please, Brother Schafer.
So first, we have Brother and Sister Akiyama,
and they will be returning to Brazil.
And next, we have Brother and Sister Arthur, and they will be returning to Ghana.
Next, we have Brother and Sister Asenov, and they will be returning to Bulgaria.
Brother Bączyński will now be serving in Germany.
Sister Bočarņikova will be serving in Finland.
Brother and Sister Bonomi will be returning to Peru.
Brother and Sister Chapman will be returning to the Dominican Republic.
Brother and Sister Chong will be returning to Korea.
Brother and Sister Dela Cruz will be returning to Micronesia.
Brother and Sister Domingos will be returning to Angola.
Brother and Sister Gabriels will be returning to Belgium.
Brother Gambatese will be returning to Argentina.
Brother and Sister Geha will be returning to the Middle East.
Sister González will be returning to Spain.
Brother and Sister Habonimana will be returning to Burundi.
Brother Kim will be returning to Chile.
Brother Latyshov will be returning to Finland.
Brother Matthew will be returning to Sri Lanka.
Brother Metz will be returning to the Dominican Republic.
Brother Mkhize will be returning to South Africa.
Brother and Sister Mwasile will be returning to Kenya.
Brother Ngoy will be returning to Congo (Kinshasa).
Brother and Sister Owen will now be serving in Angola.
Brother Parker will now be serving in the United States.
Brother and Sister Potirantakis will be returning to Greece.
Brother and Sister Raffaeli will now be serving in Angola.
Sister Rajkannu will be returning to India.
Brother and Sister Sarialp will be returning to Turkey.
Brother and Sister Susanna will be now be serving in Madagascar.
Brother Wirthmülle will be returning to Germany.
And, finally, Brother and Sister Zuiderent will be returning to the Netherlands.
I think we were really getting into that elbow bump, weren’t we?
Although, that will wear you down after all of those bumps.
But we try to follow the good example
that they’re recommending at the Health Department.
And we’re so happy
to have been able to give those special envelopes
to all these dear ones.
The Governing Body is very happy to give them.
And we know that you all are very happy to have received them
and to have reached this spiritual milestone
in your theocratic career.
In fact, now we’re not going to call you Gilead students.
You’re no longer students.
We’re going to call you Gilead graduates
because you now have your diplomas.
But now let’s raise our curtain and get a look
at the entire 148th class
of the Watchtower Bible School of Gilead.
That was a nice applause you gave to yourselves.
I got to tease them a little bit.
But what a nice-looking group
—those smiling faces, a handsome group!
And if you look very closely,
they look quite a bit smarter than they did five months ago.
They’ve learned a lot during this time.
But while you’re looking at this beautiful group,
permit me, please, to give a few statistics to give you an overview.
Now, so that you don’t try to quickly count,
we have 55 students,
or 55 graduates (I can’t say that anymore),
55 graduates of this 148th class of Gilead,
and that includes 20 couples,
11 single brothers, and 4 single sisters.
The average age is 40.1.
Now, that sounds young to me.
It’s amazing how everything changes.
But the youngest is 30.7;
the oldest, 56.1;
the average years baptized, 24.6;
the average years in full-time service, 17.9;
the average years in special full-time service, 13.1.
And listen to this: The languages spoken
by this class is 35.
This is a multilingual class for sure.
That makes us think of the great crowd
and how they would be taken from ‘all nations,
tribes, peoples, and tongues’
—35 languages represented here.
And even though they’re relatively young (as we said, the average is 40),
they’re quite experienced because on average
they have spent 73 percent of the time
since they’ve been baptized in the full-time service.
So just about three quarters of the time since they’ve been baptized
they’ve been in the full-time service.
But now we’re going to have our class letter read
by Brother Mussa Mwasile,
and you can see now why I had Brother Schafer pronounce all of the names.
But this is Brother Mussa Mwasile,
and he’s going back to Kenya.
And he’s going to read the letter from the class.
“To the Governing Body and the United States Bethel family.
“Dear Brothers:
“From the moment we received the invitation to Gilead,
“we eagerly anticipated what was to come.
“Now, after five unforgettable months,
“we fully agree with Job’s words:
“‘My ears have heard about you,
“but now I do see you with my eyes.’
“By means of our deep study of God’s Word,
“we have seen Jehovah’s amazing qualities
“on full display.
“The way he shows love and care for his people
“has been embedded in our minds and hearts.
“We are determined
“to continue to imitate his example.
“As soon as we came to school,
“the Bethel family quickly endeared themselves to us
“by their warmth, hospitality, and love.
“Their self-sacrificing example
“is one we will all cherish
“and take with us when going to our assignments.
“We have come
“to dearly love our instructors.
“Each day, they have put their heart and soul
“into their teaching and we felt
“their genuine love and concern for us.
“By means of divine instruction,
“we have seen Jehovah, our Grand Instructor,
“and his spirit-directed organization
“in new and faith-strengthening ways.
“We have been taught
“to dig into God’s Word like never before,
“and we are resolved
“to apply what we’ve learned.
“Observing the tireless work and unselfish spirit
“that the members of the Governing Body display
“motivates us to imitate their faith.
“Our hearts are filled with deep gratitude
“when we think back to the many visits,
“loving instruction, and personal attention
“that was generously provided.
“We have seen and felt their love and concern for us
“and how they unitedly work together.
“They have instilled in us a greater desire
“to imitate the head of the congregation, Jesus Christ.
“They truly have proved
“to be gifts from Jehovah
“and have become ‘so beloved to us.’
“Although there are unique circumstances
“surrounding this graduation program,
“we are not disheartened;
“rather, we are confident.
“We feel strongly that we are witnessing clear evidence
“of you being faithful and discreet.
“We have the utmost confidence and respect
“in the direction you provide
“during these momentous times.
“We praise our great God, Jehovah,
“for the gift of Gilead.
“We express our sincere appreciation
“and deep love to each one of you.
“Your brothers and sisters,
148th class of Gilead.”
Sorry, Brother Mwasile,
I forgot to give you your elbow bump.
Sorry about that.
But I took the letter, and I’ll make sure
the Governing Body gets this beautiful letter.
What a beautiful letter!
It nicely expresses your feelings
about being at Gilead,
and you say that you enjoyed being here.
Well, we say that we enjoyed having you.
It was truly a mutual
“interchange of encouragement” as mentioned at Romans 1:12.
And Brother Mussa did a beautiful job.
That was actually his first speaking assignment as a Gilead graduate.
But he really did a good job, didn’t he?
It was really good.
He’s going to do wonderful things in the future with Jehovah’s help,
just like all of you.
But we’ve really had a good time having you.
But now I get to talk five more minutes to you one more time here.
And if you recall
in the opening discussion of our program,
we talked about four areas
in which we can imitate Jesus’ modesty.
Well, briefly, let’s talk about one more aspect of modesty
that is closely related
to being aware of our own limitations
—that is being aware of the limitations of others.
And again, our role model, Jesus, set a perfect example
in this aspect of modesty.
Ponder for a moment, if you will,
what is stated at Matthew 3:16.
It talks about how after Jesus was baptized,
he came up out of the water, and then it says:
“The heavens were opened up.”
What does that mean?
Well, the Greatest Man book makes this comment:
“Evidently it means
“that while he is being baptized,
“the memory of his prehuman life in heaven
“returns to him.
“Thus, Jesus now fully recalls
“his life as a spirit son of Jehovah God,
“including all the things that God spoke to him in heaven
during his prehuman existence.”
Now, that’s an amazing comment, isn’t it?
Can you just imagine
flooding into the perfect human brain of Jesus
the memory of billions of years
of prehuman existence
—aeons and aeons of time
and countless, countless experiences
as he served as “a master worker” beside Jehovah,
as he served as “the prince of Jehovah’s army,”
as he served as Jehovah’s Spokesman,
as he served as Michael the archangel?
Now, if you think about it,
that would’ve been the greatest download of information
that had ever happened.
But here’s the point:
Like Jesus, you received a download here at Gilead, right?
Nothing like what Jesus got,
but you had a tremendous five-month download, didn’t you?
But the point is, How did Jesus use
all of this newly acquired, voluminous,
tremendous knowledge that he received?
How did he use it in his dealings with others?
Well, he never overwhelmed them
with impressive displays of knowledge.
Now, he could’ve done that, couldn’t he?
He never did that.
He was always very aware of their limitations
—very considerate, very thoughtful.
Do you remember what he said to his disciples
as recorded at John 16:12?
He said to them:
“I still have many things to say to you,
but you are not able to bear them now.”
Now, he was very thoughtful —wasn’t he?—of their limitations,
even though he had all this tremendous knowledge.
So, what a good example for us!
Additionally, even though he was perfect,
he was not a perfectionist.
In other words, he didn’t require perfection of others.
He allowed for the mistakes, the shortcomings,
the weaknesses, of others.
And if you think about this, there were many other ways he was sensitive
—he was compassionate— regarding the limitations of others.
Just one more example:
He knew his disciples at times
needed to get away from the crowds and rest.
Well, how can you dear Gilead graduates
imitate Jesus’ modesty
in being aware of the limitations of others?
Well, as we mentioned, you had a tremendous five-month download of information,
but please use it modestly.
Use it in a way that you never put more
on others than they can bear.
Use it in a way that you realize their limitations.
Everyone has limitations —some more than others—
but be aware of that.
Little by little, share the good things you’ve learned with these ones.
And always be aware
to never put more on them than they can bear.
There’s a saying, “By the mile it’s a trial;
“by the yard it’s hard;
but inch by inch it’s a cinch.”
So just little by little,
share and help the ones in your territory,
your congregation, your Bethel family.
Help them to benefit from the good things you’ve learned these last five months.
And please, by all means,
allow for the imperfections and shortcomings of others.
If the perfect One was not a perfectionist,
then even more so we as all imperfect ones,
surely, we can allow for the imperfections of others.
And we know you’re going to be determined to do that.
And please be sensitive and compassionate
concerning the physical, emotional limitations
of others as Jesus was.
But now, we’ve discussed all together
five areas in which we can imitate Jesus’ modesty.
In quick review,
we talked about the need to always remember
that (1) we have authority limitations
and try hard to stay within the bounds,
(2) we have to remember our lesser importance
compared to Jehovah’s vastly greater importance,
(3) we have to remember there are some things
we’re simply not entitled to know,
at least not now, and then some things maybe never,
(4) we want to be aware
of always fully relying on Jehovah
and never ourselves,
and (5) as we just discussed,
always be aware of the limitations of others.
If we imitate Jesus’ modesty in these five areas,
Jehovah will love us dearly
as he dearly loves his modest Son.
He’ll love us the same way.
And wherever we go, whatever privileges we have,
we will always be refreshing to others
as Jesus was.
But now, in imitation of what is done
on JW Broadcasting®,
they have a postcard at the end, don’t they?
So we’re going to have a postcard
coming from the class,
the 148th class of Gilead.
Send them a postcard.
Send them, please, your love and affection.
They send you warm love and affection
from the 148th class of Gilead.
So that’s a lot of love that they sent, and we finish by saying,
“From the 148th class
“of Gilead in the Patterson auditorium,
this is JW Broadcasting.”

title: 레너드 마이어스: 가정에서 합리적인 사람이 되십시오 (골로새 3:18-20)

ko.text: 남편들이 기억해야 할 이런 말이 나옵니다.
흔히 더 균형 잡힌 결정을 내릴 수 있습니다.”
이 자리에 계신 남편 분들은 이 말에 공감하실 겁니다.
이와 같이 행동하는 데는 여러 가지 성품이 관련되는데요,
우리는 그 본에서 무엇을 배울 수 있습니까?
먼저 첫 번째 질문을 생각해 보죠.
그는 다른 사람의 한계와 상황을 고려해 줍니다.
합리성이라는 특성에 대해 어떻게 알려 주는지
이처럼 다른 사람들이 알 수 있게 해야 합니다.
그러니까 우리가 자신을 합리적이라고 생각하는 것이
우리가 합리적이라는 평판을 얻고 있는지가 중요합니다.
“이런 것들 중 하나와 관련하여 죄과가 있게 되었다면,
그는 자기가 어떻게 죄를 지었는지 고백해야 한다.”
곧 가축 떼에서 어린 암양이든 어린 암염소든
암컷 한 마리를 속죄 제물로 가져와야 한다.”
그런데 7절에서 여호와의 합리성을 볼 수 있습니다.
“하지만 그가 양을 바칠 만한 형편이 안 되면,
죄에 대한 죄과 제물로 산비둘기 두 마리나
그런데 11절을 보면 그분은 한 걸음 더 나아가십니다.
어린 집비둘기 두 마리를 바칠 만한 형편이 안 되면,
고운 가루 10분의 1에바를 속죄 제물로 가져와야 한다.”
이처럼 여호와께서는 이스라엘 백성 개인의 경제 상황에 따라
각주를 보면 그 점을 알 수 있죠.
속죄 제물로 고운 가루 2.2리터를, 아마도 제사장에게
새 두 마리를 바치지 못해도 걱정하지 마라.
여호와께선 이 가난한 이스라엘 여자가 가져온 재물을
다른 부유한 사람이 가져온 재물만큼 소중히 여기셨습니다.
이 가난한 여자가 얼마나 행복해했을지 상상해 보십시오!
귀한 손님을 대접할 때 쓰는 가루여야 했죠.
따라서 여호와께 다른 사람만큼 드릴 수는 없어도
자신의 가장 좋은 것을 드려야 했습니다.
나를 위해 최선을 다할 거라는 것을 나는 알고 있다.’
여호와께서는 우리의 한계와 상황을 이해해 주심으로
일부 형제 자매들은 양이나 염소를 바치는 것처럼
비둘기 두 마리 정도의 봉사를 드릴 수 있는 사람도 있고요.
어쩌면 어떤 분들은 과거에 그런 봉사를 드렸을 것입니다.
마치 고운 가루 2.2리터와 같은 봉사라도 말이죠.
형제 자매들에게 지나친 기대를 해서는 안 됩니다.
그 예를 누가복음 22장에서 볼 수 있습니다.
예수께선 베드로가 곧 그분을 세 번 부인할 것을 알고 계셨죠.
당신이 돌아오거든, 당신의 형제들을 강하게 하십시오.”
베드로의 믿음이 없어지지 않도록 기도하신 겁니다.
형제들을 강하게 해 줄 것임을 확신하셨습니다.
베드로가 세 번 부인할 것을 아셨는데도 그렇게 하신 거죠.
이 내용이 어떻게 예수의 합리성을 보여 줍니까?
베드로가 처해 있었던 상황을 고려해 주신 것입니다.
그가 앞으로 할 일에 대해 확신을 나타내셨습니다.
스플레인 형제가 토요일에 그 점을 강조하셨죠?
우리는 그들에 대한 확신을 나타내야 합니다.
다른 사람들에 대해 합리적인 기대를 하십시오.
어쩌면 그들은 우리가 잘 모르거나 온전히 이해하지 못하는
어떤 어려움을 겪고 있을 수 있습니다.
“형제들이 하지 않은 일에 대해 판단하는 것보다
그들이 한 일을 칭찬해 주는 것이 훨씬 낫습니다!”
합리적인 사람은 참을성 있고 친절하고 부드럽게
또한 다른 사람의 한계와 상황을 이해해 줍니다.
여호와와 예수께서는 정말 좋은 분을 보이셨습니다.
또 우리는 사람들의 좋은 점을 보고
우리 모두 매일의 생활에서 우리가 합리적이라는 것을
모두가 알 수 있도록 최선을 다해야겠습니다.

Notice it says:
“Although he cannot always do
“as she [that is, his wife] asks,
“he often arrives at a more balanced decision
by consulting her.”
Well, those of us who are husbands
know the truthfulness of those words, don’t we?
Now, there are a number of qualities
that this statement may bring to mind.
And one of those qualities
is the quality of reasonableness.
That’s a quality that all of us need to display.
How would you describe a reasonable person?
What examples of reasonableness
do we find in Jehovah and Jesus?
And what can we learn from their example?
Well, let’s first consider that description.
Our publications have stated
that a reasonable person is patient, gentle,
and kind in his dealings with himself and with others.
He takes into consideration
others’ limitations and their circumstances.
Someone with a reputation of being reasonable
is flexible when circumstances warrant it.
It’s like that husband that we just mentioned.
When he is reasonable as he consults with his wife,
he’s willing to listen to her and, when appropriate,
to go along with her wishes.
Now notice with me at Philippians 4:5
the inspired counsel about this quality of reasonableness.
Please turn there in Philippians chapter 4,
and notice what the Bible tells us in the A portion of verse 5.
It states:
“Let your reasonableness become known to all men.”
So others should see us displaying this quality.
Another translation renders the verse:
“Have a reputation for being reasonable.”
So notice, it’s not so much how we view ourselves,
whether we feel we’re reasonable,
rather, it’s how others see us —how we are known,
if we have the reputation of being reasonable.
When you think about it,
reasonableness attracts, doesn’t it,
whereas unreasonableness tends to drive away?
Well, now that we have that description,
what examples of reasonableness do we find in Jehovah and Jesus?
Let’s consider Jehovah’s example first.
And if you turn with me to Leviticus chapter 5,
let’s look at an example of his reasonableness
with the nation of Israel.
Leviticus chapter 5,
and notice there in verse 5 to begin.
It says: “If he becomes guilty as respects one of these things
“[talking about someone who’s committed a sin, it says],
then he must confess in what he has sinned.”
Verse 6: “He will also bring his guilt offering
“to Jehovah for the sin that he committed,
“namely, a female from the flock,
either a female lamb or a young female goat, for a sin offering.”
So that was plain.
But notice Jehovah’s reasonableness in verse 7:
“If, though, he cannot afford a sheep,
“he must bring to Jehovah two turtledoves
or two young pigeons as his guilt offering for the sin.”
So that was reasonable on Jehovah’s part.
But Jehovah took it a step further.
Notice verse 11:
“Now if he cannot afford two turtledoves or two young pigeons,
“he must bring as his offering for his sin
a tenth of an ephah of fine flour for a sin offering.”
So notice, Jehovah was reasonable in what he expected,
depending on the Israelites’ financial circumstances.
As we read verse 11, you may have wondered, ‘Well, what’s a tenth of an ephah?’
Well, our footnote helps us.
You notice what it says?
“A tenth of an ephah equaled 2.2 L
(2 dry qt).”
Notice this image of an Israelite woman.
She’s of very limited means, and she’s holding out
—possibly to give to the priest— her sin offering of two quarts of flour.
It wasn’t much, was it?
Here in Leviticus, it was as if Jehovah was saying:
‘If you don’t have enough for a lamb or a goat, that’s OK.
‘If you don’t have enough for those two small birds, don’t worry.
Just bring me two quarts of flour as your sacrifice.’
Well, imagine how happy a poor Israelite like this woman would have been
that Jehovah valued her small offering
just as much as one of the costlier sacrifices
presented by her wealthier neighbors!
But did you notice an important detail there in verse 11 about the flour?
The flour that the needy Israelite
was to offer wasn’t just any type of flour.
Did you see there in the verse?
It was to be fine flour,
such as that used to prepare a meal for an honored guest.
So though the poor Israelite couldn’t give as much as others,
the little they offered to Jehovah was to be their best.
In effect, Jehovah was saying, ‘I realize you can’t offer as much as others,
but I know, I know, that you’re going to give me your best.’
What’s the lesson?
Jehovah displays reasonableness
by taking into consideration our limitations and our circumstances.
You know, some brothers and sisters can offer
in their service the equivalent of a lamb or a goat.
Others can offer the equivalent of two turtledoves or two pigeons.
And perhaps in the past, some of us
were able to offer the same in our assignments.
But right now, because of our circumstances,
because of limitations, maybe we’re not able to.
Well, what do we know about Jehovah?
He graciously and reasonably accepts our best
in his service even if that’s comparable
to two quarts of fine flour.
What a reasonable God we worship
and a good lesson for us to be reasonable
and not compare ourselves with others
or to expect more than we should of our brothers and sisters!
Now, what about Jesus’ example?
He set an example in reasonableness
by being patient and kind in his dealings
with his disciples despite their shortcomings.
Let’s notice an example.
Turn with me to Luke chapter 22,
and let’s notice an example of Jesus’ reasonableness.
Luke chapter 22
—the setting is shortly before Jesus’ death,
and he’s aware that Peter is soon going to deny him three times.
So, what did Jesus do?
He encouraged Peter.
Notice verse 32.
Jesus said: “But I have made supplication
“for you that your faith may not give out;
and you, once you have returned, strengthen your brothers.”
Notice the encouragement?
Jesus said: “I have made supplication for you.”
In other words, Jesus prayed in Peter’s behalf
that Peter’s faith not give out.
And then he told him:
“Once you have returned, strengthen your brothers.”
Jesus expressed confidence that Peter,
after a short lapse, would return to faithful service
and he would strengthen his brothers
—and that despite the fact, you notice in verse 34,
Jesus told him, ‘You’re going to deny me three times.’
Now, how does this account show reasonableness on Jesus’ part?
Well, you may remember what Jesus had said sometime earlier,
as recorded at Matthew 10:33.
He said: “Whoever disowns me before men,
I will also disown him.”
Now, that was a strong statement,
and Jesus could have applied that to Peter.
But demonstrating reasonableness, Jesus didn’t reject Peter.
Why?
Because Jesus knew that there were going to be
extenuating circumstances.
He was willing to forgive his repentant apostle
and express confidence in what Peter would do in the future.
So the lesson?
We should look for the good in our brothers.
Brother Splane highlighted that on Saturday for us, didn’t he?
Despite their imperfections,
we should express confidence and faith in our brothers.
We should be reasonable in what we expect of others.
Who knows?
They may be facing challenges that we either don’t know about
or that we don’t fully understand.
One Watchtower stated this:
“How much better it is to commend our brothers
for what they do than to judge them for what they do not do!”
Like Jesus, let’s be reasonable when love calls for it
and circumstances warrant it.
Well, what have we considered?
A reasonable person is patient, kind, and gentle
in his dealings with himself and with others.
He takes into consideration the limitations
and the circumstances of others.
Reasonableness attracts,
unreasonableness tends to drive away.
What excellent examples we have in reasonableness with Jehovah and Jesus!
Remember the fine flour and the need to look for the good in others,
expressing confidence in them.
So as we go about our day,
may we look for opportunities
to let our reasonableness become known to all men.

cn.text: 关于做丈夫的
今天引述的《守望台》文章这样说
“虽然丈夫不可能每次都按妻子的意见去做
但丈夫和妻子商量后
就能作出比较合理的决定。”
我们做丈夫的都非常同意这句话，是吗？
这让我们想到做丈夫的应该有的几个特质
其中一个特质就是通情达理
这是我们所有人都要培养的特质
那么，通情达理是什么意思呢？
耶和华和耶稣怎样表现这个特质呢？
我们可以怎样效法他们呢？
首先，什么是通情达理？
我们的出版物提到一个通情达理的人
对人对己都会有耐心，表现温和和仁慈
他知道别人能力有限
也会考虑其他人的情况
有这种特质的人
能按照不同的环境做出适当的调整
就像我们刚才提到，一个做丈夫的
如果他表现通情达理的态度
他就会跟妻子商量，如果可以
他就会听妻子的意见
我们来看腓立比书4:5
提到通情达理这个特质
请翻开腓立比书第4章
让我们一起来看看第5节的前半部分
这里说
“要让所有人都知道你们通情达理。”
所以经文说
要让所有人知道我们有这个特质
有些英文译本也说，要有通情达理的名声
请注意
这里不是说我们自己觉得自己通情达理就好
这里强调的是别人的看法
别人是不是也觉得
我们是个通情达理的人呢？
你是不是也觉得，通情达理的人很容易亲近
不通情达理的人，大家都会躲得远远的
现在我们已经知道什么是通情达理了
那么耶和华和耶稣怎样表现通情达理呢？
我们先来看看耶和华怎么做
现在请你看利未记第5章
来看耶和华怎样对以色列人
表现通情达理的态度
我们从5:5开始看
经文说
“假如有人在以上任何一件事上担负罪责
（这里说的是一个犯罪的人）
他就要承认自己犯了什么罪。”
第6节说
“他要为自己犯的罪
把抵罪祭的母羊献给耶和华
也就是用一只母绵羊羔或母山羊羔
献做赎罪祭。”
这里说的很清楚
但请留意耶和华多么的通情达理
第7节说:“但他如果没有能力献羊
就要为自己犯的罪
用两只斑鸠或两只雏鸽做抵罪祭献给耶和华。”
看上帝对以色列人真的是通情达理
“如果他没有能力献两只斑鸠或两只雏鸽
就要为自己犯的罪
用十分之一伊法的上等面粉献做赎罪祭。”
你们看，耶和华还考虑到以色列人的经济能力
他的确是个通情达理的上帝
11节提到“十分之一伊法”是什么呢？
来看看脚注就可以知道了
脚注说，十分之一伊法相当于2.2升
请看看这个以色列人妇女的图片
她很穷，拥有的不多
她拿着赎罪祭物要给祭司
她献上2.2升的面粉
2.2升的面粉一点也不多，对吗？
在利未记里
耶和华好像在说
“如果你没有能力献上绵羊或山羊，没关系
如果你没有能力献上2只小鸟，也没关系
只要献上2.2升的面粉当赎罪祭就好了！”
你能想象那些很穷的以色列人
听到了会有多高兴吗？
虽然这个妇女献的跟那些有钱的邻居献的相比
显得微不足道
但耶和华还是很重视她的祭物
11节有一个跟面粉有关的重要细节
就是那个面粉可不是随便的面粉都可以
你看到经文怎么说吗？
一定要是“上等的”面粉才行
就是招待尊贵的客人时使用的上等面粉
虽然贫穷的以色列人
不能像别人一样献上那么多
但他们献给耶和华的一定要是他们最好的东西
耶和华好像在说
“虽然你没有办法献的跟别人一样多
但我知道，你一定会把最好的给我。”
我们学到什么？
耶和华愿意做出改变
他会考虑每个人不同的能力和情况
有些弟兄姐妹做的服务
好像是献上一只绵羊或山羊
但另一些弟兄姐妹
就好像献上两只斑鸠或两只鸽子
也许我们以前在岗位上
可以为耶和华做很多事
但现在环境和情况有所改变
我们就没办法做那么多了
那耶和华怎么看我们呢？
他仁慈体贴又通情达理
只要我们献上最好的
就算只献上2.2升的面粉，他也很愿意接受
我们崇拜的上帝是多么的通情达理
我们学到:我们不要拿自己跟别人比较
也不要对弟兄姐妹要求太高
那耶稣呢？
虽然门徒一再让耶稣失望
但耶稣还是很有耐心、很仁慈地对待他们
耶稣多么通情达理啊！
我们一起来看一个例子
路加福音22章
我们来看看耶稣怎样表现通情达理
这段经文的背景是
在耶稣去世前
耶稣知道很快彼得会3次不认他
那么耶稣怎么做呢？
他鼓励彼得
请看32节
耶稣说
“可是我已经为你恳切祈求，免得你信心尽失
你回头以后
要帮助你的弟兄坚强起来。”
耶稣怎样鼓励彼得呢？
耶稣说
“我已经为你恳切祈求。”
也就是求耶和华不要让彼得失去信心
耶稣还说
“你回头以后
要帮助你的弟兄坚强起来。”
耶稣对彼得有信心
他知道虽然彼得一时软弱
但后来一定会继续为他服务
也会鼓励其他弟兄
虽然耶稣知道这些事
但34节耶稣还是对彼得说
“你会三次说你不认识我。”
你们可能还记得在马太福音10:33
耶稣在更早之前曾说过
他说，“谁在别人面前不认我，我也会不认他。”
这个措辞非常强烈
耶稣也可以用在彼得身上
但因为耶稣十分通情达理
所以他没有否定彼得
为什么呢？
因为他知道到时彼得的处境一定会很困难
耶稣很愿意原谅悔改的彼得
也相信他以后会忠心地崇拜上帝
我们学到什么呢？
我们应该看弟兄们的优点
就像斯普莱恩弟兄前几天的演讲提到的一样
虽然弟兄姐妹都不完美都有缺点
但我们还是应该对他们有信心
不要对他们有过高的期望
也许，他们遇到的困难是我们无法了解
也无法完全体会的
有一篇《守望台》文章说
“称赞弟兄做得到的事
比批评他们做不到的事，还要好！”
所以要通情达理
要知道每个人的情况都不一样
要表达对他们的爱
那我们学到了什么呢？
一个通情达理的人
会有耐心也会待人温和仁慈
对别人对自己都是这样
他知道别人能力有限
也会考虑其他人的情况。
通情达理的人很容易亲近
不通情达理的人，大家都躲得远远的
耶和华和耶稣就是通情达理的好榜样！
要记得上等面粉的故事
还有要看别人的优点，要对他们有信心
希望从今天开始
我们要让所有人都知道
我们是通情达理的人

ko.text: 세계 전역에서 우리의 활동에 큰 변화가 있었습니다.
조정을 했는데, 또 조정을 하는 경우도 있었습니다.
아시는 것처럼, 매우 갑작스럽게 이루어진 조정도 있었는데요,
이러한 신권적 인도에 잘 순종해 주셔서 감사합니다.
우린 여러분이 영적 일과를 잘 유지하면서도
전 세계 각 지역의 상황이 다 다르다는 것입니다.
그런가 하면 상황이 좀 진정된 것처럼 보이는 지역들도 있죠.
정부의 제한 조처가 어느 정도 완화되었을지 모릅니다.
이런 상황은 우리의 신권 활동에 어떤 영향을 미칩니까?
여러 지역에서 상황이 완화되고 있는 이 시기에
우리는 다음과 같은 성경 원칙을 적용할 것입니다.
과신하여 무모하게 행동해서 실제로 목숨을 잃었습니다.
하지만 잠언에 나온 것처럼 지혜로운 자는 조심성을 보입니다.
충분한 시간이 흐른 뒤에 신권 활동을 재개할 것입니다.
이렇게 하면 정부에서 제한 조처를 완화한 것이
도움이 될 만한 소중한 성경 원칙들을
생명을 구할 수 있을 뿐 아니라
첫 번째 원칙은 우리가 창조주를 존중하기 때문에
상업 활동을 재개하는 한 가지 이유는 경제 때문입니다.
우리가 결정을 내릴 때 중요하게 여기는 것은
형제들의 안전을 계속 앞자리에 둘 것입니다.
지혜가 그것을 가진 사람의 생명을 보존해 준다는 것이다.”
이 말씀과 일치하게 우리는 계속해서 생명을 보존하는
지혜롭고 균형 잡힌 결정을 내리기 위해
예를 들어, 지난 3월에 우리는 길르앗 졸업식을
하지만 그 한 가지 결정으로 베델 성원들과
졸업식에 올 뻔한 사람들의 생명을 보호할 수 있었죠.
그때까지만 해도 우리는 얼마 안 있어서
뉴욕주가 코로나의 온상이 될 줄은 몰랐습니다.
이처럼 지혜로운 결정을 내릴 수 있게 도와주신 여호와께
우리의 신권 활동에 큰 변화를 가져오더라도 말이죠.
그 점을 보여 주는 경험담을 들어 보겠습니다.
브라질 지부 위원인 안토니 카르발류 형제와
에콰도르 지부 위원인 하이메 타마요 형제의 이야기를 들어 보겠습니다.
어떤 지침이 주어진 이유가 처음에 잘 이해되지 않더라도,
그 지침에 순종하는 것이 중요하다는 점을 알게 되실 겁니다.
하지만 조직에서 신속하게 지침을 내려 준 덕분에
한 의사 자매의 이야기를 해 드리겠습니다.
자매는 왕국회관에서 모이는 걸 중단하라는 지침을 받았을 때
당국에서도 아무런 제한 조처를 취하지 않은 상황이었죠.
따라서 형제들의 대응이 좀 과한 게 아닌가 생각을 했습니다.
때때로 인간의 관점에서 이해하기 어렵다는 점을 생각하고는
그런데 회중 집회가 중단되고 얼마 지나지 않아서
그 자매는 여호와께서 우리 한 사람 한 사람을
이 자매 외에도 브라질에 있는 수많은 형제 자매들이
신권 지침에 순종함으로 큰 유익을 얻고 있습니다.
하지만 형제는 몸이 좋지 않으면 집에 있어야 한다는
우리를 보호하기 위해 주어진 것이기 때문에
그 후 몇 주 동안 그의 가족은
아무도 자신들의 집에 오지 못하게 했습니다.
친척들이 집에 찾아왔을 때에도 그들을 집 밖에서 만났습니다.
그리고 그때쯤에 왕국회관에서 모이는 게 중단됐습니다.
그런데 몇 주 뒤에 파브리시오는 코로나19 확진 판정을 받았고,
그의 가족 세 명도 확진 판정을 받았죠.
파브리시오의 가족은 조직에서 베풀어 준 지침을 따라서
그들은 거리 두기 지침을 잘 따랐는데,
코로나19 확진 판정을 받기 전에도 그렇게 한 거죠.
그렇게 한 건 모두에게 보호가 됐습니다.
정말 지혜로운 결정이었다는 걸 알게 됐습니다.
이런 결정 덕분에 바이러스의 전염을 예방할 수 있었죠.
형제들이 주어진 지침에 순종한 덕분에 보호와 축복을 받았군요.
두 번째 원칙은 로마서 13:1, 2에 근거해 있습니다.
우리는 “위에 있는 권위”인 정부에 순종해야 하는데,
정부는 여호와의 허락하에 특정한 역할을 수행합니다.
그 권위에 순종하는 것이 중요하다는 점이
다시 말해, 그 권위에 반항하는 사람은
따라서 하느님의 법에 어긋나는 것이 아니라면,
그 권위에 순종하는 것이 하느님의 뜻입니다.
뉴스를 보면 사람들이 정부의 지침을 무시하고
심지어 항의 시위를 벌이는 것도 볼 수 있습니다.
하지만 세속 정부의 권위에 반항하는 것은
우리는 건강과 안전에 대한 사람들의 생각을 존중합니다.
많은 사람이 코로나 바이러스에 감염되는 걸 걱정하기 때문에
우리가 당국의 지침에 순종하고 우리의 활동을 조정한 것은
또한 좋은 증거가 행해질 수도 있죠.
유럽의 한 나라에서는 지역 공무원들이 지부 사무실에 찾아와서
우리가 바이러스 예방을 위해 무슨 조처를 취하고 있는지 확인했습니다.
공무원들은 우리가 모든 회중 집회를 화상 회의로 열고 있고,
베델을 2주 넘게 봉쇄해 왔다는 것을 알고 깜짝 놀랐습니다.
한 공무원은 상황이 이렇게 악화될 줄을 미리 알았냐고 물어보기도 했죠.
형제들은 우리가 사람의 생명을 소중히 여기는
따라서 우리의 조치는 국제적인 수준에서 이루어지죠.
필요한 조치를 취할 수 있었던 겁니다.
심지어 정부에서 구체적인 지침을 주기 전에도 말이죠.
이 경험을 통해 알 수 있는 것처럼,
이런 경험을 들으면 베드로 전서 2:12이 생각나죠.
사람들이 ‘우리의 훌륭한 행실의 목격 증인’이 되면
우리가 살펴볼 세 번째 원칙은 이것입니다.
상황이 여러 달 동안 계속되다 보니까
어쩌면 긴장이 풀어지고 경계심을 늦추게 될 수 있죠.
경험 없는 자는 그대로 가다가 대가를 치른다.”
바이러스가 또 유행할 수 있기 때문입니다.
많은 전문가들은 성공적인 치료법과 백신이 개발되고
그때는 내년이나 그 이후가 될 수도 있습니다.
따라서 이와 같은 상황을 고려해 볼 때
회중 집회나 대회나 야외 봉사와 관련하여 조정된 마련들이
슬기로운 자는 한 걸음 한 걸음을 신중히 살핀다.”
우리는 기도하고 한 걸음 한 걸음 신중히 살피면서
집회와 야외 봉사 마련을 점진적으로 조정할 것입니다.
셋째, 안일한 태도를 갖지 않도록 조심하십시오.
지금 많은 분이 아주 힘든 시기를 보내고 있습니다.
연달아 시련을 겪고 있는 분들도 있을 겁니다.
우리도 여러분과 함께 마음 아파하고 있습니다.
앞으로 있을 큰 환난을 대비한 훈련이 되고 있습니다.
우리는 지금 이 시기에 영적 일과를 조정하고 서로를 돕고
앞으로 닥칠 더 큰 어려움에 대처할 준비를 갖추게 됩니다.
전 세계에 있는 우리의 형제 자매들이
서로를 돕고 있다는 것은 정말 격려적이지 않습니까?
여러분의 행동으로 여호와께 찬양과 영예가 돌아가고 있습니다.
여러분이 이 어려운 시기에 기울이는 모든 노력에 대해

en.text: In the face of this pandemic,
we’ve made dramatic adjustments
to our activities all over the world,
including how we meet, how we preach,
and even how we associate with one another.
We’ve even had to make adjustments to the adjustments
with the changing conditions.
As you know, some of these changes have come very quickly,
and we want to commend you for your obedience to theocratic direction.
We love you all very much and want to keep you safe
while helping you to maintain a good spiritual routine.
As we think about what happens next,
it’s important to remember that we’re not all experiencing
this global crisis the same way.
In some parts of the world,
the coronavirus is just beginning to spread more quickly.
In other places, outbreaks appear to be somewhat contained for now,
and governments are already easing restrictions.
So how will this affect our theocratic activities?
Well, as things open up in various regions,
we’re going to be guided by the principle
in Proverbs 14:16,
Proverbs 14:16,
where it says:
“The wise one is cautious and turns away from evil,
but the stupid one is reckless and overconfident.”
In this pandemic, recklessness and overconfidence
have literally cost people their lives.
But as the proverb says:
“The wise one is cautious.”
So we’ll continue to take a cautious approach.
In general, we’ll allow more time
after the government loosens a particular restriction
before we resume a theocratic activity.
This will allow the organization to monitor the impact
that any lifting of restrictions has
on the spread of the virus.
The Coordinators’ Committee of the Governing Body
recently shared some valuable principles
with Branch Committees around the world
to help guide them as governments ease restrictions
related to the spread of COVID-19.
We’d like to share three of those points with you now.
We are confident that obediently holding to these principles
will not only save lives
but glorify Jehovah.
First, out of respect for our Creator,
we place a high value on life.
Some governments may choose
to lift restrictions and reopen businesses,
in part for economic reasons.
But simply put,
our decisions are motivated by love,
not money.
So we’ll continue to make the safety of our brothers a priority
over personal convenience or preference.
Ecclesiastes 7:12 says this,
Ecclesiastes 7:12:
“Wisdom is a protection
“just as money is a protection,
“but the advantage of knowledge is this:
Wisdom preserves the life of its owner.”
So, in harmony with that,
our aim has been and will continue to be
to make wise, balanced decisions that protect lives.
As an example, back in March we made the decision
to hold the Gilead graduation with no invited guests present.
That was a big change.
But that one decision protected so many lives here at Bethel in New York
and among those who would have been guests.
Little did we know that just a short time later,
New York would become an epicenter of the pandemic.
We thank Jehovah for helping us
to make that wise decision!
What’s the lesson?
Because we place a high value on life,
we need to follow direction
even if it seems overly cautious
or means significant changes in our theocratic activities.
That obedience will help to keep all of us as safe as possible.
In the following video, note how this has proved to be the case
for the brothers in South America,
where the outbreak of COVID-19 cases
has surged in recent weeks.
We’ll hear from Brother Anthony Carvalho,
who serves on the Brazil Branch Committee,
and from Brother Jaime Tamayo,
who serves on the Ecuador Branch Committee.
Their reports show the benefits of obedience
even if at first we don’t understand the reasons for the direction.
The outbreak of COVID-19
has already taken tens of thousands of lives in Brazil,
and so we’ve come to appreciate
how the early direction
we received from the organization
was a real protection.
One example is a sister who is a medical doctor.
She said that when the branch office
gave direction to suspend meetings at the Kingdom Hall,
she honestly did not agree.
There weren’t any confirmed cases of COVID-19 in the region,
and the local government had not ordered any restrictions.
So she felt the brothers might be exaggerating the threat a bit.
But then she reasoned on how Jehovah had sometimes given his people direction
that didn’t make sense from a human standpoint,
and so she decided to obey.
Well, shortly after congregation meetings were suspended,
the government put restrictions in place.
COVID-19 began to spread rapidly in the region,
and sadly many have died.
Our sister said that she now sees
that the direction from the organization was a real protection.
She related,
“Seeing how Jehovah is caring for us in a loving and tender way,
“even on an individual level,
has increased my confidence in him.”
Well, this is just one example of many here in Brazil,
where we have truly seen the benefits
of obediently following theocratic direction.
There is no question that the early direction
we received in Ecuador saved lives.
For instance, one publisher, Fabricio,
started to have some flulike symptoms,
but his doctor told him
that it was the common flu
and not COVID-19.
Still, Fabricio followed the instructions from the organization
to stay home if you have any symptoms of illness.
Later he said, “All in our family agreed
“that it was important to follow these instructions
since they were given to protect us.”
During the following weeks,
he and his family didn’t allow anyone into the house.
Even when relatives came to visit them,
they received them outside the house to maintain a safe distance.
Around the same time, meetings at the Kingdom Hall were suspended.
Well, several weeks later,
Fabricio tested positive for COVID-19
and so did three family members.
Fabricio’s family are so glad that they followed the instructions
received from the organization.
They maintained distancing protocols
even without a positive diagnosis of COVID-19.
This protected the lives of others,
including their extended family and the congregation.
This really helped us appreciate
the wisdom of suspending congregation meetings when we did.
Doing so prevented the spread of the disease to others.
What a powerful example of how our obedience to direction
is a protection and a blessing!
Our second principle is based on Romans 13:1, 2:
We must listen
to the governmental “superior authorities,”
who are permitted by Jehovah
to care for certain functions.
The importance of listening to these authorities
is emphasized in verse 2, where it says:
“Whoever opposes the authority
“(or, according to the footnote, whoever ‘resists’ the authority)
has taken a stand against the arrangement of God.”
We know that these authorities exist by God’s permission,
and it’s his will that Christians be subject to them,
as long as what they require doesn’t conflict with his law.
News reports are filled with stories
of people ignoring the direction from the authorities
or even protesting against it.
But rebelling against secular authorities
constitutes a rebellion against God.
We love Jehovah,
so we respect the authorities.
We also listen to the authorities because we love our neighbors,
and we’re concerned with how they feel about health and safety.
We know that many people
out of concern for possible infection
are anxious about interacting with others.
Following safety guidelines from the authorities
and adjusting our activities
shows that we really care about our neighbors.
And this can even contribute to a good witness being given.
Here’s an example of that:
In one European country,
local officials visited our branch office
to check on what we were doing to slow the spread of the virus.
When the officials learned that we were holding
all our meetings by videoconference
and had already been in lockdown for over two weeks,
they were amazed!
One of them asked,
“Did you know beforehand that all of this would happen?”
The brothers explained that we’re a global organization
that puts a high value on human life,
so we were following developments on an international level.
That enabled the brothers to take the steps needed
to keep everyone as safe as possible,
even ahead of guidelines from the national and local governments.
The officials were impressed.
Doesn’t that beautifully illustrate
how our obedience reflects favorably
on our organization and our God?
It brings to mind the thought at 1 Peter 2:12.
When people become ‘eyewitnesses of our fine conduct,’
it brings glory to Jehovah.
The third principle we want to share is this:
Do not develop a casual attitude.
As this situation stretches on month after month,
it can be hard to stay vigilant.
We might be inclined to relax,
lower our guard,
especially as certain restrictions are removed.
However, Proverbs 22:3 reminds us:
“The shrewd one sees the danger
“and conceals himself,
“but the inexperienced keep right on going
and suffer the consequences.”
So we need to remain cautious and be ready for additional outbreaks.
Many experts say we may be dealing
with the spread of this virus for some time
until the successful treatments and vaccinations
become widely available,
possibly in 2021 or beyond.
This means that the adjusted arrangements
we have in place for congregation meetings,
assemblies, and the field ministry
may need to continue for some time.
When we do begin returning to our normal arrangements,
it will be a gradual process,
in accord with what we read
in Proverbs 14:15:
“The naive person believes every word,
but the shrewd one ponders each step.”
You can be assured
that we will prayerfully ponder each step
and adjust our meeting and service arrangements gradually.
And, of course, we’ll monitor the situation closely
and reinstate certain restrictions if additional outbreaks occur.
So as you face the days ahead,
keep in mind the three principles we’ve talked about:
(1) Place a high value on life,
(2) listen to the authorities,
and (3) guard against developing a casual attitude.
We know that this pandemic has hit some of you very hard.
You’ve lost jobs and income.
You young ones have had your schooling interrupted,
and you haven’t been able to be with your friends.
And tragically, a number of you
have lost family members and friends in death.
Some of you may feel like Job,
who faced one tragedy after another.
It pains our hearts to see what you’re going through,
and we’re praying for you every day.
It’s been a difficult time.
Yet, in many ways,
all of this has been training for the great tribulation ahead.
What we’re learning now about how to adapt our spiritual routines,
to support one another, and to be obedient to direction
is building us up and equipping us
for even bigger challenges in the future.
It’s been very encouraging to hear how our brothers around the world
are helping one another during this unique time
in human history.
Your actions are bringing honor
and praise to Jehovah.
Our brothers and sisters from Brazil and Ecuador
send you their warm greetings.
And on behalf of the Governing Body,
we thank you for all you’re doing,
