ko.text: 먼저 이번 방송에서 다룰 내용을 간단히 살펴보시죠.
다른 사람들을 편견 없이 대하는 방법을 배운 형제 자매들을 만나 볼 텐데요,
그들이 그렇게 할 수 있었던 이유는 무엇이었을까요?
우리 모두 어떻게 분열된 세상에서 연합을 유지할 수 있는지 알아보겠습니다.
옳은 일을 하기 위해 용기를 내야 했던 적이 있으십니까?
사무엘의 예를 통해 무엇을 배울 수 있는지 살펴보겠습니다.
예수께서는 우리가 어린아이처럼 다른 사람의 좋은 점을 보고,
사랑과 친절을 나타낼 수 있는 방법을 알려 주셨습니다.
이번 달 뮤직 비디오는 바로 그러한 교훈을 담고 있습니다.
2020년 5월 JW 방송도 정말 기대가 되지 않습니까?
올해 우리가 즐기게 될 지역 대회의 주제는 ‘항상 기뻐하십시오!’입니다.
중앙장로회는 여러분을 위해 대회 소개 동영상을 마련했습니다.
하지만 우리 모두는 대처하기 어려운 문제들을 겪습니다.
삶이 힘들 때도 어떻게 기쁨을 찾을 수 있는지 알려 줄 것입니다.
지금부터 영원히 행복하게 살 수 있게 해 주셨는지 알게 되실 겁니다.
대회 소개 동영상을 보니 작년에 있었던 즐거운 대회가 떠오르지 않으셨나요?
작년 대회에는 충실한 요시야에 관한 드라마도 있었습니다.
촬영장 뒤편에서 무슨 일이 있었는지 그 비하인드 스토리를 함께 보시겠습니다.
「요시야: 여호와를 사랑하고 악을 미워하십시오」 드라마처럼 중요한 프로젝트는
모든 작업이 여호와의 뜻과 말씀에 일치하는 것이 매우 중요하기 때문입니다.
그래서 대본을 만드는 첫 단계부터 시간을 많이 들여 주의 깊이 조사합니다.
대본이 만들어지면 스토리보드 작업을 통해 시각화시킵니다.
대본과 스토리보드 작업 외에도 정확성이 꼭 필요한 작업이 있습니다.
의상의 장식과 스타일, 색상, 심지어 천의 재질까지
역사적으로 가능한 정확히 재현하기 위해 철저히 조사합니다.
또한 드라마의 시대 배경을 정확하게 그려내는 동시에 헌금도 절약해야 합니다.
마운트이보와 같은 베델 시설에서 촬영하는 것이었습니다.
제작 팀은 쉽게 소품 변경이 가능한 3개의 다용도 세트장을 지어
다양한 장소를 연출할 수 있게 했습니다.
예루살렘 도시의 야외 장면도 실내에서 촬영되었죠.
인근 회중의 형제 자매들이 엑스트라로 출연했습니다.
성경적으로나 역사적으로 정확하게 묘사하는 데 주안점을 두고
정확성을 위해 신경 써야 할 부분들이 정말 많았습니다.
많은 부분이 녹색 스크린 앞에서 촬영되었기 때문에,
시각 효과 팀이 컴퓨터 그래픽을 통해 정밀한 배경을 만들 수 있었습니다.
또한 컴퓨터 기술을 사용해 플레이트라고 불리는,
인물의 동작을 담은 여러 화면들을 하나로 합쳐 복잡한 장면들을 완성했습니다.
마지막 축제 장면에 나오는 만 4000명의 이스라엘 백성과 많은 양들은
먼저 3D 모델을 만든 다음 복사해서 많은 군중으로 보이게 했습니다.
뉴욕주 월킬의 워치타워 농장으로 이동해 야외 촬영을 했습니다.
8월에는 마운트이보 스튜디오로 돌아와서 마지막 장면을 촬영했습니다.
4천 기가가 넘는 용량의 영상을 만들고 작업을 마무리했습니다.
그 후 뉴욕주 패터슨으로 옮겨 편집 작업을 진행했습니다.
요시야왕의 기록이 더 큰 감동을 줄 수 있도록 추가로 어떤 작업이 더 있었습니까?
색감을 조정해서 전체 영상의 품질을 높이고 알맞은 분위기를 더했습니다.
돌아가시면 안 돼요. 저 혼자 어떡해요.
또한, 발자국 소리나 바스락거리는 풀소리와 같은 음향 효과를 추가해서
영상이 더 자연스럽고 생생하게 느껴지도록 만들었습니다.
마지막으로, 드라마가 우리 마음에 더 감동을 줄 수 있도록
전 세계의 여호와의 백성들에게 힘을 주었습니다.
그분의 약속에 대해 가르치는 데 도움이 됩니다.
“오늘 내가 당신에게 명령하는 이 말씀을 마음에 새겨야 합니다.
집에 앉아 있을 때나 길을 걸을 때나 누울 때나 일어날 때나
그것을 아들들에게 부지런히 가르치고 말해 주어야 합니다.”
‘당신과 당신의 뒤를 잇는 자손이 항상 잘되려면,
당신의 하느님 여호와의 눈에 선하고 옳은 일을 해야 합니다.’
여호와께서 전 세계에 있는 자신의 백성들이 강한 믿음을 유지할 수 있도록
풍부한 영적 양식을 베푸신다는 또 하나의 증거입니다.
네, 요시야 드라마는 성경 기록을 생생히 묘사해 주었습니다!
웹사이트에서 드라마를 다시 한번 보고 싶은 마음이 드셨을지도 모르겠네요.
우리 동영상에 나오는 특정 장면들에 관해 우려하는 편지를 보내 주셨습니다.
폭력적인 장면을 전혀 보지 못하게 아이들을 보호해 왔는데,
우리 영상의 그런 장면들이 혹시 영향을 주지는 않을까 염려하신 거죠.
하지만 성경에 나오는 기록을 영상으로 표현할 때,
여호와께서 그분의 말씀에 보존되게 하신 내용을 무시할 수는 없습니다.
성경 기록은 참숭배자들의 유익을 위해 여호와께서 보존하신 것이므로
그 기록을 임의로 바꾸거나 약화시켜서는 안 될 것입니다.
하지만 아시다시피, 우린 그러한 장면을 묘사할 때 최대한 신중을 기합니다.
성경적인 선례를 역대기하 20:13에서 찾아볼 수 있을 것 같습니다.
여호사밧은 큰 무리를 이룬 몇몇 민족들이
하느님의 백성을 공격하려는 상황에 대해 말하고 있었습니다.
그는 일어날 수 있는 재난을 꽤 구체적으로 묘사했는데,
사람들이 죽임을 당할 수 있다고 언급했습니다.
그처럼 충격적인 말을 누구도 듣고 있었습니까?
어린아이들과 아내들과 자녀들과 함께 여호와 앞에 서 있었다.”
여호와께서는 어린아이들을 비롯한 모두가 앞으로 일어날 일을 알기를 바라셨습니다.
가까운 미래에 우리가 어떤 일을 겪을 것인지 현실적으로 설명해 주어야 합니다.
많은 부모들은 성경에 근거한 동영상에 나오는 생생한 장면들을
고난의 때에 우리와 함께하실 여호와에 대한 신뢰를
사실, 많은 부모님들은 요한 계시록과 같이
자세한 묘사가 들어 있는 성경 기록을
자녀들에게 읽어 줄 때에도 그렇게 해 오셨습니다.
우리는 전쟁이나 폭력적인 내용을 묘사하는 성경 기록을
자녀들이 어떤 영향을 받을지 염려하는 부모님들의 심정을
동시에 하느님의 영감받은 말씀에 담긴 중요한 세부점들도 약화시키지 않을 것입니다.
“어린아이의 좋은 특성을 본받고 나쁜 특성을 멀리하십시오!”입니다.
고린도 전서 14:20을 펴서 오늘의 주제 성구를 읽어 보겠습니다.
“형제 여러분, 이해하는 데는 어린아이가 되지 마십시오.
악에는 어린아이가 되고 이해하는 데는 어른이 되십시오.”
어린아이와 같이 되면 안 되는 부면이 있는가 하면,
어린아이처럼 되어야 하는 부면이 있다고 알려 줍니다.
이해하는 데 있어서는 어린아이처럼 되면 안 되지만,
악에 대해서는 어린아이처럼 되어야 한다는 것이죠.
어린아이와 같이 되어서는 안 되는 세 가지 부면과
어린아이와 같이 되어야 하는 세 가지 부면을 각각 살펴볼 것입니다.
이 성구에는 우리가 멀리해야 하는 첫 번째 어린아이 같은 특성이 나옵니다.
“계속 젖을 먹는 사람은 누구나 의의 말씀에 익숙하지 않습니다.
그러나 단단한 음식은 장성한 사람들 곧 분별력을 사용하여 훈련함으로
옳고 그른 것을 구별할 줄 아는 이들의 것입니다.”
따라서 피해야 할 어린아이 같은 특성 한 가지는 미성숙한 영적 식습관입니다.
아이들은 영양가와는 전혀 상관없이, 자기가 좋아하는 걸 먹고 싶어 합니다.
달달한 것만 먹으라고 하면 아주 좋아할 겁니다.
자신이 어떤 영적 식습관을 갖고 있는지 자문해 볼 필요가 있습니다.
TV를 보거나 영적으로는 별 가치가 없는 내용을 읽는 데
너무 많은 시간을 보내고 있지는 않습니까?
아니면 여가 시간을 지혜롭게 사용해서 단단한 영적 양식을 섭취하고 있습니까?
새로운 「파수대」 잡지가 나오면 눈으로 대강 훑어보면서
무슨 내용이 있는지만 얼른 확인하고 다른 일을 합니까?
아니면 더 깊은 영적 진리를 이해하기 위해 시간을 들여 연구하고 조사합니까?
개인 연구할 때 잠시 멈추어 자문해 보십시오.
‘이 점은 여호와에 대해 무엇을 가르쳐 줄까?
이 내용을 누구에게 알려 줄 수 있을까?
여호와께선 내게 무슨 말씀을 하시는 걸까?
이 내용은 이미 내가 알고 있는 점과 어떤 연관이 있을까?
이 내용을 어떻게 적용할 수 있을까?’
야고보서 1:25은 하느님의 말씀을 자세히 살피라고 권합니다.
성경을 대충 읽기만 하는 것은 세계 최고의 박물관에 가서
급하게 돌아다니면서 전시품을 힐끗힐끗 쳐다보기만 하는 것과 같습니다.
반면에 하느님의 말씀을 묵상하면서 자세히 살펴보는 것은
그 박물관에 전시된 것들 앞에 일일이 멈춰 서서,
몸을 굽히고 여러 각도에서 그 미술품과 작품들을
꼼꼼히 살펴보는 것과 비슷하다고 할 수 있습니다.
그렇게 할 때 전시품에 대해 더 잘 알게 되고 그 가치를 더 잘 인식하게 될 것입니다.
네, 우리의 영적 식욕과 식습관을 검토해 보면
성숙하지 못한 영적 식습관을 버렸는지 알 수 있습니다.
우리가 피해야 할 어린아이의 두 번째 특성에 대해 생각해 보시죠.
“그러면 우리가 더 이상 어린아이가 되지 않고,
사람의 책략과 교활한 속임수에 넘어가 온갖 가르침의 바람으로 인해
파도에 떠밀리듯 흔들리고 이리저리 밀려다니지 않게 될 것입니다.”
어린아이는 쉽게 속아 넘어가는 경향이 있습니다.
이 성구는 무엇이 옳고 그른지에 대해 쉽게 속는 것을
바람으로 인해 바다에서 파도에 이리저리 떠밀려 다니는 것에 비유합니다.
요동치는 바다 위에 떠다니는 나뭇조각이나 폭풍에 흩날리는 종잇조각은
파도가 치거나 바람이 부는 대로 아무렇게나 밀려다닙니다.
네, 사실, 어린아이들은 쉽게 속임수에 넘어갈 때가 자주 있습니다.
반짝거리는 동전과 액수가 큰 지폐를 놓고 둘 중 하나를 고르라고 하면,
살면서 우리는 어떤 선택을 하고 있습니까?
우리가 선택하는 음악이나 오락, 옷차림, 몸단장은 어쩌면 우리가 사탄과 그의 세상에
어느 정도 속고 있다는 점을 드러내지는 않습니까?
사탄은 우릴 속이려고 혈안이 돼 있죠.
여호와께서는 고린도 전서 14:20을 통해 이렇게 말씀하셨습니다.
이 성구는 우리가 어린아이와 같이 되지 말아야 할, 세 번째 특성을 알려 줍니다.
마치 장터에 앉아 친구들에게 이렇게 외치는 아이들과 같습니다.
‘우리가 너희를 위해 피리를 불어도 너희는 춤추지 않았고,
우리가 통곡을 해도 너희는 가슴을 치며 슬퍼하지 않았다.’”
예수께서는 아이처럼 행동하는 어른들에 대해 말씀하고 계셨습니다.
해야 할 일을 하기보다 노는 걸 더 좋아하는데,
이것이 우리가 피해야 할 어린아이 같은 특성이죠.
생각해 보면 아주 어린아이들은 깨어 있는 대부분의 시간을 놀면서 보냅니다.
그런데 나중에 아이들이 학교에 다니게 되면, 학교 갈 시간을 어디서 내야 할까요?
우리는 영적인 관점에서 이렇게 자문해 봐야 합니다.
‘나는 여가 시간이나 하고 싶은 일을 줄여

이곳엔 다양한 문화가 공존하지만 여전히 편견을 갖고 있는 사람들이 많아요.
다른 나라에서 온 사람들이 소외당하는 모습을 자주 봤고,
조심하지 않으면 그런 태도는 회중에까지 영향을 미칠 수 있어요.
문화적 배경이 같은 사람끼리만 어울리게 될 수 있죠.
제가 자란 곳에서는 젊은 사람들이 나이 든 사람들을 공경합니다.
하지만 나이 든 사람들은 젊은 사람들을 별로 존중하지 않아요.
회중에서 젊은 사람들을 장로로 추천할 때 큰 영향을 미칩니다.
어떤 형제가 회중에서 장로가 되기에는 너무 어리다고 생각하기가 쉬워요.
이곳에서는 사람들이 부유해 보이는 사람들과 친하게 지내고 싶어 합니다.
세련된 옷을 입지 않거나 좋은 자동차를 타지 않거나
뭘 하고 있는 건가 하고 한심하게 보기도 하죠.
그리스도인 회중에서 그런 태도를 나타내면 솔로몬이 한 말처럼 될 수 있습니다.
부유해 보이는 형제들과는 친하게 지내려고 적극적으로 행동하고
가난한 형제들과는 거리를 두게 될 수 있죠.
그런 편견은 곧바로 극복할 수 있는 게 아니었어요.
인종으로 사람을 판단할 수 있겠다는 생각이 들었어요.
그렇게 되면 회중에서 형제 자매들을 보는 관점에도 영향을 미치겠죠.
그 기사에서는 우리가 변화하는 데 성경이 도움이 된다고 했어요.
이 면에서 계속 발전하기 위해 늘 스스로를 검토해 보는 게 필요합니다.
기사에서는 우리 마음을 활짝 열라고 알려 줘요.
나와 배경이 같은 편한 사람들과만 어울리는 것이 아니라
다른 배경을 가진 형제 자매들과 같이 봉사하고,
집에 초대해서 함께 교제할 수 있죠.
사도 바울은 그에게 중요한 회중 책임을 맡겼습니다.
구체적인 연령이 성경에 나오지 않는다’고 알려 줍니다.
젊은 형제를 장로로 일하도록 추천하니까 회중에 정말 많은 유익이 있습니다.
이 기사에는 다른 사람들을 어떻게 봐야 하는지 간단한 원칙이 나와요.
우리가 가진 것에 따라 결정되지 않는다는 거죠.
저는 새로운 형제 자매를 만나면 순간적으로 그 사람을
부유한지 가난한지에 따라 판단하려는 마음이 들 때가 종종 있습니다.
하지만 그럴 때 이 원칙을 떠올립니다.
믿음을 가지고 있단 사실에 초점을 맞추게 됩니다.
그게 바로 우리를 진정한 친구가 되게 해 주는 비결이죠.
제겐 다양한 문화와 인종의 친구들이 있어요.
전 친구들을 피부색으로 보는 게 아니라 저의 형제 자매로 봅니다.
문화와 배경이 다양한 친구들과 멋진 우정을 나누고 있어요.
그 우정을 늘 소중히 여길 거예요.
회중은 우리 모두를 위한 멋진 곳입니다.
누가 부자고 누가 가난한지는 중요하지 않죠.
우리 모두는 여호와를 사랑하기 때문에 친구가 됐으니까요.
이번 달 프로그램에서 우린 어린아이와 같이 되라고 격려받았죠.
우리는 여호와의 종인 사무엘의 훌륭한 본을 통해 배울 수 있었습니다.
여호와와 형제들에 대한 사랑은 우리를 연합시켜 주었습니다.
편견 없는 태도로 사랑과 친절을 나타내야 한다는 걸 배웠습니다.
또 인종과 나이와 경제 수준에 상관없이,
서로를 차별하지 않고 대하는 법을 배운
우리 형제 자매들의 말도 들어 볼 수 있었습니다.
이제 형제들이 보내온 영상 편지를 보겠습니다.
체코에는 크고 울창한 숲, 농장, 포도원뿐 아니라
중세 시대의 모습을 간직한 성과 마을과 도시들이 있습니다.
1000년이 넘는 역사를 가진 수도 프라하는 종교적으로도 유서가 깊은 곳이죠.
하느님의 이름을 여러 교회와 건축물에서 찾아볼 수 있습니다.
회중 형제 자매들은 인근에 있는 프라하의 역사적 중심지
이 집단은 프라하 전체가 봉사 구역입니다.
여호와의 증인의 활동이 금지됐던 공산주의 정권 하에서
비밀리에 성경 출판물을 생산하는 일을 도왔습니다.
즈비네크 형제는 군 입대를 거부하고 중립을 지킨다는 이유로
공산주의 정권이 바뀐 뒤에 그는 순회 감독자로 봉사했습니다.
프라하 데유비체 회중의 우리 형제 자매들이
전 세계에 있는 여러분 모두에게 따뜻한 사랑의 안부를 전합니다.
앞서 올해에 있을 ‘항상 기뻐하십시오!’ 지역 대회의 소개 동영상을 보여 드렸는데요,
대회에 나올 드라마 예고편도 보고 싶지 않으신가요?
용감한 느헤미야의 이야기를 담고 있는 드라마입니다.
페르시아 왕의 큰 신임을 받는 한 유대인이 살고 있었습니다.
예루살렘에서 계속 순결한 숭배를 드리는 줄로만 알았습니다.
무너진 성벽도 불에 탄 성문들도 아직까지 전부 그대로야.
백성이고 제사장이고 하느님의 법은 안중에도 없어.
그들이 앞으로 닥칠 일에 맞서려면 도움이 필요했습니다.
다 자기 좋자고 사는 건데, 나만 행복하면 됐지.
다친 사람이 없으면, 계속 이렇게 두 손 놓고 있을 거예요?
우리가 뭘 어떻게 할 수 있겠습니까.
오 하느님, 저를 선하게 기억해 주십시오.
이번에도 대회를 마치면서 일요일 회기 끝에 새로운 오리지널송을 부르게 될 것입니다.
새로운 노래와 가사가 jw.org에 올라가 있습니다.
회중 형제 자매들 모두가 새 노래를 연습하시도록 권해 드립니다.
회중에 이 노래를 다운로드하는 데 어려움을 겪는 분이 계시다면,
그러면 우리 모두 이 노래로 여호와께 마음을 다한 찬양을 드리게 될 것입니다.
무척 사랑한다는 것을 꼭 기억해 주시기 바랍니다.
지금까지 여호와의 증인의 세계 본부에서 JW 방송이었습니다!

en.text: Welcome! Welcome!
Welcome to this month’s broadcast!
Here is a little sample
of what will be contained in our program.
We’ll meet brothers and sisters
who’ve learned to see and treat others impartially.
What helped them?
And how can all of us be united in a divided world?
We’ll find out.
Have you ever needed to muster up courage to do what’s right?
Are you enduring disappointment?
We’ll see what we can learn
from the example of Samuel.
And Jesus showed us how to see the good in people,
to be loving and kind
just like a child.
That’s the message
of our new music video.
Yes, there’s much to look forward to
in this May 2020 edition
of JW Broadcasting®.
“Always Rejoice!” is the appealing theme
of this year’s conventions.
The Governing Body would like to give you a preview of the program.
Let’s take a look.
Everyone wants to be happy.
But we all face problems,
problems that are hard to deal with.
So can you ever really be happy?
At the 2020 convention of Jehovah’s Witnesses,
you will learn how to find joy,
even when life is hard,
and how God has made it possible
for us to be happy now and forever!
Happiness might seem hard to find, but it isn’t!
Come and see for yourself!
That preview reminds us
of the wonderful convention program of last year,
including the feature Bible drama
about faithful Josiah.
What was involved in producing that drama?
Please watch the following video
that reveals what transpired
behind the scenes.
Where do you begin an important project
like The Story of Josiah: Love Jehovah; Hate What Is Bad?
You begin with prayerful consideration.
It’s a serious responsibility —part of being loyal to Jehovah and his Word.
Therefore, many hours of careful research goes into the first step:
writing a script.
The script is then visualized through a step called storyboarding.
But it’s not just the script and storyboarding
that requires attention to accuracy.
Costumes must be thoroughly researched so that their components,
styles, colors, and even the types of fabric
appear as historically accurate as possible.
The production must also accurately depict the times
being represented while making the best use of donated funds.
How can this be done?
For The Story of Josiah,
the solution was to film at Bethel locations,
such as the studio spaces at Mount Ebo.
Set construction began early in 2018.
The production team designed and built three flexible sets
so that with easy prop adjustments,
they could be in multiple locations.
Even the exterior Jerusalem city scenes
were filmed indoors.
Many brothers and sisters from local congregations
served as extras for the crowd scenes.
With an eye to Biblical and historical accuracy,
the makeup team transformed the actors
into characters from King Josiah’s time.
There were so many details to get right.
For a large portion of the drama, filming in front of a green screen
enabled the visual effects team to construct accurate environments digitally.
Many layers of character action, called plates, were assembled
with digital environments to produce complex visuals.
For the closing festival scene,
which required 14,000 Israelites
and many sheep,
3D models were made and duplicated to simulate the large crowd.
In July 2018, the production packed up
and moved to an outdoor location
at Watchtower Farms in Wallkill, New York.
And action!
In August, the last scene was filmed
back at the Mount Ebo studio.
After 45 days of filming
and with over 4 terabytes of footage captured,
the team had finished production.
The project moved to the editing facilities at Patterson, New York.
But what more could be done so that the account portrayed
could touch our hearts?
A colorist applied a look to the overall film
to enhance the picture’s quality and mood.
You have to get better.
I’m afraid of being alone.
Additional sound effects, such as footsteps
and the sound of dry grass being rustled,
were recorded to make the on-screen action more natural and compelling.
Finally, the musical soundtrack was composed,
recorded, and added to the movie to enhance the appeal to our hearts.
The work on The Story of Josiah: Love Jehovah; Hate What Is Bad
was done to strengthen Jehovah’s people worldwide.
You’re not alone.
Jehovah is with you.
This powerful story also assists parents as they teach their children
the power of God’s Word and promise.
“These words that I am commanding you today
“must be on your heart,
“and you must inculcate them in your sons
“and speak of them when you sit in your house
“and when you walk on the road
and when you lie down and when you get up.”
“So that it may always go well with you
“and your sons after you,
“because you are doing what is good
and right in the eyes of Jehovah your God.”
The Story of Josiah has proven to be yet another example
of how Jehovah continues to provide abundant spiritual food and support
for his people worldwide.
That video certainly brought the Bible account
to life for us!
You may want to go back and review
the full-feature Bible drama again from our website.
We might mention
that we’ve had just a few parents
write in expressing concern
that some of our videos depict scenes
that could have an effect on children
who’ve been protected from anything
even hinting at an act of violence.
We very much appreciate the concern.
However, when portraying a Bible account,
we cannot ignore the message Jehovah saw fit
to preserve in his Word.
We don’t feel comfortable watering down
the inspired insight that Jehovah
has preserved for the benefit of true worshippers.
However, as you’ve observed,
we do so as tastefully as possible.
We don’t show actual violent acts or bloodshed.
A Scriptural precedent might be found
in 2 Chronicles 20:13.
Jehoshaphat was describing
a great crowd of enemy nations
that were about to launch an attack against God’s people.
He described the possible disaster quite graphically,
referring to the possibility of death by the sword,
by pestilence, or by famine.
Who was he sharing this disturbing information with?
Second Chronicles 20:13 tells us:
“Meanwhile, all those of Judah
“were standing before Jehovah,
“along with their little ones,
their wives, and their children.”
Jehovah wanted all, including the young ones,
to understand what was coming.
Parents likewise need to give their children
a realistic idea
of what we all will face in the near future.
Many parents choose to help their children appreciate
the graphic visual imagery of a Bible-based video,
while at the same time building trust in Jehovah,
who will be with them in times of distress.
This is similar to what they’d do
when reading a graphic Biblical account
to their children from the Scriptures,
such as from the book of Revelation.
Be assured
that we’ll continue to be sensitive
to the feelings of you parents when we produce a video
that’s based on a Bible account
that includes descriptions of warfare
or other incidents of violent actions.
We’ll do so with care,
while not ignoring the powerful details
depicted in the inspired Word of God.
The theme for this program is
“Be Childlike—But Not Childish!”
First Corinthians 14:20
is our theme scripture:
“Brothers, do not become young children in your understanding,
“but be young children as to badness;
and become full-grown in your understanding.”
In this single verse,
we’re told not to be like a young child in one way
and we’re told to be like a young child in another way.
We should not be like a child when it comes to understanding,
and we should be like a child when it comes to badness.
During this discussion,
let’s focus on three ways
we should not be like a child
and then let’s talk about three ways we should be like a child.
Please turn to Hebrews 5:13, 14,
and let’s identify negative trait number one
that we do not want to imitate:
“For everyone who continues to feed on milk
“is unacquainted with the word of righteousness,
“for he is a young child.
“But solid food belongs to mature people,
“to those who through use have their powers of discernment trained
to distinguish both right and wrong.”
So the negative trait that children have
is immature feeding habits.
Think about it: Young children
have a tendency to eat what they like
regardless of its nutritional value.
Most young ones would be perfectly happy
eating ice cream, candy, cookies,
and other sweets for all of their meals.
But now we ask,
What do our spiritual appetites
and feeding habits reveal about us?
Consider: How do we spend our free time?
Do we squander voluminous hours watching television
or reading material that provides little or no spiritual nutrition?
Or do we make wise use of our free time
to take in solid spiritual food?
When we receive a new issue of The Watchtower,
do we merely scan through it, looking at a few highlights,
and then do something else?
Do we take time to research deeper spiritual truths
so as to fully understand them?
Do we take time to really meditate?
Meditation is not daydreaming.
Meditation is bridled, focused thought.
Pause your reading to ask questions such as:
‘What does this teach me about Jehovah?
‘With whom could I share this information?
‘What’s Jehovah telling me?
‘How does this fit in with other things I know about this subject?
How can I make application?’
James 1:25 encourages us
to peer into God’s Word.
According to the Reference Bible,
‘peer’ literally means to ‘stoop beside.’
To illustrate: Simply reading through the Bible
could be likened to walking quickly through the world’s greatest museum
and periodically glancing at the various displays.
You will learn something.
But meditatively peering into God’s Word
can be likened to stopping all along the museum route
and even stooping down
and closely examining from different angles
the artifacts, exhibitions, and displays.
Now our knowledge and appreciation
are going to be enhanced much more.
Yes, our spiritual appetite and feeding habits
reveal much about whether we have done away
with the trait of a young child, namely,
immature feeding habits.
Now please turn to Ephesians 4:14.
Let’s discern from this scripture negative trait number two
that we don’t want to imitate:
“So we should no longer be children,
“tossed about as by waves and carried here and there
“by every wind of teaching by means of the trickery of men,
by means of cunning in deceptive schemes.”
So, what’s the negative trait?
Young children are easily tricked, or fooled.
This scripture likens being easily tricked about what’s right or wrong
to being tossed about by the waves of the ocean
and blown around by the wind.
If you think of a piece of wood floating in a turbulent ocean
or a piece of paper in a windstorm,
there’s no stability or direction.
Both can be easily maneuvered
to go anywhere—take any position.
Well, that’s true of very young children
who often can be easily deceived.
For example, if given a choice
between a shiny coin of little value
and paper money of great value,
the shiny coin will likely be chosen.
But now, here’s the point:
What do our spiritual choices reveal about us?
Do our choices in regard to music and other entertainment,
clothing, and grooming indicate that we’re being fooled
even slightly by Satan and his world?
Yes, Satan is bent on tricking us,
but Jehovah tells us
at 1 Corinthians 14:20 (the scripture we read earlier):
“Do not become young children in your understanding.”
But now, please turn to Matthew 11:16, 17.
Here we’ll find the third negative trait of a child
that we do not want to imitate:
“With whom will I compare this generation?
“It is like young children sitting in the marketplaces
“who call out to their playmates, saying:
“‘We played the flute for you, but you did not dance;
we wailed, but you did not beat yourselves in grief.’”
Jesus was saying that adult people
were acting like children.
Children love to play.
So the negative trait of young children
is that they prefer play over responsibility.
Think about it: The vast majority
of the waking hours of a small child
are spent playing
—play, play, and more play.
Most of their life is fun and games.
But later, when the child goes to school,
where does he get the time to do so?
He has to take it from his playtime.
But now, spiritually speaking, we can ask ourselves,
‘How far have we progressed
in buying out time from our playtime?’
Ephesians 5:16 encourages us
to ‘make the best use of our time.’
Literally, according to the footnote,
this scripture is telling us
to ‘buy out the appointed time’
—that is, buy it from less important things.
So the question for all of us is,
Have we bought out the majority of our playtime
for more important spiritual responsibilities?
Now, we’ve discussed three negative traits
of a young child that we want to avoid.
If we had time, we could have discussed
other negative traits to be avoided,
such as how children tend to have a short attention span
(they’re easily distracted),
their curiosity often gets them into trouble,
and they generally need a lot of time and attention
(they’re high-maintenance).
But now let’s briefly discuss three positive traits
of a young child that we do well to imitate.
Positive characteristic number one
is at 1 Corinthians 14:20, which we read at the outset.
That scripture tells us
to “be young children as to badness.”
So, what’s the characteristic that we want to imitate?
Young children are innocent,
inexperienced, when it comes to badness.
Or put another way,
they haven’t done many truly bad things.
Like children, we don’t want
to gain knowledge or experience in what is bad.
For example, when it comes to pornography,
we want no experience whatsoever
in regard to this filthy thing of Satan’s world.
When it comes to television programs
that are designated for a “mature audience,”
remember to tell yourself,
‘I’m not old enough; I’m a young child.’
For positive characteristic number two,
let’s consider Matthew 18:2-4:
“So calling a young child to him,
“he [Jesus] stood him in their midst and said:
“‘Truly I say to you, unless you turn around
“‘and become as young children,
“‘you will by no means enter into the Kingdom of the heavens.
“‘Therefore, whoever will humble himself like this young child
is the one who is the greatest in the Kingdom of the heavens.’”
What’s the desirable trait?
Young children are humble and teachable.
Young children ask many questions because they want to learn,
but grown-ups are often hesitant to ask questions.
Why?
They don’t want to look uninformed.
But acting like we know something
when we don’t is actually dishonest
and probably motivated by pride.
The point is,
Don’t be afraid to reveal what you don’t know.
Remain humble and teachable like a child.
Now let’s identify desirable trait number three
by going to Matthew 21:15, 16:
“When the chief priests and the scribes
“saw the marvelous things he did
“and the boys who were shouting in the temple,
“‘Save, we pray, the Son of David!’
“they became indignant and said to him:
“‘Do you hear what these are saying?’
“Jesus said to them
“‘Yes. Did you never read this,
“‘“Out of the mouth of children and infants
you have brought forth praise”?’”
So, what desirable characteristic can we identify?
Young children are exuberant and enthusiastic.
Well, in like manner,
we want to remain exuberant and expressive
about Jehovah, Jesus,
the Kingdom, and other spiritual things.
Psalm 145:7 encourages us to “bubble over”
and “shout joyfully” because of these wonderful things.
And we never want to lose that childlike enthusiasm.
Well, there we have three desirable traits of a young child
that we want to do our utmost to imitate.
If we had time, we could discuss
several other positive characteristics,
such as how children tend to be trusting,
not prejudiced, and not hypocritical.
But now in review, may each of us
prayerfully strive not to be childish
when it comes to (1) immature feeding habits,
(2) being easily tricked, or fooled,
and (3) preferring play over responsibility.
On the other hand,
may each of us prayerfully strive to be childlike
when it comes to being
(1) innocent and inexperienced concerning badness,
(2) humble and teachable,
and (3) exuberant and enthusiastic
about spiritual things!
The Bible contains many accounts
of faithful men and women.
We can learn from their examples.
In the following dramatization,
notice what a family learns from Samuel.
Samuel was only my age
when Jehovah spoke to him.
He respected Eli, but he had to stand up for what was right.
I never thought that I’d have to do something similar.
I loved my brother, and I always wanted to be like him.
But those pictures of him partying with kids
from school showed he was living a double life.
I didn’t want to get him in trouble.
But I knew I had to say something.
I told him he had to tell Mom and Dad.
He warned me not to tell.
But Samuel was courageous
and “did not hide anything,”
and “Jehovah himself was with him.”
I couldn’t hide this.
Talking to my parents wasn’t easy,
but I knew it was the right thing to do.
Of course, we were proud of Danny.
But . . .
. . . at the time, we were a little distracted.
Maybe, somehow it was all just a misunderstanding.
We needed to know what was going on.
We just wanted to help him.
We couldn’t help but blame ourselves for what was happening.
Then we thought back to Samuel’s example.
Samuel, you need to listen to us.
You’re getting old, Samuel, and your sons are not like you.
They cheat, and they take bribes.
They bend Jehovah’s rules
any way they please.
Even faithful Samuel had sons who deviated from Jehovah’s standards.
We wanted to help our son.
Just as Samuel didn’t alter his course
and Jehovah stood by him,
we knew that if we did things His way,
He’d stand by us.
Did you see the loyalty the younger son showed
by bringing the matter to the attention of his parents?
Did you also notice the loyalty the parents showed
by going to the elders for assistance?
After the parents were able to talk to the elders,
we hope that the older son
was able to get the help he needed
and that the discipline brought him to his senses.
Has your child left Jehovah?
Do you blame yourself?
If so, remember
that Jehovah stood by faithful Samuel,
and He will stand by you.
He’ll help you endure.
Another challenge we face today
is remaining united
in a deeply divided world.
During the 1950’s and 1960’s,
racial tensions in the United States
greatly intensified.
How were Jehovah’s people affected during that period?
And how did they maintain unity?
Let’s look for the answers to those questions
in the following report.
My mother always said,
“Jehovah did not intend for all of us to look alike.”
In those early days,
we would work every house in the county
—black families, white families, any color.
At school, there was pressure there
to be involved with the racial activity.
We would hear about the problems and the issues.
It would be in the news, and you would know
what was going on in the South.
Some may wonder,
‘How is it that our people,
‘that is, Jehovah’s Witnesses, black and white,
‘could maintain such unity
when the world around them was falling apart?’
I grew up in central New York
—Utica, New York.
And I remember in the Kingdom Ministry  back in 1956,
there were articles about serving where the need is great.
They needed some of the black friends to serve in the South.
I married my husband, Earl McGee,
on June 2, 1956.
When we were married, Brother T. J. Sullivan gave a talk
at the Hallandale convention on serving where the need is greater.
He encouraged not only families but,
he said, newly married couples.
And so we planned for it, and he wrote the branch.
We were assigned to Florida,
and then in 1962, we started in the circuit work.
And our first circuit was in Alabama,
and it was not integrated.
We served together, Edna and I did,
in the pioneer work by assignment.
The last assignment was the Society assigning us
to North Carolina and then from there to the circuit work.
After the first circuit, which was in the Carolinas and Georgia,
we were assigned to Gilead.
I got married on April 23, 1949.
I’ve been in full-time service
70 years with my wife.
I was assigned
to Circuit 18 in Alabama.
My first circuit assignment was in Mississippi.
It had the reputation
as the worst state in the Union for race relations.
And then after we got there, there were three civil rights workers
who were killed in Philadelphia, Mississippi.
That was our circuit.
So those were the things we had to deal with.
We were busy in our ministry,
so it didn’t bother us very much.
The black worked the black, and the white worked the white.
So we just obeyed the customary law of staying segregated.
Lots of movements were happening, and people were, you know, very hostile.
When there was a march or any tension
where we were serving there in Alabama,
we wouldn’t go to the town on Saturday afternoon
to do street witnessing because if there was a rally
or something going on, we would just stay in the neighborhood.
A lot were what they used to call back then Freedom Riders,
people getting on buses going south,
and people coming in to register voters.
The fact is, some of the civil rights organizations
were set up in Mississippi and going pretty strong.
So as a result, they would think
that because we were active in going door to door,
we could just incorporate civil rights issues
and things like that into our work.
One of our classmates in the 27th class
was a black brother, a fellow student,
and we became very close friends there.
After we left Gilead, we were going to our assignments
and we stopped at a convention in Alabama.
And the convention was segregated
—one race on one side and one race on another.
And it was very difficult —painful—
for us not to be able to closely associate with our dear friend.
So we had this talk show on the television.
The circuit overseer and I went and also a Catholic priest
and an Episcopal minister.
So the Episcopal minister, a young minister,
asked what were we doing about the marching.
So I told him that we weren’t doing anything about the marching.
Well, that showed a contrast.
I’m black, and he’s white.
They weren’t stopping their marching to help us preach
the good news of the Kingdom, so we weren’t going to stop
preaching the good news of the Kingdom to help them march.
The brothers always were interested in each other.
So if there was a black congregation and a white congregation,
we had interest and fellow feeling for both.
The rule was we were not to meet together, and we couldn’t meet together.
But we could talk to one another, and we could visit one another.
So I think there was great support on both sides,
black and white brothers, back in those days.
If we had a problem getting a facility, for example,
they’d have contacts and they could get certain things done.
So, basically, we worked together.
The congregation started integrating
after certain civil rights laws were passed.
We had a big meeting of all the elders,
and we worked out the territory assignments
and whatever else was necessary
to have integrated congregations.
Some friends would feel,
and maybe rightly so at the time,
that there would be some violence if we integrated.
There probably were some Kingdom Halls damaged
and things like that as a result.
But the fact is,
there was integration going on in other places
—in the schools and things like that and in the universities and colleges.
And so it was obvious that if they could do it, then we even more so.
The process of integration
was successful
because it was under Jehovah’s direction.
Both black and white,
we had the same thing in common:
We loved Jehovah.
And despite us,
Jehovah got it done for us and brought us together.
And we have been unified ever since.
Everyone could see that we were united.
One brother was working from door to door,
black and white, and a lady came to the door (white),
and she said she was happy
to see this unity take place.
She had looked forward to it for a long time.
We have formed, with Jehovah’s help
by means of his holy spirit,
a worldwide brotherhood.
Granted, they have their imperfections,
but it is a brotherhood
and something to be truly marveled at.
The brothers began to feel
what we knew was true:
We’re all one organization.
They began to feel it.
They began to experience it.
We loved Jehovah, and we loved our brothers,
so there you have it.
How could you fail to have unity
when Jehovah had drawn you together?
Satan is the prime one to divide people.
Jesus died for the whole world of mankind,
so who would that exclude?
No one.
Did you notice what helped our brothers maintain unity
during that difficult time?
First: Despite prevailing customs,
our brothers —black and white—
supported each other, helped each other,
and worked together to advance Kingdom interests.
Second: They remained focused on the ministry
and did not get involved with social movements.
They wanted all to know that God’s Kingdom
is the only solution to mankind’s problems,
including the plague of prejudice
and racial inequality.
Third: They demonstrated love for Jehovah
and love for the brothers.
As Brother Benford said,
“How could you fail to have unity
when Jehovah had drawn you together?”
Impartiality, humility,
kindness—these are godly qualities
and childlike qualities
that our new music video illustrates.
Jesus kindly showed us That we must be as young ones,
Remembering that in a world of pride, We need a heart just like a child.
We value others, seeing what God sees through his impartial eyes.
Just like a child, we want to love one another,
With our eyes just seeing the good in each other.
Just like a child, we want to be full of kindness,
With our eyes not focused on what could divide us.
And as we’re getting older In a world that’s getting colder,
We easily could question others’ ways, Their motives, and the things they say.
And seeing others as above us is rare this day and age.
Just like a child, we want to love one another,
With our eyes just seeing the good in each other.
Just like a child, we want to be full of kindness,
With our eyes not focused on what could divide us.
Be just like a child.
While we keep growing, Serving Jehovah,
And finding joy in The part we’re playing,
We must remember That in a world of pride,
We need a heart like that of a child.
Just like a child, we want to love one another,
With our eyes just seeing the good in each other.
Just like a child, we want to be full of kindness,
With our eyes not focused on what could divide us.
Be just like a child.
What a beautiful song!
We need a childlike heart more than ever.
In many parts of the world,
it’s customary to judge people
on the basis of their race or age
or by how much money they have.
In our next segment,
we’ll hear from brothers and sisters
who have successfully resisted such influences.
I grew up in a country where people judge you according to the color of your skin.
There was black, white, mixed race,
but we all kept separate.
I needed to learn, not to see color, but to see people.
Even though it’s such a multicultural area,
there is still this prejudice that exists.
I’ve witnessed times where ones from another country
are often left isolated or are treated in a way that they’re not welcome here.
If we’re not careful, these attitudes could creep into the congregation.
We could have isolated groups
of cultures that maybe would stick together.
In the area where I grew up,
young ones show great respect for older ones.
Older ones, however, do not give much importance to young people.
This attitude, or culture,
has a major impact on recommendations of young ones as elders in the congregation.
We might say, ‘In my opinion, he is too young
to be appointed as an elder in the congregation.’
In this area, people sort of open up to you when you appear rich.
In some areas, they would even wonder
what you are doing there if you don’t have the right kind of looks
in terms of what you can afford to wear,
what kind of car you can afford to drive, what your profession is.
If we brought that with us into the Christian congregation,
then what Solomon mentions
could be the case —that we actively seek the friendship
of those whom we regard to be rich and abandon those who are poor.
I like the example in Galatians of Peter.
He grew up in an area where there was a lot of prejudice.
It wasn’t something that he overcame straightaway.
If I’m not careful, I think it would be easy for me
to slide back and see people as a different race,
and that would affect the way I view my brothers and sisters in the congregation.
The article mentions that when we use the Bible,
it helps us to make changes.
We need to constantly look at ourselves
so that we can continue to make progress.
In the article, it mentioned about ‘opening our hearts wide’
—whether it’d be working with them in the ministry
or having them over socially,
not just from the same group that we might be comfortable with,
but actually with different ones from different backgrounds.
Timothy was still a young man, but the apostle Paul
had given him heavy responsibility in the congregation.
The article mentions that ‘the Scriptures do not give an exact age
for recommendation of brothers as ministerial servants or elders.’
Recommending a younger brother as an elder in the congregation
has been a great blessing to us.
In the article, there was a little phrase
that has become a guiding principle for me.
Jehovah does not judge our relationship with him
by what we possess.
So when I meet new brothers and sisters
and for a moment I’m tempted
to judge, or view, them
according to those sentiments as to whether they are rich or poor,
that principle comes into my mind.
My focus, therefore, shifts to who they really are
in terms of their devotion to Jehovah —their faith.
That is what we build friendships on.
I have friends from different cultures, different races.
And I don’t see them as color,
but I see my brother or my sister.
I’ve got the most amazing friendships
with ones from different backgrounds and cultures
—something I will always, always cherish.
So our congregation is a wonderful place for everybody.
There is no emphasis on who is rich and who is poor.
Friendships are built on the basis of our love for Jehovah.
This month’s program
encouraged us to be childlike.
We learned from the encouraging example
of servants of Jehovah in the past.
We saw that love for Jehovah
and our brothers unites us,
even during times of social unrest.
We were reminded that, like a child,
we want to be impartial,
loving, and kind.
And we heard expressions from brothers
who have learned to treat others fairly
no matter their race, age,
wealth, or anything else
that could divide them.
Now it’s time for our video postcard,
which comes to us from the Czech Republic, also called Czechia.
Czechia is a land
of deep forests, farmland, vineyards,
as well as medieval castles, towns, and cities.
Prague, the capital, was established more than a thousand years ago.
It has a rich religious history.
God’s name can be found on many churches
and structures.
Czechia is home to more than 15,000 Jehovah’s Witnesses.
There are 32 congregations in Prague.
This is the Prague-Dejvice Congregation,
which has 84 publishers,
including 13 regular pioneers.
Their territory is large and diverse.
They preach in the historic center of Prague
in neighborhoods, parks, and on university campuses.
The congregation includes a Spanish-speaking group,
with 12 publishers,
of which 8 are regular pioneers.
This group serves the entire city.
Zbynek and Jarmila Bucifal
helped to secretly produce Bible literature
during the Communist regime,
when the work of Jehovah’s Witnesses was banned.
Zbynek was forced
to work in a coal mine for remaining neutral
and refusing to serve in the military.
After the regime change,
he served as a circuit overseer.
Our brothers and sisters in the Prague-Dejvice Congregation
send their warm, loving greetings
to all of you.
Earlier, we showed you a preview
of this year’s “Always Rejoice!” conventions.
But would you like a glimpse of this year’s feature Bible drama,
which brings to life the story of courageous Nehemiah?
Please enjoy!
Far from Israel lived a Jew
whom the king of Persia
trusted with his life.
He believed his people were carrying
on pure worship in Jerusalem
—until one day . . .
The walls of Jerusalem are broken down,
and its gates have been burned with fire.
Most of the people ignore God’s Law.
Rebuilding the walls was only the beginning.
We have many powerful enemies.
I recommend we turn
the accusation of sedition against Nehemiah.
Nehemiah is far away in Shushan.
Who is going to tell him?
This is my province!
Out here, I decide what to do.
I have a right to live where I choose,
and so do you.
They would need help to face what
was about to come next.
Every man must find
his own joy, and I intend to find mine.
Why should you complain
when everyone else approves?
If we let mere threats
frighten us into stopping, they will have
achieved their goal.
Are you going to wait
until they start killing us?
We’re powerless to stop this.
Do remember me favorably, O my God.
We know you’ll enjoy the convention.
And it’s my pleasure to announce
that we’ll conclude the convention on Sunday
with a new original song.
The song and lyrics are now available
on jw.org®.
The Governing Body requests that everyone in the congregation
please practice the new song before going to the convention.
If someone in your congregation needs help to download the song,
please help them and practice with them.
Then together we’ll sing out
with all of our heart to Jehovah’s praise.
That brings this month’s program to an end.
Please know that the Governing Body loves
all of you brothers and sisters very much.
From the World Headquarters of Jehovah’s Witnesses,
this is JW Broadcasting!

title: 성경 드라마 예고편: 느헤미야: “여호와의 기쁨이 여러분의 산성입니다”

en.text: Far from Israel lived a Jew
whom the king of Persia
trusted with his life.
He believed his people were carrying
on pure worship in Jerusalem
—until one day . . .
The walls of Jerusalem are broken down,
and its gates have been burned with fire.
Most of the people ignore God’s Law.
Rebuilding the walls was only the beginning.
We have many powerful enemies.
I recommend we turn
the accusation of sedition against Nehemiah.
Nehemiah is far away in Shushan.
Who is going to tell him?
This is my province!
Out here, I decide what to do.
I have a right to live where I choose,
and so do you.
They would need help to face what
was about to come next.
Every man must find
his own joy, and I intend to find mine.
Why should you complain
when everyone else approves?
If we let mere threats
frighten us into stopping, they will have
achieved their goal.
Are you going to wait
until they start killing us?
We’re powerless to stop this.
Do remember me favorably, O my God.

title: 존 에크란: 여호와의 손에 있는 진흙과 같이 되십시오 (로마 12:2)

ko.text: 여기 있는 이 돌과 진흙을 보실까요?
우리는 사탄의 손에서 단단한 돌같이 되어
“더는 이 세상 제도를 따라 틀 잡히지 말”라고 했죠.
내가 사랑하고 믿는 사람이 그렇게 한다면,
그러면 사탄이 우리를 틀 잡으려고 할 때
하지만 여호와께서 빚고 틀 잡아 주시려고 할 땐
우리를 틀 잡지 못하도록 막는 데 필요한,
단단한 돌 같은 특성 한 가지는 무엇일까요?
그분을 숭배하는 일을 중단하게 하려고 합니다.
러시아의 형제들에 관한 기사를 볼 때,
분명 우리 모두는 이런 생각을 하게 될 겁니다.
네, 우리는 사탄이 틀 잡으려고 할 때
형제들이 나타내고 있는 돌 같은 특성,
제가 감명 깊게 본 뉴스가 있는데,
수감되어 있는 형제들이 어떤 상태에 있는지 알고 싶다고 했습니다.
그 밖의 방법들을 저항하기 위해서도 용기가 필요합니다.
부활에 대해 돌 같은 희망을 갖고 힘을 내기 위해서는
신세계가 올 것이라는 돌 같은 용기와 믿음을 유지해야 하죠.
부드러운 진흙이 될 수 있는지 생각해 보겠습니다.
우리는 모두 당신이 손수 만드신 것입니다.”
나는 이 모양이 싫어요. 이렇게 만들지 마세요.”
우리는 여호와께서 빚고 틀 잡아 주시려고 할 때
이제, 여호와께서 우리를 빚고 틀 잡으실 때 나타내야 할
진흙 같은 특성 두 가지를 살펴보겠습니다.
여호와께서는 우리를 빚고 틀 잡아 주심으로,
우리가 이 세상 제도의 끝을 준비하면서
큰 환난으로 곧바로 이어질 사건들에 대비하도록 돕고 계십니다.
우린 어려운 시기에 무슨 지시가 있어도
솔로몬왕에 대해 좋은 말씀을 해 주셨는데요.
그는 코치에게 조언을 구해 놓고는 이렇게 말합니다.
우리가 순종을 나타낼 수 있는 좋은 기회입니다.
여행이나 다른 일들이 취소될 수 있습니다.
팔꿈치로 인사하라는 지침을 받을 수도 있습니다.
우리는 이런 규칙과 지침에 순종하기 위해
순종이 몸에 배게 할 수 있습니다.
그렇게 시간과 노력을 들여 연습할 때,
마지막 날에 살고 있음을 분명히 밝혀 주십니다.
그는 자기가 어느 시점에 와 있는지를
그게 마지막 바퀴가 아니라는 걸 몰랐던 겁니다.
우리도 다른 일을 하느라 너무 바쁜 나머지,
우리가 매일매일 내리는 결정에 나타나야 합니다.
형제 자매들과 그 점에 대해 대화하십시오.
그분의 손에 있는 진흙처럼 될 것입니다.

en.text: You know, a very simple way
to visualize Romans 12:2
is to use a rock and clay.
Now, we want to be like a rock
in Satan’s hands—resisting his molding.
But we want to be like clay
in Jehovah’s hands.
Now, being like a rock in Satan’s hand
really represents the first part of Romans 12:2
that says: “Stop being molded by this system of things.”
And being clay in Jehovah’s hands
is very similar to the thought
in the rest of Romans 12:2 that says
“Be transformed by making your mind over.”
Now, to illustrate the difference
between our reaction when Satan tries
to shape and mold us with this system of things
versus when Jehovah wants to.
I’d like you to think that maybe, you’re in a public place
—you’re at a shopping mall or someplace—
and a perfect stranger walks up behind you
and starts to massage your shoulders.
What would you do?
You would stiffen up and say: “Get away! What are you doing?”
But if someone you love and trust does that,
well, you might relax and have a very different reaction, right?
So, what is our reaction when Satan
wants to try to shape and mold us?
It’s being like a rock.
But when Jehovah wants to shape and mold us,
we want to be like clay.
Now, let’s consider one rocklike quality
that we need to resist Satan’s shaping and molding of us.
And that’s courage.
To start that discussion on courage,
let’s open our Bibles to a very straightforward,
simple statement at Psalm 56:3.
Psalm 56:3 says:
“When I am afraid, I put my trust in you.”
So Satan uses fear and intimidation and persecution
to get us to change our relationship with Jehovah,
to try to break our integrity, to stop us from worshipping Jehovah.
Now, when you read the accounts in JW News
about our brothers in Russia, I’m sure all of us have some reactions,
where you’re thinking, ‘Wow! How would I deal
with that kind of persecution?’
Or if you’re a wife, maybe you think,
‘Now, how would I deal with my husband being put into prison
and having these kinds of things done to him?’
Yes, in many ways, we are very proud
of the courage, the rocklike qualities,
that our brothers are showing when Satan tries to shape and mold them.
I was particularly moved when I read the account
about the brothers and sisters in Russia in Orenburg.
And here a group of brothers and sisters boldly went to the prison,
identified themselves as Jehovah’s Witnesses (at some risk of their own freedom),
and wanted to know how their brothers
were being treated in the prison.
Aren’t we really, truly proud of those kinds
of rocklike qualities that we see in our brothers and sisters?
But, now, it also takes courage
to resist other kinds of ways
that Satan is trying to mold and shape us.
It takes courage, for example, to change the channel
or to click the mouse away from bad entertainment.
Are we rocklike in that kind of courage?
It takes courage to face sickness or a terminal illness
and have the rocklike hope and strength
that there is going to be a resurrection.
It takes courage to watch the news these days
and see all that is going on in the world
and keep our rocklike courage and faith
that there is a new world coming
and that the end of this system is coming.
So the lesson for us is this:
Are we like a rock in Satan’s hands?
Or is it possible that we have become
soft and comfortable in this system of things?
Now, how are we doing
about being clay in Jehovah’s hands?
Isaiah 64:8
helps us
with this discussion about the clay
because it shows the choice that we’ve made—Isaiah 64:8.
It says: “But now, O Jehovah, you are our Father.
“We are the clay, and you are our Potter;
we are all the work of your hand.”
Now, sometimes when I’ve heard this read,
sometimes people say, “We are the clay, and you are the Potter.”
But, really, that word “our” is very important.
“We are the clay, and you are our  Potter.”
That means that we’ve made a choice
—that Jehovah is the one to shape and mold us.
Now, imagine clay that you go to shape and mold it, and it says:
“Ow! Hey, don’t do that! Hey, I don’t want to look like that.
Don’t change me like that.”
“OK, OK, OK.”
What kind of reaction are we having
when Jehovah is trying to shape and mold us?
Well, let’s consider two claylike qualities
that we can have when Jehovah is trying to shape and mold us.
First of all, obedience.
Now, it’s clear to all of us that Jehovah
is shaping and molding and preparing us
for the end of this system of things
and the events that are leading directly up to the great tribulation.
So will we be obedient when we get direction
—how to preach, how to do our meetings,
what assignment we may have during that turbulent time?
You know, yesterday Brother Splane
made some excellent comments about King Solomon.
Now, King Solomon had some divine instruction,
but he ignored it, and he basically said,
‘Well, you know, I can marry lots of foreign wives,
and it’s not going to have any effect on me.’
We don’t want to have that kind of attitude when it comes to divine instruction.
Or we could be like an athlete who hires a coach,
pays him lots of money, and says, “What can I do to be better?”
And the athlete says: “Well, you know, I’m the professional athlete.
I really don’t need to listen to what you have to say.”
So Jehovah is giving us counsel and advice.
We want to listen.
For example, this virus that is spreading around
is giving us an opportunity to see about being obedient.
We have many rules or guidelines that are being set for us.
We may be quarantined.
We may have trips and other things canceled.
We may be told to wash our hands
or to not shake hands, but elbow bump.
Now, of course, we can try hard
to be obedient to those rules and guidelines,
but we also have an opportunity to not just be obedient
to rules and guidelines
but be obedient to the principles behind them.
And in this case, often the principle is love of neighbor.
We’re trying to look out for others
with these rules and guidelines when it comes to the virus.
And, really, when you think about it,
any of the opportunities we have now
are a time to practice being obedient.
Really, view it as training for us.
We have an opportunity to practice being obedient for the future.
It’s at times like these that we can set a pattern of obedience,
because with time and effort and practice,
we can make obedience our first reaction
rather than a second reaction.
Well, what’s another claylike quality that we could have?
It’s spiritual focus.
Today, Jehovah is making it perfectly clear that we’re living in the last days.
Now, the people of Noah’s time,
“they took no note” of the time they were living in.
They didn’t have that claylike quality, and they were swept away.
I saw a video recently of an athlete doing a track meet.
They were running a race around the track,
and when this one athlete crossed the finish line,
he threw his hands up and he was absolutely jubilant that he had won the race.
But then he didn’t see anybody cheering for him,
and the rest of the runners were running.
He was too early. There was one more lap to go.
Well, he lost track of where he was.
He didn’t know that that wasn’t the last lap.
Well, we don’t want to lose track
of where we are in the race for life,
being so busy with doing other things.
Let the fact that we’re living in the last of the last days
influence our day-to-day decisions.
Become claylike, moldable —we’re living in the last days.
Pay attention to the Bible principles
that are mentioned to us in The Watchtower  and our meetings
and have good spiritual conversations.
And those conversations can help to remind us
of the time in which we’re living.
So the lesson for us is this:
You have chosen Jehovah to be your Potter.
So be good, obedient,
spiritually-focused clay in his hands.
Yes, we need to be like a rock in Satan’s hands,
and we need to be like clay in Jehovah’s hands.

你会有什么感觉？
你可能觉得毛骨悚然
跟他说
“走开！你要做什么？”
但如果是你的家人或朋友给你按摩
你有什么感受呢？
你肯定觉得很放松
当撒但想要塑造我们的时候
我们应该像石头一样坚硬
但是当耶和华想要塑造我们的时候
我们应该像陶泥一样柔软
那么，当撒但塑造我们的时候
我们可以怎样变得像石头一样坚硬呢？
一个方面就是要有勇气
说到勇气
我们可以先打开圣经
看一节简单明了的经文
在诗篇56:3
诗篇56:3说
“当我害怕时，我信赖你。”
所以撒但会迫害我们
他想让我们感到害怕
从而放弃与耶和华的宝贵关系
撒但想让我们不再忠于耶和华
不再崇拜他
大家在我们的网站上
看到有关俄罗斯弟兄姐妹的报导时
大概都会停下来想一下
“如果是我呢？
如果是我面对这样的迫害
会有什么样的反应呢？”
再或者
如果你是个妻子
你也许会想
“如果是我的丈夫被关进监狱里
受尽各种折磨
我会怎么面对呢？”
当撒但想要塑造俄罗斯的弟兄姐妹时
他们都像石块儿一样非常坚强
我们都为他们表现出来的勇气感到自豪
有一则新闻让我特别感动
就是俄罗斯奥伦堡的弟兄姐妹的经历
在那里有一群弟兄姐妹非常勇敢
他们跑到监狱去
说自己就是耶和华见证人
他们冒着被逮捕的风险这样做
因为他们
很想知道被囚的弟兄们现在怎么样
这些弟兄姐妹
像石块儿一样非常勇敢坚定
我们为他们感到自豪
另外
我们在做其他事情的时候
也需要有勇气才能不被撒但塑造
举例来说
当我们看到不好的娱乐节目时
我们需要有勇气
才能把它马上关掉或者转换频道
这时，我们会像石头一样坚硬吗？
当我们患了严重的疾病
甚至会有生命危险时
我们对复活的信心和希望
也像石头一样坚定吗？
现在连看新闻都需要勇气
这个世界变得越来越糟
我们需要有勇气才能面对
也需要坚信这个制度快要结束
新世界就要来临了
所以我们可以问问自己
我们对撒但来说好像石块儿一样吗？
还是我们在撒但的制度里
变得越来越柔软
觉得很舒服呢？
现在，我们再来看看
怎样在耶和华的手中做柔软的陶泥
我们一起看一看以赛亚书64:8
这节经文让我们看出
我们所做的一个选择
以赛亚书64:8
经文说
“但耶和华啊，你是我们的父亲
你是陶匠，我们是陶泥
我们全都是你亲手造的。”
大家都很熟悉这节经文
不过你留意到了吗，经文这里说
“你是陶匠，我们是陶泥。”
“你是陶匠”这句话表明
我们已经选择让耶和华作我们的陶匠
让他来塑造我们
想象一下你正在捏一块陶泥
但是陶泥对你说
“哦！嘿，别这样！
我不想变成这样，别这样捏我。”
“好，好，好，不捏你。”
那么当耶和华塑造我们的时候
我们会有怎样的反应呢？
我们要想在耶和华手中作柔软的陶泥
就需要培养两种特质
是什么呢？
首先，我们要学会服从
我们可以清楚地看出
耶和华正在塑造我们
装备我们
帮助我们做好准备
应对最后这段艰难的日子
以及即将来临的大患难
我们收到组织的指引时会乐意服从吗？
比如关于传道
关于聚会
以及在这段艰难的时期
组织给出的其他指引
斯普莱恩弟兄
曾在一个演讲里谈到了所罗门的事
所罗门得到了上帝的指引
但是他没有理会，他好像在说
“我就算娶了很多外族妻子
也不会受影响。”
我们在受到上帝指引时
可不想有这样的态度
又比如
一个运动员花了很多钱请了一个教练
他问教练：“我可以怎样提高呢？”
但他接着又说
“你看，我是个职业的运动员
根本不需要听你给我的建议。”
当耶和华给我们提出建议时
我们可不想这样
再举个例
最近在全球爆发的疫情
也让我们有机会表明
自己是不是愿意服从
组织发出了很多指引
也给了我们很多建议
我们可能需要隔离
有些计划不得不取消
我们也需要勤洗手
见面时也不会握手
而是用肘碰一下
当然
我们会努力服从这些规定和指引
不过
我们不是只表面上
服从这些规定和指引就够了
我们还会努力服从
这些规定和指引背后的原则
疫情期间
我们尤其要考虑的原则是
要爱人如己
我们遵守疫情期间的这些规定
就表明我们关心别人
请想一想
现在真的是很好的机会
让我们培养服从这种特质
我们真的应该把它视作一次很好的训练
我们好好善用这个机会
就能为将来做好准备
在这样的情况下
我们要学会把服从变成一种习惯
我们付出努力，不断练习
一段时间后
我们在收到指引时
就能乐意服从，并立刻照着去做
要像陶泥一样柔软
我们还需要培养什么特质呢？
就是要保持警醒
今天
耶和华帮助我们清楚看出
现在就是最后的日子
挪亚日子的人
毫不留意他们正处于什么时代
他们没有保持警醒
就被洪水淹死了
不久以前
我在电视上看了一场田径比赛
选手们都在圆形跑道上跑
有一个运动员跑过了终点
他高举双手开始欢呼
以为自己赢得了冠军
不过，他发现没有人为他鼓掌
其他选手都还在跑呢
原来他高兴得太早了
还有一圈没跑呢！
这个运动员
他忘记了自己到底跑了多少圈
他不知道
实际上他需要再跑一圈呢！
在永生的赛程上
我们可不想像这个运动员一样
忘记了自己跑到哪儿了
我们不想因任何事而分心
我们要记得
我们正生活在最后日子的最后阶段
我们在做任何决定的时候
都要记得这一点
我们要像陶泥一样柔软
乐意接受塑造
要留意圣经原则
这些原则
我们可以通过守望台和聚会学到
我们也要多和弟兄姐妹谈论这些事
这能帮助我们记住
我们正生活在什么时代
总结一下，我们学到什么呢？
我们选择了耶和华作我们的陶匠
所以，我们要乐意服从，保持警醒
没错，对撒但来说
我们要像石块儿一样坚硬
但在耶和华手中
我们要像陶泥一样柔软

title: 로버트 시렌코: 자존감을 높이려고 장난 삼아 이성을 대하지 마십시오 (디모데 전서 5:2)

ko.text: 젊은 여자들에게는 극히 순결하게 누이에게 하듯이” 대하라고 말합니다.
젊은 남자들에겐 극히 순결하게 남자 형제에게 하듯 해야 하죠.
이 성구가 나온 파수대 기사 “우리는 순결함을 유지할 수 있습니다”에서는
재미 삼아 이성에게 낭만적인 관심을 보이는 행동에 관해 언급합니다.
그런데 이 행동은 자기 자신에 대한 합당한 견해와 관련이 있습니다.
그럼 순결함, 이성을 대하는 태도, 자신에 대한 견해는 어떤 관련이 있을까요?
먼저, 순결함이란 생각과 행동에 있어 깨끗한 상태를 말합니다.
즉 성적 욕망이나 성적 공상을 불러일으키는 것들에서
순결함을 유지하려면 재미 삼아 이성에게 관심을 보여서는 안 됩니다.
진지한 의도 없이 이성에게 낭만적인 관심을 보이는 행동입니다.
낭만적인 관심이 있는 척하지만, 실제로 결혼하려는 의도가 없는 거죠.
이것은 부적절한 말, 눈빛, 스킨십, 어조,
은근한 미소, 심지어 옷차림이나 서 있는 자세, 걸음걸이로도 나타납니다.
독신들이 다른 독신이나 기혼자에게 그런 행동을 하기도 하고,
결혼한 사람들이 독신이나 다른 기혼자에게 그렇게 하기도 합니다.
부도덕이 만연한 이 세상에서는 동성 간에도 그런 일들이 벌어지죠.
독신들이 단지 재미 삼아 낭만적 관심을 주고받는 것도 합당하지 않지만,
이미 결혼한 사람이 다른 이성에게 그런 관심을 나타내는 것은
한 가정 법률 변호사가 이런 흥미로운 말을 했습니다.
대부분 이혼하려는 이유는 배우자가 바람을 피우기 때문입니다.
하나같이 그 관계는 딱히 나쁠 게 없어 보이는,
재미 삼아 관심을 나타내는 행동으로 시작되죠.”
고의로 다른 사람의 감정을 가지고 노는 건 잔인한 행동입니다.
그릇된 욕망과 기대를 불러일으켜서 감정적으로 큰 상처를 남길 수 있죠.
더 나아가 음행이나 간음까지 범하게 될 수 있습니다.
그런 사람들은 결코 좋은 친구도, 훌륭한 배우자도 될 수 없습니다.
세상에선 흔히들 장난 삼아 이성과 관심을 주고받으면서,
네, 이성에 대한 이런 행동은 자신에 대한 견해와 관련이 있는 것이죠.
재미 삼아 이성에게 관심을 보이는 행동은 자존심을 한껏 높이려는 자기중심적인 태도이며,
그런 사람들은 자기만족을 느끼거나 자신의 가치가 높아지는 느낌을 받기 위해
불완전한 인간은 자존감이 쉽게 극단으로 치우치는데요,
사도 바울의 말은 우리가 자기 자신에 대해 균형 잡힌 생각을 갖게 해 줍니다.
함께 로마서 12:3을 펴서 바울이 어떤 말을 했는지 보실까요?
“나에게 베풀어진 과분한 친절을 통해서 그곳에 있는 여러분 모두에게 말합니다.
자기 자신에 대해 마땅히 생각해야 하는 것 이상으로 생각하지 마십시오.
오히려 하느님께서 각자에게 주신 믿음의 분량에 따라 건전한 정신으로 생각하십시오.”
자기를 존중하는 마음은 필요하지만 지나치면 자만심이 됩니다.
자존감이 너무 낮은 사람도 있고, 너무 높은 사람도 있는데,
바울은 “그곳에 있는 여러분 모두에게 말합니다”라고 썼죠.
자기 자신을 지나치게 중요시하거나 무가치한 사람으로 여기는
바울은 이 구절에서 ‘생각하다’라는 표현을 세 번이나 사용했는데,
그는 ‘자기 자신에 대해 마땅히 생각해야 하는 것 이상으로 생각하지 말고
따라서 자기 자신에 대해 어떻게 생각하는지가 아주 중요하죠.
먼저, 자존감이 너무 낮은 경우를 살펴볼까요?
바울은 자신을 어느 정도 가치 있게 생각하는 게 필요하다고 했죠.
겸허한 그리스도인이 되려면 열등감을 가져야 한다는 말이 아니었습니다.
우리는 헌신을 통해 여호와와 개인적인 관계를 맺었고
그분의 눈에 각자가 귀중하고 소중하다는 사실을 확신해야 합니다.
여호와께서 보시는 것만큼 자신을 가치 있게 생각하지 않는 것이죠.
바울은 로마서 12장의 앞 부분에서 도움이 되는 말을 또 했는데요.
“형제 여러분, 나는 하느님의 동정심으로 여러분에게 호소합니다.
여러분의 몸을 거룩하고 하느님께서 받아들이실 만한 산 희생 제물로 바치십시오.
그것이 여러분이 이지력으로 드리는 신성한 봉사입니다.”
우리는 모두 이렇게 하기 위해 정말 애쓰고 있죠?
우린 여호와께 헌신했고 거룩한 표준에 따라 살려고 힘쓰고 있지 않습니까?
신성한 봉사를 드리면서 왕국을 위해 희생을 치르고 있지 않습니까?
하느님은 그 모든 걸 보고 크게 기뻐하시죠.
우리 모두는 여호와의 눈에 큰 가치가 있기 때문에,
이성에게 그런 경박한 행동을 해서 자존감을 높일 필요가 없습니다.
그러면 자존감이 너무 높은 경우는 어떠합니까?
그런 사람들은 자신감을 얻고, 자중심을 키우려고 하다가
그들은 자기 자신을 과대평가하며 다른 사람을 사려 깊게 대하지 않습니다.
장난 삼아 이성을 대하는 사람이 딱 그러하죠.
그 점에 관해 바울은 로마서 12:16에서 이렇게 조언하는데요, 16절입니다.
높은 것에 마음을 두지 말고 낮은 것에 이끌리십시오.
네, 자기 자신에 대해 건전하고 균형 잡힌 시각을 갖는 것이 중요합니다.
우리는 바울이 생각하는 방식에 대해 경고한 것을 기억해야 합니다.
균형 잡힌 자존감을 갖는 것은 우리의 생각에 달려 있기 때문입니다.
그의 말처럼 우리는 “건전한 정신으로 생각”해야 합니다.
다시 말해, 자기 자신을 있는 그대로 솔직하게 바라보아야 합니다.
또한 예수께서 남기신 본은 우리에게 언제나 유익한데요, 함께 살펴보시죠.
“그리스도 예수 안에 있던 이러한 정신 태도를 여러분 안에 간직하십시오.
장악하려고 곧 하느님과 동등하게 되려고 생각하지 않으셨습니다.
오히려 자신을 비우고 종의 모습을 취하여 사람이 되셨습니다.
그뿐 아니라, 사람으로 오셨을 때에 자신을 낮추어.”
네, 예수께선 건전한 정신을 갖고 계셨기 때문에
자존감이 모든 면에서 완전히 균형 잡혀 있었고, 결코 극단에 치우치지 않으셨습니다.
자신에 대해 마땅히 생각해야 하는 것 이상으로 생각지 않으셨죠.
예수께서 마리아나 마르다 혹은 다른 여자들을
장난 삼아 대하면서 자존심을 높이려는 모습을 상상할 수 있겠습니까?
바울은 예수의 정신 태도를 우리 안에 간직하라고 했죠.
앞서 읽은 빌립보서 2장의 문맥을 살펴보면 그 점을 더 잘 알 수 있는데요,
오히려 겸손하게 남을 자기보다 더 나은 사람으로 여기십시오.
여러분 자신의 일에만 관심을 갖지 말고 다른 사람들의 일에도 관심을 가지십시오.”
그러므로 자신에 대해 합당한 견해를 갖고,
이성에게 부적절한 관심을 보이지 않도록 합시다.
그래서 모두에게 계속 순결함을 나타내도록 합시다.

en.text: The scripture that we are highlighting today
is 1 Timothy 5:2,
which instructs Christian men
to treat “older women as mothers, . . .
“younger women as sisters,
with all chasteness.”
Of course, the reverse is also true:
Christian women should treat older men as fathers
and younger men as brothers, with all chasteness.
This is taken from the Watchtower  article entitled “We Can Remain Chaste,”
one portion of which discusses the matter
of flirting with the opposite sex.
My discussion is going to focus
on keeping one’s ego in check.
Now, what are the connections between chasteness,
flirting, and ego?
Well, let’s start with chasteness,
that is, purity in thought and action.
And it means “being free from all taint
of what is lewd or salacious,”
that is, what arouses or appeals
to sexual desire or imagination.
And one way to maintain our chastity
is to avoid the practice of flirting.
And what is that?
Well, flirting means ‘behaving amorously
without serious intent.’
Such a person signals romantic interest
with no intention of marriage.
It may involve an inappropriate remark, a look,
a touch, the tone of voice, a coy smile,
even the way one dresses, stands, or carries oneself.
Some single people flirt with each other
or with married folks.
Some married people flirt with single people or with other married people.
And in this degenerate world,
men flirt with men, and women flirt with women.
But it’s inappropriate for single people to send romantic signals
to each other just for amusement,
and it is morally wrong for married people
to direct that kind of attention to a person outside of their marriage.
Interestingly, an attorney who practices family law reported:
“I talk to plenty of people who are going through divorce.
“In most cases, these marriages are ending
“because someone had an affair, and in all of those cases,
the affair started out as just a little harmless flirting.”
Of course, flirting is not harmless.
To intentionally toy with the feelings of others is cruel.
It can arouse wrong desires and expectations
that may result in a lot of emotional pain.
It can also lead to worse things: fornication or adultery.
It’s no wonder that it has been said
that flirts make poor friends and worse marriage mates.
Well, in the world, flirting is viewed as a sport,
and it’s done to increase one’s own self-esteem.
Now, that’s where ego comes into the picture.
Ego is “the sense of one’s own worth.”
One source on the subject of flirting says
that it is a gigantic ego boost, an ego trip,
because the flirt is doing something for his or her own gratification,
to make himself or herself feel better.
But there’s something the apostle Paul wrote
that can balance our thinking about this trait of self-esteem
that imperfect humans tend to take to an extreme.
So let’s turn to Romans 12:3
and see what Paul has to say,
Romans 12:3;
he wrote:
“For through the undeserved kindness given to me,
“I tell everyone there among you not to think
“more of himself than it is necessary to think,
“but to think so as to have a sound mind,
each one as God has given to him a measure of faith.”
Well, self-esteem is defined
as “confidence and satisfaction in oneself,”
and it can range from self-respect to self-conceit.
Some people have too little of it; some people have too much of it.
So Paul wrote: “I tell everyone there among you.”
And what he tells us is how to avoid either extreme
of thinking too much or too little of our worth in God’s eyes.
And Paul pinpointed exactly where the problem lies
because three times in the verse he used the phrase “to think.”
He wrote that a person is “not to think more of himself
than it is necessary to think, but to think so as to have a sound mind.”
So it matters how one thinks about himself or herself.
Consider the person who has too little self-esteem.
Now, Paul said it is necessary to think something of ourselves.
It was never intended that modest, moral Christians
had to develop an inferiority complex.
Our dedicated relationship with Jehovah
makes each of us precious and desirable to God,
and we should really believe that.
So the one with low self-esteem
is not thinking enough of the right things about himself.
And what Paul wrote two verses earlier
in Romans chapter 12 can help.
So let’s look at verse 1 of Romans 12:
“Therefore, I appeal to you by the compassions of God, brothers,
“to present your bodies as a living sacrifice,
“holy and acceptable to God,
a sacred service with your power of reason.”
Now, doesn’t that describe what we are endeavoring to do?
Haven’t we dedicated our lives to Jehovah?
Aren’t we striving to live holy lives?
Aren’t we performing sacred service
and making sacrifices for the sake of the Kingdom?
Certainly.
And all that is most acceptable to our God.
Our lives have real worth in Jehovah’s eyes,
so no one should have to resort to frivolous flirting to boost their ego.
Now, consider the person who has too much self-esteem.
In his efforts to gain self-confidence, he has overshot the mark
and has crossed the line
between cultivating self-respect and arrogance.
He’s overestimated his own worth and thinks too highly of himself,
and he may behave in an unpleasant way toward others,
as does the uncaring flirt.
Well, Paul said something that applies here too
at Romans 12:16,
verse 16:
“Have the same attitude toward others as toward yourselves;
“do not set your mind on lofty things, but be led along with the lowly things.
Do not become wise in your own eyes.”
So it’s important that we have a healthy,
balanced view of our own worth.
And remember, it is the way of our thinking
that Paul was cautioning us about,
because that governs whether our self-esteem is in balance or not.
No wonder that Paul said that we ought “to think so as to have a sound mind,”
that is, to have thoughts that are based on a true premise about ourselves.
Since it always helps to look at the example of Jesus,
let’s do that, in this case, by turning to Philippians chapter 2,
Philippians 2,
beginning with verse 5;
it says: “Keep this mental attitude in you
“that was also in Christ Jesus, who, although he was existing in God’s form,
“gave no consideration to a seizure, namely, that he should be equal to God.
“No, but he emptied himself and took a slave’s form and became human.
More than that, when he came as a man, he humbled himself.”
Well, in every facet of his life,
Jesus’ sound mind kept his self-esteem in perfect balance.
He never had too little or too much.
He never thought more of himself than was necessary to think.
We can never imagine Jesus trying to boost his ego
by flirting with Mary and Martha
or with any other woman who was in his company.
Paul said, ‘keep this mental attitude in you’ —Jesus’ mental attitude.
We should think the way Jesus thinks.
Now, note the context in which we find this admonition
in Philippians 2
by reading verses 3 and 4:
“Do nothing out of contentiousness or out of egotism,
“[one Bible says: “Never act
“from motives of rivalry or personal vanity”]
“but with humility consider others superior to you,
“as you look out not only for your own interests,
but also for the interests of others.”
So we keep our egos in check,
we stay clear of any speech, dress, or flirtatious actions
that could be viewed as provocative,
and we thus maintain our chasteness toward everyone.

cn.text: 今天我们要讨论提摩太前书5:2
经文提醒基督徒男子
“劝年长的女子像劝母亲
劝年轻的女子像劝姐妹
举止态度要完全贞洁。”
反过来说也一样
基督徒女子也要用同样的方式
对待年长和年轻的男子
我们会讨论一篇守望台文章
题名为“保持思想纯洁，品行端正”
这篇文章提到了跟异性调情的一些问题
我们要学习控制自己的思想
用正确的方式看待自己
那么，贞洁、调情和自骄心之间
有什么关连呢？
我们先来谈谈贞洁
也就是在思想和行为上保持纯洁
意思是
我们完全没有猥亵下流的想法
我们也不会有不道德的欲望和幻想
保持贞洁的一个方法是
要避免跟别人调情
调情是什么意思呢？
调情的意思是
一个人用轻浮的方式对人表达爱意
或者是一个人没有结婚的打算
却用浪漫的举动吸引对方
调情可能包括一句暧昧的话，一个眼神
肢体碰触，勾引的语调，挑逗的微笑
甚至是一个人的打扮，站姿和动作
有些单身的人
跟其他单身的或已经结婚的人调情
另外，有些已婚的人
也跟单身的或已婚的人调情
在现在这个堕落的世界里
男人和男人调情，女人和女人调情
一个单身的人，不应该只为了好玩
就用浪漫的举动吸引别人
同样的，那些已婚的人
也不该用这种方法吸引配偶以外的人
有一个专门处理离婚案件的律师，他说
“在我处理过的离婚案件当中
大部分夫妻离婚
都是因为对方感情出轨，有了外遇
在这些案件中
外遇都是从一个
看起来无伤大雅的调情开始。”
调情当然不是无伤大雅的
玩弄别人的感情是很残忍的
因为这会让人产生错误的欲望和期待
深深地伤害别人
调情也可能演变成淫乱和通奸
难怪有人说
“喜欢调情的人不会是个好朋友
更不会是个好配偶。”
很多人认为调情没什么大不了
调情甚至能增加一个人的自信心
但其实这跟自骄心有关
调情会让人产生自骄心
一份关于调情的资料提到
调情会大大助长人的自骄心
一个喜欢调情的人只为了满足自己的欲望
想让自己更受人欢迎，更有吸引力
用这种方式抬高自己的价值
现在让我们看看使徒保罗说的话
他说的会帮助我们不完美的人
对自信心有合理适当的看法
让我们打开圣经到罗马书12:3
让我们看看保罗在这里说什么
罗马书12:3
保罗说
“凭着上帝赐给我的分外恩典
我对你们每个人说
不要过度看重自己
要思想健全
按照上帝赐给每个人的信心衡量自己。”
一个有自信的人会满意自己所做的
自信心会让人有自尊
但不留意的话也可能让人自大
有些人没什么自信，有些人却太有自信
所以保罗才说：“我对你们每个人说”
保罗提醒我们
要避免太过自信，觉得自己很重要
也不要认为自己一文不值
保罗很清楚地指出问题在哪里
因为他告诉我们要怎么看自己
要怎么衡量自己
我们再看看经文怎么说
经文说
“不要过度看重自己，要思想健全”
经文说得很清楚
问题的症结就在我们怎么看待自己
我们先谈谈那些对自己没有自信的人
保罗鼓励我们
我们还是要对自己有一定程度的自信
基督徒应该有谦虚的精神
但不应该觉得自己毫无价值
我们既然献身给耶和华
就应该相信
我们在他眼中是非常宝贵的、非常重要的
所以一个基督徒如果没有自信
可能就是因为他没有用耶和华的观点看待自己
保罗在罗马书12:1 所写的话
会帮助我们看出这点
让我们看看罗马书12:1
“因此，弟兄们
我凭着上帝的怜恤恳求你们
要把身体像祭牲一样献上
是活的，是圣洁的，是上帝接纳的
这样，你们就是用理智敬奉上帝。”
这节经文很清楚地提到
我们已经做了或正在做的事情
我们已经献身给耶和华
我们按照他的标准过圣洁的生活
我们忠贞地崇拜他
尽力支持宣扬王国的工作
这些事情都会让耶和华高兴
所以我们在他的眼中是非常宝贵的
因此，任何人都不应该用调情的方式
增加自己的自信心
现在我们再来谈谈那些太有自信的人
太过有自信其实并不是有自尊的表现
这样的人自信过了头，反而变成了自大
他把自己的价值提升得太高
把自己看得太重要
他不尊重别人，也不在乎别人的感受
调情的人就是这样
保罗在罗马书12:16也提到类似的事情
16节说
“你怎么看待自己，也要怎么看待别人
不要心高气傲，倒要甘于卑微
不要自以为有智慧。”
所以我们要对自己的价值
有合理平衡的看法
要记得
保罗提醒我们要控制自己的思想
因为我们怎么看待自己
会影响到我们怎样衡量自己的价值
难怪保罗告诉我们，我们要“思想健全”
也就是说我们要认识自己
也要诚实地看待自己
耶稣总是为我们立下优良的榜样
让我们看看圣经怎么说
请打开圣经
到腓立比书2章
我们从第5节开始读
“基督耶稣有怎样的思想态度
你们也要有怎样的思想态度
他本来以上帝的形态存在
却从没有想过要夺取跟上帝同等的地位
他放弃了一切，接受了奴隶的形态
成为一个人
不但这样，他成为人以后，还行事谦卑”
耶稣在生活的每一方面
都反应出健全的思想和自信心
他从没有觉得自己毫无价值
也不会过度自信，太过看重自己
耶稣绝对不会为了增加自己的自信心
跟马利亚、马大或其他女子调情
所以我们应该像保罗所说的一样
耶稣有怎样的思想态度
我们也要有同样的思想态度
现在让我们看看这段话的上文
保罗提出什么劝告
腓立比书2:3,4
“做什么都不要争强好胜，不要自命不凡”
请留意这里的脚注
脚注说
“又译‘不要以自我为中心’”
“要谦卑，看别人比自己优秀
不要只关心自己，也要关心别人。”
所以我们不应该有自骄心
我们所说的话，穿着打扮和行为举止
都不该让人产生错误的欲望
这样我们就能在一切事上保持贞洁

titles.ko: 로버트 시렌코: 자존감을 높이려고 장난 삼아 이성을 대하지 마십시오 (디모데 전서 5:2)
titles.en: Robert Ciranko: Avoid Flirting and Ego (1 Tim. 5:2)
titles.cn: 罗伯特·斯朗科：远避调情和自骄心（提前5:2）

title: 성경 읽기의 질을 높이는 방법—발췌 영상

cn.text: 当阅读圣经时
试着去了解记载的全貌
我们来看一些圣经里著名的记载
说明怎样运用想象力
你是在继亲家庭里长大的吗？
如果是，你的处境就和雅各的儿子约瑟相似
约瑟有十个同父异母的兄长
在一个大家族里长大
现在，你试着观察这个家族
你想了解家族各个成员是怎样融洽地互动
又或是怎样彼此不合
你会怎样着手呢？
首先，写下每个成员的一些特征
例如约瑟和他同父异母的哥哥
犹大
西缅
利未
但、拿弗他利等等
你对他们有多了解呢？
写下他们的个性
想想他们怎样彼此相处
有时圣经记载了一个人的事件
但我们不要忘记
每个人的行为都可能会影响到其他人
所以，当你读到某个事件发生时
想想谁会受到影响
举一个例子
在创世记
我们读到雅各的儿子吕便和璧拉发生关系
这无疑会对其他人造成影响
谁是吕便呢？
他是利亚的长子
谁又是璧拉呢？
她是拉结的女仆
利亚和拉结之间的关系
可能一直就有点紧张
尤其当你考虑到她们当初是怎样嫁给雅各的
她们的态度又会不会影响到她们的孩子呢？
要把这些因素都考虑进去
然而，璧拉也有孩子
分别是但和拿弗他利
当他们知道他们的大哥和母亲乱伦
他们会有什么感觉呢？
这又会造成另一种紧张的气氛
将这一切都考虑进去
我们就能看清整个家族发生了什么事
你可能会以为约瑟17岁时
他的哥哥们，也许已经30几岁
有些甚至大到可以当他的爸爸了
不过实情并不是这样
事实上，约瑟和他最大的哥哥吕便
只有相差7岁而已
雅各的11个儿子
其实是在他服事拉班7年当中所生下来的
这怎么可能呢？
当然有可能
因为雅各有2个妻子和2个妾
所以孩子们出生的时间不一定会相差9个月
有些孩子可能几乎同时出生
他们的年龄可能差不了多少
当约瑟17岁被卖为奴隶时
他的大哥最多只有24岁
他有些哥哥也才大他一两岁而已
所以我们谈的是一群十多岁
或二十出头的青年人
这也许可以说明
为什么他们有些人会有这样冲动的行为
谈完了儿子们
接下来，我们来谈谈他们的父亲雅各
我们可以从他身上学到很多
雅各是一个有属灵思想的人
打算结婚的年轻弟兄姐妹
你们可以好好想想
雅各不顾一切地维护他和耶和华的友谊
我们会来看一个例子
我读的时候
你们可以留意画面上的经文
我们要谈谈跟婚姻有关的事
经文说
我们学到什么呢？
雅各没有随便找个人
也许是信奉异教的女子结婚
他没有说
“7年太久了，我宁愿找个非利士女子结婚。”
他愿意等待
好能跟一个愿意跟他一起崇拜耶和华的人结婚
年轻人，只要你甘愿等候，就可以肯定
耶和华也一定会祝福你
其实，雅各也挺浪漫的
请留意创世记29:20
经文说
多么诗情画意！
雅各可能从观察他的父母，以撒和利百加
学习如何爱护妻子
我们从创世记26:8就能看出
他父母的婚姻有多稳固
创世记26:8
经文说
很显然地，以撒和利百加的关系非常亲密
婚姻十分美满
我们还可以从雅各身上学到什么呢？
创世记25:27提到有趣的一点
经文说
雅各喜欢住在帐幕，是个爱家的人
所以在便雅悯出生之前
他可能常和年纪最小的约瑟在一起
所以感情深厚
虽然雅各喜欢住在帐幕里，但他也绝不胆小
他不但身体强壮
也是一个属灵的人
年轻的弟兄可以学到什么呢？
我们知道你想变得更强壮
但应该先留意属灵的健康
有一次
雅各给他的儿子们上了宝贵的一课
教导他们怎样化解家人之间的纠纷
这个事件记载在创世记32章
我们可以学习雅各的榜样
32:6谈到雅各的哥哥以扫
带了400人来迎接雅各
在此之前，他们已经有20年没见面了
当初可不是因为一些小事而分开的
事实上，早在20年前，他们分手时
以扫就发誓
有一天他一定要杀死雅各
因为雅各从父亲那边得到祝福
让他非常不高兴
当以扫来见雅各时，为什么要带400人呢？
圣经没有说
但很可能是为了显示自己现在多么尊贵强大
雅各为此有什么反应呢？
和哥哥针锋相对吗？
用耶和华给他的祝福
表明自己的尊贵强大吗？
他有重提往事？
或者和哥哥争论吗？
说
“我一直都是对的，以扫，你错了”
他有要求对方道歉吗？
他并没有这么做
雅各无疑有很多可以自夸的地方
耶和华也给他许多祝福
在较早之前
我们谈到耶和华的天使向他显现，说
“我是耶和华
你祖父亚伯拉罕的上帝和以撒的上帝
我要把你现在躺卧之地赐给你和你的苗裔
我与你同在
无论你到哪里去，我都必保护你......
我决不离弃你。”
这是多么大的祝福！
还有，在雅各见以扫的前一晚
雅各跟天使摔跤
结果呢
得到耶和华所赐的福
他没有因此夸耀起来
相反地，他表现谦卑
甚至在他的妻子和11个儿子面前
向他的哥哥一连七次俯伏下拜
雅各没有用武力
自吹自擂的话
或武器来解决纠纷
而是谦卑自抑，像个真男人
一个真正属灵的人

title: “여호와께서 보이신 충성스러운 사랑을 주의 깊이 살펴보십시오”

ko.text: 전 제가 사랑을 나타내고 있다고 생각했지만
전 17살 때 칼 형제와 그레이스 자매를 처음 만났어요.
칼 형제는 제게 영적 아버지가 돼 주었죠.
저도 형제 곁에 있어 주려고 노력했어요.
새로운 책임이 한꺼번에 너무 많이 몰려왔죠.
다른 사람을 위해 시간을 낼 수 있을 것 같았죠.
그렇게 갑자기 돌아가실 줄 몰랐다고 하면서
사랑을 나타낼 기회를 다시는 놓치고 싶지 않았습니다.
그때 사랑을 더 온전히 나타내는 법을 배운 게
앞으로 있을 일을 대비하는 데 도움이 됐습니다.
제가 사랑을 나타내기 위해 계속 노력하길
이제 전 칼 형제와 수백 년의 우정을 쌓아 왔습니다.

en.text: Thinking back,
I thought I knew what it meant to show love,
but I had a lot to learn.
Come on.
You’ve been at this for hours.
You need sleep.
Just five minutes.
Ben, Carl’s been calling.
You really should pay him another visit.
Grace says he’s not doing too good.
I will.
I promise —just as soon as I get past this talk.
I’d known Carl and Grace since I was 17.
Carl had been my spiritual dad.
He was always there for me.
And with him being in and out
of the hospital, I tried to be there for them.
But I’d just been so busy.
It seemed like so many new responsibilities
hit me all at once.
Brother Capra, do you have a second?
Hey, Kev.
Uhh, maybe a little later, OK?
But I figured that once my schedule freed up,
I’d make more time for everyone, including Carl.
What I didn’t realize
is how quickly time can run out.
Grace said no one could know
he’d pass so suddenly and not to beat myself up about it.
But I knew I would lament that decision
for a long time.
I never again
wanted to miss an opportunity to show love.
Brother Capra, do you have a second?
Hey, Kevin. How’s it going?
Good . . .
I realized that learning to show love more fully then,
would help prepare us for what lay ahead.
Eventually, showing love
would call for even greater sacrifices.
Hands up! Get down!
Get down! Get down!
On the floor! On the floor!
Where are they?
Where are they?
Answer me!
I know you know where they are.
I’m so glad that I never gave up in learning to show love
and that Jehovah never gave up on me.
Now when I see Carl,
I have centuries of happy memories,
centuries of showing him and all of my brothers
and sisters loyal love.

en.text: ‎In chapter 17, we learned
‎about Gog’s attack on Jehovah’s people.

‎about what the coalition of nations will do.

‎That title comes from Ezekiel 38:18:
‎“‘On that day, the day when Gog invades the land of Israel,’
‎“declares the Sovereign Lord Jehovah,
‎‘my great rage will flare up.’”
‎As we study this thrilling information,

‎What provokes Jehovah’s great rage?
‎Why will his enemies not have valid cause
‎to be surprised when he unleashes his wrath?

‎Just think:
‎During the great tribulation just ahead,
‎pure worshippers will witness something truly spectacular
‎—how Jehovah will stand up for his people
‎and sanctify his holy name.
‎May this chapter move you to do all you can
‎to promote pure worship now.

en.text: ‎Have you ever wondered how Jehovah views you?
‎Some of our dear brothers and sisters
‎struggle with feelings of unworthiness.
‎It’s important for us to know that Jehovah God
‎loves and values each of his worshippers,
‎and this includes you.
‎Chapter 20 of the Pure Worship book
‎discusses the heartwarming encouragement
‎we can receive from Ezekiel’s last vision.
‎The title is “Allot the Land as an Inheritance,”
‎based on Ezekiel 45:1.
‎Please read that with me:
‎“When you allot the land as an inheritance,
‎“you should offer as a contribution to Jehovah
‎“a holy portion out of the land.
‎“Its length should be 25,000 cubits,
‎“and its width, 10,000 cubits.
‎Its entire area will be a holy portion.”
‎As you study this chapter, you will learn this reassuring lesson:
‎No matter how modest our responsibility
‎in the earthly part of God’s organization may be,
‎each of us has a secure place in the spiritual paradise.
‎How loving of Jehovah
‎to give Ezekiel a vision that’s filled
‎with such encouragement and assurance!
‎May this chapter help you to become fully convinced
‎that you are precious to Jehovah
‎and that he values all that you do in his service.
